structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation makes direct equity investments in innovative startup and growth-stage companies operating in or willing to relocate to Baltimore City. The Foundation invests in promising startups with proprietary innovations and provides growth capital to mature companies creating employment opportunities in Baltimore City. Investments are designed to generate above-market financial returns while creating jobs and delivering significant social and economic benefits to the community. The Foundation invests across diverse sectors including medical devices, diagnostics, materials, green energy, aerospace, and healthcare technologies. Beyond capital, the Foundation offers value-added support through experience, knowledge, and network connections. The Board of Trustees considers investment requests on a rolling basis five times per year during scheduled Board meetings.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct equity investments provided to for-profit companies with proprietary innovations and growth capital to mature companies. Initial investments typically range from $150,000 to $500,000. The Foundation prefers to invest alongside other sophisticated investors at closing. The Foundation accepts investment requests on a rolling basis and considers proposals five times per year during scheduled Board meetings. Beyond capital, the Foundation provides value-added support including experience, knowledge base, and network connections to portfolio companies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Five times per year; reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings
structured_extraction.program_audience: Innovative for-profit companies operating in or willing to relocate to Baltimore City, including promising startups with proprietary innovations and mature companies creating employment opportunities and generating social and economic benefits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital for business operations, expansion, innovation commercialization, and growth in Baltimore City; funds support companies creating employment opportunities in the community
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Companies must be operating in or willing to relocate headquarters and principal place of operations to Baltimore City, or be creating jobs in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit company
Must be operating in or willing to relocate to Baltimore City or creating jobs in Baltimore City
Company must have competitive advantage and/or proprietary innovation
Substantial commercial market for the innovation exists
Product or solution must have positive social or economic benefit
Company must create jobs, particularly low-skill or semi-skilled jobs
Company likely to produce above-market returns
Company leverages local strengths and resources (manufacturing, laboratories, universities, state biotech tax credit, etc.)
For startups: demonstrate promise and innovation
For mature companies: be expanding business operations in Baltimore City
Submit Company Introduction with pitchdeck or executive summary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Company Introduction with a pitchdeck or executive summary through the online application portal. Upon submission, you will receive a confirmation email. The Foundation's finance team may contact you with questions or schedule a pitch meeting. Applications are reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings. The Board of Trustees considers all requests and notifies applicants of funding decisions in a timely manner. The Foundation typically reviews only one submission from a company within a one-year period. See the Direct Investment Application Process page for detailed submission requirements.

The Foundation provides seed funding for innovative pilots, support for ongoing community programs and services, and funding for capital projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Foundation offers two grant processes: Small Grants (requests of $10,000 or less, reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline) and Regular Grants (requests greater than $10,000, reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings). Grants support seed funding for innovative pilots, ongoing community programs and services, and capital projects.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small Grant applicants: new applicants must sign up for an information session, then submit application through the grant portal. Regular Grant applicants: new applicants submit a letter of inquiry to grants@abell.org, then submit full application through the grant portal at abell.org/apply. Returning applicants can log into the grant portal to submit applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides grant funding to non-profit organizations, government agencies, and fiscally sponsored projects working to enhance the quality of life in Baltimore City. Regular grants are for requests of $10,000 or more and are reviewed five times per year according to a published schedule at the Board of Trustees meetings. First-time applicants must submit a letter of inquiry first, while returning applicants and those with verified alignment to the Foundation's priorities can proceed directly to full application submission. Grant funding can be used for seed funding for startups and pilots, support for ongoing projects, capital grants for construction or renovation, general operating support, and outreach and advocacy efforts. Grant recipients are typically required to submit interim and post-grant reports including narrative descriptions of project progress and accounting of funds expended.

structured_extraction.program_name: CollegeBound College Retention Program (retention support with last-dollar scholarships)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides financial assistance through Last Dollar Scholarships (up to $3,000 annually) combined with ongoing personal support from a retention counselor to help Baltimore City public high school students complete their college education. Retention specialists visit campuses monthly, conduct individual and group meetings with students, maintain regular check-ins, and operate a 24-hour hotline. The program serves students at nine Maryland colleges and universities through graduation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Last Dollar Scholarship of up to $3,000 annually combined with personal support from a retention counselor. Program includes monthly campus visits by retention specialists, individual and group meetings with students, email and telephone check-ins, a 24-hour hotline for students, and mid-year and summer regrouping sessions. Students receive counseling on personal lifestyle-adjustment problems and college-completion support through graduation at participating Maryland colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Craig Spilman, Jimmy Tadlock, Jamie Crouse, Patrick Young, Jamie Tang
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City public high school graduates and college students enrolled at participating nine Maryland colleges and universities who are at risk of dropping out.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial aid to cover college costs (Last Dollar Scholarship component) and retention support services including counseling, tutoring referrals, and academic guidance to help students successfully complete college.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves students from Baltimore City public high schools enrolled at nine Maryland colleges and universities including eight Maryland public university campuses and Stevenson University.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City public high school graduate
Must be enrolled at one of the nine participating Maryland colleges and universities
Must be a recipient of CollegeBound's Last Dollar Grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CollegeBound meets with incoming students in June following high school graduation to ensure they are prepared for fall enrollment. Retention specialists then visit each campus monthly for individual and group meetings, conduct email and telephone check-ins, and host mid-year and summer regrouping sessions. Students have access to a 24-hour hotline for support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 13-week hands-on construction training program that prepares low-income workers for entry-level construction jobs and apprenticeships. The program includes construction safety training, first aid and CPR certification, and construction trade skills. Graduates also receive free driver's education, assistance obtaining a driver's license, and help accessing a vehicle through Vehicles for Change for those who secure employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 13-week intensive hands-on training program with construction safety certification, first aid and CPR certification, and construction trade skills instruction. Cost per trainee is $4,000. Program provides free driver's education and assistance obtaining a driver's license and vehicle through Vehicles for Change for employed graduates. The program has achieved an 80 percent job placement rate and graduates experience an average 60 percent wage gain in the first year after graduation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Baltimore City residents seeking entry-level construction employment and career advancement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction skills training, safety certification, driver's education, driver's license assistance, and vehicle access for employed graduates

Must have a high school diploma or GED
Must pass a math test to ensure adequate basic math skills for successful program completion

Classes are held two nights a week (Mondays and Wednesdays) at 1212 North Wolfe Street. Program runs for 13 weeks with hands-on training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maritime Transportation and Logistics Training Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A 90-hour training program that prepares disadvantaged job seekers for entry-level positions in Port-related industries. The program combines 60 hours of soft skills training with 30 hours of maritime-specific instruction covering freight forwarding, logistics, material handling, stevedoring, customer service, and shipping/receiving.

Training includes 60 hours of soft skills development and 30 hours of maritime and port operations instruction. Participants also receive support in obtaining Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) cards and forklift certification. The program is funded through a Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation EARN grant and matching funds from the Abell Foundation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development for port-related employment including soft skills, maritime operations knowledge, TWIC card certification, and forklift certification.

Accepted participants attend the 90-hour training course which includes classroom instruction, soft skills development, maritime training, and employer presentations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides mission-related investments to for-profit companies, impact funds, and other organizations with innovative ideas to create positive social, economic, and other change. These investments typically take the form of loans, guarantees, equity investments, and limited partnership interests provided at below-market returns to leverage additional capital and address important social challenges. Investments typically range from $1 million to $4 million. The Foundation serves as a value-added partner, providing financial resources alongside experience, knowledge, and access to a network of local and national connections to support portfolio investment success and positive impact. Applications are reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings according to a published schedule.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mission-related investments typically range from $1 million to $4 million and are provided at below-market investment returns. Investments take the form of loans, guarantees, equity investments, and limited partnership interests. Applicants can receive concessionary investment terms with expectations of substantial mission benefits and limited risk of capital loss. The Foundation serves as a value-added partner, providing financial resources alongside experience, knowledge, and access to a network of local and national connections to support portfolio investment success and positive impact. The Foundation's Board of Trustees considers MRI requests five times per year according to a published meeting schedule.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with five Board meetings per year per published schedule
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit companies, impact funds, and other organizations with innovative ideas seeking to advance social mission priorities aligned with the Foundation's strategic goals. Organizations must be located in Baltimore City or address a substantial unmet need of Baltimore City businesses or residents, or be located in underserved communities including Opportunity Zones, inner cities, and targeted rural communities throughout the United States.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for operations and growth to advance mission-aligned goals, growth-oriented operating businesses, and community infrastructure projects located in underserved communities, including those in Opportunity Zones, inner cities, and targeted rural communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Foundation invests throughout the United States with a demonstrated focus on underserved communities including Opportunity Zones, inner cities, and targeted rural communities. structured_extraction.program_description: The Abell Foundation provides program-related investments to support projects aligned with the Foundation's mission, serving nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and fiscally sponsored projects. Investments are expected to be repaid, allowing the foundation to recycle benefits to additional nonprofit partners. Applications are reviewed at one of the Foundation's five annual Board meetings. Applicants submit a letter of inquiry first, and if approved, they proceed to a full application for Board consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: An energy efficiency program that installs energy-saving devices and provides education in residential homes to reduce household energy consumption and lower energy bills. The program replaces incandescent light bulbs with compact fluorescent bulbs, installs water-saving faucet aerators and low-flow showerheads, wraps hot water heaters with insulation, tests and adjusts thermostat settings, installs carbon monoxide detectors, and provides conservation education and tips to residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of energy-saving devices including compact fluorescent light bulbs (up to 15 bulbs per home), kitchen and bathroom faucet aerators, low-flow showerheads, hot water heater insulation, carbon monoxide detectors, and thermostat adjustment services. The program covers the full $205 cost of installation at no cost to the homeowner. Participating households have averaged approximately 10 percent savings in monthly electricity costs, or about $8 per month, with savings covering the program cost in approximately two years.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dana Stein, Executive Director; Earl Millett, Director of Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income households in eligible Baltimore City neighborhoods seeking to reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving home improvements including light bulb replacement, water-saving fixtures, hot water heater insulation, and thermostat optimization to reduce electricity and water consumption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Initially piloted in two Baltimore City neighborhoods: Belair Edison and Coldstream-Homestead-Montebello. Program was designed to target low and moderate income neighborhoods with predominantly two-story rowhouse housing.
requirements_list: Residence in eligible Baltimore City neighborhoods
Low or moderate income household status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Civic Works AmeriCorps workers visit eligible homes in teams of two to assess and install energy-saving devices at no cost to the homeowner. Residents receive education on energy conservation and printed information about installed items and additional savings tips.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frostburg Main Street Structural Stabilization Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides targeted financial support to address critical structural repairs on buildings located within Frostburg's Main Street district. The program helps property owners and businesses stabilize commercial and mixed-use buildings so they can proceed with rehabilitation and redevelopment efforts. Funding comes from Maryland's Strategic Demolition Fund and covers structural work such as foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, and roofing. The City of Frostburg and Allegany County received $250,000 in state funding to support this revitalization initiative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Frostburg and Allegany County received $250,000 in state funding under the Strategic Demolition Fund for this program. structured_extraction.program_description: A forgivable loan program that helps small businesses expand their operations in Allegany County by providing funding for productive capacity improvements. The program supports both new companies establishing themselves and existing companies seeking to grow, create jobs, increase export capacity, or improve their local community presence. Eligible businesses can receive low-interest loans ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 with the opportunity to have up to 50% forgiven based on job creation and export capacity metrics.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Forgivable loans ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 with low interest rates more favorable than traditional lenders. Loans under $10,000 require no match. Loans over $40,000 require a 1:1 match in funding. Up to 50% of the loan can be forgiven based on performance metrics defined by the applicant such as job creation and export capacity. Loan payments can be deferred for up to 6 months after loan draw.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, applications accepted subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small for-profit businesses with fewer than 15 full-time employees that are ready to expand their operations in Allegany County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion of productive capacity including tangible assets such as equipment and furniture. Ineligible uses include staff costs, salaries, acquisition or capital improvements of existing buildings, or construction of new buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be physically present in Allegany County through ownership or long-term commercial lease of a physical asset. Businesses operating from personal residencies may apply if they intend to eventually expand to a commercial location.
requirements_list: For-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with Allegany County and State of Maryland
Fewer than 15 full-time employees
Physically present in Allegany County through ownership or long-term commercial lease, or operating from personal residence with intent to expand to commercial location
Must illustrate ability to offer tangible product or service through patents, existing sales figures, taxes paid, owned assets, or available capital or financing
Must have a developed business plan approved by the local Small Business Development Center Representative
Must include line item budget with vendor estimates
Must be invited to apply by qualified member of Allegany County Economic and Community Development
Funds must be appropriated within 12 months of conditional approval
Funds must be spent within 24 months to qualify for forgiveness
A 1:1 funding match is required for loans over $40,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact Allegany County Economic and Community Development to express interest and receive a formal invitation to apply. Once invited, applicants must prepare a business plan approved by the Small Business Development Center Representative, a line item budget with vendor quotes, proof of capacity, and a fully completed application. Applications are reviewed by a selection committee and ranked by soundness of business plan, impact on local placemaking, and potential for job creation or export. Final recommendations are submitted to the Board of County Commissioners for approval. Funds are paid directly by Allegany County following agreement signing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that advances new innovations in environmental science and technology by subsidizing research and development costs for local firms working with the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory. The program provides a 1:1 matching grant of up to $50,000 per project to cover research costs contracted through the Appalachian Lab. Projects totaling more than $100,000 will receive a maximum subsidy of $50,000 (50% match). The fund is capitalized for $100,000 at the beginning of every fiscal year.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant provides a 1:1 match for research costs up to $50,000 per project. Projects totaling more than $100,000 will receive a maximum subsidy of $50,000 (50% match). Allegany County pays the Appalachian Lab directly via invoices. The fund is capitalized for $100,000 at the beginning of every fiscal year. Payments are deducted from the grantee's balance with the Appalachian Lab.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, tax-paying businesses physically present in Allegany County that are developing environmental technology solutions and conducting research through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Any costs incurred from research or lab usage contracted through the Appalachian Lab for purposes of developing a new product or service in environmental technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be physically present in Allegany County through ownership or long-term commercial lease of a physical asset. Businesses operating out of personal residencies can apply if they clearly intend to eventually expand to a commercial location.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland
Must be physically present in Allegany County through ownership or long-term commercial lease, or operating from personal residence with clear intent to expand commercially
Must clearly demonstrate ability to offer a tangible product or service (through patents, sales figures, taxes paid, assets owned, or available capital)
Must obtain a formal invitation from Allegany County Economic and Community Development or indication from Appalachian Lab staff to apply

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should complete a contact form on the website. A member of the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team will reach out to discuss the research project and help facilitate contact with the Appalachian Lab. Applicants must prepare a short narrative (1-2 pages) explaining the project, provide a costs analysis from the Appalachian Lab, and obtain a letter of approval from the Appalachian Lab. Applications are reviewed by Allegany County, with final recommendations and approval made by the Department of Economic and Community Development and the Appalachian Lab, submitted to the Board of Commissioners for final decision. Projects are scored as either 'yes' or 'no' recommendations. Awardees must provide written quarterly progress reports until project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for full-time employees of Anne Arundel County working as 9-1-1 specialists, including those who receive and process 9-1-1 emergency requests or provide support functions directly related to 9-1-1 operations or dispatch public safety services. An administrative fee of 1% may be assessed on the credit. The credit automatically terminates after 10 years or upon job termination, change in residency, or property ownership change. The credit cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program that provides funding to farm-based businesses, commercial watermen, and agricultural producers in Anne Arundel County to help them grow their operations, purchase equipment, make infrastructure improvements, and generate additional revenue. The program supports livestock producers, equine operations, produce production, product marketing, commercial watermen, and other agricultural ventures. Grants of up to $10,000 are available with recipients required to contribute at least 50% of project costs. Eligible uses include purchasing equipment, making infrastructure improvements, livestock acquisition, farm facility upgrades, fencing, plant stock, and projects that increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase the local-grown food supply, or provide agricultural education opportunities. Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible. In 2024, the program funded over $38,000 in total projects.

Grant recipients must contribute at least 50% of project costs. Matching funds may not include labor or state and federal grants or cost share. Projects must be completed within one year of the grant award. Eligible uses include purchasing equipment, making infrastructure improvements, livestock acquisition, farm facility upgrades, fencing, livestock, plant stock, barns, storage, handling areas, and projects that increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase the local-grown food supply, or provide agricultural education opportunities. Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, infrastructure improvements, livestock acquisition, farm facility upgrades, fencing, plant stock, barns, storage, handling areas, and other projects that support farm operation growth and revenue generation, including livestock production, equine operations, produce production, and product marketing. Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County funds design-build-maintain contracts with private firms to construct cost-effective nature-based stormwater best management practices on privately owned properties. Contractors front the initial implementation cost and are reimbursed by the County after the project is constructed and verified to generate water quality credits. Maintenance payments are evaluated and released annually for up to 5 years after project completion. Bid opportunities are typically announced each Fall.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A county program established in 1990 to preserve agricultural and woodland land through conservation easements, purchase of development rights, and tax credit programs. The County purchases development rights from landowners, allowing the land to remain in private ownership while permanently restricting it from development. Landowners with eligible parcels can participate through district agreements, tax credit applications, or by selling conservation easements to the county, MALPF (Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation), or Rural Legacy programs. Landowners receive financial compensation in exchange for voluntarily placing permanent easements on their property to prevent development while allowing continued agricultural use or timbering. Recent easement offers have ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre, with payment at 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value of development rights, subject to county funding availability. The easement is perpetual and runs with the deed when the land is transferred. The county provides tax credits for eligible participants. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council during the Capital Budget cycle. Current draft recommendations propose reducing the minimum agricultural land size from 50 acres to allow smaller farms to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners can participate through district agreements, tax credit applications, or by selling conservation easements. The county purchases development rights and easements at 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value of development rights. Recent offers have ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre with cash at settlement. The county provides tax credits for eligible participants through a binding 10-year agreement with the County. Tax credits are applied to the county portion of real property taxes on land and up to $100,000 of building assessments. The easement is perpetual and runs with the property deed. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council during the Capital Budget cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted during 30 days prior to April 1 and November 1 of each year; filing dates may be extended with 30 days public notice. October 1 deadline for tax credit applications to receive credit from July 1 of previous year.

Landowners seeking to preserve their agricultural property and receive financial compensation.

For easement purchase: Complete petition form (online or downloadable), print, sign, and date form, submit with all required documentation. structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County who install, reinstall, or have a Best Management Practice (BMP) for stormwater management on their property. The credit reduces stormwater runoff from structures and impervious surfaces. Eligible practices include living shoreline projects, living roofs, sidewalk infiltration planters, permeable pavers, bioretention installations, cisterns, rain barrels, rain gardens, wet ponds, and other permanent diversion and infiltration methods. The credit equals 10% of the cost of materials and installation, not to exceed a total of $10,000 over the five-year life of the credit, and reduces County property tax liability.

Credit reduces County property tax liability for new or existing residential and commercial properties with improvements approved by the Department of Public Works. Credit cannot be combined with other property tax credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration and Forestry Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds on-the-ground watershed restoration and forestry projects to reduce pollutants and stormwater flowing into local waterways in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis. The program treats and filters pollutants from impervious surfaces, engages residents in restoration and protection of local rivers and streams, implements watershed restoration practices, supports cost-effective reforestation and greening efforts, and increases protected forested land. Projects are categorized by scale: Category 1 projects have a disturbance footprint less than 5,000 square feet or less than 100 cubic yards of earth disturbance, while Category 2 projects have greater disturbance. Total funding anticipated is $1,000,000 for Anne Arundel County and $300,000 for the City of Annapolis, with individual funding requests generally not exceeding $300,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for watershed restoration, reforestation, and forestry projects that support stormwater management, water and air quality improvement, habitat and tree cover increase and protection, and reduction of flooding and erosion. Typically two categories: Category 1 projects (small-scale, disturbance footprint less than 5,000 square feet or less than 100 cubic yards of earth disturbance) and Category 2 projects (large-scale, disturbance footprint greater than 5,000 square feet or more than 100 cubic yards of earth disturbance). Total funding anticipated is $1,000,000 for Anne Arundel County and $300,000 for the City of Annapolis. Individual funding requests will generally not exceed $300,000. Matching funds are not required but are viewed favorably.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically opens in Fall and closes in Spring
structured_extraction.contact_name: Raghu Badami; Melissa Harlinski; Melissa Bragg
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified 501(c) non-profit organizations including local watershed groups, community associations and homeowners associations, service and youth groups, and faith-based organizations with at least one partner representing a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, as well as individuals and communities in Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis. NGOs, private organizations, and CIP project managers are encouraged to contact county staff to discuss potential project sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must accomplish on-the-ground restoration that treats rainwater runoff from impervious surfaces, including forestry activities and reforestation efforts. Eligible project types include shoreline restoration, stream restoration, living shorelines, rain gardens, bioretention, stormwater best management practices, impervious surface removal, greening efforts, land protection, and related watershed restoration activities. Project sites should budget extra discretionary funds for permits and bonds from local, state, and federal governments when applicable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located throughout Anne Arundel County, including the City of Annapolis. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request for Proposals (RFPs) are solicited annually, typically opening in the Fall and closing in the Spring. structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel Tornado Relief Grants / Disaster Recovery Micro Grant Program (DRMGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency grant program awarded to residents and businesses in Anne Arundel County that were damaged by a tornado and tropical storm that struck on September 1, 2021. The Disaster Recovery Micro Grant Program (DRMGP) provided non-repayable grants of $5,000 each to assist with repair and recovery costs. The program was funded by the TD Charitable Foundation with total program funding of $25,000 and targeted businesses, nonprofits, and residents with brick-and-mortar locations impacted by Tropical Storm Ida in September 2021. Funds could be used for legitimate expenses including physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment, replacement of inventory, lease or rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses support.

Funds can be used for legitimate expenses including physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment, replacement of inventory, lease or rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses support. Businesses and nonprofits must have brick-and-mortar locations in Anne Arundel County and be in good standing with the State of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for owners of qualified properties in designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, commercial revitalization districts, and the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area within Anne Arundel County. Property owners who revitalize their properties with improvements of at least $100,000 receive a property tax credit for up to five years equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment, extendable to ten years for investments of at least $10,000,000. The credit applies toward Anne Arundel County property taxes. Eligible improvements include construction of a new building, rehabilitation of an existing building, demolition and subsequent construction, façade improvements, landscaping, signage, lighting, and replacing pavement with green spaces. Eligible properties include those that are commercially or industrially zoned and undergoing renovation, rehabilitation, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a property tax credit for up to five years, extendable to ten years for investments of at least $10,000,000, equal to the incremental increase in their real property tax assessment for improvements of at least $100,000 in full cash value. Properties must be located in one of the designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, in a commercial revitalization district, or in the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area and must be commercially or industrially zoned. Properties must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property. The owner must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after receiving the notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The credit applies toward Anne Arundel County property taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of the Notice of Assessment by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses with commercially or industrially zoned property revitalizing commercial or industrial properties in designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, commercial revitalization districts, or the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area within Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property improvements to commercially or industrially zoned properties in Commercial Revitalization Areas; credit applies toward Anne Arundel County property taxes; includes construction of new buildings, rehabilitation of existing buildings, demolition and subsequent construction, façade improvements, landscaping, signage, lighting, and replacing pavement with green spaces
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, specifically in nine designated Commercial Revitalization Areas: Area 1 - Brooklyn Park (Ritchie Highway), Area 2 - Glen Burnie Town Center North (Crain Highway & Ritchie Highway), Area 3 - Glen Burnie Town Center Core (B&A Boulevard), Area 4 - Glen Burnie Town Center South (Crain Highway), Area 5 - Pasadena (Mountain Road), Area 6 - Riviera Beach (Fort Smallwood Road), Area 7 - North Odenton (MD 175), Area 8 - Maryland City/Russett (MD 198), Area 9 - Ferndale (B&A Boulevard), in other designated commercial revitalization districts, or in the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. Property must be located totally or partially within a commercial revitalization area designated by ordinance. Property must be commercially or industrially zoned.
requirements_list: Property must be commercially or industrially zoned
Property must be located in one of the designated Commercial Revitalization Areas, a designated commercial revitalization district, or the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area
Property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property
Property must be adopted by County Council ordinance and shown on official map
Improvements must total at least $100,000 in full cash value
Owner must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after receiving the notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Property excluded from tax increment development districts except Odenton Town Center Development District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must have their property certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property in a Commercial Revitalization Area, commercial revitalization district, or the Glen Burnie Sustainable Community Overlay Area. After improvements are completed and the property is reassessed, owners receive a notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The owner then applies to the County Office of Finance for the revitalization credit within 120 days of receiving that notice by completing the Commercial Revitalization District Program Property Tax Credit Application form and submitting it to Anne Arundel County Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to nonprofit organizations for program or project support that allows organizations to continue operations, increase the impact of existing programs, or pilot new programs to improve and enrich the lives of Anne Arundel County residents and communities. The program supports one-time projects and small equipment purchases. Approximately $2 million is anticipated to be available for FY2027. Collaborative projects are preferred but not required. Funding prioritizes services to underserved populations, community health and well-being, equity and inclusion initiatives, and elimination of the opportunity gap in education. Capacity building support is also available for organizational efficiency, strategic planning, governance, professional development, and technology improvements.

Funding can support program or project specific staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and a percentage of administrative overhead proportional to the program's budget relative to the organization's overall operating budget (maximum 5% of total award). One-time projects and small equipment purchases are also eligible. Capacity building support is available for strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and organizational systems. Grant funding available through annual application cycle.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural and Woodland District Agreements
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credit program available to eligible landowners who agree to establish a 10-year District Agreement on their land to preserve agriculture and woodland resources. Landowners receive a tax credit against their annual County Property Tax bill in exchange for agreeing to protective covenants. The agreement can be renewed every 10 years. Property owners commit to keep their land in agricultural or woodland use and not subdivide it, and receive a credit on the county portion of their real property tax bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a tax credit applied to the County Real Estate Tax portion of their Real Property Tax Bill for the 10-year term of the District Agreement. Property owners are invoiced only for State property taxes, County fees and charges, with the County property tax portion eliminated through the credit. The agreement can be renewed for additional 10-year periods.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications encouraged by March 31 if tax credit is sought for the following fiscal year tax bill; applications may be submitted anytime
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Anne Arundel County with eligible agricultural or woodland properties who want to maintain their property in agricultural or woodland use and benefit from property tax reductions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to County Real Estate Tax bill for eligible properties committed to agricultural or woodland preservation under a 10-year District Agreement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County. For agricultural districts: property must be within Rural Agricultural or Residential Low Density zoning districts and outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3. For woodland districts: same zoning and water/sewer requirements apply. Current draft recommendations propose reducing the minimum agricultural land size from 50 acres to allow smaller farms to participate and making the property tax credit permanent rather than requiring renewal every 10 years.
requirements_list: For Agricultural District: land must consist of 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture (or multiple contiguous properties with each at least 10 acres totaling 50+ acres under different ownership)
Must meet USDA Soil Capability Classes criteria
Must have an active Soil and Water Conservation Plan in place
Must be within Rural Agricultural or Residential Low Density zoning districts
Must be outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
For Woodland District: must consist of at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands (10-acre minimum per landowner when adding to existing woodland district)
Must have a Forest Management Plan
Must meet zoning and Water and Sewer Category requirements
District Agreements must be renewed every 10 years to maintain tax credit benefit
Property owner must commit to keep land in agricultural or woodland use
Property owner must not subdivide the land
Commitment period is 10 years
Can be renewed for additional 10-year terms
Minimum size requirement (currently 50 acres; proposed to be reduced in updated regulations)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners submit applications to the Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Staff, who can assist in determining property eligibility and preparing the District and Tax Credit applications. Staff can help evaluate USDA Soil Capability Classes, verify conservation plans, and confirm zoning. Landowners interested in the Tax District Agreement should contact Anne Arundel County planning and zoning department. Upon approval, the landowner enters into a recorded District Agreement in County Land Records. Specific application procedures are being updated as part of the program regulations revision.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds through the Maryland Department of Commerce to help Anne Arundel County small businesses impacted by COVID-19 that had not previously received state-funded COVID-19 relief grants. The program provides funding to small brick-and-mortar businesses and nonprofits to increase their online presence and digital capabilities. The program focuses on service businesses such as salons, gyms, dance studios, art classes, retail stores, and other brick-and-mortar retailers. Grants support businesses in engaging with customers, reaching new audiences, and enhancing their digital presence. Individual grants of up to $10,000 are available for the new purchase of, or subscription to, digital platforms and services including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards/loyalty programs, e-commerce platforms (online ordering and sales), website and social media advertising, website improvements, online purchasing capabilities, software upgrades, volunteer management systems, pay-online features, and reputation management software.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual grants of up to $10,000 are available for new purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services. Average grant amount was $3,200 per recipient. Total distributed: $460,800 to 144 businesses. Grants can be used to support email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards/loyalty programs, e-commerce platforms (online ordering and sales), website and social media advertising, website improvements, online purchasing capabilities, software upgrades, volunteer management systems, pay-online features, and reputation management software. The program was funded with federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds through the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small brick-and-mortar businesses and nonprofits in Anne Arundel County with one to 20 employees that were established and operating prior to March 9, 2020. Priority given to businesses that had not previously received COVID-19 relief grants from the State of Maryland. Includes woman-owned, minority-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. Particularly service-based businesses such as salons, gyms, dance studios, retail stores, and other operations seeking to strengthen their digital presence and compete in an increasingly digital economy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Digital services and enhancements including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards/loyalty programs, e-commerce platforms (online ordering and sales), website and social media advertising, website improvements, online purchasing capabilities, software upgrades, volunteer management systems, pay-online features, and reputation management software.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Applicants must have a brick-and-mortar location in Anne Arundel County and be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Anne Arundel County.

Must be located in Anne Arundel County
Must have one to 20 employees
Must have been established and operating prior to March 9, 2020
Service-based or retail business type
Priority given to businesses that had not previously received COVID-19 relief grants from the State of Maryland
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Anne Arundel County

Must operate in one of the following sectors: Retail, Beauty and personal wellness services (licensed massage, physical therapy, acupuncture), Adult and children's activity centers (gyms, dance, yoga, martial arts studios, arts and crafts businesses), or nonprofit organization
Must submit appropriate certificate or license for the sector
Must submit completed and signed W-9 form

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted via an online portal. Applicants must complete and sign a W-9 form and submit a budget outlining the proposed use of grant funds. Businesses applied through the program launched on September 14, 2021.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credit for permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, rescue workers, and fire/emergency medical services employees whose disability arose out of and in the course of employment, as well as surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit applied to Anne Arundel County real property taxes only (not state taxes or other assessments); calculated at 100% of total tax due on a dwelling based on real property assessment. Credit is applied after mandatory property tax credits, supplements, and deferrals and applies to primary residential dwelling only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Permanently and totally disabled law enforcement officers, correctional officers, career fire/rescue/emergency medical services employees, volunteer fire company/rescue squad members, and surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers and rescue workers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property tax credit on primary residence or dwelling owned and occupied by eligible applicant or surviving spouse
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must own and reside in property as primary residence in Anne Arundel County, Maryland; applicant/fallen officer must have been domiciled in Maryland within required period (5 years) before disability determination or death
requirements_list: Permanently and totally disabled by administrative body or court of competent jurisdiction, OR surviving spouse of fallen officer/worker
Disability or death must arise out of and in the course of employment
Disability or death must not result from willful misconduct, alcohol/drug abuse, or occupational disease without accidental injury
Must meet definition of eligible law enforcement officer, correctional officer, career fire/rescue/EMS employee, or volunteer fire/rescue member
Own and reside in property as primary residence in Anne Arundel County
Dwelling must be owned at time of disability determination or death
Valid Maryland government ID, death certificate (if surviving spouse), marriage license (if surviving spouse), and eligibility certification from employing agency (notarized)

structured_extraction.program_description: A planning grant awarded under the ENOUGH Act to develop a comprehensive Neighborhood Action Plan for the Brooklyn Park/Pumphrey community. The grant supports a community-driven planning process led by residents, county agencies, nonprofits, and faith-based organizations to identify critical programs and services needed to reduce child poverty and improve economic mobility for families in the area. The plan will serve as the foundation for a Track 3 implementation grant in the next funding cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Track 2 Planning Grant funding to support the development of a comprehensive Neighborhood Action Plan through a community-driven planning process. The plan development involves county agencies, nonprofits, faith-based organizations, and residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Partnership was awarded this grant and is leading the planning process through a Leadership Team, Resident Council, and larger Partner Team. Residents and stakeholders participate in monthly Leadership Team meetings and bi-monthly stakeholder and partner group meetings. Public comments and questions are welcomed at meetings or can be submitted to enoughbrooklynpark@aacounty.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that provides door-to-door rides within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line at approximately 50% of normal fares, or taxi/rides-on-demand vouchers. Qualified applicants can schedule rides with at least two hours notice and receive same-day service. The program serves eligible Anne Arundel County residents who are seniors aged 55 and older or individuals aged 18 and older with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Professional drivers operate appropriately equipped cars, vans, or SUVs to provide door-to-door transportation service. Alternatively, participants can purchase discounted transportation vouchers redeemable for rides through participating on-demand service providers (voucher values range from $10–$150 for payments of $5–$75). Fares are offered at approximately 50% of normal cost. Each qualified resident receives a county match of up to $75 per month, with a maximum of $150 in vouchers eligible to purchase per month. Same-day service is available with at least two hours notice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents aged 55 and older, or individuals aged 18 to 54 with verifiable transportation disabilities that prevent use of public transportation services; individuals with low income (≤$1,255/month single; ≤$1,703/month with spouse); ambulatory and non-ambulatory individuals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door transportation within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line (airport trips excluded), or transportation via taxi or rides-on-demand service providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Anne Arundel County residents for service within the county and up to 20 miles outside the county line. Airport trips are excluded.
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be 55 years of age or older, OR 18 years of age or older with a verifiable transportation disability that prevents use of public transportation services
Must meet income thresholds (≤$1,255/month single; ≤$1,703/month with spouse)
Must provide completed ETA Application form
Must provide completed Liability Form
Must provide copy of Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from Motor Vehicle Administration with Anne Arundel County address
For persons 18 or older with disability: must provide copy of SSI or SSDI award letter or completed Disability Verification Form (completed by qualified health care provider)
Participant must voluntarily participate
Participant responsible for scheduling own trips
Participant responsible for payment of all scheduled trips
Must adhere to all requirements set by rides-on-demand service providers
Must adhere to all requirements set by Anne Arundel County Department of Aging and Disabilities
Must sign liability waiver and indemnification agreement
Maximum $150 in vouchers eligible to purchase per month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can visit one of two locations in Anne Arundel County (2666 Riva Road, 2nd Floor, Annapolis, or 7320 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie) during walk-in hours from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., or mail the completed application and required documents to 2666 Riva Rd, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. For disability verification, submit the Disability Verification Form completed by a qualified health care provider (physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of a qualified social agency). To purchase vouchers, complete the order form, select voucher amount(s), provide payment (check or money order), and mail to the program office. After enrollment, users call the Rides-On-Demand reservations number to schedule a ride with at least two hours notice.

structured_extraction.program_name: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Taxi Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Easy Travel Access (ETA) Taxi Voucher Program offers discounted taxi vouchers to help pay for taxi fares with participating cab companies in Anne Arundel County. Eligible residents can purchase voucher books at a reduced cost and use them for transportation to run errands, visit polling places, shop, pick up groceries, and other local travel. Each voucher book costs $5.00 and is worth $10.00 in taxi fare value. Qualified residents may purchase up to 15 books per month, with the county providing a monthly match of up to $75. Vouchers can be used with participating cab companies including Associated Cab Company Inc., The Independent Taxi, and Annapolis Bay Area.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-administered program providing Anne Arundel County residents with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects with appropriate emergent marsh grasses (Spartina alterniflora and Spartina patens) for planting in marsh areas. The program supports plantings of emergent marsh grasses in intertidal zones and areas above intertidal zones. County personnel conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions and assist with project planning before providing the grasses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County residents with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects receive appropriate emergent marsh grasses for planting in marsh areas. The program provides two types of grasses: Spartina alterniflora (smooth cordgrass) for areas between high and low tides, and Spartina patens (saltmarsh hay) for areas above high tide. County personnel conduct field visits to evaluate site conditions, assist with project planning, and provide assistance in determining necessary permits and obtaining vegetation management plans.

structured_extraction.program_description: An inclusionary zoning law creating county-wide housing opportunities for essential workers by requiring developers of new residential subdivisions to offer a percentage of units at affordable prices. Modeled after Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) programs and Inclusionary Housing programs existing in over 700 jurisdictions across the United States.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private developers are required to offer 15% of rental units and 10% of for-sale units (increased to 15% under Amendment #5) at moderately priced rates. For rental units, households must earn up to 75% of area median income ($62,156 for a single person, more for families). For ownership units, households must earn up to 100% of area median income ($82,875 for a single person, more for families). Developers receive density bonuses, waived impact fees for MPDUs, and 50% reduction in Capital Facility Connection Charges for water and wastewater. Developers may pay a fee in lieu of providing units (1-3% of purchase price depending on amendments passed). Over 200 new homes and apartments would be available annually for qualified workers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Essential workers including teachers, firefighters, police officers, nurses, construction workers, and public service and service industry workers in Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis who earn up to 75% of area median income (rental) or 100% of area median income (ownership), and have been a resident of the County/City and/or employed in the County/City for the last 12 months, or are currently employed by Anne Arundel County, City of Annapolis, or Anne Arundel County Public Schools. Includes first-time homebuyers on ACDS and Housing Commission of Anne Arundel County waitlists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rental of moderately priced dwelling units in new residential subdivisions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis, available in new development areas. Applicants must be a County/City resident and/or employed in the County/City for the last 12 months, or currently employed by Anne Arundel County, City of Annapolis, or Anne Arundel County Public Schools.
requirements_list: At least one household member must be a resident of Anne Arundel County or City of Annapolis and/or employed in the County/City for the last 12 months, or currently employed by Anne Arundel County, City of Annapolis, or Anne Arundel County Public Schools
For rental: household income up to 75% of area median income ($62,156 for single person, more for families)
For ownership: household income up to 100% of area median income ($82,875 for single person, more for families)
Must not have owned a home in the last three years
Any Anne Arundel County Public Schools employee is eligible to apply and may be eligible for income requirement adjustments under certain circumstances
Must meet credit and rental application standards
Must qualify for first mortgage loan (homeownership)
Moderately priced dwelling units must meet design standards established by the county
Applicants must be qualified by ACDS (Arundel Community Development Services Inc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for moderately priced dwelling units are submitted through individual developers. Applications are qualified by Arundel Community Development Services Inc. (ACDS) and Housing Commission of Anne Arundel County (HCAAC). For-sale units must be listed on the Realtor Multiple Listing Service while rental units must be advertised in the same manner as market-rate units. Income limits are adjustable twice per year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fall 2025 Professional Development Cohort Program - Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0
structured_extraction.program_description: A professional development cohort program for nonprofit leaders on diversifying funding sources and advanced fundraising strategies. The program includes multiple in-person and virtual sessions, expert facilitation, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting, and lifetime access to resource materials and templates. Organizations can bring teams of 2-3 people to develop or update resource development plans and create financial sustainability strategies. The cohorts run from October through December, meeting multiple times per week.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A professional development cohort program running from October through December, meeting multiple times per week (in-person and virtual sessions) from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Organizations can bring up to three team members. Cost is $75 for nonprofits with budgets under $500,000 and $150 for those with budgets over $500,000 (or free depending on cohort). The program includes expert facilitation, peer learning, networking opportunities, one-on-one consulting time on related projects, in-person training sessions and online coaching, and lifetime access to resource materials, examples, and templates. Attendance at all sessions is required to complete the program successfully.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fall cohort is now full. Spring 2026 cohort offered.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit leaders and staff from 501(c)(3) organizations located in and serving Anne Arundel County who already have a basic understanding of fundraising principles or are new to the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and coaching on fundraising and sustainability topics including the evolving landscape of fundraising, building a case for support and organizational storytelling, strategic prospecting and grant development, designing a diverse fundraising plan, and developing or updating resource development plans to create financial sustainability strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nonprofits must be located in Anne Arundel County with administrative offices in Anne Arundel County and serve at least 75% of their population in Anne Arundel County.

Administrative offices located in Anne Arundel County

Agree to share outcome data to help the Nonprofit Center improve programs and services
Completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability Cohort OR attendees have baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts
At least one person from an organization must attend all sessions to complete the program successfully
Teams should consist of 2-3 people from the organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through the Nonprofit Center or submit online application through SurveyMonkey link provided on the page. Organizations can bring up to three people. At least one person from the organization must attend all sessions. Payment will be collected once the cohort is full. Application requires organization information, mission statement, founding year, 501(c)(3) status confirmation, annual budget, employee information, description of board participation in fundraising, current resource development strategies, existing fundraising plan details, and explanation of what you hope to learn.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows private landowners to establish mitigation banks on their property by planting native trees and selling reforestation credits to developers and property owners who need to offset forest loss from development projects. Landowners can generate income while helping preserve and create new forests in Anne Arundel County. Offsite reforestation banks serve critical and non-critical areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private landowners establish mitigation banks by planting native trees on their property, posting security to ensure tree survival, and placing the planted area under a perpetual protective agreement such as a conservation easement. The landowner can sell reforestation credits to developers and property owners who need mitigation for forest loss from development. In some cases, landowners can preserve existing forested areas to satisfy portions of off-site planting requirements for developers. Offsite reforestation bank services are available for critical area and non-critical area mitigation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private property owners and developers in Anne Arundel County who need to provide mitigation for forest loss or afforestation as a result of development projects. Entities requiring forest mitigation in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners use funds from selling reforestation credits to cover costs of planting native trees, posting security for tree survival, and establishing conservation easements or other perpetual protective agreements. Reforestation and forest mitigation banking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Critical area and non-critical area locations in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Off-site mitigation banks are established on private property within the county.
requirements_list: Plant native trees on private property
Post security to ensure tree survival
Place planted area under perpetual protective agreement such as conservation easement
Comply with county forest mitigation requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in establishing a mitigation bank should contact the Anne Arundel County Forestry Division for specific requirements and procedures. For questions about existing mitigation banks, contact individual banks using the Off-site Reforestation Bank Contact List.
