structured_extraction.program_description: Program for habitat enhancement work including invasive species eradication and native vegetation replanting on properties in Anne Arundel County. Activities may include pruning for vegetation health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation with replanting of native species. The program applies to properties in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or within Bog Protection Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a permitting and review process for habitat enhancement activities. Allows for site grading without separate grading permit; approval granted for two years. Applicants submit a completed Habitat Enhancement Plan application to the Forestry Program for review and approval before work begins. The approved plan must be posted onsite during work performance for inspection purposes. All required State and Federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry's approval. Sediment and erosion control compliance required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County interested in habitat enhancement and invasive species eradication.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Habitat enhancement, invasive species eradication, and native vegetation replanting. Activities may include pruning for the health and safety of vegetation, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of non-native invasive vegetation and replanting of native species. Activities shall not include clearing of vegetation for any activities related to development or work in preparation of a development application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties with tax accounts in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Work must be within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or within Bog Protection Areas.
requirements_list: Completed application with tax account number
Cover letter with contact information
Scaled site plan with specific dimensions and environmental features
Description of existing conditions and proposed work
Invasive plant eradication timeline and methods
Erosion and sediment control measures
Short-term and long-term management plan
Compliance with Anne Arundel Soil Conservation District Standard Sediment and Erosion Control Plan
All required State and Federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry's approval
Approved Habitat Enhancement Plan or available copy must be posted onsite when work is being performed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit package to Permit Center Reception Desk, 1st Floor, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, MD 21401 or email as PDF to forestry@aacounty.org. Contact the Forestry Office at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org to schedule an on-site proposal review before submitting the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Building Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for high performance buildings (residential or commercial) that meet national green building standards (LEED Silver or higher, or NGBS Silver or higher) in Anne Arundel County, reducing County property tax liability per Maryland Tax-Property Code § 9-242. The credit is available to owners of buildings meeting high performance standards and is calculated per ordinance requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Credit against County real property taxes on the building (not land) for 5 consecutive taxable years. For residential buildings: Silver rating 40% of taxes (max $1,000/year), Gold rating 60% of taxes (max $2,000/year), Platinum rating 80% of taxes (max $3,000/year). For commercial buildings: Silver rating 40% of taxes (max $4,000/year), Gold rating 60% of taxes (max $12,000/year), Platinum/Emerald rating 80% of taxes (max $12,000/year). Separate applications available for residential and commercial buildings. Credit cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County with high-performance green buildings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction in County real property taxes owed on certified high-performance buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Building must be rated LEED Silver or higher, or NGBS Silver or higher
Must provide copy of rating certificate and verification documentation
Building and systems must be regularly maintained to comply with applicable standards
Property must be assessed as commercial by Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (commercial buildings)
County officers may inspect site to verify compliance
Cannot be combined with other optional property tax credits
Statement under penalties of perjury that building and systems are regularly maintained
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the High Performance Building Property Tax Credit Application form (separate applications available for residential and commercial properties) and submit to Anne Arundel County Finance/Controller's Office on or before June 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is first sought. Include documentation demonstrating green building standard achievement (copy of rating certificate and verification workbook/signature page), statement under penalties of perjury regarding maintenance compliance, and acknowledgment that County may inspect the property. Specific form requirements are amended by ordinance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County established this program to help property owners offset expenses related to rehabilitation on historic landmarks in the county. Property owners can receive property tax credits based on qualified expenses for rehabilitation or new construction in historic districts. The program provides a tax credit of 25% of qualified expenses for rehabilitation of historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for qualified new construction in a Landmark Historic District, with a maximum tax credit of $50,000 claimable over a 5-year period and applied towards Anne Arundel County real property taxes. The credit reduces real property tax liability for qualifying historic preservation projects.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit of 25% of qualified expenses for rehabilitation of historic residential or income-producing properties, or 5% for qualified new construction in a Landmark Historic District. The maximum tax credit is $50,000, which can be claimed over a 5-year period and is applied towards Anne Arundel County real property taxes. The credit reduces real property tax liability for qualifying historic preservation projects. Unused credits can carry forward for up to five years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Part 1 form - anytime during the project planning phase; Part 3 form by March 1 immediately before the taxable year; Part 4 form by April 1 immediately before the taxable year (annually)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of historic buildings and structures in Anne Arundel County that meet designation criteria for historic landmarks or are contributing resources in Landmark Historic Districts. Properties must be at least 65 years old with high significance in history, architecture, archeology, engineering, and/or culture. This includes Anne Arundel County citizens engaged in historic preservation and planning rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified expenses for rehabilitation, restoration, preservation work, upgrades, modernization, and sensitive additions on historic properties that comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties. Qualifying work includes repairs and replacements of original features, structural repairs, roof work, masonry repointing, life-safety improvements, ADA improvements, plumbing/electrical/mechanical work, and architectural/engineering/archeological fees. Work may include interior or exterior preservation work on qualified structures, as long as the work does not compromise the Landmark status or historically significant features (or modifications must be reversible).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only. Properties must be located within Anne Arundel County and meet criteria for designation as a historic landmark or be a contributing resource within a Landmark Historic District (Davidsonville, Linthicum Heights, Owensville, Woodwardville, or districts determined eligible for National Register such as West Benning, Glen Burnie, Odenton). Properties must be listed on Anne Arundel County's Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must meet criteria for designation as a historic landmark or contribute to a historic district
Structure must be at least 65 years old
Structure must have high significance in history, architecture, archeology, engineering, and/or culture
Structure must retain integrity in location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling, and association
Structure must meet at least one criterion: National Register listing/eligibility, associated events, associated persons, distinctive design/construction, or information potential
All rehabilitation work must comply with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties
Work must not compromise the Landmark status or historic integrity of the historic resource
Historic preservation easement required to protect County investment and runs perpetually with the land
Property owner must provide proof of payment for all qualified work items
Detailed description of proposed work with existing conditions, proposed colors, materials, and dimensions required
Color photos of principal facade, proposed work areas, environmental setting, and streetscape views required
Architectural/shop drawings as required
For properties altered since previous listing, property may need re-evaluation
Cannot be combined with other optional Maryland property tax credits under Title 9 of State Code
Expenses must be for qualified rehabilitation work
Property owner must apply each year by April 1 to receive the annual tax credit
Applicant must certify information under penalties of perjury
Periodic on-site inspections by Office of Planning and Zoning permitted
Early consultation with Cultural Resources Division required during project planning
Obtain County approval from Cultural Resources Section prior to commencement of work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Four-part certification and application process: (1) Submit Part 1 Certificate of Eligibility form to confirm property meets historic criteria (at least 65 years old, high significance, integrity requirements met); (2) Hold presubmittal meeting with Cultural Resources staff early in project planning, then submit Part 2 Certification of Proposed Work form with detailed descriptions, photos, and drawings for approval before beginning work; (3) Submit Part 3 Certification of Completed Work form with supporting materials (completed work photos, itemized qualified expenditures with proof of payment, permit copies) after work completion and execute historic preservation easement; (4) Submit Part 4 Tax Credit Application to Office of Finance by April 1. Property owners must apply annually by April 1 to claim the tax credit. Each certification part receives response within 30 days. Alternatively, contact the Preservation Planning office for application details and eligibility verification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help hotels, motels, inns, and bed-and-breakfast establishments in Anne Arundel County recover from pandemic-related revenue losses by providing funds for normal operating costs or COVID-19 related expenses. The program distributes five million dollars in state funding to eligible hospitality businesses.

Funds can be used for normal operating costs such as rent, payroll, job training, taxes, and debt service, or for COVID-19 related costs such as personal protective equipment and sanitization services. Grants cannot be used for equipment, soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating costs including rent, payroll, job training, taxes, and debt service, or COVID-19 related costs such as personal protective equipment and sanitization services. Cannot be used for equipment, soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only. Applicants must be an Anne Arundel County hospitality business in good standing with the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Hotels and motels must have at least ten sleeping rooms
Bed and breakfast establishments must have at least five sleeping rooms
Short-term residential rentals do not qualify
Business must have experienced a pandemic-related reduction in year-over-year gross revenue of at least 25 percent for April to November 2020 compared to the same period in 2019
Applicant must be an Anne Arundel County hospitality business in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must submit a copy of a valid occupancy license issued by the Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits
Must submit a completed and signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check for ACH deposit of grant funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants access the application through the Hotel Relief Grant Program page on the AAEDC website. Applicants must complete the application, submit required documents including a valid occupancy license and W-9 form, and upload a voided company check. The application deadline was 5:00 p.m. on Friday, March 5.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive business education program offered by Anne Arundel County that combines education, mentorship, and financial support for small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses. The program includes seven to eight weeks of online or in-person weekly learning sessions covering business management topics such as pricing, profit margins, expenses, revenue, and sales goals. Participants interact with peer entrepreneurs, experienced facilitators, subject matter experts, and consultants in legal, human resources, and accounting. The program is led by business consultants including facilitators from the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program. Participants receive $5,000 seed grants for working capital and operational/seed investment, growth guidance, and mentor support. Graduates must attend all sessions, complete homework assignments, and deliver a final presentation on their business growth plan. A Spanish language version is planned for 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive $5,000 to $10,000 operational/seed investment grants or $5,000 seed grants for working capital upon successful completion of the program. The training consists of seven to eight consecutive weeks of weekly three-hour online or in-person learning sessions with interactive instruction on business management and operational topics, interaction with peer entrepreneurs, subject matter experts, and consultants in legal, human resources, and accounting. Participants receive consultations with business experts and participate in final presentations on their business growth plans. Participants must attend all sessions, complete homework assignments, and deliver a final presentation to graduate and receive the grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned business owners and early-stage entrepreneurs in Anne Arundel County seeking business education, growth plans, and support to improve and expand their business operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, business operating expenses, growth, and development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland. A Spanish language version is planned for 2024.
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Must be a minority-owned, woman-owned, or Veteran-owned business or other early-stage entrepreneur
Must be located in or operating in Anne Arundel County
Attend all class sessions
Complete homework assignments prior to each subsequent class
Deliver a final presentation on business growth plan at graduation
Must complete all components of the program including classes and expert consultations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested business owners apply to be part of a cohort. Selected participants attend consecutive weeks of weekly business classes, participate in consultations with legal, human resources, and accounting experts, complete homework assignments, and present their business growth plans to a panel of expert judges or at graduation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Key Bridge Small Business Direct Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency assistance program established to provide direct financial support to small businesses, port workers, first responders, families, and communities affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse on March 26, 2024. The program addresses loss of income and increased costs related to the bridge collapse, helps businesses adjust their operating models, and invests in small enterprises in communities most affected by the tragedy. Small businesses in Northern Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County can receive grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 based on business revenues, while eligible port workers in the Baltimore region can receive one-time payments of $1,000. The overall effort includes over $15 million in commitments and coordinates recovery and resilience efforts including healing, response, and memorialization. Assistance is provided in Spanish and English through designated grant partners including Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation, Baltimore Community Lending, and Latino Economic Development Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct grant funds ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 depending on the small business's revenue, and one-time payments of $1,000 to eligible port workers in the Baltimore region. Businesses can apply through one of three designated grant partners: Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation for businesses in Anne Arundel County or other Maryland areas, Baltimore Community Lending for businesses in Baltimore City or other Maryland areas, or Latino Economic Development Center for businesses in Baltimore County or other Maryland areas. Funds can be used to address loss of income, increased costs, pivot business models, and to improve or adjust commercial operations. Overall fund has over $15 million in commitments and coordinates with adjacent public relief efforts. Assistance is provided in Spanish and English.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and authorized representatives whose businesses were severely affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in March 2024 and have been in operation for at least two years as of March 26, 2024, located in Southeastern Baltimore County, Southeastern Baltimore City, Northern Anne Arundel County, or other Maryland communities with demonstrated severe impact. Port workers, first responders, families, and communities in the Baltimore region including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County are also eligible. Includes family-run and locally owned operations across diverse industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To address loss of income and increased costs related to the bridge collapse, adjust business operating models, stabilize operations, pivot business models, and improve or adjust commercial operations. Funds can be invested in long-term viability and recovery and resilience efforts including healing, response, and memorialization. Funds cannot be used for ineligible expenses that have been reimbursed by other federal, state, or local disaster assistance programs including Baltimore Port Business Assistance Program, Francis Scott Key Business Recovery Program, SBA EIDL Program, or other similar programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority given to applicants located in Southeastern Baltimore County, Southeastern Baltimore City, and Northern Anne Arundel County. Port workers in the Baltimore region including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and Anne Arundel County are also eligible. Applicants in other Maryland areas must demonstrate a compelling and demonstrable case that their business has been severely affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Baltimore area focus on communities and workers affected by the bridge collapse.
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Must have been severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Must have been affected by the March 2024 Key Bridge collapse
Must be located in Baltimore City, Southeast Baltimore County, or Northern Anne Arundel County, or other Maryland communities with demonstrated severe impact
Business must have been in operation for at least two years as of March 26, 2024
Business must have generated at least $50,000 in revenue in at least one of the two years prior to March 26, 2024
Business must have at least two employees, which may include owner(s)
Business must provide 2023 profit and loss statement, end of year 2024 balance sheet, and 2024 profit and loss statement
Applicant must submit business tax returns and upload 2023 business tax returns or Schedule C at time of application
Business or trade name must be registered with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and be in active, compliant, or good standing status
Applicant must complete, sign, and date IRS Form W-9 and upload during application process
Bank account must be a business bank account matching the grant applicant business name
Business must have been financially affected by the bridge collapse and demonstrate continued viability and sustainability

Funds cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by other disaster assistance programs including Baltimore Port Business Assistance Program, Francis Scott Key Business Recovery Program, or SBA EIDL Program
Business must demonstrate evidence of loss of revenue or increased expenses related to the Key Bridge collapse
Valid proof of identity (driver's license or passport)
Completed W-9 form signed by authorized signer per IRS guidelines
All documents must be clear, legible, and not redacted, cut off, or partial
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small businesses can complete and submit the online application at https://aaedc.submittable.com/submit/316091/key-bridge-small-business-direct-grant/eligibility or apply through one of three designated grant partners online: Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) for Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC) for Anne Arundel County, and Baltimore Community Lending (BCL) for Baltimore City. Submit application with required documentation including profit and loss statements, balance sheet, tax returns or Schedule C, IRS Form W-9, and demonstration of financial impact from the bridge collapse. Port workers can apply for the one-time payment through the CASH Campaign of Maryland at https://cashmd.org/maryland-tough-baltimore-strong-key-bridge-relief-resources. Assistance in Spanish and English is available through grant partners. Additional information available at https://bcf.org/maryland-tough-baltimore-strong-key-bridge-fund/. Applications were accepted during the application period from February 18, 2025 through March 20, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: An entrepreneurial resource hub that facilitates the licensing of Department of Defense technologies developed at federal research labs in Maryland including the National Security Agency/Fort Meade, Aberdeen Proving Ground, and Fort Detrick. The center assists in identifying which technologies are right for businesses based on interests, challenges, capabilities, and commercialization viability. Established in 2018 by DoD Office of Economic Adjustment funding as a pilot program and expanded statewide in 2019. The center provides complimentary consulting services, information, networking, education, and mentoring to help entrepreneurs and companies commercialize defense technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DefTech Center provides complimentary technical assistance including information to navigate the Technology Transfer (T2) process with federal research laboratories, networking opportunities with T2 staff, scientists, engineers, and service providers, education on topics such as market-oriented product development, intellectual property law, and customer discovery, one-on-one mentoring for clients interested in licensing technology including IP identification, market analysis, and commercialization planning, connection with product development resources through DoD Research Labs, and guidance through the technology licensing process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local entrepreneurs commercializing technology from federal labs, scientists, engineers, and innovators at Maryland federal research labs, local and out-of-state companies seeking to establish a presence in Maryland, and those developing innovative defense technology for government contracting or commercial markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The center assists with navigating the technology transfer process, patent research and IP identification, market-oriented product development, intellectual property and patent law, customer discovery, market analysis, commercialization planning, and licensing of defense technologies from Maryland federal research laboratories.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program serving Maryland. The DefTech Center partners with federal laboratories located in Maryland including the National Security Agency at Fort Meade, U.S. Army Medical Research and Materiel Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Fort Detrick, and U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command labs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the DefTech Center to learn more about defense technology commercialization and federal lab technology transfer opportunities. The center can be reached through the contact information provided or by visiting AAEDC's DefTech page for additional resources.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time relief grants applied directly to qualifying customers' billing accounts within two billing cycles. Grant amounts vary based on outstanding balance, household income, household size, type of dwelling, and other state-determined criteria. No repayment required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents facing financial hardship with unpaid utility bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment assistance for outstanding utility bill balances and arrearages
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to qualifying Maryland energy customers
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland energy customer
Must have outstanding utility bill balance or arrearages
Must meet state-determined criteria such as household income and size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Customers do not need to take any action. Relief grants will be automatically applied to qualifying billing accounts within two billing cycles.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mobile Poultry Processing Unit Rental Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rental program that provides access to a mobile poultry processing unit for agricultural businesses. The unit can be rented by farmers and agricultural operations to process poultry on their own premises. The unit includes processing supplies and equipment such as gloves, aprons, cleaning supplies, hoses, buckets, knives, thermometer, and poultry crates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental access to a mobile poultry processing unit including processing supplies and equipment (gloves, aprons, cleaning supplies, hoses, buckets, knives/processing equipment, thermometer, and poultry crates). Renters pay rental fees to use the unit for processing poultry. The program is funded through grant funds from the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses and farmers in Anne Arundel County who process poultry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental of mobile poultry processing equipment and supplies for on-farm poultry processing operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a certificate of liability insurance for a minimum of $1 million, listing AAEDC and Sarah Campbell/New Roots Farm as additional insured.
Lessee assumes all liability when towing and using the mobile processing unit.
Lessee is responsible for the cost of all repairs made necessary during the lease period beyond normal wear and tear.
Unit must be inspected upon pick-up and any damage must be reported to Sarah Campbell/AAEDC prior to rental.
Unit must be cleaned at conclusion of use.
Must have HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) and SSOP (Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures) plans customized to the operation.
All renters must complete the Maryland State Poultry and Rabbit Certification.
Post-rental form must be completed upon return of the unit.
Access to mobile processing unit and supplied equipment.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the rental application through the online form at aaedc.submittable.com. Upon approval, renters receive an email with rental details and post-rental form information. The unit must be picked up after inspection and returned clean with a completed post-rental form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides grants, support services, and resources to family caregivers and informal caregivers. Services include information about available resources, assistance locating services, temporary respite (relief) care, provision of supplies or devices to make caregiving tasks easier, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event. Financial assistance recognizes that caregiving can be fulfilling but emotionally and financially exhausting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants for respite care (temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities), supplies or devices to assist with caregiving tasks, support services, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event. Payment is issued approximately 4-6 weeks after approval and submission of required forms (W-9 form and Funds Acknowledgement form). Grant awards are based on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers and informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to older adults age 60 and older; caregivers of any age providing care to individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders; older relatives age 55 and older providing care to children under 18 or adults ages 18-59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care (temporary relief from caregiving), supplies or devices to make caregiving tasks easier, support groups, educational workshops, and other support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County. The program serves caregivers in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Primary caregiver for an older relative, spouse, or grandchild
Care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County
For respite care requests: must submit a W-9 form and a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment can be processed
Caregiver must be age 18 or older (or age 55 or older for some applicant categories)
Adult family members or informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals 60 years of age and older
Adult family members or informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders
Older relatives (not parents) age 55 and older providing care to children under age 18
Older relatives, including parents, age 55 and older providing care to adults ages 18-59 with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Family Caregiver Program by phone or email to inquire about services and apply for grants. Submit required forms (W-9 form and Funds Acknowledgement form) for respite care requests. Upon approval and receipt of forms, payment is issued in approximately 4-6 weeks. If the care recipient is enrolled in a program with a case manager, assistance may also be requested through the case manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: A zero percent loan program for technology companies and government contractors in Anne Arundel County that provide products or services supporting the cyber and defense industry. The fund serves businesses at the mezzanine stage of growth—those that have launched, invested in themselves in the early stage, had initial success, and need support to scale up. The program offers flexible financing terms and helps innovative businesses ready to grow and hire, particularly supporting small government contractors and tech entrepreneurs expand their workforce and operations while awaiting payments on federal contracts, commercialize technology, or meet government contract requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with flexible payment terms (one to five years) for technology companies and government contractors in the cyber and defense industry sector. The loan program helps innovative companies scale up to commercialize technology, meet government contract requirements, or expand operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology companies and government contractors located in Anne Arundel County or with a signed lease demonstrating intent to move into the county, at the mezzanine stage of growth, with gross revenue less than $5 million and fewer than 100 employees. Particularly targets small government contractors and cyber technology firms providing products or services supporting the cyber and defense industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion, scaling operations, commercializing technology, product development, hiring additional team members, marketing efforts, workforce expansion, and working capital while awaiting federal contract payments or meeting government contract requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease demonstrating their intent to move into Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be Anne Arundel County-based or have signed lease to move into county
Must be a technology company or government contractor
Must provide a product or service that supports the cyber and defense industry
Must be at mezzanine stage of growth (launched, invested in early stage, had initial success)
Gross revenue of less than $5 million
Fewer than 100 employees
Must be ready to grow and ready to hire
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies apply for the Next Stage Tech Fund through the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation. Application pipeline is active with strong demand reported.

structured_extraction.program_name: Non-Profit Economic Development Recovery Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support the workforce and operations of non-profit organizations serving Anne Arundel County communities. The program focuses on organizations with missions in economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, and housing. It aims to help non-profits continue their vital services and maintain staffing during economic recovery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards to support non-profit workforce and operations. Individual grant amounts are calculated after the application round closes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-serving non-profit organizations based in Anne Arundel County that serve populations in the areas of economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, and housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for non-profit workforce and operations. Funding must address pandemic economy impacts and fill remaining gaps in COVID-19 relief funding received.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only. Applicant organizations must be based in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Be based in Anne Arundel County
Have at least one W-2 employee
Demonstrate mission focus on economic development, economic recovery, health and human services, or housing
Detail how the organization serves populations in the county
Demonstrate adverse economic impact from the pandemic economy
Provide information on any COVID-19 relief funds already received
Document the remaining funding gap needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications opened on Monday, May 10 at 9:00 a.m. and closed on Friday, May 21 at 5:00 p.m. Applicants must submit: a 2019 IRS Form 990, a completed and signed IRS W-9 form, and a voided organization check or official bank letter confirming routing and account numbers. Additional information and the application link are available on the program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program offering free all-access membership to the Nonprofit Learning Lab online training service for local 501(c)(3) nonprofits in Anne Arundel County. The program provides daily training sessions with live facilitators on topics such as fundraising, strategic planning, communications, volunteer management, and board development. Members receive access to an extensive resource library, Ask the Expert program, free job board postings, and discounted Grant Station membership. Membership is limited to up to two staff members or volunteers per organization through July 15, 2026. A total of 18 slots are available.

Up to 18 total slots available.

Priority given to organizations with operating budgets under $1 million that address one or more social determinants of health and have not previously received NLL access through the Nonprofit Center. Preference for executive directors and director-level employees.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in Anne Arundel County.

Must notify program if not using service so opportunity can be offered to waiting list
Must abide by NLL Terms of Service
Membership limited to up to two staff members or volunteers per organization
May not share membership access, discount codes, or membership codes with individuals outside registered members
If more than two individuals from organization access courses, membership may be terminated
Priority given to organizations with operating budgets under $1 million that address social determinants of health
Priority given to nonprofits that have not previously received access to NLL through the Nonprofit Center
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an interest form available on the program website. The form remains open until all 18 available slots are filled. Qualified organizations will be notified of their status and will receive free all-access membership.

structured_extraction.program_description: Anne Arundel County's Clean Water Program that helps residents convert from private septic tanks to the County's public sewer system by reducing conversion costs. The program aims to improve water quality, protect the Chesapeake Bay, and enhance public health by converting up to 6,000 private septic systems over 30 years, or approximately 200 per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reduces costs for residents converting from private septic tanks to the County sewer system. Eligible residents in participating neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay can receive financial assistance to lower the expense of connecting to public sewer. Up to 6,000 private septic systems are planned to be converted over 30 years, or approximately 200 per year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents living in neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay with private septic systems who want to connect to the County's public sewer system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with the costs of converting from private septic tanks to the County public sewer system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Neighborhoods near the Chesapeake Bay in Anne Arundel County. Residents can determine eligibility by visiting www.ourwaater.com and entering their address.
requirements_list: Must be a resident in an eligible neighborhood near the Chesapeake Bay
Must currently use a private septic system
Must be located in Anne Arundel County
Property must be able to connect to County sewer system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can determine eligibility by visiting www.ourwaater.com and entering their address into the search bar. For more information, contact the program via email at info@ourwaater.org or call (410) 222-7500.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for government contracting participation

structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program that allows property owners to make energy efficient upgrades to buildings with no money down. The financing is repaid as a benefit assessment on the property tax bill over long terms of up to 20 years. The assessment transfers to new owners on property sale and can be passed through to tenants where appropriate. The program provides upfront capital to help commercial property owners save money and energy by improving their buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing with no money down, repaid as a benefit assessment on property tax bill over up to 20 years. Assessment transfers on sale of property. Upfront capital provided to help property owners reduce energy costs through building improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and industrial property owners, as well as residential property owners with 5 or more units, interested in making energy efficient upgrades to buildings in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficient upgrades to non-residential buildings or residential properties with 5 or more units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a PACE enabled area in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the legal owner of the building
Building must be a non-residential property or property with 5 or more units
Property must be located within a PACE enabled area
Mortgage not held in a CMBS (commercial mortgage-backed security)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Anne Arundel County's Financing & Tax Credit Representatives for more information. Additional details available through the Maryland Clean Energy Center at mdcleanenergy.org. Apply online through the AAEDC website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Qualified Data Center Personal Property Tax Assessment Reduction
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a 15-year reduction in personal property tax assessment for qualified data centers meeting investment and job creation requirements. The program offers 100% reduction for the first 5 years and 50% reduction for years 6-15. Available pursuant to § 7-248 of the Tax-Property Article of the State Code and as established by Anne Arundel County ordinance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% reduction in personal property tax assessment for the first 5 taxable years; 50% reduction for years 6-15 (15-year total reduction period). Reduces the assessment of qualified data center personal property used in a qualified data center for personal property tax purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15 immediately before the taxable year for which the reduction in assessment is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Data center operators with qualifying investments and job creation, including individuals or corporations that own and operate qualified data centers in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of personal property tax assessment for qualified data center equipment and infrastructure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Data center must be physically located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland. Multi-location data centers within Anne Arundel County owned/operated by the same person or entity are eligible.
requirements_list: Minimum $10 million total investment in qualified data center (real and personal property combined)
Creation of minimum 10 qualified positions
Qualified positions must be full-time, indefinite duration, paying at least 150% of applicable wage
Must file personal property tax return with State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must certify investment amount and qualified positions
Must maintain investment and position requirements throughout the 15-year reduction period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Qualified Data Center Assessment Reduction Application form to the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance and County Economic Development Corporation by the April 15 deadline immediately before the taxable year for which the reduction is sought. Application must include a copy of the state tax return and certification of investment amount and qualified positions. Applications are reviewed and approved or rejected by both agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Real Property County Tax Exemption - Community or Civic Association
structured_extraction.program_description: Exemption from Anne Arundel County real estate taxes for community or civic associations meeting specific requirements
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County real estate tax exemption for property dedicated to use by lot owners within the community. Property must be dedicated by appropriate record plat or deed restrictions, dues/fees/assessments must be solely for improvement or maintenance of roads, property, or facilities, and property use not contingent on payment of dues/fees/compensation except for assessments solely for improvement/maintenance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community or civic associations in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property dedicated to community use; dues/fees/assessments must be solely for improvement or maintenance of roads, property, or facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit community civic association or corporation
Must have not-for-profit status (e.g., 501(c)(3) determination letter)
Title held by nonprofit community civic association or corporation
Property dedicated by appropriate record plat or deed restrictions to use of lot owners within community
Current with all taxes and fees due to Anne Arundel County
Use of property not contingent on payment of dues/fees/compensation, except for assessments solely for improvement/maintenance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form; include proof of not-for-profit status; include property records from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; include record plat or deed showing dedication; submit to Office of Finance with supporting documentation

structured_extraction.program_description: A program allowing eligible residential property owners to defer payment of Anne Arundel County real property taxes. Eligibility requires residency of at least five consecutive years and meeting one of three conditions: age 62 or older; permanent total disability with qualifying benefits; or income eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Allows eligible homeowners to defer payment of Anne Arundel County real property taxes on residential properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible residential property owners in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Defers payment of residential property taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only
requirements_list: Owner or one co-owner must have resided in dwelling for at least five consecutive years

Applicant must be at least 62 years of age, OR permanently and totally disabled with qualifying benefits, OR found permanently and totally disabled by County Health Officer or Baltimore City Commissioner of Health
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must own residential real property in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Real Property Tax Payment Deferral Application and submit to Anne Arundel County Finance. Must meet all eligibility requirements including residency and age or disability criteria, plus income limits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows eligible homeowners to defer payment of water/wastewater User Connection Charges, Capital Facility Connection Charges, and Front Foot Benefit Assessment Charges until sale or title transfer of property. Deferred charges remain as a lien on the property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Deferral of water/wastewater connection and assessment charges until property sale or title transfer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners aged 60 and older or homeowners receiving permanent and total disability benefits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferred utility charges including water/wastewater connection charges, capital facility charges, and front foot benefit assessments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Single-family dwelling
Applicant must be property owner and dwelling must be principal residence
Combined gross household income cannot exceed specified limits ($72,950-$137,550 depending on household size)

Applicant must be either: (a) 60+ years old or surviving spouse of owner 60+, or (b) receiving disability benefits from Social Security, US Civil Service, Veteran's Administration, or Railroad Retirement Act
Copy of latest Maryland income tax return required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form with property and resident information, report yearly income from all sources, and attach proof of disability if applicable.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential rehabilitation work
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Property must qualify as residential rehabilitation per the ordinance definition

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing financial assistance to restaurant workers affected by COVID-19 pandemic restrictions. The program distributes funds via debit cards to low-wage restaurant workers in financial distress.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Debit card distribution providing direct financial assistance to restaurant workers. The program was allocated $2 million in supplemental county funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-wage restaurant workers in Anne Arundel County experiencing financial hardship due to COVID-19 restrictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General financial assistance for workers in financial distress.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a restaurant worker
Must be experiencing financial distress
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed through Anne Arundel County Workforce Development. Residents in financial distress can call 410-222-FOOD for assistance and to sign up for available programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Restaurant and Food Service Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial assistance to restaurants and food service businesses in Anne Arundel County. The program provides grants to help businesses affected by COVID-19 related restrictions and is reopening its application portal to distribute additional funds received from Maryland Commerce. Grants can be used for operating expenses such as rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment, sanitary improvements, and online customer engagement costs. The program is administered by the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation using funds from Maryland Commerce and Anne Arundel County CARES Act funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $10,000 for catering businesses, bed and breakfast establishments, and dine-in non-drive-through restaurants, or $5,000 for food trucks. Total program funding of $10 million available ($5 million from county CARES Act funds and approximately $5 million expected from state initiative). Funds can cover operating expenses including rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment, sanitary improvements, and online customer engagement. Grants cannot be used for expenses covered by other COVID-19 programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period expected to open in mid-November
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants, food trucks, catering businesses, and bed and breakfast establishments located in Anne Arundel County that were operating prior to March 13, 2020
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses including rent, payroll, utilities, personal protective equipment, sanitary improvements to physical spaces, and costs for implementing online customer engagement and transactions. Cannot be used for expenses covered by other COVID-19 programs, insurance-covered losses, or capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Must be located in Anne Arundel County
Must have been open and operating prior to March 13, 2020
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must submit a copy of an active food service license issued by Anne Arundel County Department of Health
Must submit a signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check to facilitate ACH deposit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants create an account and complete the application process through a portal on the AAEDC website. Applicants must submit a copy of an active food service license, a signed W-9 form, and a voided company check for ACH deposit processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: County property tax credit for retired veterans aged 65+ who own their principal residence in Anne Arundel County with assessed value of $800,000 or less. Credit equals 15% of County property tax (after mandatory credits) on up to $500,000 of assessed value. Available for up to 50 taxable years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 15% County property tax credit on up to $500,000 assessed value; applies after mandatory credits, supplements, and deferrals. Credit reduces County real property tax liability for retired veterans for up to 50 taxable years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which credit is sought (e.g., April 1, 2026 for fiscal year July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retired members of U.S. uniformed services, military reserves, or National Guard aged 65+ who are Anne Arundel County residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit only; does not apply to State taxes or other fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal residence must be located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland with assessed value of $800,000 or less
requirements_list: Age 65+ prior to fiscal year start
Retired from U.S. uniformed services, military reserves, or National Guard
Own property as principal residence
Property assessed value $800,000 or less
Must occupy property for more than 6 months of the taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Retired Veterans Property Tax Credit Application for Year 1. Re-application forms are available for years 2-50. Annual reapplication required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Runway to Success Program Powered by Southwest Airlines
structured_extraction.program_description: A travel rewards program that provides Anne Arundel County businesses with travel certificates to attend out-of-state conferences, meetings, and training workshops to enhance marketing, sales, and workforce development. Southwest Airlines provides travel awards distributed to qualified local businesses, with approved companies receiving travel awards for up to two employees that can be used with SWABIZ, Southwest Airlines' corporate booking tool, to access low fares and exclusive offers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Southwest Airlines provides travel reward certificates (up to two per recipient company) distributed to qualified local businesses. Approved companies receive travel awards that can be used with SWABIZ, Southwest Airlines' corporate booking tool, to access low fares and exclusive offers for travel to out-of-state conferences, meetings, training workshops, and industry conferences.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All ten travel awards were planned to be distributed by the end of 2017; business travel can occur any time after that deadline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County businesses with under 100 employees and annual revenue less than $10 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Travel to out-of-state conferences, meetings, training workshops, and industry conferences for marketing, sales, and workforce training purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have fewer than 100 employees
Must have annual revenue less than $10 million
Must detail marketing goals, travel plans, and staff assignments
Can cover up to two employees per approved company
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies submit applications detailing their marketing goals, travel plans, and staff assignments. AAEDC reviews and approves qualified businesses, awarding travel vouchers. Companies can also create a SWABIZ account to manage and track their travel program.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Disaster Assistance Business Recovery Center
structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary assistance center opened to support businesses and workers in Anne Arundel County impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. The center helps business owners apply for SBA disaster loans of up to $2 million to overcome temporary loss of revenue, and provides access to support services from multiple government agencies including the U.S. Department of Labor, Maryland Insurance Administration, and county agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SBA disaster loans available for up to $2 million to help businesses overcome temporary loss of revenue stemming from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and workers in Anne Arundel County impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To help businesses overcome temporary loss of revenue resulting from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse

requirements_list: Business or worker impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Business must be located in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Business Recovery Center at Arundel Christian Church, 710 Aquahart Rd, Glen Burnie. Customer Service Representatives will assist business owners in completing disaster loan applications, accept documents for existing applications, and provide the status of loan applications. Representatives from multiple agencies including U.S. Department of Labor, Maryland Insurance Administration, and county agencies are on-site to provide information and connect applicants with vital services. The program focuses on understanding the course of the illness, strategies for managing symptoms, and encouraging persons with dementia to participate in daily activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-licensed child care program operated by Anne Arundel County Department of Recreation and Parks that provides before-school and after-school care for elementary school-age children in kindergarten through 5th grade, with summer sessions and Pre-K care options also available. The program offers a safe and supportive environment with activities including snacks, homework time, outdoor play, crafts, organized games, activity stations, community service projects, and special events. Before-school care begins at 6:30am until school start, and after-school care runs from school end until 6:00pm. The program operates on an annual cycle with registration opening on a first-come, first-served basis during designated registration windows by geographic region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized state-licensed child care services providing before-school care from 6:30am until school start and after-school care from school end until 6:00pm. Summer sessions available at $190/week (standard), $210/week (field trip week), and $152/week (select sessions). School year monthly fees vary by location based on program costs and school hours. Pre-K care available at $115/week (summer) or $350-460/month (school year). A $25 non-refundable registration fee is charged for each child per session. The PM snack is included in the monthly fee. Families pay for AM program only, PM program only, or both. First payment is due by August 10 of the school year or the child will be withdrawn and the space offered to the next person on the waitlist. Late fees apply at $3/minute after 6pm pickup and $25/month for late payment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens on a first-come, first-served basis during designated registration windows by region. For 2026-2027: April 7-14, 2026 with registration windows opening at 8:00am and closing at 11:59pm on assigned dates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 5 and older entering kindergarten through 5th grade during the school year at Anne Arundel County Public Schools, with Pre-K care options for children ages 3-5 and summer programs for children entering 1st-6th grades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Licensed child care services including before-school and after-school supervision, activities, snacks (PM program), homework support, outdoor play, crafts, organized games, activity stations, community service projects, special events, and meals (breakfast, lunch, snack, dinner snack where applicable). Summer programs include field trip weeks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple school locations throughout Anne Arundel County, organized by geographic region (Southern, Central, Crofton/Davidsonville, Pasadena, North & West, and Western Anne Arundel County). Children must attend Anne Arundel County Public Schools. Program operates at 40+ child care centers throughout Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Child must be at least 5 years old by the first day of school
Child must be entering kindergarten through 5th grade for the school year
Child must be toilet trained and self-sufficient in restroom and hygiene care
Child must attend Anne Arundel County Public Schools
State-mandated required forms for admission must be completed and on file at the site on first day, including health inventory with physician's signature
Emergency Form required
Blood Lead Testing Certificate required
Immunization Certificate required for Pre-K or school-age children not at regular school
Acknowledgment of Policies form required on child's first day
Custody Orders required as needed
Medical authorization forms for medications/conditions required and renewed annually
Medical conditions, disabilities, or special needs must be noted on registration form
Minimum and maximum registration limits apply at each center
Registration is first-come, first-served basis
First payment due by August 10 or child will be withdrawn and space offered to next on waitlist
Annual registration fee required
Must follow Anne Arundel County Board of Education calendar
Withdrawal results in loss of space and priority for subsequent school years
Annual form updates required
Emergency contact information mandatory
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Create an online account at the Child Care Registration Portal using a valid email address. 2) Add child information to account. 3) Select preferred school location and session (AM and/or PM). 4) Register during assigned registration window by region. 5) Select start date and check register box. 6) Review and accept eligibility and disclosure agreement. 7) Select child's grade and previous participation. 8) Review and agree to School Age Child Care Policy. 9) Complete payment processing with credit card. 10) Upon notification of space availability, submit required state-mandated admission forms including Emergency Form, Health Inventory (parent/guardian and physician completed), Blood Lead Testing Certificate, Immunization Certificate, Acknowledgment of Policies form, Custody Orders (as needed), and Medical authorization forms. 11) Forms available at aacounty.org; Parent's Manual available for review electronically or in paper form. 12) First payment due by August 10 of the school year. 13) Register online at https://www.aacounty.org/departments/recreation-parks/. Contact Child Care Administrative Office for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program to help theaters, concert venues, and other facilities that were impacted by the Covid-19 pandemic shutdown. Grants are based on average monthly gross revenue multiplied by six, capped at $10 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants capped at $10 million based on average monthly gross revenue for each full month operational, multiplied by six. Reduced by PPP loan amount if received on or after December 27, 2020. Funds can be used for payroll, rent, utility payments, mortgage and debt payments, personal protective equipment, independent contractor payments, administrative costs, state and local taxes and fees, insurance, and capital expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Live venue operators or promoters, theatrical producers, live performing arts organization operators, museum operators, motion picture theater operators, and talent representatives that were operational as of February 29, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payroll, rent, utility payments, scheduled mortgage and debt payments, personal protective equipment, independent contractor payments, administrative costs, state and local taxes and fees, insurance, and capital expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide; Maryland businesses are eligible.
requirements_list: Must have been in operation as of February 29, 2020

Eligible entities include live venue operators or promoters, theatrical producers, live performing arts organization operators, museum operators, motion picture theater operators (including owners), and talent representatives
PPP loan received on or after December 27, 2020 will reduce SVOG amount by the PPP loan amount

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Customer & Employee Protection Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provided financial assistance to small businesses in Anne Arundel County to implement safety measures for customers and employees, purchase protective equipment, and pivot their business operations during the COVID-19 pandemic. Businesses could apply for grants up to $10,000 to cover eligible purchases and services including personal protective equipment, protective barriers, sanitation products, digital signage, technology for wellness scans and e-commerce, delivery vehicles and equipment, and professional consulting services. The program was funded by $5 million from Anne Arundel County's allocation of CARES Act funding and operated from June 3 to July 24, 2020, during which over 790 grants were approved, averaging approximately $6,370 per grant. Eligible businesses included for-profit and non-profit entities with 50 or fewer employees in good standing with the State of Maryland, with preference given to minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $10,000 to cover costs of personal protective equipment, protective barriers, sanitation products and services, disinfection UV lamps, biocide or mold bomb foggers, digital signage, technology for wellness scans and e-commerce, delivery vehicles and equipment, and professional services such as legal and human resources consultations. Grants could also support trainings and consultations on compliance regulations and best practices. The program could reimburse for purchases made after March 29, 2020. Grants averaged approximately $6,370 and the program was funded by $5 million from Anne Arundel County's CARES Act allocation. Past due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County-based small businesses with 50 or fewer employees, including non-profit entities in good standing with the State of Maryland, with preference given to minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal protective equipment for employees, protective shields and dividers, sanitation products and services, disinfection UV lamps, biocide or mold bomb foggers, digital signage and graphics, technology for wellness scans, virtual meetings, website upgrades, customer communications, marketing and e-commerce, delivery vehicles and equipment, professional consulting services for legal and human resources compliance, and trainings and consultations on compliance regulations and best practices. Past due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis
requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County based business or City of Annapolis based business
50 or fewer employees
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must submit a detailed budget with line item purchases and vendors
Must provide financial documents such as business tax returns, Schedule C, form 990, or profit and loss statement
Must submit invoices to demonstrate proof of purchases
Past due bills for ongoing expenses such as rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify
Non-profit entities are also eligible
Small business status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants completed an online application with a detailed budget, financial documents, and proof of purchases. Applicants were required to create an account on the online application portal and submit a detailed budget listing all vendors, amounts, and products or services being purchased, including vendor information (name, address, phone, website). The program operated from June 3 to July 24, 2020, and has ended. Questions could be sent by email to the program contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant initiative to help groups of small businesses afford water, sewer, and other infrastructure improvements necessary to start or expand business operations. The program focuses on projects that benefit multiple businesses and require community support. Grants cover the construction portion of infrastructure improvement projects.

Projects must benefit multiple businesses, not just a single entity. Applicants must be able to cover soft costs and associated fees related to the regulatory process. Applicants must obtain architectural documents, inspections, and letters of community support before receiving approval and funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency relief grant program administered by Anne Arundel County to help small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses and nonprofit organizations recover from damage and operational disruptions caused by natural disasters that trigger a local state of emergency. The program is funded by Maryland's video lottery terminal (VLT) loan program (slot machine tax revenue from Maryland casinos). Multiple iterations have been activated: the January 2024 program provided reimbursable grants up to $50,000 to nonprofits located within Annapolis City limits and eligible businesses in Anne Arundel County affected by the January 9-10, 2024 flooding event; the October 2021 program (officially known as the Disaster Recovery Relief Program or DRRP) provided grants to businesses affected by the October 29-30, 2021 storm and coastal flooding. The program is designed to recur when future natural disasters trigger local states of emergency. A total of $647,095 was distributed to 21 businesses across multiple iterations, with grants ranging from $1,000 to $50,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants of up to $50,000 per business or organization for disaster recovery funded by Maryland's video lottery terminal (VLT) loan program. Funds can be used for physical property repairs, equipment replacement and damage, appliance replacement, loss of income from business closures, inventory replacement, working capital, operational recovery expenses, and cleanup costs. A total of $647,095 was distributed to 21 businesses across multiple iterations, with grants ranging from $1,000 to $50,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program activated following Mayor's declaration of local state of emergency. January 2024 program began accepting applications January 16, 2024 on a rolling basis; October 2021 program began accepting applications November 1, 2021. Both programs have concluded.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery from damage and operational disruptions caused by natural disasters, including physical property repairs, equipment damage repairs, appliance replacement, loss of income from business closures, inventory replacement, working capital for business operations recovery, and cleanup costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The program is available after natural disasters that cause a local state of emergency. Grants have been provided to businesses in nearby areas including Grasonville (Queen Anne's County) and Oxford (Talbot County). Limited to businesses and non-profits with a commercial brick-and-mortar location in the City of Annapolis. Program was activated on January 12, 2024, following Mayor Gavin Buckley's State of Emergency declaration for flooding that occurred on January 9-10, 2024.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC). The program is activated following a Mayor's declaration of a local state of emergency. Applicants must submit a completed application along with supporting documentation including 2022 tax returns (schedule C or Form 990), damage statements with income loss details, photos and videos of damage, a budget for grant use, paid invoices and cancelled checks, and a W-9 form. Applicants must also be available for a site visit to review property damages. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The AAEDC reviews claims and can deploy grants quickly after emergency declaration, distributing grants of up to $50,000 per business or organization. Previous iterations of the program have concluded and are no longer accepting new applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Video Lottery Terminal Local Development Council Community Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants funded by revenue from video lottery terminals at Maryland Live! Casino, administered by the Local Development Council to support nonprofit and community organizations serving communities within a three-mile radius of the casino. Funds support infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and improvements. The program operates on a competitive basis with awards ranging from $10,000 to $40,000, with invitation-only grants also available for organizations invited by the LDC to meet identified needs or priorities. Funding serves to build nonprofit capacity, increase impact, and enable organizations to operate more efficiently and effectively to improve and enrich the general quality of life in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community grants available on a competitive basis for nonprofit organizations and community associations serving residents within a three-mile radius of Live! Invitation-only grants are also available for organizations invited by the LDC to meet identified needs or priorities, with grant amounts exceeding $40,000 possible in unique circumstances. Both non-capital grants (capacity building, operational efficiency) and capital grants (equipment, supplies, capital improvements, renovation, remodeling, restoration, or new construction of buildings) are available. Funds derived from video lottery terminal revenues.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open October 15, 2025 and close December 3, 2025 at 12:00pm. Applicants can access recorded training videos and slides to guide the application process. Submit proposal with standard elements: cover letter with board endorsement, one-page executive summary, need statement focused on people served, SMART objectives (Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time Bound), detailed methodology, line-by-line budget justification with empirical data, evaluation and reporting plan, and explanation of any industry-specific terminology. Present proposal to LDC (limited to 10 minutes presentation with 5 minutes for Q&A). Applications are evaluated against general criteria and evaluation standards. Special accommodations and language interpretation available upon request. Applicants should review the Community Grant Guidelines and tips for successful grant proposals before applying.
