structured_extraction.program_description: The Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) program administered by Anne Arundel County allows property owners to appeal their stormwater fee bill and apply for credits or exemptions for various qualifying reasons including incorrect property classification, mathematical errors, property exemptions, or financial hardship. Property owners may appeal their fee calculation on an ongoing basis or apply for credits towards their WPRF based on incorrect residential tier classification, mathematical errors, exemption status, or homeowners association property cap application. Residents may also apply for a Financial Hardship Exemption if they meet eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive credits applied towards their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee based on qualifying reasons such as incorrect property classification, mathematical error, property exemption status, or homeowners association property cap application. Residents may also apply for a Financial Hardship Exemption if they meet eligibility criteria. Appeals can be filed on an ongoing basis for reasons including property placed in wrong residential tier, incorrect property classification, homeowners association property where fee cap is not applied, mathematical or impervious surface calculation errors, property exempt status, or billing to non-owner. Credits must be requested by October 1st of the taxable year for application in that year; applications received after that deadline are applied in the next taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits must be requested by October 1st of the taxable year; appeals accepted on an ongoing basis

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A credit program for eligible property owners in Anne Arundel County to reduce their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee assessments through the implementation of proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls. Property owners who install small-scale stormwater management practices (under 5,000 sq ft of land disturbance) on their property and enter into a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement with the County can become eligible for credits of up to 50% reduction in their fee assessments. Credits are based on the water quality treatment provided by the practice and the percentage of treated impervious surface area. Eligible practices include dry wells, infiltration trenches, rain gardens, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting systems, and disconnected impervious surfaces. The program enables property owners to apply for credit towards the WPRF and outlines landowner responsibility for maintaining stormwater practices while allowing the County reasonable access for inspection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive credits against their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee assessments of up to 50% for implementing sustainable stormwater runoff controls. The credit amount is determined based on the percentage of treated impervious surface area and water quality volume treated by the practice. Property owners who enter into the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement and have their stormwater management practices approved receive an annual credit applied to their Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee. Minimum 1 inch of rainfall treated is required for full credit; partial credit is available for less treatment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private property owners in Anne Arundel County with small-scale stormwater best management practices (under 5,000 sq ft of land disturbance) that do not require County grading permit approval and do not have an existing Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for private stormwater management. Specifically, property owners who have implemented or plan to implement proactive and sustainable stormwater runoff controls, including small-scale stormwater management practices on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit can be used to reduce the annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee owed by the property owner. Eligible stormwater management practices include dry wells, infiltration trenches, rain gardens, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting systems, and disconnected impervious surfaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Real property located in Anne Arundel County, Maryland that is subject to stormwater remediation fees.
requirements_list: Eligible property owners must install small-scale stormwater best management practices (BMPs) under 5,000 sq ft of land disturbance that do not require County grading permit approval
Property owner must install stormwater management practices that are not under an existing Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management
Stormwater practices must be privately owned and maintained
Practices must be located on the landowner's parcel
Practices must provide water quality treatment (minimum 1 inch of rainfall treated for full credit)

Practices must be designed, constructed, and maintained in accordance with Anne Arundel County Standards, Stormwater Management Practices and Procedures Manual and/or the 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual
All owners listed on the property deed must sign the agreement
County staff must inspect the practices prior to WPRF Credit approval to verify proper design, construction, and maintenance
If the property is transferred to a new owner, the agreement automatically terminates and the new owner must enter into a new agreement to continue the credit
Maintain on-site stormwater management practices
Submit inspection and maintenance records to Department every 3 years
Obtain prior Department approval before altering stormwater management practices
Provide access for County inspections at reasonable times
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The property owner submits a WPRF Credit application to the County. The County provides the property owner with an unsigned draft of the Agreement specific to their property. All owners listed on the property deed must sign the draft agreement and return a hard copy by mail to the County. If the credit is approved, the County signs the agreement. County staff inspect the stormwater practices to verify compliance with County standards. If approved, the final signed agreement is provided with the WPRF credit decision. Property owners can also contact the Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works for detailed information on applying for credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arundel Community Reinvestment (ACR) Fund and Tandem Grant Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive financing and grant program for Anne Arundel County that offers zero-interest loans up to $100,000 repayable over 3 to 7 years for building exterior renovations and site improvements, limited to 90% of project costs. The companion Tandem Grant Initiative provides facade improvement grants equal to 25% of an approved ACR loan amount (up to $25,000) for eligible businesses and property owners in the county's revitalization districts and Commercial Revitalization Districts. Both programs support renovations and upgrades to building exteriors, landscaping, and site improvements for business and commercial property owners. Loan recipients may also receive a grant equal to 25% of the loan amount. The program helps drive economic activity and investment in specific areas of Anne Arundel County, including Commercial Revitalization Districts, parts of Annapolis, the county's Enterprise Zone, and certain commercial areas in South County.

Loans are repaid over three to seven years at zero percent interest for renovations and upgrades to building exteriors and site improvements, including landscaping. structured_extraction.program_description: A citywide public financing tool and Tax Increment Financing district established by Ordinance 24-443 to support the redevelopment of vacant properties throughout Baltimore City for affordable housing. The program aims to eliminate vacant housing, reduce vacant properties, increase homeownership rates, and preserve communities through neighborhood-based, block-level redevelopment in historically disinvested areas. The program is designed to transform approximately 3,900 vacant units into affordable housing over 15 years using a non-contiguous TIF model that targets vacant properties themselves rather than specific geographic areas. The program prioritizes legacy residents, small and emerging developers, women and minority-owned businesses, community-based organizations, and individuals. TIF funds are provided as grants with no requirement for repayment, delivered on a reimbursement basis. Tax Increment Funding bond proceeds ($65 million first tranche of a planned $150 million over the life of the project, with deployment expected to begin in the second half of 2025) support residential redevelopment, acquisition, rehabilitation, homeowner grants to help residents qualify for newly rehabbed homes, public infrastructure improvements including sidewalks and parks, and addressing home appraisal gaps. The program is part of the Mayor's $3 billion vacant housing elimination plan funded by City ($300 million pledged), State ($900 million pledged), and private sources. The District covers approximately 3,991 vacant properties citywide and an additional 3,934 formerly vacant properties now rehabbed and occupied across 197 neighborhoods including Broadway East, Harlem Park, Druid Heights, Park Heights, Upton, East Baltimore Midway, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello, available citywide including East and West Baltimore. The program is intended to foster equitable neighborhood development, reduce appraisal gaps, expand community development resources, and grow the City's population and tax base.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax Increment Financing grants issued to finance the acquisition, rehabilitation, and redevelopment of vacant properties into affordable housing. TIF funds are provided as grants with no requirement for repayment and are delivered on a reimbursement basis following certification by Third-Party Inspector and City's Verification Agent. Payment benchmarks: 90% upon completion of improvements, 5% upon Use and Occupancy Permit, 5% upon sales/occupancy. Funds support hard construction costs including excavation, demolition, grading, site improvements, building structure, foundations, framing, roof work, floor and ceiling work, interior finishings, exterior finish, building service equipment (electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, air conditioning, alarm systems, elevators, fire protection, computer and network cabling, telecommunications cabling), roofs, doors, windows, flooring, porch repair, and drywall. Hard costs for interior and exterior finishes, floor coverings, and stationary equipment may be subject to additional review. Homeowner grants help residents qualify for newly rehabbed homes. Funds can also be used to construct public infrastructure including streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, water and utilities, alleys, and parks required for city-sponsored homeownership development projects, close appraisal gaps, and create or preserve affordable housing. The estimated amount available for the initial round is $15-18 million, with approximately $3 million allocated to applications from legacy residents, small emerging and minority developers, residents living in the TIF District, business owners, and individuals renovating family-owned homes. The average award for housing construction is anticipated to be around $50,000, which will vary based on property size and condition, rental versus homeownership use, affordability level, and appraisal gap. There is no limit to the amount of TIF funds that can be requested for a specific project. The amount of funds available for each project is determined based on project description, budget, schedule, financing, ability to complete the project and obtain a Use and Occupancy Permit, affordability level (60%, 80%, or up to 115% of area median income), neighborhood housing market impact, and block outcome. Applicants must have source of funds to pay for costs and then be reimbursed by the program. Repayment of bonds comes from increases in property tax assessments and property tax revenues generated in the TIF district.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers (including small, emerging, women and minority-owned businesses), legacy residents, homeowners, rental property owners, community-based organizations, homebuyers, individuals with eligible vacant properties issued a Vacant Building Notice or seeking to purchase or qualify for newly rehabbed affordable homes, nonprofit organizations, CDCs, neighborhood groups, merchant associations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) status or fiscal sponsorships and partnerships, and residents living in the TIF District located in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, and redevelopment of vacant properties into affordable housing units. Hard construction costs for redeveloping vacant buildings into affordable housing for rent or homeownership including roofs, doors, windows, flooring, porch repair, drywall, and other structural and mechanical improvements. Interior and exterior finishes, floor coverings, and stationary equipment may be subject to additional review. Homeowner grants to help qualify for newly rehabbed homes. Public infrastructure construction including streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, water and utilities, parks, and alleys. Engineering and design work for public infrastructure improvements. Funds can be used to close appraisal gaps and create or preserve affordable housing. Homes can serve households earning up to 115% of area median income (approximately $150,000 for a household of four), with emphasis on making homeownership affordable at 60% and 80% of area median income. Work must be completed by licensed contractors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Citywide program limited to Baltimore City. Available throughout Baltimore City across 197 neighborhoods, including East and West Baltimore. The program targets vacant properties themselves rather than limiting to specific geographic areas, creating a non-contiguous TIF model. Properties must be located in the City-Wide Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing District established under City Council Bill 24-0595 and Ordinance 24-443. The District includes approximately 3,991 vacant properties citywide and an additional 3,934 formerly vacant properties now rehabbed and occupied across neighborhoods including Broadway East, Harlem Park, Druid Heights, Park Heights, Upton, East Baltimore Midway, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello. Properties must have been issued a Vacant Building Notice (VBN). Applicants can check property eligibility using the searchable database at https://bit.ly/TIFMAP.
requirements_list: Property must be included in City Council Bill 24-0595 and Ordinance 24-443, City-Wide Affordable Housing Development District
Property must have been issued a Vacant Building Notice (VBN) or be included in established development projects or Request for Proposals/Qualifications
Occupants cannot earn more than 115% of area median income (approximately $132,000-$150,000 for a household of four)
Work must be completed by licensed contractors and subcontractors with proof of licenses and insurance
Project must be financed and completed within 12 months of executing a Grant Agreement with DHCD
TIF funds can only be used for hard construction costs and public infrastructure
Applicants are responsible for identifying funds needed to complete redevelopment beyond TIF funding
Construction budgets must be reviewed and confirmed as eligible use of TIF Bond proceeds by the City's Bond Counsel
Awardees must execute a grant agreement with DHCD
Projects must be able to obtain a Use and Occupancy Permit
Affordability determined based on end use, neighborhood housing market impact, block outcome, property size and condition, and amount of TIF funds needed
Complete application through online form with Authorization to Submit and Signed Certifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Properties included in the TIF legislation are eligible to receive TIF funds. Some properties are part of established development projects or Request for Proposals/Qualifications. Each bond series will include properties available for open application. A variety of factors will determine which properties are included in each series. Property owners and developers submit applications through an online application process available on DHCD's website. Applications must include financial information, development budget, and project schedule. Construction budgets are reviewed by the City's Bond Counsel to confirm eligible use of TIF Bond proceeds. For legacy residents and similar applicants, applications are reviewed to confirm they meet Threshold Criteria without competitive scoring. DHCD reviews applications and awards funds based on project description, budget, schedule, financing, and ability to complete projects. Successful applicants must execute a grant agreement with the City specifying the award amount, development budget, schedule, and other City requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A dedicated funding stream created via Charter Amendment (November 2016) by Baltimore City and funded by excise taxes on real property transfers and recordation taxes to support both rental and for-sale affordable housing for very-low and low-income households. The fund generates approximately $13 million annually through a 0.06% excise tax on real property transfers valued at $1 million or more and a 0.15% excise tax on recordation taxes for transactions at $1 million or above. The fund prioritizes assistance for households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI), with at least half of funds directed to those at or below 30 percent AMI. The Fund is administered by the City's Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) and creates more housing options for low-income working families and others who need affordable places to live.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund generates approximately $13 million annually through excise taxes on real property transfers and recordation taxes. Direct funding is allocated annually by the City with annual allocations of $2 million (FY2020), $3.5 million (FY2021), $5 million (FY2022), and $7 million (FY2023 and subsequent years) to support affordable housing development, preservation, and programs for very-low and low-income households. Assistance includes support for Community Land Trusts – Single Family Homeownership, New Construction of Affordable Rental Housing, Rehabilitation of Existing Rental Projects, and 10% allocation set aside for emerging developers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Corporations, Developers, Community Land Trusts, Emerging developers (those who have completed 3-5 housing projects), Nonprofit affordable housing developers, and low-income households with incomes at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income (AMI) seeking affordable housing funding, with priority for those at or below 30 percent AMI. Priority audience includes renters at or below 30% AMI and homeowners at or below 50% AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for affordable housing development and preservation including Community Land Trust support, single-family homeownership assistance, rental housing new construction and rehabilitation, and programs for very-low and low-income households. Building and protecting affordable homes for renters and homeowners in communities with long-term historical disinvestment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund Community Land Trust Homeownership NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development makes funding available from its Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust initiatives for single family homeownership in Baltimore City. Up to $8 million is available for homeownership projects, with qualified applicants able to request up to $2,000,000 per project. Additionally, up to $500,000 is available to support Community Land Trust operating costs, with eligible applicants able to request a maximum of $100,000 per Community Land Trust entity. Funding supports projects on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated. Projects must serve households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income, with at least half of funded units serving households at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income. Priority is given to communities experiencing long-term and historical disinvestment. This program promotes equitable community development by integrating land trust homes as part of a broader mixed-income housing strategy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $8 million available to support homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts, with qualified applicants able to request up to $2,000,000 per project. Additionally, up to $500,000 available to support Community Land Trust operating costs, with a maximum request of $100,000 per Community Land Trust entity. Funding provided on a rolling basis through June 30, 2026 or until all funds are allocated. Projects must be located in Baltimore City, with priority to communities experiencing long-term and historical disinvestment. Funds may be used for acquisition, rehabilitation, construction, predevelopment, operating costs, and closing costs. Reimbursement-based funding only; no upfront funds available.

structured_extraction.program_name: B'more Fresh: Online SNAP Produce Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An online and in-store shopping incentive program that encourages SNAP participants living in Baltimore City to purchase fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables. The program distributes monthly produce vouchers and e-incentives to SNAP participants through multiple channels: online shopping through participating retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, Safeway) with curbside pickup or delivery services, and in-store digital deals at Safeway locations. After spending a minimum of $5 on SNAP-eligible items, participants receive $30 monthly in e-incentives, digital deals, or produce benefit coupons to purchase fresh and frozen produce with no added salt, sugar, or fat. Amazon Fresh and Safeway participants receive additional benefits: Amazon Fresh shoppers receive a $20 monthly delivery promotion coupon, and Safeway participants receive one free grocery delivery per month. The program is funded through ARPA investment and is currently available through December 2026.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $3.6 million ARPA investment distributing monthly fruit and vegetable vouchers, e-incentives, and produce benefit coupons to SNAP participants through multiple channels. Online shoppers can spend $5 on SNAP-eligible items with approved retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, Safeway) for curbside pickup or delivery and receive a $30 monthly e-incentive or produce benefit coupon. Amazon Fresh shoppers also receive a $20 monthly delivery promotion coupon valid toward delivery fees. Safeway in-store shoppers who spend $5 or more monthly using SNAP EBT receive three $10 digital deals (totaling $30) loaded to their Safeway for U account on the first of the following month for fresh or frozen produce with no added salt, sugar, or fat, plus one free grocery delivery per month. Produce coupons are valid for 60 days and can be earned monthly. The program is currently funded through December 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents enrolled in SNAP who want to increase purchases of fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables through online shopping with curbside pickup or delivery at Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway, or in-store shopping at Safeway locations.

Delivery coupons can be used toward delivery fees for eligible B'more Fresh items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in Baltimore City to residents with SNAP benefits. Online orders must be placed for curbside pickup or delivery in Baltimore City with a Baltimore City zip code and default address. In-store digital deals available at Baltimore City Safeway locations.
requirements_list: Must be a SNAP participant
Must be a Baltimore City resident enrolled in SNAP
Must have a valid SNAP/EBT card on file at time of purchase
Must spend minimum $5 on SNAP-eligible items to receive $30 monthly e-incentive, digital deals, or produce benefit coupon
Must shop at one of the participating retailers: Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway
Orders must be placed online for curbside pickup or delivery in Baltimore City, or at a Baltimore City Safeway location
Must have a Safeway for U account (for Safeway participants)
Must enter phone number at store checkout or through online ordering (for Safeway participants)
Must create an Amazon account with a Baltimore City address (for Amazon Fresh participants)
Must add SNAP/EBT card to Amazon Wallet with Baltimore City as default address (for Amazon Fresh participants)
Must have order delivered to receive benefit coupon (for Amazon Fresh participants)
Produce coupons valid for 60 days from issuance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: SNAP participants with active benefits in Baltimore City automatically qualify for the program. For Amazon Fresh online shopping: create or log in to an Amazon account using a Baltimore City address, add SNAP/EBT card to Amazon Wallet with Baltimore City as default address, spend $5 on SNAP-eligible items, place orders for delivery, and the $30 produce benefit coupon and $20 delivery promotion coupon will be automatically added after delivery. Redeem produce coupon within 60 days and repeat monthly for additional coupons. For other online retailers (Giant, Safeway): shop with participating retailers, spend $5 on SNAP-eligible items, place orders for curbside pickup or delivery, and the $30 voucher is automatically added after meeting the spending requirement. For Safeway in-store shopping: sign up for a free Safeway for U account on the Safeway app or at Safeway.com, use SNAP EBT card to spend $5 or more at a Baltimore City Safeway location (in-store, online, or through app), enter phone number at checkout, and digital deals will be automatically loaded to account on the first of the following month.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive preventive and urgent dental care services for low-income, uninsured, and Medicaid-eligible residents of Baltimore City. Services include exams, x-rays, teeth cleanings, fillings, and extractions for ages 12 months and older, as well as pregnant women enrolled in Medicaid. Also includes off-site preventive dental care and community education programs for children ages 5 and younger and their parents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Affordable dental care provided on a fee basis with most Medicaid and Medical Assistance plans accepted, including Maryland Healthy Smiles, Amerigroup, Priority Partners, Jai, and Maryland Physicians Care. Services include exams, x-rays, teeth cleanings, fillings, and extractions. Specialty services requiring an oral surgeon are not available. Off-site preventive dental care services and community education programs are available for children ages 5 and younger and their parents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured, and Medicaid-eligible residents of Baltimore City ages 12 months and older. Pregnant women enrolled in Medicaid also eligible. Children ages 5 and younger and their parents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Basic and urgent dental care services including exams, x-rays, teeth cleanings, fillings, and extractions. Preventive dental care and community education services. Specialty services requiring an oral surgeon are not available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residency required.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be low-income, uninsured, or Medicaid-eligible
Ages 12 months and older for general services
Pregnant women must be enrolled in Medicaid
Child must be age 5 or younger for early prevention program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call one of the clinic locations to schedule a dental appointment for in-clinic services, or contact the program for more information on how to enroll or participate in off-site preventive and community education programs. Dental visits are by scheduled appointment only.

structured_extraction.program_description: Part of Baltimore Homeownership Incentive Program (B-HIP) offering financial assistance to employees of Baltimore City and quasi-City agencies to help them purchase homes in the city. The program offers incentives to make buying a home more affordable by lowering closing costs and boosting down payment assistance. Eligible employees who have been employed for at least six months and complete a City-approved homeownership counseling class within one year before purchasing can receive assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $5,000 forgivable loan (five-year term) awarded to employees of City and quasi-City agencies who have been employed for at least six months. Applicants must complete a City-approved homeownership counseling class within one year before purchasing and contribute at least $1,000 of their own money toward the home. Funds can be used to reduce closing costs and provide down payment assistance for home purchases in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of Baltimore City and quasi-City agencies seeking to purchase homes in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, closing cost reduction, and purchase of residential property in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to homebuyers purchasing properties in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be employed by Baltimore City or a quasi-City agency
Must have been employed for at least six months
Must complete a City-approved homeownership counseling class within one year before purchase
Must contribute at least $1,000 of own money toward the home
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
Internet-connected device required
Valid email address required for registration and notifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact approved homeownership counseling agency and complete counseling requirement. Register an account through the Neighborly Software Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant using your email address. Validate email via link sent to registered email. Log in with email and password and complete the application through the online portal. Provide the Title Company's Employer Identification Number (EIN) under H. Closing Information. Contact DHCD for additional program details. Processing typically takes 10 to 15 business days after approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides subsidies to help low-income residents of Baltimore City pay for heating bills during winter months to reduce risk of hypothermia and cold-related health problems. The program assists vulnerable populations including older adults, individuals experiencing homelessness, and those without adequate home heating. Administered through the Baltimore City Community Action Partnership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidies to assist low-income residents with heating bills and home heating costs during the winter season to prevent hypothermia and cold-related health problems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income residents of Baltimore City who need assistance paying heating bills, especially vulnerable populations including older adults, individuals experiencing homelessness, and those without adequate home heating.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heating bills and home heating costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Low-income households
Resident of Baltimore City
Need assistance with heating bills
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore City Community Action Partnership at 410-396-5555 to apply or get help paying heating bills. Older adults can get assistance completing and mailing applications by contacting the Office of CARE Services at 410-396-2273. Application status can be checked online at myohepstatus.org. Individuals can also check application status or get a copy of the Energy Assistance Application online.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program that provides matching city funds to eligible candidates running for Baltimore City elective office. The program aims to reduce the role of large contributions during elections and encourage small private donations from City residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching city funds to eligible candidates. Candidates must receive a minimum number of qualifying contributions (up to $150) from Baltimore City residents to become eligible: Mayor requires at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling $40,000; Council President and Comptroller each require at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000; City Council candidates require at least 150 qualifying contributions totaling $5,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates who are Baltimore City residents and running for Mayor, Comptroller, City Council President, or City Council in a contested primary and/or general election.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public campaign financing for eligible candidates for City elective office.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Baltimore City. Candidates must be Baltimore City residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be running for Mayor, Comptroller, City Council President, or City Council
Must be running in a contested primary and/or general election
Must be certified for public funding by the State Board of Elections
Mayor candidates: at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling $40,000 in aggregate
Council President candidates: at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000 in aggregate
Comptroller candidates: at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000 in aggregate
City Council candidates: at least 150 qualifying contributions totaling $5,000 in aggregate
Qualifying contributions must be from Baltimore City residents and up to $150 each
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates must receive the minimum number of qualifying contributions from City residents, then apply for certification by the State Board of Elections to become eligible for public matching funds. The program is governed by State and City law and overseen by the City's Department of Finance in consultation with the City's Fair Election Fund Commission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Housing Department LIGHT Program
structured_extraction.program_description: LIGHT is a Baltimore City program that provides free or low-cost services to help residents make their homes safer, healthier, and more comfortable. Services include housing repairs (plumbing, heating, electrical, roof), energy efficiency improvements, lead hazard removal, and accessibility modifications. LIGHT serves as a unified access point for housing services, offering a single application that provides evaluation for three grant and loan programs plus 60+ additional programs and benefits from public and nonprofit agencies. LIGHT Coordinators assess resident needs and connect them with a network of partner agencies and programs to address water bills, energy efficiency issues, and other housing-related problems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost services to repair homes, improve energy efficiency, reduce lead hazards, and make homes more accessible. Services include grants, forgivable loans, and deferred loans for home repairs including roof, heating, plumbing, and electrical systems repairs or replacement; energy efficiency improvements such as HVAC maintenance, attic insulation, air sealing, weatherstripping, pipe wraps, and lightbulbs; lead hazard reduction including remediation, door/window treatment, floor treatment, and paint removal; accessibility modifications for people with disabilities; and water bill assistance. Forgivable loans are forgiven after 5 years if applicant remains primary resident; deferred loans are due when property is sold. Assistance is delivered through coordination with a network of partner agencies. Applicants work with LIGHT Coordinators who assess needs and connect them with appropriate programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and renters in Baltimore City who need assistance making homes safer, healthier, and more comfortable. Eligibility includes owner-occupied properties for home rehabilitation, households with pregnant women or children under 6 for lead risk reduction, and both homeowners and tenants for lead remediation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs including roof, heating, plumbing, and electrical systems repairs or replacement; energy efficiency improvements including HVAC maintenance, attic insulation, air sealing, weatherstripping, pipe wraps, and lightbulbs; lead hazard reduction including remediation, door/window treatment, floor treatment, and paint removal; accessibility modifications for people with disabilities; water bill assistance; and emergency and code violation repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner or renter in Baltimore City
Income limits vary by program and household size (ranging from $66,300-$129,100 annually depending on household size)
Homeowners must have deed in their name or explain co-owners not living in home
Current on mortgage, ground rent, and property taxes
No outstanding judgments or recent bankruptcy
No foreclosure efforts
Must carry homeowner's insurance
Lead-based paint compliance for homes built before 1978
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can apply through the online Application Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/BALTIMOREMD/participant or download a pre-application form and mail it to the LIGHT Intake & Assessment Unit at 417 East Fayette Street, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202. LIGHT Coordinators then assess needs and connect applicants with appropriate programs. Program reviews pre-application and contacts potentially eligible applicants for full application submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Requires developers of multifamily, market-rate residential projects receiving major public subsidies or significant land use authorizations to make affordable housing units available to households with limited incomes at reduced rents for 30 years. Projects must make 10% of their units available as affordable inclusionary units, with 5% available to households earning 50% of area median income and 5% available to households earning 60% of area median income. Additional units up to 5% may be available for extremely low-income and very low-income households with developer subsidy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Developers of market-rate rental projects must make 10% of units available as affordable inclusionary units for 30 years. Units must be offered to households earning 50% of area median income (5% of units) and 60% of area median income (5% of units). The difference between market-rate rent and affordable rent is covered by the High-Performance Inclusionary Housing Tax Credit administered by the city's Finance Department. Additional inclusionary units may be provided at extremely low-income (30% AMI) and very low-income levels with developer subsidy.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual Developer/Residential Project Report due by January 31 for each year of the 30-year affordability period; Inclusionary Housing Plan must be submitted with building permit application; Public comment period 30 days from publication (approximately February 14, 2026 from January 15, 2026 register)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of multifamily residential projects receiving major public subsidies or significant land use authorizations from Baltimore City; low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating affordable housing units within market-rate rental projects. Units must be newly constructed, substantially rehabilitated, or converted from non-residential use. Inclusionary units must serve tenants at specified AMI percentages and remain affordable for 30 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. The program applies to market rental projects that submit a building permit application on or after July 21, 2024, and to projects receiving major public subsidy or significant land use authorization (30+ unit increase via PUD or rezoning).
requirements_list: Include 20 or more units
Receive a major public subsidy OR benefit from significant land use authorization
Be newly constructed, substantially rehabilitated, or converted from non-residential housing use
Construction or conversion cost must exceed $60,000 per unit
Developers must submit an approved Inclusionary Housing Plan before building permit is released
Inclusionary units must be comparable in design and amenities to market-rate units and dispersed throughout project
Units must remain affordable for 30 years from Certificate of Occupancy or Use and Occupancy permit
Submit annual residential project report by January 31
Income must be verified and certified prior to lease execution and annually at lease renewal
Tenant income limits determined by HUD guidelines adjusted for household size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers must complete and submit an Inclusionary Housing Plan when applying for a building permit. The Plan must include general project information, confirmation that the project meets all criteria, project description, table identifying inclusionary units with unit types and rent amounts, project schedule, affirmative marketing plan, and site plan with unit specifications showing maximum affordable rents. Developers must execute a Declaration of Affordability with the City. DHCD staff reviews plans and presents them to the Inclusionary Housing Board for recommendation. Building permits are not released without an approved plan. Property owners submit annual reports by January 31. Tenants are screened sequentially by application date and selected from separate waitlists by income eligibility and bedroom size.

structured_extraction.program_description: Investment program for City agencies or quasi-City agencies to fund innovative projects. The Innovation Fund provides loans to Baltimore City agencies for one-time investments that improve results, increase revenue, or reduce operating costs for City services. The fund is self-sustaining, with savings or revenue generated by funded projects returned to the fund for future projects. Historical loans have ranged from $98,000 to $2,000,000, with four of eleven projects achieving full repayment status and continuing to generate revenue beyond their loan value.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for innovative projects with expected payback via new revenue, cost savings, or both. The Innovation Fund provides loans to City agencies for one-time investments. Repayment comes from savings or revenue generated by the projects. Historical loans have ranged from $98,000 to $2,000,000. Four of eleven projects have achieved repayment status and continue to generate revenue beyond their loan value. Projects must demonstrate clear intentions and benefits, present a business case with repayment plan, identify and mitigate risks, define success metrics, show equity impact, outline financial resources, and leverage partnerships.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis during the fiscal year; annual budget process submissions for inclusion in budget
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City agencies and quasi-City agencies seeking to fund innovative projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Innovative projects with measurable returns; payback via revenue generation or cost savings. Funds must be repaid through savings and/or revenue generation. Projects should align with Mayoral priorities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore City agencies only
requirements_list: Complete all proposal sections (incomplete applications not considered)
Keep free response questions to less than 150 words
Include project description, implementation plan, evaluation metrics, and budget
Obtain signatures from project managers, fiscal officer, and agency head
Clear project intentions and benefits
Business case with repayment plan
Risk identification and mitigation
Performance measures and success metrics
Equity impact analysis
Specific itemized costs and financial plan
Partnership leveraging and external funding
Professional writing standards
Projects must generate savings or revenue to repay the Innovation Fund
Projects must lead to improved results and reduced operating costs
Projects must be one-time investments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Agencies submit a detailed project proposal during the annual budget process or on a rolling basis during the fiscal year. Submit completed proposal with original signatures to Aaron.Moore@baltimorecity.gov. Proposals are evaluated by a Review Team using a rating sheet with 8 criteria (max 100 points). Those submitted during the annual budget process are eligible for inclusion in the annual budget; those received later in the fiscal year are assessed on a rolling basis. Successful projects receive loans and are monitored for savings and revenue generation to support repayment and future funding cycles.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Live Near Your Work Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between participating employers and the City of Baltimore that encourages homeownership near place of employment by providing down payment and closing cost assistance to employees. The City matches participating employers' contributions between $1,000 and $2,500, for total incentives of $2,000–$5,000 or more depending on the employer. Funds are provided as grants that do not need to be repaid and are forgivable at 20 percent per year over 5 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Minimum $2,000 grant ($1,000 from City of Baltimore and $1,000 from employer) provided as conditional assistance to be used toward down payment and closing costs. Total incentives of $2,000–$5,000 or more depending on the employer contribution match. No annual income limits. Buyer must contribute at least $1,000 towards purchase and use the property as principal residence. Loan is forgivable at 20 percent per year over 5 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of participating employers who are first-time and repeat homebuyers purchasing homes near their workplace in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to reduce closing costs and provide down payment assistance for home purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to homebuyers purchasing properties in Baltimore City near their place of employment. Participating employers may develop additional eligible neighborhood restrictions for their employees.
requirements_list: Must be employed by a participating employer
Must purchase a home in Baltimore City near place of employment
Must complete homeownership counseling from a City-approved agency within one year before writing offer
Must contribute at least $1,000 of own money toward the home
Must use property as principal residence
Settlement date must be at least 30 days after submitting application
Must have internet-connected device with modern web browser for application portal
Must have valid email address for registration and system notifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the list of participating employers. Contact DHCD or visit LiveBaltimore.com for more information. Complete required homeownership counseling from a City-approved agency. Register an account and submit an application through the Applicant Portal at portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant by accessing via modern web browser, registering with email and password, validating email, and logging in with registered credentials. Provide the Title Company's Employer Identification Number (EIN) in the Neighborly Application portal under H. Closing Information. Processing typically takes 10 to 15 business days after approval. For additional information, contact DHCD.Homeownership@baltimorecity.gov or (410) 396-3124.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Local Hiring Law and Employ Baltimore Executive Order
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive local hiring requirement for vendors, contractors, and subcontractors who do business with Baltimore City. The program applies to city-funded contracts over $50,000 and city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000. For contracts over $300,000, businesses must hire 51% Baltimore City residents for new positions. For contracts between $50,000 and $300,000 (excluding emergency and professional services), contractors must utilize local hiring services. The program provides free services including recruitment assistance, pre-screening of applicants, interview space, tax credits, and training reimbursement to help businesses meet hiring goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services provided by MOED Employer Services including tax credits, recruitment assistance, pre-screening of applicants, free interview space, and training reimbursement. MOED provides employment analysis and recruitment services for vendor hiring needs. For contracts over $300,000, businesses must meet a goal of hiring 51% Baltimore City residents for new positions. For contracts between $50,000 and $300,000, contractors receive workforce recruitment support and must submit monthly or bi-annual employment reports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vendors, contractors, and subcontractors who receive city-awarded contracts over $300,000 or work on city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000, as well as contractors with Employ Baltimore Executive Order contracts between $50,000.01 and $300,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free recruitment services, applicant pre-screening, interview space, tax credits, and training reimbursement for hiring Baltimore City residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicable to vendors and contractors working on Baltimore City-funded contracts and city-subsidized projects within Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Meet with MOED within 2 weeks after contract award to complete an Employment Analysis or schedule a workforce meeting
Post new jobs with MOED only for a period of seven days
Utilize MOED's recruitment services for new hires
For contracts over $300,000: meet the goal of 51% of all new hires being Baltimore City residents

Submit monthly employment reports (for contracts over $300,000) or bi-annual employment reports (for contracts between $50,000 and $300,000) with information on current workers, new workers, and Baltimore City residents on the project
Local hiring mandates for city-funded projects
Implementation of hiring preferences for Baltimore City residents
Collective bargaining agreement positions may be waivered but all non-union positions must be posted with MOED
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a contract is awarded by the City, the business or vendor meets with MOED Employer Services staff within two weeks to discuss staffing needs and complete an Employment Analysis. When hiring for city-funded contracts, the business sends job postings to MOED. MOED then shares job openings, pre-screens applicants, and offers free interview space. The business submits employment reports on a monthly or bi-annual basis to demonstrate compliance with local hiring requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program reduces HIV, Hepatitis C and other infections by reducing the circulation of used syringes. It helps individuals with substance use disorders overcome addiction by linking them to drug treatment services. The program provides counseling and testing for HIV and syphilis, and offers opioid overdose response training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and confidential needle exchange services, counseling, HIV and syphilis testing, opioid overdose response training, and linkage to drug treatment services provided at 11 locations during 18 weekly time slots throughout Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jeffrey Long, MPA; Valerie Pasquale, MPH; Tyler Shaw, MPH
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with substance use disorders and high-risk individuals in Baltimore City seeking harm reduction services, HIV prevention, and linkage to treatment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include needle exchange, counseling, HIV and syphilis testing, and opioid overdose response training to reduce disease transmission and connect individuals to drug treatment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available at 11 locations throughout Baltimore City during 18 weekly time slots.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk-in services are available at designated locations and times. No formal application process described.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Strategic Investment – Rapid Re-housing
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding initiative to support rapid re-housing efforts for individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The program uses a Housing First approach that rapidly connects families and individuals experiencing homelessness to permanent housing through time-limited financial assistance and targeted support services. The program aims to rehouse people experiencing homelessness, stabilize those at imminent risk, reduce unsheltered homelessness and encampments, drive progress toward racial equity, and enhance partnerships to advance person-centered approaches. Services include housing identification, rental assistance administration, and case management/support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore City received $5,663,850 in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding allocated to support rapid re-housing efforts. MOHS is selecting multiple qualified non-profit organizations to implement and operate rapid re-housing projects. Services include: (1) Housing identification and securing permanent housing; (2) Rental assistance for security deposits, moving expenses, utilities, and short- to medium-term rent subsidies (4-24 months, average annual award $500,000-$800,000); (3) Case management and wraparound support services including individualized service plans, employment/workforce referrals, health/mental health services, and connection to mainstream community resources. Rental assistance is calculated using FY2022 Fair Market Rates data. Organizations may use progressive engagement models for rental subsidies (declining subsidy, fixed percentage, or fixed subsidy models).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with capacity to implement and operate rapid re-housing services for people experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The program serves individuals and families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, including households without children, households with children, survivors of domestic violence/intimate partner violence, veterans, youth (18-24), seniors, and other vulnerable populations. Priority populations include people of color, pregnant/parenting individuals, LGBTQ+ individuals, individuals with multiple health conditions, domestic violence survivors, sexual trafficking survivors, individuals with lived experience in institutional settings, and those experiencing Category 1 or 4 homelessness with income under 30% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing identification and securing permanent housing; rental assistance (security deposits, moving expenses, utilities, and short- to medium-term rent subsidies); case management and wraparound services; supportive services including employment/workforce development, health/mental health services, utility assistance, credit repair, legal services; staff salaries for eligible positions; administrative costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City TB Program provides comprehensive tuberculosis services including case management, diagnosis, and treatment for individuals with latent TB infection (LTBI), active TB disease, and presumptive TB. Services include nurse case management, expert medical TB management, lab work, imaging, TB medications, directly observed therapy, referrals to outside services, and contact investigations for infectious TB cases. Diagnostic testing is limited to chest X-rays, sputum AFB smear, and sputum mycobacterial culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All TB services are offered free of charge. Services include nurse case management and expert medical TB management; lab work, sputa, and imaging for latent TB, active TB, and presumptive TB; TB medication for latent TB or daily directly observed therapy for active TB; referrals to outside services and providers; and contact investigations on all infectious active TB cases. Diagnostic testing is limited to chest X-rays, sputum AFB smear, and sputum mycobacterial culture.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with active tuberculosis disease, latent TB infection, or presumptive TB (being evaluated for active TB). Priority referral populations include individuals without insurance to pay for TB medications, those experiencing barriers to TB care, high-risk individuals (HIV positive, immunocompromised, history of incarceration or homelessness, recent immigrants, or contacts to active TB cases), recent immigrants, refugees, and asylum seekers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: TB diagnosis, treatment, case management, and prevention services including medications, directly observed therapy, lab work, and imaging.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available to residents of Baltimore City. The Baltimore City TB program does not perform pre-employment TB screening or offer walk-in appointments.
requirements_list: Individuals must be referred to the Baltimore City TB Program (active TB cases must be reported for case management and treatment)
All confirmed active TB disease requires microbiological or clinical confirmation
Appointments only (no walk-ins)
Recent referral to the Baltimore City Health Department through TB referral form or online Qualtrics form
Confirmed microbiologic diagnosis of TB or clinical diagnosis in some cases
Complete diagnostic evaluation before referral
Identified clinical provider for future evaluation and care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the TB Referral Form by either faxing it to the secure fax at 410-396-9403 or completing it electronically through the Qualtrics TB referral online form. Call BCHD to discuss cases without confirmed TB diagnosis prior to faxing. Include relevant radiology, lab reports, and narrative notes. For TB consultation services, call 410-396-9413. Appointments are required; the program does not accept walk-ins.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Financial Empowerment Center offers professional financial counseling and coaching services to residents as a free public service. structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore's Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) Community Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Opioid Restitution Fund provides grants to nonprofit organizations and government agencies for community-led initiatives and programs addressing the opioid epidemic in Baltimore City. Established through Mayor Brandon Scott's August 2024 Executive Order, the fund receives Baltimore's opioid settlement recoveries totaling $579.9 million and sustains impact for at least 15 years. The program funds projects that support overdose prevention, treatment access, harm reduction, recovery support, substance use prevention, treatment, recovery, and addressing social determinants of health related to opioid harms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1 (Fiscal Year 2026) provides a total of $2 million available for allocation across three funding tiers: Tier 1 up to $50,000 for low-barrier social support services (housing, transportation, food assistance, education, employment); Tier 2 up to $250,000 for full array of low-barrier harm reduction services (naloxone distribution, drug checking, syringe service programs, wound care); Tier 3 up to $500,000 for low-barrier mobile treatment services in overdose-disproportionately-affected areas with robust harm reduction. Organizations can propose project periods of up to two years. Funding amounts vary by tier. Awarded amounts may differ from proposed budgets based on scope of work and available funding. Organizations that use their full award within a single year remain eligible to apply in the following year. The Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs (MORP) serves as the lead contract administrator, managing grant applications and execution with awardees and conducting comprehensive fiscal monitoring and review of fund administration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and government agencies in Baltimore City leading community efforts to address the opioid crisis through prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction; organizations with proven experience serving populations impacted by the opioid overdose crisis in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing overdose prevention, treatment access, harm reduction, recovery support, substance use prevention, treatment, recovery, and addressing social determinants of health related to the opioid crisis. Allowable uses include salaries, contracts, materials, equipment, grants, naloxone distribution, drug checking services, syringe service programs, wound care, housing, transportation, food assistance, education, employment, evidence-based treatment services, peer support, and program evaluation. Unallowable uses include law enforcement salaries/equipment, drug courts, mandatory treatment, drug testing without clinical need, stigmatizing materials, large-scale capital construction, fundraising costs, and services already funded by Statewide Settlements. General organization overhead is capped at 15% of grant award.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals through the Mayor's Office of Recovery Programs Application Portal. The process includes creating an online account through Grant Lifecycle Manager portal, completing all required fields in the online application form, submitting proposal, scoring based on established criteria across 8 dimensions plus 2 additional point categories with point-based scoring system, application stage evaluation, and notification of awards. MORP conducts comprehensive fiscal monitoring and review of fund administration. Detailed instructions and appendices guide applicants through requirements and evaluation criteria. System auto-saves every 100 characters or when exiting fields. Applicants receive decision status on dashboard.

structured_extraction.program_name: CFY 27 Transportation Services Request for Proposals (RFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Homeless Services administers a competitive grant program to provide free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The program funds non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, and city agencies to transport people to shelters, services, employment, and housing within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Both new and renewal proposals are accepted for City Fiscal Year 2027. Services are provided during winter shelter period (October 15 through March 31) and non-winter shelter period (April 1 through October 14), prioritizing assistance based on vulnerability and severity of service needs. The performance period is July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Services include transportation to/from 8-10 designated shelters across Baltimore City and pick-up/drop-off at 11-15 designated stops throughout the day, requiring operation of 2-3 buses on fixed schedules with defined pick-up and drop-off times.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding to support non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, and city agencies to provide free transportation services to homeless individuals and families to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Estimated $400,000 available through Baltimore City General Funds. Payments structured as flat monthly rate inclusive of service and operating costs. Services must be provided during winter shelter period (October 15 through March 31) and non-winter shelter period (April 1 through October 14). Services include daily routes to/from 8-10 designated shelters and pick-up/drop-off services at 11-15 designated stops during morning (6:45 AM – 11:00 AM) and afternoon (3:00 PM onwards) hours. The 12-month contract term is July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations, for-profit organizations, city agencies, and transportation service providers seeking to provide transportation services to homeless individuals and families in Baltimore City. End users are individuals and families experiencing homelessness, including vulnerable populations, older adults, and persons with mobility issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services to shelters, services, employment, and housing for individuals and families experiencing homelessness within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Eligible uses include: personnel costs (labor and fringe benefits), vehicle procurement, maintenance, and operations, fuel and vehicle accessories, 2-way radios and mobile devices, supplies and cleaning products, insurance and liability coverage, staff training programs, administrative fees and equipment, driver wages and training, and vehicle safety features (seat belts, child safety features, accessible boarding).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Baltimore City. Services must be provided within the Baltimore Continuum of Care (BCOC) with 8-10 designated shelters and 11-15 designated stops throughout Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A bidder's conference is held on March 5, 2026 at 1:00pm to review requirements and answer questions. Organizations must submit a complete Request for Proposals package via email to mohs.hsp.application@baltimorecity.gov by March 27, 2026 at 5:00pm EST, including a Shelter Transportation Request for Proposal, Shelter Transportation Application, and Budget Proposal Template.
