structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Rehabilitation and Restoration Tax Credit (CHAP Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program administered by the Commission for Historical and Architectural Preservation (CHAP) and the Baltimore City Department of Finance that encourages property owners in Baltimore City to complete major rehabilitation and restoration projects on historic structures. Established in 1996 to help preserve and revitalize Baltimore's neighborhoods by encouraging the rehabilitation of historic structures to promote equitable and inclusive economic growth and vitality. The credit is calculated based on the investment made in qualified rehabilitation work and appears as a special credit on the property tax bill. Both residential and commercial properties are eligible if they are located in one of Baltimore City's historic districts or designated as local landmarks or contributing properties. The credit is a 10-year tax credit computed once and applied for the entire 10-year life of the credit, and is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. Projects must demonstrate a minimum investment of at least 25% of the initial full cash value of the property, with completion timelines of two years for projects up to $3.5 million and three years for larger projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year property tax credit that appears as a special credit on the property tax bill. For projects with rehabilitation costs up to $5 million, property owners receive a 100% tax credit on the increased property value for all 10 years. For projects over $5 million, the credit declines from 80% in years 1-5 to 30% in year 10. The credit is calculated by the Department of Finance based on the property's appraisal and the amount invested in qualified rehabilitation work, offsetting tax increases resulting from substantial rehabilitation projects. Projects must demonstrate a minimum investment of at least 25% of the initial full cash value of the property. Projects with rehabilitation costs up to $3.5 million have two years to complete work; projects over $3.5 million have three years. One-time extensions are available upon request. The credit is fully transferrable to a new owner for the remaining life of the credit. No new applications may be filed after August 28, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Historic property owners, home owners, business owners, developers, and first-time home buyers in Baltimore City with historically designated properties looking to rehabilitate and restore historic structures
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation work on historically designated properties including renovation, interior and exterior rehabilitation, and restoration. Eligible costs include material and labor costs, architect, engineering, and design fees, architectural design, appraisal, engineering, demolition, site preparation, restoration, alteration, interior/exterior work, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, and finish work. Ineligible costs include property acquisition, utility bills, property taxes, and holding costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Baltimore City's 33 local historic districts, designated as one of 182 local landmarks, have National Register Individual Designation, contribute to a Baltimore City Historic District, National Register Historic District, or the Baltimore National Heritage Area. Properties must be listed individually on the National Register of Historic Places, located in a National Register Historic or Landmark District, designated on the Baltimore City Landmark List, or located in a Baltimore City Historic and Architectural Preservation District (certified by CHAP as contributing). Program covers approximately 20% of Baltimore's land area with 32% of the city's population residing in eligible districts.
requirements_list: Property must be historically designated (Baltimore City Landmark, National Register Individual Designation, Contributing to a historic district or heritage area)
Property must be located in a historic district or designated as a local landmark
Property must be a historic structure
Minimum investment of at least 25% of the full cash value of the property
Work must comply with CHAP Design Guidelines
Both residential and commercial properties are eligible
Qualified restoration and rehabilitation projects are eligible
Project must receive preliminary approval from CHAP Staff before any work begins
Applicants must provide thorough photo documentation (color, high resolution) of all exterior elevations, roof, interior rooms, and significant architectural details
If building elevation or interior layout will be altered, applicants must provide existing and proposed drawings
Detailed scope of work describing interior and exterior plans, proposed materials, treatments, and alterations
Proof of ownership (HUD1, deed, signed purchase agreement, or tax bill)
Authorization to Proceed Application required only for properties in local historic districts
Enterprise Zone Verification Form required if property has commercial component
Pre- and post-improvement appraisals required by certified Maryland appraiser meeting Department of Finance requirements
Appraisals must be submitted within 90 days of application and 90 days after final Use and Occupancy Permit
$50 review fee paid online

Final certification requires high-resolution color photographs of completed work, copies of all permits (including Use & Occupancy if required), notarized cost documentation showing at least 25% investment, and final appraisal
Local historic district properties subject to design review by CHAP for exterior changes
Design review required for infill construction in local districts
Property must maintain continuing eligibility conditions throughout 10-year credit term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine if your property is eligible by checking if it is historically designated using the online mapping layer. 2. Apply online through the Historic Tax Credit Application system at propertytaxcredits.baltimorecity.gov. 3. Submit all required documentation including photos, drawings (if applicable), scope of work, proof of ownership, authorization to proceed (if in historic district), enterprise zone form (if applicable), and pre- and post-improvement appraisals. 4. Pay the $50 review fee online. 5. CHAP staff reviews the complete application and issues written approval via email. 6. Applicant completes rehabilitation work following CHAP Design Guidelines. 7. Upon project completion, submit final certification through the online system with photos of completed work, permit copies, notarized cost documentation, and final appraisal. 8. CHAP issues final certification; credit appears on next tax bill as a Special Credit. 9. For projects over $5 million, the Department of Finance must also review and approve.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive housing initiative funded through the American Rescue Plan Act that helps individuals experiencing homelessness secure permanent housing in Baltimore City. structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons with HIV/AIDS (HOPWA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The HOPWA Program is the only federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS and their families. It provides stable housing assistance and supportive services to persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families in the Baltimore-Towson Eligible Metropolitan Statistical Area. The program aims to improve quality of life through provider agencies serving the region. Housing assistance includes tenant-based or project-based rental assistance, conversion, lease and repair to facilities, new construction, and short-term rent, mortgage, and utility payments to prevent homelessness. Supportive services include permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, assistance gaining access to local, State, and Federal benefits and services, and resources and referrals for drug and alcohol abuse treatment, daycare, nutritional services, intensive care, and physical and mental health services. HOPWA funds are distributed annually through a competitive application process to eligible project sponsors and non-profit organizations to deliver housing-related services and support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing assistance includes tenant-based or project-based rental assistance, conversion, lease and repair to facilities, new construction, and short-term rent, mortgage, and utility payments to prevent homelessness. Supportive services include permanent housing placement, employment and education services, personal assistance, assistance gaining access to local, State, and Federal benefits and services, and resources and referrals for drug and alcohol abuse treatment, daycare, nutritional services, intensive care, and physical and mental health services. HOPWA provides grant funding and subsidies annually through a competitive application process, with funding amounts dependent on availability and community priorities. All counties/cities within the Baltimore-Towson EMSA except Carroll County provide housing assistance in the form of tenant-based rental assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Levels of Care for Baltimore City Hospitals Responding to the Opioid Epidemic
structured_extraction.program_description: A shared framework for establishment of services for patients with high-risk opioid use and/or opioid use disorder (OUD) in emergency department, inpatient, and outpatient settings. The program designates hospital care levels (Level 1, 2, and 3) based on their ability to screen patients for substance use disorder, provide addiction treatment including medication-assisted treatment, distribute naloxone, connect patients with peer recovery support, and ensure responsible opioid prescribing practices. The framework aims to recognize the breadth and depth of Baltimore City hospitals' response to the opioid crisis and encourage adoption of comprehensive services for patients with OUD and policies to prevent new cases of OUD.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a shared, evidence-based framework and certification process for hospitals to implement best practices in substance use disorder screening, medication-assisted treatment initiation, naloxone prescription and dispensing, peer recovery specialist services, and judicious opioid prescribing. Hospitals will be certified by the Baltimore City Health Department as having achieved one of three Levels of Care (Level 1, 2, or 3) based on meeting specified criteria. The BCHD provides support including site visits, detailed feedback, and technical assistance to help hospitals meet the standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City acute-care hospital leaders and staff seeking certification in substance use disorder treatment and opioid epidemic response.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification in the Levels of Care framework supports hospitals in implementing screening protocols, medication-assisted treatment services, naloxone distribution, peer recovery specialist employment, and opioid prescribing guidelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies to acute-care hospitals operating in Baltimore City. Services must be directly available at each hospital campus. Services at affiliated outpatient settings (surgical centers, community-based primary care offices) will not be considered part of the hospital. The initiative was launched with Baltimore City's 11 acute-care hospitals and is designed to coordinate a unified response to the opioid epidemic across the city's hospital system.
requirements_list: Screen emergency department and/or admitted patients for substance use disorder
Provide emergency department discharge protocol including referral to community-based treatment
Prescribe or dispense naloxone to high-risk patients
Initiate medication-assisted treatment for patients with opioid use disorder
Implement guidelines for judicious opioid analgesic prescribing
Provide educational materials about safe storage and disposal of opioids
Offer peer recovery specialist services or similar support services
Monitor fidelity to prescribing guidelines
Screen outpatient clinic patients for substance use disorder
Provide ongoing medication-assisted treatment in outpatient clinics
Offer MAT in appropriate outpatient clinics (primary care, specialty care clinics treating high-risk patients)
Maintain up-to-date written protocol for MAT eligibility determination
Identify personnel to provide MAT
Provide staff training during onboarding and annual curriculum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Hospitals interested in certification should review the application document. Hospitals must ensure they can meet the criteria for the level of certification they are pursuing. Hospital determinations of appropriate clinics will be reviewed with the Baltimore City Health Department during the application process. Hospitals then submit the application with supporting documentation demonstrating compliance with each criterion. Responses are saved if the applicant needs to exit before submission. The application can be completed over multiple sessions, though completion in one sitting is recommended. For questions or guidance, hospitals contact the program via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive apprenticeship program administered by Baltimore City that supports both jobseekers and employers. Jobseekers receive paid apprenticeships with hands-on training from industry experts, earning wages while completing at least 2,000 hours of on-the-job training per year plus classroom instruction. Employers receive $2,500 per apprentice to pay for training, wages, or support services. The program connects jobseekers with apprenticeship opportunities across multiple industries while helping employers recruit Baltimore City residents and access funding to support apprenticeship programs.

Scheduled pay increases are tied to skills and service. Pre-apprenticeship support including resume building and skills assessments is available. (2) Employers receive $2,500 per apprentice to pay for training, wages, or support services. Employers must provide at least 2,000 hours per year of on-the-job training under highly skilled journeyworkers and at least 144 hours of related instruction per year.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Construction and/or Rehabilitation of Existing Affordable Rental Housing NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) provides grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support new construction of affordable rental housing and rehabilitation and preservation of existing rental projects for affordable housing. This recurring program includes set asides for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers, with emerging developers defined as those who have completed at least 3 and no more than 5 projects. Projects must serve households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income, with at least half of funded units serving households at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income. The program supports both new construction and preservation of existing rental housing units and emphasizes impactful projects that leverage additional investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500,000 available from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund with set asides for Community Land Trusts and emerging developers. Funds support new construction of affordable rental housing or rehabilitation and preservation of existing rental projects for affordable housing, with individual project requests up to $1,000,000 per project. Set-asides include up to $1,000,000 for Community Land Trusts and up to $1,000,000 for emerging developers. Maximum funding is 50% of Total Development Cost or $1,000,000 per project, whichever is less. Per-unit maximums: $75,000 for 50% AMI households; $120,000 per unit for fewer than 10 units at 30% AMI; $150,000 per unit for 10+ units at 30% AMI. Up to 25% of award for predevelopment and acquisition costs (grants only), up to 10% for operating/support service costs, and up to 25% advance assessment for predevelopment/acquisition (grant awards only).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers, Community Land Trusts, emerging developers, and development organizations interested in creating new affordable rental housing or rehabilitating and preserving existing rental projects for affordable housing in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of affordable rental housing and/or rehabilitation and preservation of existing rental projects for affordable housing, including construction costs (builder's profit, overhead, construction management), architecture and engineering fees, personnel and consultant costs, City Prevailing Wage rates for all employees, debt service and operating subsidies for occupied buildings, permanent supportive housing services, predevelopment costs, acquisition of non-City-owned properties, and mixed-use project rental portions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only, with priority for Communities of Opportunity as defined by Maryland State QAP for Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, Impact Investment Areas as defined in DHCD Community Development Framework, Markets of Strength neighborhoods (Categories A-D per Baltimore City Housing Market Typology 2023), and other major revitalization areas

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing Hotel Conversion - Request For Proposals (RFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program to rehabilitate and operate permanent supportive housing at three adjacent City-owned hotel sites in Baltimore. Comprehensive onsite supportive services will include individualized service plans, case management, medical screenings, mental health assistance, and life management skills.

Properties will be conveyed to the selected developer at a nominal purchase agreement. Organizations submit proposals to rehabilitate and operate the designated hotel properties, with funding provided through the award process. Developers are responsible for securing rehabilitation funding and operating subsidies. Housing Authority of Baltimore City (HABC) will release a separate RFP for project-based vouchers in fall 2024.

Gay Street, and the parking lot at 320 N. Front Street) and convert them into permanent supportive housing with a minimum of 100 units. Funds support property acquisition and rehabilitation costs, predevelopment, construction, property management, supportive services delivery, and onsite and offsite amenities including sustainability features.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pimlico Community Development Authority Local Impact Aid Funding
structured_extraction.program_description: The Pimlico Community Development Authority (PCDA) Local Impact Aid program provides community development funding generated from video lottery terminal slots revenue for projects in the Park Heights Master Plan area and surrounding neighborhoods within a 1-mile radius of Pimlico in Baltimore City. The funding supports capital projects for economic and community development, infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, housing, and other public services and improvements. Eighty-five percent of available funds are allocated to the Park Heights Master Plan area, with the remaining 15% allocated to neighborhoods around the Park Heights Master Plan area within a 1-mile radius, including the Northwest Community Planning Forum SNAP area, Liberty-Wabash area, and Coldspring Newton. Funding is sourced from 5.5% of gross Video Lottery Terminal revenue under Maryland Education Trust Fund – Video Lottery Terminals legislation, 2007 SB 3, and provides 20 years of funding through fiscal year 2032.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local Impact Aid (slots revenue) is available for capital projects and operating grants benefitting economic and community development, infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, housing, and other public services and improvements. Capital grants are provided on a reimbursement basis at project conclusion. Operating grants follow a 40-40-20 disbursement schedule. Minimum funding requirement is $25,000 per project. Projects must be completable within two years from funding start date. Eighty-five percent of available funds must be allocated to the Park Heights Master Plan area, and the remaining 15% is allocated to neighborhoods around the Park Heights Master Plan area within a 1-mile radius. The funding is appropriated to City agencies or to agencies that administer grants or contracts with community partners. Applicants submit funding requests through an online application form and should review the Pimlico Local Impact Aid Guidelines and Scoring Rubric.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, September 29, 2025 at 11:59 PM EDT (extended deadline, FY27 cycle)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with IRS tax-exempt status (501(c)3), mission-based organizations without 501(c)3 status but with tax-exempt fiscal sponsor, faith-based organizations proposing non-religious public benefit projects, public schools proposing community-based projects benefiting students, and City agencies serving the Pimlico area, Park Heights Master Plan area, and the surrounding 1-mile radius neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating projects for economic and community development, infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, housing, organizational support and capacity building, parks and recreation, environmental improvements, transportation, workforce development, and other public services and improvements in the eligible geographic areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Park Heights Master Plan area (bounded by Northern Parkway (N), Wabash Ave. to Western Maryland Railroad (W), Liberty Heights Ave. (S), Druid Park Dr. (SE), Greenspring Ave. (E)) and surrounding neighborhoods within a 1-mile radius, including the Northwest Community Planning Forum SNAP area, Liberty-Wabash area, and Coldspring Newton in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in the Park Heights Master Plan area or within the designated 1-mile radius around Pimlico Racetrack
For capital purposes benefitting economic and community development
Applicants must follow the FY27 Pimlico Local Impact Aid Guidelines
Projects must be in the area around Pimlico Racetrack
Clear project scope, objectives, and goals aligned with outcomes
Documented methods to measure positive outcomes and report progress
Feasible implementation plan with realistic timeline
Comprehensive budget with narrative and justification
Demonstrated applicant capacity and resources to complete project
Connection to community adopted plans and strategic priorities
Address equity statement components (structural, procedural, distributional, transgenerational)
Resource leverage from internal and external organizations
Sustainability plan beyond Year 1
Minimum funding requirement of $25,000 per project
Projects must be completable within two years from funding start date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Pimlico Community Development Authority serves an advisory role in determining priorities regarding the spending plan for Local Impact Aid funding. Applicants submit funding requests through an online application form and should review the FY27 Pimlico Local Impact Aid Guidelines and Scoring Rubric. Projects are evaluated against 9 scoring criteria on a 0-5 scale plus 4 bonus criteria worth 3 points each, assessing intent/effectiveness, measurable outcomes, implementation timeline, budget feasibility, applicant capacity, community connection, equity response, resource leverage, and sustainability. PCDA advises the Mayor on priorities, and final funding decisions are made as part of the City budget approval by the Mayor and City Council. Once the spending plan is finalized, video lottery terminal Local Impact Aid revenues are appropriated to the City agency designated to implement a project or to an appropriate agency to administer a grant or contract with a community partner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ryan White Part A HIV/AIDS Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive HIV-related medical and support services to people living with HIV who lack sufficient health insurance or financial resources. The program fills gaps in care not covered by insurance, offering both core medical services and support services through the Baltimore Eligible Metropolitan Area (EMA). Services include primary medical care, medical case management with treatment adherence support, medical nutrition therapy, food bank services, legal services, housing assistance, medical transportation, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance, mental health services, substance abuse treatment (outpatient and residential), psychosocial services, and oral health services. Non-medical case management provides advice and assistance in obtaining medical, social, community, legal, and financial services. Outreach services promote access to and continuation of appropriate services at the earliest possible stage of HIV disease, including street outreach, site-based outreach, and traditional outreach. Ryan White serves as payer of last resort after other insurance options are exhausted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Core medical services include outpatient ambulatory medical care, oral health, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance for low-income individuals, medical nutrition therapy, hospice services, mental health services, substance abuse outpatient care and residential treatment, and medical case management with treatment adherence services. Support services include outreach (street outreach, site-based outreach in correctional facilities, and traditional outreach for service re-engagement), medical transportation, substance abuse residential care, legal services, housing (emergency rental/utility assistance and temporary/transitional housing), psychosocial services, childcare, and food bank services. Non-medical case management provides advice and assistance in obtaining medical, social, community, legal, and financial services. Outreach services include client needs assessments, goal setting, HIV prevention education, referrals to services, and linkage to care. Services delivered through referrals, office visits, home visits, phone support, and outreach at various settings including streets and non-traditional service locations. Individualized care plans are reviewed quarterly for cases open over 90 days. Ryan White serves as payer of last resort after other insurance options are exhausted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People living with HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) who do not have sufficient health insurance or financial resources to cope with HIV disease. Includes adult, adolescent, and pediatric clients (HIV-exposed infants and HIV-infected children, minimum age 1 year for certain services). Focus on newly diagnosed clients, undiagnosed/underserved populations, individuals in correctional facilities, post-partum women with HIV, individuals experiencing housing instability, and vulnerable populations including disproportionately African American males, those with heterosexual transmission risk factor, injection drug users, and men who have sex with men. Must meet income and residency verification requirements for the Baltimore-Towson EMA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Core medical services for people with HIV including outpatient care, oral health, health insurance assistance, nutrition therapy, hospice, mental health and substance abuse treatment (outpatient and residential), and case management. Support services including transportation, housing (emergency rental/utility and transitional housing), legal services, childcare, and food assistance. Outreach services including street outreach, site-based outreach at prisons and agency clinics, and traditional outreach for service re-engagement. Outreach worker salaries and services, client needs assessments, HIV prevention education, referrals to services, and linkage to medical care. Non-medical case management services for medical, social, community, legal, and financial assistance. Psychosocial support services including counseling, support groups, peer support, pastoral care, and bereavement services. Funds are used as payer of last resort after screening for other insurance eligibility (Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP, private insurance).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore/Towson Eligible Metropolitan Area (EMA) including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Howard County, Carroll County, Harford County, and Queen Anne's County. Additional coverage areas may include Montgomery County, Caroline County, Washington County, and Prince George's County. Residency verification required semi-annually with supporting documentation at least once per 12-month period.
requirements_list: Must have documented HIV status (one-time verification)
Must not have sufficient health insurance coverage for HIV treatment
Must not have sufficient financial resources for coping with HIV disease
Residency verification in Baltimore-Towson EMA or service area (semi-annual, with hard copy documentation required at least once yearly)
Income verification (semi-annual, with hard copy documentation required at least once yearly)
Screening for other insurance eligibility (Medicaid, Medicare, CHIP, private insurance)
Client rights documentation and informed consent required
Privacy/HIPAA compliance and release of information forms required
Crisis assessment upon intake
Treatment plan completion (within two visits for non-medical case management; within two weeks for residential substance abuse)
Proof of HIV-positive status
Initial dental evaluation for new oral health clients
Comprehensive health history documentation
CD4 and Viral Load documentation (required per 2011 Oral Health Standards of Care)
Phase 1 oral health treatment completion within 12 months
Annual oral health education and periodontal screening
Six-month reassessment of service needs for cases open over 6 months
Quarterly care plan reviews and monitoring for cases open over 90 days
Documentation of progress toward meeting established treatment goals
Connection to primary medical care providers with documented appointment dates
Client demographics and risk factors documentation
Distribution of agency policies and procedures to clients
Referral documentation
Re-engagement with primary medical care after outreach services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete intake process and provide HIV status verification (one-time), residency documentation (semi-annual), and income documentation (semi-annual). Initial assessment of service needs leads to comprehensive individualized service plan development. For non-medical case management, intakes must be completed within two visits and document presenting problem. For residential substance abuse treatment, initial evaluation by certified/licensed clinical staff must occur, with assessment completed within two weeks of admission. For oral health services, initial dental evaluation required with comprehensive health history and hard/soft tissue examination. Treatment plans must be signed by provider and document immediate actions to address presenting problem. Services are provided through Ryan White Part A-funded agencies including health departments, hospitals, community health centers, and community-based organizations. For outreach services, clients receive needs assessments, goal setting, HIV prevention education, referrals to services, and support for linkage to care. Eligibility re-determination occurs every 6 months.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sewage Onsite Support (SOS) Cleanup Program provides free cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services to Baltimore City residential customers whose homes have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events (heavy or sustained rain of at least ¼ inch within 24 hours). The program contracts with professional cleaning companies to remove health risks and restore properties. Services include drying affected rooms, disinfecting and sanitizing affected areas, and removing and disposing of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other affected property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free professional cleaning and disinfection services at no cost to residential customers. Services include disinfection and cleaning to eliminate viruses and bacteria, disposal and removal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other affected property, deodorization using professional-grade equipment, and dehumidification and drying of affected areas. All services are provided by contracted professional cleaning companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (property owners, tenants, or property managers) whose homes have experienced sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional cleaning, disinfection, and removal of property damaged by sewage backups from wet-weather events. Covers cleaning of affected areas, removal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture and other damaged property, deodorization, and drying and dehumidification of affected areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Baltimore City residential properties only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City residential customer (property owner, tenant, or property manager)
The sewage backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least ¼ inch of precipitation within 24 hours)
The backup must not be caused by clogs from wet wipes, roots, fats, oil, and grease (FOG), or maintenance-related issues
Must report the damage to DPW through 311 as soon as the sewer backup is discovered
City must confirm the damage is caused by a capacity-related wet-weather event
Cannot use both SOS Cleanup Program and Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact 311 or visit 311.baltimorecity.gov to report the sewage backup damage to DPW as soon as it is discovered. The property owner, tenant, or property manager must report the damage. DPW will send an inspector to determine the cause of the sewage backup. Once the cause is confirmed to be a capacity-related wet weather event, DPW will deploy a professional cleaning contractor team to perform cleaning, disinfection, disposal, deodorization, and drying services. The on-call contractor will contact the customer within one hour and schedule an appointment (service available 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week).

structured_extraction.program_name: Staying Alive Drug Overdose Prevention and Response Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A public health intervention that trains individuals to recognize signs and symptoms of opioid and heroin overdose and respond appropriately using naloxone (Narcan) to maximize chances of survival. The program provides free naloxone kits and overdose prevention training at various locations throughout Baltimore City, including treatment centers, syringe exchange sites, correctional facilities, and through live virtual community training sessions and in-person training requests. The program has trained over 155,000 individuals and helped save more than 18,000 lives between 2015 and 2023, and has distributed nearly 26,000 naloxone kits between 2023 and 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free naloxone (Narcan) kits dispensed at no cost to residents. Training on recognizing and responding to opioid overdoses provided through live virtual community naloxone training sessions via Eventbrite and in-person training requests. Training available at multiple sites including treatment centers, syringe exchange program sites, and the Baltimore City Detention Center. Residents can request naloxone kits through an online form or attend virtual training sessions. Naloxone can also be obtained from any Maryland Department of Health-registered Overdose Response Program, Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP), or Syringe Service Program.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-396-3733; 443-615-7792 (to request naloxone kits); 1-888-222-1222 (Poison Center); 410-433-5175 (Crisis Information and Referral Line)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, friends, family members, bystanders, individuals with substance use disorders, incarcerated individuals, healthcare providers, correctional staff, and community members interested in overdose prevention and response.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Naloxone kits for opioid overdose reversal and overdose prevention education and training for emergency response.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Reside in or be present in Baltimore City
Interest in learning overdose prevention and naloxone use
Must be willing to participate in training on overdose recognition and naloxone administration
Request naloxone kit through online form or attend training session
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can access naloxone training and kits through multiple methods: (1) submit a Naloxone Kit Request Form online, (2) register for a live virtual community naloxone training session via Eventbrite, (3) submit a naloxone training request form to schedule an in-person or custom training, (4) call 443-615-7792 to request free naloxone kits, or (5) visit any Maryland Department of Health-registered Overdose Response Program, Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP), or Syringe Service Program location in Baltimore City. Use the interactive map to find locations near you. Contact the 24-hour mental health and substance abuse help line for referrals and information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit and Reduction Program for Non-Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Program established by Maryland Legislature in 2012 mandating stormwater fees in 10 largest state jurisdictions including Baltimore City. Provides dedicated revenue source for maintaining, operating, and improving the City's stormwater management system. Aims to reduce flooding and erosion, and keep waterways cleaner. Offers fee reductions and credits to non-single-family properties based on impervious surface area management, installation of best management practices, and other qualifying conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fee credits or reductions are available for multiple categories: installing and maintaining best management practices (up to 45% credit); lots with less than 50 square feet of impervious area (Green Space Credit - 45%); small developments with 50-820 square feet of impervious area (Small Development Credit - 33%); properties holding NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permits (55% credit); owners maintaining private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor (30% credit); cemeteries with privately maintained streets open to the public; participation in public water quality improvement projects ($10 per 4 hours annually); religious structures used exclusively for places of worship or K-12 education ($1/ERU/month); and charitable nonprofit organizations with financial hardship exemptions. Maximum fee capped at 20% of real property taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications must be received within 30 days before credit period end
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners/operators of non-single-family properties in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stormwater management infrastructure including Best Management Practices (BMPs), treatment systems, green space, off-site treatment practices, and harbor discharge systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City; properties must be located within the same 8-digit watershed for off-site treatment credit eligibility
requirements_list: Property must be non-single-family
Applicant must meet program qualifications for stormwater fee credits/reductions
Must own non-single-family property in Baltimore City
May qualify for Green Space Credit if lot has less than 50 square feet of impervious area
May qualify for Small Development Credit if lot has 50-820 square feet of impervious area
May qualify for NPDES permit credit if property holds a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit
May qualify for private storm drain credit if property owns and maintains private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor
May qualify for cemetery street credit if maintaining cemetery streets open to the public
May qualify for best management practices credit for installing and maintaining practices
May qualify for participation credit for involvement in public water quality improvement projects
Religious structures and nonprofit organizations may qualify for exemptions or special fees if meeting eligibility criteria
Must complete and submit Stormwater fee credit application
Renewal applications must be submitted within 30 days before credit period end
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the stormwater fee credit application for non-single-family properties. Submit applications to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov with subject line 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION' or contact (410) 396-5398. Review the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document for eligibility details and credit amounts. Renewal applications must be received within 30 days before the credit period ends.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Credit for Single-Family Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City can reduce their stormwater fees by installing and maintaining stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels that treat runoff and decrease stormwater entering the City's drainage system, or by volunteering in organized community activities like cleanups that provide water quality benefits. Property owners receive credits on their stormwater fee based on the practices installed and maintained or the volunteer hours earned through participation in organized events. Credits reduce stormwater service charges based on measures that reduce demand on the City's drainage system or reduce stormwater management costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a credit on their stormwater fee for installing and maintaining stormwater treatment practices like trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels. Credits available for: participation in public water quality projects ($10 per 4 hours, max $30/year); tree planting ($5/year per tree, minimum 2 trees); rain gardens ($8-$16/year); rain barrels ($25 one-time per barrel); simple and advanced stormwater Best Management Practices (up to 45% fee reduction). Volunteers can earn hours toward credit on their stormwater fee through participation in organized community cleanups and activities. The credit amount is based on the hours volunteered or the practices installed and maintained.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family property owners in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and maintenance of stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels; participation in volunteer community cleanup activities; credits reduce the stormwater fee billed based on paved surfaces; stormwater management system maintenance, operation, and improvement; reducing flooding and erosion; keeping waterways clean
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a single-family property owner in Baltimore City
Property must be single-family residential
Must complete and submit the Stormwater Fee Credit Application
For volunteering: must participate in organized community activities that provide water quality benefits
For volunteering: volunteer 4+ hours at City-certified events
For best management practices: must install and maintain practices like rain gardens, tree planting, or rain barrels
For tree planting: minimum 2 trees planted after 2010, 1+ inch diameter, conforming to City guidelines
For rain gardens: minimum 50-100 sq ft size depending on type, minimum drainage area 500-1,000 sq ft

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based violence prevention program that addresses teen dating violence and youth violence through evidence-based interventions. The program works with 9th graders in schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts to build knowledge, skills, and attitudes about healthy relationships and non-violent conflict resolution. The initiative combines Safe Dates (promoting healthy relationships) and Safe Streets (promoting non-violent conflict resolution through conflict mediators). It provides access to Dating Matters Resources - a compilation of local and national resources for teens regarding healthy relationships and dating violence prevention, including information on healthy dating relationships, dating violence prevention, digital abuse, LGBTQ support, and crisis intervention services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 10-session Safe Dates training to promote healthy relationships and prevent dating violence. It includes Safe Streets conflict mediation services, school-wide awareness events, and after-school clubs. A multi-sector advisory committee guides system-level efforts and helps plan for sustainability of project strategies and partnerships. Additionally, it provides access to Dating Matters Resources including educational resources, hotlines, counseling, crisis intervention, and online chat support on healthy dating relationships, dating violence prevention, digital abuse, LGBTQ support, and crisis intervention services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 9th grade students in schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts in Baltimore City; teens, pre-teens, LGBTQ youth, and students in unhealthy or unsafe dating relationships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in healthy relationships, non-violent conflict resolution, and violence prevention through school-based programming and after-school clubs; access to educational resources, hotlines, counseling, and crisis intervention services on dating violence prevention and healthy relationships
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Schools located in or adjacent to Safe Streets Outposts in Baltimore City and surrounding Maryland areas; national resources available

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City designated Sustainable Community areas, which include specific geographic zones mapped according to six revitalization strategies. Automatically included areas: Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) zones and state-designated Transit-Oriented Developments (TODs). Additional areas may be included through boundary amendment requests reviewed on a rolling basis.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a designated Sustainable Community area
Project must align with one or more of the six SC Action Plan strategies
For boundary amendments: must submit address of proposed area and bullet points demonstrating alignment with SC Action Plan strategies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The SC Designation itself is awarded to the jurisdiction (Baltimore City). Organizations with projects in designated SC areas then become eligible for related state grant programs, tax credits, and loans. To request amendments to the SC boundary: submit request to Planning Department with area addresses and alignment documentation; Planning Department reviews with other city agencies; Maryland DHCD internal review committee makes final approval; requester receives decision letter and map is updated if approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual city program that helps homeowners avoid tax sale for unpaid city bills by deferring property tax liens, city fines, and citations. The program removes eligible homeowners' properties from tax sale in the year they apply by setting aside $2 million annually. The program does not forgive unpaid bills, and properties may qualify for tax sale again the following year if bills remain unpaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city defers unpaid property tax liens, city fines, and citations to prevent tax sale foreclosure for the year of application. The program has $2 million in annual funding. Applicants with liens are deducted from the $2 million annual balance on a first-come, first-served basis. Once the $2 million is exhausted, the program closes. Homeowners must apply every year to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City homeowners with unpaid property taxes, city fines, or citations who are at risk of tax sale and meet income and residency requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of unpaid property tax liens, city fines, and citations to prevent tax sale foreclosure and the city from selling tax liens to outside bidders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Property must be located in Baltimore City and homeowner must live in the property.
requirements_list: More than $1,000 in unpaid city bills to the City (excluding motor vehicle citations, utility bills, water bills)
Homeowner or co-homeowner residing in Baltimore City
Live in the property owned in Baltimore City
Owned and occupied home for at least 15 years
Property assessed value of $250,000 or less

Gross annual household income of $36,000 or less; OR age 65+ with annual earned income of $75,000 or less; OR adult receiving Federal Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income with annual earned income of $75,000 or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners can apply online at https://bit.ly/TaxSalePrevention or submit paper applications delivered to the Department of Housing and Community Development at 417 E. Fayette Street, Suite 1125 (11th floor), Baltimore, MD 21202. Applicants can also contact the Tax Sale Ombudsman for assistance. Applications are reviewed first-come, first-served until the $2 million allocation is exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: TreeBaltimore is a program led by the Mayor and run by Baltimore City Recreation and Parks that aims to grow and care for more trees across the city through tree planting, natural forest growth, and community education about tree care. The program provides free one-gallon trees to Baltimore City residents and businesses during spring and fall giveaway events held at farmer's markets, parks, and local community events. TreeBaltimore also orders and delivers trees to large properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, industrial areas, colleges, and places of worship. Residents can purchase discounted trees using coupons from the Growing Home Campaign ($10) or Marylanders Plant Trees campaign ($25). The program offers free Tree Steward training classes and provides technical assistance including site visits for businesses and institutions to discuss tree planting options. The Forestry Division also plants street trees on the street right-of-way and allows residents to request trees for residential properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free one-gallon trees distributed to residents and businesses during seasonal giveaway events held at farmer's markets, parks, and community events. TreeBaltimore orders and delivers trees to large properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, industrial areas, colleges, and places of worship. Residents can also purchase trees with discount coupons ($10 from Growing Home Campaign or $25 from Marylanders Plant Trees campaign). The program offers free Tree Steward training classes and technical assistance including site visits for businesses and institutions to evaluate tree planting opportunities. The Forestry Division plants street trees on the street right-of-way free or subsidized (applicants can pay for pit creation if needed). Residents can also request trees for residential properties (front or back yard) with flowering or shade varieties available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing seasonal giveaways in spring and fall
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents, businesses, institutions, community organizations, foundations, property owners, tree planters, developers, and environmental mitigation projects in Baltimore City who want to plant and care for trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and maintenance on private property, public spaces, parks, schools, businesses, places of worship, vacant lots, and street right-of-way. Trees can be used to improve air and water quality, reduce summer heat, save energy, block noise, strengthen the community, and support the citywide goal of reaching 40% tree canopy cover. Tree species selection and planting guidance based on approved species list.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and businesses located within Baltimore City limits. Preferably trees sourced from within 200 miles for local seed sources.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can pick up free trees at TreeBaltimore giveaway events held in spring and fall at farmer's markets, parks, and local community events. Community organizations can complete a Street Tree Pit Inventory to identify tree planting locations. For street tree planting, submit completed Street Tree Request and Agreement for Tree Care form via email, mail, or fax; inspector visits site to approve location. For residential property trees, submit completed TreeNeighborhood Order Form with payment to TreeBaltimore at Baltimore City Recreation and Parks, 3001 East Drive, Baltimore, MD 21217. For public right-of-way plantings, obtain permission from Forestry Division before planting. Individuals can also purchase trees using discount coupons or buy from Herring Run Tree Nursery. Organizations interested in hosting a giveaway event at their location may contact the Forestry Division.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water and Sewer Bill Adjustment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore Department of Public Works provides bill adjustments for property owners who experienced higher than normal water usage due to interior leaks, underground pipe ruptures, or situational factors such as appliance problems or fixtures. For interior or situational usage adjustments, customers receive a 50 percent deduction on excess water usage (or 100 percent for senior/hardship customers). For underground leaks repaired by a licensed plumber with documented proof, all excess water and sewer charges are adjusted accordingly. Adjustments apply to up to three consecutive months of highest usage, with one adjustment per type granted per 12-month period. Modifications effective September 1, 2022 or later include expanded adjustment eligibility and inclusion of sewer volumetric charges in calculations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bill adjustment/rebate applied to water and sewer charges. Two adjustment types available: (1) Situational/Interior Adjustments - calculated from daily average consumption prior to leak, multiplied by days of service (max 3 months), limited to 50% of overage units billed (or 100% for senior/hardship customers); (2) Underground Leak Adjustments - all excess water and sewer volumetric charges deducted with documented proof of repair by licensed plumber. One adjustment per adjustment type is granted per 12-month period. Results appear on the customer's bill approximately 4 weeks after the request is received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within sixty (60) days of the bill being issued; adjustments must be requested on or after September 1, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and residents in Baltimore City who have experienced interior leaks, underground pipe ruptures, situational water usage issues, or other factors resulting in higher than normal water consumption.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bill adjustments and credits on water and sewer charges for properties with documented interior leaks, underground leaks, or situational usage issues. Adjustments help reduce delinquency rates and stabilize utility rate increases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Baltimore City only. Applicants must be the legal property owner or an authorized person designated by the property owner. Baltimore County customers excluded from September 1, 2022 modifications.

Adjustment limited to 50% of overage units billed
Repairs must be completed before submitting form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Water and Sewer Adjustment Request form online or print it and submit to the Department of Public Works Customer Support and Services Division by mail to 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or in person at 200 Holliday Street, First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. For interior leaks, documentation of the leak issue is required. For underground leaks, a certified plumber receipt showing repair details is required. Customer will be notified by phone or letter if adjustment is approved or denied. Bill adjustments appear on the customer's bill approximately 4 weeks after the form is received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) - Diversion & Kinship Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program supporting communities in developing and implementing a coordinated community approach to prevent and end youth homelessness. This specific funding opportunity targets the development of Diversion and Kinship projects serving unaccompanied youth experiencing homelessness, including unaccompanied pregnant or parenting youth (no household member older than 24). The program connects with youth and young adults through outreach and coordinated access to quickly assess if they can be diverted from shelter. It offers short-term flexible financial assistance (up to six months) and supportive services to keep youth housed or quickly re-house them, and connects youth to host homes established through project referrals, including kinship care (relatives or close friends/fictive kin).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Baltimore City was awarded $3,699,336 in 2019 to implement a local plan. The current grant opportunity is specific to a Diversion and Kinship program for youth and young adults. Selected projects must coordinate with current YHDP projects and the full Baltimore Continuum of Care. Short-term flexible financial assistance (up to 6 months) and supportive services to keep youth housed or quickly re-house them. Financial assistance includes rental application fees, utility deposits, food, transportation, childcare, and flexible support through stipends. Funding supports staffing, HMIS, supportive services, housing problem-solving activities, and case management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unaccompanied youth under age 18 and young adults aged 18-24 experiencing homelessness, including unaccompanied pregnant or parenting youth, where no member of the household is older than 24. Priority populations include youth of color, LGBTQ+ youth, trafficking survivors, foster care-involved youth, and justice system-involved youth. Non-profit organizations providing services to this population.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing problem-solving activities (housing search, mediation, deposits, moving assistance, rental fees, arrears), supportive services (case management, employment assistance, mental health services, childcare, education, legal services), Permanent Supportive Housing, Rapid Re-housing, Family-Based Setting Diversion, Transitional Housing services, staff salaries and training, and HMIS costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy Into Bmore Fixed Pricing Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A sales program for City-owned vacant buildings and lots in Baltimore City that streamlines the disposition process by offering simplified property transfers at fixed prices. The program aims to reduce vacant properties and promote sustainable, affordable development by offering transparent pricing to eligible purchasers including homeowners, developers, nonprofits, and community land trusts. Properties are priced based on buyer type and property characteristics, ranging from $1 for homeowners and community land trusts to $3,000 for larger developers. The program helps future homeowners, community groups, and developers buy and restore these properties for residential or mixed-use purposes.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned vacant properties are sold at fixed prices: homeowners purchasing vacant buildings or lots for primary residence pay $1; 501(c)(3) nonprofits with 50 or fewer employees pay $1,000 for buildings and $500 for lots; nonprofits with 51+ employees and for-profit developers pay $3,000 for buildings and $1,000 for lots; community land trusts pay $1. Homeowners must have $90,000 available for renovations and maintain the property as a primary residence for 5 years. Properties must be developed for residential, mixed-use, or green space purposes with occupancy permits obtained within 12 months of settlement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with Phase One priority period April 1 - June 30, 2024; Phase Two (Charm City Roots) launched April 15, 2024; Phase Three begins July 1, 2024

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and renovation of vacant City-owned buildings and lots for residential, mixed-use, nonprofit, or green space development. Homeowners must use properties as primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program applies to properties within Housing Market Typologies E-J in Baltimore City. Properties must be listed on BuyIntoBmore website. Nonprofits must be 501(c)(3) organizations
Application fee of $100 required (refunded if rejected, credited to settlement if approved)

DHCD reviews applications and renders approval or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. If multiple applications received for same property and all applicants pass vetting, applications reviewed by order of submission. Applicants unable to pass vetting given five business days to remedy issues. Board of Estimates approval is required for property disposition. Settlement must occur within 90 days of agreement execution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Energy Conservation Devices Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for property owners in Baltimore County who install solar or geothermal energy conservation devices that meet national safety and performance standards on their property to heat, cool, supply electricity, and provide hot water. The credit is 50 percent of the eligible cost or $5,000, whichever is less. For a hot water supply system, the credit is $1,500. Maximum credit by system type: Heating System $5,000, Hot Water Supply System $1,500, Electricity Generation $5,000, Cooling $5,000. The credit cannot exceed county property taxes owed in a given year; excess credits may be carried forward for up to two additional years. A waiting list is currently in effect due to the $1.5 million annual budgetary limitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for single and multifamily residential and eligible commercial properties with solar or geothermal energy conservation devices meeting national safety and performance standards. The credit is 50 percent of the eligible cost or $5,000, whichever is less. For a hot water supply system, the credit is $1,500. Eligible costs include parts, components, accessories, and installation expenses incurred within 12 months before application. Maximum credit by system type: Heating System $5,000, Hot Water Supply System $1,500, Electricity Generation $5,000, Cooling $5,000. The credit cannot exceed county property taxes owed in a given year; excess credits may be carried forward for up to two additional years. A waiting list is currently in effect due to the $1.5 million annual budgetary limitation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Baltimore County who have installed or are planning to install qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar energy devices (heating, cooling, electricity generation, hot water) and geothermal energy devices (heating, cooling, hot water) including installation costs that meet national safety and performance standards. The credit reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential structures located in Baltimore County, Maryland only. The credit does not transfer with the property, and a change of ownership will cause the credit to terminate.

Property must have solar or geothermal energy conservation device installed that meets national safety and performance standards from recognized testing laboratory
Eligible costs must have been incurred within 12 months before initial application
Detailed receipts with amounts, payment dates, and Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office Permit Number must be submitted
Expenses must not include interest charges
Device must meet national safety and performance standards
Devices must be solar or geothermal (excludes household appliances)
Application must be submitted no later than June 1 of the year preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
Total annual credits capped at $250,000 per fiscal year on first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Gather required documentation including detailed receipts for installed devices and evidence that device meets national safety and performance standards set by nationally recognized testing laboratory. Include the Permit Number for electrical inspection by Baltimore County Electrical Inspection Office. Step 2: Complete application form with property and contact information. Step 3: Apply online through the provided form, or apply by mail or in person by printing and completing the Energy Conservation Devices Tax Credit application and sending it to the Office of Budget and Finance at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. Applications are reviewed by Director of OBF or designee and are placed on a waiting list in the order received due to the annual $1.5 million budgetary limitation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Grant Program - Septic System Upgrade Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Baltimore County's Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability, Ground Water Management Section that provides funding to property owners to upgrade failing septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) units for nitrogen removal, install holding tanks, or connect properties to public sewer systems. The program is part of bay restoration efforts aimed at reducing nutrients entering the Chesapeake Bay by requiring upgrades to failing systems in sensitive areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for BAT installation, holding tank installation, or connection to public sewer. For BAT installation, the grant covers the cost and installation of the BAT unit plus two years of maintenance. For public sewer connections, the grant covers connection costs, sewer system connection fees, and permits. For holding tanks, funding is provided for qualifying properties. Residential properties with household income less than $300,000 per year receive 100 percent funding. Non-profit entities receive 100 percent funding. Non-residential and commercial properties receive 50 percent funding of project cost. Grant funds may not be used for drainfield costs (except for qualifying low-income owners) or permit and recordation fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County property owners with septic systems, including residential (owner-occupied and rental) and commercial properties, particularly those with failing systems or systems in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Septic system upgrades including BAT installation, holding tank installation, connection to public sewer systems, and maintenance of BAT systems for two years
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. Priority given to failing systems or non-conforming systems located within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (property within 1,000 feet of mean high tide).
requirements_list: Must be a septic system user in Baltimore County
Must meet online eligibility criteria
Property must be located in Baltimore County
For public sewer connection: property must have frontage and/or legal access to public sewer
For holding tanks: property must qualify for holding tanks
Property owner must submit signed application form
Must submit copy of property owner's most recent 1040 federal tax form (pages 1-2, SSNs blacked out)
Proof of income required
Allow access for Department site inspection
For BAT installation, property owner must sign and record agreement committing to maintenance by qualified operator
County may conduct periodic inspections to ensure BAT unit operates satisfactorily
Prioritization based on system status and location relative to Chesapeake Bay Critical Area

If approved, sign agreement acknowledging maintenance requirements and allowing County inspections.

structured_extraction.program_name: Blind Individual and Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax relief program that exempts qualified blind individuals or their surviving spouses from real property tax obligations on their principal residence. Eligibility requires central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with corrective glasses, or a visual field defect with widest diameter no greater than 20 degrees on the better eye, with permanent impairment of both eyes. Eligible individuals may also receive a retroactive refund of property taxes paid in prior years (up to three years) if an exemption was authorized but not granted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Blind individuals or their surviving spouses receive an exemption from property taxation on their principal residence. Individuals may be eligible for a refund of property taxes paid during taxable years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, retroactive up to three years.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption on principal residence

requirements_list: Must be a blind individual or surviving spouse of a blind individual
Central visual acuity of 20/200 or less in better eye with corrective glasses, OR visual field defect with widest diameter no greater than 20 degrees on better eye
Permanent impairment of both eyes
Legal owner of property

Maryland residency (proof required: Driver's License, ID, voter registration, or prior year tax return)

Properties located in one of the County's three Enterprise Zones with cleanup costs exceeding $1 million receive an additional 20 percent credit. The credit applies for 10 years for sites in Enterprise Zones and 5 years for sites outside these zones.

Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50 percent property tax credit on the increased Baltimore County real property tax liability for a Qualified Brownfields Site for 5 years. Properties located in one of the County's three Enterprise Zones, Commercial Revitalization Districts, or with cleanup costs exceeding $1 million receive an additional 20 percent credit (70% total). The enhanced credit extends to 10 years if in an enterprise zone. The credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax obligations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit is applied to property tax liability for redevelopment projects on qualified brownfields properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to properties located in Baltimore County that have been designated as Qualified Brownfields Sites by the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development. Properties must be contaminated by oil or hazardous substances, located in densely populated urban areas, substantially underutilized, or in Commercial Revitalization Districts, and subject to Baltimore County jurisdiction with an adopted local ordinance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Children In Need of Supervision (CINS) / Youth Mentoring Team
structured_extraction.program_description: An award-winning, integrated program providing mentoring, education, training, and family support services to Baltimore County youth and families. Services address issues including running away, ungovernable behavior, truancy, crime prevention, substance abuse, and family conflict resolution. Support includes conflict resolution between parents and children, mentoring, problem-solving education, training on multiculturalism and substance abuse prevention, listening and empathic support, family collaboration to solve issues, referrals to professional therapists and community resources, coordination with other providers such as school resource officers and mobile crisis, and assistance to community centers and schools. All services are provided free of charge to eligible Baltimore County residents.

Services include conflict resolution, problem-solving education, training on multiculturalism and substance abuse prevention, listening and empathic support, family collaboration, referrals to professional therapists and external programs, and coordination with other service providers. Services are provided free of charge to Baltimore County residents. Services do not include formal psychotherapy, formal diagnosis, prescribed medication, testing, formal evaluations, or home visits.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring, education, training, support, and referrals to address crime prevention, decision-making, substance abuse, truancy, family conflict resolution, and related family support needs

structured_extraction.program_description: CountyRide is a specialized transportation service serving Baltimore County for older adults, adults with disabilities, and rural residents. The program provides specialized transportation services for seniors, persons with disabilities, and rural residents. Trips are scheduled based on availability, with medical trips given preference and scheduled up to two weeks in advance. Non-medical trips can be scheduled up to one week in advance. Services include wheelchair accommodations, escorts for those needing special assistance at no additional cost, and rides Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.
