structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit designed to assist law enforcement personnel, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service to Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax on the dwelling and continues annually without reapplication for the lifetime of the disabled person unless the Director requests proof of continued eligibility. Eligibility applies to public safety workers who sustained work-related line of duty injuries, with eligibility beginning in July 2009.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit provides a 100 percent credit of Baltimore County real property tax on dwellings and continues year to year without reapplication unless the Director requests proof of continued eligibility. The credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax obligations and does not extend to surviving spouses or other residents of the dwelling. Applies to public safety workers and volunteers who sustained work-related line of duty disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who are permanently and totally disabled as a result of employment in Baltimore County, and currently residing in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit reduces or eliminates Baltimore County real property tax obligations for the disabled worker's residential dwelling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The dwelling must be located in Baltimore County, Maryland and must be the legal residence of the applicant. Applicant must have been domiciled in Maryland at the time of disability determination. The credit applies only to Baltimore County real property tax obligations.
requirements_list: Must be permanently and totally disabled as determined by appropriate administrative body or court
Disability must have resulted from or occurred during employment as a Baltimore County law enforcement officer or active service with Baltimore County fire, rescue, or EMS
Disability must not result from willful misconduct or alcohol/drug abuse
Must own and occupy the dwelling as legal residence (maximum 2 families)
Dwelling must have been owned and occupied at time of disability determination, OR acquired within 2 years of disability determination, OR acquired after qualifying for credit on former dwelling
Cannot combine credit with other Baltimore County real property tax credits or payment-in-lieu programs
Applicant must provide proof of disability date and dwelling ownership with application
Credit only applies during the lifetime of the disabled person and does not extend to surviving spouses or other residents
Verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice must be submitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain application from Baltimore County website or Customer Services Section, Office of Budget and Finance, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. Submit the completed application along with verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice. Employees should submit to the Baltimore County Employee Retirement Office; volunteer rescue workers should submit to the Baltimore County Fire Department. The agency official certifies line-of-duty disability status, and the Director of the Office of Budget and Finance approves or denies the application. Credit continues year to year without reapplication unless the Director requests evidence of continued eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Free iPads or Chromebooks for Seniors
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that distributes iPads and Chromebooks to eligible older adults in Baltimore County. Recipients receive devices, training, assistance with internet connectivity programs, and ongoing technical support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 250 iPads and 600 Chromebooks to eligible older adults at no cost. Recipients also receive training on device use, assistance applying for the Affordable Connectivity Program for reduced or free internet, and ongoing technical support through BCDA programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults age 60 and older who reside in Baltimore County or are members of a Baltimore County Senior Center and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: iPads and Chromebooks for personal use, with training provided to help recipients learn to use the devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center.
requirements_list: Age 60 years or older
Reside in Baltimore County or be a member of a Baltimore County Senior Center
Qualify as low-income (200 percent or less of poverty level; Single: $27,180, Couple: $36,620)
Have the ability to learn the device
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application. Upon receipt of an eligible application, the BCDA Office of Communications will schedule the applicant to attend a training or pick-up event, assess need for internet assistance, offer brief training on the device, and connect the individual with additional BCDA programs and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program for residential taxpayers who have experienced temporary financial hardship and need additional time to pay their property taxes. The program allows eligible taxpayers to make installment payments instead of paying the full amount by the deadline.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved applicants can make installment payments on their residential property taxes instead of paying in full by the standard deadline. Eligibility is based on demonstrated hardship, repayment ability, and financial disclosure. Approval is valid only for the fiscal tax year in which the application is made. All future taxes must remain current to maintain eligibility.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential taxpayers in Baltimore County who have experienced temporary financial hardship and need additional time to pay property taxes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of residential property tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residential taxpayers in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a residential taxpayer
Must have experienced a temporary financial hardship
Must demonstrate repayment ability
Must provide financial disclosure
Must file application by end of February to avoid property tax sale
All future taxes must be kept current to maintain eligibility
Eligibility is limited to the fiscal tax year in which application is made
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must file an application by the end of February. The application requires financial disclosure and demonstration of hardship and repayment ability. Upon approval, the taxpayer enters an installment payment arrangement for the fiscal year of application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Outcomes in Pregnancy and Early Childhood (HOPE) / Healthy Families and Babies Born Healthy Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: Perinatal services providing public health nursing, community health worker, and social worker support to promote healthy pregnancy, delivery, and postpartum and newborn care for Baltimore County residents. Teams of public health nurses, community health workers and social workers provide services including in-person home visits, virtual home visits, and referral and linkage to other community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Teams of public health nurses, community health workers and social workers provide services including in-person home visits, virtual home visits, and referral and linkage to other community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant and postpartum individuals who are Baltimore County residents, and infants up to 18 months of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to promote healthy pregnancy and delivery, postpartum and newborn support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be pregnant, postpartum, or parent of an infant up to 18 months of age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online referral form at baltimorecountymd.jotform.com/232846003085048

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for commercial and institutional buildings in Baltimore County that achieve at least a silver rating under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Green Building rating system or the American National Standards Institute's National Green Building Standard (NGBS) rating system. The credit reduces Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligations. Eligible buildings include new construction (LEED-NC), core and shell (LEED-CS), existing buildings (LEED-EB), and buildings meeting NGBS standards, including income-producing residential buildings of at least 50 units. Credit amounts vary by rating system and level achieved, ranging from 10% to 80% of real property tax for 3 to 5 years depending on the certification type.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for commercial and institutional buildings achieving at least silver rating under LEED (new construction, core and shell, or existing buildings) or NGBS rating systems. Credit amounts vary: LEED-NC (silver 50%, gold 60%, platinum 70% for 5 years); LEED-CS (silver 40%, gold 50%, platinum 80% for 5 years); LEED-EB (silver 10%, gold 25%, platinum 50% for 3 years); NGBS (silver 50%, gold 60%, emerald 80% for 5 years). The credit reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations. Only one High Performance Building Credit per building is allowed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought, or at any time if filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit or if the property has prior credits under § 11-2-202
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and institutional buildings in Baltimore County with qualifying green building certifications, including income-producing residential buildings of at least 50 units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligations for high-performance buildings meeting energy efficiency standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Building must be located in Baltimore County
Building must achieve at least a silver rating based on LEED (LEED-NC, LEED-CS, or LEED-EB) or NGBS rating system
Must provide documentation from a professional LEED or NGBS Rater certifying the property meets high performance building definition and the rating level achieved
Application must be filed under oath with sufficient supporting documentation
Only one High Performance Building Credit per building allowed

Application must be submitted on or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought, or at any time if filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit or if the property has prior credits under § 11-2-202
Director grants or denies application within 45 days; application deemed denied if not granted within 45 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Application for High Performance Building Tax Credit form along with appropriate documentation including proof of high performance building certification to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204. Application must be filed under oath on or before June 1 preceding the first taxable year or at any time if filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit. Director will grant or deny within 45 days. Appeals are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credit program for owners of new or renovated residential structures that meet high energy efficiency standards. The credit amount is based on the certification level or percentage of energy efficiency achieved and is deducted from Baltimore County real property tax obligations. The credit runs for three consecutive years from the first year awarded (or five years if carbon neutral).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit that reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations based on energy efficiency certification. Credit amounts range from 40-100% of total county property tax depending on certification level: LEED Silver provides 40% reduction, Gold provides 60% reduction, Platinum provides 100% reduction; NGBS Silver provides 40% reduction, Gold provides 60% reduction, Emerald provides 100% reduction; or minimum 30% increased energy efficiency. The credit runs for three consecutive years beginning with the first year awarded, or five years if carbon neutral. Only one tax credit per property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of new or renovated residential structures in Baltimore County meeting high performance energy efficiency standards
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit reduction for owners of high-performance homes meeting approved energy efficiency standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only
requirements_list: Must achieve one of the following: LEED Silver or higher rating certified by Certified LEED Rater, OR NGBS Silver or higher rating certified by acceptable practices, OR minimum 30% increased energy efficiency certified by Certified HERS rater, Certified ASHRAE professional, or Certified Passive House consultant
For existing structures: baseline measurement before renovation and final measurement after completion required
For new construction: design phase energy modeling required
For renovated structures with HERS pathway: HERS Rating must be completed before and after renovation
Only one tax credit per property
Application must be submitted no later than June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which credit is sought
Property tax account/parcel number required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Obtain required certification - LEED rating from Certified LEED Rater, NGBS rating from accepted practices, or energy efficiency measurement from Certified HERS rater, Certified ASHRAE professional, or Certified Passive House consultant. Step 2: Submit completed application with property owner information, parcel number, and supporting certifications to the Office of Budget and Finance by June 1. Step 3: Director reviews application and grants or denies within 45 days; deemed denied if not approved within 45 days. Appeals available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists with payment of services in the home or in assisted living for individuals assessed at nursing home level of care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for home or assisted living services for individuals age 18 and older who are assessed at nursing home level of care and meet Medical Assistance institutional eligibility rules. Single person income up to $2,901/month with $2,000 assets; two people income up to $5,802/month with $3,000 assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals age 18 and older needing home or community-based services at nursing home level of care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for services in the home or assisted living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Age 18 and older
Must be assessed at nursing home level of care
Must meet Medical Assistance institutional eligibility rules
Single person income: $2,901/month maximum (includes $20 disregard)
Two people income: $5,802/month maximum
Single person assets: $2,000 maximum
Two people assets: $3,000 maximum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore County Department of Aging for application details and procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program that provides services and support to help qualified low-income adults remain in their homes or assisted living facilities instead of nursing homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides Medical Assistance coverage for prescriptions, doctor visits, and hospitalizations. HCBS waiver covers in-home care, adult day care, medical supplies, and home-delivered meals based on individual need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified low-income adults age 18 and over who are at risk of nursing home placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home care, adult day care, medical supplies, home-delivered meals, prescriptions, doctor visits, and hospitalizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older
Must meet income requirements
Must meet medical needs requirements
Must be at risk of nursing home placement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To place your name on the Registry waitlist, contact Maryland Access Point (MAP) of Baltimore County by calling 410-887-2594.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit that limits the tax burden on property owners whose property assessments have increased. The credit reduces county and state tax liability by capping assessment increases and is automatically applied to qualifying property tax bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit limits the county tax increase to four percent over the previous year's taxable assessment (Maryland state limit is ten percent). The credit reduces county and state tax liability and is automatically reflected in the property tax bill. Amount varies based on the assessment increase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners whose principal residence is located in Baltimore County and whose property assessment has increased.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces property tax liability on the owner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in Baltimore County and must be the owner's principal residence.
requirements_list: The dwelling must be the owner's principal residence

The owner must have lived in the property for at least six months of the year, including July 1 of the year for which the credit is applicable (unless temporarily unable due to illness or special care needs)
The property was not transferred to new ownership during the previous tax year
There was no change in the zoning classification by the homeowner resulting in an increased property value
A substantial change did not occur in the use of the property
The previous assessment was not clearly erroneous
An owner can receive a credit on only one property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homestead Credits are automatically added to tax bills when assessments are increasing to offset the increase of the taxable assessment. No application is required—the credit is automatically applied based on property status.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps eligible low-income families and elderly and disabled persons pay their rent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rent assistance for eligible low-income families and elderly and disabled persons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families, elderly persons, and disabled persons in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must be facing housing assistance need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at a District Office. Paperwork required for application processing. Contact Department of Social Services for eligibility criteria and paperwork requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Early intervention program serving families with children under three years of age presenting with developmental delays or disabilities. Research-based services are coordinated based on family needs and priorities at no cost to families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Research-based early intervention services provided at no cost including supports and services to help children develop positive social and emotional skills, acquire and use knowledge and skills, and use appropriate behaviors to meet needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under three years of age with developmental delays or disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early intervention services to support child development and family goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Child must be under three years of age

Child must demonstrate 25 percent delay in one or more areas of development, atypical development in one or more areas of development, or have a diagnosed condition placing them at risk for developmental delays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Make a referral online at referral.mditp.org or by calling 443-809-2169. Referrals can be made by parents, health care providers, child care providers, social workers, family members or others familiar with child's development. Upon referral, the local Infants and Toddlers site contacts the family to schedule an initial evaluation. If eligible, an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) is developed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workshop covering strategies for effective job interviews, including interview preparation, attire, getting to the interview, commonly asked questions, and follow-up.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A virtual workshop covering strategies for effective job interviews, including interview preparation, attire, transportation to the interview, commonly asked questions, and follow-up techniques.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in interview preparation and professional communication skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County through virtual workshops.

structured_extraction.program_name: Introduction to LinkedIn: A Self-Guided Tour
structured_extraction.program_description: A self-guided tour workshop teaching how to create a LinkedIn profile, build a network of contacts, search and apply to jobs, and use LinkedIn for daily job search activities.

Upon completion, participants may schedule an appointment with Career Center LinkedIn facilitators for additional support and access to job search resources through LinkedIn.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in LinkedIn profile creation, professional networking, and job search using LinkedIn.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County through virtual workshops and appointments at Career Centers.
requirements_list: Must have access to a computer, tablet, or smartphone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the self-guided LinkedIn tour. Upon completion, schedule an appointment with Career Center LinkedIn facilitators for questions and additional resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Juvenile Offenders In Need of Supervision (JOINS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A juvenile diversion program based on restorative justice principles that serves threshold offenders (first-time, nonviolent offenders or juveniles at the beginning of a delinquency pattern). Participants engage in community restitution projects while receiving mentorship to develop personal growth and self-esteem.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants in the JOINS program complete community restitution projects under the mentorship of JOINS officers and youth mentors. The program aims to reduce recidivism, promote accountability, help youth make amends, build self-esteem, and restore victims through restitution and program participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Threshold offenders: first-time, nonviolent juvenile offenders or juveniles deemed to be at the beginning of a pattern of delinquency in Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community restitution projects, mentorship, and personal development activities for participating youth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County juveniles
requirements_list: Must be a threshold offender (first-time, nonviolent offender or beginning pattern of delinquency)
Every juvenile arrest is screened for JOINS eligibility
Youth must participate in community restitution projects and mentorship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Every juvenile arrest is automatically screened for JOINS program eligibility. If selected, youth participate in community restitution projects and mentorship.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Poisoning Prevention and Asthma Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Voluntary home visiting program providing education and support to families to improve child health by reducing and eliminating lead, asthma triggers and other environmental hazards. Includes in-home visits and case management services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One to six home visits provided by community health workers and nurses focusing on reduction and elimination of lead, asthma triggers and other environmental hazards. Free case management services via telephone also available with education on ways to reduce lead hazards, cleaning tips and nutrition guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents under age 19 with asthma or elevated blood lead levels, and families with children age 6 or younger with elevated blood lead levels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home support focusing on reduction and elimination of lead, asthma triggers and other environmental hazards, and case management services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Home visiting component: Must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid, be a Baltimore County resident, be under age 19 and diagnosed with moderate to severe asthma or have elevated blood lead level (BLL) of 3.5 µg/dL or greater
Case management component: Must be a Baltimore County resident, have BLL of 3.5 µg/dL or greater, be age 6 or younger

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Broadband Infrastructure Grant Program (Connect Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_description: State funding programs to expand broadband network infrastructure to unserved homes in Baltimore County. The FY21 State Infrastructure Grant awarded $3.75 million in state funding combined with $1.87 million from Comcast and $700,000 from Baltimore County to support construction and activation of broadband service to over 850 homes, mainly in the northwest corner of the County. The FY22 Network Infrastructure Grant (Connect Maryland) awarded just over $7.7 million in state funding combined with $2.1 million from Comcast and $900,000 from Baltimore County to support broadband infrastructure construction for approximately 900 additional homes, with the project expected to complete in 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funding combined with Comcast and Baltimore County contributions to support broadband infrastructure construction and activation. FY21 program: $3.75 million state + $1.87 million Comcast + $700,000 Baltimore County for 850+ homes. FY22 program: $7.7 million state + $2.1 million Comcast + $900,000 Baltimore County for approximately 900 homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County government and residents in unserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure construction and activation to provide reliable service to unserved homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, including northwest corner of the County and supporting approximately 1,750+ homes across both program phases.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide workforce development program that uses regional partnerships to connect residents with careers in offshore wind energy, construction, manufacturing, and logistics industries through job trainings and apprenticeship programs. The program offers job training and apprenticeship opportunities in carpentry, electrical work, heavy equipment operation, HVAC, welding, CNC programming, forklift operation, trucking (CDL), diesel mechanics, logistics, and maritime specialties, with support services including child-care assistance, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire provision, and transportation assistance. Participants can train with multiple companies in the area and earn certifications valuable in the job market.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job training and apprenticeship programs in carpentry, electrical work, heavy equipment operation, HVAC, welding, CNC programming, forklift operation, trucking (CDL), diesel mechanics, logistics, and maritime/transportation/distribution/logistics specialties for offshore wind industry jobs. Certifications are provided and valuable in the job market. Support services available include child-care assistance, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire provision, and transportation assistance. Participants can train with multiple partner companies in the area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 18 or older interested in careers in wind energy, construction, manufacturing, and logistics industries. Targeted opportunities for Baltimore City residents, youth, and returning citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training and apprenticeship programs with certifications in welding, electrical, manufacturing, maritime/transportation/distribution/logistics, and related specialties. Support services include child care assistance, financial aid, tools, work attire, and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Maryland residents statewide. Targeted opportunity for Baltimore City and Baltimore County residents, youth, and returning citizens.
requirements_list: Be 18 years of age or older
Have a high school diploma or GED or equivalent
Able to pass a drug test
Authorized to work in the United States
Must be a Maryland resident
Background-friendly (applicants with criminal records are welcome to apply)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Career Navigators by email or phone to express interest, or fill out the interest form at bit.ly/applywind. Career Navigators pair applicants with partner organizations based on career interests. Applicants can also complete an inquiry form on the website indicating job training or apprenticeship interests.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program funded by the State of Maryland that coordinates transportation services for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients who reside in Baltimore County and need transportation to access medically necessary services. The program provides shared-ride transportation for ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher-bound recipients who have no other means of transport to medical appointments, as well as transportation for facility discharges and transfers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Medical Assistance Program covers the full cost of transportation services. There is no cost to eligible clients. Transportation is provided by contracted vendors (Hart to Heart for wheelchair and ambulance rides, and TransDev/Veolia for shared rides to medical appointments). Services operate Monday through Saturday from as early as 5 a.m. to as late as 8 p.m. Medical facility discharges and transfers are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year. Transportation modes include ambulatory, wheelchair, paratransit, public transit, sedan/cab, or ambulance services, with mode determined by medical necessity and clinical justification. Rides must be pre-scheduled one to seven days in advance and requested at least 24 hours before the appointment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who are Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients and need transportation to medically necessary services but have no other means of transport available.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from medically necessary medical appointments, services, discharges, and transfers that are covered by Medical Assistance. NOT for hospital discharges/transfers in certain circumstances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must have active and eligible Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
Must have no other means of transportation available
Medical certification required from physician, PA, CRNP, or dentist stating medical necessity and inability to use public or ADA transportation due to medical condition
Underlying medical diagnosis must be documented
Clinical justification for selected transportation mode required
Certification valid for one year from signing date; must be renewed at least annually
For Hart to Heart: diagnosis must support medical necessity of mode of transport
For TransDev: physician must certify inability to use public or ADA transportation
Clients using Mobility may not use MA Transportation except under extreme circumstances
Children 17 and under must be accompanied by an adult
Residents of Skilled Nursing Facilities must be accompanied during transport

Must provide specific information when scheduling: caller name and phone, recipient name/SSN/DOB/MA number/Medicare number, pickup and destination addresses with room numbers, physician name and reason for transport, appointment date and time, transport type, and other pertinent ride information
Clients must be ready for pickup at designated time
Trips must be pre-scheduled, booked one to seven days in advance
Same-day transportation not offered except under extreme circumstances
Must call to cancel at least 30 minutes before scheduled pickup time
Conduct jeopardizing safety may result in suspension of services
For out-of-area transports: services must be medically necessary and unavailable at closer facility; specialty services not available through client's MCO
If ambulance transport needed: must answer all three qualifying questions; if not bed-confined, must check applicable clinical intervention reasons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact Baltimore County Department of Health at (410) 887-2828 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:45 p.m.) or Hart to Heart at 443-573-2037 or TransDev at 410-783-2465. 2. Provider/physician completes Maryland Statewide Medical Assistance Provider Certification Form with patient information, medical diagnosis, symptoms, transportation mode selection, and clinical justification. 3. Have your physician, PA, CRNP, or dentist sign the Baltimore County Certificate for Medical Transportation form or appropriate certification form. 4. Submit the completed form to the Baltimore County Department of Health or the contracted vendor as appropriate. 5. Once approved, schedule your rides with the contracted vendor one to seven days in advance. 6. Be ready for pickup at your designated ready time (90 minutes before appointment for TransDev, one hour before for Hart to Heart).

structured_extraction.program_description: A portable outreach resource vehicle that brings police department programs and services directly to neighborhoods in Baltimore County for community engagement and education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Mobile Community Center (MCC) is deployed to community events to facilitate community meetings, crime prevention presentations, critical incident support, family conflict resolution, youth traffic safety programs, youth development activities, and outreach to vulnerable populations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and neighborhoods in Baltimore County hosting community events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community engagement, education, and outreach services provided via the Mobile Community Center vehicle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. The MCC is deployed only to community events held within Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Contact local precinct 60 days prior to event
Identify a 50-foot by 50-foot level pad site for deployment
An additional 25 feet is needed for tow vehicle to remain attached
MCC will be deployed for approximately three hours
Vehicle arrives approximately one hour prior to event for setup
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local precinct 60 days prior to your event to request the Mobile Community Center deployment.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Family Caregivers Support Program (NFCSP) - Baltimore County Caregivers Program (Baltimore County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial support, consultations, education, and resources to family and informal caregivers age 18 and older caring for Baltimore County residents over age 60, older relatives over age 55 with primary care responsibility for children under 18, and adults aged 18 to 59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides annual stipends to support respite care (paying for someone to stay at home while the caregiver is away or for care recipient to stay at nursing home for one or two nights) and medical supplies not covered by Medicare such as incontinence supplies. The stipend amount varies yearly and a waitlist may be enacted if funds are limited. The stipend can be applied for once per year for up to five years, with one stipend per household for one care recipient. The program also offers individual caregiver consultations (one-time, one-hour private consultations with a caregiver specialist), outreach and educational events, access to a 24/7 caregiver website (Trualta), support groups, and a quarterly newsletter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family and informal caregivers age 18 and older taking care of Baltimore County residents over age 60, older relatives over age 55 with primary care responsibility for individuals under 18, and adults aged 18 to 59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care costs, medical supplies not covered by Medicare, and supportive services to help caregivers provide quality care and take better care of themselves.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to caregivers assisting individuals who reside in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Caregiver must be age 18 or older

Care recipient must be over age 60 and reside in Baltimore County, OR be an older relative over age 55 with primary care responsibility for individuals under 18, OR be an adult aged 18 to 59 with disabilities
One stipend per household for one care recipient
Ineligible for stipend if care recipient is receiving hospice care or is being paid by another source such as Medicaid
Stipend can be applied for once a year for up to five years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To arrange a Caregiver Consultation and apply for financial support, complete an intake by calling the Caregivers Program at 410-887-4724. For financial support eligibility details, contact the program directly. There is no charge for the consultation service.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit against Baltimore County real property tax imposed on dwellings repaired or reconstructed after a natural disaster. Also recognizes tax credit against State of Maryland real property tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% of property tax on the natural disaster allowance for fiscal years 2006-2009; 50% of property tax on the natural disaster allowance for fiscal years 2010-2012. Credit cannot reduce tax liability below taxes owed based on base value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30, 2005 (if assessment notice issued by September 1, 2005); OR within 30 days after assessment notice is issued
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with legal interest in dwellings at time of damage who are otherwise eligible for homestead credit under § 9-105 of Tax Property Article.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief for repair and reconstruction of disaster-damaged dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dwelling must be located in Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Dwelling eligible for Homestead credit under § 9-105 of Tax Property Article
Dwelling damaged or destroyed by natural disaster and subsequently repaired or reconstructed
Revaluation must result in assessment exceeding last assessment
Homeowner must have had legal interest in dwelling at time of damage

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary liquor license for bona fide nonprofit organizations that are raising money for charitable reasons. This license allows nonprofits to serve alcoholic beverages at a single event.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approval to serve and sell alcoholic beverages at a single charitable event.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for visual and performing arts, science and humanities programs, performances, exhibitions and lectures.

Must offer visual and performing arts, science and humanities programs
Arts activities must take place in eligible jurisdictions
Must serve Baltimore County residents

Must submit all required attachments

Demonstrates financial and organizational responsibility

structured_extraction.program_description: Free training sessions that teach individuals how to recognize, respond to, and prevent opioid overdoses and how to administer intranasal naloxone to reverse an overdose. Attendees receive a completion certificate, a prescription for naloxone, and a naloxone kit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free two-hour online training sessions via Webex on how to use intranasal naloxone to reverse an opioid overdose. Participants learn what opioids are, how to recognize and respond to overdoses, and how to prevent them. Upon completion, attendees receive a certificate, a prescription for naloxone, and a naloxone kit (distributed one to three days after training).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals concerned that a loved one is at risk for overdosing on heroin or prescription pain medication, and those with certificates expiring within the next three months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and naloxone medication kit to reverse opioid overdoses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Preregistration required
Individuals can request special accommodations such as language interpretation or large print materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Preregister for training sessions online. A link to the training application will be sent prior to the start of training. Attendees participate in a two-hour online training via Webex. Upon completion, attendees receive a certificate and information about naloxone kit distribution.

Arts organizations, museums, drama groups, music groups or similar entities
Located in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A search-and-rescue program partnering with Project Lifesaver International to provide timely response for children and adults with Alzheimer's, autism, and related conditions who wander or go missing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled clients wear a small personal transmitter (wristband or ankle band) that emits an individualized tracking signal. Trained emergency teams respond when a client goes missing. Caregivers call 911 to notify Project Lifesaver. Average recovery time is 30 minutes—95 percent less than standard operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers of children and adults with Alzheimer's, autism, and related conditions who may wander.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal transmitter equipment and emergency response services for locating missing individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Enrollee must be a child or adult with Alzheimer's, autism, or related cognitive conditions or disorders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Baltimore County Police Department website.

structured_extraction.program_description: An urban reforestation initiative that focuses on specific Baltimore County neighborhoods each spring and fall, planting large numbers of canopy trees in County rights-of-way and providing free front yard trees to homeowners upon request. The program combines and adapts the County's Operation ReTree and Street Tree Replacement programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County plants large numbers of native canopy trees in Baltimore County rights-of-way and provides free front yard trees to homeowners. Trees are installed with initial one year of maintenance and 100 percent survival guarantee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County homeowners in targeted neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free front yard tree plantings and street tree plantings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County (specific neighborhoods targeted each spring and fall)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Project ReTree page to learn more and request trees. Homeowners in targeted neighborhoods can request free front yard trees.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Historical Restorations and Rehabilitations
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County tax credit program that encourages owners of historic properties to restore and rehabilitate their properties. Residential properties receive a 20 percent county property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work that can be extended for up to 10 years. Commercial properties receive a 10-year tax freeze on the increased assessment resulting from rehabilitation work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential owner-occupied dwellings receive a 20 percent county property tax credit for eligible rehabilitation work, extendable for up to 10 years. Commercial income-producing properties receive a 10-year tax freeze on the increased assessment attributable to rehabilitation work. Eligible rehabilitation work includes exterior repairs (roof, windows, painting, stucco) and interior work (painting, electrical, plumbing, heating, air conditioning systems). Total rehabilitation cost must exceed $1,000 and must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards, meaning materials must be repaired or replaced in kind.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Baltimore County seeking to restore or rehabilitate their properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior repairs (roof repair, window repair or replacement, painting, stucco work) and interior work (painting, upgrading electrical and plumbing systems, heating and air conditioning)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Baltimore County and designated as historic. Eligible historic designations include: contributing structures in a County Historic District, contributing structures in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or on the Final Landmarks List.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic

Property must be either a contributing structure in a County Historic District, a contributing structure in a National Register Historic District, or individually listed on the National Register of Historic Places or on the Final Landmarks List
For residential properties: owner-occupied dwelling
Total cost of rehabilitation work must exceed $1,000
Rehabilitation work must be in conformance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (materials must be repaired or replaced in kind)
All rehabilitation projects must be approved by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission before any work begins
For commercial properties: rehabilitation work must result in an increased assessment attributable to the rehabilitation work (work must be substantial)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Department of Planning's County Historic Tax Credit frequently asked questions. Pre-approval by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission is required before the commencement of any work. Contact Preservation Services for information and to apply. Owners of residential properties used for rental or investment purposes must complete a commercial application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Time-limited rental assistance for homeless households that qualify. The program helps identify and secure housing, provides case management, and offers time-limited rental assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited rental assistance for households that qualify. Services include housing search assistance and case management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness who meet program eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance and housing stabilization services for qualified households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness
Must contact Coordinated Entry to be placed on waitlist for referral
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Coordinated Entry hotline at 410-887-8463 (select option 1, available 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday through Friday) to be placed on a waitlist for referral.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit available to property owners who make qualified improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties in designated commercial revitalization districts in Baltimore County. The credit is applied against Baltimore County real property tax obligations. Tax credits equal 100 percent of the increase in County taxes for senior housing developments and mobile home parks in revitalization districts, 50 percent for senior housing outside districts, or 100 percent of County property taxes for commercial property in designated districts. Credits run for five years, or ten years if improvements exceed $10 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits equal 100 percent of the increase in County taxes for senior housing developments and mobile home parks in revitalization districts, 50 percent for senior housing outside districts, or 100 percent of County property taxes for commercial property in designated districts. Credits run for five years, or ten years if improvements exceed $10 million. Qualified improvements must have a full cash value of $100,000 or more as reflected in State Department of Records and Taxation records.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of a notice of assessment by SDAT that includes the improvements
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners who make qualified improvements to eligible properties in Baltimore County, including owners of mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties in designated revitalization districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction on improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties in designated commercial revitalization districts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, specifically properties located in designated commercial revitalization districts (with some eligibility outside districts for senior housing).
requirements_list: Owner must make qualified improvements with a full cash value of $100,000 or more
Property must be documented with the State Department of Records and Taxation (SDAT)
Property must be located in designated commercial revitalization district
Property must be mobile home park, senior housing development, or commercially zoned
Properties used for railroads, public utilities, or covered by the Maryland Condominium Act are not eligible
Detailed receipts for all related expenses must be submitted with the application
Application must be filed with Director of Budget and Finance within 120 days of SDAT assessment notice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File an Application for Revitalization Tax Credit with the Director of Budget and Finance within 120 days after SDAT issues a notice of assessment that includes the improvements. Include detailed receipts for all related expenses. For improvements to commercially zoned properties in revitalization districts, contact the Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team at 410-887-3480. Mail the completed application to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 149, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workshop teaching effective strategies for writing a resume, including introduction and summary of education, experience, and expertise.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A virtual workshop teaching effective strategies for writing a resume, including how to write an introduction and summary of education, experience, and expertise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers needing help developing or improving their resumes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in resume writing techniques and job application strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Baltimore County through virtual workshops.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the virtual workshop. Check the Upcoming Events list for specific dates and times.

structured_extraction.program_description: A monthly financial assistance program providing subsidies to eligible Baltimore County residents age 62 and older to help pay for assisted living services in licensed group homes with 4 to 16 residents. The program covers meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision for elderly residents who are frail and unable to live independently. Financial assistance is available up to $1,000 toward assisted living group home facility costs for a limited number of eligible residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial assistance paid on behalf of eligible residents to cover the cost of assisted living services in licensed group homes. Subsidies provide up to $1,000 toward assisted living group home facility costs, covering meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision. Eligibility based on income and asset limits: single person income up to $4,358/month with assets up to $20,064; for two people, only applicant's income is considered with assets up to $26,400. Available to a limited number of eligible assisted living group home residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income seniors age 62 and older who are residents of Baltimore County and require personal care assistance; those who are frail and unable to live independently.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost of assisted living services in licensed group homes including meals, personal care, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Baltimore County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Age 62 and older
Must require personal care assistance and complete a Functional Assessment
Monthly income cannot exceed $4,358 for an individual
Assets cannot exceed $20,064
Must be a resident in or approved for entrance into a facility with a service agreement with the Department of Aging
Resident of assisted living group home
Limited number of eligible assisted living group home residents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Department of Aging Housing Office at 410-887-4632 or Maryland Access Point at 410-887-2594 to obtain the SALS application and learn more about eligibility. Contact the Baltimore County Department of Aging for application details, eligibility verification, and enrollment procedures.

Topics include smartphones, online shopping, video chat, online health resources, and protecting personal information online.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week summer employment program for Baltimore County youth ages 14 to 21 that provides paid work experience in private and public sector worksites, along with financial literacy training and employable skills development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth participants earn $15 per hour for up to 25 hours per week (up to five hours per day) over six weeks. Youth are matched with employers based on interests, employer needs, and worksite locations. The program runs July 6 through August 14, 2026. Employers host youth workers for summer positions with positions funded at $2,500 per youth; can be onsite or virtual.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) who died in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the property tax obligation and continues year after year without needing to reapply. The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 100 percent of Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation. The credit continues annually without the need for reapplication. The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program. Other charges listed on the tax bill are not included in the credit calculation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30 in the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers or rescue workers, including volunteers, who died in Maryland while employed by Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces or eliminates Baltimore County property tax obligations on residential dwellings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The death must have occurred in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of employment with Baltimore County. The dwelling must be the legal residence of the applicant in Baltimore County. The fallen hero or surviving spouse must have been domiciled in Maryland at the time of death. The credit applies only to Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligations.
requirements_list: The decedent must have been a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteer) employed by Baltimore County
The death must have occurred in Maryland during the course of or as a result of employment

The dwelling was owned by the decedent at the time of death, OR the decedent or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland as of the date of death and the dwelling was acquired within two years of death, OR the dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling
The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program
The dwelling is the legal residence of the applicant
The dwelling is occupied by no more than two families
The surviving spouse has not remarried
Death certificate or evidence of eligibility is required
Line-of-duty death certification is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Surviving Spouse of a Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker with personal, property, and service information. Attach a death certificate or evidence of eligibility. Submit to Ms. Kathy Farren, Office of Budget and Finance, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 149, Towson, Maryland 21204. The Retirement Section verifies line-of-duty status and the Director of the Office of Budget and Finance approves or denies the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax exemptions for non-transient room rental collections (accommodations for more than 90 consecutive days) and for occupancies by federal, state, or county officials when on official business. Eligible operators submit exemption certificates to reduce their transient occupancy tax liability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemptions from the 9.5% transient occupancy tax for room rental collections from non-transient accommodations (90 consecutive days or more) and for facilities used exclusively by federal, state, or county officials on official business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County hotel, motel, and short-term rental businesses that meet exemption criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemptions reduce the transient occupancy tax owed on qualifying room rental income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland

For non-transient exemption: accommodations must be for at least 90 consecutive days

For government official exemption: occupancy must be for exclusive use by and paid by or from the funds of U.S. Government, State of Maryland, Baltimore County, other jurisdictions, or foreign government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit exemption certificate through the online form indicating exemption type, dates of coverage (at least 90 days apart for non-transient), and business identification. Certify that all qualifications have been met. Provide information about the person submitting the return.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community cat management program that humanely reduces the community cat population by providing spay or neuter surgery, vaccinations, ear-tipping, microchipping, and flea treatment for unowned outdoor cats. The program registers feral cat caregivers, provides guidelines for maintaining healthy and lawful community cat colonies, and offers trap loans and mediation services. The program helps prevent unwanted litters, reduces strain on animal shelters, improves cat health and quality of life, and decreases nuisance behaviors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or subsidized spay or neuter surgery, rabies vaccine, FVRCP vaccine, left ear-tipping, abdominal tattoo, microchipping, topical flea treatment, and veterinary exam while sedated. Drop-off is 8 a.m. and pick-up is 3 p.m. the same day. Participants receive a Health Summary and Rabies Vaccine Certificate for each cat. Program also provides registration support, trap loans (humane traps with replacement value of $90 each and dividers with replacement value of $25 each), veterinary resources, mediation services, humane trapping instructions, and informational materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Feral and community cat caregivers, trappers, transporters, and Baltimore County residents in good standing with Baltimore County Animal Services who care for unowned outdoor cats and wish to humanely reduce the community cat population through sterilization and vaccination.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides surgical services (spay/neuter), vaccinations (rabies and FVRCP), microchipping, ear-tipping, and flea treatment for eligible unowned outdoor cats. Trap loans are available for those who own the property where trapping will occur. Registration assistance and program guidelines support community cat colony management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cats must be unowned community cats living outdoors at an address within Baltimore County, Maryland. Caregivers must operate within Baltimore County and obtain property owner permission before trapping on non-owned property.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with Baltimore County Animal Services by completing the Feral Cat Caregiver registration form with participant information, colony details, role(s), and submitting a signed agreement to comply with program guidelines. Schedule a TNR surgery appointment by contacting the TNR Coordinator. Bring the cat in a trap or transfer cage to the facility at 13800 Manor Road, Baldwin, Maryland by 8 a.m. Pick up the cat at 3 p.m. the same day and return it to where it was trapped. For trap loans, contact the TNR Coordinator to request a loan, complete the Trap Loan Agreement form, review Humane Trapping Instructions, pick up equipment from BCAS, describe any existing damage at pickup, and return equipment as agreed. All appointments and return dates are scheduled before the loan is given.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability offers free reforestation projects to Baltimore County landowners as part of the Phase II Chesapeake Bay Watershed Implementation Plan. The program converts lawn or grass areas to forest by planting approximately 200 native trees per acre on private land. EPS staff work with landowners to develop and execute reforestation plans on their property, including site preparation, tree planting with stakes and shelters for deer protection, and three-year maintenance with a 90 percent survival warranty. Trees are planted in staggered rows and the program includes seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, and shelter upkeep during the maintenance period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EPS provides free reforestation services including site assessment, planting plan development, contractor procurement, site preparation, and tree and shelter installation. The county plants approximately 200 native trees per acre on eligible properties with stakes and shelters for protection from deer and pests. Large rural reforestations include three years of maintenance with a 90 percent survival guarantee each year for three years, including seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, and shelter upkeep.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County landowners with at least one acre of open space (lawn or grass) available for reforestation

EPS conducts two inspections during the initial maintenance period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual grants that support locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations to identify and implement restoration projects and educational activities relating to actions specified in Small Watershed Action Plans and Total Maximum Daily Load Implementation Plans. The program aims to increase resident participation in county watershed restoration planning and leverage additional external funding for environmental restoration work in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $30,000 are available to cover staff hours dedicated to conducting environmental restoration activities and increasing public awareness of environmental stewardship. The grant funds operating expenses to foster staffing capacity for ongoing restoration work and watershed education and outreach. Fringe benefits up to 30 percent of salary and indirect costs up to 10 percent of combined salary and fringe may be included. In some cases, grants exceeding $30,000 may be awarded to established and highly productive organizations with at least three years of prior funding and exemplary performance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and community nonprofit organizations in Baltimore County with active membership and a demonstrated history of conducting resident-based and community restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff salaries for conducting restoration planning and implementation, and watershed education and outreach. Fringe benefits for employee expenses such as health insurance, paid sick leave and paid vacation leave. Indirect costs for overhead expenses including accounting, financial management, insurance, office rent and supplies, and telephones and internet. Materials and equipment are not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All work must be implemented in Baltimore County. Organizations must be locally-based with active membership in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Be a locally-based watershed association or community group with membership in Baltimore County
Be registered as a 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(6) organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects
Have fulfilled all grant requirements on past grants if previously funded through this grant program
Maintain a minimum ratio of one hour of staff time for every $30 in grant funds requested
Offer a Stream Watch program to engage volunteers to observe stream reaches and report potential pollution
Participate in Baltimore County Watershed Planning steering or implementation committees
Link all planned restoration actions to applicable Small Watershed Action Plans, Total Maximum Daily Load Implementation Plans, and the Trash and Litter Reduction Strategy
Follow Baltimore County guidance on tree plantings, tree giveaways and stormwater best management practices
Coordinate with DEPS on inspection and verification of past planting projects and best management practices per Maryland Department of Environment guidelines
Provide latest financial statements (audited, Form 990, unaudited, or treasurer's report)
List all county, federal, state, and other grants and loans awarded in current and last two fiscal years
Identify if funding benefits real property and provide property details
Identify officers, board members, and major shareholders (greater than 10%)
Describe population served and anticipated community benefits
Specify project completion date
Disclose any in-kind services or non-cash contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications require three key steps. First, complete the DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions by addressing organization eligibility, restoration and stewardship plans, grant deliverables by quarter, Stream Watch participation, watershed planning involvement, linking actions to watershed plans, education and outreach activities, capacity building, project guidance and inspections, and past year accomplishments. Second, complete the standard Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance form. Third, submit all required supporting documents including a screenshot of good standing status from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, budget proposal, and financial statements. Submit all materials as separate PDF files with specified file naming conventions to the contact email by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Employment and Real Property Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available to businesses in Baltimore County Enterprise Zones (Chesapeake, Southwest, and Federal Center at Woodlawn) that invest in property and create jobs or expand operations. Both County and Maryland tax credits are available. The Real Property Tax Credit applies to companies that improve their property and lasts for 10 years—covering 80% of the property tax increase from new investment for the first five years, decreasing by 10% annually for the next five years. The State Income Tax Credit is for hiring new, full-time employees, offering a one-time credit of up to $1,000 per employee, increasing to $3,000 for hiring workers meeting 'disadvantaged' criteria, with additional credits available for continued employment in years two and three. The program encourages redevelopment in older industrial and office areas and promotes the use of empty or underused properties. An electricity price reduction program (BGE Rider 7) is also available for qualifying businesses with significant load increases.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit offering 10-year reduction on property taxes after major capital improvements, covering 80% of the property tax increase from new investment for the first five years and decreasing by 10% each year for the next five years. Income tax credit allows businesses a one-time state income tax deduction of up to $1,000 per new full-time employee created, increasing to $3,000 for hiring workers meeting 'disadvantaged' criteria, with additional credits available for continued employment in years two and three. Personal property tax credits available for Focus Area Zones only. BGE Rider 7 electricity rate reductions available for 200kW+ load increases with 10+ new full-time equivalent employees. Both County and Maryland tax credits available for qualifying businesses expanding or adding employees in Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: no later than December 31 to receive a property tax credit on the next July 1 tax bill

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property improvements, job creation, and business expansion in Enterprise Zones. The program provides tax credits (not direct funds) for qualifying businesses that make new investments in real property, acquire buildings and land, purchase new machinery and equipment, conduct new construction, or rehabilitate existing buildings. Retail businesses are generally excluded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses located within Baltimore County Enterprise Zones including Chesapeake (designated June 15, 2015), Southwest (designated December 1996, renewed 2003 and 2013), and Federal Center at Woodlawn (designated June 2011). The Federal Center at Woodlawn zone is bounded by Windsor Mill Rd, Security Blvd, Rolling Rd, Woodlawn Dr, Gwynn Oak Ave, Featherbed Ln, Greengage Rd, Dogwood Rd, Fairbrook Rd, Essex Rd, Lord Baltimore Dr, Saint Lukes Ln, Windsor Blvd, Castlemoor Rd, Clays Ln, Belmont Ave, Richwood Ave, and Ambassador Rd. Businesses must be in one of these designated Enterprise Zones and can use provided zone maps or the My Neighborhood Interactive Map to determine eligibility.
requirements_list: Business must be located within a designated Baltimore County Enterprise Zone (Chesapeake, Southwest, or Federal Center at Woodlawn)

Must submit completed eligibility application
Most businesses are eligible, but retail businesses are generally excluded
Must make a new investment in real property, acquire buildings/land, purchase machinery/equipment, or conduct new construction/rehabilitation
Property owner concurrence/co-signature required if developer applies on behalf of owner

Applicant must answer all questions in Sections A and B of application
Agreement to provide all data requested by Zone Administrator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download and complete the eligibility application form and verify address eligibility using the interactive map or detailed zone maps. 2. Submit completed application to Enterprise Zone Coordinator at Baltimore County Department of Economic Development, Historic Courthouse Suite 100, 400 Washington Avenue, Towson, Maryland 21204 by December 31 to receive a property tax credit on the next July 1 tax bill. For property tax credits, submit prior to project completion and User/Occupancy Permit issuance. Applicants can contact the coordinator by phone at 410-887-8000, fax at 410-887-8017, or email at businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov. 3. After the department reviews your application, you will receive a letter confirming eligibility. 4. For the property tax credit, the county will automatically notify the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. 5. To claim the income tax credit, submit Maryland Tax Form 500CR with your annual tax return. 6. If hiring a 'disadvantaged' employee to receive a higher credit, you must get that employee certified. 7. For BGE Rider 7 electricity discounts, contact BGE Manager of Economic Development at (410) 470-8999.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Facade Improvement Grant offers matching funds to assist with exterior building upgrades and facade improvements for small commercial and industrial properties in Baltimore City. Administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation, the program helps businesses and property owners enhance storefronts, signage, awnings, and other improvements that strengthen both businesses and neighborhoods. The program provides multiple FIG options with varying maximum awards ranging from $7,500 to $50,000 depending on property type and investment level. Grants are structured as matching funds with reimbursement provided after project completion. Eligible properties include commercial buildings, vacant and corner commercial properties, industrial properties, shopping centers, and properties in need of redevelopment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple FIG options available: Citywide FIG ($7,500 maximum with 1:1 match), Corner Property FIG ($15,000 maximum with 1:1 match and $50,000 minimum investment), Vacant Building FIG ($15,000 maximum with 1:1 match and $50,000 minimum investment), Industrial FIG ($15,000 maximum with 1:1 match for properties 10,000+ sq ft in industrial zones), and Shopping Center FIG ($50,000 maximum covering 10% of costs with $100,000 minimum investment). Matching funds provided as reimbursement after project completion. Grants must be approved before work begins and are reimbursed after the project is complete. Available for facade improvements including signage, exterior painting, storefront improvements, lighting, awnings, masonry, murals, and landscaping features.
