structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers a personal property tax credit to grocery stores that locate or undergo significant renovations in targeted Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas. The program provides a 10-year, 80 percent credit against personal property tax for supermarkets meeting requirements for offering healthy food. Personal property typically covers furniture, fixtures, and equipment. The program aims to increase access to healthy food choices and support economic development in underserved communities. The program went into effect on January 31, 2016 and was amended in 2018. Implemented by the Baltimore Development Corporation.

For renovated stores, the requirement varies by floor space: $5 per square foot for 20,000 square feet or less, $8 per square foot for 20,000 to 45,000 square feet, and $10 per square foot for more than 45,000 square feet.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Spaces Grant, administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC), helps business owners and property owners offset the cost of installing outdoor seating, parklets, landscaping, lighting, and other features that expand a business's use of outdoor space. The program offers reimbursement grants of up to $5,000 for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching funds reimbursement grant of up to $5,000 for qualified expenses. Businesses must provide 1:1 matching funds and pay for the entire project first. Award amounts depend on available funding and are made at the sole discretion of BDC.

Outdoor lighting including string lights and illuminated trees. Pots, planters, planter boxes, and trellises. Plants and landscaping (limited to 25% of total grant). Mobile vending structures. Architectural and design services (limited to 25% of project cost). Improvements can be made in sidewalk space, adjacent parking spaces, private outdoor seating areas, and community spaces open to the public.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available citywide in Baltimore City, Maryland. Eligible locations include sidewalk space and adjacent parking spaces (public right-of-way), private outdoor seating areas and courtyards on private property, and community spaces on public or private property open to the general public.
requirements_list: Property must be a business location in Baltimore City or vacant property with conditions
Applicant must have a signed lease (for businesses and nonprofits) or be a commercial property owner
Applicants without commercial leases must have a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) from property owner
Vacant property owners must meet conditions regarding occupancy and lease execution before reimbursement
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application
Work must not be completed prior to application approval
Applicant must provide matching funds at 1:1 ratio
Applicant must pay for all project costs before receiving reimbursement
Project construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter
Applicant must be in good legal standing with federal, state, and local authorities
For projects in the public right-of-way, a Curbside Commercial Permit or Minor Privilege Permit is required
For community-led projects, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is required
Applicants must obtain two quotes for work done by third-party contractors
The cost of architectural or design services cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost
The cost of plants and landscaping is limited to 25% of the total grant amount
The grant recipient must maintain the improvements for three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request an application by filling out a form on the BDC website or by contacting BDC. structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grants that help homeowners reduce risk from natural hazards such as flooding and cliff erosion. The program covers up to 75% of project costs for eligible mitigation projects, with homeowners responsible for the remaining 25% and any cost overruns. Common project types include acquisition and demolition of high-hazard properties and elevation of structures in flood plains.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 75% of project costs for hazard mitigation projects. The homeowner is responsible for 25% of costs and any cost overruns. Project types include acquisition and demolition of properties and elevation of structures above the Base Flood Elevation. Funding timeline extends up to two years from application initiation to funding awards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: NLT July 1st for Pre-Screening Questionnaire; August 31st for final application materials submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Calvert County with high-hazard properties, including properties along cliffs and NFIP Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and demolition, or elevation of structures above the Base Flood Elevation for flood mitigation. Projects must reduce risk from natural hazards such as flooding or cliff erosion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Calvert County, Maryland. Specific eligibility depends on hazard type—cliff mitigation projects for properties along cliffs, and flood mitigation projects for properties in flood plains with NFIP insurance.
requirements_list: Property must be high-hazard (cliff properties or flood plain properties with NFIP insurance)
NFIP Repetitive Loss or Severe Repetitive Loss properties most competitive for funding

For acquisition and demolition: property appraisal, plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance copy (flood only), documentation of past flood events (flood only), certified imminent threat letter from engineer (cliff only), itemized demolition cost estimate

For elevation: plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance policy documentation, documentation of past flood events, elevation certificate, certified structural stability letter from engineer, itemized elevation cost estimate
Homeowner responsible for 25% of project costs and any cost overruns
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Pre-Screening Questionnaire by July 1st. County Division of Emergency Management contacts residents to provide additional information. Submit final application materials by August 31st. County develops subapplication and submits for initial review by mid-November. Final subapplication submitted to FEMA by late January. FEMA issues funding decisions by late summer. Funding allocated to states and projects begin mid-spring. Timeline from initiation to funding can take up to two years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows Agricultural Preservation District landowners to sell TDRs to the county, which retires them rather than transferring them. structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of property in Agricultural Preservation Districts who wish to sell development rights to the county.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted September through December. Applications are reviewed December through January. Offer letters are sent January through February. Transactions conclude in June.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Replacement capital grants to offset County support service charges for special events. Maximum grant amount is Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000) per organization, or five (5) grant applications per fiscal year (July-June), whichever comes first. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Grant funds are transferred directly from the County Department of Economic Development to appropriate county departments and offices to pay fees directly; no money passes through the applicant organization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be filed at least thirty (30) days prior to the special event
structured_extraction.contact_name: Calvert County Events and Marketing Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Calvert County businesses and nonprofits planning to hold special events that demonstrate destination awareness potential, ability to increase overnight stays, and potential for increased visitor spending.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting Calvert County support service charges required to support a special event as defined by Chapter 82 of the Calvert County Code.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Calvert County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Calvert County business or nonprofit
Must be in good standing as reported by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have no outstanding Calvert County violations (zoning violations), overdue taxes or assessments
Must have first reviewed the Special Events Permit policy and process
Must have completed and submitted a special events application for the current fiscal year
Must have received an estimate of Calvert County support services costs from the Calvert County Events and Marketing Coordinator
Applicant must be an adult (18+)
Application must be filed at least thirty (30) days prior to the special event
Special event must create destination awareness for Calvert County
Special event must have the ability to increase overnight stays in Calvert County
Special event must have the potential to increase visitor spending in-market
Special event must have a measurable positive economic impact
After event occurs, permittee must report special event attendance numbers and success measures to the Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Special Events Permit policy and process. 2. Complete and submit a special events application for the current fiscal year. 3. Receive an estimate of Calvert County support services costs from the Calvert County Events and Marketing Coordinator. 4. Complete the Tourism Development Incentive Fund Grant application. 5. File the application at least thirty (30) days prior to the special event. 6. Receive a confirmation or denial letter via email within ten (10) business days of the application arrival date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows landowners to sell the development potential of their property to another party through the recording of restrictive covenants. The sale permanently restricts the sending property from development, while TDR purchasers can use the rights to increase density on designated receiving properties. The program aims to preserve farms and forest lands by redirecting development to targeted growth areas.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts (APDs) can certify and sell Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) at $6,230 per TDR. TDRs are calculated at 1 TDR per acre, minus 5 TDRs per existing residence, plus 5 TDRs per grandfathered unused lot. TDRs can be sold through private transactions or through the county TDR Reserve program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property in Agricultural Preservation Districts who wish to sell development rights, and developers or property owners in designated receiving areas who wish to purchase TDRs to increase density potential.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: TDR proceeds go to the selling landowner. Purchasing TDRs allows buyers to increase the density potential of their property in designated growth areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural Preservation Districts (APD) in Calvert County are sending areas. Designated receiving areas in Calvert County can utilize TDRs to increase density.
requirements_list: Property must be in an Agricultural Preservation District (APD)
TDR certification application must be approved by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) and the Board of County Commissioners (BOCC)
TDR certification must be recorded in Land Records
Purchasing TDRs requires property to be in a designated receiving area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners apply to certify TDRs using the Application for Certification of Development Options form. Staff calculates TDRs based on acreage and existing structures. Applications are reviewed by APAB and require BOCC approval before certification is recorded. Once certified, TDRs can be sold privately or through the TDR Reserve program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-operated revolving fund program that allows citizens to buy and sell TDRs through the county government instead of private transactions. The county purchases TDRs from Agricultural Preservation District owners and sells them to developers. This provides an alternative to private TDR market negotiations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selling TDRs to the Reserve: $6,230 per TDR offered on a first-come, first-served basis with a 1% administrative fee. Purchasing TDRs from the Reserve: Price equals the amount paid by the county for the TDR plus 1% administrative fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural Preservation District landowners wishing to sell TDRs, owners of TDRs conveyed from original APDs, and developers or property owners in designated receiving areas wishing to purchase TDRs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from selling TDRs go to the landowner. Purchasing TDRs allows property owners to increase density potential within designated residential growth areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County Agricultural Preservation Districts and designated receiving areas.
requirements_list: For sellers: Must own TDRs either originally certified from an APD or conveyed from an original APD
For buyers: Property must be in a designated receiving area
Available on first-come, first-served basis subject to available funding and TDR supply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners apply to sell TDRs using the Application to sell TDRs form. Developers or property owners apply to purchase TDRs using the Application to purchase TDRs form. Transactions are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fee Financial Hardship Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that grants waivers (exemptions) from paying the Bay Restoration Fee to residential dwellings and properties that demonstrate substantial financial hardship. Eligible applicants in participating Maryland counties may receive a reduction or complete exemption from the Bay Restoration Fee billed on their real property tax bill or sanitary district (sewer) bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants receive a waiver (exemption) from paying the Bay Restoration Fee. The exemption reduces or eliminates the fee billed on the real property tax bill or sanitary district (sewer) bill for a specified time period, typically 1 year. The exemption must be applied for annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents and taxpayers who are homeowners or lease holders demonstrating substantial financial hardship
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bay Restoration Fee exemption on real property tax or sanitary district sewer bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Calvert County and Talbot County. In Calvert County, applicants must be county residents. In Talbot County, applicants must be billed the fee on their real property tax bill or Talbot County Sanitary District (sewer) bill.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the eligible county
Must be a homeowner or lease holder of record

Must meet two of the following conditions: (1) receives energy assistance subsidy, (2) receives public assistance, supplemental security income (SSI), or food stamps, (3) receives veterans or social security disability benefits, or (4) meets the income criteria
Taxpayer must be billed the Bay Restoration Fee on either their real property tax bill or sanitary district sewer bill
Must meet hardship qualifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Residential Application form, complete it with required documentation, and submit to the appropriate county. For Calvert County, mail the signed application to Calvert County Government, Attn: County Treasurer, 175 Main Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678. For Talbot County, submit the Bay Restoration Fee Hardship Application to the Finance Office by mail or in person. Contact the respective county office to check application status.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners from underserved communities seeking affordable capital and business support.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Real estate investors and owner-operators seeking to preserve and improve affordable housing while generating financial returns.

structured_extraction.program_name: Greenline Ventures Small Business Capital Fund I
structured_extraction.program_description: A $20 million loan fund that provides loans at favorable or better-than-market rates to underserved small businesses in distressed census tracts. The fund leverages New Markets Tax Credits with mission-driven capital to offer flexible and patient financing for working capital, business growth and expansion, equipment financing, and business acquisition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $250,000 to $2 million with flexible terms from 12 months up to 7 years. The fund provides flexible collateral, security requirements, amortization, recourse, covenants, and interest rates/fees tailored to borrower needs. Loans can be used for working capital, business growth and expansion capital, equipment financing, and business acquisition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Underserved small businesses in distressed census tracts seeking working capital, growth capital, equipment financing, or acquisition financing. The program targets businesses that benefit economically struggling communities and low-wage workers, with emphasis on minority and women-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, business growth and expansion capital, equipment financing, business acquisition, and general business operational needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the United States in distressed census tracts. The program serves all 50 states, Washington D.C., U.S. territories, and Indian Country, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Located in a distressed census tract
Underserved small business

Objectives include job creation and retention, worker training, improving employee benefits, boosting minority or women-owned businesses, reducing environmental impacts, or assisting low-income workers
Small business status required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact Greenline Ventures directly through their website at greenlineventures.com or through Calvert Impact Capital, which serves as the administrative agent for the fund.

structured_extraction.program_name: Greenline Ventures Small Business Capital Fund II

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below market-rate loans for small businesses to support working capital, business growth and expansion, business acquisition, and equipment financing. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans provided with flexible terms including collateral, security requirements, amortization, recourse, covenants, and interest rates/fees tailored to small business needs. Underserved status
Alignment with impact objectives including job creation, training programs, minority or women ownership, or environmental impact reduction

eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Long-term, fixed-rate, non-recourse financing up to 25% of the capital stack for energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy installations, and building modernization. Repayment terms range from 20 to 30 years. PACE Equity provides end-to-end execution through its Fast Track Funding process, which includes in-house energy engineering expertise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and developers in commercial, multifamily, senior housing, hospitality, and retail sectors looking to finance energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy installations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including HVAC, lighting, windows, roofing, and seismic support, as well as renewable energy such as solar installations. Funds support building modernization, redevelopment, and ground-up new construction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across North America, including the United States in the following states: Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Texas, Utah, Virginia, and Wisconsin.
requirements_list: Commercial building ownership or development project
Energy efficiency or renewable energy improvements planned
Project feasibility for financing up to 25% of capital stack
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through PACE Equity directly. The company offers a Fast Track Funding process that leverages in-house energy engineering expertise to optimize funding potential.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $150 million fund and partnership of local and national community finance organizations designed to support the recovery of small businesses and nonprofits through access to flexible, affordable capital and free business support services across the South and Southeast. The program provides flexible, affordable business loans with low interest rates (below 5%), quick approval process, no collateral required, and interest-only payments for the first year. The fund provides loans of up to $100,000 through a network of Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), along with free business support services and advisory assistance. The program expanded access to credit for un- and under-banked small businesses and is focused on historically underbanked communities, particularly those owned by women and under-represented racial and ethnic groups.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible, affordable loans of up to $100,000 provided through a network of Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) with low interest rates (below 5%), quick approval process, no collateral required, and interest-only payments for the first year. Applicants receive free business support services and advisory support from their matched lender. The program provides working capital, business operations funding, marketing, equipment purchases, inventory, hiring and employee compensation, and business expansion for small businesses and nonprofits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application portal scheduled to open in April
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofits with fewer than 50 full-time employees in historically underbanked communities, particularly those owned by women, BIPOC entrepreneurs (77% of recipients are BIPOC), and under-represented racial and ethnic groups, that have been historically underbanked or struggle to access capital from traditional sources. Includes first-time business borrowers (81% had never applied online for business loans).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business recovery, working capital, general operating capital, marketing (66%), hiring more staff (59%), equipment and machinery purchase (25%), inventory purchase (23%), building acquisition/improvements, and business expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through 16 Southern states with loans distributed through 12 Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs): Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Fewer than 50 full-time employees
Small business or nonprofit status
Historically underbanked or limited access to traditional capital
Located in an eligible state
No collateral required to qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants register their interest at www.TheSoarFund.org and will be notified when the application portal opens. Once live, applicants complete an online application through the SOAR webpage followed by application with matched CDFI lenders who will assist with the application and provide advisory support. CDFI agents spend time with applicants throughout the process.

Investments are made through partnerships with microfinance institutions and community development financial institutions (CDFIs).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizations and projects that create opportunities for women around the world
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Global focus; organizations and projects worldwide are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can invest in WIN-WIN through Calvert Impact. Organizations seeking funding should contact Calvert Impact directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development program that connects high school students with local manufacturers and technical/industrial employers. Students learn about manufacturing career opportunities, tour local plants, interact with engineering and technical employees, and can apply for internships with participating companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides high school students with facility tours at local manufacturers, career education about manufacturing opportunities, and access to internship positions (half-day during school year or full-time in summer) with participating companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Top pre-engineering and technical high school students at Caroline County high schools who are nominated by teachers and meet attendance requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program facilitates internship opportunities and career education; students gain work experience through internships at manufacturing companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Caroline County high school students at each of the county's high schools.
requirements_list: Nomination by high school teacher
Top pre-engineering or technical student
Must meet attendance requirements
Must demonstrate genuine commitment to future career
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students are nominated by their teachers. Selected students participate in facility tours at local manufacturers, learn about the industry and specific companies, and can then apply for internship positions with participating companies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary subscription program that protects Caroline County residents and businesses from unexpected medical expenses by ensuring that enrolled individuals and businesses will not be charged for emergency ambulance transportation to the hospital. Enrollment fees support Caroline County's emergency medical providers, including eight volunteer fire companies and county paramedics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual subscription plans covering emergency ambulance transportation costs. Individual plans cost $25 per year. Family of two plans cost $45 per year. Family of three or more plans cost $75 per year. Business plans cost $100 per year for up to 5 employees, with each additional employee costing $10 per year. structured_extraction.program_description: State incentive program providing tax credits and tax exemptions to businesses located in designated Enterprise Zones in Caroline County, Maryland. The program encompasses the Federalsburg Enterprise Zone (established 2015, including all three industrial parks, most downtown and commercial areas, and industrial properties just outside Federalsburg town limits) and the North County Enterprise Zone (established 2018, including most commercial and industrial property in Ridgely, Greensboro, and Goldsboro). Businesses in these zones are eligible for two types of tax credits: a general Maryland income tax credit for new employees and a ten-year real property tax credit on improved or expanded properties. The real property tax reduction schedule provides: Years 1-5: 80% reduction, Year 6: 70% reduction, Year 7: 60% reduction, Year 8: 50% reduction, Year 9: 40% reduction, Year 10: 30% reduction, with regular tax rates resuming after Year 10. For the income tax credit, a qualified employee must be hired after the business entity is certified, work at least 35 hours per week, and earn at least $10.88 per hour or 150% of federal minimum wage. Additional credits are available for economically disadvantaged workers. Tax breaks apply only to the increased value from improvements, not existing property value. The State of Maryland reimburses 50% of uncollected tax revenue to local jurisdictions. The program is designed to grow existing businesses, create jobs, revitalize communities, spur development and investment in economically disadvantaged areas, and increase income levels and employment rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tax credit/exemption options: (1) General Maryland Income Tax Credit: $1,000 per qualified new employee hired after certification, who works at least 35 hours per week and earns at least $10.88 per hour or 150% of federal minimum wage; additional credits available for economically disadvantaged workers; minimum 5 newly created positions required; (2) Real Property Tax Credit/Exemption: ten-year credit against county and municipal property taxes on increased assessed value from improvements or expansion. Reduction schedule: 80% for Years 1-5, 70% for Year 6, 60% for Year 7, 50% for Year 8, 40% for Year 9, 30% for Year 10, with regular rates resuming after Year 10. Tax breaks apply only to increased value from improvements, not existing property value. Minimum $100,000 investment required for real property tax credit eligibility. The State of Maryland reimburses 50% of uncollected tax revenue to local jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Caroline County Small Business Loan Program is a revolving loan fund that provides loans to small businesses and agriculture-based businesses in Caroline County, Maryland to help them start, expand, or scale operations, or to close funding gaps after traditional financing has been arranged. The program serves as a funding source for working capital and other business needs that typically cannot be financed through traditional lenders. Maximum loan amounts are $20,000, though most loans are less than $10,000. Funds can be used for equipment, processing machinery, packaging equipment, inventory, marketing, payroll, working capital, and other startup or expansion costs. Loan funds cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimbursement to owners or equity partners, buyout of partners, or payment of delinquent federal, state, or local taxes. Loans must be repaid according to agreed-upon terms through a promissory note to the County Commissioners of Caroline County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A revolving loan fund that provides gap funding loans to small businesses and agriculture-based businesses for business location, expansion, start-up costs, or to close funding gaps after traditional financing has been arranged. Maximum loan amount is $20,000, though most loans are less than $10,000. Applicants specify the loan amount requested and the number of months for repayment. Funds can be used for commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, inventory purchase, machinery or equipment purchase, business start-up costs, up to 12 months of operating capital, equipment, processing machinery, packaging equipment, inventory, marketing, payroll, and working capital. Loan funds cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimbursement to owners or equity partners, buyout of partners, or payment of delinquent federal, state, or local taxes. Loan repayment is required regardless of business standing and is required if the business relocates outside Caroline County. Funds must be repaid with interest according to agreed-upon terms.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds can be used for commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, inventory purchase, machinery or equipment purchase, business start-up costs, up to 12 months of operating capital, equipment, processing machinery, packaging equipment, inventory, marketing, payroll, working capital, and other startup or expansion costs, but cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimbursement to owners or equity partners, buyout of partners, or payment of delinquent federal, state, or local taxes.

The business must demonstrate that the project benefits the county by developing vacant or underutilized property, eliminating blight, or creating permanent full-time jobs. The curriculum emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and real-world applications. Participants receive instruction from renowned business coach Will Holmes and business mentors with expertise in operations, marketing, human resources, law, and accounting. The program includes weekly classroom sessions (Tuesdays 6-9 p.m. via Zoom), one-on-one mentor sessions, weekly assignments, and a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Graduates receive a Certificate of Completion.

Program covers business fundamentals including organizational infrastructure, marketing, accounting, financial management, legal structure, access to capital, leadership, human resources, taxes, and insurance. The program includes weekly classroom sessions, one-on-one mentor sessions, mentorship and collaboration opportunities, weekly assignments, and a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation. Graduates receive a Certificate of Completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps businesses, residentially-based businesses, Internet Service Providers, and non-profit organizations deploy broadband infrastructure and gain access to higher internet speeds throughout Carroll County. The program offers matching reimbursement grants to offset qualified expenses related to broadband infrastructure deployment, internet service costs, and last-mile connections to unserved or underserved areas. Businesses can be home-based. The program leverages Carroll Broadband, a county-owned fiber optic network, and earmarks funding to expand high-speed internet infrastructure. Up to 50% of qualified project expenses are reimbursed, with a cap of $25,000 per approved project and $100,000 per entity or service provider per fiscal year, subject to allocations approved by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners. The program supports expansion of broadband service and achievement of service redundancy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% matching reimbursement of qualified project expenses with a cap of $25,000 per approved project and $100,000 per entity or service provider per fiscal year, dependent on allocations approved by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners. The program earmarks funding to assist businesses, residentially-based businesses, non-profits, and Internet Service Providers. Grant funds help cover capital investment in broadband infrastructure, equipment, and construction to deploy broadband service and making last-mile connections to unserved or underserved areas of the county to provide broadband internet access with a minimum of 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload speeds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, residentially-based businesses, home-based businesses, non-profit organizations, and Internet Service Providers located in or serving Carroll County, Maryland seeking to deploy broadband service, provide internet to their business operations, expand broadband access in underserved or unserved areas, or achieve service redundancy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investment in broadband infrastructure, equipment, and construction; wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service; internet service costs for business operations; and making last-mile connections to meet commercial, industrial, and residential broadband needs in underserved or unserved areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland only, with focus on unserved or underserved areas of the county. Underserved areas lack access to fixed internet with 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload speeds from two or more providers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Grant Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency grant program established by Carroll County to provide one-time working capital assistance to small businesses, sole proprietors, and home-based businesses with disrupted operations due to COVID-19. The program offers grants to help businesses with payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, and other ordinary business operating costs. Multiple phases were released, including Phase 1 ($500,000), Phase 2 ($250,000), and Phase 3 ($93,000 in grants of $1,250 each to approximately 74 additional eligible businesses), with an additional $200,000 allocated for sole proprietors and home-based businesses, totaling approximately $843,000+ designed to assist approximately 674 Carroll County small businesses. Funded by a combination of public and private contributions including Baltimore Gas & Electric. The program provides interim relief to help businesses while they work with banks, insurance providers, and pursue federal and state assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant awards of $1,000 to $1,250 per business to support working capital needs. Phase 1 provided $500,000, Phase 2 provided $250,000, and Phase 3 provided $93,000 in grants. An additional $200,000 was allocated for sole proprietors and home-based businesses. Funds can be used for payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, and other similar expenses that occur in the ordinary course of business operations incurred due to COVID-19 disruptions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on first-come, first-served basis with multiple phases including Phase 1 starting April 7, 2020 at 5:00 PM, Phase 2, and Phase 3 starting April 29, 2020 at 5:00 p.m. until funding exhausted. structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County Workforce Development places youth ages 16-18 in paid summer employment positions with local businesses for a six-week program (typically July through mid-August). Participants—especially those who have never worked or face barriers to employment—gain work experience, professional development, and mentoring across various fields including recreation, retail, human resources, warehouse, technology, office roles, childcare, restaurants, and agriculture. Carroll County Government hires youth participants, handles all paperwork, and covers all wages ($11.75 to $12.50 per hour), employment taxes, and insurance through dedicated grant funding. Participating businesses receive no-cost trained workers while youth engage in paid employment, professional and soft skills development through enrichment days, business panels with community leaders, career assessments, job fairs, mock interviews, and hybrid in-person and virtual soft skills instruction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Carroll County Government covers youth participant wages at $11.75 to $12.50 per hour, employment taxes, and worker insurance for a six-week summer program (typically July through mid-August). Youth participants receive paid employment experience, professional and soft skills development through enrichment days, business leader panels, career assessments, job fairs, mock interviews, and hybrid in-person and virtual instruction. Grant funding supports summer employment placements. Businesses receive no-cost trained youth workers for positions in recreation, retail, childcare, restaurants, office work, farms, and other roles, with youth serving as mentors and temporary staff providers.

Funds support professional development activities, soft skills training, on-site job skills training, classroom instruction in essential workplace skills, and youth participant enrichment during six-week summer employment positions. Businesses use youth workers for positions in recreation, retail, childcare, restaurants, office work, farms, and other sectors.

structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County offers a tax credit to businesses that create new jobs, incentivizing job creation by rewarding businesses that expand or construct facilities and create new full-time positions. Qualifying for-profit businesses that construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet and employ 25 or more new full-time positions within the first 24 months can claim a tax credit against county property taxes on new or expanded property and personal property. New positions must be new to the state, and employees must be paid at least 125% of the Average Weekly Wage as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor (with at least 50% of new positions meeting this wage requirement). The credit amount decreases over six years: 52% of increased property tax for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, and 26% for years five and six. The county economic development team provides guidance on program requirements and assists eligible businesses with the application process.

Businesses must construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet and employ 25 or more new full-time positions within the first 24 months. New positions must be new to the state and at least 50% must be paid at least 125% of the Average Weekly Wage as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor.

For existing buildings, the credit is 75% if improvement costs are more than 25% of the assessed property value, or 50% if costs are 25% or less. For new construction, the credit is 50% if improvement costs for the building's exterior exceed 50% of the property's assessed value. The total credit cannot exceed the total cost of improvements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Cecil Grown Micro Ag Grant Program provides grants to support the growth, diversification, and long-term sustainability of existing and new agricultural businesses in Cecil County. Funding supports capital improvements, value-added production, agritourism infrastructure, strategic marketing, technology adoption, research, and other investments that strengthen the county's agricultural economy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants offered in three tiers: Seed Grants up to $2,500 for small-scale projects, Growth Grants up to $5,000 for operational upgrades and infrastructure improvements, and Impact Grants of $7,500 to $10,000 for higher-impact projects. All awards are cost-reimbursable, meaning awardees must pay project expenses upfront and submit receipts for reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural operators and farmers in Cecil County, Maryland. Existing and new agricultural businesses physically located in Cecil County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production, equipment and capital improvements; value-added processing and product development; agritourism and farm experience infrastructure; strategic marketing and market development; technology innovation and implementation; research, education and pilot projects; climate resiliency and conservation improvements; animal welfare improvements; and business diversification or new enterprise. Funds cannot be used for debt repayment, general operating expenses, staff salaries, vehicles or trailers (unless permanently mounted equipment), land or real estate purchases, or expenses outside the approved project period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland. Programs must be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland and operating there. Projects must not operate outside of Cecil County.
requirements_list: Operate an existing agricultural business (not conceptual or idea-stage)
Be physically located in Cecil County, Maryland
Be actively producing agricultural goods or services
Be able to cover project costs upfront and request reimbursement
Be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal by the stated deadline
All funded projects must be fully completed by May 30, 2026
Submit reimbursement requests with all receipts and required documentation no later than June 15, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a complete application through the County's OpenGov portal by the deadline. Applications must include detailed project budget with vendor information and cost estimates, quotes or estimates for all major purchases, and description of project impact and outcomes. Applications are reviewed by Cecil County Office of Economic Development staff and external reviewers using a standardized scoring rubric. Awardees must pay project expenses upfront, then submit receipts and documentation for reimbursement.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marketing and promotional materials to help promote and identify products grown or raised in Cecil County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate a farm or agricultural business in Cecil County, Maryland. Raw agricultural crops must be grown in Cecil County. Value-added products must use at least 75% inputs grown in Cecil County.
requirements_list: Operate a farm or agricultural business in Cecil County, MD

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax deferral program that allows eligible elderly and permanently disabled homeowners in Cecil County to postpone payment of a portion of their county property taxes. The deferred amount is the increase in county property taxes from year to year, up to a maximum of 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of initial application. No interest is charged on the deferred amount, and the deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property. Deferred taxes must be repaid when the homeowner sells, ceases to occupy the property as principal residence, fails to reapply annually, income exceeds $60,000, or upon the homeowner's death. The deferral is calculated after any Homeowner's Tax Credit is deducted from the tax bill. This applies only to the County portion of property taxes, not State or Town portions. A deferral of County Property Tax is granted under The Annotated Code of Maryland, Tax-Property Article Section 10-204.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners can defer the portion of their Cecil County property taxes that exceeds the prior year's County property taxes. The maximum total deferral cannot exceed 50% of the property's assessed value at the time of initial application. No interest is charged on deferred amounts. Deferred taxes are recorded as a lien against the property. This applies only to the County portion of property taxes, not State or Town portions. Deferred taxes must be repaid when the homeowner sells, ceases to occupy the property as principal residence, fails to reapply annually, income exceeds $60,000, or upon the homeowner's death. The deferral is calculated after any Homeowner's Tax Credit is deducted from the tax bill. Base amount of taxes must be paid to maintain the deferral.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 for first-time applicants; May 1 for renewal/returning applications (Deferral Agreement due by June 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Cecil County residential property owners age 65 or older, or permanently disabled homeowners receiving federal retirement or disability benefits or certified as permanently disabled by a physician, with combined household income not exceeding $60,000 who have lived at their property for at least 5 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Defers payment of Cecil County property taxes that exceed the prior year's tax amount. Only applies to County portion, not State or Town taxes. Maximum deferral is 50% of assessed property value at the time of initial application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland. Applies only to County property taxes, not State or Town portions. Property must be owner-occupied principal residence.
requirements_list: Residential property owner
Lived at property for at least 5 years
Age 65 or older, OR permanently disabled receiving federal retirement/disability benefits, OR permanently disabled as certified by a physician
Combined gross household income does not exceed $60,000
Owner-occupied property (principal residence)
Proof of age and/or disability required
Proof of income required
Must reapply annually
If property co-owned, all owners must sign application
Must continue to occupy the property as principal residence
Must pay the base amount of taxes to maintain the deferral
Cannot exceed 50% of the assessed value of the property as the total deferred amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can download the application form (PDF) from the website, pick up an application at the Cecil County Finance Office (200 Chesapeake Boulevard, Suite 1100, Elkton, MD 21921), or call 410-996-5385 to request an application by mail. Submit completed application with proof of age/disability and proof of income by September 1 (first-time applicants) or May 1 (renewal applicants). Signed Deferral Agreement must be received by June 1 for renewal applicants to be included in July tax bill. The Finance Office will process the application and include the deferral amount on the property tax bill. Applicants must reapply each year to continue receiving the deferral.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil Catalyst is a low-interest loan program designed to encourage small business growth, new investment, business retention, and job creation in Cecil County. The program provides funding to creditworthy businesses and individuals who have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional sources due to limited equity, collateral requirements, or marginal cash flow. The program targets small businesses, including start-ups, and promotes job growth. Loans are offered at Prime Rate plus 2% fixed for up to 5 years, with repayment terms varying by use of funds. For loans exceeding 5 years, the rate adjusts to a new fixed rate based on the Prime Rate on the first day of the 59th month, plus 2%, starting with the 61st monthly payment.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $5,000 to $75,000 (maximum may be increased by the Loan Review Committee with County Executive approval for loans exceeding $75,000). Interest rate is Prime Rate (as published in the Wall Street Journal on the date of application) plus 2% fixed for up to 5 years. For loans exceeding 5 years, the rate adjusts to a new fixed rate based on the Prime Rate on the first day of the 59th month, plus 2%, starting with the 61st monthly payment. Loans may be unsecured or secured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion. All loans require personal guaranty of business principal(s)/owner(s), except limited partners in a limited liability partnership. Repayment terms vary by use: Real Estate up to 10 years with 20-year amortization and balloon payment at month 120, Equipment 3 to 10 years depending on useful life, Working Capital 1 year interest-only with balloon payment at month 12 and option to extend for two additional 1-year periods, Physical Improvements 5 years maximum. One-time non-refundable application fee of $100 plus customary closing costs including title and lien searches, recordation fees, taxes, and legal fees due at settlement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Creditworthy small businesses, startups, and individuals in Cecil County who have difficulty obtaining traditional financing and can demonstrate ability to repay, seeking to grow, invest in their business, retain operations, or create jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Any legitimate business purpose approved by the Loan Review Committee including leasehold improvements, acquisition of real property (must occupy 51% of improvements on the subject parcel), construction, renovation and rehabilitation, machinery and equipment, and working capital (may include loan fees imposed by third-party lenders).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Cecil County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be creditworthy
Applicant must demonstrate acceptable debt-to-income ratio demonstrating ability to repay loan in full
All loans require personal guaranty of business principal(s)/owner(s), except limited partners in limited liability partnerships
For real property acquisition, must occupy 51% of improvements on the subject parcel
Loans may be unsecured or secured at the Loan Review Committee's discretion
Applications reviewed by qualified underwriter selected by Loan Review Committee
For loans exceeding $75,000, must demonstrate capitalization meeting loan underwriting standards
Non-refundable application fee of $100 is required
Borrower pays for all closing costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact the Office of Economic Development at 410-996-6292 or via email to discuss your project. Step 2: Complete the application form and submit it along with required supporting documents via email to the Economic Development Manager. Step 3: The Loan Review Committee will review the loan application package and underwriting decision and subsequently approve or deny the loan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Small Local Business Enterprise Program (SLBE)
structured_extraction.program_description: Charles County's certification program that gives certified local small businesses exclusive access to certain county government procurements under $50,000 and preferences for larger government contracts. The program supports for-profit, independently owned businesses headquartered in Charles County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified SLBE vendors receive exclusive access to county procurements under $50,000 (informal procurements) as long as at least three qualified SLBE firms are available. For formal procurements valued between $50,000 to $500,000, SLBE firms receive cost preferences: up to 10 percent cost advantage over lowest bidder for Invitations to Bid and Requests for Quotation, or up to 10 points for Requests for Proposals. The advantage is prorated based on documented SLBE firm participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, independently owned businesses with headquarters in Charles County, or branch/satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50 percent of annual gross sales or has 50 percent of full-time employees there.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses must meet Maryland Small Business Reserve industry-specific thresholds for gross sales and employees. Program does not provide direct financial assistance but rather preferential access to county procurement opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50 percent of the company's annual gross sales or has 50 percent of its full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business and independently owned (no brokers or subsidiaries)

Have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of annual gross sales or has 50% of full-time equivalent employees in Charles County
Meet Maryland SBR industry specific thresholds for gross sales and employees
Be certified in the State of Maryland's Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program
Be registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must first obtain certification in Maryland's Small Business Reserve Program and register with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA). Then download and submit the Charles County SLBE application to qualify for the program.
