structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application to the Historic Preservation Division for review and approval before signing a contract or starting work. Applications are reviewed by the Historic Preservation Commission on a scheduled basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that allows restaurants in Annapolis to expand outdoor dining into private parking lots they own or lease, or onto sidewalks and streets, with city permits and approvals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city issues permits for restaurants to operate outdoor dining in parking lots, on sidewalks, or on streets. Restaurants pay a $4,228 permit processing fee, which can be paid in full upfront or in two installments of $2,114 each (second payment due two months after application). The permit authorizes seasonal or year-round outdoor dining operations after approval from multiple city departments including Public Works, Fire Marshal's Office, and Planning & Zoning Code Enforcement. Restaurants in historic districts must follow Historic Preservation Commission guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Restaurants in Annapolis that want to expand outdoor dining operations into parking lots, sidewalks, or designated streets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permits for outdoor dining operations in parking lots, sidewalks, or streets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to restaurants located in Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Restaurant must identify the type of outdoor dining (seasonal parking lot, sidewalk cafe, or street cafe)
Must provide a letter from parking lot property owner authorizing use if necessary
Must provide restaurant street address
Must provide pictures of the space and site plan with measurements
Must identify types of barricades proposed for patron protection and provide safety information
Must identify number of impacted parking spaces
Must pay $4,228 permit processing fee or pay in two installments ($2,114 each)
Restaurants in historic districts must adhere to Historic Preservation Commission guidelines
May need tent or temporary structure permit if operating outside historic district

If serving alcohol, must obtain updated Alcoholic Beverage Control Board license and submit letter to the Board with site plan, plan to prevent service to minors, specific dates and hours of operation, and parking lot owner permission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete application with required information including outdoor dining type, property owner letter if needed, restaurant address, photos, site plan, barricade specifications, and number of impacted parking spaces. 2. Pay the $4,228 permit fee (full payment or two installments). 3. Application is routed to Public Works for access safety review, Fire Marshal's Office for emergency vehicle access, Planning & Zoning for operational capacity, Historic Preservation Office for historic district restaurants, and other agencies as needed. 4. After city agencies determine there are no significant objections, the Department of Planning & Zoning issues the parking lot dining permit. 5. Permitted restaurants must provide survey information to the city during the pilot study. 6. Restaurants in historic districts must follow Historic Preservation Commission guidelines. 7. A tent or temporary structure permit may be required before operations begin.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annapolis Recreation and Parks Department AM/PM Child Care
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers before-school and after-school child care programs at select elementary schools in Annapolis. Programs are available at Annapolis, Germantown, Hillsmere, Mills-Parole, and West Annapolis elementary schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care services provided at before-school and after-school times. Before school care costs $120 per month and after school care costs $300 per month for the 2026-2027 school year. A $35 non-refundable registration fee applies. Child care vouchers are accepted. Registration is on a first-come, first-served basis as space allows.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for returning families began April 13, 2026; registration for new families began April 15, 2026. Ongoing registration on first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-age children attending elementary schools in Annapolis during the 2026-2027 school year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Before-school and after-school child care supervision and services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at five elementary schools in Annapolis: Annapolis, Germantown, Hillsmere, Mills-Parole, and West Annapolis.
requirements_list: Children must be attending one of the five participating elementary schools
Registration on first-come, first-served basis as space allows
Child care vouchers accepted with required Child Care Scholarship Program paperwork completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration can be completed online through the secure portal or in person at the Pip Moyer Recreation Center. A $35 non-refundable registration fee is required. Families using child care vouchers must first complete required paperwork through the Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Around Each Corner Youth Poetry Book
structured_extraction.program_description: A youth poetry contest and publication project that invites young people to share poetry about their stories, backgrounds, experiences, lives, and traditions. Selected poems are published in a book celebrating the City of Annapolis's diversity and the creative potential of its youth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants submit poetry for consideration. Selected poems are published in an annual poetry book. The program provides a platform for youth creative expression and publication.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people enrolled in Annapolis educational institutions, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Poetry submissions for publication in an annual book
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College.
requirements_list: Be enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, home school, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College
Submit poem by August 17, 2026 by filling out the poem application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the poem application form online or email poems to rjsmith@annapolis.gov. Applications are accepted from March 5, 2026 to August 17, 2026. Selected poems are published in the Around Each Corner poetry book with a presentation scheduled for October 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program created to support the Police Department and the City by providing a grant to fund a new initiative and harness collective resources of government agencies to reduce crime and enhance public safety through information-sharing, warrant service, prosecutions, targeted enforcement on dangerous offenders, and community outreach programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a grant to fund police initiatives focused on crime reduction and public safety through partnerships with county and state law enforcement agencies, parole and probation, housing authority, state's attorney office, department of juvenile services, health department, and community members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies and law enforcement partners working to reduce crime and enhance public safety in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding a new police initiative focused on crime reduction, information-sharing, warrant service, prosecutions, targeted enforcement, and community outreach programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis, Maryland and surrounding Anne Arundel County through partnerships with County and State law enforcement agencies.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Partnership-based program with participating agencies including County and State law enforcement, Parole and Probation, Annapolis Housing Authority, Anne Arundel County State's Attorney Office, Department of Juvenile Services, Health Department, and community members.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust - Chesapeake Conservation Climate Corps
structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long service program that places Climate Coordinators with host organizations to support climate adaptation and community resilience initiatives. Participants work on implementing climate action plans, researching climate policy, and engaging communities on environmental projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a stipend of $33,280 annually paid bimonthly, health care coverage (if not otherwise covered), 15 professional development trainings, 4 all-cohort project days, 4-10 networking visits, 1 capstone project, 1 grant opportunity, and funding to attend a regional professional conference. The program runs for one year from August 19, 2026 to August 19, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in high school, college, and recent college graduates ages 18-25 seeking experience with climate adaptation and sustainability initiatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participant stipend for a year of full-time service supporting climate adaptation, resilience planning, research on climate policy and legislation, and community engagement on environmental projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland with approximately 50 Corps Members placed at host organizations. The City of Annapolis is hosting one position.
requirements_list: Age 18-25 at the start of the program
U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, or documentation confirming permission to work in the U.S. during the year-long term of service
Applicants interested in working with the City of Annapolis should indicate this during the application process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should visit the Chesapeake Climate Corps application portal and indicate during the application process if they are interested in working with the City of Annapolis.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis Housing Rehabilitation Program provides forgiveness loans to eligible homeowners for home improvements performed by licensed contractors. Assistance is provided in the form of home improvement work at no cost unless the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home improvement work performed by a licensed contractor at no cost to the homeowner up to a maximum of $30,000 per household. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years, the homeowner must repay the full amount within 11 years. After the 11th year, the loan is reduced by 20% per year for five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied homeowners in Annapolis with household income less than 60% of Area Median Income
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom remodeling
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis, Maryland only
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
Combined household income less than 60% of Area Median Income
Property must be resident's sole and principal residence
Proof of income for all people living in the home
Proof of homeownership
Proof of homeowners insurance
Proof that mortgage payments are up to date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Property Rehabilitation Program pre-application and mail it to Arundel Community Development Services, Inc., 2666 Riva Road, Suite 210, Annapolis, MD 21401

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps low and moderate-income households in Annapolis pay rent, security deposits, and utility bills to stabilize housing, prevent eviction, prevent utility shutoffs, and provide security deposit assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct financial assistance to help pay rent and utility bills. Approved funding amounts are based on the applicant's qualifications. Payments are made directly to the landlord or utility company. Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate-income renters living in Annapolis who are at risk of homelessness or housing instability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent, unpaid utility bills, and security deposits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be living in the City of Annapolis and renting in a household with a current and valid City rental license.
requirements_list: Living in the City of Annapolis
Income at or below 80% AMI (Area Median Income)
Demonstrate risk of homelessness or housing instability with past due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, or other evidence
Holds a lease or sublease in applicant's name
Employed or employed within the last 90 days or retired
Renting in a household with current and valid City rental license
Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due
Must provide verification of household income (W-2, pay stubs, tax returns, bank statements, or proof of retirement)
Must provide rental/lease agreement or sublease
Must provide photo ID for all adult household members
Must provide at least one of: eviction notice or landlord correspondence indicating arrears, or unpaid utility bill or utility shut-off notice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application at the provided survey link. Provide household information and income details. Submit required supporting documentation including income verification, lease agreement, photo ID, and evidence of housing instability. Application processing can take 4-6 weeks. Applicants can also apply in person at the Robinwood Community Services office or request assistance by contacting the Office of Community Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers low-interest loans to help property owners in the downtown Historic District pay for fire sprinkler system retrofits on their buildings.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 5-year loans at 1% annual percentage rate (APR) for fire sprinkler retrofits. Loan amounts up to $25,000, available until the annual allocation of the fund is exhausted. Priority given to those proposing residential use in upper floors and those utilizing a certified minority contractor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted until annual fund allocation is exhausted; fire sprinkler installation must be completed by April 6, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with buildings located on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District who are required to install fire sprinkler systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fire sprinkler system retrofits for buildings in the downtown Historic District
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District with a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection
requirements_list: Property must be located on Main Street or Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District
Property must have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection
Licensed contractor must create a sprinkler retrofit plan for the building
Building permit must be obtained before work commences
Fire sprinkler system must comply with National Fire Protection Association Standard 13
Completed application must be reviewed by the Finance Office, Fire Marshal, and City Office of Law
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Have a licensed contractor create a plan for the building sprinkler retrofit by going to Maryland OneStop. 2. Complete the online loan application (scan the QR code or use keyword 'sprinkler loan' at www.annapolis.gov). 3. The Finance Office reviews the application and shares it with the Fire Marshal who consults with the permit office and signs off. 4. The City Office of Law draws up a contract. 5. Once the contract is completed and building permits are issued, payment is disbursed as a check to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free trees distributed to Annapolis residents in partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation. The program includes an online mapping tool to help identify the best locations for planting trees in yards based on cooling, energy, and money-saving benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees provided to residents. Registration includes access to a research-based online mapping tool that calculates optimal tree planting locations for maximum cooling, energy savings, and financial benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Annapolis residents interested in receiving free trees and using mapping technology to optimize planting locations for maximum environmental and financial benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free trees for planting in residential yards to increase cooling, reduce energy costs, and provide financial savings benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis residents only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration opens September 15. Residents enter simple information about their home and yard into an online mapping tool to identify the best planting location, then receive free trees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides grants to support community development projects and initiatives in eligible areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provides funds to help low-income homeowners make repairs to their homes and provides social services to organizations that serve low-income populations in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to low-income homeowners for home repairs and to social service organizations serving low-income populations in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners and social service organizations serving low-income populations in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs for low-income homeowners and social services for low-income populations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only.
requirements_list: Must be low-income homeowner or social service organization serving low-income populations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City facilitates an annual CDBG application process for federal funds. Public hearings are held to gather input on the allocation of CDBG funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that provides financial incentives for residents and lawn care businesses to transition from gas-powered leaf blowers to electric models. Residents receive up to $100 in rebates, while landscape and lawn care businesses receive up to $1,500.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates up to $1,500 for lawn care and landscape businesses and up to $100 for residents to purchase electric leaf blowers. Applicants must fill out an application, provide proof of residency, and proof of purchase to receive the rebate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and lawn care and landscape businesses operating in the city
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf blowers to replace gas-powered models
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within the City of Annapolis limits only
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Annapolis or a lawn care and landscape business operating in Annapolis
Must provide proof of residency
Must provide proof of purchase of an electric leaf blower
Must complete a rebate application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants fill out an application online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website, provide proof of residency, and submit proof of purchase to receive the rebate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides operating and capital grants to non-profit organizations that meet city priorities. Operating grants support day-to-day costs of running the organization. Capital grants support the purchase of property, construction, remodeling or expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides operating grants to support day-to-day costs and capital grants to support purchase of property, construction, remodeling, expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment. Funding is subject to availability and prioritizes organizations demonstrating impact, collaboration, and diverse funding sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving Annapolis residents that align with city priorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs for day-to-day operations, or capital costs including purchase of property, construction, remodeling, expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be serving Annapolis residents. Organizations must demonstrate that at least 75 percent of programming and work benefits and engages City residents.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt non-profit organization
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have administrative and financial capacity to carry out the project successfully
Must provide maximum public benefit in relation to cost
Must demonstrate ability to leverage additional funds

Must clearly demonstrate one or more of the four city priorities: sustaining and empowering youth, families and individuals; preserving and enhancing community character; contributing to vibrant economy; or promoting community revitalization, economic development and environmental sustainability
Must show strong collaboration with community members, local churches, schools, or other organizations
Must demonstrate that at least 75 percent of programming and work benefits and engages City residents
Must have diverse funding sources outside city funding
Past grant recipients must show consistency with grant reporting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed FY 2027 Community Grant Application form. Required documents include: copy of last audit or financial statements (or most recent IRS Form 990 if audited financials unavailable), organization budget for current year, Board of Directors list with addresses and phone numbers, copy of IRS determination letter showing 501(c)(3) status, Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, copy of most recent annual report if applicable, Memorandum of Understanding or support letters if applicable, and summary of City support over the previous year. Applications must be submitted by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Annapolis Children and Families Success Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program supporting community-based organizations to open, expand, and enhance child care and youth development programs in Annapolis. Funds programs that provide structured activities for youth including recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, enrichment, and life skill building, with a focus on serving low-income families and youth from underserved neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per organization for implementing child care and youth development programs. A minimum of five organizations will be funded. First 75% of funds disbursed in the week of August 25th following contract execution. Remaining 25% disbursed upon completion and final reporting.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Iesha Young, Manager, Office of Community Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations with 501(c)3 status or for-profit businesses providing scholarships or free programs serving low-income youth and families in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support opening, expanding, or enhancing child care and youth development programs providing structured activities for youth ages not specified, including enrichment, recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, and life skill building. Funds are not intended to cover general operational expenses beyond what is necessary for successful project implementation and evaluation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be provided at a physical location within Annapolis, with preference for programs in low-income neighborhoods and projects run by community leaders.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)3 status or be a for-profit business
Programs must provide scholarships or free activities to participants
Physical program location must be within Annapolis
Programs must provide structured activities for youth with adult oversight
Grantees must submit mid-program and final reports
Grantees must participate in three meetings with Office of Community Services staff
Applications must be completed through the online portal or approved for paper submission
All application sections and questions must be completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application through the online application portal. If unable to use the portal, contact Iesha Young for approval to submit paper application at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email to communityservices@annapolis.gov. Applications open June 16th and close July 25th at 4:30pm. Grant decisions will be made by August 8th, award letters sent by August 13th via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Food Friday is a community assistance program providing food support to food-insecure individuals and families in the City of Annapolis. The program distributes weekly boxes filled with fresh and canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods to combat food insecurity and ensure access to essentials for a healthy life. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian dietary needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each week, participants receive a box filled with fresh and canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian dietary needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food-insecure individuals and families who live in the City of Annapolis and are currently facing hardship and need assistance with food.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and non-perishable foods to address food insecurity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to residents of the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Must live in the City of Annapolis
Must be currently facing hardship and in need of food assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can sign up for their Food Friday box through an online application form available on the city website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Front Yard and Street Tree Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Free trees provided to Annapolis residents and property owners who request them for planting in front yards or the public right-of-way. City contractors plant the trees at no cost, and applicants agree to care for the trees for the first three years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tree(s) planted by city contractors at no cost to the applicant. Applicants must agree to water and care for the tree for the first three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents or property owners interested in greening their neighborhood and supporting urban forest growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free trees for planting in front yards or public right-of-way to increase the urban forest, improve air quality, reduce stormwater runoff, and provide shade and cooling benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a City of Annapolis resident or property owner with a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way or front yard.
requirements_list: Be a City of Annapolis resident or property owner
Have a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb) or in the front yard
Agree to water and care for the tree for the first 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online web form to request a tree or trees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer effort that encourages individuals and organizations to plant and maintain flower and vegetable gardens in public spaces throughout the City of Annapolis. The City provides plant materials, mulch, trash bags and gloves, and community members volunteer to plant, clean up, and beautify the town.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides plant materials, mulch, trash bags, and gloves to volunteers. Volunteers organize and execute community gardening and beautification projects on public property throughout Annapolis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and organizations of all ages who want to volunteer to beautify public spaces in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting and maintaining flower and vegetable gardens, litter and trash pick-up, and planting trees in public spaces throughout the City of Annapolis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on public property in the City of Annapolis and require permission from the property owner.
requirements_list: Project site must be located on public property in the City of Annapolis
Must receive permission from the property owner
Must attend an organizational meeting
Must complete and submit a material order form by March 4
Must recruit volunteers to assist with project activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend an organizational meeting (February 4 or March 4 at 6 p.m. at Pip Moyer Recreation Center) for ideas and resources. Select a neighborhood or community project site on public property with owner permission. Complete and submit the material order form by March 4. Recruit volunteers to help with preparation, planting, and year-round maintenance. Pick up plant materials on April 24 at Truxtun Park Pool. Participate in the annual GreenScape planting day (April 25, 2026) and maintain the project year-round.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Repair - Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County provides home repairs for qualifying county homeowners in need using Community Development Block Grant dollars. The program can assist with most types of repair needs and provides up to $10,000 worth of home repairs at no cost to qualified applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 worth of home repairs provided at no cost to the homeowner
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied homeowners in Annapolis with household income less than 50% of Area Median Income who demonstrate a legitimate repair need
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Most types of home repair needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis, Maryland
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
All persons on deed must reside in the home needing repair
Combined household income less than 50% of Area Median Income
Demonstrate a legitimate repair need
Unable to perform the work themselves
Owned home for more than 2 years
Plan to reside in the home for at least two years after repairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Home Repairs and mail it to Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County, 819 Ritchie Hwy, Suite 2000, Severna Park, MD 21146

structured_extraction.program_name: Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for the installation of fire sprinkler systems on properties in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for installation of fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Annapolis who install fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit Application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides down payment and closing cost assistance to homebuyers purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) home in the City of Annapolis. The program offers up to $10,000 in assistance through a zero-percent interest loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Annapolis provides up to $10,000 as a zero-percent interest loan for down payment and closing costs on MPDU home purchases. No payments are required until the property is sold or transferred, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property through a Deed of Trust. Borrowers must contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from their own funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers with an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility who have completed HUD-certified homeownership counseling and are prequalified by a lender.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for the purchase of an MPDU home in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Must be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program
Must be prequalified by a participating lender or a lender of your choice
Must contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from own funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MPDU Eligibility Certificate Holders receive application information in their Home Buyer Packet when the City notifies them of MPDU availability. Applicants can also contact the Office of Community Development at 410-263-7961, ext. 7727 for information and application materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A city-funded tree planting program designed to restore the City of Annapolis's forest canopy and help achieve 50% urban tree canopy by 2050. The program plants trees at homes, congregations, businesses, schools, and across various communities throughout Annapolis. The program relies on volunteer community leaders trained through the Tree Trooper program to help identify properties needing trees and oversee tree planting projects. From September 2023 to December 2025, the program planted 380 trees across various communities. Participants receive free training through the Tree Trooper program consisting of 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free tree planting services at eligible properties including homes, congregations, businesses, schools, and across neighborhoods and communities in Annapolis. Trees are provided and planted at no cost to property owners and communities. City-funded tree planting projects are implemented across neighborhoods. Participants interested in becoming Tree Trooper volunteers receive free training consisting of 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, congregations, businesses, schools, and communities in Annapolis seeking to restore forest canopy. City of Annapolis residents and communities. Community volunteers interested in becoming Tree Troopers to help coordinate tree planting projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting at homes, congregations, businesses, schools, and across communities to restore the City of Annapolis's forest canopy and increase urban tree canopy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to properties and projects within the City of Annapolis, Maryland. Some communities qualify for free trees based on eligibility determined by Chesapeake Bay Foundation's Urban Tree Grant Eligibility Map.
requirements_list: Must be located within the City of Annapolis
Properties must be identified as needing trees
Projects located within City of Annapolis
Complete interest form via QR code or aawsa.org/replant
Property must be in eligible community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To become a Tree Trooper volunteer, visit the website (aawsa.org/tree-trooper) and fill out the interest form under 'Become a Tree Trooper'. Training includes 4 virtual sessions and one in-person planting event in the fall. Property owners and communities can fill out interest form by scanning QR code or visiting aawsa.org/replant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reduced Transit Fare Program for Persons With Disabilities, Seniors and Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A program offering reduced fares on Annapolis Transit fixed-route bus services for people with disabilities, senior citizens age 60 and over, Medicare cardholders, and students. Qualified individuals pay one-half of the regular fare on regular bus service and passes. Students living within the City of Annapolis ride free during school months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified individuals pay one-half of the regular fare on any regularly scheduled fixed-route bus at a bus stop. Reduced fares apply to single trips and to passes (day, weekly, monthly, and annual passes). Students living within the City of Annapolis receive free rides during school months. Reduced fares do not apply to curb-to-curb ADA Complementary Paratransit service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities, senior citizens age 60 and over, Medicare cardholders, and students enrolled in schools or colleges within the Annapolis Transit service area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public transit fares for fixed-route bus service in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis Transit service area within the City of Annapolis. Students living outside the City of Annapolis but within the Annapolis Transit service area are also eligible.
requirements_list: Show valid photo identification at bus stop

For people with disabilities: Annapolis Transit Reduced Fare Photo ID Card, ADA Complementary Paratransit Photo ID Card, Disability ID from another transit agency with government photo ID, or other qualifying government ID
For seniors (60+): Government-issued photo ID showing age 60 or over, Maryland Photo ID Card, or Medicare card (if under 60) with government photo ID

For students: Valid school-issued photo identification with name, address, gender, school name, and issue date. Student must be enrolled in parochial, private, public school, college, or Naval Academy within Annapolis Transit service area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for an Annapolis Transit Reduced Fare Photo Identification Card for persons with disabilities, submit the Application for Reduced Transit Fare Identification Card for Persons with Disabilities. To apply for ADA Paratransit Service, submit the ADA Paratransit Service Application. Students present valid school-issued photo ID when boarding. Seniors can apply for a no-cost Maryland Photo ID at any Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides assistance to individuals suffering from addiction and substance abuse by allowing them to voluntarily go to any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County Police or Fire Station to request help. The Mobile Crisis Response Team evaluates individuals and determines the appropriate treatment path.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individuals can go to any Annapolis or Anne Arundel County Police or Fire Station and request assistance. Public Safety Officers assess medical needs and contact the Mobile Crisis Response Team (MCRT). The MCRT evaluates the individual and determines the treatment path. If medical transport is needed, the person is transported to the hospital where the MCRT meets them. The program is available to local residents suffering from any form of addiction or substance abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local residents suffering from addiction or substance abuse
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Substance abuse treatment and crisis response services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals in Annapolis and Anne Arundel County at designated Police and Fire Stations
requirements_list: Must be a local resident
Must be seeking assistance for addiction or substance abuse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Go to the nearest firehouse or police station in Annapolis or Anne Arundel County, ring the doorbell, and ask for a Safe Station. Public Safety Officers will assess medical needs and connect individuals with the Mobile Crisis Response Team for evaluation and treatment determination.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Annapolis Fire Department offers CPR and First Aid training courses to the general public for a nominal fee. Individuals, groups, and businesses can participate in these training classes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CPR and First Aid training courses offered for a nominal fee to individuals, groups, and businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: General public, including individuals, groups, and businesses interested in CPR and First Aid certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CPR and First Aid training and certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the City of Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals, groups, or businesses can fill out the form on the Save a Life CPR Class page or email the instructors at CPR@annapolis.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan and grant program administered by the City of Annapolis Community Development Division to help eligible homeowners address major systems deficiencies and correct hazardous conditions that may endanger the health and welfare of occupants. The program provides rehabilitation assistance to low and moderate income homeowners to ensure their homes are safe, healthy, and habitable. Loans and grants are budgeted by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and are available to eligible homeowners in Annapolis. Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. can assist in determining eligibility and processing applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans and grants provided to eligible homeowners for addressing major systems deficiencies and correcting hazardous conditions that may endanger the health and welfare of occupants. Various loans and grants are budgeted by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Assistance is available to low and moderate income homeowners to make their homes safe, healthy, and habitable.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Denise J. Ruffin, Housing Affordability Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income homeowners in Annapolis with major home systems deficiencies or hazardous conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home rehabilitation, repairs, and correcting major systems deficiencies and hazardous conditions in residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner
Must be low or moderate income homeowner
Must be City of Annapolis resident
Must meet eligibility criteria as determined by the City of Annapolis Office of Community Development
Must be an eligible homeowner
Must meet eligibility criteria as determined by Arundel Community Development Services, Inc.
Property must have major systems deficiencies or hazardous conditions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the City of Annapolis Office of Community Development. Contact the Housing Affordability Specialist to determine eligibility and begin the application process. Arundel Community Development Services, Inc. can also assist in determining eligibility and processing applications at 410-222-7600.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Special Assistance Roster is a registry that helps the City identify and coordinate assistance for vulnerable residents during emergencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sprinkler and Electrical Cost Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An assistance program administered by the City of Annapolis that helps cover the costs of installing or upgrading sprinkler and electrical systems for property owners and businesses in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help cover the costs of sprinkler and electrical system installation or upgrades.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses in Annapolis needing sprinkler or electrical system assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or upgrade of sprinkler and electrical systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Annapolis, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Finance Department or submit the Sprinkler and Electrical Cost Assistance Program form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteers in At-Risk Communities - Boots on the Ground Community Engagement Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds community-based organizations to work in at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis through hands-on outreach, engagement, and relationship building. Organizations develop programs that build resilient, empowered communities through trauma-informed programming, mentorship, mental health support, and community engagement strategies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $200,000 in total one-time grant awards available. Each organization receives a maximum of $20,000. Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood. Funding period is September 2023 through June 30, 2024. A maximum of 10% of funds may be used for overhead costs. All other funds must be used for community engagement programming, mentorship, mental health services, trauma-informed approaches, and relationship-building activities. Allowable costs include personnel, travel, meals & incidental expenses (M&IE) per GSA rates, electronic equipment up to $1,200, and volunteer stipends/incentives tied to program outcomes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - application will remain open until funds are used
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations with 501(c)(3) status working in designated at-risk neighborhoods in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentorship programs, mental health services and counseling, trauma-informed programming, community engagement and dialogue, neighborhood-targeted outreach, activities that build community ownership and resilience, destigmatizing practices, services connecting residents to needed resources, personnel costs, travel expenses, meals & incidental expenses per GSA rates, electronic equipment (laptops, computers, tablets, printers) up to $1,200, and volunteer stipends/incentives directly tied to program outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Annapolis city limits. Organizations must target one specific Annapolis neighborhood from the following list: Bay Ridge Gardens, Harbour House/Eastport Terrace, Madison Apartments, Bywater, Robinwood, Annapolis Gardens, Admiral Oaks, Clay Street/Obery Court/College Creek Apartments, Woodside, Parole, Allen Apartments, Admiral Farragut, Quiet Waters, or Watergate Village.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)(3) status
Must focus on one specific Annapolis neighborhood
Must include one-on-one contact with residents in the target community
Must use a trauma-informed approach
Must demonstrate community needs assessment
Must include a practical work plan with timeline, objectives, dates, and logistics
Must include SMARTIE goals and objectives
Must include performance measures and expected outcomes
Must submit itemized budget proposal with all funds explained
Must attend quarterly meetings with City staff
Must submit reports at mid-grant and end of grant period
Cannot focus on one-time engagement projects
Cannot organize only pop-up events
Cannot conduct projects outside Annapolis limits
Cannot focus on more than one Annapolis neighborhood
Electronic equipment costs must align with staff Level of Effort (LOE) percentage
Equipment funding must be proportional to staff assigned to project
Volunteer stipends must be directly tied to program outcomes
Stipend payments must follow documented schedule and frequency
M&IE rates must follow GSA per diem standards
Justify any cost-sharing arrangements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all parts and questions in the online application portal at https://arcg.is/1XSnbT. If unable to submit through the portal, contact communityservices@annapolis.gov for approval to submit a paper application at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email. Submit a completed itemized budget proposal using the provided template or applicant's own template. Include application questions document responses. All applications must be complete to be deemed fundable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship fund that offsets the cost of program registration fees for eligible participants in the Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funds cover either 100% or 50% of program registration fees depending on income level. Families with Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) at or below 300% of the federal poverty line receive 100% coverage. Families with AGI between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line receive 50% coverage. Funds are distributed as available and are not guaranteed for all programs at all times.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Participants in the Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program registration fees for Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a Rectrac account (set up at www.playfrederick.com)
Must complete the Participant Questionnaire including accommodation information
For 100% scholarship: AGI must be 300% or less of the federal poverty line for the most recent tax year
For 50% scholarship: AGI must be between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line for the most recent tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested participants must set up a Rectrac account by visiting www.playfrederick.com, clicking 'register for programs', and creating a new account. Participants must then complete the Participant Questionnaire including accommodation information. Participants must provide AGI (Adjusted Gross Income) information from the most recent tax year to verify income eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program that allows local businesses, community organizations, faith groups, families, and friends to organize cleanups to remove trash from streets and streams in Frederick.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides coordination and support for cleanup groups. Participants can either start a new Adopt-a-Road group by filling out a form, or register as a participant to volunteer with existing groups or be matched with a regular cleanup group.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses, community organizations, faith groups, families, and friends in Frederick who want to volunteer for environmental cleanup.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program support for street and stream cleanup activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To start an Adopt-a-Road group, fill out a form at airtable.com/appXHp5V576mr3YA6/pagvlJolFSyk927v3/form. To volunteer for cleanups, register as a participant at airtable.com/appXHp5V576mr3YA6/pagvtC2enqD7oc6nN/form to volunteer with a group of your choice or be matched with a group.

structured_extraction.program_name: Application for HOA Tree Planting Assistance

structured_extraction.program_name: Art in City Hall Monthly Exhibition
structured_extraction.program_description: A rotating exhibition series that showcases artwork from the City's collection and work by local artists through collaborations with nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups. The program emphasizes inclusivity by highlighting historically underrepresented communities. All exhibitions are free and open to the public and typically remain on display for one to three months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides exhibition space and curatorial support for local artists and organizations to display artwork. Exhibitions are free and open to the public for one to three months.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laila Jadallah, Manager of Arts and Culture
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local artists and organizations seeking exhibition opportunities in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exhibition space to display and promote artwork in City Hall
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Submit art exhibition proposal
Preference for inclusivity and historically underrepresented communities
Proposals do not accept solo artist exhibitions
Priority given to proposals highlighting histories and contributions of historically underserved and underrecognized communities in Frederick
2026 season focus: proposals exploring Frederick's shared future in celebration of the United States' 250th anniversary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a proposal through the Request for Proposals process. Download the RFP document and follow the application instructions. Proposals are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Historic Preservation Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for historic properties in Frederick that undergo qualified preservation and rehabilitation work. Applicants can submit applications through the City of Frederick's online portal or direct submission to the Planning Department.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit available to property owners who rehabilitate or preserve historic properties in Frederick. Tax relief is provided for qualifying historic preservation and rehabilitation projects. Applications can be submitted through the online OpenGov portal or directly to the Planning Department.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief for qualifying historic preservation and rehabilitation projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within the City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be historic and designated or eligible for historic preservation designation
Work must qualify as historic preservation or rehabilitation
Property must undergo eligible rehabilitation or preservation work
Compliance with historic preservation standards required

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department provides community garden plots for City residents to grow fruits and vegetables for personal use. Plots are located at Willow Brook Park and are approximately 25 feet by 50 feet each.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Garden plot rental at Willow Brook Park costs $60 per season (March to November). Each City resident household can rent a maximum of two plots. The rental provides access to an approximately 25 feet by 50 feet plot for growing fruits and vegetables for personal use.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications and renewals for the 2025 season are now closed. No additional plots are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who want to grow fruits and vegetables for personal use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing fruits and vegetables for personal use only; not for commercial sales.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a City of Frederick resident. Program is located at Willow Brook Park, 350 McClellan Drive in the Willow Brook subdivision off Opossumtown Pike.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Maximum of two garden plots per City residence
Plot holder is responsible for all maintenance and upkeep including cultivating, weeding, and watering on a weekly basis
Garden plots must be used for growing fruits and vegetables for personal use only; not for commercial sales
No invasive plants are permitted
No unauthorized expansion of plot into surrounding paths or encroaching on other plots
Plots are subject to inspection by City staff at any time
Plots that become heavily weeded or are not regularly maintained will receive notification to bring plot into compliance within two weeks
Applicant is responsible for updating and maintaining current contact information with the City Parks Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply and pay for your plot via Visa or Mastercard through the online sign-up system. Each year plots are offered for renewals first. Then any available plots are offered to new plot holders. Application must be made by the beginning of each season.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing funding support to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations that create or enhance services benefiting City of Frederick residents. The program awards grants to supplement existing funds for community promotion activities and events that positively impact the greatest number of City residents. Funds are available after July 1 of the fiscal year and will be distributed following completion of a letter of agreement between the City and the organization. Partial award amounts may be given. Applications can be submitted online, by email, mail, or hand delivered to City Hall, and the City reviews applications using a scorecard.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City awards grant funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. Funding is distributed after July 1 of the fiscal year. Separate applications should be submitted for each specific type of community promotion activity or event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit charitable and civic organizations serving City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To create or enhance services and community promotion activities that positively impact City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to nonprofit organizations serving the City of Frederick
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit charitable or civic organization
All applicants must attend one of two mandatory virtual information sessions (December 15, 2025 or January 15, 2026)
Must have reporting up to date if previous funding has been granted
Must submit interim report by January 31, 2027
Must submit final report by July 31, 2027
Organizations may submit separate applications for each specific type of community promotion activity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Program Overview document. 2. Ensure all reporting is current if previously funded. 3. Attend one of two mandatory virtual information sessions (December 15, 2025 at 1:00-2:00 PM or January 15, 2026 at 12:00-1:00 PM). 4. Complete the online application through Foundant. Applications can also be sent by email, mail, or hand delivered to City Hall. Accessibility accommodations and computer/internet access solutions are available upon request. The City reviews applications using a scorecard that is available for review.

structured_extraction.program_description: A weatherization assistance program for homeowners and renters without a working heating or cooling system. Funding for heating upgrades is available during winter months and cooling upgrades during summer months. Provides free HVAC repairs or replacements to restore essential climate control.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded HVAC repairs and tune-ups for households without functioning heating (winter) or cooling (summer) systems. Work is completed at no cost to eligible homeowners and renters. Program prioritizes emergency heating and cooling system upgrades.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Heating funding available in winter months; cooling funding available in summer months
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals currently receiving at least one of the following assistance benefits: Energy Assistance (OHEP), SSI, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, or DHCD Rehab Program, residing in City of Frederick, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency HVAC repairs and services to restore heating or cooling functionality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, MD 21701
requirements_list: Currently receiving at least one of: Energy Assistance (OHEP), SSI, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, or DHCD Rehab Program
Primary residence in City of Frederick, Maryland
Currently without a functioning heating or cooling system
Renters must have landlord permission via signed building owner agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Crisis Program application through the City of Frederick Form Center online portal. Optional account creation available to save progress and auto-populate fields. Email copy of form available upon request. Once approved, HVAC repair or replacement work is scheduled and completed at no cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational initiative providing individualized financial counseling to help clients stabilize and improve their financial well-being. Counselors work with clients to set goals, repair credit, build budgets, and manage income and savings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost individualized financial counseling provided on a one-to-one basis. Counselors assist with goal-setting, credit repair, budgeting, and income and savings management.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial empowerment counseling and financial goal-setting
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick
requirements_list: Desire to stabilize and improve financial well-being
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Financial Coaching Client Intake Packet and contact Steven Rose at (301) 600-2077 or srose@cityoffrederickmd.gov to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Support and guidance for homeowners in default facing foreclosure. Assistance includes filing the Request for Mediation form, gathering necessary documentation, and guidance through the mediation process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost counseling to assist homeowners in default with the foreclosure mediation process. Counselors help file mediation forms, gather necessary information, and may accompany clients to mediation. Assistance with mortgage assistance applications is also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners facing mortgage default or foreclosure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Foreclosure prevention counseling and mortgage default assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Homeowner in default status
Seeking assistance with mediation process
Completion of Mortgage Default Intake Packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default Client Intake Packet and contact the Housing Counselors. Counselors assist with filing Request for Mediation form and preparing for mediation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free curbside composting service provided in partnership with Key City Compost. Residents can dispose of vegetable peels, coffee grounds, food waste, and other compostable materials through a curbside pickup program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides free curbside composting service to residents. Compost bins are provided and residents can sign up online for free pickup service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick City residents interested in composting and reducing waste.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Composting of food waste and organic materials through curbside pickup service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can sign up online at bit.ly/3NfVNWQ. The signup process takes about 2 minutes. After registration, curbside composting pickup service begins.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: State and County tax credits providing decreasing tax abatement on building improvements for 7 years for rehabilitation of existing structures located along Route 40 West (Golden Mile corridor) and in the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District. The program applies to both commercial and mixed-use properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and businesses (for-profit and non-profit) rehabilitating structures in the Golden Mile corridor and downtown arts and entertainment district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax abatement on building improvements for rehabilitated commercial and mixed-use structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the Golden Mile corridor (Route 40 West) and the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District in the City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Rehabilitation of existing structures
Located in eligible area (Route 40 West Golden Mile corridor or Downtown Arts and Entertainment District)
Commercial or mixed-use property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the Golden Mile Tax Credit Application form available from the Planning Department.

Must provide completed budget worksheet at individual consultation

Counselors review leases, discuss security deposit issues, explain rent court processes, and describe eviction procedures. Legal advice is not provided but clients may be referred for legal assistance.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental counseling and tenant-landlord relationship guidance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County only
requirements_list: Landlord or tenant status in Frederick County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing Counselors directly by phone or email to schedule a counseling appointment.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to reduce lead hazards in residential properties, administered through the City of Frederick Community Development Division as part of the DHCD Lead-Hazard Reduction Grant program.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction in residential properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time reduction to water and sewer charges for residential customers whose bills are unusually high due to an interior or exterior leak.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a one-time bill adjustment for water and sewer charges when a residential customer's bill is at least 2x normal usage based on the average of the last three billing cycles. After the leak is repaired and the Water Department confirms normal usage has resumed, the bill is adjusted from the first service day on the protested bill to the first normal reading.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential water and sewer customers in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of water and sewer charges for bills resulting from leaks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland only. Program is open to residential customers but not to apartments, condominiums, or multi-family structures served by one meter.
requirements_list: Must be a residential customer of the City of Frederick
Water and sewer bill must be at least 2x normal usage based on the average of the last three billing cycles
Must not be an apartment, condominium, or multi-family structure served by one meter
Leak must be repaired
Water Department must confirm normal usage has resumed after repairs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Utility Billing at 301-600-1421. The Water and Sewer Finance Team will instruct the resident to have the leak repaired and/or coordinate with the Water Department to inspect the property. Once repaired, the Water Department performs two readings to ensure usage has returned to normal. After confirmation, the bill is adjusted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Counseling for homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments. Housing counselors help determine the best course of action to protect home investment and credit rating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost counseling provided to homeowners currently delinquent on mortgage payments. Counselors assess options and help clients determine the best course of action to address delinquency and protect credit rating.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mortgage default counseling and guidance

Homeowner status
Completion of intake packet
Documentation of mortgage default or risk of default
Residency in City of Frederick

structured_extraction.program_name: Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) (City of Frederick)
structured_extraction.program_description: Assists Frederick County residents with paying heating and electric bills through grants that do not need to be repaid. Grant amounts vary based on income level and fuel type.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-repayable grants to help pay heating and electric bills. Grant amounts vary based on household income level and fuel type used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County residents who need assistance paying heating and electric bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heating and electric bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: OHEP serves Frederick County residents only.
requirements_list: Completed and signed application listing all household members
Copy of photo ID for the applicant
Copy of Social Security Cards for everyone in the home
Proof of income for 30 days for all household members (includes unemployment, Social Security, etc.)
Proof of residency (lease or mortgage statement)
Copy of electric and heating bills
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be completed online at https://myohepstatus.mymdthink.maryland.gov/, printed from dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/, or completed using the PDF application form. Paper applications can be mailed to PO Box 3929 Frederick, MD 21705, emailed to ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov, or dropped off at 420 East Patrick Street lobby.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reimbursable grants that support the LGBTQ+ community in Frederick during Pride Month 2026. Funding is available to community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants distributed after July 1, 2026. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting LGBTQ+ pride events that promote visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick during June 2026
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events must be hosted in June 2026 in the City of Frederick
requirements_list: Host an event in June 2026 that promotes visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick
Submit an event budget and project budget
Submit final report by December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the online portal at the grant interface portal. Requests received via email, phone, or direct mail will not be reviewed. Applications close on May 1, 2026. Funds are distributed after July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program enables eligible youth under age 18 to receive 50% off all youth programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible youth receive 50% off the registration fees for all youth programs operated by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth under age 18 who live in the City of Frederick and meet one of the three eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration fees for youth programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland. Proof of city residency is required.
requirements_list: Must be under age 18
Must be a resident of the City of Frederick

Must meet one of three eligibility criteria: (1) eligible to receive free or reduced-price lunch through Frederick County Public Schools, (2) live in household receiving benefits from Food Supplement Program (FSP) or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or (3) live in one of three public housing communities (Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village) owned by the Housing Authority of the City of Frederick
Must provide proof of city residency (driver's license, MVA-issued ID, water bill, or electric bill)
If using free or reduced lunch eligibility, must provide letter from FCPS
If using FSP or TCA benefits, must provide orange Independence Card from Frederick County Department of Social Services
If using public housing eligibility, must provide proof of residency in Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register at the Wm. Talley Recreation Center Registration Desk located at 121 North Bentz Street, Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 6:30 pm. Must provide proof of eligibility and city residency. Once eligibility is approved, households may register online, in person, or by phone and the fee reduction automatically applies.

structured_extraction.program_description: HUD-required comprehensive counseling for senior homeowners considering a reverse mortgage (Home Equity Conversion Mortgage). Counselors help seniors understand how reverse mortgages work, explore alternative options, and answer questions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual appointment-based HUD-required comprehensive reverse mortgage counseling. Fee is $100 and may be waived based on income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners age 62 and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reverse mortgage counseling and education

Homeowner status
Completion of intake packet
