structured_extraction.program_description: A $700,000 emergency relief program that provides one-time, flexible bridge funding to eligible local nonprofits who sustain critical services and serve Frederick's most vulnerable residents. The program addresses significant disruptions in funding for nonprofits that deliver life-sustaining services including food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, and mental health care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 per award. One-time, flexible bridge funding (non-renewable). Funds must be used to support community needs or essential services in areas such as food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, and mental health care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing (including 501(c)(3) and other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects) that operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting community needs or essential services. Nonprofits must demonstrate how funds were used through reporting requirements including a summary of fund use, basic financial breakdown, and snapshot of service impact.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves the City of Frederick. Applicants must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
requirements_list: Be a nonprofit organization in good standing, including 501(c)(3), other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects
Operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents
Deliver programs that support community needs or essential services
Have experienced a loss in state or federally funded grants and/or subgrants that disrupted program timelines or operations
Have lost a previously reliable funding source due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes
Demonstrate an increased demand for services compared to the same time last year due to specific federal cuts within a similar or adjacent service
Priority given to applicants who demonstrate a loss in state or federally funded grants that have disrupted program timelines or operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create an account on the City's application portal or log in if you have an existing account. Ensure all reporting is up to date if you have received previous funding from the City. Starting October 15, 2025, eligible organizations can apply through the online portal on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local tax credit supplement for senior homeowners in Frederick, Maryland. The City of Frederick supplements the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program for eligible seniors who meet income and age requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A supplemental tax credit for homeowners. When a City taxpayer files for the State credit, the State determines if the taxpayer is eligible for the City supplement and processes both credits together. The specific credit amount is not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior homeowners in Frederick who are at least 70 years old with combined gross income of $40,000 or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to homeowners' tax liability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners in the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Must be at least 70 years old as of the end of the calendar year preceding the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Must have combined gross income of $40,000 or less
Must own or have a legal interest in the property

The dwelling must be your principal residence where you live at least six months of the year, including July 1 (unless you are a recent home purchaser or unable to do so because of health or need of special care)
Net worth, not including the value of the property or any qualified retirement savings or Individual Retirement Accounts, must be less than $200,000
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $60,000 (State requirement)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program. The State will determine if you are eligible for the City supplement tax credit and process both credits together.

structured_extraction.program_description: Interest-free loan program funded by the City of Frederick's Community Development Block Grant that provides down payment and closing cost assistance for first-time homebuyers purchasing homes in Frederick. Borrowers can access up to $25,000 with no payments required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the primary residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $25,000 interest-free loan based on Area Median Income (AMI): $25,000 at 50% AMI; $15,000 at 51-69% AMI; $10,000 at 70-80% AMI. No payments required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the borrower's primary residence. Program provides assistance to first-time homebuyers in Frederick to help them purchase homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers and low/moderate income residents interested in purchasing a home in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchase
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland only; home must be located in The City of Frederick
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer
Resident of City of Frederick
Prospective homebuyer
Purchased home in City of Frederick
Home must be buyer's primary residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Housing and Human Services for application details or call (301) 600-2077 to register for homebuyer education.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides property owners with credits against their stormwater management utility fee in exchange for implementing stormwater best management practices on their property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive credits against their stormwater management utility fee by implementing eligible stormwater best management practices, such as rain gardens, rain barrels, or other green infrastructure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick property owners interested in reducing stormwater runoff and their utility fees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of stormwater best management practices such as rain gardens, rain barrels, bioswales, and other green infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners should complete the Stormwater Management Utility Fee Credit Application form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for High Performance Buildings
structured_extraction.program_description: A municipal tax credit program that provides financial incentive for property owners who construct or retrofit buildings to meet high performance and energy efficiency standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit is available for high performance buildings. Details on eligibility criteria, credit amount, and application procedures are provided in the program form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers in Frederick constructing or retrofitting high performance buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or retrofit of buildings to meet high performance and energy efficiency standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Building must meet high performance standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners should obtain and complete the Tax Credit for High Performance Buildings form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides residential tree planting support through a 50/50 cost share for containerized trees in the spring. The program helps City of Frederick residents increase tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and potentially reduce energy costs. The program also includes a separate HOA FILO (First In, Last Out) Planting Application component for homeowners associations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides a 50/50 cost share for containerized trees. Residents purchase trees at a discounted price that reflects the cost shared by the City. Trees are available for order and pickup during the spring season. HOAs can participate through the FILO Planting Application program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The storefront is open from February 1st until all trees sell out. Pickup is scheduled for March 28th.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who want to plant trees on their residential property (front or back yard), and homeowners associations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and planting containerized native trees on residential property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland. Program is for City of Frederick residents only. Applicants must live within the city limits of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Maximum of 5 trees per resident per year
All trees must be ordered and purchased together in one transaction
Trees must be planted in residential yard (front or back)
Renters must have landlord permission
Trees selected from Tree Frederick approved list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Enter your address to verify City of Frederick residency. Step 2: Select trees from available options on the Tree Frederick online storefront. Step 3: Pay for trees at discounted prices (reflecting the 50/50 cost share). Step 4: Pick up trees on the scheduled pickup date at Harry Grove Stadium. HOAs can apply through the HOA FILO Planting Application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A weatherization program that helps low- to moderate-income residents make their homes more energy-efficient by conducting a full home audit and providing free upgrades. Work includes air sealing, insulation, ventilation upgrades, lighting replacements, and appliance replacements. Residents can save an average of $372 or more per year on energy bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded weatherization services including air sealing, insulation improvements, HVAC upgrades, energy-efficient lighting, health and safety improvements, and thermostat installation. Homeowners and renters receive free in-home energy audit to determine eligible work. Average annual savings of $372 or more on energy bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties. Landlords with rental properties up to 4 units are also eligible. Nonprofits serving income-eligible clients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Weatherization improvements including air sealing, insulation, heating and cooling system upgrades and repairs, energy-efficient lighting, health and safety improvements like combustion appliance venting and carbon monoxide detectors, and programmable or smart thermostat installation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income at or below stated threshold based on household size (ranges from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
Primary residence in Frederick, Carroll, or Washington County
Renters must have landlord permission via signed building owner agreement
Landlords must provide proof of ownership
For rental properties: apartment buildings may contain up to 4 units per building for State weatherization funds; buildings with more than 4 units reviewed case-by-case
Home must be permanent single-family dwelling or multi-family property
Income verification and supporting documentation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit an application online through the City of Frederick form portal. For renters, an application must be filled out with supporting income documentation, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development approves all applications. Once approved, a qualified professional will audit the home's energy use and determine eligible weatherization work. All approved work is completed free of charge.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown allocates American Rescue Plan Act funding to eligible nonprofit organizations for project proposals in categories including Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, and Transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants may be awarded up to a maximum of $50,000 per category. The total allocation is $600,000 in ARPA funding for nonprofit organizations.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project proposals in one or more of the following categories: Children & Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health/Health Disparities, Transportation.

Submit Project Budget including all current and anticipated funding sources
Provide evidence of active SAM.gov registration showing the Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Submit application and all supporting documents by 4:00 p.m. September 1, 2023
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and all supporting documents including IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter, Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT, Project Budget, and evidence of active SAM.gov registration. Submit to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org by 4:00 p.m. September 1, 2023. Questions regarding the application process may be emailed by 4:00 p.m. August 25, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts & Entertainment District Tax Incentives and Admissions & Amusement Tax Exemption Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive tax incentives and support for artists and arts entrepreneurs who locate their arts and entertainment enterprises within Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District. The program includes two primary components: (1) a 50% property tax credit for 10 years on the increase in assessment resulting from renovation projects to create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises, and (2) an exemption from Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax for enterprises dedicated to visual or performing arts. The property tax credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by the qualifying artist or arts and entertainment enterprise and cannot be combined with the Enterprise Zone property tax credit. The program provides technical assistance and support for arts and entertainment businesses and activities in the designated district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two primary forms of tax incentives for arts and entertainment enterprises located in Hagerstown's A&E District: (1) A 50% property tax credit for 10 years on the increase in assessment from renovation projects creating artist housing or arts and entertainment enterprise space, applying only to the portion of the building occupied by the qualifying artist or enterprise and cannot be combined with the Enterprise Zone property tax credit; (2) An exemption from Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax for enterprises dedicated to visual or performing arts. Businesses must qualify for the exemption and notify the Maryland State Comptroller's Office. Additional technical assistance and business development support is available through the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment organizations and businesses locating enterprises or activities in Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District, including those undertaking renovation projects to create artist housing or arts and entertainment enterprise space.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for arts and entertainment enterprises including galleries, theaters, restaurants, performance venues, and other arts-related businesses within the district, as well as property improvements to create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises, business development, community engagement, and admissions and amusement tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the designated Arts & Entertainment District in Hagerstown, Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located within Hagerstown's Arts & Entertainment District
Business must be in the arts and entertainment sector
Property must be located in Hagerstown's Arts and Entertainment District
Project must create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises
Tax credit applies only to the portion of building occupied by qualifying artist or enterprise
Cannot be combined with Enterprise Zone property tax credit
Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts (for Admissions and Amusement Tax exemption)
Must register with Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For property tax credits: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for district eligibility and support options. For Admissions and Amusement Tax exemption: Register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (CRA) form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department and Fire Marshal's Office provide in-service training opportunities to businesses and industries in the City on fire safety topics such as fire extinguisher safety and crowd management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-service training provided to businesses and industries covering fire safety topics including fire extinguisher safety and crowd management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and industries operating in the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-service training on fire safety topics for business and industry personnel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses and industries located in Hagerstown.
requirements_list: Must be a business or industry located in the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Electronically submit an in-service training request form or call the Hagerstown Fire Department at 301-790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: Income-qualified homeowners can receive a grant of up to $15,000 for eligible emergency repairs and/or a low-interest loan to complete comprehensive improvements to their property. An emergency repair is defined as a situation that is life threatening or prohibits someone from living in decent, safe, and sanitary conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant of up to $15,000 for eligible emergency repairs and/or a low-interest loan to complete comprehensive improvements to the property. Federal CDBG income requirements apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified homeowners in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency repairs and comprehensive property improvements that address life-threatening conditions or prevent decent, safe, and sanitary living conditions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Income qualification required (Federal CDBG income requirements apply)
Must be a homeowner
Repairs must qualify as emergency repairs (life threatening or preventing decent, safe, and sanitary living conditions)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development before applying. Applicants can call 301-739-8577 ext. 133 or ext. 134. Submit a Homeowner Application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support for-profit microenterprises (businesses with 5 or fewer employees) located in Hagerstown by providing funding for equipment acquisition, inventory purchase, business infrastructure, training, and operational expenses. The program aims to create jobs, retain employment, and support business growth for low-to-moderate income business owners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $5,000 per business. Funding is administered as reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts. No private match is required. Only one business per household is eligible to receive funding, and priority is given to first-time applicants. Previous awardees must wait three years before reapplying, with a maximum of two grants awarded per household.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with no fixed deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit microenterprise business owners with low-to-moderate income who operate businesses in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of business equipment, purchase of inventory, necessary fixed assets (machinery, IT equipment, vehicles), professional services including marketing and business promotion, technological infrastructure and upgrades, entrepreneurial training, and operational expenses including payroll, utilities, rent or mortgage for commercial locations. Funding cannot be used for real property improvements, political or sectarian activities, utilities or rent for residential spaces, repayment of existing debt, or reimbursement of costs incurred prior to grant approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located within the corporate boundaries of the City of Hagerstown. Roving (mobile) businesses must document that at least two-thirds of their business occurs within Hagerstown and must have been in operation for at least six months.
requirements_list: Business must have 5 or fewer total employees including owner(s)
Business must be a private, for-profit business
Business and owner(s) must be in good standing with the City and State of Maryland
Business and owner(s) must comply with all City of Hagerstown regulations including the Land Management Code

Business must be established and operating for at least 12 months at time of application (businesses with less than 12 months of operation must submit a business plan and documentation of business counseling consultation)
Business owner must have income at or below HUD income limits based on household size
Business cannot restrict access for minors (18+)
Business cannot be a rental or property investment business
Business cannot be cannabis-based
Applicants must not have received a grant from this program within the last three years (except as noted for reapplicants)
Roving businesses must have been in operation for at least six months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants begin by completing a pre-screening questionnaire available online. City staff will then contact the applicant to confirm receipt and provide an application form. Upon submission of the completed application with all required documents, the City reviews for eligibility. Approved applicants receive grant funding as reimbursement upon submission of approved receipts for eligible purchases.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to revitalize vacant storefronts in Hagerstown's Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District by bringing first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards, decreasing blight, preserving structures, and creating employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants with no minimum amount and a maximum of $50,000 per project. Funds are only disbursed after staff verify all work has been completed to code, including all required site inspection approvals, and final receipts have been provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and developers with vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrades to vacant first-floor commercial spaces to bring them up to current code standards, including rectifying code violations and completing renovations according to City Code.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District in Hagerstown, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area. Priority is given to properties on Main Street and in proximity to Public Square.
requirements_list: Property must be a vacant storefront in the CC-MU Zoning District
All projects must comply with federal, state, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
All upgrades must be performed to City Code standards
A development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components must accompany the application
Final receipts must be provided for all work completed
Projects will be regulated through the City's Planning and Code Administration Department

Grant award eligibility determined by: Economic Impact of Project, Proximity to Public Square, Renovation Budget, Square Feet Being Revitalized, Condition of Building/Code Violations, and Length of Prior Vacancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form with an accompanying development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components to the Department of Community & Economic Development. A cross-department Review Committee will evaluate applications using established criteria. Once approved, applicants receive a Letter of Commitment from the City which may be used to assist in financing. Funds are disbursed only after all work is verified as complete and compliant with code, all required site inspections are approved, and final receipts are provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center and City-Wide Redevelopment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program supporting redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's City Center and citywide areas. The program offers two funding tracks: City Center Focus grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000 for projects in the designated city center area, and City-Wide grants ranging from $5,000 to $25,000 for projects throughout Hagerstown. All developers must provide a minimum 2:1 match. Eligible uses include property improvements, renovations, and infrastructure enhancement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: (1) City Center Focus: Grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000 for projects in the city center area, with projects typically ranging from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. (2) City-Wide: Grants ranging from $5,000 to $25,000 for projects citywide, with projects typically ranging from $15,000 to $75,000 or more. All developers must provide a minimum 2:1 match.
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and businesses undertaking redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's City Center and citywide areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment projects including property improvements, renovations, infrastructure enhancement, and citywide development initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City Center and City-Wide areas within Hagerstown, MD
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 match from developer required
Project must be in city center area or city of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application and guidelines provided in the program documentation. Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for specific application requirements and process details.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Wide Down Payment and Rehabilitation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to provide assistance with down payments and property rehabilitation for properties citywide in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to assist with down payments and property rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property buyers and property owners undertaking rehabilitation in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for property purchases and property rehabilitation and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City-wide in Hagerstown, MD.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for application requirements and eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Sign and Façade Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides matching grants to businesses and property owners to enhance their building's appearance with improved storefront designs, façade elements, and attractive signage in Hagerstown. The program aims to enhance the overall presentation of commercial properties and contribute to the visual appeal of downtown. Grants support commercial building façade improvements and signage installation through two tracks: Commercial Sign grants range from $250 to $1,500, and Façade grants range from $2,500 to $7,500, with applicants required to provide a 1:1 matching investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% matching grant program with two tracks: Commercial Sign grants range from a minimum of $250 (with $250 applicant match for $500 total project) to a maximum of $1,500 (with $1,500 applicant match for $3,000 total project). Façade grants range from a minimum of $2,500 (with $2,500 applicant match for $5,000 total project) to a maximum of $7,500 (with $7,500 applicant match for $15,000 total project). All projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings. The program is subject to funding availability and operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and tenants undertaking façade and signage improvements in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial signage and façade improvements for commercial or mixed-use buildings; commercial building façade renovation and new signage installation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to commercial and mixed-use buildings located within Hagerstown city limits, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings
Applicant must provide a 1:1 matching investment
All projects subject to funding availability and first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should submit a Commercial Sign & Façade Grant Application and follow the full program guidelines. Projects require approval before reimbursement. Contact the DCED Team for specific application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Defined geographic area in Washington County, Maryland where economic incentives are available to new and existing businesses that expand through capital investments and/or job creation. Approximately 5,500 acres within three state-designated Enterprise Zones approved by the State of Maryland for a 10-year period. Eligible businesses receive tax incentives including real property tax credits, income tax credits for wages paid to new employees, and exemption from commercial building excise tax.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State Inc Tax Credit Up To $1,000 per non-disadvantaged employee (one-time); up to $3,000/$2,000/$1,000 over three years for economically disadvantaged employees. Local Real Property Tax Credits: 80% of property taxes on increased assessment (years 1-5); decreasing percentages years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Exemption from Commercial Building Excise Tax: No commercial building excise taxes on new construction in enterprise zones. State of Maryland reimburses 50% of local revenue lost from the real property tax credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Property tax credits must be submitted prior to project completion date and issuance of Use/Occupancy Permits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating or relocating to the Enterprise Zone, developers, property owners, and companies making property improvements within designated Enterprise Zone areas in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements including building acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation, new machinery and equipment, and job creation within the designated enterprise zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within designated Enterprise Zone areas in Washington County, Maryland. Approximately 5,500 acres total across three state-designated zones: City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (~4,000 acres) and Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (~1,500 acres). Specific minimum investment or job creation thresholds apply based on location.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the designated Enterprise Zone
Application submission required prior to project completion and permit issuance for property tax credits
Property owner concurrence/co-signature required if developer/company applies on behalf of owner
Qualified employees must meet Maryland Department of Commerce requirements
Provision of all data requested by Enterprise Zone Administrator
New jobs must be full-time, permanent (35+ hours per week)
New jobs must pay 150% of federal minimum wage
New jobs must be maintained for at least six months before claiming credit
Business type must be Manufacturing, Warehousing, Research and Development, Corporate/Regional Offices, Service Industries, or Mercantile/Retail (special conditions apply)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development. Businesses should work with Linda Spence, Enterprise Zone Administrator, at the contact information provided. Application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of Use/Occupancy Permits. Complete program guidelines and application forms are available through the department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps property owners install or upgrade fire suppression systems compliant with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards. The program covers costs for fire suppression systems and related water service infrastructure to reduce financial barriers to installation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $50,000. Applicants must provide a 1:1 matching contribution. The grant funds installation or upgrade of NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems, water service lines, meter vaults, and related utility infrastructure for residential, commercial, professional office, retail, and mixed-use buildings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified - operates on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers of residential, commercial, professional office, retail, and mixed-use buildings in Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for installation of automatic sprinkler systems, costs related to water service or fire line increases, installation or upgrade of meter vaults, installation or replacement of sprinkler heads and piping, and replacement of mains and backflow devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
requirements_list: Fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use projects
Projects must be within the City's Sustainable Communities Area
Applicants must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown
Minimum 1:1 matching funds required from applicant
Fire suppression projects related to water service installations associated with renovation projects with service meters that are four inches or larger
Application must align with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should complete the Fire Suppression System Grant Application form and submit it along with supporting documentation. Questions or requests for additional information can be directed to the Planning & Economic Development Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department provides free smoke detectors and installation to eligible residents in single-family to three-family dwellings, with one detector per living level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke detectors and professional installation provided to residents of 1 to 3 family dwellings, with one detector per living level.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Hagerstown living in 1 to 3 family dwellings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free smoke detectors installed on each living level of eligible homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents living in 1 to 3 family dwellings in Hagerstown. Residents of apartment buildings with 4 or more units should contact their landlord.
requirements_list: Must live in a 1 to 3 family dwelling
One free detector per living level
Landlords in buildings with 4 or more units are responsible for electric detectors per City code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click on the smoke detector request form to submit a request or call the Hagerstown Fire Department at 301-790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost incentives to reduce barriers to homeownership within the City of Hagerstown. The program provides support through a forgivable loan-to-grant program designed to reduce vacant homes and boost new homeownership. No payments are required to the City if conditions are met, and the loan converts to a grant when eligibility requirements are satisfied.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost incentives provided as a forgivable loan-to-grant program. No payments are required to the City if conditions are met. The program is structured so that the loan converts to a grant when eligibility requirements are satisfied. Properties must be owner-occupied and can include single-family homes, townhomes, and condos.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Funding has been exhausted for FY2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers in the City of Hagerstown, with priority given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for home purchases within the City of Hagerstown. Properties must be owner-occupied and can include single-family homes, townhomes, and condos.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for properties located within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Hagerstown
Applicant must intend to owner-occupy the property
Applications must be submitted at least 30 days prior to settlement
Priority given to first-time home buyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant properties
Properties can include single-family homes, townhomes, and condos
Eligible properties include single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums
Property must meet city standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development for full program information and to request an application. Submit the completed Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative Application at least 30 days prior to settlement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides financing to small businesses and developers in Hagerstown for growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, facade enhancement, and other eligible business purposes. The program offers fixed-rate loans with flexible terms to support various business development needs, including land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery or equipment purchase, building construction, leasehold improvements, and working capital.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $200,000 or 80% of total project cost (whichever is less), with a minimum of $5,000. Micro-enterprise loans available up to $5,000, and working capital loans up to $30,000. Interest rate is prime plus 1% (minimum 3%). Loan term may not exceed 7 years (5 years for working capital). Borrowers must provide a minimum of 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less). Repayment begins within one month of project completion or equipment purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and developers with annual business sales less than $5,000,000 organized as proprietorships, partnerships, limited liability companies, or corporations, operating in or relocating to Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growth and expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, facade enhancement, land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery or equipment purchase, building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities, working capital, and other eligible business purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available within Hagerstown city limits, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business sales must be less than $5,000,000 annually for each of the last two years
Organized as proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, or corporation
Minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs
For new restaurants open 3 years or less: minimum 40% cash equity investment of total project costs
Credit check required
Non-refundable application fee based on requested loan amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with required documentation including Program Guidelines, credit information, and equity investment verification. Application fee is required. Complete program guidelines and application form are available on the city website. Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic District and Landmark Designation - County Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for owners of historic structures in designated historic districts and landmarks that undertake restoration or addition projects meeting National Park Service standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit of 10% of the owner's expense for restoration or 5% of the expense for new construction attached to an existing structure. Projects must meet the National Park Service's Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic structures in designated historic districts and landmarks in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration and additions to historic structures that meet National Park Service standards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Hagerstown's designated historic districts and for designated landmarks
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated historic district or be a designated landmark
Projects must meet the National Park Service's Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Exterior improvements must be reviewed by the City's Historic District Commission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Hagerstown Planning Office for information about applying for the tax credit

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic District and Landmark Designation - Federal and State Grants and Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Eligibility to apply for federal and state grants and state low-interest loans for historic preservation projects in designated historic districts and landmarks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Owners of designated historic structures are eligible to apply for federal and state grants and state low-interest loans to support historic preservation projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic structures in designated historic districts and landmarks in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Hagerstown's designated historic districts and for designated landmarks
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated historic district or be a designated landmark
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Hagerstown Planning Office to inquire about available federal and state grants and state low-interest loans for historic preservation projects

structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps qualified individuals or families purchase affordable homes within the City of Hagerstown. The city purchases vacant properties, renovates them, and sells them at appraised value to eligible applicants who are pre-qualified for mortgage loans and meet income guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city purchases vacant properties within city limits, renovates them to like-new condition, and sells them at current appraised value to qualified applicants. Applicants must be pre-qualified for a mortgage loan and have annual household income below the maximum amounts specified by household size (ranging from $52,500 for one person to $98,950 for eight persons). The program may be combined with other mortgage assistance programs, including the Maryland Mortgage Program and first-time homebuyer incentives. Real estate agents receive a 2.5% commission if the purchase is completed through this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners/prospective homeowners in Hagerstown seeking to purchase their first or next home who are pre-qualified for a mortgage loan and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a renovated residential property within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland area. Properties must be located within the city limits of Hagerstown, Maryland. Applicants must be purchasing homes within the City of Hagerstown.
requirements_list: Must be pre-qualified for a mortgage loan
Annual household income must be below the maximum limit for household size
Must submit mortgage loan pre-qualification letter with application
Must be purchasing property within City of Hagerstown limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact a local mortgage company or bank to be pre-qualified for a mortgage loan. Ask about the Maryland Mortgage Program, first-time homebuyer incentives, and assistance with down payment and closing costs. Once you receive a pre-qualification letter, schedule a tour of available homes and submit the Homeownership Program Application with proof of mortgage pre-qualification. Submit the application to the Department of Housing & Community Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to support life safety infrastructure improvements in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support life safety infrastructure upgrades and improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners addressing life safety infrastructure requirements in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Life safety infrastructure improvements including fire safety, accessibility, and building safety upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown city limits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for program details and application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Middle Neighborhoods Emergency Repair Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding for emergency home repairs that prevent homeowners from living in safe, decent, and sanitary conditions. The program covers 75% of repair costs up to a maximum of $15,000, with homeowners responsible for the remaining 25% and any costs exceeding the grant limit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant covering 75% of emergency repair costs, up to $15,000 maximum. Homeowners must contribute 25% of project cost and pay any amount exceeding the $15,000 grant limit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Hagerstown meeting income limits. Maximum annual household income ranges from $78,750 for one person to $148,425 for eight persons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency repairs that bring homes to safe, decent, and sanitary living conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed limits based on household size
Emergency repair must prevent homeowner from living in safe, decent, and sanitary conditions
Homeowner must contribute 25% of project cost
Must be contacted by Department of Housing & Community Development before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development to learn about full program details and eligibility. Applicants are strongly encouraged to call before applying. Submit homeowner application to the department.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Partners in Economic Progress Program offers incentives to building owners to renovate buildings within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center while attracting businesses to the renovated buildings. The program provides financial incentives and regulatory support to property owners and businesses seeking to establish or expand operations in Hagerstown through economic development and business growth initiatives.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant equal to City Property Tax for 5 years; 2 free EDUs (Equivalent Dwelling Units) valued at $13,800; 1 year free parking and 50% discount for 4 years; rent assistance up to $30,000 paid to property owner/landlord for first 2-3 years of business operation; waiver of development fees including building permits, plan review fees, occupancy and zoning fees; expedited review through Planning Department and Historic District Commission; use of Maryland Building Rehabilitation Code; 2 hours of consultation on historic tax credits paid for by the City. Support and encouragement for economic progress and business development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and businesses looking to invest in renovated commercial, residential, or mixed-use properties within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center, as well as businesses seeking to establish or expand operations in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrade of buildings and commercial properties. Eligible businesses may use rent assistance for occupying first-floor retail, restaurant, or commercial spaces in PEP-approved buildings. Economic development and business growth initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program limited to properties located within the PEP Zone in the City Center of Hagerstown, Maryland, within Hagerstown city limits.
requirements_list: Project must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center
Minimum investment of $250,000 for commercial projects, $100,000 for residential projects, $200,000 for mixed-use projects
Minimum investment calculation excludes property acquisition costs
Commercial projects required to participate in Enterprise Zone Program
Applicant cannot be delinquent on City or County taxes or other financial obligations to the City
Building and all core systems must meet all City of Hagerstown Code requirements
For residential and artist live-work spaces, minimum square footage requirements apply
Prior renovation projects eligible if renovation activities completed after January 1, 2007
Business must be new or existing business moving into PEP Zone or existing business expanding within PEP Zone
Business must occupy first-floor retail/restaurant space or non-storefront commercial spaces in PEP-approved buildings
Business must maintain lease and operate for minimum of 4 years
Rent assistance available only in PEP-eligible buildings where owners completed minimum investment
Subject to zoning approval for eligible business types
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must comply with eligibility criteria, obtain building permits for proposed work, and implement approved development plan and schedule. Submit application to City for approval. If approved, applicant must submit progress reports every six months on project milestones, report square footage per use type at construction completion, and submit annual reports on Enterprise Zone Tax Credit amounts if applicable. Any changes to approved development plan must be resubmitted for review and approval by the PEP Committee. Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for program details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing a 50% reduction in plot fees for community garden plot holders in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% reduction in plot fees is available to community garden plot holders. Full payment must be submitted with the application, and the reduction must be approved by the Operating Committee of the Association.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community garden plot holders in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Plot fee reductions for community garden participation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a community garden plot holder
Must submit a separate Plot Fee Assistance application form with Garden Application form
Reduction must be approved by the Operating Committee of the Association
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Plot Fee Assistance application form along with the Garden Application form. Send full payment with application. The reduction in fees must be approved by the Operating Committee of the Association.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to help property developers rehabilitate rental properties to market rate standards. The program provides matching grant funds for renovation projects, with grants ranging from $7,500 to $20,000 requiring a minimum 2:1 match from the developer. Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 must involve renovation of two or more units within a single property or parcel. Total project costs can range from $22,500 to $60,000 or more.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $7,500 to $20,000 with a required minimum 2:1 match from the developer. Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 must include renovation of two or more units within a single property or parcel. Total project costs can range from $22,500 to $60,000 or more. Funds are used for rehabilitation of rental properties to market rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property developers and rental property owners in Hagerstown interested in rehabilitating rental properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and renovation of rental properties to bring them to market rate standards. Funds must be used for renovation of rental units within a single property or parcel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to rental properties located within the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Minimum grant of $7,500 to maximum of $20,000
Requires minimum 2:1 match from the developer
Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 must renovate two or more units within a single property or parcel
Rental properties must be rehabilitated to market rate
Complete program guidelines apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should refer to the complete program guidelines and application form for detailed instructions on how to apply for the Rental Property Rehabilitation Grant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Single Family Rehabilitation Loans and Residential Rehabilitation Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Low interest loans for comprehensive renovations to single family or multi-family structures. Single family homeowners may also qualify for a grant for eligible emergency repairs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low interest loans for renovations to single family or multi-family structures. Single family homeowners may also qualify for grants for eligible emergency repairs. Loan funding is contingent upon Hagerstown Loan Review Authority approval and subject to funding availability. Federal CDBG income requirements apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single family homeowners and multi-family property owners in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Comprehensive renovations to single family or multi-family structures, and eligible emergency repairs for single family homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Federal CDBG income requirements apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing & Community Development for full program information. Applicants are strongly encouraged to call before applying. Loan funding is subject to Hagerstown Loan Review Authority approval and funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for for-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use zone to increase business efficiency, provide competitive advantage, and improve storefront beautification through eligible improvements and services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $750 per business for eligible uses including storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment, software or hardware, marketing or professional services, and other related improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 22, 2026, or until all allocated program funds have been distributed
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use zone in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment or software and hardware, marketing or professional services, and storefront beautification improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone in Hagerstown, Maryland. A zone map is available with the application.
requirements_list: Business must be for-profit
Business must be located within the CC-MU zone
Must submit completed application and vendor forms
Must provide Business Status from Maryland Business Express
If approved, applicant must purchase the product or services
Must submit receipt by June 5, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Spring Sprout Grant Application and vendor forms. Print a copy of your company's Business Status from Maryland Business Express. Submit application before May 22, 2026. If approved, purchase the product or services. Submit the receipt before June 5, 2026. The City will then disburse the approved amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to support spring and seasonal initiatives and projects in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support spring and seasonal projects and initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations undertaking spring and seasonal projects in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spring and seasonal projects, community initiatives, and business development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown city limits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department for application details and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that provides Maryland renters with free information and assistance about tenant rights and responsibilities, including lease reviews, eviction procedures, housing code enforcement, substandard housing issues, security deposits, and lead paint concerns. The program offers direct service, research, and advocacy to advance housing justice through information, education, and referrals to legal service providers. Services cover rental search, landlord research, application processes, lease agreements, move-in procedures, lease renewal, property sales, quiet enjoyment, retaliation protections, and fair housing laws.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free information, education, and assistance with tenant rights through multiple channels including an intake form for direct assistance, one-page fact sheets for download, a comprehensive tenant guide, and fair housing fact sheets. They offer lease reviews, information about eviction procedures, guidance on code enforcement and substandard housing issues, security deposit information, and referrals to legal service providers and other agencies that can assist Maryland renters. The program explicitly does not provide financial assistance. Direct assistance is available through an online intake form with response within 24-48 hours, or by calling the tenant hotline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents seeking rental housing and tenants with landlord-tenant disputes, particularly low-income communities and communities of color, and working families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides information, education, and advocacy services related to tenant rights and housing justice. Services include educational guidance, dispute resolution assistance, and advocacy support. The program does not provide financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland counties and Baltimore City, with emphasis on serving Baltimore City and various local jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Maryland
Must be seeking rental housing or experiencing landlord-tenant issues
Tenants must be current on rent to receive retaliation protections
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can use the online intake form to request assistance (response within 24-48 hours), call the tenant hotline Tuesday-Friday 10 AM-2 PM, access one-page fact sheets and a comprehensive tenant guide as self-help resources, or contact the District Court Self-Help Center. The program also provides referrals to legal service providers and other agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program designed to help owners and managers of rental properties reduce drugs and other illegal activity on their properties. The program educates landlords and residents to improve neighborhood livability by reducing crime. It consists of three phases: management training (a 4-hour basic course introducing best practices for achieving crime-free properties), premises security assessments of rental properties, and resident training. While voluntary, some property owners or managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program with no obligation to continue. Includes three phases: a 4-hour management training course for property owners and managers (held at Washington County Free Library, Room #334), premises security assessments of rental properties, and resident training. There is no charge for participation. The training is voluntary but may be required for properties that receive a certain number of notices from the city.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and managers of rental properties in Hagerstown; Multi-housing property owners/operators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance in crime prevention, property management, and resident education to reduce illegal activity and improve neighborhood conditions and livability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to rental property owners and managers in Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Ownership or management of rental properties in Hagerstown
Voluntary participation
Some properties may be required to attend if they receive a certain number of notices from the city
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Lt. John Lehman at 301-797-6408 or jlehman@hagerstownpd.org to register or enroll. Download and complete the registration form. The program is free and participants can choose to continue or stop participation at any time. Classes are cancelled if no one registers 48 hours prior to the class start time.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community education program offered by the Rockville City Police Department that runs from June through July 2026. The program meets 7-9 p.m. on Wednesday evenings from June 3 to July 22, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training program held Wednesday evenings for 9 weeks from 7-9 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community residents interested in police education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not specified - training program (no direct funding)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the provided DocuSign form

structured_extraction.program_description: Commissions, purchases, or accepts donations of works of site-specific public art to be installed on property owned by the City of Rockville. Established in 1978 to be a driving force behind Rockville's unique cultural identity. Works of art reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes of the surrounding site and reflect the city's dynamism and diversity, beautifying surroundings and fostering a strong sense of community. Includes permanent and temporary art projects with focus on visual arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is funded by an annual appropriation based on the city's budget from the previous year. Funding supports the commission, purchase, or donation of artworks to be installed on City of Rockville property. Commission budgets are all-inclusive, covering design, fabrication, installation, and site enhancements. Two-year warranty included with commissions. Maintenance and refurbishment funding available through AIPP operating budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents and citizens, emerging and established artists, community members and businesses interested in creating public artworks for installation on City of Rockville property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Art design, fabrication, installation, and site enhancements (landscaping, lighting); maintenance and refurbishment of public art collection; removal and disposal of artwork if necessary; artist honorariums and compensation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland publicly accessible spaces. Priority areas: gateways, Metro stations, Town Center, parks, and neighborhood sites.
requirements_list: Artworks must be site-specific
Works should reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes of the surrounding site
Artworks must reflect the city's dynamism and diversity
Works of art must become property of the City of Rockville
Artist integrity and attribution rights must be protected per Visual Artists Rights Act
Durability, life expectancy, and safety considerations required in selection
All works included in city inventory with documentation
Transparent acquisition and commissioning process
High quality artwork standards
Collaborative approach between artists and site designers/contractors
Community input and involvement in selection process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Three selection process options: Full and Open Competition, Limited Invitational Competition, or Direct Invitation. Review by project committee, art consultant, and Cultural Arts Commission. Final approval by Mayor and Council. Community input encouraged.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides and installs free basic inverted-U style bike racks for business owners and property managers to enhance bicycle parking near storefronts and offices. The racks are installed either in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement and are available for public use. Racks are adequate for short-term bicycle parking and help businesses provide secure parking for customer and employee bicycles. Racks are provided on a first come, first serve basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville purchases and installs basic inverted-U style bike racks at no cost to the applicant. Applicants can request 1 or 2 racks. Racks require a parking space of 72 inches by 24 inches. If placed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path, a minimum five-foot clear walkway must be maintained after installation. Racks are adequate for short-term bicycle parking and are available for public use.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local businesses in Rockville who want to provide bicycle parking near their storefront, shop, or office, including those without existing bicycle parking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of bicycle parking racks for short-term parking to provide secure parking for customer and employee bicycles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant business must be located in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business owner or property manager
No bicycle parking currently available near shop or office
Only business owners or property managers can apply on behalf of a business
Parking space must be 72 inches by 24 inches
If racks are placed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path, there must be at least a five-foot clear walkway once the racks are installed
Racks may be installed in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement
Must comply with City's Bicycle Parking Guidelines
Non-property owners must obtain property owner permission if racks placed on private property
Applicant must be liaison between City and property owner for private property installations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the Bike Rack Grant Program Application Form. Complete the application and send it by email to bikeways@rockvillemd.gov or by mail to City of Rockville Bike Rack Grant Program, c/o Bryan Barnett-Woods, Rockville City Hall, 111 Maryland Ave., Rockville, MD 20850. Hours are Monday through Friday. Contact the Traffic and Transportation Division for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative solar purchasing program that allows residents and small business owners to buy or lease rooftop solar systems together. The group purchase approach typically secures prices about 20% lower than individual installations. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Group purchasing discount of approximately 20% off standard solar installation rates. Members can purchase or lease panels based on group pricing. Roof evaluations are provided, and participants receive individual proposals before deciding whether to sign a contract.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents and small business owners interested in installing solar systems on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rooftop solar system installation, battery storage, and electric vehicle charger purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and small businesses in Rockville, Maryland. Roof suitability evaluation required.
requirements_list: Property owner or authorized to install solar on property
Roof must be suitable for solar installation
Participants can register on the contact list with no obligation to purchase
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the Capital Area Solar Switch Together contact list online. After registration, participants can check if their roof is suitable for solar. The program offers roof evaluations, individual proposals, and group pricing options. Members then choose whether to purchase or lease panels with the selected installer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Outreach and Restoration Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Chesapeake Bay Trust, in partnership with the City of Rockville, administers grants to nonprofit organizations for projects within Rockville city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources. Examples include permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to nonprofit organizations for environmental and restoration projects within Rockville city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations operating within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources, including permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that assist or benefit underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Project must be located within Rockville city limits
Project must reduce stormwater pollution or protect natural resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at https://cbtrust.org/grants/outreach-and-restoration/

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Rockville Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville requires some for-sale properties to be available to residents at affordable prices through the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program. This program provides access to affordable homeownership for qualifying first-time homebuyers by making properties available at 50% to 80% of Area Median Income levels. Buyers must obtain bank financing and commit to owning the home as their primary residence for 30 years. Non-U.S. citizens may apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program makes for-sale properties available at affordable prices (50% to 80% of Area Median Income levels) to qualifying first-time homebuyers. Buyers must obtain bank financing and commit to owning the home as their primary residence for 30 years. Maximum household income limits apply based on household size and range from $57,400 to $141,610 annually depending on household composition and area median income tier. Lenders provide pre-qualification letters establishing maximum purchase price, loan amount, interest rate, and terms (30 years). Credits for permanent home improvements up to 10% of original purchase price are available during resale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers and individuals and families seeking affordable homeownership opportunities in Rockville, including those who are residents or work in Rockville and non-U.S. citizens, with household incomes between 50% and 80% of area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a moderately priced dwelling unit as primary residence. Funds cannot be used for rental properties or investment properties. Eligible improvements for resale include: completion of unfinished areas, built-in appliances, HVAC systems, water heaters, flooring, countertops, decks/patios, fencing, and handicapped accessibility improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only in the City of Rockville, Montgomery County, Maryland. Priority on the waiting list is given to households with members who currently live or work in Rockville, have a household member older than 55, or have larger household sizes.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer
Must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000
Home must be primary residence for full 30-year MPDU period and may not be rented
Must qualify for bank financing
Must commit to own home for 30 years
All household members over 18 must submit proof of income
Household gross income must be within specified limits at time of sales agreement
Must attend a First-Time Homebuyer Class from HUD-approved counseling agency
Must obtain mortgage pre-approval letter from lender
Must complete MPDU Homeownership Program Application and renewal every two years
Income restrictions apply
Non-U.S. citizens may participate
Pre-qualification letter must be notarized and valid for one year from letter date
Applicants must disclose all household income sources with no exceptions
Lender must verify household income, assets, and credit score
For resale: submit HUD-1 settlement sheet and document any home improvements with original receipts
Home improvements must be permanent and add market value; owner labor not credited
10% improvement limit strictly enforced and not waivable
Building permits required for certain improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Attend a First-Time Homebuyer Class conducted by Housing Initiative Partnership or any HUD-approved counseling agency and obtain completion certificate. 2) Obtain a mortgage pre-approval letter from your bank lender on company letterhead using the sample lender letter provided; letter must be notarized and is valid for one year. 3) Complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online or request hard copy or PDF version by email. Application must be renewed every two years. 4) After approval, receive MPDU certificate by email within three to four weeks and placement on city waiting list. 5) When MPDU properties become available, seller or developer contacts eligible households on waiting list.
