For resale/refinance: submit MPDU Resale/Refinance Request form with personal information, property address, and improvement documentation including readable receipts and building permits.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Rockville Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Rental Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides affordable rental housing through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) program, offering income-restricted rental properties at below-market rates. The program serves individuals and families, including non-U.S. citizens, seeking affordable rental housing. MPDU rentals are available in properties throughout the city with rental rates based on a formula in the MPDU law. As of July 1, 2025, rental rates for buildings initially leased before 2024 range from $1,322 for studios to $1,890 for three-bedroom units. For buildings initially leased 2024 and later, rates range from $1,400 for studios to $1,999 for three-bedroom units. Rates are reviewed and recalculated annually in June. Housing Choice Vouchers can be used toward MPDU rental payments. Designated rental units remain MPDUs for 30 or 99 years depending on the date of first rental.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidies through income-restricted MPDU properties in Rockville at below-market rates based on a formula in the MPDU law. As of July 1, 2025, rental rates for buildings initially leased before 2024 range from $1,322 for studios to $1,890 for three-bedroom units. For buildings initially leased 2024 and later, rates range from $1,400 for studios to $1,999 for three-bedroom units. Rates are reviewed and recalculated annually in June. Housing Choice Vouchers can be used toward MPDU rental payments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 30 days of recertification letter date (for annual recertification)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families seeking affordable rental housing in Rockville, including non-U.S. citizens, with household income at or below specified limits. Priority given during 90-day offering period to persons currently living within City of Rockville corporate boundaries, persons currently working within City of Rockville corporate boundaries, and persons over age 55.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing in Rockville
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available for rental properties located throughout the City of Rockville, Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed maximum limits based on family size (ranging from $68,840 for one person to $106,210 for five people for FY 2026)
Minimum household income limit is 2.5x MPDU rent adjusted for bedroom count
Family size includes dependents claimed on submitted federal tax forms
Must not currently own or have owned residential property within last 5 years
MPDU unit must be household's primary residence; no subletting without written permission from HCD
Household composition must meet size limits per bedroom
Annual income re-certification required within 30 days of receiving re-certification form
Credit checks and income tests required (same as standard rental applicants)
Must provide federal income tax returns, W-2s, and recent pay stubs for verification
Must vacate within 180 days if income exceeds maximum limits at re-certification
Failure to recertify results in 60-day eviction notice
Legal custody documentation required for dependent occupants
Applicants must apply through the rental properties themselves
Contact individual properties for specific eligibility requirements and availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit their MPDU applications through the rental properties where units are available. The application process includes: completing the Certification/Re-Certification Form, submitting income verification documentation (federal tax returns, pay stubs, W-2s, and six-month bank statements), signing the MPDU Renter's Agreement Form, and signing the MPDU Lease Addendum. Annual re-certification is required within 30 days of receiving the re-certification form. Property managers use the MPDU Rental Application Form to process applications. The City maintains a list and map of all affordable housing opportunities. Contact the City's Housing and Community Development Department for general information about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that funds housing and community development projects benefiting low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods in Rockville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants to fund housing and community development projects. FY 2025 projects received between $19,945 and $75,000. Funds support projects such as single-family home rehabilitation, housing upgrades, community facility improvements, and permanent supportive housing maintenance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government agencies, and qualified entities serving low- and moderate-income households and neighborhoods in Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing rehabilitation, community development projects, facility upgrades, improvements to permanent supportive housing, and other projects benefiting low- and moderate-income residents and neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to applicants serving the City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods
Must comply with HUD requirements
Eligible organizations must complete the Eligibility Form through the online grant portal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Review FY 2027 guidelines document. 2) Attend a virtual technical session (Aug. 21, 2025 or Sept. 16, 2025). 3) Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com and complete the Eligibility Form to determine if your organization qualifies. 4) Complete and submit the full application by Oct. 10, 2025. 5) Attend the public hearing at Rockville City Hall on Sept. 8, 2025 to provide testimony about community needs (optional but encouraged).

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program that helps neighbors and community organizations work together to accomplish common goals that support the health, vitality, and inclusivity of their neighborhoods. The program requires applicants to secure matching funds (cash and/or in-kind donations) equal to or greater than the amount requested from the Empowerment Fund. The City of Rockville offers these grants to groups willing to match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours. Grants typically range from $500 to $1,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grant funds typically ranging from $500 to $1,000. Applicants must provide matching funds through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours (valued at $29.95/hour) equal to or greater than the amount requested. Funds can be used for building community, community improvement projects, or livability initiatives. Grant recipients must submit project documentation including receipts, at least two visual items, and a brief report on project outcomes. All funds are subject to taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighbors and organizations living or operating within Rockville city limits who want to work together on community goals. Eligible groups include neighborhood associations, civic associations, homeowners associations, community groups, groups of neighbors, and student groups. Each group must have at least three members and designate one individual to manage grant contracts and funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project costs and community empowerment initiatives including building community through programs or projects that promote neighborhood association development, sustainability, inclusion and diversity. Community improvement projects that enhance shared spaces or strengthen community identity. Livability initiatives that strengthen social connections, increase safety, address neighborhood challenges, serve low-income residents, or welcome newcomers. Bonus points awarded if two or more neighborhoods or community groups collaborate.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must benefit residents living within Rockville city limits in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Group must have at least three members
One individual must be designated to manage grant contracts and funds
If applying on behalf of an established organization, must provide documentation of authorization
Total Cash Matching Funds plus In-Kind Donations must equal or exceed Empowerment Funds Requested
Volunteer hours must be detailed with specific contributions and are valued at $29.95/hour
After project completion, must submit receipts showing proper use of funds
Must submit at least two visual items such as photos or printed materials
Must submit a brief report outlining whether the project met its stated goals
All funds are subject to taxes
Unused funds must be returned by Dec. 18, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Community Empowerment Matching Grant Budget Worksheet to estimate costs and matching funds. Create an account on the online grant portal at grantinterface.com and submit the completed application and budget worksheet by 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 5, 2025. Award notifications are sent by Feb. 13, 2026. Grant recipients then submit project documentation through the online portal by Dec. 18, 2026, including receipts, visual items, and a project report.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Services and Enrichment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides grants annually to local nonprofit organizations that partner with the city to support community services and enrichment programs that benefit city residents and visitors. This program combines the former Human Services Nonprofit Grant and Community Organization Grant Programs. It supports diverse service areas including human services, caregiving, arts, education, youth development, elderly support, health services, housing services, and social programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants totaling approximately $1.5 million with approximately 40 applicants typically awarded each year. Organizations must provide human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville. Funding supports diverse program categories including scholarships, emergency response, theater, cultural festivals, arts education, science education, historic preservation, clothing distribution, elderly support, emergency shelter, permanent housing, daycare, food pantry, health clinic, language classes, mental health, parenting support, youth development, and job training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations providing human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community services and enrichment programs including home care services, food distribution, health care clinic operations, educational programming, mental health counseling, emergency and permanent shelter operations, case management services, youth development, and therapeutic recreation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must serve individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville, Maryland. Primary focus on Rockville residents; Montgomery County residents considered for some services.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must provide human services or community enrichment programs
Must serve individuals residing in the corporate city limits of Rockville
Must submit audit, financial statement, or compilation for most recent completed operating year
Must submit IRS Form 990 for most recent completed operating year
Must submit board roster identifying officers, term limits, addresses, and phone numbers
Must submit report from last formal and/or informal program evaluation if applicable
Must submit document of application submission authority signed by executive director and board president on organizational letterhead
Must submit Budget, Outputs, and Outcomes Worksheet
Staff attendance at mandatory technical assistance session required
Must provide supporting documentation with invoices for reimbursement
Must meet quarterly and year-end reporting deadlines
Must respond to City communications within 10 weekdays
HIPAA compliance required if healthcare provider, or client consent authorization required
Insurance coverage requirements must be met before contract execution
Successful grant candidates must report data quarterly
Must track number of individuals served and measure engagement in services
Must assess program outcomes and completion rates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Review eligibility requirements and view the eligibility quiz and outputs/outcomes by service area. 2) Register for and attend one of four virtual technical sessions offered in September and early October 2025. 3) Complete eligibility quiz to confirm qualification. 4) Visit the online grant portal, create an account, complete the Eligibility Form to confirm qualification, and complete the full application by the deadline. 5) Upload all required documents including financial statements, IRS Form 990, board roster, program evaluation report, application submission authority document, and budget worksheet through the online grant portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A shared solar program that provides solar energy access to people who cannot install panels on their own properties due to roof constraints, shade, or living situation. Shared solar systems are located elsewhere in the community and provide electricity benefits to participating subscribers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Access to shared solar installations located in the community. Participants with an electric bill can access solar energy benefits. Discounted income-eligible programs are available for qualifying households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents and renters who cannot install solar panels on their properties due to roof constraints, shade, or living situation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community solar subscriptions providing shared access to solar energy generated by centralized installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the Pepco service territory, which includes Rockville and surrounding areas in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an electric bill
Cannot have suitable rooftop solar potential or desire shared solar access
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Solar United Neighbors for information on community solar opportunities in the Pepco service territory. Discounted income-eligible programs are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Fee waiver program for residential renewable energy and energy efficiency projects during April only. Waives permitting fees for qualifying single-family residential projects including solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging systems, and geothermal HVAC upgrades.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Waives permitting fees for solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging systems (up to specified capacity), and geothermal HVAC upgrades. Includes associated electrical work and panel upgrades necessary for system installation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homeowners in Rockville, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit fee waivers for renewable energy and energy efficiency installations including solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging systems, and geothermal HVAC upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Single-family residential property
Completed permit application with plans identifying location, nature, and extent of work
For rooftop solar: licensed engineer statement verifying structural capacity to support array
Energy storage systems limited to 20kWh maximum for fee waiver eligibility
Structural modifications, site modifications, and right-of-way permits excluded from waiver
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply via City of Rockville's permitting system during the month of April. Refer to the program details document for specific instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Eat Fresh Rockville SNAP/EBT FMNP-WIC Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A farmers market subsidy program that provides matching funds (up to $15 per customer per market) when customers use SNAP/EBT or Farmers Market Nutrition Program (FMNP)-Women, Infant, and Child (WIC) benefits to purchase locally grown produce, meat, cheese, and dairy at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 1:1 match of up to $15 in Maryland Market Money tokens for each customer visit when they use SNAP/EBT cards or FMNP-WIC checks at the Rockville Farmers Market. Matching funds are provided once per customer per market visit. Customers exchange SNAP/EBT tokens or FMNP-WIC receipts for free matching tokens to spend on eligible foods.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Recreation and Parks Department, Special Events Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families with SNAP/EBT benefits (including P-EBT) or FMNP-WIC checks who shop at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of locally grown fruits, vegetables, meat, cheese, and dairy products at the Rockville Farmers Market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to customers shopping at the Rockville Farmers Market, located at the corner of Route 28 and Monroe Street in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have active SNAP/EBT card (including P-EBT) or valid FMNP-WIC check
Must shop at the Rockville Farmers Market during operating hours (Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.)
Matching funds provided once per customer per market visit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For SNAP/EBT cardholders: Visit the market, find the information tent at the market entrance, provide your SNAP/EBT or P-EBT card, get SNAP tokens, and receive 1:1 matching Maryland Market Money tokens up to $15. For FMNP-WIC users: Visit the market with your FMNP-WIC check, purchase eligible produce from vendors, obtain a receipt, take the receipt to the information tent at the market entrance, and exchange it for free matching Maryland Market Money tokens.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers an online, same-day (express) process that allows eligible residential permits to be reviewed and issued within the same business day.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville provides expedited same-day review and issuance of eligible residential permits. Applications are accepted on Tuesdays from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling - applications accepted Tuesdays 8:30 a.m. - 12:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residential property owners with eligible construction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expedited review and issuance of residential permits for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to residential properties within the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Must be for an eligible residential project
Applications accepted on Tuesdays only between 8:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Express Permit Program page to see the list of eligible projects. Submit application on Tuesday between 8:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. for same-day review and issuance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A municipal program that distributes free trees to residents of Rockville during the fall season to support urban tree canopy and environmental sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees are distributed to eligible residents during the annual fall tree giveaway event.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trees for planting on residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can participate in the fall tree giveaway event. Sign up for the Environment and Sustainability Newsletter to receive updates on the specific dates and application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps City of Rockville residents and homeowners take steps to prevent damage from future flooding events by providing reimbursement for approved flood mitigation improvements. The program reimburses eligible homeowners up to 50% of costs for approved flood-proofing measures, including both yard-level practices (grading, berms, French drains, flood walls) and house-level practices (window protection, sump pumps, flood gates, waterproofing materials). Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. This complements flood insurance and encourages proactive flood-proofing measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to 50% reimbursement of total costs for approved flood mitigation measures, with a maximum of $5,000 per applicant. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Eligible homeowners can apply for reimbursement after making flood-proofing improvements to their property. Approved measures include gutter and downspout maintenance, grading improvements, protective equipment, basement protection, utility protection, windows, doorways, flood stoppage equipment, sump pumps, flood gates, waterproofing materials, flood vents, drain tiles, and utility elevation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville homeowners and property owners seeking to protect their properties from flooding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved flood mitigation improvements to residential properties, including flood-proofing modifications, yard-level practices (grading, berms, French drains, flood walls), house-level practices (window protection, sump pumps, flood gates, waterproofing materials), gutter and downspout maintenance, basement protection, utility protection, flood vents, drain tiles, utility elevation, and responsible stormwater solutions to reduce flood risk.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents and property owners in Rockville, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a resident or property owner in Rockville
Must own a home or residential property
Must have made improvements to property for flood mitigation
Improvements must be approved measures
Itemized receipts or invoices required for reimbursement
Must check local building codes and regulations before starting
Must obtain proper permits (Inspection Services Division and Public Works permits)
Hire licensed professionals (electricians, plumbers) for certain installations
Call Before You Dig (Miss Utility) 48 hours in advance before excavation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Rockville Environmental Management Division or call 240-314-8870 to obtain eligibility criteria and the list of approved flood mitigation measures. Submit itemized receipts or invoices for reimbursement after making approved improvements. The program reviews and processes applications on a first-come, first-served basis. Approved applicants receive reimbursement for up to 50% of costs, up to $5,000 maximum.

structured_extraction.program_description: An amendment to the Montgomery County Heritage Area Management Plan that provides a comprehensive heritage conservation and promotion initiative integrating historic preservation, education, tourism, cultural programming, and capital improvements across Rockville. The program focuses on heritage resources including locally designated properties, National Register-listed and eligible buildings, and emphasizes interpretation, urban design, preservation, and economic development strategies. It aims to re-focus public attention on the City's significant historical, cultural and natural resources and provides action plans to coordinate collaboration for successful heritage area development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants to local jurisdictions for acquisition, development, preservation, and restoration of heritage properties (up to 50% funding with 25% match available in-kind). Non-capital grants to non-profits and local jurisdictions for exhibits and educational/recreational products (up to $50,000 for non-capital grants). Tax credits including Sustainable Communities Rehabilitation Tax Credit for property owners whose property is listed or eligible for listing in National Register of Historic Places. Funding also available for capital improvements (parks, signage), programming and events support, educational curriculum development, and infrastructure development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and organizations in the Heritage Enterprise Zone area seeking to acquire, develop, or rehabilitate historic or tourism-use buildings; Rockville residents; visitors and tourists; school students; cultural organizations; heritage/historical organizations; city departments and commissions; civic associations; business organizations; diverse populations including ethnicity, age, socioeconomic status, people with disabilities, senior citizens, and low-income residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, development, public interpretation, programming, and rehabilitation of historic and non-historic buildings in active tourism use; park renovations and infrastructure restoration; historic property maintenance; sidewalks and paths; trail systems; cemetery renovations; streetscape improvements; ADA parking and accessibility improvements; unified signage and wayfinding; science center and museum development; educational programs and exhibits; special events and Heritage Days programming; curriculum development and teacher training; marketing and promotion materials; facility development; historic structures reports
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Rockville, Maryland within the City of Rockville limits, Montgomery County Heritage Area, and specific designated historic districts and sites including the 483-acre Town Center area, areas along greenways (Watts Branch, Rock Creek), King Farm Farmstead Park, Wootton's Mill Park, and Glenview Mansion
requirements_list: Property must be in the Heritage Enterprise Zone area or designated historic districts within Rockville
For tax incentives: building must be non-designated historic or non-historic in active tourism use, or listed/eligible for listing in National Register of Historic Places
Multi-year programming for historic districts with community and business support required
ADA compliance for programs
Data-driven evaluation criteria
Diverse population involvement in planning
Partnership coordination required
Accessibility for all ages and income levels
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Historic Preservation Division for information on grant and loan application processes and tax incentive procedures. Grant application sites include Maryland Heritage Area Authority, Montgomery County Heritage Area, Preserve America, National Park Service, and Maryland Historical Trust/Certified Local Government programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time financial assistance to eligible City of Rockville residents living in housing with documented energy inefficiencies. The program helps residents access weatherization services, home energy assessments, and comprehensive energy audits while supplementing up to $1,000 for utility efficiency retrofits. The program refers residents to appropriate available public and private resources to supplement the financial assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,000 in financial assistance to supplement the cost of energy-efficient retrofits, including weatherization services, home energy assessments, and comprehensive energy audits. Also provides utility bill assistance for water, gas, and electric.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income City of Rockville residents including seniors, families with children, renters and homeowners, and residents with no formal address who meet income guidelines and have been approved for other energy assistance programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient upgrades including insulation, blower door air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and tuning, refrigerator retrofit, and health and safety items such as moisture and mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair and replacement, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, lead hazard removal, and approved electrical repairs. Also includes utility bill assistance for water, gas, and electric.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves City of Rockville residents who reside within the corporate city limits of Rockville and have resided there for at least 180 days (approximately 6 months) prior to application. Eligibility includes homeowners, renters, shelter residents, or residents with no formal address. Use the City's address finder at rockvillemd.gov/services to determine if an address is within city limits.
requirements_list: Must reside in Rockville city limits for at least 180 days (approximately 6 months) prior to application
Must meet income eligibility based on household size (2018 limits: 1-person $24,280 to 5+ persons $58,840+)
Must be a homeowner, renter, shelter resident, or person with no formal address
Must use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating purposes
Must have utility account with approved supplier (PEPCO, BGE, Delmarva Power, SMECO, First Energy, or other)
Must provide photo ID and proof of residency
Must provide Social Security documentation for all household members
Must provide recent paystubs and income documentation
Must provide proof of home ownership or lease
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills
Must provide signed affidavit of income
Can be renter or homeowner (renters need landlord verification)
Cannot have applied for MEAP, LIEEP, or WAP within the past 30 days

Must have applied and already been approved for Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), EmPOWER Maryland Low-Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP), Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), or Enhanced Weatherization Program
Must provide documentation of comprehensive home energy audit
Renters must provide landlord or property manager approval for energy-efficient retrofits
Must agree to reside at the property for one year post-retrofit
Must provide documentation of three months of utility bills post-retrofit
Property must be applicant's primary residence
Must demonstrate previous rent payments have been made for the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Initial intake with Community Services Division staff member where address verification is conducted. Complete the application form and return it to the Community Services Division at hcd@rockvillemd.gov. The community services referral coordinator will refer residents to appropriate available public and private resources to supplement the financial assistance when needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Promotes positive, team-oriented activities and physical exercise for Latino male students through soccer leagues, field trips, life skills workshops, academic guidance, and Student Service Learning opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive free participation in soccer leagues, field trips, life skills workshops covering financial education, emotional coping, home repair, and gang/drug/alcohol prevention. Academic guidance and tutoring support provided. Case management provided to families. Transportation provided within City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Latino male students in grades 6 through 12 enrolled in Free and Reduced-price Meals Program attending Earle B. Wood or Julius West middle schools or Richard Montgomery or Rockville high schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Soccer league participation, field trips, life skills workshops, academic tutoring and support, college visits, and Student Service Learning opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program participants must be students attending schools in or near Rockville and enrolled in eligible schools. Transportation provided to stops within City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Enrolled in grades 6-12
Enrolled in Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARMS) Program for low-income families
Attending one of four specified schools: Earle B. Wood Middle School, Julius West Middle School, Richard Montgomery High School, or Rockville High School
Attend weekly meetings after school
Attend weekly practices
Attend all games (weekends)
Attend all field trips
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students may be referred by school counselors or administrators, or may self-refer. Submit the Student Referral Form provided on the program page. Contact Alexandra Moran at the Housing and Community Development Department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Historic Preservation Tax Credit (City of Rockville)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program that encourages restoration and preservation of privately owned historically designated properties. The county provides a tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs expended on documented expenses for exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of properties designated historic by the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 25% of qualified costs for exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation work. Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year. The tax credit is applied against the following year's property taxes. Any unused portion may be carried forward for up to five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic properties in Rockville that are designated as historic by the Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior maintenance, restoration, or preservation of historically designated properties, including work such as exterior painting, roof repair, window repair, chimney repairs, gutter replacement, repointing brick or stone, and professional services like architectural and engineering fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Rockville and designated as historic by the City of Rockville. Properties listed only in the National Register of Historic Places are not eligible for this county tax credit.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic by the Mayor and Council of Rockville
Work must be certified eligible by the Historic District Commission (HDC)
Owners must spend a minimum of $1,000 in a calendar year
Work must be approved by the HDC or be ordinary maintenance that does not require HDC review
Application must include copies of receipts for materials or paid receipts from a licensed contractor
Application must include photographs showing before and after work
Owner's labor costs are not eligible, but costs of materials may qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Historic Preservation Division to learn about the program and eligibility. The HDC determines the eligibility of expenditures and sends findings to the Montgomery County Department of Finance for processing. The director of finance may require further documentation and notifies the applicant of approval or disapproval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Requires most private development projects in the City of Rockville to include an expenditure for a publicly accessible art project based on an annually adjusted fee schedule. The program promotes general welfare by requiring and encouraging the use and incorporation of publicly accessible art in private development to preserve and enrich the character and environment of the community, improve quality of life, ameliorate the harshness of increased urbanization, and foster economic vitality. Governed by Chapter 4 "Arts and Cultural Affairs," Article IV of the Rockville City Code (ordinance 3-04).
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private developers are required to include an expenditure for a publicly accessible art project based on an annually adjusted fee schedule. Developers have multiple options to comply with the ordinance, including: installing or commissioning site-specific artwork; contributing to the Art in Public Places Program; providing arts space or arts-based infrastructure; or making monetary donations to eligible arts organizations or the Friends of the Arts Fund. Fees are adjusted annually per Builder's Cost Index. Maximum 10% of required contribution may apply to consultant fees.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Anne O'Dell, Arts and Culture Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private developers undertaking qualifying development projects in Rockville
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Consultant and artist fees, freight and shipping, fabrication and installation of artwork, purchase of arts-based infrastructure, construction costs associated with arts spaces, public art creation and installation in private development projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Most private development projects are subject to the requirement
Some projects are exempt from the requirement
Developers must follow the fee schedule and compliance options outlined in the ordinance and guidelines
Projects must calculate fees based on unit count (residential) or square footage (commercial/industrial)
MPDUs/equivalents excluded from fee calculation
Six contribution options available: on-site art, art presentation, monetary contribution, arts space, arts infrastructure, or combined options
Artist contract must be signed before project completion
Implementation requirements submitted in connection with land use approval applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the AIPD application form with project details, calculate the required contribution amount based on project type and size, select contribution option(s), and submit with required attachments to your assigned planner. Review the ordinance, implementation manual, and guidelines to determine if a project is subject to the requirement and which projects are exempt. Arts and Culture Program staff provide support if circumstances prevent completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: Optional preliminary building review for certain commercial projects. Allows contractors to begin limited interior demolition and framing of non-bearing partitions while construction documents undergo full review, prior to permit issuance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permits limited interior non-structural demolition and framing of non-bearing partitions before full permit issuance. No mechanical, electrical, or plumbing rough-ins permitted. Once approved, a placard is issued permitting work to begin while full construction documents undergo complete review.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial construction contractors and project applicants with interior alteration, renovation, or new tenant projects in Rockville with no change of use or occupancy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expedited preliminary review and placard issuance for limited commercial interior work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to commercial properties within the City of Rockville, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial/nonresidential project
Interior alteration, renovation, or tenant fit-out of existing building
No exterior work
No change of use or occupancy
Not mixed-occupancy
Must be classified as ONE of the following per International Building Code: Group B, E, F-2, M, R-1, R-2, R-3, S-2, U
No external approvals required (e.g., Montgomery County Health Department)
No alterations to fire-resistance-rated assemblies
No mechanical, electrical, or plumbing rough-ins permitted
Quick Start Placard must be posted at job site before work begins
Compliance with all applicable City Codes required
Work performed at applicant's sole risk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Commercial Construction Quick Start Permit Application through MGO Connect. City staff will determine if the project qualifies. If approved, an expedited preliminary review is performed and a placard is issued.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program administered by the City of Rockville in partnership with Chesapeake Bay Trust that helps eligible residents and organizations install small-scale stormwater management and sustainable landscaping projects on their properties to reduce pollution, prevent flooding, improve water quality, and create wildlife habitat. Eligible projects include native plantings, rain gardens, rain barrels, cisterns, trees, permeable pavers, green roofs, and removal of impervious pavement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for eligible stormwater management and sustainable landscaping projects with a lifetime maximum of $5,000 per property. Specific rebate amounts vary by project type: Conservation Landscaping ($5-$6 per square foot), Rain Garden ($10 per square foot), Pavement Removal ($3-$6 per square foot), Rain Barrel ($1 per gallon), Cistern ($1 per gallon), Tree Canopy ($150 per tree), Permeable Paver Retrofit ($14 per square foot), and Green Roof ($9 per square foot). Program also provides free educational workshops and free on-site stormwater runoff evaluations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible properties in the City of Rockville, including detached homes, townhomes, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits interested in stormwater management and environmental landscaping.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management and sustainable landscaping practices including native plantings, rain gardens, rain barrels, cisterns, trees, permeable pavers, green roofs, removal of impervious pavement, swales, pervious hardscapes, gutters, downspouts, retaining walls, terracing, and other best management practices to reduce runoff, pollution, and improve water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland only. Properties within City of Rockville watersheds including Rock Creek Watershed, Watts Branch Watershed, and Cabin John Creek.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City of Rockville
Property must be a detached home, townhome, homeowners association, condominium association, religious institution, private school, nonprofit, or multifamily property
Lifetime maximum rebate of $5,000 per property
Installation of eligible sustainable landscaping and stormwater management practices
Prior to implementation, seek technical assistance from licensed professional engineer, landscape architect, or certified erosion and sediment control professionals
Site-specific designs addressing individual site needs are essential
Call Miss Utility (811 or 1-800-257-7777) before digging
Obtain necessary permits from applicable regulatory agencies
Rain gardens must be located at least 10 feet from house, 40 feet from septic system or steep slope, and drain within 48 hours
Underground tanks must be minimum ¼ full at all times and not beneath vehicle/machinery traffic paths
Swales must have minimum 2% longitudinal slope with vegetation established before winter storms
Pervious pavement must be 2-5 feet above seasonally high groundwater and 100 feet from drinking water wells
Retaining walls over 3 feet high must be designed by engineer
Regular maintenance required for all systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the City of Rockville or Chesapeake Bay Trust website. Contact the Public Works Department, Environmental Management Division at 240-314-8870 or environment@rockvillemd.gov for application details. The trust will review and process applications, perform site visits, and is available for questions. Contact the City of Rockville for RainScapes Rebate application information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance programs providing reduced-price memberships to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center and scholarships to help low-income families and individuals who are residents of the City of Rockville afford recreation activities, programs, and childcare services. The programs serve both general populations and youth ages 18 and younger.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reduced-price memberships to the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center and financial assistance through the Youth Recreation Fund to help low-income residents access recreational activities and programs. Individual membership: $15.00/year; Family membership: $25.00/year. Daily admission prices: $1.00 for Adults, $0.50 for Children (ages 1-17). General program: applicants must submit an Application for Reduced Price Membership in person and meet prescribed income guidelines. Youth Recreation Fund: participants ages 18 and younger pay $15 toward each program fee, with the fund covering remaining balance up to $100 maximum per person per session (family maximum $1,000 per session); for summer camps, fund covers up to $175 per youth per camp session (family maximum $1,000 per child).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families and individuals who are residents of the City of Rockville, including youth ages 18 and younger, seeking financial assistance to participate in recreation programs, activities, and childcare services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Membership to Rockville Swim and Fitness Center, program fees for recreation programs including camps, sports leagues, swim lessons, dance, music, visual arts, theater, after-school programs, and preschool (Montrose Discovery Preschool).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to residents of the City of Rockville within corporate limits, Maryland as determined by the city's address finder.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the City of Rockville within corporate limits
Proof of residency (water bill, tax bill, or state-issued photo ID)
Proof of income eligibility: TCA, SNAP, Medical Assistance, TEMHA, Rental Assistance, SSI, or shelter residence documentation
Must meet prescribed income guidelines

Must submit completed Application for Reduced Price Membership in person at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center (for general memberships) or contact Recreation and Parks Department (for Youth Recreation Fund)
Adult members must verify address with state-issued ID
Must be approved before membership or scholarship can be granted
For Youth Recreation Fund: must be ages 18 and younger
Participant must pay $15 toward each program fee (or as otherwise specified for that program)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application in person at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. Provide required proof documents (copies) including proof of residency and proof of income eligibility. Provide applicant information and household member details required. Sign release and waiver forms. For the Youth Recreation Fund, call 240-314-8620 or email registration@rockvillemd.gov. Applicants must be approved before membership or scholarship can be granted. A limited number of scholarships are available. Contact registration@rockvillemd.gov or 240-314-8620 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency financial assistance provided to eligible Rockville residents in need of temporary relief for evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs. The program also provides referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial and employment counseling, and other types of assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary financial assistance for rent, utilities, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, and food. The program also provides referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial and employment counseling, and other assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Rockville residents experiencing financial hardship, including furloughed federal employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with evictions, utility shut-offs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves residents currently living within Rockville city limits for a minimum of six months.
requirements_list: Must be a current resident of Rockville for a minimum of 6 months
Must first apply through Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services
For rent assistance: must have a current eviction notice from court or final eviction notice from Montgomery County Sheriff
For utility assistance: must have a current utility shut-off notice or service must already be disconnected
Must demonstrate financial need due to job loss, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or other financial emergencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants first apply for emergency assistance through Montgomery County DHHS. If eligible, Montgomery County DHHS submits a referral to the City of Rockville on behalf of the resident. Residents who receive a referral then schedule an appointment with the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department by calling 240-314-8300.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Safe Waters: Swim Scholarship Program for Youth with Autism
structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted scholarship program providing financial support for inclusive swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), established to honor the memory of Ace Alexander and promote water safety, physical development, and family engagement. Scholarships support up to 10 children with a confirmed ASD diagnosis in a safe, inclusive, and supportive swim instruction environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funds for one child for one class season of swim lessons at Rockville Swim & Fitness Center. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until all 10 scholarships are awarded. Financial support covers tuition for swim lesson instruction in a supportive environment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until the 10 scholarships are awarded
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth with autism residing in Rockville; must be accompanied by an adult. Children ages 3 to 10 with a confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis who are residents of Rockville, MD and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Swim lessons registration fees at Rockville Swim & Fitness Center
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must reside in the City of Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3 to 10
Child must have Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis
Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Commitment to attend in-person swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
Established youth readiness to engage in group swim lessons
Adult must be present at facility or on deck during lessons

Proof of residency required: Current City of Rockville water and sewage bill (property owners), property tax bill (in client name and address), or state-issued identification card or driver's license with City of Rockville address

Must meet financial requirements including: Award letter verifying eligibility for TCA, SNAP, TEMHA, or WPA; proof of medical assistance; proof of public housing or HUD Section 8 housing or HOC rental assistance; proof of shelter residency; SSI documentation; MCPS Free and Reduced Meals Program (FARMS) eligibility; Care for Kids healthcare program; Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP); Montgomery County HHS Rental Assistance Program; Maryland unemployment benefits; or WIC eligibility
Up to 10 children will receive support through this program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form with personal information, disability description, and preferred course number; submit by email to programaccess@rockvillemd.gov; selection by Rockville Safe Waters Committee. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the 10 scholarships are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to seniors for trips, classes, and memberships through the City of Rockville Department of Recreation and Parks
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 50% of actual cost with a maximum subsidy of $50.00 per quarter for trips, classes, and memberships
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors ages 60 and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trips, classes, and memberships
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville residents
requirements_list: Must be ages 60 and older
Must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Proof of income required (W-2, benefit letters, pay stubs, tax forms, etc.)
Participant must pay 50% of actual cost
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form with personal information, income details, and proof of income documentation; staff signature required. For additional information and to apply, call 240-314-8810.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible Rockville homeowners to apply for assistance to make improvements to their homes, including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation. The program prioritizes correcting code deficiencies and is funded by the Community Development Block Grant Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides home improvement work at no cost to eligible homeowners. The maximum expenditure per household is $25,000. If the home is sold, rented, or transferred within five years after completion of the work, the homeowner must pay back a percentage of the contract price, reduced by 20% per year for five years. No monetary loans are involved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in Rockville who meet gross income requirements based on family size and annual household income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home improvements including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, and lead-based paint remediation. The program is intended to correct code deficiencies, not make property improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to owner-occupied homes in Rockville that are the primary residence of the owner.
requirements_list: Household gross annual income must not exceed limits based on family size (ranging from $68,500 for one-person to $129,100 for eight-person households as of May 2024)
Home must be the owner's primary residence
Owner must not own another home or condominium
Owner must not owe more than the home's assessed value
Total assets must not exceed $150,000
Property taxes must be current
If home was built before 1978, lead testing is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Mail a completed eligibility assessment application to the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department at 111 Maryland Ave., First Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Step 2: After acceptance, you will be notified to complete the eligibility review by submitting federal and state tax returns, income statements, current homeowner's insurance policy, mortgage and home equity loan statements, and checking and savings account statements. Step 3: Application materials are reviewed and work is prioritized by the rehabilitation specialist. The review process may take seven to ten business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A character-building program that recognizes students in grades 1-5 who demonstrate trustworthiness, earnestness, respect, responsibility, involvement, fairness, industriousness, and care. Participants complete 6 out of 16 good deeds such as volunteering at local charities, helping neighbors, or keeping a clean school environment. Successful participants receive a free refurbished bicycle and helmet and are recognized by the Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a free refurbished bicycle and helmet to selected participants (limited to 80 spots). Participants must complete 6 out of 16 good deeds and submit a mailed form by April 30, 2026. Selected awardees receive their bikes at a special event in May where they are recognized by the Mayor and Council.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Feb. 14, 2026 for registration; April 30, 2026 for mailed form postmark deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in grades 1-5 who live in or attend school in Rockville and want to build character while earning a free bicycle.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance provides a free refurbished bicycle and helmet for eligible youth participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be in grades 1-5
Must complete 6 out of 16 good deeds
Must submit mailed form by April 30, 2026 postmark deadline
Limited to 80 participants
Registration closes February 14, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register your child online by February 14, 2026 at the registration link. 2) Wait for notification by late February if selected for the program. 3) Start completing good deeds by March 1, 2026. 4) Submit completed mailed form by April 30, 2026 postmark deadline. 5) Receive bike at special event on May 16, 2026 where you are recognized by the Mayor and Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: Admission and Amusement Tax Exemption for A&E Districts
structured_extraction.program_description: Exemption from admission and amusement tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges for qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists are exempt from the admission and amusement tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges in the A&E District.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment enterprises and qualifying resident artists in the A&E District
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax exemption on admission and amusement charges
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualifying businesses and individuals operating within the designated Arts and Entertainment District in Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be located in the designated A&E District
Must qualify as an arts and entertainment enterprise or qualifying resident artist
Tax exemption applies to gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation to determine if your establishment qualifies as an A&E enterprise. The local office will evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for businesses investing in advanced technology infrastructure, including high-speed fiber internet.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit for businesses implementing advanced technology infrastructure such as high-speed fiber internet. Specific credit amounts and application requirements are not provided on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses investing in advanced technology infrastructure in Salisbury
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advanced technology investments such as high-speed fiber internet
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses in Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application details available at the Advanced Technology Tax Credit page

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible residents to defer payment of utility bills during times of financial hardship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Utility bills can be deferred, allowing residents to postpone payment obligations during periods of financial difficulty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Salisbury residents experiencing financial hardship who need to defer utility bill payments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferment of utility billing obligations (water, sewer, and other utility charges).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Salisbury, Maryland only.

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy a Home, Build a Business
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to help recent graduates of Salisbury University start a business and establish residency in Salisbury by providing business and real estate resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides business and real estate resources to help recent Salisbury University graduates start a business and become homeowners in Salisbury.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recent graduates of Salisbury University looking to start a business and move to Salisbury
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup and home purchase support through resources and guidance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Recent graduate of Salisbury University
Interested in starting a business
Interested in purchasing a home in Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Salisbury or visit the program website for more information on how to apply and access resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to assist businesses within the Main Street District recover from the negative impacts of COVID-19. Each business is eligible for up to $20,000 as a one-time grant award with no repayment required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of up to $20,000 per business entity with no repayment required. Funds can be used for paid sick leave for employees affected by coronavirus, maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions, covering increased costs for materials due to supply chain interruptions, making rent or mortgage payments that are past due or future due, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing PPE or implementing safety measures, building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, or business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered business entities in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury that have a physical establishment in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury and have been negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees unable to work due to COVID-19, maintaining payroll and retaining employees during business disruptions, meeting increased costs for materials due to supply chain interruptions, making rent or mortgage payments past due or due in the future, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing PPE or implementing safety measures, building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19, or other COVID-related recovery needs demonstrated in the budget narrative.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury, Maryland. Applicants unsure if their address is in the approved area should contact the provided email address for verification.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5
One-time grant award per business entity

Not eligible: home-based businesses, churches, banks and financial institutions, investment real estate entities (unless applying for payments for a business located in Main Street or COVID-related investments on a property there), food trucks, government agencies, contractors or construction or service repair-based businesses (unless applying for COVID-related investments on a property in Main Street area)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application during the open application period. Applications are graded by a committee based on the degree the business was negatively impacted by COVID, how the funds would help the business recover, and how much the business contributes to the vitality of the Main Street area. Applicants are notified of grant awards and then must submit proof of use of funds and a narrative describing how the funds were used.

structured_extraction.program_description: A micro-grant program that provides one-time grants to small businesses in Salisbury impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and state executive orders. Funded by donations from Delmarva Power and the City's Revolving Loan Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 with no repayment due. Limited to one award per business entity. Funds can be used for paid sick leave, maintaining payroll, obtaining materials, rent or mortgage payments, repaying obligations, or purchasing PPE and safety measures.
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Salisbury Office of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury that were impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees unable to work, maintaining payroll and retaining employees, obtaining materials due to interrupted supply chains, making rent or mortgage payments, repaying obligations due to revenue losses, and purchasing PPE or safety measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury. Businesses within the Revolving Loan Boundary area are eligible for both Delmarva Power and Revolving Loan Fund grants. Businesses outside the Revolving Loan area are eligible for the Delmarva Power-funded portion of the program.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the Revolving Loan Boundary map (or outside but still eligible for Delmarva Power funds)
Must have no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020
Must be engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland's State of Emergency with associated license/permit
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5, 2020

Not eligible: home-based businesses, churches, medical service providers, non-profit organizations, banks and financial institutions, investment real-estate entities, food trucks, national franchises, government agencies, or contractors/construction/service repair based businesses
Must demonstrate tangible and immediate need for funding
Must certify that funds will be used for stated need
Must complete disbursement form and produce receipts within 60 days of City approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online or by email. The application is reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness. Applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated to fully close) or Tier 2 (mandated to partially close). Tier 1 applicants receive first priority and approved applications enter a lottery system. If funds remain, Tier 2 applicants enter a lottery. Awardees are selected at random and receive grant checks via mail.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury provides grants to help low-income homeowners make critical repairs to bring their owner-occupied homes into compliance with city codes. The program covers repairs to mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; building components like roofs, foundations, floors, and walls; energy conservation improvements; lead paint hazard reduction; and accessibility modifications for disabled persons. The program is administered through partnerships with Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County and Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 per property (unless extenuating circumstances apply) to cover costs of home repairs including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, roofing, windows, doors, energy conservation, lead paint remediation, and accessibility improvements. Funds are distributed as grants, not loans. A five-year lien is placed on the property after the grant is received.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-546-1551 (Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County) or 410-543-4626 (Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners who own and occupy single-family homes within the City of Salisbury corporate limits and meet income and credit eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repairs that bring the house into compliance with city codes, including repair or replacement of defective mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; repair or replacement of defective building components and surfaces (foundations, roofs, porches, stairways, floors, ceilings, walls, doors, windows, siding, and trim); energy conservation activities (insulation, caulking, weather-stripping); lead paint hazard reduction; accessibility modifications for disabled persons; and incipient repairs and general property improvements of a non-luxury nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury corporate limits.
requirements_list: Total gross household income before taxes must be below 80% of Area Median Income (income limits range from $52,500 for a household of one to $98,950 for a household of eight)
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by the entireties (not tenants in common)
At least one owner on the deed must reside in the property
Applicant must have legal capacity to incur obligations under the program
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous three months
Applicant must be free of any tax liens or judgments
Bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of two years
If combined with a loan, collections must be on a payment plan and other negative credit must be addressed
Property taxes and City-issued invoices must be current
Applicant must have clear title to the property
All existing mortgages must be current for the previous three months
Property must be free of all judgments including IRS liens
Applicant must insure the property for the entire loan term; flood insurance required for properties in 100-year flood plain
Owner-occupants must not own any house other than the one to be rehabilitated and must not have substantial assets enabling them to secure rehabilitation funds from other sources
After receiving a grant, applicant is not eligible again until the five-year lien term expires
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact either Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County (410-546-1551) or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (410-543-4626) for further information and to apply. The two subrecipient non-profit organizations administer the application and award process and perform the repairs.

The program includes structured learning, mentoring, resume writing guidance, and soft skills development through collaboration with Junior Achievement volunteers. Participants work up to 28 hours per week and receive employment income alongside skill development. The program runs during summer months (typically June 22 to August 14) and provides both paid employment wages and comprehensive workforce development.

Participants work in City of Salisbury departments and receive workforce readiness training, career-specific skills development, mentoring, resume writing guidance, and soft skills instruction through Junior Achievement collaboration. The program provides comprehensive skill development through structured work experience and summer employment wages.
