structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Tax Abatement Program for Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury offers a tax abatement program that reduces property taxes for owners converting rental properties to owner-occupied family residences within Salisbury city limits. Property taxes are fully abated (waived) for the first five years of program participation. Beginning in year six, taxes are gradually reinstated at 20% per year over four years until year ten, when full property taxes are due. The property owner must continue occupying the residence as an owner-occupied family home throughout the nine-year confirmation period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Years 1-5: 100% exemption from city property tax. Year 6: taxed at 20% of prevailing rate. Year 7: taxed at 40% of prevailing rate. Year 8: taxed at 60% of prevailing rate. Year 9: taxed at 80% of prevailing rate. Year 10+: full prevailing tax rate applies. An incentive is provided to support the purchase of rental properties and their conversion to owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Director of Internal Services, City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual property owners converting rental properties to owner-occupied family residences in Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction and financial assistance for purchase and conversion of rental properties to owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within corporate limits of City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least three years immediately prior to conversion, or is owned by a person or entity that rehabilitated the property after rental use for three consecutive years
Property must be converted to an owner-occupied, family residence
Owner must intend to occupy the home within one year of closing date
Property must be a single-family detached dwelling
Owner must return annual confirmation of family use and occupancy to the City for nine years
Property must qualify for the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at the City Finance Office located at 125 N Division St. Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801. Applications can be found on the City of Salisbury website. Contact the Finance Office at 410-548-3110 for application details. Interested parties can obtain additional information through the participation form and FAQ resources provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) – Entitlement Communities
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides annual grants to the City of Salisbury, an entitled metropolitan city, for community development activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, economic development, housing improvements, and improved community facilities and services. The program supports affordable housing, community development, and economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income residents. Activities must benefit low- to moderate-income residents, aid in the prevention or elimination of slums and blight, or meet other community development needs of particular urgency. The City of Salisbury receives annual CDBG funds on a formula basis from HUD and allocates these funds to support subrecipient organizations (non-profit organizations and government agencies) in implementing eligible community and economic development activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Salisbury receives annual CDBG funds on a formula basis from HUD. For program year 2021 (7/1/2021–6/30/2022), the city received $399,903 in total CDBG funds, with $70,000 designated for administrative costs and $329,903 for program and project funds. Subrecipients (non-profit organizations or government agencies) can apply for either public service or capital grants. Funds are awarded on a reimbursement basis only—applicants must have sufficient operating funds to cover project expenses, provide documentation (paid invoices, cancelled checks), and wait to be reimbursed. The maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000. No more than 20 percent of the grant can be spent on planning and administrative costs. No more than 15 percent can be spent on public service activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government agencies undertaking community and economic development projects in Salisbury that benefit low and moderate-income persons or address slums and blight or other urgent community development needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and clearance of real property, public improvements and facilities (senior centers, recreation centers, day care centers), public services (child care, health care, job training, recreation programs, drug abuse counseling, homeless services), relocation assistance, rehabilitation of residential and commercial buildings, historic preservation, lead-based paint hazard evaluation and reduction, code enforcement, assistance to microenterprises, homeownership assistance, technical assistance to nonprofits, and assistance to institutions of higher education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the City of Salisbury, Maryland, an entitled metropolitan city that receives CDBG funds on a formula basis from HUD.
requirements_list: Activities must be eligible under CDBG regulations
Activities must benefit persons of low and moderate income, OR aid in the prevention or elimination of slums and blight, OR meet other community development needs of particular urgency
Subrecipients must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization and must provide supporting documentation confirming this status
Any capital project proposed on property not held by the subrecipient must include written approval from the property owner
Subrecipients requesting funds for community services must be either developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in service for an existing program

Each activity must be eligible and meet one of the following national objectives: benefit to persons of low and moderate income, aid in prevention or elimination of slums and blight, or meet other community development needs of particular urgency
Applicants must have sufficient operating funds available to cover project expenses upfront and wait for reimbursement
Maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Salisbury determines what activities it will fund based on community perception of local needs and priorities. The City prepares an Annual Action Plan for each CDBG Program Year to guide use of funds. Eligible non-profit community groups or organizations may apply for either a public service or capital grant, becoming subrecipients. Applicants must submit documentation of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status and any required property owner approvals. The City reviews applications to ensure activities are eligible and meet national objectives. Once approved, grantees must expend funds on project expenses, provide the City with copies of paid invoices, cancelled checks, and other requested documentation, and then wait to be reimbursed for those expenditures. Refer to the City of Salisbury CDBG Program Guidelines document for detailed application procedures and eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program that recognizes Salisbury businesses that implement environmentally friendly practices and demonstrate environmental sustainability. Businesses earn points by implementing green practices across categories like waste reduction, energy efficiency, water conservation, and community environmental engagement. Certification levels are awarded based on total points: bronze (10-14 points), silver (15-19 points), or gold (20+ points).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses apply using a checklist-based scoring system and indicate which environmental practices they currently implement. Points are awarded based on practice categories: 1 point for basic waste reduction practices (non-plastic straws, reusable cups, compostable utensils, biodegradable containers, recycled bags); 2 points for practices like energy-efficient lighting, native plants, recycling, food donation, local food purchasing, bicycle racks, environmental donations, and recycled paper products; and 3 points for advanced practices including water and energy efficient fixtures, clean energy use, designating a Green Advocate, stormwater management, green cleaning products, reusable bag programs, or custom practices. Certified businesses receive a sticker to display at their entrance, a photo with the Mayor for social media sharing, and logo placement on the City's website highlighting green businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in Salisbury, Maryland that want to demonstrate environmental sustainability practices and earn green business certification and recognition.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable — this is a recognition and certification program, not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to businesses located in Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Salisbury, Maryland
Meet minimum point threshold: bronze (10-14 points), silver (15-19 points), or gold (20+ points)
Implement eligible green practices from the criteria list
Designate a Green Advocate to serve as primary contact and attend City Sustainability Advisory Committee meetings at least once per year
Must complete and submit the Green Business Certification application form
Must accurately report current environmental practices from the provided checklists
Must provide business name, manager/contact name, business address, phone, and email
Must attest to the accuracy of provided information through digital signature
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses complete an online application form available at https://salisbury.md/green-business-certification-application. The form requires business contact information and a checklist of current environmental practices across three point categories. Applicants indicate which green practices their business implements and earn points accordingly. Each practice has assigned point values. The total score determines certification level. Participants submit their checklist for verification by the City. Upon approval, businesses receive certification materials, a sticker to display at their entrance, recognition including a photo with the Mayor, and logo placement on the City's website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the City of Salisbury that helps property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury connect to high-speed fiber internet service provided by Maryland Broadband along Main Street. The program reimburses eligible construction costs for bringing fiber into private properties. Grants are available in amounts not to exceed $2,500 on a first-come, first-served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in amounts not to exceed $2,500 and are made on a reimbursement basis only. Eligible costs are limited to the construction cost of bringing fiber into the private property and ending at the termination point where the modem will be located. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - contingent upon availability of appropriated funds
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants in Downtown Salisbury who want to connect to high-speed fiber internet service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction costs for bringing fiber into private properties, including materials to seal or cover the incoming fiber. Funds cannot be passed along to those using the service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Historic District of Salisbury. Downtown Salisbury, using existing conduits that have been abutted to buildings as part of the Main Street project. Property must be located within the Downtown Salisbury Historic District.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury Historic District
Applicant must be the legal property owner or a tenant with written approval from the property owner
Licensed contractor must perform the work
Historic District approval required if necessary
No digging up of sidewalks or work that alters the Main Street Construction project improvements allowed
Construction costs cannot be passed along to service users
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form with property information, project details, and proposed method for bringing fiber into the building. Include a photograph showing where fiber will be tapped and how it will run into the property. For reimbursement grants, submit copies of all receipts and paid invoices. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

Application must be received within two years from December 31st of the calendar year in which equipment was purchased to qualify for the maximum 5-year exemption term
A separate application must be submitted for each year of exemption
Exemption must be approved by the Salisbury City Council
A copy of the Maryland Personal Property Return must be submitted for each year of the exemption
Equipment schedule must include a description, original cost, and date of acquisition for each item claimed
County exemption must be received first
Submit detailed explanation of how requirements are met, including raw materials, products produced, or R&D activity

Applicants must follow guidelines including maintaining emergency access, preserving pedestrian walkways, ensuring six-foot social distancing, using temporary fencing, providing adequate ingress/egress for groups over 50, and providing ADA-accessible facilities. Applicants must also obtain separate approvals from the Health Department and Liquor Board as needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Foundation of Howard County Community Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual community grantmaking program administered by the Community Foundation of Howard County designed to support evolving needs and opportunities across Howard County through flexible grants to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. The program awards grants to nonprofits working to strengthen quality of life through essential services, education, arts and culture, health and wellness, community engagement, environmental programs, mental health services, food security, financial stability, and other community-focused initiatives. Grants support both operating and programmatic needs as well as special projects. Recent awards have ranged from $1,000 to $30,000 per organization. In 2024, $185,500 was distributed across 50 nonprofits, and in 2025, $225,000 was distributed among 32 nonprofit organizations. In 2023, $200,000 was distributed across 49 organizations. The program has been enhanced with a $125,000 contribution from Columbia Association combined with additional CFHC funds to create a pool of over $200,000 in available grants. The Community Foundation has set a goal of growing the fund to $500,000 to expand support and respond to increasing community needs. Applications are reviewed by a grants committee comprised of Community Foundation board members, community volunteers, and a Columbia Association representative, and evaluated based on criteria including future impact on the community, sustainability, and alignment with the Foundation's mission. Nonprofits must be registered 501(c)(3) organizations meeting IRS charitable guidelines. The program provides flexible operational grant support to nonprofit organizations providing programs and services that transform the community and improve quality of life, with funds helping organizations carry out goals without requiring activities directly attributable to the grant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive operational grants awarded to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. Up to $37,500 for organizations with operational budgets above $100,000; up to $10,000 for organizations with operational budgets below $100,000. Award amounts have historically ranged from $1,000 to $30,000 per organization. In 2023, $200,000 was distributed across 49 nonprofits; in 2024, $185,500 was distributed across 50 nonprofits; and in 2025, $225,000 was distributed among 32 nonprofit organizations. Grants are distributed from a pool of over $200,000. Unrestricted funding to help organizations carry out goals without requiring activities directly attributable to the grant. Funds support organizational operational needs including day-to-day costs such as rent, utilities, supplies, and salaries. Grant decisions are based on future impact on the community, sustainability, and alignment with the Foundation's mission. Applications are submitted through the grant portal at grantinterface.com.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations serving Howard County, Maryland in human services, arts and culture, education, health, environment, mental health, food security, and community affairs, working to strengthen quality of life through essential services and community engagement. Applications are accepted from grassroots organizations and established institutions. Faith-based organizations are eligible if services are non-discriminatory and religious activities are voluntary.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizational operational needs and unrestricted sources of income for general organizational support, including day-to-day costs of running nonprofit organizations such as rent, utilities, supplies, and salaries that strengthen quality of life across Howard County. Cannot fund capital campaigns, debt retirement, endowments, expenses already incurred, for-profit entities, individuals, medical research, political organizations/campaigns, private foundations, or religious instruction/doctrine programming.

requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or have a qualified fiscal sponsor meeting 501(c)(3) requirements

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofits apply through the Community Foundation's annual Community Grants Program. Applications are available online at www.cfhoco.org and are accepted through an online portal. Applicants can attend an information session or schedule a one-on-one meeting with program staff. Organizations can access a grant applicant tutorial for guidance on account creation and application submission. Applications are submitted through the grant portal at grantinterface.com. Applications are reviewed by a grants committee comprised of Community Foundation board members, community volunteers, and a Columbia Association representative through a volunteer-led grant review process using a grantmaking rubric and scoring methodology. Grant recipients are announced following the review period. Recipients are required to submit grant reports after receiving funds. CFHC provides reports to Columbia Association including recipient lists, project summaries, and financial accounting.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permanent, flexible philanthropic fund established by the Community Foundation of Howard County to provide financial support to nonprofits and individuals affected by economic hardship and local crises. Initially created in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the fund now serves as a central repository for donations during emergencies, mobilizing community support and coordinating grants for recovery and resilience. The fund supports small independent contractors, service workers, and nonprofit organizations serving frontline services in the community. When a crisis occurs, the foundation issues a public appeal, assembles a review or advisory committee, and issues grants to nonprofit partners or collaborates with local agencies to deliver services. Funds support various needs including rent, utilities, food, and services provided by nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants distributed to eligible nonprofits and individuals in Howard County facing financial hardship or affected by local crises. The fund aggregates donations during emergencies and distributes grants to nonprofit partners and direct relief programs. Funds can be used for various needs including rent, utilities, food, recovery and resilience during local crises, flood relief, and pandemic response. Examples include the November 2025 'Neighbors in Need' campaign supporting food assistance, which raised and distributed more than $12,000 between Columbia Community Care and the Howard County Food Bank.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small independent contractors, service workers, nonprofit organizations, and residents of Howard County experiencing financial hardship or affected by local emergencies and crises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payments, utility bills, food, recovery and resilience during local crises, flood relief, pandemic response, and support for nonprofit organizations delivering frontline services to the community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland. The fund is activated in response to local emergencies and crises.
requirements_list: Applicants must be residents or organizations serving Howard County

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Donations can be made online through the Community Foundation website, via check mail, or by calling the foundation. When a crisis occurs, the Community Foundation issues a public appeal to raise donations. The foundation then assembles a review or advisory committee to vet needs and issues grants to nonprofit partners or partners with local agencies to deliver services. Nonprofits may apply for grants or collaborate on service delivery when the foundation issues requests for proposals or emergency grant rounds. Grant distribution to eligible recipients is managed by the foundation in collaboration with nonprofit service providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit program that rewards donors who contribute to permanent, qualified endowed charitable funds at eligible community foundations across Maryland. Donors receive a tax credit equal to 25% of their contribution, which can be applied to Maryland state income tax, corporate income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax. The credit can be used by both individual donors and businesses to support permanent endowment funds that benefit local communities. Credits are available on a first-come, first-served basis and are limited each calendar year. Only new contributions are eligible; donations from donor-advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers do not qualify. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, and a five-year pledge allows annual tax credit applications each year if funding remains in the tax credit pool.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Foundation of Howard County / Frederick / Anne Arundel / Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors who contribute $500 or more to a qualified permanent endowment fund at an eligible community foundation receive a 25% state tax credit. The credit can be applied to personal income tax, corporate income tax, insurance premiums tax, or public service company franchise tax (only one type per contribution). The maximum credit is $50,000 per calendar year, representing donations up to $200,000 per year. Credits are available on a first-come, first-served basis and are limited each calendar year. Only new contributions are eligible; donations from donor-advised funds or IRA charitable rollovers do not qualify. Contributions can be made by personal check or publicly traded securities. A five-year pledge allows annual tax credit applications each year if funding remains in the tax credit pool.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last each calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual donors and businesses who want to support permanent charitable funds and endowments in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contributions fund permanent, qualified endowed charitable funds held by approved community foundations. These endowments support local community needs through grant programs and charitable activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is statewide and available across Maryland to donors contributing to qualified permanent endowment funds at eligible approved community foundations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contributor completes Section I of the Certification of Contribution Form with contribution details. The Community Foundation verifies the contribution in Section II and provides required documentation (Waiver of Information, Thank You Letter from Foundation, and Proof of Donation). DHCD reviews and certifies tax credit eligibility in Section III and issues an approval letter. The Foundation and Donor must complete and sign the Donor and Foundation Acknowledgment Form prior to contribution acceptance. The Foundation submits all completed forms to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development annually. Contact the administering agency or local community foundation to verify that credits are available for the calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency grant program established by Howard County funders to provide rapid financial assistance to nonprofit organizations addressing COVID-19 needs in Howard County. The program offered multiple rounds of funding to 501(c)(3) nonprofits providing operating support for food security, housing, childcare, healthcare, and mental health services, as well as support for the local healthcare system and frontline healthcare workers. structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Community Foundation of Howard County that empowers high school students to learn about philanthropy firsthand by engaging with community nonprofits and evaluating grant proposals. Student participants learn about local issues such as homelessness, hunger, domestic violence, and local arts and cultural opportunities. The program distributes grants to selected nonprofit organizations each year, with awards ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 per grant. In response to COVID-19, the program has also awarded relief grants to Howard County nonprofits addressing emergency community needs. Students work in the community to raise money, build endowment funds, and make grants to nonprofit organizations, preparing young people to be active, lifelong community citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Community Foundation of Howard County / Frederick / Anne Arundel / Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.assistance_description: High school students (sophomores and juniors) receive training in philanthropy and nonprofit evaluation. Students learn about community needs, participate in fundraising, build endowment funds, and make grants to nonprofit organizations. The program distributes grants to nonprofit organizations, with funds available ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 per grant. As the YIP fund grows, the amount granted out by students each year will increase. Grant awards have included $30,000 across ten nonprofits in COVID-19 relief rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Howard County high school students in grades 10 and 11 interested in learning about philanthropy and community needs, and Howard County nonprofits addressing issues such as hunger, homelessness, domestic violence, environmental concerns, arts and cultural opportunities, and community emergency response.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student participants learn about philanthropy and evaluate nonprofit grant proposals. Nonprofits that receive grants use funds for their operations and programs, including food access, support for domestic violence victims, meal delivery for elderly residents, transportation services for seniors, school supplies for students, and community relief efforts.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested sophomores and juniors from Howard County high schools can apply to be part of Youth in Philanthropy. Submit printed and signed application form via regular mail (not online). Complete application with student information, parent/guardian consent, photo release, and essay responses. structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program for established business owners who want to purchase owner-occupied commercial real estate, including accommodations, warehouses, retail centers, office buildings, and venues. The loan is guaranteed by the U.S. Small Business Administration and provides long-term, fixed-rate financing for commercial properties and equipment. The financing structure typically includes a third-party lender (bank or mortgage company) financing up to 50% of eligible project costs, FSC First financing up to 40% of eligible project costs, and the business providing at least 10% owner's equity, allowing businesses to obtain up to 90% total financing. For start-ups or businesses with less than 3 years of profitable operating history, the owner's equity requirement increases to 15% and the CDC portion reduces to 35%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans up to $5.5 million for healthy expanding businesses. The financing structure typically includes: a third-party lender (bank or mortgage company) financing up to 50% of eligible project costs, FSC First financing up to 40% of eligible project costs, and the business providing at least 10% owner's equity. The business can obtain up to 90% total financing. For start-ups or businesses with less than 3 years of profitable operating history, the owner's equity requirement increases to 15% and the CDC portion reduces to 35%. Loans have a 20-year term for real estate and 10-year term for machinery and equipment with straight amortization. Fixed interest rates are determined at underwriting. The down payment is typically 10% cash.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners in Prince George's County seeking financing for expansion, real estate acquisition, and facility improvements in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private revolving loan fund providing financing to established businesses with at least 3 to 5 years of operating history for expansion purposes. Funds may be used for real estate acquisitions, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, working capital, inventory, and human capital increases. Loans range from $25,000 to $350,000, with a maximum of $100,000 for startups. Loan terms up to 10 years with interest rates determined at underwriting. Requires 10% cash down payment for existing firms and 20% for startups. FSC First takes junior lien position on pledged assets. Loan proceeds can be combined with traditional bank financing and may be disbursed through controlled disbursements.

Loan proceeds can be combined with traditional bank financing and may be disbursed through controlled disbursements (joint payee checks).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate acquisitions, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases (excluding rolling stock), working capital expenditures, inventory, and human capital increases for business expansion.

10% cash down payment for existing firms, 20% for startups
Business and personal assets as collateral
Prince George's County location
Feasible startups may apply with maximum $100,000

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program for businesses whose services are needed by natural gas utilities, including engineering, hauling, construction, catering, and related sectors. The fund supports Maryland-certified diverse suppliers and other for-profit businesses in financing operations, services, and expansion needed by natural gas utilities. The program helps both established and emerging businesses grow through creative and innovative business financing solutions. FSC First is the designated fund manager.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 with terms up to 5 years depending on fund availability. Interest rate determined at time of underwriting. Personal guaranty required. No prepayment penalty. Application fee of 1% of loan amount. The program supports businesses whose services are needed by natural gas utilities for expansion, construction, and operational growth in sectors including underground pipe and fitting, paving, engineering, hauling and removal, general construction, catering, staffing and employment agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses in Maryland, including Maryland-certified diverse suppliers and established or emerging companies whose services are needed by natural gas utilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To finance operations, services, business expansion, construction, and operational growth for businesses working in the natural gas industry, including underground pipe and fitting, paving, engineering, hauling and removal, general construction, catering, staffing and employment agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland. Maryland-certified diverse supplier status may be required depending on program track.
requirements_list: Maryland-certified diverse supplier status may be required
Business must be in the natural gas industry or provide services to natural gas utilities
May have difficulty obtaining capital through traditional sources
Personal guaranty required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application form provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation provides one-time, project-oriented grants to support capital projects, equipment, technology, and defined initiatives in Maryland, primarily in the greater Baltimore area. The Foundation invests in nonprofits working on housing, health, education, economic mobility, arts, environment, historic preservation, and community development. Approximately 60% of funding supports capital/brick and mortar projects, 30% for equipment, and 20% for nonprofit capacity building or one-time needs. The foundation seeds new models that require philanthropic dollars to pilot but have paths to sustainability. The foundation supports non-profit organizations with defined project beginnings and endings and prioritizes shovel-ready projects that address long-term community priorities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time, project-oriented grants for capital projects, equipment, and technology with defined beginnings and endings. Approximately 60% for capital/brick and mortar projects, 30% for equipment, 20% for nonprofit capacity building or one-time needs. Requests under $50,000 are decided monthly on a rolling basis. Requests over $50,000 follow a quarterly cycle with LOI closing dates and proposal deadlines. The foundation favors project-based funding over annual operating support or ongoing operational assistance. Special consideration is given to sustainable building practices and energy conservation in construction or renovation projects. Payments are made within one month of signed grant agreements. Environmental and historic preservation projects can be funded throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; LOIs accepted anytime. Decisions on requests under $50,000 made monthly. Decisions on requests over $50,000 made after posted closing date on website. Applicants notified within 10 days of posted closing date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status serving Maryland, primarily the greater Baltimore area, working on housing, health, education, economic mobility, arts, environment, historic preservation, and community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects, equipment, technology, and one-time project-oriented initiatives. Projects must be shovel-ready. The foundation does not fund individuals, special events, advertising space, deficit financing, debt reduction, political activities, general operating/annual giving, or recurring expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The France-Merrick Foundation concentrates its grant-making within the State of Maryland and primarily within the greater Baltimore area. Nearly 90% of recent grants support Baltimore City and/or Baltimore County. Anne Arundel, Howard, and Carroll counties receive occasional funding depending on priorities and competitive proposals. Environmental and historic preservation projects can be funded throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization holding 501(c)(3) status under the Internal Revenue Code or have a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent in good standing
Applicant must have at least three officers on Board of Directors (president, secretary, treasurer)
Applicant must have at least 51% 'unrelated' voting board members (not related by family or business partnerships)
Applicant must have financial stability to sustain the project being funded
Applicant must demonstrate adequate administrative capacity, financial stability, and program effectiveness
Applicant must describe evaluation criteria, methods, and expected outcomes in their requests
Requests should be for one-time, project-oriented initiatives with defined beginnings and endings
Submit Letter of Inquiry on official letterhead signed by CEO/Executive Director

Letter of Inquiry must include: legal organization name, mailing address, Tax ID, contact information, organization description, project description, total project cost, funding gap, amount requested, and project timeline
Two-year waiting period must pass after final payment of previous grant before submitting new funding request
Project must align with Foundation's Areas of Focus
Prior France-Merrick grantees are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit a 1-3 page Letter of Inquiry through the online portal. Foundation acknowledges LOIs within 24 hours on business days. Step 2: For requests under $50,000, decisions are communicated the first week of each month with a one-month timeline to prepare and submit a proposal. For requests over $50,000, LOI decisions communicated within 10 days of the closing date, followed by a one-month proposal preparation period. Step 3: If invited, submit a detailed proposal including project budgets, organizational budgets, board lists, and audits. Program officer may conduct site visit. Step 4: Proposal reviewed by Grants Committee; requests over $50,000 also presented to Board of Directors. Step 5: If approved, sign grant agreement outlining terms and reporting requirements. Step 6: Payment made within one month of signed agreement. Final reports due approximately one year after final payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Foundation funds projects aimed at restoring and maintaining sites and properties of historical and architectural significance in the Baltimore region and in Maryland. The Foundation invests in projects that strengthen the capacity of the regional preservation movement and prioritizes projects that positively impact community development and contribute to environmental sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support restoration and maintenance of historic sites and properties. Sample grants range from $48,000 to $200,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations working on historic preservation projects in the Baltimore region and Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoring and maintaining sites and properties of historical and architectural significance. Projects that strengthen the capacity of the regional preservation movement, positively impact community development, and contribute to environmental sustainability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Baltimore region and Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The France-Merrick Foundation's Meet the Moment Fund is a grantmaking strategy providing short-term financial support to organizations working to prevent and address disruptions that negatively impact essential community needs and services, support strategic responses to sustain organizations and vital services, and invest in collaborative structures and practices to meet complex needs with reduced resources. The Fund uses an expedited review process to accelerate grant decisions and devotes up to 40 percent of the Foundation's annual distribution to this initiative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time operating grants provided on a rolling basis with expedited review. Grants support bridge funding for organizations awaiting new, withheld, or restructured resources; costs related to smoothing service discontinuation or workforce reductions, transitioning clients to new providers, and determining revised business models; costs related to organizational collaborations, restructurings, consolidations, wind-downs, and mergers; and costs related to developing or implementing new ideas or approaches to support sector capacity building, pooled or aligned funds, cohorts for planning, and shared services. Up to 40 percent of the Foundation's annual distribution is devoted to this Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with expedited review process, decided once a month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that serve the Baltimore area and advance Foundation priorities in housing, health, education, economic mobility, arts, environment, historic preservation, and community development. Prior France-Merrick Foundation grantees are eligible and encouraged to apply. Organizations must be facing risks and losses due to changes in public policy or funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time operating support including bridge funding, gap support for nonprofits addressing disruptions to essential community services (health, housing, safety, education, environmental protection), costs related to service discontinuation or workforce reductions, transitioning clients to new providers, determining revised business models, organizational collaborations or restructurings, consolidations, wind-downs, mergers, and developing or implementing new ideas or approaches to support the sector.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must serve the Baltimore area.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or represented by a fiscal sponsor

Must advance Foundation priorities related to preventing and addressing disruptions to essential community needs and services, supporting strategic responses to sustain organizations and vital services, or investing in collaborative structures to meet complex needs with reduced resources
Must have a plan for operating sustainability
Fund is not intended to sustain programs or organizations impacted by long-term funding cuts without a plan for future operating sustainability
Prior France-Merrick grantees are eligible and encouraged to apply
Applications responding collaboratively in Baltimore and advancing the Foundation's Areas of Focus are welcomed
Submitted request must be on official letterhead and signed by CEO or Executive Director
Must include legal organization name, mailing address, and 501(c)(3) Tax ID number
Must provide contact information for point person
Must include board of directors list with professional affiliations and giving information
Must include current organizational operating budget (12 months)
Must include latest audit if applicable
Must include copy of 501(c)(3) IRS determination letter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in applying should reach out to a program officer to discuss their idea before submitting. Requests are submitted via the Foundation's online portal (bbgm-apply.yourcausegrants.com) as a 2-3 page request on official letterhead, signed by the CEO or Executive Director. The request should contain information about the organization's mission, populations served, current budget and finances, the proposed idea or project, funding loss or policy change impact, proposed pathway to sustainability, and project timeline. Requests must include attachments with board information, operating budget, latest audit if applicable, and 501(c)(3) determination letter. The Fund uses an expedited review process to accelerate grant decisions. Requests are accepted on a rolling basis and decided once a month.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free one-and-a-half-hour training covering Frederick County alcohol laws and regulations for licensees, managers, employees, and others in alcohol service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free classroom training available to all licensees, managers, employees, and anyone in alcohol service. Covers laws and regulations related to holding an alcoholic beverage license in Frederick County. Beginning with the 2026 renewal period, at least one manager from each licensed establishment must complete the training prior to license renewal.

Beginning 2026, at least one manager per licensed establishment must complete training before license renewal

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to improve economic viability of the agriculture industry by encouraging Frederick County agricultural producers to expand or diversify their business operations. Eligible applicants can receive grants for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible agricultural producers for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities. Applicants develop a business plan, prepare a detailed budget broken down by categories (materials, advertising, travel, other), and submit an economic impact description. Projects are scored on a 100-point rubric evaluating project description, budget and capital needs, innovation, economic impact, and business plan components (executive summary, operations, marketing plan, financial plan). Applicants who have not previously received a Frederick County Agricultural Innovation Grant receive 10 bonus points.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The next cycle will open October 1, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Becca Tucker, Senior Business Development Manager of Agriculture
structured_extraction.program_audience: Crop or livestock producers, value-added producers, agricultural cooperatives, seafood processors, and primary or secondary timber products processors currently operating in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities for agricultural operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland. Applicants must be currently operating in Frederick County for at least one year.
requirements_list: Must be currently operating in Frederick County for at least one year
Must have recorded at least $2,500 in annual sales OR include an outline of investment in the operation and its impact on future sales in the business plan
Must provide documented evidence of outreach to Frederick County Planning and Zoning discussing project requirements

Must fall into one of these categories: crop or livestock producer, value-added producer as defined by Maryland law, agricultural cooperative, seafood processor, or primary or secondary timber products processor
Must develop a comprehensive business plan including executive summary, operations section, marketing plan, and financial plan
Must contact Frederick County Zoning Office to ensure the planned project is an allowed use
Projects involving waste discharge must contact Frederick County Health Department first
Projects involving land in a Land Preservation Easement must obtain verification that the project is an allowed use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Develop a business plan using available resources such as suggested table of contents, University of Minnesota draft plans, Maryland Small Business Development Center, or Maryland Women's Business Center. Step 2: Contact Frederick County Zoning Office with project description, property address, existing structures to be used, and whether public members will be invited to the building. Step 3: If project involves waste discharge, contact Frederick County Health Department. Step 4: If project involves land in a Land Preservation Easement, contact the appropriate county office for verification. Step 5: Prepare a detailed budget broken down by materials, advertising, travel, and other categories, including other funding sources. Step 6: Prepare a description of capital needed, including equipment or facilities to be acquired and estimated useful life. Step 7: Write an economic impact description explaining the project's impact on farm enterprise and job creation. Step 8: If the property owner or immediate family member is not the applicant, submit a signed rental agreement with terms. Submit completed application for evaluation using the 100-point scoring rubric.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual membership program that allows Frederick County residents to subscribe for coverage of ambulance transport services, reducing out-of-pocket costs for emergency medical services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual membership fees provide coverage of Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Life Support (ALS) ambulance transports within Frederick County. Membership rates are $15 per person for senior citizens (age 60+), $25 per year for individuals, and $50 per year for households. Members pay no additional out-of-pocket expenses for covered emergency transports after insurance reimbursement is applied. Subscription covers BLS and ALS transports by Frederick County EMS and emergency calls resulting in transport by a Frederick County fire and rescue company, but does not cover helicopter transports or private ambulance transports.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coverage of ambulance transport charges for emergency medical services calls resulting in transport to medical facilities

Coverage applies only to residents living in the subscribing household

structured_extraction.program_description: Serves individuals who are medically, technically and financially eligible for services in a community setting. Provides long-term care services and supports for people who qualify for nursing facility level of care but prefer to receive services in the community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides coverage for home and community-based long-term care services including assisted living, personal assistance services, nurse monitoring, support planning services, environmental assessment, environmental accessibility adaptations, assistive technology, behavior consultation services, respite care services, personal emergency response system, home delivered meals, dietitian and nutritionist services, family and consumer training, medical adult daycare, senior center plus services, and transition services.

Services emphasize voluntary engagement and dignity

structured_extraction.program_description: Frederick County awards competitive grants to eligible non-profit organizations serving the needs of County residents. The program supports initiatives in priority areas including homelessness and housing solutions, quality of life, public health, and the arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to non-profit organizations. The program targets four priority areas: addressing homelessness and housing solutions (including housing insecurity, affordable housing, financial literacy, aging in place initiatives); quality of life initiatives (childcare, senior support, youth empowerment, community inclusion, transportation innovation); public health programs (food insecurity, mental health, behavioral health, substance use disorder, intimate partner violence, health equity, maternal health); and supporting the arts (cultural enrichment, arts as community connection, placemaking, community arts programming).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing homelessness and housing solutions, quality of life initiatives, public health needs, or arts and cultural programs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open on December 2, 2025 and close on January 20, 2026 at 4:00pm. Organizations submit applications through the Foundant portal at grantinterface.com. Technical assistance Q&A sessions are available on multiple dates in December 2025 and January 2026 to answer questions and troubleshoot technical issues. Applications will be evaluated from January to March 2026. The County Executive presents the proposed budget and announces awardees in April 2026. The County Council adopts the FY27 budget and finalizes awards in May 2026. The grant period of performance begins in July 2026.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home energy improvements including air sealing, insulation, window and door weatherization, duct sealing, energy efficient lighting, water heater and HVAC upgrades, and repairs related to implementing energy improvements

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial subsidy program that assists employees and employers in forming and operating vanpools as a cost-effective and low-stress commuting option. The program provides monthly financial assistance to qualifying vanpool participants and operators by covering the cost of empty seats during the first 12 months of operation. Subsidy amounts are based on van size, number of passengers, and eligible operating expenses (lease costs and gasoline). The per-seat subsidy is calculated by dividing total eligible operating expenses by the number of seating positions available (excluding driver), then multiplied by the number of empty seats. Maximum monthly subsidies range from $500 for 15-passenger vans in months 1-6, decreasing to $300-$180 depending on van size in months 7-12. The program is particularly suited for employees who commute 30 miles or more and serves routes throughout the region, including destinations in Washington DC, Bethesda, Gaithersburg, Rockville, Manassas VA, and Fort Belvoir VA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly financial subsidy for unfilled vanpool seats during the first 12 months of operation. The per-seat subsidy is calculated by dividing total eligible operating expenses (lease cost and gasoline) by the number of seating positions available (excluding driver). The total subsidy equals the per-seat amount multiplied by the number of empty seats. Maximum monthly subsidies range from $500 for 15-passenger vans in months 1-6, decreasing to $300-$180 depending on van size in months 7-12. The program covers the cost of empty seats in new and existing vanpools while they are filling up, with the subsidy decreasing as more employees join.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers, employees, and individuals in Frederick County who want to form vanpools or participate in existing vanpools, particularly those with commutes of 30 miles or more and shared commutes to work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly subsidy payments to offset empty seats in vanpool vehicles during the first year of operation, and financial assistance for vanpool participation and formation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Vanpools must begin or operate in Frederick County. Vanpools serve routes throughout the region, including destinations in Washington DC, Bethesda, Gaithersburg, Rockville, Manassas VA, and Fort Belvoir VA.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible vanpool participant or operator
Employees must commute 30 miles or more
Vanpool must be new or existing
Assistance limited to first 12 months of operation
Vanpool must have eligible operating expenses including lease costs and gasoline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees, employers, and vanpool operators can connect with Frederick County Employer Connection and Transit's Rideshare Coordinator through their employer or directly, or contact Frederick County Transit Services to inquire about vanpool routes and eligibility. Frederick County Employer Connection can help workplaces form vanpools and learn more about getting started. Transit Services will assist in finding riders and determining subsidy eligibility.

A team from Frederick County's Grant Management Department evaluates applications, verifies eligibility, and makes award recommendations to the County Executive for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Service Coordination for Seniors and Personal Care Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program administered by Frederick County that helps low-income and frail, health-impaired seniors remain in their homes and communities. The program includes needs evaluation, service coordination, and case management through Service Coordinators, registered nurses, and Community Health Workers who assess individual needs, develop service plans, and identify and refer clients to community-based services. Eligible individuals receive in-home aide services and gap-filling service dollars to help pay for services such as personal care aides, chore services, and homemaker services. There is no cost to individuals for the evaluation and care management services.

Case managers help locate and arrange services, provide support in accessing them, and advocate with service providers. The program provides gap-filling service dollars and in-home aide services to eligible individuals to help pay for services identified through needs evaluation. Services include personal care assistance with bathing, dressing, and meal preparation, as well as chore services, homemaker services, and other community-based supports. There is no cost to individuals for the evaluation and care management.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County New Jobs Tax Credit and Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for businesses that construct or expand in Frederick County priority funding areas and create full-time jobs. The program provides property tax credits for both standard and enhanced expansions. Standard credits apply to businesses expanding or constructing by at least 5,000 square feet and creating at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years, with credits decreasing over six years (52% for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, 26% for years five and six). An Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit provides a 12-year property tax credit equal to 58.5% of the property tax imposed on the increase in assessment for large-scale expansions of at least 250,000 square feet that create at least 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, or alternatively at least 2,500 full-time jobs with an additional 500 positions, all paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The enhanced credit also applies to substantially renovated adjoining or neighboring real property (where renovation involves complete renovation of at least 50% of each building). The program is available for businesses already established in Frederick County or relocating from outside Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses that construct or expand in a priority funding area and create full-time jobs may qualify for a New Jobs Tax Credit. Standard credits require at least 5,000 square feet of expansion or new construction and creation of at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years. Credits decrease over six years: 52% for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, and 26% for years five and six. An Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is available for businesses that expand by at least 250,000 square feet and create a minimum of 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, or alternatively at least 2,500 full-time jobs with an additional 500 positions, all paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage. The enhanced credit provides a 12-year tax credit equal to 58.5% of the property tax imposed on the increase in assessment of new or expanded premises and any substantially renovated adjoining or neighboring real property (where renovation involves complete renovation of at least 50% of each building). Tax credits are available for new construction only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses planning to expand or construct facilities and create new jobs in Frederick County priority funding areas, including large businesses planning major expansion or construction projects. The program is for businesses already established in Frederick County or relocating from outside Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County Government offers subsidies to help residents in difficult-to-serve areas of Garrett County afford broadband service connection costs when the quoted price exceeds their budget.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidies to cover a portion of the cost for internet service providers to bring broadband service to unserved addresses. Payments are made directly to the internet service provider. Customers may be asked to contribute up to 10% of the requested subsidy amount if possible. Program funding and per-project funding are limited. Internet service providers must also contribute to each project and must participate in the ACP (Affordable Connectivity Program) to qualify. Subsidies cover only valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service, not direct customer expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Garrett County residents who have been quoted a price for broadband service that exceeds their budget and are located in difficult-to-serve areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidies are used to cover the cost of bringing broadband service infrastructure to unserved addresses in Garrett County. Funds pay for valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service, including internet service provider infrastructure costs. Direct customer expenses cannot be paid or reimbursed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves difficult-to-serve addresses in Garrett County, Maryland. Addresses must not already be served by a broadband provider offering minimum 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload service. If an address can be served by any provider without subsidy, the address is ineligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Garrett County resident seeking broadband service
Applicant must have received a quote from an internet service provider that exceeds their budget
Address must be unserved by broadband (minimum 100 Mbps download, 20 Mbps upload) or cannot be served by an available provider without subsidy
Internet service provider must be willing to participate in the program
Internet service provider must contribute to the project and participate in ACP (Affordable Connectivity Program) to qualify
Applicant may be asked to contribute up to 10% of the requested subsidy amount if possible
Only valid expenses directly related to broadband connection qualify; direct customer expenses do not qualify
Permits, easements, and other legal requirements must be satisfied
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A resident contacts an internet service provider requesting service. The provider assesses the situation and develops a budget to reach the home. If the customer cannot afford the full amount, they can ask the provider to request a subsidy or contact the Broadband & Energy Manager directly at broadband@garrettcountymd.gov or 301-914-1543. The County will work with the internet service provider to develop a project budget. If the subsidy is approved, the internet service provider may begin the project. Permit, easement, and legal requirements may delay actual connections.

structured_extraction.program_name: Garrett County Property Tax Credit for New or Expanding Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for new and expanding businesses in Garrett County that make improvements to business property. The program provides tax incentives against the county's portion of real property tax on improvements. Tax credits are applied for five years, starting at 50% of the assessed value and decreasing by 10% each year to 10% in the fifth year. New improvements must increase the tax assessment by at least $100,000 to qualify. The program is implemented by the Board of Commissioners and the Department of Economic Development. After five years, the property returns to the tax rolls at full assessed value.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for new and expanding businesses in Garrett County. The primary mechanism is a tax credit against the county's portion of real property tax levied on improvements to a business property. The credit is applied for five years, starting at 50% of the assessed value of new improvements in the first year, decreasing to 40%, 30%, 20%, and 10% in years 2-5 respectively. The new improvement must increase the tax assessment by at least $100,000 to qualify. Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007. The credit can be combined with enterprise zone credits but combined credits cannot exceed 100% of tax. Does not apply to State or municipal property taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New businesses locating in Garrett County and existing businesses expanding in Garrett County making improvements to business property with assessments of at least $100,000
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property capital improvements including expansion, renovation, or new construction to a business property with a minimum of $100,000 in improvements required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anywhere in Garrett County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be new or expanding
New improvement must increase the tax assessment on improvements to the property by at least $100,000
Improvements must be reflected on tax bills after June 30, 2007
Must make a minimum of $100,000 in real property capital improvements
Real property must be owned or occupied by applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the Garrett County Department of Economic Development of its intent to apply, ideally right after completing property expansion, renovation, or improvement. Second, the business fills out and submits an application form from the department with business, investment details, and employee information. If the business qualifies, the department verifies the assessment and calculates tax credits over the 5-year period and sends a certificate of eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Management Assistance Grants support specific, well-defined organizational development initiatives of nonprofit organizations, principally funding the engagement of qualified consulting expertise. These grants support initiatives such as strategic planning, program evaluation, feasibility studies, merger exploration, fund development and sustainability, resource development planning, donor prospect identification and development, board fundraising engagement, financial management systems improvement, IT assessment and planning, board development, executive coaching, succession planning, and improving systems of service delivery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funds to engage qualified consulting expertise for organizational development initiatives including strategic planning, fund development and sustainability, financial management systems improvement, program evaluation, IT assessment and planning, board development, executive coaching, succession planning, improving systems of service delivery, and mergers and strategic alliances. Prior approval from the foundation's program officer is required before submitting an application. A 25% cash match is required for organizations with budgets under $250,000; a 50% cash match is required for organizations with budgets of $250,000 or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Smaller, well-established nonprofit organizations with operating budgets typically less than $2 million in the metropolitan Baltimore area, particularly Baltimore City, seeking consulting assistance for organizational development, strategic planning, program evaluation, merger exploration, governance development, or fund development
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engagement of qualified consulting expertise for organizational development initiatives including strategic planning, fund development and sustainability, financial management systems improvement, program evaluation, IT assessment and planning, board development, executive coaching, succession planning, improving systems of service delivery, and mergers and strategic alliances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Metropolitan Baltimore, primarily Baltimore City. Organizations must carry out work principally in metropolitan Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization as defined in Section 501(c)(3) and Section 509(a) of the Internal Revenue Code
Must have completed at least two full budget years
Must demonstrate program outcomes already achieved
Must carry on work principally in metropolitan Baltimore, primarily Baltimore City
Not intended for start-up support for new nonprofits
Must pledge cash match (25% for budgets under $250,000; 50% for budgets $250,000 or more)
Must speak with Program Officer before submitting an application
Must interview at least two consultants before submitting an application
Must not discriminate on the basis of race, creed, color, physical handicap, or gender
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before submitting an application, call or email the foundation's program officer to briefly describe your initiative and discuss its general eligibility for grant consideration. Follow the guidelines provided in the Management Assistance Grant Guidelines document. Speak with the Program Officer before submitting your application and interview at least two qualified consultants before applying. Applications submitted without prior approval will not be considered. Visit https://goldsekerfoundation.org/apply/ for application instructions and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Enables local jurisdictions to implement or maintain a Day Reporting Center providing community-based services and treatment to individuals under pretrial or probation supervision or sentenced directly to a Day Reporting Center. The program aims to reduce recidivism, jail and prison populations, and corrections-related costs. Highly structured non-residential programs offering comprehensive services to non-violent individuals. Participants live at home and report to the center regularly, often daily, receiving services including counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, drug treatment, educational remediation, job training, and intense supervision to address criminogenic needs such as antisocial thoughts, substance abuse, anger, employment, education, and life skills.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding ranging from $135,000 to $270,000 per award (up to two awards available; total anticipated funding $270,000) to support implementation or continuation of Adult Day Reporting Centers. Funding supports personnel (counselors, case managers, peer recovery staff), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel, contractual services, equipment (under $10,000), program supplies, drug and alcohol test kits, and medications for opioid and substance use disorder treatment. Grants are reimbursed on a quarterly basis based on actual expenditures.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Breyann Williams (Grant Monitor), Jacqueline Adams (Fund Manager), Dorothy Lee (Fiscal Specialist), Brandi Cahn (Assistant Director, Justice Reinvestment), and Lindsey McCullough (Justice Reinvestment Coordinator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies and nonprofit organizations seeking to establish or operate Day Reporting Centers for individuals under pretrial or probation supervision.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (salaries, fringe benefits for counselors, case managers, peer recovery staff); operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications); travel; contractual services; equipment (items under $10,000); program supplies; drug and alcohol test kits; medications for opioid use and substance use disorder treatment; workforce development services; housing services; and behavioral healthcare services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland local government agencies and eligible nonprofit organizations. Priority given to ENOUGH-eligible communities with high levels of concentrated child poverty.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS) only; paper and email applications are not accepted. Applicants must obtain a User ID before April 1, 2026. Training and technical assistance is provided prior to the application deadline. The SFY 2027 funding opportunity includes a technical assistance webinar. Applicants must complete all required forms including Certified Assurances, Federal Anti-Lobbying Certification, Organizational Capacity Questionnaire, and narrative sections. Grants are reviewed and selected for funding based on application quality and alignment with program goals.

structured_extraction.program_name: Body Armor for Local Law Enforcement (BARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded grant program that provides funding to local law enforcement agencies to purchase and procure body armor and stab-resistant vests to protect sworn law enforcement officers. The program assists agencies in acquiring new protective body armor and replacing existing body armor if testing or age indicates replacement is needed. Primary purpose is to protect the lives of law enforcement officers engaged in crime prevention efforts.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds for purchasing ballistic-resistant body armor and stab-resistant vests compliant with NIJ standards, including ballistic/trauma plates, tactical carriers, undershirt carriers, and vest-mounted accessories (MOLLE systems). The program also assists with replacement of existing body armor based on age or wear. Funding is limited to sworn officers only. A 50% cost share (match) requirement from local government funds is required. Funding is reimbursed quarterly.

structured_extraction.program_name: Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP/BSCI)

The program supports crisis intervention court proceedings, extreme risk protection orders (ERPO) to temporarily remove guns from people who pose a threat to themselves or others, mental health courts, drug courts, veteran treatment courts, and behavioral health deflection programs. Funds support state crisis intervention programs including ERPO programs, training for ERPO program staff, communication and public awareness initiatives, and law enforcement funding for safe firearm storage and tracking.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act Regional Navigator Program (RNPG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Connects youth survivors of sex and labor trafficking (up to age 24) with trauma-informed services and support. Each county has a designated Navigator to coordinate care. Provides safety planning, case management, housing, mental health services, legal support, and screening for child sex trafficking. The program develops a network of regional navigators to coordinate and provide identified or confirmed child sex trafficking victims with specific services. Law enforcement and local Departments of Social Services notify Regional Navigators in their jurisdiction to obtain needed services for children identified as victims of sex trafficking. The program currently operates across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions and supports youth at high risk for trafficking.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided through Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) to support regional navigator positions and services for child sex trafficking screening and victim support. Funds can be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, training, and other eligible expenses. Supports direct services including safety planning, case management, housing, mental health services, legal support, forensic interviews, and public awareness. Regional navigators coordinate and deliver trauma-informed services to identified or confirmed child sex trafficking victims and youth at high risk for trafficking, including those engaged in concerning CSAM behaviors or exchanging CSAM.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth survivors of sex and labor trafficking up to age 24, youth at high risk for trafficking, youth engaged in concerning or extreme CSAM behaviors or exchanging CSAM, community-based nonprofit organizations, designated Child Advocacy Centers, Rape Crisis Centers, law enforcement agencies, and local Departments of Social Services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for personnel, operating expenses, contractual services, equipment, supplies, training, direct victim services including health/safety, mental health assistance, legal assistance, forensic interviews, case management, safety planning, housing coordination, public awareness, technology, and coordination activities to support regional navigator programming and delivery of services to child sex trafficking victims and youth at risk for trafficking.
