The program supports children's justice initiatives through contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other expenses. Development of innovative programming focused on front-end, intake, and investigative stages of child welfare. Direct services are not permitted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Use Program (COSSUP) / Comprehensive Opioid Use Site-based Program (COAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy that funds comprehensive opioid, stimulant, and substance use response efforts across Maryland communities. The program supports police-led diversion and deflection programming (including Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion/LEAD), detention-based referrals, evidence-based medication-assisted treatment, harm reduction, prevention, recovery support services, and coordination between criminal justice and health systems. The program is designed for short-term initiatives to expand existing programs (not for new program development/implementation), with priority given to expanding Medication for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD) and Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) for justice-involved individuals. The program is supported by federal funding distributed over multiple years, with Notices of Funding Availability released annually.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding distributed over multiple years to support police-led diversion and deflection programming, detention-based referrals, treatment access, opioid overdose prevention, harm reduction, recovery services, and workforce expansion efforts in Maryland. Funding is reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures. Allowable expenditure categories include personnel (salaries, fringe benefits, direct staff), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage, photocopying), equipment (items with useful life >1 year and cost ≥$10,000), contractual services, travel (mileage, transportation, meals, lodging per State of Maryland rates), training, and other justified project costs. Indirect costs up to 15% of Modified Total Direct Costs using de minimis rate if no negotiated rate exists. Funds must increase program activities beyond existing funding levels and cannot supplant State or local funds.

Funds support police-led diversion and deflection initiatives, Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD), detention-based referrals, medication-assisted treatment, harm reduction efforts, evidence-based substance use disorder treatment, prevention programs, recovery support services, and coordination between criminal justice and health systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: A remedial program that provides financial assistance and support to innocent victims of crime in Maryland. The program helps cover medical expenses for physical injuries, psychological injury treatment from certain crimes, lost wages due to inability to work after a crime, bereavement leave up to two weeks or $2,000, temporary or permanent disability costs, funeral expenses in homicide cases, loss of support when a homicide victim was providing the claimant's main support, up to 30 days in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for an injured child, crime scene cleanup, and other Board-approved expenses. The Board may also provide emergency and supplemental awards. CICB is the payer of last resort and all other reimbursements must be used before a possible award.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reimbursement for eligible expenses including medical and dental expenses related to physical injury; expenses for psychological injury from certain offenses; loss of earnings directly related to inability to work following the crime; bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000; total or partial permanent or temporary disability; funeral expenses in homicide cases; loss of support when a homicide victim was providing support; up to 30 days in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime; crime scene cleanup; and other expenses approved by the board. Minimum threshold of $100 in reimbursable expenses or lost wages required to qualify. For lost wages, victim must have lost at least two continuous weeks' earnings or support (or more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs). CICB is the payer of last resort and all other reimbursement must be used before a possible award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: within 3 years from the date of the crime or death of the victim; within 3 years of when the claimant knew or should have known of abuse in child abuse cases; 180 days of the crime
structured_extraction.program_audience: Innocent victims of crime in Maryland, including persons who suffer physical or psychological injury from crime; surviving family members of homicide victims; persons who assumed funeral expense responsibility for homicide victims; dependents of homicide victims; spouses or children of homicide victims; family members of incarcerated individuals who suffered abuse; crime victims or their guardians; persons injured while preventing a crime or assisting police; persons injured or killed by drunk drivers; secondary victims; and parents or legal guardians of minor victims (minimum 18 years old to apply).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical and dental expenses for physical injury; psychological treatment expenses from certain offenses; lost wages directly related to crime; bereavement leave; disability expenses; funeral and burial expenses; crime scene cleanup; loss of support; childcare-related lost wages for parents or guardians caring for injured children; and other board-approved expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves innocent victims of crime throughout Maryland statewide. The crime must have occurred in Maryland. Exceptions may apply for acts of terrorism.
requirements_list: Must be an innocent victim of crime
Report the crime to appropriate authorities within 48 hours of the crime occurring (unless good cause is shown)
Have incurred at least $100 in reimbursable expenses or lost wages
Cooperate with law enforcement authorities (unless good cause is shown for non-cooperation)
Not have substantially caused, provoked, or contributed to the crime that caused the injury
Crime must be reported to police within 3 years
To receive lost wages, victim must have lost at least two continuous weeks' earnings or support (or more than $100 in other unreimbursed eligible costs)
Claim must be filed within 3 years from the date of crime or death of victim (or within 3 years of discovering child abuse)
Physical injury or death must be directly related to the crime
Serious financial hardship must result from the crime
Claimant must be at least 18 years old (parents/guardians apply for minors)
Victim must not have been participating in crime during incident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a crime report with police within 48 hours of the crime. Victims submit an Application for Crime Victim Compensation. Claim forms are available from the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, online at the Department of Public Safety website in English and Spanish, or by calling (410) 585-3010. Complete and submit the claim form to the Board. The board provides claims examination with efficient processing, emergency and supplemental awards, interpretation services, and victim advocacy services including application assistance, status updates, resource referrals, coordination between involved parties, notification and accompaniment to hearings, and community education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward J. Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (BJAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (Maryland's State Administering Agency) that provides funding to support a broad range of state and local criminal justice initiatives critical to Maryland's public safety and effective criminal justice administration. The program supports initiatives that reduce gaps in service impacting violent crime, crime victims, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, rehabilitation, and behavioral health. Funding helps improve sentencing and correction policies, reduce crime, provide public safety, protect victims, track DNA, train local law enforcement, and provide technology to law enforcement. Funding is distributed to eligible government agencies, law enforcement, nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, and higher education institutions throughout Maryland. Local governments eligible per the BJAG Allocations List are eligible to apply for these grants on an annual basis. The program is funded by the Bureau of Justice Assistance under 34 U.S.C. 10151-10726.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding to support law enforcement and criminal justice programs and initiatives. Funds support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, training, and other eligible categories for criminal justice initiatives addressing violent crime, victim services, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, rehabilitation, and behavioral health. Funding is provided under the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program for successive fiscal years, allocated based on BJAG formulas. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis and must supplement, not supplant, existing state and local funding. Up to $2,000,000 available for SFY 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, nonprofit organizations (including community-based and faith-based), higher education institutions, and criminal justice coordinating council member organizations working on criminal justice initiatives. Units of local government eligible per the BJAG Allocations List.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs (salaries, wages, fringe benefits), equipment (with restrictions; $10,000+ per unit requires prior approval), operating expenses, supplies, contractual services, training and technical assistance, information systems, travel, and other expenses to support criminal justice programs addressing violent crime, victim services, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, rehabilitation, and behavioral health. Prohibited: luxury items, real estate, construction, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying, food/beverage, certain vehicles, drones, weapons systems, camouflage uniforms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland to eligible state and local agencies and organizations. Applicants must identify specific primary jurisdictions served with zip codes. Projects can serve statewide, county-wide, or local areas. Bonus points for projects partnering with Governor's Office for Children's ENOUGH Grant Program initiative (27 eligible communities with high concentrated child poverty).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), typically in August. Applicants must register on SAM.gov with a valid UEI by August 29, 2025. Applications are submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS) only, with deadline typically in September (September 10, 2025 for SFY 2026). Technical assistance calls are available to applicants. Eligible agencies work with the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy in connection with grant applications. Applications are reviewed and final selections are based on eligibility, relevance, and merit. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis upon approval and submission of quarterly reports.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides temporary shelter environments and supportive services through a network of local domestic violence services programs. It offers comprehensive services to meet the specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families, including prevention of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence; immediate shelter and supportive services for victims and their dependents; and specialized services for children exposed to violence, underserved populations, and victims from racial and ethnic minority populations. These programs help establish, maintain, and expand projects that increase the likelihood that victims will benefit from services and ensure appropriate linkages to other community-based services. The program fosters a coordinated community approach to serving domestic violence victims that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other related support agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support the establishment, maintenance, and expansion of domestic violence services programs. Eligible expenses include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports temporary shelter, supportive services, prevention services, specialized services for children exposed to violence, and services for underserved populations and racial and ethnic minority victims. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed through the Grant Management System (GMS). The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), which is projected for June. Applications are typically due in July.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to support local law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in developing and implementing strategies specifically intended to reduce gun-related crime in Maryland. The program supports goals of removing illegal firearms from communities and reinforcing prevention, disruption, and prosecution strategies. Eligible uses include contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other related costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 25 awards ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Total anticipated funding: $926,940 for SFY 2027. Grant funds support law enforcement agencies and prosecutors addressing firearms-related violence. Eligible uses include salaries and overtime for crime analysts, support staff, law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and legal staff; travel; contractual services; equipment; operating expenses; and other related costs. Quarterly reimbursement basis unless otherwise stated.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to law enforcement agencies and prosecutors across all Maryland jurisdictions. All Maryland counties are eligible; however, funding priority is given to entities not currently receiving MCIN funds. ENOUGH-eligible communities may receive bonus points.

structured_extraction.program_name: Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support the investigation and prosecution of internet crimes against children through funding for local law enforcement agencies, the Maryland Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, and designated child advocacy centers. Funds support salaries, training, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, and travel. The program aims to reduce victimization of Maryland's children by protecting them from abuse or neglect, addresses Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and impact of childhood trauma, and develops coordinated criminal justice strategies at state and local levels. Minimum $2 million allocated to local law enforcement and the Maryland Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. Up to 25% of funds may support child advocacy centers.

Minimum $2 million allocated to local law enforcement and the Maryland Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. Up to 25% of funds may support child advocacy centers. Funds distributed on quarterly reimbursement basis following timely submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports. Funds can be used for salaries, training, equipment, contractual services, operating expenses, travel, and other approved categories.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-booking/pre-arrest diversion program that allows law enforcement to connect eligible participants with intensive case management and community-based services instead of criminal justice involvement. The program uses a harm-reduction framework to divert individuals with substance use disorders and mental health disorders away from incarceration and toward treatment, recovery, and support services.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding from the U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) through COSSUP/COAP programs to support law enforcement and service provider partnerships for diversion programming. Funding supports intensive case management services, housing support (transitional and permanent), substance abuse treatment, mental health services, legal assistance, service coordination and referrals, trauma-informed case management, peer recovery coaching, and warm hand-offs to community-based treatment providers. Award amounts have ranged from $291,118 to $1,194,674. Funding also supports training for law enforcement and public health professionals, coordination with local stakeholders, and implementation of diversion and deflection programs for individuals with substance use disorders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law enforcement agencies, health departments, service providers, and individuals with substance use disorders and mental health disorders in participating Maryland counties. Includes justice-involved individuals, low-level offenders, youth and adults, individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability, and high-risk populations identified by law enforcement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Police-led diversion services, detention-based referrals, case management, substance use disorder treatment referrals, mental health counseling, job training and educational resources, benefit coordination, primary health care services, housing support, peer recovery coaching, trauma-informed case management, warm hand-offs to community-based treatment providers, medication-assisted treatment (MAT/MOUD), medical insurance assistance, harm-reduction services, and overdose prevention and treatment access programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide program with specific LEAD implementation and services in 10 counties plus Baltimore City: Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Carroll County, Frederick County, Harford County, Howard County, St. Mary's County, Washington County, Wicomico County, and Worcester County. Additional detention-based referral programs operate in some counties.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy awards federal funds to support law enforcement-led diversion efforts in designated Maryland communities. Applicant agencies must coordinate with state and local stakeholders including the Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Administration, Office of the Public Defender, health departments, law enforcement agencies, and community-based service providers. Subrecipients must complete and timely submit data, develop recruitment and retention strategies for program staff, and adhere to the LEAD model and Maryland's Implementation Manual.

Provides up to $5,000 per recipient to support specialized law enforcement training. Grant funds may be used for non-degree courses and to cover related expenses, including travel, lodging, registration fees, and training materials. In certain cases, funds may also be used to bring trainers directly to a law enforcement agency. Advances coordinated criminal justice strategies rooted in collaboration, information sharing, and knowledge transfer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Legal Services for Crime Victims Fund (LSCV)
structured_extraction.program_description: Administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, this fund provides Maryland crime victims with legal representation in the court system. The fund uses money from unclaimed restitution to award annual grants for legal counsel to help victims of crime and delinquent acts protect their rights. Annual grants are awarded based on unclaimed restitution collections, which fluctuate yearly. Legal counsel is defined as legal advice, consultation, or representation provided by a licensed attorney.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded to provide legal counsel for victims of crime and delinquent acts. Maximum award is $75,000 per organization with total funding of $150,000 available for approximately 2 awards. Funding period: July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027. Grants are reimbursable quarterly based on expenditures. Eligible expense categories include personnel (staff attorneys, directors of legal services), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage, printing), travel at Maryland state rates (72.5¢ per mile), contractual services, equipment, and other costs.

Non-profit agencies (including faith-based and community organizations), local government agencies, and state government agencies that provide statewide legal services to crime victims.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal counsel for victims of crime and delinquent acts, including legal advice, consultation, and representation by licensed attorneys. Funds can be used for personnel (staff attorneys, directors, fringe benefits up to 30% of salary), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage, printing), travel at Maryland state rates (72.5¢ per mile), contractual services (consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day), equipment ($10,000+ per unit), supplies, and other eligible costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Available throughout all Maryland counties and must be accessible in every Maryland jurisdiction including Baltimore City. Service providers must provide statewide legal counsel.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Warrant Apprehension & Absconding Grant Program (WAAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports law enforcement agencies across Maryland with reducing the number of open warrants, especially warrants for violent crimes, and apprehending individuals who have absconded from a court-ordered drug and alcohol treatment facility or supervision. The program aims to improve quality of life and create safer communities through violent crime reduction by apprehending wanted individuals, and supports the development of coordinated criminal justice strategies and data-driven decision-making.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support law enforcement agencies in warrant apprehension and absconding operations. Total anticipated funding is $1,000,000 for SFY 2026 with up to 30 awards available. Individual award amounts range from $10,000 to $75,000, tiered by agency size: small agencies (up to 50 sworn officers) receive up to $30,000; medium agencies (51-300 sworn officers) receive up to $50,000; large agencies (over 300 sworn officers) receive up to $75,000. Grants are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Funded categories include personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, travel, and other allowable costs.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies and local government agencies across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs (salaries, fringe benefits, overtime for officers serving warrants and analysts identifying wanted/absconded individuals); operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications, data entry); travel (mileage, transportation, meals, lodging per Maryland/GSA rates, extradition travel); contractual services (consultants); equipment (surveillance, communication systems); supplies for safe warrant execution (shackles, handcuffs, masks); and other eligible expenses related to warrant apprehension and absconding apprehension operations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Markell Hendricks Youth Crime Prevention and Diversion Parole Grant Program (YCPD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance to local law enforcement agencies for youth crime prevention and diversion programs in high-crime areas. Focuses on creating outreach and programming to divert youth who have committed threshold offenses from formal processing into the juvenile justice system, including youth involved in school-based offenses. Goal is to reduce the number of youth entering the juvenile justice system by providing supportive services within communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $50,000 available for SFY 2026 with anticipation of one (1) award. Funding supports personnel (diversion specialists, police officers, youth counselors), operating expenses, travel, contractual services, and equipment for youth crime prevention and diversion programs. Quarterly reimbursement basis. Intent of two additional years of level funding for SFY 2027 and SFY 2028, provided program is in good standing and demonstrating positive outcomes. Funding contingent on availability and subrecipient success through quantitative metrics.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Yvette Williams (Grant Monitor), Will VanWisse (Fiscal Grants Manager), and Jennifer Krabill (Funding Manager)

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel salaries and fringe benefits for diversion specialists, police officers, and youth counselors; operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications); travel expenses (mileage, meals, lodging); contractual services and consultant services; equipment ($10,000+ per unit) and supplies under $10,000; indirect costs with NICRA; case management, crisis intervention, group therapy, and partnerships and collaborations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability for eligible local law enforcement agencies serving high-crime areas. Priority given to Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_description: A coalition of criminal justice agencies that collaborates and coordinates tactics, resources, and intelligence through comprehensive data sharing, cross-jurisdictional partnerships, effective policies, and supporting technologies. MCIN focuses on identifying, disrupting, and dismantling gangs and violent criminal networks involved in the distribution of illegal drugs, the use of firearms in crimes of violence, human trafficking, or other inherently violent criminal enterprises through enforcement, prevention, intervention, and information sharing. The program provides funding to improve intelligence infrastructure and support strategies for collecting information that lead to investigations identifying and dismantling criminal networks, to employ subject matter experts trained to investigate such networks, and to pay for expert prosecutors to prosecute these cases at the federal and state levels.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that prevents incidents of family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence by making temporary shelter environments and supportive services available through a network of local domestic violence service programs. These programs support the establishment, maintenance, and expansion of comprehensive services to meet the specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families, including those in underserved communities and racial/ethnic minority populations. The program fosters a coordinated community approach to serving domestic violence victims that includes partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other related support agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide formula-based and competitive federal and state funding to support domestic violence prevention and victim services. Funding covers personnel salaries and fringe benefits, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, equipment, training, and other expenditures for services including 24-hour hotlines, safe accommodations, therapeutic counseling, legal counseling, court accompaniment, community awareness activities, abuse intervention programs, specialized services for children exposed to domestic violence, services for underserved populations and racial/ethnic minorities, and safety planning assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides advocacy and support services to victims of crime through the creation of new ideas and the enhancement of existing programs in Maryland. Administered by the State Board of Victim Services under the authority of the Governor to provide funding to victim services providers. The fund ensures implementation of the Declaration of Crime Victims' Rights Amendment to the Maryland Constitution and the Federal Guidelines for treatment of and assistance to crime victims and witnesses. Created by Maryland General Assembly in 1991 Legislative Session, supports child advocacy centers, and implements Article 47 of Maryland Declaration of Rights.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that assists community organizations, nonprofit organizations, and local governments to fund security operations during times of high pedestrian traffic in entertainment districts that experience a higher than average number of calls for police assistance in response to reported crimes. The program strengthens security through collaborative efforts among local governments, community organizations, and law enforcement by supporting enhanced security and crime prevention activities to reduce criminal activity, improve crowd management, and enhance public safety.

Grants are reimbursable on a quarterly basis, with monthly reimbursement available for nonprofits with awards over $50,000.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding from savings resulting from reforms under Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act. PIGF supports evidence-based programming to safely reduce Maryland's prison population, improve reentry outcomes, reduce impacts of incarceration on communities, provide resources to victims of crime, and connect nonviolent offenders with behavioral health needs to community treatment and support.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded through JRA savings. Eligible categories include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, other, personnel, and travel. Outcomes of funded programs are monitored by the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board and performance measures are set by the Local Government Justice Reinvestment Commission. Funding ranges: $50,000 - $450,000 with Category A (State agencies up to $450,000; Nonprofits up to $200,000) and Category B (Local government up to $350,000; Nonprofits up to $200,000).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other expenses for evidence-based programming related to reducing prison population, improving reentry outcomes, reducing incarceration impacts, providing victim resources, and connecting offenders with behavioral health treatment. Specific funding for reentry services and case management, workforce development and employment training, housing and transitional housing support, behavioral health services and mental health treatment, substance use disorder treatment and recovery support, educational programming, mentorship and peer support services, medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD), victim restitution infrastructure improvements, and deflection/diversion program implementation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Police Accountability, Community, and Transparency Grant (PACT)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports law enforcement agencies and criminal justice organizations across Maryland with developing effective accountability procedures to achieve lawfulness and legitimacy while enhancing community relations and transparency. The program supports efforts to advance public policy, enhance public safety, reduce crime and juvenile delinquency, and serve victims. Funds are intended to ensure law enforcement agencies comply with the Maryland Police Accountability Act of 2021 requirements by July 1, 2026, while increasing safety and training for law enforcement, promoting safe communities, and encouraging community engagement between law enforcement and the communities they serve.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Anticipated $4 million in total grant funding with plans to make up to 50 awards ranging from $20,000 to $300,000. Grants are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Funds can be used for personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits, staff hiring, mental health professionals, victim advocates, training providers), operating expenses (Police Accountability Board/Committee startup/expansion, rental space, printing, communications), travel (officer training attendance, project meetings, mileage, lodging, meals per state rates), contractual services (consultants, training providers, evaluation services), equipment (body-worn cameras, weapon/holster notification systems, VR training simulators, $10,000+ per unit), software (Early Intervention Systems, misconduct databases), supplies, and other allowable costs ($10,000 or less equipment). Funding prioritized for projects aligning with established PACT Grant Program priorities. Federal funds must supplement, not supplant, existing state/local funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Program for Preventing Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection for Rape Victims
structured_extraction.program_description: Established under Chapter 431 of 2019, this pilot program provides eligible victims of alleged rape, sexual offense, or child sexual abuse with a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care for the prevention of HIV infection. The program reimburses physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies for nPEP therapy and related follow-up care when a victim is at risk for contracting HIV as a result of sexual assault. Pharmacies receive established rates as determined by the Health Services Cost Review Commission. The program also covers forensic medical services, medical screening, laboratory services, medications (antibiotics, emergency contraception), vaccines, and HIV follow-up care referrals.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement program that pays for a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care for sexual assault victims at risk of HIV infection. Reimbursement covers nPEP therapy, medication, HIV testing, laboratory services (HIV rapid test, CBC, CMP, Hepatitis panel, pregnancy tests), sexual assault forensic exams, and related follow-up care provided by physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies. Pharmacies receive established rates as determined by the Health Services Cost Review Commission. The medication regimen must begin within 72 hours of the sexual assault. Follow-up care within 180 days of the sexual assault is reimbursed. The total amount paid annually may not exceed $750,000. Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of alleged rape, sexual offense, or child sexual abuse in Maryland who are at risk of HIV infection. Reimbursement is provided to physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) medication, HIV exposure risk assessment, laboratory testing (HIV rapid test, CBC, CMP, Hepatitis panel, pregnancy tests), sexual assault forensic exams, and follow-up care for prevention of HIV infection following alleged sexual assault. The medication regimen follows Centers for Disease Control guidelines and includes recommended follow-up care at four to six weeks, three months, and six months. Medications include antibiotics, emergency contraception, and vaccines as part of comprehensive sexual assault response.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Services provided for crimes occurring in Maryland or other states are eligible. Services provided outside Maryland will not be reimbursed. The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy has partnered with Terrapin Pharmacy, a Maryland-based pharmacy, to provide medication to patients when hospitals cannot provide the full 28-day medication supply.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Victims receive nPEP medication through participating medical providers and pharmacies. Forensic Nurse Examiners or healthcare providers determine eligibility and assess HIV exposure risk. Physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies should complete the nPEP Reimbursement Form and/or SAFE Reimbursement Form in their entirety and submit it within 90 days from date of service with documentation of the nPEP treatment and follow-up care provided. Reimbursement is made from the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund. Contact SARU at saru.claims@maryland.gov or 410-697-9338 for questions. An HIV Patient Navigator assists with cost and reimbursement questions. The National Clinician Consultation Center (888-448-4911, Monday-Friday 9am-8pm EST; weekends/holidays 11am-8pm) is available for PEP consultations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, government agencies, and other entities with facilities and membership that can be targeted for hate crimes. The program was established in 2020 to help nonprofits enhance security measures for facilities at risk of hate crimes and addresses documented and recent risks of hate crime victimization. The program supports security enhancements and the development of criminal justice and victim services strategies through collaboration between law enforcement, victim services, and communities targeted for hate crimes. Funding supports efforts to prevent and respond to hate crimes in Maryland communities, focusing on organizations serving or having members from protected classes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Substance Abuse Treatment (RSAT) for State Prisoners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing funding for residential substance abuse treatment services in correctional and detention facilities. Assists state and local government agencies in developing and implementing substance use disorder treatment programs in state, local, and tribal correctional and detention facilities. Serves pre-trial defendants, individuals in correctional facilities, and citizens in need of post-incarceration treatment and community reintegration assistance. Also creates and maintains community reintegration services for offenders after release from incarceration. The program aims to break the cycle of drugs and violence by reducing demand for, use, and trafficking of illegal drugs. Programs may include residential, jail-based, and aftercare components with relapse prevention and community reintegration services.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to states and units of local and tribal government for developing and implementing residential substance abuse treatment programs. Funds may be used to implement residential, jail-based, and aftercare programs including medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorders, reentry planning, community-based treatment, and case management. Grant funding is distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Categories of funding available include personnel (treatment counselors, case managers, program directors), equipment, operating expenses, travel, contractual services, and other project-related costs. Consultant rates capped at $81.25/hour or $650/day unless pre-approved.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State prisoners and detainees in jails with substance use disorders; pre-trial defendants; individuals in correctional facilities; citizens in need of post-incarceration treatment and community reintegration assistance; individuals with co-occurring substance use disorder and mental health disorders. Applications involving partnerships with community-based substance abuse treatment programs will be given priority consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and implementation of substance abuse treatment programs in correctional and detention facilities; residential treatment programs lasting at least 6 months; medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorders; integrated treatment for co-occurring substance use disorder and mental health disorders; trauma-informed programming with evidence-based group and individual treatment services; urinalysis testing; aftercare/reentry services and community reintegration; phased programming based on behavioral and recovery milestones; personnel (salaries, fringe benefits, treatment counselors, case managers); operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications, supplies, facility costs); travel and per diem; contractual services with treatment providers; equipment; software licenses; educational materials. Excluded: alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction/renovation, fundraising, lobbying, meals, trinkets, prizes/entertainment, vehicles, UAS/UAV, supplanting state/local funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: STOP (Services, Training, Officers, Prosecutors) Violence Against Women Formula Grant Program (STOP VAWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program encourages the development and strengthening of effective, victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, and court strategies to combat violent crimes against women in Maryland. It funds law enforcement, prosecution, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers, and supports criminal justice entities in holding offenders accountable. The program allocates funds in specific ratios: 25% to law enforcement, 25% to prosecution, 30% to nonprofit victim services, and 5% to court entities, with up to 15% at state discretion. Ten percent of victim service allocation must support linguistically and culturally specific services for underserved populations. At least 20% of total funds must meaningfully address sexual assault. The program also provides comprehensive support for addressing domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, strangulation, and sex-trafficking through training, victim services, court improvements, and community coordination.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula grants distributed among victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers. Funds can support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other eligible categories. Funding supports specialized training and certification programs, victim advocacy positions, 24/7 hotlines, shelter, counseling, legal representation, court advocacy, and coordinated community response teams. Services must be culturally competent and trauma-informed.

Primary beneficiaries include domestic violence survivors, sexual assault survivors, dating violence victims, stalking victims, sex-trafficking victims, and underserved populations including immigrant/refugee communities, LGBTQ+ individuals, disabled persons, deaf/hard of hearing individuals, and those with limited English proficiency.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reimbursement for physical examinations, evidence collection, and emergency treatment of individuals injured from alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. The program reimburses hospitals, physicians, pharmacies, and laboratories directly on behalf of victims to prevent re-victimization and ease the medical-forensic claims process. Includes coverage for forensic medical examination services, laboratory services, medications, and HIV prophylaxis (nPEP).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct reimbursement to medical providers (physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, laboratories) for medical-forensic services. Physicians receive usual and customary fees not to exceed $80 for rape or sexual offense exams, or $80 per hour up to 5 hours for child sexual abuse cases. Hospitals receive established rates from Health Services Cost Review Commission for emergency room, outpatient clinic, and in-hospital care. Laboratories and pharmacies receive established rates for laboratory tests and HIV prophylaxis medication. Full course of nPEP (non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis) medication provided at no cost to eligible survivors. Drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) testing reimbursement available for qualified forensic toxicology laboratories.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Aid for Police Protection Fund (SAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A formula-driven funding program that provides financial assistance to counties and qualifying municipalities to help offset costs associated with local law enforcement services. The program is intended to ensure residents throughout the State have access to adequate police protection regardless of jurisdiction's tax base or fiscal capacity. State funds supplement resources for police protection in local communities through two primary funding components: Formula Funds and Enhancement Funds (based on violent crime rates per UCR). Funds are distributed based on a formula derived through a subdivision's population, number of police officers in the agency, total jurisdictional taxable income, and crime rates. Annual fund distributions are calculated according to the previous year's operations costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supplemental funding to promote equitable access to effective law enforcement services and support consistent public safety standards across Maryland. Funds are allocated through Formula Funds and Enhancement Funds. The formula includes: expenditures for police protection, basic/over-basic expenditure shares, minimum/incentive/additional grants, crime lab adjustments, D.C. proximity adjustment, municipal grant, and supplemental grant. Funds are distributed quarterly via Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT). No match is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: State's Attorney's Office Case Automation System Enhancement Grant Program (SACM)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program assists State's Attorney Offices in establishing or enhancing automated case management systems to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of case management through advanced technology solutions. The program aims to modernize case management using advanced technology, improve data accuracy and efficiency in case tracking and decision-making, and support fairness and equity by tracking key data on defendants and victims.

The program serves nonprofit and faith-based organizations throughout Maryland. It focuses on improving victim services through resources that assist victims in achieving self-sufficiency, improving victim safety, and increasing awareness of victim rights and available resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title II Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention Formula Grant (JJAC)
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds support reform in Maryland's juvenile justice system and focus on initiatives and strategies that support the Developmental Approach to Juvenile Justice Reform, including accountability without criminalization, alternatives to justice system involvement, individualized response based on assessment of needs and risks, confinement only when necessary for public safety, fairness, sensitivity to disparate treatment, and family engagement. The program aims to improve outcomes for children and youth within the juvenile justice system by increasing and strengthening programs in the areas of aftercare and reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation. The program expands community-based alternatives to confinement and brings the state into compliance with federal limitations on holding youth in adult jails or lock-ups using a developmentally appropriate and trauma-informed framework.

Funds are distributed on a reimbursable quarterly basis (or monthly for nonprofits with awards over $50,000) based on actual expenditures. Eligible categories include personnel (direct salaries, wages, and fringe benefits), operating expenses, travel, contractual services, equipment, supplies and materials, training, registration fees, and other costs related to juvenile justice initiatives. A 10% cost-sharing requirement applies. Funds support programs focusing on aftercare, reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports effective violence reduction strategies, specifically gun violence, through evidence-based and evidence-informed health programs. These programs use public health principles to demonstrate measurable positive outcomes in preventing gun violence. The program also supports hospital-based violence intervention programs that provide intensive counseling, case management, and social services to individuals recovering from violence-related injuries. Grant funding supports violence intervention and prevention initiatives across Maryland communities, serving community organizations, nonprofits, government agencies, academic institutions, and independent researchers focused on violence prevention. The program is established by §4–902 of the Public Safety Article.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants supporting violence intervention and prevention initiatives. Maximum award: $300,000. Period of award: July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027. Mandatory 33% cash or in-kind cost share required. Funding can be used for personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits up to 30%), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel, contractual services, equipment ($10,000+ per unit with useful life >1 year), and other approved categories for evidence-based or evidence-informed violence reduction programs and hospital-based violence intervention programs. Grant funds issued on quarterly, reimbursable basis. Acceptable program models include Hospital-based Violence Intervention Programs (HVIPs), Street Outreach (e.g., Cure Violence Global), Cognitive Behavioral Theory (CBT), Group Violence Intervention (GVI), Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED), adapted versions of existing models, or locally developed approaches informed by research and best practices.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Melissa Bitting (Grant Monitor), Sharon Leason (Fund Manager), and Abangolee (Lee) Caulcrick (Fiscal Grants Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofit organizations, county government agencies, nonprofit faith-based organizations, nonprofit institutes of higher learning, local government agencies, local health departments, local hospitals, local law enforcement, state government agencies, state law enforcement, and State's Attorney's Offices working to reduce community gun violence, particularly in disproportionately impacted communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel (salaries, wages, fringe benefits up to 30%), operating expenses (rental space, printing, communications), travel (mileage, transportation, meals, lodging per Maryland rates), contractual services (behavioral healthcare, clinical providers, training providers, consultants, evaluation), equipment ($10,000+ per unit with useful life >1 year), project supplies and office supplies, training and professional development, staff development, program implementation and evaluation activities, technical assistance, crisis response and short-term stabilization services, case management, mentoring and advocacy services, conflict resolution and mediation activities, referrals to supportive services (behavioral health, employment, education, housing), and street outreach and violence interruption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must define and provide zip codes for catchment areas and service sites. Projects can be local (specific county), multijurisdictional (multiple counties), or statewide (all Maryland counties).

structured_extraction.program_name: Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) and Victims' Fund

The Anne Arundel County component provides direct financial reimbursement to crime victims for losses directly caused by their victimization, including emergency home repairs for safety, insurance deductibles, and replacement of items needed to resume school or work.

structured_extraction.program_description: A socioeconomic procurement program that directs participating state agencies to spend part of fiscal year procurement expenditures with certified MBE businesses. The program ensures socially and economically disadvantaged small, minority, and women-owned businesses have access to state procurement and contracting opportunities. It structures procurement procedures to establish MBE goals and sub-goals. The program provides certification that gives eligible businesses greater economic opportunities through procurement advantages, with a statewide aspirational goal of 29% participation across 70 participating state agencies and departments. Support includes access to the T.I.P.S. Small Business Webinar Series (free training offered twice monthly), MBE certification, monthly application assistance workshops, and connections with MBE Liaisons in participating agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program facilitates access to state procurement and contracting opportunities for certified minority-owned, women-owned, and small businesses. Certified MBEs can have their work counted toward established contract goals on state-funded contracts. MBEs can perform as prime contractors or subcontractors. Credit toward MBE goals varies by type: manufacturers and furnish and install services receive 100% credit, suppliers/wholesalers/regular dealers receive 60% credit, and brokers receive credit for reasonable fees/commissions only. Support includes access to the T.I.P.S. Small Business Webinar Series (free training offered twice monthly), MBE certification through the Office of Minority Business Enterprise, monthly application assistance workshops, and connections with MBE Liaisons in participating agencies across 70 state agencies and departments. Access to state procurement contracts is available through the eMMA (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage) system.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State procurement expenditures for goods and services; state contract work; participation in state procurement solicitations for goods, services, manufacturing, or furnish and install work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland with participation from 70 state agencies and departments; procurement of goods and services for Maryland DHS and 24 local social services departments.

Firms should connect with the MBE Liaison at their participating agency when named to perform on a contract. structured_extraction.program_description: A procurement program that provides Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) with a designated price preference when bidding on state contracts, allowing small businesses to win contracts even if their bid is slightly higher than non-small business competitors.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBP Program provides a base price preference of up to 5% of the total contract value for Certified Small Businesses. An additional 2% preference may be added for veteran-owned small businesses and an additional 3% preference may be added for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses. Procurement agencies will accept the most favorable responsive bid from a responsible CSB if the bid does not exceed the most favorable responsive bid from a non-small business by the applicable preference percentage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Small Businesses (CSBs), including veteran-owned and disabled-veteran-owned small businesses, seeking to bid on state contracts with a competitive price advantage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not specified - program provides price preference advantage rather than direct financial assistance.

Additional documentation may be required to verify CSB eligibility prior to award
Veteran-owned or disabled-veteran-owned status must be verified for additional preference
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First become certified as a Certified Small Business (CSB) by registering on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA), completing the online self-certification application, and attesting to meeting the CSB Eligibility Standards. structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program provides Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) with socioeconomic procurement advantages and greater economic opportunities by establishing an exclusive marketplace where small businesses compete only against other small businesses rather than larger, more established companies. Under the enhanced program announced in January 2021, all executive branch procurement units must reserve procurements valued between $50,000 and $500,000 for small business bidding. The program designates approximately 20% of all open state-funded solicitations advertised on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) as SBR procurements, where only Certified Small Businesses can be awarded contracts as prime contractors. This creates a level playing field and provides certification and procurement advantages to eligible small businesses seeking to bid on and win state contracts. Directs participating state agencies to spend part of their fiscal year procurement expenditures with certified SBR businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBR Program designates approximately 20% of all open state-funded solicitations advertised on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) as SBR procurements. When a solicitation is designated as SBR, only Certified Small Businesses can be awarded the contract as prime contractors. The program reserves government contracts valued between $50,000 and $500,000 for small businesses, with state agencies encouraged to consider higher dollar procurements as well. This gives small businesses exclusive bidding opportunities on state contracts and procurement advantages through certification, allowing them to compete only against other small businesses rather than larger established companies. Reserved procurement opportunities exclusively for certified small businesses to compete as prime contractors.

Participants can sign up to receive email notifications when registration opens each month. structured_extraction.program_description: Free training sessions for small business owners, entrepreneurs, and individuals including minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses. The program offers both in-person classroom sessions and virtual webinars conducted throughout the year. In-person classes are held on the fourth Tuesday of each month (except December) at the Governor's Coordinating Offices at 100 Community Place in Crownsville, Anne Arundel County, with morning sessions at 10 am and afternoon sessions at 2 pm. Virtual webinars are conducted twice monthly at 10 a.m. Classes are 2 hours long and taught by subject-matter experts from state agencies, small business resource organizations, and experienced small business owners. Topics covered include state and federal procurement processes, e-Procurement platform navigation, prevailing wage laws, cash flow management, federal contracting, negotiation strategies and closing techniques, proposal writing, capabilities statements, contract price analysis, financial capacity building, business communication, contract management, prime contracting, emergency preparedness, small business operations, business planning, and networking. Participants receive instructor slide decks and video recordings for later reference.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's VSBE Program is a socioeconomic procurement program that provides contracting opportunities on state-funded procurements for qualified veteran-owned small businesses. The state directs designated agencies and departments to spend at least 3% of the dollar value of their procurement contracts with certified VSBE firms. Certification is free and firms must renew every 3 years. The program helps veteran-owned businesses compete for state contracts as prime contractors or subcontractors, providing greater economic opportunities through certification and procurement advantages. Registered vendors receive email notices of procurement opportunities from state agencies and departments valued over $15,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program certifies veteran-owned small businesses and provides them access to state-funded procurement contracts as prime contractors or subcontractors. There is no cost to register in the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform or to obtain VSBE certification. Registered vendors receive email notices of procurement opportunities from state agencies and departments valued over $15,000. Firms must renew certification every 3 years effective September 1st, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnership Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County receives annual HUD entitlement grants through the CDBG and HOME programs to address serious community challenges and expand affordable housing. The CDBG Program funds projects providing decent affordable housing, services to vulnerable populations, job creation, and business opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons. The HOME Program provides grants to expand the supply of decent, safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for low-income families and to expand the capacity of nonprofit Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to develop and manage affordable housing. Funding can be spent on housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services for the benefit of the County's low- to moderate-income citizens. Projects and activities must be submitted to and approved by HUD through a 5-year Consolidated Plan. Harford County receives annual allocations as an entitlement jurisdiction and distributes funds to nonprofit organizations, CHDOs, and in some cases for-profit entities to support capital projects benefiting low- to moderate-income persons, reduce slum and blight, and expand affordable housing supply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County receives annual CDBG and HOME allocations from HUD as an entitlement jurisdiction. Funding amounts depend on a pre-determined HUD formula. Funds are distributed annually to nonprofit organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and in some cases for-profit entities and government agencies throughout Harford County. CDBG funds support capital projects benefiting low- to moderate-income persons or reducing slum and blight, including housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services. HOME funds support affordable rental housing, supportive housing with services, and capacity building for nonprofits and CHDOs. The county requires a 25% non-federal match for HOME activities. Affordability requirements for HOME-assisted properties vary: $15,000 to $40,000 assistance requires 15 years affordability; over $40,000 requires 15 years; new construction rental housing requires 20 years; refinanced rental housing requires 15 years. Funds are not available to individuals directly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)(3) status, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), nonprofit developers, existing housing programs, government entities, and in some cases for-profit entities in Harford County serving low- to moderate-income persons. Community development organizations and housing-related entities.

Activities must meet one of three national objectives: (1) benefit low-to-moderate-income persons through housing, limited clientele benefit, area benefit, or jobs; (2) address slum and blight; or (3) address urgent needs. HOME: Activities that improve housing opportunities and expand affordable housing supply including affordable rental housing, supportive housing with services such as case management and job readiness training, and capacity building for nonprofits and CHDOs. Funding can support housing, infrastructure, revitalization, and services. Community development activities and housing investments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County offers agricultural land preservation programs to protect productive agricultural land and woodland, ensuring the continued production of food and fiber and supporting agriculture's vital role in the local economy. The program includes two options: (1) Purchase of Development Rights Program allows agricultural landowners to permanently preserve their property by selling development rights to the county or state, receiving payment and extinguishing all development potential through easement contracts. Landowners retain full ownership of the land but are unable to subdivide for commercial or residential purposes, with the easement binding all subsequent property owners. (2) Agricultural Preservation District is a five-year commitment program that limits subdivision of agricultural parcels in exchange for property tax credits of $50 per acre, offsetting up to 50 percent of the parcel's Harford County property tax. Both programs allow landowners to continue food and fiber production. The district agreement and tax credit remain in effect after the five-year term until the property owner requests termination.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County offers two preservation options: (1) Purchase of Development Rights where landowners receive payment for selling development rights to the county or state, with the property thereafter subject to an easement prohibiting future development and the landowner retaining full fee simple ownership while being bound by easement terms that prevent further commercial or residential subdivision; (2) Agricultural Preservation District providing property tax credits of $50 per acre, offsetting up to 50 percent of parcel property tax, with credits remaining in effect for five years and continuing indefinitely unless terminated. Both programs include property tax credits of up to $50 per acre, not to exceed 50% of county real property taxes. Landowners receive payment for selling their development rights and/or a tax credit. Minimum requirement: at least 50 acres in both county and state programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Harford County landowners with at least 50 acres seeking to preserve their property and limit subdivision, with preference for owners of at least 50 acres interested in preserving agricultural land and woodland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preserving agricultural land and woodland for continued food and fiber production through easement agreements and property tax credits for agricultural properties committed to limiting subdivision; development rights purchase payments and tax credits for agricultural land and woodland preservation; enables continuation of food and fiber production

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Enterprise Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A designated geographic zone program in Aberdeen, Havre de Grace, Edgewood, and Joppa that provides tax credits to businesses that invest in Enterprise Zone areas. The program encourages job creation, business retention and expansion, and development of vacant or underutilized properties in older industrial areas. Two types of tax credits are available: Local Real Property Tax Credits (up to 10 years on capital investments, 80% credit on increases in assessed value for first five years, then decreases 10% annually for remaining five years) and State Income/Job Tax Credits (one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created, or $6,000 total per economically-disadvantaged employee distributed over three years).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits: Local Real Property Tax Credits (up to 10 years on capital investments, 80% credit on increases in assessed value for first five years, then decreases 10% annually for remaining five years) and State Income/Job Tax Credits (one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created, or $6,000 total per economically-disadvantaged employee distributed over three years). Credits support capital investments in construction and renovation of real property within designated Enterprise Zones and job creation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments in construction and renovation of real property within the Enterprise Zone, job creation, and business operations in designated Enterprise Zones.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A county tax credit program for property owners who complete qualified historic rehabilitation and restoration work on Harford County Historic Landmarks. The program provides tax credits based on the increased assessment value resulting from rehabilitation or restoration, as well as a tax credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses up to $7,500 (capped at $7,500 for expenses of $75,000 or more). Credits reduce real property taxes for certified historic properties designated by the Historic Preservation Commission and must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a tax credit that reduces county real property taxes based on the amount their assessment increased due to rehabilitation or restoration, plus a tax credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses up to $7,500 (based on expenses of $75,000; expenses may exceed $75,000 but the 10% tax credit is capped at $7,500). There is no limit on the number of tax credits granted; however a previous tax credit amount must be exhausted before another credit can be granted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of Harford County Historic Landmarks seeking to rehabilitate or restore their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses for historic properties designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only within Harford County. Properties must be designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks by the County Council or certified historic properties designated by the Historic Preservation Commission.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as a Harford County Historic Landmark by the County Council or certified as a historic property by the Historic Preservation Commission
Rehabilitation plans must be approved by the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission through an Application for Certificate of Appropriateness (COA) prior to conducting any work
Work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines
Applicant must obtain Certificate of Appropriateness before beginning work
When the project is complete, applicant must submit a Certification of Completed Work Application
Work must be certified as completed according to plans approved in the COA and adhering to Historic Preservation Guidelines
Staff site visit and review by the Historic Preservation Commission at their monthly public meeting required prior to approving the application
Itemized expenses spreadsheet must be submitted with the Certification of Completed Work Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Part 1: Submit an Application for Certificate of Appropriateness to the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission for approval of rehabilitation plans prior to beginning work. Part 2: Upon project completion, submit a Certification of Completed Work Application with an itemized expenses spreadsheet. A staff site visit and review by the Historic Preservation Commission at their monthly public meeting will occur prior to final approval. A fillable tax credit application form is available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports festivals, events, exhibits and other programming initiatives that foster collaboration between two or more organizations to attract visitors from outside the county's borders and drive overnight hotel stays within the county. Funds are used for direct tourism-related marketing costs and event expenses. Grants are awarded to the lead nonprofit partner organization, which is responsible for distributing funds to partner organizations based on the agreement outlined in the application. Funding amounts are determined by the County Executive at their discretion based on committee recommendations.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified nonprofit organizations that are tourism-related (whose activities, events, and programs primarily attract visitors from outside the borders of Harford County with a targeted approach to result in one or more overnight hotel stays) and Harford County municipalities. Applicants must be 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) organizations in good standing with the State of Maryland and registered in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct tourism-related marketing costs and event expenses for festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming. Funds cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, capital building projects, retirement, debt reduction, or equipment such as computers and copiers used for daily office functions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Harford County. Nonprofit organizations must be registered in Harford County with the State of Maryland to be eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) organization or Harford County municipality
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must be in good standing with Maryland Office of the Secretary of State, Charitable Organization Division
Nonprofit organizations must be registered in Harford County with the State of Maryland
Requires partnerships between two or more organizations (for-profit partnerships must have nonprofit as lead recipient)
Activities and events must primarily attract visitors from outside the borders of Harford County
Must demonstrate focus on attracting overnight hotel stays
Events or programs must align to create overnight travel opportunities and be held over an extended period or consecutive days
Must demonstrate ability to pursue additional funding sources
Must provide letters of commitment from all partnering organizations
Must have track record of delivering successful initiatives
If history of non-compliance with past Harford County grant programs, funding may be denied or disbursed in installments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through an online portal. Applicants must provide detailed documentation including lists of board members and key staff, proof of good standing status, 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) documentation, most recently filed Form 990, balance sheets and income statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024, letters of support from all partnering organizations, and a proposed budget for grant funds only. The review committee evaluates applications based on criteria including collaboration, overnight stay incentives, cultural and recreational offerings, and community economic impact. The County Executive makes final funding decisions based on committee recommendations.
