structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded rent subsidy program administered by county Public Housing Agencies that helps very low-income families, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and other low-income individuals afford decent, safe, and sanitary rental housing in the private market. Eligible households receive a voucher that allows them to rent units of their choice, including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments, with the program subsidizing a portion of the rent. The program uses a waiting list system with local preferences for applicants who live or work in their county, including families with dependent children, working families, elderly families, disabled families, veterans, surviving spouses of veterans, and homeless individuals. Monthly housing assistance payments are made to landlords on behalf of tenants, with tenants paying the remaining rent from their own resources. Rental units must meet health and safety standards and Housing Quality Standards, are inspected prior to contract signing and at least annually thereafter, and must comply with all State and County codes. Payment standards and allowable rent limits vary by bedroom size and jurisdiction. Families can remain in the program as long as they are eligible based on income and family composition and remain in compliance with family obligations, provided funding continues. The program promotes housing choice and economic self-sufficiency, and allows portability options where families may find housing within or outside Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County; Cecil County; Baltimore County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families receive a Housing Choice Voucher that subsidizes a portion of their monthly rent payments for eligible housing units. Vouchers allow eligible tenants to find their own housing in the private market, including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments. Household income must meet federal Income Limit Guidelines for very low-income families, extremely low-income families, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities. The Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contract between the landlord and the housing authority determines the maximum subsidy based on HUD-established fair market rents and payment standards. Monthly housing assistance payments are made to landlords on behalf of tenants, with tenants paying the remaining rent from their own resources. Families must find housing within 60-120 days that meets Housing Quality Standards and allowable rent limits. Families can remain in the program as long as they are eligible based on income and family composition and remain in compliance with their family obligations. Rental units must meet Livability Code standards and Housing Quality Standards for health and safety, comply with all State and County codes, and are inspected prior to contract signing and at least annually thereafter. Rent must be reasonable compared to other rents in the neighborhood. Families may find housing within or outside Maryland using the program's portability option where available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing waiting list (varies by county; Baltimore County currently not accepting preliminary applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income families, the elderly, persons with disabilities, single people, families and individuals with incomes below set income limits seeking rental housing assistance. Local preferences include applicants who live or work in their county, families with dependent children, working families, elderly families, disabled families, veterans, surviving spouses of veterans, and homeless individuals. Selection based on date and time of application with local/county preference.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental assistance for eligible housing units in the private market that meet health and safety standards and Housing Quality Standards, including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments. The family's present dwelling may qualify. Units must meet housing quality standards and rent must be reasonable compared to other rents in the neighborhood. Units may be located within or outside Maryland where portability options exist.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Application: Family completes preliminary application and head of household's name is placed on the Housing Agency's waiting list. 2. Selection: Name is selected based on date and time of application with preference given to county residents (approximately 3 years wait time for Cecil County). 3. Enrollment: When selected from the waiting list, enrollment interview is scheduled and eligibility is determined. At interview, families must provide required documentation including Social Security numbers, citizenship or immigration status, and detailed income and family information. 4. Certification: If eligible, family attends briefing session on program operations, rules, regulations, and family obligations. 5. Housing selection: Family finds housing within 60-120 days that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards and allowable rent limits, and may select housing within or outside Maryland where portability exists. 6. Housing review: Voucher holder reviews Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Certification Requirements and ensures property meets minimum performance standards including smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. 7. Landlord notification: Voucher holder presents Request for Lease Approval form to owner. 8. Owner submission: Owner completes and returns the form to the Housing office. 9. Rent verification: Housing office verifies rent is at or below fair market rent for the area and is reasonable compared to other rents in the neighborhood. 10. Inspection: Housing office schedules and conducts HCV inspection. 11. Remediation: Owner corrects any deficiencies if unit does not pass inspection. 12. Lease negotiation: Family agrees with landlord on lease terms and owner enters into lease agreement with tenant. 13. Contract finalization: Housing office finalizes Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) contract details and determines approval or disapproval of lease and unit. 14. Program participation: Upon approval, Housing Agency and landlord enter into contract on behalf of family, and owner begins receiving monthly housing assistance payments with remainder of rent paid by tenant. Application status can be checked by calling 1-877-204-9098 or contacting your local Housing Agency.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that stabilizes neighborhoods affected by foreclosures and abandonment through the purchase and redevelopment of foreclosed, abandoned, and short-sale homes. The program provides grants to states, units of general local government, nonprofit entities, and consortia to acquire, rehabilitate, demolish, and redevelop foreclosed and abandoned properties. Acquired and rehabilitated houses were sold to households earning at or below 120% of the Area Median Income, with at least 25% of funds serving households at or below 50% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding for neighborhood stabilization activities including acquisition of foreclosed and abandoned properties at discounted prices, rehabilitation to meet applicable codes and standards, demolition of blighted structures (limited to 10% without exception), land banking, homebuyer assistance, housing counseling, and general administration (up to 10%). Financing mechanisms include soft-seconds, loan loss reserves, and shared-equity loans. All benefits must serve persons at or below 120% of area median income, with 25% of funds serving persons at or below 50% of area median income. Grantees must expend 50% of NSP2 funds within 2 years and 100% within 3 years. Properties must be purchased at minimum 1% discount per property and 5% average discount across all properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fixed-rate loan product set 1% below market rate that helps homebuyers and homeowners purchase and rehabilitate homes in eligible Healthy Neighborhoods throughout Baltimore City. The program uses a "two close" loan structure: a short-term construction loan that is refinanced into a long-term permanent loan upon renovation completion. The program targets specific blocks with high homeownership and engaged residents to strengthen the real estate market and community connections. Loans are available in target blocks of neighborhoods including Liberty Heights (Ashburton, Callaway-Garrison, Central Forest Park, Concerned Citizens of Forest Park, Dorchester, Forest Park, Garwyn Oaks, Hanlon-Longwood, Howard Park, and West Forest Park), Belair-Edison, Berea, and Four By Four, as well as 60+ other Healthy Neighborhoods designated communities in Baltimore. Borrowers contribute 3% of the purchase price from their own funds and may borrow up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraisal value. No private mortgage insurance is required. Design assistance from an architectural firm is available to help plan improvements and review contractor proposals. Maximum loan amount is $375,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-rate loan set 1% below market rate for purchasing and rehabilitating homes using a two-close structure (short-term construction loan refinanced into long-term permanent loan upon completion). After a 3% down payment from personal funds, borrowers may finance up to 110% of the after-rehabilitation appraisal value of the property. Maximum loan amount is $375,000. No private mortgage insurance required. Interest-only payments during construction period; principal + interest + escrow upon completion. Design assistance from an architectural firm is available. Properties may contain 1-4 properly zoned residential units. Minimum 45-day processing timeline recommended (60 days for complex renovations). If a neighborhood does not have target blocks listed, the loan product can be used in the entire neighborhood.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prospective homebuyers intending to be owner-occupants in Healthy Neighborhoods designated communities, interested in purchasing and rehabilitating homes in eligible target blocks and neighborhoods of Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers tax credits to owners of commercial and industrial properties located along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County to support transformational economic development, business development, and revitalization. The program provides a tax credit up to a maximum of $100,000 per property. Eligible applicants may receive up to 125% of approved expenses if costs exceed the initial estimate, not to exceed the $100,000 cap. The full credit is available over five years if the property's taxes are high enough. The credit stays with the property, not the owner, if it is sold.
structured_extraction.agency: Howard County Department of Planning & Zoning
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit up to a maximum of $100,000 per property. You may be eligible for up to 125% of approved expenses if costs exceed the initial estimate, not to exceed the $100,000 cap. The full credit is available over five years if the property's taxes are high enough. The credit stays with the property, not the owner, if it is sold.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications open each July and are reviewed on a rolling basis until the annual allocation is used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and industrial properties along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: exterior renovations or cleaning; structural improvements to the facade; replacing false facades; restoring architectural features; adding streetscape items like landscaping, walkways, or lighting; repairing doors and windows; new signs, canopies, or awnings; visible roof repairs; screening for utility or trash areas; enhanced exterior lighting; fencing that does not hide the building; sidewalks; new construction that improves the property's appearance; and necessary interior structural work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County, Maryland.
requirements_list: You must be current on property taxes.
The property must have no outstanding violations for zoning, licensing, permits, or fire codes.
Proposed improvements must comply with the Route 1 Manual and county development standards.
Approval for the tax credit does not replace the need for any required building or sign permits.
The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the agency to discuss your proposed project. If you decide to apply, submit an application with contractor cost estimates and photos of the property's current condition. County staff review the application to ensure you meet all requirements. An inter-departmental committee then votes to approve or deny the project. You must not begin any work until you receive a Certificate of Eligibility. After completing the work, submit a final application with a maintenance agreement and invoices by April 1st. A county representative will inspect the site to verify the work was completed as approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to support translational research projects at Johns Hopkins University that demonstrate commercialization potential. Provides seed funding for projects at proof-of-concept stage to advance toward commercialization, supporting de-risking of technology through preliminary data generation. Awards support translational research projects from idea stage through licensing, with flexible amounts typically capped at $50,000 per award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-dilutive grants with award amounts flexible and typically capped at $50,000, determined based on project needs. Typical awards are $50,000 over 3-9 months. Funding supports ongoing technology development in phases, with recurring opportunities to apply at different project stages. Supports milestones including formulation optimization, in vivo studies, regulatory strategy development, and commercialization pathway advancement. The Louis B. Thalheimer Fund and Zizic Translational Fund are evergreen funds where twice the award amount is repaid to the fund from license revenues before distribution to Johns Hopkins and inventors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: JHU faculty and researchers with translational research projects at proof-of-concept or early development stage seeking to advance technology toward commercialization
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In vivo studies and preclinical validation, formulation optimization and manufacturing development, regulatory consulting and IND pathway planning, animal studies and analytical services, materials, reagents, and characterization services. No indirect costs permitted; no faculty salary support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Johns Hopkins University-based research. Faculty must have full, joint, or courtesy appointment at Johns Hopkins University.
requirements_list: Technology must be formally disclosed to Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures with assigned case number
Technology must not be subject to pre-existing exclusive licenses, non-exclusive licenses, or options
At least one investigator must have full, joint, or courtesy faculty appointment at Johns Hopkins University
Only one application per Lead Principal Investigator per application cycle
Non-confidential application (will be shared with industry experts)
Concise demonstration of how funds impact commercialization
Clear articulation of project needs and commercialization milestones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a non-confidential pitch deck using provided template through the application portal. Applications evaluated by committee of industry experts based on innovation, scientific merit, prospective market impact, technical feasibility, and commercialization potential. Finalists notified and collaborate with JHTV team to refine presentation for in-person pitch.

structured_extraction.program_description: An occupational skills training program that brings quality instruction and skill training to marginalized communities, leading to employment within the elevator and escalator repair industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Occupational skills training program that provides quality instruction and skill training to participants, with the goal of leading to employment in the elevator and escalator repair industry.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals from marginalized communities seeking occupational skills training and employment in the elevator and escalator repair industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Skills training and instruction in elevator and escalator repair.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual award recognizing innovative early-to-mid career faculty members committed to translating research beyond academia into real-world products or services. The award provides financial support during crucial early career years when research funding may be limited.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $250,000 award to support research translation and commercialization activities including key or exploratory experiments, lab support, conference attendance, CRO work, and publication of findings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-to-mid career faculty members at Johns Hopkins University who are focused on translating research into real-world applications and commercializable products or services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research translation and commercialization activities including key or exploratory experiments, lab support, conference attendance, contract research organization work, and publication of findings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to full-time tenure-track faculty members in any division at Johns Hopkins University.
requirements_list: Full-time tenure-track (or equivalent) faculty member
At Assistant or Associate Professor stage preferred
Demonstrated commitment to translating science into real-world products or services
Award will significantly expand ability to commercialize scientific discoveries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Faculty members may nominate a colleague through a two-tier review process. Nominations require nominator contact information, nominee contact information, nominee CV, letter of nomination (up to 3 pages), one-page summary of research and planned use of award funds, and a sample work product. Finalists advance to second tier and submit letter of support from Dean or Department Chair. Final selection made by president and provost.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $30,000 or $80,000 for Johns Hopkins University faculty and community partners collaborating on community-based projects and research. Funding supports the bidirectional exchange of community-based and university-based knowledge, values, and expertise to address specific community needs through collaborative efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two tiers of funding: up to $30,000 for established partnerships (existing at least one year) or up to $80,000 for firmly established partnerships (existing at least two years), with award terms of up to two years. Funding may support salary including fringe, graduate students, undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, equipment, travel, and events. Funds should be split between Johns Hopkins and community partners, with the majority typically going to community partners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for 2026-2027 cycle have closed. Applications for 2027-2028 cycle will open in Fall 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Johns Hopkins University tenure-track and tenured faculty of any rank collaborating with community partners on community-based projects and research.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary including fringe, graduate students, undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, equipment, travel, and events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: While the majority of awardees are expected to work in Greater Baltimore or Washington, D.C., proposals from any geographic location are welcome as Johns Hopkins University is embedded in local communities across the world.
requirements_list: Must be led by a tenure-track or tenured Johns Hopkins faculty member from an eligible school/division (APL, BSPH, CBS, KSAS, Peabody, SAIS, SOE, SOGP, SOM, SON, or WSE)
Faculty must have 1 to 3 named community partners who acted as partners in proposal development
May include 1-2 Johns Hopkins faculty co-applicants
Community partners may be individuals or organization members
Only one Project/Research proposal per lead PI accepted (no limit as co-PI)
Staff, students, postdoctoral fellows, and non-tenure-track faculty are not currently eligible as PIs or co-PIs
Partnerships must have existed for at least one year for $30,000 grants or at least two years for $80,000 grants
At least half of the budget must be allocated directly to the community partner or to project costs benefiting the community directly
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit title, abstract (approximately 250 words), a three-page proposal with six sections (specific goal/hypothesis, collaboration history and depth, approach, expected community impact and measurement, publicization of outcomes, sustaining funding sources), detailed budget with justification, current CV or biosketch for all project leads and co-applicants, and a letter of affirmation from each community partner describing their role and expectations. All materials must be uploaded as one combined PDF file. Use 12-point font with margins no smaller than 0.5 inch.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $100,000 to enhance the work of Johns Hopkins University institutes, centers, and programs that have historically supported community-academic partnerships. Funding supports community-based academic engagement including research, teaching, fellowships, internships, and projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of up to $100,000 over a term of up to two years. Funding may be used for salary, graduate students, undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows or technicians, supplies, equipment, travel, and events. Fringe must be included in all salary requests. Support may also cover activities or services of a particular community partner. For coursework support, each semester should require no more than $10,000 in grant support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for 2026-2027 cycle have closed. Applications for 2027-2028 cycle will open in Fall 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Staff and faculty in leadership positions at Johns Hopkins University institutes, centers, or programs that have historically supported community-based academic engagement as a significant part of their mission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary, graduate students, undergraduate students, postdoctoral fellows, technicians, supplies, equipment, travel, events, and community partner activities or services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: While the majority of awardees are expected to work in Greater Baltimore or Washington, D.C., proposals from any geographic location are welcome as Johns Hopkins University is embedded in local communities across the world. Proposed work should take place in a geographic area local to the institute, center, or program.
requirements_list: Must be submitted by staff or faculty in leadership positions at institutes, centers, or programs with a history of community-based academic engagement
Each institute, center, or program may only submit a single application
Institute, center, or program must employ at least one FTE (not including the applicant) dedicating at least 75% of effort to the applying entity
Applicants must be full-time at Johns Hopkins University
JHUAPL staff potentially eligible (contact Anne Roberts-Smith before applying)
Institutes, centers, and programs that previously received grants are eligible to apply for renewal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a title, a three-page proposal with six sections (name and mission, proposed use of funds, experience and qualifications, innovation on current practices, expected impact and measurement, potential sustaining funding sources), and a detailed budget with justification. Proposal must use 12-point font with margins no smaller than 0.5 inch.

structured_extraction.program_name: Johns Hopkins Live Near Your Work Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Financial incentive program providing downpayment and closing cost assistance to Johns Hopkins University employees purchasing homes in Baltimore. The program helps employees afford to buy homes in eligible Baltimore City neighborhoods, including Remington, Better Waverly, Waverly, Bayview, Highlandtown, Patterson Park, Ednor Gardens, Charles North, Mount Vernon, and Greenmount West. Since its founding in 2009, Johns Hopkins has provided over $10 million in assistance to more than 1,500 employees for home purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $17,000 in downpayment and closing cost assistance for Hopkins employees purchasing in eligible neighborhoods. The program provides financial incentives including grants and subsidies for home purchases. Since the program's founding in 2009, Johns Hopkins has provided over $10 million to more than 1,500 employees for home purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Johns Hopkins University employees seeking to purchase homes in eligible Baltimore City neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Downpayment and closing cost assistance for home purchases in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible in ten specific Baltimore City neighborhoods: Remington, Better Waverly, Waverly, Bayview, Highlandtown, Patterson Park, Ednor Gardens, Charles North, Mount Vernon, and Greenmount West. Homes must be located in Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Johns Hopkins University employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees can apply through the Johns Hopkins Human Resources benefits office for assistance with home purchases in Baltimore.

The program is open to any applicant from the greater Baltimore area, not just Johns Hopkins affiliates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program supports social entrepreneurs through an annual cohort model. Winners receive funding support, with documented examples including $25,000 awards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Social entrepreneurs from the greater Baltimore area seeking to build innovative solutions to community challenges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building innovative, sustainable, and scalable solutions to create a healthy and prosperous world.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore area, not restricted to Johns Hopkins affiliates.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program operates on an annual cohort basis, selecting a new group of social entrepreneurs each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training and development program for design and construction firms to build capacity and skills in the construction industry. The program accepts applications from design and construction companies for participation in cohorts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides training and technical assistance to design and construction firms to build their capacity and capabilities in the construction industry. Participants are accepted into cohorts that begin in March of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Design and construction firms
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and training in construction and design
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is based at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Firms must complete an online submission form at the provided link. Submission of the form does not guarantee participation but helps the team assess interest and plan next steps.

Selected competitors pitch their business ideas for prizes, and attendees gain insights from a business resource panel on funding and incentives for startups and growing businesses.

Event includes networking opportunities with resource partners and a business resource panel focused on funding and incentives for startups and growing businesses.

Selected competitors pitch 5-minute presentations featuring bold ideas, strong value propositions, and real growth potential

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives a tax credit to commercial or industrial property owners who make a capital investment in their property. The credit applies against the increased property value for ten years when a business moves in to operate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a ten-year tax credit on the increased property value from a capital investment. The credit is 50% for the first five years. It is 25% for years six and seven. For years eight through ten, the credit is 15%.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial or industrial real property owners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to capital investments made on commercial or industrial real property where a business locates to operate.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial or industrial real property owner.
Must make a capital investment on the property.
A business entity must locate on the property to conduct business.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Application for Commerce Zone Tax Credit from the program website. Submit the application to the county.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credits for Businesses That Create New Jobs (County)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a tax credit to businesses in Kent County. To qualify, a business must build a new facility or expand an existing one and hire at least 10 new full-time employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a six-year tax credit on the increased assessed value of the property. The credit is 52% for the first two years, 39% for the third and fourth years, and 26% for the fifth and sixth years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Kent County that are expanding their physical location and creating new full-time jobs.
requirements_list: Must construct or expand business premises by at least 5,000 square feet.
Must employ at least 10 individuals in new, full-time positions.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must complete and submit the Application for the Job Creation Tax Credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Accelerating Community Excellence (ACE) Loan Program provides loans to small businesses, particularly minority-, women-owned, and underserved entrepreneurs in Montgomery County and throughout Maryland. The program is funded by a portion of proceeds from video lottery terminals at Maryland's six casinos and is managed by the Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation (MCEDC) with the Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC) serving as the fiduciary agent. At least 50% of VLT program funds must be deployed to eligible small businesses located within a targeted radius surrounding Maryland's six casinos. The remaining 50% of funding supports eligible Montgomery County small businesses for business development, expansion, and operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The ACE program provides loans to small businesses for business development, expansion, and operations. At least 50% of VLT program funds must be deployed to eligible small businesses located within a targeted radius surrounding Maryland's six casinos. Since there are no Montgomery County casinos, the MCEDC-managed ACE program targets the remaining 50% of funding to eligible Montgomery County small businesses that are minority-, women-owned, or serve underserved communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-, women-owned, and underserved small business owners in Montgomery County, Maryland, and small businesses throughout Maryland within targeted areas near Maryland's six casinos
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Small business development, expansion, and operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, and throughout Maryland. At least 50% of funds target areas within a certain radius of Maryland's six casinos.
requirements_list: Business must be minority- or women-owned or serve underserved communities
Must be small business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can start the ACE application by completing a pre-qualification form available on the website. Contact LEDC for additional information on the loan application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Aceleradora de Negocios de Comida (Food Business Accelerator)
structured_extraction.program_description: A bilingual, 12-week intensive program for food entrepreneurs and business owners seeking to scale their operations. The program provides advanced growth strategies, expert-led training, networking opportunities with industry professionals, comprehensive curriculum covering finance, marketing, restaurant operations, and licensing. Participants receive a 16-hour Food Manager Course with certification, one-on-one technical support, financial literacy training, and potential access to credit-building or seed loans up to $2,500. The program also offers assistance with temporary commercial kitchen placement (conditions apply) to support participants in achieving sustainable business growth and increased revenue.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 12-week intensive bilingual program including advanced growth strategy training, expert-led sessions, hands-on workshops, networking with industry professionals, 16-hour Food Manager Course and Certification, one-on-one technical support, financial literacy training and financial knowledge, and potential access to credit-building or seed loans up to $2,500. Assistance with temporary commercial kitchen placement (conditions apply) is provided to support business scaling, menu optimization, and operational efficiency.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications Currently Closed - Waitlist Opens Soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food entrepreneurs and business owners in DC, Maryland, and Virginia seeking to scale their operations and increase revenue. The program especially encourages applications from businesses generating more than $3,500 monthly, businesses offering healthy options, businesses in underserved neighborhoods, and committed entrepreneurs ready for transformative growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business scaling, expansion, and growth including sales improvement, menu refinement and diversification, financial management optimization, operational efficiency, and potential initial financing needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves food business owners in DC, Maryland, and Virginia with emphasis on the Washington DC metro region and surrounding Maryland areas including National Capital region and Southern Maryland.
requirements_list: Food business currently generating more than $3,500 monthly
Committed entrepreneur ready for transformative growth experience
Located in DC, Maryland, or Virginia
Seeking business growth and scaling operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed. A waitlist will open soon for interested applicants to join the program. Participants will engage in an intensive 12-week curriculum covering finances, marketing, restaurant operations, licensing, and practical business growth strategies.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business planning, marketing, licensing and permitting, credit building, and business financing.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Loan Program - Frederick County, MD
structured_extraction.program_description: A micro-loan program that provides fixed-interest-rate loans up to $10,000 to support early-stage businesses in Frederick County. The program helps micro-business owners establish commercial credit borrowing history and access capital for business growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed-interest-rate micro-loans up to $10,000 for businesses that have graduated from the EmPOWER Mentorship Program. No application or closing fees. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, real estate, franchise fees, and inventory purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County business owners who have successfully graduated from the EmPOWER Mentorship Program, with priority on underrepresented entrepreneurs including minorities, women, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment, real estate, franchise fees, inventory purchases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Any business operating in Frederick County is eligible if they have graduated from the EmPOWER Mentorship Program.
requirements_list: Must have successfully graduated from the EmPOWER Mentorship Program through FCOED
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must be current in all credit report accounts (excluding medical payments and traffic tickets)
No minimum credit score requirement
Must provide completed application
Must provide last 3 months of bank statements and last month of pay stubs (if self-employed, only bank statements)
Must provide government-issued photo identification
Must provide voided personal check

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Venture Incubator / Incubadora de Negocios de Alimentos
structured_extraction.program_description: A hybrid training program designed to help aspiring and early-stage food entrepreneurs transform their food business ideas into successful ventures. The program is offered in two formats: an 8-week English-language program and a 10-week Spanish-language program (Incubadora de Negocios de Alimentos). Participants receive weekly classes, personal one-on-one coaching, and comprehensive curriculum covering business planning, product development, marketing, operations, financial management, and legal essentials. The program culminates in Food Manager Certification (16 hours, sponsored by LEDC), a minimum viable product or actionable business launch plan, elevator pitch training, and preparation for accessing financing. Participants are expected to launch or advance their food business within 90 days of program completion.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hybrid training program combining in-person and virtual instruction. English-language track: 8 weeks with 2 hours per week instruction and personal coaching from an LEDC Small Business Coach. Spanish-language track (Incubadora de Negocios de Alimentos): 10 weeks with 2 hours per week on Wednesdays (6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.) and one-on-one business coaching every two weeks. Both programs include comprehensive curriculum on business planning, product development, marketing and sales, operations and financial management, legal essentials, and Food Manager Certification (16 hours sponsored by LEDC). Programs result in actionable business launch plans, minimum viable products, and preparation for financing access. Limited to 25-30 participants per cohort for the Spanish-language track.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and entrepreneurs with a food business concept seeking to launch or grow within 90 days, including those at the idea stage, early-stage food business owners, culinary professionals, and chefs aiming to own a business. Program serves both English-speaking and Spanish-speaking entrepreneurs based in the DMV area (DC, Maryland, Virginia).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to develop and launch a food business, including curriculum on business planning, product development, marketing strategies, operations optimization, financial management, legal compliance, market opportunity identification, and Food Manager Certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to individuals and entrepreneurs based in DC, Maryland, and Virginia (DMV area).
requirements_list: Based in DC, MD, or VA
Have a food business concept or idea
Spanish-language program requires Spanish-speaking ability
Early-stage food business development required for Spanish-language program
Limited to 25-30 participants per cohort for Spanish-language program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply to the program. Interested individuals are encouraged to contact the program for more information. Accepted participants engage in either an 8-week English-language program or a 10-week Spanish-language program with personal coaching from an LEDC Small Business Coach. Programs culminate in Food Manager Certification and a concrete action plan for launching or advancing the food business.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grow with Google: AI Series for Businesses

The program combines in-person instruction with practical applications of Gemini AI, Google Slides, Google Forms, and Google Profiles to streamline MVP development and market testing. A cohort of 30 selected entrepreneurs receives structured guidance, peer learning, and mentorship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hands-on in-person workshop series combining instruction with practical applications of Google tools including Gemini AI, Google Slides, Google Forms, and Google Profiles. Includes structured guidance, peer learning, and mentorship for developing an MVP and validating market demand. The program serves a cohort of 30 selected entrepreneurs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used for learning and developing a Minimum Viable Product (MVP), validating market demand, and leveraging Google's business ecosystem for growth.

requirements_list: Startup entrepreneurs committed to building and scaling their startups
Selected from a cohort of 30 entrepreneurs

structured_extraction.program_name: LEDC's NextGen Impact Fund Loan powered by SELF
structured_extraction.program_description: LEDC, a nonprofit Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI), partners with SELF to provide unsecured personal loans for homeowners to fund home renovation and improvement projects that promote energy efficiency, clean energy alternatives, renewable energy, storm protection, water conservation, and disability accessibility improvements. The program offers alternative financing based on ability to pay rather than credit score, serving homeowners who may not qualify for traditional bank loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured personal loans ranging from $3,000 to $25,000 (up to $50,000 for solar products) with fixed interest rates of 5.0%-10.5% (7.4%-8.5% for solar). Loan terms range from 3-8 years (up to 7 years for solar). Origination fee is 2.5% (1.25% for military). Project coordination fee is 2.99%. No minimum credit score required. No fees charged to homeowners for financing. Approval is based on ability to pay rather than credit history, with approval typically taking 24 hours to one week.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, including low and moderate-income (LMI) households and people with low credit scores, in Maryland, Virginia, and Washington DC who own their homes and want to finance eligible home renovation and improvement projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovation and improvement projects including solar products and installations (PV panels, water heaters, attic fans, backup batteries), energy efficiency improvements (HVAC, lighting, insulation, ductwork, weatherization, pool pumps), roofing and storm resilience projects (storm/wind protection, windows, roof repair/replacement, hurricane shutters, doors), water conservation and quality improvements (irrigation, lateral line replacement, rain barrels, cisterns, septic conversion, low-flow fixtures, heat pump water heaters, sewer and water work), health and safety modifications (mold remediation, disability accessibility, wheelchair ramps, aging-in-place modifications, widening hallways, walk/roll-in showers), air conditioning, and EV chargers and electric generators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: LEDC is certified to lend in Maryland, Virginia, and Washington DC. Program serves the National Capital region including Maryland counties within that area.

Homeowner must own the home
Home must be located in Maryland, DC, or Virginia
Must be current on property taxes
Home mortgage loans must be current with proof
Applicant must prove ability to pay (employment income, Social Security, Disability, wages, retirement, disability, etc.)
Must have disposable income to repay the loan
Primary applicant cannot have a bankruptcy in the past 12 months
Applicants with any credit score accepted; some may require a co-signer based on credit history or product being financed
Co-signer or cash collateral may be required depending on payment history
Applicant must be at least 18 years old (typical lending requirement)
Manufactured homes must be affixed to the ground (mobile homes with license plates do not qualify)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners can apply online or by contacting LEDC. LEDC pre-screens contractors, checks pricing, and provides project coordination from start to finish. The application is reviewed by the underwriting team, which evaluates ability to pay. Approval typically takes 24 hours to one week depending on client response and document submission. Once approved and the loan closes, the contractor receives a Notice to Proceed and work begins. After installation and inspection (if applicable), final paperwork is submitted and payment process begins.
