structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing counseling and guidance to help homeowners avoid foreclosure through loan modifications, short sales, or other long-term solutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The page does not specify geographic eligibility, but LEDC is based in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.
requirements_list: Be a homeowner struggling with mortgage payments
Be willing to work with a housing counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact LEDC by phone at 202-540-7401 or email at housing@ledcmetro.org to speak with a housing counselor. Counselors will assess your financial situation and help you identify the best options.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps small business owners, particularly in the cleaning industry, adopt sustainable practices and boost their operations. The program teaches Pollution Prevention (P2) concepts, P2 Plan development, and the environmental and health impacts of traditional cleaning products. Participants receive guidance on incorporating safer, eco-friendly cleaning practices into business operations, employee training, and client proposals. Eligible businesses can receive a $2,000 grant to support their transition to greener practices and make a positive environmental and community impact.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training program that teaches Pollution Prevention (P2) concepts, P2 Plan development, and environmental and health impacts of cleaning products. Participants receive guidance on incorporating safer, eco-friendly practices into business operations, employee training, and client proposals. A $2,000 grant is available to eligible businesses that adopt sustainable practices and implement green operational improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, particularly small business owners in the cleaning industry, seeking to adopt sustainable practices and improve their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance on pollution prevention, eco-friendly cleaning product development, sustainable business practices, and to adopt sustainable practices and implement green operational improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through Latino Economic Development Center; serves Maryland-based businesses statewide.
requirements_list: Operating cleaning business or seeking to adopt sustainable practices
Interest in sustainable and eco-friendly practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend an info session to learn more about the program and how to apply. Info sessions are offered in Spanish (July 23 at 12:00 PM, August 6 at 6:00 PM) and English (August 13 at 6:00 PM). Businesses enroll in the Smart Clean Program to receive training on Pollution Prevention concepts and P2 Plan development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Talleres de Vivienda - Housing Education Classes
structured_extraction.program_description: Educational workshops and courses that provide knowledge, resources, and expert guidance for homebuyers to navigate the home purchase process and achieve housing goals. Courses range from introductory overviews to comprehensive 8-hour seminars covering budgeting, financing, local programs, and resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and low-cost housing education courses offered in Spanish and English. Courses include: 2-hour introductory courses on home buying basics; 8-hour comprehensive homebuyer seminars covering budgeting, financing, and first-time homebuyer preparation; specialized courses on energy efficiency and electrification; and courses on affordable housing programs and inclusive zoning. After completing a course, participants can meet one-on-one with a HUD-certified housing counselor for personalized guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and first-time homebuyers seeking to purchase a home in Washington DC, Maryland (Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Baltimore), and Virginia. Courses are offered in Spanish and English.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training to prepare for homeownership, including understanding the home purchase process, financial preparation, mortgage options, local programs and resources, energy efficiency, and affordable housing opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Courses are offered for Washington DC, Maryland (Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Baltimore), and Virginia. Virginia courses are provided through Virginia Housing.
requirements_list: Desire to learn about home buying process
Registration required for courses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals register for courses through Google Forms links provided on the program page. Courses are offered both virtually and in-person. After completing a course, participants can schedule individual consultations with HUD-certified housing counselors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cohort-based initiative designed to empower women and Latina food entrepreneurs with comprehensive support for business launch and scaling. The program combines LEDC's Wealth & Wellness curriculum with its Food Ventures Initiative Incubator and Accelerator, providing technical assistance, bilingual business and financial training, mentorship, and access to affordable capital through a dynamic combination of in-person and online sessions. The program will reach approximately 100 to 150 participants through five cohorts over two years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides bilingual training, tailored technical assistance, hands-on business and financial training, mentorship, and access to affordable capital to food entrepreneurs. Support integrates financial empowerment, business education, and strategic investment through a combination of in-person and online sessions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women and Latina food entrepreneurs from the DMV region with a special focus on communities across the Greater Washington region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building and growing food ventures, including restaurant and food business operations, and scaling sustainable culinary businesses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves the DMV (District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia) region with a focus on the Greater Washington region and Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Must be a woman entrepreneur
Must be a food entrepreneur
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are selected through a cohort-based application process. Complete the Interest Form to join the interest list. Five cohorts will be launched over the next two years with applications opening on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 4-week program designed to empower young entrepreneurs and individuals aged 18-25 by helping them transform their business idea into a viable and sustainable venture. The program provides targeted support including business education and personalized coaching.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personalized business coaching, help developing business plan, training on entrepreneurial mindset and confidence building, and support for launching a business. Sessions held Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 6:30 pm to 8:00 pm for 4 weeks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young entrepreneurs and individuals aged 18-25 looking to start a business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business planning, skill development, and coaching to launch a new business venture.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is located in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be aged 18-25
Must have a business idea to develop
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete RSVP form on the program page to register for the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Highway Safety Office – Law Enforcement Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers grants to state, county, and local law enforcement agencies. The funds help pay for overtime enforcement, equipment, and other traffic safety projects. The goal is to reduce motor vehicle crashes, injuries, and deaths on Maryland roads.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants on a reimbursement basis. This means grantees must spend their own money first and then get paid back. The funds cover costs for officer overtime, equipment, and training for traffic safety initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State, county, and local law enforcement agencies in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for officer overtime, equipment, and training. The activities must focus on highway safety priorities like preventing impaired, distracted, or aggressive driving, and improving seat belt use and pedestrian safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must target high-crash locations and corridors identified through crash data.
requirements_list: Grants are provided on a reimbursement-only basis.
Enforcement operations must be data-driven and target areas with the greatest need based on crash data.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the online Grants & Projects for Safety (GPS) portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program established by MARBIDCO to help meet unique financing needs of Maryland's rural and agricultural businesses. Provides moderate-cost loans for equipment purchases or working capital when traditional commercial financing is unavailable. Designed to help farm and rural businesses innovate, diversify, and exploit emerging market opportunities. Complements financial services by working jointly with other public sector lending agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equipment and working capital loans ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 8 years with up to 12 months of interest-only periods possible. Operating loans have terms of 1 to 2 years with up to 6 months of interest-only periods possible. Interest rates are 4.75% with a partnering public sector lender, 6.75% without, or an additional 0.25% reduction for Home Town Hero veterans. Loan origination fee of 1% applies. Typical equity contribution of 10% of the project's total cost is required. Personal guarantee by business owners is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, resource-based businesses, food or fiber production or processing businesses, and rural businesses in Maryland that need financing for equipment and working capital but cannot obtain commercial financing from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases and working capital for agribusinesses, including value-added food processing, agri-tourism/rural recreation, timber growing or harvesting, primary/secondary wood processing, environmental/water quality, biomass/energy production, niche market production, and aquaculture/fishing/seafood operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Note: Upper Shore Regional Council offers an additional equity incentive grant for farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties.
requirements_list: Applications must be originated by the applicant and a partnering lending organization
Minimum loan amount of $15,000
Maximum loan amount of $100,000
Typically 10% equity contribution required
Personal guarantee by business owners required
If applying with a public-sector lender, that lender must commit to specified matching financing
If applying without a public-sector lender, a commercial lender must provide a credit denial letter or complete the commercial lender referral form
Cannot obtain commercial financing from traditional lenders
Balance sheet submission required
Income statement for past 2 years required
Pro forma income statement for upcoming year required
Farm/business debt repayment schedule required
Personal debt repayment schedule required
Current loan information from lending institution required
Business address and location information required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed applications to MARBIDCO by mail or email with required attachments including balance sheet, income statements for past 2 years, pro forma income statement for upcoming year, farm/business debt repayment schedule, personal debt repayment schedule, and current loan information from lending institution. Applications must be originated by the applicant and partnering lending organization. Cooperative Extension agents, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may assist. Applications are processed as they are received on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program designed to strengthen Maryland's local food system by providing funding to help small farmers and fishing operations aggregate their products to sell to wholesale and institutional markets. Grants support investments in capacity and infrastructure for small-scale farmers and farm entities to expand sales opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for projects that help small farmers and fishing operations aggregate their certified local products to sell to institutional or wholesale buyers. Funds support investments in infrastructure and capacity to strengthen the local food system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small farmers and fishing operations in Maryland seeking to expand sales to wholesale and institutional markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects and investments in infrastructure and capacity to aggregate certified local farm and fish products for sale to institutional or wholesale buyers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a certified local farm or farm entity
Must be a small farmer or farming organization
Project must involve aggregating certified local farm or fish food products
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application round opened January 21, 2025 with a deadline of February 28, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program established by MARBIDCO to help Maryland's forest products businesses with working capital and equipment purchases. The program aims to help forest products-related businesses innovate and exploit emerging market opportunities, while complementing private commercial lenders by making rural business financing available and affordable. The program utilizes more liberal underwriting guidelines than normal, including a minimum cash flow coverage ratio of 1.0/1.0 and relaxed collateral security requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $150,000 for equipment purchases or working capital. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 6 years. Operating/working capital loans have terms of 1 to 2 years. Interest rates are fixed at a minimum of 6.25%, established on a case-by-case basis based on credit risk. A 1% loan origination fee applies. Equity requirement is typically 5-10% of the project's total cost. Personal guarantee required from all business owners. A commercial lender must participate and provide a letter of referral. Maximum outstanding aggregate portfolio balance for the entire program cannot exceed $400,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are processed as they are received (rolling deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland forest products businesses and rural business owners, including forest products-related businesses on the Eastern Shore and Western Shore.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, working capital for operations, operating expenses (fuel, chemicals, salaries, repairs, insurance, utilities, etc.), and debt repayment for forest products businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The program specifically mentions it can help with both Eastern Shore and Western Shore forest products businesses. Note: An equity incentive grant component is available for farmers in Upper Shore counties (Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's) through a partnership with the Upper Shore Regional Council.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a forest products-related business, including value-added secondary wood processing, timber growing/harvesting, or biomass/energy product businesses
Commercial lender participation required (lender must provide letter of referral)
Equity contribution of 5-10% of total project cost required
Personal guarantee required from all business owners
Maximum outstanding aggregate portfolio balance for the entire program cannot exceed $400,000
Financial documentation including gross farm/business income, cost of goods sold, detailed expense records, farm or business debt repayment schedule, and personal debt repayment schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be originated by the applicant and include detailed financial statements and debt schedules. Cooperative Extension agents, Maryland Forest Service, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may assist in application development. Complete the application form and submit it along with required attachments (including a form to be completed by a financial institution describing current loan obligations) to MARBIDCO. Applications are processed as received. Contact MARBIDCO office for guidance prior to completing an application due to portfolio balance limitations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Hometown Hero Interest Rate Reduction for Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: An interest rate reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points) offered to U.S. military service members and veterans for specific MARBIDCO loan programs in agriculture and forestry.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An interest rate reduction of 0.25% or 25 basis points applied to eligible MARBIDCO loan programs including the Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund (MRBIFF), Maryland Vineyard/Hopyard/Orchard Planting Loan Fund, Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, and Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program. Applicants must meet military service requirements and maintain at least 50% veteran ownership and 50% veteran management control in the operation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. military service members currently serving or veterans with honorable discharge who own and manage agricultural or forestry businesses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For agribusiness equipment, working capital, vineyard/hopyard/orchard planting, forestry equipment and working capital, and large animal veterinary practice support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for qualifying agricultural and forestry operations in Maryland.
requirements_list: Currently serving in any branch of the United States Military with a letter of support from commanding officer or designated representative, OR has served and received an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) characterization of service with proof via Department of Defense Form DD-214
Minimum of 50% veteran ownership in the operation
Minimum of 50% veteran management control in the operation
Practical farm and/or business experience required (may be supplemented by academic or hands-on training)
Business plan required
Borrower financial information required
Applicant must notify MARBIDCO at time of loan application of intent to seek Hometown Hero interest rate reduction eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MARBIDCO to determine which programs may be right for your business. Submit loan application for one of the eligible MARBIDCO loan programs along with required documentation including business plan, financial information, and proof of military service. Notify MARBIDCO at application time of intent to seek Hometown Hero interest rate reduction eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Agriculture & Resource-Based Industry Project Cost Share Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An ongoing grant program that matches rural business development investments made by local governments and rural regional development councils to support agricultural and resource-based businesses in Maryland. The program supports retention and growth of Maryland's existing and emerging agricultural and resource-based businesses and provides guidance to county and municipal economic development officials. The program provides cost-sharing support for projects that assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries, including agritourism activities, businesses that produce foodstuffs or goods that grow in soil or water, and packaging, value-added processing, and marketing of such products.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides matching grants to local governments and rural regional development councils for agricultural and resource-based business development projects. Maximum grant amounts are $10,000 for general projects, $5,000 for Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) matching grants, and $3,000 for deer fences or farm operation solar systems/generators for commercial business energy. There is a limit of $25,000 in total grants that can be awarded to any single government jurisdiction in any given fiscal year, and a $15,000 lifetime maximum for individual farmer or business applicants (designees). Water and air quality improvement projects that contribute to business sustainability are also eligible. MARBIDCO grant amount cannot exceed the local government's investment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and regional economic development offices, farmers, rural business owners, and young/beginning farmers in Maryland's agricultural, forestry, and seafood industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries, including agritourism activities, businesses that produce foodstuffs or goods that grow in soil or water, and packaging, value-added processing, and marketing of such products. Water and air quality improvement projects that contribute to business sustainability are also eligible. Specific eligible projects include Food Safety Modernization Act compliance, deer fences, farm operation solar systems or generators for commercial business energy, biomass/energy production, aquaculture/fishing, niche market production, and primary and secondary wood processing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to local and regional economic development offices in Maryland's rural regions. Known partner jurisdictions include Anne Arundel, Cecil, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne, Salisbury-Wicomico, Town of Mount Airy, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Project must fit within MARBIDCO's statutory economic development profile
Project must assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries
If project directly benefits an individual farmer or business owner, that farmer or business owner must make a financial contribution to the project
Applications must be submitted by a local or regional economic development office
Governmental entity's funds must be own-source, not pass-through
Businesses that produce foodstuffs or goods that grow in soil or water are generally eligible
Packaging and value-added processing and marketing of agricultural products are eligible
MARBIDCO grant amount cannot exceed local government's investment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form and submit it to MARBIDCO Local Government Grant Program, Attn. Daniela Merkle, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or electronically to dmerkle@marbidco.org. All applications must be submitted by a local or regional economic development office, not individual farmers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) Agricultural Loans and Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO is a quasi-governmental organization that provides low and moderate-cost agricultural loans and targeted specialty incentive grants to support Maryland's agricultural, forestry, and seafood industries. MARBIDCO helps Maryland's farm, forestry, and seafood businesses prosper through targeted financial and other services that retain existing resource-based industry production and commerce, promote rural entrepreneurship, and nurture emerging or expanding agricultural enterprises. MARBIDCO offers more than 20 targeted loan and grant programs designed to help farmers, watermen, aquaculture businesses, seafood processors, wood processing businesses, vineyard operators, veterinarians, and beginning farmers secure affordable capital and credit for equipment, commercial facilities, real estate purchases, farmland access, and other agricultural and resource-based business needs. The organization works cooperatively with commercial lenders, Farm Credit Associations, USDA offices, and other federal, state, and local government agencies to maximize rural lending opportunities and assist innovative business enterprises and start-up operations that may have difficulty securing traditional financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO offers low and moderate-cost agricultural loans for equipment, commercial facilities, real estate purchases, and farmland access financing. The organization also provides targeted specialty incentive grants for local farm food aggregation, certain agribusinesses, farm, livestock, and resource-based businesses. Assistance is available for innovative business enterprises and start-up operations that may have difficulty securing traditional financing. MARBIDCO works with commercial lenders, Farm Credit Associations, and USDA offices to help maximize rural lending opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commercial farmers, foresters, seafood industry workers, watermen, aquaculture businesses, seafood processors, wood processing businesses, vineyard operators, veterinarians, beginning farmers, and farm, forestry, and seafood businesses seeking affordable capital and credit for agricultural and resource-based business operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases, commercial facilities, real estate purchases, farmland access financing, and capital and credit for agricultural and resource-based business operations and industry development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the State of Maryland for agricultural, forestry, and seafood industries.
requirements_list: Must be involved in commercial farming, forestry, or seafood industries
Beginning farmer programs available for farmland access financing and young farmers
Assistance available for innovative business enterprises and start-up operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MARBIDCO's experienced staff can consult with individuals and businesses to determine which programs are the best fit. The organization works cooperatively with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA offices, and other federal, state, and local government agencies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program, established by MARBIDCO, helps attract and/or retain licensed large animal veterinarians in Maryland. It assists veterinarians obtain commercial financing to purchase trucks and specialized equipment needed to provide veterinary care services to large animals such as cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, and goats. The program is particularly designed to help veterinarians carrying large student loan debt. Loans range between $25,000 and $100,000 at a 4.50% interest rate with terms ranging from 3.5 to 5 years depending on loan amount.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans between $25,000 and $100,000 at a 4.50% interest rate to purchase trucks or specialized equipment for large animal veterinary services. Loan terms range from 3.5 years (for $25,000-$39,999) to 5 years (for $80,000-$100,000). A maximum 6-month interest-only repayment option is available. Applicants must pay at least 10% of costs out of pocket. Loan origination fee is 0.25%. Collateral security cannot exceed 95% of fair market value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed large animal veterinarians in Maryland with clinical experience, particularly those with minimum $50,000 in student loan debt, establishing or expanding veterinary practices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of trucks and specialized equipment necessary for providing large animal veterinary care services for cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, or goats
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Maryland and agree to have a majority of their large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term. Available statewide.
requirements_list: Hold a license to practice veterinary medicine in Maryland
Have clinical experience providing veterinary care to large animals (cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, or goats)
Reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled
Agree to have a majority of large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term
Pay for at least 10% of the costs of items being purchased with loan proceeds
Minimum eligible credit score of 620
Provide personal guarantee if the business entity is the borrower
Evidence of current student loan debt of minimum $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and sign the application form with all required attachments. Submit the original application by mail to MARBIDCO Large Animal Veterinarian Loan, Attn: Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or by email to brawlings@marbidco.org. Applications are processed as they are received.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers loans to eligible applicants to help start up or expand small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facilities in Maryland, increasing the processing of meat, poultry, and catfish. Large-sized meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible. The program complements USDA's Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program and assists with expansion of livestock processing capacity in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $250,000 to $2,500,000 at 4.00% fixed interest rate with a 0.25% loan origination fee (capped at $5,000). Loan proceeds can be used to purchase real estate, construct a new or expand an existing livestock processing facility, and purchase livestock processing equipment. MARBIDCO will match an approved applicant's equity contribution on a dollar-for-dollar basis up to 10% of project costs, with the maximum equity grant capped at $250,000. Borrower must provide at least 7.5% of project cost as equity contribution. Applicants constructing new facilities must demonstrate minimum working capital of at least 10% of project cost. Loan terms correspond to useful life of assets being financed, following an initial interest-only period of up to 12 months. Personal guarantees required unless borrower provides 20% equity contribution including MARBIDCO's equity grant. Can be standalone or work with other commercial lenders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected livestock processing facility operators (meat, poultry, and catfish processors) in Maryland, including individual owners and guarantors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase real estate, construct a new or expand an existing livestock processing facility, and purchase livestock processing equipment. Priority given to construction of new facilities, especially in underserved parts of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Priority given to underserved parts of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be USDA-inspected livestock processing facility (meat, poultry, or catfish)
Must be small- or medium-sized (large-sized meat and poultry processing companies not eligible)
Must provide at least 7.5% of project cost as equity contribution
Applicants constructing new facilities must demonstrate minimum working capital of at least 10% of project cost (in cash or through bank line of credit)
Personal guarantees required from business owners (unless 20% equity contribution provided)
All projects must be submitted to USDA for approval before funds are disbursed
Self-certification that recipient/business does not hold top four market share in meat and poultry processing sector
Labor standards certification (maintain wages, benefits, and opportunities for workers)
Environmental Assessment completion (by USDA RD State Office)
Drug-free Workplace Certification (USDA RD Form AD-1049)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must originate all applications and submit application with required USDA RD forms and certifications. Completed applications must be sent to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, c/o Allison Roe, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403. Applications are processed in the order received, subject to availability of funds. MARBIDCO completes Intermediary Certification and must submit all projects to USDA RD State Office for Environmental Assessment and approval before disbursing funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established by MARBIDCO to finance the cost of eligible seafood processing projects, including historic oyster shucking facilities. The program facilitates an increase in the amount of oyster shells retained in Maryland and returned to the Chesapeake Bay. Authorized by Senate Bill 830 (2022 legislation).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $25,000 to $250,000 (capped at $25,000 per full-time job or seasonal full-time job created or retained). Fixed interest rate of 3.25% with no loan origination fee. Loan term corresponds to the useful life of assets being financed, following an initial interest-only period of up to 6 months. Requires a minimum 3% equity contribution from the borrower. In Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties, MARBIDCO will match the equity contribution dollar-for-dollar up to 5% of project cost (capped at $12,500).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications processed as received (no stated deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed Maryland Seafood Dealers with at least three years of experience or TFL-holders with at least five years of experience who want to establish or expand oyster processing facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To renovate or construct a new oyster processing facility, expand an existing one, or purchase oyster processing equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Enhanced incentive matching available in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed Maryland Seafood Dealer for at least three years OR a TFL-holder for at least five years
Must agree to obtain a Seafood Dealer License if approved for financing
Must have paid all applicable taxes and fees for the last five years
Must provide a business plan including financial projections
Must demonstrate minimum working capital of 15% of project cost (for new facilities) or 10% (for other applicants)
Must provide at least 3% equity contribution towards project cost
Personal guarantee normally required; owners of business entities must provide guarantees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed as received and must include all required attachments as listed in the application checklist. Completed applications should be submitted to skubofcik@marbidco.org or mailed to MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program specifically funded by the Maryland General Assembly to assist agricultural producers with cold storage facility development and acquisition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for cold storage facility development and acquisition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers needing cold storage capabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage facility development and acquisition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Affordable, subsidized loan financing available to commercial watermen and others wishing to start or expand shellfish remote-setting aquaculture operations. Remote setting is a process for growers to produce cost-effective seed oysters for aquaculture. Partnership between MARBIDCO, Maryland DNR, and industry organizations. Loans range from $5,000 to $30,000 with 5-6 year terms, featuring interest-only first year, final year payment forgiveness for borrowers in good standing, and a 5.25% interest rate.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program providing below-market-rate gap financing to established and beginning businesses in Maryland's resource-based industries, including agriculture, forestry, fishing, hunting, poultry production, and other agricultural enterprises. MARBIDCO provides up to a maximum of 40% of the financing needed for a project in partnership with commercial lenders or public instrumentalities, with the condition that a commercial lender or public instrumentality provides at least an equal financial commitment. MARBIDCO takes the junior collateral lien position behind commercial lenders and works to graduate borrowers to conventional commercial financing over several years. Financing supports farm and land purchases, agricultural enterprise diversification and expansion, equipment purchases, production and processing activities, environmental or water-quality enhancement projects, and other business development needs. The program also includes a co-lending participation loan option using a "First Lien / Last Out" structure where MARBIDCO purchases up to 49% interest in first priority promissory notes to assist borrowers, particularly young/beginning farmers and those diversifying into value-added processing, who would have difficulty securing financing through traditional commercial lenders alone.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market-rate and low-interest gap financing provided in partnership with commercial lenders such as Farm Credit Associations, commercial banks, USDA Rural Development, and Farm Service Agency (FSA). MARBIDCO provides up to a maximum of 40% of the financing needed through either direct loan or participation loan options, with a commercial lender or public instrumentality providing at least an equal financial commitment. MARBIDCO takes the junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender. The participation loan option uses a "First Lien / Last Out" structure where MARBIDCO purchases up to 49% interest in first priority promissory notes at a below-market rate (currently 4.25% fixed). The Lead Lender may add up to 75 basis points (0.75%) as a servicing fee, resulting in a blended interest rate that provides overall lower cost of capital. Financing loans support farm and land purchases, agricultural enterprise diversification and expansion, capital equipment purchases, production and processing activities, food/feed/fiber production and processing projects, equine and horticulture operations, renewable energy projects, environmental or water-quality enhancement projects, and other business development needs.

Repayment terms: substrate and seed up to 5 years (1-3 years interest-only plus 2 years principal and interest); capital equipment up to 7 years (1-3 years interest-only plus 4 years principal and interest); blended purchases up to 6 years (1-3 years interest-only plus 3 years principal and interest). structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (Next Gen)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program offered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that assists young and beginning farmers with down-payment and financing assistance for the purchase of farmland. The program includes both a general track for farmland of any size and a specialized Small Acreage Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program (SANG) track for properties between 10 to 49 acres. The SANG track provides 30% to 60% of the fair market value (land only) in exchange for a permanent agricultural conservation easement on qualifying properties, with easement valuations capped at $6,000 per acre of MARBIDCO funding. The program works with farmland conservation programs and commercial lenders to help farmers buy agricultural land. Buyers receive down payment assistance (up to 51% of a land-only Fair Market Value appraisal, capped at $500,000) for properties qualifying for county Agricultural District programs. As part of the process, development rights are temporarily extinguished on the farmland being purchased, and the land will eventually be permanently preserved. After real estate settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Agricultural District program. If no permanent easement is obtained within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement. Most approved purchases can be completed in 6 to 8 months. The program helps preserve agricultural land from future development and helps young or beginning farmers overcome the barriers of high farmland costs and limited access to capital.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Down-payment and financing assistance for the purchase of farmland. The program provides buyers with up to 51% of a land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property for purchase assistance, capped at $500,000. For the SANG track (properties between 10 to 49 acres), MARBIDCO purchases permanent agricultural conservation easements valued at 30% to 60% of the fair market value (land only), with a cap of $6,000 per acre of MARBIDCO funding. These easements serve as down payment assistance to meet commercial lender equity requirements. A commercial lender must be involved in the transaction. The program works in conjunction with farmland conservation programs and commercial lenders to help young and beginning farmers acquire agricultural property. After settlement, borrowers must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in their county's Agricultural District program. If no permanent easement is obtained within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement. Low-interest loans are available through collaboration with commercial or farm credit lenders.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for rural land preservation assistance are made on a competitive basis. Contact your county agricultural preservation program office at least one month before submission to discuss the suitability of the subject farm for permanent preservation. Ensure required paperwork from the property seller is received by the county office one month in advance. Collaborate with a commercial or farm credit lender to apply for down-payment assistance. Applications are reviewed by a Review Committee made up of individuals with experience in agricultural lending, land conservation, and agriculture and resource-based business. The committee ranks applications and makes recommendations to the MARBIDCO Board of Directors. For SANG track applications, submit all required forms and attachments to the MARBIDCO office in Annapolis by 4:00 p.m. on the last business day of each month. structured_extraction.program_name: Micro Loans for Business Owners and Entrepreneurs
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive lending program provided by Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE) that offers microloans, small business loans, and Credit Builder Loans to both new and existing businesses, entrepreneurs, and individuals who lack access to traditional lending sources. The program serves unemployed and poor entrepreneurs, self-employed individuals, start-up business owners, and those denied by traditional lenders. MCE provides microloans up to $35,000 for individual entrepreneurs and small business loans up to $50,000 for businesses with fewer than 10 employees, as well as larger MCE Business Loans ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 for business expansion. The Credit Builder Loan product offers loans ranging from $500 to $5,000 for qualifying micro businesses, with $500 to $2,500 loans having 12 to 18 month terms and $2,501 to $5,000 loans having 12 to 36 month terms. MCE Business Loans offer terms up to 10 years with interest rates starting at 6 percent. Credit Builder Loans help businesses build credit history while accessing resources to start and grow their operations. Interest rates are assessed based on risk and loan amount. Loans are available to both new and existing businesses regardless of years in operation. The program fills the gap left by banks hesitant to lend to new businesses and those who have been denied traditional financing. Along with loans, the program provides counseling, training, and financial, marketing, and management support including business consulting, business planning, cash flow analysis, and specialized business training workshops. MCE is the only micro-enterprise organization in the state certified as SBA, USDA, and CDFI Intermediary Lender. Credit Builder Loans serve as an alternative to high-interest credit cards and help businesses improve their credit rating. Consultations are provided to new and aspiring entrepreneurs where a business consultant assesses client needs, helps develop a business plan, and assists in securing needed assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microloans up to $35,000 for individual entrepreneurs and small business loans up to $50,000 for businesses with fewer than 10 employees. MCE Business Loans range from $5,000 to $35,000 for new businesses or $35,001 to $100,000 for business expansion, with terms up to 10 years and interest rates starting at 6 percent. Credit Builder Loans range from $500 to $5,000, with $500 to $2,500 loans having 12 to 18 month terms and $2,501 to $5,000 loans having 12 to 36 month terms. Unsecured or secured loans available. Interest rates are assessed based on risk and loan amount. Loans are available to both new and existing businesses regardless of years in operation, with no minimum years in operation requirement. The program serves those who lack collateral, steady employment, verifiable credit history, and cannot meet traditional lender qualifications. Funds may be used for business expansion, equipment purchases, working capital, starting a new business, general business development needs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies, materials, inventory, and vehicle purchases. Application fees include $50 non-refundable application fee (MCE Business Loans: $100), $25 non-refundable credit report fee per applicant, and $50 underwriting/closing fee (MCE Business Loans: 1 percent underwriting fee plus legal reserve fee ranging from $250 to $1,500). Security may be required up to the full amount of the loan. MCE conducts semi-annual site visits to assess business function and progress. MCE staff provide business consulting, business planning, cash flow analysis, and specialized business training workshops. The program includes counseling, training, and financial, marketing, and management support along with loans. Available through both peer lending groups and individual lending models.

Businesses that provide a service or product to the community and need to build credit history. For-profit business owners and entrepreneurs located in specified Eastern Shore counties, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion, equipment purchases, working capital, starting a new business, general business development needs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, supplies, materials, inventory, and vehicle purchases. Business startup and growth. Machinery, equipment, furniture, fixtures, supplies, materials, inventory, working capital, and truck or car purchases. Start-up costs and general business operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland with statewide service area. MCE Business Loan products and Credit Builder Loan products also available in the 8 counties of Maryland's Eastern Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester) or Baltimore County, Baltimore City, or Anne Arundel County. Maryland Capital Enterprises is the only micro-enterprise organization in the state certified as SBA, USDA, and CDFI Intermediary Lender.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete a comprehensive personal information supplement form or MCE Credit Builder Loan Application form and can apply through Maryland Capital Enterprises for microloans, small business loans, or MCE Business Loans. The form includes general application information with personal details and identification, employment information, personal financial information with detailed asset and liability accounting, stocks and bonds holdings, real estate ownership details, household expenses, three personal references, two alternate contact persons for outreach, credit history, business synopsis or business plan, collateral information, vendor list, and contractor licensing information. Each loan application is evaluated on a case-by-case basis, with the borrower specifying what funds will be used for. A loan officer or Loan Committee processes the application and notifies the applicant of the decision. MCE conducts investigation of credit records, credit history, legal and financial obligations, and criminal records. MCE will attempt to approve loans and provide alternate resources if unable to approve. Applicants work with MCE staff to access loans through either peer lending groups or individual lending models. Upon approval, loan agreement is executed with mandatory semi-annual site visits during repayment. The organization provides counseling, training, and financial, marketing, and management support along with loans. Consultations are provided to new and aspiring entrepreneurs where a business consultant assesses client needs, helps develop a business plan, and assists in securing needed assistance. Submit the MCE Business Loan Application online or on paper with required documentation including business plan, 2-year cash flow projections, 2-year personal federal tax returns, 3 months personal bank statements, profit and loss statements (if applicable), business federal tax returns (if applicable), explanation of credit, quotes for items to be purchased, and reference letters. Complete the client intake form online or on paper. Submit a comprehensive loan application packet including the MCE Business Loan Application, Personal Information Supplement, detailed business plan, cash flow projections, personal and business tax returns, bank statements, balance sheet, explanation of credit history, and certificate of good standing. Include proof of being turned down by a traditional lender. Submit comprehensive business plan with supporting documentation and financial statements and credit information. Supply references and personal financial details. Submit the non-refundable application fee by credit card phone payment or money order by mail. The application will be reviewed in-house and a credit report may be ordered if needed. The Loan Committee reviews applications and makes lending decisions based on business plan thoroughness, credit history, collateral, and other factors. Applicants may receive credit counseling if required. Applicants are notified of approval status and loan terms are finalized before closing. structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center in partnership with MEA designed to accelerate the development of Maryland-sited solar photovoltaic and solar-plus-storage projects that support community solar and affordable multifamily housing solar installations benefiting low- and moderate-income households. The program addresses critical pre-construction and early-construction financing gaps that delay viable solar projects by providing short-term bridge loans ranging from $500,000 to $1,500,000 maximum per developer. Loans carry a fixed interest rate based on SOFR plus a spread determined by project risk and impact, with an initial interest rate cap at 7%. Borrowers make interest-only payments during the loan term (typically 12 months with optional 6-month extension) with principal repaid at maturity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term bridge loans ranging from $500,000 to $1,500,000 maximum per developer, typically 12 months in term with optional 6-month extension. Fixed interest rate based on SOFR plus a spread determined by project risk and impact, with initial interest rate cap at 7%. No additional fees including origination or legal fees. Borrowers make interest-only payments during the term with principal repaid at maturity. Loans require first-priority UCC lien and/or guaranty as collateral. Funds may be disbursed in one draw or multiple draws based on approved uses and project milestones. Financing addresses pre-construction and early-construction gaps for solar photovoltaic and solar-plus-storage projects located in Maryland. Loans must be repaid prior to construction financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: C-PACE is a statewide financing mechanism that allows commercial and business property owners to finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, resiliency, and environmental remediation measures through property-assessed clean energy loans. The program provides turn-key, low-cost, standardized financing services for commercial buildings and building retrofit projects. Property owners can finance 100% of qualifying improvements at competitive loan terms with repayment periods of 10-30+ years, with no money down. The loan is structured as a property tax assessment and repaid through long-term surcharges on property tax bills that transfer with the sale of the property. Projects typically range from $50,000 to $100,000 and beyond, up to multi-million dollar renovations. Property owners can realize positive cash flow from day one. Underwriting focuses on the underlying building rather than owner credit. Financing is available through both public and private sources, including through a network of registered private capital providers. Tax credits including solar investment tax credit (ITC) can be fully realized, and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS) are available. The program operates through participating counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation, with Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Frederick County operating independent or county-specific programs and all other counties routing through MDPACE managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Capital providers offer flexible financing options to finance both the C-PACE component and senior debt as part of projects. Long-term, fixed-rate financing for clean energy and energy efficiency improvements can be amortized over extended periods with flexible repayment terms, including 15 to 25 years, with the option to capitalize interest to defer initial payments. Financing is provided by private lenders and secured by a property assessment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property-assessed loans for energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy, resiliency, and environmental remediation in commercial and business buildings. Loans are typically 10-30+ years in length (standard 20-year terms available) and can be amortized over 15 to 25 years with flexible repayment terms. Loans are repaid through property tax bills with voluntary tax assessment securing the loan. There is no upfront cost to the property owner. Property owners can finance 100% of qualifying improvements, ranging from $50,000 to multi-million dollars with no maximum loan amount. Combined loan-to-value (CLTV) ratio cannot exceed 100% of assessed or market value (whichever is greater). Underwriting focuses on the underlying building rather than owner credit, and building owners with Non-Investment Grade Credit are eligible. Interest can be capitalized to defer initial payments for up to 36 months. Loan repayment transfers with the sale of the property. Private financing options are available through a network of registered MDPACE capital providers (such as Greenworks Lending and Nuveen Green Capital) who offer flexibility to finance both the C-PACE component and senior debt. Tax credits including solar investment tax credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation benefits (MACRS) are available. Projects can provide positive cash flow from day one. Surcharge payments are collected annually or semi-annually through real property tax bills as a separate line item and do not accelerate upon property sale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners, builders, businesses, nonprofits, property owners, capital providers, contractors, and local governments in Maryland counties that have enacted C-PACE-enabling legislation seeking to fund energy efficiency, renewable energy, and building improvement projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, water conservation, renewable energy, resiliency measures, environmental remediation (asbestos, lead paint, mold removal, indoor/water quality), solar equipment installation, building heat recovery systems, flood mitigation, stormwater management, fire and wind resistance improvements, energy storage, alternative vehicle charging, capital-intensive building retrofit and new construction projects, and clean energy projects on commercial and business buildings. Projects can range from appliance replacement to large-scale renovations. Building envelope improvements, HVAC system replacements, lighting upgrades. Includes costs for energy audits, feasibility studies, design, installation, construction, insurance, and loan closing costs. Hard costs (direct installation/construction), ancillary costs (necessary supporting construction), and soft costs (indirect project costs including project management, engineering, legal, permitting, appraisals, Phase 1 and Phase 2 Environmental Site Assessments).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in participating Maryland counties and municipalities that have passed C-PACE-enabling legislation and signed a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Frederick County operate independent or county-specific programs. All other participating counties operate through MDPACE managed by the Maryland Clean Energy Center. City of Baltimore participates with annual-only surcharge payment schedule requirements. Specific loan administration procedures vary by county based on local enabling legislation. Available statewide in Maryland through registered MDPACE Capital Providers for commercial and mixed-use properties. County-specific variations are delineated in the MDPACE County Matrix (Appendix F).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your county's C-PACE program administrator or the Maryland Clean Energy Center finance team via email at info@md-pace.com or by phone at 301-660-4718 to get an application started. Alternatively, apply through MD-PACE at md-pace.com or contact the provided email or phone number, which works with a network of registered private capital providers to deliver upfront financing. Property owners interested in C-PACE financing should contact their local county or municipality to determine if C-PACE is available in their jurisdiction. The program funds clean energy and efficiency projects including geothermal systems, energy efficiency measures, energy resiliency measures, mechanical equipment upgrades, combined heat and power, renewable energy production, micro grids, islanded generation, co-generation, and building envelope updates.

The program supports climate technology and clean energy innovators during the initial development phase of their ventures. The program is aimed at very early-stage concepts at Technology Readiness Level 1-3 with no prior investment and minimal commercial engagement. Graduates are eligible to continue into MEIA's Launchpad or Accelerator programs.

Tailored resources and services designed to support climate technology and clean energy companies during the pre-accelerator phase of their business development. Participants work between February and March with sessions held between January 13 and March 24.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEIA is a comprehensive three-phase investment readiness and startup acceleration program administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center that accelerates the commercialization of advanced energy and climate technologies from Maryland's businesses, universities, and laboratories. The program supports and funds inventors, scientists, and startup founders who are building climate technologies with the potential to help Maryland meet its climate goals and build upon a new growth industry. The program addresses key challenges including limited time to focus on business building, difficulty finding co-founders and advisors, navigating complex ecosystems, and accessing industry connections and capital. MEIA helps clean energy entrepreneurs, inventors, and founders develop their companies into investment-ready ventures by connecting them with experts, investors, and resources. Program phases include Phase 0 (Pre-Accelerator) to lay the foundation, Phase 1 (Launchpad) to gain tools and support, Phase 2 (Manufacturing Accelerator) to drive growth and scalability, and Phase 3 (Climate Technology Founders Fund) to propel startups forward. Program activities include accelerator services, mentorship from experienced advisors, training, networking opportunities, technical assistance, demo days, pitch competitions, site visits, and investment readiness programs. Participants can join one or all phases and benefit from specialized guidance, industry connections, and partner networks. The program has facilitated over $90 million in funding for participants and created over 175 jobs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEIA offers a three-phase program consisting of Phase 0 (Pre-Accelerator), Phase 1 (Launchpad), Phase 2 (Manufacturing Accelerator), and Phase 3 (Climate Technology Founders Fund). Participants receive investment readiness programs, pre-accelerator cohorts, mentorship from experienced advisors, connections to funding networks and investors, technical guidance, expert connections, networking support, business development resources, and opportunities to pitch to investors. The program provides accelerator infrastructure and comprehensive participant services to support business building, co-founder and advisor connections, ecosystem navigation, industry connections, and capital access. Financial support is available subject to fund availability and approval by the Fund Oversight Committee. The program funds climate technology projects and startup companies. The Climate Technology Founders Fund was established to empower entrepreneurs working on emission-reducing technology solutions. The program has facilitated over $90 million in funding for participants and created over 175 jobs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage clean energy and climate technology innovators, inventors, scientists, and entrepreneurs from Maryland businesses, universities, and laboratories looking to bring new technologies to market, develop investible companies, commercialize advanced technologies, secure funding, and attract investment.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Entrepreneurs, inventors, and founders can express interest in applying through the MEIA website. Participants can join one or all phases of the program. The program runs cohorts throughout the year, including pre-accelerator phases, summer pre-accelerator programs, and fall investment readiness programs. Applications are accepted during designated periods on a regular cycle. The application process details are available on the MEIA inventors page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $5 million revolving fund launched by the Maryland Clean Energy Center in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration, designed to accelerate the deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems across affordable housing communities in Maryland. The fund provides capital for early-stage development to address financing gaps that delay or stall clean energy projects at affordable housing properties. The $4.5 million revolving line of credit finances early-stage development costs including engineering and design, interconnection and commissioning, and procurement and construction of solar and energy storage systems, with an additional $500,000 dedicated to program administration and oversight. As projects are completed and the line of credit is repaid, the capital is recycled back into the fund to finance new projects.

An additional $500,000 is dedicated to program administration and oversight. structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service grant administered through the Maryland Clean Energy Center to expand renewable, clean thermal energy through locally-sourced woody biomass. The program identifies high potential facilities with little access to renewable energy and high dependency on heating oil located near large forest stands needing active forest management. It helps facilities switch from fossil fuels to thermally-led woody biomass systems. The program includes a comprehensive wood fuel supply chain analysis assessing availability of wood fuel stocks across Maryland and surrounding counties, supporting forest industry and renewable energy industry expansion while improving forest health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides services including USFS Wood Education and Resource Center engineering and analysis services, IMPLAN analyses to show regional economic impact, bid-ready designs, wood supply chain development, pathway into economic development partners and funding programs, and community education and outreach materials. Funding supports wood fuel supply chain analysis, forest resource assessment, sustainability evaluation studies, and cost-benefit analysis of biomass heating systems.

Also serves foresters, loggers, mill and plant owners, policymakers, stakeholders, private landowners, timber harvesters, forest managers, arborists, municipal operations, wood fuel manufacturers, and pellet producers.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal USDA Rural Development program that provides matching grants and guaranteed loans to help agricultural producers and rural small businesses reduce energy costs and consumption by installing renewable energy systems or energy-efficient technologies. The program supports energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy system installation, helping applicants cut costs, save energy, and strengthen their businesses. Available to farms and small businesses located in rural areas nationwide, including Maryland. Also provides energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Renewable Energy Systems and Energy Efficiency Improvements Assistance: Grants ranging from $1,500–$500,000 for renewable energy system installation or energy efficiency improvements; Guaranteed loans up to $25 million for renewable energy systems and energy efficiency improvements. Energy Audit and Renewable Energy Development Assistance Grants: Up to $100,000 aggregate per recipient for fiscal year 2015. Eligible renewable energy systems include wind, solar, renewable biomass (including anaerobic digesters), small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from these renewable resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2015 (for $20,000 or less set-aside and general grants); June 30, 2015 (for unrestricted grants); February 12, 2015 (for energy audits and renewable energy development assistance grants); Continuous cycle for guaranteed loan-only applications

structured_extraction.program_name: Basic DME (Durable Medical Equipment) Re-Use Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Department of Aging that provides durable medical equipment such as canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, bedrails, manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, and mechanical lifts to Maryland residents in need. Equipment is provided at no cost through a re-use program and beneficiaries keep the equipment permanently. Equipment is available for pickup at designated satellite locations throughout the state or at the main Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, Maryland for complex equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides durable medical equipment at no cost to eligible individuals. Equipment includes basic items (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, bedrails) and complex equipment (manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts). Equipment is provided as a one-time allocation and remains with the beneficiary indefinitely. Equipment is picked up in person by appointment at designated satellite sites around the state for basic equipment, or at the main Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, Maryland for complex equipment. No delivery or installation is provided.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment can be used for mobility assistance (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters), bathroom safety (shower chairs, tub transfer benches, toilet safety rails), bedroom support (bedside commodes, bedrails, home hospital beds), and mechanical lifting assistance (mechanical lifts).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Equipment can be picked up at satellite sites around the state for basic equipment, or at the main Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, Maryland (11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623) for complex equipment such as wheelchairs, power scooters, and hospital beds.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nearly $134,000 in total grants distributed among six non-profit organizations. Individual grant awards ranged from $11,500 to $27,000 to support dementia care services, day programs, training initiatives, and support for caregivers and individuals with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias. Funding supports home- and community-based supportive services, day center scholarships, dementia training programs, transportation services, companionship and home visits, intergenerational programs, and dementia programming at adult day centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations providing services to individuals with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for comprehensive home- and community-based supportive services, day program scholarships, dementia care training programs, transportation services, companionship and home visits, intergenerational programs, and dementia programming at adult day centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. FY24 grants were awarded to organizations serving Worcester County, Kensington/Montgomery County, Baltimore, Salisbury/Wicomico County, and multiple regional centers (Baltimore, Hagerstown, Silver Spring).
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization
Must provide or support services for individuals with ADRD and their caregivers
Must implement comprehensive home- and community-based supportive services or improve coordination of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-profits are selected to receive grants for ADRD initiatives.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide no-wrong-door gateway to long-term services and supports that helps older adults, individuals with disabilities, caregivers, and professionals access health and support services. MAP specialists provide information, referral, options counseling, eligibility screening, and navigation assistance. Options Counseling is a person-centered service where trained counselors help individuals and caregivers plan and make informed decisions about long-term care by matching their needs, preferences, and values with available community services, developing personalized action plans, making referrals to appropriate agencies, and planning for current and future needs. Services are delivered through multiple access points including phone, email, in-person visits, and local MAP office locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MAP offers information, referral services, and Options Counseling to help individuals and caregivers access long-term services and supports. Services include assistance with health, transportation, income assistance, financial aid, senior and community centers, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, and volunteer opportunities. Person-centered Options Counseling helps individuals plan and make informed decisions about long-term care by matching their needs, preferences, and values with available resources, developing personalized action plans, and planning for current and future needs. Services are delivered through phone, email, in-person visits, and 20 local MAP office locations in all counties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 50 or older, adults age 18 or older with disabilities, caregivers for elderly and adults with disabilities, professionals, and all Maryland residents seeking aging, disability, and long-term services and support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigation assistance, information, referral, and Options Counseling to access programs and services for long-term services and supports including health, transportation, income assistance, financial aid, senior and community centers, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, and volunteer opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland with 20 local MAP office locations in all counties.
requirements_list: Be age 50 or older, OR be an adult age 18 or older with a disability, OR be a caregiver for an elderly person or adult with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465) or visit marylandaccesspoint.211md.org to reach a 211 Maryland information and referral specialist, or contact your local MAP office in person, by phone, or by email. Specialists will listen to your needs, identify local resources, and direct individuals with long-term and complex needs to their local MAP office for Options Counseling and navigation assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use - Complex DME
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides durable medical equipment at no cost to eligible Maryland residents. The program redistributes used complex medical equipment including manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars. Equipment is provided to eligible individuals based on medical need and availability. Once received, equipment belongs to the recipient permanently.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free complex durable medical equipment provided based on medical need and stock availability. Equipment includes manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars. Equipment must be picked up by appointment at the Cheltenham Re-Use Center or arranged satellite sites throughout Maryland. No delivery or installation services are provided. Once received, equipment belongs to the recipient permanently.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who need complex durable medical equipment and have a healthcare professional who can complete the required medical evaluation
