structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Complex durable medical equipment including manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars for individuals with mobility or medical equipment needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Complex DME equipment must be picked up by appointment at the main Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, MD, or at satellite locations throughout the state.
requirements_list: Completed Complex Request Form with all three parts (Part A completed by requestor, Parts B and C completed by healthcare professional)
Request must be completed by or on behalf of the equipment user, or by a family member, caregiver, or trusted individual

Healthcare professional completing parts B and C must be a Physician, Physician Assistant, Nurse Practitioner, Physical Therapist, or Occupational Therapist (power wheelchairs and power scooters require Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only)
Maryland resident status (implied)
Medical need as determined by healthcare professional
Requestor must sign a Liability Waiver and Release agreement
Equipment must be picked up by the requestor, beneficiary, or another designated individual (delivery is not available)
All required fields on the form must be completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requestor completes Part A of the Complex Request Form. Applications can be submitted online through Maryland OneStop or by hard copy. For online applications: create an OneStop account, verify email, complete Part A, then select whether the healthcare provider will complete Parts B and C online or via hard copy. For hard copy applications: download and print the form, complete Part A, and pass to healthcare professional for Parts B and C completion, then submit by mail, email, or fax. Program staff reviews the completed form and contacts requestor to confirm equipment availability and schedule a pickup appointment. Equipment pickup is by appointment only at designated sites.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Aging that collects, sanitizes, and refurbishes gently-used durable medical equipment and makes it available at no cost to Maryland residents of any age who need equipment for mobility and safety. The program serves individuals with any illness, injury, or disability, including children, and those who have exhausted other means of obtaining equipment through insurance or other sources. Equipment available includes canes, crutches, walkers, knee scooters, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, rollators, manual and transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, bed rails, and mechanical lifts. Products are available for pickup at several distribution centers across Maryland. The program improves quality of life by providing access to mobility equipment and helping people avoid costlier levels of care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides durable medical equipment at no cost to eligible Maryland residents. Equipment includes basic items (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails) and complex items (manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, bed rails). Equipment is collected via donation, sanitized, repaired, and redistributed at no cost to eligible recipients. For basic equipment, applicants can apply online. Complex DME equipment requires input from a qualified medical professional. Equipment is available for pickup at several distribution centers across Maryland. Service is subject to availability, and pick-up appointments are scheduled; delivery is not available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of any age with any illness, injury, or disability who require durable medical equipment for mobility and safety, including children, and have exhausted other means of obtaining equipment through insurance. Also serves healthcare providers who can request equipment on behalf of patients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Durable and home medical equipment for mobility and accessibility needs including wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, lifts, shower chairs, bathroom safety equipment, and other assistive devices to help individuals remain safe at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents with pickup and collection locations at several distribution centers across Maryland. The beneficiary of the equipment must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have any illness, injury, or disability
No age restrictions
Must have exhausted all other means of obtaining durable medical equipment including through insurance coverage (Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance)
Individuals with insurance coverage should attempt to obtain equipment through insurance providers first
Request for complex equipment must be initiated by a healthcare professional (Physical Therapist, Occupational Therapist, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP)
For power wheelchairs and power scooters, request must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only
Equipment subject to availability
Request process requires completion of appropriate DME Request Form (Basic or Complex)
Pick-up is required; delivery is not available
Need support to remain safe at home and connected to communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Fill out the appropriate DME Request Form based on equipment type needed (Basic DME Request Form or Complex DME Request Form). For basic DME equipment, applicants can apply online. For complex DME equipment, a healthcare professional (PT, OT, MD, DO, PA, or CRNP) assesses patient need and completes Parts B and C of the Request Form in black or blue ink; patient or caregiver completes Part A, signs the Liability Waiver and Release Agreement, and provides their signature. 2. Submit completed form by mail to Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use, 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623, by email to DME.MDOA@maryland.gov, or online. Healthcare providers can also initiate requests on behalf of patients by completing a Complex DME Request Form. 3. Program staff will process the request and contact you via phone to notify if equipment is in stock. 4. If equipment is available, a pick-up appointment will be scheduled at a distribution center. 5. Equipment pick up is by appointment only. Contact the Maryland Department of Aging DME Program at 240-230-8000 or visit their website for information on how to request equipment and collection site locations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center
structured_extraction.program_description: Offers free high-tech assistive technology to Maryland residents with disabilities. Supports the Technology First framework by providing innovative resources paired with training and support to help users integrate technology into daily life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free high-tech assistive technology including closed-circuit TVs, video magnifiers, magnifiers, iDevices, adapted computer keyboards and mice, switches, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, and eye-gaze systems. Products available for pickup at designated locations with training and support provided to help integrate technology into daily life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: High-tech assistive technology to support communication, computer access, and daily living activities, including training for using innovative resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide with a pickup location
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an online application form. Contact Shawn Bateman at 410-554-9232 or MDTAP.AT-Reuse@maryland.gov for information about available products and pickup locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: An anti-health care fraud project that enlists senior volunteers to teach Medicare and Medicaid clients how to recognize and report health care fraud, waste, abuse, or error. The program provides free, confidential assistance to senior Medicare and Medicaid consumers through trained volunteers. It educates beneficiaries on how to protect their Medicare and health insurance cards from fraudulent activities and uses trained volunteers to accomplish program goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides individual counseling available in person or by phone, home counseling visits for Medicare beneficiaries who are physically unable to visit a service site, community educational meetings to help seniors learn about and report health care fraud, waste, abuse or error, and access to information and services through a website. Services are provided by trained SMP volunteers at no cost to beneficiaries. Trains volunteers to educate Medicare beneficiaries about health insurance fraud and misuse prevention.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, seniors, caregivers, and families seeking to learn about and report health care fraud, waste, abuse, or error.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education on recognizing and reporting Medicare and Medicaid fraud, waste, abuse, and billing errors. Assistance with reviewing insurance statements and billing documents. Educational resources and training on Medicare fraud prevention and health insurance protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with counselors and services available in all 24 Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Be a Medicare or Medicaid beneficiary or their caregiver, family member, or someone seeking information about health care fraud prevention
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Senior Medicare Patrol counselors in your county by phone for free and confidential assistance. County-specific phone numbers are provided for all 24 Maryland counties. You can also contact the main line at 877-808-2468 to request free My Health Care Trackers or for other assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A three-year pilot program that supports villages in taking advantage of operational efficiencies and existing systems, skills, and resources to expand services to more residents in the geographic region. The program supports the Montgomery County Village Consortium to implement this model.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-year pilot program providing support and funding to enable villages to expand services to more residents in their geographic region by leveraging operational efficiencies and existing systems, skills, and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The Montgomery County Village Consortium and village organizations serving older adults in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion of village services to additional residents in the geographic region through operational improvements and resource sharing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County - specifically the Montgomery County Village Consortium is selected to implement the pilot program
requirements_list: Must be the Montgomery County Village Consortium
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MDOA must select the Montgomery County Village Consortium to implement the pilot program for a three-year period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Aging through local Maryland Access Point offices, Area Agencies on Aging, and county-level coordinators, including St. Mary's County Department of Aging & Human Services. The program provides comprehensive support to family caregivers caring for someone older than age 60, caregivers of any age caring for people with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, and grandparents and other relatives over age 55 who are caring for children age 18 or under or adult children with disabilities. Services include information and referral, assistance with locating resources, education, training, financial assistance for respite care (up to $800 per year in some jurisdictions), and support for out-of-pocket caregiving expenses. Some jurisdictions, including St. Mary's County, offer one-time respite grants to offset the cost of hiring a caregiver. Funds can be used to hire providers for respite services or to reimburse for out-of-pocket expenses. The program helps reduce caregiver depression, anxiety, and stress, enabling caregivers to provide care longer and avoiding or delaying the need for costly institutional care. Monthly updates are provided via email or mail where available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers five types of caregiver services including financial assistance for respite care (up to $800 per year in some jurisdictions), supplemental services, education, training, and information and resource navigation for eligible family caregivers. Some jurisdictions provide one-time respite grants to offset costs of hiring a caregiver of the family's choice, with award amounts contingent upon availability of funds. Funds can be used to hire providers for respite services or to reimburse out-of-pocket caregiving expenses. Available through local Maryland Access Point offices, Area Agencies on Aging throughout the state, and county-level coordinators. Monthly caregiver updates provided via email or mail where available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult family members or other informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals 60 years of age and older; caregivers of any age providing care to individuals with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders; grandparents and other relatives (not natural or adoptive parents) age 55 and older providing care to children age 18 or under; grandparents and other relatives (not natural or adoptive parents) age 55 and older providing care to adults age 18-59 with disabilities; and families caring for aging family members, seniors caring for grandchildren under 18, and parents caring for adult children with disabilities. No income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and referral, education, training, respite care (up to $800 per year), supplemental services, reimbursement for out-of-pocket caregiving expenses, one-time respite grants to offset the cost of hiring a caregiver, and support for family and informal caregivers to care for loved ones at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland through local Maryland Access Point offices, Area Agencies on Aging, and county-level caregiver program coordinators, including Calvert County, Frederick County, and St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or older (or 55 or older for grandparents/relatives caring for children or disabled adults) and serving in an informal caregiving role
Care recipient must be age 60 or older, OR any age with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, OR a child under 18, OR an adult age 18-59 with disabilities
Grandparent or relative caregivers cannot be the child's natural or adoptive parent
No income requirements
Family member must be aging or grandchild must be under 18 years old or adult child with disability must be 18 years or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Access Point office at 1-844-MAP-LINK (TTY #711), your county caregiver program coordinator, or your local Area Agency on Aging for more information. For St. Mary's County, contact Program Coordinator Lisa Berry at 301-475-4200, ext. 1056, or email Lisa.Berry@stmaryscountymd.gov. County programs may require submission of a respite application form and W-9 form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program supporting neighborhoods or housing developments where a large percentage of residents have aged in place. Provides programming, service coordination, and community support to concentrated areas where low-income older adults face problems of declining health, isolation, financial hardship, and language barriers. Encompasses three complementary projects—Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, and Traditional NORC—each tailored to meet specific needs of older adults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants to community-based organizations to provide programming, service coordination, and community support in concentrated areas of low-income older adults. FY26 awarded $1.3 million total to 7 community-based organizations with individual grants ranging from $75,000 to $325,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations and government agencies serving concentrated populations of low-income older adults in Maryland, including Holocaust survivors and residents at risk of elder abuse
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programming, service coordination, and community support for older adults in naturally occurring retirement communities; elder abuse prevention services; support for Holocaust survivors; traditional NORC aging-in-place services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland to organizations serving concentrated areas of low-income older adults
requirements_list: Must be a community-based organization or government agency
Must serve concentrated areas with large populations of low-income older adults
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Grant Availability page for information on NORC and other funding opportunities and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A daily check-in service that places automated telephone calls or text messages to Maryland residents age 60 and older at a regularly scheduled time between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. If the participant does not answer, up to two additional automated calls are made, and if those go unanswered, an alternate contact is called to check on the participant. If both the participant and alternate do not answer, the local non-emergency service is notified.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Daily automated telephone calls or text messages placed between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. within a pre-selected one-hour time block. The service is available every day of the year except for 6 holidays (New Year's, Memorial Day, 4th of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas). Phone lines are open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 60 and older who have a landline phone or cell phone (TTY available). Participants and alternates should not have automated call blocking technology enabled.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Daily wellness check-in calls or text messages to verify the safety and well-being of older adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any Maryland resident age 60 or older.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years of age or older
Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a landline phone or cell phone
Should not have automated call blocking technology enabled (or should disable it for this program)
Must select an alternate contact or accept an assigned Limited Alternate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two ways to apply: (1) Click REGISTER NOW on the Senior Call Check sign-up page, or (2) Call toll-free 1-866-502-0560 to request a hard copy application mailed to your home. Once an application is submitted, the applicant receives a verification call to confirm information and conduct a successful test automated call to both the participant and alternate where applicable. After all information is validated, a Welcome Packet is mailed with the start date and chosen communication method. Daily calls begin after verification is complete.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides access to legal advice, counseling, and representation to older Marylanders, with legal support to local Ombudsmen, Health Insurance Counselors, and Public Guardianship managers. Priority is given to issues involving income maintenance, nutrition, public/disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination/civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal advice, counseling, and representation to eligible seniors. Area Agencies on Aging contract with local attorneys and law centers to provide services. There is no cost for legal assistance with priority issues. Preference is given to older adults with the greatest economic or social need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any resident of Maryland who is 60 years of age and older, or caregivers of that person.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal advice, counseling, and representation for priority issues including income maintenance, nutrition, public and disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination, civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years of age or older or a caregiver of such a person
Must be a resident of Maryland
Preference given to older adults with greatest economic or social need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging's Maryland Access Point (MAP) to seek assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, unbiased counseling and assistance program for Medicare-eligible beneficiaries, their families, caregivers, and senior citizens. SHIP provides trained staff and volunteer counselors to help people understand Medicare coverage options and costs, compare and enroll in plans, choose between Medicare Advantage and Medigap, pay for Medicare and prescriptions, resolve billing issues and appeals, identify healthcare fraud and marketing violations, and access other resources. Services are delivered through one-on-one consultations, group presentations, self-enrollment computer labs, and referrals to additional resources across all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City, with regional offices in areas such as La Plata, Waldorf, and Western Charles County, and county-specific programs including Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, confidential one-on-one counseling and community education provided by trained staff and volunteer counselors in all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Services include plan comparison and enrollment assistance, coverage and cost explanations, Medicare Supplement Plans and Medicare Advantage information, financial assistance program eligibility guidance, preventive services information, billing issue resolution and appeals assistance, fraud reporting, identification of prescription drug assistance programs, assistance with Medicare premium payments through programs like QMB (Qualified Medicare Beneficiary) and SLMB (Specified Low Income Medicare Beneficiary), and referrals to other resources. No direct financial assistance is provided; the program offers guidance on navigating Medicare benefits and enrollment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare-eligible beneficiaries, their families, caregivers, and senior citizens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with Medicare plan selection, enrollment, understanding coverage options, resolving billing issues and appeals, accessing financial assistance programs, prescription drug assistance, and Medigap policies. The program offers free technical assistance and counseling services to help beneficiaries navigate Medicare benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City through local SHIP offices and Information and Assistance Offices in areas such as La Plata, Waldorf, and Western Charles County, with senior activity centers also serving St. Mary's County, and county-specific programs in Anne Arundel County. Services are available in Maryland and nationwide through partner organizations.
requirements_list: Must be Medicare-eligible or a family member or caregiver of a Medicare-eligible beneficiary
Income and asset guidelines apply for assistance with prescription drugs and Medicare premiums
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the statewide SHIP line at 410-767-1100 to connect with your local SHIP office, or contact your county-specific SHIP counselor directly using the provided phone directory. Regional offices can be reached at 301-609-5712 (La Plata area), 240-448-2816 (Waldorf area), or 301-934-9305 (Western Charles County). One-on-one appointments can be scheduled with a SHIP counselor. Self-enrollment computer labs are offered at participating libraries and senior centers during open enrollment periods.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging's Assistive Technology Program has partnered with centers for independent living across the state to make available a variety of portable ramps to Marylanders who need short-term solutions for getting in and out of their homes. Ramps are typically loaned for up to 120 days (4 months) and are fully compliant with ADA requirements. Borrowers arrange pickup from their local Center for Independent Living and coordinate return at the end of the loan period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of portable ramps compliant with ADA requirements, typically available for up to 120 days (4 months). Borrowers arrange pickup from their local Center for Independent Living and coordinate return at the end of the loan period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders who need short-term accessibility solutions for home entry and exit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing portable ramps for temporary accessibility needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Centers for Independent Living
requirements_list: Need for short-term ramp access
Ability to arrange pickup and return of ramp
Must arrange pickup and return through local Center for Independent Living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Center for Independent Living to inquire about borrowing a portable ramp. Ramps are typically loaned for up to 120 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that supports the village concept, which provides a holistic approach to aging in place by addressing the practical, social, and emotional needs of older adults within a supportive community framework. The program empowers older adults to maintain their independence, dignity, and sense of belonging as they navigate the challenges and opportunities of aging.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Support and funding for village organizations throughout Maryland to provide services and programs that address practical, social, and emotional needs of older adults seeking to age in place.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Village organizations and senior village networks serving older adults in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs and services addressing practical, social, and emotional needs of older adults within supportive community frameworks that enable aging in place
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to village organizations throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a village organization serving older adults
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Grant Availability page or Maryland's Village Model Directory for information on Village Support and Expansion Projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to individuals, vendors, and businesses to develop and showcase proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste in Maryland. The fund encourages development and implementation of economically feasible technologies that protect public health and environment by reducing nutrients from animal waste. Eligible technologies may reduce nutrient levels in animal waste, change its form or function for other uses, or generate energy and marketable products from waste. Technologies evaluated include anaerobic digestion, gasification, pyrolysis, composting, and manure injection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $750,000 is available for Fiscal Year 2026 to fund innovative animal waste management technology projects. Financial support for animal waste treatment technology projects including technology development, installation, and operation. Projects must demonstrate potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being, offer alternative waste management solutions, and have positive economic development impact. Assistance includes permit help and technical support. Additional consideration is given to projects addressing climate and community benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due October 17, 2025; Full grant proposal due December 23, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, vendors, and businesses with innovative animal waste technology solutions; Farmers; Agricultural producers; Dairy operations; Crop farmers; Poultry operations; Vulnerable and historically marginalized communities near waste facilities; Minority and low-income rural communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and implementation of proven innovative technologies for managing animal waste, including nutrient reduction, waste form/function conversion, energy generation, and marketable product development from animal waste. Installation of animal waste treatment technologies (anaerobic digesters, composters, gasification/pyrolysis systems). Infrastructure development (buildings, generators, interconnection lines). Renewable energy generation equipment. Environmental monitoring and community engagement. Manure injection, lagoon covering systems, and Digester Affected Food (DAF) processing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Priority consideration for concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs). Special focus areas include Frederick, Washington, Carroll, and Garrett counties (cattle production), and Worcester, Caroline, Somerset, and Wicomico counties (poultry production). Eastern Shore has poultry litter management focus. Northern Maryland emphasizes cattle production.
requirements_list: Projects must involve animal waste generated by on-farm animals or through animal production processes involving Maryland livestock
Projects must demonstrate potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being
Projects must offer alternative waste management solutions for the agricultural sector
Projects must have positive economic development impact in the state
Projects in the research and development stage are ineligible
Technologies must be proven, not in research and development stage
Must address nutrient management requirements
Environmental justice considerations and community engagement required
Greenhouse gas emissions reduction initiatives encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants submit a Letter of Intent by the deadline. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the department in consultation with the Animal Waste Technology Evaluation Committee. High-ranking projects are invited to submit a full grant proposal by the subsequent deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state program established in 2020 by House Bill 1488 and modified in 2023 (HB 63) and 2024 (SB 290) that encourages state agencies and public universities to purchase at least 20 percent of their food from farms with nutrient management plans, seafood dealers licensed as Tidal Fish Dealers, and Chesapeake Invasive Species Providers. The program maintains a directory of certified local farms and providers that state institutions can use when making food procurement decisions to increase economic opportunity and participation of qualified Maryland farms and seafood processors in state government procurement.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers, seafood dealers, and invasive species providers can become certified and listed in the online directory at no cost. Certification requires farms to have nutrient management plans, seafood dealers to be licensed as Tidal Fish Dealers with Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or invasive species providers to meet program requirements. State agencies and universities then use this directory to source food purchases, with a goal of 20 percent of total food procurement value coming from certified providers. Directory listings must be renewed annually with renewal prompts at 90 days, 7 days, and final day. This creates a market subsidy by giving certified farms, dealers, and providers preferential access to state purchasing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual deadline: September 30 each year for state agency reports and waiver requests; October 31 for waiver reports to Board of Public Works; Directory renewal prompts at 90 days, 7 days, and final day before expiration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers with nutrient management plans, seafood dealers licensed as Tidal Fish Dealers with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, and Chesapeake Invasive Species Providers who want to supply food to Maryland state agencies and public universities. Also targets state agencies, public four-year universities, food service management companies, and prime contractors and subcontractors involved in food procurement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance to farmers, dealers, or providers. It facilitates market access by maintaining a certified directory that state agencies and universities use for food procurement. The subsidy value comes from increased sales opportunities through state purchasing, with state agencies and universities required to achieve a 20 percent procurement goal from certified local providers. Providers can distribute products more than one hour away from their farm.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide to all Maryland farms, seafood dealers, and invasive species providers that meet certification requirements. State agencies and public four-year universities must attempt to achieve the 20 percent purchasing goal from certified providers.
requirements_list: Must be a farm with a nutrient management plan registered with Maryland Department of Agriculture, or an apiarist or aquaculturist meeting nutrient management requirements
OR must be a seafood dealer licensed as a Tidal Fish Dealer with Maryland Department of Natural Resources
OR must be a Chesapeake Certified Invasive Species Provider
Must register through the online application on Maryland OneStop
Must select applicant type (Farm or Seafood Dealer) and complete all required fields marked with red asterisks
MDA verifies certification status based on nutrient management plan, Tidal Fish Dealer license, or invasive species provider qualification
No cost to become certified
Must update directory information once annually with renewal prompts at 90 days, 7 days, and final day
Subject to annual renewal

State agencies and universities must submit annual reports by September 30 and structure food procurement to achieve 20% of total food dollar value from Certified Local Providers through prime vendors, subcontractors, or direct purchase
State agencies and universities must consult the Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory and make good faith efforts to source from listed vendors
Waiver requests available for agencies/universities unable to meet 20% goal, with documentation of efforts and limitations required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers, seafood dealers, and invasive species providers register through the online application on Maryland OneStop (https://onestop.md.gov/) by searching for 'Certified Local Farm and Fish Program Application'. Applicants select their type, complete all required fields marked with red asterisks, and submit via the green Submit button. They receive confirmation and can view/print their submission. The Maryland Department of Agriculture verifies that the applicant has a nutrient management plan (or equivalent for apiarists and aquaculturists), is licensed as a Tidal Fish Dealer with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or meets invasive species provider requirements. Once verified, the applicant receives certification notification and is added to the online directory with contact information, product list, and certification number. Directory information must be updated annually. State agencies and universities consult the directory and make good faith efforts to source 20% of their food procurement from certified providers, submitting annual reports and waiver requests by September 30 each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Department of Agriculture registers commercial weighing and measuring devices used throughout Maryland to ensure that consumers receive the correct amounts of products they purchase. All scales and meters used during sales transactions where products are bought or sold must be registered each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual registration of commercial weighing and measuring devices such as scales, gasoline meters, and grain moisture meters used in sales transactions. A certificate of registration is issued upon payment of the appropriate fee. Devices must be approved by the National Type Evaluation Program (NTEP) operated by the National Council on Weights & Measures if manufactured or installed in Maryland after October 1, 1992.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that buy or sell commodities by weight, measure, or count, including gasoline stations, grocery stores, delis, candy stores, jewelry stores, laundromats, package shipping stores, quarries, hardware stores, home heating oil companies, propane distributors, and other similar businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration of commercial weighing and measuring devices used in sales transactions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Pre-approval required by calling (410) 841-5790 to notify the Department of Agriculture
Devices must be registered annually
Registrations must be renewed by May 31 each year

Commercial weighing and measuring devices manufactured or installed in Maryland after October 1, 1992 must be approved by the National Type Evaluation Program (NTEP) operated by the National Council on Weights & Measures
Information required for pre-approval includes make, model, serial number and the number of devices installed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Call (410) 841-5790 to notify the Department of Agriculture that a commercial weighing or measuring device has been placed into commercial service and provide the required information. Step 2: Complete the Device Registration Application form provided by the Department of Agriculture. Step 3: Pay the appropriate registration fee via the Weights and Measures Payment Portal or by submitting payment with the application. Step 4: Email the completed application form and payment to mda.weights@maryland.gov. Step 5: Upon receipt of the application and fee, a certificate of registration is mailed to the applicant. Average processing time is five days. Registrations must be received prior to May 31 for annual renewal.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Income Tax Subtraction Modification for Conservation Equipment helps farmers offset costs to buy certain types of conservation equipment to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, and protect local water quality. The incentive allows farmers to subtract eligible equipment purchases from taxable income on Maryland individual and corporate tax returns. Farmers can subtract 100% of eligible equipment costs from taxable income (50% for vertical tillage equipment), with excess subtraction carrying forward up to five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers can subtract 100% of eligible conservation equipment purchases from taxable income on Maryland individual and corporate tax returns (50% for vertical tillage equipment). Excess subtraction may carry forward up to five years, providing tax relief to offset equipment costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural businesses engaged in agricultural production who purchase conservation equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: No-till planting equipment, liquid manure injection equipment, poultry or livestock manure spreading equipment, deep no-till rippers, global positioning devices, optical sensing and nutrient application systems, and vertical tillage equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Equipment must have useful life of at least four years
Equipment must be owned for at least three years after tax year subtraction is taken
Equipment purchased after specified dates (varies by equipment type; earliest 12/31/1985, latest 12/31/2012)
Equipment must meet specific functional requirements per type
Certification through local soil conservation district required
Must provide signed and dated equipment receipt with serial numbers
Equipment must be used in agricultural production
Nutrient Management Plan required for certain equipment
Maryland Department of Agriculture approval required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the certificate application with equipment and taxpayer information, obtain Soil Conservation District certification, and submit to the Maryland Department of Agriculture for approval to claim the tax subtraction on Maryland tax returns.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal-state partnership program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture in conjunction with the Federal Farm Service Agency, the Maryland Department of the Environment, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, Soil Conservation Districts, and Maryland Forest Service. The program provides payments above normal rental rates to landowners for establishing riparian forest buffers, retiring highly erodible lands, restoring wetlands and shallow water habitats, and taking environmentally sensitive cropland out of production for 10 to 15 years to protect and improve water quality and wildlife habitat. The program includes a main rental component that pays landowners and farmers attractive rental rates, a bonus payment component for riparian forest buffers and other conservation practices, and a state-funded easement component (instituted in 2009 by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources) that makes CREP Contract Areas permanent through state-funded conservation easements. Farmers who plant new riparian forest buffers next to streams qualify for a one-time signing bonus of up to $1,000 per acre and additional $100 per acre incentive from the State of Maryland. Forest buffer plantings receive a 100% rental rate bonus, while herbaceous buffers receive an 80% rental rate bonus. Under the easement component, landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts can add up to ten times their contract acreage to their CREP easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. The conservation easement is a perpetual legal agreement filed with county land records that specifies restrictions on land use, prohibits new structures, and transfers with the property to all future owners, remaining effective in perpetuity. After the federal contract expires, landowners can enter into a permanent easement agreement with the State of Maryland to maintain approved conservation practices forever. The program also provides cost share assistance as a percentage of total cost to accomplish forest improvement practices, usually between 50% and 75% of the practice cost. A forest stewardship management plan is typically required first. Participation is voluntary and provides steady, dependable land rental income along with cost-share assistance for streamside buffers, wetlands, livestock fencing and related stream protection practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides multiple forms of assistance: (1) Attractive land rental payments to take environmentally sensitive cropland out of production for 10 to 15 years and plant conservation buffers and practices that protect water quality and provide wildlife habitat; (2) One-time signing bonus and one-time bonus payments of up to $1,000 per acre from the State plus $100 per acre additional incentive for farmers who plant new riparian forest buffers next to streams, with forest buffer plantings receiving 100% rental rate bonus and herbaceous buffers receiving 80% rental rate bonus; (3) Purchase of conservation easements on properties with existing Federal FSA CREP Contracts, making those contract areas permanent through state-funded easements with 75-100% cost share; (4) Sign-up bonuses, yearly rental payments, maintenance payments, and cost-share assistance for streamside buffers, wetlands, livestock fencing and related stream protection practices; (5) Perpetual conservation easements that create a written legal agreement allowing landowners to maintain their land in approved conservation practices forever after federal contract expiration; (6) Cost share assistance provided as a percentage of total cost to accomplish forest improvement practices, usually between 50% and 75% of the practice cost. Landowners can add up to ten times the amount of acreage in their CREP Contract to their CREP easement. Once an easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity. Contracts are 10-15 years for the initial contract period. After the federal contract expires, the landowner agrees to enter into a permanent easement agreement with the State of Maryland. The program covers all Maryland setback requirements and helps finance required stream protection practices for livestock operations. Funding must be allocated prior to the beginning of any work.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Sign-up for Maryland CREP is ongoing until acreage goals are met; re-enrollment deadline is June 1 of the year after contract expiration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners and farmers with environmentally sensitive cropland, particularly those with cropland used in two of the five most recent years or marginal pasture adjacent to streams, including those with existing Federal FSA CREP Contracts who wish to enroll in permanent easement provisions. Private landowners and livestock operators are also eligible. Landowners with eligible property who wish to implement forest improvement practices are also eligible. Tenants are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land rental income in exchange for taking cropland out of production and installing conservation practices including riparian forest buffers, retiring highly erodible lands, restoring wetlands, establishing shallow water habitats, livestock fencing, and/or purchase of conservation easements to make CREP Contract Areas permanent through perpetual easements that maintain approved conservation practices. Land must be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan. Cost share assistance may also be used to defray costs of forest improvement practices recommended in a forest stewardship management plan. The program covers all Maryland setback requirements and helps finance required stream protection practices for livestock operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland with goal to enroll 100,000 acres of environmentally sensitive land in the Chesapeake Bay watershed through USDA Farm Service Agency offices and the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Eligibility depends on property size and availability of funds. Cropland next to streams or highly erodible land within 1,000 feet of streams is particularly targeted. All Maryland counties are now eligible as of January 2024.
requirements_list: Must own or farm environmentally sensitive cropland
Must agree to take land out of production for 10 to 15 years
Must plant eligible conservation buffers and practices
Eligible areas must have been planted as cropland in two of the five most recent years
Marginal pasture adjacent to streams is eligible if suitable for riparian forest buffer planting
Must have an existing FSA CREP Contract in order to apply for the easement program component
Conservation practices must be installed
No commodity crops can be grown on enrolled land during contract period
Haying, grazing, and harvesting for agricultural or commercial purposes prohibited during contract period
Participation commitment of 10-15 years required for initial contract
Must agree to keep the land in an approved conservation practice forever after the federal contract expires for easement component
Land must be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan
No new structures may be built on enrolled lands
Landowner must have an existing or completed federal CREP or CRP contract
Landowner must have already installed the prescribed CREP or CRP conservation practice(s)
Voluntary participation
Landowner must have eligible land for conservation practices
Maintain conservation practices for the contract term
Landowner must have property of eligible size
Forest stewardship management plan must be written for the property
Funding must be allocated prior to beginning any work
Practice must be recommended in the forest stewardship management plan
Must be a farmer or rural landowner
Must commit to removing environmentally sensitive agricultural land from production for 10-15 years
Must install conservation practices to protect streams and create wildlife habitat
Must allow annual monitoring visits for easement component
Must notify easement holder of proposed changes
Must notify easement holder when selling or transferring property
Must comply with easement restrictions
Must pay property taxes and maintain land
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enrollment is non-competitive and open. Contact the program manager, your local USDA Farm Service Agency office, USDA Service Center in Maryland, your county forester, or your local soil conservation district for assistance with CREP application and enrollment. Visit the CREP page for application instructions. Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts can apply to sell a CREP conservation easement that can include additional acreage up to ten times the contract acreage amount. Applicants work with Maryland DNR to develop a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan tailored to their specific land and situation. A conservation easement legal document is created specifying the restrictions on land use and the conservation practices to be maintained. The easement is then filed with the county land records and conveyed to a qualified government agency or nonprofit conservation organization. The county forester can help by furnishing technical specifications, setting up recommended practices, and arranging for contract crews to perform the practice. After the federal contract expires, the landowner agrees to enter into a permanent easement agreement with the State of Maryland. Additional information is available in the CREP Start to Finish guide.

structured_extraction.program_description: A premium incentive program that pays farmers higher rates to plant cover crop mixes on the same fields for 3 consecutive years using enhanced practices to improve soil health, increase biodiversity, and improve water quality. The program provides base payments of $125 per acre per year for growing approved cover crop mixes, with optional add-on practices that can increase payments up to $180 per acre per year. Farmers sign a 3-year contract and may enroll up to 500 acres.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Base payment of $125 per acre per year for growing approved cover crop mixes on the same fields for 3 consecutive years. Optional add-on practices can increase payments up to $180 per acre per year. Farmers sign a 3-year contract and may enroll up to 500 acres. Enhanced grants are provided for cover crop practices to farmers participating in conservation programs. Optional add-ons must be new practices not used in the previous 3 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural landowners operating agricultural land in Maryland who want to improve soil health through cover cropping practices and use enhanced practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement payments for growing multispecies cover crops with required compositions (at least 50% cereal grain or ryegrass and 25% legume) and managing them to maintain living roots and residue for soil and water quality benefits. Cover crop establishment and maintenance; soil health improvement; water quality enhancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland farmers who meet eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Must meet Maryland's definition of an agricultural operation
If leasing land, must confirm enrolled acres will be under your care for the entire 3-year term

Must be in good standing with Maryland Nutrient Management Program, Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program, Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation Program, and other MDA conservation grant programs
Must submit current Nutrient Management Plan Certification with application
Must sign 3-year contract to grow cover crop mixes on same fields
May enroll up to 500 acres
Must maintain living root system on enrolled fields throughout the year
Must manage cover crops to achieve at least 30% residue for soil health and water quality
Fall cover crops must be planted within 10 days of harvesting previous crop or planted 'green' into standing crop, with planting deadline of October 15
Must plant multispecies cover crops with cereal grain or ryegrass at least 50% of mix and legume at least 25%
Only no-till or conservation tillage may be used throughout 3-year contract
Optional add-ons must be new practices not used in the previous 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district for assistance with applications and claim for payment forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cost-share grant program to help farmers plant cold-hardy cereal grains, legumes, and other fall cover crops following harvest of spring/summer crops. Cover crops recycle unused nutrients, prevent erosion, improve soil, remove greenhouse gases, and protect fields from extreme weather.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share grants to help farmers pay for seed and planting costs for fall cover crops. Cost-share rates vary year to year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Late June and early July (annual enrollment window); Planting deadline: early November; Early incentive deadline: October 10th; 2026-2027 sign-up opens June 22, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed and planting costs for fall cover crops; seed testing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Plant cover crops after corn, soybeans, sorghum, tobacco, vegetables, hemp, sunflowers, sod, or millet
10-acre minimum acreage
Must be in good standing with Conservation Grants and Nutrient Management programs
Must have completed Nutrient Management Plan Certification
Plant by early November to qualify; additional incentives if planted by October 10th
Termination by June 1, 2026
Certification required with local soil conservation district within one week of planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program manager or visit the Cover Crop Program page for application instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture Weights and Measures program requires registration of Electric Vehicle Service Equipment (EVSE chargers) used in commercial transactions with customers. The program includes a registration period, visual inspections, and testing to ensure chargers meet state and national standards, including NIST Handbook 44 specifications. EVSE charger owners must register their devices and pay a registration fee of $150 per port. Registration includes assignment of an account number, issuance of an invoice, and placement of weatherproof registration decals once fees are paid. Chargers that pass all requirements receive an MDA certification decal indicating the month and year of certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EVSE charger owners must register their devices with the department at a fee of $150 per port. Registration includes assignment of an account number, issuance of an invoice, and placement of weatherproof registration decals once fees are paid. The program provides visual inspections and technical testing to ensure devices meet National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Handbook 44 specifications for electrical vehicle fueling equipment. Chargers that pass all requirements receive an MDA certification decal indicating the month and year of certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 31, 2025 for open registration period; January 1, 2026 all chargers must be registered before use
structured_extraction.contact_name: Alison Wilkinson, Chief, Weights and Measures Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of Electric Vehicle Service Equipment (EVSE) chargers used in commercial transactions with customers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration and compliance with Maryland Weights and Measures requirements for electric vehicle charging equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. All EVSE chargers used in commercial transactions with customers located in Maryland must be registered.
requirements_list: EVSE chargers must be used in a commercial transaction with a customer to establish a charge
Each individual location must be separately registered with one form per location
All required information must be completed on the registration form
Number of ports must be specified on the registration form
Registration fees of $150 per port must be paid upon receipt of invoice
Starting January 1, 2026, all EVSE chargers must be registered before being available for customer use
Chargers installed after January 1, 2023 must have a National Type Evaluation Program (NTEP) Certificate of Conformance
Visual inspection must be passed to verify EVSE charger meets specifications
Unattended EVSE must have clearly displayed responsible party information including name, address, and phone number
Electricity must be sold in units of kilowatt-hours (kWh)
Charger must comply with NIST Handbook 44 specifications and standards
Do not send payment until receiving official invoice from Weights and Measures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one Device Registration Application form per individual location to the Weights and Measures Program at weights.measures@maryland.gov. Include the number of ports and complete all required information. The department will contact you within 5 business days to confirm account and may request additional information. An account number will be assigned and an invoice for registration fees will be emailed. Pay all fees upon receipt to complete registration. A mail group can be created for applicants with multiple locations to receive all notifications at one email address. After registration is complete, the charger will receive a registration decal. Visual inspections and testing will follow according to the program phases.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides farmers with a menu of conservation incentives that promote clean water, healthy soil and climate solutions. Includes Conservation Buffer Initiative, Tree Planting Incentives, CREP Signing Bonus, Cover Crop Plus, and Conservation Equipment Tax Break.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple forms of assistance including one-time bonus payments ($1,000/acre for forest buffers under CREP and Conservation Buffer Initiative), $2 per tree planted for tree-planting practices, cost-share funding for conservation practices (up to 87.5-100% depending on practice), and tax subtraction modification for conservation equipment purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural landowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streamside buffer planting, tree planting, cover crop implementation, conservation equipment purchases, riparian forest buffers, windbreaks, silvopasture, and hedgerows
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or agricultural landowner
Must implement eligible conservation practices
Contract terms of 10-15 years for CREP
Three consecutive years of cover crop planting for Cover Crop Plus
Must maintain living root system for cover crops
Must use qualifying conservation practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact local soil conservation district for free technical assistance and help with conservation needs. Contact the program manager or visit the Ecosystem Incentives Program page for specific sub-program application instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registration program for producers and packers of eggs in Maryland, including those who grade, package, and distribute eggs. Registration ensures that distributors and packers meet Maryland standards for quality, weight, labeling, and food safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Registration and oversight program. Egg producers and packers with fewer than 3,000 chickens register for free. All other producers, packers, and distributors pay a flat annual registration fee of $30 plus a variable fee of $0.08 per 30 dozen eggs sold to retailers, food service facilities, or consumers (fee does not apply to eggs sold to wholesalers). Registrations renew annually by December 31.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 15th for renewal; new registrants can apply at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Egg producers, packers, and repackers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a registration and regulatory oversight program, not a funding program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Premise must be located in Maryland; available statewide
requirements_list: Complete application form with accurate information
Pay applicable registration fees ($5.00, $30.00, or $30.00 depending on business type)
Must comply with Maryland Egg Law standards for quality, weight, labeling, and food safety
Must renew registration annually by December 31
Issue invoices, delivery tickets, or receipts to Maryland retailers and/or food service facilities
If employing one or more persons in Maryland, file certificate of compliance with State Workmen's Compensation Laws or provide policy/binder number
Maryland Poultry registration number if premise is located in Maryland
Notify Department within 15 days of changes in corporate or flock status
Producers and packers with more than 3,000 chickens should be familiar with USDA National Poultry Improvement Plan
Shell egg packers and producer-packers with more than 3,000 chickens must comply with 7 CFR Part 59 regulations administered by the USDA
Safe handling statement in bold capitals in box with hairlines (minimum 1/16" height) on cartons/cases
Packer/distributor name and address on labels (minimum 1/16")
Packer registration number on labels (minimum 1/16")
Lot designation on labels (minimum 1/16")
Product identity as 'eggs' on principal display panel (minimum 1/4")
Net quantity in weight or count on labels
Grade classification (AA or A) and size on principal display panel (minimum 1/4")
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant completes an application form provided by the Department of Agriculture. Two application forms are available: Producer/Packer Application or Distributor Application. Average processing time is 40 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fall Manure Transport and Injection Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Cost-share grants to help farmers inject all types of liquid manure into their fields for spring or fall-planted crops, supporting nutrient management compliance and water quality protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share grants funding manure injection services. Up to $45 per acre for use of purchased injection equipment (invoice required). Transport costs based on travel distance between manure source and field. Funds may be used to hire custom operators, rent or lease equipment, or offset operating costs associated with manure injection.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers managing manure in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hire custom operators, rent or lease manure injection equipment, offset operating costs associated with manure injection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland counties. Contact your soil conservation district for specific details.
requirements_list: Manure must be injected below soil surface
Applicants must be in good standing with Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program
Applicants must be in good standing with Maryland Nutrient Management Program
Additional restrictions may apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact or visit your local soil conservation district for application instructions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture helps Maryland farmers, processors, breeders, waterfront businesses, and other producers overcome technical issues in exporting by providing access to experts in overseas shipping, navigating global trade complexities like language and business practices, and facilitating exports to over 35 countries. The program introduces Maryland businesses to international buyers and helps facilitate mutually beneficial relationships through guidance on international trade complexities, partnerships with USDA, Foreign Agricultural Service, U.S. Department of Commerce, and U.S. Export Assistance Center.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Marketing staff and trade experts provide comprehensive guidance on international trade complexities through direct resources and partnerships with USDA, Foreign Agricultural Service, U.S. Department of Commerce, and U.S. Export Assistance Center. Services include identifying and evaluating export opportunities, developing trade leads and strategies, making introductions to overseas buyers and distributors, organizing international trade missions and shows, providing access to export research and programs, conducting outreach meetings and training seminars, and furnishing technical export assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based companies and farmers, processors, breeders, waterfront businesses, producers, and suppliers seeking international market expansion and looking to export their products internationally
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: International trade development, market research, export strategy, participation in trade missions and trade shows, and buyer connections for agricultural and other products
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program serving Maryland businesses exporting to international and global markets over 35 countries
requirements_list: Completion of International Marketing Assistance Form
Submission to International Marketing Director
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses seeking assistance should complete and return the International Marketing Assistance Form to Stone Slade, the International Marketing Director at stone.slade@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to provide leadership training, education, and support to farmers committed to implementing environmentally sustainable and conservation-focused agricultural practices, promoting environmental stewardship across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Leadership training, education, and technical assistance for environmentally engaged and conservation-focused farming practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers seeking to improve environmental practices and committed to environmental sustainability in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, education, and technical resources for sustainable and conservation-focused farming
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: MDA Spay and Neuter Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture funds local organizations to provide free spay and neuter services to low-income pet owners throughout Maryland. Services are delivered through MDA-funded projects at partner animal welfare organizations and veterinary clinics. Surgeries may include a free rabies vaccine. The program supports cats and dogs owned by eligible residents. Services cover specific areas or zip codes within participating counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free spay and neuter surgeries for cats and dogs, with some projects also including a free rabies vaccine. Services are provided at partner veterinary clinics and animal welfare organizations. All projects have limited funding. Projects may cover specific areas or zip codes within listed counties.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; projects active as long as grant funds allow
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income pet owners in Maryland who own cats and/or dogs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free spay and neuter surgeries for owned pets; may also include rabies vaccination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects cover specific areas or zip codes within participating counties in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, and Wicomico counties. Check the list on the page to see if there is an active MDA-funded project in your area.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a low-income pet owner (specific income thresholds not specified on this page)
Pet must be owned (not a stray)
Pet must be a cat or dog (some projects accept dogs only)
Applicant must contact the organization listed for their county to verify eligibility and confirm the project is active in their specific area or zip code
Must qualify based on income criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the list on the page to see if there is an active MDA-funded project in your area. Contact the organization listed for your county to verify eligibility and apply for services. If there is no active project in your area, contact your local animal shelter or non-profit animal welfare organizations to learn about other low-cost surgery options. You may also call (410) 222-8900 or visit the Maryland Department of Agriculture website for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary food safety certification program for fruit and vegetable producers that implements Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices. The program provides basic food safety requirements and is intended for direct marketers, smaller farms, and larger farms as a starting point for comprehensive GAP food safety programs. Producers that pass the MDA inspection are awarded a certificate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA provides training and one-to-one assistance in developing, writing and implementing food safety programs for GAP/GHP certification. Producers receive inspection and certification upon passing. Training sessions offered regionally January through March annually. Program funded by USDA Specialty Crop Grant to minimize costs to producers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fruit and vegetable producers in Maryland, including smaller and direct market farms, larger farms selling wholesale, and farms with packing facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of food safety practices addressing water quality, manure and compost use, worker health and hygiene, contamination prevention from wildlife and animals, post-harvest handling, packing house sanitation, pest control, and container sanitation. Program funded by USDA Specialty Crop Grant to minimize costs to producers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any Maryland producer of fruits and vegetables.

structured_extraction.program_description: MALPF is a statewide program established in 1977 that purchases agricultural preservation easements and development rights to permanently restrict development on prime farmland and woodland throughout Maryland. The program operates statewide across all 23 counties and has preserved more than 350,000 acres through a public investment of over $900 million. The program helps preserve productive agricultural land and woodland, curb urban development expansion, protect wildlife, and maintain environmental quality of the Chesapeake and Coastal Bays and their tributaries. Eligible farmland and woodland owners can protect their property from conversion to non-agricultural uses by having an agricultural preservation easement or development rights easement purchased, with easement restrictions remaining effective in perpetuity. Landowners retain ownership, operational control, and the ability to sell or transfer the property. Properties are ranked based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Easement payments range from recent lows of $600 to over $10,000 per acre, calculated as the asking price, the difference between appraised fair market value and agricultural value (whichever is less), or a maximum of 75% of the appraised fair market value of the land. The program allows qualifying owners to retain options for residential lots, tenant housing, and agricultural subdivisions under specified conditions. The program is completely voluntary and involves establishing permanent protective easements on agricultural property. Participants can use proceeds for purposes including financing the purchase of a farm or additional farmland, retirement, estate planning and settlement, financing improvements to an existing farming operation, investing in production and marketing of new farm products, financing restoration of a historic home, or paying off existing debt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MALPF purchases Development Rights Easements and Agricultural Preservation Easements on qualifying agricultural properties and eligible farmland/woodland. Easement payment is calculated as the asking price, the difference between appraised fair market value and agricultural value (whichever is less), or a maximum of 75% of the appraised fair market value. Recent payments have ranged from $600 to over $10,000 per acre. The program is completely voluntary. Landowners can use the proceeds for purposes including: financing the purchase of a farm or additional farmland, retirement, estate planning and settlement, financing improvements to an existing farming operation, investing in production and marketing of new farm products, financing restoration of a historic home, or paying off existing debt. Applications are accepted according to county cycles, ranked competitively by local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Boards relative to other applicants, approved by County Commissioners, and submitted to MALPF. Offers are made based on available funding. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity, restricting the land to agricultural use. Applications can be submitted to sell permanent protective easements, create lot exclusions, and subdivide properties.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of Development Rights Easements and Agricultural Preservation Easements to permanently preserve agricultural land and woodland and protect them from conversion to non-agricultural uses. Landowners can use the proceeds for purposes including: financing the purchase of a farm or additional farmland, retirement, estate planning and settlement, financing improvements to an existing farming operation, investing in production and marketing of new farm products, financing restoration of a historic home, or paying off existing debt.

Properties must be located outside a ten-year water and sewer service area and within county boundaries with zoning permitting farm use. Properties are ranked based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Property must be consistent with county master plans and comprehensive land-use plans.
