structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted in the spring of each cycle year according to county schedules through a competitive application process. Eight-stage process: (1) Submit application, (2) County approval, (3) Appraisals, (4) Calculate values, (5) Round One offers, (6) Round Two offers, (7) Accept/reject offer, (8) Settlement. Applicant properties are ranked by the local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board relative to other applicants, approved by County Commissioners, and submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st. MALPF and local governments make offers based on available funding. The process includes application, valuation of the asking price, review, and settlement. Applications can be submitted to sell permanent protective easements, create lot exclusions, and subdivide properties. Submit a completed application (available as fillable PDF or Word document) either physically to your county planning office or by email to the program administrator, with required entity documents if the farm is owned by an entity. Work with County Program Administrator on typed application. County Program Administrator completes Part B with planning/zoning information. Contact your local program administrator or Foundation staff for specific county application procedures and deadlines. Interested landowners should contact their county planning staff to learn more and complete an application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program (MACS)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide cost-share program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture that provides financial incentives to farmers and livestock producers to install best management practices (BMPs) on their farms to protect water quality. Eligible practices include soil erosion control, nutrient management, stream protection, livestock management improvements, livestock watering facilities, livestock exclusion fencing, stream crossings, riparian forest buffer planting, animal waste storage facilities, grassed waterways, spring developments, cover crops, conservation cover, critical area plantings, dead bird composting facilities, diversions, field borders and windbreaks, filter strips, grade stabilization structures, lined waterways and outlets, sediment basins, strip cropping, terrace systems, and contour farming. Farmers can also receive assistance to transport excess poultry litter off the farm. The program helps farmers protect waterways, improve livestock health, safeguard water quality, reduce soil and nutrient runoff, and comply with nutrient management requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share assistance covering up to 87.5 percent of the cost to install eligible best management practices on agricultural land. Up to 100% cost-share available for riparian forest buffer planting at $2 per tree planted. Eligible BMPs include livestock watering facilities, livestock exclusion fencing, stream crossings, riparian buffers, animal waste management systems, conservation cover, cover crops, critical area plantings, dead bird composting facilities, diversions, field borders and windbreaks, filter strips, grade stabilization structures, grassed waterways, lined waterways and outlets, nutrient management services, sediment basins, spring developments, strip cropping, terrace systems, and contour farming/orchards. Assistance also available for poultry litter transport off the farm.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of best management practices including livestock watering facilities, livestock exclusion fencing, stream crossings, riparian forest buffers, animal waste management systems, conservation cover, cover crops, and other conservation practices to control soil erosion, manage nutrients, protect streams, improve livestock health, safeguard water quality, and reduce soil, nutrients, and animal wastes from entering state waterways.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Department of Agriculture Spay and Neuter Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive grant program designed to reduce the number of cats and dogs surrendered to and euthanized in Maryland shelters by providing competitive grants to nonprofit animal welfare organizations, local governments, and government animal shelters that promote and provide spay and neuter services. The program provides free spay and neuter services for pets of low-income Marylanders, colonies of unowned outdoor cats, and free-roaming, unowned, and feral cats in Maryland. Services may include free rabies vaccination. Organizations may deliver services through an in-house clinic, partnerships with veterinarians and clinics, or a combination of both. Two grant opportunities are available annually: one for low-income pet owners and community cats, and one specifically focused on feral cats. Funding is distributed to eligible organizations across Maryland, with grants released in allocations based on spending progress. Grant funding levels are determined annually by the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board and approved by the Maryland State Secretary of Agriculture. The program is funded through fees levied on pet food manufacturers who sell cat or dog feed in Maryland. Individual residents of participating counties may access services through participating organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and subsidies are provided to eligible nonprofit animal welfare organizations (must have 501(c)(3) tax exempt status), local governments, and government animal shelters to fund spay and neuter services. Minimum grant: $5,000; Maximum grant: $75,000 (or 25% of organization's annual operating budget, whichever is less). Organizations with budgets under $20,000 may request maximum of $5,000. Services are provided at no cost to recipients and may include rabies vaccination. First allocation is 50% of surgery funding plus 100% of rabies vaccine and other funding; second allocation is released once 35% of budget is spent. Funds support spay/neuter surgical procedures (all-inclusive: materials, veterinary services, pre- and post-operative medicines/exams), rabies vaccinations, transportation assistance, outreach and education materials, HQHVSN training for veterinarians and surgical staff, equipment for licensed operational clinics (cumulative total cannot exceed $5,000), and emergency medical expenses (up to 5%, case-by-case approval). This is a supplemental grant opportunity, not intended as sole or primary funding source. Organizations may apply for one or both grant opportunities but only one of each type in a grant cycle. Grant funding levels are determined annually by the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board and approved by the Maryland State Secretary of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 application window closed April 17, 2026; FY28 application window will open in January 2027; typically opens in early January and closes in early April

Targeted to low-income communities and populations to maximum extent possible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding must be used to promote and provide spay and neuter services for pets of low-income Marylanders, unowned outdoor cat colonies, and free-roaming feral cats. Permitted uses include: spay/neuter surgical procedures with all-inclusive costs (materials, veterinary services, pre- and post-operative medicines/exams), rabies vaccinations (required for all animals; capped at $5.00 per dose if separate line item), anesthesia and surgical materials, HQHVSN training for veterinarians and surgical staff, outreach and education materials (flyers, brochures, posters, multilingual materials), transportation assistance at IRS nonprofit/charity mileage rates for pet owners and animals to/from clinics, equipment for licensed operational clinics (cumulative total cannot exceed $5,000), emergency medical expenses (up to 5% of grant budget, case-by-case approval), staff and coordinator positions with strong justification, ear-tipping and microchipping procedures (for feral cats), and fostering costs for young kittens. Funding cannot be used for: spay and neuter of shelter or rescue animals prior to placement; owned pets under feral cat-focused grants; personnel/staff funding not directly related to project; overhead, office equipment, supplies, uniforms; capital campaigns and construction; giveaways (except educational materials); flea treatments or de-worming (unless medically necessary); co-pays or conditions on service provision.

Active projects cover specific counties and areas within those counties. Not all areas of each county may be covered. Projects may be limited to specific zip codes within counties. Applicants must target specific, focused areas (zip codes preferred over entire counties) that are realistic and manageable for applicant capacity. Individuals should contact the organization listed for their county to verify if their area is covered.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit animal welfare organization with 501(c)(3) tax exempt status, government animal shelter, local government, or eligible for-profit service provider
Must be in Good Standing with SDAT (State Department of Assessments and Taxation) and Secretary of State
Non-profit applicants fundraising in Maryland must have Maryland Charitable Registration Permit
Must provide IRS Form W-9 (signed and dated within six months of application)
Must promote and provide spay and neuter services
Services must be available to pets of low-income Marylanders, unowned outdoor cat colonies, or free-roaming feral cats
Spay and neuter services must be permitted under local law where applicable
For animal shelters in Maryland: must comply with Maryland Animal Shelter Standards of Care
Free-roaming, unowned, or feral cats only for feral cat projects
Owned pets and animals in shelter/rescue custody not eligible for feral cat-focused grants
Services are for already-owned pets only; animals in shelter/rescue custody not eligible except for Pet-Focused grant
Specific area or zip code coverage varies by project
Limited funding - projects continue as long as grant funds allow
Project must meet Program requirements
Organization must be eligible to apply
For individual applicants: live within eligible county or service area
For individual applicants: own a dog or cat
For individual applicants: income limits may apply (e.g., under $60,000 annually in some counties)
Must be able to provide spay and neuter services
No co-pays permitted; sterilization costs must be all-inclusive
Cannot condition spay/neuter services on purchase of other services
Must demonstrate coordination with animal control and shelter data
Must show capacity increase above normal operations
Equipment requests require price quotes and supplier identification
All feral cats must be ear-tipped or microchipped for identification
Joint applicants (two or more organizations working together) permitted
Applications may encompass more than one county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For nonprofit and government organizations: Carefully read FY Guidelines and Instructions before applying. Verify your organization meets requirements and is eligible. Organizations must verify organization is in Good Standing with SDAT and Secretary of State. Organizations may apply for one or both grant opportunities but only one of each type in a grant cycle. Submit required documentation including W-9 form (signed and dated within six months), SDAT Good Standing verification, and Charitable Registration Permit if applicable. Once submitted, no changes may be made and resubmissions are not allowed. The Spay and Neuter Advisory Board meets annually to review grant applications and makes recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture regarding grant approvals and funding. After approval, grantees must submit Quarterly Grant Progress Reports and a Final Report. For individuals seeking services: Check the list of active projects by county and contact the organization listed for your county to verify if your area is covered and for information on how to access services. Submit the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application and required documents to the appropriate county animal services or administering organization to be contacted for scheduling.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program designed to minimize the risk of Salmonella enteritidis contamination of chicken shell eggs and establish standards for egg quality. Participants implement management and monitoring practices to prevent contamination, receive oversight and technical advice from the Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, and may market eggs under the Maryland's Best logo. The program does not guarantee eggs are free of Salmonella enteritidis contamination but assures producer and processor commitment to management and monitoring practices to prevent contamination.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical advice, compliance inspections, monitoring visits, and management and monitoring guidelines for egg producers and processors. Participants receive oversight from MDA and Maryland Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, participate in training sessions on quality control and recordkeeping, and access to the Maryland's Best logo for eggs meeting program standards. Participants bear the financial burden of the program, including costs for sampling supplies, culturing, training, and program monitoring (quarterly MDA plant visits for processors).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Poultry producers and shell egg processors in Maryland who want to voluntarily participate in quality assurance and food safety practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants pay for sampling supplies, culturing costs, training, and program monitoring. This is a technical assistance and oversight program where participants use the program's guidelines for management practices, monitoring, testing, washing, refrigeration, labeling, and quality control of shell eggs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to egg producers and processors throughout Maryland. Processing of eggs from flocks outside Maryland may be allowed at the Department's discretion based on equivalent flock status programs. Entire production complex must enter the program for biosecurity purposes (not individual poultry houses). Eggs must be from Maryland flocks in good standing.
requirements_list: Voluntary participation
Implementation of management and monitoring practices to prevent Salmonella enteritidis contamination
Obtain chicks from U.S. certified sources
Placement of SE-clean chicks
Rodent control measures
Cleaning and disinfecting between flocks
Environmental monitoring of pullet and layer houses
Continuous testing of eggs from environmentally positive houses
Proper on-farm handling of eggs
Diversion of SE-positive eggs for pasteurization
Compliance with processing guidelines including washing, refrigeration, labeling, and quality control
Maintain records that all eggs are from Maryland flocks in good standing
Monitor and record wash water temperature (minimum 90°F, 20°F warmer than eggs) every two hours
Monitor and record wash water pH (minimum 10) every two hours
Maintain corrective action records when parameters fall below minimums
Maintain approved rodent control program
Pack Maryland's Best eggs only in new cartons or new fiber filler flats
Maintain plant sanitation records during processing
Cooperate with MDA monitoring and prevention procedures
Participate in training on quality control and recordkeeping
Maintain approved monitoring logs
Obliterate MDA logo from non-compliant cartons
Adopt Standard Operating Procedures for sanitation and egg quality
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Producers and processors apply to participate in the program by submitting MEQAP applications. For processors, applicants sign the Processor Participation Agreement form. MDA provides oversight and compliance inspections, including quarterly plant visits for processors. Participants commit to implementing the required management and monitoring practices outlined in the production and processing portions of the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax credits to farmers who donate eligible food products to certified food banks and food pantries. Farmers receive a Maryland income tax credit based on the wholesale value of their donated food as determined by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's price listings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers receive a Maryland income tax credit of up to $5,000 per year based on the value of their donated food. In certain cases, the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture may approve an increase allowing a farm to receive up to $10,000 in total credits per year. The value is determined using the U.S. Department of Agriculture's wholesale price listings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who donate eligible food products to certified food banks and food pantries; non-profit organizations or charities that accept eligible food donations can become Tax Credit Certificate Administrators to facilitate the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for farmers who donate eligible food products to certified food banks and food pantries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to farmers across Maryland. Certified food banks and pantries are located throughout the state including Anne Arundel County, Baltimore, Salisbury, and the Washington DC metropolitan area.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer with eligible food products to donate
Must donate to a certified food bank or food pantry approved by the Maryland Department of Agriculture

Non-profit organizations accepting donations must become a Tax Credit Certificate Administrator by completing and submitting the Application for Tax Credit Certificate Administrator for the Maryland Food Donation Pilot Program
Food donations must be eligible products
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: If you are a non-profit organization or charity accepting food donations, become a Tax Credit Certificate Administrator (TCCA) by completing the Application for Tax Credit Certificate Administrator for the Maryland Food Donation Pilot Program and submitting it to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Step 2: Upon approval, your organization receives a signed agreement and assigned TCCA number. Step 3: Once approved as a TCCA, submit eligible food donations from a qualified farm by completing the Producer Donation Form. Step 4: Submit completed forms to the Maryland Department of Agriculture Marketing Office by mail at 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401 or by email to cassie.shirk@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Food and Agricultural Resiliency Mechanism Grant Program (MFARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that helps food-insecure people access nourishment while providing farmers and seafood providers with a market to sell their products. The program builds food system resiliency by leveraging Maryland agricultural and seafood products to support food banks and charitable emergency food providers in alleviating food insecurity. The program supports farm-to-foodbank initiatives and agricultural resilience through grants ranging from $5,000 minimum to $40,000 maximum.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $5,000 minimum to $40,000 maximum to purchase agricultural and seafood products from certified local farms and fish providers registered in the Certified Local Farm and Fish (CLFF) Directory. Funding is distributed as 80% upfront payment upon signed grant agreement and 20% dispersed based on final program and financial report. Organizations can spend more than 20% on food with flexible non-food spending. Total funding availability is $200,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland food banks, charitable emergency food providers, nonprofit organizations focused on food insecurity and food access, faith-based and bona fide religious organizations, food-insecure residents, low-income residents, and students in low-income schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of Maryland-grown produce and products from Certified Local Farm and Fish (CLFF) Directory providers, transportation, distribution, staff costs, and supplies. 80% of funding allocated toward food costs and 20% toward operational expenses, though organizations can request flexible allocation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Purchased produce must go to Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland food bank, charitable emergency food provider, nonprofit focused on food insecurity and food access, or faith-based/bona fide religious organization
Must be registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Nonprofits must be registered as a charity with the Maryland Secretary of State
Religious organizations must be registered with Secretary of State or provide exemption letter
Must submit a signed W-9 form within past 2 years with matching address
Farm/fish provider partners must be registered in the Certified Local Farm and Fish (CLFF) Directory
Farmers and nonprofit farmers must have a nutrient management plan
Must provide signed letters of support from producers on letterhead
Must have infrastructure to support fresh, local food storage and distribution
Minimum grant request: $5,000
Maximum grant request: $40,000
Reporting requirements apply; sample reports available on OneStop public profile
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit grant application through the OneStop platform at onestop.md.gov/forms/farm-to-foodbank-69a87083f59d9602c8faff1b with farm/fish partner information and letters of support from Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory providers.

structured_extraction.program_description: State regulatory program that licenses and regulates the production of hemp in Maryland. This USDA-approved program provides written authorization permitting persons to cultivate, store, handle, or market hemp for seed, grain, fiber, hurd, or CBD production. Does not apply to institutions of higher education or persons producing hemp under the Hemp Research Pilot Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Official licensing and regulatory authorization to cultivate, store, handle, or market hemp. Program includes regulatory sampling and testing for THC compliance (0.3% threshold), inspection services, testing methodology and quality assurance, and disposal guidance for noncompliant crops. License valid through December 31 of calendar year with annual renewal deadline of December 1.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual renewal by December 1 of year license expires
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, partnerships, corporations, limited liability companies, associations, and other business entities seeking to legally cultivate and produce hemp in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cultivation, storage, handling, marketing, and processing of hemp for seed, grain, fiber, hurd, or CBD production. Growers bear costs for disposal of noncompliant crops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Hemp operations must be located within Maryland state boundaries on legally described parcels with GPS coordinates provided.
requirements_list: Applicant must be at least 18 years old
Cannot have felony conviction related to controlled substance in preceding 10 years
Provide FBI criminal background report dated within 60 days
Submit complete application with: full name, address, phone, email, legal land description, GPS coordinates, detailed map, and intended hemp plant portion to market
Demonstrate legal right to cultivate on proposed land
Grant Maryland Department of Agriculture access for inspection and sampling
Maintain valid hemp grower license
Submit annual production reports by December 1
Report to Farm Service Agency and USDA
Report drug felony convictions within 15 days
Retain records for 3 years
Ensure THC testing compliance (≤0.3% on dry weight basis)
Dispose of noncompliant hemp according to regulations
Grower must be present during official sampling
Submit hemp disposal reports with licensee name/address, license number, location information, GPS coordinates, disposal agent information, and seed-to-harvest documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Maryland one-stop portal at https://onestop.md.gov/forms/hemp-production-application-maryland-5fe9fe9b9ccc2801029ea653. Submit complete application with required documentation including FBI criminal background report, legal land description, GPS coordinates, and detailed map.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program for growers interested in partnering with a higher education institution or the Maryland Department of Agriculture to grow industrial hemp under a research program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Registration and facilitation of industrial hemp growing sites for research purposes in partnership with higher education institutions or the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Growers interested in partnering with higher education institutions or the Maryland Department of Agriculture to conduct research on industrial hemp
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Growing, cultivating, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transporting, marketing, or selling industrial hemp for research purposes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must partner with an institute of higher education or the Maryland Department of Agriculture
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a PDF application and mail it with supporting documents to the Maryland Department of Agriculture at 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Annapolis, MD 21401

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports Maryland's horse industry. The board promotes horse-related activities and recreation. It also supports educational projects, job training, and planning for facilities to help the local horse economy grow. The board advises the Secretary of Agriculture and licenses stables in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The board supports the horse industry through promotional activities, educational and research projects, and development efforts like job training and facilities planning. The website's navigation indicates that grants are available, but this page does not provide specific details.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People and businesses in Maryland's horse industry, including horse owners and stable operators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Horse Industry Board Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program supporting diverse equine-related projects including education, therapy, rescue, career development, and community outreach. Funding supports projects that promote horses, benefit the equestrian community, or create new opportunities for the Maryland horse industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial awards ranging from $250 to $2,000 for equine industry projects. Grants support research, educational and promotional projects supporting the horse industry and equestrian community in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults seeking equine careers, youth, veterans, first responders, at-risk youth, underserved populations, people with disabilities, riders of all disciplines and backgrounds, equine professionals, horse owners and enthusiasts, non-profit organizations, clubs and associations, businesses, farms and stables, government entities, schools, educational institutions, and other horse industry participants and equestrian organizations that support the horse industry or equestrian community in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational programs and clinics, therapeutic services, training and professional development, educational materials and exhibits, community outreach events, equipment and infrastructure, marketing initiatives, and other projects that support horses or the equestrian community or develop new opportunities for the Maryland horse industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, serving Maryland residents and communities. All licensed stables are automatically on the email distribution list.
requirements_list: Projects must support horses or the equestrian community
Projects must develop new opportunities for the Maryland horse industry
Grant requests should not exceed $2,000
Projects should be completed by June 30
Projects must serve Maryland residents and communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in applying should sign up for the email distribution list to receive FY2026 Grant Guidelines and updates. Applications are typically due in early October with recipients announced in early January. Contact MHIB Executive Director Anne Litz at 667-408-0407 or [email protected] for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: An optional voluntary registration program for farm operations that gross $5,000 or less in organic agricultural sales annually and are exempt from USDA organic certification requirements. Registered exempt operations are listed on the MDA website while maintaining compliance with USDA National Organic Program regulations. These operations do not require USDA certification but may register with MDA to be recognized as registered exempt organic operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Optional registration service for exempt organic producers with annual registration fee of $30. Registered exempt operations are listed on the MDA website. Annual registration updates are required to maintain listing. Registration allows small organic operations to maintain compliance with organic standards and be recognized by the state.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted at any time; annual updates required to maintain listing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farm operations in Maryland that gross $5,000 or less in organic agricultural sales annually and wish to register as exempt with the state.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration enables farms to be listed on MDA's website as a registered exempt organic operation and maintain compliance with organic standards without full USDA certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to farm operations located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must gross $5,000 or less in organic agricultural sales annually
Must operate in accordance with all USDA National Organic Program regulations, including recordkeeping requirements
Must maintain required recordkeeping
Must update registration annually to maintain listing on MDA's website
Operation must grow and process organic foods
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Organic Exempt Application form along with the $30 annual registration fee to MDA, or contact MDA Organic Certification Program for registration details and application procedures. Annual updates are required to maintain the listing on MDA's website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture certifies farm operations that grow and/or process foods sold as organic to USDA National Organic Program standards. MDA is a USDA-accredited certifying agent for producers located in Maryland. The program assures consumers that organic products were grown and processed according to prescribed organic agriculture and food production standards. Farms with gross organic agricultural income exceeding $5,000 annually must be certified to label products as organic. MDA reviews the organic system plan for compliance, conducts an inspection of the operation, and issues a certificate to applicants that have met all requirements. The program also offers a registration program for exempt operations with gross agricultural income from organic sales of $5,000 or less. Certification covers crops, livestock, wild crops, and on-farm handling/processing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MDA provides USDA-accredited organic certification for farm operations meeting National Organic Program standards. Certification covers crops, livestock, wild crops, and on-farm handling/processing. New applicants pay a $500 application fee and must develop an Organic System Plan. Current certified producers must submit annual updates by April 1 for $500 to maintain certification. MDA reviews the organic system plan for compliance with National Organic Program standards, conducts an inspection of the operation, and issues a certificate to applicants that have met all requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 (annual renewal deadline); new applicants may apply at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farm operations in Maryland seeking to grow or process foods labeled as organic, including farmers and agricultural producers. Operations with gross organic agricultural income exceeding $5,000 annually must be certified.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables farms to label and sell agricultural products as 100 percent organic, organic, or made with organic ingredients, allowing operations to sell, label, or represent their products as organic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to farm operations located in Maryland only. MDA does not certify farms outside of Maryland.
requirements_list: Crop and livestock operations must be located in Maryland
Must gross more than $5,000 in organic agricultural sales annually to require certification
Operations must meet USDA National Organic Program standards
Certification covers crops, livestock, wild crops, and on-farm handling/processing only
Processing and handling operations are not eligible for MDA certification as standalone operations
Farm operation must grow and/or process organic foods
Operation must comply with National Organic Program regulations
Must develop an Organic System Plan (OSP) for new applicants
Must maintain recordkeeping as required by NOP standards
Certified producers must submit annual updates by April 1 each year to maintain certification
Submit application with organic system plan
Pay $500 certification fee for new applicants and $500 annual renewal fee
Crop recordkeeping documentation required for certification
Livestock recordkeeping and documentation
Grazing days tracking
Grazing season record maintenance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants complete all applicable forms from the certification packet (crop/pasture, livestock, wild crops, or on-farm processor/handler) and submit them along with the $500 application fee and organic system plan to MDA. MDA reviews the application for compliance with National Organic Program standards. If compliant, MDA schedules an inspection. MDA then reviews the application and inspection report to determine if the operation meets all standards and issues a certificate to applicants that have met all requirements. Certified producers maintain certification by submitting an annual OSP update and $500 renewal fee by April 1 each year. Applications are available through downloadable forms and packets for crop producers, livestock producers, and on-farm processors/handlers. Completion of appropriate recordkeeping forms is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland farmers and agricultural producers find and create profitable markets for their products. It supports them in selling locally, nationally, and internationally.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides marketing services to connect consumers with local Maryland products. It helps farmers find new buyers and provides information on federal resources and agricultural policies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers can use this program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program providing farmers and landowners with incentive payments to establish and maintain conservation buffers on farmland to improve stream health, wildlife habitat, and Chesapeake Bay water quality. The program offers payments for establishing forest buffers, grass buffers, and watercourse access control areas adjacent to eligible agricultural lands, with payment rates ranging from $500 per acre for existing grass buffers to $4,500 per acre for riparian forest buffers with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of project costs up front and 25% after verification of planting. Additional one-time tree bonus payments of $1,000 per acre and annual maintenance payments up to $330 per acre per year are available for forest buffers during the first five years. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years. Free technical assistance is provided by local soil conservation districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to a maximum of $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of project costs up front and 25% after verification of planting. Additional one-time tree bonus payments of $1,000 per acre are available for forest buffers. Annual maintenance payments up to $330 per acre per year are available for forest buffers during the first five years. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years. Free technical assistance is provided by local soil conservation districts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual open enrollment period runs from November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners who are responsible for managing eligible agricultural lands, particularly those with marginal land next to streams or floodplains.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing and maintaining conservation buffers including forest buffers, grass buffers, and watercourse access control areas to improve water quality and wildlife habitat. Eligible uses include planting trees next to streams, installing riparian forest buffers, installing livestock exclusion fencing, and forest buffer maintenance including mowing, spot spraying, and tree shelter maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Eligible land must be cropland next to a stream or ditch with established cropping history, or areas adjacent to watercourses with highly erodible or hydric soils. Buffers must be adjacent to pasture or on cropland with highly erodible land (HEL) or hydric soil.
requirements_list: Farmers and landowners must be responsible for management of eligible lands
Farmers who lease land must certify an active lease for the buffer term or provide landowner agreement
Farmers and landowners must be in good standing with USDA and state cost-share programs
Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification required and must be submitted with application
Eligible land must be cropland next to stream or ditch with established cropping history in pasture, commodity crops, or hay
Land must not be actively enrolled in state (MACS) or federal programs (CRP, CREP, EQIP) or mandated by easement
Forest buffers must be 35-100 feet wide
Grass buffers must be 10-100 feet wide
Watercourse access control areas must be 10-100 feet wide, or at least 35 feet wide if establishing woody vegetation
Plant within 1 year of signed agreement date
Mowing and hay harvesting for own use allowed; nutrient applications not permitted
Must apply during annual open enrollment period
All landowners on property deed(s) must sign agreement
Compliance with Maryland Agricultural Code Ann. §§8-801-8-806 and COMAR 15.20.06-08
Soil & Water Conservation Plan recommended
Buffer must exclude livestock from buffer area
Must be certified by MDA representative and approved by Soil Conservation District
Maintenance payments require invoices/receipts for work performed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district to apply. Applications are accepted during the annual open enrollment period (November 1 through April 30). Download the application form and submit it along with a map showing buffer location and acreage, a signed Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form, and a signed IRS Form W-9. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Submit completed application checklist with required documentation including Resource Improvement Code(s), color map of buffer area(s) with premise address, and Certificate of Resolution, Power of Attorney, or equivalent authorization document. Local SCD reviews and certifies; DNR signature required as applicable. For maintenance payments, submit Claim for Payment form with supporting documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that awards funding to Maryland farmers and organizations working with farmers to implement innovative soil health conservation practices that improve soil health, sequester carbon, and/or reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The program supports the adoption and testing of new conservation management practices, including cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture planting, agroforestry, and other soil health improvement strategies. Selected applicants receive up to $50,000 to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices, with grant recipients receiving a portion of funds (not to exceed 30%) upfront and the remainder distributed annually following verification of progress. Agroforestry practices such as alley cropping and critical area plantings are eligible and help build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of up to $50,000 awarded to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices. Grant recipients receive a portion of funds (not to exceed 30%) upfront, with the remainder distributed annually following verification of progress. Funds may be used to support implementation of conservation practices including equipment purchase, project staff time, and research costs to support soil health management strategies that minimize soil disturbance, maximize soil cover, enhance biodiversity, and increase living roots presence. Agroforestry practices such as alley cropping and critical area plantings are eligible. Funds support adoption of soil health practices and conservation systems that improve soil health, sequester carbon, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open enrollment period typically begins in January and runs for approximately 8 weeks. The 2025-2026 application period is currently closed. FY 2026 application cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers, individual farmers or groups of farmers operating in Maryland, and individuals or organizations working with farmers in Maryland. Agricultural landowners interested in implementing soil health and agroforestry practices. Agricultural organizations and producers with soil health projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of conservation practices including purchase of equipment, project staff time directly related to project implementation, and research costs. Funds support soil health management strategies that minimize soil disturbance, maximize soil cover, enhance biodiversity, and increase living roots presence. Agroforestry practices such as alley cropping and critical area plantings are eligible uses. Adoption of soil health practices, implementation of conservation systems, carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas reduction projects, cover crop implementation, adaptive/prescribed grazing management, and establishment of annual or perennial grass and/or forbs for pasture, hay, or cover.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Open to agricultural operations operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Agricultural operation(s) applying or partnering must have gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more of donated agricultural products if non-profit) and/or manage 8 or more animal units (8,000 pounds of live animal weight)
No minimum or maximum acreage requirements
Applicants must provide proof of compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements by submitting a Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form at time of application
Must propose enhanced soil health practices
Agroforestry practices such as alley cropping or critical area plantings are eligible
Grant supports 3 years of practices
Competitive application process
Must be selected through competitive process
Must answer all narrative questions
Must submit project budget separately
Must include 3-year implementation timeline
Must demonstrate soil health goals and measurements
Application limit: 10 pages (not including images)
Must complete Cover Crop Template if applicable, detailing cropping plans and rotation
Must submit grazing plan template if applicable (completed)
Must attach paddock division maps if applicable (current and proposed)
Recommended to work with NRCS or technical advisor (University of Maryland Extension) for plan development
Can substitute existing NRCS grazing plan with maps
Must complete Grass and Forb Planting Template if applicable with project details
Detailed planting plans for species selection and planting timeframes/methods
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application during the open enrollment period (typically January through approximately mid-February) including project narrative, project budget, and relevant templates based on conservation practices proposed. Submit project narrative and budget via email as Word/PDF attachment or print and mail. Applications are assessed based on narrative questions and ranking criteria. Download and complete relevant templates (Cover Crop, Grazing, Grass and Forb Planting, etc.) and submit via email or mail. Visit the Healthy Soils website for more information and to submit your application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program to test the feasibility of controlling non-biting midge populations using Bactimos (Bti) WG Biological Larvicide, a naturally occurring soil bacterium. The program aims to determine the impact of Bti treatments on midge populations in aquatic environments and identify the most cost-effective dosage and frequency of treatments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Application of Bactimos WG (Bti strain AM65-52) to control non-biting midge larvae in mud/detritus at bottom of lakes and ponds. The program involves the direct application of Bti treatments via boat and/or helicopter to suppress midge populations in freshwater aquatic environments. This is a government-conducted environmental management initiative using biological pest control/larvicide application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential areas, municipalities, and industries affected by non-biting midge swarms, including paint, paper, pharmaceutical, and food processing industries, and hotel and tourism industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Larvicide application targeting midge larval habitats in freshwater aquatic environments such as lakes and ponds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Freshwater aquatic environments in Maryland with midge problems, specifically the Back River area in the Baltimore region.
requirements_list: Target midge larvae in mud/detritus at bottom of water bodies
Applications designed for optimized spray application equipment

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that reimburses organic producers and handlers for a portion of their USDA-accredited organic certification fees. Eligible applicants can receive reimbursement for 75% of certification fees, up to a maximum of $750 per scope.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Producers and handlers certified by USDA-accredited certifiers are eligible to receive reimbursement covering 75% of their organic certification fees, up to a maximum of $750 per scope. Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer is issued a certificate. Maryland producers must submit a Cost Share Application to the MDA Organic Certification Program. Non-MDA certified producers must be located in Maryland and submit a copy of their certification fees invoice with their cost share application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As of August 2025, USDA has not yet announced funding for 2025. Application forms will be posted when funding is announced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Producers and handlers in Maryland who are certified or seeking certification from USDA-accredited organic certifiers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for organic certification fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Funding is subject to annual USDA appropriations through the Farm Bill.
requirements_list: Must be certified or applying for certification from a USDA-accredited certifier
Must be located in Maryland
Reimbursement cannot be issued until the producer receives a certificate
Non-MDA certified producers must submit a copy of their certification fees invoice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Maryland producers submit a Cost Share Application to the MDA Organic Certification Program. Non-MDA certified producers must include a copy of their certification fees invoice. Application forms are posted when USDA announces funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service that collects and properly disposes of unusable or unwanted pesticide materials for farmers and agricultural producers. The program collects any product with an EPA or USDA registration number, identifies unknown materials through testing, and arranges transport to EPA-approved disposal facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program collects pesticide materials directly from storage sites and transports them to EPA-approved disposal facilities at no cost to farmers. An MDA inspector schedules a site visit to verify information before collection. A licensed hazardous waste hauler is contracted to collect and transport materials. Commercial businesses may be allowed to participate at MDA's contract cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers and farmers throughout Maryland, including current or retired farmers, orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of unusable or unwanted pesticide materials
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout all of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an agricultural operation (farm, forest, nursery, greenhouse, etc.) or current or retired farmer or agricultural producer (orchardist, nurseryman, greenhouse operator, or Christmas tree grower)
Must complete and submit the registration form to the Pesticide Regulation Section with grower name, mailing address, county, and telephone number
Must provide contact person name and daytime telephone number
Must provide site address and county of stored pesticides with directions and/or map to pesticide storage site
Must provide accurate inventory of pesticides for disposal with product details (brand name, active ingredient, EPA/USDA registration number, formulation, container type, quantity, size, condition)
Materials must have an EPA or USDA registration number or be identifiable as pesticide
Unknown materials will be sampled and tested by MDA prior to collection
An MDA inspector will conduct a site visit to verify information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers and agricultural producers complete the registration form (available as fillable PDF) and submit via email to rob.hofstetter@maryland.gov or mail to the Pesticide Regulation Section. MDA reviews the registration and determines service areas. MDA staff then contacts the registrant to arrange inspection and verification of pesticides. Samples may be collected for analysis if pesticides are not in original containers or are unknown. Once MDA has a complete inventory of materials, a licensed hazardous waste hauler collects the pesticides directly from the storage site and transports them to an EPA-approved disposal facility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Poultry and Rabbit On-Farm Processing Certification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program for FSIS inspection-exempt producers to slaughter and process poultry and rabbits on-farm for intrastate sales. The program covers chickens, turkeys, domestic ducks, domestic geese, and rabbits. Participants must attend MDA training, follow food safety, biosecurity, processing, and recordkeeping standards, and allow MDA access for inspections. Certified producers can sell whole or parts (not ground) intrastate to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program provides training certification for on-farm poultry and rabbit processing. Certified producers can sell whole or parts (not ground) of poultry and rabbits intrastate to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets. Program allows slaughter and processing of up to 20,000 poultry of the producer's own production annually or rabbits. Annual certification fee is $75.00. Training is offered online (self-paced with approximately 6 hours of materials) and requires passing an open-book exam with 80% or higher score.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2025 (for renewal applications); no deadline for initial registration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small-scale poultry and rabbit producers seeking to process animals on-farm for intrastate commercial sale to restaurants, retailers, and farmers markets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program supports on-farm slaughter and processing of poultry and rabbits for intrastate commercial sale. Annual certification fee is $75.00.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for producers residing in any county; intrastate sales only within Maryland
requirements_list: Attend MDA training (online course covering poultry production, biosecurity, federal and state regulations, and environmental requirements)
Pass open-book exam with 80% or higher score
Slaughter less than 20,000 poultry per year of own production and/or rabbits
No slaughter of sick animals
Clean animal production areas with rodent control measures
Processing location protected from contamination
Cleanable and sanitizable equipment
Potable water only; annual water testing if non-municipal source
Adequate lighting (if processing outside at night or in enclosure)
Access to toilet and hand washing facilities
Proper temperature monitoring and chilling protocols (chill to 40°F within 4-8 hours depending on weight; store at 40°F)
Personnel health and hygiene standards
Written GMPs, SSOPs, and HACCP plan
Compliant non-food compounds
Proper packaging, labeling, and weights
Appropriate offal and wastewater disposal
Comply with MDE wastewater regulations
Comply with USDA/FSIS inspection-exempt requirements
Provide product labels for approval
Maintain compliance with MDA program requirements and applicable federal, state, and local laws
Allow MDA access to conduct inspections
Correct any non-compliances identified during inspections within specified timeframe
Submit to follow-up inspections if non-compliances are found
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested producers should register for the online training course. Course requires a valid email address and internet access. Complete self-paced online training materials (approximately 6 hours) covering poultry/rabbit production, biosecurity, regulations, and processing requirements. Take open-book exam and achieve 80% or higher score to receive training certificate. Submit completed certification application with farm details, animal types/numbers, slaughter dates, class completion documentation, wastewater compliance method, and product labels for approval. Pay $75.00 annual certification fee. Once certified, producers can sell poultry and rabbits intrastate.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that builds resilience in the middle of the food supply chain by supporting expanded capacity for aggregation, processing, manufacturing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of locally and regionally produced food products. The program provides more and better markets to small farms and food businesses, supports development of value-added products, encourages fair prices and fair wages, and establishes new and safe job opportunities. Excludes meat, poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, fiber, landscaping products, tobacco, and dietary supplements.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of grants: Infrastructure Grants ranging from a minimum of $100,000 to a maximum of $3 million for three-year projects, and Simplified Equipment-Only Grants ranging from $10,000 to $100,000. Grant applicants are required to contribute 50% of the total proposed project cost as a match to federal funding. For historically underserved farmers and ranchers and small businesses qualifying under the Small Business Administration (including small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and veteran-owned small businesses), the required match is reduced to 25% of the total proposed project cost. Infrastructure Grants support facility expansion, construction, cold storage equipment, expanding capacity for processing, aggregation and distribution, employee training, food safety compliance, and modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and information technology systems. Equipment-Only Grants are reimbursement-based with no matching requirements and no indirect costs allowed, supporting equipment purchases including special-purpose vehicles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers and processors, groups thereof, nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities meeting SBA small business standards, local government entities, tribal governments, and institutions (schools, universities, hospitals) establishing cooperative or shared infrastructure that benefit local and regional food producers and businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of locally and regionally produced food products including specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, aquaculture, and other eligible food products, excluding meat, poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, fiber, landscaping products, tobacco, and dietary supplements. Specific uses include cold storage equipment, facility expansion and construction, capacity expansion for processing and distribution, employee training, food safety compliance, packaging and labeling improvements, special-purpose equipment, special-purpose vehicles (delivery, refrigerated trucks), and modernizing manufacturing and information technology systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Facilities must be physically located within Maryland.
requirements_list: Infrastructure Grants: minimum $100,000, maximum $3,000,000
Equipment-Only Grants: minimum $10,000, maximum $100,000
Infrastructure Grants are for three-year projects
General applicants must contribute 50% match to federal funding
Historically underserved farmers and ranchers and qualifying small businesses must contribute 25% match
Equipment-Only Grants require no matching funds and are reimbursement-based
Projects support aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of eligible food products
Meat, poultry, wild-caught seafood, animal feed, fiber, landscaping products, tobacco, and dietary supplements excluded from eligibility
For-profit entities must meet SBA small business size standards and primarily benefit local/regional producers
Projects benefiting multiple producers are more competitive than those benefiting individual producers
Environmental compliance and NEPA review required
Projects must have defined physical location with GPS coordinates and address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application packet including an Infrastructure Grant application or Simplified Equipment-Only Grant application by the deadline. Required forms include USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire, Match Verification Template Letter, and Evidence of Critical Resources and Infrastructure Template Letter. Applications must include a project budget using the RFSI Budget-Match Worksheet. Applicants must provide GPS coordinates and physical address of project location. Applications are reimbursement-based, requiring recipients to submit invoices for already-paid expenses. AMS staff complete environmental compliance evaluation and may request additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to urban and small-scale producers who want to plant cover crops but do not qualify for traditional cover crop grant programs. Growers plant less than 10 acres of cover crops and receive reimbursement based on paid receipts, up to $1,500 per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,500 per year per grower. Growers are reimbursed based on paid receipts for cover crop seed and planting costs. Eligible species include single cereal grains or cover crop seed mixes that can be planted in open plots/fields, raised beds, or high tunnels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual growers, organized for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations that produce farm products generating at least $1,000 in annual sales or donations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cover crop seed and planting costs for eligible agricultural operations growing farm products in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to operations located in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas of Maryland.
requirements_list: Operation must produce a farm product generating minimum of $1,000 in annual sales or donations
Farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland
Grower must plant less than 10 acres of cover crop
Grant recipients must comply with all local, state, and federal regulations and secure required permits

Eligible products include agricultural, horticultural, vegetable, fruit products; livestock, meats, poultry, eggs, dairy; equine operations; wool, hides, feathers, honey; and forest, orchard, garden, or water products
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the 2026 Small Acreage Cover Crop Program Application form and the Requirements and Agreement form from the website. Complete the application and agreement. Submit during the enrollment period (March 16 through April 24, 2026). Reimbursement is provided based on paid receipts.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance to support small-scale agricultural operations in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas. The program aims to increase community access to healthy foods by helping farmers improve their management of natural resources through adoption of Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants in the spring and fall and Water and Power Grants for qualifying operations located in urban areas. Grant amounts and specific terms are available through the specific grant programs listed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, for-profit agricultural businesses, and non-profit organizations operating small-scale farms that produce farm products generating a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for management of natural resources and adoption of Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices. Specific uses available through individual grant programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural operations must be located in urban, peri-urban, rural, or suburban areas of Maryland. Farm products must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Operation must produce a farm product that generates a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually
Grantee is responsible for all local, state, or federal regulations and permits necessary for the agricultural operation
Farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland

Eligible agricultural products include: any agricultural, horticultural, vegetable, or fruit product of the soil whether raw or canned, frozen, dried, pickled, or otherwise processed; livestock, meats, marine food products, poultry, eggs, or dairy products; equine operations; wool, hides, feathers, or honey; any product of farm, forest, orchard, garden, or water
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the program administrator or visit the specific grant program pages for detailed application procedures. Two main grant types are offered: Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants (spring and fall) and Water and Power Grants (for qualifying urban operations).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture awards competitive grants to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops including fruits and vegetables, culinary herbs and spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees and nursery crops. Funded through the USDA Specialty Crop Block Grant Program, the grants support projects that benefit a broader group of similar producers or an industry segment, not just individual businesses. The program provides funding for specialty crop production, research, and marketing. The program anticipates approximately $400,000 in funding available to be awarded through a competitive review process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture awards grants to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops through projects with broader industry impact. The program anticipates approximately $400,000 in funding available under the USDA Specialty Crop Block Grant Program to be awarded through a competitive review process. Proposals must demonstrate that the project will have broader impact for a group of similar producers or an industry segment, not just benefit a single organization, business, institution or individual. Grant funds are subject to USDA's General Terms and Conditions effective December 31, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual farmers, nonprofits, and other organizations seeking to enhance the competitiveness of Maryland specialty crops through projects that benefit broader groups of producers or industry segments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that enhance competitiveness of specialty crops such as fruits, vegetables, herbs, spices, honey, hops, grapes, maple syrup, Christmas trees and nursery crops. Project funds support activities with broader industry impact, such as field days, farm tours, and adoption of new production methods. Allowable uses include supplies and materials (including computing devices under $5,000), training related to project objectives or grants management, and domestic and foreign travel with approved budget or prior written approval. Unallowable uses include sponsorship costs, trade show attendance/displays, meeting room reservations, and exhibits/demonstrations/space rental not aligned with grant purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Proposals must demonstrate that the project will benefit a broader group of similar producers or an industry segment
Grant funds will not be awarded for projects that only benefit or provide profit to a single organization, business, institution or individual
Grant awardees must comply with USDA's General Terms and Conditions effective December 31, 2025
Must complete all 4 pages of the application
Must complete and upload the SCBGP Project Profile Template
Must fill out all required fields (marked with red asterisks)
Provide project title, start date, and end date
All applicants must complete the SCBGP Project Profile Template to be considered for grant funding
Must maintain accounting systems meeting 2 CFR §200.302 Standards for Financial and Program Management
Computing devices must have acquisition cost less than $5,000
Travel must be provided in approved budget or have prior written approval
Travel policies must comply with GSA Federal Travel Regulation standards
Materials and supplies must be used for direct performance of Federal award
Training must relate to project objectives or Federal grants management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants register and login to the OneStop portal, search for the Maryland Specialty Crop Block Grant Application, and complete a 4-page application form. Applicants must download, complete, and upload the SCBGP Project Profile Template, review the entire application, and submit. The Maryland Department of Agriculture conducts an annual competitive review process guided by industry, nonprofit and government stakeholders to award grant funds. Applicants should review the OneStop End User Guide and SCBG Allowable and Unallowable Costs documents before applying. Applicants will receive a form confirmation upon submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A bonus payment program available to farmers and landowners who install qualifying conservation practices through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program. The incentive provides additional payment per tree planted to help Maryland achieve its tree-planting goal for capturing greenhouse gas emissions that contribute to climate change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers receive $2 for each new tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice. This payment is in addition to the regular cost-share rate. Available for windbreak establishment ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), silvopasture ($2 per tree plus up to 87.5% cost-share), riparian forest buffer ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), hedgerow planting ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), and tree and shrub establishment ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners in Maryland who participate in the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting trees as part of approved conservation practices including windbreaks, silvopasture, riparian forest buffers, hedgerows, and tree and shrub establishment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Install qualifying conservation practices through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program
Plant new trees as part of approved conservation practice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program and meet the approved conservation practice requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program supporting the planting and establishment of trees on agricultural and other lands to improve environmental conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and technical assistance for tree planting projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners and organizations interested in tree planting in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and establishment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's lawn fertilizer law helps protect the Chesapeake Bay from excess nutrients entering its waters. The program establishes fertilizer application restrictions, requires certification for lawn care professionals who apply fertilizer, and enforces best management practices for homeowners and businesses to prevent nitrogen and phosphorus from washing into waterways. The program provides certification of individual fertilizer applicators and business licensing for commercial fertilizer application companies, along with training in fertilizer products and proper application techniques.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides training and certification for lawn care professionals who apply fertilizer. Certification exams are offered throughout the year (February 9, April 13, June 8, August 19, December 3, 2026). Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certificates are valid through December 31 of each year and can be renewed yearly for a $100 fee with verification of recertification training. Fertilizer Applicator Business Licenses are $50 (waived for government agencies). The program also provides educational resources, guidelines, and technical assistance to homeowners and businesses on proper fertilizer application practices, soil testing procedures, nutrient management, and equipment calibration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple exam dates in 2026: February 9, April 13, June 8, August 19, December 3; applications must be submitted before announced examination dates; Annual Report due by March 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professional lawn care applicators, lawn care companies, golf course managers, public parks management, airport turf managers, athletic field managers, business property managers, cemetery managers, homeowners, and other organizations that fertilize lawns and turf areas on non-agricultural land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, certification, business licensing, and compliance with fertilizer application regulations to protect the Chesapeake Bay from excess nutrients. Soil testing, nutrient management, equipment calibration, and best management practices for turfgrass maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program applies statewide across Maryland, including all counties, municipalities, golf courses, parks, recreation areas, businesses and residential lawns. Exam locations available in Anne Arundel, Montgomery, Washington, and Wicomico counties (Annapolis, Derwood, Boonsboro, Salisbury).
requirements_list: Lawn care professionals must be certified by the department or work under direct supervision of a certified individual
Professional Fertilizer Applicator Certificates must be renewed annually by December 31 each year
License holders must file an annual activity report by March 1 covering the previous year
All applicators must follow University of Maryland fertilizer recommendations
Single fertilizer application may not exceed 0.9 pound total nitrogen per 1,000 square feet
Phosphorus may only be applied when a soil test indicates it is needed or when lawn is being established, patched or renovated
Fertilizer blackout dates are November 16 through March 1 for most applicants
Lawn care professionals may apply nitrogen between November 16 through December 1 at maximum rate of 0.5 pound per 1,000 square feet
Enhanced efficiency controlled release products may be applied at no more than 2.5 pounds per year
Keep fertilizer 10 to 15 feet from waterways
Do not fertilize if heavy rain is predicted or ground is frozen
Complete PFA certification application form
Provide Fertilizer Application Business License (MDA-F) number or completed business license application
Government-issued photo ID required for testing
Pass exam with 70% or better score
At least one Maryland Certified Professional Fertilizer Applicator on staff for businesses
Employees must be registered with the State
Maintain application records for minimum 3 years
Display MDA-F license number on company vehicles (2-inch lettering on both sides)
Comply with COMAR 15.20.10 regulations
Soil testing required prior to initial phosphorus application and prior to second nitrogen application
Annual spreader calibration requirement
Reduce commercial fertilizer by nutrient content of compost or organic amendments applied
Sweep fertilizer from hardscapes back onto turf
Maintain constant walking speed (~3.5 mph)
Inspect equipment daily
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For lawn care professionals seeking certification: Review exam dates (February 9, April 13, June 8, August 19, December 3, 2026) and register for the certification exam through the 2026 Turfgrass Certification Exam Schedule. Complete required training and study materials including the Maryland Professional Lawn Care Manual. Pass the certification exam with 70% or better score. Attend review session (encouraged but not mandatory). For business licenses: Download and submit the Fertilizer Applicator Business License Application with $50 fee (waived for government agencies). Ensure at least one certified professional fertilizer applicator on staff. Renew annually. Annual activity reports must be filed by March 1. Recertification training is available through classes and recorded webinars listed on the Training Page.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices Audits
structured_extraction.program_description: Voluntary USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Specialty Crops Inspection Division audit program that provides objective third-party verification of farms, packing facilities, storage facilities, and wholesale distribution centers. MDA conducts audits of fruit and vegetable producers and handlers to determine compliance with USDA's Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices standards and Pre-Harvest and Post-Harvest Harmonized standards. Multiple audit types available including Produce GAPs Harmonized Audits, Mushroom Specific GAP Audits, and Tomato Audit Protocols covering field operations, harvesting, post-harvest, packing facilities, storage, transportation, and food defense procedures. The program is conducted through a cooperative agreement with USDA/AMS and provides national recognition for producers and handlers.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDA conducts USDA audits of fruit and vegetable producers and handlers. Third-party verification of Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices compliance.
