MDA currently has USDA Specialty Crop grant money to assist Maryland producers in offsetting USDA audit costs. Payment covers audit fees and travel expenses for initial and unannounced audits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial audit request must be made no later than 2 weeks prior to end of growing/harvesting/packing season
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers and handlers of specialty crops, including farms, packing facilities, storage facilities, and wholesale distribution centers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Audit services to verify GAP/GHP compliance, including audit fees and travel expenses for initial and unannounced audits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland producers and handlers of fruits and vegetables. Applicants must comply with all Federal, State, and local laws and regulations.
requirements_list: Must be a producer or handler of fruits and vegetables
Must meet USDA Good Agricultural Practices and Good Handling Practices standards
Conform to 7 CFR Part 51 and applicable Federal, State, and local regulations
Schedule audit using SC-237A form
Complete all required form fields
Select at least one audit service type
Provide farm/facility and applicant information
List commodities to be audited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Producers request a USDA GAP/GHP audit no later than 2 weeks prior to end of growing/harvesting/packing season using the audit request form. MDA conducts the audit in cooperation with USDA/AMS. Upon meeting standards and USDA acceptance criteria, producers receive USDA certification with national recognition.

structured_extraction.program_name: Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial assistance for water and power infrastructure improvements for urban agriculture operations and projects in Maryland. The program helps urban farms and community gardens purchase and install equipment to access water and electricity needed to sustain their operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant provides up to 87.5% of the total project cost, with a maximum funding limit of $75,000 per application. Eligible expenses include water meters, water pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, electrical lines, or other equipment authorized by the department. Grant funding supports water and power infrastructure improvements for urban agriculture operations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted as long as funds remain available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Urban farms and community gardens that produce farm products generating a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually and are located in urban areas or incorporated municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of water and power infrastructure equipment including water meters, water pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, electrical lines, or other equipment authorized by the department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operations must be located in urban areas as defined by the United States Census Bureau and any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland. Property location can be verified using the interactive map provided. Statewide Maryland.
requirements_list: Produce a farm product that generates a minimum of $1,000 in sales or donations annually
Comply with all local, state, or federal regulations and secure required project permits
Located in urban areas as defined by the United States Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland
Applicant must have controlled the land for at least 5 years, either through ownership or leasing
Bids required from authorized contractors for work on public roads, sidewalks, water mains, and transformers, and from private contractors for on-site installation services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the interactive map to verify that your property meets the location criteria. If your property qualifies, download the application packet and submit. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis as long as funds remain available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA-funded nutrition grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture that provides annual benefits to WIC participants and low-resource seniors to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers' markets. WIC participants receive $30 annually and eligible seniors receive $35 annually. Benefits can be redeemed at authorized farmers' markets between June 1 and November 30th. WIC participants can sign up during clinic appointments beginning in June, while eligible seniors can apply online or connect with their local Area Agency on Aging.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants in the WIC program receive an annual benefit of $30 to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers' markets. Low-resource seniors participating in the Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program receive an annual benefit of $35. Benefits can be used between June 1 and November 30th at any of the 100+ authorized farmers markets throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2026 Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program application opens on June 1st
structured_extraction.program_audience: WIC participants and low-resource seniors eligible for the Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program, and farmers authorized to accept FMNP benefits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh fruits and vegetables at authorized farmers' markets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at all 100+ authorized farmers markets in the state
requirements_list: Must be a WIC participant or eligible low-resource senior
WIC participants can sign up during clinic appointments beginning in June
Eligible seniors can apply online or connect with their local Area Agency on Aging
Benefits must be used between June 1 and November 30th
Farmer must be authorized by the Maryland State Department of Agriculture to accept FMNP benefits
Farmer must complete training session with Maryland Department of Agriculture
Farmer must complete farmer application on Maryland's One Stop
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: WIC participants can opt to sign up during their clinic appointments beginning in June. Eligible seniors can apply online at mda.maryland.gov starting June 1st or can connect with their local Area Agency on Aging for support. Farmers attend a Maryland Department of Agriculture training session, complete the farmer application on Maryland's One Stop, and once approved, receive a Farmer Agreement to sign electronically.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for qualified recipients seeking to purchase health insurance through the Maryland Health Connection marketplace. Qualified recipients may receive funds to help pay their monthly insurance premiums or receive a tax credit at the end of the year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to pay monthly health insurance premiums or tax credit at end of year for qualified recipients purchasing coverage through Maryland Health Connection marketplace.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified individuals and families seeking health insurance coverage
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health insurance premiums through Maryland Health Connection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Qualified recipient
Seeking to purchase health insurance through Maryland Health Connection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through Maryland Health Connection website

structured_extraction.program_name: Assessment Exemption for an Improvement Required for the Health or Medical Condition of a Resident
structured_extraction.program_description: Real property tax exemption for improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings that are medically necessary or required for the health or medical condition of a resident. The exemption is based on the value added by the health-related improvement and may not exceed 10% of the total market value of the property. Exemption is granted for the current tax year in which the application is received and is removed for the next full tax year after transfer of property or if the individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from property tax valuation for improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings required by the health or medical condition of a resident. Exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value of the property (10% of land and improvement combined). Exemption is granted for the current tax year in which the application is received and is removed for the next full tax year after transfer of property or if the individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide loan and financial assistance program that helps limited income, elderly, and disabled homeowners avoid tax sale foreclosure. The program diverts vulnerable homeowners from the tax sale process into an alternative loan program, minimizes tax collection costs, and allows homeowners to remain in their homes. The program provides short-term loans to help homeowners pay delinquent property taxes, removes eligible homeowners from the tax sale process for at least three years, and provides individualized assistance to navigate the tax sale process and connect with resources and support to help them keep their home. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving federal disability benefits, or those whose dwelling has been their principal residence for 10 years or more. Donations are accepted through a donation portal to fund loans for at-risk homeowners. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland property tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation that protects homeowners against large assessment increases on owner-occupied residential properties designated as the homeowner's principal residence. The program limits the annual increase in taxable assessments by capping the amount of assessment increase on which eligible homeowners pay county, municipal, and state property taxes each year, regardless of property value or income level. Caps are set at 1-10% (set annually by county resolution), with State of Maryland tax capped at 10% (5% in the Town of Kensington), County tax capped at 5-8% (8% for Cecil County as of July 1, 2007; 10% for Montgomery County), and municipal tax capped at 5%, with individual jurisdictions potentially setting lower caps. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to implement this cap. Homeowners establish eligibility through a one-time application submission to the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or their county tax office, though the credit is automatically applied to properties listed as 'Principal Residence' in some jurisdictions. The program is not applicable in the first year following the purchase of a home. When reassessment exceeds the annual limit, homeowners pay no property tax on the assessment increase above that limit, resulting in substantial tax credits each year on their property tax bills. Eligibility is determined by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation based on qualification criteria.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit against state, county, and municipal property taxes that caps the annual increase in taxable assessments. The cap is set at 1-10% (set annually by county resolution), with 10% for state-taxable assessments (5% in the Town of Kensington), 5-8% for county-taxable assessments (8% for Cecil County as of July 1, 2007; 10% for Montgomery County), and 5% for municipal-taxable assessments, with individual jurisdictions potentially setting lower caps. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to implement this cap. The homeowner pays no property tax on the assessment increase above the limit. Any annual assessment growth in excess of the cap becomes a credit applied to the property tax bill. The credit is automatically applied to properties listed as 'Principal Residence' in some jurisdictions; in others, homeowners must apply annually beginning in 2008. Homeowners establish eligibility through a one-time application submission to the Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation or the appropriate county tax office. Homeowners can apply online at https://sdathtc.dat.maryland.gov/ or https://onestop.md.gov/, by mail, or by fax, and receive substantial tax credits each year on their property tax bills. A one-time application must be filed with SDAT by May 1, 2026 to ensure the credit appears on future tax bills beginning July 1, 2026.

Different caps may apply in individual towns and jurisdictions. Applications submitted to state department of assessments or appropriate county tax office.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by visiting the SDAT Real Property Search page, selecting your county, finding your property, and checking the Homestead Application Status row. Step 2: If no application is on file, obtain your Real Property Account Number (from an SDAT letter or the SDAT website), then file using one of these methods: (1) Apply online at https://sdathtc.dat.maryland.gov/ or https://onestop.md.gov/ (recommended) for fastest service; (2) Mail a completed paper application to Department of Assessments and Taxation, Homestead Tax Credit Division, 700 East Pratt Street, 2nd Floor Suite 2700, Baltimore, Maryland 21202; (3) Fax completed paper application to 410-225-9344. Homeowners can also download and submit a PDF form. The credit is automatically applied to properties listed as 'Principal Residence' in eligible areas. In some jurisdictions, starting in 2008, homeowners must apply annually. New purchasers of properties will be mailed a homestead application by the Department once the new deed is recorded and records have been updated. A one-time application must be filed with SDAT by May 1, 2026 for the County ITOC credit to appear on future bills beginning July 1, 2026. In-person service appointments can be scheduled through the provided booking system. Homeowners should verify their property is enrolled in the program through the state and can check the status of their application by looking up their property in the Real Property database at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide tax credit program that provides annual rent relief to eligible renters to help offset the share of rent that goes toward property taxes. The program is modeled on the Homeowners' Tax Credit Program (Circuit Breaker Program) based on the concept that renters indirectly pay property taxes through rent and should receive similar protection as homeowners. Eligible renters receive direct check payments based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and a tax threshold determined by income and family size. The credit is calculated based on total gross household income and monthly rent amount. Montgomery County supplements the State credit with an additional 50% of the State credit amount, with no separate application required for the County Supplement.

The credit is calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and a tax threshold determined by income and family size. Utilities included in rent reduce the amount eligible for credit. Property tax credits for renters whose rental payments include property taxes. Montgomery County supplements the State credit with an additional 50% of the State credit amount, with no separate application required for the County Supplement. Applications are available at all senior activity centers. Tax credit is applied to state income tax liability.

Tax Credit Services are also available for in-person assistance at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202. Applications are also available at all senior activity centers and senior centers in Calvert County. Applications are due by October 1 each year. Determine total gross household income and monthly rent, then visit dat.maryland.gov/renters to apply. Once approved by the State, the State sends the credit information to Montgomery County. The County then calculates the County Supplement (50% of the State credit) and sends a check directly to the renter. Submit application with required documentation including federal tax returns and related forms.

structured_extraction.program_description: MarylandSaves is a statewide workplace retirement and savings program administered by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation that allows employees and self-employed individuals to save for retirement and build emergency savings through payroll deductions or voluntary contributions into portable WorkLife Savings Accounts (Roth IRAs). The program is offered at no cost to employers, with no employer contributions required, no administrative fees, and no fiduciary liabilities. Employers who register and send payroll contributions by the annual deadline (December 31) receive an annual $300 Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) filing fee waiver. Alternatively, employers already offering a qualified retirement plan can claim the waiver without registering. Employees can contribute a portion of their paycheck to accounts with the potential to grow through investment returns, maintain full control over contribution amounts, and access funds when needed for emergencies or retirement. Default contributions start at 5% and increase automatically by 1% annually up to a maximum of 10% unless changed. The first $1,000 of contributions goes into an Emergency Savings Fund earning no asset-based fees, with remaining contributions invested in target retirement date funds. Participation is voluntary with flexible enrollment, adjustment, and opt-out options. Most Maryland employers are required under state law to offer some form of retirement savings plan, though businesses with no employees or running manual payroll are exempt from registration requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides portable retirement and savings accounts with no employer contributions required and no administrative fees for employers. Employers receive an annual $300 SDAT filing fee waiver if they register and send payroll contributions by December 31 each year, or if they claim the waiver online after certifying they already offer a qualified retirement plan. The program features no fiduciary liabilities for employers and provides a free enrollment platform for employers to offer employees a WorkLife Savings Account with payroll deduction. Automatic payroll deductions fund a Roth IRA account with a default contribution rate of 5% of gross pay, increasing automatically by 1% annually up to a maximum of 10%. The first $1,000 of contributions goes into an Emergency Savings Fund earning no asset-based fees. Remaining contributions are invested in target retirement date funds. Employees contribute a portion of their paycheck to accounts with the potential to grow through investment returns. Participants can adjust contribution rates (minimum 1%), withdraw funds for emergencies or retirement, customize investment choices, designate beneficiaries, and maintain accounts through career changes without complicated rollovers. Default enrollment is available with the option to adjust or opt out entirely. Account fees include a $30 annual fee plus asset-based fees ranging from 0.18% to 0.85% depending on investment option chosen. Businesses with no employees or running manual payroll are exempt from registration requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers with at least 2 years of operation, at least one employee over age 18, and an automated payroll system (or those already offering a qualified retirement plan); Maryland workers and employees at least 18 years old seeking to build emergency savings and retirement savings through their workplace; self-employed individuals in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employer registration and setup for a workplace retirement savings program; employee and self-employed individual contributions for emergency savings and retirement savings through portable WorkLife Savings Accounts (Roth IRAs). Contributions grow tax-free and withdrawals in retirement are not subject to federal income tax.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland employers, workers, and self-employed individuals meeting eligibility criteria. Individuals must perform services for work within Maryland. The $300 filing fee waiver applies to businesses that conduct commercial activities in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For employers: Visit marylandsaves.vestwell.com/register/employer to register by providing your SDAT number and Access Code. Complete the 7-step onboarding process which includes business setup, password creation, payroll information, bank information, employee information, contribution setup, and ongoing maintenance. You will upload your current employee roster with personal information (name, contact info, date of birth, SSN). Alternatively, if already offering a qualified retirement plan, claim the annual filing fee waiver online using EIN and SDAT number. Businesses exempt from registration can certify exemption online. After registration, maintain compliance by continuing to send payroll contributions and updating employee records. Employers can also invite a payroll representative to help facilitate registration. For employees: If your employer participates, you are automatically enrolled with a 5% contribution rate and can customize your account or opt out within 30 days of enrollment. You can adjust your contribution rate (1-100% of compensation in whole number percentages), select alternative investment options, or rejoin the program at any time. Online enrollment takes minutes. For self-employed individuals: Create an account online or by phone at 1-833-811-7437/1-833-811-7438 by providing Social Security number, date of birth, and residential address. Set up automatic contributions (semi-monthly or monthly with minimum of $5.00) or make an initial contribution by check or bank account, then select investment options from available funds including Emergency Savings Fund, Target Retirement Date options, Bond Index, and Global Growth Stock options. Participation is voluntary with the option to enroll, adjust contribution rates, or opt out at any time.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides investors with refundable income tax credits equal to a percentage of their eligible investment in a Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Company (QMBC). The credit percentage and maximum amount vary based on the company's location and whether it qualifies for enhanced credits through Opportunity Zone or RISE Zone programs. Standard credits are 33% up to $250,000, or 50% up to $500,000 for companies in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. Enhanced credits are available for Opportunity Zone fund investors (65% up to $575,000 for Level 1 or 75% up to $750,000 for Level 2) and RISE Zone investors (50% up to $500,000). Credits are issued on a first-come basis until the fiscal year budget is exhausted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive a refundable income tax credit equal to 33% of an eligible investment in a QMBC up to $250,000, or 50% up to $500,000 if the QMBC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County. Enhanced credits are available for Opportunity Zone fund investors (65% up to $575,000 for Level 1 or 75% up to $750,000 for Level 2) and RISE Zone investors (50% up to $500,000). The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. Credits are issued on a first-come, first-served basis until the fiscal year budget is exhausted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Form B QMBC applications begin August 19, 2025; Form A Investor applications deadline September 15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m.; Online Electronic Queue Investor Registration begins September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies engaged in research, development, or commercialization of innovative biotechnology

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through Commerce's online system in two stages. First, the QMBC must submit Form B application beginning August 19, 2025. Second, investors submit Form A application (which varies by investor type: Form A1 for individuals, Form A2 for corporate investors, Form A3 for pass-through entities) with deadline of September 15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. Investor applications are eligible for the Online Electronic Queue Investor Registration opening September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST. Applications are processed first-come, first-served based on submission order in the queue. If approved, Commerce issues an Initial Certificate of Approval authorizing the investment. After the investor provides proof of investment, Commerce issues a Final Certificate of Approval awarding the tax credit. The investor claims the credit on their Maryland Tax Return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that supports innovation infrastructure development in critical technology sectors including advanced manufacturing, aerospace, agriculture, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, blue technology, cybersecurity, defense, energy and sustainability, life sciences, quantum, and sensors and robotics. The program provides grants of up to $2 million to support projects that establish tools and resources for growing industries, including acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, installation, improvement, or equipping of innovation infrastructure projects, research and manufacturing facilities, equipment, training and shared lab concepts for technology startups and emerging industries. Matching funds are required: 200% of the grant amount for grants up to $1 million, and 400% for grants over $1 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants of up to $2 million to support innovation infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors. For grants up to $1 million, applicants must provide matching funds equal to at least 200% of the grant amount. For grants over $1 million, applicants must provide matching funds equal to at least 400% of the grant amount. Grant awards may be used to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip eligible innovation infrastructure projects, including establishment of research and manufacturing facilities, equipment, training and shared lab concepts for technology startups and emerging industries, wet laboratories, cyber ranges, and specialized training spaces. Funds must be spent within two years of agreement date and projects must be fully operational within two years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide tax credit program providing an income tax credit to Maryland companies and qualified investors. Small Maryland companies with 50 or fewer employees receive an income tax credit equal to 50% of the purchase price for cybersecurity goods, products, or services purchased from Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Sellers. Additionally, qualified investors receive a refundable income tax credit for investments in Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies. The program has a total of $4 million available each year, with $3 million allocated for technology purchases and $1 million for service purchases. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, covering up to $100,000 in purchases. The tax credit must be claimed for the tax year in which a purchase is made.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit equal to 50% of the purchase price (or net purchase price) for cybersecurity goods, products, or services from Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Sellers for Maryland companies with 50 or fewer employees. Maximum credit is $50,000 per year, covering up to $100,000 in purchases. Refundable income tax credit available for qualified investors investing in Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies. Eligible technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. Services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework. The tax credit must be claimed for the tax year in which a purchase is made.

Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. If approved, you will receive a Certificate of Approval, which must be attached to your Maryland income tax return. Qualified investors may invest in Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies and claim the refundable income tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce runs the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which provides grants and loans to small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry, with a particular focus on minority-owned, women-owned, and socially equitable businesses. The fund also provides grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities for cannabis-related programs and to business development organizations to train and assist licensed small businesses. Funding is available for Social Equity Applicants with a conditional cannabis license, with amounts varying by license type: up to $131,250 for dispensaries, $183,750 for processors, and $525,000 for growers, with smaller amounts for micro-license holders.

The grant is paid in installments as the business meets specific milestones. Funds can be used for license applications, operating costs, capital expenses, and targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry.

structured_extraction.program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax exemption program that allows data centers operating or expanding in Maryland to receive an exemption from the state's 6% sales and use tax on qualified data center personal property. The exemption is available for 10 years, with potential extension to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years. Businesses must be certified as Qualified Data Centers by the Maryland Department of Commerce, create new full-time positions, and meet investment thresholds based on location (Tier 1 areas require $2 million minimum investment; other areas require $5 million).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible data centers receive an exemption from Maryland's sales and use tax on qualifying data center personal property for 10 years, extendable to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years. Investment thresholds vary by location: $2 million for Tier 1 areas (including specific counties and Opportunity Zones) and $5 million for other areas of the state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Data center businesses that plan to locate or expand in Maryland and create new full-time positions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax exemption applies to the purchase of qualified data center personal property used in data center operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide throughout Maryland but has different investment requirements based on location. Tier 1 areas include specific counties (Baltimore City, Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester) and all Opportunity Zones, which have a lower investment threshold of $2 million. All other areas of the state require a $5 million investment threshold.
requirements_list: Must be certified as a Qualified Data Center by the Maryland Department of Commerce

Qualified positions must pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage
Qualified positions must be filled for at least 12 months and be new to Maryland
Invest at least $2 million in qualified data center personal property if located in a Tier 1 Area
Invest at least $5 million in qualified data center personal property if located in any other area of the state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Eligibility Application to the Maryland Department of Commerce. Commerce reviews the application and issues a Certificate of Eligibility. Finally, Commerce notifies the Comptroller's Office, which issues the sales and use tax exemption certificate to the business.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Opportunities Program Fund (Sunny Day)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports extraordinary economic development opportunities that create and retain employment as well as create significant capital investments. Projects must generate significant jobs in areas of high unemployment and are evaluated on a competitive basis consistent with the state's strategic economic development plan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided on a competitive basis. Applicants must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of the Sunny Day assistance requested. Provides funding for economic development opportunities with significant employment creation and capital investment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and organizations planning large-scale economic development projects that create and retain jobs and require significant capital investment, particularly in areas of high unemployment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments to create and retain employment and economic development initiatives that generate significant jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program with priority for areas of high unemployment.

Priority for areas of high unemployment

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Security Clearance Costs (ESCC) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland tax credit program that provides income tax credits for for-profit business entities that incur qualified federal security clearance administrative expenses, construction and renovation costs for Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs), and first-year leasing costs for qualified small businesses performing security-based contract work. The program provides three types of tax credits: (1) Security Clearance Administrative Expenses Tax Credit up to $200,000 per taxable year for qualified security clearance administrative expenses including processing applications, maintaining computer systems, and training employees; (2) Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) Costs Tax Credit equal to the lesser of 50% of costs or $200,000 for single SCIF, or up to $500,000 per calendar year for multiple SCIFs; (3) First Year Leasing Costs Tax Credit for qualified small businesses up to $200,000 for first-year rental payments. Total credits capped at $2 million per calendar year for all businesses, with pro-rata distribution if exceeded.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three types of tax credits: (1) Security Clearance Administrative Expenses Tax Credit up to $200,000 per taxable year for qualified security clearance administrative expenses including processing applications, maintaining computer systems, and training employees; (2) Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) Costs Tax Credit equal to the lesser of 50% of costs or $200,000 for single SCIF, or up to $500,000 per calendar year for multiple SCIFs; (3) First Year Leasing Costs Tax Credit for qualified small businesses up to $200,000 for first-year rental payments. Total credits capped at $2 million per calendar year for all businesses, with pro-rata distribution if exceeded.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified expenses include processing federal security clearance applications, maintaining or upgrading computer systems required for security clearances, training employees in clearance administration, construction or renovation of accredited SCIFs, and first-year rental payments for leased spaces used for security-based contracting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. SCIF construction/renovation and leased spaces must be located in Maryland.

For-profit business entities or individuals with 500 or fewer employees
Expenses must be for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, but before January 1, 2028

For First Year Leasing Costs credit, business must be a qualified small business: independently owned and operated, not a subsidiary, not dominant in its field, and employed no more than 25 individuals in most recently completed fiscal year
Must meet small business definition under Tax General Article §7-218
Security clearance expenses must be administrative in nature, not wages for employees applying for clearance
SCIF must be accredited by appropriate federal agency

Rental agreement and proof of payment required for leasing costs
Small Business Affidavit required for First Year Leasing Costs credit

Cash transactions generally not eligible

Business must incur qualified security clearance costs or conduct security-related business in Maryland

Application must include detailed itemized accounting and supporting documentation (invoices, proof of payment, rental agreements as applicable). Commerce certifies approved credit amount by December 15th of same year. Applicant then files amended Maryland income tax return with Comptroller of Maryland, attaching copy of Commerce certification. Credit is claimed on Maryland Tax Form 500CR. See website for full details and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive export assistance program that helps Maryland's small and mid-sized companies offset costs of international marketing and trade show participation. The program provides up to $5,000 in annual reimbursement for expenses associated with international marketing initiatives and export market expansion, including international travel, trade shows, translation services, airfare, brochures, website development, and other international marketing project expenses. Additionally offers up to 20 hours of assistance per year from the Maryland Department of Commerce's trade experts around the globe for export-related technical services. All assistance must directly relate to export products or services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $5,000 in annual reimbursement for expenses incurred by Maryland companies for international marketing initiatives, including international travel, trade shows, translation services, airfare, brochures, website development, and other international marketing project expenses. Additionally offers up to 20 hours of assistance per year from the Maryland Department of Commerce's trade experts around the globe for export-related services. Grants are provided on a monthly basis to help cover traveling and marketing costs for international trade shows. All assistance must directly relate to export products or services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: International marketing initiatives, export market marketing and promotion, international travel, trade shows, translation services, airfare, brochure translation, website development, and other international marketing project expenses; export-related technical assistance services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland companies statewide.

Contact the office at least two weeks before the application deadline to start the process. Submit request for reimbursement through Maryland Department of Commerce. Applications are submitted on a monthly basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable tax credit for film production entities that incur qualified costs in Maryland. The credit covers up to 28% of direct costs for most productions (30% for television series), with a maximum of $10 million per project. Qualified Maryland Small Films can receive up to 28% of direct costs with a maximum of $125,000 per project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified film productions can receive a refundable tax credit of up to 28% of their direct costs. Television series can receive a credit of up to 30% of direct costs. The maximum credit per project is $10 million. Qualified Maryland Small Films can receive a tax credit of up to 28% of direct costs, with a maximum of $125,000 per project. The credit applies to direct costs for film production in Maryland using qualified Maryland vendors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Film production companies, including Maryland-based small film companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct costs for film production in Maryland, including goods and services from qualified Maryland vendors. A detailed list of authorized direct costs is available on the program website.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide. At least 50% of the principal photography must take place in Maryland.
requirements_list: Production costs must be incurred in Maryland
Total direct costs must be over $250,000 ($25,000 for Maryland Small Films)
At least 50% of principal photography must happen in Maryland
Applicants must show proof of financing and national distribution
Principal photography must start within 120 days of receiving a Letter of Qualification

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an Application for Qualification with all required documents before starting any work in Maryland. Applications can be submitted by email, mail, or in person. The Department reviews complete applications in the order received and issues a Letter of Qualification or denial within 30 days. After production is complete, submit an Application for Final Tax Credit Certification no later than 180 days after the completion date.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a state income tax tax credit to small businesses for hiring qualified veterans. Employers may qualify for a credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee in the first year of employment, with a maximum credit of $1,800 per veteran. The credit applies to the first year of employment and small businesses can claim up to five veterans per tax year. The program was available for wages paid during tax years 2017 through 2020.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive a state income tax credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee in the first year of employment, with a maximum credit of $1,800 per veteran. The credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time employees hiring qualified veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit offsets a business's state income tax liability based on wages paid to a newly hired, qualified veteran.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a small business with 50 or fewer full-time employees
Must hire a qualified veteran after January 1, 2017
Veteran must meet program qualifications
A business may claim the credit for up to 5 qualified veteran employees per tax year
The tax credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To receive the credit, a business submits application forms, employee self-certification, W-2s or paystubs, and military discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce for certification. After receiving the certificate, the employer files it with their state tax return using Maryland Tax Form 500CR.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit and incentive program that encourages eligible businesses to expand or relocate in Maryland and create new jobs. The program provides tax credits to businesses that create new full-time positions, with enhanced credits for businesses locating in revitalization areas (enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, DHCD Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, or Tier 1 Counties) and for businesses hiring qualified veteran employees. Manufacturing businesses creating new jobs may receive a 10-year credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible new position, plus a $1,000 credit for businesses employing eligible apprentices. Small businesses can receive $2,500 per qualified veteran employee hired for at least one year. Warehousing and distribution businesses locating in Priority Funding Areas receive credits calculated as the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of annual wages per new employee. The program promotes manufacturing growth in Maryland by providing tax incentives for manufacturing job creation, encourages manufacturers to invest in new equipment through accelerated and bonus depreciation, and funds job training and apprenticeship programs to strengthen Maryland's workforce. In 2019, the program was expanded to include non-manufacturers that locate or expand in Opportunity Zones. The credit is applied against Maryland state income tax liability and may be carried forward for five years if the business does not have sufficient tax liability to use the full credit in the credit year. The Maryland Department of Commerce certifies credits on a first-come, first-served basis up to $4 million per calendar year. Benefits also include real property tax exemptions, waiver of state fees, and tax refunds for certain purchases.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit taken against Maryland state income tax liability. The credit is $3,000 per new full-time job, or $5,000 per new job if the business locates or expands in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, DHCD sustainable community, priority funding area, or Tier 1 County). The credit increases to $4,000 per job filled by a qualified veteran employee or $6,000 per job filled by a qualified veteran employee in a revitalization area. For small businesses hiring qualified veteran employees, the credit is $2,500 per qualified veteran employee who has filled the position for at least one year. For manufacturing businesses, a 10-year credit equal to 5.75% of wages per eligible new position is available, plus a $1,000 credit for businesses employing eligible apprentices. For warehousing and distribution businesses, the credit is the lesser of $1,000 or 2.5% of annual wages for each new employee in a qualified position. Unused credits may be carried forward for five taxable years following the credit year. A business may not earn more than $1 million in a credit year. The program is capped at $4 million in tax credits per calendar year. Benefits also include real property tax exemptions, waiver of state fees, tax refunds for certain purchases, and funding for job training and apprenticeship programs. New businesses locating in Tier 1 Counties may be eligible for a refundable credit against the state's income tax, a credit against the state's portion of real property tax, a refund of sales and use tax, and a waiver of fees charged by the State Department of Assessment and Taxation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses that locate or expand in Maryland and create new full-time jobs, including manufacturing businesses creating new jobs, small businesses that hire qualified veteran employees, new and existing manufacturing businesses, non-manufacturers locating or expanding in Opportunity Zones, and warehousing and distribution businesses locating in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability. May be carried forward for five years if the business does not have sufficient tax liability to use the full credit in the credit year. Job creation in areas that need it most. Equipment investment through accelerated and bonus depreciation. Job training and apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Reduced job creation requirements apply for businesses located in Priority Funding Areas (25 jobs required instead of 60) and enhanced credits apply for businesses located in revitalization areas. Warehousing and distribution businesses must locate facilities within Priority Funding Areas. Tier 1 Counties (Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester) have a 10-job minimum requirement. Additional counties with 10-job minimums include those with annual average employment less than 75,000 or median household income less than two-thirds of statewide median household income. Enhanced 10-job minimum counties also include Calvert, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Queen Anne's, Saint Mary's, and Talbot.

Department of Commerce certifies the business and calculates the credit amount. 5. Claim the credit on Maryland Tax Form 500CR and attach a copy of the Final Certificate of Eligibility. Contact Caroline County Economic Development for assistance if applicable. Interested manufacturing companies or warehousing and distribution companies should contact the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants provided to support expansions, promotions, agricultural projects, research, and business development for breweries, distilleries, wineries, and other alcohol manufacturers in Maryland. The program fosters the creation and expansion of the state's alcohol manufacturing industry and supports initiatives to attract visitors, create promotional events, educate the public about the industry, research local agricultural products for beverages, and support minority ownership.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Breweries, distilleries, wineries, and other alcohol manufacturers in Maryland. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or (6) status, as well as state and local government units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansions, promotions, and agricultural projects. Funds can be used to expand state breweries, distilleries, or wineries, attract new visitors, create special promotional events, educate the public about the industry's history, research local agricultural products for beverages, and support minority ownership in these businesses.

requirements_list: Grant awardees must submit a Final Report within 60 days after the grant term ends.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the program's tips and hints document. Applications must be submitted online by the deadline. The Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion reviews applications and makes recommendations to the Secretary of Commerce, who gives final approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Telework Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A $1 million state-funded grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that helps Maryland businesses and nonprofits implement telework policies. The program provides grants to help eligible organizations purchase equipment, hardware, software, and technical services necessary to develop and implement telework policies. Grants of up to $25,000 are available to eligible businesses and nonprofits.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 1 applications were due by Friday, January 6, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. If additional funding is available, a second round of competitive grant applications may open in early 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses and nonprofits in good standing with the state that have a physical location in Maryland. Preference given to businesses with under 50 employees, including minority-owned businesses, female-owned businesses, Hispanic/Latino-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hardware, software, technical equipment, and technical services necessary to implement telework policy. Cannot be used for previously purchased equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have a physical location in Maryland. Program available statewide to all Maryland counties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state small business revolving loan fund program supported by federal Economic Development Administration funding. Provides financing to small and underserved businesses to upgrade or modernize operations, develop or expand commercial applications for technology, enter into and compete in new or different markets, or address business growth and working capital needs. The program was recapitalized with $770,000 in additional CARES Act funding from EDA to support small businesses impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. Loans of up to $150,000 are available for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, site improvements, business growth, and operational modernization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Revolving loan fund program with loans of up to $150,000 for small businesses. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, site improvements, business growth, and operational modernization. Funded primarily through the Economic Development Administration with recapitalization from CARES Act funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees in all regions of Maryland, including manufacturers, wholesalers, retail companies, technology firms, service companies, and skilled trades. Program also designed to support small businesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition, site improvements, business growth, and operational modernization. Can be used to upgrade or modernize operations, develop or expand commercial applications for technology, or enter into and compete in new or different markets.

The Department will review and process each application using standard commercial credit criteria. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) - Advantage Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: Advantage Maryland (MEDAAF) is a state program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce providing flexible conditional grants, loans, and equity investments to support economic development initiatives and job creation in Maryland. The program assists businesses and local jurisdictions making significant investments and creating jobs across the state. Eligible uses include business attraction and retention, infrastructure support, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, local strategic planning, business expansion project costs, and facility improvements. The program offers five financing capabilities: strategic economic development opportunities, local economic development opportunities, direct assistance to local jurisdictions or MEDCO, regional or local revolving loan funds, and special purpose programs. Conditional grants, loans, and equity investments are provided on a competitive basis to companies making significant capital expenditures and job creation commitments. Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas and involve eligible industry sectors. Examples include conditional loans ranging from $700,000 to $1.4 million for manufacturing expansion and other qualifying projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Advantage Maryland offers five financing capabilities: strategic economic development opportunities, local economic development opportunities, direct assistance to local jurisdictions or MEDCO, regional or local revolving loan funds, and special purpose programs. Conditional grants, loans, and equity investments are provided on a competitive basis to companies making significant capital expenditures and job creation commitments. Assistance amounts and terms vary based on project scope and economic development impact. Loans may be structured to assist with project expansion costs, with examples including conditional loans ranging from $700,000 to $1.4 million for manufacturing expansion and other qualifying projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, MEDCO, and for-profit and non-profit businesses involved in economic development initiatives and job creation within Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments, business expansion, business attraction and retention, infrastructure support, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, local strategic planning, facility improvements, and manufacturing operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas as defined by Maryland's Growth and Development Strategy. Program is available statewide throughout Maryland.

Contact the business development representative in your region for more information about applying. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for Foreign Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps international companies test the U.S. market at a low cost. It gives companies access to business facilities, resources, and advisors. The program also provides funding for costs related to entering the market.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding to help cover costs for entering the U.S. market. This includes physical, programmatic, and other related expenses. Companies can also use business facilities and receive mentoring and networking services for up to six months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foreign companies that want to explore entering the U.S. market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for costs related to entering the U.S. market, including expenses for physical space, program participation, and other related costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide through a network of partner organizations. Companies must physically locate in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be legally registered as a business in its home country for at least one year.
Must have at least five full-time equivalent employees.
Must have at least $500,000 USD in sales revenue and/or external investment in a single year (2023 or 2024).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online portal. The Department of Commerce will help you find a partner organization. To receive funds, you must sign an agreement with a Global Gateway partner.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects through the insurance of financial obligations and the issuance of taxable and tax-exempt bonds. The program facilitates capital access for small- and medium-sized businesses, historically disadvantaged businesses, businesses in rural areas, manufacturers, not-for-profit entities, and day care providers. MIDFA issues private activity revenue bonds and provides credit insurance in the form of loan guaranties. Taxable bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for primarily fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for fixed asset financing at tax-exempt rates, with eligibility limited by Federal tax law to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects. Conventional credit insurance insures up to 80% (not to exceed $2.5 million) of transactions, with export transactions insurable up to 90%. Bond program credit insurance insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA facilitates capital access by issuing private activity revenue bonds and can provide credit insurance in the form of a loan guaranty to reduce lender's risk. Taxable bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for primarily fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds provide access to long-term capital markets for fixed asset financing at tax-exempt rates, with eligibility limited by Federal tax law to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects. Conventional credit insurance insures up to 80% (not to exceed $2.5 million) of transactions made by a financial institution, with export transactions insurable up to 90%. Bond program credit insurance insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million of taxable or tax-exempt bonds.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Commercial and industrial businesses must be located in a Priority Funding Area (with the exception of retail). Manufacturers, not-for-profit entities, and day care providers may have broader eligibility. Program operates statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant and technical assistance program providing education, technical guidance, financial assistance, and grants to small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers to invest in Industry 4.0-related technologies, machinery, robotics, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, and digital business practices to remain competitive and drive growth while implementing advanced, energy-efficient manufacturing technologies. Grants range from $25,000 to $500,000, covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3-50 employees) and up to 50% for mid-sized manufacturers (51-250 employees). Anticipated outcomes include increased productivity and sales, cost savings, and retention and skill training of employees. Funding has been increased to $6 million in FY2026.

Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction

Eligible costs include machinery, equipment, software, training, advanced sensors, AI, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, ERP systems, robots, systems integration projects, smart laser machines, bending machines, coating ovens, automated printers, welding robots, automation systems, process control systems, IoT platforms, CNC machines, SCADA systems, quality inspection equipment, and related manufacturing equipment. The program is designed to bridge the gap between the award date and the actual receipt date of government funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers enhanced tax credit benefits to businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. Enhancements are available for several economic development tax credit programs including the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit (for creating at least 50 qualified positions), More Jobs for Marylanders, Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Focus Area Income Tax Credit, Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit, and Maryland Innovation Investment Tax Credit. Businesses can apply for Level 1 or Level 2 enhancements, with Level 2 offering the highest credit amounts. To receive these benefits, a business must first qualify for one of the underlying state economic development tax credit programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides enhanced tax credits for businesses in Opportunity Zon es. Businesses receive larger tax credits than what is normally available through other state programs through Level 1 or Level 2 enhancements, with Level 2 offering the highest credit amounts. The specific credit amount depends on the base program, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, or Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit. Enhancements are available for job creation, manufacturing, and innovation incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and investors operating within designated Maryland Opportunity Zone s.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job creation, expansion, and qualifying business investments. This program enhances the value of other state tax credits by providing a larger reduction in state tax liability.

For most credits, the business must be a Qualified Opportunity Zone Business that has received an investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
For investment-based credits like the BIITC or IITC, the investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
To qualify for Level 2 enhancements, the business must meet additional community engagement requirements, such as having local residents on its board or a community benefits agreement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MSBDFA promotes the viability and expansion of small businesses in Maryland through affordable, flexible financing products, with emphasis on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs, minorities, women, veterans, and those with credit challenges, collateral gaps, and limited financial resources. The program expands business ownership by providing multiple financing products including lines of credit, term loans, surety bonding, contract financing, and equity investments ranging from $25,000 to $2,000,000. Funded with $5 million in state allocation and $45 million in federal SSBCI funding over 7 years to expand small and minority business low-interest loan opportunities, the program supports small businesses that do not meet established credit criteria of financial institutions and those unable to obtain adequate financing through normal lending channels. Products include Contract Financing Program, Equity Participation Program (EPIP), Long Term Guaranty Program, State Small Business Credit Initiative, and Surety Bonding Program. Equity investments may take the form of purchase of qualified securities, convertible debt, interest in a limited partnership or limited liability company, simple agreements for future equity (SAFE), preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, or other debt and equity investments. Term loans have fixed rates ranging from 5% to 8%, lines of credit from 4% to 8%, and professional/technical assistance loans at 2%. SSBCI-eligible loans can have rates as low as 2%. Application fee is $250 non-refundable for debt and equity. Commitment fee is $500. Surety bonding premiums are 2% to 3%. Loan guaranty annual fees range from 0.5% to 1.5%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSBDFA offers multiple programs including Contract Financing Program, Equity Participation Program, Long Term Guaranty Program, State Small Business Credit Initiative, and Surety Bonding Program. Contract Financing provides direct loans up to $2,000,000 at prime to prime+2% for government contract work. Flexible term loans from $25,000 up to $2,000,000 with 3 to 10 year terms at WSJ prime +/- 3%; loan guarantees up to 80% of principal and interest with interest rate subsidies up to 4 percentage points; contract financing lines of credit up to $2,000,000 at prime + 2%; subordinated term loans, lines of credit, demand loans, and letters of credit with interest rates as low as 2%; equity investments from $25,000 up to $1,000,000 with 3 to 7 year terms at 7-12% interest or 15-22% equity returns in the form of preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, purchase of qualified securities, convertible debt, interest in a limited partnership or limited liability company, simple agreements for future equity (SAFE), or other debt and equity investments; surety bonding services including bid, performance, or payment bonds up to $2.5 million issued directly or guaranties up to 90% of losses not exceeding $1.35 million, with premiums of 2-3% of required bond amount. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required with lender maintaining 20% at risk. All loans and equity investments must be recaptured by the end of the seventh year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Maryland, particularly those in socially and economically disadvantaged areas, unable to obtain adequate financing through normal lending channels, with emphasis on economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs, minority-owned businesses, women, veterans, and those with credit challenges, collateral gaps, and limited financial resources seeking loans or equity investments for expansion and growth, as well as those interested in franchise purchases, business acquisitions, and technology-based businesses.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland. Company must have its principal place of business in Maryland. Available statewide. Primary focus areas include Prince George's County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Charles County, Harford County, Frederick County, and Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Commerce program supporting winery and vineyard operators through grants for establishment of new operations or capital improvements, and income tax credits for qualified capital expenses. The program provides financial assistance to individuals and for-profit entities to establish a new winery or vineyard in Maryland or complete capital improvements at an existing operation. Grants and income tax credits equal 25% of qualified capital expenses, with a maximum of $500,000 per tax year in total tax credits; if applications exceed this amount, credits are prorated. Qualified expenses include purchasing and installing equipment or agricultural materials for wine production or grape growing.

Maximum total tax credits of $500,000 per tax year; if applications exceed this amount, credits are prorated. Qualified capital expenses include equipment, agricultural materials, barrels, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants for wine production or grape growing.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of new wineries or vineyards; capital improvements and expansion at existing operations; qualified capital expenses including equipment, agricultural materials, barrels, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants for wine production or grape growing. Capital expenses must be qualified expenses for business operations

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program that promotes economic development and environmental improvement by identifying and redeploying underutilized brownfield properties that may be complicated by the presence or potential presence of hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants. The program provides financial incentives including real property tax credits, grants, and loans to help organize and assess brownfield properties, perform environmental evaluations, and conduct remedial action cleanups. Property owners receive significant real property tax credits for cleaning up and redeveloping brownfield sites. After completion of voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan, a site may qualify for a real property tax credit of 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value. Properties in enterprise zones may receive the tax credit for up to 10 years instead of 5 years, with potential additional credits up to 20%. The program provides three types of financial incentives: 1) low interest loans or grants for Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments; 2) property tax credits in jurisdictions with enabling legislation for the difference in assessed property value before and after cleanup and/or redevelopment; and 3) low interest loans or grants for site remediation. Incentives are designed to stimulate redevelopment in areas where cleanup will have environmental, economic development, and urban revitalization benefits. The program operates through participating counties and municipalities, encouraging environmental improvement and revitalization especially in distressed urban areas.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial incentives are provided through grants, loans, and real property tax credits. Property owners receive a real property tax credit of 50% to 70% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessed value for five taxable years after site cleanup or corrective action plan. In participating jurisdictions, the state provides a 50% credit and the jurisdiction may optionally provide an additional credit not to exceed 20% of the remaining property tax. For properties located in designated enterprise zones, the tax credit period may be extended up to 10 years. An additional 20% property tax credit is available for properties in an enterprise zone or commercial revitalization area. An additional 20% credit is available when voluntary cleanup or corrective action costs exceed $1,000,000. Grants and loans support organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups, Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, and site remediation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and operators with brownfield sites in participating jurisdictions who have obtained inculpable person status and completed or are completing remediation through the Maryland Department of Environment's Voluntary Cleanup Program. Properties must be industrial or commercial sites located in densely populated urban centers or areas where cleanup will have environmental, economic development, and urban revitalization benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits applied to the increase in assessed value of brownfield sites after cleanup or corrective action, grants and loans for Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, and conducting remedial action cleanups, supporting economic development and environmental remediation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Site must be located in a participating jurisdiction. Participating counties are Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester. Participating municipalities include Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown. Properties must be located in densely populated urban centers and generally underutilized. Participating jurisdiction must have enacted BRIP legislation and the property must be completed or enrolled in Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP). Properties must meet program requirements for location and cleanup documentation.

Upon qualification, the Department of Commerce issues a letter that can be taken to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit. For tax credits, contact the Department of Commerce BRIP website. For grants and loans, contact the Department of Commerce through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF), or contact the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development at 410-767-6390 for information on application process and availability of funds. Local jurisdictions including Cecil County provide additional enrollment procedures through their Finance Office.

For businesses with owners called to active duty, funds can cover general business expenses caused by deployment. For businesses involving service-disabled veterans, funds can help make a home, vehicle, or workplace accessible.

Available for businesses owned by military veterans, Reservists, National Guard personnel, or small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that employ such persons.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs for Marylanders Incentive Program

The program stopped accepting new applicants on June 1, 2024. Only companies that enrolled before that date can participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive a refundable state income tax credit equal to 4.75% of the wages for each new qualified job created. The benefit is available for 10 years for projects in Tier 1 areas and 5 years for projects in Tier 2 areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program sunsetted June 1, 2024. Not accepting new applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for manufacturing businesses and non-manufacturing businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. New applications are no longer accepted.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a refundable tax credit based on wages paid for newly created jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program prioritizes projects in Tier 1 Areas. These include specific counties and any Opportunity Zone in Maryland. All other areas are Tier 2.
requirements_list: Must have enrolled in the program before June 1, 2024.
Eligible manufacturers must be in NAICS sectors 31, 32, or 33.
