A qualified non-manufacturing job must pay at least $50,000 per year.
Qualified jobs must be full-time and filled for at least 12 months.
Businesses that moved from one Maryland county to another after June 1, 2017, are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This program is closed to new applicants. Companies that are already enrolled must submit an Initial and Final Tax Credit Application each year during their benefit period to receive the tax credit.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive Maryland state income tax credit program for businesses that make significant capital investments and create qualified jobs. The credit amount depends on the level of eligible project costs and the number of new jobs created within a 24-month period. The program is available to for-profit and non-profit businesses statewide, with enhanced benefits for projects located in Priority Funding Areas in designated Tier 1 counties. Businesses creating 10-24 qualified positions qualify for a maximum $1 million credit; 25-49 positions qualify for $2.5 million; 50+ positions qualify for $5 million. The credit is based on costs related to acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, and equipping an economic development project, including moving costs from outside Maryland.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An income tax credit of up to $5 million based on job creation and eligible project costs. Businesses creating 10-24 qualified positions qualify for a maximum $1 million credit; 25-49 positions qualify for $2.5 million; 50+ positions qualify for $5 million. The credit is based on costs related to acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, and equipping an economic development project, including moving costs from outside Maryland. Eligible costs include land acquisition, performance and contract bonds, insurance, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, utility installation, interest costs prior to and during acquisition and construction and for two years after completion, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunication equipment, office furniture and equipment, and costs to move a business from outside Maryland and furnish and equip the new location. Minimum $500,000 in eligible costs required. The credit may be carried forward for up to 14 years. Beginning the fourth year after the credit year, businesses may apply the credit against state income tax liability and request a refund limited to payroll withholding attributable to qualified positions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses throughout Maryland that invest in economic development projects and create new, full-time jobs. Enhanced incentives available for projects in Priority Funding Areas in Tier 1 counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs related to acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, and equipping an economic development project. Eligible costs include land acquisition, performance and contract bonds, insurance, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, utility installation, interest costs prior to and during acquisition and construction and for two years after completion, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunication equipment, office furniture and equipment, and costs to move a business from outside Maryland and furnish and equip the new location. Minimum $500,000 in eligible costs required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) in a Tier 1 County to receive enhanced benefits. As of December 2025, Tier 1 counties are Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester (Worcester remains eligible through September 2026 under the 24-month look back provision). PFAs include state enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, Department of Housing and Community Development Sustainable Communities, incorporated municipalities, areas between the I-495 beltway and Washington D.C. and the I-695 beltway and Baltimore City, and growth areas designated by each county. The program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must declare intent to Maryland Commerce in writing before incurring eligible costs or creating new qualified jobs
Business must be certified as a qualified business entity eligible for the One Maryland Tax Credit
Business must create at least 10 new, full-time qualified positions at the project within 24 months
Positions must be full-time, pay 120% of State Minimum Wage (as of January 1, 2024, this equals $18.00/hour), be filled for 12 months, and be a net new job to Maryland
Business must incur at least $500,000 of eligible project costs
Project must be primarily engaged in an eligible activity
Full-time position requires at least 840 hours of employee time during at least 24 weeks in a 6-month period (average 35 hours per week)
Jobs must be net new to the state and not created through change in ownership, consolidation, merger, restructuring, or contractual shift from existing Maryland business
Business has 12 months from intent date to start the project and 3 years to complete it
Business may not claim both One Maryland Tax Credit and Job Creation Tax Credit in the same tax year
Minimum $1 million, $2.5 million, or $5 million in eligible project costs depending on tier
Must make capital investment in the project
Must create new qualified jobs within 24-month period
Commitment to job creation
Capital expenditures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Notice of Intent to Maryland Commerce declaring intent to seek certification. Register for an account in Commerce's online system and submit a Preliminary Application with employment affidavit projecting job and wage data. Commerce issues a Preliminary Certificate of Eligibility if the business is projected to qualify. Once the project is started, the business has 3 years to complete it. After incurring eligible project costs, creating at least 10 qualified jobs, and maintaining those jobs for 12 months, the business applies for final certification by submitting a Final Application listing qualified positions, employees, eligible costs, and supporting documentation. Commerce will issue a Final Certificate with the credit amount, which the business attaches to its tax return. Full details and application materials are available on the Maryland Department of Commerce website (ChooseMaryland.org). Caroline County Economic Development office is available to assist with applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide workforce training grant program that provides matching grants to help businesses offset the costs of eligible on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, purchase of training software, and train-the-trainer scenarios to benefit new and incumbent workers. The program supports employee training and development for businesses expanding in Maryland and creating new jobs, with matching grants reimbursing up to 50% of qualified training project costs, minimum grant award of $10,000, and maximum of $200,000 per year. Training focuses on new technologies and production processes to improve employee productivity, workforce quality, and job stability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants that reimburse up to 50% of qualified training project costs. Minimum grant award is $10,000 (requiring total project cost of at least $20,000). Maximum grant award is $200,000 per year. Grants help offset costs of on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, training software purchases, train-the-trainer programs, curriculum development, course materials, and instructor salaries and expenses for employee development and job creation initiatives. Employers pay for training first, then submit certificates and documentation for review and reimbursement upon successful completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, particularly small and mid-sized manufacturing and technology companies, expanding operations, adding jobs, and training new and incumbent workers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, training software purchases, train-the-trainer programs, curriculum development, course books and materials, instructor salaries and expenses for employee development, workforce quality improvement, and job creation initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland employer.
Must have a minimum of ten full-time employees.
Must not be in arrears with any State taxing agency.
Must not be in default with any Commerce program.
The total training project cost must be at least $20,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers apply for the grant through the Maryland Department of Commerce by contacting the regional representative for their county or region. After application approval and agreement finalization, the employer pays for training. Upon successful completion, the employer submits certificates and purchase order or invoice documentation for review and reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides Maryland businesses with state income tax credits for investing in qualified research and development activities conducted in Maryland. The credit equals ten percent of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year that exceed the Maryland Base Amount. The total statutory cap is $12 million with a small business set-aside of $3.5 million, and no single applicant may receive a credit exceeding $250,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit is equal to ten percent (10%) of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year in excess of the Maryland Base Amount. The total statutory cap is $12 million with a small business set-aside of $3.5 million. A single applicant may not receive a tax credit exceeding $250,000. For small businesses, credits certified after December 15, 2012 are refundable to the extent that the tax credits exceed the income tax liability for that taxable year. Credits can be carried forward for 7 years if tax liability is insufficient to use all credits in the current year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: NO LATER THAN NOVEMBER 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which the Maryland Qualified Research and Development expenses were incurred
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses (corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, sole proprietorships) and individuals that incur qualified research and development expenses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified Research and Development Expenses as defined by Section 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code incurred in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Qualified research and development must be conducted in Maryland. Businesses must incur qualified R&D expenses in Maryland to qualify.
requirements_list: Business must incur Qualified Research and Development Expenses as defined by § 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code in Maryland
Business must submit an application to Commerce by November 15th for expenses incurred in the previous calendar year
For small business designation: net book value assets (at beginning or end of taxable year, as reported on balance sheet) must total less than $5,000,000
Small businesses must submit documentation showing net book value assets of less than $5 million
If first year incurring R&D expenses, Maryland Base Amount equals zero
For partial or short year taxpayers, Maryland Adjusted Base Amount applies
Credits can be carried forward for 7 years if tax liability is insufficient to use all credits in the current year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce no later than November 15th of the calendar year following the tax year in which the Maryland Qualified Research and Development expenses were incurred. Small businesses must also submit documentation showing they had net book value assets of less than $5 million. Commerce will issue a tax credit certificate with the approved credit amount by February 15th of the calendar year following the end of the year in which a business submits an application. After receiving certification, the business may file an amended tax return for the year it is certified or claim the credit on an income tax return filed for any of the following 7 tax years. The business must attach a copy of the Department's certification to its tax return.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account - Video Lottery Terminal Fund (VLT) / VLT Small Business Flex Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide loan program that uses 1.5% of proceeds from video lottery terminals at Maryland's six casinos to provide investment capital and flexible financing to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. Administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce through multiple fund managers, including FSC First (the intermediary lender) and the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC), with local administration also available through county economic development offices such as Cecil County. At least 50% of allocations are directed to businesses in targeted areas surrounding six Maryland casinos (Maryland Live in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County), with the remaining 50% available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. The program provides loans ranging from $500 to $250,000 with terms up to 10 years, flexible repayment options, interest rates of 5-12%, and rapid underwriting and approval turnaround (two weeks). Funds support business acquisition, equipment, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, working capital, marketing, personnel, inventory expansion, and professional consulting assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $500 to $250,000 with terms up to 10 years and interest rates of 5-12% determined at underwriting. At least 50% of allocations are deployed to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in targeted areas surrounding six Maryland casinos (Maryland Live in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County). The remaining 50% is available statewide to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. Funds can be used for business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, leasehold improvements, equipment purchase, start-up costs, working capital, professional services, refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances, business development, facility improvements, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, marketing, personnel hiring, inventory expansion, employee retention, and operations. Flexible repayment options and rapid underwriting with two-week approval turnaround available. Collateral includes business and personal assets; personal guaranties required. Technical assistance and business counseling provided before and after loan closing.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Stew Smith, Stephen Primosch, Tim Smoot, Maurice Ames, Stanley Jacobs, Jeffrey P. Pillas, Darshni Patel, Chris Funk, Laurie M. Boyer Babb, Victoria Zelefsky
structured_extraction.contact_email: jsmith@fscfirst.com, sprimosch@aaedc.org, tim.smoot@mmgcapitalgroup.com, mames@marylandcapital.org, sjacobs@baltimorecountymd.gov, jpillas@baltimoredevelopment.com, dhpatel@hceda.org, cfunk@tccwmd.org, laurie@thinkmoco.com, vzelefskyassociates@comcast.net
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses classified as small by the Small Business Administration, including minority-owned, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses located in targeted areas surrounding Maryland casinos and throughout Maryland seeking flexible financing for growth, operations, acquisition, and employee retention.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, leasehold improvements, equipment purchase, start-up costs, working capital, professional services, refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances, business development, facility improvements, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, marketing, personnel hiring, inventory expansion, employee retention, and general business growth and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: At least 50% of funds are deployed to eligible businesses within target areas surrounding six Maryland casinos (Maryland Live in Anne Arundel County, Hollywood Casino Perryville in Cecil County, Rocky Gap in Allegany County, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City, and National Harbor in Prince George's County). The remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business classified as small by the Small Business Administration
Must be minority-owned, women-owned, or veteran-owned (or other eligible small business)
Located in targeted areas surrounding Maryland casinos (for 50% of funds) or anywhere in Maryland (for remaining 50%)
Business and personal assets available as collateral
Personal guaranty required
For-profit entities legally organized
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the fund manager serving your area or submit an application through the FSC First online application portal. Multiple fund managers administer the program through various lending entities and loan funds, with local administration also available through county economic development offices. Fund managers offer two-week underwriting and approval turnaround for eligible applicants. Financial business counseling provided before and after loan closing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Soft Landing Exchange for Maryland Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps Maryland companies test expansion into new international markets affordably. It provides access to facilities, resources, and networking through a global network of partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible companies can receive a grant of up to $10,000. This money helps pay for program costs and travel expenses like flights, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies that want to expand into new international markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can cover participation costs charged by the partner program, as well as travel, lodging, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to companies located anywhere in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, click the 'Apply Now' button on the program webpage to access the online grant application.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a refundable tax credit to theatrical production companies. The credit equals 25% of the production costs spent in Maryland. The credit is refundable, meaning the company can receive a payment even if it owes no state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a refundable tax credit of 25% for qualified production costs spent in Maryland. The maximum credit is $2 million for a single production.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted before beginning any work on the theatrical production in the State.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit theatrical production companies creating National Touring or Pre-Broadway productions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can cover direct production costs in Maryland. This includes set construction, special effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, and staging. It also covers salaries for work in Maryland, advertising, facility and equipment rentals, vehicle leases, food, lodging, and travel to Maryland for employees.
requirements_list: Estimated total direct production costs in Maryland must exceed $100,000.
The production must be a for-profit National Touring or Pre-Broadway live stage theatrical production.
National Touring Productions must have at least two public performances in Maryland and then perform for four or more weeks in at least four cities outside the state.
Pre-Broadway Productions must have at least eight public performances in Maryland and be prepared for a Broadway presentation within twelve months of its final Maryland performance.
The applicant must demonstrate it has financing for the project.
Productions with total direct costs over $250,000 must provide an independent, third-party auditor's report.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Application for Qualification by email before starting any work in Maryland. The Department will review it and send a Letter of Qualification within 30 days if approved. Second, submit an Application Addendum before the first rehearsal. Third, after the production finishes, apply for the final Tax Credit Certificate within 180 days. You must include final documents and an auditor's report if your costs were over $250,000. Finally, file your state income tax return with the certificate to claim the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Access Maryland provides funding to state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks to make continued accessibility upgrades consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessible Design Standards of 2010. The program ensures that individuals with a range of physical disabilities can fully interact and engage with buildings, parks, universities, and other state-owned facilities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program receives requests from state agencies, prioritizes the requests, recommends projects for funding, and provides oversight through the design and construction phases. Funding is provided for accessibility upgrades at state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks seeking to make accessibility improvements to their facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility upgrades consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessible Design Standards of 2010 to remove physical barriers and improve access to programs, services, and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks across Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be at state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, or state-owned parks
Upgrades must be consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessible Design Standards of 2010
State agencies and universities must maintain ADA Transition Plans that outline the removal of physical barriers and include a budget and schedule for improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: State agencies submit requests to the Maryland Department of Disabilities. The Department reviews and prioritizes requests, recommends projects for funding, and provides oversight through the design and construction phases.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assistive Technology Reuse and Recycling Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Gently used assistive technology is collected via donation, sanitized, refurbished, and made available for free or at low cost to individuals who cannot otherwise afford to purchase assistive technology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost refurbished and repaired assistive technology devices are provided to individuals and organizations that cannot otherwise afford new equipment. In 2021, 236 devices were refurbished and 358 low-cost or free devices were provided, resulting in $556,441 in total savings to consumers.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Denise Schuler, AT Specialist; James Whitney, AT Clinician
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities, older Marylanders, organizations, and agencies unable to otherwise afford new assistive technology
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology devices for living, working, learning, and community participation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through MDTAP and reuse partners including Lollipop Kids Foundation, Equipment Connections for Children, and Loan Closet of Howard County
requirements_list: Must demonstrate financial need or inability to purchase new assistive technology
Must have a disability or be an older Marylander
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDTAP or one of the reuse partners to inquire about available refurbished equipment. Partner organizations assess needs and make devices available at no or low cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides information and resources for home accessibility modifications in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Directory and resources for home accessibility modifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home modifications for accessibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only.

structured_extraction.program_name: Centers for Independent Living Technical Assistance (CIL-TA) Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance project that partners with Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living to enhance operational infrastructure and program sustainability. The project is overseen by the Maryland Department of Disabilities in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Aging and works to enhance Aging and Disability Resource Centers (ADRCs) which serve as one-stop shops for older adults and people with disabilities to find information on and access long-term services and supports.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and training provided by the Maryland Center for Developmental Disabilities at Kennedy Krieger Institute to enhance operational infrastructure and program sustainability of Centers for Independent Living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living and Aging and Disability Resource Centers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and training to enhance operational infrastructure and program sustainability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide

structured_extraction.program_description: A service for Marylanders living with combined hearing and vision loss (DeafBlind) that provides equal access to communication through the facilitation of all types of communication including American Sign Language, close-vision, and tactile sign language. A skilled signer copies sign language from video callers and provides visual information to the DeafBlind individual through close-vision, tactile sign language, tracking, or other communication methods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides facilitators who can accommodate various communication preferences including spoken English, sign language (Close-Visual, Tactile, ProTactile), and tracking; services can be provided at residences, libraries, coffee shops, or other locations. Communication Facilitator service provides skilled interpreters who facilitate communication during video calls between DeafBlind consumers and video callers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DeafBlind consumers (must first complete and be approved through DeafBlind Consumer Application)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Communication facilitation services to enable DeafBlind individuals to communicate with friends, family, coworkers, and others through video calls.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Marylanders statewide
requirements_list: Must complete DeafBlind Consumer Application first
Must be approved for the program
Must complete the Communication Facilitator Service Request Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete DeafBlind Consumer Application (available at MDRelay.org); upon approval, complete and email the CF Service Request Form to CF.Scheduler@Maryland.gov

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities who do not qualify for other Department programs offering access to adapted vehicles. The program prioritizes individuals in areas with limited access to public transportation. CAP operates as a pilot initiative from October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2030.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provision of adapted vehicles to eligible individuals through donations and federal grants. Services include vehicle modifications and adaptations. No financial outlay from recipients; vehicles and services are provided through the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who need adapted vehicles and do not qualify for other Department adapted vehicle programs. Prioritized: residents in areas with limited access to public transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adapted vehicle acquisition and provision. Vehicle modification and adaptation services for personal use as the primary driver.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland, with prioritization for areas with limited access to public transportation.
requirements_list: Be an individual with a disability who uses a mobility aid
Be the vehicle's primary driver
Possess a valid driver's license with appropriate adaptation restrictions, OR possess a current (within last 12 months) prescription for vehicle modifications

Have been turned down for a financial loan through the AT Financial Loan Program within the Maryland Department of Disabilities, OR voluntarily self-disqualify by not applying to the AT Financial Loan Program
Must not qualify for other Department adapted vehicle programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should email mdtap.general@maryland.gov for further information on the qualification process and to join the driver-eligibility list. Individuals may also donate working adapted vehicles through the same contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Choice Homes provides affordable rental homes in Montgomery County for people with disabilities who have extremely low income. The program is a partnership between the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County and the Maryland Department of Disabilities, offering 30 affordable rental units for a 15-year period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay 30% of their monthly household adjusted income for rent and utilities. The program provides project-based affordable housing with rents tied to the Community Choice Homes units for 15 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who have extremely low income and household income at or below 30% of area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing and utilities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must live or work in Montgomery County at time of referral, or have lived or worked in Montgomery County within 5 years of referral and currently live in an institution or group living setting.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 30% of area median income with priority for 10-30% AMI
Income must include cash payment from SSI or SSDI at initial eligibility determination
Age 18 to 62 at time of leasing
Current registration on HOC Housing Path Waitlist
Lives or works in Montgomery County at time of referral or within 5 years and currently in institution or group living
Criminal background cannot include lifetime sex offense registry requirement or methamphetamine production conviction on federally assisted housing
Must be on Weinberg Apartment waitlist and indicate interest in Montgomery County
Must comply with program requirements including maintaining eligibility, applying for rent subsidies, completing tenant training, making timely rent payments, and adhering to lease terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Persons with disabilities must contact their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete pre-screening and application. Case managers register applicants on the Weinberg Apartment waitlist through www.Socialserve.com. Participants must enroll on the HOC Housing Path waitlist. HOC verifies eligibility including income and criminal background.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual and small group training sessions held in the participant's home or at an accessible community location. structured_extraction.program_audience: Community First Choice participants interested in self-directing their personal assistance services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and information on self-directing personal assistance services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Participant in Community First Choice program
Referred to the program through Supports Planner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are referred to the CFC SD Training Program through their Supports Planner.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides individual and family supports to 400 people with developmental disabilities on the DDA waiting list, with an overall budget cap of $25,000 per year per recipient.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps financial institutions in 12 states, including Maryland, provide affordable housing and to help first-time homebuyers with down payments and closing costs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payments and closing costs for home purchase

structured_extraction.program_name: Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation's Affordable Rental Housing Opportunities Initiative for Persons with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and the State of Maryland to provide affordable rental housing options for persons with disabilities. The program provides rental assistance and capital grants as incentives for owners of eligible rental housing developments with non-profit involvement to designate units for occupancy at affordable rents specifically for very low-income persons with disabilities. Weinberg-funded units house non-elderly, disabled persons at 10-30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI), with tenants paying 30 percent of their income for rent and utilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free assistive telecommunications equipment to qualified Maryland residents age three and older who have difficulty using a standard telephone. The program serves individuals who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties. Equipment options include text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTYs for people who are deaf/blind, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, Speech-to-Speech (STS) phones, video phones, captioned telephones, phones with large buttons for low vision, picture phones for memory loss, hands-free phones for mobility issues, amplified phones, tablets, and wheelchair pad phone switches. All applicants receive a free one-on-one evaluation to determine the right equipment solution. Equipment is selected during evaluation to meet individual needs and is mailed to the applicant via UPS 4-6 weeks after the evaluation is completed. Initial training is provided during evaluation, and additional free training sessions can be arranged. Equipment must be returned if applicant moves out of state; applicant may keep equipment if traveling or establishing temporary residence elsewhere while maintaining Maryland residency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free assistive telecommunications equipment provided at no cost to qualified applicants on long-term loan. Equipment options include text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTYs, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, Speech-to-Speech (STS) phones, video phones, phones with large buttons, picture phones, hands-free phones, captioned telephones, amplified phones, tablets, and wheelchair pad phone switches. Equipment is selected during a free one-on-one evaluation to meet individual needs and is shipped via UPS to the applicant's home. Initial training is provided during evaluation, and additional free training sessions are available. Equipment must be returned if applicant moves out of state. Equipment repair and maintenance for normal wear and tear is covered at MAT discretion.

Must be age three or older

Must be on a fixed income or recipient of Social Security (SSA) benefits, Veterans (VA) benefits, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or pharmacy, medical or housing assistance
Must have home phone service, high speed/WiFi, or be applying for phone service and/or high speed/WiFi
Applicants under age 18 must have application signed by parent or legal guardian
Must provide proof of eligibility documentation

Must provide copy of telephone or utility bill

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review qualification criteria to determine eligibility. 2. Complete the application online at mat-apply.org or download and complete the paper application. 3. Have the application's Disability Certification Form (Part 4) certified by a licensed physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, or rehabilitation counselor. 4. Enclose proper documentation such as Social Security Administration Award Letter or other proof of eligibility, copy of photo ID, and copy of telephone or utility bill. 5. Digitally sign the application through the online portal (no mailing required for online applicants) or mail completed forms to the MAT Program address at State of Maryland – MAT Program, 301 W. Preston St., Suite 1008A, Baltimore, MD 21201. Once received, the application will be reviewed for approval and you will receive an acceptance letter approximately two weeks after application is received. If approved, you will receive information on scheduling your free evaluation with a MAT specialist. After evaluation, equipment is ordered and shipped to home via UPS 4-6 weeks after evaluation is completed. Initial training is provided during evaluation; additional free training sessions are available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) Low-Interest Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Disabilities Assistive Technology Program (MDTAP) offers low-interest loans to help Maryland residents with disabilities, older Marylanders, and their families purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, accessibility modifications to homes and vehicles, and adapted and non-adapted vehicles to support independence, work, learning, and employment goals. Loans are available with extended repayment terms and lenient lending parameters, ranging from $500 to $70,000 depending on equipment type and qualifications. All loans have below-market interest rates that remain fixed for the term of the loan.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with extended repayment terms and lenient lending parameters. Loan amounts range from $500 to $70,000 depending on equipment type: unsecured assistive technology loans up to $10,000, unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000, non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000, and adapted vehicles up to $70,000. All loans have below-market interest rates that remain fixed for the term of the loan. Interest rates vary based on creditworthiness and are disclosed at the time of application processing and approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: Community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support for eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder ages 0 to 21 to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services include adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation and training, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, therapeutic integration, and service coordination. Participants receive full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, and other services. The program is administered at the state level by the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland State Department of Education with local service coordination through county education agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Services include: Adult Life Planning (family-centered support for accessing adult community services), Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical home adaptations), Family Consultation and Training (consultation and training for families), Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance in the home and community), Residential Habilitation (community-based residential placement), Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance), Therapeutic Integration (structured after-school and weekend programs), and Service Coordination through local education agencies. Participants qualify for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, and other services. Financial eligibility requires monthly income not exceeding 300% of SSI benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000 or $2,500 depending on eligibility category.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 day deadline to accept invitation, establish contact, complete technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application; 30 day deadline to provide updated/additional information if registry eligibility not met initially; 15 day deadline to submit information if financial application and checklist not submitted within 30 days

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services and support including adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation and training, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, therapeutic integration, service coordination, and full Medical Assistance benefits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available throughout Maryland including all counties. Applicants must reside in Maryland. Local service coordination through county education agencies.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Ages 0 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Reside in Maryland

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 0-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 hours or more of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through exit from high school
Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of SSI benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000 or $2,500 depending on eligibility category
Be eligible for Maryland Home and Community Based Services Waiver for Children
Contact the Autism Waiver Registry at 866-417-3480 to be eligible to apply when a vacancy occurs
Technical eligibility assessment required
Medical eligibility assessment required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families must contact the Autism Waiver Registry at 1-866-417-3480 to be placed on a list of individuals interested in Autism Waiver services. Initial screening is conducted by MDH provider during admission call based on parent report. When a vacancy occurs, eligible families receive a letter confirming addition to waitlist and are asked to apply for the program. The application process involves: contacting local education agency (LEA) Autism Waiver contact, completing technical eligibility checklist within 45 days, submitting financial application within 45 days, and providing documentation of diagnosis, educational classification, special education service receipt, ICF-IID level of care determination, and financial eligibility. A 30-day extension is available if registry eligibility is not met initially. LEA or MSDE tracks application progress.

structured_extraction.program_name: Addressing Disparities in Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and Obesity in Maryland Communities
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds organizations to provide community-based interventions addressing social determinants of health in order to reduce health inequity among Maryland's racial and ethnic minorities. The program focuses on upstream factors outside healthcare delivery that are necessary to reduce health disparities and maintain healthy communities. Grant activities support interventions addressing safe housing, transportation, neighborhoods, racism, discrimination, violence, education, job opportunities, income, access to nutritious food, physical activity opportunities, and health language and literacy skills. Grantee activities are monitored through narrative reports and performance measures throughout the funding period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to eligible organizations to develop and implement community-based interventions addressing social determinants of health including safe housing, transportation, neighborhoods, racism, discrimination, violence, education, job opportunities, income, access to nutritious food, physical activity opportunities, and health language and literacy skills. structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland program based in local health departments that provides comprehensive evaluation and personalized care planning to help frail, aged, and disabled adults and children remain living safely in the community. structured_extraction.assistance_description: A licensed Registered Nurse conducts a comprehensive on-site evaluation in the client's home to assess needs and develop a personalized care plan. The program identifies and connects clients with available community services including Community First Choice (which provides assistance with activities of daily living) and Community Personal Assistance Services (which provides similar support services).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are at risk of being placed in a care facility, have chronic medical conditions, or need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, meal preparation, or mobility. Individuals must meet specific medical and financial criteria, such as Medicaid eligibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program creates personalized care plans and connects clients to community resources. Clients may qualify for specific support programs such as Community First Choice or Community Personal Assistance Services to help with activities of daily living including bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, light chores, and accessing the community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Queen Anne's County. The referral form on this page is exclusively for Queen Anne's County residents. For services in a different county, applicants should contact their local Health Department.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at risk of being placed in a care facility or face a change in normal living situation, OR have chronic medical conditions, OR need help with activities of daily living
Must meet specific medical and financial criteria for specific programs accessed through AERS, such as Medicaid eligibility for Community First Choice or Community Personal Assistance Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an AERS Referral Form for Queen Anne's County residents. To apply by phone, contact Maryland Access Point (MAP) at 844-627-5465. Alternatively, reach the local Queen Anne's County MAP Coordinator directly at 410-758-0848. A licensed Registered Nurse will conduct an on-site evaluation and develop a personalized care plan.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assistance in Community Integration Services (ACIS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The ACIS Program is a Medicaid program that delivers housing and tenancy-based case management services and supports to eligible individuals who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless, or at risk of institutional placement. The program helps participants live safely and independently in their home and community through community integration assessments, person-centered planning, connection to social services, landlord coordination, and training and resource support. Services include stable housing and support services but do not cover room and board or rental costs. The state awards 1,520 spaces to providers for delivering these services. Providers must deliver a minimum of three services per month for each member to receive monthly reimbursement through Maryland Medicaid. This is a 2026 provider solicitation awarding spaces to new and existing providers and lead entities. The program is authorized under Maryland's Section 1115 HealthChoice Demonstration and tests innovative programs resulting in healthier outcomes for Medicaid participants. Statewide expansion was approved January 12, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing and tenancy-based case management services including community integration assessments, person-centered community integration plans, help connecting with social services, coordination with landlords for accommodations, training and resource support, and Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) development and assessment to help manage housing. Provides stable housing and support services for eligible Medicaid enrollees. Services assist participants with finding and securing appropriate housing and support participants in tenant obligations. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs. The state awards 1,520 spaces to providers for delivering these services. Providers must deliver a minimum of three qualified services per month for each member to receive monthly reimbursement through Maryland Medicaid. Reimbursement is $725 per member per month for delivering minimum three qualified services and $100 per member per year for compliance activities and Housing Support Care Plan completion. Funding is 50% State General Funds and 50% Federal Funds. Claims must be submitted within 12 months of service delivery date. Providers can bill once per calendar month per participant. HSCP must be approved for compliance reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Online Provider Solicitation available starting January 1, 2026. Letter of Intent due March 13, 2026 at 5 p.m.; Full Application/Request for Responses due March 27, 2026 at 5 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: ACIS providers including local health departments, county government agencies, and other local governmental agencies; Medicaid enrollees in Maryland aged 18 and older (with exceptions for minors as head of household with qualifying disability) who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, at risk of institutional placement, fully enrolled in Maryland Medicaid, and enrolled in HealthChoice MCO or Fee-For-Service Medicaid who meet health criteria involving chronic conditions or frequent emergency room or hospital use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and tenancy-based case management services, community integration services, Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) development and assessment, supportive housing planning, connection to social services, landlord coordination, training and resource support, compliance activities, and stable housing and support services. Does not cover room and board or rental costs. Reimbursement for service delivery and compliance activities. Funding cannot supplant or duplicate existing federal funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Statewide expansion was approved January 12, 2025 and is available to all jurisdictions who apply and receive Maryland Department of Health approval. Local health departments or other local government agencies may apply to become ACIS providers and deliver services within their jurisdiction. Current individual service areas include Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County. Statewide expansion authorized with 1,520 total participant spaces.
requirements_list: Must be a local governmental agency, including local health department, other local government agency, county government entity, or consortium of entities serving a county or multiple counties
Must be members of their local Continuum of Care (CoC) Program
Individual case managers are not eligible to enroll as ACIS providers
Must be enrolled as a Maryland Medicaid provider to deliver and bill for ACIS services
Must have valid Medicaid Provider Number
Must provide a minimum of three qualified services per month for each member to receive reimbursement each month
Medicaid participants must be experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness OR facing institutional placement
Medicaid participants must have Medicaid in Maryland
Medicaid participants must be 18 years or older (exceptions for minors as head of household with qualifying disability)
Medicaid participants must be fully enrolled in Maryland Medicaid and enrolled in HealthChoice MCO or Fee-For-Service Medicaid
Medicaid participants must have two or more chronic conditions OR use emergency room or be in hospital more than four times per year
Medicaid participants must choose to be in the ACIS program
Medicaid participants must live in a service area (or county applying to become provider)
Must submit a letter of intent (LOI) by March 13 at 5 p.m.
Must submit a Request for Responses/Application by March 27 at 5 p.m.
Monthly attestation that all employees and contractors have been searched against exclusion databases (OIG, SAM.gov)
Must enter into HIPAA-compliant data sharing agreements with MDH
Must submit timely quarterly and annual reports
Must respond to state inquiries within one business day; provide information within five business days
Must ensure no duplication or supplantation of federal funding
Must comply with applicable federal regulations (42 CFR 441.700-441.745)
Claims must be submitted within 12 months of service delivery date
Housing and Support Care Plan (HSCP) must be approved for compliance reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For providers: Online Provider Solicitation available starting January 1, 2026. Obtain the mandatory letter of intent (LOI) template and instructions by emailing mdh.medicaidacis@maryland.gov. Submit the LOI by March 13 at 5 p.m. Attend the optional applicant webinar scheduled for March 9. Submit the Request for Responses/Application form by March 27 at 5 p.m. Applications are reviewed from March 27 to April 24. Award notifications are sent May 1. Program onboarding begins May 18. Claim submission pathways include: EDI (via 837 batch files through MMEE portal), eMedicaid (web-based CMS 1500), or Paper Claims (CMS 1500 forms via mail/secure email). Electronic filing recommended for faster processing. For individuals interested in enrolling in ACIS services, contact your county health department or local government agency for information about enrollment and eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides assistive technology and services to Marylanders with developmental disabilities enrolled in DDA waiver services to support independence, activities of daily living, community participation, and quality of life. requirements_list: Must have a developmental disability
Must be enrolled in DDA waiver services
Must work with Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) to identify technology needs
Technology must be included in person-centered plan (PCP)
May require assistive technology assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) or the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration for information. Work with your CCS to include Assistive Technology and Services in your person-centered plan, documenting the technology in relevant Focus Area Exploration sections and the Technology section of your PCP.

structured_extraction.program_name: CRF Tobacco Use Prevention and Cessation Program - Local Public Health Component
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide tobacco prevention and cessation program funded by the Cigarette Restitution Fund that authorizes Local Health Departments to develop tobacco control initiatives in coordination with Community Health Coalitions. The program addresses four goal areas: preventing tobacco use initiation among young people, promoting quitting among adults and youth, eliminating exposure to secondhand smoke, and addressing disparities in tobacco use among different population groups. Funding supports community initiatives, school-based prevention programs, enforcement initiatives, and cessation initiatives including smoking cessation classes, counseling, and nicotine replacement therapy support. Program elements include training for community leaders and healthcare providers, public education campaigns, and coalition building.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local Health Departments receive funding to develop community initiatives, school-based programs, enforcement initiatives, and cessation initiatives including smoking cessation classes, counseling, and nicotine replacement support (patches, prescription medications). Funding also supports coalition building, training for community leaders and health providers, and public education campaigns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people, adults, pregnant women, healthcare providers, schools, community organizations, faith-based organizations, and populations experiencing tobacco use disparities. Community Health Coalitions include local management boards, public school systems, hospitals, clinics, law enforcement, businesses, religious organizations, media, and institutions of higher learning.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco prevention and cessation activities including community education, school-based prevention curricula, enforcement of tobacco sales regulations, smoking cessation counseling and classes, nicotine replacement therapy support, training for healthcare providers and community leaders, and administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available across all Maryland counties through Local Health Departments.
requirements_list: Local Health Officers must document Community Health Coalition demographics to ensure representation of county diversity

Community Health Coalitions should include local management boards, public school systems, hospitals, clinics, physicians, healthcare providers, law enforcement, businesses, religious organizations, media, and institutions of higher learning
Community-based groups representing minority, rural, and medically underserved populations must be included
Must include youth representatives familiar with all communities and cultures in the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Health Officers coordinate with Community Health Coalitions and the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to develop and implement tobacco prevention and cessation initiatives within their counties, following CDC Best Practices for Comprehensive Tobacco Control Programs and the Task Force Report to End Smoking in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Children's Medical Services Program helps low-income, uninsured, or underinsured children and youth ages 0-21 years in Maryland access specialty care services for chronic illnesses or disabilities. The program has modernized to offer a more secure and user-friendly experience with streamlined processes and expedited service delivery.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cigarette Restitution Fund Cancer Prevention, Education, Screening and Treatment Program (CRF-CPEST)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides and administers grants and funding to local health departments, academic centers, health systems, and hospitals to reduce cancer mortality and cancer disparities in Maryland through prevention, education, early detection, screening, diagnosis, and treatment services. It coordinates the state's use of the Cigarette Restitution Fund and the Maryland Cancer Fund (a tax checkoff program funded by public donations) to create lasting public health initiatives that reduce mortality and morbidity rates for cancer and tobacco-related diseases. The program provides no-cost screening, diagnosis, and treatment services to eligible low-income, uninsured, and underinsured Maryland residents. Grants are awarded to local programs for cancer prevention, early detection, diagnosis and treatment activities targeting seven priority cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), and oral cancers. Community Health Coalitions create and submit cancer control plans as part of the application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and funding are provided to local health departments, academic centers, health systems, and hospitals to support cancer prevention, education, screening, diagnosis, and treatment services targeting seven priority cancers: lung and bronchus, colorectal, breast, cervical, prostate, skin (melanoma), and oral cancers. The program is funded through the Cigarette Restitution Fund and the Maryland Cancer Fund (a tax checkoff program supported by public donations). Eligible low-income, uninsured, and underinsured Maryland residents receive no-cost screening, diagnosis, and treatment services through participating local programs.

It provides free smoking cessation counseling and nicotine replacement therapy (patches) to eligible residents, along with education on tobacco use prevention and cessation assistance to community groups, school groups, and businesses.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Medicaid program that provides essential home and community-based services to enable individuals of any age to live independently in their own homes and communities. The program consolidates personal care services across the Living at Home Waiver and Older Adults Waiver programs, making them available as a state plan benefit through a Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver (1915(c)). It serves eligible Medicaid individuals who would otherwise require institutional or nursing facility level of care. Services include personal assistance services for activities of daily living (such as bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, and light chores), skilled nursing services, nurse monitoring, support planning services, environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, assistive technology and technology support, personal emergency response systems, consumer training, home delivered meals, therapeutic foster care services, transition services, case management, family training, medical day care, respite care, behavior consultation services, nutritionist/dietitian services, and senior center plus services. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Health and available statewide, with local implementation through county Aging and Disability Services divisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capitated managed care services provided through a Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver (1915(c)) including personal assistance services for activities of daily living (such as bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, and light chores), skilled nursing services, nurse monitoring and support planning services, environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, assistive technology and technology support, personal emergency response systems, consumer training, home delivered meals, therapeutic foster care services, transition services, case management, family training, medical day care, respite care, behavior consultation, nutritionist/dietitian services, senior center plus services, assisted living services at various levels, and services that substitute for human assistance. Services are provided to eligible Medicaid individuals of any age who would otherwise require institutional or nursing facility level of care, enabling them to live independently in their own homes and communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals eligible for long-term care services under Maryland's Medicaid program, including those of any age who are Maryland residents, Medicaid-eligible, receive full community Medicaid benefits, and would otherwise require institutional or nursing facility level of care and can live in the community. Eligible populations include aged (65+), physically disabled (ages 18-64), individuals with brain injury, HIV/AIDS, medically fragile conditions, technology-dependent individuals, individuals with autism, developmental disabilities, intellectual disabilities, mental illness, and serious emotional disturbance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home and community-based long-term care services and supports including personal assistance services for activities of daily living (such as bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, and light chores), skilled nursing services, nurse monitoring, support planning services, environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, assistive technology and technology support, personal emergency response systems, consumer training, home delivered meals, therapeutic foster care services, transition services, case management, family training, medical day care, respite care, behavior consultation, nutritionist/dietitian services, senior center plus services, assisted living services at various levels, and services that substitute for human assistance. Services support community living and avoid institutionalization.

Services are available in all Maryland counties including Cecil County. Waiver capacity allocated and managed on a statewide basis with local implementation through county Aging and Disability Services divisions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid 1915(c) Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver program operated by the Maryland Department of Health's Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDA) that is approved by the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) for a five-year period and allows individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities to receive services in community settings as an alternative to institutional care. The program helps participants live more independently in their homes and communities through three categories of services: Meaningful Day Services (including employment services, career exploration, community development services, day habilitation, and medical day care), Support Services (including assistive technology, behavior support services, environmental assessment and modifications, family mentoring, caregiver training, housing support, nursing support, personal support, respite care, support broker services, transition services, transportation, and vehicle modifications), and Residential Services (supported living, shared living, group homes with standard or enhanced supports, and enhanced support communities). Services are provided through both self-directed and traditional agency-based service models and are tailored to meet the unique needs of each individual. Additional support is available through Nursing Support Services and Clinical/Behavioral Services. Services are person-centered and flexible, based on individual needs and choices. The program is subject to waiver amendments for program changes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides Medicaid-funded services under a federally approved Medicaid Waiver program including Meaningful Day Services (employment services, career exploration, community development, day habilitation, medical day care), Support Services (assistive technology, behavior support services, environmental assessment and modifications, family mentoring, caregiver training, housing support, nursing support, personal support, respite care, support broker services, transition services, transportation, vehicle modifications), and Residential Services (supported living, shared living, group homes with standard or enhanced supports, and enhanced support communities). Additional support is available through Nursing Support Services and Clinical/Behavioral Services. Services are provided through a self-directed model where individuals hire and manage their own staff, or a traditional agency-based model where a licensed provider manages staff and services. Services are person-centered, flexible, and tailored to individual needs and choices, provided in various community settings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families who seek to live more independently in their homes and communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meaningful Day Services (employment, career exploration, community development, day habilitation, medical day care), Support Services (assistive technology, behavior support, environmental modifications, family mentoring, caregiver training, housing support, nursing support, personal support, respite care, support broker services, transition services, transportation, vehicle modifications), and Residential Services (supported living, shared living, group homes with standard or enhanced supports, enhanced support communities). Additional support is available through Nursing Support Services and Clinical/Behavioral Services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an intellectual or developmental disability
Must be determined eligible for DDA services
Must meet Medicaid waiver application process requirements

Must complete DDA Waiver Application Process
Must meet specific technical criteria

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals must complete the DDA Eligibility Application Process first to determine if they qualify for DDA services. Then they must complete the DDA Waiver Application Process to enroll in the Community Pathways Waiver. Applicants must meet technical, medical, and financial eligibility criteria both initially and on an ongoing basis. Participants can choose between self-directed and traditional agency-based service models. Coordinators of Community Services and DDA Advocacy Specialists are available to help with planning. More information and application details are available on the DDA website. The Maryland Provider Directory can be used to locate service providers.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Person identifies housing need and meets with Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) to express housing interest and request Housing Support Services. requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must meet the DDA's developmentally disabled eligibility criteria
Must have an approved person-centered plan
Must meet the institutional level of care of an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (ICF/IID)
Must meet financial eligibility criteria based on applicant's income and assets only (not family income or assets)
Must be on the DDA Waiting List or in a specified reserved priority category

Participants must initially and annually meet all eligibility requirements including submitting annual or updated financial statements and documentation, completing an annual person-centered plan, and being recertified to meet the medical level of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Coordinator of Community Services assists the individual with completing the DDA Waiver application packet and exploring service delivery models, services, and provider options based on assessed needs. Once completed, the coordinator submits the packet to the DDA regional office. The Regional Office assesses the application and supporting documentation to determine if the applicant meets technical and medical eligibility criteria. The Eligibility Determination Division reviews financial documents and databases to determine financial eligibility. Applicants meeting all criteria receive an enrollment letter with an effective date. Those not meeting criteria receive a denial letter with information about appeal rights.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid buy-in program that allows workers with disabilities to maintain or obtain Medicaid coverage based on their disability status and work status rather than income limits. Participants pay monthly premiums based on their income level, ranging from $0 for those earning less than $15,960 annually (couples less than $21,640) to 7.5% of monthly countable income for higher earners. Premium amounts are tiered based on individual or couples income ranges. A hardship exemption is available for those temporarily unable to pay premiums. Premiums are effective January 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid coverage for employed individuals with disabilities. Monthly premium amounts range from $0 to 7.5% of monthly countable income depending on income level. Individuals with income less than $15,960 (couples less than $21,640) pay no premium. Those with higher incomes pay sliding-scale premiums up to 7.5% of monthly countable income for income above $95,760 (couples above $129,840). Premiums are effective January 1, 2026. A hardship exemption is available for those temporarily unable to pay premiums. Medicaid coverage is provided for eligible employed individuals with disabilities who would otherwise be ineligible due to their earnings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Workers aged 16 to 64 with disabilities who meet Social Security's medical criteria and earn income subject to taxation. Includes employed or self-employed individuals. Must live in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicaid health insurance coverage for employed individuals with disabilities and individuals who would otherwise be ineligible due to their earnings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must live in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be at least 16 years old but not yet 65 years old
Be working for pay or self-employed with earnings subject to taxes
Have a disability meeting Social Security's medical criteria
Be a U.S. Citizen or qualified non-citizen
Live in Maryland
Meet the $10,000 asset limit (joint assets and assets only the applicant owns count; spouse's assets do not count if married)
Employees must have pay stubs showing taxes withheld; self-employed individuals should pay estimated taxes
Earnings must be subject to taxes (cannot be working under the table)
Must provide Social Security number for all household members applying
Must disclose citizenship/immigration status information
Must provide true, complete, and correct information
Must report all changes affecting eligibility or benefit amounts within 10 days
Must verify and report shelter, medical, or dependent care expenses
Must cooperate with Department in securing payments from private/public health insurance and liable third parties
Verification of birth, Social Security card, marriage/divorce certificates, Medicare card, and immigration/citizenship papers (if applicable)
Four recent consecutive weeks of pay stubs or signed employer statement showing regular pay
Earnings records and recent tax returns for self-employed individuals
Verification of other income sources (Social Security, disability benefits, unemployment, veterans benefits, insurance payments, rental income, trust fund income, etc.)
Documentation of resources (bank statements, savings accounts, stocks, bonds, property/vehicle registrations, tax bills)
Health insurance identification card(s) for applicant and household members
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the EID Program application form (Form 9701), provide all required documentation, sign and date it, and mail to the Eligibility Determination Division, EID Program, Maryland Department of Health, 6 St. Paul Street, 4th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202. Applicants must submit pay stubs (4 weekly, 2 bi-weekly, or 3 monthly consecutive weeks) or Schedule C for self-employed individuals, bank statements including first day of application month, and documentation of assets, resources, income, and benefits. An interview (by phone or in person) may be conducted. Case managers will review the application and determine eligibility, providing written notice of approval or denial within 30 days of receipt. Eligibility workers may request additional information. Application forms and instructions are available online. Applicants can also seek assistance from disability agencies in Maryland or Centers for Independent Living.

structured_extraction.program_name: Expanding Access to Primary Care and Building Health Care Infrastructure Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive grant program that funds multiple grantee organizations to expand access to primary care services and build health care infrastructure across Maryland.
