Grants support initiatives such as care coordination programs and services addressing chronic disease disparities, behavioral health needs, and social determinants of health.

Grant funds support staff salaries for clinical and administrative personnel, equipment and supplies, technology infrastructure and electronic medical records systems, billing and collections systems, mobile health clinic operations, care coordination and case management services, health education and screenings, transportation services, and programs addressing social determinants of health including food security, housing assistance, and language services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports salaries for clinical and administrative personnel, opening and operating new health centers and school-based health centers, care coordination services and case management, medical equipment and supplies, technology infrastructure and electronic medical records systems, billing and collections systems, mobile health clinics, health screenings and education, patient navigation, transportation services, and programs addressing social determinants of health including food security, housing assistance, and language services. Programs targeting chronic disease disparities and behavioral health needs among vulnerable populations are prioritized.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Grants support programs serving jurisdictions throughout Maryland, including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Charles County, Calvert County, St. Mary's County, Harford County, Cecil County, Washington County, Frederick County, Wicomico County, Somerset County, Dorchester County, Caroline County, Kent County, Queen Anne's County, Talbot County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, and Allegany County. Programs serve both urban and rural areas across the state.

structured_extraction.program_description: A special category of eligibility and priority for services that helps young people ages 21-22 transitioning from school to adult life. The program provides employment services and other day services to eligible students leaving school who are found fully eligible as developmentally disabled, preventing them from being placed on the DDA waiting list. Services include supported employment, day programs, adult vocational training, day habilitation, and coordination of services through targeted case management and person-centered planning. The initiative is administered by the Department of Disabilities Administration (DDA) in collaboration with the Division of Rehabilitative Services (DORS). The program helps transitioning youth and families navigate a path toward a 'good life' as adults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DDA and DORS in collaboration fund supported employment, day habilitation, adult vocational training, and other day services for eligible transitioning youth. Services include Coordination of Community Services (CCS), person-centered planning, career discovery and exploration, employment training and support, and skills learning. Services are individualized and may include employment support, meaningful day services, and coordination of services through targeted case management and person-centered planning. An Employment First approach prioritizes community employment options. Individuals are eligible from their 21st birthday until their 22nd birthday, or for one year after the date of graduation if graduation occurs after the student's 21st birthday.

requirements_list: Must be found fully eligible as developmentally disabled
Must have a severe chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole mental illness diagnosis) or combination of impairments
Disability must be manifested before age 22
Disability must be likely to continue indefinitely
Must result in inability to live independently without external support or continuing and regular assistance
Must reflect need for a combination and sequence of special, interdisciplinary or generic care, treatment, or other services that are individually planned and coordinated
Must be ages 21-22 or within one year after graduation if graduation occurs after 21st birthday
Students with developmental disabilities preparing to graduate from school system
Should contact at age 14 for TY-specific services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for DDA services using the Transitioning Youth category, individuals should contact their regional DDA office or work with Coordinators of Community Services (CCS) agencies who assist people in accessing DDA services and other service delivery systems. It is recommended to contact the regional office at age 14 to begin planning. Once found eligible as developmentally disabled, individuals in the transitioning youth age range receive priority for services. Applications must be submitted before June 30 of the eligibility year. Once eligible, individuals receive targeted case management and person-centered planning to identify desired services and support needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative implemented under the Maryland Health Improvement and Disparities Reduction Act of 2012 to reduce health disparities, improve health outcomes, and reduce health costs and hospital admissions in five designated Health Enterprise Zone locations. The program provided grants to community coalitions and health care providers, along with access to incentives including income tax credits, hiring tax credits, and loan repayment assistance. Two of the five zones are located in rural areas: Greater Lexington Park in St. Mary's County, and Dorchester and Caroline Counties. In 2013, the CHRC awarded five HEZ grants collectively totaling $4 million per year over a four-year duration. Though this specific grant program ended several years ago, many of the services initiated continue to be provided to residents.

Community coalitions in each Health Enterprise Zone receive grant funding to address health disparities in their designated areas. The program also provides access to incentives including income tax credits, hiring tax credits, and loan repayment assistance. Though this specific grant program ended several years ago, many of the services initiated continue to be provided to residents.

Interpreter services are available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program between Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and Maryland Department of Health created to help families reduce lead exposure and asthma triggers in homes built before 1978. The program identifies and removes lead hazards, conducts minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed, and provides in-home case management services through county health departments. Services are provided at no cost for Maryland families with children who have been exposed to lead or have asthma and meet eligibility criteria. In-home environmental case management services are provided to reduce exposures to lead and asthma triggers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Lead hazard removal and remediation services, minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed, and in-home case management services provided at no cost to eligible families. Services include identifying and removing lead hazards from homes where children have been exposed, conducting minor repairs to seal lead paint, environmental assessments to mitigate asthma triggers (dust, pests, mold, pets, tobacco smoke), and providing in-home environmental case management to reduce exposures to lead and asthma triggers. Services are provided by county health departments. Availability varies by jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families in eligible counties with children age 18 or younger who have elevated blood lead levels of 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher, or moderate to severe asthma, are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard removal and remediation services, minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed, and in-home environmental case management services to reduce lead exposures and asthma triggers in homes where children have been exposed to lead or have asthma.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in participating Maryland counties including Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Charles County, Dorchester County, Frederick County, Harford County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, and Wicomico County, with availability varying by jurisdiction. Child must reside in one of the eligible counties.
requirements_list: Child must be 18 years old or younger
Child must live in Maryland
Child must have a recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter or higher OR have moderate to severe asthma with frequent attacks or daily medication use
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure happened
Family resides in one of the participating counties

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hospital Preparedness Program supports and enhances the ability of hospitals and health care systems to provide effective care and save lives during emergencies and disasters that exceed the day-to-day capacity of the health care and emergency response systems. The program provides federal grants to health care system partners across Maryland, including hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions. Funds are used to enhance the ability to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and other emergencies. The program also supports the development of regional health care coalitions that bring together diverse health care organizations to improve overall health care system preparedness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health awards federal funds in the form of grants to health care system partners across Maryland. These partners include hospitals and free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions. Federal grants are awarded annually to support regional health care coalitions, joint training and exercise opportunities, shared assets and equipment, and coordinated preparedness planning.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hospitals, free-standing emergency departments, community health centers, state-managed facilities, poison control centers, emergency medical services, home care and hospice agencies, and regional health care preparedness coalitions across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to enhance the ability to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and other emergencies that pose a threat to the health and safety of the community. Funds support the development of regional health care coalitions, joint training and exercise opportunities, shared assets and equipment, and coordinated preparedness planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves all of Maryland through four regional health care coalitions: Region I and II covering the four westernmost counties (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick), Region III covering central Maryland (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Carroll, Harford, Howard, and Baltimore City), Region IV covering the Eastern Shore (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester), and Region V covering southern Maryland and the National Capital Region (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The page does not provide specific application process details. Applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Health Office of Preparedness and Response for information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows qualified hospitals to immediately determine Medicaid eligibility for certain individuals and enroll them for temporary coverage without waiting for full application processing. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hospitals that qualify can immediately screen individuals for Medicaid eligibility and enroll eligible individuals for temporary coverage lasting up to 60 days. The program ensures hospital reimbursement for services provided during the temporary coverage period even if the individual is later found to be ineligible for Medicaid. Individuals gain immediate access to coverage and opportunity to connect to longer-term coverage options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hospitals participating in Maryland Medicaid and their staff members. Individuals likely to be eligible for Medicaid who receive services at participating Maryland hospitals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covers Medicaid-eligible services provided during the temporary 60-day coverage period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to qualified Maryland hospitals participating in Maryland Medicaid.
requirements_list: Hospital must be a participating Maryland Medicaid provider in good standing with the Maryland Department of Health
Hospital employees must attend required HPE training
Hospital staff must pass HPE certification test prior to making HPE determinations
Hospital must have a primary HPE contact to request training and coordinate the program
Individuals must meet Medicaid eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Hospital completes and submits the MDH HPE Application and Agreement to the Maryland Department of Health. Maryland Department of Health registers those on the list for training. Hospitals then screen individuals for Medicaid eligibility and enroll eligible individuals in temporary coverage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Increasing access to integrated behavioral health services
structured_extraction.program_description: A grants program that funds nonprofits and government agencies to increase access to behavioral health care and substance use disorder treatment services, with a focus on improving mental health outcomes, decreasing substance use, increasing employment and housing stability, and reducing overdose rates. Services are tailored to vulnerable populations including low-income individuals, African American communities, sexual and gender minorities, homeless individuals, incarcerated individuals, pregnant and postpartum women, youth and adolescents, and those affected by the opioid crisis. Grant amounts range from $10,000 to $1,600,000 with multi-year funding cycles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $1,600,000 awarded to nonprofits and government agencies to fund behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment programs. Funding supports salaries for clinical staff, peer recovery specialists, and support personnel; operational and administrative costs; program expansion; equipment and technology; training and technical assistance; data collection; telehealth and mobile health services; crisis stabilization; medication-assisted treatment; case management and care coordination; harm reduction services; residential treatment beds; mobile crisis teams; and wraparound services addressing social determinants of health such as food insecurity, housing, employment, and transportation. Grants support integration of primary care with behavioral health services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits and government agencies providing behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment services to low-income individuals, homeless populations, individuals with substance use disorders, individuals with serious mental illness, families affected by addiction, incarcerated individuals, minorities facing health disparities, African American communities, sexual and gender minorities, pregnant and postpartum women, and youth and adolescents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries for clinical staff, peer recovery specialists, and support personnel; operational and administrative costs; program expansion; equipment purchases and technology; training and technical assistance; data collection; telehealth services; mobile health units and mobile crisis teams; crisis intervention and stabilization services; medication-assisted treatment; case management and care coordination; harm reduction services; residential treatment beds; capital improvements; integration of behavioral health with primary care services; and wraparound services addressing social determinants of health such as food insecurity, housing, employment, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—the program funds grantees throughout Maryland serving multiple counties and regions including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Central Maryland, Southern Maryland, Eastern Shore, Western Maryland, and National Capital regions. Some grants are county-specific or serve multiple counties within regions, while others serve statewide populations.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or government agency
Must provide behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, mental health services, or integrated primary care and behavioral health services
Must serve low-income, uninsured, vulnerable, or underserved populations
May require focus on specific populations such as minorities, homeless individuals, justice-involved persons, pregnant women, youth, or individuals with serious mental illness
Must demonstrate capacity to serve the target population and geographic area
Must demonstrate capacity to deliver evidence-based services

Some grants require integration of primary care with behavioral health services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit competitive grant proposals detailing their proposed behavioral health initiatives, target populations, service delivery model, expected outcomes, budget, and organizational capacity through a competitive grant process managed by the Maryland Department of Health's Center for Health-Related Professions (CHRC) or similar division. structured_extraction.program_name: Local Public Health Core Tobacco and Chronic Disease Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive statewide tobacco and chronic disease control program providing grants and technical support to all local health departments in Maryland. The program includes community initiatives to mobilize community actions through coalition participation, grassroots campaigns, and tobacco prevention education; school-based initiatives promoting tobacco use prevention education for students in kindergarten through twelfth grade with peer support and parent involvement; and cessation initiatives promoting quitting tobacco products among adults, youth, and pregnant women through individual and group behavior change sessions, free cessation aids, policy interventions, and Maryland Quitline referrals. The program takes an integrated approach that collectively addresses tobacco use, chronic disease, and related health risk factors using health equity principles to address disparities and inequities, encouraging local health department staff to work collaboratively as a team.

Technical support and guidance is provided from the state health department for integrated programming that addresses tobacco use, chronic disease, and related risk factors using a health equity approach. Funding supports community initiatives, school-based prevention, and cessation programs including free tobacco cessation aids and Maryland Quitline referrals.

structured_extraction.program_description: The LISS Program, operated by the Maryland Department of Health's Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDA), provides funding for eligible services and items to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Maryland who are not receiving other DDA services, including those on the DDA waiting list. The program grants limited funding (up to $1,000 for FY2026) for services and items supporting identified needs, including personal and attendant care, respite care, adaptive items, assistive technology, childcare, community integration, educational services, home modifications, identification services, summer camps, transportation, and wellness services to maximize independence, productivity, and integration within the community. The program serves children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living in their own home in the community. Eligible applicants are selected through a random selection process conducted in multiple rounds throughout the fiscal year and must verify their identity, disability status, residency, and that the requested service or item is delivered by an eligible vendor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides limited funding up to $1,000 per individual for eligible services and items for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are selected through a random selection process. Eligible services include adaptive items, assistive technology, personal and attendant care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modifications and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic programs, transportation, and wellness services. Applicants must be Maryland residents and must verify their identity, disability status, residency, and that the identified eligible service or item is delivered by an eligible vendor. The program is administered through two regional providers: Maryland Community Connection serves Southern Maryland and Eastern Shore counties (Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), and Penn-Mar Human Services serves Western and Central Maryland counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Washington).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children living at home with their family and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities living in their own home in the community who are Maryland residents and not receiving any support services from the DDA, including those on the DDA waiting list. Applications can be submitted by the individual (if over 21 without legal guardian), parent, legal guardian, caseworker, or other authorized representative.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Adaptive items, assistive technology, personal and attendant care, childcare, community integration and recreational services, educational services, home modifications and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic programs, transportation, and wellness services (including behavioral support services and medical/therapeutic services and items) to support identified needs and maximize independence, productivity, and community integration for individuals with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents throughout the state of Maryland. Program is administered through two regional providers covering all Maryland counties: Maryland Community Connection serves Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico and Worcester. Penn-Mar Human Services serves Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard and Washington.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of the state of Maryland
Must have an intellectual or developmental disability with an eligible diagnosis as documented
Must not be receiving other services from the DDA or be on the DDA waiting list
Must request funding for an eligible service or item
Must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and identified eligible service or item delivered by an eligible vendor
Must meet LISS eligibility requirements
Individual must be living in their own home in the community
Applicants under 21 without a court-ordered legal guardian must have a natural or adoptive parent submit the application
Applicants with a court-ordered legal guardian must have the legal guardian submit the application
Applicants over 21 without a legal guardian may have a parent, relative, friend, case manager, or social worker assist with submission under their direction
Applicant must submit a Random Selection Application during the designated application round
Proof of identity (Social Security card, birth certificate, passport, permanent resident card, military ID, or driver's license)
Proof of developmental disability (medical letter, approved IEP within 3 years, or DDA eligibility letter)
Services/items must be purchased or received during the fiscal year (July 1 - June 30)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Random Selection Application during each Round with the applicant's demographic information. For FY 2026, online applications open July 14, 2025 and close September 15, 2025. 2. Use the access link provided on the DDA website under Resources to submit the application online. 3. The application can be completed by the applicant or with assistance from a parent, legal guardian, relative, friend, case manager, or social worker, but vendors cannot complete it on behalf of the applicant. 4. Upon submission, you will receive a confirmation receipt with a confirmation number via email. 5. The access link is open to the public during each Round only and closes after each Round. 6. Random Selection is conducted (September 30, 2025 for FY 2026) and applicants are notified via letter within twenty business days of the Random Selection completion. Selected applicants will be contacted by a representative of the LISS agency serving their county for assistance with the LISS process. 7. For approved services/items, applicants must submit required documentation (proof of payment via bank/credit card statement or canceled check, completed W-9 form, service-specific required documents including invoices, quotes, licenses, photo IDs). 8. Reimbursement is processed directly back to the LISS Program account. Visit DDA's website or access the LISS Applicant and Reference Guide for additional application process details.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEGAN Place (Meaningful Environment to Gather and Nurture Place)
structured_extraction.program_description: A supportive, non-judgmental, and restorative grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Health to improve perinatal health outcomes and reduce infant mortality in Harford County. The program provides comprehensive care coordination and community outreach services integrated with family planning and reproductive health services, targeting at-risk pregnant and postpartum women and their families, with specific emphasis on low-income, minority women and women with substance use disorders. Services include family support programs, evidence-based interventions, and family resiliency skill-building. The project establishes a supportive community space where participants receive comprehensive perinatal health services. Grants have supported both the establishment and operation of the MEGAN Place facility as well as expansion of family planning and reproductive health services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative administered by the Maryland Department of Health that provides recommended vaccines for free to uninsured and underinsured adults aged 19 and older. The program expands access to critical immunizations and reduces barriers to vaccination by distributing state-purchased vaccines at no cost through local health departments across Maryland. Funded through $2.8 million allocated in partnership with the Maryland General Assembly. Vaccines available include COVID-19, influenza, measles, mumps, rubella, pneumonia, respiratory syncytial virus, shingles, pertussis, meningitis, tetanus, diphtheria, hepatitis A and B, polio, varicella, rotavirus, haemophilus influenzae type B, human papillomavirus, and human rabies (in specific circumstances). Currently vaccines are accessible through local health departments in Baltimore, Garrett, Montgomery, and Somerset counties, with expansion to other counties planned. The program operates statewide through participating local health department locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state-purchased vaccines at no cost to eligible individuals through local health departments. Available vaccines include pneumonia, shingles, meningitis, tetanus/diphtheria/pertussis, hepatitis A and B, polio, measles/mumps/rubella, varicella, rotavirus, haemophilus influenzae type B, human papillomavirus, human rabies (specific circumstances required), influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus. Underinsured means health insurance does not cover recommended vaccines or has high deductibles creating a financial burden. Appointments are required at most locations. Currently available in Baltimore, Garrett, Montgomery, and Somerset counties, with expansion to other counties planned.

Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, breast ultrasounds, surgical consultations, breast biopsies, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, cervical biopsies, and patient navigation assistance such as scheduling appointments, finding transportation, and interpretation services. The program also offers linkage to treatment services as needed. Works with local health departments, health systems, and hospitals to improve screening rates among medically underserved populations. Funded by the Centers for Disease Prevention and Control (CDC) and the Maryland Cigarette Restitution Fund, the program provides grants to local health departments and health systems to deliver these services.

Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, breast ultrasounds, surgical consultations, breast biopsies, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, cervical biopsies, and patient navigation services. Patient navigation includes help scheduling appointments and follow-up, finding transportation, interpretation services, and linkage to treatment as needed. Grant funds support outreach, education, follow-up services, hiring community health outreach workers, and contracting with private physicians, radiologists, surgeons, and medical laboratories.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and federally funded statewide program that provides free or subsidized health insurance coverage to eligible uninsured children under age 19 and pregnant women of any age whose family income exceeds Medicaid limits but is insufficient to afford private health insurance. The program is designed to ensure all eligible Maryland children and pregnant women have medical insurance. Coverage is provided through Maryland's HealthChoice managed care organizations and includes dental care, doctor visits, hospital care, immunizations, lab work and tests, mental health services, prescription medicine, substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, and vision care. Children and pregnant women with countable income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level receive full health benefits with no enrollment fees; those up to 300% of the federal poverty level may qualify with a premium.

Coverage includes doctor visits, check-ups, immunizations, prescription drugs (no copays for children under 21 and pregnant women), lab/x-ray services, urgent care, emergency services, hospital services, prenatal/postpartum care, family planning, home health, vision/glasses (children under 21), behavioral health, dental care, and transportation services. Children under age 19 and pregnant women of any age whose countable income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level receive full health benefits with no enrollment fees or payments required. Those with income up to 300% of the federal poverty level may qualify with a premium.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC), administered by the Maryland Department of Health, awards competitive grants to expand access to affordable, high-quality health care services in underserved areas throughout Maryland. Grants support programs addressing barriers to accessing health care across all jurisdictions, including expanding primary care access, reducing infant mortality, increasing dental care access, integrating behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment services, supporting maternal and child health, assisting medically vulnerable populations, facilitating health information technology adoption among safety net providers, and advancing health equity and addressing social determinants of health. The CHRC issues an Annual Request for Applications (RFA) approximately once per year, typically making several million dollars available in grant funding. The FY 2026 RFA made $7 million available across six areas of focus: hospital community partnerships, support for medically vulnerable populations including older adults and individuals with disabilities, chronic disease prevention and management, maternal and child health, dental health, and behavioral health for adults including mental health and substance use disorder services. The CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling $396 million since its inception, supporting programs in every jurisdiction of the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CHRC awards $7 million in grants through competitive Annual Requests for Applications (RFAs) issued approximately once per year. Anticipated award amounts range from $300,000 to $750,000 per grant for funding up to 3 years. The application process involves two stages: Letters of Intent (LOI) followed by full proposals submitted via Smartsheet. Full applications must include transmittal letter, grant application cover sheet, executive summary, full project proposal, contractual obligations and assurances, IRS Form W-9, legal and financial disclosure, budget form with narrative, organizational documentation (including list of officers and board of directors or governing body, organizational chart, overall organization budget, resumes of key personnel), letters of commitment from collaborators or Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs), Logic Model, Workplan, most recent IRS Form 990 or Business Tax Return, audited financial statements or alternative financial documentation, and certificate of good standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation dated within one year of submission. Grant proposals are evaluated by independent subject matter experts on criteria including use of evidence-based practices, ability to collect and report outcomes data, demonstration of community need, program sustainability, and likelihood of overall program success. Funds may support project staff salaries and fringe benefits (limited to 25% of salaries), contractual services, data collection and analysis, project-related travel, supplies, minor equipment, furniture, IT/telecom, minor infrastructure improvements, staff training/development, program marketing, and indirect costs (limited to 15% of direct costs or higher if federally approved). Funds cannot be used for major equipment purchases or leases, construction projects, clinical trials, unapproved medical devices or drugs, or lobbying/political activity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due March 30, 2026 by 3:00 pm EDT; Full proposals due April 23, 2026 by 3:00 pm EDT (approximately once per year through Annual RFA)

Programs serving vulnerable and underserved populations including low-income individuals, uninsured and underinsured individuals, older adults, individuals with disabilities, medically vulnerable populations, racial and ethnic minorities, and non-English speakers. Organizations in low-income neighborhoods, including those in ENOUGH Act eligible communities, receive additional consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs addressing barriers to accessing health care and social determinants of health including food security, transportation, and health insurance coverage; hospital-community partnerships; chronic disease prevention and management; expanding primary care access; dental care and oral health services; behavioral health and substance use disorder services; maternal and child health; support for medically vulnerable populations including older adults and individuals with disabilities; reducing infant mortality; facilitating adoption of health information technology among safety net providers; and advancing health equity. Funds may support project staff salaries, fringe benefits, equipment/furniture, IT/telecom, minor infrastructure improvements, supplies, travel, staff training/development, contractual services, program marketing, data collection and analysis, and indirect costs.

Additional consideration for applicants serving areas eligible under the ENOUGH Act initiative, including 116 high-need census tracts identified in the ENOUGH Initiative Community Eligibility Map or Census Tract List.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Consortium on Coordinated Community Supports
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide framework that develops and implements comprehensive behavioral health services for Maryland students. The Consortium supports grants to organizations providing prevention, behavioral health screenings, counseling, addiction treatment, family support, crisis planning, telehealth services, support groups, and wraparound services to address student behavioral health needs. The program operates through local Community Supports Partnerships consisting of Hubs and community behavioral health providers that coordinate with schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In the first year of the grant program, the Consortium supported 127 grants totaling $110 million. These grants supported services in 80% of Maryland schools, resulted in hiring 542 practitioners, and served more than 104,000 students through April 2025. The second round of grant awards was made on June 11, 2025 (contract period July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) to support programs in all 24 jurisdictions, with grantees planning to serve more than 165,000 students statewide. Anne Arundel County is home to one Community Supports Partnership Program that brings together 13 service providers and is expected to serve approximately 12,000 students.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations providing behavioral health services to Maryland students; Maryland schools and students with behavioral health needs and related challenges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for behavioral health services including prevention, screening, counseling, addiction treatment, family support, crisis planning, telehealth, support groups, and wraparound services for students.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all Maryland jurisdictions and supporting services in 80% of Maryland schools through local Community Supports Partnerships.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The CHRC Commissioners make grant awards on a regular cycle. Grantees are selected through a competitive process to establish Community Supports Partnerships consisting of a Hub and community behavioral health providers that coordinate with schools. The second round was announced on June 11, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Dent-Care Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MDC-LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A student loan repayment program for dentists and dental hygienists designed to increase access to oral health services for Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP) recipients by providing educational loan repayment assistance. The program recruits dental professionals to treat vulnerable populations covered by MMAP. Full-time dentists receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment, part-time dentists receive up to $25,000 per year, and dental hygienists receive up to $10,000 per year (full-time) or $5,000 per year (part-time) for a two-year commitment. Recipients may receive up to $30,000 toward student loan debt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time dentists receive up to $50,000 per year for a three-year commitment (40 hours per week). Part-time dentists (20-39 hours per week) receive up to $25,000 per year for a three-year commitment. Dental hygienists receive $10,000 per year for a two-year commitment (full-time, 40 hours per week) or $5,000 per year for a two-year commitment (part-time, 20-39 hours per week). Recipients may receive up to $30,000 toward student loan debt. Participants must treat a minimum of 30% Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients as part of their total patient population per year. The number of recipients per award is determined based on available funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) / State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides educational loan repayment assistance to health professionals including physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants, medical residents, nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and nursing support staff who commit to working in areas of Maryland experiencing healthcare professional shortages. The program pays verified education loan holders directly to repay qualifying undergraduate or graduate education loans obtained for study leading to practice as a health professional. Participants must commit to a service obligation at an eligible practice site in an area with healthcare professional shortages. Service obligations range from 1 to 3 years depending on credential and employment status (full-time or part-time). The program serves physicians, physician assistants, nurses, and nursing support staff at public, non-profit, or for-profit eligible practice sites that serve underserved populations or have workforce shortages and provide services to all patients regardless of ability to pay. Recipients may reapply after completion of initial service obligations, with maximum total awards up to $200,000 for physicians and physician assistants. Funding comes from the U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration and state-level resources. The federal State Loan Repayment Program component specifically supports physicians and physician assistants serving 2-year obligations in health professional shortage areas or medically underserved areas in primary care or mental health, requiring a 1:1 match from the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program. For nurses and nursing support staff: Advanced practice registered nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) can receive up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time with a 2-year service obligation. Registered and licensed practical nurses can receive up to $50,000 full-time or $25,000 part-time with a 2-year service obligation. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) can receive up to $5,000 full-time or $2,500 part-time with a 1-year service obligation.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loan repayment assistance up to $100,000 for full-time physicians, physician assistants, and medical residents, with smaller amounts for part-time service. Advanced practice registered nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS) can receive up to $100,000 full-time or $50,000 part-time. Registered and licensed practical nurses can receive up to $50,000 full-time or $25,000 part-time. Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA) can receive up to $5,000 full-time or $2,500 part-time. Physicians and physician assistants may also receive up to $50,000 per year for a 2-year service obligation in a health professional shortage area or medically underserved area, with potential to reapply for a maximum total award of $200,000 or two 2-year obligations at $50,000 per year. Assistance is provided through direct payment to verified education loan holders to repay qualifying undergraduate or graduate education loans for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses. Loans must have been obtained for study leading to practice as a health professional and cannot have been obtained after licensure. Service obligations range from 1 to 3 years depending on credential and employment status. Full-time is defined as 40 or more hours per week; part-time is 20-39 hours per week.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The 2026 MLRP Application Cycle is now closed. The annual application cycle is from March 1 through April 15.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Health professionals including physicians with MD or DO degrees, physician assistants, final-year medical residents, nurses, advanced practice registered nurses (including nurse practitioners, certified nurse-midwives, certified registered nurse anesthetists, and clinical nurse specialists), registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and nursing support staff (including certified medication technicians, certified medicine aides, certified nursing assistants, and geriatric nursing assistants) who are U.S. citizens or nationals with education loan debt and valid Maryland licenses willing to work in areas of healthcare professional shortages in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used for educational loan repayment assistance to support health professionals in paying down student loan debt obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as a health professional. Eligible loans must be for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses during such study. Loans obtained after licensure are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide in Maryland. Eligible practice sites must be located in areas of Maryland experiencing healthcare professional shortages, medically underserved areas, or state-designated health professional shortage areas. Practice sites must be physically located in Maryland. Eligible practice sites must be public or non-profit exempt under IRC 501(c)(3) or (4), or for-profit sites in areas with health care workforce shortages or public health need. Participants must work at a practice site physically located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a health professional in an eligible credential category (physicians with MD or DO degree, physician assistants, medical residents, nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, or nursing support staff)
Must be a United States citizen or national
Must have completed training in an accredited training program
Must possess an active and valid license without restrictions or encumbrances to practice in Maryland
Must personally owe education loan debt for undergraduate or graduate study leading to health professional practice

Must have a valid employment contract to work at an eligible Maryland practice site effective by July 1 following application

Must work part-time (20-39 hours per week) or full-time (40+ hours per week) with minimum 80% of work hours dedicated to direct patient care; Exception: OB/GYN physicians must provide at least 50% of normally scheduled clinical hours in ambulatory care setting; Exception: Certified nurse-midwives must provide at least 50% of hours in ambulatory care
Must meet employment verification requirements for year 2 renewal
Must complete cultural competency training and assessment
Must complete lender verification forms and provide documentation of existing educational loans

Eligible practice sites must be public or non-profit exempt under IRC 501(c)(3) or (4), or for-profit sites in areas with health care workforce shortages or public health need
Eligible practice sites must provide services to all patients regardless of ability to pay

Eligible practice sites must provide discounts to those between 100-200 percent of poverty guidelines

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Annual application cycle runs from March 1 through April 15. Applicants must verify eligibility in three critical areas: discipline, participant, and practice site. The application requires verification of active Maryland license, education loan debt documentation, valid employment contract at an eligible practice site, and commitment to service obligation. Practice sites must be pre-approved by MLRP at time of application. Participants must demonstrate compliance with eligibility criteria during application and throughout the service obligation period. Final-year medical residents follow a specific process outlined for a three-year service obligation (final year of residency plus two years at an eligible practice site). Upon award, participants must complete offer acceptance documentation including a promissory note, service obligation agreement, and lender verification. In year 2, participants must submit renewal documentation including employment verification, impact data collection, and cultural competency training completion. Participants must agree to participate in reporting requirements including verification of ongoing employment, submission of aggregate de-identified data regarding patient populations and health care quality outcomes, and completion of an organizational assessment tool evaluating integration of National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services in Health Care. Service obligations typically commence July 1 following the application cycle. Application materials are available from the Maryland Department of Health website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland MOM (Maternal Opioid Misuse) Case Management Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A suite of innovative maternal and child health services that focuses on improving care for pregnant and postpartum Medicaid participants diagnosed with opioid use disorder or with a history of opioid use. The program provides enhanced case management services led by Medicaid's nine managed care organizations to improve maternal and infant health outcomes. Case managers meet with participants at least monthly to develop personalized care plans addressing mental and physical health needs, treatment goals, lifestyle supports, and overdose prevention. Services include prenatal and postpartum visits, behavioral health treatment linkage, person-centered care planning, screening for depression and anxiety, social determinants of health assessment, connection to prenatal care, substance use disorder treatment, mental health services, medication for opioid treatment, housing assistance, and other supportive services. Care plans are shared through CRISP, the statewide health information exchange, to coordinate services across providers. Services are provided during pregnancy and up to one year after birth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free case management services provided at least monthly by Medicaid's nine managed care organizations. Services include health care utilization support, prenatal and postpartum visit coordination, behavioral health treatment linkage, person-centered care planning, goal-setting, screenings for depression and anxiety, social determinants of health assessment, overdose prevention education, medication for opioid treatment support, care coordination with providers through CRISP health information exchange, housing assistance, and connection to recovery services and local resources. Services are available during pregnancy and up to one year postpartum.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals and individuals up to one year postpartum who are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid and have opioid use disorder or a history of opioid use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced case management and care coordination services for pregnant and postpartum individuals with opioid use disorder or history of opioid use, including behavioral health treatment, prenatal and postpartum care support, medication for opioid treatment, screening services, overdose prevention education, housing support, and connection to recovery services and local resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland to all Medicaid participants.
requirements_list: Must have health insurance through Maryland Medicaid
Must be pregnant
Pregnant or postpartum
Must use or have used opioids
Diagnosed with opioid use disorder (OUD)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can enroll through the enrollment portal at https://health.maryland.gov/EnrollMOM. Enrollment is also encouraged through referrals from health care providers and community organizations. Alternatively, individuals can contact their health care provider or health care plan for assistance in starting prenatal care and enrolling in the program. Marylanders across all sectors are encouraged to identify and refer potential participants to the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Medicaid covers medically necessary Applied Behavior Analysis therapy services for members under age 21. ABA is an evidence-based treatment for individuals with autism spectrum disorder that uses various techniques to increase useful behaviors like communication and social skills, and reduce behaviors that may interfere with learning or be harmful. Services are delivered in home, community, clinic, or school settings and include behavior identification assessment, adaptive behavior treatment, family guidance, and group services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid covers medically necessary ABA therapy services for eligible members under age 21. Services include ABA assessments and reassessments, behavior identification supporting assessments, ABA therapy (individual, group, and social skills), parent/caregiver training, direction/remote direction of behavior technicians, and telehealth services for supervision, parent training, and group parent training. Carelon Behavioral Health Maryland administers the program and provides clinical, operational, and provider assistance and expertise. A fee schedule is available for covered services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Medicaid recipients under age 21 diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder who reside in home/community settings and need ABA therapy services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Applied Behavior Analysis therapy services including assessment, treatment, family training, group services, and skill generalization for individuals with autism spectrum disorder. Services delivered in home, community, clinic, or school settings as medically necessary.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available across Maryland through Medicaid.
requirements_list: Member must be under age 21
Member must be Medicaid-eligible
Member must be diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
Treatment must be medically necessary
Services must be provided by an enrolled ABA provider
Services are discontinued if no longer medically necessary, treatment goals achieved, or no measurable progress
Home-based services are the standard model for skill generalization
Clinic-based services require specific medical justification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers must enroll with Maryland Medicaid and register with Carelon Behavioral Health Maryland to deliver ABA services. Licensed psychologists must complete and submit an attestation form to mdh.aba@maryland.gov and register with Carelon Behavioral Health via https://maryland.carelonbh.com/behavioral-health-providers/join-the-network/. Members and their families should work with their healthcare provider to access covered services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows qualified pharmacists and pharmacies to enroll with Maryland Medicaid as Pharmacist Prescriber provider types to prescribe contraceptives and receive reimbursement for patient assessments related to contraceptive prescribing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified pharmacists and pharmacies can enroll as Pharmacist Prescriber provider types with Maryland Medicaid. Once enrolled, Pharmacist Prescribers may bill and receive reimbursement for patient assessments to determine whether to prescribe contraceptives and which contraceptive to prescribe. Reimbursement is made via CMS-1500 form submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified pharmacists and pharmacies in Maryland seeking to prescribe contraceptives and receive Medicaid reimbursement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for patient assessments rendered to determine whether to prescribe contraceptives and which contraceptive to prescribe.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Pharmacies must have a location in Maryland to enroll.
requirements_list: Pharmacy must obtain a new type 2 National Provider Identifier (NPI) through the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES)
Pharmacy must enroll as a group pharmacist prescriber and affiliate with at least one qualified pharmacist
Individual qualified pharmacist must enroll as a Pharmacist Prescriber renderer and must have a type 1 NPI
Pharmacist must be qualified per Maryland regulations for contraception prescribing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pharmacy obtains a type 2 NPI through NPPES at https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/. Pharmacy enrolls as a group pharmacist prescriber and affiliates with a qualified pharmacist. Individual qualified pharmacist enrolls as a Pharmacist Prescriber renderer (obtaining a type 1 NPI if needed). Complete enrollment and billing information is available at health.maryland.gov/providerinfo.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Commission oversees the award of competitive grants from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund to support pediatric cancer research conducted by physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, and other organizations and persons. Competitive grants are awarded to support pediatric cancer research projects.

Grants are reviewed through a competitive process managed by the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Research Commission, which evaluates proposals based on developed criteria, standards, and requirements.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pediatric cancer research.

Applications must be complete and satisfy established criteria

structured_extraction.program_description: Connects humanitarian immigrants, including refugees, asylees, parolees, and victims of trafficking, with culturally and linguistically appropriate mental health services to help them adjust to their new circumstances and address trauma they may have experienced from persecution, war, torture, or separation from family.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Rural Health Program (RHTP) - Service Expansion and HIT Advances + Behavioral Health Expansion + Innovative Care
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding opportunity to support service expansion, health information technology advances, behavioral health expansion, and innovative care delivery models in rural Maryland through the Rural Health Transformation Program, a cooperative agreement with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Funding supports healthcare organizations, providers, health systems, and partners serving rural Maryland communities in implementing innovative care delivery models and expanding access to behavioral health services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding provided through the Rural Health Transformation Program cooperative agreement with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to support rural health initiatives focused on service expansion, health information technology advances, behavioral health services, and innovative care delivery models in rural areas. Supports workforce recruitment and retention (with minimum five-year service obligation), infrastructure improvements and equipment upgrades, health information technology advances, behavioral health expansion initiatives, innovative care delivery models, and grow-your-own clinical workforce programs. Maximum administrative costs capped at 10% of total award. Infrastructure and equipment investments limited to 20% of total funding per budget period. Provider payments limited to 15% of total funding per budget period. Rural Tech Catalyst Fund limited to lesser of 10% or $20 million per state. Total funding of $50 billion ($25 billion baseline funding equally distributed to all recipients + $25 billion workload funding based on technical score).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Assigned Grants Management Specialist and Project Officer
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural healthcare organizations, providers, health systems, and partners serving rural Maryland communities. State governments, rural healthcare providers and facilities, clinical workforce, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service expansion, health information technology advances, behavioral health expansion, and innovative care delivery models in rural areas. Workforce recruitment and retention incentives (minimum 5-year commitment), training and education programs, infrastructure and equipment upgrades, telehealth and HIT advances, behavioral health services expansion, childcare facilities for clinical workforce, evaluation services, audits and payment integrity programs, minor renovations/alterations (≤20% of total funding per budget period with CMS approval), provider payments for health services (≤15% of total funding per budget period), electronic medical record (EMR) system replacement (max 5% if HITECH-certified system already in place as of September 1, 2025), Rural Tech Catalyst Fund initiatives (max 10% or $20 million of budget period funding). structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland WIC program is a federal nutrition assistance program that provides nutritious supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals to health and social services for eligible low-income pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding mothers, infants, and children up to age 5. The program helps young children grow up healthy and strong through food assistance and supportive services. Participants receive benefits that provide access to nutritious supplemental foods including infant formula, milk, cheese, eggs, beans, peanut butter, fruits, and vegetables through authorized WIC vendors via electronic benefits transfer (eWIC card) and through the MyBenefits system. The Maryland WIC mobile app (available on iOS and Android) and Client Portal at wicclientportal.health.maryland.gov provide convenient access to the program. WIC provides nutrition assistance to eligible individuals who meet income guidelines and have a nutritional need or medical risk factor. Nutrition counseling and health referrals support overall wellbeing and connect participants with community health and nutrition services. Benefits are issued monthly and can be used at authorized retailers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive monthly food benefits through a benefits card (administered via MyBenefits system or eWIC card) that can be used to purchase eligible WIC foods at authorized vendors. Benefits include access to nutritious supplemental foods such as infant formula, milk, cheese, eggs, beans, peanut butter, fruits, and vegetables. The program also provides nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals to health and social services. WIC benefits are available to eligible pregnant women, non-breastfeeding postpartum women, new mothers (up to six months after delivery), breastfeeding mothers (up to one year after delivery), infants, and children under age five. This program provides participants with healthy foods, nutrition counseling, and support for breastfeeding. It also connects families to other health services. Applicants can have a job or be unemployed, own a home or live with friends or relatives, be married or single, or be a father, mother, guardian, or grandparent applying for benefits for an infant or child under age five. Applicants can access the program through the Maryland WIC mobile app (available on iOS and Android), through the Client Portal at wicclientportal.health.maryland.gov, through the MyBenefits portal, or by contacting a local WIC agency.
structured_extraction.contact_email: wic@maryland.gov, wic.program@maryland.gov, wic.breastfeeding@maryland.gov, mdh.wic@maryland.gov, wicinfo@maryland.gov, mdh.wicvendor@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding mothers, new mothers (up to six months after delivery), nursing mothers (up to one year after birth), parents, caregivers, infants, and children up to age 5 who meet income and nutritional risk eligibility criteria. Can be a father, mother, guardian, or grandparent applying for benefits for an infant or child under age five. Must live in Maryland and have a medical or nutritional risk factor. Healthcare providers, store owners and vendors, and farmers may also interact with the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Benefits can be used to purchase nutritious supplemental foods at authorized WIC vendors and retailers including infant formula, milk, cheese, eggs, beans, peanut butter, and fresh fruits and vegetables. Approved foods for nutrition and food assistance through an eWIC card or MyBenefits system. Nutrition assistance, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support for eligible pregnant women, new mothers, breastfeeding mothers, nursing mothers, infants, and children under age five.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide throughout Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents. Specific local WIC agencies serve each county through local county health departments and agencies, with multiple office locations including Dundalk, Essex, Lansdowne, Reisterstown, Rosedale/White Marsh, Towson, and Woodlawn in Baltimore County. Apply through the WIC office in your county, via the Client Portal, or through local WIC clinics.
