structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for WIC, make an appointment with your local county WIC agency by calling 1-800-242-4WIC (1-800-242-4942), using the Client Portal at wicclientportal.health.maryland.gov, downloading the Maryland WIC application through the Maryland WIC mobile app (available on iOS and Android), contacting the WIC program by email, applying through the MyBenefits portal, or contacting a local WIC clinic. Bring each person applying for benefits to the first appointment, including infants and all children up to age five. Bring required documents for proof of household income, identity, and address. Baltimore County locations include Dundalk, Essex, Lansdowne, Reisterstown, Rosedale/White Marsh, Towson, and Woodlawn. Visit the resources link on the program page for additional information on how to join and access application details. A list of local agencies is available through the Maryland WIC Program. Applications are processed at the local agency level. County WIC offices will conduct eligibility determination based on income, residency, and nutritional need. Applicants can check their eligibility and schedule appointments using the program's online client portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, confidential phone, text, or web-based support service available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week to help Maryland residents age 13 and older quit tobacco and nicotine products, including vaping. The program provides trained tobacco cessation coaches who offer one-on-one counseling, personalized quit plans with quit dates, follow-up support and encouragement, web and text message services, and free nicotine replacement therapy (patches, gum, lozenges, inhalers) while supplies last. Specialized services are available for expectant and new parents, youth ages 13-17 through the Live Vape Free program, and pregnant individuals, with coaches speaking multiple languages including English and Spanish. Coaches address psychological, behavioral, and physical aspects of tobacco addiction and can refer participants to local resources and in-person cessation classes. Pregnant participants can enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation. Healthcare providers can refer patients through the Fax to Assist program or via email for HIPAA-compliant referrals with outcome reporting. The program helps develop quit plans, discuss health benefits of quitting, provide medicine options, and offer ongoing support with family and friend support strategies. Those currently in substance use disorder recovery treatment are also welcome.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free phone, web, and text message support available via phone (1-800-QUIT-NOW or 1-800-784-8669), text (READY to 34191), or online at quitnow.net/maryland. Youth ages 13-17 can also text VAPEFREE to 873-373 to enroll in the Live Vape Free program. Services include one-on-one counseling from trained coaches available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; personalized quit plans with quit dates; follow-up support and encouragement; web and text message support; free supply of nicotine replacement therapy (patches, gum, lozenges, inhalers) while supplies last; free educational booklets and printed and web-based self-help materials; referrals to local resources such as health department cessation classes or counseling; discussion of health benefits of quitting; medicine options explained and approved by a doctor; and family and friend support strategies. Intensive multi-call programs are available for youth ages 13-17 and pregnant women. Pregnant participants can enroll in a specialized incentive program to receive gift cards for participation while supplies last. Healthcare providers can refer patients through the Fax to Assist program or via email for HIPAA-compliant referrals with outcome reporting. Non-smokers can access information to help family members, friends, or patients quit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 13 and older who want to quit tobacco or nicotine products, including vaping. Specialized services available for youth ages 13-17, expectant parents, new parents, and pregnant individuals. Those currently in substance use disorder recovery treatment are also welcome. Healthcare providers can refer patients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tobacco cessation coaching, personalized quit planning, nicotine replacement therapy products, web-based and text message support, educational materials, gift card incentives for pregnant participants, referrals to local in-person cessation classes or counseling, and intensive multi-call programs for youth and pregnant women.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents age 13 and older.
requirements_list: Must be at least 13 years old
Must be a Maryland resident
Willingness to quit tobacco use
Must be willing to work with trained coaches on tobacco addiction
Interested in quitting tobacco
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can enroll by calling 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669), texting READY to 34191, or visiting https://quitnow.net/maryland to enroll online. Youth ages 13-17 can enroll in the Live Vape Free program by texting VAPEFREE to 873-373. Healthcare providers can refer patients through the Fax to Assist program or via email for HIPAA-compliant referrals with outcome reporting. Upon enrollment, callers receive free confidential counseling, a personalized quit plan with a quit date, follow-up support, and a free supply of nicotine replacement therapy while supplies last. Pregnant participants should register for the incentive program during their enrollment call. Typical calls last 15-25 minutes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded entitlement program administered by the Maryland Department of Health and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that provides childhood immunizations at no cost to eligible children ages birth to 18 years through enrolled healthcare providers throughout Maryland. The program removes cost as a barrier to vaccination by supplying vaccines to enrolled healthcare providers and administering them through public health clinics to eligible children, including those who are uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid-eligible, or American Indian/Alaska Native. Enrolled providers receive vaccines at no charge along with training on safe storage, handling, and federal compliance requirements. Vaccine administration fees are provided on a sliding scale based on family size and income, with no child denied vaccination based on inability to pay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Routine childhood vaccines recommended by ACIP and influenza vaccine during influenza season are provided at no cost to enrolled healthcare providers. Vaccines are shipped directly from McKesson Specialty distributor. Enrolled providers and physicians receive all routinely recommended vaccines free of cost to provide to eligible children. Practices receive vaccines at no charge and training on safe storage, handling, and federal compliance requirements. Public health clinics also provide childhood immunizations with vaccine administration fees on a sliding scale based on family size and income. No child is denied vaccination based on inability to pay the administration fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children 18 years of age or younger who are Maryland Medicaid recipients, uninsured, underinsured (have health insurance that does not cover vaccines), or American Indian/Alaskan Native. Enrolled medical practices and healthcare providers with responsible physicians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Routine recommended childhood immunizations and influenza vaccines for eligible children, including those who are uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid-eligible, or American Indian/Alaska Native.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at enrolled medical practices and healthcare provider offices.
requirements_list: Child must be 18 years old or younger
Child must be Maryland Medicaid eligible, uninsured, American Indian or Alaskan Native, underinsured (no vaccine coverage), or covered by Medical Assistance
Enrolled physician must have Maryland state license
EHR/EMR system required for newly enrolled providers
Digital data logger (DDL) with valid calibration certificate required for each vaccine storage unit plus backup
Stand-alone or pharmaceutical-grade vaccine storage units required
Annual educational training required for enrolled physician, practice contact, and backup contact
Must offer all medically appropriate ACIP-recommended vaccines to VFC-eligible patients
Vaccine administration data must be submitted within 7 days to ImmuNet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Healthcare providers can submit a letter of interest on business letterhead to mdh.izinfo@maryland.gov with specified information. VFC staff sends enrollment documents via email. A VFC Site Reviewer visits to verify compliance before vaccine shipment. Initial vaccine order is placed by VFC; thereafter bi-monthly orders are placed through the ImmuNet system.

structured_extraction.program_description: Behavioral health and veteran support services program providing care coordination, peer support, and referral services for US uniformed service members, veterans, and their families in Maryland. The program focuses on suicide prevention, lethal means safety, safety planning services, and supportive services for veteran families and housing stability support. Services are provided at no cost and are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers care coordination, peer support, referral services, suicide prevention, lethal means safety, safety planning, housing stability support, and supportive services for veteran families at no cost. Services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week through a toll-free phone line.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Service members (Active Duty, Guard and Reserve), veterans, transitioning service members, and their families in Maryland, regardless of discharge status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care coordination, peer support, referral to behavioral health and medical providers, community partners, and first responders. Suicide prevention, lethal means safety, safety planning, supportive services for veteran families, housing stability support, and educational opportunities for service members, veterans, and their families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to service members, veterans, and their families throughout Maryland with regional coordination across Eastern Shore, Southern, Central, and Western regions.
requirements_list: Must be a current or former US uniformed service member (Active Duty, Guard, or Reserve), a veteran, or a family member of such individuals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program by phone at 1-877-770-4801 to connect to services. Calls are accepted 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland's Mouths Matter Fluoride Varnish and Oral Health Screening Program for Kids
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide preventive oral health program that provides fluoride varnish treatments and oral health screenings for children to improve dental health outcomes and prevent tooth decay. Services are provided at no cost or reduced cost to eligible children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides fluoride varnish treatments and oral health screenings for eligible children at no cost or reduced cost through preventive oral health services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preventive oral health services including fluoride varnish applications and oral health screenings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland - statewide program

structured_extraction.program_name: Maternal, Infant and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides voluntary, evidence-based home visiting services for expectant parents, infants, young children, and their families. Trained professionals visit families at home to offer support and help families strengthen attachment, promote optimal child development and safety, and reduce the risk of child maltreatment. The program provides home visiting services to pregnant women and early children through evidence-based approaches.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides federal grant funding to support the implementation of evidence-based, voluntary family support programs. Funds support home visiting services, and up to 25% of funding can be allocated for 'promising' home visiting models, which must be rigorously evaluated. The program helps families strengthen bonds, promote child development and safety, and reduce the risk of child abuse.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Expectant parents, pregnant women, infants, young children, and their families, particularly those in at-risk communities in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support evidence-based home visiting programs. These programs aim to improve parenting skills, promote healthy child development, ensure child safety, strengthen family bonds, and provide support to pregnant women and early children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates statewide but prioritizes funding for communities identified as having the highest risk based on a statewide needs assessment.
requirements_list: Grants may only support evidence-based home visiting programs that meet specific federal criteria.
Up to 25% of funding can be allocated for 'promising' home visiting models, which must be rigorously evaluated.

structured_extraction.program_name: MedStar Franklin Square Hospital Diabetes/Food Security and Primary Care Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Addresses disparities in chronic disease, food access, and other health disparities for African-American residents. The program provides healthy food to patients, connects them to a dietician and Community Health Advocate, and delivers 20 hours of health education. Primary Care Center and Family Health Center services include access to primary care, specialty care, preventive services, and behavioral health assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $290,000 (Grant 23-001) to support program operations and services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Healthy food provision, dietician consultations, Community Health Advocate services, health education, primary care, specialty care, preventive services, and behavioral health assistance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_name: MedStar Good Samaritan Food Farmacy Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Designed for adult patients with Type 2 Diabetes who may be experiencing heart failure or food insecurity. Provides ongoing one-on-one care from Community Health Advocate and dietitian, customized healthy food for meal preparation at no cost, consultations, food storage capability, and safe food pickup and delivery. Connects patients to holistic health resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $93,000 (Grant 21-001) to support Food Farmacy program operations and community health services.

May have heart failure or food insecurity

structured_extraction.program_description: A group-based prenatal and postpartum care program for pregnant Medicaid members. Participants meet in groups of approximately 8-10 people who are due around the same time for 90-minute to two-hour visits. The program includes provider medical exams, group education sessions, and peer support covering topics such as pregnancy management, labor and delivery preparation, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy nutrition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free group-based prenatal and postpartum care provided through Medicaid Managed Care Organizations. The program includes medical exams, group education sessions, and peer support. Each visit lasts 90 minutes to two hours and covers topics such as pregnancy management, labor preparation, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and nutrition. The program is offered at no cost to eligible Medicaid members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals who are Maryland Medicaid members
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prenatal and postpartum care, medical exams, group education sessions covering pregnancy, labor, delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, nutrition, and stress management

Must be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO) using the phone number on your insurance card. Your MCO will help you find a CenteringPregnancy provider in your area and assist with enrollment in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing access to trained birth workers (doulas) who deliver physical, emotional, and informational support to pregnant individuals and birthing parents before, during, and after birth. Doulas offer prenatal visits, attendance at birth, and postpartum support focused on person-centered, culturally responsive care. Services include prenatal education and preparation, birth support and attendance, postpartum support, breastfeeding education, community resource information, and mental health and self-care support. All services are provided at no cost to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Doula services are provided at no cost to eligible Medicaid members. Services include three components: prenatal visits (typically in the birthing parent's home), attendance at birth, and postpartum visits. Prenatal and postpartum visits cover topics such as labor anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health and self-care, communication skills for medical appointments, breastfeeding education, and community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals and birthing parents who are Maryland Medicaid members, with emphasis on supporting racial, ethnic, and cultural diversity
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Doula services including prenatal support visits, birth attendance, and postpartum support. Services cover education on labor and birth, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health and self-care, communication skills, breastfeeding education, and community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland Medicaid members.

Must be pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO) to access doula services. Your MCO will connect you to a doula as soon as one becomes available and provide information about the services offered.

structured_extraction.program_description: An income-based, limited benefits plan providing free family planning and reproductive health services to Maryland residents who are not eligible for full Medicaid coverage. The program offers no premiums, deductibles, or copays for eligible services. Benefits include birth control in all forms (prescription, over-the-counter, IUD, implant, and emergency contraception), exams and counseling about birth control options, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), hepatitis, and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. Coverage can begin immediately upon eligibility determination.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free coverage for family planning services including birth control (prescription, over-the-counter, IUD, implant, and emergency contraception), exams and counseling about birth control options, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), hepatitis, and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. No premiums, deductibles, or copays for covered services. Program does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation. Coverage starts immediately upon approval.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-456-8900 (Pregnancy and Family Planning Helpline) or 1-855-642-8572 (Maryland Health Connection)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of all ages who are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens, meet the income limit for family planning eligibility, and do not qualify for full Medicaid coverage or other Medicaid programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family planning and reproductive health services including birth control (prescription, over-the-counter, IUD, implant, emergency contraception), exams and counseling about birth control options, screening tests for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), hepatitis, and HIV, cervical and breast cancer screening and diagnosis, and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. Program does not cover prenatal care, infertility services, or non-emergency medical transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents. Applicants must be a Maryland resident and U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen and meet income limits.

For specific application instructions and information, visit the apply page or call the Pregnancy and Family Planning Helpline at 1-800-456-8900 or Maryland Health Connection at 1-855-642-8572.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides resources, screenings, support, and services for healthy child development from birth to age 3. The program adds a child development specialist to the pediatric care team to work with families during health care visits, offering support on child growth, parenting resources, breastfeeding support, self-care, stress management, and mental health. Services include tracking child development, providing parenting resources and guidance, breastfeeding support, mental health and stress management guidance, and connecting families to additional resources like housing or transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free developmental screening and support services provided by a child development specialist working with the pediatric care team. Services are fully covered for eligible Medicaid members with no cost to participants. Services include tracking child development, providing parenting resources, breastfeeding support, stress management guidance, mental health resources, and connecting families to additional resources like housing or transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and families with children under three years old who are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child development support, parenting resources and guidance, breastfeeding support, mental health resources, stress management, and connections to community services such as housing and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Maryland Medicaid Managed Care Organizations to all Maryland Medicaid members.
requirements_list: Child must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Child must be newborn to under 4 years old
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is your Medicaid insurance plan. You can find their number on your insurance card. The MCO will help you find a HealthySteps provider in your area.

structured_extraction.program_description: Home Visiting Services provide support and teach parenting skills to pregnant people and birth parents before and after birth. Services are delivered by specially trained professionals or nurses who visit families in their homes to teach about child development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, nutrition, planning, and mental health support. Services continue after pregnancy up to the child's second or third birthday depending on the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home Visiting Services are free for eligible Medicaid members. Services are provided by specially trained professionals or nurses who conduct home visits to support pregnant people and families with young children. Two evidence-based home visiting models are offered: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership. The type of services and home visitor is tailored to family needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant people and birth parents who are Maryland Medicaid members
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visits to teach parenting skills, child development, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, planning for the future, and mental health and stress control support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland Medicaid members
requirements_list: Be a Maryland Medicaid member
Be pregnant or have delivered a child within three months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Reach out to your Managed Care Organization (MCO). Your health care provider or health plan can help find the right home visiting program for you.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state Medicaid program that provides health coverage and financial assistance for community-based care to older adults who meet medical and financial criteria. The program supports individuals who would otherwise require nursing home placement, with waivers available for either assisted living or in-home care services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance and health coverage through Medicaid for community-based care including assisted living or in-home care services for eligible older adults who would otherwise require nursing home placement.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assisted living or in-home care services and health coverage.

Would otherwise require nursing home care
Must be eligible for Medicaid

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to licensed medical day care centers. The centers use the funds to offer health, social, and support services to functionally disabled adults. This helps individuals stay in their homes and communities instead of moving to a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides contracts to licensed adult day care providers. The state sets the payment rates for these services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Day care centers are under contract 7/1/16 - 6/30/21.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the delivery of health, social, and related support services in a structured group setting for functionally disabled adults.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Health Departments submit yearly budgets. Day care centers operate under contract with the state.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home and community-based services waiver that provides medical day care services in a community-based setting as an alternative to nursing facility care. The program helps individuals get services and support in their home and community instead of in an institution. Services include skilled nursing and nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, nutrition services, social work services, activity programs, daily living skills training, therapy, personal care, and transportation. All Medicaid-covered services and benefits are included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides medical day care services for at least four hours a day, up to seven days a week, delivered by licensed medical day care providers. Services include activity programs, meals, medication monitoring, nutrition services, skilled nursing and nursing assessments, social work services, therapy, personal care, and transportation. All Medicaid-covered services and benefits are also included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 16 or older who need nursing facility level of care, have full Medicaid coverage, and are not enrolled in another home and community-based waiver.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Skilled nursing and nursing assessments, medication monitoring, meals, nutrition services, social work services, activity programs, daily living skills training, therapy, personal care, and transportation. All Medicaid-covered services and benefits are also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local health departments and Maryland Access Point.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medications for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD) Training and Mentoring
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free training and mentoring services for eligible healthcare providers to effectively use buprenorphine and other medications to treat opioid use disorder in high-need communities. Completion of the training will count toward meeting MATE Act training requirements for practitioners registering for or renewing a DEA license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training and mentoring services for healthcare providers on using buprenorphine and other medications to treat opioid use disorder in high-need communities

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and mentoring for opioid use disorder treatment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Microsoft Cybersecurity Program for Rural Hospitals
structured_extraction.program_description: The program offers assistance to help rural hospitals keep their health services safe and secure with affordable access to Microsoft security solutions and building cybersecurity capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Affordable access to Microsoft security solutions and technical assistance for building cybersecurity capacity
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural hospitals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity solutions and capacity building

structured_extraction.program_description: This office works to end health differences among population groups. It uses state resources, offers expert advice on health fairness, and helps shape policies and communications to improve health for all.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The office provides project grants and technical assistance. Specific grant programs include the Minority Outreach and Technical Assistance (MOTA) and Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and individuals working to reduce health disparities in Maryland. This includes government bodies, non-profits, for-profits, and higher education institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that address social factors affecting health and aim to eliminate health disparities among different population groups.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should call the office for information on the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community-based health education and health promotion program targeting racial and ethnic minority populations and other disadvantaged populations in Maryland. The program focuses on six key health areas: asthma, cardiovascular disease, cancer, obesity/diabetes/prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health. Services include general health education, longitudinal health promotion programming for enrolled participants, outreach, technical assistance, community engagement, partnerships, and linkage to care. The program supports community health worker outreach and engagement to reduce health inequity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 18 competitive grant awards ranging from $25,000 to $75,000 for one-year funding period (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027). Funding is reimbursement-based with no advance/startup payments available. Optional second-year continuation contingent on satisfactory performance, with non-competitive renewal option available for FY 2028. structured_extraction.program_description: Performance-based incentive program for nursing facilities based on staffing measures, resident satisfaction, MDS outcomes, and staff immunization rates. Facilities are ranked on overall performance, P4P eligibility, and improvement metrics. One percent of the Medicaid nursing facility budget is distributed annually, with 85 percent going to top-performing facilities and 15 percent to facilities showing improvement from the previous year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Facilities receive financial awards based on performance score (P4P) or improvement score (P4I) across measurement categories including staffing levels (20-35 points), staffing stability (15 points), resident satisfaction survey (30 points), MDS outcomes (30 points), and staff immunization rates (5 points). Facilities receive a $/MA Day rate multiplied by Medicaid days for total award. One percent of the Program's nursing facility budget is awarded each year. Facilities cannot receive both P4P and P4I awards simultaneously. Awards are distributed as cash payments that facilities can use at their discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nursing facilities participating in Medicaid with 45 or more beds that are not continuing care retirement centers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct payments to facilities based on performance metrics. Facilities that achieve high performance scores on quality indicators receive cash awards. Funds can be used at the facility's discretion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all nursing facilities throughout Maryland that participate in Medicaid
requirements_list: Have 45 or more beds
Are not continuing care retirement centers (CCRCs)
Participate in Medicaid
In the previous year ending March 31, must not have been identified as a federally-designated special focus facility
Must not have had a denial of payment for new admissions (DPNA) by CMS in the previous year ending March 31
Must not have been determined to have provided substandard quality of care as defined in federal Medicaid regulations
Maintain minimum staffing levels based on acuity
Achieve benchmark scores on resident satisfaction surveys
Meet MDS outcome measures
Maintain staff immunization rates greater than 90%
Submit required cost reports and MDS data
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nursing facilities are automatically evaluated based on data submitted to the Maryland Department of Health including cost reports, payroll data, wage surveys, MDS submissions, and MHCC resident satisfaction survey responses. Performance is assessed using staffing levels, staff stability, MDS quality indicators, family satisfaction survey responses, and staff immunization rates. Facilities receive scores and are ranked. Top-performing facilities receive 85 percent of the award pool, and most-improved facilities receive 15 percent. Awards are distributed accordingly. No traditional application process is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health authorizes organizations as OADPOPs (formerly known as Syringe Services Programs) to provide a wide range of harm reduction and substance use disorder services. Services include needle and syringe distribution and collection, infectious disease prevention, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery services, case management, HIV, hepatitis C, and STD testing, PrEP/PEP, reproductive health education, wound care, overdose prevention education, naloxone distribution, fentanyl, xylazine, medetomidine, and benzodiazepine testing strips, medication for opioid use disorder, personal care kits, food access referrals, housing and emergency shelter access, telehealth services, and emergency shelter access at select sites. Technical assistance and support are provided to approved programs by the MDH Office of Overdose Prevention & Education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health authorizes and provides technical assistance, guidance, and support to approved organizations to operate as OADPOPs. There are 30 authorized OADPOPs in 21 counties across Maryland. Organizations receive authorization and support to provide sterile injection supplies, counseling, testing, treatment referrals, and overdose prevention education. Authorized organizations provide on-site and off-site/referral services including needle and syringe distribution and collection, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery services, case management, HIV and hepatitis C testing, overdose prevention education, naloxone distribution, fentanyl, xylazine, medetomidine, and benzodiazepine testing strips, wound care, reproductive health education and services, PrEP/PEP, medication for opioid use disorder, personal care kits, food access referrals, housing and emergency shelter access, telehealth services, immunizations, and mental health service referrals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking approval to operate an OADPOP, including local health departments and community-based organizations; people who use drugs seeking access to services; individuals seeking substance use disorder treatment and recovery services; those needing infectious disease prevention services; vulnerable and underserved populations; individuals at risk of opioid-related disease and overdose; unhoused individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating an authorized OADPOP to provide hypodermic needle and syringe distribution and collection, substance use disorder counseling, treatment and recovery services, case management, HIV, hepatitis C, and STD testing, PrEP/PEP, reproductive health education and services, wound care, overdose prevention education and naloxone distribution, fentanyl, xylazine, medetomidine, and benzodiazepine testing strips, medication for opioid use disorder, personal care kits, emergency shelter access and housing assistance, food access referrals, telehealth services, immunizations, mental health services, and related harm reduction services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. There are 30 authorized OADPOPs operating in 21 counties across the state. Programs may be located in local health departments or community-based organizations throughout the state. Applicants must specify jurisdictions where they propose to operate. Community-based organizations may establish multi-county programs with approval from all involved local health officers.
requirements_list: Must be a local health department or community-based organization
Must submit an application using the web form provided by the Maryland Department of Health
Must read and follow the OADPOP Application Guidance document thoroughly before submitting an application
Must be authorized by the Maryland Department of Health to operate as an OADPOP
Must comply with Maryland Health-General §24-901 to 909 and COMAR 10.52.01.01-10.52.01.09
Must develop program operating procedures for needle/syringe distribution, collection, and disposal
Must provide community outreach and education plan
Must establish referral protocols to substance abuse treatment, HIV/viral hepatitis/STI testing, reproductive health services, and wound care
Must maintain staff expertise in harm reduction and working with injection drug users
Must comply with Department-approved staff training requirements
Must maintain confidentiality per Health-General Article §24-906(b)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs seeking approval to operate an OADPOP must complete the following application process: (1) Review the OADPOP Application Guidance document thoroughly, (2) Complete and submit an application using the web form at https://www.cognitoforms.com/mdh3/syringeservicesprogramapplication, (3) Contact MDH for more information about the program, application, and requirements at mdh.syringeservices@maryland.gov. The Office of Overdose Prevention & Education (OPE) reviews applications, manages program reporting, issues program guidance, and provides technical assistance and support to approved programs. Programs whose approval is revoked may appeal in writing to the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services within 30 calendar days of the revocation notice postmark date; the Deputy Secretary responds within 60 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Statewide Maryland program providing free naloxone distribution and overdose education through approved entities. Services include naloxone kits, fentanyl test strips, xylazine test strips, benzodiazepine test strips, medetomidine test strips, overdose education, and comprehensive harm reduction services. Multiple service delivery models include fixed sites, vending machines, mobile/outreach services, and mail delivery. Additional services may include syringe services, wound care, HCV/HIV testing, HIV PrEP/PEP, medication for opioid use disorder, substance use disorder counseling and treatment, housing assistance, food access, personal care kits, telehealth services, and RAD (Rapid Analysis of Drugs) testing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free naloxone kits with overdose education and training. Mail delivery of naloxone available in certain Maryland counties. Off-site or referral services: housing assistance, food access, HIV PrEP/PEP, medication for opioid use disorder, substance use disorder treatment and recovery services, case management, peer support, and telehealth services. Access available through fixed sites, 24/7 and limited-hours vending machines, mobile outreach, and mail delivery.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at risk of opioid overdose; people who use drugs; people with substance use disorders; unhoused individuals; incarcerated individuals; community members seeking overdose education and naloxone access; anyone can obtain naloxone without a prescription or proof of certification.

requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
For mail delivery: reside in a participating county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To obtain naloxone in person: locate a public Overdose Response Program using the interactive map or PDF list provided on the Maryland Department of Health website. Contact the program and visit in person. To receive naloxone by mail: use the interactive map to find an ORP offering mail delivery service, or contact a nearby ORP to ask if they offer mail delivery. No prescription, certification, or training required. Access available during program hours or via 24/7 vending machines at select locations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Promoting Food Security, Reducing Obesity, and Addressing Diabetes
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive statewide grant program that funds 45 grantee organizations across Maryland to address health disparities related to food security, obesity, and diabetes. The program supports various interventions including diabetes prevention and management programs, chronic disease screening and management, food security and nutrition education initiatives, and health education services targeted at vulnerable and underserved populations. Services include community health worker outreach, diabetes self-management education, nutrition counseling, food access initiatives, care coordination, mobile clinics, telehealth services, and addressing social determinants of health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $1,600,000 awarded to nonprofit organizations, government agencies, health care providers, health departments, and community organizations to expand access to diabetes prevention, management, food security, and health education services. Funding supports staffing for community health workers, equipment, program implementation, nutrition education, food distribution, mobile clinics, telehealth services, care coordination, and comprehensive health services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and underserved populations; individuals with diabetes, prediabetes, or obesity; racial and ethnic minorities; unhoused and housing insecure individuals; seniors; immigrants and limited English proficiency populations; children in Title I schools; vulnerable homebound individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Diabetes prevention and management programs; food security and nutrition education; community health worker salaries and training; chronic disease screening and testing; mobile health clinics and telehealth services; care coordination and case management; lifestyle interventions including fitness programs and cooking demonstrations; addressing social determinants of health; emergency department diversion through better disease management; transportation assistance; food distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through 45 grantee organizations serving multiple counties and regions including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Washington, Cecil, Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Allegany, Garrett, and Calvert counties. Some programs target specific communities or zip codes within their jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Providing Dental Care for Low-income Children and Adults Grants (51 Grants)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that funds dental care expansion projects across all Maryland counties. Through 51 individual grants, this program supports non-profit organizations and health departments in expanding access to preventative, diagnostic, emergency, and restorative dental services for low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and other underserved residents, including Medicaid beneficiaries, homeless individuals, individuals in recovery from substance use disorders, and undocumented populations. Individual grant amounts range from $10,000 to $745,000, with each grant supporting specific organizations and jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual grants ranging from $10,000 to $745,000 awarded to community health centers, health departments, and nonprofit organizations to expand dental care capacity. Funding supports staff salaries (dentists, dental hygienists, dental assistants, case managers, community health workers), dental equipment and supplies, facility expansion and relocation, patient transportation, health insurance enrollment assistance, case management and care coordination, oral health education, and direct dental services including preventative, diagnostic, emergency, and restorative care. Grant amounts are specific to each grantee organization and jurisdiction served.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, health departments, community health centers, hospitals, and other health-related entities seeking to expand dental care services. Beneficiaries include low-income children and adults, uninsured individuals, Medicaid beneficiaries, homeless individuals, individuals in recovery from substance use disorders, undocumented populations, and other underserved residents in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports staff salaries (dentists, dental hygienists, dental assistants, case managers, community health workers), dental equipment and supplies, facility expansion and relocation, patient transportation, health insurance enrollment assistance, case management and care coordination, oral health education, dental services delivery (preventative, diagnostic, emergency, and restorative care), and program administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: An internship program designed to introduce students to roles within public health and expose them to different subject areas. The program provides practical experience to enhance knowledge gained from studies and prepare interns to enter the public health workforce. Students work in various departments of the Maryland Department of Health including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications. Specific internship tracks include data modernization, epidemiology (with focus on viral hepatitis), infectious disease surveillance, healthcare administration, health education, and health policy positions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship positions offering hands-on work experience in public health. Students receive hourly wages: $17.15 per hour for undergraduate students and $20.15 per hour for graduate students. The Summer 2026 cohort runs from June 3 to August 11, 2026. Fall 2024 cohort internships available across multiple specialties including epidemiology, health informatics, healthcare administration, health education, infectious disease, and health policy. Positions provide resume experience, skill development in data management, statistical analysis (SAS, Tableau), program development, and practical training in public health specialties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate students with completion of at least 60 credit hours, graduate students enrolled at accredited colleges or universities in good academic standing, recent graduates from undergraduate or graduate programs, current students (junior/senior level), Master's in Public Health or Public Policy degree holders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship positions in various public health specialties including behavioral science, biostatistics, community health, epidemiology, health education, health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, infectious disease, preparedness and response, public health accreditation, and public health communications. Specific work includes data visualization development, epidemiological profiling, health equity intervention support, data modernization, outbreak investigation, surveillance, program development, and healthcare regulatory compliance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available statewide to students enrolled at accredited colleges or universities. Primary internship locations include Baltimore, Maryland (Baltimore City), with some positions in Catonsville, Sykesville, and Prince George's County. No geographic restriction is stated for student location.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rare and Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The REM program is a voluntary Medicaid program that provides medical case management and other services for eligible individuals with specific rare and expensive medical conditions. The program helps participants develop care plans, find needed services, and access specialized medical support through an assigned case manager. Services include needs assessment, care plan development, application assistance, service monitoring and plan adjustments, education and information, and covered services such as certified nursing assistant services, home health aide services, chiropractic services, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, private duty nursing shift services, nutrition counseling and supplements. All standard Medicaid covered services and benefits are included.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides medical case management services including needs assessment, care plan development, help applying for services, ongoing monitoring and plan adjustments, education and information, as well as covered services such as certified nursing assistant services, home health aide services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, chiropractic services, and private duty nursing shift services. All standard Medicaid covered services and benefits are included.

The program develops a formalized referral process for patients with urgent oral health needs and aims to provide a permanent dental home for patients at Chase Brexton while reducing avoidable dental-related emergency department visits. structured_extraction.program_name: Reducing Avoidable ED Visits and Promoting Care in the Community - Johns Hopkins School of Medicine Prince George's County Sickle Cell Disease Project
structured_extraction.program_description: This project addresses disparities associated with the high prevalence of sickle cell disease and lack of access to a local comprehensive sickle cell project in Prince George's County, with specific focus on Upper Marlboro, Laurel, and Capital Heights. The project aims to reduce the number of adults who present to UMCP hospital for acute pain requiring hospital admission, and to improve access to sickle cell disease modifying treatment and transition services for adolescents and young adults to reduce hospitalizations. The comprehensive sickle cell project includes a new infusion clinic at UM Capital Region Medical Center. Community health workers identify participants who lack resources to facilitate access, coordinate their care, and provide sickle cell disease education. A nurse navigator facilitates interventions to address social determinants of health needs, and a nutritionist develops individualized food plans for each participant.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland, with focus on Upper Marlboro (zip code 20773), Laurel (zip code 20707), and Capital Heights (zip code 20743).

structured_extraction.program_name: Reducing Avoidable ED Visits and Promoting Care in the Community - Total Health Care
structured_extraction.program_description: One-year grant supporting a program with Total Health Care to reduce emergency department visits for non-emergency conditions by clients accessing Maryland General Hospital's emergency department. Placed Outreach Coordinators in the hospital's emergency department during peak usage hours to educate patients on appropriate emergency department use and assist patients in connecting with a primary care provider in the community. Program reported an 8% reduction in emergency department visits at Maryland General Hospital from the year prior to grant implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $100,250 (Grant 08-022) for a one-year project placing outreach coordinators in Maryland General Hospital's emergency department to educate patients on appropriate emergency department use and connect them with primary care providers in the community. Staffing, patient education, and primary care provider linkage services included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City individuals accessing Maryland General Hospital emergency department for non-emergency conditions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach coordinator salaries and operations; patient education on appropriate emergency department use; primary care provider connection and referral services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland (Maryland General Hospital)

structured_extraction.program_name: Reducing Avoidable ED Visits and Promoting Care in the Community - University of Maryland Upper Chesapeake Health Harford County

Provides case management and linkages to community supports, culturally competent diabetes self-management education, diabetes prevention education, and peer support including virtual and Spanish language support groups for individuals with diabetes and their families.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management and community support linkages; culturally competent diabetes self-management education; diabetes prevention education; virtual and Spanish language peer support groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Reducing Avoidable ED Visits and Promoting Care in the Community - Wicomico County Health Department EMS Mobile Integrated Health Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Two-year project aiming to reduce preventable 911 calls through the use of a team consisting of an emergency medical technician and a registered nurse. The team identifies frequent callers to 911 for non-emergent conditions and conducts welfare checks, case management, safety planning, and refers patients to primary care physicians, medical specialists, and in-home care providers. The program offers potential to reduce avoidable EMS and hospital utilization services and is replicable in other rural areas of the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $90,000 (Grant 18-006) to fund a two-year project consisting of an emergency medical technician and registered nurse team to identify frequent 911 callers for non-emergent conditions and provide welfare checks, case management, safety planning, and referrals to primary care physicians, medical specialists, and in-home care providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wicomico County residents who frequently call 911 for non-emergent conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency medical technician and registered nurse team salary and operations; welfare checks; case management; safety planning; referrals to primary care and medical specialists; in-home care provider connections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland; 108 E. Main Street, Salisbury, MD 21801

structured_extraction.program_description: Workforce development program that advances training, reduces stigma, increases understanding of trauma and trauma-informed approaches, and supports linkages to behavioral health and quality care for people who use drugs. The program trains Master Presenters to sustainably disseminate information to the broader community and federally qualified health centers. It measures community and workforce stigma levels using the Shatterproof Addiction Stigma Index. Free, on-demand training courses cover topics including Adverse Childhood Experiences, Medications for Addiction Treatment as Overdose Prevention, Comprehensive Care Framework for People Who Use Drugs, Social Determinants of Health, and Stages of Change.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free, on-demand training courses available through an online platform. Courses cover topics including Adverse Childhood Experiences, Medications for Addiction Treatment as Overdose Prevention, Comprehensive Care Framework for People Who Use Drugs, Social Determinants of Health, and Stages of Change. The program also provides technical assistance, supports Master Presenter training, and measures stigma levels to support workforce development and community education efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Healthcare providers, federally qualified health center staff, community members, and workforce professionals serving people who use drugs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance on harm reduction, addiction treatment, trauma-informed approaches, and social determinants of health
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Regrounding Our Response website to access free, on-demand training courses. Contact the program email for technical assistance, Master Presenter training information, or more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reminders for Stroke Risk Identification: Transcranial Doppler (TCD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps parents schedule and keep track of yearly transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasound screenings for children with sickle cell disease. The TCD scans check blood flow in the brain to identify children at high risk for stroke, allowing early intervention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reminders and support to parents to ensure that eligible children receive annual TCD screening tests. The program helps coordinate scheduling and keeps families informed about the importance of these tests.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and caregivers of children ages 2 to 16 years old with certain types of sickle cell disease.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance. It provides scheduling reminders and support services to ensure children receive recommended TCD screening tests.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for eligible children with sickle cell disease.
requirements_list: Child must be between 2 and 16 years old
Child must have certain types of sickle cell disease
Family must enroll in the program to receive reminders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can enroll in the program by emailing [email protected] or calling (410) 614-0052. Program staff will provide reminders to schedule annual TCD screening appointments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year federal funding initiative to strengthen and modernize health care in rural areas across Maryland while improving access to healthy, locally sourced food. The program supports health care access and affordability by enhancing the health workforce pipeline, implementing innovative care models and technology advances, and creating post-harvest infrastructure for small farms to increase access to healthy fresh food in rural communities. Funding supports health workforce training and retention programs, clinical provider and allied health professional apprenticeships, sustainable access initiatives, innovative care models, technology advances, post-harvest infrastructure development for small farms, food system aggregation infrastructure, regional food hub development, local foods purchasing strategies, nutrition education, and regional coordination to address food insecurity in rural communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funding through cooperative agreement for rural health transformation initiatives. Supports clinical workforce recruitment and retention (with 5-year service commitment), infrastructure improvements (minor renovations capped at 20%), equipment, training, telehealth capabilities, childcare support, transportation assistance, and related rural health initiatives. Administrative costs capped at 10%. Funds cannot supplant existing federal, state, or local funding or duplicate other programs. Total $50 billion funding ($25 billion baseline + $25 billion workload-based) distributed across multiple budget periods spanning December 29, 2025 – October 30, 2030.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase 1 – Call for Letter of Intent Deadline: Friday, May 15, 2026; Phase 2 – Full Application Due: Friday, July 10, 2026; Non-Competing Continuation (NCC) applications due 60 days before end of current budget period (Budget Period 1 NCC due: August 30, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state government administering rural health transformation initiatives, rural healthcare providers and facilities, clinical workforce in rural areas, small farms, food system organizations, regional food hubs, local food producers, retailers, rural communities, and entities seeking to improve access to healthy, locally sourced food in rural communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clinical workforce recruitment and retention with 5-year rural service commitment; workforce training, certifications, and education programs; minor renovations and repurposing of existing buildings (capped at 20%); special purpose medical equipment; childcare facilities for clinical workforce; telehealth equipment and infrastructure; infrastructure and capital expenditures (up to 20% cap per budget period); workforce incentives including relocation assistance, travel subsidies, recruitment and retention bonuses; program evaluation and administrative costs (capped at 10%); health workforce development; innovative care models; technology advances; post-harvest infrastructure for small farms; food system aggregation infrastructure; regional food hubs; local foods purchasing strategies; nutrition education; institutional procurement of local foods by schools and hospitals; regional planning and coordination; EMR system replacement (up to 5% if previous HITECH system in place); provider payments for clinical services (up to 15% per budget period with justification); technology initiatives (up to 10% or $20M); equipment and supplies; travel per Federal Travel Regulations; indirect costs; IRB review costs; cybersecurity planning and implementation. Prohibited uses: pre-award costs, construction or building expansion, clinician salaries with non-compete clauses, duplicate payments for billable clinical services, lobbying, covered telecommunications/video surveillance equipment, cosmetic upgrades, independent R&D costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with focus on rural areas within the state. Eighteen of 24 Maryland jurisdictions are recognized as rural: Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Priority for rural food insecurity hot spot areas as defined by the Rural Health Transformation Program. Clinicians benefiting from recruitment/retention initiatives must practice within Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shepherd's Clinic EMPOWER Project - Reducing Avoidable ED Visits and Promoting Care in the Community
structured_extraction.program_description: The EMPOWER project aims to control hypertension and prevent cardiovascular complications among Black residents of Baltimore City who have a higher comparative rate of uncontrolled hypertension. Interventions include utilizing remote patient monitoring, training and diversifying the care team, expanding current social determinants of health resources, and deploying community health workers for community blood pressure screenings. Community hypertension education is provided, and patients are offered wellness services such as yoga and meditation classes, nutrition counseling, cooking demonstrations, and gardening tips. The project addresses social determinants of health needs including food security, transportation, health literacy education, and language services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant award of $460,000 to support hypertension control and cardiovascular disease prevention through remote patient monitoring, care team training and diversification, community health worker deployment and blood pressure screenings, hypertension education, and wellness services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Remote patient monitoring equipment; care team training and expansion; community health worker deployment for blood pressure screenings; hypertension education; wellness services including yoga, meditation, nutrition counseling, cooking demonstrations, and gardening tips; addressing social determinants of health including food security, transportation, health literacy, and language services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Maryland

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conducting annual random unannounced inspections of tobacco retailers; ensuring compliance with federal Synar Amendment and 2024 Tobacco Retailer Modernization Act requirements; monitoring compliance with age verification and product storage standards; preventing youth access to tobacco products; enforcing retailer compliance standards through follow-up inspections

structured_extraction.program_description: A monthly WIC benefit that provides eligible participants with funds to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables. Children receive $26 per month, pregnant women receive $47 per month, and breastfeeding mothers receive $52 per month. structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development in partnership with the Maryland Department of Aging that provides zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years and grants to help homeowners age 55 and older finance accessibility improvements to their homes. The program enables aging in place through modifications such as grab bars, railings, widened doorways, ramps, accessible showers, lever handles, and modifications to accommodate first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms. County-specific programming is available through local departments of aging, including Frederick County and Baltimore County. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property, though deferral may continue if transferred to a family member who occupies it as their primary residence. If the borrower still lives in the home at the end of 30 years and cannot repay, the deferral period can be extended. If the original borrower dies and a family member occupies the home as their principal residence, the loan is not immediately due. Grants up to $25,000 are available to senior homeowners who do not qualify for loan funding. The program is available statewide through local County Housing Offices, Area Offices on Aging, and Maryland Access Point Agencies, including all 19 local Area Offices on Aging. In Frederick County and Baltimore County, special loans with interest rates based on household income are also available for single family and small rental properties, with deferred payment options for lower-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for terms of up to 30 years with anticipated loan amounts of $10,000 to $15,000, and maximum loan amount up to 110 percent of property value (accounting for superior mortgages). Loans are available for up to 85 percent of the property value. There is no set loan limit in some cases. Interest rates range from 0% to 6.0% depending on income level. Monthly payments are not required during the deferral period but can be arranged at the homeowner's request. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property, though the deferral continues if transferred to a family member who continues to live there as primary residence. If the borrower still lives in the home at the end of 30 years and cannot repay, the deferral period can be extended. If the original borrower dies and a family member occupies the home as their principal residence, the loan is not immediately due, though interest rates may increase based on income limits. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loan is satisfied as a lien on the property. Grants up to $25,000 are available to senior homeowners who do not qualify for loan funding, and may include lead hazard reduction component. In Frederick County and Baltimore County, special loans with interest rates based on household income are available, with loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments secured by a mortgage. Deferred payment of principal and interest is available for households with income below 50 percent of Washington, D.C. MSA median income or subject to specific county income limits. If refinancing is done without cash-out, repayment is not required. Baltimore County income limits: single person $6,079/month maximum; two people $6,950/month maximum.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their home as their principal residence and wish to make accessibility improvements to remain in their homes and enable aging in place. Low and moderate-income families and seniors seeking accessible home improvements. Homeowners in Baltimore County and Frederick County age 55 and up seeking accessibility improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Actual costs of making the house accessible or functional for the resident, including widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, lever handles, adding first floor laundry facilities or bathrooms, changing door and sink hardware to lever handles, adding bedrooms and bathrooms on the main level, rehabilitation, energy conservation, handicapped accessibility, plumbing, wells, sewer, and lead hazard reduction. Up to 40 percent may be used for general property improvements including kitchen and bathroom remodeling, carpeting, and landscaping. Additions for caregivers are considered on a case-by-case basis. Can also fund essential home repairs through the related Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Loan Program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents. Income limits vary by geographic area (Washington DC PMSA vs. Rest of State) and household size, ranging from 30% to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). The household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the Statewide or Washington DC MSA median, except in Baltimore County and Frederick County where specific income limits apply. In Frederick County and Baltimore County, availability includes single family and small rental properties. Applications are available through local County Housing Offices, Area Offices on Aging, and Maryland Access Point Agencies throughout the state, including all 19 local Area Offices on Aging.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices, Area Offices on Aging, or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency, and in-home appointments can be scheduled. Applicants can also call Senior Information and Assistance at 410-887-2594 to apply and learn more. In Frederick County, applicants should contact the Frederick County Division of Housing or their local Area Office on Aging. In Baltimore County, applicants should contact the Baltimore County Department of Aging. After submission, the application is processed by the department and the applicant is contacted. Once approved, DHCD staff or local government housing network staff will inspect the property and prepare a work write-up listing all work to be done. The homeowner obtains bids from contractors, hires the contractor of their choice, and work is inspected and authorized for payment as it progresses. DHCD sends two-party checks made to both homeowner and contractor.

structured_extraction.program_description: A revitalization tool established by State legislation to fund projects that build on the strengths of Baltimore City and surrounding communities. The initiative targets existing communities that have experienced physical, economic, or social decline, demonstrating how strategic investment in local housing and businesses can lead to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have appreciable neighborhood revitalization impact, supporting community and economic development projects in the Baltimore region targeting specific neighborhood improvements. The initiative provides $20 million in capital and $2 million in operating funding available for eligible projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide effort designed to eliminate vacant properties, strengthen neighborhoods, and increase access to homeownership. The program provides grants and loans to public and nonprofit partners to acquire, stabilize, rehabilitate, demolish and other pre-development activities, clearing the way for new green space, affordable housing and mixed-use developments. The program features a $30 million statewide funding pool for fiscal year 2026, with funding drawn as redevelopment milestones are completed in a performance-based structure. Organizations can use funds to acquire, stabilize, and renovate vacant buildings, buy and combine vacant lots for new housing or community green space, and conduct urgent demolition and pre-development work.

The program offers financing for projects that address vacant properties, including acquisition, stabilization, renovation, demolition, and pre-development activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide financing program that provides unsecured loans to Maryland homeowners to improve energy efficiency and comfort by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling (HVAC) systems, windows, doors, insulation, weatherproofing, and other whole-house envelope improvements. Up to $30,000 in financing is available with terms up to 10 years at 6.99% APR (minimum loan amount $5,000). The loan is unsecured and based on verification of credit and ability to pay. Licensed and insured contractors can participate by helping homeowners finance their projects. Homeowners can save on their utility bills.

The loan is based on verification of credit and ability to pay. Approved energy-saving upgrades include replacement and upgrade of appliances, HVAC systems, windows, doors, insulation, weatherproofing, whole-house envelope improvements, ENERGY STAR equipment, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic (capped at 1:1 match to energy efficiency measure costs), lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, and ceiling and ventilation fans. Up to 25% of energy measure costs can be used for health and safety improvements necessary for the energy improvements. Licensed and insured contractors must provide W-9 Form, Certificate of Insurance, and MD HVACR License or MHIC License.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrants program, offered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, provides direct grant funding to support small businesses seeking to expand their business or establish a commercial location. structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding awarded through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to support recovery activities following Hurricane Sandy in October 2012. Provides funding for housing rehabilitation, replacement housing, and economic recovery in disaster-affected areas, targeting low and moderate income households and small businesses impacted by Hurricane Sandy. The program received $8.6 million in federal funding to help communities recover from storm damage including heavy rains, high winds, snow, and coastal flooding.

All funding supports housing, infrastructure, and other recovery activities authorized under the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act.
