structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides state tax credit allocations to qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to support local projects and services. Donors who contribute $500 or more to a qualified nonprofit organization receive tax credits equal to 50% of the value of their contribution, in addition to standard charitable deductions. These credits represent a dollar-for-dollar reduction of Maryland state income tax owed. Nonprofits receive allocations of state tax credits that they can use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services. Projects can be capital and/or operating and typically involve activities such as education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, enhancing neighborhoods and business districts, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Donors also receive the standard charitable contribution deduction on both Maryland and federal tax returns.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donors (individuals and businesses) that contribute $500 or more to a qualified 501(c)(3) organization's approved project(s) earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of money, goods, or real property contributions. These tax credits are in addition to deductions on both Federal and State taxes and reduce Maryland state income tax liability dollar-for-dollar. Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made. The credit is claimed by attaching a Tax Credit Certificate (Form 502CR for individuals, Form 500CR for businesses and financial institutions) to the tax return. For example, a $2,000 donation generates $1,000 in tax credits. Donations can be made by check, online, or approved in-kind contributions including real property. Nonprofit organizations receive allocations of state tax credits to support operating and capital projects across community development. Technical assistance and training resources including videos and FAQs are provided to assist applicants.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating involving education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, enhancing neighborhoods and business districts, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Donations can be made by check, online, or approved in-kind contributions including real property.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofit organizations apply annually through a competitive application process via the Application Portal. The organization certifies the donation to the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development, which sends the donor a Tax Credit Certificate. At tax filing time, the donor attaches the certificate to their Maryland tax return (Form 502CR for individuals or Form 500CR for businesses/financial institutions) and claims the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that supports a range of direct services designed to assist low-income individuals and families with achieving self-sufficiency through a network of Community Action Agencies in Maryland. The program addresses the causes and conditions of poverty by supporting low-income individuals, families receiving TANF, homeless individuals, migrant or seasonal farmworkers, and elderly low-income individuals in the areas of employment, education, better use of available income, housing, nutrition, emergency services, health, youth development, and community revitalization. Through annual awards to eligible entities, CSBG funds support community services and self-sufficiency initiatives. Community Action Agencies receive 90 percent of the federal funds allocated to Maryland to operate programs and services, while the state may use five percent as discretionary funding to support activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. The program utilizes Results Oriented Management and Accountability (ROMA) for performance measurement.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community Action Agencies and eligible entities receive direct funding through grants and contracts. Community Action Agencies receive 90 percent of the federal funds allocated to Maryland to operate programs and services that address poverty. The state may use five percent of the federal allocation as discretionary funding to support activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. Funds may also be used to provide training and technical assistance including Organizational Standards training, ROMA compliance, governance and tripartite board requirements, and support coordination and communication among eligible entities. Direct services include employment and training coordination, emergency food and nutrition services, youth development programs, housing assistance and suitable living environment support, education and literacy initiatives, emergency assistance for immediate and urgent needs, case management, and information and referral services. Training and Technical Assistance budget: $210,464 (Year One); $210,464 (Year Two).

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that provides free energy efficiency services, improvements, and utility bill assistance to limited-income households. The program is delivered through a network of local service providers including nonprofits, local governments, and for-profit home improvement contractors. Services include installation of energy conservation materials, equipment, and major appliances at no charge, such as insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items. The program includes an energy audit, recommended upgrades, and a follow-up evaluation. All services are provided at zero out-of-pocket cost to eligible homeowners. The program also provides utility bill assistance for electricity, gas, and water to eligible low-income utility customers. Households are screened for all three income-qualified programs (Weatherization Assistance Program, Limited Income Energy Efficiency EmPOWER Program, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program) upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Weatherization services are available in EmPOWER utility service territories. Program includes multiple sub-programs: Whole Home Efficiency, Base Efficiency, MEEHA (Maryland Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability), MEET (Maryland Energy Efficiency Tune-up), and energy kits with direct-install measures. The program operates under a whole-house approach with sophisticated analysis to maximize energy and dollar savings, and is funded and regulated through the EmPOWER Maryland Act. Services are provided through Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs) including nonprofits, community action agencies, and local governments, as well as State Weatherization Contractors (SWCs). The program operates on a three-year cycle with program plans defining methods, delivery, and services. Covers single-family site-built homes, manufactured homes, and low-rise multifamily buildings. Retrofitting services aligned with Maryland Standard Work Specification-Aligned Field Guide and National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Standard Work Specifications. Provides technical guidance and job aids for weatherization work including air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, window/door installation, and water heating improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free installation of energy efficiency improvements and major appliances including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items. Utility bill assistance for electricity, gas, and water. Services provided at no charge to eligible homeowners. Income limits apply: household income must be at or below 250% of Federal Poverty Level or 80% Area Median Income (AMI), whichever is higher; single person up to $5,708/month; two people up to $6,520/month. Households must have a utility account with participating utility companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, and Washington Gas). The program is delivered through a network of service providers; nonprofits and local governments respond to Requests for Applications (RFA) conducted at least every 3 years, and for-profit contractors respond to Requests for Proposals (RFP) when issued. Job cost cap: $16,000 per single-family home. Health and safety repairs: up to $1,000. Incidental repairs: up to 30% of total job cost for priority list jobs. Energy kits with direct-install measures (low-flow showerheads, smart power strips, outlet gaskets, pipe insulation, faucet aerators) provide expected savings of 209 kWh per kit. For renters, HVAC funding up to 85% of project cost. Programs support both single-family and multifamily housing. New offerings include funding for High Performance Building Design Certifications and Active Solar Heating Systems. Installation includes materials, labor, permits, and testing. For multi-unit projects, landlord contribution requirement is 15% if system not owned by tenant. Provides materials, labor, and technical specifications for air sealing, insulation (attics, sidewalls, rim joists, basement walls, crawlspaces, subfloors), duct sealing and insulation, subfloor insulation, manufactured home belly insulation, crawlspace vapor retarders, clothes dryer venting, exhaust fan ducting, LED lighting, lighting controls, safety equipment (smoke/CO alarms), pipe and tank insulation, low-flow water devices. Health and safety measures are mandatory before energy measures proceed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited-income households in Maryland who meet income qualifications and are customers of participating utility companies in EmPOWER utility service territories, as well as organizations interested in providing energy efficiency services. Includes homeowners and renters, multifamily property owners and managers, hard-to-reach households, homes in disrepair, elderly (60+), families with young children, persons with disabilities, critically ill individuals, and individuals with medical conditions requiring functional heating/cooling/water heating systems. Eligible households include recipients of SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD assistance, Medicaid, and other benefit programs. Priority given to elderly persons (age 60+), families with children, persons with disabilities, and households with high energy cost burdens. Vulnerable populations including those with critical medical needs may receive fast-tracked services. Single-family home and manufactured housing residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades and major appliances including insulation, hot water systems, lighting, furnace work, refrigerator retrofits, health and safety improvements, energy conservation materials, weatherization services, utility bill assistance for electricity, gas, and water for low-income households. Includes HVAC system replacements, heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, air sealing, smart thermostats, electrification measures, windows, active solar heating systems, LED lighting installations, building shell improvements, and non-energy repairs within allowable expenses. Also includes storm windows/doors, screen doors, cool/green roof installation, exterior siding repair/replacement, roof replacement, lead-based paint abatement, masonry repair and chimney work, vent installation, combustion appliance modifications, freezer replacement, dishwashers, clothes washers, dryers, dehumidifiers, ceiling fans, advanced power strips, faucet aerators, showerheads, water pipe and tank insulation, thermostatic shut-off valves, ductless mini-split heat pumps, and direct install measures such as LED bulbs, smart strips, and occupancy sensors. Air sealing, insulation installation (batts and blown), weatherstripping, thermal boundary improvements for attics, sidewalls, rim joists, basement walls, crawlspaces, and subfloors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves customers of six participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, and Washington Gas throughout Maryland in EmPOWER utility service territories. Available statewide with specific income-based eligibility. Service by utility territory includes Capital region, Central region, and Washington D.C./Baltimore metropolitan corridor. Specific territory-based restrictions apply for certain measures (BGE and WGL territories for gas systems). Applicants must have addresses within areas identified as having a Final EJ (Environmental Justice) Score Percentile at or above 90 for geographical categorical eligibility. See https://energy.maryland.gov/pages/facts/empower.aspx for service territory map. Service territories include Allegany County and Garrett County (with higher R-value attic insulation requirements at R-60), BGE territory, WGL territory, Pepco territory, and Delmarva territory. Maryland homes; homes built before 1978 have potential lead paint considerations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For individual homeowners: Complete an online pre-application or submit a paper application with required documents at Dhcd.Maryland.gov. Once approved, a local agency will contact you to schedule an energy audit. After audit review, a contractor will schedule the recommended improvements. A follow-up evaluation is conducted after work is completed. Standard application requires income documentation, Social Security cards, photo ID, utility bill, and proof of benefits. Quick application available with proof of benefit program enrollment. For service providers: Nonprofits and local governments respond to Requests for Applications. For-profit contractors respond to Requests for Proposals when active. Notification posted on DHCD website and distributed via email to vendor working list. Households may be screened for available programs. Households are screened for all three income-qualified programs upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Energy audit conducted at home with conditions assessed and documented with photos. Work coordinated through Network Partners. Contact Seth Fawcett or the main program line for application details. Home visit assessment of energy consumption patterns with analysis of 12 months recent energy consumption data. Physical examination of energy-related home components. Installation of direct install measures (LED bulbs, low-flow fixtures, thermostats, etc.). Client education on no-cost maintenance tasks. Follow-up recommendations for additional services. Distribution through subgrantee network via email, conference calls, Q&A sessions, and website posting.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch – Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A State of Maryland grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides financial assistance to county jurisdictions and direct assistance to homeowners and businesses to help cover capital construction costs of installing broadband internet service to properties that have difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from broadband infrastructure, long driveways, or other geographic challenges. The program addresses unserved and underserved Maryland households and properties in geographically difficult areas with broadband speeds below 25 Mbps. Counties develop sub-grant programs with Internet Service Provider partners for service installation to difficult-to-serve locations. Funding is distributed through the U.S. Treasury's American Rescue Plan Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund. Carroll County implements a specific component for homeowners with long driveways that exceed provider installation distances, providing up to $14,000 per property to connect homes to broadband service when a provider already passes the property. In Baltimore County, the program is supported by state funding of $1.1 million combined with Comcast contribution of $500,000 and Baltimore County contribution to support broadband build-out costs, assisting over 100 properties. In Queen Anne's County, the program is working with the State and two ISPs to connect 130 unserved addresses. Garrett County and Somerset County also participate in the program, expanding subsidies for broadband expansion to homes and businesses with long driveways or other difficult-to-serve properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,100,000 available to county jurisdictions in initial rounds. In the first round, 18 jurisdictions received awards totaling $19.6 million in Fiscal Year 2024 funding, providing internet access to approximately 2,400 unserved Maryland households. Counties develop sub-grant program with ISP partner(s) for service installation. Maximum funding per location is $8,000, though Carroll County's long driveway program provides up to $14,000 per property for specific circumstances. 25% match required of eligible project costs. Direct grants and subsidies also available to homeowners and businesses to help cover installation costs. In Baltimore County, state funding of $1.1 million is combined with Comcast contribution of $500,000 and Baltimore County contribution to support broadband build-out costs for over 100 difficult-to-serve properties. Property owners may be required to assist with some construction costs for their individual properties. Funding is distributed through the U.S. Treasury's American Rescue Plan Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund. Only one grant available per house or address. Grant is not retroactive and cannot reimburse if homeowner already paid to connect.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions developing sub-grant programs with ISP partners, homeowners, businesses, and local governments in hard-to-reach areas with properties set far back from roads where broadband installation is expensive. Local jurisdictions seeking to expand broadband infrastructure to unserved and underserved households in their communities. Property owners in difficult-to-serve areas, particularly in Baltimore County, Carroll County, Garrett County, and Somerset County with extreme private property concerns such as long driveways. Residents and business owners with difficult-to-serve properties such as long driveways or limited access to broadband infrastructure in areas with speeds below 25 Mbps. Carroll County residential households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband internet service installation to remote or geographically challenging properties, including covering costs where properties are set far back from existing infrastructure. Infrastructure expansion to provide high-speed internet access to unserved and underserved homes with broadband speeds below 25 Mbps, particularly in areas with geographic challenges, distance from existing broadband infrastructure, or extreme private property concerns. Broadband service connection to homes with driveways longer than provider standard installation distances. Broadband expansion and connection to underserved homes and businesses. To pay for connecting a home to existing broadband infrastructure when the driveway length exceeds what internet service providers typically cover for free during standard installation. Broadband expansion and improvement projects to serve difficult to reach/underserved properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to county jurisdictions, eligible homeowners, and businesses through local counties. In the first round, every jurisdiction that applied for the program received funds. Queen Anne's County has identified 130 unserved addresses to be addressed through this program. Baltimore County has identified over 100 difficult-to-serve properties eligible for assistance. Carroll County focuses on homeowners with long driveways exceeding provider installation distances and requires homes to have existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure passing by the property with homes not located in areas scheduled for future broadband installation. Garrett County and Somerset County specifically target difficult-to-serve properties and underserved areas with broadband speeds below 25 Mbps. Carroll County, Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County jurisdictions submit applications outlining their sub-grant program structure, ISP partnerships, and identification of difficult-to-serve properties. Homeowners and businesses apply through county programs. Local governments and internet service providers partner with the Office of Statewide Broadband to receive awards. Addresses are selected through the State's bidding process with qualifying ISPs. Build-out in participating counties was scheduled to begin late summer 2024 and complete in 2025. In Carroll County, interested homeowners must complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey at https://carrollcountymd.jotform.com/form/230754830587059 and answer yes to the long driveway question, providing name, full address, phone number, and email. The survey helps Carroll County Government understand internet needs of residents and determine where internet access is strong and lacking; data will assist county, state and federal agencies with projects to improve rural broadband availability. The online survey collects internet service details, speed test results, service availability, and optional contact information. After submission, the county checks the property address for eligibility with the service provider and applicants receive an email regarding the eligibility status of their property. Once the grant is awarded to Carroll County, all qualifying individuals will be notified by email and provided with application information. In Garrett County and Somerset County, interested applicants should contact the respective county Broadband Division for more information about the application process and eligibility. Applications are available through the FY24 Application Package.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction, rehabilitation, and preservation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors based on a State Qualified Allocation Plan. Investors receive tax credits over a 10-year period for funding qualified affordable housing projects. Credits provide tax savings and can be monetized through syndication to investors. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible outside of the competitive process. Funding is awarded through competitions held once or twice annually, with priority given to projects in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis according to criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building, as determined by the IRS. Projects must be placed in service within two years of allocation and remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside for nonprofit sponsors only. Credits provide tax savings over 10 years and can be monetized through syndication to investors. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Competitions are held once or twice annually. Income and rent limits vary by county and are updated annually based on Area Median Family Income (AMFI) percentages (20%-80%). Income and rent limits for properties with Placed in Service (PIS) date of May 15, 2023 or later are available; properties with earlier PIS dates must refer to Hold Harmless provisions and Novoco calculator. Rent limits are calculated at 30% of income limit as affordability index, divided by 12 for monthly rent.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis according to criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Competitions are held once or twice annually. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible outside of the competitive process. Developers apply to their state housing finance agency during annual allocation periods. Applications typically require project plans, financial projections, tenant demographics, and commitment letters. Submission via CDA Form 202 and electronic portal. State agencies review applications competitively and award credits. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return and then syndicate credits to investors. Property owners and managers must submit annual end-of-year tenant demographic reporting via online portal, including property, building, unit, event, and tenant data. Utility allowances must be prepared by a licensed engineer or qualified professional on DHCD's approved listing. For more information about the current Qualified Allocation Plan and application process, applicants should visit the Multifamily Document Library or contact the Housing Development Programs office.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with ground leases who wish to redeem (buy out) their leases and occupy the property as their principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and redemption of ground leases, and transactional costs (title search and loan closing).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well. The program serves homeowners statewide who own and occupy their property as a principal residence in Maryland.

Ground rent lease created before July 2, 1982 (or after with specific provisions)
Valid homeowners insurance and flood insurance required
Income verification documentation required
Tax returns and W-2 statements required
Deed copy required
Property tax bills required
Bank statements required
Ground rent billing statement required
Can apply even if behind on ground rent payments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete Ground Rent Redemption Loan Application with borrower/co-borrower information, income, assets, liabilities, and debt history. Submit supporting documentation including income verification, tax returns, deed, insurance policies, property tax bills, bank statements, and ground rent billing statement. Application can be submitted face-to-face, by phone, fax, mail, email, or internet.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Group Home Program helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or modify existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs, including developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, homeless individuals, and victims of sex trafficking. It also funds refinancing of mortgages on existing group homes. The program uses state funds from the Group Home Financing Program and proceeds from tax exempt mortgage revenue bonds under the Special Housing Opportunities Program. Financing is available through federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program funds and state sources.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to finance newly constructed buildings, acquisition or acquisition and rehabilitation of existing residential buildings, or refinance mortgages on existing group homes. Loans are provided through federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program funds and state sources. Interest rates vary from 0 to 7 percent depending on the source of funds and project cash flow. Maximum term is generally 30 years, though may extend to 40 years. Maximum loan amounts vary by geographic location, ranging from $289,470 to $525,091, with 15% increases available for high housing cost areas (Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard Counties). Maximum loan amount may not exceed $125,000 per bedroom plus 15% in high cost areas. Nonprofit sponsors are expected to contribute 5 percent towards the project. Individual sponsors are required to make a 10 percent equity contribution. Deferral provisions available generally not exceeding 2 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations seeking to provide group homes or assisted living facilities for special needs populations including developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, homeless individuals, and victims of sex trafficking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, modification, and refinancing of group homes and assisted living units. Eligible uses include acquisition costs, rehabilitation and construction costs, professional fees (architect, legal, appraisal), reserve for replacement requirements, and development and closing costs. Eligible modifications include repair or replacement of major systems such as heating, roofing, electrical or plumbing; accessibility modifications such as ramps and grab bars; lead paint abatement; general repairs and upgrades such as painting and floor coverings; and minor improvements to bring property into compliance with occupancy codes. MBE participation required for projects exceeding $250,000 in construction costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless, for existing construction, a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis. Property must be in Maryland and comply with local government zoning codes. Federal HOME Investment Partnerships Program funds available in all Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties (entitlement jurisdictions receive their own HOME funds allocation). Maximum loan amounts vary by county/city.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to help Maryland residents create safer and healthier living environments through comprehensive assessments and remediation of identified health and safety hazards in residential properties. Eligible homeowners can receive up to $15,474 in grant funds to cover the actual cost of critical repair work on owner-occupied single-family homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $15,474 in grant funds to cover the actual cost of critical repair work on owner-occupied single-family homes, including comprehensive assessments by a Healthy Homes Evaluator and remediation of identified hazards such as mold, gas leaks, roof repairs, asbestos abatement, radon mitigation, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, water mitigation, structural repairs, and pest treatments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with household income at or below 80% of the Area Median Income who own single-family residences in eligible counties. Priority given to households with children under six years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs and hazard mitigation including mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage, radon mitigation, electrical hazard removal, plumbing repairs, water and well repairs, septic and sewer repairs, window and door repairs for health and safety concerns, structural repairs, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects are limited to counties including Allegany, Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, Prince George's, Saint Mary's, and Washington. Income limits vary by location within the Washington DC PMSA region versus Rest of State.

Property must be an owner-occupied single-family residence
Property must be located in one of the eligible counties
Priority given to households with children under six years old

Work proposal must be reviewed and approved by DHCD's Healthy Homes Evaluator
Contractor must provide current MHIC License or applicable trade license
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing from Maryland BusinessExpress
Contractor must provide completed W-9 form
All necessary zoning and building permits must be submitted before Order to Proceed is issued

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Households are recommended to start with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment. Applicant completes the Combined Energy Rehabilitation Application. DHCD reviews the application for eligibility. Applicant selects one or more licensed contractors and obtains bids for desired work. Applicant provides work proposal with photos documenting issues, reviewed by DHCD's Healthy Homes Evaluator who may visit the property. Contractor provides required documentation including MHIC License, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. Applicant signs Grant Agreement and Rehabilitation Grant Agreement. Contractor and owner sign mutual Rehabilitation Agreement. Order to Proceed issued after grant funds are encumbered and all permits submitted. Contractor performs work with on-site monitoring by the Healthy Homes Evaluator. Owner signs Certificate of Completion before contractor receives final payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding for projects that divert at-risk households from homelessness, rapidly connect homeless individuals with benefits and permanent housing, serve vulnerable populations, implement evidence-based practices, and deliver services in safe, inclusive, equitable, and accessible manner. The program provides street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, homeless management information systems (HMIS), and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides funding for homeless services and activities including street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, homeless management information systems (HMIS), and administrative costs. Funding covers rental assistance (short-term, medium-term, rental arrears), financial assistance (application fees, security deposits, utility deposits/payments, moving costs), and supportive services (case management, housing search/placement, mediation, legal services, credit repair). Up to 24 months of rental assistance during any 3-year period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Organization Profile Review due Friday, March 21st, 2025; Application due Friday, April 25th, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless and at-risk populations; unaccompanied youth; domestic violence survivors; unsheltered individuals; individuals with complex medical and behavioral health needs. Lead agencies for the 16 Maryland Continuums of Care (CoCs) and Local Homeless Coalitions (LHCs) submit applications on behalf of homeless services providers in their community.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, homeless management information systems, and administrative costs. Specific allowable uses include rental assistance (arrears, security deposits, first/last month's rent, utility deposits/payments, moving costs), case management, transportation, meals, health services, mental health services, substance use treatment, legal services, education, employment assistance, life skills training, child care, hotel/motel vouchers, and direct cash transfers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all of Maryland through the 16 Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that provides grants to eligible Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic to help pay for critical home repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. The program offers up to $10,000 in standard grants, with exceptions up to $15,000 for extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 in grant funding per project to cover critical health and safety home repairs. Funds support critical repairs including heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing/septic repairs, wells, roof repair or replacement, mold or mildew remediation, lead paint or asbestos removal, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards. Exceptions up to $15,000 available for extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who occupy their property as a primary residence and have experienced financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety home repairs in primary residences only, including non-remodeling repairs that would cause involuntary displacement if unaddressed. Eligible repairs include mold/mildew remediation, asbestos removal, HVAC repairs, electrical repairs, plumbing/septic repairs, wells, roof repair/replacement, lead paint hazard reduction, structural/maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary residence must be located in Maryland statewide across all 24 counties.

Income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI)

Must reside in the primary residence

The proposal must include photos and come from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Households are recommended to start with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund of the State of Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program established by the American Rescue Plan Act to help homeowners experiencing financial hardship with mortgage payments and other housing costs due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The program provides grants to cover mortgage arrears and zero-interest loans (not due until the first mortgage loan is paid off) to assist homeowners who have fallen behind on mortgage payments. Recipients may also receive additional assistance with payment reassessment, loan forgiveness, or home repairs through the HAF Whole Home Repair Program. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers this program, which expects to receive approximately $250 million in total assistance. This is a limited funded program scheduled to end September 2026 or when funds are exhausted, whichever comes first. Homeowners statewide are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grants to cover mortgage arrears and zero-interest loans (not due until the first mortgage loan is paid off) to assist homeowners struggling with mortgage payments or other housing costs, including water bills and home repairs. Recipients may also receive additional assistance with payment reassessment or loan forgiveness at the end of their forbearance plan. Financial assistance is available to qualifying homeowners impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Example awards include $10,000 grants paired with $30,000 zero-interest loans, and grants for home repairs through the HAF Whole Home Repair Program. The program is expected to provide approximately $250 million in assistance and is scheduled to end September 2026 or when funds are exhausted, whichever comes first.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mortgage arrears, current mortgage payments, water bills, home repairs, and other housing costs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check eligibility and apply by contacting the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development at 833-676-0119, visiting their website, or reaching out to housing counseling services such as Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore. A housing counselor will work with the applicant to apply for the Homeowner Assistance Fund. Complete an Expression of Interest Form and be added to the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development's email list. Information and eligibility requirements are available through the State of Maryland website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal rental assistance program providing vouchers to eligible low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families to rent housing in the private market. Administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and local Public Housing Authorities. Promotes adequate and affordable housing, economic opportunity, and suitable living environments free from discrimination. Includes special-purpose vouchers such as Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Mainstream Housing Choice Vouchers, Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2), and Section 811 Project Rental Assistance for individuals with disabilities. Also includes homeownership assistance option for eligible families with minimum 3 years of rental assistance participation.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tenant-based Section 8 rental assistance vouchers enabling families to rent housing throughout their jurisdiction in the private market. Families select their own housing and vouchers help pay the difference between what they can afford and actual rent. Special-purpose vouchers available including: Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH) with 180 vouchers available; Family Unification Program (FUP) vouchers; Mainstream vouchers (50 available as of 2017); Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2) vouchers; and Section 811 Project Rental Assistance for individuals with disabilities. Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program available to help families establish household improvement goals and enhance economic stability. Payment standards vary by jurisdiction. Affirmative marketing and counseling services provided to support families renting outside poverty and minority concentration areas. Mobility counseling and housing search services available through MDhousingsearch.org. Monthly housing assistance payments made to landlords on behalf of eligible families. Homeownership option available for eligible participants with minimum 3 years of rental assistance history, providing assistance for down payment and purchase of single-family homes, condominiums, or manufactured homes. Monthly homeownership assistance payments supplement family contribution toward mortgage, taxes, insurance, utilities, maintenance, and repairs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton locations currently accepting applications

structured_extraction.program_audience: Families at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI - extremely low income); families at or below 50% AMI (very low income); families at or below 80% AMI (low income); elderly families; families with disabilities; families with children; races and ethnicities with disproportionate housing needs; victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking; child and adult victims of abuse; veterans; non-elderly disabled persons; homeless individuals and families; displaced persons; near-elderly persons; single persons; persons transitioning from institutional settings; families seeking housing in areas of low income or minority concentration; families currently participating in Housing Choice Voucher Program; disabled families; families meeting minimum income requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing rental assistance through vouchers; housing quality improvements; public housing maintenance and renovation; mixed-finance housing development; Section 504 accessibility modifications; housing modifications for accessibility; affirmative fair housing marketing and outreach; landlord engagement and support; housing search assistance; Family Self-Sufficiency program services; monthly rental assistance payments to owners; utility allowances for tenant-paid utilities; security deposits; down payment and homeownership purchase assistance; home purchase financing; mortgage principal and interest; mortgage insurance premiums; real estate taxes and assessments; homeowner's insurance; maintenance and repairs; homeowner association dues
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Public Housing Authorities. Currently reopening waitlists for Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester) and the Town of Elkton as of April 1, 2026. Specific jurisdiction waitlist information: Allegany County: 172 families on waiting list (9% annual turnover); Caroline County: 159 families on waiting list (8% annual turnover, closed 24 months); Frederick County: 4,106 families on waitlist (70.48% priority to families with children, closed 120 months); Garrett County: 344 families on waitlist (open); Elkton County: 260 families on waitlist (closed 5 months); Kent County on waiting list; Somerset County: 435 extremely low-income renter families with housing needs; Talbot County: 785 extremely low-income renter families with housing needs (100 families on waiting list, 15% annual turnover); Wicomico County: 2,735 renter families with housing needs at ≤30% AMI and 2,821 elderly families (147 families on waiting list, 15% annual turnover); Worcester County: 845 renter families with housing needs at ≤30% AMI and 1,566 elderly families (waiting list closed 24 months, not expected to reopen). Services available throughout jurisdictions enabling access outside areas of poverty and minority concentration. Applicants must reside in or work within served Maryland jurisdictions. Portability available for eligible families to move outside jurisdiction to any jurisdiction with compatible Housing Choice Voucher programs within the United States and territories. Program encourages leasing in areas outside poverty and minority concentration. Homeownership assistance may extend to other jurisdictions with operating Housing Choice Voucher Homeownership Programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a preliminary application through the Waitlist Status Portal or through PHA waiting lists. Applications are accepted during the announced application period. In-person assistance available at specific locations for individuals needing support. Family Self-Sufficiency program enrollment available to establish household improvement goals. Counseling services provided on unit location outside poverty and minority concentration areas. Specific categories may be admitted even when list is generally closed. Mandatory briefing for eligible families. Voucher issuance (60-day validity for housing search). Request for Tenancy Approval (RFTA) submission with proposed lease during voucher term. Applicant screening for drug-related and violent criminal behavior. Criminal record verification and disclosure procedures. Citizenship and immigration status verification. Income and family composition examination. Informal hearing process available for disputes. Annual recertification process with 90-120 days advance notice. Third-party verification of income, assets, and deductions required. Pre- and post-purchase homeownership counseling for homeownership option participants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides low- or no-interest loans to public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and reward counties pursuing innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program enables counties to acquire existing private-sector housing in conjunction with local housing authorities or housing developers. Funded projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized rental housing with specified affordability requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans to public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers. Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate; long-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. Maximum $2,500,000 per project award. $5 million total FY 2026 funds available. Up to 3 projects will receive awards. Only 1 award per jurisdiction. Loans are secured by lien on property with promissory note. Funds may be used for new construction, acquisition of existing private-sector housing, or rehabilitation of rental housing including multifamily properties, apartment buildings, townhouses, and single-family homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities, county governments, and housing developers proposing innovative approaches to affordable housing development and increased housing production.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Low- or no-interest loans for acquisition of existing private-sector housing, land acquisition and new construction, or major rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental properties. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units for households earning 50% or less of area median income or at least 40% for households earning 60% or less of area median income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located in Maryland. Preference scoring for projects within 3/4 mile of transit rail station, within ENOUGH Act eligible census tracts, Just Communities designated areas, or Communities of Opportunity.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit the Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package and CDA Form 202. Applications are evaluated on experience with housing projects (10 points for sufficient experience, 4 points for limited experience with some problems, 1 point for limited/no experience), record of prompt problem resolution, and experience with similar projects. Scoring also includes preference points for location and other criteria specified in the RFP. Waiver requests are available for applicants seeking exceptions. An application fee of $2,500 is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program for accessibility or visibility renovations to homes; supports modifications that enable independent living for individuals with disabilities or sensory impairments. The program helps Maryland residents make their homes more accessible by providing up to 50% of renovation costs back, up to $5,000 per year. The credit applies to renovations on your own home. Applicants must submit completed applications and supporting documents by the annual deadline to be considered for a tax credit certificate.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Income tax credit for homeowners who have completed accessibility renovations to their homes during the tax year. Up to 50% of renovation costs back, with a maximum tax credit of $5,000 per year. Total program capacity is up to $1,000,000 in tax credits per year. If demand exceeds this amount, credits may be reduced. The credit is claimed on your Maryland tax return after completing eligible accessibility renovations. Applicants who are approved receive a tax credit certificate issued by DHCD by August 31st.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of accessibility features including: no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, accessible doorways, roll-in showers, chairlifts, elevators, visual alarms, accessible parking spaces, kitchen/bathroom modifications, and other ADA-compliant accessibility improvements to make homes more accessible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland properties only (state: MD required). Available to Maryland residents who file taxes in Maryland and throughout the state.

Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit a completed application to DHCD by June 1st of current calendar year and provide any additional information requested

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help residential property owners install, repair, or replace indoor plumbing systems, including wells, septic systems, water and sewer connections, plumbing fixtures, and lead pipe removal. Loans are available with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay, with maximum loan terms of 30 years. Deferred loans are available for borrowers needing health, safety, or accessibility improvements, and deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for borrowers with incomes below 30 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on household income level and ability to pay. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Deferred principal and interest may be available for borrowers with no repayment capability at 50% and 30% AMI levels. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-to-moderate income households and owner-occupants of single-family homes with incomes at or below specified limits based on household size and geographic location (Washington DC PMSA vs. Rest of State).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or improvement of indoor plumbing systems including wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping, connections to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment, additions or modifications for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative septic and water systems, and lead pipe removal inside homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Income limits vary by geographic location (Washington DC PMSA counties: Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's Counties vs. Rest of State). Applicants should contact their local housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs.
requirements_list: Properties must be single-family, owner-occupied houses or rental residential properties
Properties must be structurally sound
Household income must not exceed specified limits based on household size and geographic location (income limits range from 30% to 80% of Area Median Income)
Plumbing must be inoperative or unsafe
Must be an individual with limited income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409 (Baltimore area) or 877-218-8101 (statewide toll-free). Loans are originated, packaged and closed by DHCD's Special Loan Program network of local administering agencies including county housing offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps remove lead paint from residential buildings and daycare centers. The assistance applies to both single-family homes and multi-family properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance essential public infrastructure projects. The program provides long-term capital financing with favorable terms, manages bond issuance complexities, and reduces costs through economies of scale and pooling of local demand. The program accommodates projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds are issued and loan proceeds are provided to local governments. The interest rate on loans is subject to market conditions at the time of bond sale. Loan terms are set at the option of the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need capital financing for essential public infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks, public space improvements, streetscape improvements, transportation enhancements, public safety vehicles and equipment, water production and treatment systems, water storage and distribution systems, storm water control and sewer facilities, government office and meeting facilities, police/fire/transportation/education/health/recreation/maintenance facilities, and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that have legal authority necessary for constructing, operating and maintaining the proposed project, pledging security for and repaying the loan, and pledging income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or agency thereof
Must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various shared state revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government or its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government must complete an application that provides information similar to what bond rating agencies require to evaluate creditworthiness. Local governments can submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions to request technical assistance from the Community Development Administration. Applications can be submitted online at https://dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/r5qnekm1sfg0sf. When bonds are issued depends on the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Office of Statewide Broadband to further the state's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. The program provides funding to local jurisdictions, 501(c) nonprofit entities, and community-based anchor institutions to support digital inclusion through planning and implementation projects, with a total of $2 million available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks are available: Digital Inclusion Planning provides financial assistance for up to 50 percent of the cost of a Digital Inclusion Plan with a maximum grant request of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. Digital Inclusion Program Implementation provides financial assistance for up to 100 percent of implementation, expansion, or continuation of Digital Inclusion Program(s) with a maximum grant request of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Total funding available is $2 million. Grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the applicant's intended population and ability to deploy funds responsibly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit organizations serving Maryland, and community-based anchor institutions. Priority will be given to projects serving covered populations including individuals with household income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minorities, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to develop a digital inclusion plan or implement digital inclusion activities, facilitate broadband adoption for covered populations to provide educational and employment opportunities, implement training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or other workforce development programs, and construct, upgrade, expand, or operate new or existing public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to applicants providing services within the state of Maryland.

Applications must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding

Digital Inclusion Planning: maximum $30,000, minimum $5,000

Application submission opens Tuesday, February 15, 2022 and closes Thursday, March 31, 2022. All applications must be fully complete at submission. Funding announcements will be made on or before April 15, 2022. Applicants submit either a planning or implementation proposal with detailed budgets and project plans.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to close gaps for K-12 students and school staff who lack necessary internet access or devices needed to connect to classrooms. structured_extraction.program_name: Main Street Maryland Program - Operating Assistance Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development administers the Main Street Maryland Program, which supports community development and revitalization in Maryland's historic downtowns and commercial districts through historic preservation, design, and the Main Street Approach. The program helps communities grow their local economy, improve downtown appearance, and strengthen the image of traditional business districts while maintaining historical and cultural character and facilitating positive rehabilitation and adaptive reuse projects. The program provides operating assistance grants and comprehensive technical assistance to designated Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods, helping them build capacity to achieve community revitalization and economic development goals. The program supports downtown and neighborhood commercial district revitalization through funding and technical assistance based on the Main Street Approach, which focuses on Economic Vitality, Design, Promotion, Organization, and Clean, Safe, and Green principles.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants and technical assistance for Main Street program operations and downtown revitalization. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive approximately $33,000 each. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive approximately $25,000 each. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Funds can be used for operating expenses including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, or other costs related to administering the Main Street program, as well as downtown revitalization, business growth and expansion, improvement of downtown appearance, community placemaking, historic preservation-based redevelopment, and rehabilitation and adaptive reuse projects. The program also provides technical assistance and support through the Main Street Approach focusing on Economic Vitality, Design, Promotion, Organization, and Clean, Safe, and Green principles. Communities receive guidance on revitalization efforts, training programs for Aspiring Main Streets, and resources for sustainable revitalization. A funding match is not required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government officials and leaders, nonprofit organizations, community stakeholders, and volunteers. Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods seeking to revitalize their downtown and neighborhood commercial districts, as well as Maryland communities interested in historic district revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation and design projects, rehabilitation and adaptive reuse projects, local Main Street program operations, community revitalization initiatives, operating expenses including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, or other costs related to administering the Main Street program, downtown revitalization, business growth and expansion, improvement of downtown appearance, and community placemaking. Projects and activities should align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the community's transformation strategy and must be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods located in Sustainable Community areas and within Priority Funding Areas as determined by the Maryland Department of Planning throughout Maryland. Additional consideration given to projects in designated ENOUGH Act areas and Just Communities areas. The program serves communities across Maryland with over 50 communities currently supported by the program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. New users must register first by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form, which may take up to 72 hours for approval. Make sure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting your application, as applications missing documents may be disqualified. A virtual Application Training was scheduled for Tuesday, March 3, 2026 from 1-2 PM. Individual technical assistance sessions are available through Calendly. Interested communities should: 1) Check if the community is ready; 2) Learn about the Main Street Approach; 3) Build support from local leaders and community members; 4) Visit existing Main Street communities; 5) Set goals for the program; 6) Contact Main Street Maryland staff with application.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps make housing more affordable for Maryland households with low incomes. It provides funding for various housing-related costs. These costs include construction, nonprofit developer support, resident services, and operating expenses. A Board of Trustees governs the program, which the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development manages.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding as grants for capacity building, operating costs, and support services. It offers deferred-payment loans or recoverable grants for capital costs. These are repayable if the project is sold or no longer serves low-income residents. Pre-development awards are typically loans that must be repaid.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: capital costs for rental and homeownership housing; financial help for nonprofit developers to build their capacity; supportive services for residents of affordable housing; and operating costs for affordable housing projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that supports the growth and success of small businesses in Maryland by enabling private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund from fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland. The program helps small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, that may have difficulty obtaining business financing. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000, with borrower and lender each contributing a percentage (typically 1.5 percent each), matched by the state for a total reserve of up to 6 percent of the original loan amount. Loans can have terms up to ten years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program enhances credit by establishing a loan loss reserve fund. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. The borrower and lender each contribute a percentage (typically 1.5 percent each), and the Maryland Capital Access Program matches that combined amount. For example, 1.5 percent from the lender plus 1.5 percent from the borrower equals 3 percent, matched by a 3 percent state contribution for a total reserve of 6 percent of the original loan amount. The program can be combined with other loan programs and used for lines of credit and term loans. Loans can have terms up to ten years and can cover up to 100 percent of losses for participating lenders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations with fewer than 50 employees, located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas. Businesses must meet SBA size standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project financing for start-up costs, business expansion, working capital, and other projects for businesses located in Priority Funding Areas. Loan proceeds cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, institutional facilities like community halls or hospitals, adult entertainment facilities, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas approved by the Maryland Department of Planning for State funding in accordance with the Smart Growth Act of 1997. The program is available to businesses located in Maryland.

Most Maryland small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, are eligible
Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Loan amount must be between $10,000 and $1,000,000
Loan term may not exceed ten years

Enrolled loans must comply with restriction list including prohibition on passive real estate ownership, residential housing developments, institutional facilities, adult entertainment facilities, and sectarian religious instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls the appropriate loan. The lender, borrower, and Maryland Capital Access Program each deposit contributions into a reserve account. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form with summary information to the Maryland Capital Access Program. In case of loan default, the lender files a one-page claim form at charge-off.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide public housing rehabilitation program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through local administering agencies including county housing offices and nonprofit organizations. The program provides special loans designed to improve single-family homes and small rental properties for low and moderate-income families through rehabilitation, energy conservation, accessibility improvements, hazard reduction, and bringing properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. The program serves owner-occupants and rental property sponsors with household income not exceeding 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, addressing critical health and safety issues to bring properties into code compliance. The program also helps Maryland homeowners address critical repairs and provides energy efficiency improvements to make homes more comfortable, efficient, and affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on applicant income and ability to repay. Maximum loan amount is generally $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans may have deferred payments for families with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Up to 40 percent of amortizing MHRP loans may be used for general property improvements. Loans are administered statewide through local administering agencies including county housing offices and nonprofit organizations. Grants/rehabilitation funding also available for critical home repairs with maximum funding of $50,000 per project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and rental property sponsors with household income not exceeding 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Low and moderate-income families in Maryland. Homeowners receiving benefits (SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD assistance, Medicaid, OHEP Utility Bill Pay Assistance, Maryland Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Program, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids). Homeowners with documented medical conditions requiring functioning heating/cooling/water heating.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property rehabilitation costs including critical health and safety repairs such as mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer issues, window and door repairs for health, safety or security, structural repairs, accessibility modifications, fall prevention measures, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, pest treatments, energy conservation improvements, heating/cooling system repairs, water heater repairs, weatherization services, general property improvements such as kitchen and bathroom remodeling, carpeting, and landscaping. Includes bringing homes into compliance with building codes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applications are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. In Frederick County, applications are processed through the Frederick County Division of Housing. Applicants should contact their local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs. Two regions: Washington, DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties) and Rest of State (all other Maryland counties).
