structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact local housing office by county or Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409 or toll free (Maryland only) 877-218-8101. In Frederick County, homeowners and sponsors download the appropriate application and submit to the Frederick County Division of Housing. Provide a work proposal from a licensed and insured contractor with photos documenting issues. Submit contractor documentation including license, insurance certificate, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9. Submit completed rehabilitation application and checklist with all required documentation. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies including county housing offices and nonprofit organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative designed to reduce interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses by providing up to a 2% discount on loans obtained from participating banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Borrowers receive up to a 2% discount on interest rates for qualifying loans from participating banks. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office deposits an amount equal to the loan with the issuing bank at a reduced interest rate. Loans must be for term loans or fixed-rate loans with one disbursement. Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years. Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount. Loans can be combined with other loan programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects or activities located in Maryland. Loan proceeds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Loan projects or activities must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Borrower must be a certified minority business enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, or a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Borrower must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining the qualifying loan
Borrower must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to continue receiving the interest rate reduction benefit
Loan must be obtained from a participating lender designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program. The department verifies eligibility and forwards the application to all enrolled banks. The department provides the borrower with a list of participating banks. The borrower contacts participating banks to complete full application requirements. The bank underwrites the loan according to standard underwriting with a reduced interest rate. Upon loan approval, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Microenterprise Loan Program expands opportunities for microenterprise development and creates new opportunities for small business development in Maryland communities. It provides entrepreneurs and small businesses with flexible financing through partnerships with community-based microlenders and Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs), including FSC First, Baltimore Community Lending, Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc., Eastern Shore Entrepreneurship Center, Prince George's Financial Service Corporation, and other intermediary partners who originate and administer the loans and provide training and technical assistance. Microloans range from $25,000 to $50,000 with interest rates up to 12% and loan terms from 2 to 5 years. The program supports both feasible startups and established businesses seeking to expand within designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 with interest rates up to 12% and loan terms from 2 to 5 years. Collateral required, which may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. No prepayment penalties. Interest rates and final terms determined at time of underwriting. Additional funds may be added to the project by the Intermediary. Funds can be used for working capital, marketing, planning and feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, human capital increases, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Microentrepreneurs, small business owners, established businesses, and feasible startups in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning and feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, human capital increases, leasehold improvements, equipment purchases, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Sustainable Community areas and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. Specific service areas vary by intermediary partner.

Applications can be submitted through FSC First's online application portal at https://pgfscfirst.tfaforms.net/6. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides significant support to homebuyers through 30-year fixed-rate competitive rate mortgage loans, down payment assistance, and Partner Match Programs to help overcome upfront financial barriers associated with down payment and settlement expenses. The program offers financial incentives and other assistance to help homebuyers purchase homes. Includes the Homeownership for Individuals with Disabilities Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides 30-year fixed-rate competitive rate mortgage loans and down payment assistance through Partner Match Programs to help homebuyers with down payment and settlement expenses. The program offers associated financial incentives for eligible homebuyers purchasing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible homebuyers in Maryland, including individuals with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mortgage financing, down payment assistance, settlement expenses, and home purchase
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homebuyers purchasing in Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be eligible homebuyer
Must be purchasing in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development in partnership with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO). The program provides up to $50 million in loans, equity investments, and other financial assistance to support small businesses with limited growth opportunities, particularly targeting small technology and life sciences businesses, communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) businesses. Funds are allocated through multiple programs including capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, the TEDCO-administered Venture Equity Fund, Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, Seed Funds Equity program, and Social Impact Funds. The program focuses on supporting entrepreneurs and businesses across Maryland, with particular emphasis on underrepresented entrepreneurs and businesses in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50 million allocated in loans, equity investments, and other financial assistance. Funds are issued through participating lenders and programs with specific loan amounts, terms, and equity investment structures determined on a case-by-case basis. Multiple program tracks focus on capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture capital and startup funding through equity investments. The Social Impact Funds program provides investment and support to entrepreneurs demonstrating disadvantages.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Maryland with limited opportunities for growth, particularly small technology and life sciences businesses, socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), underrepresented entrepreneurs, businesses in underserved communities, and small and micro businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing and growth through capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture capital and startup funding for technology-based and life sciences businesses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, targeting communities and areas with high concentration of small, micro, and SEDI businesses, and technology-based businesses across the state
requirements_list: Must be a small business
Technology-based or life sciences business preferred for some program tracks
Limited growth opportunities preferred
SEDI status or location in targeted community areas may be considered
Entrepreneurs must meet specific eligibility criteria for respective program tracks (Venture Equity Fund, Seed Funds, Social Impact Funds, or other designated SSBCI lending partners)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply directly through the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication or work with one of the designated SSBCI lending partners including Lendistry, City First Enterprises, FSC First, and Community Development Fund. Applicants may also apply through one of the TEDCO program tracks: Social Impact Funds, Seed Funds, or Venture Funds. Each program has its own application process and requirements. Technical assistance is available through MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program assists small town and city governments with building their administrative capacity by providing grants to hire professional staff to work as a circuit rider to multiple towns assisting with specific municipal functions and activities. Grant funds can only be used to pay for salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two year period.

Grant funds can only be used to pay for salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff over a two year period. The annual funding allocation is determined by an appropriation of the General Assembly each year. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

The municipalities within a circuit must be within reasonable proximity to each other.

Applications are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment and support. Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program helping homeowners make valuable repairs and enhancements to improve their homes' energy efficiency and quality of life. The program offers grants and low-interest loans for energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacement, insulation replacement, accessibility features for seniors and those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, structural repairs, and other home maintenance issues. Loans feature interest rates up to 4% (potentially as low as zero), with payments that may be deferred and no application fee. Assistance is based on the type of work needed and household income and ability to repay.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and low-interest loans up to a maximum interest rate of 4%, which may be as low as zero. Payments may be deferred and there is no application fee. Loans and grants are based on the type of work needed and household income and ability to repay. Funding can be used for energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacement, insulation replacement, accessibility features, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, structural repairs and maintenance, Energy Star appliances, air quality improvements, lighting retrofits, and energy conservation materials.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacement, insulation replacement, accessibility features for seniors and those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, structural and maintenance repairs, Energy Star appliances, air quality improvements, lighting retrofits, energy conservation materials, and HVAC system upgrades

requirements_list: Homeowner in Maryland

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call toll-free 1-844-369-4150 for home repair improvements or 1-855-583-8976 for energy efficiency improvements to start the application. Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application. Applicants may also apply through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program that provides flexible funding to help small businesses and nonprofits start, rehabilitate, or expand fresh food retail operations—such as grocery stores or farmers markets—in underserved areas called food deserts and designated Sustainable Communities. The program emphasizes sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers.

eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible financing provided through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program for startup, rehabilitation, or expansion of fresh food retail businesses and nonprofits in food desert areas and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofits offering healthy food options, particularly those that source fresh food from Maryland farmers and serve food desert areas or Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Startup, rehabilitation, or expansion of businesses and nonprofits offering fresh food options in underserved areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or a designated Sustainable Community. Food deserts are defined as communities that lack easy access to healthy foods including fresh fruits and vegetables, typically in the form of a supermarket or grocery store. Local governments submit applications to designate areas as Food Desert Areas.
requirements_list: Must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community

Community-based lending intermediaries originate and administer loans and provide technical assistance. Intermediaries must apply to become partners with the department and renew their status every five years or when their awarded funds are fully committed to borrowers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. The program increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing by leveraging federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to support new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing with a minimum of five units. Multiple credit enhancement structures are available including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac TEL, and FNMA MBS Collateral options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years, with permanent loans up to $20 million and 35-40 year amortization periods. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program, including FHA, GNMA, Freddie Mac, and FNMA options. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration/Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers seeking to build, acquire, or rehabilitate multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, substantial rehabilitation and permanent financing of multifamily rental housing containing a minimum of five units. Loans may be provided to refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance is in conjunction with rehabilitation of the housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. Projects must be located in designated Priority Funding Areas.

The Department accepts a variety of financing structures for multifamily tax-exempt bonds with indicative interest rates, fees, and costs documented in the Multifamily Program Financing Option Comparison document. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants or loans to reduce electric or gas consumption and direct greenhouse gas emissions in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Supports energy efficiency improvements, limited health and safety or incidental repairs, greenhouse gas emission reduction measures, building electrification, solar installations, and EV charging stations. Includes replacement of fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment such as heat pumps and the Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) Roadmap Program option. Gas reducing measures are available in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territories. Funding is available for cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation upgrades for existing, major renovation, and new construction projects that are above minimum code and performance standards and claim at least 20% energy savings. Includes electrical panel upgrades, other electrical system improvements, building energy conservation measures, alternative energy generating systems, and heat pump water heaters. The Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program component provides grants for large multifamily buildings to replace fossil fuel-powered equipment and systems with electric equipment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants or loans with 0% interest and deferred payments. The main MEEHA program has allocated $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. The Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program component has allocated $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Grants available for greenhouse gas reduction projects (up to $15,000 per dwelling unit, with project cap of $1.25 million); grants and loans available for energy efficiency projects. Funds are provided during construction as work is completed and verified. Loan terms feature 0% interest with deferred payments. Payment processing typically takes 4-5 weeks after approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified owners and operators of affordable multifamily rental housing developments and large multifamily buildings seeking to improve energy efficiency, reduce utility consumption, or reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions. Commercial building owners and operators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to reduce electric or gas consumption including HVAC systems, insulation, lighting, air sealing, appliances, domestic hot water systems, fenestration, and duct sealing. Projects that reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions in multifamily buildings through replacement of fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment such as heat pumps. Solar photovoltaic installations and EV charging station installations. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing measures that reduce electric or gas consumption. Energy efficiency and conservation upgrades including electric kitchen equipment, electrical panel upgrades, alternative energy generating systems, and heat pump water heaters. Building electrification costs (up to 10% of electrification measure funding), energy audits, and new construction certifications.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit MEEHA Application to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov or submit 202 application form if also applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs. A Qualified Energy Professional conducts an energy audit (for rehabilitation) or energy certification review (for new construction). The Qualified Energy Professional submits the Funding Request Form to DHCD on behalf of the project owner, organizing photos by measure category. For GHGRP applicants, set up Energy Star Portfolio Manager account. DHCD reviews the Funding Request and sends a scope confirmation spreadsheet. Once approved, DHCD prepares and executes a funding agreement. Project begins construction and submits requisitions with supporting documentation. DHCD inspects installed measures and processes payment. After construction, project enters affordability period with ongoing monitoring and benchmarking reports.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to relend to small businesses using SSBCI funds combined with required private capital match. The program supports lending to businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, very small businesses, and those in CDFI investment areas. Loan sizes range from targeted loans up to $350,000 to larger portfolio loans based on CDFI capacity from $500,000 to $15,000,000, with private capital match requirements varying by business type and size.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to CDFIs for relending to small businesses. Loan sizes range from targeted loans up to $350,000 to larger portfolio loans based on CDFI capacity from $500,000 to $15,000,000. Private capital match requirement: 4:1 ratio for non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees, or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees. CDFIs must have 20 percent at risk. Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venture capital program dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of outstanding early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. The program provides bridge financing to businesses that have already raised early-stage equity and are seeking additional investors to reach their next funding milestone. Assistance is delivered through venture debt with repayment in principal and interest or convertible note structure, with target SSBCI portion ranges from $500,000 to $2,500,000 and aggregate funding rounds less than $20,000,000.

Aggregate funding round must be less than $20,000,000. SSBCI must be on at least a pari passu basis (equal priority) with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Typical bridge rounds are greater than $2,000,000.

Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to support businesses reaching their next equity raise and scaling operations.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund provides competitive grants to support commercial and residential development activities in targeted areas of the National Capital region for revitalization. The program focuses on areas where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact. Competitive grants support projects including down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant properties, improvements to residential and business properties, energy efficiency upgrades, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing, retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition. Approximately $19 million in capital funding and $1.2 million in operating funding are available for strategic economic development projects in designated areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants totaling approximately $19 million in capital funding and $1.2 million in operating funding to support commercial and residential development projects including down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant properties, improvements to residential and business properties, energy efficiency upgrades, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing, retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition. The program also provides technical assistance and information to applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, and community development organizations in targeted revitalization areas in the National Capital region of Prince George's and Montgomery Counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial and residential development projects that support Sustainable Communities Action Plan goals, including down payment assistance for homebuyers, property acquisition and rehabilitation, property improvements, energy efficiency upgrades, affordable housing development, mixed-use development, community open space and public infrastructure enhancement, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities within specified areas: In Prince George's County, at least in part within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia; OR in Montgomery County, within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify specific address eligibility.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants must be local governments or community development organizations

Application training available via webinar. For additional application procedures and information, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by Maryland's Department of Housing and Community Development to help create and preserve decent, safe, and sanitary affordable rental housing for households with the lowest incomes, specifically targeting extremely low-income households earning 30% or less of the Area Median Income. The program provides funding for production, preservation, rehabilitation, acquisition, and new construction of affordable rental housing, particularly in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds support extremely low-income rental housing projects through construction, rehabilitation, property acquisition, soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. Federal funding of $3,000,000 for Federal Fiscal Year 2025 (October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026), with 90% allocated for production/preservation/rehabilitation of affordable rental housing and 10% retained for administrative and planning expenses. Assistance may include grants, equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest-bearing loans or advances, and deferred payment loans. Operating or rental assistance is limited to no more than one-third of annual allocation. Projects require a 40-year affordability period. Funds are often combined with other federal, state, and local housing resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, for-profit developers, government entities, and other qualified housing development entities seeking to develop and preserve affordable rental housing for extremely low-income households. Includes family projects and elderly projects serving extremely low-income families and seniors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or rehabilitation of rental housing, property acquisition, related soft costs, resident relocation costs, and limited operating costs or operating reserves for HTF-assisted units. Cannot be used for refinancing existing debt. Funds support development and preservation of affordable rental housing. Projects must budget for operating expenses, reserves for replacement, and debt service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland, with priority consideration for projects in priority funding areas, Qualified Census Tracts (QCT), Difficult Development Areas (DDA), Communities of Opportunity, and rural areas. Rural areas include Allegany, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties. Also includes areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits, areas between the Washington, DC beltway and DC boundary, Federal and State enterprise zones, certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas, and rural villages designated in county comprehensive plans as of July 1, 1998.

Must have experience developing or managing affordable multifamily rental housing
Must comply with HTF program requirements and reporting
Must be familiar with other housing funding programs used in the project
Must meet minimum threshold requirements
Must provide certification of compliance with HTF requirements for the full period of the project
Market Study required, not more than 6 months old, prepared by independent professional
Minimum 5% vacancy rate underwriting required
Projects must meet all applicable state and local codes, ordinances, and zoning requirements
Accessibility requirements must be met
40-year affordability period required
Family projects must have reasonable access to jobs, quality schools, and economic and social benefits
Projects in QCT/DDA must contribute to concerted community revitalization plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a project application requesting HTF funds, or DHCD staff may recommend HTF funds during project review in consultation with the project sponsor. DHCD awards funds on a competitive and non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis depending on fund availability. Applications are accepted throughout the year and awarded based on readiness to proceed. Funds must be committed within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant agreement. If selected, the applicant receives a Notice of Award stating DHCD's intent to provide HTF funds. Download application documents from the Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide loan participation program under the State Small Business Credit Initiative designed to assist small businesses and nonprofit organizations with financing through a network of lending partners. The program provides below-market interest rates with flexible terms up to 30 years and can lend up to $5 million for new or expanded business spaces. Priority support is provided for businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in specific counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas, and BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones. Gap financing is available for businesses in Sustainable Communities targeted for redevelopment. Eligible uses include working capital, owner-occupied real estate acquisition and renovation, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, and mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, restaurants, child care facilities, markets, office space, retail, and manufacturing facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 with flexible terms up to 30 years. Interest rates based on underwriting analysis. Requires 10% applicant cash contribution, personal guarantees, and collateral. Private capital match requirement of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/very small businesses or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/very small businesses, with minimum 1:1 match required. Up to 30% program match available. Gap financing available for businesses in designated Sustainable Communities. Associated fees include $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% commitment fee.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on first-come, first-serve basis; currently at capacity until July 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses with 500 or fewer employees and nonprofit organizations seeking financing for projects in targeted geographic areas. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, new construction, rehabilitation, expansion, machinery and equipment, working capital, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, restaurants, child care facilities, markets, office space, retail, manufacturing facilities, and other costs associated with opening, operating, or expanding a Maryland small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in Allegany County, Garrett County, Somerset County, or Wicomico County; Transit-Oriented Development areas designated by the Maryland Department of Transportation; or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones. Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI investment area in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Application Portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication or directly through partner lenders. New users create an account using the Registration link; returning users log in with existing credentials. There is a $250 application fee. For an initial consultation, complete the Pre-Application Consultation Form and a team member will contact you. Upon loan approval, applicants receive a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires meeting underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to disbursement of loan proceeds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local jurisdictions, schools, libraries, nonprofits, and other community organizations to extend broadband service to unserved areas by funding capital construction costs and network infrastructure development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 for 70% to 90% of capital construction costs, with required match of 10% to 30%. Funding supports broadband infrastructure projects, network expansion, and digital access initiatives. Local jurisdiction is applicant and fiscal agent; may work with ISP partner.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs, broadband network infrastructure development, internet connectivity expansion, digital access for schools and community centers, and residential broadband access projects to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas

May partner with ISP
Match of 10% to 30% required
Local jurisdiction or ISP may own funded assets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit project proposals with service area maps, engineering plans, cost estimates, and memorandum of understanding between local jurisdiction and ISP partner

structured_extraction.program_description: Matching grants to support the operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations that stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. NHS corporations partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments and the State to provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, homebuyer education, and community organizing. The program supports a portion of the operating costs for three Neighborhood Housing Services corporations through formula grants.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants up to $50,000 per eligible NHS corporation that do not exceed one-third of the organization's annual operating budget. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation serving low- and moderate-income households in targeted neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations to support homeownership programs, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community organizing activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: NHS of Baltimore and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center serve several neighborhoods in Baltimore City and Baltimore County. Salisbury NHS serves residents in the West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods of Salisbury, Maryland. Montgomery Housing Partnership Inc. serves Montgomery County.

Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local NHS corporation and participate on its board of directors
Grant amount does not exceed $50,000 and does not exceed one-third of annual operating budget
State grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the specific NHS corporation directly or submit application through the Department of Housing and Community Development's Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Neighborhood Revitalization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development supports the construction of Net Zero homes, which are energy efficient homes that produce as much or more energy than they use. The program provides low interest construction loans and loan enhancements for builders, developers, owners, investors, and non-profits building new Net Zero homes or performing deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower. Financing is available for projects properly zoned for residential use and constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low interest construction loans available with interest rates ranging from 2% to 5% depending on HERS score and whether more than 50% of units are at or below 60% of Area Median Income. Loan to value up to 90%. Administration fee of 1% of total loan, appraisal fee of $290, and title fees. Loan enhancements available for applicants securing loans from private lenders. Construction period typically 12 months with 12 month loan repayment period for projects for sale. Direct loans and loan enhancements for construction are offered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Accepting applications until available funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, investors, and non-profits building new Net Zero homes or performing deep energy retrofits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or deep energy retrofit of homes to achieve Net Zero status with HERS rating of 50 or lower. Must be properly zoned for residential use and constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland for projects that are properly zoned for residential use.

Properly zoned for residential use
Must be constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes
Qualified to do business in Maryland

Review the list of required documentation and submit any additional documents requested by the department. Submit the completed application by email to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov and carbon copy Thomas.Walz@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Strategic and targeted investment by Maryland DHCD to address fresh food unavailability in communities. The program supports development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets providing fresh food in areas with limited or no access to nutritious food options. NourishMD expands access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers, with awards ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 and up to $2 million in total funding available. Grants support capital-related needs including equipment purchases, buildout and facility upgrades, inventory expansion, and infrastructure for SNAP/EBT acceptance, with the aim of building stronger, healthier, and more economically resilient communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 with up to $2 million in total grant funding available. Funds support improved healthy food access including equipment purchases, buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance. A $250 processing fee is deducted from the award amount. Supplemental loan funding is also available through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program, subject to financial review.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, small food-focused retail stores with no more than 25% of gross sales from alcohol or tobacco, and other small food-focused stores serving communities with high food insecurity as measured by the Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases such as refrigeration and shelving, buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Businesses do not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the grant program.

Operate at least 5 days per week year round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items
Meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
For small retail stores with majority of inventory/sales being food-related: no more than 25% of gross sales from alcohol or tobacco
A $250 processing fee is deducted from the award amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a complete application through the DHCD online portal. The application period opened January 20, 2026 and closed February 20, 2026. Applications are reviewed February through March 2026, with funding recommendations finalized in April 2026. Award notifications are sent in May 2026, followed by Board of Public Works approval and disbursements in June 2026. Applicants can schedule an initial consultation for additional support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal and local tax incentive program that encourages investors to reinvest unrealized capital gains into qualified Opportunity Funds dedicated to investing in low-income or underserved urban and rural communities. The program offers three main federal tax benefits: temporary deferral of capital gains taxes on reinvested gains until the earlier of investment disposal or December 31, 2026; a step-up in basis providing a 10% increase for investments held at least 5 years and an additional 5% for investments held at least 7 years, potentially excluding up to 15% of the original gain from taxation; and permanent exclusion from taxation of capital gains from sale or exchange of qualified Opportunity Fund investments held at least 10 years (applies only to gains accrued after the investment). The program pools capital to support investments in small businesses and real estate within designated Opportunity Zones throughout Maryland and nationwide, with the goal of improving communities and quality of life for residents in distressed areas. Additional investment opportunities and tax incentives are available in designated Opportunity Zones within participating municipalities such as Salisbury, Denton, and Federalsburg. There is no authorized cap on the amount of capital available through Opportunity Zone investments, and the program is designed to be flexible, allowing various types of investments. Eligible Opportunity Zones are economically distressed communities with a low-income census tract status, individual poverty rate of at least 20 percent, and median family income no greater than 80 percent of the area median. The program provides incentives through year 2027 and is supported by federal Treasury designations as well as local economic development initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and local tax incentives and technical assistance available to businesses, investors, and entrepreneurs that start, expand, or invest in designated Opportunity Zones, with access to additional capital. Three federal tax incentives for qualified Opportunity Fund investments: (1) Temporary deferral of capital gains taxes on reinvested gains until the earlier of investment disposal or December 31, 2026; (2) Step-up in basis increasing by 10% for investments held at least 5 years and an additional 5% for investments held at least 7 years, excluding up to 15% of original gain from taxation; (3) Permanent exclusion from taxation of capital gains from sale or exchange of Opportunity Fund investments held at least 10 years. There is no authorized cap on the amount of capital available through Opportunity Zone investments. Tax breaks are provided to private investors on capital gains from projects located in designated Opportunity Zones. Program designation encourages investment in designated economically distressed areas. Local tax incentives and investment opportunities also available in specific municipalities including Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County for business and residential projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, non-profit organizations, investors, entrepreneurs, individuals, and small businesses looking to start, expand operations, make investments, or reinvest capital gains in designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland and nationwide. Investors seeking to reinvest capital gains into low-income or underserved communities. Private investors seeking to invest in projects within designated Opportunity Zones. Investors interested in making capital gains investments in economically distressed communities designated as Opportunity Zones. Fund investors making investments in designated Opportunity Zone areas. Investors interested in business and residential projects in Opportunity Zone designated areas. Private investors with unrealized capital gains.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup, expansion, community development activities, economic vitality, workforce and affordable housing development, new infrastructure, start-up businesses with rapid scaling potential, capital improvements to underutilized assets, capital investments in small businesses and real estate within designated Opportunity Zones. Reinvestment of capital gains into Opportunity Funds that invest in low-income or underserved urban and rural communities. Capital investments in projects located within the designated Opportunity Zones. Investment and business development in economically distressed areas. Investments in eligible property located in designated Opportunity Zones through qualified opportunity funds. Project investments in Opportunity Zones in Denton and Federalsburg. Business and residential projects in Opportunity Zone areas. Investment in Qualified Opportunity Zone property (stock, partnership interest, or business property).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in designated Opportunity Zone areas and low-income census tracts throughout Maryland and nationwide. All Maryland Opportunity Zones designated by the U.S. Treasury. There are 149 designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland out of 589 eligible census tracts. Zones are economically distressed communities with a low-income census tract status, individual poverty rate of at least 20 percent, and median family income no greater than 80 percent of the area median. In Maryland, specific locations include designated Opportunity Zones in Anne Arundel County (four tracts: one in Odenton and three in Brooklyn Park), Calvert County, Garrett County (including Keyser's Ridge Business Park approximately 240 acres, Southern Garrett Business & Technology Park 4.2-acre site, and commercial pads along Francis Sanders Drive in Mountain Lake Park), Washington County (Hagerstown), Caroline County (Federalsburg and Denton), and Wicomico County (Salisbury). Of 149 designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland, these represent county-level and municipal locations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors work with qualified Opportunity Funds to reinvest capital gains. The deferred gain must be recognized on the earlier of the date the Opportunity Zone investment is sold or December 31, 2026. Opportunity Funds pool capital and direct investments to eligible projects within Opportunity Zones. Investors interested in Opportunity Zones should review the map of approved Opportunity Zones in Maryland at https://maryland.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=1cc479d2dc3948239f0c47bda8b6967e. Consult the Opportunity Zone Map and contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development or the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation for application details and information about commercial revitalization and reinvestment opportunities in designated Opportunity Zones. For Hagerstown-specific information, contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department. For Caroline County-specific information (Denton and Federalsburg), contact Caroline County Economic Development. For Salisbury-specific information, contact the City of Salisbury business department. Additional information and FAQs are available through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development website, Treasury.gov, and IRS.gov. Investors should also contact the U.S. Treasury for detailed information on how to participate in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses purchase or renovate commercial real estate they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program is funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI). Loans range from $500,000 to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years, and borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of $500,000 to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. Borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Senior or subordinate loan positions are available. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Loan can be used for purchasing or renovating commercial real estate.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing or renovating commercial real estate, including buying the space where the business currently operates, moving to a new location, purchasing property for the first time if the business does not have a storefront, or buying property as part of company expansion. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households through partnerships between the state and local governments. It also supports non-governmental entities in creating housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs integrated within traditional rental housing developments. The program provides loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income, with deferred repayment for up to 40 years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million (without a per unit cap) for small projects (40 units or fewer). For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, eligible household income cannot exceed 30% of the Area Median Income. Loan repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the borrowing entity continues to own the housing and rent it to income-eligible households. Profits from sale of the project must be used for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, non-profit and for-profit rental housing developers, and non-governmental entities. Projects must house low-income households or individuals with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing for developing and preserving affordable rental housing. Eligible housing types include apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects should be located in priority funding areas where possible.
requirements_list: Local government must make a contribution of land or equal value from non-state resources
Local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it

Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50% of statewide median income adjusted for family size (or 30% of Area Median Income for individuals with disabilities or special needs units)
Residents must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds, or neighborhood (except occupants of individuals with disabilities or special needs units)
Housing must remain affordable and income-restricted for the loan term
Non-governmental entities must be applying specifically for individuals with disabilities or special needs units
Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications are evaluated and processed based on meeting the program's purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library. If Partnership Rental Housing Program funding is requested in conjunction with other department funds, the application requirements and applicable deadlines of the other funding must be met. Contact the program representative for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Revitalization and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive partnership initiative between the State of Maryland and Baltimore City combining demolition, site preparation, and redevelopment activities to address vacant and blighted buildings and catalyze revitalization, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore City neighborhoods. Phase I involved $75 million in state investment plus $18.5 million from Baltimore City for demolition of blighted properties, with the city providing in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. The Maryland Stadium Authority managed demolition, grading, seeding, and fencing of sites. Phase II leveraged an estimated $600 million through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in these communities. The program supported demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, site preparation, and redevelopment activities, with focus on half- and whole-blocks of blight to maximize neighborhood impact. It included workforce development services, training programs, and partnerships with local trade organizations and non-profit organizations to provide job-seeking residents with employment opportunities linked to Project C.O.R.E. activities. The Strategic Demolition Fund component provides $50 million in capital funding specifically for accelerating the elimination of vacant properties. The initiative aimed to improve economic opportunity and quality of life, create jobs, green space, and affordable housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $75 million in state investment plus $18.5 million from Baltimore City over four years for demolition of blighted properties and stabilization of sites, plus additional $50 million capital funding available specifically for accelerating the elimination of vacant properties. The city provided in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. The Maryland Stadium Authority managed demolition, grading, seeding, and fencing of sites. Phase II leveraged an estimated $600 million through Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in these communities. The program supported demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, site preparation, and redevelopment activities, with focus on half- and whole-blocks of blight. It included workforce development services, training programs, and partnerships with local trade organizations and non-profit organizations to provide job-seeking residents with employment opportunities linked to Project C.O.R.E. activities. The initiative resulted in affordable housing development, green space creation, and commercial development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents and communities, property owners, job-seeking residents, small businesses, developers, Baltimore City agencies, nonprofit community development organizations, and public, private, and nonprofit development partners working on urban revitalization, redevelopment, and demolition projects in neighborhoods with blighted and vacant properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition and deconstruction of vacant and blighted buildings and city blocks, site preparation including grading, seeding, and fencing, stabilization of properties and sites for future rehabilitation and redevelopment, redevelopment activities, greening initiatives, workforce development and training programs, creation of affordable housing, green space, and commercial development. Funding supports new investment in Baltimore City neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project C.O.R.E. focuses on Baltimore City neighborhoods with half- and whole-blocks of blight and does not expand beyond Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Projects must be in Baltimore City
Properties must be vacant and blighted
Focus on half- and whole-blocks of blight
Residents living in affected areas received relocation assistance in accordance with the federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 if needed
First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations and residents submit applications for demolition funding and revitalization projects through a transparent and ongoing community engagement process. Property owners and residents can suggest properties for demolition, stabilization, or greening. The Baltimore City Department of Housing identifies potential properties for demolition, which are reviewed by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for final approval. The Maryland Stadium Authority serves as project manager. First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination. Application training is available via webinar. Applications accepted by June 26 at 3 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive statewide grant program that provides financial support to place-based economic development organizations (Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other entities) and eligible businesses to activate vacant buildings and storefronts, support small business growth, create jobs, improve commercial corridors, and increase local economic activity. Place-based organizations receive grants and sub-grant funding to existing or new businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment purchases. Businesses that open or expand in previously vacant retail or commercial spaces may receive grants up to $250,000 annually for one or two years to help with rent payments, operating costs, and business investment, with award amounts based on sales and use tax generated by the business. The program aims to fill vacant retail and commercial buildings across Maryland. Eligible businesses must open and become operational by December 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $300,000 per applicant for designated Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other place-based economic development organizations. Organizations use these funds to sub-grant to existing or new businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment purchases to activate vacant spaces. Businesses that open or expand in previously vacant retail or commercial spaces may receive up to $250,000 annually for one or two years based on sales and use tax generated. Tier 1 areas (Baltimore City, Allegany, Baltimore, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince George's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester counties, plus Opportunity Zones and State-designated Main Streets) receive up to $250,000 annually for 2 years. Tier 2 areas receive up to $250,000 annually for 1 year. Funds can support rental assistance, renovation, equipment, staff costs, capital improvements, marketing, inventory and supplies, utilities and similar business operations. Cannot be used for executive salaries or bonuses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline stated; applications open September 8 on rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations such as Main Streets programs, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and similar entities; existing or new businesses in designated Sustainable Communities and throughout Maryland that generate sales and use tax and plan to open or expand into previously vacant retail or commercial spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance, renovation, and equipment for businesses to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in local business districts; rent payments and operating costs in the first year; staff costs, capital improvements, marketing, inventory and supplies, utilities and similar costs related to sustaining and growing the business. Cannot be used for executive salaries or bonuses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Business must be located in Maryland and occupy a retail or commercial space that has been vacant at least 6 months prior to application. Tier 1 areas are eligible for 2-year awards; Tier 2 areas are eligible for 1-year awards.
requirements_list: Must be a designated Main Street, Arts and Entertainment District, or other place-based economic development organization
Located in a designated Sustainable Community
Must have identified priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts
Eligible businesses must be existing or new
Business must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Business must open or expand in a retail or commercial space that has been vacant at least 6 months prior to application
Business must generate sales and use tax
Financially viable business whose operations will continue forward
Must be opening or expanding into vacant retail and commercial properties
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland OneStop Portal at onestop.md.gov before applying. Review the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) and sample application in advance. Submit application online starting September 8. Place-based organizations identify priority vacant spaces and receive grants to then sub-grant to businesses for activation of vacant retail and commercial properties. Applicants should gather required documents and prepare answers before the application opens. Check the Opportunity Zone map to determine if the vacant property qualifies for Tier 1 status.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides loans to eligible developers and organizations to rehabilitate or create rental housing in priority funding areas. Funds may be allocated along with federal HOME moneys and are designed to work with tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other private or public funds. Loans have a term of up to 40 years at 2 percent interest per annum, repayable from cash flow, with a maximum loan amount of $2 million. Funds may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to the development of housing. The program supports the development and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a term of up to 40 years, bearing interest at a rate of 2 percent per annum, and repayable from cash flow. The maximum loan amount should not exceed $2 million. Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to the development of the housing. Funds support rental housing development and preservation. The program awards funding through competitions held one or two times a year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, limited profit, or nonprofit developers, nonprofit organizations, county governments, municipalities, or local housing authorities seeking to develop rental housing projects and affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Newly constructed or rehabilitated rental housing including congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters and shared living facilities. Projects may be restricted to elderly residents. In some cases, small commercial rehabilitation housing projects may be considered.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All new construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas. Statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Available throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Located in priority funding areas
Develops or preserves affordable rental housing
Eligible residents must have incomes of no more than 60 percent of the area median income
Owner must reserve the same proportion of units for low-income tenants as the Rental Housing Program Funds represent to the total financing
Priority given to projects that restrict units to tenants with incomes below 60% of median income
Priority given to projects that restrict units to low-income tenants for more than 40 years
Priority given to projects that provide tenant service packages
Priority given to projects that use non-State funds in addition to State funds
Priority given to projects that provide quality housing in a good location
Priority given to projects sponsored by teams with demonstrated development and management ability
All new construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year and are evaluated against criteria established by the Department. The program awards funding through competitions held one or two times a year. Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The program funds projects that are financed through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. The goal is to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis through competitive funding rounds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate loans funded from state general obligation bonds. The standard loan terms are a 40-year amortization period with 2% simple interest, with payments limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans are due on sale, refinancing, transfer of property, or event of default. The maximum state loan amount per project is $2.5 million, though this limit may be waived in certain circumstances such as addressing interest rate volatility, balancing department resources, or supporting projects with significant economic impact and job creation. Funding is limited to the amount necessary to make the project financially feasible and viable per IRC Section 42.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, county governments, and municipalities seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing through partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Rental Housing Works funding must be used solely in conjunction with projects financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. Projects must comply with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects requesting Rental Housing Works funding must meet the requirements for both the Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credits, including compliance with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan and Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide.
requirements_list: Project must be financed using the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Required zoning for use and density of development must be in place at time of application with proper documentation from local zoning office
Award of competitive public and private funding sources necessary for project's financial feasibility must have been made
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator
Board of Public Works must approve all Rental Housing Works funding awards
Rental Housing Works loans are subordinate loans
Rental Housing Works loans may not be used as cash collateral for short-term bonds
Projects must meet threshold criteria and scoring criteria for bond loans as outlined in the Guide
Completed CDA Form 202 with RHW funds clearly identified
Certification that competitive funding sources necessary for project feasibility have been awarded
Completed Certification to RHW Application Submission Package
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with an application for the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits. Applicants request an electronic submission package and submit applications through the DHCD portal (Procorem). Applications are reviewed and awards are made through competitive funding rounds. Applicants must submit a completed Application Submission Package with required threshold documentation including full-time equivalent jobs created. The department tracks applications by date of receipt and reviews them in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program applications. Applications are scored using evaluation criteria in the Guide. Projects passing threshold are scheduled for kick-off meetings where timelines and critical path schedules are distributed. Projects must proceed according to the agreed schedule. Projects are funded on a 'first-ready, first-served' basis. RHW application may be submitted concurrently with or after other DHCD program applications.
