structured_extraction.program_name: Section 811 Project Rental Assistance Program for People with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal rental assistance program providing comprehensive supportive housing for persons with significant disabilities and extremely low incomes. The program offers project-based rental assistance ensuring tenants pay no more than 30% of their monthly income toward rent, with the subsidy attached to the unit in affordable housing developments. Participants have access to voluntary Medicaid-funded supportive services including case management, housing retention support, and community-based services. The program enables persons with disabilities receiving Medicaid-funded services to live in integrated, independent community settings with access to transportation, shopping, and employment/educational opportunities. Operating as a 30-year federal program modernized under the Frank Melville Supportive Housing Investment Act of 2010, it represents a partnership between HUD, HHS Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, state housing and health agencies, and disability service systems. The program helps eligible individuals with disabilities access and maintain affordable housing while preventing institutionalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project-based rental subsidies ensuring tenants pay no more than 30% of monthly household income toward rent and utilities. Monthly rental assistance is provided directly to property managers/developers with subsidy attached to the unit rather than the individual. Program includes comprehensive supportive services: case management for housing access and retention, housing assessment and counseling, good tenant training covering lease understanding, apartment safety, housekeeping, rent payment protocols, financial management and entitlement counseling, peer counseling/mentoring, crisis intervention and emergency financial assistance, vocational services and recreational/social connections, legal assistance, transportation support, move-in assistance and security deposit coordination, utility/energy bill assistance through state programs, neighbor conflict resolution, and unit health/safety monitoring. Voluntary Medicaid-funded supportive services are available independent of housing arrangement. Lease terms include initial 1-year agreements with rent remaining stable unless income changes. Annual recertification, inspection, and reporting requirements apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-elderly persons with disabilities aged 18-62 at lease signing with significant disabilities and extremely low incomes at or below 30% of Area Median Income. Includes individuals with physical disabilities, mental health conditions, developmental/intellectual disabilities, learning disabilities, psychiatric conditions, sensory disabilities, and traumatic brain injury. Priority populations include: persons currently institutionalized in nursing homes or group homes or at risk for institutionalization, DDA Community Pathways Waiver participants, Mental Hygiene Residential Rehabilitation Program participants, homeless individuals receiving Medicaid, families with children experiencing housing instability, and persons fleeing domestic violence. All applicants must be Medicaid recipients with access to voluntary supportive services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental assistance payments ensuring affordability at 30% of income; case management coordination; supportive services delivery including housing assessment, counseling, training, and retention support; unit inspections; lease renewals; move-in assistance; security deposit coordination; utility and energy bill assistance; emergency financial assistance; legal assistance; and transportation support for housing access and retention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all counties. Applicants select county/counties where they wish to reside. Specific program units located in vibrant and choice communities ranging from densely urban to residential suburban neighborhoods in developments that received federal and/or state funds for construction or rehabilitation, including LIHTC developments and other federally or state-financed affordable housing developments. Preference for integrated community settings with access to transportation, shopping, employment, and educational opportunities.

Age 18 to 62 at lease signing
Income at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI)
Receiving SSI/SSDI or other qualifying income
Medicaid recipient with access to voluntary Medicaid-funded services and supports
Not a registered sex offender
No conviction for methamphetamine possession on PHA property
Pass criminal background and credit checks consistent with Fair Housing Law
Ability to pay rent on time
Ability to maintain unit with care and be good neighbor
Photo identification
Social Security Award letters
Social Security Card
Paystubs
Proof of income (SSI/SSDI, pension/VA benefits, bank statements)
Asset verification (life insurance, retirement accounts)
Proof of citizenship (birth certificate, passport, Social Security card)
Government-issued photo ID (driver's license or state-issued ID)
Comply with lease terms and obligations
Annual recertification requirement
Annual inspection requirement
Annual reporting requirement
Home maintenance ability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications accepted throughout the year. Applicants are referred through qualified service provider entities including Mental Health Administration (MHA)/Behavioral Health and Disabilities Administration, Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), Area Agencies on Aging (AAA), Centers for Independent Living (CIL), and Money Follows the Person (MFP) programs. Contact case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to begin pre-screening and application process. Case manager conducts initial housing intake assessment and assists with obtaining credit reports, reviewing financial information, and completing eligibility packet documentation. Social Serve, Inc. (811 PRA Referral System) manages the Unit Registry and Applicant Referral System at 1-877-496-4954 (8:30 a.m.-5:00 p.m. EDT, Monday-Friday). Obtain eligibility packet from property manager. Complete all required documentation and forms. Submit to 811 PRA property manager with typical two-week submittal timeframe. For existing/turnover units, applicants must be ready to transition and move within 60 days; for newly constructed or newly rehabbed developments, must be ready within 180 days. Download application documents from the Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions and community development organizations for capital improvement and community development projects in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not received prior investment. The program supports neighborhood improvement and anchor institution partnerships with up to $10 million in capital funding available. Funding supports workforce training, skilled trades education, entrepreneurship hubs, and community access projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions and community development organizations for capital improvement and community development projects. Up to $10 million in capital funding available for community development projects located in Sustainable Communities and areas of blight. Funding also supports workforce training, skilled trades education, entrepreneurship hubs, and community access projects. Anchor institutions must provide evidence of matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received from the Fund (1:1 match requirement).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions including institutions of higher education and hospital institutions, community development organizations, and local governments in Maryland that support neighborhood improvement and community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects, workforce training facilities, skilled trades education centers, entrepreneurship hubs, and community access infrastructure that support neighborhood improvement in Sustainable Communities or underinvested areas of the state.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not been invested in, and/or areas of blight. Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility. Projects must support the improvement of a neighborhood.

Must provide matching funds equal to 100% of the financial assistance requested
Must be located in Sustainable Communities or underinvested areas
Project must support the improvement of a neighborhood

Application training available via webinar. Anchor institutions apply competitively through DHCD's State Revitalization Program. For more information and application details, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To improve or create transitional housing facilities and emergency shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans that are fully deferred, secured by a mortgage. Generally, the maximum loan is 100 percent of the value of the property. Alternatively, low-interest loans (0% to 6% based on ability to pay) with maximum loan of $50,000 and maximum term of 30 years for critical repairs including mold remediation, roof repair, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, structural repairs, accessibility improvements, and other health and safety repairs. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income of 50 percent or less of HUD income limits (or up to 80 percent in certain circumstances).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes to bring properties up to applicable building codes and standards or minimum housing quality standard. Includes critical health and safety repairs such as mold remediation, roof repair, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, structural repairs, accessibility improvements, and other code compliance items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide in Maryland across all counties, including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince Georgeos County, and Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Owner must occupy the single-family home

Household income generally cannot exceed 50 percent of HUD income limits (some loans may be made to families with incomes up to 80 percent of these limits if they have circumstances making them ineligible for other DHCD financing)
Property must be a single-family home
Household income cannot exceed 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All loan requests are processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that catalyzes economic development and job production in Maryland communities by supporting demolition and redevelopment activities that improve the economic viability of grey field development (underutilized developed land). The program provides funding for strategic demolition of blighted and derelict structures, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels, site development, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs. Projects must have high economic and revitalization impact. The program offers approximately $10 million in capital funding available for strategic demolition projects to remove vacant and abandoned properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Fund provides financial assistance (capital grants) totaling approximately $10 million to support demolition of derelict and blighted structures, site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels, site development, construction-level architectural and engineering designs, remediation of hazards, infrastructure improvements (sewer, stormwater, electrical, parking), building renovations, historic preservation adaptive reuse, and community placemaking. Projects must have high economic and revitalization impact. Funding is provided to demolish unused and deteriorating non-contributing structures and vacant/abandoned properties to enable redevelopment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, municipalities, nonprofit Community Development Organizations, foundations, housing authorities, and Main Street organizations working on revitalization projects in eligible geographic areas. Organizations addressing vacant properties in designated counties located outside of Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition and remediation of deteriorated/unsafe buildings and blighted, derelict, non-contributing structures, and vacant/abandoned properties; infrastructure improvements (sewer, stormwater, electrical, parking); site acquisition and assembly to create redevelopment-sized parcels for solicitation or planned development; site development; construction-level architectural and engineering designs; building renovations; historic preservation adaptive reuse; and community placemaking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Strategic Demolition Fund is available statewide to eligible applicants whose projects are located in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones. Specific eligibility in Opportunity Zones applies in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Projects must be in designated Sustainable Communities outside of Baltimore City. Eligible geographic areas can be determined using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, nonprofit Community Development Organization, foundation, or housing authority
Project must be in a Sustainable Community or an Opportunity Zone in eligible geographic areas
Project must be in a Sustainable Community or an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico Counties
Applicant located outside of Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application by June 26 at 3 p.m. For more information and application instructions, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Entities apply through DHCD's State Revitalization Program for strategic demolition funding. First-time applicants should contact a regional project manager for eligibility determination. Application training available via webinar.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state designation program that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. The program gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. It combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development under a single geographic designation. The program provides a geographic designation that qualifies applicants for eligibility with other state programs including Community Legacy and Strategic Demolition Fund, and includes planning and coordination support from state agencies. The designation is valid for five years once approved. The program encourages cross-governmental collaboration by providing designated Sustainable Communities with access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A geographic designation that provides local governments access to state resources and qualifies them for funding from other state programs. Includes capital funding grants, gap financing/subordinate financing loans, grants for demolition and land assembly, tax credits (Job Creation Tax Credit, Low Income Housing Tax Credit), below-market interest rate loans, loan forgiveness programs, and technical and planning assistance. The designation is valid for five years and includes planning and coordination support from state agencies. Areas must be within a Priority Funding Area, demonstrate a targeted approach, be near town centers or transportation centers, and show financial need for revitalization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community development organizations, nonprofit organizations, local development agencies, local development corporations, anchor institutions, and small businesses seeking to revitalize older communities and promote sustainable development within Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation enables access to state funding for historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, commercial revitalization, mixed-use development projects, streetscape improvements, business retention and attraction, homeownership encouragement, and projects that strengthen existing communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area. All 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City have approved Sustainable Communities designations. The proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center. Inner beltway Sustainable Communities within and surrounding Baltimore City are eligible for BRNI resources. Communities between the District of Columbia and Interstate 495 are eligible for National Capital Strategic Economic Development Funds.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Must show targeted approach
Must be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization
Must include support for nonprofit organizations, commercial districts, residential communities, and public amenities
Defined geographic area with existing built environment requiring revitalization
Sustainable Community Action Plan required
Local government resolution supporting boundary designation and Action Plan
For new designations, must have meeting with Sustainable Communities Program staff before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request an application template by emailing program staff with subject line including program name, type (new or renewal), and community name. 2. Submit application including defined geographic area, Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives, and local government resolution supporting the designation and Action Plan. 3. An interagency panel reviews the application, led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. 4. Panel presents application to Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 5. Once approved, designation is valid for five years.

Technology-based business

structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant program assists local governments and nonprofits with operating costs and professional services associated with local housing and community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, design services, comprehensive studies, housing assessments, capacity building, and other related administrative expenses. Grants up to a maximum of $50,000 are provided for operating expenses and technical assistance. Funding does not require a match, and all projects or activities should be completed within one year. Capital project costs are not supported through this program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $50,000 are provided for operating costs and professional services associated with administering community and housing revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, design services, comprehensive studies, housing assessments, capacity building, and other related administrative expenses. Funding does not require a match. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. Capital project costs are not supported through this program. Operating funds support specific project activities outlined in award agreement; supports community reinvestment, housing, economic development, and historic preservation initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit organizations involved in community and economic revitalization activities. Nonprofits, community action agencies, housing resource centers, community development corporations, Main Street organizations, preservation organizations, government departments, and universities working on housing and community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs and professional services related to administering community and housing revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, design services, comprehensive studies, housing assessments, capacity building, and other related administrative expenses. structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership program that increases property values and provides wealth-building homeownership opportunities by accelerating development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. The program addresses the appraisal gap—the difference between development costs and market sale price—by having the State cover this gap through UPLIFT funding in historically redlined communities. The program couples development financing with grants and loans to nearby "Legacy Homeowners" living in energy inefficient and deteriorated housing. It encourages single-family housing development for homeownership and prioritizes projects that transform the largest proportion of vacant properties in project areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State provides financing to cover the appraisal gap—the difference between total eligible development costs and market sales price. Developer loans are offered at 0% interest in second lien position for the construction period, with amounts up to $75,000 per unit. Homebuyers receive promissory notes from the State covering the appraisal gap at 0% interest with no principal payments during the loan term, automatic 20% annual principal reduction, and full forgiveness in 5 years. Additional assistance includes down payment assistance to homebuyers and support for legacy homeowners through grants and loans. Financing covers acquisition, construction, soft costs, professional and third-party fees, developer fees, and neighborhood engagement activities.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers (for-profit and nonprofit), Public Housing Authorities (PHAs), local small businesses, community-based organizations engaged in revitalization efforts, qualified development teams, housing developers with experience building/renovating 3+ unit projects within the last 5 years, and homebuyers earning up to 80% AMI.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring, developing, building, and selling quality affordable housing in targeted low-income neighborhoods and designated Sustainable Communities. Funds support construction and rehabilitation of residential housing, property acquisition, professional and third-party fees (architecture, engineering, environmental, legal), developer fees, neighborhood engagement activities, down payment assistance for homebuyers, legacy homeowner support grants and loans, infrastructure and site improvements, and on-site and off-site development costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program targets low-income census tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% AMI or poverty rate 25%+) and designated Maryland Sustainable Communities. Priority given to projects in ENOUGH Initiative areas and Just Communities census tracts. Projects must be located in both a Low-Income Census Tract AND a Maryland Sustainable Community. New construction projects must NOT be in FEMA Flood Zones (waivers available with documentation for Zones C and X). Projects must be within defined project areas with substantial vacant/dilapidated properties. Projects must be located within a single municipality, jurisdiction, or targeted area as defined in concerted community revitalization plan. Refer to the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map for specific eligible locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded residential energy conservation program helping income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland reduce heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation measures and home weatherization improvements. WAP addresses both energy efficiency and health and safety issues by providing free energy conservation materials, products, and services at no cost to eligible households, with no lien or claim filed against the home. Services include energy audits, safety testing, heating and cooling system repairs and maintenance, insulation installation in attics, floors, walls, basements and crawl spaces, air sealing with caulk and weather-stripping around windows and doors, water heater insulation and pipe wrapping, LED bulb replacement, low-flow showerheads, faucet aerators, carbon monoxide and smoke alarm installation and replacement, furnace cleaning/tuning/safety repairs/burner retrofit or replacement, and replacement of inoperable or inefficient Energy Star-rated appliances such as water heaters, heating/cooling systems, refrigerators, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and window AC units. Energy improvements help lower energy costs by an average of 30 to 35%. The program is available statewide through local weatherization agencies and in Baltimore City through the LIGHT program, serving low-income residents with incomes at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level or 60% of State Median Income. Free weatherization services are installed by contractors procured through a statewide network of Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs) and subgrantees including Community Action Agencies, nonprofit organizations, and local governmental agencies. An energy auditor conducts an evaluation to identify areas of heat loss and air infiltration. Baltimore City residents may apply through either the state program or the Baltimore City LIGHT program. Baltimore County residents have specific income thresholds: single person income up to $3,547/month; two people income up to $4,639/month. Households are screened for this and other energy assistance programs upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. Technical field guidance aligns with Standardized Work Specifications (SWS) for air sealing, insulation installation, duct sealing, window/door replacement, water heating efficiency, ventilation, and water conservation measures, with emphasis on lead-safe practices for pre-1978 homes. The program conducts comprehensive health and safety assessments including combustion gas safety testing, lead-based paint evaluation, mold/moisture assessment, radon precautions, and structural integrity evaluation. Mandatory health and safety measures vary by housing type (single-family, manufactured home, multifamily) and are guided by DOE priority lists.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free energy conservation services and home modifications provided through local weatherization agencies and the Office of Energy Efficiency, as well as through the Baltimore City LIGHT program. Services include energy audits, safety testing, heating and cooling system repair and maintenance, blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation installation in attics, floors, walls, basements and crawl spaces, caulking and air sealing around windows, doors and crawl spaces, water heater system improvements and tank insulation, pipe wrapping, LED bulb replacement, low-flow showerhead installation, faucet aerators, carbon monoxide and smoke alarm installation or replacement, furnace clean/tune/safety repairs/burner retrofit or replacement, and replacement of inoperable or inefficient Energy Star-rated appliances such as water heaters, heating/cooling systems, refrigerators, dishwashers, washers, dryers, window AC units, and bath fans. Weatherization work includes furnace and air conditioning repair/replacement for at-risk occupants with medical documentation, asbestos testing/encapsulation/remediation, biological and sanitary condition assessment, building structure and roofing inspections, code compliance work, and combustion gas safety testing. Technical procedures align with SWS standards for air sealing of knee walls, sill plates, rim joists, subfloor penetrations, and sidewalls; insulation installation methods using batts and blown insulation; weatherstripping and door sweep installation; crawlspace moisture control with vapor retarders; duct sealing and insulation; and proper PPE usage including fit-tested respirators. Homeowners and renters receive a home inspection and energy audit to identify necessary services. No lien or claim will be filed against the home. Applicants are automatically referred to WAP unless they opt out on the OHEP application. Qualified applicants are contacted by WAP office prior to receiving benefits. Weatherization services are provided by contractors procured through Local Weatherization Agencies, with each subgrantee procuring contractors through open competition adhering to OMB regulations. Financial assistance for installation of energy conservation materials with income limits for Baltimore County: single person income up to $3,547/month; two people income up to $4,639/month. Health and safety measures are funded separately and do not count toward SIR or average per-unit cost calculations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners, renters, and low-income households in Maryland seeking to reduce energy expenses and improve home safety and comfort. Priority given to households with members older than 60, people with disabilities, households with children under 5 years old, and households with high energy usage or energy burden. Both owner-occupied and tenant-occupied properties are eligible. Also serves single-family homeowners, manufactured home residents, and low-rise multifamily residents. Also serves contractors, organizations, and weatherization professionals requiring training and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation improvements and installations including attic insulation, air sealing with caulk and weather-stripping, water heater tank insulation and pipe wrapping, LED bulb replacement, low-flow showerheads, faucet aerators, heating and cooling system cleaning, maintenance, repair and replacement, carbon monoxide and smoke alarm installation or replacement, furnace repair and maintenance, replacement of inoperable or inefficient Energy Star-rated appliances such as refrigerators, dishwashers, washers, dryers, window AC units, and bath fans. Includes window replacement, door installation, duct sealing and insulation, mechanical ventilation system installation per ASHRAE 62.2, radon precautions, fire extinguishers (when solid fuels present), asbestos remediation, structural repairs, code compliance work, health and safety testing and remediation (combustion gas testing, lead-safe work practices, mold/moisture assessment). Also includes training, certification, workforce development, quality assurance activities, and documentation/monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local weatherization agencies in each territory and the Maryland Office of Energy Efficiency, including all Maryland counties, Baltimore County, and Baltimore City. Prince George's County residents can apply through the state office. Baltimore City residents may apply through either the state program or the Baltimore City LIGHT program. Owner-occupied and tenant-occupied properties in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and throughout Maryland are eligible. Applicants must have incomes at or below specified thresholds. Applicants must demonstrate income eligibility and the house must be structurally sound. Services available in Western Maryland (average temperatures: 65°F July, 28°F January) and Eastern Maryland (average temperatures: 75°F July, 35°F January). Pre-1978 housing subject to lead-safe work protocols.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For households: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) or call the Maryland Office of Energy Efficiency at 1-855-583-8976, 844-400-3423, or 1-800-756-0119 to apply. Applicants may be automatically referred when they apply for OHEP assistance unless they decline on their application. An application must be submitted. Once eligibility is determined, the local weatherization agency will schedule an energy audit inspection. An energy auditor conducts an evaluation of the home to determine areas needing improvement and identify specific improvements needed for each home. WAP office contacts qualified applicants directly. If the condition of the dwelling permits, energy improvements will be provided at no cost. Upon completion of weatherization work, the home receives a Quality Control Inspection by a Weatherization Assistance Program inspector to ensure energy measures are installed according to program guidelines. Households are screened for all three income-qualified programs (WAP, Limited Income Energy Efficiency EmPOWER Program, and Maryland Energy Assistance Program) upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. For contractors and agencies: Contractors contact their local Weatherization Agency serving their county to bid on weatherization work. Local Weatherization Agencies apply through Requests for Applications conducted at least every 3 years. Notification posted on DHCD website and distributed via email. Comprehensive training required for program personnel including BPI HEP Energy Auditor, Quality Control Inspector, Retrofit Installer Technician, and Crew Leader certifications. Hancock/HEAT software training and administrative/financial management training provided. New staff must obtain certification within 60 days of hire. Work must comply with Standard Work Specifications (SWS) aligned with NREL guidance and include energy modeling for alternative HVAC systems where applicable. Subgrantees must maintain Hazard Communication Plans with annual reviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the Maryland Department of Human Services with local county and regional administration including the City of Hagerstown, Washington County Community Action Council, and Montgomery County, is a comprehensive, federally funded energy assistance and weatherization program operating year-round through local county offices and community action agencies. MEAP helps eligible low-income Maryland households and kinship caregivers pay utility bills, repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems, and receive weatherization support and home energy improvements. The program provides utility grants and assistance to prevent utility shut-offs for those having difficulty paying electric, gas, water, heating oil, propane, wood pellets, wood, or kerosene bills without requiring a turn-off notice to qualify. Eligible low-income homeowners, renters, boarders, residents of public housing, sub-metered homes, informal kinship caregivers, and children in kinship care receive free repair, replacement, and weatherization improvements to non-functioning heating, cooling, and water heating systems based on home assessment and funding availability. Low-income residents receive annual heating assistance grants awarded to their heating suppliers, arrearage retirement assistance grants up to $2,000 for past due electric bills and up to $1,000 for past due gas bills, and one-time heating assistance grants per heating season with amounts determined by fuel type, household income, and geographic location within Maryland. Payments are made directly to fuel suppliers and utility companies on behalf of customers. The program minimizes heating crises and makes energy costs more affordable for low-income Marylanders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development / Maryland Department of Human Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance, utility grants, and weatherization support to help pay electric, gas, water, heating oil, propane, wood pellets, wood, and kerosene utility bills and prevent service disconnections. Payments are made directly to the fuel supplier and utility company on the customer's behalf. The program provides free repair, replacement, and weatherization improvements to heating, cooling, and water heating systems for eligible households. One-time heating assistance grants per heating season are sent directly to heating supplier or landlord, with grant amount determined by fuel type, household income, and geographic location. Income-based eligibility with monthly income limits for fiscal year 2026 ranging from $2,608 for a household of one to $10,859 for a household of ten. Arrearage Retirement Assistance provides grants up to $2,000 for past due electric bills and up to $1,000 for past due gas bills for customers with arrearages of $300 or more, with eligibility once every five years. Annual heating assistance grants are awarded to heating suppliers. Customers receive benefits once per fiscal year (July-June). Applications are accepted year-round between July and May each year through participating agencies and local county offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides assistance to eligible low-income households in Maryland to pay off outstanding electric and gas utility arrearages (past-due bills). Eligible customers may receive a grant of up to $2,000 towards past-due electric bills and up to $1,000 towards past-due gas bills, with a minimum past-due balance of $300 required. Grant amount is determined by the outstanding arrearage balance and is sent directly to the utility company. Customers may receive an arrearage grant once every five years, though households with vulnerable members (age 60+, children under 2, or medically fragile members) may be eligible to receive benefits again if the previous benefit was less than $2,000 in EARA and $1,000 in GARA and current past-due balance exceeds $300. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count towards the five-year limitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $2,000 for past-due electric bills and up to $1,000 for past-due gas bills. Customers must have a past-due bill of $300 or greater to qualify. Grant amount is determined by the outstanding arrearage balance and is sent directly to the utility company. Customers may receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Households with vulnerable members (age 60+, children under 2, or medically fragile members) may be eligible to receive benefits again if the previous benefit was less than $2,000 in EARA and $1,000 in GARA and current past-due balance exceeds $300. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count toward the five-year limitation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Center for Excellence in Resource Family Development (CfE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year federal grant program from the HHS Children's Bureau designed to develop and implement a model to recruit, prepare, and support resource families (foster and kinship families) while promoting reunification with birth families. The program aims to improve child and family well-being through increased timely reunification or guardianship, and prevention of re-entry after reunification or guardianship. Resource parents receive evidence-based training (KEEP or KEEP SAFE), participation in learning and support groups, increased case management support, mobile response and stabilization services for mental health crises, planned and emergency respite care services, compensation for time spent in training, and compensation for days when holding a bed for an enrolled youth. Birth families are offered Parenting through Change for Reunification (PTC-R) training and other support services. Participating sites receive technical assistance, quality improvement support through a Learning Collaborative, and data collection support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $8,000,000 federal cooperative agreement from the Children's Bureau. Resource parents participating in the CfE receive compensation for time spent in training and for days when holding a bed for an enrolled youth. Participants receive evidence-based training including prerequisite modules and the KEEP (16-week) or KEEP SAFE support program. The program provides mobile response and stabilization services available within one hour for mental health crises, planned and emergency respite care with consistent providers, increased case management support, peer support through cohorts, and access to mental health crisis assistance in the home. Birth families receive Parenting through Change for Reunification (PTC-R) training. Participating sites receive technical assistance, quality improvement support through a Learning Collaborative, and data collection support. Resource parents receive $25 gift cards per household per completed training module and increased board rates upon training completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Resource parents (foster and kinship caregivers), birth families of children in out-of-home care, child welfare workers, and local department of social services staff. Participants are selected by their local department of social services. Participating sites are selected local departments of social services committed to implementing the model. Children must be ages 4 and older for KEEP participation; ages 13 and older for KEEP SAFE participation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in resource parent skills and birth parent support services, mental health crisis response in the home, respite care, compensation for caregiving and training time, support for reunification and permanency work, resource parent recruitment materials and efforts, trainer development and certification for facilitators, and technical assistance for system-wide improvements to foster care practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Pilot implementation in five Maryland counties: Baltimore County, Carroll County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County. These jurisdictions were selected in Spring 2021 based on readiness, capacity, foster care entry rates, existing programs, partnerships, and diversity of the jurisdiction. Priority was given to jurisdictions with high percentages of children in congregate care settings and high foster care entry rates. DHS aims to implement recruitment in areas with the highest number of child removals to help children remain in their communities of origin. Statewide expansion is planned.
requirements_list: Resource parents must be committed to the values and expectations of the CfE
Resource parents must prioritize reunification and shared parenting
Resource parents must demonstrate commitment to the safety, permanency, and well-being of children
Resource parents must be able and willing to engage authentically and respectfully with birth families
Resource parents must practice trauma-responsiveness and cultural humility
Resource parents must work closely with birth parents and help build their capacities
Resource parents must commit to actively establish and maintain positive relationships with birth parents and extended family members
Resource parents must invite birth parents into the home on a regular basis and maintain regular communication about the child's health and well-being
Resource parents must commit to co-parenting with birth parents
Resource parents must sign CfE commitment form outlining training commitments and ongoing practices
Resource parents must have child currently placed in home
Children must be age 4 and older for KEEP; ages 13 and older for KEEP SAFE
Permanency goal of reunification or guardianship for family of origin participation
At least one individual in home must complete 12 of 16 KEEP/KEEP SAFE sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Resource parents are selected by their local department of social services to participate. Interested individuals should contact their local DSS office. Resource parents will participate in prerequisite training, the KEEP or KEEP SAFE evidence-based program (16-week support groups), and ongoing support through case management and peer cohorts. Birth families are identified and referred by their local department of social services. Sites apply to participate in the CfE through a standardized application assessing readiness and capacity, evaluated using a rubric. Selected sites implement the model with their existing and newly recruited resource families through participation in a Quality Improvement Collaborative.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) / My Groceries To Go!
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal food assistance program that works to improve the health of low-income elderly persons by supplementing their diets with nutritious USDA Foods. Provides monthly supplemental food to eligible seniors and uses food distribution as an avenue to connect seniors with information about nutrition, programs, and services. Participants can pick up their monthly package through a food bank or local sponsor, have an authorized designee pick it up, or have food packages delivered directly to their home in some communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly distribution of USDA Foods in pre-packed packages according to food package guide rates. Participants receive one pre-determined USDA food package distributed monthly. Distribution methods include self pick-up, group pick-up at senior housing, senior centers, community centers, Area Agencies on Aging, or other organizations where older adults congregate, or home delivery to homebound elderly who are physically unable to pick up benefits. Includes nutrition education on a quarterly or more frequent basis and information about other health and public assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income seniors 60 years or older with incomes at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level living in eligible counties. Also serves homebound elderly who are physically unable to pick up benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: USDA food packages containing nutritious commodities to supplement the diets of eligible low-income seniors and reduce food insecurity. Funds also support nutrition education activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local agencies in Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years or older
Income must be at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level based on household size
Must live in an eligible county served by a local CSFP agency
Must verify name, age, and address using acceptable government-issued identification
Cannot receive CSFP benefits at more than one distribution site simultaneously
Cannot be served more than once per month
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of Maryland's CSFP providers to apply: The Salvation Army Central Maryland Area Command (Baltimore City partnership), Capital Area Food Bank (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties partnership), or Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission. Each provider has contact information available on their respective websites. Applications must be completed using the CSFP Application Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A job-training and support services program for non-custodial parents owing child support in Washington County. The program assists unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment to establish a pattern of regular child support payments. The program offers free training in industries including welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality, with the goal of helping parents overcome employment barriers and achieve financial independence. Services include hard skills training, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, help resolving employment barriers, and access to work-related items such as clothing, tools, and textbooks. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job training and support services including hard skills training in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality; soft skills training; job readiness; job search and placement assistance; industry-recognized certifications; work experience; transportation assistance; referrals to community services; help resolving employment barriers; and access to work-related items such as clothing, tools, and textbooks. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that replaces 100% of Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) benefits confirmed to be stolen from SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program), cash assistance, or Pandemic-EBT (P-EBT) accounts. Eligible individuals can submit a claim to recover stolen benefits dating back to January 1, 2021.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program replaces 100% of stolen EBT and P-EBT benefits. Replacement benefits are loaded onto a replacement EBT card within 10 business days or sooner after claim approval. Benefits can be recovered for thefts occurring as far back as January 1, 2021. Previously denied claims or partial replacements issued between March 2023 and January 2024 are being reviewed for retroactive reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals receiving SNAP, cash assistance, or P-EBT benefits whose accounts have been compromised by theft or unauthorized use
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of stolen food assistance, cash assistance, or pandemic EBT benefits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents receiving EBT benefits
requirements_list: Must be an EBT cardholder in Maryland
Must complete an EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form
Must report the theft within 45 days of becoming aware of it
Cannot have willingly given your EBT card and PIN to someone who then stole your benefits
Benefits must have been stolen without the permission of the cardholder
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form online through the Maryland Benefits portal (marylandbenefits.gov) or submit a paper form in person at a Local Department of Social Services office. 2. Type your name on the signature line and submit the form. 3. DHS will contact you within 10 business days with a decision about your claim. 4. If approved, replacement benefits will be loaded onto your replacement EBT card. Assistance completing forms is available by phone through SNAP Community Partner Organizations or in person at Local Department of Social Services offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and subsidy program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, Office of Home Energy Programs, providing financial assistance to eligible low-income households in Maryland to help pay electric utility bills and make utility expenses more affordable. The program is available statewide and also through regional partnerships including St. Mary's County via the Tri-County Community Action Committee, Washington County through the Washington County Community Action Council, and Prince George's County. Assistance is provided once per program year (July through June). Grant amounts are determined by household income relative to household size, electric usage over the past 12 months, average kilowatt-hour costs, and household primary heat source. Grants are sent directly to the electric company to assist with current or past due bill payments. Eligible households include single persons with income up to $2,608/month and households of two with income up to $3,525/month with no asset test. Customers are placed on budget billing with their utility company to spread annual bills into even monthly payments. Only one application is required for both EUSP and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP). Households receiving SNAP or TCA benefits in Maryland are categorically eligible with no application needed. The program helps Maryland's families pay their utility bills, minimize heating crises, and make energy costs more affordable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance with electric utility bills and utility expenses provided once per program year (July-June). Grant amount is determined by household income relative to household size, electric usage over the past 12 months, average kilowatt-hour costs, and household primary heat source. Grants are sent directly to the electric company to assist with current or past due bill payment. Single person income up to $2,608/month with no asset test; two people income up to $3,525/month with no asset test. Participants are placed on budget billing with their utility company to spread annual bills into even monthly payments and avoid seasonal bill spikes. Only one application required for both EUSP and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP). Applications accepted between July and May each year, or year-round in some county-administered locations. Program helps families minimize heating crises and make energy costs more affordable.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - FY2025 applications began July 1, 2024; Applications accepted between July - May each year statewide; Year-round applications accepted in Prince George's County

Income-eligible households

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Office of Home Energy Programs online at MarylandBenefits.gov, by mail, by phone at 1-800-332-6347, in-person at local offices, through secure drop boxes at local Energy Assistance offices, or at senior activity centers. For St. Mary's County, contact the Tri-County Community Action Committee. For Washington County, visit https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment at Washington County Community Action Council, 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740, (301) 797-4161. For Prince George's County, apply online 24/7 at dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/, by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov, by mail to 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, or by fax at 301-909-6331. Only one application required for both EUSP and Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP). Complete applications with all required documents must be submitted. After receiving a complete application packet, OHEP staff review applications and make determinations. Applications can be checked online at myohepstatus.maryland.gov or by contacting local offices. Application forms and instructions are available in English and Spanish.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Assistance to Families with Children
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency cash assistance and resources to families with dependent children under 21 who are facing immediate housing crises or other emergencies. Assistance covers eviction notices, mortgage foreclosures, utility shutoffs (gas and electric), delinquent water bills, and burial assistance. The program provides one-time emergency cash for rent payments, emergency fuel or heating assistance, utility payments, and other emergency expenses to prevent eviction, foreclosure, and utility shutoffs. Funds are available through local departments once every two years when funds are available. Available statewide through the Maryland Department of Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency cash assistance available to families with dependent children facing eviction notice, mortgage foreclosure, emergency fuel shortage, utility emergencies, delinquent water bills, burial assistance, or other qualifying emergencies. Assistance helps prevent eviction, foreclosure, and utility shutoffs. Assistance is available to a household once every two years when funds are available. Program provides direct financial assistance to resolve immediate crisis situations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and residents with dependent children under 21 facing emergency situations or immediate housing crises where the emergency was not caused by a family member quitting a job.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rent payments, eviction prevention, mortgage foreclosure assistance, emergency fuel or heating assistance, utility shutoff prevention, delinquent water bill assistance, burial assistance, and other emergency expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services.
requirements_list: Must have at least one related child under 21 living in the household
Must have one or more children under 21 living with them
Must provide proof household can maintain ongoing monthly rent and utilities
Must be facing immediate housing crisis
Must present proof that the emergency was not caused by a family member quitting a job
Must present an eviction notice or proof from utility company that services have been or will be cut off, or other proof of an emergency
Social Security number required for everyone receiving services
All household members must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent resident aliens, refugees, or asylees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply at your local department of social services in person, by mail, fax, or other electronic means. You can also apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov or through the state online benefits portal at mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us. Submit identification, proof of address, valid Social Security number, court order or summons if applicable, utility shut-off notice if applicable, a record of monthly expenses and bills paid for at least 30 days, proof of household income for past 2 months (wage stubs, benefit letters from Social Security Administration, Veterans Assistance Benefits, or Unemployment Insurance Program), current checking or savings account statement and current balance, proof of emergency, proof of other cash or non-cash resources, and other pertinent information that may be required to process your application.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing support and all services provided to youth in out-of-home placement, including independent living skills development while pursuing education, vocational training, employment, or addressing barriers to employment.

requirements_list: Youth was in the care and custody or guardianship of a Maryland local department of social services on their 18th birthday
Youth left foster care prior to age 21
Youth is not older than 20 years 6 months at the time of application
Youth cannot have exited foster care due to reunification, adoption, guardianship, marriage, or military duty

Must agree to enter into one of the following within 30 days of signing the agreement: completing secondary education or equivalent credential program; enrolled in post-secondary or vocational training; participating in a program to promote or remove barriers to employment; employed at least 80 hours per month; or incapable of doing any of the above due to a medical condition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services to apply for enhanced aftercare voluntary placement services. Work with your case worker or Independent Living Coordinator.
