The program offers utility bill assistance and one-time bulk fuel heating purchases to help prevent shutoffs. Households can receive assistance once every 12 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to resolve outstanding energy bills through a combination of funds and resources, or one-time bulk fuel heating purchases. Emergency fuel and utility assistance for households with impending utility shutoffs or no power. Utility bill assistance available for low-income households. Applications accepted Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am - 12:00 pm, based on availability, with at least 14 days allowed for a response.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications available Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am - 12:00 pm, based on availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households facing an energy crisis such as a utility turn-off notice or impending shutoff in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of outstanding energy bills, emergency fuel, or bulk fuel heating purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a turn-off notice or impending turnoff notice or have no power
Must have a completed application for Energy Assistance through the Office of Home Energy Programs, or exceed Energy Assistance income limits
Eligible for assistance once every 12 months
Low-income household
Meet program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application online at https://fuelfundmaryland.org/apply on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps eligible low-income households pay off past-due natural gas balances on their accounts. The maximum arrearage benefit for gas is $1,000, with a minimum of $300.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant to pay off past-due natural gas balances. Maximum benefit is $1,000 per household, with a minimum past-due balance of $300 required. Arrearage benefits can be received once per five-year period, though households with vulnerable members (age 60+, children under 2, or medically fragile members) may be eligible to receive benefits again if the previous benefit was less than $2,000 in EARA and $1,000 in GARA and current past-due balance exceeds $300.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in Maryland with past-due natural gas balances that meet income eligibility guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past-due natural gas account balances.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed 200% of the federal poverty level
For households receiving SNAP or TCA benefits in Maryland: categorically eligible with no application needed
Minimum past-due balance of $300 required
Must provide valid government-issued photo identification
Must prove primary residency at the address
Must provide social security cards or equivalent federal documentation for all household members
Must provide utility bills and heating bills if applicable
Must document all household income for members age 18 and over for the 30 days preceding application
Arrearage benefits can only be received once per five-year period unless household contains vulnerable members meeting specific criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through MarylandBenefits.gov, by mail, by phone, in-person at local offices, or through secure drop boxes at local Energy Assistance offices. Complete applications with all required documents must be submitted. Applications can be checked online at myohepstatus.maryland.gov or by contacting local offices. Local offices automatically review prior arrearage applications to determine if applicants are eligible to receive benefits again.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible applicants with the opportunity to apply for qualifying jobs before employment announcements are made public. Through state Hiring Agreements legislation, current and former Temporary Cash Assistance recipients, youth in foster care, and noncustodial parents have access to employment opportunities with participating companies that operate under a state procurement contract. Applicants are prescreened, providing Maryland businesses with a ready workforce and eligible employers with tax credits for hiring targeted populations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants can access early job opportunities before public announcements. Applicants are prescreened, providing Maryland businesses with a ready workforce. Participating companies receive prescreened applicants and may be eligible for tax credits for hiring targeted populations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current and former Temporary Cash Assistance recipients, youth in foster care, and noncustodial parents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment opportunity access and placement assistance for qualifying jobs with participating companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through companies operating under state procurement contracts.
requirements_list: Must be a current or former Temporary Cash Assistance recipient, youth in foster care, or noncustodial parent

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports Maryland veteran farmers by branding their products with the Maryland's Best – Homegrown by Heroes logo and offering business assistance services. Veterans can participate by selling freshly produced local products and accessing other business services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veteran farmers can brand products with the Maryland's Best – Homegrown by Heroes logo and receive business assistance services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veteran farmers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Product branding and business services for veteran-operated farms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must own a farm in Maryland
Must first sign up with the Farmer Veteran Coalition at farmvetco.org
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Veteran farmers interested in participating must first sign up with the Farmer Veteran Coalition at farmvetco.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists individuals and families who are at risk of becoming homeless or facing a housing crisis through prevention services to help them avoid eviction and maintain stable housing. The program provides one-time crisis grants to landlords to prevent eviction, case management, counseling, budgeting training, education on tenant rights and responsibilities, and mediation services between landlord and tenant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time crisis grants provided to landlords to prevent eviction. Case management and counseling services provided to households. Training on budgeting and life skills. Education on tenant rights and responsibilities. Mediation services between landlord and tenant. Assistance for individuals and families at risk of eviction to help prevent homelessness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families who are at risk of becoming homeless, facing a housing crisis, or at risk of eviction. Qualifying households must have a lease in their name and the ability to pay rent moving forward.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preventing eviction and maintaining permanent housing. Training on budgeting and life skills. Education on tenant rights and responsibilities. Eviction prevention and homelessness prevention services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland through local departments of social services.
requirements_list: Must be at risk of being evicted or becoming homeless
Must have a lease in their name
Must have the ability to pay rent moving forward
Must be determined by local DSS or service provider to be able to continue to stay in permanent housing or move to other permanent housing
Must comply with a documented case plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services or DHS for more information and to apply for the program. Use the Maryland Community Services Locator to find services in your area.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides aide services in the consumer's home to help adults with disabilities with personal care (dressing, bathing, transferring, grooming, eating), household chores (cooking, laundry, light cleaning, shopping), and other activities of daily living. The program helps adults remain living at home and avoid unnecessary moves to nursing homes or other institutional placements. Ongoing case management is also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-home aide services are provided to help with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living. Depending on the applicant's income and family size, the applicant may need to contribute toward the hourly cost of the aide service on a sliding scale basis. The fee is paid to the Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Maryland who have functional disabilities and need assistance with personal care, chores, and/or activities of daily living to remain in their own homes. Preference is given to vulnerable adults with no willing or capable caregiver available, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with personal care (dressing, bathing, transferring, grooming, eating), household chores (cooking, laundry, light cleaning, shopping), and other activities of daily living to enable adults with disabilities to remain living at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to adults residing in Maryland. Applicants should contact the local department of social services in the county or city where they live.
requirements_list: Must be aged 18 or older
Must reside in Maryland
Must have functional disabilities
Must need assistance with personal care, chores, and/or activities of daily living
Must need assistance to remain in own home or avoid institutional placement
Applicant's income and family size will be assessed for sliding scale fee determination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals or their caregivers should call the local department of social services in the county or city where the applicant lives. The local department representative will arrange a home visit to conduct an interview with the applicant to determine their specific needs. A ranking scale is used to prioritize service based on greatest need and availability of funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to promote the safety and well-being of children and their families by strengthening parents' ability to create a safe and stable home environment while keeping the family together. The program provides support for families affected by substance use, parental resources, referrals for therapy and behavior support, education plans, healthcare assistance, and connections to community providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants work with their local department of social services and caseworkers to develop a family plan. Services include support for substance use issues, parental resources, therapy and behavior support referrals, education planning, healthcare assistance, and community provider connections.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children seeking to maintain family unity and improve household safety and stability
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for family safety planning, parental skill development, substance use support, mental health and behavioral referrals, education assistance, and healthcare coordination
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland via local departments of social services
requirements_list: Must be referred to or contact local department of social services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services to learn more about In-Home Services and begin participation

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, statewide program providing time-limited services to youth ages 18-21 who have exited foster care. The program supports eligible youth in achieving self-sufficiency through financial assistance (including room and board), referrals, and counseling. Services include financial assistance to purchase goods and services needed for self-sufficiency, as well as referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited financial assistance for room and board and to purchase goods and services needed for self-sufficiency; referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance. Services are provided through the local department of social services in the jurisdiction where the youth resides.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18-21 who have exited foster care and need support transitioning to self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for room and board and to purchase goods and services needed for self-sufficiency; counseling, employment, education, and medical services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through the local department of social services in the jurisdiction where the youth resides.
requirements_list: Exited out-of-home placement after their 18th birthday but have not attained age 21, or exited via adoption or relative guardianship after their 16th birthday
Was in foster care until age 18
Currently under 21 years old
Need continued help in making the transition to self-sufficiency
Need housing or other assistance
Participate in the development of a service agreement and sign and comply with its terms
Services are voluntary and based on need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services or caseworker to apply for services. Work with your case worker or Independent Living Coordinator to develop a service agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Agency introduced the Instant Ticket Lottery Machine Program to benefit Maryland Veterans' Service Organizations. Instant Ticket Lottery Machines are lottery vending machines with spinning video reel animation. 10 percent of the proceeds from sales of tickets from these machines are distributed to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 10 percent of proceeds from instant ticket lottery machine sales are distributed to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to benefit Maryland Veterans' Service Organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Veterans' Service Organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for veterans' service organizations through proceeds from instant ticket lottery machines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Veterans' Service Organization

structured_extraction.program_description: An employment and training program that provides career support services and unsubsidized employment placement services for noncustodial parents who owe child support and are unemployed or underemployed in Baltimore County. The program links employers with parents who want to pay child support and assists in obtaining and maintaining competitive employment to establish a pattern of regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CCBC provides employment case management, benefits eligibility specialist services, career counseling, and unsubsidized employment placement services. Part-time case managers and benefits eligibility specialists coordinate services among courts, social services, and American Job Centers. The program connects noncustodial parents with employers seeking workers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who owe child support, are unemployed or underemployed, and have a Baltimore County child support case.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment services including career counseling, case management, job placement assistance, and employment support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-custodial parties with a Baltimore County child support case. The program serves eligible individuals through services coordinated in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Have a Baltimore County child support case
Be unemployed or underemployed
Be able to commit to working upon program completion
Must be a noncustodial parent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Job Network at the Community College of Baltimore County to apply. The Baltimore County Office of Child Support refers eligible work-ready noncustodial parties to the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists relative caregivers to identify and navigate resources and services in effort to support their minor relatives to remain safe in their communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides navigation assistance and resource identification to help relative caregivers support minor relatives and keep them safe in their communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Relative caregivers caring for minor relatives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a resource navigation and technical assistance service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services that provides financial assistance to low-income households to help pay for water and wastewater bills, including assistance with past due utility bills. The program helps prevent service disconnection and restore services for households with disconnected water or wastewater. Financial assistance grants range from $100 to $2,000 based on household income, household size, and the arrearage amount owed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Water and wastewater assistance grants ranging from $100 to $2,000. Benefits are based on household income, household size, and the arrearage amount owed. Financial assistance is applied to water and wastewater bills for low-income households, including assistance with past due water and wastewater utility bills. Benefits can be used to pay arrearages (balances 30 days or more past due), restore disconnected services, prevent disconnection, and cover standard charges and reconnection fees. Benefits are paid directly to the public water supplier or treatment works. A minimum arrearage balance of $100 is required to qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income renters, homeowners, and residents of public housing in Maryland with past-due water and/or wastewater bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of water and wastewater arrearages, restoration of services, prevention of disconnection, standard billing and reconnection fees, and assistance with past due water and wastewater utility bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents who are responsible for paying water and/or wastewater costs.
requirements_list: Must have past due water or wastewater utility bills
Must meet income requirements
Must be a low-income homeowner or renter
Household gross income must meet eligibility limits based on household size (income calculated over 30 days preceding application)
Minimum arrearage balance of $100 on water and/or wastewater account
Proof of identity (government-issued photo ID)
Proof of household composition (Social Security cards or federal government-issued documents)
Water and/or wastewater utility bill or termination notice
Documentation of arrearage balance due
Documentation of all household income for all household members
At least one household member must have legal status with a Social Security number

Categorical income eligibility: at least one household member must be receiving Office of Home Energy Programs (MEAP), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), means-tested veterans' benefits, or Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) benefits at time of application, OR income must fall within gross income limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MyDHR or https://mymdthink.maryland.gov/home/#/, call the program phone number to request a phone appointment, or submit a paper application. Applications can be downloaded and completed, then mailed to 1301 Piccard Dr. 4th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850, dropped off at that address, emailed to ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov, or faxed to 240-777-4099. Applications are available in English and Spanish. Submit all required documents with application to avoid delays. Applications are processed first come first served until funding is depleted. Office will review application and documents within 14 days of receiving a complete application and make a final determination within 45 days. Contact Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services or Maryland Department of Human Resources to check eligibility and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commission for Women Internship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A mentoring and leadership development program that provides internship opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students interested in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement. Interns work with staff and volunteer Commissioners on policy research, communications, legislative monitoring, community outreach, event coordination, and social media management to advance social, political, and economic opportunities for women in Maryland. This paid internship provides hands-on work experience and mentorship while being mentored by staff and volunteer commissioners. Interns conduct research on issues affecting women in Maryland, monitor legislation, assist with outreach, support policy and legislative committees, coordinate public programs and events, develop newsletter content, and manage social media.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internship providing hands-on work experience, mentoring, and leadership development. Interns are compensated at $16.85 per hour with a required 20-hour per week minimum commitment (hours flexible based on schedule). Internships are hybrid, combining remote work and in-person time at the Commission for Women office in Rockville, Maryland. Available during fall, spring, and summer terms. Rolling admissions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students with demonstrated interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement. Ideal candidates are proactive and ambitious with strong writing and research skills, comfort with social media, and experience with community or student organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Interns conduct research on issues affecting women in Maryland, monitor legislation, assist with outreach, support policy and legislative committees, coordinate public programs and events, develop newsletter content, and manage social media related to women's issues and opportunities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to students from anywhere in Maryland. The internship office is located in Rockville, Maryland, with hybrid work arrangements available.
requirements_list: Undergraduate or graduate student status
Demonstrated interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement
Strong writing and research skills
Comfort with social media
Experience with community or student organizations
Ability to commit to minimum 20 hours per week
Availability during fall, spring, or summer terms
Ability to work hybrid (remote and in-person in Rockville, Maryland)
Can participate in in-person interviews
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a résumé, cover letter stating reasons for applying and topics of interest within the commission, dates and hours of availability, a list of goals you wish to achieve during the internship, and a writing sample of 2-3 paragraphs via email to Ariana Kelly, Executive Director. Applicants will participate in an in-person interview. Rolling admissions means applications are reviewed and considered continuously.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit that provides an additional match to the federal EITC for low- to moderate-income working individuals and families. Eligible filers claiming dependents receive a 50% match of the federal EITC, and single filers unable to claim dependents receive a 100% match of the federal EITC. The Maryland EITC reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed by eligible individuals who claim the federal EITC on their federal return. ITIN filers may also be eligible. Additionally, free tax preparation and filing services are available through IRS-certified volunteers at nonprofit and local agency sites, including the new Direct File service for online federal and state filing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State tax credit providing either 50% match of federal EITC (for filers with dependents) or 100% match of federal EITC (for single filers without dependents). Eligible ITIN filers may receive this credit. The credit reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed. Additionally, free tax preparation and e-filing services are provided by IRS-certified volunteers at nonprofit and local agency locations. Refunds can be direct deposited into up to three separate bank accounts. A Direct File tool allows eligible taxpayers to file online directly with the IRS and Maryland with no hidden fees.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-332-6347, Maryland United Way Helpline 211 or 1-800-492-0618, CASH Campaign of Maryland 410-234-8008, Comptroller of Maryland 1-800-638-2937, VITA 410-685-0525 or 1-800-492-0618
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working people with low to moderate income who have claimed the federal earned income tax credit, including ITIN holders and those with or without dependents. Also includes individuals earning less than $67,000 in 2024 seeking tax preparation assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State and local income tax reduction or elimination; general tax refund; tax preparation and filing services; direct deposit of refunds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to all Maryland residents in 17 eligible counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, and Wicomico).
requirements_list: Must qualify for and claim the federal earned income tax credit on federal return
Must file a Maryland state tax return
ITIN filers may be eligible
Social Security card or ITIN proof for each family member
Photo ID for each taxpayer
W-2 forms for all 2024 jobs
Form 1099-G (unemployment income)
Other tax-related documents (1099 forms)
Letter from child care provider (if applicable) with address, tax ID, child name, and amount paid
Banking information for direct deposit
Prior year tax return copy
Form 1095-A (health insurance form, if received)
Every adult on return must come to sign
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must claim the federal EITC on their federal return and file a Maryland state return. Free tax preparation assistance is available through VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) program, CASH Campaign of Maryland locations, and IRS-certified volunteers at nonprofit and local agency sites. The IRS EITC Assistant tool can help determine eligibility and estimate credit amounts. Alternatively, eligible taxpayers can use the Direct File service to prepare and file taxes online directly with the IRS and Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual grant program that funds non-profit and government-operated emergency food providers such as soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs to purchase and distribute food to individuals and families facing emergency food needs in Maryland. Grants are allocated to all 24 Maryland jurisdictions based on population, poverty, and unemployment indicators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants allocated to all 24 jurisdictions in Maryland. Total program allocation: $1,241,661. Maximum award: $50,000; minimum award: $2,000; first-time grantees capped at $2,000. Award period: July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026. Funds are used to purchase and distribute food at no charge to those in emergency need. Organizations must provide food in a clean, appropriate environment with posted hours and community outreach.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and government-operated emergency food providers including soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs that distribute food to individuals and families facing emergency food needs. Serves disabled individuals, unemployed persons, veterans, homeless individuals, seniors (60+), adults (18+), and children (0-17).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and distributing food to provide groceries and meals to individuals and families in emergency need at no charge. Funds may also be used for preparation and serving of meals, and distribution of food bags, boxes, or backpacks. Organizations must provide food in a clean, appropriate environment with posted hours and community outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: MEFP funds are allocated to all 24 jurisdictions in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt feeding organization with non-profit status (IRS 501(c)(3)) or a local government-run program administered and operated directly by a government agency or in partnership with a government entity
Must have a Federal tax-ID number
Must have an anti-discrimination policy
Must meet MEFP criteria and abide by MEFP guidelines including submitting requested reports and receipts
Must distribute information to constituents on the earned income tax program, food stamp program, and other benefits when provided by DHR
Must demonstrate evidence of sound financial and program management
Must have ability to distribute food for emergency need
Must provide food at no charge to those in need (neither cash nor service requirement)
Must maintain clean, appropriate environment for food storage and/or preparation
Must post hours so people know when to access the program and conduct community outreach
Must designate a person to submit reports
Must have physical location providing related services (community services, church outreach services, housing services)
Must be an Emergency Food Provider for at least three years
Must demonstrate community support through cash or food donations from outside entities
Must maintain satisfactory site reviews; food storage areas subject to staff touring and inspection
Program records must be available for review; current year financial statements required upon request
Single audit reports required upon request
Receipts for MEFP purchases required upon request
Quarterly reporting required with receipt documentation and certification of expenditures; tracking of participant demographics
Unsatisfactory site review results in 60-day corrective action plan period; MEFP spending suspended until corrective action plan accepted and satisfactory review achieved
Failure to implement corrective action plan results in award revocation and return of unspent funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through an annual application process submitted via electronic form and are evaluated for eligibility based on MEFP criteria. Eligible applicants receive grants based on available funding and demographic need indicators. Applicants must submit requested reports and complete quarterly reporting using the provided template. Grantees must maintain satisfactory site reviews and provide documentation upon request.

structured_extraction.program_description: A summer nutrition benefits program that provides supplemental food benefits to eligible school-aged children (ages 5-18) during summer months when they do not have access to school meals. The program builds on Maryland's existing Summer SNAP program and implements the federal Summer EBT Program, serving school-aged children across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Eligible children receive $40 for June, July, and August (a total of $120) per eligible student loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card. Benefits are issued in the last week of each month and can be used to purchase eligible food items at stores and vendors that accept EBT, including most grocery stores, some farmers markets, and some online retailers. Benefits expire 122 days after issuance. The program aims to expand reach to serve approximately 540,000 students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible students receive $40 loaded onto an EBT card in each of June, July, and August for a total of $120 per student. Benefits are issued in the last week of each month. For families already receiving SNAP benefits, Maryland SUN Bucks is automatically applied to the existing Independence Card. Families without SNAP receive a separate white Maryland SUN Bucks card. Benefits can be used to purchase eligible food items at stores and vendors that accept EBT, including most grocery stores, some farmers markets, and some online retailers. Benefits expire 122 days after issuance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted year-round; benefits issued June through August. August 31, 2024 deadline for summer 2024 benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-aged children (ages 5-18) in Maryland who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and their families, or whose households receive SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Medicaid benefits, or are in out-of-home care
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To purchase eligible food items such as groceries. Cannot be used for alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, pet food, soap, household supplies, vitamins, medicines, or prepared hot food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to children enrolled in Maryland schools that participate in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP). Most public schools participate; some charter and private schools do. Virtual schools and homeschools do not qualify. All 24 Maryland local jurisdictions are eligible.
requirements_list: Child must be enrolled in a Maryland school that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP)
Child must be aged 5-18
Child must meet income eligibility guidelines (based on National School Lunch Program guidelines)

Child must meet at least one of the following criteria: (1) applied for and received free or reduced-price meals at school in the last school year, (2) household receives SNAP, TCA, or Medicaid benefits, (3) child is in foster care, homeless, migrant, or runaway, or (4) applied for and determined eligible for FARMS before August 31, 2025
All children regardless of immigration status who meet income eligibility requirements are eligible
Over 90% of eligible families receive benefits automatically if they meet criteria
Some families must apply online or in person at a local Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Most eligible students are automatically enrolled using data from partner agencies (schools, SNAP, TCA, Medicaid). Automatic enrollment applies if the child applied for and received free or reduced-price meals, is aged 5-18 in a household receiving SNAP/TCA/Medicaid, or is in foster care. For families already receiving SNAP benefits, Maryland SUN Bucks is automatically applied to their existing Independence Card. Children not automatically enrolled can apply online at marylandbenefits.gov or MD THINK, or submit a paper application in person at a local Department of Social Services. Applications are accepted year-round. After approval, benefits are loaded onto an EBT card and mailed to the address on file with the child's school. The card must be activated by calling 1-800-997-2222. To activate, you need the card number and the child's date of birth and must enter 0000 when prompted for the last 4 digits of the Social Security Number, then set a new four-digit PIN.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps families access assistive technologies such as wheelchairs, low vision aids, adapted telephones, ramps and other home modifications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Medicaid program designed to help Maryland residents who need long-term care services pay for their cost of care and related medical services. The program covers nursing home care costs, doctor services, hospital care, and other Medicaid-eligible medical services for low-income individuals who meet financial, technical, and medical eligibility requirements. Includes a look-back at financial history (five years prior to application) to determine eligibility. Available throughout Maryland, with the Office of Long Term Care specifically serving Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County, and Montgomery County administered through its local office. Also covers waiver services and services in state institutions and community-based care providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid coverage that helps pay for nursing home care costs, doctor services, hospital care, and other medical care services for eligible individuals. Covers long-term care facility services, waiver services, and related medical expenses. Applicants may be required to pay a portion of their income to the nursing home, determined by the program. Coverage includes authorization for Medicare Part B and medical assistance card benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who require long-term care services, including those in nursing homes, state institutions, or receiving waiver services. Particularly low-income individuals, elderly, disabled individuals, and veterans. Must be U.S. citizens or lawfully admitted immigrants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for nursing home care costs, long-term care facility services, waiver services, doctor services, hospital care, medical bills incurred in past 3 months, and other Medicaid-eligible medical care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Must be a Maryland resident. The Office of Long Term Care at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228 specifically covers applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County. Montgomery County administered through 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Can own property in or out of state.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and federally funded program that provides comprehensive health benefits for disabled and low-income Marylanders. Administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, it offers health care insurance coverage for aged, blind, and disabled adults, as well as families with low income, individuals living in nursing homes, and those who are medically needy. The program pays medical bills for eligible needy and low-income individuals and offers comprehensive health care insurance coverage including doctor visits, exams, prescription costs, hospital bills, Medicare premium payments, and other medical expenses. Applicants can receive retroactive coverage for medical bills from the three months prior to application if they have outstanding medical expenses. Spend down provisions allow those exceeding income limits to qualify by covering certain medical expenses. Available statewide throughout Maryland with year-round enrollment available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive health care insurance and payment of medical bills for eligible individuals using state and federal funds. Coverage varies based on income and assets. Assistance includes doctor visits, exams, prescription costs, hospital bills, Medicare premium payments, and other medical expenses. Applicants can receive retroactive coverage for medical bills from the three months prior to application if they have outstanding medical expenses. Spend down provisions allow those exceeding income limits to qualify by covering certain medical expenses. Coverage includes inpatient and outpatient hospital care, X-ray and laboratory services, prescription medication, emergency dental care, family planning, limited transportation to providers, home health services, physical therapy, and personal care services. Year-round enrollment available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Re-Engaging Individuals through Successful Employment (RISE) is an employment program that helps unemployed and underemployed noncustodial parents in the Mid-Shore region of Maryland secure and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment through training, job placement, retention services, and support to remove barriers to employment. The program assists noncustodial parents in establishing a pattern of regular child support payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides employment training and placement services, retention services, and assistance removing barriers to employment. Training programs include forklift training, flagger certification, ServSafe, HVAC, security training, commercial driver's license (CDL), bartending, and welding. Services include hard skills training in in-demand industries such as healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, and biotechnology, soft skills training, job readiness, job search and placement, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, and access to work items such as clothing, tools, textbooks, and work clothing. A personal career navigator and success coach provide ongoing support.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and employment support in healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology and other in-demand industries. Support can cover specialized training certifications, work clothing, tools, textbooks, and transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Mid-Shore region of Maryland, including Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset Counties on the Eastern Shore.

Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should contact one of the Program Coordinators for their county or region to schedule an intake session. structured_extraction.program_description: The NETWorks Program serves non-custodial parents owing child support by providing a broad scope of resources to overcome barriers to employment and increase the likelihood that they will be able to provide for themselves and their families. The program assists unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment to establish a pattern of regular child support payments. The program offers one-time financial support for employment-related expenses and works to remove employment barriers through case management, training initiatives, and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial support to help participants pay for identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation costs related to job interviews. Case managers work with participants to remove employment barriers, including potentially expunging criminal records. Training initiatives include GED courses, driver improvement courses, regional flagger certifications, work experience offerings, and Commercial Driver's License (CDL) courses. Employment services and support to help noncustodial parents find and maintain jobs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents owing child support who are unemployed or underemployed and referred through the Tri Pep Program or have a direct connection to IVA services or a court-ordered referral for employment services in Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Participants must agree to program stipulations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, transportation costs for traveling to and from job interviews, GED courses, driver improvement courses, flagger certifications, work experience, Commercial Driver's License courses, and job placement services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties on the Eastern Shore. The program serves non-custodial parents in these three counties who are customers of the Tri Pep Program.

The program aims to help unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents transition into obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment, achieve financial stability, increase child support payments, and build rewarding careers. The program partners with local staffing agencies and recruiters to develop employment plans.

The program partners with local staffing agencies and recruiters to develop employment plans for noncustodial parents seeking to obtain and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program encourages noncustodial parents to make consistent child support payments by reducing state-owed arrears. Participants who make full child support payments for one year receive a 50% reduction in state-owed arrears. Those who maintain full payments for two years have the remaining balance eliminated entirely. Eligibility requires income less than 225% of the Federal Poverty Level. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made before program participation, and consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-owed arrears (debt owed to the state when the custodial party received public assistance) are reduced by 50% after one year of full child support payments, or eliminated entirely after two years of full payments. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made before program participation. Consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development program that provides public assistance customers with resources and training to pursue entrepreneurial dreams and own a small business. Participants receive business courses covering topics including fundamentals of entrepreneurship, creating a business plan, marketing research, social media engagement, and applying for a business loan. Courses are conducted virtually and/or in classroom settings over a six-week period with eight sessions. Participants also receive ongoing consulting and professional development support through partnerships with local Departments of Social Services and the Maryland Small Business Development Center. Training is provided free of charge. The program is offered in multiple jurisdictions across the Eastern Shore, Western Maryland, Central Maryland, and Anne Arundel County regions, with coverage in Howard County and additional counties including Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, Garrett, Allegany, and Washington.

Training is provided free of charge. Participants must attend all sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) Program / Medicare Buy-In Program / Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) / Qualifying Individual (QI) Program / Qualifying Disabled & Working Individuals (QDWI) / Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive state Medicaid program designed to help low-income Medicare beneficiaries pay Medicare costs and protect them from out-of-pocket cost-sharing expenses. The program includes four distinct Medicare Savings Programs: QMB pays full amount of monthly Medicare premiums and Medicare co-pays and deductibles for those with incomes up to 100% of federal poverty level and assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple. SLMB pays only the monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance premium and may cover deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments for those with incomes between 100-120% of poverty with the same asset limits. QI program helps pay Medicare Part A and Part B premiums and may cover deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments for eligible individuals. QDWI provides assistance for qualifying disabled and working individuals. All programs are available statewide through local departments of social services in Maryland. Applicants receive identification cards (QMB) or letters (SLMB) upon eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple programs available: QMB pays full amount of monthly Medicare premiums and Medicare co-pays and deductibles for those with incomes up to 100% of federal poverty level and assets up to $9,090 individual/$13,630 couple. SLMB pays only the monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance premium and may cover deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments for those with incomes between 100-120% of poverty with same asset limits. QI program pays Medicare Part A and Part B premiums and may also cover deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments for eligible individuals. QDWI provides assistance for qualifying disabled and working individuals. State Medicaid program pays Medicare Part B premiums and cost-sharing amounts for eligible individuals. When you apply, the program determines which of the four Medicare Savings Programs you qualify for based on your income and assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Medicare beneficiaries in Maryland with modest assets; individuals and married couples receiving or having applied for Medicare benefits; Maryland residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments

Regional offices in Montgomery County (Silver Spring, Rockville, Germantown) provide in-person application services.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the QMB/SLMB/QI/QDWI application form available for download from the program page or apply in person or by mail to your local department of social services, at local health departments, or online at https://marylandbenefits.gov.
