structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Covered graduation expenses including class rings, senior pictures, prom attire, and graduation fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to foster youth throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a foster youth in Maryland
Must be eligible for Chafee expenditures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your case worker for more information about eligibility requirements and details. A Chafee Flyer is available with more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: MORA provides employment assistance to help refugees achieve economic self-sufficiency through a network of grantee organizations. Services include job readiness training, resume writing, case management, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation services, and post-placement support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment services including job readiness training, resume writing, case management to address employment barriers, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation during job interviews, and post-placement support. Services are provided at no cost to eligible refugees through MORA grantee organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees admitted to the United States through the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) who are able to work and seeking employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment preparation and job placement services for refugees to achieve economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area (Baltimore), Suburban Washington Area (Silver Spring and Greenbelt), and Frederick Area.
requirements_list: Must be a refugee admitted through the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll directly at one of the program provider locations listed. Providers include International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA), and Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC) in various Maryland locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: RFEP addresses childcare barriers for refugee parents attending English language classes and developing skills for future employment using a multi-generational approach. The program provides simultaneous programming for young children ages 0-5 and their parents, including English classes and tutoring, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups, and support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multi-generational programming providing English classes and tutoring for parents, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups for children ages 0-5, and support services to enable parent participation in ESOL courses while addressing childcare barriers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee families with young children ages 0-5 and parents eligible for ESOL courses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language training, childhood enrichment, playgroups, and support services for refugee families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Must be refugee eligible for ORR (Office of Refugee Resettlement) services
Children must be ages 0-5
Parents must be interested in attending ESOL courses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Solutions in Hometown Connections directly for enrollment and program details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Health education services provided in partnership with the Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health to increase health literacy, support navigation of healthcare, and organize wellness groups including mental wellness and peer support for eligible refugee clients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Health education services provided to eligible refugee clients to increase health literacy, coordinate and support navigation of healthcare, and organize wellness groups including mental wellness and peer support services. Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugee and asylee clients in Maryland seeking health education and wellness support services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education, health literacy support, healthcare navigation assistance, and wellness group services including mental wellness and peer support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible refugee clients. Services are provided in coordination with medical screening locations.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible refugee or asylee client
Clients interested in services may inquire during their medical screening appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Clients interested in Refugee Health Promotion Program services may inquire during their initial medical screening appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Short-term medical coverage providing refugee populations ineligible for Medicaid with similar health benefits. Families may be eligible for up to 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: RMA provides short-term medical coverage with similar benefits to Medicaid for refugees and asylees who do not qualify for Medicaid. Coverage lasts up to 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or grant of asylum. Applicants must first complete Medicaid application requirements through Maryland Health Connection. Those screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees, asylees, individuals with eligible humanitarian parole status, and victims of trafficking who are ineligible for Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical coverage for healthcare services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to eligible refugees and asylees.
requirements_list: Must be a refugee, asylee, have eligible humanitarian parole status, or be a victim of trafficking
Must be ineligible for Medicaid
Must have income over Medicaid threshold (over-scale income)
Must complete Medicaid application requirements first through Maryland Health Connection
Eligibility limited to 12 months after arrival in U.S. or grant of asylum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first complete Medicaid application requirements through Maryland Health Connection at marylandhealthconnection.gov. Upon being screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid, clients may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal at MarylandBenefits.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Health assessment program administered by the Maryland Refugee Health Program in collaboration with state and local health departments to provide newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other immigrants with comprehensive health assessments, appropriate follow-up care, and referrals to prevent and control communicable diseases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive health assessment exams to newly arrived refugees and asylees. The initial health assessment should be completed within 90 days of U.S. arrival or grant of asylum, with the complete exam within 180 days. Services include physical and mental health screenings, immunizations required for school enrollment, health assessment, treatment, and referral to a primary care physician for preventive health and ongoing care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health assessment and screening services, immunizations, referral to primary care, and follow-up care coordination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local health departments and federally-qualified health centers. Specific clinics operate in Baltimore Metropolitan Area (Baltimore City and surrounding counties) and Suburban Washington Area (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties).
requirements_list: Must be a newly arrived refugee, asylee, eligible parolee, or other eligible immigrant
Screening should occur within 90 days of U.S. arrival or grant of asylum
Complete exam should be finished within 180 days of arrival or grant of asylum
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals who meet eligibility requirements may visit their local Health Department or contact one of the federally-qualified health clinics providing Refugee Medical Screenings services to inquire about and schedule an initial health screening.

structured_extraction.program_description: RSIG supports school-aged refugee youth (primarily ages 0-18) in achieving academic success and provides support for public school systems to serve refugee populations. The program ensures students have access to academic support outside the classroom, parents are engaged in their children's education, and school staff have cultural competence to address refugee needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provides academic support services outside the classroom for refugee students, professional development and cultural competence training for school staff, and support for parent engagement in school activities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Silver Spring; International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore; Baltimore City Community College (BCCC)
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-aged refugee youth ages 0-18, their parents, and public school systems serving refugee populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic support services for students, professional development for school staff on cultural competence, parent engagement activities in schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through IRC and BCCC offices in Silver Spring and Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be school-aged refugee youth (primarily ages 0-18)
Must be eligible for ORR services
Must be enrolled in or attending public school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the International Rescue Committee offices in Silver Spring or Baltimore, or Baltimore City Community College for program enrollment and details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered and federally-funded temporary financial assistance program that provides cash support to eligible refugees and asylees until they can secure employment and become economically independent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary financial assistance provided to eligible refugees and asylees. Eligibility is limited to those who have held an eligible and documented immigration status in the U.S. for less than the established RTCA eligibility period (currently 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant). Applicants must be ineligible for other cash assistance programs, not full-time students in institutions of higher education, and must meet income eligibility guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugees and asylees who have documented immigration status and meet income and other eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary financial assistance for eligible refugees and asylees to support basic living expenses until they can secure employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Individuals in all Maryland counties may access Refugee Cash Assistance statewide through designated resettlement agencies, either remotely or in-person.
requirements_list: Have held an eligible and documented immigration status in the U.S. less than the established RTCA eligibility period (currently 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant)
Are ineligible for other cash assistance programs including TANF, SSI, OAA, AB, APTD, and AABD
Are not full-time students in institutions of higher education
Meet income eligibility guidelines
Must complete all required paperwork and provide proof of eligible immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact one of the designated local Resettlement Agencies in Maryland to apply. MORA administers RTCA in partnership with local Resettlement Agencies. Agencies are located in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, and Frederick Area. Applicants can contact these agencies to determine eligibility and submit applications either remotely or in-person.

structured_extraction.program_description: RYMP promotes positive civic and social engagement and supports academic and vocational achievement of refugee youth ages 15-24. The program provides grant funding to support academic achievement, vocational and career advancement, and social inclusion, with eligible youth matched with mentors who provide personalized guidance and support to facilitate social integration and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding supports mentorship services that match eligible youth ages 15-24 with trained mentors who provide personalized guidance, academic support, vocational and career advancement assistance, and social support to facilitate economic self-sufficiency and social integration.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC); International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore; International Rescue Committee (IRC) Silver Spring; Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee youth ages 15-24 seeking academic achievement, vocational and career advancement, and social inclusion support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentorship services providing personalized guidance, academic support, vocational and career advancement assistance, and social support services for refugee youth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through Resettlement Agency providers.
requirements_list: Must be refugee youth ages 15-24
Must be eligible for ORR services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the local Resettlement Agency providers: Ethiopian Community Development Council, International Rescue Committee Baltimore, International Rescue Committee Silver Spring, or Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area for enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Responsible Parents Employment Network (RPEN) in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: An employment program for noncustodial parents in Anne Arundel County designed to engage, empower, and support them in obtaining and maintaining unsubsidized, competitive employment to establish a pattern of regular child support payments and help them find employment and maintain financial responsibility for their children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employment services and support including employment training and job placement services to help noncustodial parents find and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Otis Merritt IV, Young Father's Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Anne Arundel County, particularly young fathers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training and job placement services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent
Must be unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Young Father's Coordinator at the provided phone number or email address.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Restaurant Meals Program allows eligible meal service providers to accept SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits as payment for meals. Eligible SNAP recipients—including elderly (age 60+), homeless, and disabled individuals—can use their EBT (Electronic Benefit Transfer) cards to purchase prepared or hot food from participating restaurants and delis. SNAP households experiencing homelessness can also use their EBT cards to purchase meals at a discounted price from restaurants that have contracted with the federal government to participate in the program. Benefits do not change; recipients simply have the option to use their SNAP benefits at restaurants instead of grocery stores.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible SNAP recipients use their EBT card to purchase prepared meals at participating restaurants. The program allows them to spend their existing SNAP benefits on hot and prepared food items instead of only groceries. Recipients do not pay sales tax on meals purchased through the program. Meal service providers must submit a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with DHS and complete the USDA FNS application form #FNS-252-2 to become authorized to accept SNAP benefits. Providers must comply with SNAP regulations, prevent workers from violating SNAP rules (cash trading, unauthorized benefit use, credit account payments, ineligible item purchases, customer discrimination), and are subject to disqualification for violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible SNAP recipients: Elderly people age 60 and older, disabled individuals, homeless people, and SSI recipients in Maryland, including their spouses in certain circumstances. Restaurant owners and meal service providers seeking to participate in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of prepared meals and hot food from participating restaurants and delis. Cannot be used to purchase alcoholic beverages or non-food items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available at participating restaurants across Maryland. Eligible recipients can use their benefits at participating restaurants in other states that also run the Restaurant Meals Program.
requirements_list: Must be a SNAP recipient (for individual beneficiaries)
Must be age 60 or older (including spouses), OR experiencing homelessness, OR disabled (including spouse of disabled individual if they are the only case participants) (for individual beneficiaries)
Must have available balance on EBT card (for individual beneficiaries)
Must use EBT card at a participating restaurant (for individual beneficiaries)
Eligibility is reviewed at every SNAP redetermination (for individual beneficiaries)
Applicant must be principal administrator, executive director, or owner (for meal service providers)
Must submit Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with DHS (for meal service providers)
Must submit USDA FNS application form #FNS-252-2 (for meal service providers)
Must comply with Food and Nutrition Act and SNAP regulations (for meal service providers)
Cannot be both a restaurant and traditional retailer (for meal service providers)
Must prevent workers from violating SNAP rules: cash trading, unauthorized benefit use, credit account payments, ineligible item purchases, customer discrimination (for meal service providers)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For eligible SNAP recipients: Eligible SNAP recipients automatically receive eligibility at certification or redetermination if they meet the age, homelessness, or disability criteria. No separate application is required for the Restaurant Meals Program. Recipients can find participating restaurants on the DHS website or ask their Eligibility Worker. To use benefits, recipients call 1-800-997-2222 or visit www.connectebt.com to check their EBT card balance, then present their EBT card at the time of purchase at participating restaurants. For meal service providers: Submit completed MOU and FNS-252-2 Application Form to DHS; DHS elevates forms to FNS; FNS issues certification number if qualified. Applicant certifies information accuracy and understands program responsibilities and SNAP compliance requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Roberta's House, Inc. Support Services Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grief counseling to individuals and families whose lives have been impacted by violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grief counseling services provided to individuals and families impacted by violence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families whose lives have been impacted by violence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grief counseling services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide.
requirements_list: History of being impacted by violence

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services to inform, educate, and assist individuals and families throughout Maryland regarding Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. The program connects eligible individuals with local community-based organizations that provide free information, outreach, and application support. Services are designed to reach people who may qualify for SNAP but are unaware of the program, while also addressing misinformation and stigma associated with receiving SNAP benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community-based organizations authorized by the Maryland Department of Human Services provide free outreach, education, and technical assistance to help individuals and families apply for SNAP benefits. Services include information about SNAP eligibility and benefits, help with the application process, and efforts to address misinformation and stigma. The program is delivered through a statewide network of community-based organizations, with customers able to access services through organizations serving their specific area or any statewide organization if no local option is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families who may qualify for SNAP benefits but are not aware of the program, or who need assistance applying for SNAP food assistance benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program funds outreach and education services to inform the public about SNAP benefits, provide technical assistance and application support, and address misinformation and stigma associated with receiving SNAP benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates statewide throughout Maryland through a network of community-based organizations. Each organization serves specific counties or regions. Customers can contact any of the listed community-based organizations or any statewide organization if no local organization is available in their area.
requirements_list: Individuals and families must be interested in learning about or applying for SNAP benefits
Individuals must meet SNAP eligibility criteria to receive benefits (eligibility details available through the organizations or on separate SNAP eligibility pages)
Service is free
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact any of the listed SNAP outreach community-based organizations directly for free assistance. Organizations are authorized by the Maryland Department of Human Services to provide information and help with SNAP applications. Customers can look up organizations serving their area or contact any statewide organization if none is listed for their county.

structured_extraction.program_name: STEP Up (Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents (STEP Up) is a job-driven pilot program serving Baltimore City noncustodial parents with a child support obligation. The program offers free job training and support services to help parents overcome employment barriers and start careers in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, building deconstruction, culinary arts, retail customer service, solar energy installation, brownfields remediation, residential energy efficiency weatherization, and administrative professional skills. Support includes hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentialing, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers such as criminal record or suspended driver's license, provision of work-related items such as clothing, tools, or textbooks, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants who successfully complete the program can earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free job training and employment support services including hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentialing, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers such as criminal record, legal services, or driver's license suspension, access to work-related items such as clothing, tools, and textbooks, and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants who successfully complete the program can earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents with a Baltimore City child support case who can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training and career development in healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, building deconstruction, culinary arts, retail customer service, green construction, solar energy installation, brownfields remediation, residential energy efficiency weatherization, machining, and administrative professional skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves noncustodial parents with a Baltimore City child support case. Initial program enrollment takes place at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services located at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave. Baltimore, MD 21215 Suite 4645.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent with a child support obligation
Must reside in Baltimore City or have a Baltimore City child support case
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (410) 844-7001 x 7144 to schedule an enrollment session at the Baltimore City Office of Child Support Services located at Mondawmin Mall, 2401 Liberty Heights Ave. Baltimore, MD 21215 Suite 4645. During the initial enrollment, participants will join a training program offered by one of the STEP Up employment partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows parents or responsible adults to surrender an unharmed newborn (up to 60 days old) without fear of arrest or prosecution. The program protects newborns from danger or death and protects the mother or responsible adult from legal action. Newborns receive necessary medical care and are placed with a permanent, stable family through adoption via the Local Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A newborn (up to 60 days old and unharmed) can be surrendered at a designated facility (hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and fire companies). The surrendered newborn receives necessary medical care and is then discharged to the Local Department of Social Services for placement with a permanent family through adoption. No prosecution or arrest risk applies to the parent or responsible adult.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals, parents unable or unprepared to care for a newborn, mothers who gave birth, and responsible adults (18+ years old) designated by the mother.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Newborns 60 days or younger and unharmed can be surrendered safely at designated facilities where they receive necessary medical care before being placed with the Local Department of Social Services for permanent family placement through adoption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland at designated hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and fire companies in all 24 counties and Baltimore City. Call 2-1-1 to locate the nearest Safe Haven facility.
requirements_list: Newborn must be 60 days old or younger
Newborn must be unharmed (no evidence of physical injury or failure to provide proper care as determined by a licensed health care practitioner)
Direct handover must occur to designated facility staff member; newborn cannot be left unattended
Responsible adult must be 18 years or older
Surrender must be at a designated Safe Haven facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Present the newborn at a designated facility and state 'This is a Safe Haven baby.' Optional: provide health and family health history information (not required to answer). Staff will arrange necessary medical attention and placement with the Local Department of Social Services for adoption.

structured_extraction.program_description: Training program related to Safe Haven services.

A statewide program that provides youth ages 16-21 in out-of-home placement an opportunity to learn and practice independent living skills while receiving services and housing support. Youth live semi-independently in various settings including renting a room, living in their own apartments, or staying on campus in a dorm, while developing competencies in housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social-emotional well-being. Each month, eligible youth receive support to help cover living expenses. Services are provided through local departments of social services with supervision and case management support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth receive housing and living support services along with assistance in independent living skill development. Each month, SILA youth receive financial support to help cover living expenses including rent, utilities, and other costs associated with semi-independent living. Services are provided through the local department of social services. Youth must contribute to the cost of living through earned income from employment, scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, or Social Security.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth ages 16-21 in out-of-home placement who are working toward self-sufficiency and transitioning from foster care. Applicants must be sufficiently mature, able to manage money, continually enrolled and regularly attending school or vocational training, have a goal of self-sufficiency, and be willing to contribute to the cost of semi-independent living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and living expenses including rent, utilities, and other costs associated with semi-independent living while participating in secondary education, vocational training, or employment; developing independent living skills in housing, health care, education, employment, financial literacy, and social-emotional well-being.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through each of Maryland's 24 local departments of social services. Specific services also available in Baltimore City through BCDSS and the Ready by 21 program.
requirements_list: Between 16-21 years old
Sufficiently mature
Demonstrate an ability to manage money
Continually enrolled in and regularly attending school or vocational training, or working at least 80 hours per month
Have a goal of self-sufficiency
Maintain employment
Needs help in transitioning to self-sufficiency
Capable of contributing to the cost of living through earned income, scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, Social Security, or any combination
Agree to and maintain the terms of a service agreement
Youth not meeting above requirements may be eligible if they have a documented disability in living skills and the case plan documents how the disability can be accommodated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services or work with your case worker to apply for SILA services. In Baltimore City, you can get a SILA application and information packet from your BCDSS case worker, your attorney, or by calling the Ready by 21 program at 443-423-6120. Work with your Independent Living Coordinator and case worker to complete the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Services Helping the Involvement of Non-Custodial Parents and Employment (SHINE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, comprehensive 12-month case management program designed for noncustodial parents obligated to pay child support. The program helps participants overcome barriers to employment, secure financial stability, and strengthen relationships with their children through employment services, legal aid, family resources, and basic needs support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 12 months of free case management including job readiness activities, skill building, resume development, interview training, access to vocational and GED training, documentation assistance, legal aid, parenting resources, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing assistance, transportation resources, financial aid, and work clothing. Participants meet regularly with a Non-custodial Parent Employment Program Specialist to monitor progress and track compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents seeking employment and involvement with their children. In practice, participants are typically those in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support and ordered by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing for outstanding arrearages or referred by the Child Support Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants access services including employment support, job training, vocational education, GED classes, document acquisition, legal assistance, parenting resources, mental health services, substance abuse treatment, housing assistance, transportation support, financial assistance, child care resources, and work essentials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents. Program currently operates in Allegany County with participants typically ordered by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing or referred by the Child Support Administration.
requirements_list: Noncustodial parent obligated to pay child support
Seeking stable employment and requiring support to comply with child support order
Must not have known physical or mental disabilities that prevent working
Must meet with NPEP Specialist for intake and assessment
Required to provide weekly job search activity updates
Required to report current employment status and income
Required to report child support payment history
Must immediately report all changes of address, phone number, or employment status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are typically referred by Court or Child Support Administration. The process begins with an intake assessment form completion and intake appointment at the appropriate DSS office where a Non-custodial Parent Employment Program Specialist (NPEP) conducts a strengths and needs assessment to identify barriers to employment. Participants review compliance policies and then enter a 12-month case management phase with regular monitoring and reporting requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to ensure that eligible refugees aged 60 years or above receive appropriate services to address the unique needs faced by older clients through programming that is culturally and linguistically sensitive and age appropriate. Primary goal is to increase integration and independent healthy living for older ORR-eligible populations through case management, connecting to mainstream senior programs, citizenship application assistance and exam preparation, and other activities designed to promote well-being and social integration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management, connection to mainstream senior programs, citizenship application assistance and exam preparation, and activities designed to promote well-being and social integration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees aged 60 years or above
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support older refugees in achieving independent healthy living and social integration
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Services available in Suburban Washington and Baltimore Metropolitan Area
requirements_list: Must be refugee aged 60 years or above
Must be ORR-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC) for Suburban Washington area, or Baltimore City Community College (BCCC) and International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Baltimore for Baltimore Metropolitan Area

structured_extraction.program_description: A core case management program that provides assistance to vulnerable adults seeking to remain or become self-supporting and self-sufficient. The program builds on the strengths of the adult's community and family support system, seeks to prevent abuse, neglect, or exploitation, and reduces unnecessary institutionalization. Services include information and referral, crisis intervention for up to 60 days, and comprehensive case management with individualized service plans, all provided without fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services provided without fee including information and referral to connect adults with appropriate agencies, crisis intervention for up to 60 days with intensive help and guidance during life crises, and case management. A social worker conducts a comprehensive assessment of the adult's needs and resources and develops an individualized plan of service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 65 and older with functional disabilities regardless of income, and adults under age 65 with disabilities whose income does not exceed 80% of the State median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to help adults remain or become self-supporting and self-sufficient, prevent abuse and neglect, and secure appropriate care, including case management, information and referral services, and crisis intervention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services in each county.
requirements_list: Age 65 or older with functional disabilities (no income limit)
Under age 65 with functional disabilities and income not exceeding 80% of State median income
Must apply through the local department of social services in your county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply to the local department of social services in your county. Find your local office through the DHS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides annual grants to emergency food providers to purchase equipment such as freezers and other appliances that increase their capacity to purchase, store, and distribute food. Funds are available for all Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants for equipment purchases including freezers and appliances to increase capacity to purchase, store, and distribute food.

structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP is the largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation, providing monthly food assistance benefits to eligible low-income individuals and families, including kinship caregivers and children in their care, to help them buy nutritious food for good health. Benefits are issued electronically on a debit-like card (EBT), known as the Independence Card, and can be used to purchase groceries and food items at authorized retailers, including participating online grocery services. The program assists low-income households in having a more nutritious diet by increasing their purchasing power for food purchases. A household is defined as people living together who buy food and prepare meals together. Benefits are calculated based on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Thrifty Food Plan and Maximum Allotment formula, which estimates the cost of nutritious, low-cost meals, and depend on household size and monthly income after deductions and allowable expenses. Applicants must file an application and meet all financial and technical eligibility factors prior to receiving benefits. Some people with little or no money may qualify for expedited SNAP benefits right away with only an interview and identity verification. Benefits should be accessible no later than 30 days from the date the application is received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SNAP provides monthly food assistance benefits to eligible low-income households and kinship caregivers through electronically issued debit cards (EBT), such as the Independence Card. The amount is based on the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Thrifty Food Plan and Maximum Allotment formula and depends on household size, monthly income after deductions, and allowable expenses. Maximum benefit amounts range from $339 for a 1-person household to $1,421+ for households with 8 or more people with no income. Households must contribute some of their own cash along with benefits to cover monthly food needs. Applicants must file an application, be interviewed, and meet all financial and technical eligibility factors prior to issuance of benefits. Benefits should be accessible no later than 30 days from the date the application is received. Some people with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits right away with only an interview and identity verification. Benefits can be used for shopping in stores or online for eligible food products at authorized retailers, and cash benefits can be accessed from ATMs. Benefits cannot be used for non-food items, prepared meals, or hot foods. Expedited benefits may be issued within 7 days for those with minimal resources. Applications can be submitted online, by phone, mail, fax, or in person at county offices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families including those who are unemployed, work part-time, earn low wages, receive public assistance, are elderly or disabled, are homeless or unhoused, informal kinship caregivers, and children in kinship care, or who meet income, financial, and technical eligibility requirements and live in Maryland. U.S. citizens and certain eligible immigrants are eligible. Most students ages 18-49 enrolled full-time in college are not eligible unless they meet specific exceptions such as working at least 20 hours per week, participating in work-study, or caring for dependents. Households with gross monthly income under 130% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of groceries and nutritious food items from authorized retail locations, including participating online grocery services, for household consumption. Benefits can be used to buy food for nutritious low-cost meals and nutrition assistance. Eligible foods include fruits, vegetables, grains, proteins, and dairy products. Benefits cannot be used for non-food items, prepared meals, or hot foods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland across all counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester). Applicants can file applications with their Local Department of Social Services, by mail, by fax, by phone at 1-800-332-6347 or 1-833-373-5867, or online through MarylandBenefits.gov or the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal. Applicants must be US citizens or eligible noncitizens and be Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be submitted online at MarylandBenefits.gov or the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, in person at a local department of social services, county office, or regional office location based on zip code, by phone at 1-800-332-6347 or 1-833-373-5867, by mail, or by fax. Documents can be photographed or scanned and emailed. The local office will accept a signed application the same day it is received. Applications are reviewed the same day to determine eligibility within 7 days. If not interviewed on the day of application submission, the local department will contact the applicant to schedule an interview. Applicants must be interviewed and meet all financial and technical eligibility factors prior to receiving benefits. Those with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits with only an interview and identity verification. A case manager will explain program rules, help complete the application, and request proof of information provided. Applications can be submitted to the front desk by 11am for same-day interview (Monday-Thursday). Applications can be dropped off any day for expedited screening or later interview date. Face-to-face interview required. Applicants are seen on a walk-in basis or by appointment. An interpreter is available for applicants with limited English proficiency. Application processing involves verification of income, household size, and expenses. After the interview, the local department sends a notice indicating approval amount and benefit duration or denial reason. Case processing takes up to 30 days or more. Complete Application for Assistance form DHS/FIA 9701. Provide household member information, income, resources, and shelter costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland offers free employment and training services to SNAP recipients to connect them with job-driven training programs. Programs run for an average of 12 to 16 weeks and train participants for employment in industries such as welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, computer technology/IT, retail trade, educational services, and arts and entertainment. All SNAP E&T programs offer job placement, retention, and support services. The program includes hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement services, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers, and access to items needed to work such as clothing, tools, or textbooks. All participants receive support from a personal career navigator and success coach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free industry-specific training programs for an average of 12 to 16 weeks that provide hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness, job search and placement services, industry-recognized certifications and credentials, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers including assistance with criminal records and legal services, and access to items needed to work such as clothing, tools, or textbooks. All participants receive support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Many programs include job placement, retention, and support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SNAP recipients age 16 and over who receive monthly SNAP benefits, do not receive Cash Assistance/Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), and are able to work upon completion of the program. Participation is voluntary for most SNAP recipients, but Able Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) may be required to enroll to maintain benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive free training in job-driven sectors including welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, computer technology/IT, and retail trade. Support services include transportation, work clothing, tools, textbooks, and resolution of employment barriers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland statewide.

Must receive monthly SNAP benefits
Must not receive Cash Assistance/Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)
Must be able to work upon completion of the program
Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) must be working or actively enrolled in an employment and training program to maintain SNAP benefits beyond three months
Individual SNAP E&T programs may have additional eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no application for SNAP E&T. Interested individuals who receive SNAP benefits should contact their local Department of Social Services or call the DHS helpline at (800) 332-6347 to enroll. For those not currently receiving SNAP, first apply for SNAP benefits online at marylandbenefits.gov or in person at a local department of social services. A list of SNAP E&T providers is available through a public database.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides monthly pass-through payments to custodial parents and caregivers receiving cash assistance through Maryland's Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) program. When a noncustodial parent makes current child support payments, the Department of Human Services forwards a portion of that payment to the custodial party based on the number of children in the household. The maximum payment is $100 per month for one child or $200 per month for two or more children in the TCA household, or the court-ordered amount, whichever is less. Payments are based on current support only; arrears payments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly pass-through payments to custodial parties based on current child support paid in the prior month. Families receive up to $100 per month for one child or $200 per month for two or more children, whichever is less than the court-ordered amount. Payments are based on current support only; arrears are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Custodial parents and caregivers who are receiving cash assistance through the Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) program and have an active child support case with current support payments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly financial assistance passed through to custodial parties to help support children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for eligible recipients authorized to receive cash assistance through the state's Temporary Cash Assistance program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), which is Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) program, provides time-limited cash assistance to families with dependent children under 18 years of age when available resources and services do not fully meet the family's needs. The program promotes individual responsibility and self-sufficiency through employment support, work activities, and preparation for economic independence. Cash benefits are issued through the Electronic Benefit Transfer System (EBT) plastic card known as the Independence Card, with funds available from the 2nd to the 4th of every month based on the first letter of the applicant's last name. Assistance amount is based on the family's assistance unit size and cannot exceed the benefit level when combined with earned and unearned income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited monthly cash assistance provided to eligible families with dependent children to help meet family living expenses and support employment activities and work preparation. Cash benefits are issued through the Electronic Benefit Transfer System (EBT) plastic card known as the Independence Card, with applicants able to withdraw money from automatic teller machines (ATM) or buy things at participating stores. Cash benefits are made available from the 2nd to the 4th of every month, based on the first letter of the applicant's last name. Assistance amount is based on the family's assistance unit size and cannot exceed the benefit level when combined with earned and unearned income. Eligibility is based on household size and income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with dependent children under 18 needing financial assistance when available resources and services do not fully meet the family's needs. Families with low income and children are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance for family living expenses. Funds can be withdrawn from automatic teller machines (ATM) or used to buy things at participating stores to help families meet basic needs while they prepare for work and independence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services, including Montgomery County and Howard County. In Montgomery County, services are available at three locations: Mid-County DHHS Building in Rockville, DHHS Silver Spring Center in Silver Spring, and Up-County Regional Services Center in Germantown. Applicants must be US citizens or meet alien status and be Maryland residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through MarylandBenefits.gov at https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/, online at the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal, by fax, email, or mail to any OESS office location or local Department of Social Services office. Someone may also submit an application on the applicant's behalf. For Montgomery County: Step 1: View the DHHS Orientation video and download the DHHS Packet. Step 2: Complete and submit the orientation packet by email to Employment.Services@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or fax to 240-777-4166. Step 3: Apply for Child Support Enforcement Services using the DHS online application at benefits.maryland.gov. Step 4: Cooperate with Substance Abuse Screening program. Step 5: Once approved, comply with the Work Program by contacting Equus at MDMontCoTANF@equusworks.com or 301-740-7700. Step 6: Bring required documents to an interview at one of the three DHHS locations. Schedule face-to-face interview. Documents can be photographed or scanned and emailed. All applications must be signed by the head of household or authorized representative. Family must meet income guidelines and complete specific work and child support requirements before approval. Applicants must begin work activity before case is approved and provide weekly attendance verifications. Case processing takes up to 30 days or more.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal nutrition assistance program that provides emergency food and administrative funds to eligible agencies to distribute nutritious USDA foods to low-income individuals and families in Maryland. The program supplements the diets of low-income Americans and alleviates hunger through partnerships with the Maryland Food Bank and Capital Area Food Bank, serving all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides USDA Foods (such as canned fruits, canned vegetables, fruit juice, dried egg mix, meat, poultry, fish, dried beans, pasta products, milk, rice, grits, cereal, and soups) to eligible soup kitchens, food pantries, shelters, residential programs, and other eligible recipient agencies (ERAs) and emergency feeding organizations (EFOs) throughout all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Administrative funds are also provided to cover costs of warehousing, delivery, and distribution of TEFAP foods. Food types vary based on state preferences and agricultural market conditions. The program is administered through partnerships with the Maryland Food Bank (serving 22 jurisdictions) and the Capital Area Food Bank (serving Montgomery and Prince George's counties). Technical assistance and information are available.
structured_extraction.contact_name: TEFAP Administrator, Bureau of Special Grants, Family Investment Administration, Maryland Department of Human Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines; SNAP recipients; Medical Assistance recipients; TANF recipients; Unemployment recipients; Energy Assistance recipients; homeless populations; homebound and handicapped individuals; seniors; and other economically disadvantaged populations. Eligible organizations include food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, religious organizations, community action agencies, and other tax-exempt organizations serving low-income populations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of USDA Foods (Entitlement and Bonus foods) to eligible individuals and families for household consumption and prepared meals through food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, and schools. Administrative funds for ordering, receiving, tracking, storing, and distributing TEFAP foods, including warehouse operations, staff salaries, transportation, and program administration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. To find the nearest TEFAP provider: residents in all Maryland counties except Montgomery and Prince George's should visit www.mdfoodbank.org and use the 'Find Food' link. Residents in Montgomery or Prince George's counties should visit www.capitalareafoodbank.org and use the 'Get Help' link. Food allocation is based on each jurisdiction's poverty and unemployment rates.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For eligible organizations: work with the Maryland Food Bank or Capital Area Food Bank to register as an eligible recipient agency or emergency feeding organization. For individuals and families seeking TEFAP assistance: locate your nearest provider by visiting the appropriate food bank website for your county (www.mdfoodbank.org for most counties; www.capitalareafoodbank.org for Montgomery and Prince George's) and entering your zip code. Complete the Maryland Self-Disclosure Form with household information and verify eligibility through one of the six eligible categories. An applicant or authorized proxy completes the self-disclosure form with household information and eligibility category verification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reliable used vehicles to eligible low-income families and individuals for two years or 24,000 miles to help them access better job opportunities, reduce commute times, improve family health, and enhance overall quality of life. The program increases mobility, makes higher-paying jobs or shifts more accessible, and supports recipients of or eligible for the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides reliable used vehicles to eligible families and individuals for a two-year period or up to 24,000 miles through a network of partners across the state, including local departments of social services and Vehicles for Change, the statewide TAP partner. The vehicle assistance enables access to better job opportunities, reduces commute times, improves family health and circumstances, and enhances overall wellbeing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recipients of or eligible for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program and other eligible low-income families and individuals across Maryland who need reliable transportation to access employment and achieve financial independence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reliable used vehicles to enable access to better job opportunities, reduce commute times, improve family health, support employment and mobility, and enhance overall quality of life.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through a network of partners including local departments of social services and Vehicles for Change, the statewide TAP partner. Contact your local department of social services to determine eligibility.

Must be low-income
Must be a family or individual needing reliable transportation to access employment
Must be seeking employment or working to achieve financial independence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested potential participants should inquire through their local department of social services TAP Coordinator or contact Vehicles for Change, the statewide TAP partner. Contact your local department of social services to find out whether you qualify.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance program designed to protect low-income families from utility service disconnections during the heating season by providing assistance to maintain continuous utility service. Administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs and available statewide, with specific county-level administration in Prince George's County. The program allows Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) eligible households to enter into a year-round equal monthly payment plan (budget billing) with their utility company. Monthly payments are calculated based on estimated average annual utility usage minus MEAP benefits awarded, creating level payments throughout the year. All MEAP-eligible customers may participate in this year-round budget billing protection from service interruption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help income-eligible households pay utility and fuel bills and reduce utility, heating, and cooling expenses. The program allows MEAP-eligible households to participate in an equal monthly payment plan with their utility company. Monthly payment amounts are calculated based on estimated average annual utility usage minus MEAP benefits awarded. Protection from utility service disconnection during the heating season for eligible low-income customers. Participation requires year-round equal monthly budget billing. Failure to make consecutive payments may result in removal from USPP. Customers must be able to make regular monthly payments.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection against utility service disconnection; utility bills, fuel bills, heating expenses, and cooling expenses through a structured equal monthly payment plan; requires participation in equal monthly budget billing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to MEAP-eligible households, with specific county-level administration in Prince George's County and specific services available in the City of Frederick.

Application forms and instructions available in English and Spanish. Check application status online at myohepstatus.org.
