structured_extraction.program_description: A program that empowers incarcerated and unemployed or underemployed noncustodial fathers in Baltimore County to develop employment and life skills as they prepare to transition back into the community or obtain and maintain unsubsidized, competitive employment. Participants receive job readiness training, resume writing assistance, interviewing techniques, background and credit check assistance, employment law education, legal resources, federal bonding information, expungement assistance, dressing for success training, soft skills development (communication, self-confidence, social skills, time management, problem solving, anger management), and connections to employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides job readiness workshops, resume writing, cover letter writing, interview techniques, background and credit check assistance, employment law education, legal resources, federal bonding information, expungement assistance, dressing for success training, and self-directed job search support. Employment services and support to help noncustodial fathers find and maintain jobs. A full-time Job Developer and two full-time Social Workers assist participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial fathers incarcerated at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center or unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Baltimore County with court-ordered child support obligations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job skills development and employment preparation including soft skills training, employment support, and job placement services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, limited to fathers incarcerated at the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center in Towson, Maryland and unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents in Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be incarcerated at Baltimore County Men's Detention Center or unemployed or underemployed
Must have a minimum of 120 days remaining on sentence (if incarcerated)
Must be a noncustodial parent with court-ordered child support obligation or must be unemployed or underemployed
Should possess a positive attitude and eagerness to create a better life
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested fathers should contact the Program Coordinators or call the DHS helpline for enrollment information

structured_extraction.program_name: Wounded Warrior and Veteran Outreach Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides outdoor and recreational activities such as hiking, biking, boating, fishing, swimming, horseback riding, team building ropes courses, hunting and camping for wounded warriors and veterans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Veterans receive recreational and outdoor activities including hiking, biking, boating, fishing, swimming, horseback riding, team building ropes courses, hunting, and camping.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wounded warriors and veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreational and outdoor activities for wounded warriors and veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran or wounded warrior

structured_extraction.program_description: A no-cost employment and training program that empowers non-custodial fathers to become more responsible and active participants in their children's lives. The program provides job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, parenting classes, case management, and legal assistance to help fathers overcome barriers to employment and establish a pattern of regular child support payments. Services include support through partner organizations for housing, foreclosure, family law, debt matters, and recovery services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-cost training for careers, job readiness and employment development, life skills counseling, parenting classes, case management services, and legal assistance through partner organizations for housing, foreclosure, family law, and debt matters. Services also include support through partner organizations like Recovery Outreach System Care Team (ROSC), The Homeless ID Project, WRAP (Wellness Recovery Action Plan), and Chesapeake College's ACE (Accelerating Connections to Employment Program).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial fathers and non-custodial parties who are unemployed or underemployed in Baltimore County, Caroline County, and Talbot County and can commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for careers to support self and family; job readiness and employment development; life skills counseling; legal assistance for housing, foreclosure, family law, and debt matters; and employment support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to participants with a child support case in Baltimore County, Caroline County, or Talbot County. The program is hosted at the Caroline County Social Services Building, 300 Market Street, Denton, Maryland, in partnership with Caroline County Department of Social Services.
requirements_list: Must be a non-custodial party with a child support case in an eligible county
Must be unemployed or underemployed
Must be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should contact program coordinator Isaiah Greene at 410-819-4471 or isaiah.green@maryland.gov, or Lori Keel at lori.keel@maryland.gov, or call the DHS helpline at 1-800-332-6347 to start the enrollment process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Active Duty Military Servicemember or Spouse License Recognition
structured_extraction.program_description: Allows active duty servicemembers or their spouses holding valid occupational licenses in another state to practice in Maryland without obtaining permanent licensure, provided they maintain good standing and remain under military orders for Maryland assignment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Letter of recognition allowing practice in Maryland under VAEIA without permanent licensure; valid only during military orders assignment in Maryland. There is no fee associated with this application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military servicemembers or their spouses with out-of-state occupational licenses ordered to Maryland for military service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program does not provide financial assistance. It provides recognition of out-of-state occupational licenses to allow practice in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must have military orders assigning duty station in Maryland. Applicants must reside in Maryland as a result of military orders.
requirements_list: You or your spouse is an active duty military servicemember
You reside in Maryland as a result of military orders
You hold a valid, good-standing occupational license from another U.S. state or territory
You have actively used your occupational license in the two years immediately preceding the order to relocate to Maryland
Your license must be maintained in good standing in its original jurisdiction for the duration of the military orders
License must be issued by a U.S. state or territorial licensing authority
Marriage certificate if applying as military spouse
Proof of Maryland residence
Verification of active licenses from original licensing authority
Compliance with Maryland laws, regulations, and discipline guidelines
No felony/misdemeanor convictions or prior license denials/suspensions/revocations (or documentation if applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the license recognition application form. Save the form to your computer before filling it out to ensure changes are saved. Submit the completed application with required documents via email to the appropriate board or commission. The Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing will review the application and issue an official letter of recognition if requirements are met. Board representatives may contact applicants to request additional documents required for specific licenses.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 26 Continuation Grant for Consolidated Adult Education & Family Literacy Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A continuation grant program that supports consolidated adult education and family literacy services across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Continuation grant funding for adult education and family literacy services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult education and family literacy service providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Consolidated adult education and family literacy services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the agency for information and documents related to the grant.

structured_extraction.program_description: ARPA-funded initiative providing $15 million to support employers working on infrastructure projects throughout Maryland to attract and retain workers. The program addresses barriers hindering workforce participation and retention through flexible, creative solutions supporting both transportation and utility infrastructure and information technology infrastructure. Employers can implement employee support programs and payroll incentives to recruit, train, and retain workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to employers to support infrastructure projects through employee support programs (transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, child and dependent care, wages during training, other approved services) and payroll incentives (signing bonuses, retention bonuses, wages during training). Maximum benefit per employee is $10,000. Grant caps: $500,000 for employers with 750+ employees; $400,000 for 500-749 employees; $300,000 for fewer than 500 employees.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, first-come, first-served basis until program funds are exhausted. All funds must be spent by December 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based employers negatively impacted by COVID-19 and actively engaged in construction or maintenance of infrastructure projects. Supports full-time employees (excluding executive-level staff, superintendents, foremen, site supervisors, or controllers) based in Maryland working on qualifying infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support employee support programs including transportation assistance, housing/rental assistance, child and dependent care, wages during training, and payroll incentives including signing bonuses, retention bonuses, and wages during training for employees working on qualifying infrastructure projects. Maximum $10,000 per employee.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland for employers with infrastructure contracts or engaged in infrastructure projects.
requirements_list: Employers must be Maryland-based and negatively impacted by COVID-19
Must be actively engaged in construction or maintenance of infrastructure projects within Maryland or have a contract to perform such work by January 1, 2024

Qualifying infrastructure projects include roads, bridges, tunnels, transit facilities, walking/biking facilities, rail, ports, airports, broadband, energy grids, drinking water and wastewater facilities
Applicants must have full-time employees based in Maryland currently working on or beginning work on infrastructure contract by January 1, 2024
Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation required
Signed W9 form required
Business must be in good standing with MD Comptroller and not owe outstanding unemployment or other taxes
Programs must identify which benefits will be provided, how employees will access and be approved for benefits, and benefit amounts and allowances per employee
Maximum benefit per employee: $10,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis until program funds are exhausted. Employers must submit a grant application identifying proposed benefits, employee access procedures, benefit amounts, and infrastructure project details. All funds must be spent by December 1, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: MOSH Free Safety and Health Seminars
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Occupational Safety and Health provides free educational seminars to employers and employees across Maryland. The program is designed to reduce occupational injuries and illnesses through education. Participants can enroll in half-day, full-day, and two-day seminars at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free half-day, full-day, and two-day educational seminars on occupational safety and health topics for Maryland employers and employees. No cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and employees across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational seminars on occupational safety and health topics to reduce workplace injuries and illnesses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants can register for seminars online at the provided registration link.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that supports learners who have completed three GED® tests and need assistance with costs for the fourth and final exam. The program offers short-term assistance for classes, tutoring, practice tests, and exam fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term assistance for classes, tutoring, practice tests, and exam fees for the fourth GED® module test.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who have passed three of four GED® tests and need financial assistance to complete their Maryland High School Diploma.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classes, tutoring, practice tests, and exam fees for the fourth GED® module.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland test takers.
requirements_list: Must have passed three of the four GED® test modules
Must need assistance with costs of practice tests and exam fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Access to Banking Act - Assessment Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An assessment credit program that incentivizes Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions to establish new branches and retain existing branches in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. State-chartered banks and credit unions pay an annual regulatory assessment fee, and this program offers credits against that fee for qualifying branch activities in LMI areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assessment credit against annual regulatory assessment fees for Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions that establish new branches or retain existing branches in low-to-moderate income communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment credits applied against annual regulatory fees for establishing or retaining branches in low-to-moderate income communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; branches must be located in low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland state-chartered bank or credit union
Must establish a new (de novo) branch or retain an existing branch in a designated LMI community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions should subscribe to OFR emails for updates on how to apply for and earn the assessment credit. For questions about filing an application or paying an application fee, contact Stephen Clampett, Assistant Commissioner.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venture fund created to invest in financial technology (fintech) innovations and tools that help Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions better serve low-to-moderate income (LMI) communities. The fund invests in fintech firms developing financial products that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in LMI areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MCIV Fund is seeded with up to $2,500,000 in initial equity capital investment from OFR's Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund. Through June 30, 2028, the Commissioner may match investments made by Maryland state-chartered banks or credit unions in amounts equal to assessment credits earned by those institutions. Investment returns or capital returns flow back to OFR's Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fintech firms developing financial innovations for LMI communities; Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions interested in participating
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investment in fintech firms developing financial products and innovations that enhance access to capital, funding, and financial services for small businesses in low-to-moderate income communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; investments focus on innovations serving low-to-moderate income communities throughout Maryland
requirements_list: For fintech firms: must be developing financial technology innovations that enhance access to capital and financial services for small businesses in LMI communities
For banks and credit unions: must be Maryland state-chartered depository institutions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fintech firms and Maryland state-chartered depository institutions interested in the MCIV Fund should subscribe to OFR emails for updates regarding next steps, eligibility criteria, and the application process. For questions, contact Stephen Clampett, Assistant Commissioner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Temporary financial assistance providing up to 26 weeks of benefits to qualified individuals who are unemployed through no fault of their own. The program provides weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 depending on prior wages earned, helping bridge the time between job loss and new employment. Eligibility requires earning at least $1,176.01 during one quarter of the base period (the 18 months before filing) and a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters. The program also establishes rates and collects taxes from Maryland employers to finance benefits and conducts appeals for claimants and employers when disputes arise.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly payments ranging from $50 to $430 depending on prior wages earned. Maximum of 26 weeks of benefits. Eligibility requires earning at least $1,176.01 during one quarter of the base period (the 18 months before filing) and a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed individuals in Maryland who meet eligibility requirements, including federal employees on furlough and federal contractors whose last official duty station was in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary financial assistance during unemployment while seeking reemployment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents and individuals whose last official duty station was in Maryland (for federal employees).
requirements_list: Be unemployed through no fault of your own
Be ready to work hours normal for your job as soon as possible without restrictions
Have earned at least $1,176.01 during one quarter of the 18-month base period
Have earned a minimum of $1,800 over at least two quarters of the base period
Register in the Maryland Workforce Exchange system after filing a claim
Document weekly job search activities by recording at least 3 activities showing you looked for work
Complete a weekly certification to continue receiving benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Verify eligibility using the benefit access guide and gather required information including Social Security number, address, employment history from the last 18 months, and employer details. Step 2: File a claim online through the Maryland Unemployment Insurance Portal (BEACON) or by phone at 410-949-0022, 1-800-827-4839 (24/7), or 667-207-6520 (Monday-Friday 8am-4pm). Step 3: Register for a Maryland Workforce Exchange account after filing a claim. Step 4: Document weekly job search activities by recording at least 3 activities showing you looked for work. Step 5: Complete weekly certifications starting every Sunday to continue receiving benefits. Decisions on claims take up to 21 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Business Works is a workforce training and development program for businesses and current workers interested in upgrading their skills. The Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation partners with local businesses and organizations to support strategies for retention, growth, expansion, and layoff aversion through employer-based skills training. The program provides funds to businesses for training current employees in in-demand occupations, including classroom-based training, in-house staff training, and apprenticeships.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are provided to businesses for training current employees in in-demand occupations. Training can include classroom-based training, in-house staff training, and apprenticeships. Requires a dollar-to-dollar match from the business. Maximum training cap is $4,500 per trainee per project or series of projects. Maximum request per year is $40,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Maryland, with priority given to small businesses with 250 employees or fewer, local and regional businesses providing in-demand products or services, and businesses facing potential layoffs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom-based training, in-house staff training, apprenticeships, and other skills development opportunities for current employees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, with targeted focus on small businesses in Maryland
requirements_list: Small businesses with 250 employees or fewer prioritized
Must be a local or regional business providing in-demand products or services
Dollar-to-dollar match requirement from the business
Maximum training cap of $4,500 per trainee
Maximum request per year cannot exceed $40,000
Focus on in-demand occupations
Business must want to train employees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation Employer Services at 443-984-3014 for more information and application guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-engaged program that helps reduce the impacts of warming temperatures by enhancing the natural environment, creating shade, and supporting water uptake by soil and trees through technical assistance and support for tree planting and environmental enhancement projects to increase climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and support for tree planting and environmental enhancement projects to increase climate resilience and reduce warming impacts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local organizations, community groups, and individuals throughout Maryland interested in planting trees and enhancing the natural environment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and natural environment enhancement for climate adaptation and resilience.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual grant recognizing individuals representing Maryland land trusts for outstanding leadership, partnership, and innovation in conservation projects or organizational development. Funding is awarded to the land trust on behalf of the individual to support land trust programming, increase capacity, and foster stronger, better connected land trusts that protect natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 awarded annually to a Maryland land trust on behalf of an individual who demonstrated outstanding leadership, partnership, and innovation in land conservation. Funding supports land trust programming, capacity building, and organizational development while recognizing outstanding leadership in conservation projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals representing Maryland land trusts who have demonstrated outstanding leadership in land conservation, and local land trusts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support land trust programming, capacity building, innovation, and organizational development to foster stronger land trusts that protect natural resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland land trusts statewide
requirements_list: Individual must represent a Maryland land trust
Demonstrate outstanding leadership in land conservation
Show partnership and/or innovation in a conservation project or organizational development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click the provided link to apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust Keep Maryland Beautiful grants portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows the sampling, removal, or possession of aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for scientific research, educational projects, collections of display animals, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys. It covers activities that may not be permitted under commercial or recreational fishing licenses. The permit is not for collecting animals for sale or personal use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permits are issued annually for a $10 fee payable by check, money order, or electronically through the online payment system. Organizations must submit an application form and maps of intended sampling locations. A summary report of activities is required annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations conducting scientific research, educational projects, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys on aquatic organisms in Maryland waters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sampling, removal, or possession of aquatic organisms from Maryland waters for scientific research, educational projects, collections of display animals, ecological monitoring, or in-stream surveys. This permit may not be used to collect animals for sale or personal use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for sampling locations in Maryland waters. Specific location of collection activity must be identified with maps.
requirements_list: $10.00 application fee (paid online or by check/money order)
Complete all application information (print or type)
Provide project proposal with justification, objectives, species, and numbers
Identify specific locations of collection activity with maps
List sampling gear to be used
List all collectors in addition to principal officer
Provide principal officer name, title, phone, email
Provide organization name and address
Specify county of collections
Submit signed certification statement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Aquatic Scientific Collection Permit application form (available in PDF or online form). Submit completed application with required maps and payment to email or mail address provided. Email maps of intended sampling locations to the department. Submit the $10 annual fee by check, money order, or through the online payment system. Submit an annual summary report of activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service program administered through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides grant funds for angler education, outdoor ethics development, stewardship and conservation education to increase public understanding of the nation's water resources and associated aquatic life forms. The program assists public and private schools (pre-K through 12) and environmental education centers that are part of the public school system by providing funding for aquatic-based educational projects, outdoor learning initiatives, and supporting educators focused on environmental education throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds provided to public and private schools (pre-K through 12) and environmental education centers that are part of the public school system for aquatic-based educational projects. Grants are administered through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to support projects that promote angler education, outdoor ethics, stewardship, conservation, and outdoor learning initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private schools (pre-K through 12), environmental education centers that are part of the public school system, and educators focused on outdoor environmental education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquatic-based educational projects including angler education, outdoor ethics, stewardship and conservation education, and outdoor learning initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to educators throughout Maryland. Part of the national Sport Fish Restoration Program.
requirements_list: Must be a public or private school (pre-K through 12)
Environmental education centers must be part of the public school system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grants administered through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for aquatic-based projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program for schools to culture aquatic organisms in tanks or aquariums for educational purposes
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permit to culture aquatic organisms at school facilities; allows for tank/aquarium culture operations. Permits are issued annually to cover a school year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School principals and teachers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquatic organism culture for educational studies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Schools located in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an individual school
Facility inspection may be required before permit issuance
Collection of wild aquatic organisms requires separate Scientific Collection Permit
Complete application with all information provided
Species to be cultured and source/provider must be specified
Additional details may be necessary before release is permitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form; submit via email to aquastudies.dnr@maryland.gov or by mail (contact for mailing instructions); facility inspection may be required

structured_extraction.program_description: The Backyard Buffers Program assists Maryland homeowners and property owners with waterways on or adjacent to their property to create streamside buffers of native trees and shrubs. The program provides free 'buffer in a bag' packages containing 20-30 native tree and shrub bare-root seedlings (approximately 1 to 2 feet in height), along with fact sheets on tree species, planting techniques, maintenance information, and additional learning materials. Technical assistance is available to design and implement streamside buffers and establish riparian forest buffers along streams and waterways. Streamside buffers provide multiple benefits including wildlife habitat creation, reduced peak summer temperatures, reduced sediment and fertilizer entering waterways, streambank stabilization, erosion prevention, and improved water quality. The program is available through county coordinators across all Maryland counties. Packet reservations are typically taken during March on a first-come, first-served basis, with bags available for pickup at designated local sites in time for the spring planting season. Supplies are limited and vary by county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free 'buffer in a bag' containing 20-30 native tree and shrub bare-root seedlings (approximately 1 to 2 feet in height), plus fact sheets on tree species, planting techniques, and maintenance information. Technical assistance to design and implement streamside buffers and establish riparian forest buffers using native trees and shrubs. Packets are reserved during March on a first-come, first-served basis and picked up at designated local sites in spring. Supplies are limited and vary by county.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically during the month of March; limited bags available on first-come, first-served basis; pickup in time for spring planting season
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland property owners, particularly residential homeowners with 5 acres of land or less who have a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river flowing through their property or living adjacent to such a waterway. Program is for smaller landowners who are not eligible for agricultural cost-share programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating a streamside buffer of native trees and shrubs to establish riparian forest buffers along streams and waterways to provide wildlife habitat, reduce peak summer temperatures, reduce sediment and fertilizer entering waterways, stabilize streambanks, prevent erosion, and improve water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through county-specific coordinators in all 24 Maryland counties based on program capacity and funding availability. Each county has a designated coordinator and funding is limited and varies by county. Contact local Backyard Buffers County Coordinator for county-specific availability.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland property owner
Must own property with 5 acres or less
Must have a drainage ditch, stream, creek, or river flowing through property or live adjacent to such a waterway
Must be a smaller landowner not eligible for agricultural cost-share programs
Property must be suitable for riparian forest buffer establishment
Limited quantities available each year
First-come, first-served basis for reservations
Reservations typically taken in March
Pickup in spring before planting season
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Backyard Buffers County Coordinator by phone or email during March to sign up and reserve tree packets. Sign-up methods vary by county (phone, email, online form). Packet reservations are typically taken during the month of March, with bags available for pickup at a designated local site in time for the spring planting season. Applications are first-come, first-served. Contact the Backyard Buffers Program for assistance with designing and implementing a streamside buffer.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training and workshop program that offers outdoor skills classes and recreational opportunities for women 18 years of age and older. Workshops enable women to learn about outdoor recreation in a casual, hands-on environment with classes covering firearm safety, fly fishing, preserving harvest, archery, camping, gardening, wildlife identification, traditional crafts, and other outdoor skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers free or low-cost hands-on outdoor skills training workshops for women. Weekend workshops include over 30 different classes covering topics such as firearm safety, fly fishing, game preservation, nature crafts, hiking, archery, camping, gardening, wildlife tracking, and photography. Beyond BOW workshops provide one to three day specialized training in specific activities like fishing clinics, backpacking, goose hunting, field-to-table game preparation, and survival skills. Evening programs and activities are also included. Hands-on practice and field experiences are included in instructional courses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration information for 2026 weekend workshop coming soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women 18 years of age and older who are interested in learning outdoor recreation skills in a supportive, non-threatening environment. Beginner to intermediate skill levels welcome.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outdoor skills training and hands-on learning experiences for recreational activities including hunting, fishing, hiking, boating, firearm safety, wildlife game preparation, archery, camping, gardening, wildlife tracking, and photography.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Workshops are offered in various locations throughout the state tailored to showcase regional resources and outdoor opportunities.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must be a woman
Some courses require prerequisites (e.g., Basic Firearms Safety required before advanced shooting courses)
Maryland Nontidal Sport Fishing license required for fishing classes
Specific clothing and equipment requirements for certain classes (e.g., Blacksmithing requires long sleeves, long pants, and closed-toe shoes)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator or check the mailing list for registration information. Registration details are posted in advance of each workshop. For the 2026 weekend workshop scheduled August 7-9, more information regarding registration is coming soon. Participants can join the mailing list through GovDelivery to stay updated on workshop schedules and registration openings.

structured_extraction.program_description: A centennial celebration contest inviting Maryland residents to explore forests and find trees over 15 feet in circumference for a chance to win prizes up to $500. Participants submit photos, measurements, and location details to enter.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Prizes of up to $500 awarded to contest participants who successfully identify and measure qualifying big trees during the centennial contest period (May 24 to September 1). Winners selected based on tree measurements and submissions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents interested in trees and forestry
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prize money for identifying and measuring big trees that meet contest criteria
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents
requirements_list: Tree must be over 15 feet in circumference
Photos, measurements, and location details must be submitted
Measurements must be accurate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants explore Maryland forests during the contest period, find and measure trees over 15 feet in circumference, submit photos, measurements, and location details to enter the contest.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public donation program that collects voluntary contributions from the general public to support largemouth bass and smallmouth bass management and conservation in Maryland. Donations are used for enhancing aquatic habitat, supplies for black bass tournament directors, hatchery operations to raise and stock bass, and similar conservation efforts. Projects are selected annually by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and the Black Bass Advisory Committee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The public donates money in any amount to support black bass conservation projects in Maryland. Donations can be made by check or through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal. For donations of $1,000 or less, checks should be mailed payable to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' noted in the memo line. For donations greater than $1,000, donors should contact Martha Bruder directly. Donations are not tax-deductible. Funds are used to support habitat enhancement, tournament supplies, equipment purchases such as bead filters to increase hatchery capacity, and other conservation initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of the general public interested in supporting black bass conservation in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhancing aquatic habitat, supplies for black bass tournament directors, hatchery operations, equipment purchases, and other largemouth bass and smallmouth bass conservation projects selected annually by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and the Black Bass Advisory Committee
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to support black bass conservation throughout Maryland
requirements_list: For donations by check of $1,000 or less, payable to Maryland Department of Natural Resources with memo line 'Black Bass Conservation Fund'
For donations greater than $1,000, contact Martha Bruder directly
Donations can be made through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal under Merchandise section
Checks of $1,000 or less can be mailed to Martha Bruder at 580 Taylor Avenue, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Donors can contribute by mailing a check (for amounts of $1,000 or less) payable to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to Martha Bruder at 580 Taylor Avenue, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401 with 'Black Bass Conservation Fund' noted in the memo line. Donations can also be made through the Maryland Outdoors licensing portal under the Merchandise section. For donations over $1,000, contact Martha Bruder at martha.bruder@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program that provides reimbursement for damage caused by black bears to landowners and farmers, along with technical assistance and education for nuisance bear problems. The program is supported through the sale of Black Bear Conservation Stamps and related products, with revenues funding bear management, damage reimbursement, and conservation efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides reimbursement for significant damage caused by black bears to property and agricultural operations. Revenues from Black Bear Conservation Stamps support bear management initiatives, technical assistance, and educational materials for landowners dealing with nuisance bear problems. Funds are generated through the purchase of stamps and products sold through the online store.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners, farmers, and the public who experience damage from black bears or encounter nuisance bear conflicts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for damage caused by black bears to property and agricultural operations, technical assistance, educational materials, bear management, and nuisance bear problem mitigation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland. Black bears are present in Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties with sightings in central and southern counties. Particular focus on Western Maryland where black bear populations have increased.
requirements_list: Experience significant damage from black bears
Be a farmer or agricultural operator, or landowner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners and farmers experiencing black bear damage can contact the Wildlife and Heritage Service to submit a claim for reimbursement, obtain technical assistance, or request educational materials. The public can also support the program by purchasing black bear conservation stamps and products through the online store.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grants and technical support to increase the capacity of local and regional organizations to develop and implement climate adaptation initiatives.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizational capacity building and development of climate adaptation initiatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program authorized by the Clean Water Act that provides funding to Maryland and other Chesapeake Bay watershed jurisdictions to implement the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement. The program supports projects that advance the Agreement's goals, including reducing nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution to improve water quality, sustainable fisheries, vital habitats protection, toxic contaminant reduction, watershed health, stewardship, land conservation, environmental literacy, and climate resiliency. Specific funding is available through Outcome 4: Environmental Education and Stewardship, which provides grants of up to $75,000 annually to improve student and community ability to take action benefiting Chesapeake and coastal ecosystems through professional development and training, curriculum expansion, outdoor learning, and stewardship activities. Grants support learning experiences including transportation and facility fees for student and community access to natural areas, environmental engagement and stewardship programs, environmental educator professional development, community environmental education programs, and supply costs for environmental investigations and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants awarded to support implementation of Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement goals. Grants of up to $75,000 available annually through federal allocation with up to $100,000 total funding available for CBIG. Proposals above $75,000 threshold require discussion with the outcome contact. CBIG funds require a 1:1 non-federal match from the recipient or partner organizations. Funds support learning experiences and educational opportunities including transportation and facility fees for student, teacher, and community access to natural areas, environmental engagement and stewardship programs, environmental educator professional development and training, community environmental education programs, and supply costs for environmental investigations, field equipment, and stewardship projects. Funding becomes available September 1 following the December application deadline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-governmental organizations, non-profits, local and state agencies, schools and school systems, higher learning institutions, and University of Maryland system institutions serving K-12 students or communities within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed, as well as state agencies and non-profit organizations working on Chesapeake Bay restoration and watershed protection statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that support implementation of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement management strategies with focus on reducing nonpoint source nutrient and sediment pollution to improve water quality, sustainable fisheries, vital habitats, toxic contaminants reduction, healthy watersheds, stewardship, land conservation, environmental literacy, and climate resiliency. Funds support transportation and facility fees for student, teacher, and community access to natural areas, environmental engagement and stewardship programs, environmental educator professional development and training, community environmental education programs, and supply costs for environmental investigations, field equipment, and stewardship projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed or statewide as authorized under Section 117(e)(1)(A) of the Clean Water Act for Maryland and other signatory jurisdictions of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement. Project locations can include public lands, schoolyards, community property, and private property.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a 1:1 non-federal match to leverage federal CBIG funding
Projects must support implementation of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement management strategies
Projects must be located within Maryland's portion of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed
Track One serves formal K-12 education systems; Track Two serves communities or public education
Projects should address local watershed and land-use issues based on sound environmental education principles and focus on learning experiences leading to stewardship action
For Track 1: must demonstrate connections to curriculum standards, hands-on learning experiences, systemic programming capability, and professional development opportunities
For Track 2: must demonstrate connections to environmental best practices, hands-on learning opportunities, systemic programming capability, and training opportunities
Applicants must detail how they support local communities and enhance outreach to groups demonstrating need
Community involvement and stakeholder planning required
Track 1 applicants must provide environmental literacy plan or evidence of environmental literacy programming
Transmittal letter signed by authorized executive required on official letterhead
Letters of support required from leadership and participating partners
Must support implementation of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement
Project must address one or more of the Agreement's goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through Grants Gateway Outcome 4. Submit required attachments including transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive, letters of support from school or organization leadership and participating partners, and for Track 1 organizations an environmental literacy plan or evidence of environmental literacy programming. Proposals are scored on demographics and need, education and stewardship connections, program development, and budget feasibility. Applications are also coordinated through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Chesapeake & Coastal Service in coordination with EPA Region 3 and the Chesapeake Bay Program Office. Funding becomes available September 1 following the December application deadline. Contact the Chesapeake and Coastal Service for additional information about funding opportunities and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (CBNERR-MD)
structured_extraction.program_description: A place-based partnership program between the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and Maryland that supports research, education, and natural resource management at three locations: Monie Bay in Somerset County, Otter Point Creek in Harford County, and Jug Bay in Prince George's and Anne Arundel Counties. The Reserve works with local communities and regional groups to address natural resource management issues such as climate change impacts, non-point source pollution, habitat restoration, and invasive species management. The Reserve protects estuarine habitat as natural field laboratories for research and living classrooms for education, and provides training to improve coastal resource management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NOAA and Maryland Department of Natural Resources provide funding, technical assistance, and national guidance. Programs support research, education, and training on natural resource management and coastal resource management, including habitat restoration, invasive species management, and climate change adaptation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local communities, regional groups, researchers, educators, students, and organizations working on natural resource management and coastal protection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research projects, education programs, training for coastal resource management, habitat restoration, invasive species management, climate change adaptation, and addressing non-point source pollution in estuarine areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to three specific sites: Monie Bay in Somerset County, Otter Point Creek in Harford County, and Jug Bay in Prince George's and Anne Arundel Counties.
requirements_list: Located at or working within one of the three Reserve sites
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Partnership-based program administered by Maryland Department of Natural Resources in coordination with NOAA and local site partners.

Grants or equity investments ranging from $50,000 to $450,000 are available for eligible companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants or equity-investment funding ranging from $50,000 to $450,000 for Maryland-based startup companies working on innovative technologies for Chesapeake Bay restoration, air and water quality improvement, reduction of non-point source nutrients and sediment, and environmental innovation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Urban Tree Canopy Goals
structured_extraction.program_description: A regional initiative to increase urban tree canopy coverage in Chesapeake Bay communities to improve water quality by reducing stormwater runoff and surface water volume in urban areas. The program provides technical assistance for assessing existing and potential urban tree canopy, setting goals for expansion, and implementing strategic urban forest management strategies across the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance provided by the Chesapeake Bay Program, MD DNR, the US Forest Service, the University of Vermont Spatial Analysis Lab, and other partners to help communities assess existing and potential urban tree canopy using remote sensing data and GIS analysis. Assistance includes tree canopy mapping, goal-setting frameworks using the Forest Opportunity Spectrum (FOS) methodology, implementation planning, and guidance on tree planting prioritization. Communities work with technical assistance partners to adopt local tree canopy goals and develop implementation strategies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland municipalities and counties participating in the Chesapeake Bay Urban Tree Canopy Goal effort, including urban residents, local government officials, community planners, and property owners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree canopy assessment and mapping, strategic urban forest management planning, goal-setting and implementation planning, tree planting site identification and prioritization, stormwater management, water quality improvement, and watershed restoration within the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to communities in Maryland within the Chesapeake Bay watershed, particularly the Upper Potomac, Middle Potomac, Upper Western Shore, Lower Western Shore, and Patapsco/Back tributary strategy watersheds. Thirty-six Maryland communities have committed to participation including Annapolis, Baltimore, Baltimore County, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Greenbelt, Hyattsville, and Rockville. The program targets at least five local jurisdictions per state for urban forest assessments.
requirements_list: Community must commit to participation in the Urban Tree Canopy Goal effort
Community must assess existing and potential urban tree canopy using remote sensing data and GIS methodology
Community must adopt local tree canopy cover goals with specified percent increase targets and timeframes
Community must identify priority planting sites with rationale
Community must obtain governing body resolutions or endorsements
Community must submit implementation plan to State or District of Columbia
Community must provide annual progress reporting on canopy goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities commit to participation and work with technical assistance partners to assess existing and potential urban tree canopy using satellite imagery and GIS analysis. Communities then develop and adopt local tree canopy goals using the Forest Opportunity Spectrum framework, establish implementation plans with priority planting sites, obtain governing body endorsements, and submit plans to their State or District of Columbia. Annual progress is monitored and reported.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay and Endangered Species Fund Tax Checkoff
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax checkoff program that allows Maryland taxpayers to contribute to the Chesapeake Bay and Endangered Species Fund by donating on line 35 of Form 502. Donations are divided evenly between Chesapeake Bay restoration grants provided by the Chesapeake Bay Trust and rare species programs run by the Wildlife and Heritage Service at the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Contributions support Chesapeake Bay education and restoration projects, stream cleanups, tree plantings, habitat research and protection, and conservation of Maryland's rare, threatened, and endangered species.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Taxpayers donate funds through their Maryland tax return (Form 502, line 35). Donations are tax-deductible in the year following the contribution. Funds are divided evenly between Chesapeake Bay restoration grants and rare species conservation programs. The funds support Chesapeake Bay education and restoration projects, stream cleanups, tree plantings, habitat research and protection, and rare species conservation programs throughout Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Chesapeake Bay education and restoration projects for students, stream cleanups and tree plantings by community volunteers, habitat research and protection for threatened plants and animals, and protection of Maryland's rare, threatened and endangered species

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Forest Lands Hunting Tract Lottery
structured_extraction.program_description: A lottery program that allows hunt clubs to lease available hunting tracts on Chesapeake Forest Lands for ten-year terms. Selected clubs receive exclusive hunting rights to designated forest tracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hunt clubs that win the lottery receive a ten-year lease agreement granting exclusive hunting rights to a selected forest tract. Lease prices vary by tract, ranging from $14 to $16 per acre annually. The program provides access to maintained hunting lands and allows camping on the property with permits ($50 for deer season, $25 for turkey season). Lessees gain rights to hunt and use premises for hunting-related activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunt clubs with at least two members licensed to hunt in Maryland, with members at least 18 years of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunting rights and access to leased forest tracts for hunting seasons. Lease payments provide revenue to the state.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available on Chesapeake Forest Lands located in Somerset and Wicomico counties on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Specific tracts managed by the Chesapeake Forest Office in Snow Hill, Maryland.

One person must be designated as club president
Each member may submit one lottery form only

Hunt clubs are expected to help maintain access roads, gates, and signs on leased property
Camping trailers require permits and must be removed from the property February 1 - March 31
Cannot assign or sublet lease
Must comply with all state and federal regulations (ADA, OSHA, building standards)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit the tracts before making a selection. 2. Complete the online Lottery Entry Form by the deadline (August 21, 2025 at 11:59 pm). 3. Each club member may submit one form. 4. A random automated online drawing is held on August 22, 2025 at 2:00 pm. 5. Winners are contacted by phone or email within 2 business days. 6. Winners must make payment and submit required paperwork by September 10, 2025 at 4:00 pm to secure the lease.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state funding program that accelerates Bay restoration by providing financial resources for efficient, cost-effective non-point source pollution control projects. The program focuses on restored streams and floodplains, enhanced riparian buffers and forests, improved wetland ecosystems, and comprehensive stormwater management throughout the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays watershed. Approximately $29 million is provided for ecological restoration efforts, with funds geographically targeted based on cost-effectiveness analysis to reduce the greatest amount of nonpoint source pollution entering the Bay. The program incorporates co-benefits into project selection to promote holistic projects and consistently identifies all co-benefits of practices and their locations. The program also supports innovative restoration technologies through the Innovative Technology Fund. Technical assistance is provided to local governments and non-governmental organizations. The program is a long-standing, reliable funding source that engages local partners in achieving watershed goals and incorporates updated science from the Comprehensive Evaluation of System Response (CSER) report, shifting priorities from deep bay trenches to local, shallow-water habitat and community impacts. It is a key funding source for the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Trust Fund provides grants to support non-point source pollution control and ecological restoration projects including stream restoration, floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, improved wetland ecosystems, stormwater management, and innovative restoration technologies. Projects must provide cost-effective and measurable nonpoint source pollution reductions along with co-benefits. The program also funds restoration of aquatic resources (submerged aquatic vegetation, oyster reefs), climate resilience improvements, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, and beneficial use projects including marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, shoreline stabilization, oyster restoration, fish passage improvements, and habitat connectivity projects. Technical assistance is provided to local governments and non-governmental organizations. Approximately $29 million is provided for restoration efforts. Funds are geographically targeted to reduce the greatest amount of pollution entering the Bay and are leveraged to maximize impact. Agricultural technical assistance and best management practice implementation, cover crop program subsidies, grants to farmers for BMP adoption, manure management program support are also included.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, communities, non-governmental organizations, state colleges and universities, Soil Conservation Districts, agricultural entities and farmers, project applicants and planners, restoration practitioners, conservation organizations, and public land managers focused on Bay watershed restoration, water quality improvement, and non-point source pollution control projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stream and floodplain restoration, riparian buffer and forest enhancement, wetland ecosystem improvement, stormwater management, innovative restoration technology projects, restoration of aquatic resources including submerged aquatic vegetation and oyster reefs, climate resilience improvements, carbon sequestration, wildlife habitat creation, recreational opportunities, environmental justice benefits, beneficial use of dredged material projects, marsh enhancement, beach nourishment, island restoration, shoreline stabilization, living shorelines, tree planting and maintenance projects, oyster reef restoration, fish passage improvements, habitat connectivity and green infrastructure projects, conservation easements, urban tree planting, green streets projects, cover crop programs, and best management practice implementation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays watershed areas statewide, with geographic targeting based on cost-effectiveness analysis to reduce the greatest amount of nonpoint source pollution entering the Bay. Funding distributed across all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City, with priority areas identified through Trust Fund Targeting Map layers including SPARROW model priority areas, 16 coastal counties and Baltimore City for certain coastal restoration initiatives, and five pilot watersheds representing diverse land uses and geographies under the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.

Complete Co-Benefits section of Common Application

The Trust Fund works with state agencies and local partners to administer funds and hold everyone accountable for results.

structured_extraction.program_description: A single point of entry for Maryland's coastal communities and organizations seeking technical and financial assistance to restore local waterways, foster healthy ecosystems, increase resilience to climate impacts and coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise, strengthen local economies, and develop the next generation of environmental stewards. Grants and technical assistance are made possible through funding from the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, Coastal Resiliency Program, Waterway Improvement Fund, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), and Environmental Protection Agency's Chesapeake Bay Program. Supports projects that foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies that are resilient to coastal hazards and climate change impacts, including local stormwater management, flood planning, ecosystem restoration initiatives, and Chesapeake Bay and coastal education projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and technical assistance made possible with funding through the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, the Coastal Resiliency Program, the Waterway Improvement Fund, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Environmental Protection Agency's Chesapeake Bay Program. Financial assistance supports projects that foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies that are resilient to coastal hazards and climate change impacts. Supports local stormwater management, flood planning, ecosystem restoration, and Chesapeake Bay and coastal education projects through a grants portal. Technical assistance and training are also available to local communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's coastal communities and organizations, local governments, nonprofits, community organizations, educators, and other entities working on waterway restoration, climate resilience, local economic development, environmental education, and Chesapeake Bay and coastal-related projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restore local waterways, increase resilience to climate impacts and coastal hazards, strengthen local economies, develop the next generation of environmental stewards, foster healthy ecosystems and communities, support local stormwater management, flood planning, ecosystem restoration projects, and Chesapeake Bay and coastal education projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland, with focus on coastal communities affected by coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway for financial assistance and technical support. Technical assistance and training are available to local communities. Submit applications through the Grants Gateway portal.

The program provides technical assistance, planning support, and management strategies to help commercial fishing operations develop resilient and climate-adaptive fishing practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance, planning support, and management strategies to help commercial fishing operations adapt to climate change, develop resilient fishing practices, and take advantage of new fishing opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial fishing community, seafood industry professionals, and fisheries managers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, planning, technical assistance, and development and implementation of climate-adaptive fisheries management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, particularly coastal areas and inland waterways with commercial fishing operations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Work with DNR to develop climate-adaptive fisheries management strategies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program funded with EPA Clean Water Act Section 319(h) funding to support forest-related goals for the Maryland Coastal Bays region. The strategy includes environmental goals for forest extent and forest interior species habitat, quality of life goals for maintaining rural character and viable working forests, and enhances forest-related actions including riparian forest buffer establishment in Coastal Bays watersheds. The program provides technical assistance for riparian forest buffers, supports forestry actions in the five watersheds of the Coastal Bays, and offers information compilation on forest inventory, species composition, and programs available to assist landowners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance for riparian forest buffer establishment in Coastal Bays watersheds, including buffer planting and forest management guidance. The program supports afforestation and forest management assistance to private landowners and includes information compilation on forest inventory, species composition, and programs available to assist landowners. Buffer planting increased from less than 3 miles per year to 5.3 miles (126 acres) in 2000 and 14.05 miles (216 acres) in 2001.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners and communities in the Maryland Coastal Bays region interested in forest management, riparian buffer restoration, and sustainable forest practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Riparian forest buffer planting and establishment, afforestation, forest management planning, and technical assistance for forest-related goals in Coastal Bays watersheds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Five watersheds in the Maryland Coastal Bays region in Worcester, Wicomico, and Somerset counties on the Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners can contact the Forest Service for technical assistance on forest management and riparian buffer establishment in eligible Coastal Bays watersheds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of Natural Resources buys land under threat of rising sea levels and manages the area to protect nearby communities and habitats from climate impacts through conservation easements and land acquisition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR purchases land threatened by rising sea levels through conservation easements and manages the land to provide protection for adjacent communities and natural habitats from sea level rise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property threatened by rising sea levels; communities in coastal areas requiring coastal protection
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition and management for coastal protection and habitat preservation from sea level rise
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Coastal areas of Maryland vulnerable to rising sea levels

structured_extraction.program_description: A program dedicated to assisting Maryland's coastal communities in addressing short- and long-term coastal hazards such as high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. The program connects local government staff and partners to essential information, tools, training, and financial assistance to build resilience in coastal communities. It includes guidance for incorporating sea level rise projections into planning and regulatory projects, as well as requirements for developing and updating nuisance flood plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance through the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway, technical assistance to local communities, and training opportunities for local practitioners. Additional support includes links to information, federal and state resources, tools, and visualizations. Technical guidance is provided for incorporating sea level rise projections into projects and developing nuisance flood plans. Resources include mapping tools, visualization platforms, and step-by-step worksheets for coastal resilience planning.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; ongoing guidance and nuisance flood plan updates required every five years (October 2025 and October 2030)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's coastal communities, local government staff, local practitioners, planners, decision-makers, county and municipal governments, emergency management officials, and private property owners working on coastal resilience and hazard mitigation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that foster healthy ecosystems, communities, and economies that are resilient in the face of coastal change, including addressing high tide flooding, storm surge, and sea level rise. Funding supports planning, design, and implementation of adaptation projects; nuisance flood plan development; and climate resilience strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland coastal communities along the Chesapeake Bay, Coastal Bays, and Atlantic Ocean shorelines. Specific application includes Maryland's Coastal Zone, which extends from three miles out in the Atlantic Ocean to inland boundaries of 16 counties and Baltimore City bordering the Atlantic Ocean, Chesapeake Bay, and Potomac River up to the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Projects over $500,000 using 50% or more state funds must follow Coast Smart Construction Program guidelines if located within vulnerable boundary
Must consider community input and stakeholder engagement
Should incorporate current RSLR projections
Nuisance flood plans must be submitted or updated every five years
Plans must include inventory of flood hazard areas, identification of flood thresholds, documentation of flood events, analysis of vulnerable communities, and identification of critical facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Coastal Resilience Program or access the Chesapeake and Coastal Grants Gateway for specific application procedures and deadlines. For sea level rise guidance projects, use the step-by-step worksheet to select appropriate RSLR estimate based on project characteristics and flood risk tolerance. For nuisance flood planning, develop or update plans using provided guidance templates and tools, coordinating with relevant county and state departments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A science-based training program provided by Maryland Department of Natural Resources that helps coastal communities, organizations, professionals, community leaders, and decision makers learn about complex restoration and conservation issues related to climate change, coastal resilience, and Chesapeake Bay watershed health. The program promotes knowledge to advance clean and healthy streams, rivers, and watersheds throughout the Chesapeake Bay region and Maryland's coastal areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Science-based educational training and technical assistance on restoration, conservation, coastal resilience, watershed management, and adaptation to sea level rise and coastal flooding. The program provides knowledge and professional development to community leaders, decision makers, and coastal professionals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Coastal communities, organizations, professionals, community leaders, and decision makers working on restoration, conservation, watershed health, and coastal resilience throughout Maryland, particularly in the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training programs, educational events, and professional development related to coastal resilience, restoration, conservation, watershed management, adaptation to sea level rise, and coastal flooding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, with particular focus on coastal communities and the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participate in training programs and educational events offered by the Coastal Training Program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) Grant - Section 306 and Section 306A
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding provided through the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 legislation for the administration and implementation of Maryland's Coastal Zone Management Program, as well as for specific coastal projects. Funding includes Section 306 grants for program administration, Section 306A grants for land acquisition, easements, low-cost construction projects such as public access improvements, and habitat restoration projects, and Section 309 grants for coastal zone enhancement projects. The program supports coastal zone enhancement, creation of enforceable coastal policies, community resilience to sea level rise, and implementation of the Coastal Nonpoint Source Pollution Program. Section 306 and Section 306A funding require 1:1 non-federal match by non-federal fund sources, while Section 309 funding does not require match. Maryland currently receives approximately $2.5 million annually in base Section 306 funding from NOAA's Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management. Total funds awarded range from $4.5 to $4.7 million per grant cycle, including federal funds and non-federal match. Grants are structured in 18-month periods from October 1 to March 31 two years later, with individual contracts typically lasting 12 months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants of $4.5 to $4.7 million total (including federal funds and non-federal match) awarded for 18-month periods from October 1 of one year to March 31 two years out. Maryland receives approximately $2.5 million annually from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management (OCRM). Grants are subdivided into Sections 306, 306A, and 309, each with specific objectives. Section 306 funding supports administration and implementation of Maryland's Coastal Zone Management Program and requires 1:1 non-federal match.
