Section 306A funding supports acquisition of fee simple and other interests in land such as easements, low-cost construction projects such as public access improvements, and habitat restoration projects, and requires 1:1 non-federal match plus additional NOAA documentation before approval. Section 309 funding supports coastal zone enhancement projects and does not require match. Under each separate contract normally 12 months in duration, funded projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies, non-profit organizations, and local partners working on coastal zone management, coastal resource protection, and related environmental policy initiatives in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administration and implementation of Maryland's Coastal Zone Management Program; development of programs, plans and strategies to address specific coastal issues; acquisition of fee simple and other interests in land such as easements; low-cost construction projects such as public access improvements; habitat restoration projects; coastal zone enhancement projects that create new enforceable policies in wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, and aquaculture; creation of enforceable coastal policies; sea level rise community resilience; and Coastal Nonpoint Source Pollution Program implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland coastal zone areas based on tidal shoreline and coastal population; statewide administration with local partner coordination.
requirements_list: Non-federal funds must match federal funding 1:1 for Section 306 and Section 306A funding
Section 306A funding requires additional documentation from NOAA before approval
Section 309 funding does not require match
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed through the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management with coordination and administration by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Under each separate contract normally 12 months in duration, funded projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) Grant - Section 309
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding provided through the Coastal Zone Management Act of 1972 legislation for coastal zone enhancement projects that create new enforceable policies in nine identified areas: wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, and aquaculture. Section 309 funding does not require a non-federal match.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funding for coastal zone enhancement projects that create new enforceable policies in one of nine identified areas: wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, or aquaculture. Grants are normally 18 months in duration from October 1 of one year to March 31 two years out. Section 309 funding does not require a non-federal match. Projects are reimbursed for funds expended once work is completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies implementing coastal zone enhancement projects in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coastal zone enhancement projects that create new enforceable policies in wetlands, coastal hazards, public access, marine debris, cumulative and secondary impacts, special area management plans, ocean resources, energy and government facility siting, or aquaculture
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - applicable to Maryland's coastal zone
requirements_list: Project must create new enforceable policies in one of nine identified areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed through the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Office of Ocean and Coastal Resource Management

structured_extraction.program_name: Communicating About Climate Change with Confidence
structured_extraction.program_description: A training program teaching communication techniques including values, metaphors, art, storytelling, and solutions-focused approaches to help teachers, park staff, nonprofit workers, and other public communicators address climate change confidently in public interactions. Participants learn a toolkit to build confidence in climate communication and support collective behavior change for climate action. The program provides vetted and reliable resources for productive conversations centered on climate solutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Minimum 90 minutes training, with 3 hours preferred for best results. Attendees receive vetted and reliable resources for productive climate conversations centered on solutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teachers, park staff, nonprofit workers, and anyone who addresses climate change in public interactions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in climate communication techniques and resources for productive climate change conversations centered on solutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Coreen Weilminster at Coreen.weilminster@maryland.gov to learn more about scheduling the training.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program that supports tree planting projects and builds organizational capacity to scale tree planting and maintenance initiatives in overburdened, underserved communities across Maryland. The program welcomes proposals that directly support tree planting projects or increase the capacity of organizations to scale up their tree planting and maintenance initiatives. Designed in accordance with 2020-2025 Maryland Forest Action Plan goals. The program reduces barriers to tree planting and provides local partners with flexible access to funds that can be leveraged to secure additional resources without requiring matching funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Track A (Site Readiness): minimum $5,000, maximum $50,000 for activities including stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal leading to replacement tree planting. Track B (Implementation): minimum $5,000, maximum $50,000 for tree planting projects requiring pre-application technical assistance from Maryland Forest Service or authorized partnership agencies. Track C (Capacity Building): minimum $50,000, maximum $250,000 per year for staff or contractual support, workforce development, expansion or creation of new pilot programming. 100 percent of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities and matching funds are waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government entities, Federally Recognized Tribes and Tribal organizations, non-profit organizations, public and state-controlled institutions of higher education, and community-based organizations working at community, municipal, regional, and watershed scales in overburdened and underserved communities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Track A: site readiness activities like stump removal, hazardous tree removal, vegetation removal, and concrete removal leading to tree planting. Track B: tree planting projects in disadvantaged communities with low tree canopy. Track C: staff or contractual support, workforce development, and expansion or creation of new pilot programming related to urban forestry. Also includes volunteer coordination, project management, supplies and equipment, subcontractor/contractor services, and two-year tree maintenance planning and implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve disadvantaged communities as identified in the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool (CEJST) across Maryland. One hundred percent of work must take place in or benefit designated disadvantaged communities. Applicants must provide watershed, county, and legislative district information with latitude and longitude coordinates of project location.
requirements_list: Projects must directly or indirectly result in trees being planted in overburdened, underserved communities
Must be identified in the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool (CEJST) Disadvantaged Communities Map
100 percent of work must take place in or benefit disadvantaged communities
Matching funds are waived and must be passed on to any sub-awardees
Track B projects require pre-application technical assistance from Maryland Forest Service or authorized representative from 5 Million Trees for Maryland partnership agencies

Eligible entities include local government entities, Federally Recognized Tribes and Tribal organizations operating within the United States or its territories, non-profit organizations, public and state-controlled institutions of higher education, and community-based organizations
Applications may be submitted under Tracks A and B together, but Track C applications may not be combined with another Track
Executive Officer and Project Leader must be two separate individuals who are decision-makers (board member, employee, or approved organizational position—not contractors)
Project Leader's email must match application submission email
Individuals associated with for-profit entities cannot serve in Executive Officer or Project Leader roles
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All applications are submitted through an online system. For questions regarding the application process, contact Samara Pyfrom at 410-974-2941 ext. 147 or spyfrom@cbtrust.org. Track B projects require pre-application technical assistance from Maryland Forest Service or authorized partnership agencies before submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Community Parks and Playgrounds Program provides grant funding to local governments, municipal corporations, and non-profit organizations to restore existing park and green space systems and create new park and green space systems throughout the state, including Baltimore City. The program invests in the future of Maryland's established communities by developing and revitalizing parks and playgrounds. Grants support the development of new parks, rehabilitation or expansion of existing parks, purchase and installation of playground equipment, development of environmentally-oriented parks and recreation areas, development of new trails or extension of existing trails, creation of access points to water recreation resources, and purchase of land to create new parks. A total of $97.4 million has been approved for 908 park and playground projects. Annual funding varies between $2.5 million and $5.5 million, with recent allocations including $5 million in FY'26 (funding 26 projects), $5 million in FY'25 (funding 30 projects), and $2.5 million in FY'24 (funding 20 projects). The program also provides reimbursement for planning grant projects and supports capital renewal initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible grants to local governments, municipal corporations, and non-profit organizations for park and playground development and revitalization projects. Grants can fund up to 100% of the proposed project cost with no local matching funds required. Grants are capital funds supporting development of new parks, rehabilitation or expansion of existing parks, playground equipment installation, trail development, water recreation access points, and land acquisition. Funded projects must last a minimum of 20 years (or perpetuity for land acquisition projects). The program operates on a reimbursement basis, with applicants paying costs upfront and receiving reimbursement for contract costs, direct purchases, force account/in-house labor, in-kind services, and equipment. Partial project reimbursements are permitted, and advance payments may be considered in limited cases. Funding amounts have ranged from $2.5 to $5.5 million annually, supporting hundreds of projects across the state. A total of $97.4 million has been approved for 908 projects.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tiffany DePaoli, Katelyn Mayberry, Michael McQuarrie
structured_extraction.program_audience: Governing bodies of municipal corporations, Baltimore City, non-profit organizations, and local governments seeking to develop and revitalize parks and playgrounds throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects for park facilities and elements that will last a minimum of 20 years, including park development, rehabilitation, expansion, improvement, playground equipment installation, trail development, water recreation access points, and land acquisition for new parks. Funds cannot be used for operating and maintenance costs. Reimbursement available for contract costs, direct purchases, force account/in-house labor, in-kind services, and equipment. Eligible uses include basketball courts, tennis courts, pickleball courts, playgrounds, fitness trails, pool improvements, pavilions, restrooms, dog parks, bocce ball courts, waterfront improvements, splash pads, sports court resurfacing, lighting, inclusive playgrounds, nature centers, walking paths, and other recreational amenities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to municipal corporations, Baltimore City, and eligible non-profit organizations throughout Maryland. Projects must be located within the applicant's jurisdiction or service area, specifically within blue areas on DNR eligibility map.
requirements_list: Applicants must be governing bodies of municipal corporations, Baltimore City, or eligible non-profit organizations

Applicants must demonstrate capacity to plan, implement, and maintain the project (sufficient and qualified staff or contractor, effective administrative procedures and systems, evidence of past success)
Projects must be open and available to all users, not restricted to specific interest groups
Projects must be located within the municipal corporation's jurisdiction, Baltimore City, or applicant's service area

The applicant must hold rights to develop on the property (ownership, easement, long-term lease with 20+ years remaining without termination for convenience clause, or project-specific Joint Use Agreement)
Projects must be capital projects with a minimum 20-year lifespan (or perpetuity for land acquisitions)
Projects cannot have been started prior to grant award
For property acquisitions, cost must be supported by two independent appraisals
For acquisitions, land must be maintained for public use in perpetuity
Contingency costs cannot be included in project estimates
Projects must be completed as proposed; only minor changes are permitted
Project must involve park and playground development or revitalization
Projects replacing facilities previously funded by POS Local or CPP are only eligible after 20 years have passed (or 15 years for LPPI-funded projects)
Playground surfacing cannot exceed 90 ppm lead or contain added PFAS chemicals
Compliance with all Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations
Public use at all reasonable hours; open to all persons regardless of protected characteristics
Compliance with ADA and Civil Rights Act
Consistency with National Playground Safety Standards
Acknowledgement sign installation required prior to project completion
Submit invoices/requisitions with itemized costs
Provide proof of payment (canceled checks or payment evidence)
Documentation retention for three years after final reimbursement
Compliance with local, state, and federal procurement procedures
Payment certification from fiscal authority or project coordinator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit complete digital application submissions with detailed project information by August of any calendar year (deadline: August 20, 2025 at 3:00 p.m.). Local grants staff prepare and distribute application materials and may conduct grant writing workshops. Applications are evaluated by DNR staff based on consistency with program purpose, eligibility requirements, and criteria, as well as applicant responses. Recommendations are provided to the Secretary of DNR for possible inclusion in the Governor's budget. Selected projects undergo State Clearinghouse review and must be approved by the Board of Public Works (BPW) before funds are encumbered. Applicants are notified by May of the following calendar year whether their project was selected for the upcoming fiscal year's budget. After BPW approval, grant recipient is notified of the award. Since the program is reimbursable, grant recipients must pay costs upfront and submit reimbursement requests with supporting documentation (invoices, canceled checks, cost summaries).

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps address the impacts of climate-related hazards by supporting risk understanding, planning for hazard mitigation, and implementing projects that use nature-based features to improve community resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides grants to address climate-related hazards including understanding risk, planning for hazard mitigation, and implementing nature-based projects to improve community resilience.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities in Maryland seeking to address climate-related hazards and improve resilience
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Understanding risk from climate-related hazards, planning for hazard mitigation, implementing projects using nature-based features to improve community resilience
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the designated grant program manager to learn if your project qualifies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A compensatory mitigation program established by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to provide direct monetary compensation and support to commercial and charter fishing vessel owners, operators, crew members, and fishing businesses who have been impacted by the construction, operation, or decommissioning of the US Wind offshore wind energy project. The program includes three interconnected components: direct compensation through a claims-based Mitigation Fund, the Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP), and a Multi-Use Fishing Community Resilience Fund. Compensation is based on estimates of vessel revenues derived from historical and current federal and state fishery landings data from the affected offshore project area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490) near the Delmarva Peninsula.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive mitigation package with three main components: (1) Compensatory Mitigation Fund providing direct monetary compensation claims-based on documented economic losses from project construction ($1,546,864), operation over 5 years post-construction ($1,893,510), and decommissioning ($2,014,757); (2) Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP) providing vouchers up to $2,500 per fisher for new entrant training, established no later than 120 days prior to offshore construction commencement; (3) Multi-Use Fishing Community Resilience Fund supporting facility displacement, West Ocean City Harbor maintenance (dredging, dock and shore stabilization), and programmatic funds for gear development, business development, vessel resilience, new entrant incentives, and charter fisher marketing. Total fund allocation of approximately $5.46 million across all three components.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be made no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period, may be extended up to five years after date of loss if data unavailable or for good cause shown. NETP established no later than 120 days prior to Offshore Construction Commencement Date. Funds become available once offshore project construction begins.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial vessel owners, operators, and crew members; charter fishing businesses; fishing businesses; new entrant fishers; local fishing communities in Maryland and Delaware who have fished in the Atlantic Ocean offshore wind project area (Lease Area OCS-A 0490) near the Delmarva Peninsula, regardless of home port location. Primary geographic focus for Resilience Fund components is Worcester County and West Ocean City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct monetary compensation for documented economic losses from construction, operation, and decommissioning of the offshore wind energy project; training and education for new entrants; facility displacement support; harbor maintenance and infrastructure including dredging, dock stabilization, and shore protection; gear development; business development and marketing; fishing vessel resilience support; and charter fisher marketing initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial and charter fishermen and fishing businesses from any location who have fished in the federal waters off the Atlantic coast of Delaware and Maryland, specifically the U.S. Exclusive Economic Zone and Lease Area OCS-A 0490 (approximately 80,000 acres, approximately 11.5 miles off the Maryland coast). Resilience Fund components primarily focused on West Ocean City Harbor area (12929 and 12933 South Harbor Road) and Worcester County.
requirements_list: Commercial or charter fishing vessel owner, operator, or crew member
Fishing business or individual engaged in fishing activities
Must have demonstrated fishing history in or near Lease Area OCS-A 0490 or affected offshore wind project area
Must document impact from construction, operation, or decommissioning of wind energy project
Must be able to provide evidence of past landings from the affected area
For NETP: demonstrate new entrant status to commercial fishing
For Resilience Fund facility displacement: facility must be directly affected by O&M facility operations at West Ocean City Harbor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds become available once offshore project construction begins. Claims process operates on a claims-made basis with documentation of economic impacts required. Participation is voluntary and not mandatory. For NETP: voucher system established through preferred vendor training providers no later than 120 days prior to construction commencement. For Resilience Fund: funding triggered 30 days after financial investment decision (FID) closing or per timeline in Resilience Fund Option Funding Chart. Details on participation procedures available through the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind and MDNR.

structured_extraction.program_description: Deer Cooperators are businesses licensed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to provide deer control assistance using non-lethal and lethal deer management techniques to resolve deer problems in areas where hunting is not viable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Licensing for businesses to provide deer management services. Permits for year-round operations available for human safety concerns (airports, test tracks, etc.). Permits for agricultural or other areas without human safety concerns can be used from January 15 to April 15 annually. Community consensus and DNR approval required annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses providing deer control services in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-lethal and lethal deer management techniques to resolve deer problems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland where deer hunting is not a viable option
requirements_list: Must be a licensed business
Must obtain DNR approval
Must obtain community consensus on annual basis
Year-round permits require human safety concern (airports, test tracks, etc.)
Agricultural or other area permits limited to January 15 - April 15
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kevin Lamp at Wildlife & Heritage Service to inquire about licensing and permit requirements. Community consensus and DNR approval required annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: Allows landowners, agricultural lessees, or designated employees to request DNR investigation of severe deer damage for population reduction purposes. The Wildlife and Heritage Service issues permits on a county-by-county basis to authorize management actions for resolving deer damage to commercial agricultural and forestry operations including farms, orchards, nurseries, and woodland areas with forest/planting management plans.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR investigates severe deer damage; if approved, permits landowners, agricultural lessees, and designated employees to take a specified number of antlerless deer (or antlered deer in limited circumstances for buck rubbing damage) using legal hunting methods. Permits authorize management actions to resolve legitimate deer damage to commercial agricultural and forestry operations. Permits are issued on a county-by-county basis through designated WHS staff. Permits are valid up to one year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Master Confirmation Log Sheet due by March 15 following permit expiration
structured_extraction.contact_name: Wildlife and Heritage Service staff (by county)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, agricultural lessees, and designated employees experiencing severe deer damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, and woodland areas with forest management plans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permits authorize taking and utilization of deer; encourages donation to charitable food programs. Permits authorize management actions to resolve deer damage to commercial agricultural and forestry operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide across all Maryland counties. Property must be in Maryland. Specific firearm restrictions apply in shotgun-only counties and certain counties including Harford, Montgomery, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Carroll, Frederick, and St. Mary's have modified distance requirements for archery. Applicants should contact the WHS staff member assigned to their county.
requirements_list: Be a landowner, agricultural lessee, or designated employee (W-2 recipient) of a farm, orchard, or nursery
Have legitimate damage to commercial farm crops, orchards, nurseries, or certain managed forests caused by deer
Demonstrate severe deer damage and economic loss
Permittee/agents must possess valid Maryland hunting license and firearm
Must meet Maryland Hunter Education and Safety Requirement
No Natural Resources Article violations within 2 years prior to application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Wildlife and Heritage Service staff member assigned to your county during normal business hours. To schedule a wildlife permit appointment, email wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or call 410-260-8540. Appointments at the Tawes State Office Building must be scheduled in advance; walk-in customers are not accepted without confirmed appointments. For detailed information about the permit process, refer to the Deer Management Permit General Conditions document.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows authorized individuals and businesses to conduct deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land in Maryland. The permit fee is $100 and expires 1 year from the date of issuance. Applicants must specify their method for disposing of deer carcasses at the time of application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The permit authorizes the permittee to remove and handle deer carcasses on private land. The permit fee is $100 and expires 1 year from the date of issuance. Applicants must specify their method for disposing of deer carcasses at the time of application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses seeking to remove and handle deer carcasses on private land.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deer carcass removal and handling operations on private land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must provide the method for disposing of deer carcasses at time of application
Permit applies only to private land
Permit valid for 1 year from date of issuance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Deer Salvage Permit Application Form by email to georgia.johnson@maryland.gov or wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, by phone at 301-501-0202 or 410-260-8540, or by mail to Wildlife Permit Coordinator, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Appointments are required to visit the Tawes State Office Building. Schedule appointments by emailing wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or calling 410-260-8540.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that empowers landowners across Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia to manage their forests for healthier wildlife habitat, cleaner water, wildfire resilience, and sustainable woodlands. The program blends hands-on training, demonstration and interpretive projects, and community outreach to improve forest management across public and private lands. The program focuses on forest management techniques including timber harvesting, prescribed fire management, invasive species control, early successional habitat creation, habitat connectivity, landscape mosaic maintenance, and riparian buffer restoration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides hands-on training through the Delmarva Woodland Stewards course covering topics such as forest management best practices, riparian buffers, agroforestry, prescribed fire, vegetation management, invasive species control, timber harvesting techniques (regeneration harvest, seed tree harvest, shelterwood harvest, selection harvest, and timber stand improvement), and wood product markets. Training is delivered through University of Maryland Extension with approximately 60 participants trained to date from Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia. The course includes a daylong field trip to help participants visualize concepts and integrate learning into forest stewardship plans for their land. The program also provides demonstration and interpretive projects, including an 8-site wildlife-friendly forest management demonstration network on Maryland's Eastern Shore with interpretive signage and trails. Demonstrates landscape-scale GIS analysis for wildlife habitat connectivity in the Pocomoke River watershed, inland sand dune identification and restoration opportunities, and targeted tree planting for riparian buffer establishment. Provides technical guidance on prescribed fire management to achieve objectives including undesirable species control, pest reduction, disturbance-dependent ecosystem maintenance, wildfire risk reduction, nutrient cycling, and increased wildlife forage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, conservationists, community members, forest managers, wildlife habitat stewards, and land managers in Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia interested in forest management, wildlife habitat, and sustainable woodlands
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in forest management practices, development of forest stewardship plans, forest management demonstrations, prescribed burn implementation, tree planting for riparian buffer restoration, habitat connectivity improvements, invasive species management, early successional habitat creation and maintenance, landscape mosaic management, inland sand dune restoration, and afforestation plantings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to landowners across the Delmarva peninsula, primarily focused on Maryland's Eastern Shore including Cecil, Kent, Queen Ames, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, and Worcester counties, as well as Delaware and Virginia. Specific focus areas include the Pocomoke River watershed, Browns Branch watershed in Queen Ames County, and areas with fire-dependent and fire-adapted ecosystems.
requirements_list: Landowner or community member interested in forest management
Willingness to attend training or participate in program activities
Interest in implementing forest stewardship practices on their land
For riparian buffer planting: property within riparian buffer zones (100-foot or 300-foot width)
For prescribed fire: trained professional must conduct burns with proper safety equipment including flame-resistant clothing, leather boots and gloves, hard hat, and radio
For inland sand dune projects: sandy soils with ≥75% sand content and locally significant elevation change
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners can contact Charly Sager at the Maryland Forest Service to learn about training opportunities and participation options. University of Maryland Extension offers periodic Delmarva Woodland Stewards courses. Individuals can also join the Eastern Shore Prescribed Burn Association mailing list by filling out an interest form. Participants in training courses are encouraged to integrate learning into forest stewardship plans for their land. For riparian buffer opportunities, outreach begins with private land 100-foot buffer opportunities in priority areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Developing a Climate-Resilient Fishery Management Plan for State-Managed Fisheries
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources develops a climate-resilient fishery management plan for state-managed fisheries. The project connects interested and impacted parties in Maryland fisheries to exchange existing climate and fisheries data and industry knowledge, and collaboratively develop a climate resilient fishery management plan. The plan will enable the department to prepare for and respond to environmental and climate change, ensuring continued, equitable access to fishing resources for all users.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The department is forming a workgroup to assist with the development of the fishery management plan. The workgroup serves as a forum for exchanging knowledge, identifying climate-driven challenges and opportunities, and developing the fishery management plan's goals and objectives. Workgroup membership represents diverse forms of knowledge including science, management, industry, and culture.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Interested and impacted parties in Maryland fisheries including recreational and commercial fishing communities and fisheries management systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing a climate-resilient framework for utilizing adaptation and resilience strategies to manage fisheries
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland state-managed fisheries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Additional information about the workgroup will be posted on the webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual awards that recognize tournament organizers' efforts to protect black bass resources and include youth participants in sportfishing tournaments. The program spreads knowledge of black bass conservation and watercraft safety, and provides supplies and equipment to support competitive sport fishing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards include supplies and equipment up to $500 value per award. Up to two awards are given per year. Supplies may include items such as fish redistribution waiver, hand scales, rulers, cull clips, barbless tackle, thermometers, life jackets, aerators, ice, mesh bags, shade canopies, cattle tanks, rubber nets, or weigh-in systems. Tournament participants who complete the online Bass Class receive a Certificate of Completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black bass tournament organizers who are Maryland residents and youth anglers ages 16-25 seeking to participate in or organize competitive fishing tournaments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation supplies and equipment for tournaments to promote bass conservation and survival, such as fish redistribution waiver, hand scales, rulers, cull clips, barbless tackle, thermometers, life jackets, aerators, ice, mesh bags, shade canopies, cattle tanks, rubber nets, or weigh-in systems. Bass safety education materials and certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for tournaments. Tournament organizer or co-organizer must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Tournament organizer or co-organizer must be a Maryland resident
All tournament participants must have a valid Maryland fishing license if required by law
Tournament must have at most 49 boats
At least 50% of angler participants must be between 16 and 25 years old, inclusive
Organizer or co-organizer must identify at least one best management practice when obtaining a permit for the tournament
All tournament participants must complete the online Bass Class from Fishing and Boating Services
Organizer or co-organizer must submit a narrative of 100 words or less describing supply needs and justification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically to Ryan Gary at ryan.gary@maryland.gov by May 1, 2025. Applicants will be notified of their standing by June 1, 2025. The department will make supply purchases on behalf of the applicant beginning July 1, 2025. Awards and supplies will be received by August 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Elk Neck State Forest Fuelwood Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A permit-based program allowing individuals to collect firewood from designated areas within Elk Neck State Forest for personal use. Participants can harvest down, damaged, or standing dead trees from trails areas on a daily permit basis, limited to five loads per calendar year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individuals obtain daily permits for $10.00 per day to harvest firewood (up to one standard load per day, five loads per calendar year). A standard load is defined as one pickup truck load stacked wood not exceeding the cab height, not to exceed one cord. No resale of material is permitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking firewood for personal household use from Elk Neck State Forest
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Harvesting and collection of firewood for personal use only; no resale permitted
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Elk Neck State Forest, Cecil County, Maryland. Specifically within the Trails Area defined as down, damaged, or standing dead trees within 200 linear feet of main driving trails, encompassing approximately six miles of main driving trails and 11 miles of total driving trails.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an individual
Firewood must be for personal use only; no resale permitted
Limited to no more than five standard loads per calendar year
Limited to one standard load per day
Standard load defined as one pickup truck load stacked wood not exceeding cab height and not exceeding one cord
Dump trucks and other heavy service vehicles prohibited
No splitting of material permitted on forest property
No operations permitted September 1 through January 31 each year
No weekend or after-hours operations permitted
Maximum three permittees per day
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant completes a Google form to apply for a permit. Forest staff contact the applicant to schedule a date for payment and start date. After payment and permit issuance, permittee is taken to the defined area. Upon obtaining the daily limit, the operator contacts forest staff for load inspection before departing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Forest Service offers a cost-sharing program to help public land managers, local governments, and conservation organizations treat ash trees infested with the emerald ash borer pest. The program provides financial assistance covering 50 percent of professional pesticide treatment costs when trunk injections with emamectin benzoate are conducted by licensed pesticide applicators on public lands. Additionally, the Forest Service provides educational guidance and technical information to homeowners and professional arborists on identifying ash trees and protecting them from emerald ash borer through insecticide treatment options, timing, costs, and environmental protection measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 50/50 cost share for trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate conducted by licensed pesticide applicators on public land. Applicants must develop a treatment response plan and work with licensed pesticide applicators. The program also provides educational guidance on insecticide treatment options including soil drench, trunk injection, and basal spray methods, with information on treatment timing, costs, and environmental protection guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public land managers, local governments, conservation organizations, homeowners with ash trees, and professional arborists managing ash trees affected by the emerald ash borer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional pesticide treatments (trunk injections with emamectin benzoate) to treat ash trees infested with the emerald ash borer pest. Educational resources on treatment options and environmental protection measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for public lands, conservation areas, and homeowners.
requirements_list: Treatment must be conducted by a licensed pesticide applicator
Applicant must be a public land manager, local government, or conservation organization
Applicants should conduct a tree inventory and develop a response plan that includes treatment
Tree must have less than 30% canopy loss for treatment
Trees should be measured at 4.5 feet above ground level (DBH)
Avoid insecticide application within 25 feet of water bodies
Do not apply when heavy rainfall expected within 24 hours
Follow all label directions for specific pesticide products
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should conduct a tree inventory, develop a response plan that includes treatment, and work with licensed pesticide applicators. Contact Colleen Kenny at the Maryland Forest Service to discuss treatment options, cost-sharing arrangements, and specific application procedures. For educational resources and to report infested trees, visit extension.umd.edu/hgic.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit required for properly accredited persons of known scientific attainment who wish to collect rare, threatened, or endangered species from the wild for scientific or educational purposes, or to capture, mark, and release such species. Public educational institutions also need this permit to salvage and maintain rare, threatened, or endangered specimens for educational purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A permit is issued for a one-year period, valid through December 31 of the issuing year. The permit allows the holder to legally collect, capture, mark, and release rare, threatened, or endangered animal species designated with I, T, E, or X State Status, and plant species with T or E State Status for scientific or educational purposes. An annual report must be filed by December 31 of the issuing year. A federal permit from the United States Fish and Wildlife Service and/or United States Department of Agriculture may be required to collect and/or possess migratory birds or federally listed species.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline specified; applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (410) 260-8540; toll-free in Maryland: 1-877-620-8DNR; TTY: Maryland Relay via 1-800-735-2258 or 711
structured_extraction.program_audience: Properly accredited persons of known scientific attainment seeking to collect rare, threatened, or endangered species for scientific or educational purposes, and public educational institutions that need to salvage and maintain rare, threatened, or endangered specimens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Collection and capture of rare, threatened, or endangered animal and plant species from the wild for scientific or educational purposes; marking and release of such species; salvage and maintenance of rare, threatened, or endangered specimens for educational purposes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; applicant must specify specific areas where collection will take place
requirements_list: Applicant must be a properly accredited person of known scientific attainment OR a public educational institution
Must complete an Endangered Species permit application
Must submit a $10 fee (check or money order payable to Department of Natural Resources)
Must file an annual report by December 31 of the issuing year; failure to submit may result in revocation of existing permits or rejection of future applications
A federal permit from the United States Fish and Wildlife Service may be required for migratory birds or federally listed species
A federal permit from the United States Department of Agriculture may be required for certain species
The permit is valid through December 31 of the issuing year
Must provide project proposal with reason for study, objectives, and justification
Must specify species (common and scientific names), numbers, age classes, and sex
Must specify collection methods and time period
Must specify final disposition of specimens
Must list all collectors in addition to applicant with their names, addresses, and titles
Must certify information under penalty of perjury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an Endangered Species permit application and mail it along with a $10 check or money order (payable to Department of Natural Resources) to the Wildlife Permits Coordinator at MD DNR - Wildlife and Heritage Service, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Applicants can also request the permit by email at wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at (410) 260-8540. Applicants unsure which permits they need can complete a Collection Permits Questionnaire. The Tawes State Office Building is open by appointment only.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides financial and technical assistance to help agricultural producers, landowners, and private non-industrial forest landowners install or implement conservation practices on eligible agricultural and forestland. The program offers cost-share payments for structural and management practices, with a focus on livestock and agricultural production as well as forestry management. Participants can receive reimbursement for eligible costs including stewardship plan preparation, reforestation, tree planting, site preparation, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, timber stand improvement, nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, and wildlife habitat enhancement. Cost-share payments typically cover 50% of eligible practice costs, though limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers may be eligible for cost shares up to 90%. Funding is allocated with 60% earmarked for livestock production practices. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500-2,000 acres. Payments are generally limited to $10,000 per person annually and $50,000 total over the 5 to 10 year life of the contract. Up to 200 conservation practices are available depending on location. A forest stewardship management plan is typically required before work begins, and a 15-year commitment requirement typically applies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share financial assistance and technical guidance for eligible forest management, reforestation, agricultural, and environmental quality improvement practices. The program pays between 50% and 90% of eligible practice costs depending on participant status. Limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers may be eligible for cost shares up to 90%; most other practices are funded at 50-75% (typically up to 65%). Funding is allocated with 60% earmarked for livestock production practices. Landowners complete approved practices, pay for goods and services, and submit invoices and payment documentation for reimbursement. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500-2,000 acres. Payments are generally limited to $10,000 per person annually and $50,000 total over the 5 to 10 year life of the contract. A 15-year commitment requirement typically applies. A forest stewardship management plan or conservation plan is typically required, and funding must be allocated prior to the beginning of any work. Up to 200 conservation practices available depending on location. The government's share cannot exceed 90 percent of the projected cost of structural and vegetative practices for eligible participants.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dan Rider or local department forester
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, private non-industrial forest landowners, farm and forestry producers, farmers, and individuals or entities engaged in livestock, agricultural production, or forestry management who own eligible land and wish to implement conservation and forest improvement practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible practices include stewardship plan preparation, reforestation of open land, tree planting, site preparation for natural or artificial reforestation, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, planting of seedlings for timber and forest product management, nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, grassed waterways, and other structural and vegetative practices to improve agricultural and woodland practices, restore landscapes, and provide environmental quality improvements on private land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland and in designated geographic priority areas. Eligible land includes cropland, rangeland, grassland, pasture, and private non-industrial forestland. Eligibility depends on property size and availability of funds. Up to 200 conservation practices included depending on location. Targets areas with higher concentrations of on-farm or off-farm problems, especially water quality problems. Landowners work with their local county forester, USDA NRCS technical service providers, or local NRCS offices.
requirements_list: Own eligible land (cropland, rangeland, grassland, pasture, or private non-industrial forestland)
Forest landowners must own at least 5 forest acres but not more than 1,000 acres
Agree to maintain forestry practices for at least 15 years
Land must have the potential to be harvested for products including logs, timbers, pulpwood, firewood, woodchips, poles, piles, posts, and other primary forest products
Cannot have received program assistance for the same practice in any of the 15 years preceding application (Woodland Incentive Program)
Cannot have received federal cost-share assistance for the same practice in the 5 years preceding application
Forest stewardship management plan or conservation plan must be written for the property
Funding must be allocated prior to beginning any work
Practice must be recommended in the forest stewardship management plan or conservation plan
Practices must be implemented in conformance to NRCS standards and specifications
All practices must be identified as eligible by the State Conservationist with advice of the State Technical Committee
Participants must develop and implement an approved conservation plan
Plan must address relevant conservation needs and objectives
Practices must be approved by local forester before implementation
Must be a limited resource producer or beginning farmer or rancher for 90% cost share
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local county forester, USDA NRCS office, or Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Local work groups and conservation districts assist in identifying eligible practices for locally identified resource concerns. Farmers may also apply through USDA Service Centers located in each county. Work with Maryland Forest Service staff and USDA NRCS technical service providers to apply for specific practices. The forester can help by furnishing technical specifications, setting up recommended practices, and arranging for contract crews to perform the practice. Participants work with NRCS to develop a conservation plan addressing their specific conservation needs. If approved, landowners complete the approved practices and pay for goods and services. The local forester or NRCS staff inspects the practice to ensure proper implementation. Landowners submit copies of invoices and payment documentation for processing and receive a reimbursement check for the cost-share percentage. Upon approval, the farmer and NRCS enter a 5 to 10 year contract with payment terms. Practices must be approved through the State Technical Committee process.

structured_extraction.program_description: An exciting competition program for high school students in grades 9-12 to learn about Maryland's natural resources. Student teams of five work together throughout the school year to study various natural resource topics on a hands-on basis with expert training. Topics covered include Aquatics, Forestry, Soils, Wildlife, and a fifth issue topic. Teams compete at the county level, then state level, with winners invited to compete nationally.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR provides hands-on training in natural resource topics taught by field experts. Participating teams compete at county and state levels, with opportunities for national competition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students in grades 9-12 interested in learning about and competing in natural resource education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training and competitions focused on aquatics, forestry, soils, wildlife, and related natural resource topics
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland with county and state-level competition structure
requirements_list: Teams consist of 5 students
Students must be in grades 9-12
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information on how to get involved, check the program page at https://dnr.maryland.gov/education/Pages/envirothon-aquatics.aspx

structured_extraction.program_name: Every Kid Outdoors Day Use Pass
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program pass that allows U.S. fourth graders and their family members free access to federal lands and waters, as well as Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Day-use pass provided by the federal Every Kid Outdoors program that grants free access to federal lands and waters as well as Maryland State Parks. Available to U.S. fourth graders and their family members.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. fourth graders and their family members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Day-use entry to federal lands, waters, and Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland and at federal lands nationwide.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. fourth grader or family member of a fourth grader
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain pass through the National Park Service Every Kid Outdoors program at everykidoutdoors.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Explore the Patuxent Teen Leadership Paddle
structured_extraction.program_description: A week-long canoeing expedition for high school students that combines outdoor adventure with leadership and teamwork skill-building. Participants navigate the Patuxent River, conduct water quality tests, study plant communities, participate in stewardship projects, camp by the riverside, and prepare meals together. The program culminates in a presentation to local leaders, friends, and family. Participants pay a tiered fee with three pricing options: Tier III at $200 (reduced rate subsidized by Friends of Jug Bay and CBNERR-MD), Tier II at $250 (partially subsidized to cover staff, utilities, and operational costs), or Tier I at $300 (reflects full actual cost including maintenance, food, and administrative expenses). Scholarships are available from Friends of Jug Bay for participants who need additional assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay a tiered fee for the week-long program. Three pricing tiers are available: Tier III at $200 (reduced rate subsidized by Friends of Jug Bay and CBNERR-MD), Tier II at $250 (partially subsidized to cover staff, utilities, and operational costs), and Tier I at $300 (reflects full actual cost including maintenance, food, and administrative expenses). Scholarships are available from Friends of Jug Bay for participants who need additional financial assistance beyond Tier III. Program participation covers instruction, camping, meals, equipment, water quality testing, educational programming, and stewardship project participation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, first come, first served
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in environmental leadership, outdoor adventure, river conservation, and developing stewardship skills for the Patuxent River and natural resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a week-long canoeing expedition including instruction, meals, camping, equipment, educational programming, water quality testing, and stewardship activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is based on the Patuxent River and serves students from the Patuxent River region. Participants from any geographic location can apply as long as they are high school students able to attend the program session.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Able to participate in a week-long camping and canoeing expedition
COVID vaccination is recommended for all participants and staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply online using a Google Form accessible from the program website. Applications are accepted on a rolling, first come, first served basis until spots are filled. Applicants interested in scholarships or needing additional financial assistance should contact the program coordinator directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venison donation program that collects deer harvested by hunters and farmers and processes them into meat to be distributed to food banks and community organizations serving less fortunate people in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FHFH pays the full cost of processing donated deer at approved meat processors. Participating processors charge a special discounted fee to process donated venison, and FHFH covers this fee for donors. The program collects cash donations from churches, foundations, businesses, and individuals to fund the processing costs. An average deer yields 40 pounds of meat at approximately $1.64 per pound or about 41 cents per serving.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunters and farmers in Maryland who wish to donate harvested deer, as well as cash donors and volunteers. Venison is distributed to community organizations such as church pantries, food banks, Salvation Army, and emergency assistance programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Processing and distribution of venison from donated deer to food banks and community organizations serving people in need.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Deer can be brought to participating meat processors during Maryland's bow, muzzleloader, and firearms seasons.
requirements_list: Deer must be legally tagged
Deer must be field dressed before bringing to a participating meat processor
Donor must bring deer to a participating approved meat processor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Hunters and farmers field dress their legally tagged deer and bring them to a participating meat processor. The processor handles the donation paperwork and FHFH pays the processing fee. Cash donations and volunteer inquiries are handled through the FHFH organization website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Estate Tax Exclusion for Conservation Easement Property
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal estate tax benefit that allows landowners with donated conservation easements to reduce their taxable estates. Conservation easements reduce the appraised value of land for estate tax purposes by limiting development potential. Additionally, a federal estate tax exclusion allows 40% of land value up to $500,000 per owner to be excluded from estate taxes for land subject to a donated easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Land subject to a donated conservation easement is valued at its restricted use value rather than maximum development potential for estate tax purposes, reducing the taxable estate. An additional federal estate tax exclusion allows up to 40% of the land value, capped at $500,000 per owner, to be excluded from estate taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with substantial estates who have donated conservation easements and wish to reduce estate tax liability
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Estate tax reduction and exclusion for land under conservation easement; reduces taxable estate value for federal estate tax calculation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all landowners in Maryland and nationwide with land subject to donated conservation easements
requirements_list: Land must be subject to a donated conservation easement
Easement must limit development potential
Exclusion applies up to 40% of land value with maximum of $500,000 per owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consult with a tax advisor or estate planning attorney to determine how a conservation easement affects estate tax liability. Donate a conservation easement to a qualified organization. The exclusion applies automatically to the estate valuation process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Income Tax Deduction for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal tax program allowing donors to claim income tax deductions for donating qualified real property interests (conservation easements) to qualifying conservation organizations. Governed by Internal Revenue Code Section 170(f) and regulations under 26 CFR § 1.170A–14. Landowners who donate a perpetual conservation easement to a qualified organization can deduct the value of the easement from their federal income taxes. The deduction can be taken in one year if the value is 50% or less of adjusted gross income, or spread over up to 15 years if greater. Qualified farmers or ranchers may deduct up to 100% of adjusted gross income.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners can deduct the appraised value of a donated conservation easement from federal taxable income. Deduction value equals the fair market value of the property before the conservation restriction minus the fair market value after the restriction. If the easement value is 50% or less of adjusted gross income, the full deduction can be taken in the year of donation. If greater, the deduction can be spread over 15 years. For qualified farmers or ranchers, the deduction limit is 100% of adjusted gross income instead of 50%. Deduction reduced by any financial or economic benefits received by donor or related persons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual property owners and donors of real property interests; Partnerships and S corporations; Corporations; Trusts and estates; Farmers and agricultural land operators; Landowners with scenic or conservation value property; Qualified conservation organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax deduction for conservation easement donations for: outdoor recreation, wildlife/habitat protection, open space preservation, historic preservation, scenic enjoyment, agricultural preservation, forestry preservation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal (nationwide); property must be located within the United States; must comply with Federal, State, or local governmental conservation policy; appraiser must be licensed or certified in state where property is located
requirements_list: Donation must be of a qualified real property interest (perpetual conservation restriction)
Contribution must be exclusively for conservation purposes
Conservation purpose must be protected in perpetuity with legally enforceable restrictions
Restrictions must be recorded in land records of the jurisdiction
Easement must be conveyed to a governmental unit or qualified section 501(c)(3) charitable organization
Qualified appraisal required, conducted in accordance with generally accepted appraisal standards (USPAP)
Appraisal must comply with § 1.170A-13(c) of existing regulations
IRS Form 8283 must be attached to federal tax return

Form must include statement identifying conservation purposes, fair market value before and after donation, whether donation was required by contract or permit, and description of any related interests in nearby property
Written agreement between donor and donee certifying donee qualifications and resources
For historic structures: photographs of entire exterior and description of all restrictions required
For historic structures: visual public access required for scenic easements and historic properties
Significantly public benefit must be demonstrated
Restrictions on transfer designed solely to ensure conservation dedication permitted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a qualified appraiser to determine the value of the conservation easement donation. Complete IRS Form 8283 with appraiser. Send Form 8283 and required statement to Maryland Environmental Trust for donee acknowledgement signature. Allow minimum 10 business days for processing. If donation value exceeds $500,000, provide copy of appraisal to IRS along with the form. Attach completed Form 8283 to federal income tax return. Include qualified appraisal with tax return; submit written agreement with donee organization; file required documentation with tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: Permit application for operating fee fishing lakes/ponds in Maryland; requires maintenance of fish stocking records, disease reporting, and annual reporting. A permit that grants permission to operate a fishing facility on privately-controlled lands and waters where customers pay a fee to fish. The permit allows paying customers to catch and keep fish without needing a Maryland Recreational Fishing License. Fish must be artificially propagated by commercial hatcheries or purchased from licensed fish sellers. The permit authorizes operation of a fee fishing facility on private land or water and allows fish to be taken without regard to seasons, creel, or possession limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Authorization to operate a fee fishing lake/pond facility with regulatory oversight. The permit is issued annually for a $25 fee (non-refundable) payable by check, money order, or electronically. The permit authorizes operation of a fee fishing facility on private land or water and allows fish to be taken without regard to seasons, creel, or possession limits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual renewal at beginning of calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners, organizations, Rod & Gun Clubs, campgrounds, and fee fishing lake/pond operators who want to operate fee fishing facilities on their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: $25.00 permit fee (non-refundable application cost) for establishing and operating a fee fishing facility where customers pay to catch fish.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland on privately-controlled lands and waters.
requirements_list: $25.00 permit fee required (non-refundable)
Must own, lease, or control the land and water where the facility operates
Fish must be artificially propagated by commercial hatcheries or purchased from licensed fish sellers
Must maintain shipping and receiving records by species at the facility or another specified location
Must obtain a fish stocking permit prior to stocking additional fish
Must notify DNR immediately upon discovery of any disease affecting fish at the facility
Invasive or nonnative species must be euthanized onsite and not returned to any Maryland body of water
All fish removed must be identified by metal tag or bill of sale if transported by tank
Must report findings to the Maryland Invasive Species Tracker if invasive species are found
Submit annual activity report
Provide site map with directions (initial application)
Provide facility sketch showing ponds, inflow, and effluent
Workmen's compensation insurance certificate (if employing staff)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fee Fishing Lake Permit application form online or submit via email. Include a map of the fishing location with directions and facility sketch showing ponds, inflow, and effluent. Submit the application electronically via the online form or email to paylakes.dnr@maryland.gov. Pay the $25 annual fee by check, money order, or through the online payment system. Mail/email required documents to paylakes.dnr@maryland.gov. Permits are issued annually with renewal at the beginning of the calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_name: First Responder Annual State Park and Trail Passport
structured_extraction.program_description: A discounted annual pass available to Maryland resident first responders and law enforcement officers, providing $40 off the standard price. The pass offers unlimited day-use admission for everyone in a single vehicle (up to 10 people) to Maryland state parks and facilities, unlimited boat launching at applicable state park facilities, and a 10 percent discount on state-operated concession items and boat rentals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $40 discount on the annual pass cost. Pass provides unlimited day-use admission for vehicle occupants (up to 10 people), unlimited boat launching, and 10 percent discount on concession items and boat rentals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident law enforcement officers, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and similar emergency personnel
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discounted pass provides day-use entry to state parks, boat launching privileges, and discounts on concessions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible first responders statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must serve as law enforcement officer, emergency medical technician, firefighter, or similar emergency personnel
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Purchase online at shopdnr.com with $40 discount applied

structured_extraction.program_description: A free recreational fishing award program that showcases Maryland as a destination for sport fishing. Anglers of all ages can catch and report trophy-sized fish from over 60 eligible species across five categories (Atlantic Coast, Chesapeake Bay, Nontidal, Catch and Release, and Invasive) at or above a certain minimum size. The program encourages participation from youth, families, and residents, and provides opportunities to submit fishing stories and photos to the department's Angler's Log.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free recreational fishing award program that recognizes trophy-sized fish catches. Participants can submit their catches and fishing experiences for recognition and inclusion in the department's Angler's Log and Youth Angler's Log.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any angler fishing legally in Maryland, including youth, families, residents, and visitors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recognition and awards for catching trophy-sized fish from eligible species
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for any angler fishing legally in the state
requirements_list: Must be fishing legally in Maryland
Must catch a fish from one of over 60 eligible species
Fish must meet or exceed the specified minimum size for the species and category
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anglers catch and report trophy-sized fish by landing any eligible species at or above the minimum size. They can submit their stories and pictures about their fishing experiences for inclusion in the Angler's Log or Youth Angler's Log.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program that provides participants with the skills and knowledge to run beginner fishing lessons through their organization. Participants receive instruction in fishing techniques and knowledge to teach beginner fishing lessons. Upon completion, participants who complete the training qualify to borrow fishing gear from the state for extended use at no cost. Training is offered Tuesday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, November through April.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training provided Tuesday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, November through April. Participants receive instruction in fishing techniques and knowledge to teach beginner fishing lessons. Upon completion, organizations can borrow fishing gear from the state at no cost for extended use during their fishing lessons. Organizations must report on use of borrowed equipment and maintain and return all equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specified deadline; training scheduled in advance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth organizations, schools, scout troops, parks, nature centers, 4-H clubs, libraries, summer camps, and community groups seeking to teach or offer beginner fishing lessons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in fishing instruction skills and techniques; borrowing of state-owned fishing gear for conducting educational fishing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Training may be scheduled November through April.
requirements_list: Must have at least 10 participants to request training
Must be 18 years of age or older
Must have and/or acquire a fishing license prior to the training
Must report on use of borrowed equipment
Must maintain all borrowed equipment
Must return any borrowed equipment upon completion of fishing lessons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in the Fishing Instructor Training should contact Chelsea Kenworthy to request a training date. It is recommended to schedule far in advance as availability is limited and may require booking a year in advance for particular dates or times of year. Trainings are scheduled Tuesday through Thursday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, November through April.

structured_extraction.program_description: A professional development program that trains educators in bird education and conservation through workshops. Participants learn Flying WILD activities and receive an activity guide focused on celebrating birds and wildlife education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educators attend 3-6 hour workshops led by certified trainers. The workshop includes hands-on opportunities to try Flying WILD activities. After completing the workshop, participants receive the Flying WILD: An Educator's Guide to Celebrating Birds. Participants can also purchase the guide directly from the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies online store.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Educators interested in bird education and wildlife conservation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and educational materials for teaching bird education and conservation to students
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through training partners in Maryland, including the Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury and Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds (Montgomery County)
requirements_list: Must be an educator
Must attend a 3-6 hour workshop with certified trainers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact one of the two training partners in Maryland to inquire about available training opportunities and workshop dates. Trainers include the Ward Museum of Wildfowl Art in Salisbury and Jen Scully at Black Hill Nature Programs in Boyds. Alternatively, check the professional development page for additional training opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland Department of Natural Resources program that provides financial incentives to private landowners to conserve and responsibly manage their forestland. The program minimizes the loss of Maryland's forest resources during land development through identification and protection of forests and other sensitive areas. Landowners with five or more contiguous forested acres enter into a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement guided by a professionally prepared forest management plan and receive reduced and stabilized property tax assessments—generally at the agricultural rate—for a minimum 15-year term, with assessments frozen for the life of the agreement. Enrolled land requires development of a forest stewardship plan that includes practices supporting fish and wildlife, natural heritage, recreation, soil and water, and forest products. The program recognizes the benefits that private forests provide to water quality, wildlife habitat, carbon storage, air quality, and rural economies. Participants receive a forest management plan drawn up by a forester and technical assistance throughout the enrollment process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners with five or more contiguous acres of forestland receive reduced property tax assessments—generally at the agricultural rate—which remain frozen for the life of the agreement. The minimum term of an agreement is 15 years.
