Forest land in conservation agreement is generally reduced and frozen at a low agricultural property tax rate through a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement that establishes the length of agreement and responsibilities of both owner and Department. Tax reduction is based on enrollment in a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement recorded in county land records and guided by a forest management plan prepared for the property. Participants also receive a forest management plan drawn up by a forester and technical guidance throughout the enrollment process. The program provides a significant tax incentive to landowners who enroll forested land into a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private property owners with five or more contiguous forested acres who are committed to long-term forest stewardship and sustainable forestry practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management planning, forest land conservation, forest land management according to a prepared management plan that protects forests and sensitive areas during land development, reduced property tax assessments to maintain forest cover and support responsible long-term forest management, and forest stewardship practices related to fish and wildlife support, natural heritage and recreation, soil and water management, and forest products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Any property owner with qualifying forestland anywhere in the state may apply through their local Maryland Forest Service office.
requirements_list: Own a property with five or more contiguous forested acres
Agree to enter into a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement with a minimum 15-year term
Follow a forest management plan prepared specifically for the property
Property must be primarily forested (house sites, crop land, and other non-forest open spaces are not eligible)
Eligible land includes forested tracts, newly reforested land after one growing season, and Christmas tree plantations harvested at maturity
Landowner must agree to manage forest land according to a management plan prepared for the property
Forested land must be enrolled into an FCMA
Development of a forest stewardship plan is required
Plan must include schedule of stewardship practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office to determine if a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement is right for your property and to begin the application process. Interested landowners should contact their local Maryland Forest Service office to determine if a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement is right for their property. Forestry staff are available to answer questions, explain program requirements, prepare or review forest management plans, and guide landowners through the enrollment process. Landowners interested in enrolling forested land should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources with details about their property and forest stewardship goals.

structured_extraction.program_description: License required to operate forest products business in Maryland; issued by the Department for every type of forest products manufacturing plant. Forest harvest operations that disturb more than 5,000 square feet or 100 cubic yards of soil must have an approved erosion and sediment control plan.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual license permitting operation of forest products business; required before erecting sawmill or manufacturing plant or changing location. The application process involves submitting an application and payment online through Submittable (preferred) or sending a hardcopy application with a check for the $20.00 licensee fee. Renewal notices are sent annually. The program provides access to forestry services, permitting guidance, information on tax benefits for forest management, and connections to licensed consultants and industrial foresters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons engaged in forest products business, including sole proprietors and companies engaged in sawmill operations, logging, firewood dealers, mulch suppliers, land clearing companies, tree removal companies, and lumber brokers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a licensing/permitting program rather than a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland to all forest product operators.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in a forest products business
Must submit application on Department form
Demonstrate compliance with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act (Title 9, Labor and Employment Article)
Pay $20.00 fee
Report location prior to erection of plant or change of location
Certificate of Insurance for Workers' Compensation or certification as sole proprietor with no employees
Forest harvest operations disturbing more than 5,000 square feet or 100 cubic yards of soil must have an approved erosion and sediment control plan
Must maintain current FPO license to legally operate; must renew annually by December 31st for the following calendar year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form and provide personal/company information, select primary/secondary business types, report products bought/sold, estimate annual consumption, identify timber harvest counties, and provide workers' compensation documentation. Apply online through the Submittable portal with payment (preferred), or download the PDF application form and mail it with a check for the $20.00 licensee fee to the Maryland Forest Service address (201 Baptist Street Suite #22, Salisbury, Maryland 21801). License renewal is also available through the same process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit required for any person who wants to raise, breed, protect, or sell native game birds in Maryland, including bobwhite quail, ring-necked pheasant, wild turkey, ruffed grouse, and waterfowl species regulated by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The permit specifies which game bird species may be bred, raised, protected, or sold and for what purpose, and includes requirements for fencing and other measures to protect native wildlife. Licensed species may be sold live to other permitted individuals, licensed game breeders, retriever trainers, regulated shooting areas, or other permit holders, or dead for human consumption. The permit fee is $5.00 and expires December 31 after issuance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A permit issued for raising, breeding, protecting, or selling native game birds. The permit fee is $5.00. Licensed species may be sold live to licensed game breeders, retriever trainers, regulated shooting areas, or other permit holders, or dead for human consumption. The permit expires December 31 after issuance. Authorization to hold specified wildlife species for game husbandry purposes at designated locations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses in Maryland who want to raise, breed, protect, or sell native game birds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit allows the holder to raise, breed, protect, and sell native game birds subject to specified conditions and restrictions. Permit authorization for holding wildlife species.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must specify county where activity will be conducted.
requirements_list: $5.00 application fee
Complete all application pages
List species to be held and sources of acquisition
Specify location where activity will be conducted
Provide current information (name, address, phone, email, date of birth)
Provide Social Security Number/Tax ID/Federal ID
List related state and federal licenses/permits
Comply with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act (Article 1-401); provide insurance binder or certificate, or certify self-employment exemption
Certify information under penalty of perjury
Must keep a ledger of species raised or acquired, numbers killed, and numbers sold within 48 hours of occurrence
Must keep bills of sale or similar documents as long as animals remain in possession
Must allow Department inspection of records and premises at any reasonable hour
Game birds moved within Maryland must be accompanied by itemized bill of sale from licensee
Game birds shipped out-of-state must have bill of lading attached to shipping container
Fencing and other requirements specified in license to prevent mixing of native wildlife and captive game birds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form to Permits Coordinator at Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis, MD 21401 with $5.00 fee. Applications may also be submitted by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or by phone at 410-260-8540. Appointments may be scheduled by email or phone.

structured_extraction.program_description: A lifetime pass for residents and visitors age 62 and older that provides free day-use entry to Maryland State Parks that charge service fees, half-price camping (Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays) on one site including campsites and mini-cabins, and waived boat launching fees. The pass is non-transferable and requires a $10 processing service fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Golden Age Pass is a one-time lifetime purchase with a $10 processing service fee that provides free day-use entry to all state parks that charge service fees (for cardholder only, unless a per-vehicle fee applies, then free entry for everyone in vehicle). Camping is discounted at half-price for one site Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays (includes campsites and mini-cabins, excludes full-service cabins and houses). Boat launching fees at Maryland State Parks are waived. This is a non-transferable, lifetime pass valid only after the physical card is received by mail (7-10 days delivery time). Pass holder must present original pass at check-in and must be part of camping party during entire stay. For automatic gate access at participating parks (Bohemia River, Point Lookout, Rosaryville, Sandy Point, or St. Mary's River State Parks), supplementary magnetic swipe cards can be requested at no charge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and visitors age 62 and older who wish to visit Maryland State Parks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or discounted access to state park facilities including day-use entry, camping, and boat launching.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland State Parks statewide that charge service fees, including parks with automatic gate systems (Bohemia River State Park, Point Lookout State Park, Rosaryville State Park, Sandy Point State Park, and St. Mary's River State Park).
requirements_list: Must be 62 years of age or older
Must provide valid age verification document (U.S. Passport, Birth Certificate, Driver's License, or State Issued ID) when applying or purchasing
Cardholder must present physical pass at check-in for camping
Cardholder must be part of the camping party during entire stay
Camping available Sunday through Thursday excluding holidays
Camping benefit limited to one site
If lost or stolen, must apply for and purchase new pass
Physical pass must be in possession to enter state park
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can purchase the pass online at shopdnr.com or shopdnr.com/marylandstateparkpassports.aspx or at designated state parks. Online applicants must upload a scanned valid age verification document (U.S. Passport, Birth Certificate, Driver's License, or State Issued ID). If unable to upload proof of age online, applicants can complete the order without the attachment and mail a copy of the valid document along with the online purchase confirmation to Maryland Park Service, 580 Taylor Avenue E-3, Annapolis, MD 21401, Attn: Golden Age Pass Application. The physical pass will be mailed by USPS within 7-10 days after purchase. Golden Age Pass holders using automated gate parks (Bohemia River, Point Lookout, Rosaryville, Sandy Point, or St. Mary's River State Parks) can request a supplementary magnetic swipe card at no charge by contacting the corresponding park office after receiving their pass.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grants Gateway Outcome 3 - Resiliency Through Restoration Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and federal program that serves as a single point of entry for organizations seeking technical and financial assistance to restore local waterways, increase resilience to climate impacts, strengthen local economies, and develop environmental stewards. Supports design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of comprehensive and integrated coastal and stormwater restoration projects to address erosion, flooding, and sea level rise in communities and on public lands throughout Maryland. Projects use nature-based restoration techniques including shoreline restoration (with living shorelines preferred), beneficial use of dredged material, tidal marsh restoration, dune restoration, rain gardens, bioswales, and other green stormwater practices to enhance community resilience and protect against climate change impacts. The program provides funding and technical support for restoration projects that build community resilience to climate change impacts. Funding is provided by the State of Maryland and the National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration through rolling Grants Gateway Outcome 3 solicitations. Design and permitting projects typically cost between $30,000 and $100,000. Construction projects are not funded for CY2026/FY2027 due to funding limitations.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of restoration projects. Design and permit projects typically cost between $30,000 and $100,000. Permit fees are not eligible. Funding is available through rolling Grants Gateway Outcome 3 solicitations with availability depending on fund source and state/federal approvals. For CY2026/FY2027, only design and permitting proposals are eligible; construction projects are not funded at this time due to funding limitations. Projects typically must be completed within 24 months. Projects on private lands are eligible if they demonstrate community-wide benefit. Matching funds or cost savings measures are encouraged, with leveraging funds through the Shoreline Erosion Loan Program highly encouraged where applicable. Technical support is also provided for restoration projects. Funding available July 1, 2026 to October 1, 2026 depending on fund source and state/federal approvals. Technical assistance and site visits available through November 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities, local governments, and non-profit organizations seeking to restore waterways, increase climate resilience, and strengthen local economies. Communities and organizations working on climate adaptation and restoration projects seeking to implement community-wide coastal protection and stormwater management projects in Maryland, particularly those serving BIPOC and marginalized communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restore local waterways and design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of restoration projects including shoreline restoration, living shorelines, beneficial use of dredged material, tidal marsh restoration, dune restoration, rain gardens, bioswales, and other green stormwater and restoration practices that provide community and ecosystem benefits. Increase resilience to climate impacts, strengthen local economies, develop environmental stewards, and provide restoration projects that protect communities from erosion, flooding, and other climate change impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects can be located throughout Maryland on public or private lands, with priority in Maryland's coastal areas and Chesapeake Bay region and Atlantic Coastal Bays area. Private land projects must demonstrate community-wide benefit. Available statewide in Maryland through Grants Gateway Outcome 3 funding and through Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund.
requirements_list: Applications must be submitted through Grants Gateway Portal online only
User registration required (username/password for portal access)
Enhance habitat through coastal restoration or nature-based practices; living shorelines preferred; structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded
Address climate change impacts and reduce community flood risk or erosion impacts
Provide community-wide benefits to a majority of community members and protect community infrastructure and assets
Incorporate climate change data addressing short term (1-10 years) and long term (10+ years) impacts
For coastal projects, consider marsh migration and 2023 Sea Level Rise Projections for Maryland
For stormwater projects, consider Northeast climate assessment trends and Intensity-Duration-Frequency curve data
Demonstrate readiness and ability to proceed with work beginning within 6 months
Support BIPOC and marginalized communities through resilience, water quality, habitat, public access, health, job creation, recreation, or cultural benefits
Document critical or community infrastructure benefiting from the project
Partner with local government and implement recommendations from local plans or assessments
Restore public lands or allow public access and serve as demonstration site
Demonstrate community support and engagement opportunities
Support technical innovations such as beneficial use of dredged material
Provide conceptual-level or greater designs
Provide up to 1:1 matching funds or cost savings measures
Shoreline projects screened through Maryland's Coastal Resiliency Assessment
Community public property is prioritized; funding on private residential properties can be difficult to obtain
Permitting fees are not eligible
Local governments or eligible non-profit organizations must apply
Transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive required
For projects on private lands, landowner agreements and HOA/Community Land Authorizations required
For projects in sea level rise impact areas, Appendix A from Guidance for Using Maryland's 2023 Sea Level Rise Projections required
For non-profit applicants, letter of support from local government representative required
Current designs if applicable
Communication and Engagement Strategy required using template from Grants Gateway site
Photographs of current site conditions and flooding impacts required
Budget Template for Outcome 3 required
Complete Budget Table required
Design projects must address coastal flooding/erosion or stormwater-related rainfall flooding
Projects must achieve at least one of the specified outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register on Grants Gateway Portal with username/password for portal access; submit proposal through Grants Gateway Outcome 3 portal online only. Contact Nicole Carlozo to discuss project ideas and arrange site visits. Technical assistance available through November 30, 2025. Proposals are reviewed and selected based on eligibility criteria including habitat enhancement, climate change impact reduction, community-wide benefits, and incorporation of climate change data. Review period January-March 2026; project selection April-May 2026; notification May-July 2026. Required attachments include: transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive, landowner agreements for private land projects, appendix for sea level rise estimate if applicable, letter of local government support for non-profit applicants, current designs if applicable, communication and engagement strategy using template from Grants Gateway site, photographs of site conditions and flooding impacts, and complete budget table using template from Grants Gateway website. Competitive projects demonstrate readiness to proceed, support BIPOC and marginalized communities, document critical infrastructure benefits, partner with local government, restore public lands, demonstrate community engagement, support technical innovations, and provide matching funds or cost savings. Applicants should consult current solicitations for specific phase funding availability and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program providing grant funding and technical assistance to eligible applicants for enhancing public health and livability of overburdened and underserved communities by implementing projects to preserve, create, and improve public greenspace. Established through legislation in 2023, funding and technical assistance increase access to green space in underserved and overburdened communities throughout Maryland through partnerships with community organizations and local groups. Eligible projects include community gardens, gathering spaces, woodlands, green networks with corridors, parks, trails, and urban farms. Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity, and projects must be operated and maintained for at least 15 years from completion. Funding comes from the state share of Program Open Space subject to annual budget actions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to 100% of project costs for reimbursable grant funding and technical assistance for project costs including land acquisition in fee simple or perpetual conservation easement, site clearing and development for public greenspace use, administrative costs (not to exceed 3% of grant amount), and program compliance costs for easement monitoring (not to exceed 1.5% of grant amount for acquisition). Eligible projects include community gardens, gathering spaces, woodlands, green networks with corridors, parks, trails, and urban farms. Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity. Projects must be operated and maintained for at least 15 years from completion. Funds cannot be used for maintenance or operating costs. Grant is reimbursable, requiring applicants to pay costs upfront before receiving reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted. Advanced payments may be considered case by case.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land Trusts, nongovernmental organizations, county governments, municipal governments, and community organizations serving overburdened and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition costs (fee simple or conservation easement), site clearing and development for community greenspace, related due diligence expenses such as appraisals and environmental assessments, administrative costs for project implementation, program compliance costs for easement monitoring, tree planting, habitat restoration projects, playground surfacing with environmental and health standards (≤90 ppm lead, no added PFAs), and preservation, creation, and improvement of public greenspace. Funds cannot be used for maintenance, operations expenses, or business ventures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability in Maryland. Projects must be located in census tracts designated as overburdened communities or underserved communities as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool or census tract data, or on properties adjacent to such communities if the applicant holds a conservation easement or owns the property in fee simple. Applicants must use the Greenspace Equity Qualifying Census Tracts map or MDEnviroScreen tool to verify eligibility. Focus on overburdened communities in Baltimore, Charles County, and Frederick areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants use the MDEnviroScreen tool or Greenspace Equity Qualifying Census Tracts map to determine whether a property is located in an overburdened or underserved community. Applicants then complete and submit the Greenspace Equity Program Grant Application and Project Agreement with all necessary attachments including evidence of support from local government and community members, collaborative partnerships, and cost estimates. Submit application form with supporting documentation identified on the Accompanying Document Checklist. Applications are evaluated based on program consistency, eligibility, applicant responses, geographic diversity, and evaluation criteria. Selected projects must undergo State Clearinghouse review and Maryland Board of Public Works approval before funds are encumbered. Funding is awarded through a competitive grant selection process. Grant is reimbursable; applicants pay costs upfront and request reimbursement. Partial reimbursements permitted. Advanced payments may be considered case by case.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to eligible non-profit, government, and land trust organizations to obtain independent appraisals in advance of submitting an acquisition application for the Greenspace Equity Program Grant. Funds help eligible applicants prepare property appraisals needed to apply for greenspace acquisition projects in overburdened and underserved communities. Competitive grants cover costs for up to two independent property appraisals. Applicants selected for appraisal funding must complete appraisals to submit an acquisition application in the FY 2028 Greenspace Equity Program Grant round.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program providing funding to cover costs of independent appraisals for property acquisition projects in overburdened and underserved communities. Up to $100,000 total funding available for this appraisal round. Funds cover up to 100% of independent appraisal costs. Eligible applicants may request funding for appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers that meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP). Appraisals must be completed in time to submit an FY 2028 acquisition application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and government organizations, including land trusts, county governments, and municipal governments, seeking to acquire land for public greenspace and enhance public health and livability in overburdened and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to pay for independent appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers of properties proposed for greenspace acquisition to enhance public health and livability in overburdened and underserved communities. Appraisals must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be located in overburdened or underserved communities as determined by the MDEnviroScreen tool. Properties adjacent to overburdened or underserved communities are also eligible when applicant holds conservation easement or owns fee simple.

Applicant must provide management and funding plan for property post-acquisition

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete and submit the FY 2027 Greenspace Equity Program Appraisal Funding Grant application and project agreement with all necessary accompanying documents to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov by the deadline. Use the MDEnviroScreen tool to determine if a property is located in an overburdened or underserved community. Applicants selected and approved for funding must procure and complete the independent appraisals meeting USPAP standards. Incomplete or late applications may not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal hunting permit program that collects harvest information from hunters of migratory game birds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals interested in hunting migratory game birds in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit allows hunters to harvest migratory game birds during designated seasons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through eRegulations website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between Maryland Forest Service, Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay, and the Maryland Forestry Foundation, this program provides participating landowners with a free tree planting project of an acre or more on open land they want to convert into forest, including supplies, labor, and at least 3 years of maintenance and technical advice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating landowners receive a free tree planting project of an acre or more on open land they want to convert into forest. The program provides tree seedlings, labor for installation, and at least 3 years of maintenance and technical advice. The landowner must maintain the newly planted forest for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with open land they want to convert into forest.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting projects on open land to establish new forests, including maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Have open land suitable for tree planting (one acre or more)
Agree to maintain the newly planted forest for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program to apply for a free tree planting project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to encourage physical activity in parks of western Maryland and Caroline County through partnerships between the Department of Natural Resources, local health departments, and healthcare providers. Healthcare providers refer patients to the program with prescriptions for increased physical activity and participation in state park programs to improve health outcomes and reduce chronic conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides physical activity programs and recreational opportunities at state parks for individuals referred by healthcare providers. Participants receive guidance on exercise regimes and new activities available in parks to help reduce chronic conditions such as obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and depression.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members referred by their healthcare providers who are looking to increase physical activity and improve their health through outdoor recreation in state parks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical activity and recreational programs offered at state parks to promote exercise and outdoor activity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in western Maryland at Rocky Gap, Herrington Manor, New Germany, and Deep Creek Lake state parks, and in Caroline County at Tuckahoe and Martinak state parks.
requirements_list: Referral from a participating healthcare provider
Clearance from healthcare provider that patient is physically able to increase physical activity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Patients are referred to the program by participating healthcare providers who prescribe participation in Healthy Parks Healthy People programs at nearby state parks.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program providing classroom learning opportunities about horseshoe crabs, a fascinating marine organism. The program includes various activities and learning modules for students to understand horseshoe crab ecology and biology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DNR provides educational programs and resources about horseshoe crabs for classroom use, including learning activities and materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and educators interested in learning about horseshoe crabs and marine resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Classroom education and hands-on learning activities about horseshoe crabs and their ecosystems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For involvement details, check the program page at https://dnr.maryland.gov/ccs/Pages/horseshoecrabs.aspx

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide training program that provides hunter safety education and certification for first-time hunters and others seeking to learn safe and responsible hunting practices. The program offers classroom-based courses, hybrid online-plus-in-person courses, and specialized advanced courses in bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, and tree-stand safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free classroom-based hunter safety education courses taught by certified volunteer instructors. Participants can choose between a multi-day fully in-person traditional course (free) or a hybrid option combining online training through Hunter-Ed.com (fee charged by provider) followed by a free one-day Field Day Workshop. All courses cover firearm equipment, shooting skills, tree-stand safety, hunting skills, ethics, wildlife conservation, and survival skills. Students must pass a 50-question test (80% to pass) and demonstrate safe firearm handling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone wishing to hunt in Maryland, including first-time hunters, youth, adults, non-residents, and persons disqualified from firearm possession who wish to hunt using non-firearm methods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunter safety and competency certification required to purchase a Maryland hunting license for the first time. The certification satisfies state requirements and is accepted nationwide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Training teams are organized throughout the state and schedule classes independently.
requirements_list: Persons under 13 must attend fully in-person classroom course
Persons 13 and older may choose hybrid (online plus Field Day Workshop) option
Must successfully complete training requirements
Must pass 50-question test with 80% passing score
Must demonstrate safe firearm handling to instructor
Must demonstrate ability to safely carry firearm and navigate obstacles on hunter safety trail walk
Must participate in live-fire range event (some classes may have waivers)
Must obtain a free DNR ID number prior to hunting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a class through the registration website. For traditional classroom courses, register through register-ed.com. For hybrid courses, complete online training through Hunter-Ed.com first, then register for Field Day Workshop. Classes are posted as scheduled and fill quickly. Contact Chief Instructor for specific class details or to request accommodations.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Modification for Reforestation and Timber Stand Improvement
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a financial incentive for forest landowners to manage their forest land by allowing them to deduct the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices from their Maryland state income tax liability. Applicants must own or lease between 3 to 1,000 acres of forest land capable of growing more than 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year, available for the primary purpose of growing and harvesting trees. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years and are subject to periodic inspection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants may deduct the cost of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices (less any cost-share assistance received through other programs such as WIP or EQIP) from their Maryland state income tax liability. Eligible costs include labor, machinery, chemicals, seeds, seedlings, and consultant fees. Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years from final certification and are subject to three inspections at 5-year intervals. If practices are not maintained, the tax savings must be repaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest owners and lessees in Maryland who own or lease between 3 to 1,000 acres of commercial forestland capable of growing more than 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year, available for the primary purpose of growing and harvesting trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation and timber stand improvement practices on commercial forestland between 3 to 1,000 acres, including labor, machinery, chemicals, seeds, seedlings, and consultant fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Participants must own or lease commercial forestland in Maryland and be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must own or lease between 3 to 1,000 acres of commercial forestland
Forest land must be capable of growing more than 20 cubic feet of wood per acre per year
Land must be available for the primary purpose of growing and harvesting trees
Christmas tree and ornamental tree operations are not eligible
Only forest management practices installed on 3 to 1,000 acres may receive the tax modification in any one year
Practices must remain in effect for at least 15 years from final certification
Minimum 400 healthy sprouts/seedlings per acre for reforestation
Three inspections at 5-year intervals will occur
Must obtain certification by Maryland-licensed professional forester
Completion of DNR Form 393 required
Documentation of total forest acreage owned in Maryland
Documentation of property location and county
Detailed accounting of practice costs and cost-share assistance received
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain DNR Form 393 from local DNR Forest Service office or print original. Complete form with taxpayer and property information. Obtain professional forester certification and signature with professional seal. Submit four copies: one with Maryland income tax return, one retained by taxpayer, one retained by certifying forester, and one to Forest Stewardship Supervisor.

structured_extraction.program_description: In partnership with the University of Maryland's Maryland Industrial Partnership Program (MIPS) and the Environmental Protection Agency, the State funds research and development projects and seed capital initiatives focused on developing innovative technologies that reduce nutrient and sediment pollution, restore the Chesapeake Bay, mitigate carbon dioxide emissions, and provide other environmental solutions. The program supports students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System in developing innovative technologies to address non-point source nutrients and sediment pollution, and provides seed capital to Maryland companies to commercialize new technologies for bay restoration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides up to $1,000,000 annually in support. Grants ($500,000 available per year) ranging from $30,000 to $100,000 support research and development projects focused on developing pollution-reduction technologies, Chesapeake Bay restoration, carbon emissions mitigation, and other environmental solutions. Equity investments ($500,000 available per year) provide seed capital and commercialization support for technologies developed by Maryland companies. Both components include technical assistance for technology development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based companies, students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System, and environmental entrepreneurs interested in developing technologies for Chesapeake Bay restoration and environmental solutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology development and innovation, research and development partnerships, demonstration-scale projects, reducing nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment from non-point sources, supporting development of successful Maryland businesses, and creating and retaining green jobs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based applicants only. The Research and Development fund is for personnel within the University of Maryland System. The Seed Capital fund is for any company based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a student, faculty member, or staff member from the University of Maryland System for the Research and Development fund
Must be a Maryland-based company for the Seed Capital Fund
Projects must focus on reducing non-point source pollution or supporting Bay restoration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Sarah Lane at 410-260-8788 or sarah.lane@maryland.gov for general questions. For specific information on the Research and Development fund, contact Ronnie Gist at rgist@umd.edu. For information on the Seed Capital Fund, contact Scott Christensen at schris14@umd.edu. Visit the Maryland Industrial Partnership website at www.mips.umd.edu for additional application information and details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A land trust capacity, excellence and stewardship grant intended to increase land trust capacity, support programming and innovation and foster stronger, better connected land trusts that protect all natural resources. Grants of up to $10,000 are awarded to Maryland land trusts. All grants require a 100 percent match from the land trust of in-kind services and privately raised funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant of up to $10,000 to increase land trust capacity, support programming and innovation, and foster stronger, better connected land trusts that protect natural resources. Requires 100 percent match from land trust of in-kind services and privately raised funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland land trusts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increase land trust capacity, support community programming and innovation, foster stronger land trusts that protect natural resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland land trust
Must provide 100 percent match of in-kind services and privately raised funds

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program administered by the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), a unit of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, supporting volunteer-based nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, school groups, science and ecology clubs, and other nonprofit youth groups across Maryland. The program funds environmental conservation efforts, natural resource protection, capacity building, and community stewardship initiatives through multiple grant tracks including the Community Stewardship grant, Capacity Building for Land Trusts grant, Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grant, Bill James Environmental Grant (up to $1,000 for youth environmental education projects), and Aileen Hughes Grant for land trust leadership. With 40 consecutive years of grantmaking as of 2026, grants support environmental education, stewardship projects, litter removal, natural resource protection, and tree planting in urban and rural areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants for environmental projects through multiple tracks including Community Stewardship grants for environmental education, engagement, and greening projects; Capacity Building for Land Trusts grants supporting land trust capacity, community programming, and innovation; Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grants for reforestation and afforestation projects on agricultural land; Bill James Environmental Grant offering up to $1,000 for youth environmental education projects; and Aileen Hughes Grant for recognition of land trust individuals' leadership and innovation. Approximately $205,134 was awarded in 2026 across multiple grants. Applications are submitted online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website with the application portal opening on September 1 and awards announced on March 20, with funds distributed by April 15 of the following year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer-based nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, school groups, science and ecology clubs, other nonprofit youth groups, municipalities, schools, neighborhoods, civic associations, and local nonprofits engaged in environmental conservation and stewardship in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental education and stewardship projects, community cleanup initiatives, litter removal, natural resource protection, capacity building for land trusts, tree planting on agricultural lands, citizen stewardship activities, youth environmental education initiatives, and land conservation and stewardship.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in urban and rural areas across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be volunteer-based nonprofit group, community, land trust, school group, science and ecology club, or other nonprofit youth group
Eligible organizations include schools, nonprofit groups, land trusts, community organizations, and civic associations
For land trust partnerships: must co-hold conservation easements with MET, have executed and current Cooperative Agreement, and be actively working on conservation projects with MET
Organizations may need to meet accreditation standards or Terrafirma insurance requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit their application online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. The application portal opens on September 1. The deadline to apply is March 31 annually. The program announces award winners on March 20. Grantees receive funds by April 15 of the following year and must submit final reports after completing the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Keep Maryland Beautiful Program - Capacity Building Mini-Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Capacity building mini-grant program that provides funding to land trusts with cooperative agreements with Maryland Environmental Trust to support their operations and programming.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mini-grants provided through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program to support capacity building for land trusts with cooperative agreements with Maryland Environmental Trust.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit land trusts with cooperative agreements with Maryland Environmental Trust
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capacity building activities for land trust operations and programming
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to land trusts across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a local non-profit land trust
Must have a Cooperative Agreement with Maryland Environmental Trust
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Land Trust Assistance Manager for information on applying for mini-grants.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program supporting Maryland land trusts to build sustainable organizations by increasing organizational capacity, developing community programs and services, implementing Standards and Practices, and increasing public support for conservation and stewardship activities. Grants strengthen the operational and programmatic capacity of land trusts through targeted funding support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 awarded to Maryland land trusts to increase organizational capacity, develop community programs and services, implement Standards and Practices, and increase public support for conservation and stewardship activities. The program has provided 177 grants totaling over $545,000 to 45 Maryland land trusts, with local land trusts providing matching funds of more than $775,000. Grants strengthen the operational and programmatic capacity of land trusts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and regional land trusts operating in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To increase organizational capacity, develop community programs and services, implement Standards and Practices, and increase public support for conservation, stewardship, and related land trust activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to land trusts statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a registered land trust in Maryland
Focus on increasing organizational capacity, developing community programs, or implementing standards and practices
Focus on building sustainable land trusts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click the application link provided to apply through the Keep Maryland Beautiful grant portal at cbtrust.org (Chesapeake Bay Trust).

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) partners with local land trusts and conservation partners to meet mutual land conservation and stewardship goals. MET sometimes partners with governmental entities or larger regional/national land trusts to protect Maryland's treasured landscapes and natural resources. Services include cooperative agreements, easement co-holding arrangements, conservation project partnerships, information and referrals, monitoring resources, trainings, record keeping guidance, publications and model easement documents, access to the online Land Trust Toolbox, and capacity building mini-grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance including monitoring resources and trainings, record keeping guidance, publications and model easement documents, access to MET's online Land Trust Toolbox, and capacity building mini-grants through the Keep Maryland Beautiful Program. Cooperative agreements providing access to Maryland funding programs (Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, Land Trust Grant Fund, Program Open Space, Rural Legacy Program, Greenspace Equity Program), property tax exemptions and credits eligibility, joint conservation easement acquisitions and stewardship, and educational opportunities. Easement co-holding arrangements with independent authority to enforce terms. Access to Terrafirma conservation defense insurance and land trust accreditation support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and regional land trusts, conservation organizations, governmental entities, and national land trusts working with Maryland Environmental Trust
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land conservation, easement acquisitions, stewardship goals, monitoring of conservation easements, capacity building, and supporting easement programs and stewardship activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to land trusts and conservation partners across Maryland with service areas ranging from single towns or watersheds to multiple counties and geographic regions
requirements_list: Must be a charitable, tax-exempt organization under IRC Section 501(c)(3)
Must be a 'qualified organization' under IRC Section 170(h)(3)
Must adopt Land Trust Alliance's 2017 Standards and Practices
Must be in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must co-hold conservation easements, have executed and current Cooperative Agreement, or be actively working on conservation projects with MET
Land trusts may be incorporated in any state
New requests for Cooperative Agreement require review and approval by the Land Trust Outreach Committee and MET's Board of Trustees
Requests must be submitted at least 30 days in advance of a Land Trust Outreach Committee meeting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Maryland Environmental Trust to discuss participation or status of land trust's Cooperative Agreement with MET. New requests for Cooperative Agreement require submission to Land Trust Outreach Committee and MET Board of Trustees with at least 30 days advance notice. Meeting dates are posted online.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides interest-free loans to local land trusts. The loans help them buy land and conservation easements for preservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers interest-free loans to help with the purchase of conservation lands and easements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually Rolling applications. Deadlines are set by real estate settlement dates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local land trusts and individuals who want to purchase conservation lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase conservation lands and easements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Land and Water Conservation Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) is a federal funding program that provides grants to Maryland for land acquisition and development or renovation of recreation facilities. The program provides 50/50 matching grants to state and local governments for purchasing and developing public outdoor recreational areas and facilities based on the state's approved Land Preservation and Recreation Plan. Funds support projects to improve outdoor recreation through the acquisition of land and development or renovation of recreation amenities. The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based grants with a maximum request of $3,000,000 (representing a $6,000,000 project when matched 1:1 with non-federal funds) and a minimum request of $50,000 (representing a $100,000 project). LWCF funding must be matched dollar-for-dollar with non-federal funds. Acceptable federal matching sources include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration, Program Open Space, and Community Parks and Playground grants. Funds are issued after project completion. Projects must be completed within 3 years of award date with possibility of 2-year extension. Federal grants are awarded to Maryland based on the state's Land Preservation and Recreation Plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government entities including state agencies, federally recognized tribes, counties, municipalities, and special districts for land conservation and public recreation purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition for conservation and park purposes and development or renovation of recreation amenities. The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland to all eligible government entities.
requirements_list: Must be a government entity (state agency, federally recognized tribe, county, municipality, or special district)
LWCF funding must be matched 1:1 with non-federal funds
Entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use
Projects must be completed within 3 years of award date (with possibility of 2-year extension)
Project must reflect policies and priorities of Maryland's current Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan
State's Land Preservation and Recreation Plan must be approved by the National Park Service to qualify for funding

Acceptable federal funding sources for matching include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration, Program Open Space, and Community Parks and Playground grants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: LWCF grants follow a 2-step application process. Step 1: Applicants submit projects to DNR for consideration during the Open Project Selection Process (OPSP) by June 24 at 5pm to molly.pickel@maryland.gov. Optional individual meetings are available May 1-29 to review application proposals. Step 2: Successful applicants are invited to prepare a full application for submission to the National Park Service. DNR will notify applicants by September 15 if they have been selected to submit a federal application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides management incentives to landowners who wish to create and protect habitat for Maryland's wildlife on their property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides incentive payments to landowners for implementing wildlife habitat management practices on their land.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and private landowners in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating and protecting wildlife habitat on private land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Landowner status
Willingness to create or protect wildlife habitat
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact regional Wildlife and Heritage Service offices for information on program enrollment and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program demonstrating the environmental, societal, and financial benefits of incorporating dredged material into shoreline restoration projects through living shoreline techniques.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and demonstration projects for living shoreline restoration incorporating dredged material.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and organizations in Maryland interested in shoreline restoration using living shorelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living shoreline restoration projects incorporating dredged material.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for local governments and certain nonprofit organizations funded through FY 2022 and FY 2023 capital budgets for park and recreation projects. The program supports both acquisition of land for new parks or additions to existing parks, and development/construction of indoor and outdoor park infrastructure. Funds are administered similarly to Program Open Space local grants for acquisition and development projects with an emphasis on public access. Projects must be accessible to the general public and cannot require memberships, exclude the public due to higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities. The matching requirement is waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to local governments and certain nonprofit organizations for park and recreation projects including both acquisition of land for new parks or additions to existing parks, and design, construction, and capital equipment of indoor and outdoor park infrastructure. Funds support acquisition costs (land, improvements, appraisals, title work, surveys) and development costs (design, construction, capital equipment). Reimbursement-based funding. The matching requirement is waived. No funds shall be used for projects that are inaccessible to the general public, require memberships, exclude the public because of higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and certain nonprofit organizations for park and recreation projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition for parks and playgrounds; park and recreation projects including design, construction, and capital equipment; incidental costs such as appraisals, title work, surveys, legal fees, and settlement fees. Projects must be accessible to the general public without membership requirements or exclusionary use fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local governments and certain nonprofit organizations throughout Maryland; Priority Funding Areas noted as relevant consideration; projects may have additional requirements if located within Coast Smart Climate Ready Action Boundaries
requirements_list: Projects must be accessible to the general public
Projects cannot require memberships
Projects cannot exclude the public because of higher use fees
Projects cannot include residential or elaborate lodging facilities
Matching requirement is waived
Must align with County's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP)
For acquisition projects: two licensed real estate appraisals required
For acquisition projects: title must be held in fee simple or alternative description provided
For acquisition projects: deed with covenant protecting land from conversion per Natural Resources Article §5-906(e)(7) and (8)

For development projects $500,000+ within Coast Smart Climate Ready Action Boundaries that include structures: must meet Coast Smart Siting and Design Criteria and complete Coast Smart Project Screening Form
Itemized detailed cost estimate required
Must comply with all applicable Local, State, and Federal statutes and regulations
Maryland Board of Public Works approval required for acquisition projects
Local government procurement procedures must be followed
Evidence of title required for each parcel
Settlement sheet required for each parcel
For acquisition projects: canceled checks required for land purchases and incidental costs
Support documents must be retained for three years after final reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments and certain nonprofit organizations submit acquisition or development project applications. For acquisition projects: submit completed LPPI Acquisition Project Application and Project Agreement form along with LPPI Funding Authorization Form and supporting documentation including two appraisals and evidence of title. For development projects: submit completed LPPI Development Project Application and Project Agreement form with itemized cost estimate, project description, location details, funding sources breakdown, and development schedule. Applications are reviewed by DNR and presented to Maryland Board of Public Works for approval. Reimbursement requests are submitted separately with invoices, cost summaries, and supporting documentation to county program administrator.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that allows Virginia-licensed charter boat operators to provide fishing guide services in Maryland tidal waters, specifically the Chesapeake Bay. The permit is issued to Virginia charter boat licensees who can document fishing activity from 2001 and 2002.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A nontransferable permit issued at no charge that allows a Virginia-licensed charter boat operator to conduct charter fishing trips in Maryland tidal waters without needing a Maryland commercial fishing guide license. The permit is valid only for vessels originating charter fishing trips from Virginia tidal waters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Virginia-licensed charter boat operators who want to offer fishing guide services in Maryland waters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit authorizes provision of fishing guide services in Maryland tidal waters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Valid only for charter fishing trips originating from Virginia tidal waters and operating in Chesapeake Bay Maryland tidal waters
requirements_list: Must be licensed by Virginia to operate a charter boat in Virginia jurisdictional tidal waters
Must provide documentation of fishing activity for 2001 and 2002 based on Virginia Marine Resources Commission licensing and reporting requirements
Must submit completed application form
Must provide proof of Virginia Charter Boat licensee status in 2001 and 2002
Must provide copy of current Coast Guard license
Must provide copy of current Virginia Charter Boat license
Must possess all appropriate federal and state licenses and the required permit when operating a charter boat
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application form (Fishing Guide Reciprocity Application) along with proof of Virginia Charter Boat licensee status in 2001 and 2002, a copy of your current Coast Guard license, and a copy of your current Virginia Charter Boat license. Allow at least one week for processing. Applications cannot be processed at licensing service centers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary land protection program that allows landowners to protect their property through a Deed of Conservation Easement, a legal agreement that restricts future development while allowing the landowner to retain ownership, live on the property, farm it, and pass it to heirs. The program protects natural areas, farmland, forest, historic property, scenic lands, and exceptional urban properties. The easement is recorded in county land records and applies to all future owners. Maryland Environmental Trust provides long-term monitoring and permanent legal protection of the property. MET also partners with local land trusts, governmental entities, and regional/national land trusts to co-hold conservation easements and meet mutual land conservation and stewardship goals. Offers full gifts (no money changes hands) or partial gifts (bargain sales where landowner receives cash for part of easement value and makes charitable contribution of balance).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who donate a conservation easement may be eligible for: a federal income tax deduction for the appraised value of the easement as a charitable gift (up to 50% of adjusted gross income for 16 years; up to 100% for farming/ranching/forestry income); a Maryland state income tax credit (up to $5,000 per year for up to 15 years, maximum $80,000 total); lower estate and inheritance taxes due to reduced development potential; and a Maryland property tax credit (no property tax on unimproved land for 15 years from donation date). The program provides long-term monitoring and permanent legal protection of the property. Landowners retain ownership and may continue living on, farming, or selling the property. Form 8283, Required Statement, and appraisal must be submitted no less than 10 working days before tax return is due. MET also co-holds conservation easements with partner organizations and land trusts, establishing cooperative agreements that outline organizational relationships and support active conservation projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Form 8283, Required Statement, and appraisal must be submitted no less than 10 working days before tax return is due (for federal tax deduction); temporary commercial event requests must be submitted 60 days prior to planned event
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners with properties containing significant agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values, and exceptional urban properties, especially those providing public access. Also includes local land trusts, governmental entities, and conservation organizations seeking to partner on land conservation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protect and permanently restrict future development of land while maintaining current use for farming, forestry, residence, or other permitted activities defined in the easement agreement. The program does not provide direct funding; tax benefits and property tax exemptions are available to participating landowners. Properties may generate income through ecosystem services marketing including forest/wetland mitigation and conservation banking if 5+ acres. Ecological stewardship measures (ESM) and temporary commercial activities (festivals, weddings, agritourism events) are permitted under specified conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, from the forested mountains of Garrett County to the shores of the Chesapeake Bay. Coverage includes Central Region (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County), Eastern Region (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Southern Region (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, St. Mary's), and Western Region (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Washington). Applies to both rural and urban settings.
requirements_list: Property must contain significant rural agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values, or be an exceptional urban property
Properties are accepted on a case-by-case basis
Landowner must agree to voluntarily protect the land with a Deed of Conservation Easement and enter a permanent legal agreement restricting future uses
Landowner must work with Maryland Environmental Trust to establish easement terms, potentially with land trust partners
A qualified appraiser must establish the value of the easement for tax benefit calculations
Verification of property ownership required
Management plans (forest, soil, or wildlife) if available
Copies of any mortgages or deeds of trust and subordination agreements from lenders
Corporate/organizational documents if entity owns property
Tax and legal advisor consultation recommended
Qualified appraisal required following 26 C.F.R. § 1.170A-13 and § 1.170A-14 and Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h)
Appraisal must be signed by qualified appraiser (IRS-qualified and USPAP-compliant) before MET involvement
Landowner must complete IRS Form 8283 with all required information
Appraisal must accurately reflect easement terms, restrictions, and prohibitions
Easement must demonstrate donative intent (not regulatory requirement, contract condition, or quid pro quo)
Property owners must warrant no knowledge of hazardous waste violations
Exhaustive list of existing structures required (Exhibit C)
Baseline Documentation Report required with Exhibits A-G
Written approval required from Grantees for specified reserved rights and activities
Property subject to inspection and monitoring by Grantees
Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws required
Rural properties generally require minimum 25 acres (with exceptions); 5+ acres minimum for ecosystem services marketing eligibility
Perpetual easements preferred; term easements only in unusual circumstances
Board of Trustees approval required; Maryland Board of Public Works approval if required
No new buildings permitted (structures allowed with limitations)
Consistency with local comprehensive plans and state land protection objectives
Soil conservation district standards for agricultural best management practices must be followed
Forest Stewardship Plan required within one year if active forest management
Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan required within one year
Maintenance of 100-foot buffer along waterbodies
For temporary commercial events: 60-day advance written request with sketch/photo of location and post-event inspection
Mineral rights must be intact, leased, or severed with appropriate documentation and restrictions; surface mining restrictions apply for federal tax deduction eligibility
Notice of ownership changes to grantees required
Clustering of dwelling units near existing structures required when permitted
Minimum lot size requirements for subdivisions of primary dwelling units
Processing typically requires three or more months from first contact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Landowner considers long-term plans and goals for protecting the property. 2. Contact the Conservation Easement Program Team or county easement planner to determine if the program matches goals and if property is eligible. 3. Property visit and evaluation by MET staff. 4. Work with Maryland Environmental Trust and potentially land trust partners through the easement process to negotiate terms and research property. 5. MET drafts easement deed. 6. Legal review by all parties. 7. Landowner obtains appraisal by qualified appraiser and secures lender subordination agreements if applicable. 8. All parties (including co-grantees if applicable) sign the agreement. 9. Board of Trustees and Board of Public Works approval obtained. 10. Easement recorded in county land records with Circuit Court clerk. 11. Maryland Environmental Trust provides long-term monitoring and permanent legal protection. 12. Delivery of executed documents to landowner.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants of up to $2,000 awarded to nonprofit groups or communities for an ongoing project or activity that has demonstrated success in solving an environmental issue.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 for ongoing environmental projects with demonstrated success
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit groups and communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Ongoing projects or activities addressing environmental issues
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Project or activity must have demonstrated success in solving an environmental issue

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides reimbursement grants to marinas for the purchase, installation, operations, maintenance, upgrades, and replacement of marine sewage pumpout facilities. These systems allow boaters to properly dispose of sewage from boat holding tanks and portable toilet waste, helping protect Maryland waters. Funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act (Sport Fish Restoration and Boating Trust Fund) and 25% by the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund, the program reimburses marinas up to $20,000 for new pumpout installations and up to $18,000 for upgrades or replacements of existing systems. Maryland law requires new and expanding marinas with more than 10 slips and all marinas with 50 or more slips berthing boats over 22 feet to have a pumpout facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $20,000 for new pumpout installations and up to $18,000 for upgrades or replacements of existing systems. Funding covers equipment purchase, installation labor (contractor or approved in-house labor), local permits, and associated equipment and materials. Materials must comply with Build America, Buy America regulations. The program is funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act (Sport Fish Restoration and Boating Trust Fund) and 25% by the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund. Applicants must pay for equipment upfront and can submit paperwork for immediate partial reimbursement on equipment costs. Final reimbursement payments are made after final inspection. County permit fees for first-time installations are reimbursable. Grants available for up to one year after approval date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marina owners and operators in Maryland seeking to install new or replace existing pumpout facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout equipment and facilities. Equipment must pump out boat holding tanks and portable toilet waste. Installation labor (contractor or in-house). Local permits and associated materials. Does not cover additional slips or on-shore facilities. Must comply with Build America, Buy America regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all marinas in Maryland waters.
