structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Download and complete the DNR Maryland Pumpout Grant Application form. Step 2: Submit completed application with a project proposal including descriptions, equipment prices, at least two or three competitive installation bids, and installation location drawing. Step 3: Complete Part I of the Coordinated Environmental Review Form; DNR will coordinate with local health department and Maryland Department of the Environment for Parts II and III. Obtain all required local permits and submit to DNR. Step 4: Complete the Watershed and Climate Services Risk Assessment Form. Step 5: Obtain MDE approval before installation and Health Department approval for plans and specifications. Step 6: Once all approvals and permits are in hand, DNR will approve the application and issue an approval letter. Proceed with purchase and installation according to the approved proposal and notify DNR of project completion. Step 7: Submit the Pumpout Installation Reimbursement Invoice with receipts, proof of payment, paid invoices, cancelled checks, and a current-year W-9 form. Step 8: DNR conducts final inspection and processes reimbursement payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Abandoned Boat and Debris Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides reimbursable grants and expertise to assist authorized public agencies in the removal of abandoned boats and hazardous debris from state waters. The program supports clean, safe, and enjoyable recreational boating on Maryland waterways. Abandoned boats and debris pose hazards to navigation and the environment. Funds are generated from the Waterway Improvement Fund, which is created from a 5% excise tax paid to the State when a boat is purchased and titled in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are 100% reimbursable for up to $25,000 for abandoned vessels and debris removal. Reimbursement is contingent upon compliance with all terms and conditions of the grant. Applications are accepted in July and funds are obligated immediately upon approval. Applicants must submit the application form along with required documentation. After removal work is completed, a reimbursement form must be submitted to receive reimbursement. Reimbursable costs include contractor services, materials and supplies, equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Authorized public entities in Maryland such as local governments and municipalities with ownership, management, or jurisdiction over aquatic lands where the vessel or hazardous debris is located.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Removal and disposal of abandoned boats and hazardous debris from state waters. Debris that poses a hazard to navigation or limits access to a public boating access facility or shipping channel is eligible for removal. Reimbursable expenses include contractor costs, materials and supplies, equipment rental, and in-house labor and equipment costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State waters of Maryland. Only authorized public entities in Maryland with ownership, management, or jurisdiction over the aquatic lands where the vessel or hazardous debris is located may apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an authorized public agency in Maryland (local government, municipality, etc.) with ownership, management or jurisdiction over aquatic lands where the vessel or debris is located
Abandoned boats must be proven to be abandoned in accordance with Natural Resources Article §8-721
Debris must pose a hazard to navigation or limit access to a public boating access facility or shipping channel
Project must involve removal of abandoned boats or hazardous debris from state waters
Reimbursement is contingent upon compliance with all terms and conditions of the grant
Invoices or requisitions for payment must be submitted
Copies of canceled checks or electronic fund transfer printouts required
Before and after photos of removal required
Proof of contractor selection via public bidding process required (unless applicant has existing blanket purchase order)
For abandoned vessels: proof of abandonment and compliance with Natural Resource Article §8-721 (NRP-419 Abandoned Boat Report, letter to registered owner, public notice)
Recipient must retain subcontractor contracts for three years after final reimbursement
Non-discrimination compliance required
Local procurement procedures must be followed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted in July. Authorized public entities submit the application form (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF format) along with required documentation. Funds are obligated immediately upon approval of the grant application. After removal work is completed, applicants submit a reimbursement form (available in MS Word or Adobe PDF format) with required supporting documentation to the Department of Natural Resources, Boating Services Unit. Allow one month for processing of reimbursement requests.

structured_extraction.program_description: Specialized hunter safety training courses provided by state certified instructors covering bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, and tree-stand safety. These advanced courses are fully in-person training events lasting 4 to 6 hours, designed to prepare hunters for advanced hunting techniques and certifications required by other states, counties, or municipalities for organized hunting events or special permits. Courses include classroom instruction covering hunting fundamentals, wildlife conservation, equipment, shot placement, safety practices, tree stand types, safety equipment like harnesses and fall arrest systems, suspension trauma, fall recovery, and manufacturer guidelines, plus field exercises and supervised range sessions with proficiency testing. Bow Hunter Course includes distance estimation, game recovery, tree stand setup, and archery range proficiency. Muzzleloader Course covers loading techniques, ammunition, muzzleloader history and parts, range shooting, and safety. Tree Stand Safety Course includes harness demonstration, tree stand setup, fall recovery training, and suspension trauma awareness. Certification lasts a lifetime.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full in-person training courses lasting 4 to 6 hours, provided by state certified instructors in specialized hunting methods. Includes classroom sessions with multiple choice tests requiring an 80% passing score, field exercises demonstrating key concepts, and supervised range sessions with proficiency evaluation. Bow Hunter Course: distance estimation, game recovery, tree stand setup, 80% on 50-question test, minimum 3 hits on vital 3-D deer target on approved archery range. Muzzleloader Course: loading techniques, ammunition, muzzleloader history and parts, range shooting, minimum 3 shots fired, 80% on 25-question test (marksmanship not evaluated). Tree Stand Safety Course: harness demonstration, tree stand setup, fall recovery training, suspension trauma awareness, 80% on 25-question test. Students must demonstrate safe and mature behavior. Proper clothing required for outdoor sessions. Courses available at various locations throughout the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunters interested in specialized training in bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, or tree-stand safety, and those seeking certification for hunting opportunities in Maryland and other states or jurisdictions that require specialty certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advanced specialty training in specific hunting methods and safety practices including bow hunting, muzzleloader hunting, waterfowl hunting, and tree-stand safety. Certification lasts a lifetime. Training and certification in tree stand safety, fall prevention, and emergency response.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; specialty courses are scheduled independently by training teams and posted on the DNR website. May be required by other states or local jurisdictions for specific hunting activities.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate ability to behave in a mature and safe manner
Bow Hunter Course: minimum 3 hits on vital 3-D deer target on approved archery range during range session
Bow Hunter Course: 80% passing score on 50-question multiple choice test
Muzzleloader Course: minimum 3 shots fired from muzzleloading firearm
Muzzleloader Course: 80% passing score on 25-question multiple choice test
Tree Stand Safety Course: 80% passing score on 25-question multiple choice test
Proper clothing required for outdoor sessions
General safety violations may result in course failure
Must participate in demonstrations covering harness donning, tree stand setup, and fall recovery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a scheduled course through the Advanced Hunter Education Courses registration system on the DNR website or through the online registration link provided. Check class schedules on the DNR website and select desired specialty course. Attend classroom instruction, field exercises or demonstrations, and range sessions. Take written test with 80% passing score and demonstrate practical skills to instructors. Upon successful completion, receive course certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) Certification Program and Summer Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive training and certification program for individuals demonstrating competency in Maryland Biological Stream Survey sampling protocols and taxonomic standards. The program includes in-person training combining classroom, laboratory instruction, and field protocol demonstrations for stream sampling and biological assessment. Participants learn benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, fish sampling, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment protocols. Certifications are available in six areas: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Training is delivered through spring and summer sessions, with summer 2026 training scheduled for May 26-29, 2026 at Bowie State University. Certifications remain valid for 1-3 years depending on type, with mussel taxonomy remaining valid indefinitely with annual documentation. Certifications are required or requested by some Maryland counties and state agencies for conducting stream biomonitoring work and regulatory compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-person training with classroom, laboratory, and field instruction held at Bowie State University during spring and summer sessions. Participants may register for 1-2 days at $75 per day, or for 3 or more days for a total of $200. Summer 2026 training is four days (May 26-29, 2026). Certification in six areas available: benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leader, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Certifications are valid for 1-3 years depending on type (physical habitat assessment valid for 1 year; benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, laboratory processing, fish crew leader, and fish taxonomy valid for 3 years; mussel taxonomy valid indefinitely with annual documentation). Payment is made through the DNR Outdoor Store.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; registration is open now; summer 2026 training scheduled May 26-29, 2026; field audits must be scheduled before March 15 (benthic macroinvertebrate sampling) or June 15 (fish certifications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, including professionals, non-professionals, students, interns, seasonal employees, and volunteers, seeking training and certification in Maryland Biological Stream Survey protocols and taxonomic standards for stream sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate identification, fish identification, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment. Certifications are required or requested by some Maryland counties and state agencies for regulatory compliance or professional credentialing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification covers benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, benthic macroinvertebrate laboratory processing and subsampling, fish crew leadership, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and physical habitat assessment methodologies according to MBSS protocols. Certifications validate competency and are required or requested by some Maryland counties and state agencies for stream biomonitoring work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents and individuals. Spring and summer training sessions held at Bowie State University. Certifications recognized by Maryland counties and state agencies for stream monitoring compliance. Benthic macroinvertebrate sampling training conducted during spring index period. Fish sampling certifications qualified for Maryland stream sites. Mussel taxonomy certifications apply to rivers and streams with threatened and endangered mussel species in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an individual (only individuals can be certified, not organizations or firms)
Must attend MBSS spring and/or summer training sessions to be eligible for corresponding certifications
Must pass written tests to proceed with certification
Must pass field audits for sampling and taxonomy certifications
Must pass laboratory audit and written test for laboratory processing certification
Documentation of prior experience using regional mussel survey protocols required for mussel taxonomy certification

For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling Certification: attend annual spring training (3 seasons required); pass written test; complete one field audit in first year with BIBI score variance ≤1.0 from QC officer's sample
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing/Subsampling Certification: attend training; pass written test; complete laboratory audit
For Fish Crew Leader Certification: attend MBSS summer training annually (valid for 3 field seasons); pass written test; complete one field audit before June 15 in first year

For Fish Taxonomy Certification: score ≥90% (minimum 36/40) on written test; complete one field audit in first year identifying all fish from electrofishing pass(es) with ≥15 species richness and no more than one misidentification; 100% accurate species identification required; specimens under 30mm (TL) not counted; specimens with identification uncertainty must be preserved/vouchered; knowledge of state-listed and invasive/problematic fish species required

For Physical Habitat Assessment Certification: attend presentations and field demonstrations at MBSS summer training; pass written test; complete field audit; pay registration fee in advance via credit card (no walk-ins); valid for 1 year

For Mussel Taxonomy Certification: score ≥90% on mussel taxonomy test and 100% on threatened and endangered species identification test; conduct at least 20 surveys within last 10 years OR 10 surveys within last 5 years with two letters of reference; maintain minimum annual experience (handle 5 individuals of each threatened and endangered mussel species per year or 0.5 museum hours per species); no misidentification of non-listed species as threatened/endangered species
SFS certifications in EPT East and North American Chironomidae required for benthic macroinvertebrate taxonomy
Annual documentation of training or fieldwork for mussel taxonomy renewal; report continuing professional experience annually by February 15
Fish Taxonomist equipment requirements: formalin, voucher jars/containers, labels, digital camera, decontamination solution
Fish Taxonomist photo documentation of capture characteristics for identification required
Fish Taxonomist voucher labeling must include geographic coordinates, stream name, and collector information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online for training using the provided registration link or Google Form. For Physical Habitat Assessment, register through DNR online store and pay registration fee in advance via credit card. Attend MBSS spring and/or summer training sessions, pass written tests at training, and complete field or laboratory audits as required by certification type. Make payment through the DNR Outdoor Store at shopdnr.com. Upon successful completion, certified individuals are listed in the MBSS Registry of Certifications on the MBSS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary certification program that recognizes marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs committed to environmental stewardship and protecting Maryland's waterways from pollution by minimizing harmful chemicals, excess nutrients, and debris. The program promotes and celebrates voluntary adoption of measures to reduce pollution from marinas and recreational boats, recognizing designated Clean Marinas as environmentally-responsible businesses. The program provides technical assistance through introductory workshops, self-assessment tools, site visits with recommendations, and mentoring from certified operators. Participants pledge to implement best practices, undergo facility assessment and certification, and maintain Clean Marina status through annual affirmations and periodic reaffirmation visits. Certified facilities receive recognition including an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, an aluminum sign, a free online business card, news releases, and promotional advertisements in regional boating publications. The program also educates boaters about their role as stewards of waterways.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance through introductory workshops, self-assessment tools (Clean Marina Award Checklist and Guidebook), site visits by Clean Marina staff with recommendations, mentoring from certified Clean Marina operators, and confirmation visits to verify compliance. Certified marinas receive recognition including an Award Certificate signed by the Governor, a burgee and flag, an aluminum sign, a free online business card, news releases, and promotional advertisements in regional boating publications. The program also provides educational materials for boaters and resources to help operators minimize pollution and protect environmental resources. Certification recognizes facilities that implement environmental best management practices across vessel maintenance, petroleum control, emergency planning, sewage handling, waste management, marina management, stormwater management, and facility design and maintenance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within one year of pledge date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marina, boatyard, and yacht club operators in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental stewardship and pollution prevention at marine facilities. Marinas implement environmental improvements at their own expense; this is a technical assistance and certification program rather than a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to marinas, boatyards, and yacht clubs throughout Maryland statewide on Maryland waterways.
requirements_list: Sign the Clean Marina Pledge committing to keep Maryland's waterways free of harmful chemicals, excess nutrients, and debris
Assess facility using the Clean Marina Award Checklist and Maryland Clean Marina Guidebook

Implement pollution prevention practices for applicable activities including vessel maintenance and repair, petroleum storage and transfer, sewage disposal, waste management, stormwater runoff, and facilities management
Implement recommended changes to meet Award criteria
Schedule and pass a confirmation visit by Clean Marina staff and a certified Clean Marina operator
Meet or exceed minimum required scores across eight environmental management areas: Area 1 (85%), Area 2 (80%), Area 3 (80%), Area 4 (80%), Area 5 (85%), Area 6 (80%), Area 7 (75%), Area 8 (70%)
Comply with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations
Annually sign and return an Affirmation of Good Standing
Participate in reaffirmation meetings at least every third year
Apply to MDNR for certification within one year of pledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Learn about the program by attending an introductory workshop (held each winter), downloading documents from the web page, or contacting the Clean Marina office. Step 2: Sign the Clean Marina Pledge and send a photocopy to the office while displaying the original publicly. Step 3: Assess your facility using the Award Checklist and Guidebook, optionally requesting an informal site visit from Clean Marina staff who will provide recommendations. Step 4: Implement pollution prevention practices and recommended changes with support from Clean Marina staff or mentor operators. Step 5: Schedule a confirmation visit once you believe you meet minimum standards. Step 6: A Clean Marina staff member and a certified operator will verify compliance on the Award Checklist. Step 7: If standards are met, the Clean Marina advisory committee reviews the scores. Step 8: Upon approval, you receive your certification and awards. Step 9: Maintain status through annual Affirmations and periodic reaffirmation meetings.

structured_extraction.program_description: An award-winning AmeriCorps service program that engages young adults ages 17-25 in extensive natural resource management, park conservation, and community service projects across Maryland's state parks, public lands, classrooms, non-profit organizations, and watershed projects. Members work in crews on diverse projects including tree planting, trail maintenance, habitat restoration, invasive species removal, chainsaw operation, hemlock treatments, educational programming, Chesapeake Bay improvement, and environmental restoration. The program provides opportunities for service in the community and environment by preserving, protecting, enhancing, and restoring Maryland's natural resources through dedicated one-year service commitments. Members participate in paid work programs with comprehensive health care benefits (medical, prescription, dental, vision, and accidental death and dismemberment coverage through Cigna Healthcare with $175 deductible and 80% reimbursement on eligible expenses), low-cost park housing (average $150/month including utilities on a first-come, first-served basis with preference given to out-of-area members), uniforms (work shirts and sweatshirts with $200 boot reimbursement and $150 pant reimbursement), and professional skills development including First Aid, CPR/AED, wildland fire fighting certification, environmental education, chainsaw skills, trail maintenance, canoe trip leading, and Leave No Trace ethics. Members work Monday through Friday typically 7:00 a.m. to 3:30/4:30 p.m. from mid-September to late June. Upon completion, members receive a $6,000 completion award and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate to prepare for careers in natural resource conservation or park operations and management. Shadow opportunities are available from October through early June each year for those unsure if the program is right for them.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Members participate in AmeriCorps service positions with paid compensation and comprehensive benefits. Young adults ages 17-25 dedicate one year to service work focused on natural resource management, park conservation, and community service projects from mid-September to late June, working Monday through Friday typically 7:00 a.m. to 3:30/4:30 p.m. Health care benefits include medical, prescription, dental, vision, and accidental death and dismemberment coverage through Cigna Healthcare with a $175 deductible and 80% reimbursement on eligible expenses. The program provides a uniform consisting of work shirts and sweatshirts, a $200 boot reimbursement, and a $150 pant reimbursement. Low-cost state housing is available at an average cost of $150 per month including utilities on a first-come, first-served basis with preference given to out-of-area members, accommodating 3-5 members per state-owned house. Professional skills development training includes First Aid, CPR/AED, wildland fire fighting certification, environmental education, chainsaw skills, trail maintenance, canoe trip leading, Leave No Trace ethics, and Foundation for Search Operations training. Upon completion of the service year, members receive a $6,000 completion award and a Conservation Steward Apprenticeship Certificate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Interviews scheduled beginning in May; hiring target of August 19th; program start September 9th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 17-25 interested in environmental service, conservation, and natural resource management who want to develop professional skills and gain career experience in park and conservation fields. Applicants must have or be willing to acquire a high school diploma or GED and demonstrate dedication and commitment to service. Must be willing to work in all kinds of outdoor conditions, be a team player with a positive attitude, and have personal or public transportation to designated job sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service in natural resource management, park conservation, and community service projects. Program provides member compensation, comprehensive health care benefits, housing, uniforms, and equipment reimbursement as part of the service year experience while members engage in conservation work on public lands, in classrooms, with non-profit organizations, and on watershed and Bay tributary projects. Participants gain professional skills in conservation and park management through paid work experience and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Maryland Department of Natural Resources across state parks, forests, public lands, and the Chesapeake Bay region. Applicants can specify preferred geographical location(s) within Maryland for work placement. Specific crew locations vary across different regions of Maryland. Housing is available on a first-come, first-served basis with preference given to out-of-area members. Applicants must be Maryland residents at the time of application. Shadow opportunities are available from October through early June each year.

Must be willing to dedicate one year to service

Demonstration of dedication and commitment to service

Pass AI pre-screening questionnaire
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create account on BuildWithin portal, submit Service Year application, complete AI pre-screening questionnaire, submit MCC-specific application, and participate in virtual interview with MCC staff. Interviews are scheduled beginning in May, with hiring target by August 19th and program start September 9th. For detailed instructions, visit the MCC How to Apply page at https://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/pages/mcc.aspx. Crew supervisors assist with housing coordination and member placement. Shadow opportunities are available for those unsure if the program is right for them.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid five to six-week summer employment program where youth work on hands-on outdoor conservation and park maintenance projects in Maryland State Parks and other public lands. Participants work Monday-Thursday on conservation projects, with Fridays featuring enrichment days with environmental education and recreational activities. The program provides job and life skills training through outdoor experiential activities, career preparation opportunities, wages, stipends, daily meals (breakfast, snack, lunch, afternoon snack), transportation to and from park locations, work uniforms, instruction in hand tools, equipment operation, landscaping, basic construction, natural resources, and leadership skills. The program culminates in a graduation ceremony and includes professional networking with conservation professionals, preparing youth for future success in the workforce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A paid five to six-week summer program providing work experience, wages, and stipends for conservation and park maintenance work. Participants receive daily meals (breakfast, snack, lunch, afternoon snack), transportation to and from park locations, and work uniforms. Comprehensive job and life skills training includes instruction in hand tools and equipment operation, landscaping, basic construction, trail and bridge building, environmental restoration, outdoor recreation, park service careers, natural resources, and leadership development. Youth work Monday-Thursday on hands-on conservation projects in crews of 4-6 members, with Fridays designated as enrichment days featuring environmental education and recreational activities. Program culminates in an end-of-season camping trip and graduation ceremony.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disadvantaged youth ages 14-19 (particularly ages 15-17), including youth from Baltimore City and surrounding Maryland communities seeking summer employment and career skills development opportunities to work on outdoor conservation and park maintenance projects and gain hands-on experience in Maryland State Parks and public lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participant wages and stipends for summer conservation work; daily meals, transportation, and work uniforms; training in hand tools, equipment operation, landscaping, basic construction, trail and bridge building, environmental restoration, park service careers, natural resources, outdoor skills, and leadership development; trail building and maintenance; invasive species removal; native tree and plant planting; carpentry and construction projects; bridge and pier deconstruction/construction; facility improvements; habitat restoration and park improvements; camping and enrichment activities; conservation and maintenance of Maryland State Parks and other public lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland's State Parks and public lands managed by the Maryland Park Service, including parks such as Assateague State Park, Gunpowder Falls State Park, Patapsco Valley State Park, Seneca Creek State Park, Susquehanna State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, Rocky Gap State Park, Cunningham Falls State Park, Sandy Point State Park, and other Maryland State Parks and Complexes.
requirements_list: Work in partnership with community youth organizations
Work Monday-Thursday on conservation projects with Fridays as enrichment days
Five to six week summer program commitment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested youth should contact the program or community youth organizations for application information. Details are available on the main CJC program website. Applications are typically accepted annually for the summer program. Check the program website for updates on opportunities to join future iterations of the program. Contact: Fred Banks (Maryland Park Service Program Director) at 1-800-830-3974 or Frederick.Banks@Maryland.gov. Additional program managers include Anthony Peters (SCA Program Manager) and Tiffany Hergett (SCA Program Assistant) through the Student Conservation Association partnership.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal State Fire Assistance hazard mitigation grant program that provided funding to volunteer fire departments for the installation of dry fire hydrants in rural areas. Dry fire hydrants are non-pressurized pipe systems permanently installed in water sources such as lakes, streams, or ponds that allow firefighters to draft water for fire suppression operations. The program provided all-weather access to water for fire departments and operated as a multi-year statewide installation program from 2003 to 2007.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants paid for 100% of material and installation costs for dry hydrant installation. The program provided grant funding to volunteer fire departments for the installation of dry fire hydrants. From 2003 to 2007, the program installed 114 new dry hydrants across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer fire departments in rural areas of Maryland, emergency management centers, and local communities at wildfire risk
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of dry hydrants (materials and labor) in water sources such as lakes, streams, ponds, marinas, and creeks to provide reliable water sources for fire suppression
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties with focus on communities identified as at risk from wildfire per state fire assessment. Rural areas where pressurized fire hydrant systems are not available.
requirements_list: Location must be a water source (pond, creek, lake, marina, etc.)
Communities must be identified as at risk from wildfire
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sub-grants awarded to volunteer fire departments for dry hydrant installation at eligible locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Environmental Trust was formed in 1967 to conserve, improve, stimulate, and perpetuate Maryland's aesthetic, natural, scenic, and cultural environment. MET administers several programs focused on land conservation, monitoring and stewardship, supporting local land trusts, and promoting environmental appreciation and care through multiple initiatives including the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Environmental Trust offers land conservation programs, monitoring and stewardship services, assistance to local land trusts, and the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program to support environmental conservation and stewardship across Maryland. The organization provides technical assistance and grant funding to support open space conservation and environmental improvement activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, local land trusts, government agencies, and individuals working to conserve Maryland's natural and cultural environment and promote open space conservation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation of open space, environmental improvement, monitoring and stewardship activities, support for local land trust operations, and Keep Maryland Beautiful initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Chesapeake Bay Foundation initiative that provides free plant material, implementation, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. The program also offers funding for conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, and includes access to grazing mentors and technical assistance through the CBF-led Maryland Grazers Network and Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance. Participants also receive technical assistance related to farm economics and marketing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free plant material, implementation labor, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. Livestock producers can receive funding for conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, grazing infrastructure support, grazing mentors, and technical assistance related to farm economics and marketing through the Maryland Grazers Network and Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and livestock producers interested in streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, and rotational grazing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, pasture conversion for rotational grazing, grazing infrastructure, and grazing technical assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide and through the Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance regional network.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Rob Schnabel or visit m2balliance.org for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program run in partnership with Maryland that protects environmentally important forests from conversion to non-forest uses through the purchase of perpetual conservation easements from willing landowners. The program aims to prevent forest fragmentation and maintain viable working forests and natural benefits by protecting watershed and water quality, public recreation, scenic resources, cultural and historical values, traditional forest values, fish and wildlife habitat, endangered species habitat, and ecological values. The program provides up to 75 percent federal cost-share for the purchase of conservation easements to protect forest land and requires at least 25 percent non-federal match from state, local, NGO funds, or landowner donation. To be eligible, a property must be in a Forest Legacy Area and be at least 75 percent forested, with the remaining land in a compatible use such as agriculture. Conservation easements are legal agreements that restrict future activities on land to preserve its conservation values.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Federal Government supplies up to 75% of funding for purchasing conservation easements at market value. At least 25% of funding must come from State, Local, NGO funds or can be donated by the landowner. Funding supports the purchase of perpetual conservation easements from willing sellers. The state may purchase conservation easements or deed interests in forest property. Landowner retains ownership but restricts future use through conservation easements that may include development rights, public access rights, grazing rights, and farming rights. Eligible use of funds includes property appraisal, title search, forest management planning, and property surveys. Only private forest within a Forest Legacy Area is eligible, with at least 75% of the area under easement required to be forested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners and families with forest property in designated Forest Legacy Areas who are willing to sell development rights and seek to preserve forestland, particularly those facing development pressure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase conservation easements that restrict future activities on forest land to protect conservation values. Landowners can use funds received from the sale of conservation easements on private forest land. Eligible uses include property appraisal, title search, forest management planning, and property surveys. At least 75% of the easement area must be forested; the remaining 25% must be in compatible land use such as agriculture. Easements may convey development rights, public access rights, grazing rights, and farming rights.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program available only in areas identified as Forest Legacy Areas in Maryland's Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need. These are geographically defined areas with high economic and environmental values for Maryland's wildlife, wood products industry, water quality, and residents. Properties must be located in Maryland with identifiable town, assessor's plat/lot, and deed reference.
requirements_list: Completed application (4 copies: 1 original, 3 copies)
Property must be in a Forest Legacy Area
Property must be at least 75 percent forested
Remaining land must be in compatible use such as agriculture
Applicant must provide 25 percent non-federal match
Private forest ownership
Willing seller and willing buyer arrangement
Landowner must apply
Signed consent agreement
Map showing property location and relation to major roads, protected open space, and ecological features
Legal description and/or copy of deed
List of encumbrances and liens
Property plan-map with specific requirements (scale, north arrow, date, title, forested/non-forested areas, wetlands, structures)
Written forest management plan approved by State, updated every 15 years
Disclosure of financial need, health considerations, and family situations
Assessment of conversion threat to non-forest use
Consistency with local land use comprehensive plans
Property will be evaluated and ranked based on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners in Forest Legacy Areas who wish to sell development rights submit a completed application package with required documentation. Applications are evaluated and ranked annually based on forest importance, threat of development, strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives, and regional scoring criteria. Properties undergo inspection. Highest ranked applications enter the national ranking process for federal funding consideration. If funded, the project enters negotiation and acquisition phase for easement terms. If negotiations do not produce acceptable terms or federal funding is not received, landowners may apply again in future years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fully in-person, multi-day hunter safety training program providing comprehensive education and certification. The course covers firearm equipment and safety, shooting skills, tree-stand safety, hunting skills, primitive hunting equipment and techniques, ethical hunting practices, wildlife conservation, preparation and survival skills, and Maryland-specific hunting information. Students complete classroom instruction, a trail walk demonstration, a written test (50 questions, 80% pass required), and range training with live fire to earn a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license. The program is free and provided by state-certified instructors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free multi-day in-person hunter safety education and certification program provided by state-certified volunteer instructors. The classroom course lasts 12 to 16 hours spread over multiple days and includes classroom sessions, a 50-question multiple choice test (80% pass required), a trail walk evaluation demonstrating safe firearm handling and ethical decision-making, and a supervised range session with a minimum of two rounds of live fire. Upon successful completion, students receive a Certificate of Competency required to purchase a Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Classes scheduled throughout the year; classes fill quickly
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time hunters and anyone interested in hunter safety education in Maryland. Persons under age 13 must attend the fully in-person classroom course option and must have an adult 18+ accompany them.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunter safety and firearm competency training covering firearm equipment and safety, basic shooting skills, tree-stand safety, basic hunting skills, primitive hunting equipment and techniques, responsible and ethical hunting, preparation and survival skills, wildlife conservation, and Maryland-specific hunting preparation. Training leads to certification required for purchasing a first Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Classes are scheduled independently by volunteer training teams across the state at various training facilities and posted on the DNR website.
requirements_list: Pre-registration is required
Must demonstrate mature and safe behavior
Safe muzzle control is required (pointing a firearm at another person results in course failure)
General safety violations may result in course failure
Must score at least 80% on the 50-question multiple choice test
Must successfully complete the trail walk evaluation demonstrating safe firearm handling and decision-making
Must demonstrate ability to safely handle hunting firearms including proper carry techniques, identification of safe zones of fire, safe use of safety mechanisms, and proper loading and unloading
Must attend all classroom sessions, the trail walk, and the range session
Must complete range training with live fire (some facilities may waive this requirement)
Must make legal, safe and ethical decisions in hunting scenarios
Persons under 13 years old must have an adult 18+ accompany them
Must have DNR ID number prior to hunting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-register for a scheduled classroom course through the Hunter Education Classroom Course registration system. Classes are scheduled independently by certified training teams across the state and posted on the DNR website. Students should note any special instructions when registering and ensure they have proper clothing for outdoor sessions. Attend the multi-day in-person training session and complete all components including classroom instruction, written test, trail walk evaluation, and range session with live fire. Upon successful completion of all components, students receive a Certificate of Competency.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part hunter education program combining online training with an in-person field day workshop to obtain a Maryland Certificate of Competency required to purchase a hunting license. Students age 13 and older complete self-paced online instruction through approved vendors (Hunter-Ed.com, Ilearntohunt.com, Recademics.com, or Recademics.com for 1st Responders), pass a 50-question test with 80% score, then attend a one-day in-person Field Day Workshop provided by state-certified instructors. The field day includes classroom review, a second 50-question test, trail walk evaluation, and live-fire range session. Upon successful completion of both components, students receive a Certificate of Competency required for first Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hybrid hunter safety education combining online self-study through approved vendors (fee charged by provider) and a one-day in-person Field Day Workshop provided free by state-certified instructors. Students must pass a 50-question online exam with 80% score, receive a voucher valid for one year, then attend field day workshop including classroom instruction, second 50-question test (80% required), trail walk evaluation, and live-fire range session (or approved waiver). Upon successful completion of both components, students receive Maryland Hunter Education Certificate of Competency.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Vouchers from online provider valid for one year after issue date; Field Day Workshops scheduled throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 13 and older who wish to hunt in Maryland and need to obtain a Certificate of Competency to purchase a hunting license, particularly those interested in self-paced online learning combined with hands-on in-person training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hunter safety, firearm competency, tree stand safety, ethical hunting practices, and Maryland-specific hunting regulations training through combined online and field workshop components, leading to certification required for purchasing first Maryland hunting license.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Online component available anywhere; Field Day Workshops scheduled by volunteer training teams throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must be at least 13 years old
Must complete online training component through an approved vendor (Hunter-Ed.com, Ilearntohunt.com, Recademics.com, or Recademics.com for 1st Responders)
Must pass the online 50-question exam with 80% or higher score
Must receive a voucher from the online provider to register for the field day workshop
Voucher must be used within one year of issue date
Must attend and successfully complete the in-person field day workshop
Must pass the field day workshop 50-question exam with 80% or higher score
Must successfully complete the trail walk evaluation
Must successfully complete the range session with live-fire shooting (or approved waiver)
Must demonstrate safe and mature behavior throughout the course
Must demonstrate safe firearm handling and field competency to an instructor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select and enroll in one of the approved online training providers (Hunter-Ed.com, Ilearntohunt.com, Recademics.com, or Recademics.com for 1st Responders). Step 2: Complete the online training and pass the 50-question exam with 80% score. Step 3: Receive a voucher from the online provider. Step 4: Use the voucher to register for a field day workshop from the Maryland FDW Class Schedule within one year of voucher issue. Step 5: Attend the one-day field day workshop and complete all required components (classroom, test, trail walk, range session). Step 6: Upon successful completion of both components, receive the Maryland Certificate of Competency.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program training instructors to teach safe and responsible hunting practices to novice hunters. The program seeks to develop instructor teams to teach certified hunter education courses throughout the state, continuing Maryland's hunting heritage and ensuring first-time hunters have the knowledge, skills and attitude to be safe and responsible in the field.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteer instructors receive training through an instructor training program. Teams that commit to teaching a minimum of three classes a year will be provided with instructor training at their facility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with at least three years of hunting experience who have the ability to work with young people and desire to provide quality training to novice hunters. Sporting clubs are encouraged to develop instructor teams.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer service teaching hunter education courses to novice hunters covering safe and responsible hunting practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have three years of hunting experience
Ability to work with youngsters
Desire to provide quality training to hunters
Must complete an application
Must pass a background investigation
Must attend an instructor training program
Teams must commit to teaching a minimum of three classes per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective instructors must complete an application, pass a background investigation, and attend an instructor training program. For further information contact Maryland's Hunter Education Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A mandatory certification program for anyone who wants to trap furbearers (muskrat, beaver, raccoon, fox, opossum, mink, skunk, river otter, fisher, weasel, and coyote) in Maryland under a Furbearer Permit. The course teaches trapping laws, regulations, safety, ethics, techniques, and animal welfare practices. Training is provided by volunteer instructors to teach safe and legal trapping practices. This certification is required to obtain a Furbearer Permit and legally trap any furbearer in the state. The educational program covers trapper responsibilities, furbearer identification, skinning and pelt preparation, responsible trapping practices, selective trapping techniques, water and land sets, cable devices, trap line management, disease and parasite prevention, and firearm safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trapper education certification provided through two options: instructor-led classroom courses lasting 4 to 6 hours conducted by volunteer instructors, or a test-out option with a proctored 50-question multiple choice exam. Both options require completion of a trapper education workbook. Training materials (manual and workbook) are provided free of charge and can be downloaded as PDFs or ordered by mail at no cost. Classes are scheduled throughout the year statewide, and test-outs are available year-round. The curriculum covers Best Management Practices developed by wildlife biologists, trappers, and researchers, including furbearer management, trapping regulations, trap types, equipment, selective trapping techniques, water and land sets, cable devices, trap selectivity, safety procedures, pelt preparation, and responsible trapping ethics.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any person who wants to trap furbearers in Maryland. This is a mandatory requirement for anyone attempting to trap furbearers under a Furbearer Permit, effective August 1, 2007 (unless they held a permit during the 2006-2007 season). The program serves hunters, trappers, and outdoor users seeking education on responsible trapping practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trapper education and certification training required to legally trap furbearers in Maryland. Educational materials and instruction covering trapping principles, techniques, safety, fur handling, and pelt preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Classroom courses are scheduled independently by training teams throughout the state. Test-outs are available year-round.

Must present completed workbook to instructor at classroom course or proctor at test-out
Must score 80% or higher on the 50-question multiple choice test to pass

Proficiency with trap types (foothold, body-gripping, cable devices)
Understanding of safety procedures and disease prevention
Ethical conduct toward wildlife, landowners, and public
Proper pelt preparation and handling techniques
Responsible behavior toward other trappers and outdoor users
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a classroom course or test-out through the provided registration link or registration system. Complete the trapper education workbook. For classroom courses, attend the scheduled in-person training session and present your completed workbook. For test-out, contact the Safety Education Office at 410-643-8502 to schedule a proctored exam at a public location with a staff member. Pass the 50-question exam with 80% score. Upon successful completion, receive trapper certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program for children ages 2-17 that combines recreational opportunities and hands-on environmental education activities including hiking, games, crafts, fishing, biking, wildlife observation, plant and tree identification, water safety, campfire safety, and constellation study. Participants explore Maryland parks and natural areas, learn about conservation and stewardship, discover recreational opportunities, and celebrate their culture and heritage through play, learning, and service in the outdoors while being mentored by Park Rangers and natural resource professionals. The program is bilingual (English/Spanish) and available at over 70 Maryland State Parks statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational programming offered at Maryland State Parks in sessions lasting 1 to 1.5 hours each, typically totaling approximately 6 hours. Sessions are often offered over a series of six weekly sessions or combined into mini summer camps or school's out camps. Children are divided into age categories: Sprouts (ages 2-4), Park Pals (ages 3-6), Junior Rangers (ages 7-10 and 11-14), and Teen Rangers (ages 15-17). To earn Junior Ranger status, children must attend all sessions. Some parks offer self-guided options where participants complete six park programs and collect program leader initials to advance through progressive ranger levels. The program includes guided activities, educational materials, ranger-led programs, and park access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children ages 2-17 and families interested in environmental education, conservation, and outdoor recreation at Maryland State Parks
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational activities, outdoor exploration, environmental learning, conservation training, stewardship education, and recreational opportunities at state parks and natural areas. Park entrance fees may apply.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at over 70 Maryland State Parks including Deep Creek Lake State Park, New Germany State Park, Seneca Creek State Park (Gaithersburg, Montgomery County), Cypress Branch State Park, Janes Island State Park, Tuckahoe State Park (Millington, Queen Anne's County), and parks throughout Western Maryland, Central Maryland, and the Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Children must be within the specified age range for the session they attend
Children must attend all sessions in a series to earn Junior Ranger status
Adult supervision recommended or required for certain activities such as campfires
Park entrance fees may apply for some activities
Participants in self-guided programs must obtain Junior Ranger card and collect program leader initials at six park programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families contact the specific park where they wish to participate or register online via park website for self-guided options. Contact information for park coordinators is provided in the program schedule. Sessions are offered throughout the summer at various Maryland State Parks. Some sessions are self-guided while others follow a structured weekly schedule. For self-guided programs, participants obtain a Junior Ranger card, attend six park programs, collect program leader initials, and may submit a photo of completed card. Graduation or advancement to the next ranger level occurs upon completion of all sessions or collection of required initials. An end-of-summer family picnic celebration with park rangers, games, and nature activities is held for program completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A series of comprehensive training courses designed for logging professionals. The program covers best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety and OSHA requirements, and first aid and CPR training. Master Loggers must complete initial training (five core courses) and attend at least one continuing education course each year to maintain their designation. Program attendance is voluntary, and courses range from $20 to $40. Participants can include loggers, landowners, foresters, and others interested in forestry and timber harvesting practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training courses in five initial areas (best management practices for timber harvest design, logging aesthetics, forest management principles and wildlife management, field practicum, and logging safety/OSHA/first aid/CPR) plus annual continuing education courses. Courses range from $20 to $40. Upon completion of initial training, participants receive Master Logger endorsement and must attend at least one continuing education course annually to maintain status. Participants may be subject to periodic jobsite visits to maintain designation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Logging professionals, landowners, foresters, and all interested individuals. Program attendance is completely voluntary.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training covers forest management principles, forest ecology, proper harvest design and layout, erosion prevention, logging aesthetics, safety practices, wildlife management, life-saving skills, best management practices for environmental protection, and continuing education on topics such as log grading and marketing, environmental regulations, and timber estimation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The program maintains a Directory of Maryland Master Loggers that is updated biannually.
requirements_list: Complete five initial training courses
Completion of initial training in five core areas to become a Master Logger
Must attend at least one continuing education course each year to maintain Master Logger designation
May be subject to periodic job site visits to maintain designation
No prior experience required; attendance is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can contact the program coordinator to enroll in training courses. Courses are offered regularly throughout the year. Upon completion of the five initial training courses, participants receive Master Logger endorsement. To maintain the designation, Master Loggers must complete at least one continuing education course annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide training program run by the University of Maryland Extension and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that teaches interested people about natural history and ecology. Participants complete 60 hours of classroom instruction and field experience with experts, pass content knowledge assessments, complete a final project demonstrating interpretation skills, and then volunteer 40 hours annually to earn and maintain the title of Master Naturalist. Graduates participate in community science, teach classes, lead field trips, and support habitat restoration and public outreach. The curriculum focuses on Maryland natural history, flora and fauna identification, ecological principles, human-nature relationships, scientific methods, and teaching/interpretation skills. Training includes hands-on experience and advanced training in specialized topics is available. Topics covered include forestry management, birds, wetlands, Chesapeake Bay, ecology, plants, insects, mammals, soils, and interpretation/teaching.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 60 hours of in-depth classroom instruction and field experience led by experts. Classes are held Wednesdays 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. at MD DNR headquarters in Annapolis, with four Saturday field days for hands-on practice. Participants must pass content knowledge assessments throughout the program and complete a final project demonstrating interpretation skills on a topic of their choice. Advanced training in specialized topics is available. Upon certification, participants commit to 40 hours of annual volunteer work to maintain their Master Naturalist certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for spring 2026 class is now closed
structured_extraction.program_audience: General public of all age groups including youth, young adults, adults, and seniors who are interested in learning about Maryland's natural history and ecology and are willing to volunteer time to share nature education with others and assist in ecological research and community science efforts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in natural history, flora and fauna identification, ecological principles, human impacts on the landscape, scientific methodology, and teaching and interpretation skills for participation in community science, teaching, field trips, habitat restoration, and public outreach activities. Training covers forestry management, birds, wetlands, Chesapeake Bay, plants, insects, mammals, soils, and interpretation/teaching. The program covers training costs and participants gain knowledge to become certified naturalists through volunteer service in community environmental projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to residents of all Maryland counties. Training is currently offered at the MD DNR headquarters in Annapolis. Curriculum focuses on the natural history of Maryland's Coastal Plain and broader natural history topics. Additional training courses may be available through University of Maryland Extension in other locations.

Successfully complete 60 hours of classroom and field training
Pass content knowledge assessments throughout the program
Complete a final project demonstrating interpretation skills on a topic of choice
Pass a final exam
Commit to 40 hours of volunteer work in the first year with the hosting organization
Maintain 40 hours of annual volunteer work to retain certification
Pass background check with no criminal convictions more serious than parking/speeding offenses
Provide three non-family references with complete addresses
Have internet access or someone to assist with online materials
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed volunteer application form with personal information, experience, references, and background authorization. Program Facilitator contacts references and verifies information. For the spring 2026 class, registration is closed. Participants attend 60 hours of in-depth classroom instruction and field experience with experts, complete a final exam and project, and earn the title Master Naturalist upon successful completion. The program runs biennial (every even year). Those interested in future training can request to be placed on a waiting list for future training sessions. Additional information and application details are available through the University of Maryland Extension Master Naturalist Program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that pairs skilled veteran hunters with first-time or lapsed hunters to teach hunting skills, techniques, firearm safety, and species-specific hunting knowledge. The program includes technical lectures, range time, and ongoing mentorship through preferred communication methods (in-person, text, call, or email). The program encompasses specialized mentored hunting events such as the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt, a 2.5-day muzzleloader hunting event held in Accident, Maryland that provides orientation, facility tours, range time, meals, and equipment at no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mentorship pairing, technical lectures covering firearm safety and hunting techniques, species-specific hunting knowledge, and ongoing support through phone, email, text, or in-person meetings at no cost. Additional specialized events include multi-day hunting experiences with orientation, facility tours, range time, meals, and most equipment provided. Mentors and mentees are matched to work together throughout the program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 15, 2025 (for specific events; ongoing applications through learnhunting.org)
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time hunters, lapsed hunters (those who have not purchased a hunting license in the past two seasons), and youth of all ages interested in learning to hunt or participating in specialized hunting events.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Learning hunting techniques, firearm safety, species-specific hunting knowledge, muzzleloader hunting skills, facility tours, range practice, meals during events, and preparation to become an active hunter as a means of gathering food and as a lifestyle choice.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland via the learnhunting.org website administered in partnership with the International Hunter Education Association. Specialized events such as the National Deer Association Mentored Deer Hunt are held in specific locations including Accident, Maryland (Garrett County).
requirements_list: Must be a first-time hunter or lapsed hunter
Must complete Hunter Education course (required for mentored hunts)
Current hunting license or Apprentice License required for certain events
Participants are selected and paired with mentors
Must be willing to engage with mentor through preferred communication method
Space is limited and subject to application review for specialized events
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective mentees and mentors apply through the learnhunting.org website. For specialized events, applicants complete a registration form (Google Form link provided). Participants are selected and paired with available mentors or invited to events. Selected participants coordinate meetings and communication based on their preference (in-person, text, call, or email). Technical lectures and range time are provided as part of the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A required stamp for all migratory game bird hunters in Maryland. The stamp applies to hunters of coots, doves, rails, snipe, waterfowl, and woodcock, including persons not required to have a hunting license and holders of senior hunting licenses. Proceeds fund migratory game bird research and habitat enhancement on the state's public lands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $15.00 stamp required for migratory game bird hunting. Hunters must possess the printed receipt showing proof of purchase while hunting. The Harvest Information Program (HIP) permit is issued in conjunction with the stamp. Migratory game bird hunters are not required to sign and attach the stamp to their license.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who hunt migratory game birds in Maryland, including those not required to have a hunting license and senior hunting license holders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds fund migratory game bird research and habitat enhancement on the state's public lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Since 1974, stamp sales have provided more than $7 million for migratory game projects.
requirements_list: Must hunt migratory game birds (coots, doves, rails, snipe, waterfowl, or woodcock)
Must possess printed receipt showing proof of purchase while hunting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Purchase the stamp and retain the printed receipt as proof of purchase for presentation while hunting.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established through a Memorandum of Understanding between the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and US Wind, Inc. to mitigate impacts to commercial and charter fishers resulting from construction, operation, and decommissioning of the US Wind offshore wind energy project. The fund supports programs and projects ensuring sustained, long-term commercial fisheries landing infrastructure and service solutions, enabling safe and profitable fishing through initiatives supporting short- and long-term resilience for the fishing industry and local harbor areas. Funds address displacement and impacts from the US Wind Operations & Maintenance facility development at West Ocean City Harbor.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Resilience Fund consists of three components: (1) Facility Displacement Component providing financial support to displaced fishing facilities/operators including coastal zoning analysis, capital funds, bulkhead stabilization, business interruption funds, and shoreside services; (2) West Ocean City Harbor Maintenance Component supporting dredging, dock and shore stabilization; and (3) Programmatic Funds Component supporting gear development, business development/marketing, fishing vessel resilience fund, new entrant incentives, and charter fisher marketing support. The fund also includes the Navigational Enhancement and Training Program (NETP) providing equipment upgrades (up to $10,000 for commercial/inspected for-hire vessels; $5,000 for charter vessels) and training support (up to $1,000 per participant for training). Compensatory Mitigation Fund provides claims-based compensation for direct economic losses during three project periods: Construction Period ($1,546,864), Operations Period 5 years from Commercial Operation Date ($1,893,510), and Decommissioning Period ($2,014,757). Funding structure based on three displacement options: Option 1 (full displacement), Option 2 (partial displacement), and Option 3 (no displacement).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be made no later than two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period, extendable to five years if data unavailable or good cause shown. Funding released on the later of estimated timeline need or 30 days after financial investment decision (FID) closing.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Josh Kurtz; Katherine Charbonneau; Catherine McCall
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial fishing operations, charter/for-hire recreational fishing industry, individual fishers, registered Maryland commercial fishers, and related shoreside support businesses impacted by US Wind offshore wind energy development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and financial support for fish landing facilities, bulkhead stabilization, business interruption support, harbor maintenance and dredging, dock and shore stabilization, gear development, business development and marketing, fishing vessel resilience initiatives, new entrant incentives to the fishing industry, charter fisher marketing support, equipment upgrades, and training programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: West Ocean City Harbor area (specific parcels at 12929 and 12933 South Harbor Road), federal waters approximately 11.5 miles off the coast of Maryland (Lease Area OCS-A 0490), Atlantic coast of Delaware and Maryland, U.S. Exclusive Economic Zone, and Worcester County jurisdiction.

Located in or serving the West Ocean City area or impacted by US Wind offshore wind project
Registered Maryland commercial fisher or eligible third-party institution
Funding triggered by displacement of existing fishing operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participation is voluntary. The MOU is for the benefit of the fishing industry but participation is not mandatory. Claims for compensatory mitigation must be submitted within two calendar years after the end of the applicable Project Period (extendable to five years if data unavailable or good cause shown). Equipment and training funds available through voucher system. Specific application procedures and timeline details are available through the Regional Fund Administrator process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Natural Resources Police Cadet Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid training program for individuals between 18-20 years of age that provides hands-on experience in law enforcement through classroom and field training. Cadets learn about becoming a Maryland Natural Resources Police Officer and prepare for the police academy through training in boater and hunter safety courses, self-defense, specialized units, and other law enforcement skills. Upon completion, cadets enroll in the Maryland Natural Resources Police Academy to become certified police officers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid training program with annual salary between $36,093 and $55,376. Cadets participate in paid training including boater and hunter safety courses, self-defense, specialized units training, and classroom instruction. Benefits include annual leave (10-25 days per year depending on tenure), 6 personal days per year, 12 paid holidays plus election year holiday, 15 days of sick leave per year, military leave, comprehensive state health insurance (vision, prescription drug, dental, life, behavioral health), and enrollment in the Law Enforcement Officers Pension System (LEOPS) with lifetime retirement benefits at 50% of salary after 25 years of service or at age 50.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Men and women between 18-20 years of age interested in becoming Maryland Natural Resources Police Officers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and preparation for law enforcement careers in natural resources policing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

United States citizen or permanent legal resident who is an honorably discharged veteran with pending citizenship application
High school diploma, GED certificate/diploma, or college degree
Pass background check and comprehensive background investigation

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospect Day consists of three parts: (1) Initial Background Screening where applicants complete NRP 571 Initial Personal Information Sheet; (2) Functional Fitness Agility Test (FFAT) with no rest breaks between exercises, evaluating ability to pull/drag 150-pound dummy 15 feet, run up and down two flights of stairs, climb over 4-foot barrier, lift minimum 50 pounds onto 22-inch tabletop, and run 300 yards; (3) Law Enforcement Aptitude Battery (LEAB) written test. Following Prospect Day, applicants undergo comprehensive background investigation, polygraph examination, oral interview by hiring board, psychological examination, medical evaluation, and drug screening.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Natural Resources Police Reserve Officer Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer program that provides civic-minded volunteers with training and equipment to support the Maryland Natural Resources Police mission. This non-confrontational volunteer program is not designed to train citizens to be police officers. Reserve Officers perform non-law enforcement assignments including community outreach, education programs on boating and hunting safety, search and rescue operations, and vessel maintenance. Reserve Officers are not sworn law enforcement and do not have powers of arrest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reserve Officers have opportunities to volunteer in the following areas: Public Relations, Search & Rescue, Outreach Programs, Vehicle/Vessel Maintenance, Awareness & Education Programs, Courtesy Boat Inspections, Boating Safety, Office Administration, Hunting Safety, and Children's Programs. Volunteers receive training necessary to perform their duties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic-minded volunteers age 18 and older who are U.S. citizens, Maryland residents, with no felony convictions and willing to volunteer a minimum of 100 hours annually.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer service hours supporting non-law enforcement assignments such as public relations, search and rescue operations, outreach programs, vehicle and vessel maintenance, awareness and education programs, courtesy boat inspections, boating safety, office administration, hunting safety, and children's programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents statewide.
