U.S. Citizen
Maryland resident
No felony convictions or disqualifying arrests
No natural resources or other misdemeanor convictions within the last five years
Possess a valid driver's license and have a good driving record
No drug use except doctor-prescribed medications
Occupation or part-time employment must not conflict with the agency's mission, policies, and lawful mandate
Willing to and capable of performing a minimum of 100 hours of non-financially compensated service annually
Have a home telephone and/or a mobile cellular phone
Have access to the internet and electronic mail capability
Willing to submit to a background investigation including natural resources violation check, motor vehicle driving records check, fingerprint and criminal record check

Background investigation will be conducted including fingerprinting, criminal history check, employment history verification, and reference checks. Applicants may be required to attend an oral interview with the Regional Administrator or designee.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program supports equitable access to outdoor recreation for communities that have been historically underserved. It funds community-based projects that help Marylanders overcome social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to outdoor recreation, including distance and transportation, cost of activities and entry fees, equipment costs, lack of exposure to outdoor recreation, and feeling unwelcome. Funds support projects that create outdoor recreation opportunities, provide outdoor and environmental education and stewardship, build community capacity for long-term engagement with outdoor access, or connect outdoor recreation to physical, emotional, or community health benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants ranging from $2,500 to $7,500. No matching funds required, though leveraging other resources is encouraged. Approximately 5 awards are expected to be distributed. Funds may be used for program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals. Projects must be completed by September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, tribal entities, school districts, government agencies, and for-profit organizations with a mission aligned with outdoor equity that are based in Maryland, serving communities in Maryland, and hosting activities within Maryland. Focus on communities historically underrepresented in outdoor recreation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals related to outdoor recreation equity and access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland, serving communities within Maryland, and hosting the event, recreation, or activity within Maryland. The program serves all of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Tribal entity, school district, government agency, or for-profit organization with a mission aligned with outdoor equity
Must be based in Maryland, serving communities in Maryland
Must host the event, recreation, or activity within Maryland
Must demonstrate readiness to manage and complete a small-scale community project within one year
Project must be completed by September 30, 2026
Must complete a W-9 form with the State of Maryland to receive funds

Must address at least one focus area: creating outdoor recreation opportunities, outdoor and environmental education and stewardship, community capacity-building, or connecting outdoor recreation to health benefits
Final report must be submitted no later than October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application by completing a Google Form by June 30, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. The form requires: organization information and contact details, description of the community or population served, description of planned activities and goals, explanation of how work advances equity and access, community engagement approach, itemized budget with narrative, timeline with key milestones, evaluation plan for tracking success, and optional letters of support or collaboration. Applications are reviewed based on project alignment with focus areas, demonstrated need and community involvement, clear scope and goals, feasibility and budget clarity, and project outcomes and evaluation plan. Awardees must submit a final report by October 15, 2026 including project outcomes, community impact, participant demographics, and lessons learned.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Park Service Youth Group Camping and Day-Use Pass
structured_extraction.program_description: A biennial pass offered by the Maryland Park Service to non-commercial youth organizations that provides free day-use entry to Maryland state parks (excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day) and allows youth groups to camp in designated youth group areas at participating state parks and forests, subject to site availability. The pass is valid for two years and is not renewed. Group members must be between six and eighteen years old, with a minimum ratio of one adult supervisor for every five youth required (may be waived by facility manager). Reservation transaction fees and charges for special facilities such as shelters, boat concessions, and special events are not covered by the pass.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A biennial (two-year) pass that provides free day-use entry to Maryland state parks (excluding weekends and holidays from Memorial Day through Labor Day) and allows camping in designated youth group camping areas at participating parks and forests, subject to site availability and reservation requirements. A minimum ratio of one adult supervisor for every five youth is required (may be waived by facility manager). Group members must be between 6 and 18 years old. The pass is non-transferrable and must be presented upon arrival. Service charges for special facilities such as shelters, boat concessions, and special events are not covered by the pass.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free day-use entry to Maryland state parks and camping in designated youth group areas at participating parks and forests.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across all Maryland state parks and forests with designated youth group camping areas, including Eastern Region (Assateague State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, Tuckahoe State Park, Wye Island NRMA, Janes Island State Park, Sassafras NRMA), Central Region (Elk Neck State Park, Gunpowder Falls State Park, Patapsco Valley State Park), Southern Region (Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Newtowne Neck State Park, Sandy Point State Park, Smallwood State Park), and Western Region (Fort Frederick State Park, Greenbrier State Park, Green Ridge State Forest, Potomac-Garrett State Forest, Rocky Gap State Park, Swallow Falls State Park, Washington Monument).

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual pass that provides unlimited day-use entry for everyone in a vehicle (up to 10 people) to all Maryland State Parks and facilities, unlimited boat launching at all state park facilities, and a 10 percent discount on state-operated concession items and boat rentals. State resident first responders and law enforcement officers (including emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and similar emergency personnel) receive a $40 discount. The pass is valid for one full year from the date of purchase.

Pass provides unlimited day-use entry for vehicle occupants (up to 10 people), unlimited boat launching at all state park facilities, and 10 percent discount on state-operated concession items and boat rentals.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Property Tax Credit for Conservation Easement Land
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit granted for land on which a perpetual conservation easement has been donated to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The credit is effective for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following the easement donation. The program exempts unimproved and non-commercial portions of land from property taxes for 15 years from the date of donation. Credits generated from conservation easements also provide offsets against state income tax liability. After the 15-year credit period, unimproved land will be assessed at the highest agricultural rate. The credit does not apply to residential improvements or to a minimum of one acre around residential improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners who donate a perpetual conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust or Maryland Department of Natural Resources receive a property tax credit exempting unimproved and non-commercial land from property taxes for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following the easement donation. The tax credit is applied to 100% of the assessment on unimproved and non-commercial portions of property placed in easement, representing a direct offset against property tax liability (state, county, municipal corporation, and special district taxes) and generates credits against state income tax liability. County-level tax credits also vary by county in terms of value, duration, and eligibility requirements. After 15 years, unimproved land will be assessed at the highest agricultural rate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before October 1 annually to receive credit for that taxable year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland property owners with land subject to perpetual conservation easements who have donated or are interested in donating conservation easements to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit reduction applied to state, county, municipal corporation, and special district property taxes on unimproved and non-commercial portions of property placed in easement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland landowners only; statewide throughout Maryland. However, county-level tax credits vary by county. Ten counties offer county tax credits (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Calvert, Charles, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's), while 14 counties offer no county tax credit (Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Kent, Saint Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester). Application filed with County Office of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.

Attach a copy of the recorded Deed of Conservation Easement and Board of Public Works approval letter to the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state law that requires trees cleared or cut during construction projects using State funds to be replaced on an acre-for-acre basis. The law applies to construction activities resulting in 1 acre or more of forest clearing. Replacement must occur on public lands within two years or three growing seasons of project completion, with priority given to the same county or watershed. If on-site replacement is not feasible, the constructing agent can purchase credits from a forest mitigation bank or deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund to support tree planting by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The Reforestation Fund also finances forest health initiatives, emergency response, and pest damage recovery.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Construction projects clearing 1 or more acres of forest must mitigate forest impacts through one of three methods: (1) replant on an acre-for-acre basis on public lands within two years or three growing seasons, prioritizing the same county or watershed; (2) purchase credits from a forest mitigation bank if on-site replacement is not possible; or (3) deposit funds into the Reforestation Fund at a rate of ten cents per square foot or $4,356 per acre, which the Department uses to plant replacement trees, support forest health initiatives, and respond to forest health emergencies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to construction start; before any forest removal occurs; during initial design stages
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniel Coy, Urban & Community Forestry Supervisor
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies; private entities using State funding for construction projects; constructing agencies responsible for highway construction and other construction activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on public land in affected county or watershed; forest mitigation bank credits; prevention and response to forest health emergencies; replacement of trees destroyed by pest control treatments; forest health initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies statewide to all construction projects utilizing State funding and resulting in 1 or more acres of forest clearing. Priority for reforestation location: (1) construction site or project right-of-way; (2) public land in county and watershed where construction occurred; (3) public land in any county or watershed in the State; (4) forest mitigation bank credits in watershed where construction occurred. Regional offices serve: Central Region (Montgomery, Howard, Baltimore, Harford, Carroll, Cecil Counties); Eastern Region (Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester Counties); Southern Region (Anne Arundel, Prince George's, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's Counties); Western Region (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick Counties).

Forest clearing must result in 1 or more acres of forest removal
Submission of the project's construction plans showing forest areas to be removed and removal amounts
Completion of the Reforestation Site Review Form during initial design stages, prior to construction start

Replacement must be accomplished within two years or three growing seasons of project completion

Identification of estimated acres to be cleared and acres available for on-site replacement
Identification of off-site locations if on-site replacement is impossible

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the project's construction plans and completed Reforestation Site Review Form to the appropriate regional Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service office based on the project location. Submission must occur during initial design stages, prior to any forest removal. The DNR will complete a field review within 20 working days to verify acreage and identify suitable reforestation sites.

structured_extraction.program_description: A historic preservation program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that allows qualified individuals and non-profit organizations to restore, protect, and maintain historic buildings and properties located on Maryland public lands such as state parks. This public-private partnership grants curators lifetime tenancy rights in exchange for funding, maintaining, and interpreting historic properties at no cost to the State. Curators enter into agreements with the state to undertake restoration projects and receive lifetime residency rights in exchange for making significant initial improvements (minimum $150,000-$300,000), ongoing maintenance, and periodically sharing the property with the public. All improvements become state property upon completion. Curators become stewards of both historic and natural resources while living in restored historic properties that comply with the Secretary of Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides individuals and non-profit organizations with the opportunity to restore and reside in historic properties on public lands. Curators receive lifetime residency and tenancy rights in exchange for restoration and ongoing maintenance. Curators must invest a minimum of $150,000-$300,000 in initial improvements with restoration projects completed within five to seven years, and are responsible for ongoing maintenance, utilities, and applicable taxes. The state insures the structure against fire and flood and provides the property and oversight. Curators do not pay rent to the Department of Natural Resources. All improvements and permanent fixtures become state property upon completion. The program does not provide direct financial assistance but grants curators the right to occupy and restore designated properties. Selected curators receive a Right of Entry to conduct tests and stabilization work, and then enter into a Curatorship Agreement with the State.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: As houses are advertised for being in need of a Curator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and non-profit organizations interested in historic preservation who wish to restore, maintain, and share historic buildings and properties on Maryland state park land, and who are interested in becoming stewards of historic and natural resources. Applicants must be committed to historic preservation and have the skills, knowledge, interest, and financial means to restore historic properties. Maryland residents only.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration, rehabilitation, and maintenance of historic structures and associated outbuildings located on state parkland or natural resource areas, including structural repairs, systems upgrades (electrical, plumbing, heating), lead paint remediation, roof and siding repairs, window restoration, installation of smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, contract labor, and materials. Work must comply with the Secretary of Interior's Standards for Historic Preservation, current standard building codes, and include modern accommodations while preserving historic character. Curators must use funds of their own to restore and maintain the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Historic structures located throughout Maryland on state parkland and natural resource areas managed by the Department of Natural Resources. Properties are distributed across the state from Western Maryland mountain regions to Assateague Island. Nearly 50 curatorships in operation statewide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals and organizations should review the Program Policies, Frequently Asked Questions, and Preparing Proposals guidance. Applicants are encouraged to contact the Curator Program Manager before submitting. Submit a curatorship proposal including cover letter, resume(s), detailed restoration schedule with cost estimates, Personal Financial Statement form with comprehensive asset and liability disclosure, and planned restoration work to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Park Service. Complete Personal Financial Statement form disclosing all assets and liabilities with detailed descriptions in designated sections. Proposals are submitted electronically or by mail (not by fax). Proposals are scored by an interagency panel including the area manager, DNR regional engineer, Maryland Historical Trust representative, and Curator Program Manager. The initial review of proposals by the committee can take approximately three months. After a winning proposal is selected, the process from proposal to final approval by the Maryland Board of Public Works generally takes about six months. Selected applicants receive a Right of Entry to conduct tests or stabilization while the Curatorship Agreement is drafted. A Curatorship Agreement is required and must receive Board of Public Works approval. Once approved, the property must pass lead paint testing before the curator may take residence, and the Department may require inspections of electrical, plumbing, and septic systems. Department staff inspect the property regularly to monitor progress and ensure compliance with historic preservation standards and environmental impact laws.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Rural Legacy Program is a statewide land conservation program enacted in 1997 that protects agricultural, forestry, natural, cultural, and historic resources in designated Rural Legacy Areas through acquisition of conservation easements and fee simple purchases. The program provides grants to local governments and private land trusts to conserve large blocks of working rural lands and large, contiguous tracts of Maryland's most precious cultural and natural resource lands for future generations by protecting natural, cultural, agricultural, and forest land, preserving farmland, forests, wetlands, wildlife habitat, and historic sites. The program creates public-private partnerships between land trusts and local governments to protect working landscapes critical to Maryland's economy, environment and quality of life while enhancing natural resources and environmental protection. Rural Legacy Areas are delineated areas within counties that include both working farms and ecologically significant landscapes. The program encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas and competitively apply for funds to complement existing land conservation efforts or create new ones. Landowners who participate can sell or donate their development rights while retaining ownership and the ability to continue farming or raising livestock. The program uses an objective scoring approach to review and allocate its limited grant funds based on resource significance, development threats, historic and cultural value, economic importance, application quality, partnership strength, and matching funds. A major focus includes increased stream buffer protection through required 100 foot grass and/or forest buffers. Funds come from Maryland Program Open Space dollars and general obligation bonds from the state's capital budget, with county governments also able to contribute. Currently there are 35-41 Rural Legacy Areas throughout the state, with designated acreage exceeding 1.3 million acres total. The program focuses on protecting Maryland's best natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural areas and most significant rural landscapes vulnerable to sprawl development while supporting a sustainable land base for natural resource-based industries. Since 1997, it has awarded over $403.5 million. Conservation easements restrict property use to preserve conservation attributes through deed restrictions, allowing reserved rights for agricultural uses, forestry, dwelling units, commercial activities, and passive recreational uses while preserving conservation purposes. Easements allow continued agricultural operations, forestry management, and residential use within specified parameters. The program's model conservation easement restricts development and land uses to protect conservation values with permanent restrictions running with the land in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: RLP grants funds to local program sponsors (local governments and land trusts) to purchase conservation easements and fee simple interests in rural land, as well as to support the acquisition of agricultural land, forest land, open space, wetlands, wildlife habitat, and historic sites within designated Rural Legacy Areas throughout the state. The program purchases easements from willing landowners to protect rural areas vulnerable to sprawl development, with easement restrictions remaining effective in perpetuity. Development rights purchase programs offer easement offers ranging from $8,000 to $10,000 per acre with cash at settlement. Landowners who participate receive financial compensation for selling or donating their development rights. Local Sponsors must apply annually to receive funding to support land conservation efforts. Matching funds are required and considered in evaluation. The program uses an objective scoring approach to allocate its limited grant funds. Grants have included funding such as $3,127,000 to support land preservation projects that maintain rural character and agricultural heritage. Funds are encumbered after approval by the Board of Public Works. Funds come from Maryland Program Open Space dollars and general obligation bonds from the state's capital budget, with county governments also able to contribute. Approved applications result in a Grant Agreement that allows sponsors to proceed with individual acquisitions as defined in project agreements. Funding supports the purchase of fee-simple interests or easements on agricultural, forest, or water-resource lands with emphasis on stream buffer protection. FY 2025 funding totals $15,329,028. Conservation easements restrict industrial uses, require buffer maintenance for waterways, limit impervious surface to 2%, allow agricultural/forestry operations, permit limited dwelling units and structures, and preserve conservation attributes. Easement requirements include soil conservation and water quality plans, forest management plans, and riparian buffers, with sponsors encouraged to negotiate minimum 100-foot riparian buffers into easement terms. Incidental costs eligible for reimbursement include surveys, appraisals, title searches, legal fees, and settlement costs, with administrative costs up to 3% of grant amount and program compliance costs for easement monitoring up to 1.5% of easement purchase cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m.; January 15th for GIS data submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profit conservation organizations, and land trusts serving as sponsors for Rural Legacy Areas; farmers, landowners, agricultural and property owners seeking to preserve land and conserve working rural lands throughout Maryland; groups and sponsors interested in establishing new Rural Legacy Areas or managing established Rural Legacy Areas to preserve agricultural land, forest land, and open space; organizations and government entities seeking to preserve agricultural and forest land in designated Rural Legacy Areas; agricultural and property landowners in specified Rural Legacy Areas; landowners interested in protecting Maryland's natural resources and stream buffers through preservation easements; agricultural landowners; forest landowners; fee simple property owners; property owners with agricultural, natural, or cultural resource land; landowners with property suitable for conservation easement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of conservation easements and fee simple land interests for the conservation of natural, cultural, agricultural, forest, historic resources, wetlands, wildlife habitat, and historic sites within designated Rural Legacy Areas. Funds support land preservation for working farms and ecologically significant landscapes to maintain rural character and agricultural heritage, prevent sprawl development, protect resource-based industries including agriculture, forestry, tourism, and recreation, as well as land acquisition and preservation of agricultural land, forest land, open space, wetlands, and historic sites. Land acquisition through conservation easements to preserve agricultural, forestry, and ecologically valuable properties that support natural resources and protect Chesapeake Bay and local waterway health. Purchase of easements to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development and preserve natural resources, agricultural value, forestry, recreation and tourism. Development rights purchase and easement preservation with emphasis on stream buffer protection. Funds support protection of farmland, forestland, Civil War historic sites, greenbelt areas, and other significant natural and cultural resources, including protection of view sheds around state parks, national battlefields, and the Appalachian Trail, providing water quality benefits to major waterways and reservoirs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland in designated Rural Legacy Areas. Currently there are 35-41 Rural Legacy Areas throughout the state with total designated acreage exceeding 1.3 million acres. Designated Rural Legacy Areas include Agricultural Security Corridor, Anne Arundel County South, Baltimore County Coastal, Bear Creek, Bishopville-Showell, Calvert Creeks, Coastal Bays, Deer Creek Valley, Dividing Creek, Fair Hill, Foreman Branch, Gunpowder Valley, Harriet Tubman, Huntersville, Lands End, Little Pipe Creek/Upper Patapsco, Long Green Valley, Manor, Mattapany, Mid-MD Frederick/Carrollton Manor, Mid-MD Montgomery, Mid-MD Washington County, Mountain Ridge, Nanjemoy-Mattawoman Forest, Nanticoke, North Calvert, Patuxent River, Piney Run Watershed, Quantico Creek, Upper Patapsco Watershed, Upper Patuxent River Reservoir Watershed, and Zekiah Watershed. Rural Legacy Areas are delineated within Maryland counties and include both working farms and ecologically significant landscapes. Rural Legacy Areas are proposed by county governments and land trusts and designated by the Rural Legacy Board. Currently 36 designated Rural Legacy Areas exist across all 23 Maryland counties. New applicants and existing sponsors in Rural Legacy Areas are eligible to apply. Applicants must target properties within these designated areas. Local sponsors (county governments and land trusts) propose Rural Legacy Areas for designation and funding. In Washington County, program only purchases easements within a specified boundary surrounding the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, Boonsboro and the Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville and Gapland. Properties must be located within approved Rural Legacy Areas in Maryland. Designated areas serve Eastern Shore counties, northern coastal bays watershed, Chesapeake Bay tributaries and watersheds, and referenced Maryland Priority Funding Areas for mitigation purposes.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Sponsors must apply annually to the Rural Legacy Board for participation in the Program and to receive funding to support land conservation efforts. Applications are submitted to the Rural Legacy Office by the second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m. Groups interested in establishing a new Rural Legacy Area should read the Rural Legacy Program Grants Manual and meet with the appropriate RLP Program Administrator. The Full Application must be completed and adhere to GIS Submittal Guidelines. For established areas, use the Abbreviated Application form and Property List Form. Applicants submit either a full application (for new Rural Legacy Areas) or an abbreviated application (for grant renewals and boundary expansion requests) along with a property list form, GIS data following the submittal guidelines, and other required documentation. GIS data for protected lands must also be submitted by January 15th (or next business day if weekend/holiday/state offices closed) following the established submittal guidelines. Applicants must coordinate with county/counties to identify local preservation programs within RLA and submit GIS data for locally-administered land preservation programs before annual grant application. Applications are evaluated using established evaluation criteria based on resource significance, development threats, historic and cultural value, economic importance, application quality, partnership strength, matching funds, and sponsor capability. State agencies review applications February through April. The Rural Legacy Advisory Committee, a panel of eleven volunteers appointed by the Governor, reviews all applications and makes recommendations to the Rural Legacy Board. The Rural Legacy Board, comprised of the Secretaries of the Departments of Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Planning, reviews applications and recommends to the Governor and Board of Public Works which Rural Legacy Areas will be designated and funded. The Board's recommendations are then reviewed and approved by the Maryland Board of Public Works, comprised of the Governor, the Comptroller, and the Treasurer. Site visits of proposed new areas or expansions occur April through May. The Advisory Committee makes recommendations in June-July. After Board of Public Works approval in August-September, the Rural Legacy Board transmits a Grant Agreement to the Sponsor for signatures. Grant Agreements are prepared in September-October. Once executed, the Sponsor can proceed with individual acquisitions as defined in project agreements. Qualifying landowners apply for the program prior to February 1st of each cycle year. Landowner interest is the basis for requesting County funds during the Capital Budget cycle. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council. Applications are ranked based on property characteristics and easements are purchased from highest-ranked qualifying properties. For property acquisitions, sponsor submits complete BPW (Board of Public Works) package with required documents. Program staff reviews and prepares BPW item. Project scheduled for BPW agenda. BPW approval required before payment processing. Upon settlement, sponsor closes out file with documented evidence of expenditures. Completed application with cover sheet, narratives, budget forms, maps, GIS data, and photos should be submitted to Rural Legacy Program. All attachments should be in Word or PDF format.

structured_extraction.program_description: A law requiring the maintenance and reproduction of pine resources on harvested forest areas to provide recreational, aesthetic, wildlife, and environmental benefits while supporting wood fiber for commerce and industry.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The law requires eligible harvested land to be regenerated to pine through seed trees or pine seedlings according to a pine reforestation plan. At least 8 cone-bearing loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine per acre must be left as seed trees, which should be healthy, wind-firm, and well distributed. Regeneration is deemed successful when at least 400 loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine seedlings are present, well distributed, and free to grow.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dan Rider or local DNR forester
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest landowners and timber harvesters with harvested areas of at least 5 acres that were at least 25% loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest and will not be converted to non-forest use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pine forest regeneration and reforestation on harvested land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies statewide to harvested forest areas in Maryland that meet size and species requirements and will remain forested.
requirements_list: Harvested area must be at least 5 acres in size
Area must have been at least 25% loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest
Land will not be converted to non-forest use such as agricultural or residential
Regeneration must occur through seed trees or pine seedlings per an approved pine reforestation plan
If using seed trees, at least 8 cone-bearing loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine per acre must be left
Seed trees must be healthy, wind-firm, and well distributed
Successful regeneration requires at least 400 loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine seedlings that are well distributed and free to grow
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact local DNR forester or the Maryland DNR Forest Service for guidance on compliance with the Seed Tree Law requirements and reforestation planning.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Estate Tax Benefit for Conservation Easements
structured_extraction.program_description: A state estate tax benefit that reduces the taxable value of land subject to a conservation easement. Conservation easements limit the development potential of land, resulting in the property being valued at its restricted use value rather than its maximum development potential value for Maryland state estate tax purposes. This reduced valuation lowers the overall taxable estate and associated estate tax liability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Land subject to a conservation easement is valued at a lower appraised value for Maryland state estate tax purposes because the easement restricts development potential. The restricted use value is used instead of maximum development potential value, thereby reducing the taxable estate and associated estate tax liability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners and residents with estates that include land subject to conservation easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces state estate tax liability by lowering the appraised value of land under conservation easement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; available to Maryland landowners only.
requirements_list: Land must be subject to a conservation easement that restricts development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consult with a tax advisor or estate planning attorney to determine how a conservation easement affects Maryland state estate tax liability. The reduced valuation applies automatically through the state estate tax calculation process when land is encumbered by a conservation easement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Income Tax Credit for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit for Maryland residents and pass-through entities who donate perpetual conservation easements to eligible Maryland organizations, including the Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. Donors can claim up to $5,000 per year for up to 15 years, with a maximum total credit of $80,000, based on the appraised value of the donated easement. The credit is calculated by multiplying the appraised easement value by the individual's percentage ownership of the property. For pass-through entities, total aggregate credits claimed by members cannot exceed $200,000 per taxable year. Additional benefits include federal income tax deduction, property tax credits, and federal estate tax exemptions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit equal to the appraised value of a donated conservation easement, up to a maximum of $5,000 per year per individual or pass-through entity. Unused credit can be carried forward for up to 15 additional years, for a maximum total credit of $80,000. When multiple individuals jointly donate an easement, each is separately entitled to up to $5,000 per year. For pass-through entities, total aggregate credits claimed by members cannot exceed $200,000 per taxable year. The credit is reduced dollar-for-dollar by any payment received for the easement. Property tax exemption applies to 100% of assessment on unimproved and non-commercial portion of property placed in easement for 15 consecutive years beginning July 1 following donation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 (for Conservation Property Tax Credit); ongoing for income tax credit
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and pass-through entities who donate perpetual conservation easements to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces state income tax liability and property tax for donors of conservation easements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. The easement must be conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation and approved by the Board of Public Works.
requirements_list: Easement must be perpetual
Easement must be conveyed to Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, or Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation
Easement must be approved by the Board of Public Works
Total credit cannot exceed the appraised value of the easement
Any payment received for the easement must be deducted from the credit
Maximum credit per year is $5,000 or state income taxes owed, whichever is smaller
Individual cannot claim both a state income tax deduction and state income tax credit for the same conservation easement donation
For pass-through entities, total aggregate credits claimed by members cannot exceed $200,000 per taxable year
Qualified appraisal required to determine easement value per IRS criteria
Joint owners must each calculate their own state tax liability and percentage ownership
Land must be unimproved and non-commercial for property tax credit eligibility
Easement must be approved after June 30, 1986 by Board of Public Works
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Obtain a qualified appraiser to determine the value of the donated conservation easement. Complete Maryland Form 502CR for individuals or Form 500CR for pass-through entities. Attach the form to your Maryland tax return and file with your state return. For property tax credit, application must be filed on or before October 1 to receive credit for that taxable year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Income Tax Deduction for Conservation Easement Donations
structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax deduction for Maryland residents who itemize deductions on their federal income tax return and wish to deduct conservation easement donations on their Maryland state tax return. Individuals cannot claim both the state income tax deduction and the state income tax credit for the same easement, and deductions are subject to applicable state limitations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individuals who itemize deductions on their federal income tax return may deduct conservation easement donations on their Maryland state income tax return, subject to applicable state limitations. The deduction is applied against state income tax liability. An individual cannot claim both the state income tax deduction and the state income tax credit for the same conservation easement donation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who itemize deductions on federal income tax returns and donate conservation easements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State income tax deduction for conservation easement donations, applied against state income tax liability
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must itemize deductions on federal income tax return
Cannot claim both state income tax deduction and state income tax credit for the same easement
Subject to state limitations on charitable deductions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Itemize deductions on your federal tax return. Calculate the eligible deduction amount for your Maryland state return. Include the deduction on your Maryland state income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative supporting riparian forest buffers along streams and shorelines throughout the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. The program coordinates efforts among state, local, federal, and nonprofit agencies to expand and maintain streamside and shoreline forests. Riparian forest buffers reduce nitrogen by 60 to 90 percent and provide multiple benefits including wildlife habitat, aquatic health, air quality improvement, streambank stability, and carbon storage. The program operates to increase forest buffers along streams and rivers throughout Maryland. The program focuses on establishing riparian forest buffers of at least 35 feet in width along watercourses using native, non-invasive woody trees and shrubs, accepting both artificial (planted) and natural regeneration methods. Over 1,300 miles of riparian forest buffers have been planted since 1996. The program includes long-term monitoring of forest buffer establishment, growth, effectiveness, and ecological benefits including water quality improvements, nutrient reduction, timber value potential, and stream health restoration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides cost-share incentives through the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) and Conservation Security Program (CSP) to landowners and organizations who establish and maintain riparian forest buffers on their property. CREP contracts typically provide: 50% USDA cost-share plus 37.5% Maryland Agricultural Cost-Share (87.5% total), 40% Practice Incentive Payment (PIP), and $200 signing bonus. Soil rental rates average $59-$66 per acre depending on buffer type (hardwood or pine). Contract terms range from 10-15 years with renewal eligibility, and typical CREP contracts average $3,700+ per acre over 15 years, with annualized costs approximately $206 per acre per year. Incentives include land rent compensation, soil rental rates, signup incentive payments, and practice incentive payments covering approximately 40 percent of eligible installation costs. Additional technical assistance is provided by MD DNR Forest Service, NRCS, and local, state, and federal agencies. Incentive rates were designed to stimulate buffer plantings along streams and rivers in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. The program coordinates funding for planting stock (seedlings, saplings, ball-and-burlap trees), site preparation, tree planting, maintenance support including weed control and tree protection, and training on buffer establishment, maintenance, and invasive species management. Establishment costs average $1,000 per acre. Support includes planting coordination and planning, direct financial assistance through programs (CREP, Buffer Incentive Program, 5-103, etc.), and support for both artificial planting and natural regeneration methods. Planting sources include volunteer groups, contractors, or other options. Buffer fencing options are available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 1 and July 1 for fall and spring submissions, respectively
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, volunteer groups, contractors, government agencies, local governments, watershed organizations, conservation organizations, agricultural landowners, private landowners, land trusts, educational institutions, schools and volunteer groups, and organizations with property along streams and rivers in Maryland, particularly within the Chesapeake Bay Watershed, working to establish and maintain riparian forest buffers. Program targets private landowners, farmers, developers, and agricultural operators on eligible lands. Federal, state, private, and other public entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the planting of seedlings and young trees to create riparian forest buffers along streams and shorelines, including site preparation, tree planting, and ongoing maintenance. Funds help establish and maintain riparian forest buffers on streamside and shoreline properties to reduce nutrient runoff and provide benefits for wildlife, aquatic habitat, air quality, streambank stability, and carbon sequestration. Funding covers planting stock (seedlings, containerized saplings, ball-and-burlap trees), herbicide treatments, tree protection mechanisms (tree shelters, weed mats, collars, repellents), cooler storage for seedling transport, and the development of maintenance teams for post-establishment care. Funds also support monitoring and evaluation of vegetation survival, growth, water quality metrics, benthic macroinvertebrates, stream morphology, bank stability, stream temperature, and timber values. Potential future timber harvest income is available to landowners after contract completion. Funds may support foregone agricultural production value over contract terms. Stream buffer establishment through vegetation planting (trees, seedlings, understory species).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland, with particular focus on the Chesapeake Bay Watershed and Maryland Coastal Bays region (Newport & Sinepuxent Bays, Big Mill Pond/Chincoteague Bay tributaries). The program has focused on specific watersheds including the Monocacy, Antietam, Catoctin, Potomac, Chester/Sassafras, and Watershed Restoration Action Strategy (WRAS) watersheds. Priority areas include Southern Maryland and Eastern Shore, Frederick, Carroll, and Allegany County areas, Somerset and Worcester Counties, and operates throughout Maryland's 38,870 miles of riparian area to increase forest buffers along streams and rivers. The program prioritizes high-nutrient loading watersheds, areas draining 38 to 19,000 acres, small rural watersheds with 2-11% impervious surfaces, and areas with low riparian forest buffer coverage, poor water quality, and proximity to drinking water intakes. Western Maryland and Garrett Counties regions are targeted for hardwood buffer plantings, while Eastern Shore counties are targeted for pine buffer plantings. Piedmont, Blue Ridge, Ridge and Valley, Eastern Shore/Coastal Plain, and Mountain physiographic provinces are eligible. Potomac Watershed Partnership focus areas and Governor's Land Conservation Plan priority areas are included. Program covers multiple Maryland counties including Dorchester, Talbot, Queen Anne's, Kent, Cecil, Harford, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, Montgomery, Frederick, Washington, Allegany, and Garrett, with multiple watershed/stream segments identified by codes.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To participate, landowners should submit the buffer reporting form or complete the Riparian Forest Buffer Planting Form to the RFB Coordinator at MD DNR-Forest Service, Tawes State Office Building E1, Annapolis, MD 21401. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with submission deadlines of January 1 (for fall planting) and July 1 (for spring planting). To include a forest buffer in the statewide accounting, submit the buffer reporting form for statewide accounting. The program uses targeting processes to identify cooperating landowners, particularly in priority watersheds. Landowners should work with local soil conservation districts, NRCS representatives, and technical service providers to develop buffer plans and submit applications. Form submission includes documentation of buffer area, planting source, technical assistance type, property owner information, location details by tax map, parcel, waterbody name, and grid coordinates.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee provides funding for community-based tree planting, maintenance, education, and community forestry initiatives throughout Maryland to enhance the state's urban forest. The program strives to unite and encourage citizens to protect and enhance Maryland's community trees and forest ecosystems. Grants support projects on public lands such as parks, school campuses, streetscapes, town centers, and municipal properties in urban and suburban settings. Grants up to $1,000 are provided to communities, schools, organizations, and municipalities for planting and maintaining street trees to increase urban tree canopy, engage community members, and build local capacity for long-term environmental stewardship. Projects with matching funds or in-kind support are given priority. Funding flows through the USDA Forest Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,000 provided for community-based tree planting, maintenance, education, and community forestry projects on public lands such as parks, school campuses, streetscapes, town centers, and municipal properties. Funding covers tree purchase and planting (non-invasive species only), tree planting supplies, signage with MUCFC acknowledgement, and equipment for tree planting (with detailed future use plan required). Projects with matching funds or in-kind support are given priority. Funding flows through USDA Forest Service.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By 11:59 p.m. on January 15 and July 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Citizens, community organizations, volunteers, Master Gardeners, civic groups, Scout troops, and youth organizations seeking to plant trees and enhance forest ecosystems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree seedlings, mulch, tools, tree purchase and planting (non-invasive species only), tree planting supplies, signage with MUCFC acknowledgement, equipment for tree planting (with detailed future use plan), volunteer workshops, and project materials for community forestry initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All funded projects must occur on public lands within Maryland. Projects must be located on public property (school grounds, parks, town centers, or municipal properties) throughout all Maryland counties.
