For educational projects: must raise public awareness about the value of trees in urban environments, include draft content or images for signage or publications, description of target audience and distribution plan, explanation of how the project addresses an unmet informational need, and clear MUCFC credit on all materials

Final reports are due one month after the proposed completion date with project summary, accounting of expenditures with receipts, monitoring/maintenance plan, volunteer hours documentation, tree species planted list, and impact metrics
Any unused funds must be returned with the final report
Failure to submit a final report or return unused funds may disqualify applicants from future grants
Maximum grant award: $1,000 per project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Grant Guidelines. 2. Submit a project application online or by email to the MUCFC Grants Chair by the deadline (January 15 or July 15 by 11:59 p.m.). 3. Obtain approval from the MUCFC and local County Forestry Board signature prior to starting the project. 4. Complete the project on public lands with volunteer involvement. 5. Submit a final report one month after the proposed completion date including project summary, budget accounting with receipts, monitoring/maintenance plan, volunteer hours, tree species planted, and impact measurements. Any unused funds must be returned with the report. Contact Wanda MacLachlan for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A full-time, paid, year-round employment program that empowers U.S. Military veterans by engaging them in conservation service work on Maryland's public lands and State Parks. Members work in the Maryland Park Service and Department of Natural Resources performing park operations, trail maintenance, facilities improvement, educational programs, and habitat restoration while receiving competitive wages, health insurance benefits, professional skills development training, and certifications. The program leverages veterans' unique background, diverse job skills, and service ethic to address pressing conservation needs while developing veterans professionally through on-the-job experience. Members receive certifications including Emergency Medical Responder, Wildland Fire Fighter, Chainsaw Use and Care, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Trail construction and maintenance, Basic Tool Use and Safety, Basic Carpentry, and Small Craft Safety. Work is typically 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with some projects involving overnight stays and weekend hours. Uniforms, personal protective gear, and a $200 boot reimbursement are provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full-time, paid, year-round employment with competitive wages and health insurance benefits through the Student Conservation Association. Members receive professional skills development training and multiple certifications including Emergency Medical Responder, Wildland Fire Fighter, Chainsaw Use and Care, Environmental Education and Interpretation, Trail construction and maintenance, Basic Tool Use and Safety, Basic Carpentry, and Small Craft Safety. The program provides work uniforms, personal protective gear, and $200 boot reimbursement. Members serve one-year terms with possibility of contract renewal. Standard work schedule is 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with some projects involving overnight stays and weekend work.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ranger Sara Marcinak, Director of Conservation Corps
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. Military veterans interested in conservation service, natural resource management careers, environmental stewardship, and land management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-time work in conservation and park operations including trail building and maintenance, facilities improvement projects, educational programs and interpretation, recreation management, park operations, volunteer coordination, special events assistance, mentorship of Conservation Jobs Corps members, forest enhancement and tree planting, stream/bay/wetland restoration, stream surveys, habitat restoration, and invasive species removal on Maryland State Parks and public lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The program is based at Merkle Natural Resource Management Area in Prince George's County, Maryland and works regularly throughout the Southern Maryland Regional Complex, which includes Calvert Cliffs State Park, Cedarville State Forest, Chapel Point State Park, Chapman State Park, Hallowing Point Waterfront Recreation Area, Rosaryville State Park, and Smallwood State Park.
requirements_list: Prior service in the U.S. Armed Forces
Education or experience in park operations, recreation, education, business, administration, forestry, social sciences, or natural resources-related field is preferred
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds repeatedly and use hand tools including heavy tools such as pulaskis, sledge hammers, and chainsaws
Ability to travel to and from park locations and various work sites
Willingness to serve for one year with possibility of contract renewal
Ability to attend mandatory overnight trainings and projects for up to one week at a time
Willingness to work on certain weekends
Commitment to service and interest in natural resources and outdoor recreation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Ranger Sara Marcinak, Director of Conservation Corps, via email at sara.marcinak@maryland.gov or by phone at 443-370-8246 for application information and procedures. The program is currently accepting members.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that provides technical assistance to private landowners for creating, developing, rehabilitating, and preserving waterfowl habitats on their lands. Landowners enter into ten-year renewable license agreements with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to increase and improve wetland habitats for breeding, migrating, and wintering waterfowl. The program combines tax incentives with on-site technical assistance from Wildlife and Heritage Service biologists to help prepare approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plans and conduct annual inspections.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who complete approved waterfowl habitat development and management projects can claim expenditures as tax contributions to the state of Maryland. Participants receive annual documentation from the Wildlife and Heritage Service biologist following inspection of project status on a standard form provided for tax purposes. Technical assistance is provided to help prepare the Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan, and landowners enter into ten-year renewable license agreements that are mutually developed with the Wildlife and Heritage Service.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Richard Walls, Migratory Game Bird Habitat Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in Maryland who own or control land suitable for waterfowl habitat development and management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved projects creating, developing, rehabilitating, and/or preserving waterfowl habitats on private lands, including establishing semi-permanent water, nesting and resting habitat, and food and cover for ducks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Projects must be on private lands within the state. Property location must be specified with directions from nearest town.
requirements_list: Minimum of ten contiguous acres of habitat that will provide food and/or cover for ducks
At least one acre of semi-permanent water with nesting and resting habitat within or near the semi-permanent water
Private lands used for commercial hunting enterprises are not eligible
Landowner must enter into a ten-year renewable license agreement with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Landowner must develop and follow an approved Waterfowl Habitat Management Plan
Landowner signature required
Map of project area required showing nearest town, access roads, and property location
Project area size specified in total acres and acres of semi-permanent water/wetlands
Type of land use documentation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review project eligibility rules to determine if your proposed project area qualifies. 2. Complete the Maryland Waterfowl Restoration Program Application Form and mail it to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Wildlife & Heritage Service at PO Box 68, Wye Mills, MD 21679, or call 410-827-8612 extension 103. 3. The Regional Habitat Biologist for your county will review your application and contact you to arrange an inspection of your project area for eligibility. 4. Upon approval and entry into the program, you receive an official information kit with all program documents and useful publications. 5. The Wildlife and Heritage Service annually documents the status of approved projects and provides documentation for tax purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship funding available to wildlife rehabilitators through the Maryland Wildlife Rehabilitators Association, which also provides information on continuing education offerings in other states.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships available to support wildlife rehabilitators in pursuing continuing education and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wildlife rehabilitators in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarships for continuing education and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based organization serving wildlife rehabilitators.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Wildlife Rehabilitators Association through their website for information about scholarship availability and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free membership program for youth ages 5 to 15 that provides stickers, access to special youth fishing events, fishing information, tips, opportunities, and a platform to share fishing stories and photos through the Youth Angler's Log. Members learn about fishing and can participate in youth fishing activities across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free club membership including 2 stickers for members. Members receive email updates and news about fishing, access to fishing information, opportunities, and tips. Members gain access to special youth fishing events held throughout Maryland and can participate in the Youth Angler's Log to share fishing experiences and learn about fishing. Educational resources about fishing are provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 5 to 15 interested in learning about and practicing fishing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program membership and participation in youth fishing events and educational activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through special youth events held in various locations throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must be between ages 5 and 15
Parent/Guardian signature required
Provide name, address, birthday, parent/guardian contact information
Complete sign-up form (either printed and mailed or submitted online)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the sign-up sheet by either downloading and mailing it to Angel Wright at 580 Taylor Ave, B-2, Annapolis, MD 21401, faxing to 410-260-8279, or using the online registration form. Optional: sign up for email updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that registers and recognizes exceptional trees throughout Maryland based on their size. The program identifies the largest trees of each species in Maryland to help identify potential genetic improvements and species range and reproduction. Citizens nominate trees, volunteers measure them using a formula combining circumference, height, and crown spread, and qualifying trees are registered in a statewide database. Tree owners receive certificates, congratulatory letters, species lists, and bumper stickers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free non-invasive measurement and registration services for large trees. Trees are measured at 4.5 feet circumference, height, and crown spread, then scored using an official formula and compared to state champions. Trees that score within 70% of the current state champion receive a certificate of registration. Tree owners receive a certificate of registration, a congratulatory letter, a list of all registered trees of that species in Maryland, a county-specific brochure, and a bumper sticker. The program provides recognition and documentation of exceptional trees but does not provide financial assistance or funding for tree maintenance. Measurements are non-invasive and do not harm trees or impact property rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who own or wish to nominate trees in their community; property owners with large trees nominated for the program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; no funding or financial assistance is provided. The program recognizes and registers big trees. Tree measurement and registration services are provided at no cost to property owners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Trees on public property can be measured without written permission if appropriate. Private property trees require written permission from the owner.
requirements_list: Tree must have a circumference of at least 9.5 inches (diameter of 3 inches)
Tree must have a height of at least 13 feet
Tree must be native or naturalized to Maryland (can grow and reproduce on its own)
Written permission from the tree owner is required for private property trees
Tree species must not be exotic or invasive (exotic species are not eligible for championship status)
Tree owner information required
Nominator identification required
Measurer qualifications must be documented
Physical measurements required: circumference (feet/inches), height, average crown width
Total points calculated for qualification using official formula; tree must score within 70% of current state champion
Location/appearance/health assessment required
GPS coordinates required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Citizens nominate trees by submitting a nomination form. Written permission from the tree owner is required. The owner signs and returns the permission form to John Bennett at P.O. Box 328, North East, MD 21901 via mail, FAX (410-287-0010), or email with facsimile signature. Trained volunteers from the Maryland Big Tree Program Committee and local Forestry Board members measure the nominated trees using the established formula. If the tree qualifies, it is registered and assigned a permanent number.

structured_extraction.program_description: A citizen science and oyster restoration program where waterfront property owners and volunteer groups grow young oysters in wire mesh cages suspended from private piers for approximately nine to ten months. Participants receive oyster spat (young oysters) at no charge and nurture them in protective cages at their properties. After the growing period, the oysters are collected and planted on sanctuary areas closed to harvesting to enhance the oyster population and ecosystem. The program provides technical guidance, training, and care instructions throughout the process. The program is designed to foster stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay and create living oyster reefs in sanctuaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free oyster spat (young oysters) in wire mesh cages for participants to grow, along with training on cage maintenance and care. Participants receive cages and an information package on oyster care at pickup. The program covers the supply of oysters and cages at no charge. Technical guidance is provided on maintaining the oysters, including rinsing weekly or biweekly, winter care to prevent freezing, occasional scrubbing, and fouling management. Participants are responsible for providing pier or wharf space and maintenance for up to four cages over approximately nine to ten months. Participants can continue receiving new oyster spat if they choose to remain in the program. DNR provides guidance and advice for program implementation and selects sanctuary areas for planting oysters.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Waterfront property owners, community associations, non-profit organizations, RiverKeeper organizations, local government, and public schools in Maryland with existing piers or wharves who are interested in oyster restoration and becoming Chesapeake Bay stewards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants use the cages and oyster spat provided to grow young oysters in suspended wire mesh cages requiring regular maintenance including rinsing weekly or biweekly and winter care to prevent freezing. After approximately nine to ten months, the grown oysters are collected and permanently planted on sanctuary areas (areas closed to oyster harvesting) to enhance the ecosystem. Oysters cannot be harvested or eaten. Areas around private piers are not routinely tested and approved for shellfish harvest and pose health risks from pathogenic contamination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is active in 32 different tributaries and creeks across Maryland in the Chesapeake Bay area. Participants must have a pier or wharf located in one of the tributaries selected for the program with appropriate salinity levels to support oyster survival and growth and at least four feet of water at low tide. For creeks and coves, oysters may be moved to the main river or an adjacent river for planting on sanctuaries.
requirements_list: Must own or have access to an existing pier or wharf with at least four feet of water at low tide
Pier or wharf must be located in one of the tributaries selected for the program with suitable salinity for oyster survival and growth
Must be willing to provide maintenance for up to four cages of oysters for up to ten months
Must demonstrate interest in the welfare of the Chesapeake Bay and becoming a Bay and oyster steward
Must rinse oysters weekly or biweekly by lifting cages out of water or using a hose
Must maintain cages during winter to keep oysters submerged and prevent freezing
Must keep cages clean and manage fouling growth through occasional scrubbing
Ability to keep oysters submerged at all times, including during winter months
Do not consume oysters grown at private piers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the program through the online Oyster Gardening Registration form by March 31. After registration, you will be notified by the local sponsor that cages containing oyster spat are ready for pickup in your local community. At pickup, you will receive a briefing and information package on oyster care. Attach the cages to your pier or wharf using provided rope so they hang at least 6 inches off the bottom and are well below the water surface. Maintain the cages throughout the growing period. In about nine to ten months, program representatives will contact you to arrange collection of the oysters for sanctuary planting, typically near the end of May or early June.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tree planting incentive program that provides rebate coupons worth $25 off the purchase of native and recommended trees at participating retail nurseries and garden centers across Maryland. Citizens and organizations can participate to plant new trees that provide ecological, economic, and quality of life benefits including improved air and water quality, reduced energy costs, increased property values, and beautified neighborhoods and highways. The $25 rebate coupon is applied at the register at the time of purchase for one native or recommended tree with a retail value of $50 or more.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $25 rebate coupon applied at the register at the time of purchase for one native or recommended tree with a retail value of $50 or more. The coupon must be filled in completely and signed by the customer. One coupon per tree purchased. Valid only for trees listed on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List at participating retail nurseries and garden centers. Coupons are honored only at MPT participating nurseries for retail sales only; wholesale tree sales do not qualify. The program reduces the cost of purchasing native trees from participating nurseries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland citizens and organizations who want to purchase and plant native and recommended trees to improve air and water quality, reduce energy costs, increase property values, and beautify neighborhoods and highways.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of one native or recommended tree with a retail value of $50 or more from participating retail nurseries and garden centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at all participating retail nurseries and garden centers in Maryland.
requirements_list: Coupon must be filled in completely and signed by the customer
Valid for trees listed on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List only
Coupon valid for retail sales only; wholesale tree sales do not qualify
Tree must have a retail value of $50 or more
One coupon per tree purchased
Tree must be native species
Must be purchased from a participating nursery
Trees must be native species to Maryland or cultivars of native species
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Print or obtain the coupon from the program website. Step 2: Complete and sign the coupon. Step 3: Find a participating MPT nursery in your area. Step 4: Present the completed coupon at the register when purchasing an eligible native tree with a retail value of $50 or more, and the $25 discount will be applied at the time of sale.

structured_extraction.program_description: Multi-state wildfire training academy offering comprehensive wildfire training courses for the Mid-Atlantic region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers wildfire training courses held June 8-12, 2026 at Garrett College in McHenry, Maryland. Registration opens to the public on March 9, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Wildfire professionals and students in the Mid-Atlantic region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildfire training and certification courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training held in Garrett County, Maryland; available to Mid-Atlantic region participants.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration opens to the public on March 9, 2026. Visit midatlanticfirecompact.com for registration details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide hiking challenge commemorating Maryland's 250th anniversary where individuals or teams hike 250 miles across Maryland State Parks in 2026, register online, track their miles, and earn prizes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants complete a trail challenge by hiking 250 miles across Maryland State Parks. Registration is online and participants track their miles to earn prizes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and teams of any age interested in hiking and outdoor recreation across Maryland State Parks
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants engage in hiking activities at Maryland State Parks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland State Parks statewide
requirements_list: Must register online
Must hike 250 miles in Maryland State Parks during 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online on the program website, then participate in hiking activities at Maryland State Parks, track your miles, and complete the challenge.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Park Service leases agricultural land within Monocacy Natural Resources Management Area to interested farmers for short-term agricultural use. The program promotes farming on lands with prime agricultural soils and a history of farming, helping to maintain open spaces, provide pastoral views, and supply locally sourced food for nearby communities while supporting wildlife habitat.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Park Service leases parcels of agricultural land to farmers. Available properties include the Henderson property (103.27 acres) and Rock Hall Chadwick property (43.59 acres). Interested farmers submit bids for the property of their choosing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers interested in leasing agricultural land within Monocacy NRMA for short-term use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural production on leased land with prime agricultural soils.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Frederick County, near Dickerson. Monocacy River Natural Resources Management Area comprises 1,800 acres along the Monocacy River.
requirements_list: Land must have prime agricultural soils
Land must have a history of being farmed
Farmer must submit a completed bid form for the property of their choosing
Bid must be returned by 12:00pm on the stated deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested farmers review available properties (Henderson property or Rock Hall Chadwick property), complete the hyperlinked bid form for their chosen property, and return the form via mail or in person to Seneca Creek State Park by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: NOAA Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training (B-WET Chesapeake) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers to foster stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support hands-on watershed education for students and teachers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, non-profits, and educational organizations offering watershed education to students and teachers in the Chesapeake Bay region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting hands-on watershed education and fostering stewardship of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Chesapeake Bay watershed region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for grants through the NOAA Chesapeake Bay Watershed Education and Training program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual seven-day residential educational camp for high school students interested in careers in natural resources and climate resilience. The camp covers traditional forestry, GIS and GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology, taught by natural resource professionals. Students age 16 and older can earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by attending the full week and passing an exam. Credits are transferable to most Maryland community colleges and several four-year colleges and universities. Partial scholarships are provided by local Forestry Boards to selected students from each county. The curriculum is designed by natural resources professionals in partnership with the state's Forestry Boards to help prepare young people for careers in natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seven-day residential camp held July 20-26, 2025, providing hands-on training in natural resources careers and climate resilience. Participants can earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland that are transferable to most Maryland community colleges and several four-year colleges and universities. Partial scholarships provided by local Forestry Boards to two students from each county.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for NRCC 2025 are now being accepted
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students age 16 or older interested in careers in natural resources and climate resilience
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training and professional development in forestry, GIS, GPS, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, watershed ecology, and climate-related fields, with opportunity to earn transferable college credits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; two students from each Maryland county are recruited by their local Forestry Boards and provided partial scholarships
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Must be at least 16 years old by the first day of camp to earn college credits
Must complete entire week to earn college credits
Must pass an exam to earn college credits
Must be recruited and selected by local Forestry Board in your county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: High school students are recruited by their local Forestry Boards, who conduct interviews and select two students from their counties to receive partial scholarships. Applicants can submit camp applications through the Maryland Forestry Boards website at http://www.marylandforestryboards.org/nrcc.cfm or the Maryland Forestry Foundation website for more details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program providing equipment installation/upgrades and training for safe navigation and fishing activities in and around wind turbines in Lease Area OCS-A 0490 (approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland). The program is designed to help Maryland and Delaware commercial and charter fishing vessels directly or reasonably expected to be impacted by offshore wind energy development. Participants may select from eligible equipment upgrades and training options such as radar training or navigation equipment upgrades on vessels. The program includes a voucher system and partnership with preferred vendors for marine electronics and navigation services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NETP makes funds available through a voucher system to provide eligible Maryland and Delaware commercial, for-hire, and charter fishing vessel operators with equipment upgrades and training. Equipment upgrade vouchers: up to $10,000 for commercial and U.S. Coast Guard inspected for-hire vessels; up to $5,000 for charter vessels. Training vouchers: $1,000 available per vessel for up to two participants for professional mariner certification, radar training, or other maritime training relevant to safe navigation and fishing activities around wind turbines. Additionally, $35,000 is available for experiential training development at Maryland Maritime Institute of Technology and Graduate Studies (MITAGS) including simulation facility development. Participants may recover reasonable income loss and registration fees during training participation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Five years following Commercial Operation Date (COD) of the Project; 120 days prior to Offshore Construction Commencement Date for initial enrollment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland and Delaware commercial fishing vessel operators, U.S. Coast Guard inspected for-hire fishing vessel operators, charter vessel operators, and crew members directly or reasonably expected to be impacted by offshore wind turbines in Lease Area OCS-A 0490.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment installation and upgrades for safe navigation around wind turbines, training for safe navigation and fishing activities, professional mariner and radar certifications, maritime training, registration fees, and reasonable income loss recovery during training participation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland and Delaware commercial fishing operations with vessels operating in federal waters off Maryland and Delaware coasts, specifically around Lease Area OCS-A 0490 (approximately 11.5 miles east of Ocean City, Maryland). Primary focus on West Ocean City Harbor area and surrounding offshore waters.
requirements_list: Commercial fishing vessel or U.S. Coast Guard inspected for-hire fishing vessel or for-hire charter vessel
Must be from Maryland or Delaware
Vessel and operators must be directly or reasonably expected to be impacted by offshore wind energy development in Lease Area OCS-A 0490
Registered Maryland commercial fishers for certain program components
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants select from available equipment upgrade and training options through a voucher system. Enrollment and application procedures are administered through MDNR in partnership with US Wind, Inc. Training and equipment are delivered through preferred vendors identified during program development. Additional information is available through the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind and MDNR Coastal and Chesapeake Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Permit program for aquaculture operations in Maryland, including tank culture, pond culture, and educational projects for any person engaged in aquaculture or related activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free permit authorization to operate non-shellfish aquaculture facility including tank culture, pond culture, and educational projects. Valid for five years, renewable for additional five-year terms. Technical assistance is provided for growing methods and aquatic disease control upon request. No permit fee is charged.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aquaculture operators; commercial producers; hobbyists; educational institutions; researchers; any person engaged in aquaculture or related activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating an aquaculture facility to rear fish or other permitted species for tank culture, pond culture, and educational projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Facility must be located in Maryland. Applies to tidal waters of the state and inland aquaculture facilities. Applicant must specify which county facility is located in.
requirements_list: Must obtain an aquaculture permit before operating a facility
Must obtain permit before conducting aquacultural activities involving finfish in tidal waters
Health certification and species origin documentation
Facility location map with directions
Facility description and sketch including inflow/effluent
Location of nearest body of water that could receive discharge
Solid waste management plan for mortalities and byproducts
Entrapment systems for hybrid or non-native species
Statement of operational goals and expected production
Workers' compensation compliance certificate (if employing staff)
Must renew permit every five years
Maintain shipping/receiving records by species for 3 years
Notify Department of disease discoveries immediately
Submit annual report summarizing efforts, activities undertaken, production techniques utilized, and number or amount of finfish or other permitted species stocked and/or harvested
Allow Department facility inspections
Notify Department of significant facility changes
Failure to submit annual report or conduct planned activities may result in permit revocation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application form (both sides); attach required supporting documents including health certification, facility map, facility description and sketch, solid waste management plan, and workers' compensation certificate if applicable; submit to DNR. For renewals and amending permits, resubmit the application noting desired changes. Annual reports are required for each permit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Offshore Blind & Shoreline License Application for Riparian Landowners
structured_extraction.program_description: A license program for riparian landowners to operate offshore blinds and conduct waterfowl hunting activities along shorelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Riparian landowners seeking to operate offshore blinds for waterfowl hunting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: License permits operation of offshore blinds and shoreline hunting activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland for riparian property owners.
requirements_list: Must be a riparian landowner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for license through Maryland DNR.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to offer participants an opportunity to experience Maryland's natural, cultural, historical and recreational resources firsthand through camping experiences at state parks. The program lends camping gear free of charge to participants and provides access to campsites at selected Maryland state parks. Gear includes tents, sleeping pads, chairs, stoves, lanterns and other equipment to help families and groups reconnect with each other and the outdoors in a comfortable, safe and relaxing setting. Gear is available at seven participating state parks across Maryland including Cunningham Falls, Swallow Falls, New Germany, Rocky Gap, Patapsco Valley, Pocomoke River, and Janes Island State Parks. Campsites include picnic tables, fire pits, and some sites have electric hook-ups. Restrooms and shower facilities are available nearby.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free lending of camping gear including tent, sleeping pads, chairs, stove, lantern and more. Campsites are available at participating state parks with nightly fees ranging from $25-$39 depending on park and amenities. Campsites include picnic tables and fire pits with some sites offering electric hook-ups. Restrooms and shower facilities are available nearby. Program includes gear list, food menu suggestions, and recipe ideas for camping.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families, individuals, and groups interested in camping; no age restrictions for children; up to 6 people per campsite.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Camping equipment and campsite reservations at participating state parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available at seven participating state parks across Maryland: Cunningham Falls State Park, Swallow Falls State Park, New Germany State Park, Rocky Gap State Park, Patapsco Valley State Park, Pocomoke River State Park, and Janes Island State Park.
requirements_list: Participants must bring own sleeping bags, food, and personal items
Maximum 6 people per campsite
Pet owners must notify park in advance for designated pet camping loops
Importation of personal firewood prohibited due to Emerald Ash Borer threat
Must contact the participating park office directly by phone to make a reservation and specify Operation Campout participation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the desired participating state park directly by phone to check available dates and reserve Operation Campout camping gear and campsite. Phone numbers and email addresses for each participating park are provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit that authorizes the sale of finfish from facilities outside Maryland for stocking in Maryland waters. Suppliers must meet fish health inspection requirements and provide documentation of approved sources and pathogen testing. The program requires annual fish health inspections with statistically-based representative sampling of all fish lots for certifiable pathogens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a permit that allows out-of-state fish suppliers to sell finfish for stocking in Maryland waters. Applicants must submit fish health inspection reports documenting that fish are free from viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections using AFS Bluebook or OIE Manual protocols. The permit requires annual renewal with updated health inspections. For brokers obtaining fish from multiple facilities, isolation facility documentation with biosecurity protocols is also required. Inspection documentation must include species, lot number, age, sample sizes, diagnostic results, origin of lots, number of fish per lot, water supply information, inspector name/address/phone, and inspector signature/date. No financial assistance is provided; this is a regulatory permitting program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide funding program supported by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that helps communities assess vulnerabilities and implement measures to increase resilience to climate change impacts, particularly tidal flooding and precipitation-based flood events. The program supports communities to understand and enhance capacity to plan for impacts from coastal and precipitation-based flood events. Applicants can receive financial assistance through grants or technical assistance through a DNR contractor to develop risk assessments, identify adaptation strategies, and create conceptual designs for flood mitigation projects. The program supports planning projects to improve understanding of flood impacts, develop risk assessments, identify adaptation strategies, and create conceptual designs for flood mitigation. Additionally, the program provides guidance for incorporating Relative Sea Level Rise (RSLR) projections into planning, regulatory, and site-specific projects using a six-step framework.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum request of $125,000. Proposal requests typically range from $40,000 to $100,000 for projects with a maximum duration of one year. Funding becomes available October 1, 2026. Applicants can receive direct financial support through a grant award or technical assistance through a DNR contractor to develop risk assessments, identify adaptation strategies, and create conceptual designs for flood mitigation projects. Funding helps communities assess tidal flooding vulnerabilities and implement resilience measures through vulnerability assessments, tidal flood planning, and resilience-building initiatives. Guidance includes RSLR estimates based on Baltimore, Cambridge, Lewes, Solomons Island, and Washington DC tide gauges using growing emissions pathway (RCP 8.5) projections, with three risk tolerance levels (high: 17% probability, medium: 5% probability, low: 1% probability).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, local jurisdictions, non-governmental organizations, and institutions of higher education seeking to address flood resilience and climate adaptation planning within Maryland's Coastal Zone. Also serves decision-makers, planning professionals, regulatory officials, and project managers at local, state, and federal levels working on flood resilience projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must support understanding of flood impacts and vulnerabilities at community scale, including risk assessments, identification and incorporation of adaptation strategies into current planning processes, and development of conceptual designs or engineered solutions. Projects may address short-term (1-10 years) and long-term (+10 years) flood impacts from high tide flooding, sea level rise, and precipitation events. Vulnerability assessments, tidal flood planning, resilience-building initiatives, and implementation of resilience measures. Funds support planning projects that result in risk-reduction strategies and higher regulatory standards that propel implementation of on-the-ground adaptation projects. Includes adaptation strategies including no action, avoid, accommodate, resist, and relocate options based on RSLR projections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone. Planning projects can encompass both public and private lands within the coastal zone. The project area can address flooding impacts at the community, county, or municipal level. Available throughout Maryland. Guidance applicable to areas with six tide gauge reference locations: Annapolis, Baltimore, Cambridge, Solomons Island (MD), Lewes (DE), and Washington (DC). Capital projects over $500,000 with 50% state funding located waterward of the Coast Smart Climate-Ready Action Boundary (CS-CRAB) must follow program guidelines.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit proposal through Grants Gateway portal at webportalapp.com/sp/login/grants_gateway. Proposals are reviewed based on completeness, local need, technical and financial feasibility, use of climate resources and tools, alignment with flood risk reduction strategies, community engagement, identified partners, and commitment to program change. Selected projects receive either direct grant funding or technical assistance from a DNR contractor. Technical guidance is provided through RSLR projections, flood impact assessment methodology, and adaptation options framework.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal competitive grant initiative under the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Act aimed at enhancing parks, recreational opportunities, and conservation areas in urban and underserved communities. Funds acquisition and development of parks and outdoor recreation areas, as well as renovation of existing facilities. Complements LWCF Stateside and Local Assistance Program formula grants. Supports public-private partnerships to leverage project support and empowers communities through local public greenspace investment, fostering resilience and sustainable landscape development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants for land acquisition and development of outdoor recreation facilities. Estimated range of $300,000 to $15,000,000 per award with 25-40 awards anticipated per calendar year. Requires 50% (1:1) non-federal cost share. Projects developed cooperatively between NPS and recipients. Applications undergo a two-stage process: pre-application review by DNR for eligibility and completeness, followed by full application submission to the National Park Service (NPS). Selection timeline: 3 months to selection, 15 months to award (dependent upon negotiations).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted anytime before June 1 and November 1 each year. Spring Round: April 15 (pre-applications to DNR), June 1 (full applications to NPS), September 1 (notification). Fall Round: September 15 (pre-applications to DNR), November 1 (full applications to NPS), February 1 (notification). All deadlines at 11:59 PM Eastern Time Zone.

Municipalities, parks departments, and non-profit organizations in Maryland communities with populations of 25,000 or more that are determined to be underserved.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition for new or expanded parks and recreation areas. Development and renovation of outdoor recreation facilities and amenities. Projects must align with state's Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan (SCORP). Maximum 25% of budget for non-physical development costs.

In Maryland, available statewide. Projects must be located in a community having a population of 25,000 or more in the 2020 Census and within a community determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications occur in two annual rounds with deadlines on June 1 and November 1 each year (11:59 PM Eastern Time Zone). For Spring Round: submit pre-applications to DNR by April 15 (DNR reviews for eligibility and completeness), submit full applications to NPS by June 1, receive notification by September 1 if moving to final application. For Fall Round: submit pre-applications to DNR by September 15, submit full applications to NPS by November 1, receive notification by February 1 if moving to final application. For technical submission difficulties, contact ORLP_Inquiries@nps.gov. For technical support, contact Grants.gov Customer Support at 1-800-518-4726. Contact Molly Pickel at 443-223-4302 or molly.pickel@maryland.gov to discuss potential projects and coordinate with DNR throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The PLANT Award (People Loving and Nurturing Trees) is a formal recognition program administered by the Maryland Forest Service that acknowledges Maryland communities demonstrating exceptional tree care, stewardship, planting, and promotion efforts. The program recognizes communities of all types and sizes—including schools, municipalities, homeowners associations, parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, civic groups, churches, and faith-based organizations—as an accessible entry point for building long-term urban and community forestry programs. Awards are offered at four levels: Bronze (for single events or one-time efforts such as tree plantings and Arbor Day activities), Silver (for communities beginning to organize such as forming tree committees or starting inventories), Gold (for communities actively managing their trees through policies and planning), and Green (for established programs with sustained effort and dedicated expertise). Participation provides statewide recognition and encourages continuous improvement in tree stewardship.

Participation provides statewide recognition and encourages continuous improvement in tree stewardship.

Nonresidents must provide proof of current state and federal falconry permits. The trapping season runs from September 20 through October 20, 2025, with a mandatory call-in system to report captures by 8 pm the day of capture.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 1969, Program Open Space Local is Maryland's flagship annual land conservation and recreation grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The program provides financial and technical assistance to local subdivisions (counties and municipalities) for the planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land and open space areas. Funds are allocated annually to the 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City based on a formula. POS Local supports projects to acquire and/or develop land for public recreation or open space, or planning projects to complete the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan. Eligible uses include planning, acquisition, and development of parks, forests, wildlife management areas, playgrounds, ball fields, tennis courts, boating facilities, swimming pools, fishing sites, hunting areas, golf courses, hiking trails, greenways, historic sites, and formal gardens. Development projects require a 10% or 25% local match based on the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan results. Acquisition and planning projects do not require a local match. Funding comes from a 0.5% state property transfer tax and federal funds from the U.S. Department of the Interior's Land and Water Conservation Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: POS Local funds are allocated annually to the 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City based on a formula. Grants may fund projects to acquire and/or develop land for public recreation or open space, or planning projects to complete the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan. Development projects require a 10% or 25% local match based on the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan results. Acquisition and planning projects do not require a local match. Development projects must have a minimum 20-year life span. Acquisition projects must be maintained in perpetuity. Grants are reimbursable, with partial project reimbursements and advances permitted on a case-by-case basis. Eligible uses include planning, acquisition, and development of parks, forests, wildlife management areas, playgrounds, ball fields, tennis courts, boating facilities, swimming pools, fishing sites, hunting areas, golf courses, hiking trails, greenways, historic sites, and formal gardens. Funding comes from a 0.5% state property transfer tax and federal funds from the U.S. Department of the Interior's Land and Water Conservation Fund, the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969, and the Land and Water Conservation Fund of the National Park Service. Up to 75% of appraised value of donated land can be used as matching share on development projects. Planning grants available up to $25,000 annually. Reimbursement available for contract costs, direct purchases, supplies, materials, services, equipment rental, in-house labor, and equipment for parks and playgrounds projects.

Grants are capital funds and cannot be used for operating and maintenance costs. Projects must be open and available to all users. Contract costs, direct purchases, supplies, materials, services, equipment rental, in-house labor, and equipment eligible for reimbursement. Infrastructure improvements including utilities, roads, water/sewer systems eligible. Trail and linear park development eligible. Acknowledgment signage costs eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participating jurisdictions must prepare and regularly update a Local Land Preservation, Parks, and Recreation Plan to remain eligible for annual grants. The proposed project must be included in the county's Annual Program for that fiscal year. Local governments develop projects and submit applications to DNR using available application and project agreement forms. A complete application is submitted to the Local Grants Administrator for review of completeness and consistency with program requirements. The application is then submitted to the State Clearinghouse and other DNR units for review. After reviews are complete, the project is scheduled on the next available Board of Public Works agenda. Individual projects must be brought to the Maryland Board of Public Works for approval before funds can be encumbered. For reimbursement requests, applicants submit Request for Reimbursement form with supporting documentation including invoices, proof of payment, and cost summaries. The entire process takes approximately 2-3 months or longer if there are questions or issues to resolve. Applicants should contact the Local Grants Administrator for information on the application process. Prepare and assemble required attachments before completing application. Contact POS Program Administrator for site inspection and application review. Refer to Program Open Space Grants Manual for detailed eligibility and requirements.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the Pumpout Operations and Maintenance Grant Application form available online. Submit application and maintain pumpout logs documenting usage. Contact pumpouts.dnr@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to receive mitigation funds for the incidental take of Puritan tiger beetles, a species listed as threatened and endangered by both state and federal government. Permits are required to alter habitat supporting this species, and if incidental take occurs, mitigation for that loss is required in order to obtain a permit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DNR receives mitigation funds from permit applicants when incidental take of Puritan tiger beetles occurs as a result of habitat alteration activities. Entities that alter habitat supporting this species and cause incidental take must provide mitigation funding as a condition of obtaining a permit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities seeking permits to alter habitat that supports Puritan tiger beetles
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mitigation for the incidental take and habitat loss of Puritan tiger beetles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - applicable in areas where Puritan tiger beetle habitat exists in Maryland
requirements_list: Permit required to alter habitat supporting Puritan tiger beetles
Mitigation required if incidental take occurs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact the Wildlife and Heritage Service to obtain the Puritan Tiger Beetle Habitat Conservation Program guidelines and submit mitigation funds as required by their permit conditions.

structured_extraction.program_name: RT-130 Annual Wildfire Safety Refresher and Work Capacity Test
structured_extraction.program_description: NWCG certified training courses offered by the Maryland Forest Service providing annual wildfire safety refresher training (RT-130) and work capacity physical fitness testing for Agency and Wildland Fire Crew members intending to participate in out-of-state fire crews. The Work Capacity (Pack) Test consists of a 3-mile hike wearing a 45-pound pack that must be completed in 45 minutes. RT-130 Annual Fireline Safety Refresher training is a 4-hour session. In-person training sessions are held at two Maryland locations: March 13, 2026 at Sandy Point State Park in Anne Arundel County and March 25, 2026 at Fort Frederick State Park in Washington County. Training is provided free of charge.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free NWCG certified training courses including RT-130 Annual Wildfire Safety Refresher and Work Capacity Test (Pack Test) offered at two locations in Maryland in March 2026: March 13 at Sandy Point State Park in Anne Arundel County and March 25 at Fort Frederick State Park in Washington County. Pack Test: 3-mile hike wearing 45-pound pack, must be completed in 45 minutes. RT-130 Annual Fireline Safety Refresher: 4-hour training session (12:30-16:30). Training includes annual wildfire safety refresher certification and physical fitness work capacity assessment for wildfire personnel.

Arrive 15 minutes prior to scheduled time slot.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit issued by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Wildlife and Heritage Service that allows the holder to establish and operate a regulated shooting area (RSA) where captive-raised game birds (pheasants, bobwhite quail, chukar partridge, Hungarian partridge, turkeys, and mallard ducks) can be released and shot. The permit is available for both commercial operations (open to the public) and non-commercial operations (closed to the public or with closed membership). Upon receipt of an application, a copy of a tax map showing the tract of land to be licensed, and payment of an annual fee of $150, the Wildlife and Heritage Service issues the permit, which is valid from the date of issuance until the following June 30. The Department may issue the permit after determining that establishment and operation does not conflict with public interest and will not have adverse impact on conservation of native game species.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Wildlife and Heritage Service issues a permit to operate a commercial or non-commercial regulated shooting area upon receipt of an application, a copy of a tax map showing the tract of land to be licensed, and payment of an annual fee of $150. The permit is valid from the date of issuance until the following June 30. The permit authorizes the licensee to raise and release properly marked, captive-raised birds on the designated tract of land. Retriever training may also occur on the premises at any time of the year. The department may issue the permit after determining that establishment and operation does not conflict with public interest and will not have adverse impact on conservation of native game species.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications to release free-flying mallard ducks must be received before September 1 annually; other applications may be made at any time. Annual reports are due by April 30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, and organizations seeking to establish and operate a regulated shooting area for captive-raised game birds in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The permit authorizes the establishment and operation of a regulated shooting area where captive-raised pheasants, bobwhite quail, chukar partridge, Hungarian partridge, turkeys, and mallard ducks may be released and shot on a licensed tract of land. Retriever training may also occur on the premises at any time of the year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The Department of Natural Resources may issue a permit after determining that the establishment and operation of the RSA does not conflict with any reasonable prior public interest and will not have adverse impact on the conservation of native game species. Applicants must provide a tax map clearly showing the tract of land to be licensed. Minimum 50 acres required for flighted mallard ducks; minimum 100 acres for all other species. Property must be in one tract or combined land and water.

Upon receipt of these materials, the Wildlife and Heritage Service may issue the permit. Requests can be submitted by email to wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, by phone at (410) 260-8540 or 1-877-620-8DNR (toll-free in Maryland), or by mail to Permits Coordinator, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service, 580 Taylor Ave., E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Appointments at the Tawes State Office Building can be scheduled by emailing wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov or calling (410) 260-8540. Applicants should consult the RSA Regulations for detailed application procedures, qualifications, and record-keeping requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A regulatory system that manages trees growing within public road rights-of-way, ensuring that tree work—including planting, pruning, and removal—is done safely, responsibly, and in accordance with state law.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides permitting and regulatory oversight for roadside tree work. Applicants must obtain a Roadside Tree Permit before performing any tree work in a public road right-of-way. The program offers two types of permits: Project Permits for individual tree work and Blanket Permits for entities responsible for routine or recurring maintenance. The Forest Service evaluates applications, conducts on-site inspections, and issues permits with conditions such as replanting or long-term maintenance requirements. The program also provides authorization for individuals to become Roadside Tree Experts through examination and training, enabling them to apply for permits and oversee tree care work. Approval is provided for tree care activities including removal, pruning, clearance from utilities, ground disturbance, root protection, pesticide use, and tree planting in roadside rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline stated; applications accepted on an ongoing basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, municipalities, utilities, landowners, governmental entities, tree care professionals, and authorized agents that need to perform tree work in public road rights-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permits allow for planting new trees, pruning existing trees, or removing trees that pose safety or health concerns in public road rights-of-way. Tree species selection for roadside planting from approved recommended list.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies statewide throughout Maryland. Important note: Residents of Montgomery County must contact the Montgomery County Permits Office at (240) 777-6335 to obtain the county's roadside tree permit.

Public agency employees must pass Maryland Public Agency Roadside Tree Care Expert exam (70% score; 98 of 140 questions).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Roadside Tree Permit Application form. 2. Mail or deliver the completed application along with payment to your local Forest Service office. 3. A Forest Ranger from the local DNR Project Office will conduct an on-site inspection of the tree(s). 4. The Forest Ranger may contact the applicant for additional information or to suggest modifications. 5. If approved, a permit is issued by mail or email. If denied, a written denial notice is sent with reasons and appeal instructions. 6. Applicants may request a formal appeal within 10 working days of denial by submitting a cover letter requesting reevaluation, a detailed explanation of new or omitted information, and a copy of the original denied application to the Project Manager. For Roadside Tree Care Expert certification: Attend preparatory course (offered annually per region), study the provided guide, and pass the 140-question exam.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive grant program designed to help Maryland adapt to climate change by enhancing nature's ability to store carbon and buffer climate impacts. The program funds construction, design/build, and design proposals for living shoreline restoration projects, which are nature-based coastal protection structures that use vegetation, wood, and stone to stabilize shorelines while providing habitat benefits. The initiative also supports tree planting, marsh restoration, and community engagement activities. Living shorelines are prioritized over structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments. The program focuses on large-scale projects that protect substantial areas of adjacent wetland and tidal marsh habitat, with a collective target of 400 acres of high quality tidal marsh protection. Funding is available through open solicitations for organizations, entities, and property owners throughout Maryland and specifically on the Lower Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded through a Request for Proposals process to support living shoreline restoration projects and broader climate resilience activities. The program funds construction, design/build, and design proposals for living shoreline projects. The living shoreline component aims to award large-scale projects that collectively protect a total of 400 acres of adjacent high quality tidal marsh habitat. Broader program funding also supports tree planting, marsh restoration, and community engagement activities. Total funding available is $17 million with a minimum request of $1 million (smaller design-only requests may be allowed with DNR approval). No match requirement; leveraged funds are encouraged. Project period runs from July 2026 to August 2029. Specific funding amounts and phase availability are detailed in open solicitations. Applicants submit proposals through a Request for Proposals process and respond to required narrative questions. Details vary by solicitation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 6, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET for living shoreline projects
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, entities, and property owners implementing climate resilience and living shoreline projects on Maryland's Lower Eastern Shore and throughout the state, including non-profits, for-profits, government entities, local jurisdictions, and institutions of higher education seeking to provide community resilience benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for living shoreline construction, design/build, and design proposals that provide erosion control and coastal protection while protecting adjacent wetland and tidal marsh habitat, as well as tree planting, coastal habitat restoration, and community engagement activities to enhance carbon storage and buffer climate impacts. Allowable expenses include design and engineering services, permit application fees and documentation, community engagement and coordination, contractor/consultant services, native plants/vegetation and project materials, staff time directly associated with project work, and indirect costs per federal NICRA or de minimis rate.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Living shoreline projects must be located in the Chesapeake Bay portions of Dorchester, Somerset, or Wicomico Counties on Maryland's Lower Eastern Shore. Proposed projects must be in eligible zones as shown on the project targeting map. Sites must have active erosion, and projects must protect extensive adjacent high-quality tidal marsh habitat.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit proposals through a Request for Proposals process. Applicants can reference the budget template and landowner agreement template provided. Site visits can be requested by contacting the program coordinator. Visit the Roots for Resilience Open Solicitations page at dnr.maryland.gov/climateresilience/Pages/Roots-for-Resilience-Open-Solicitations.aspx to learn more about current opportunities and application requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Schoolyard Forests Program is a Five Million Trees partnership initiative with the Maryland Association of Environmental & Outdoor Education that helps schools create outdoor spaces supporting student well-being, enrich learning, and strengthen connections to the natural world. The program promotes healthier campus landscapes with nature access for students of all backgrounds and develops partnerships with municipalities, schools, and students to increase tree canopy cover, create nature discovery pathways, and support local climate resiliency. Schools receive campus planning and technical support to identify opportunities for improving outdoor spaces and caring for existing trees. The program offers hands-on assistance and training for facilities teams, teachers, and staff to build comfort and confidence with long-term stewardship. Educational and student-centered opportunities integrate outdoor learning into the school day through campus mapping, nature-based activities, seed collection, and environmental literacy projects. The program provides engagement and celebration events including Earth Month and Arbor Day programs, youth career exploration through demonstrations and experiences, and microgrants and classroom support materials for schools advancing toward Green School certification or developing outdoor projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free forestry and landscaping services including: teacher workshops, landscape stewardship manual, specimen tree inventory and mapping, Arbor Day and Earth Day activities, forest health assessments, professional development and continuing education, hazard tree evaluation and removal, native tree planting, edible food plots, and summer tree maintenance. Schools may receive campus planning and technical support to identify opportunities for improving outdoor spaces and caring for existing trees. The program offers hands-on assistance and training for facilities teams, teachers, and staff to build comfort and confidence with long-term stewardship. Educational and student-centered opportunities integrate outdoor learning into the school day through campus mapping, nature-based activities, seed collection, and environmental literacy projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; formal application process being developed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public school students and staff across Maryland of all backgrounds. District-level facility teams and community partners working directly with school campuses are also welcome.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree canopy increase, nature pathways, climate resiliency, tree planting, landscaping, forest health assessments, educational activities, stewardship training, engagement events, youth career exploration, campus mapping, nature-based activities, seed collection, environmental literacy projects, Earth Month and Arbor Day programs, and classroom support materials for schools advancing toward Green School certification or developing outdoor projects.

Online application is available at https://marylandforestservice.submittable.com/submit/341708/schoolyard-forests-application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Permit/license for scientific collection of wildlife species in Maryland. Allows properly accredited persons of known scientific attainment to collect wildlife, nests, or eggs from the wild for scientific or educational purposes. The permit also covers capture, mark, and release of wildlife, and allows public educational institutions to salvage wildlife and maintain specimens for educational purposes. The permit is issued for one calendar year (valid through December 31 of the issuing year) and requires a $10 fee. An annual report must be filed by December 31 of the issuing year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A permit/license that authorizes the holder to collect wildlife, nests, and eggs from the wild for scientific or educational purposes, and to capture, mark, and release wildlife. The permit is valid through December 31 of the issuing year. A $10 fee is required. An annual report must be filed by December 31 of the issuing year; failure to submit may result in revocation of permits or rejection of future applications. Federal permits from USFWS and/or USDA may be required for collection of migratory birds or federally listed species.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Collection of wildlife, nests, or eggs from the wild for scientific or educational purposes; capture, mark, and release of wildlife; salvage of wildlife; and maintenance of specimens for educational purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Applicant must specify county and specific areas where collection will take place.

structured_extraction.program_description: A six-week educational program for senior citizens offered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Participants learn about plants, animals, park rangers, conservation, history, and stewardship through expert-led talks, exercise, fellowship, games, and hikes led by rangers, historians, naturalists, and DNR experts. Sessions are held at various state parks and natural resource management areas across Maryland. Program activities include herpetile exploration, birding basics, knot-tying, yoga, paddle trips, canoeing/kayaking, tree planting, stargazing, historic tours, and edible trail tours. Participants who complete all six weekly sessions become certified Senior Rangers and are invited to a statewide gathering.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six-week educational program consisting of weekly sessions (typically two hours per session) at various state parks and natural resource management areas across Maryland. Sessions include expert-led talks, exercise, fellowship, games, and outdoor hikes featuring nature exploration, outdoor skills, and fitness activities. Program fee of $40 ($30 for Golden Age Passholders). Participants who complete all six sessions become certified Senior Rangers and are invited to a statewide gathering. No direct financial assistance is provided beyond the program itself.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens April 1 for 2026 sessions. Spring sessions typically close in late April, fall sessions in September.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens age 55 and older interested in learning about parks and nature and staying active. Golden Age Passholders are eligible for program fee discounts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational sessions covering plants, animals, park rangers, conservation, history, stewardship, nature exploration, outdoor skills, and fitness through expert-led talks, exercise, games, hikes, birding, yoga, paddle trips, canoeing/kayaking, tree planting, stargazing, and historic tours. Program participation fee is $40 (or $30 with Golden Age Passholder discount).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at multiple Maryland state parks and natural resource management areas including Seneca Creek State Park, Bohemia River State Park, Elk Neck State Park (Chesapeake City and North East), Patapsco Valley State Park, Fair Hill NRMA, Tuckahoe State Park complex, White Marsh Park, Southern Maryland Recreational Complex (Calvert Cliffs State Park and Merkle NRMA), Janes Island State Park, and Eastern Shore parks (Martinak, Sassafrass, and Wye Island). Specific park locations: Bohemia River State Park at 4030 Augustine Herman Hwy, Chesapeake City, MD; Elk Neck State Park Nature Center at 242 Thackery Point Rd, North East, MD 21901.
