Space is limited and availability varies by park and session date. Registration opens April 1 for spring sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides technical and financial assistance to landowners and organizations for completing structural and non-structural shore erosion control and streambank restoration projects, including living shoreline restoration projects along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries, as well as other bodies of water throughout Maryland. Non-structural projects use bioengineering to create protective vegetative buffers, while structural projects are used in areas with high erosion rates. Assistance includes design, site evaluations, problem assessments, recommended solutions, and guidance on project planning and implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for non-structural projects awarded in the form of short-term loans and matching grants. Specifically: 75% interest-free loans for projects on private and public lands using State special funds; 75%-25% matching grants for projects on public lands using Federal funds. Technical assistance includes site evaluations, problem assessments, recommended solutions, and guidance on project planning and implementation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and organizations abutting bodies of water in Maryland seeking assistance with streambank or shoreline erosion control and living shoreline restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, construction, management and financing of streambank or shoreline erosion control projects using structural or non-structural techniques, and living shoreline and restoration projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any property owner or organization with property abutting a body of water in Maryland, including properties along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Statewide coverage.
requirements_list: Property must abut a body of water in Maryland
Owner or organization must file an application requesting assistance
Property may be on private or public lands
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owner or organization files an application requesting assistance in the design, construction, management and financing of a streambank or shoreline erosion control project or living shoreline restoration project. The program provides technical assistance through site evaluations and problem assessments. Financial assistance is awarded as loans and grants upon approval. Contact Wesley Gould or the designated program manager to learn if your project qualifies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides technical and financial assistance to waterfront property owners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, counties and municipalities experiencing shoreline erosion. The program offers 0% interest loans for living shoreline projects to help protect properties from shoreline erosion and control shore erosion along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Loans are available to individuals, groups of homeowners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, and counties. The program finances the construction and implementation of living shoreline projects using techniques and materials such as sand, native plants, rock, headland breakwaters, sills, groins, and biologs. Technical support is provided through site visit evaluations and problem assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% interest loans for living shoreline projects. Loan terms range from 5 to 20 years depending on the techniques implemented and associated costs. For individuals and groups of homeowners, a cash contribution is required only for loans greater than $60,000. Each loan includes an administrative fee ranging from 3% to 10% based on project construction cost. Funds are dispersed as work is completed, with the loan applicant receiving distributions upon providing proof of payment to the department. A county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district or shore erosion control lien must be established. Technical support includes site visit evaluations and problem assessments for shoreline erosion issues.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Waterfront property owners, individuals and groups of homeowners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, counties and municipalities experiencing shoreline erosion along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living shoreline construction, design, and implementation to protect shorelines from erosion while maintaining natural coastal processes and protecting or creating natural habitat. Materials eligible for funding include sand, native plants, rock, headland breakwaters, sills, groins, and biologs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for shoreline properties along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries in Maryland.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include individuals, groups of homeowners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, and counties
For individuals and groups of homeowners, cash contribution required only for loans exceeding $60,000
A county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district or shore erosion control lien must be established
Applicants must provide proof of payment to the department for fund dispersals
Property must be experiencing shoreline erosion
Work must be below the average high tide line in tidal wetlands or tidewater
Living shoreline techniques must be used; structural solutions such as bulkheads and revetments are not funded
Must be addressing shoreline erosion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the MD DNR Grants Gateway. Interested applicants can fill out a technical assistance request form to indicate interest in the Shoreline Erosion Control Revolving Loan Fund. The department assists with establishing the required county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district or lien. Applicants receive site visit evaluations and problem assessments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Solar Generation Facilities - Pollinator-Friendly Designation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Enables the Department of Natural Resources to certify photovoltaic ground-mounted solar facilities greater than 1 acre as pollinator-friendly. Developed through Ch. 372, Acts of 2017, informed by the Power Plant Research Program's Pollinator Work Group with stakeholders including beekeepers, renewable energy developers, DNR's Wildlife and Heritage Service, University of Maryland, USFWS, USGS, and Maryland Farm Bureau. Developers can apply to have their facilities certified as pollinator-friendly, which involves submitting an application with facility information and a pollinator habitat management plan, undergoing site inspection by a DNR-approved inspector, and managing the site according to approved practices. Upon approval, the certification is valid for two years and can be renewed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides certification and recognition for solar facilities that meet pollinator-friendly standards. Developers must submit an application with facility information and a pollinator habitat management plan, use an appropriate seed mix for the Maryland region, undergo site inspection by a DNR-approved inspector, and submit a final assessment scorecard and management plan. Upon approval, the certification is valid for two years and can be renewed within 90 days of expiration. The program involves technical guidance on habitat management but does not provide direct financial assistance. A written letter from the Department designates that a solar generation facility is pollinator-friendly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of solar generation facilities (proposed or existing ground-mounted photovoltaic facilities) located in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program is not a funding program. It provides certification and technical assistance for implementing pollinator-friendly habitat management at solar facilities. Applicants must use Maryland region-appropriate seed mixes for their pollinator habitat management plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for ground-mounted photovoltaic solar generation facilities at least 1 acre in size located anywhere in Maryland. Developers must use seed mixes appropriate for their specific Maryland region.
requirements_list: Facility must be photovoltaic, ground-mounted, and at least 1 acre in size
Submit application to Power Plant Research Program with facility name, location, tax map information, acreage, contact details, and brief facility description
Include a pollinator habitat management plan with application
Use a seed mix appropriate for the Maryland region
Undergo site inspection and review by a DNR-approved site inspector
Submit final Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning and Assessment Scorecard within 30 days of site inspection completion
Submit final pollinator habitat management plan and letter from site inspector confirming site has been planted and managed in accordance with habitat plan
Site must be planted and managed in accordance with approved habitat plan prior to certification
Respond to any Department requests for additional information within 30 days or application will be terminated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers submit an application to pprp@maryland.gov with facility information and a proposed pollinator habitat management plan. The Department reviews the application and the site undergoes inspection by a DNR-approved inspector. Following site inspection, the developer must submit a final scorecard, management plan, and inspector letter within 30 days. Upon approval, the facility receives pollinator-friendly designation (written letter from the Department) valid for two years. Renewal can be requested within 90 days of certification expiration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Special Rivers Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A water quality improvement program funded by the US Environmental Protection Agency since 1983 to encourage restoration, enhancement, and management of forests in the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The program supports riparian forest buffer restoration, watershed planning, stream corridor restoration, land conservation, stewardship, and community engagement. It implements technical assistance and funding for riparian forest buffer restoration (at least 30 miles per year), forest stewardship planning for private and public forests (at least 1,800 acres per year), and education and outreach on forest benefits for watersheds and water quality (reaching at least 600 people per year including students, general public, and resource professionals).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance and funding for riparian forest buffer restoration and maintenance (at least 30 miles per year), forest stewardship planning for private and public forests (at least 1,800 acres per year), and education and outreach on forest benefits for watersheds and water quality (reaching at least 600 people per year including students, general public, and resource professionals).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, communities, students, resource professionals, and organizations in the Chesapeake Bay watershed interested in forest restoration and watershed management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Riparian forest buffer establishment and maintenance, forest stewardship planning, stream corridor restoration, land conservation, and education and outreach programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four project areas: Susquehanna area watersheds (Elk River in Cecil County to upper and middle Patuxent watersheds in Howard and Montgomery County, including Deer Creek, Bush River, Gunpowder, Jones Falls, Gwynns Falls, and Patapsco watersheds in Baltimore, Carroll, and Harford Counties), Monocacy area watersheds (Upper and Lower Monocacy, Double Pipe, Catoctin, Antietam, Conococheague, Licking Creek and adjacent direct drainages to the Potomac River in Montgomery, Howard, and Frederick counties), Anacostia/West Chesapeake area (portions of Prince George's, Montgomery, and Anne Arundel Counties), and Town Creek Ecosystem Management Project (Allegany County, Maryland and Bedford County, Pennsylvania).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners and organizations can work with local foresters to develop forest stewardship plans and participate in riparian buffer restoration projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Park Day-Use Area Admission Fee Waiver for Active Duty Military and Maryland National Guard
structured_extraction.program_description: Members of the Maryland National Guard and active duty military personnel receive a waiver of day-use entrance service charges at Maryland state parks when displaying their active duty military identification card to the gate attendant. The waiver applies to the military identification card holder only. Other facility service charges are not waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Day-use entrance fees are waived at all Maryland state parks for eligible active duty military personnel and Maryland National Guard members. The waiver applies to the military identification card holder only. No other facility service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active duty military personnel and Maryland National Guard members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Day-use admission to Maryland state parks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland state parks statewide.
requirements_list: Must be active duty military personnel or a member of the Maryland National Guard
Must display active duty military identification card at the gate attendant
Waiver applies to identification card holder only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Display active duty military identification card to the gate attendant at any Maryland state park day-use area to receive the waiver.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Park Day-Use Area Admission Fee Waiver for Veterans
structured_extraction.program_description: All applicable day-use entrance charges are waived for veterans of the United States Armed Forces at Maryland state parks. The waiver applies to the veteran only unless a per-vehicle charge is in effect, in which case the per-vehicle fee is waived. This waiver is available to both resident and out-of-state veterans. Other facility use service charges are not waived.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Day-use entrance fees are waived at all Maryland state parks for eligible veterans. The waiver covers the veteran only unless a per-vehicle charge applies, in which case the per-vehicle fee is waived. No other facility use service charges are waived.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans of the United States Armed Forces, both Maryland residents and out-of-state veterans
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Day-use admission to Maryland state parks
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland state parks statewide. Open to both resident and out-of-state veterans.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran of the United States Armed Forces
Waiver applies to veteran only, not others in the same vehicle unless per-vehicle charge is in effect
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Present veteran status verification at the gate attendant at any Maryland state park day-use area to receive the waiver.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 1966 to fund projects that improve and promote recreational and commercial capabilities, conditions, and safety of Maryland's waterways for the benefit of the general boating public. Provides financial support to local governments and public jurisdictions for capital projects and services benefiting the boating public in Maryland, including constructing or renovating boating access facilities, dredging high-use channels and harbors, purchasing fire and rescue vessels, ice breaking, navigation aids, derelict boat and debris removal, clean marina management, marine sewage pumpout program services, shore erosion control, and boating safety services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple grant types and interest-free long-term loans for waterway improvement projects. Grant programs include: 100% Local Government Grants (up to $500,000); 100% State Grants for specific projects; Dredging Grants (100% or with 50/50 match); Matching Fund Grants (50/50 cost share); Marine Fire/Rescue Grants (max $80,000 state cost share); Small Project Grants (not to exceed $25,000). Interest-Free Long-Term Dredging Loans available (up to 25 years). Funding supports construction, renovation, maintenance of boating access facilities; dredging channels and harbors; purchase of fire and rescue vessels in partnership with local fire companies; marking channels and harbors; aids to navigation; clearing debris and obstructions; construction of jetties and breakwaters; design and construction of dredge material placement and beneficial use. Applications submitted through Grants Gateway within Outcome 5, typically between July and September for the following fiscal year funding consideration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Usually July through mid-September (annual solicitation); funds become available July 1st of each fiscal year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Carla Fleming; Matt Negley; Jennifer Jackson; Isaac Wilding; Jillian Seagraves
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and public jurisdictions in Maryland, county and municipal governments, volunteer fire departments, emergency response organizations, federal agencies, and the general boating public seeking to improve boating infrastructure, navigation, access, safety, and waterway conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, renovation, and maintenance of boating access facilities; dredging channels and harbors; purchase of fire and rescue vessels in partnership with local fire companies; ice breaking; navigation aids and marking channels; derelict boat and debris removal; construction of jetties and breakwaters; clean marina management; marine sewage pumpout program services; shore erosion control; boating safety services; design and construction of dredge material placement and beneficial use; engineering and permitting costs; clearing debris and obstructions from navigable waters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland jurisdictions. Established under Annotated Code of Maryland Section 8-707 of the State Boat Act. Regional staff contacts available based on county location. Eastern Region covers Caroline, Queen Anne's, Kent, Talbot, Dorchester, Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties. Southern Region covers Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties. Central and Western Regions cover Baltimore City and County, Carroll, Cecil, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Frederick, Washington, Allegany, and Garrett counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, public jurisdiction, county government, town government, city government, state agency, or federal agency
Projects must benefit the general boating public
Projects must meet priorities of motorized and commercial boating public
For fire and rescue vessels, partnership with local fire companies required or authorized volunteer fire department/emergency response organization
Applications submitted through Grants Gateway within Outcome 5
All necessary federal, state, and local permits must be obtained before construction
Plans, specifications, and changes require DNR review and approval
Licensed Marine Contractor required for tidal wetlands projects
Applicant must operate and maintain the project long-term
Projects must be ready to proceed to construction
Small project grants not to exceed $25,000; Marine Fire/Rescue state share not to exceed $80,000
Grant period typically not to exceed 1 year; unused balances revert after one year unless extended
Bid solicitation and DNR approval required
For dredging projects: submit completed Dredging/Navigation Needs & Benefits Form with supporting documentation including boat count surveys, satellite photos, photographs, boat ramp launch receipts
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local governments create a user profile in Grants Gateway and submit applications within Outcome 5, typically between July and mid-September for the following fiscal year funding consideration. Applicants work with regional staff contacts based on their county location. For dredging projects, submit completed Dredging/Navigation Needs & Benefits Form with supporting documentation including boat count field surveys, satellite photos, photographs of boat ramps and facilities, and launch receipts. Contact the designated grant program manager to learn if your project qualifies. For construction projects, submit bid solicitation to DNR for approval, obtain required permits, provide contract documentation and plans/specifications, and coordinate inspections. Reimbursement requests require transmittal letter on official letterhead, Request for Reimbursement Form per project, copies of invoices with payment evidence, documentation of in-house labor and equipment, most recent grantee checklist, and photographs for final reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A do-it-yourself pheasant hunting opportunity offered on public lands across Maryland where pheasants are stocked for eligible hunters to hunt during specified dates. The program provides access to pheasants stocked on designated public lands and is free to participate in. Selected participants receive a permit letter and map showing the specific release area where pheasants are stocked. Hunters supply their own gear and firearms and are responsible for obtaining a required hunting license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides stocked pheasants on public lands for hunting at no cost. Selected participants receive a permit letter and map showing the specific release area where pheasants are stocked. Hunters supply their own gear and firearms and are responsible for obtaining a required hunting license. The program is free to participate in and there is no cost to apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth (junior) hunters, apprentice hunters, first-time full season license buyers, and lapsed hunters (those who have not purchased a hunting license in three of the last five years).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants use the assistance to hunt stocked pheasants on designated public lands. Hunters must supply their own firearms, gear, and hunting license.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public lands across the state of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a youth (junior) hunter, apprentice hunter, first-time full season license buyer, or lapsed hunter
Lapsed hunter defined as one who has held a Maryland hunting license in the past but has not purchased a hunting license in three of the last five years
Must have Hunter Education certification
Must have a current hunting license or Apprentice License
Must follow all small game hunting regulations and shooting hours
Must supply own gear and firearms
Only selected individual can carry and use firearm
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants log into their MD Outdoors account and enter the lottery. If no account exists, one must be created at no charge. Applicants select first, second, and third location choices and one of two hunt days (November 22 or 23, 2025). A random drawing is held and selected applicants are notified by email by October 31, 2025. Winners receive a permit letter and map showing the pheasant release area. Selected applicants are also listed on the webpage by their DNRId.

structured_extraction.program_name: Strategic Framing for Climate Change Communication
structured_extraction.program_description: A two-day in-person training program that teaches strategic framing as a communication approach to engage audiences in thinking about how to create or support climate change solutions. Participants learn about strategic framing, values, and solutions while developing ability to clearly and confidently communicate climate change issues. Instruction is provided by National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) facilitators from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two-day in-person training program focusing on strategic framing, values, and solutions to improve participants' ability to communicate about climate change clearly and confidently. Facilitated by NNOCCI experts from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community leaders, educators, communicators, and professionals who address climate change and want to communicate about climate change solutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in strategic communication approaches and framing techniques for climate change.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact program administrator for enrollment and scheduling. Instruction provided by NNOCCI facilitators from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program where classroom teachers, environmental education centers, nature centers, and schools raise hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish with hands-on aquatic science lessons aligned with NGSS and Maryland Environmental literacy standards. Participants raise fish in classrooms from October through May, conduct lessons using provided curriculum materials, and then release the fish at approved sites in late spring. The program includes an optional aquaponics component. The Maryland Department of Natural Resources supplies starter and replacement aquarium supply kits, fish, food, teacher's manual, lesson plans, and data sheets. DNR also reimburses 50% of bus transportation costs (maximum 3 buses) and 100% of substitute teacher costs (maximum 3 substitutes) for the spring release event, subject to annual budget availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides starter and replacement aquarium supply kits (subject to annual budget and availability on a first-come-first-serve basis), hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish and fish food, a teacher's manual and data sheet, lesson plans and background information aligned with state standards, educational curriculum materials including worksheets and activity cards, and reimbursement for fish release trip costs including 50 percent of bus costs (maximum 3 buses) and 100 percent of substitute teacher costs (maximum 3 substitutes). DNR also funds substitute teacher coverage for mandatory training workshops. Optional aquaponics materials are included in the training component.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, nature centers, schools, and non-formal educators seeking to provide hands-on aquatic science education to K-12 students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fish and aquarium supplies for classroom-based aquatic science education, teacher training and lesson resources, aquaponics materials, and reimbursement for costs associated with releasing fish at approved sites including substitute teacher hours and bus transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to schools and education centers throughout Maryland (all 24 counties eligible). Fish pickup locations are offered in Baltimore County, Frederick County, and Prince George's County, with additional options at the Cedarville Fish Hatchery in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, environmental education center, nature center, or school
New participants must attend mandatory teacher training workshop (held every 3 years for returning participants)
Must register annually by May 15th
Must pick up fish on designated days in October
Must conduct lessons and raise fish from October through May
Must maintain water quality parameters: Total Ammonia <2.5ppm, Unionized Ammonia <0.12ppm, Nitrite and Nitrate <40ppm, pH 6.5-8.5, Temperature 65-80°F
Must inventory materials upon receipt and report missing/broken items immediately
Must release fish by June 30th at an approved release site or request permission to keep longer
Must return all equipment to Maryland DNR in Annapolis if discontinuing program
Must submit required demographic form via Google Form by deadline or lose eligibility for following year
Must follow aquatic studies permitting guidelines
Must submit reimbursement documentation by June 30th with itemized expenses and receipts
Must complete ARE reporting form by July 31st
School Principal signature and certification required for reimbursement claims
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teachers and education centers register annually by submitting the registration form by May 15th. Acceptance is first-come-first-serve based on budget availability with decisions made after the May 15 deadline. New participants and those due for refresher training must attend the mandatory teacher training workshop (required every 3 years). Participants pick up aquarium supplies, bluegill fish, and food on one of two designated October dates or at alternate locations. Teachers conduct lessons with students during the October-May period using provided curriculum materials and maintain water quality records. In late May or early June, participants organize fish release events at approved sites (DNR staff assistance available with minimum 2 weeks advance notice). Participants submit reimbursement documentation with itemized expenses and receipts on organization letterhead by June 30th, with required School Principal signature and certification. Finally, participants complete the ARE reporting form by July 31st. Required demographic form must be submitted annually via Google Form to maintain eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A no-cost program that provides free fishing gear for loan at various locations throughout Maryland. The program is designed to help new anglers and their families build confidence and skills while enjoying Maryland's outdoors. Participants can borrow basic fishing equipment including rod and reel setups at public libraries, state parks, nature centers, and local parks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of basic fishing gear including rod and reel setup with bobber, split shot sinker, swivel, and hook. Availability varies by site. Some sites allow multi-day loans. Individual loans and group programs are available at various locations. Borrowers must complete a registration form and return the equipment on the agreed return date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, families, and groups interested in learning to fish. Particularly designed for new anglers and those who want to try fishing without purchasing equipment. Kids under 16 do not need a fishing license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing fishing gear for recreational fishing. Equipment can be used on-site or off-site depending on the loaner location's policies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple locations throughout Maryland including state parks, public libraries, nature centers, and local parks across various counties. See detailed location table for specific sites and their service areas.
requirements_list: Complete the Tackle Loaner borrower registration form
Provide your own bait
Return equipment by agreed return date
Contact site directly to confirm procedures and availability
Group programs require reservations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Find a nearby loaner site from the available locations list. 2. Complete the Tackle Loaner borrower form. 3. Visit the chosen site to check out the fishing gear. 4. Go fishing with the borrowed equipment. 5. Return the equipment to the site on the agreed return date. It is recommended to call ahead to confirm availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national program administered through the American Tree Farm System that recognizes and certifies private forest owners committed to sustainable forestry. The program provides professional sustainable forest certification, educational resources, networking opportunities, and technical guidance for landowners managing their forests for water quality, wildlife habitat, soil conservation, biodiversity, and recreation while producing forest products. Participants receive certification of their woodlot as sustainably managed, periodic free inspections and consultations with certified professional foresters, information and updates on legislative issues, access to woodland management resources including MyLand Plan, participation in national awards programs, and recognition programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides professional sustainable forest certification at no cost to members. Landowners receive free periodic inspections and consultations with certified professional foresters, information and updates on legislative issues affecting forest owners, participation in national awards programs, and access to woodland management resources including MyLand Plan. There is no cost for membership.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners in Maryland who own 10 or more acres of forested land and are committed to sustainable forestry practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide financial assistance or funding. It offers professional certification, technical guidance on forest management, and networking to support sustainable forestry practices that balance wood production with environmental stewardship, including forest product harvesting, water quality, wildlife habitat, soil conservation, biodiversity, and recreation opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. The program currently includes 964 tree farmers in Maryland (757 certified) managing nearly 110,000 acres. Landowners must contact their local Maryland Forest Service office.
requirements_list: Own 10 or more acres of forested land
Have a written and implemented forest management plan that accounts for forest product production, water quality, wildlife habitat, soil conservation, biodiversity, and recreation opportunities

Meet the Standards of Sustainability including commitment to practicing sustainable forestry, compliance with laws, reforestation and afforestation, air/water/soil protection, fish/wildlife/biodiversity conservation, forest aesthetics, protection of special sites, and conducting forest product harvests according to a management plan
Submit to inspection by a certified tree farm inspector on a five-year cycle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office to inquire if your property qualifies as a Tree Farm. If you meet the criteria, a free inspection of your land can be arranged by contacting a certified inspecting forester in your area. A listing of certified foresters will be provided by the local office. You can also visit the American Tree Farm System website for additional program information. The State Tree Farm Committee will certify your woodlot as a sustainably managed Tree Farm once you meet the Standards of Sustainability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Cost-effective reforestation or afforestation projects on qualifying agricultural land. Supports Maryland's goal of planting and maintaining 5 million sustainable native trees by 2031. Increases tree canopy, creates forest habitat, provides livestock shade, improves water quality, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small-scale projects (less than 2 acres): maximum $10,000. Large-scale projects (greater than 2 acres): maximum $50,000. Funds are to be used from March 30, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners and land managers seeking to plant trees on agricultural lands in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting design and plan development, permit acquisition, planting activities (contractual or volunteer services), and monitoring and maintenance for first two years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural lands throughout Maryland (statewide).
requirements_list: Complete planting design and plan
Obtain required permits
Provide planting activities
Provide monitoring and maintenance for first two years with survivorship rate per Maryland State Forest Conservation Technical Manual (Third Edition, 1997)
Projects on individual private, commercial private, community-owned, nonprofit, and government-owned property are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust portal. Application period opens September 1 with a December 1 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that helps Maryland citizens and communities restore tree cover on public land and community open space. The program provides access to affordable native trees for planting at schools, parks, streets, and other public areas. Citizens and organizations can make gifts of trees to be planted in honor or memory of individuals or for special occasions, or purchase quality native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery partnership. Individuals can purchase gift trees at $40 per tree or a grove of ten trees for $400. Free delivery is available to three locations across the state each spring and fall, with direct delivery to sites available for an additional fee. Trees are planted during the next appropriate growing season and, when possible, in the county where recipients live.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides quality native trees at reduced cost through a wholesale nursery partnership and allows citizens to make gifts of trees to be planted on public lands and open spaces. Individuals can purchase gift trees at $40 per tree or a grove of ten trees for $400. Free delivery is available to three locations across the state each spring and fall. Groups can arrange direct delivery to their site for an additional fee. Trees are planted during the next appropriate growing season.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least one week before desired certificate arrival date for Gift of Trees orders
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents, local governments, community groups, schools, parks, volunteer organizations, and individuals interested in planting trees on public land and community open space, including those who want to give trees as gifts to be planted on public lands or to honor or celebrate family and friends.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and planting native trees and shrubs on public lands, schools, parks, playgrounds, schoolyards, streets, and along creeks and streams; trees can be planted in honor or memory of individuals or for special occasions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland on public lands and open spaces. Free delivery provided to three locations across the state each spring and fall.
requirements_list: Organization must have permission from land owners to plant trees
Trees must be planted on public land or community open space
Organization must complete the Tree-Mendous order form
Order must be placed at least one week before the desired certificate delivery date
Organization must qualify to order from Tree-Mendous program
For Gift of Trees, plantings generally occur on public lands and community spaces in areas of greatest need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in ordering trees should send their organization's information and location to ryan.mayenschein@maryland.gov to request access to the password-protected order form. The order form is an agreement between the program and the organization to plant quality native trees on public land. Individuals and organizations can also contact the Tree-Mendous Maryland Program to make a gift of trees for planting on public lands. Individuals can fill out and submit a separate order form for each gift recipient. A certificate suitable for framing is mailed to the recipient within a week of the order. Trees are planted during the next appropriate growing season (spring or fall).

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program that provides financial aid, starter kits, chiller equipment, hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs, fish food, and reimbursement for fish release trip costs to help classroom teachers, environmental education centers, nature centers, and higher education institutions raise trout and conduct aquatic resources lessons with students in grades K-12. Students raise trout from eggs to fingerlings with hands-on learning aligned with NGSS, Common Core standards, and Maryland Environmental literacy standards. Educators collaborate with the Potomac-Patuxent Chapter of Trout Unlimited and the Department of Natural Resources Aquatic Resources Education program. Educational materials cover topics including trout anatomy, water quality, macroinvertebrates, fish populations, human health, and invasive species. Students release their trout into state-approved cold water streams or lakes. The program introduces youth to cold water conservation as a first step toward becoming future protectors and advocates for clean and healthy streams, lakes, and rivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial aid for schools as the budget allows, including one starter kit and one chiller per new school (starter kit costs approximately $700 not including chiller), one replacement kit for returning schools (approximately $220), hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs and fish food. DNR provides tanks, chillers, trout, and educational materials to participating classrooms. Reimbursement covers 50 percent of total bus costs (maximum of 3 buses) and 100 percent of substitute teacher costs (maximum of 3 substitutes) for fish release trips, subject to availability. DNR-funded equipment provided if school qualifies; teacher training; technical advisory support; volunteer network support; priority support for first two years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens January 1st; Memorandum of Intent deadline March 15th; Invoice packages due June 30th; Reporting form due July 31st. Last day to submit funding request: March 15, 2026; New teacher seminar: Saturday, October 24, 2026; Pre-cycling tank deadline: November 12, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, nature centers, and higher education institutions serving students in grades K-12. Students grades 3-12, educators, school administrators, visitors, and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports classroom aquatic resources education including raising trout, conducting science lessons aligned with NGSS, Common Core, and Maryland Environmental literacy standards, educational activities covering trout anatomy, water quality, macroinvertebrates, fish populations, human health, and invasive species, and organizing fish release events at approved sites. School provides: insulation board, surge power strip, buckets, measuring spoons, pipettes, baking soda, safety glasses, turkey baster, towels. Optional supplies: gloves, algae scraper, tweezers. Annual replacement. Approved expenses for substitute teachers, bus transportation, and goods/services related to trout education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland and eligible portions of the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, environmental education center, nature center, or higher education institution
Must serve grades K-12 (with emphasis on grades 3-12)
New and returning participants must register every year
Must submit signed Memorandum of Intent by March 15th

Fish releases must occur at approved state cold water streams or lakes
Reimbursement packages must be submitted by June 30th and include invoices, proof of purchase, and updated W-9 form
Reporting form must be completed and submitted by July 31st; failure to report results in unenrollment
Itemized list of all approved expenses with receipts required

Certification that payment has not been previously received

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register by January 1st every year and submit signed Memorandum of Intent by March 15th. Attend fall teacher training workshop (October 24, 2026 for new teachers). Receive fish eggs in early December. Raise fish and conduct lessons October through May. Pre-cycle tanks by November 12th deadline. Conduct fish releases at approved sites in April or May. structured_extraction.program_description: A free lifetime non-transferable pass that provides free entrance to public lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, including state parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas. The pass covers the holder and one additional accompanying person for free day-use access. Holders with a valid Maryland hunting license and a mobility impairment may also hunt from a vehicle under the ADA/504 program with physician certification. The Hunt From a Vehicle permit enables the permit holder and one non-hunting companion to remain inside a vehicle while hunting in designated areas, with specific safety restrictions including vehicle immobilization while shooting, unloaded weapons while in motion, and prohibition of loaded weapons on public roadways. The pass does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping fees, boat launches (except where included in day-use charge), rentals, bus parking, or other concessions and special charges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free lifetime non-transferable pass that provides free entrance to public lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, including state parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas. The pass allows the holder and one accompanying person free day-use access. Eligible individuals with mobility impairments may hunt from a vehicle under the ADA/504 program when possessing a valid Maryland hunting license and physician certification. The Hunt From a Vehicle permit enables the permit holder and one non-hunting companion to remain inside a vehicle while hunting in designated areas. The vehicle must be at a complete stop with the motor turned off while shooting. All weapons must be unloaded while the vehicle is in motion. The permit holder cannot shoot or have a loaded weapon while on public roadways. The pass does not waive additional boat launch service charges except where the launch charge is included in the day-use service charge. The pass does not cover automated gate entrance systems, camping fees, rentals, bus parking, or other concessions and special charges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities as defined under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, including those with mobility impairments seeking to hunt from a vehicle on Maryland public lands; non-profit organizations serving clients with disabilities; veterans with VA disability determination; individuals with MVA disability parking certification; individuals with licensed health care professional disability certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free day-use entrance to public lands managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources including state parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas. Eligible individuals may hunt from vehicles in designated areas with a valid Maryland hunting license and physician certification for mobility impairment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland residents with qualifying disabilities on designated public lands and hunting lands throughout Maryland, including state parks, state forests, and wildlife management areas managed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
requirements_list: Must have a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a record of such an impairment, or be regarded as having such an impairment
Valid identification may be requested when the UDP is presented
For Hunt From a Vehicle permit: applicant must have a mobility impairment
For Hunt From a Vehicle permit: a physician must certify the permit application
Permit holder must have the Universal Disability Pass on their person while hunting
Vehicle must be at a complete stop with motor turned off while shooting, aiming, or firing
Only the permit holder, other permittees, and one companion may be in the vehicle while hunting
All weapons must be unloaded while vehicle is in motion
Cannot shoot or have a loaded weapon in vehicle while on public roadway or roadway shoulder

Must provide one of: VA disability determination letter, MVA disability parking certification, or certification from licensed health care provider (physician, chiropractor, optometrist, podiatrist, or nurse practitioner)
Condition may be permanent or temporary
Non-profit applicants must provide current non-profit status certification
Non-profit applicants must provide certification from licensed health care provider documenting clients' disabilities that substantially limit major life activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Licensing & Registration Service at 410-260-3220 or their local Maryland DNR Regional Service Center to apply. Service centers are open by appointment only. Applications for the Hunt From a Vehicle permit are available from Wildlife and Heritage Service regional offices or online. A physician must certify the permit application. Complete application form with personal information and submit one required documentation type (VA letter, MVA certification, or health care provider certification). Health care provider certification includes condition details and provider credentials.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to organizations to help cover the costs of butchering and processing deer that are donated to programs serving low-income Marylanders and people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 maximum available on a first-come, first-served basis. Funds may be split among applicants. Grant awards cover costs of butchering and processing deer at a maximum reimbursement of $60 per deer. Administrative costs are not eligible. Grantees are responsible for identifying and contracting with processors and coordinating venison distribution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipal corporations, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that operate programs providing nutritional support or food for low-income individuals or people experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Butchering and processing costs for deer hunted in compliance with Maryland hunting laws and regulations and donated to food assistance programs. Deer must have a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds. Administrative costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all eligible organizations in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county government, municipal corporation, or 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
Deer must be hunted in compliance with state hunting laws and regulations
Deer must be donated to a program administered by the applicant that provides nutritional support or food for low-income individuals or people experiencing homelessness
Deer must have a dressed weight of at least 50 pounds
Maximum reimbursement of $60 per deer for butchering and processing
Administrative costs are not eligible for reimbursement
Grantee responsible for identifying and contracting with processors
Grantee responsible for coordinating distribution of venison
Quarterly reports required with specific data on hunting confirmation numbers, processors, costs, pounds of venison, and recipient organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Venison Donation Grant Program Application and submit it electronically to Brian Eyler at brian.eyler@maryland.gov. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial, technical, and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments to enhance wildland fire suppression capabilities, improve firefighter safety, promote use of wildland personal protective equipment, and support wildland fire training. The program awards matching grants of up to $3,500 per department on a 50/50 cost-share basis and provides basic wildland fire training classes, including tuition for National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) courses. Applications are submitted via web-based form with decisions communicated by October 15.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $3,500 per department on a 50/50 cost-share basis. Federal reimbursement grants are provided after approval and certification of receipt and payment, reimbursing up to 50 percent of eligible costs (maximum $3,500). The department pays first, then Maryland Forest Service reimburses within 45 days of receiving required documentation. Grants can be used for wildland firefighting personal protective equipment, power tools, firefighting equipment, communication equipment, all-terrain and utility vehicles for wildland firefighting, equipment rehabilitation, and wildland firefighting training including tuition for National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) courses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments serving areas or communities with a population of 10,000 or less (based on latest Census). Area fire departments and fire districts may qualify if their service area includes at least one rural area or community with population of 10,000 or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildland firefighting personal protective equipment, wildland firefighting power tools, wildland firefighting equipment, fire communications equipment, off-road all-terrain and utility vehicles for wildland firefighting, equipment to support ATV/UTV wildland firefighting operations, rehabilitation of wildland firefighting equipment, and wildland firefighting training including tuition for National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) courses. Cannot be used for capital improvements, vehicle purchases, structural firefighting equipment, hazardous material response, rescue, emergency medical services, fire hose larger than 2.5 inches in diameter, or equipment with no application to wildland firefighting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Eligible rural volunteer fire departments must serve areas or communities with a population of 10,000 or less (based on latest Census). Area fire departments and fire districts may qualify if their service area includes at least one rural area or community with population of 10,000 or less.
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer fire department serving a rural area or rural community with population of 10,000 or less (latest Census)
Area fire departments (fire districts, first due area, etc.) may be eligible if service area includes a rural community of 10,000 or less
Purchases must occur between January 1 and December 31 of the grant year
Equipment must be NFPA approved wildland firefighting related
Equipment must have application to wildland firefighting (equipment with no wildland firefighting application is disqualified)
Grants cannot be used for capital improvements, vehicle purchases, or structural firefighting, hazardous material response, rescue, or emergency medical equipment
Applications are scored using a points system with priority given to equipment primarily for wildland firefighting
Standard points deduction applied if VFD received grant in any of the three prior years
Grants awarded in order of highest points to lowest until federal funding is depleted
Must provide a 50/50 cost share match
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit web-based application before September 15, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. After submission, receive confirmation email with responses. Notification of approval or denial by October 15, 2025. If awarded, receive supporting documentation including Memorandum of Understanding. Make purchases between January 1 and December 31, 2025. Submit supporting documentation by January 15, 2026. Maryland Forest Service reimburses within 45 days of receiving required documentation based on 50/50 cost-share agreement (maximum $3,500 payment). Applications are scored using a points system with priority given to equipment primarily for wildland firefighting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Warrior Hike "Walk Off The War" Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An outdoor therapy program that supports combat veterans transitioning from their military service by thru-hiking America's three National Scenic Trails (Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, and Continental Divide Trail). The program provides equipment and supplies required to complete a thru-hike, coordinates trail town support with veteran and hiking organizations along the trails, and assists with future employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Warrior Hike provides equipment and supplies required to complete a thru-hike on the Appalachian Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, or Continental Divide Trail. The program coordinates trail town support (including food, transportation, and lodging) with veteran and hiking organizations located along the trails, and assists with employment placement through partnered companies and veteran hiring services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans who served in combat zones and are honorably discharged
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Thru-hiking equipment and supplies; trail support coordination; employment services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Appalachian Trail (14 states: Georgia to Maine); Pacific Crest Trail (3 states: California to Washington); Continental Divide Trail (4 states: New Mexico to Montana)
requirements_list: Must have served in a combat zone
Must be honorably discharged
Must desire to thru-hike one of the three National Scenic Trails
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Warrior Hike website at warriorexpeditions.org/apply/

May need to provide VCR and TV depending on program selected

structured_extraction.program_description: Program for processing waterfowl (Canada geese and other species) in Maryland. The license authorizes a person or entity to conduct waterfowl processing operations by receiving, processing, and handling wild waterfowl that has been legally harvested and properly tagged according to state and federal laws and regulations. Processors must maintain detailed logs of received birds including customer information, species, harvest location, and delivery dates. The license is issued at no fee, is valid for one year (expiring June 30), and may be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Department issues a Waterfowl Processing Operation Permit/License at no fee. The license authorizes the operation to legally receive, process, and handle wild waterfowl in Maryland. Permit holders must maintain detailed processing logs documenting species, customer information, harvest location, and dates. The license is valid for one year, expiring on June 30 following the date of issuance, and may be renewed annually by submitting a completed renewal application and returning all log books prior to March 1st. The license authorizes the holder to conduct operations under Maryland and federal regulations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Prior to March 1st (for returning all books); Annual
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-260-8538, 410-260-8540, Toll-free in Maryland: 1-877-620-8DNR, TTY: Maryland Relay via 1-800-735-2258 or 711
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and businesses conducting waterfowl processing operations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to receive, process, and handle wild waterfowl that has been legally harvested and properly tagged in accordance with state and federal laws and regulations. Processors must maintain detailed logs of all birds received, including species, customer information, harvest location, and delivery dates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Applicant must specify the county and location where waterfowl processing activity will be conducted.

Applicant must specify county of operation
May not receive or have in custody any wild waterfowl that is not properly tagged as required by state and federal laws and regulations
Must maintain detailed processing logs documenting species, customer information, harvest location, and dates
Must keep records of the number of each species of wild waterfowl processed
Must record the location (county and state) where each wild waterfowl was taken
Must record the date each wild waterfowl was received
Must record the name and address of the person from whom each wild waterfowl was received
Must record the date each wild waterfowl was disposed of
Must record the name and address of the person to whom each wild waterfowl was delivered

Must return all books (used or unused) prior to March 1st each year
Must submit records to the Department annually prior to March 1st

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A person desiring a waterfowl processing operation license shall apply on a form supplied by the Department or obtain the Waterfowl Processing Operation Permit Application form. Print or type the application and complete all required information and pages. Applications can be requested by email at wildlifepermits.dnr@maryland.gov, by phone at 410-260-8538 or 410-260-8540, or by mail to the Permits Coordinator at Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Wildlife and Heritage Service, Tawes State Office Building, 580 Taylor Ave E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Submit the completed application to the Permits Coordinator. Permit holders will receive processing log books from the Permits Coordinator, which must be completed during operations and returned prior to March 1st each year. The Tawes State Office Building is open by appointment only. Wildlife permit appointments can be scheduled by email or phone. There is no application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides technical and financial assistance to local communities and governments for watershed protection, restoration, and related projects and initiatives through a collaborative approach. The program connects and coordinates various resources available across the state, partnering with The Environmental Finance Center, Chesapeake Bay Trust, and University of Maryland. Assistance includes grants for planning and designing water quality improvement projects, as well as technical assistance, project management, help with financing strategies, and training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical and financial assistance provided to local communities and governments to implement watershed protection and restoration activities through a collaborative approach. The program provides grants for planning and designing water quality improvement projects, technical assistance, project management, help with financing strategies, and stakeholder outreach support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profits, universities, and community groups in Maryland that want to work on watershed protection and restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance can be used for design, watershed planning, and program development. The program also provides technical help with project management, financing strategies, and stakeholder outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Youghiogheny watershed, or the Maryland Coastal Bays. Statewide availability for local communities and governments in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To get help, communities fill out a Request for Resources & Services Form. A separate Request for Proposals is available for the grant program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program providing technical planning and design assistance, grant funding for watershed planning, and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration programs and projects that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Planning projects include watershed characterization, survey, assessment, action plans, or financing plans. Design requests are accepted for the full suite of non-point source best management practices. The program supports shoreline restoration and living shoreline projects managed by the Chesapeake Bay Trust.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding and technical planning and design assistance for watershed restoration and protection projects. Planning projects include watershed characterization, survey, assessment, action plans, or financing plans. Design requests are accepted for the full suite of non-point source best management practices. Partners and contractors support local governments and non-profit organizations in developing watershed plans, assessments, and designing best management practices and non-point source BMPs. The program supports shoreline restoration and living shoreline projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations undertaking comprehensive watershed protection, restoration, and shoreline restoration activities in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical planning and design assistance, design services, watershed planning, and programmatic development for watershed protection and restoration projects, including watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, design of non-point source best management practices, and living shoreline projects that lead to improved water quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in the program should fill out the Request for Resources & Services Form or submit proposals for technical planning and design assistance. Applicants can contact Carrie Decker via email or phone for more information, or contact the Chesapeake Bay Trust for application details, requirements, and the list of preferred contractors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year pilot program that provides collaborative, science-based funding and technical assistance to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. The program combines funding from multiple state agencies and existing programs to support watershed restoration projects that improve water quality, habitat, public access, and community resilience. The program provides Implementation Grants covering up to 50% of project implementation costs, Operations Grants for project administration, and Water Quality Monitoring Grants. For FY 2026, funding includes up to $2 million per watershed for implementation and operating grants (with $20,000 included for operational expenses) and $250,000 per watershed for water quality monitoring. Project sponsors must provide 50% matching funding from sources outside the Whole Watershed Fund. Additional support is available through the Maryland Agricultural Cost Share Program and Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides Implementation Grants covering up to 50% of project implementation costs (up to $2 million per watershed for FY 2026 with $20,000 for operational expenses), Operations Grants for project administration, and Water Quality Monitoring Grants totaling $1.25 million ($250,000 per watershed). Project sponsors must provide 50% matching funds from sources outside the Whole Watershed Fund. Funding is distributed quarterly based on reimbursement requests to the single designated Project Sponsor per watershed. Additional support is available through the Maryland Agricultural Cost Share Program and Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Next Request for Proposals due October 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal, county, and regional agencies; nonprofit organizations; faith-based groups; homeowners associations; soil and water conservation districts working on watershed restoration projects in selected Maryland watersheds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, engineering, and legal document drafting (permits, easements); implementation of best management practices; habitat restoration; pollution reduction; stormwater management; water quality improvement; climate resilience; public access improvements; community engagement; workforce development; ecosystem monitoring; and maintenance needs related to watershed restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is limited to five selected watersheds: Antietam Creek (Washington and Frederick Counties, extending into Pennsylvania), Baltimore Harbor (Baltimore City and Baltimore County), Upper Choptank River (Caroline, Dorchester, and Talbot Counties, extending into Delaware), Newport Bay (Wicomico and Worcester Counties), and Severn River (Anne Arundel County). Future rounds may expand to additional watersheds.
requirements_list: One project sponsor identified per participating watershed to administer the project
Project must be endorsed by each county and municipal corporation in which the project will occur
Matching funds of 50% required, with outside funds coming from sources other than the Whole Watershed Fund sources
Only projects implemented after July 1, 2025 are eligible for funding or match
Project sponsor must hold at least 4 community meetings per year with local government representation
Project sponsor must provide opportunity for public comment on preliminary designs of major or large-scale actions
Applicant must demonstrate partnerships and collaborative approach
Projects must align with multi-faceted goals including pollution reduction, habitat creation, climate resilience, environmental justice, and public access
Applicant must document interest from affected property owners for restoration or conservation actions on their property
Project must demonstrate habitat restoration and pollution reduction benefits
Project must emphasize cost-effective, measurable pollution reduction actions
Project must support local land use policies and conservation programs
Project must minimize loss of trees and natural habitats
Project must demonstrate opportunities to reduce environmental disparities in overburdened or underserved communities
Project must anticipate at least five co-benefits including habitat creation, aquatic resource restoration, carbon sequestration, climate resilience, employment, public health, or recreational access
Project must create partnership opportunities among nonprofits, for-profits, community organizations, and government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals in response to a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the State Management Team. The RFP is issued every five years, with the next deadline of October 1, 2029. Proposals are evaluated based on watershed selection criteria including water quality benefits, pollution reduction potential, cost-effectiveness, environmental justice opportunities, and partnership strength. One Project Sponsor is selected per watershed through an evaluation process conducted by the State Management Team. Selected project sponsors work with the SMT to develop an Implementation and Financing Plan with measurable outcomes before receiving grant disbursements. Funds are distributed quarterly based on reimbursement requests. The SMT meets with project sponsors and local government six times per year to review progress.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides information and guidance to residents on ways to attract and support wildlife in residential areas through backyard habitat creation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and advice for creating backyard habitats for wildlife.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional training and certification courses in wildlife rehabilitation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Boating Access Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program that provides funding for public recreational boating access projects, including boat ramps, parking lots, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, and piers. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources as part of the Waterway Improvement and Infrastructure Program through the Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration program. Provides up to 75% federal funding with a minimum 25% local/state match required. Funding comes from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat and small engine fuels, apportioned to states by formula with at least 15 percent of each state's allocation directed to boating access. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 annually in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access. Funding is distributed through the Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Program administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding for construction and renovation of publicly owned boat ramps, parking lots, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, and piers for recreational trailered motorboats. Up to 75% federal funding with minimum 25% local/state match required. Maryland receives approximately $500,000 annually in Sport Fish Restoration funding for boating access. At least 15% of each state's federal apportionment must go towards boating access. Funding comes primarily from excise taxes on fishing equipment and motorboat/small engine fuels. Funding is distributed through the Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration Program administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government jurisdictions in Maryland seeking to construct or renovate publicly owned boat ramps for recreational boating.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of public boat ramps, parking lots, access roads, bulkheads, breakwaters, and piers. Renovation and improvement of existing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Federal program administered by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service with state apportionment.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public jurisdiction or local jurisdiction
Projects must focus on publicly owned boat ramps
Boat ramps must be designed for recreational, trailered motorboats
Local jurisdiction obtains all necessary permits
Submit project plans and specifications for Department approval
Advertise project for bid; submit bid tabulations and recommended award for Department approval
Facility must be reasonably available to public with physical access, equitable fees, and open periods
ADA accessibility guidelines must apply; appropriate signage required
Fees must be approved by Department; no user discrimination; same charges for all users
Fees kept in separate account for operation and maintenance
Maintain facility for useful life of 20-40 years
At least 15% of state apportionment must go toward boating access
