structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County East Side Revitalization Community-Wide Assessment Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant-funded program supported by the United States Environmental Protection Agency that provides comprehensive environmental assessments and technical assistance for brownfield revitalization in Baltimore County's East Side communities. The program offers property owners and community members free Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, participation in the Maryland Department of Environment Voluntary Cleanup Program (with a $6,000 VCP application fee waiver), and Technical Review Services (approximately $500–$1,500 in TRS fees covered). Phase I ESAs identify environmental conditions through document review and site inspection, while Phase II ESAs include environmental sampling of soil, groundwater, and surface water with laboratory analysis. The program provides state authorization of environmental site conclusions and remedies, connects property owners with state and local incentive programs including the Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) Tax Credit, and facilitates redevelopment of underutilized properties. Community members can also help identify potential brownfields using the Brownfields Scout form. All assessment services are provided at no cost to eligible property owners. Properties must meet prioritization criteria including location in an Opportunity Zone, proximity to Pulaski Highway, location in locally-designated growth areas, or location within EPA-approved Total Maximum Daily Load restriction watersheds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a $300,000 EPA grant covering Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, participation in the Maryland Department of the Environment Voluntary Cleanup Program (with a $6,000 VCP application fee waiver), and Technical Review Services (approximately $500–$1,500 in TRS fees). Phase I ESAs identify environmental conditions through document review and site inspection. Phase II ESAs include environmental sampling of soil, groundwater, and surface water with laboratory analysis. Property owners and community members also have access to information about state and local incentive programs, including the Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) Tax Credit. All services are provided at no cost to facilitate environmental remediation and property preparation for cleanup and redevelopment.

The Maryland Department of Planning has flexibility to expand the target area beyond the East Side if grant funds cannot be fully expended in the initial target area.

structured_extraction.program_name: Office for Blindness & Vision Services (OBVS) - Employment or Vocational Rehabilitation Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps people with vision loss, blindness, or deaf-blindness obtain competitive employment. Part of Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). Staffed by specially trained teachers, counselors, and technical specialists. Services include career guidance and exploration, assistive technology training (such as screen reading software, magnifiers, and low vision aids), career training or academic education, independent living skills training, orientation and mobility training, job placement support, and counselor support. The program also oversees the Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind, which prepares legally blind individuals to operate vending, gift, or food service businesses in public facilities. Services are provided at DORS offices throughout Maryland.

Also prepares legally blind individuals to operate vending, gift, or food service businesses in public facilities through the Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind. Services are provided at DORS offices throughout Maryland through three regional offices: Baltimore (serving Baltimore City, Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, Harford Counties), Wheaton (serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, Washington Counties), and Annapolis (serving Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester Counties).

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development program connecting individuals ages 18 and older residing in Maryland with organizations for a minimum 9-month paid full-time service opportunity. The program serves recent high school graduates, GED recipients, high school completion certificate earners, and individuals looking to pivot careers or reenter the workforce. Participants engage in full-time service positions earning at least $15 per hour for 30-40 hours per week over at least nine months. The Service Year Option pathway is for ages 18-24 with a high school diploma, GED, or Certificate of Completion, while the Maryland Corps pathway is for all adults 18+ with no education requirement. Members receive on-the-job training, mentoring, professional development, networking opportunities, civic engagement experiences, and access to a service success coach. Host Site Partners receive state grant-supported funding to offset salary and benefits costs, dedicated Member Success coaches, apprenticeship credential support, and access to a Learning Management Platform. The state covers approximately two-thirds of member wages through cost-reimbursement grants (up to $20,000 per year per full-time member), while host sites cover the remaining third plus payroll taxes and benefits. Upon program completion, participants receive a $6,000 taxable completion award and have the opportunity to earn Department of Labor registered apprenticeship credentials. Organizations benefit from building their talent pipeline while members gain professional skills and contribute to meaningful community projects in schools, nonprofits, public agencies, and local businesses across Maryland.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: DSCI provides cost-reimbursement grants to Host Site Partners to offset costs of Member salary and benefits, reimbursing up to $20,000 per year per full-time member (40 hours per week). The state covers approximately two-thirds of member wages while host sites cover the remaining third plus payroll taxes (approximately 11%) and benefits. Members are W-2 employees earning at least $15 per hour working 30-40 hours per week for a minimum 9-month term. Organizations must pay approved member costs upfront and submit quarterly reimbursement requests. Upon successful completion, participants receive a $6,000 taxable cash completion award. Members receive professional development training, on-the-job mentorship, access to a service success coach, workforce development opportunities, and potential Department of Labor registered apprenticeship credentials. Host Site Partners provide fringe benefits including health insurance and wraparound services such as childcare and transportation support. Health insurance is required for members who need coverage and can be provided through the organization's plan or by reimbursing at least 50% of monthly premiums for Maryland Health Exchange enrollment. Alternatively, organizations may use a DSCI-sponsored payroll provider who becomes the employer of record. DSCI reserves approximately 10 paid work hours per week for professional development activities. Service placement and support provided through partner organizations including nonprofits, government agencies, businesses, and schools.

Particularly targets recent high school graduates from the classes of 2024, 2023, 2022, and 2021, as well as individuals interested in pivoting careers or reentering the workforce. Also welcomes Maryland-based organizations (nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, schools, universities) seeking to hire service-minded young adults for full-time positions.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Member Applicants: 1) Complete an application on DSCI's Application and Matching Portal at serve.maryland.gov or through the BuildWithin application platform. 2) DSCI reviews applications continuously and may reach out with follow-up questions. 3) Once conditionally accepted, use the portal to explore and apply to positions with Host Site Partner organizations. 4) Interview with Host Site Partners and accept an official offer. 5) Attend Pre-Service Orientation to meet DSCI team and other Members. 6) Begin minimum 9-month service term at your Host Site. 7) Work with a Service Success Coach, participate in professional development, and complete required trainings. 8) Graduate and receive $6,000 completion award and Department of Labor credentials if requirements are met. 9) Join Alumni community for ongoing support and next-step planning. For Host Site Partner Organizations: 1) Submit HSP application on DSCI's Application and Matching Portal including position descriptions for Members. 2) Attend required webinar reinforcing program requirements and milestones. 3) DSCI reviews applications on rolling basis and may request clarification. 4) After acceptance and position approval, use portal to explore potential Members, interview candidates, and extend offers. 5) All HSPs and Members attend required program orientation. 6) MC/SYO officially launches August/September with Members beginning 9-month service placement. 7) Organizations become Host Site Partners and begin managing their grant once the award is confirmed. 8) Organizations must set up required systems, access award documents, and understand their reporting and financial responsibilities. 9) Graduation ceremony held in June annually; Members conclude service June or July upon successful completion. Email applytoserve@maryland.gov to schedule a virtual or in-person program overview.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deployment and demonstration of innovative technologies and practices in highway transportation projects across all project phases including planning, financing, design, construction, and operations.

structured_extraction.program_description: An employer commuter benefit program where employers offer employees a choice between a parking space at work or a cash benefit. The program works best for employers that lease parking and is typically implemented at the time of new lease or lease renewal. Commuters who carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work can receive a cash payment from their employer in exchange for surrendering a dedicated paid parking space. Employers who participate can claim a tax credit of up to $100 per person per month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers provide a cash allowance to participating employees equal to the parking subsidy. Employers who offer Cash in Lieu of Parking can claim a Maryland Commuter Tax Credit of 50% of commuter benefit costs, up to $100 per employee per month. This results in reduced parking costs and reduced parking demand for employers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers offering free or subsidized parking; Employees who carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash benefit to employees who opt out of parking; Reduced parking lease costs for employers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must provide cash allowance equal to parking subsidy
Participating employees must choose alternate mode of transportation and forgo parking space
Employer must be leasing parking spaces
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Commuter Choice Maryland for assistance with implementation. Contact hours: Monday–Friday 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Travel Demand Management (TDM) program that works with employers to maximize traveler choices and deliver transportation solutions. The program promotes alternative options to driving alone including public transportation, ridesharing, vanpooling, walking, biking, teleworking, Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, and alternative work schedules. It aims to reduce congestion, conserve energy, protect the environment, and facilitate economic opportunity. Employers receive technical support and recognition for implementing commuter benefits programs, including employee surveys, Employer Transportation Plan development, and promotional materials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Commuter Tax Credit: 50% of eligible commuter benefits costs up to $100 per employee per month for transit, vanpool, Guaranteed Ride Home, or Cash-in-Lieu of Parking programs. Federal payroll tax-free commuter benefits up to $270 per month. Three options available: employer-supported subsidy, employee pre-tax deduction, or combination. Technical assistance includes employee transportation survey development, Employer Transportation Plan creation with specific goals, promotional materials, enrollment support, and program evaluation guidance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers of any size seeking to implement or expand commuter benefits programs, and their employees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commuter benefits including transit passes, vanpool subsidies, parking incentives, telework support, and bike amenities; program administration; technical assistance for Transportation Demand Management strategies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; workplace must be located in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland employer
Workplace must be located in Maryland
Complete Maryland Commuter Tax Credit registration form at CommuterChoiceMaryland.com
Conduct employee transportation survey
Develop Employer Transportation Plan with specific goals
File appropriate tax forms (MW508CR and MW508 for §501(c)(3)/(4) organizations or 500 CRW for other businesses) with Maryland tax return
Set up payroll deductions if applicable
Promote program to employees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through CommuterChoiceMaryland.com, complete the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit registration form, conduct an employee transportation survey, develop an Employer Transportation Plan with goals, and submit required tax forms with Maryland tax return. Contact the Commuter Choice Maryland Team at CommuterChoice@mdot.maryland.gov or 410-865-1100 for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter Choice Maryland MD 295 Corridor Pilot
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that supports employers and employees near MD 295 between West Nursery Road and I-95 with commuting solutions. The program provides free support for employers to establish or improve commuter benefit programs, including one-on-one support, workshops, custom resources, and targeted outreach to employees. Employers can earn recognition, save money on taxes through commuter benefits (up to $1,200 per employee per year through the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit and federal payroll tax savings), and boost recruitment and retention. Employees receive targeted outreach and information to encourage them to try new commuting options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive free technical assistance and resources including tips on commuter perks, education on how commuter benefits can save money (up to $1,200 per employee per year through the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, federal payroll tax savings, and parking cost reductions), one-on-one support from the Commuter Choice Maryland team, free commuter survey development, custom resources and materials, and recognition through the Employer Partner Program. The program provides support for employers to establish or improve commuter benefit programs with targeted outreach to employees about commuting options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and employees located along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95, including office managers, HR representatives, benefits administrators, and individual commuters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing or improving commuter benefit programs, promoting alternative commuting options, and reducing commuting costs through commuter benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available along the MD 295 corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95, spanning from the Inner Harbor in the north to BWI Airport in the south, covering Baltimore City and Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Employer must be located in the MD 295 pilot corridor between West Nursery Road and I-95
Commitment to meet with MDOT team and participate in program activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested employers and commuters can contact Commuter Choice Maryland via email or phone for more information and to participate in the program. Employers fill out a form or email the program team to express interest and commit to program activities including meeting with MDOT and earning the Employer Partner Badge.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free mobile app that rewards commuters with cash and other incentives for using sustainable transportation options such as carpooling, vanpooling, public transit, biking, walking, and multimodal commuting during peak commute times. Users download the app, register with their email, log their eligible commute trips, and earn points redeemable for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. The app helps commuters plan their commute and find optimal travel options while earning rewards for completing sustainable trips. Commuters earn points for eligible weekday commute trips during peak hours (6:30am-9:30am or 4:00pm-7:00pm), with points ranging from 10 to 100 per trip depending on transportation mode, with higher values for ridesharing, transit, biking, or walking. Maximum earnings of $600 per calendar year, with higher tier rewards up to $90 in value.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commuters earn points for commute trips completed during peak hours (6:30am-9:30am or 4:00pm-7:00pm on weekdays). Points are awarded based on transportation mode, with higher values for sustainable options like transit, carpooling, biking, and walking (10-100 points per trip). Points can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Users can earn up to $10 after 20 trips, with higher tier rewards up to $90 in value. Maximum earnings are $600 per calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters traveling into the Washington, DC area (as defined by the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments service area) or anywhere within Maryland who work at a physical location during peak commuting hours on weekdays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commute trips to work at a physical location during weekday peak commute times (6:30am-9:30am or 4:00pm-7:00pm) using carpooling, vanpooling, public transit, biking, walking, or multimodal transportation. Earned points can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commuters traveling into the Washington, DC area (as defined by the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments service area) or anywhere within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be employed (telecommuting and unemployment do not qualify)
Must commute to a physical work location
Trips must occur on weekdays (Monday-Friday)
Trips must occur during morning peak times (6:30am-9:30am) or afternoon peak times (4:00pm-7:00pm)
Only one morning and one evening trip earn points per day
Must register for CommuterCash app to participate
Trips must be work commutes from home or vice versa
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the CommuterCash app from Apple App Store or Google Play. Register an account with your email address. Log your eligible commute trips in the app during peak hours. Earn points based on transportation mode used. Redeem accumulated points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits through the app interface.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that implements short-term, cost-effective demonstration projects at intersections and corridors with a history of traffic fatalities or crashes to improve safety and test innovative solutions. Projects use temporary materials such as flex posts, speed cushions, planters, and asphalt art to pilot street safety interventions over an eight-week implementation timeline. The program is part of Maryland's Complete Streets Leadership Academy initiative and includes workshops, technical support, and data collection to evaluate outcomes before potential permanent installation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for materials procurement for quick-build demonstration projects including temporary traffic-calming materials (speed cushions, flex posts, planters, thermoplastic markings, paint) and pedestrian/bicycle safety improvements. Includes engineering and technical support from Stantec, installation support by SHA maintenance shops, participation in Leadership Academy workshops on Complete Streets strategies, walk audits, and guidance on data collection and community engagement. Project implementation typically follows an eight-week timeline from design to installation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (cities, towns, counties) seeking to improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, particularly communities with identified safety hotspots, recent Safe Streets for All (SS4A) projects, or MDOT Pedestrian Safety Action Plan focus areas. Includes government staff from planning, engineering, and public works departments, community members, advocates, adjacent businesses, and pedestrians and cyclists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Procurement of materials for quick-build demonstration projects including speed cushions, flex posts, thermoplastic markings, paint, temporary curbs, and tubular markers. Engineering and design support, installation and implementation, data collection and monitoring, public engagement and outreach, community surveys, and staff time support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State-owned routes and Maryland state highways with identified safety concerns. Priority given to areas with existing SS4A plans, bike/pedestrian planning initiatives, and MDOT Pedestrian Safety Action Plan projects. Projects must be located on SHA-maintained roads.
requirements_list: Location must have a history of traffic fatalities or crashes
Participation in Leadership Academy workshops
Collaboration with regional SHA district offices
Eight-week implementation timeline
Site selection based on existing SS4A plans, bike/ped planning, and PSAP projects
Use of pre-approved materials and configurations
Local government participation and staff commitment
Partnership with SHA for state highway projects
Community engagement and outreach required
Data collection including speed studies and intercept surveys
Coordination between local agencies and SHA
Comprehensive community outreach and feedback gathering
Consideration of impacts on existing services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions collaborate with MDOT and SHA to identify eligible locations and implement quick-build projects. The process includes location selection with dialogue between partners, participation in Leadership Academy workshops and walk audits, budget identification, weekly coordination meetings between county and state partners, community engagement, and data collection guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: IRS guidance on the employment tax treatment of fringe benefits provided by employers, including transportation/commuting benefits. Covers tax exclusion rules, valuation methods, and withholding/reporting requirements for fringe benefits. Employers can provide transportation benefits (commuter highway vehicle rides and/or transit passes, and qualified parking) up to $340 per month (2026) that are excluded from employee wages for income tax purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can provide transportation fringe benefits as a pre-tax benefit, a subsidy, or a combination of both, up to IRS-set monthly limits. This reduces employees' taxable income and allows employers and employees to save on taxes. For 2026: monthly exclusion limit of $340 for qualified parking and $340 for commuter transportation/transit passes. Employers can choose to cover part or all of an employee's eligible commuting costs, or allow employees to set aside pre-tax income to pay for commuting expenses. Benefits must be provided under a bona fide reimbursement arrangement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers in Maryland who want to offer tax-advantaged commuting benefits to employees; tax professionals; HR departments; employees receiving transportation benefits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible commuting costs including transit passes, vanpool leases, parking, tolls, and bike-sharing memberships; commuter highway vehicle rides; qualified parking expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland; United States-wide
requirements_list: Commuting costs must be eligible under IRS rules
Benefits must not exceed IRS-set monthly limits ($340 for qualified parking; $340 for commuter transportation/transit passes in 2026)
Employers must follow IRS valuation rules for transportation benefits
Must withhold and report employment taxes appropriately
Employer must not favor highly compensated or key employees (discrimination rules apply)
Commuter highway vehicles must seat at least 6 adults with 80% mileage for employee transport
Must establish bona fide reimbursement arrangements where applicable
Employers must determine value of fringe benefits no later than January 31 of the following year
Benefits must be provided to employees (not self-employed individuals or 2% S corporation shareholders)
Employee must verify proper use of working condition benefits
Documentation required for substantiation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers can implement the federal fringe benefit by offering pre-tax deductions to employees or providing employer subsidies for commuting costs, or a combination of both. Employers must establish a bona fide reimbursement arrangement and follow IRS valuation and reporting requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ferry Programs (Passenger Ferry, Electric or Low-Emitting Ferry Pilot, and Rural Ferry Program)

Programs fund capital investments such as acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and modernization of ferry vessels, terminals, and supporting infrastructure, as well as planning efforts and operating assistance in rural areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding for capital investments including acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and modernization of ferry vessels, terminals, and supporting infrastructure, as well as planning efforts and operating assistance to maintain essential service. Focus on enhancing system condition, reliability, capacity, and advancing low- and zero-emission technologies.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments including acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and modernization of ferry vessels, terminals, and supporting infrastructure; planning efforts; operating assistance for rural ferry services.

requirements_list: Projects evaluated based on demonstrated need
Benefits to service quality and community access
Consistency with local and regional priorities
Readiness for implementation including financial and technical capacity
Geographic diversity and safety considered
Accessibility and support for economic opportunity considered

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to six free rides home per year for registered commuters who regularly bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work. It ensures a way home during personal emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to six free rides home per year for eligible registered commuters during personal emergencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commuters who regularly bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rides home for eligible commuters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for registered commuters.
requirements_list: Must regularly bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work
Must be registered with the program

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program established in 2012 that supports bicycle infrastructure and bicycle network development throughout Maryland. Administered by the Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility (OATM) at MDOT, the program provides grant support for design, minor retrofit, and construction of bikeway projects that maximize bicycle access and enhance last-mile connections to work, school, shopping and transit. It prioritizes funding projects which improve safety and access for disadvantaged communities and supports the development and improvement of biking infrastructure and networks to create safe and connected bicycle transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for three project types: Design (feasibility studies and engineering plans up to 65% design phase, up to $400,000), Minor Retrofit projects (low-cost treatments such as route signing, pavement markings, Complete Streets treatments, up to $200,000), and Construction projects (bikeway infrastructure including shared-use paths, bicycle bridges, and protected bike lanes, up to $500,000). Applicants must provide a minimum of 20 percent of total project cost as match, which can be cash or in-kind contribution. Up to 10% or $10,000 can be used for educational and promotional materials directly related to infrastructure.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April-May (applications accepted mid-May annually); Letters of Intent accepted December-April
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local governments, state agencies, metropolitan planning organizations, transit entities, non-profit organizations, and federal public lands agencies seeking to develop bicycle infrastructure and networks, with priority for disadvantaged communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for design plans and feasibility assessments of proposed bikeways, engineering and preliminary design services, low-cost bicycle treatments such as route signing, pavement markings, drainage grate replacement, bicycle counters, racks and repair stations, construction of bikeway infrastructure including shared-use paths, bicycle bridges, and protected bike lanes, Complete Streets intersection treatments, and up to 10% or $10,000 for educational and promotional materials directly related to infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must meet at least one or more eligibility criteria: access to transit within three miles of a rail station or major bus hub, county priority designation, location in a Sustainable Community or Bicycle and Pedestrian Priority Area, access to Main Streets or major institutions, access to low-income areas for disadvantaged communities, provision of significant safety interventions, or provision/enhancement of access along missing trail links. Projects on State right-of-way require submission of Complete Streets objective statement (required as of FY27). Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must meet at least one eligibility criterion
Projects must have reached at least 65 percent design at time of application for construction projects
Applicants must provide minimum 20 percent of total project cost as match
Complete Streets objective statement required for projects on State right-of-way (as of FY27)
Project Workplan submission required within 6 months of award
Project Grant Agreement execution required within 12 months of award
Quarterly update reports required
Final Report and design plans required before final reimbursement
Maintenance responsibility identified prior to project agreement execution
Facilities must be maintained for minimum 5 years
Design projects must identify maintenance/ownership entities
Procurement compliance with applicable laws
Records retention for 3 years from final reimbursement claim submission
Design projects: minimum 10-foot width
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants are encouraged to submit a letter of intent to MDOT at cbydume@mdot.maryland.gov during the December-April window. The letter of intent should include project title, project description, physical limits, estimated project cost, anticipated funding request amount, and contact information. Formal applications open in April and run through mid-May. Applications are submitted for specific project development phases. Contact Quinn Wallace or the Bikeways program team for additional application details and Grants Roadshow support sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local and Regional Project Assistance Program (BUILD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive funding for planning and capital projects delivering significant local or regional improvements to surface transportation infrastructure
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Planning, preparation, or design work for eligible capital projects, and capital improvements to surface transportation infrastructure including highway and bridge projects, public transportation, passenger and freight rail, port infrastructure, airport surface transportation components, intermodal projects, and culvert replacement and stormwater improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, tribal governments, transit agencies, port authorities, multistate and multijurisdictional transportation organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, preparation, design work, and capital improvements to surface transportation infrastructure including highway and bridge projects, public transportation, passenger and freight rail, port infrastructure, airport surface transportation components, intermodal projects, and culvert replacement and stormwater improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland, including rural areas, urban areas, Areas of Persistent Poverty, Historically Disadvantaged Communities, and Tribal lands.
requirements_list: Applicants must be states, District of Columbia, U.S. territories and possessions, units of local government, public agencies or publicly chartered authorities established by one or more states, special purpose districts or public authorities with transportation function, federally recognized Tribal governments, consortia of Tribes, transit agencies, or multistate/multijurisdictional groups composed of eligible entities
Federal agencies, nonprofits, private entities, and individuals are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Sean Winkler for application details and the Grants Roadshow support sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) certification allows firms to meet minority business participation goals on state-funded contracts issued by counties and cities within Maryland. MBE certified firms can fulfill minority participation goals on State contracts and distinguish themselves from competitors. Firms may hold MBE certification in addition to Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) certification for federally-funded contracts. There is no cost to apply for certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification that allows eligible minority-owned firms to participate in state-funded contracts issued by MDOT, counties, and cities within Maryland. The certification enables firms to fulfill minority participation goals on State contracts and distinguish themselves from competitors. There is no cost to apply for certification. The certification process takes several months once a complete application package is received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority-owned businesses and disadvantaged business enterprises seeking to participate in state and local government contracts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification enables firms to bid on and participate in minority business participation programs for state-funded contracts from MDOT, counties, and cities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland firms or out-of-state firms applying for MBE certification must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT)
requirements_list: Firm must be registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT)
Complete Uniform Certification Application
Submit Personal Net Worth (PNW) Statement
Submit all required documentation in PDF format
Complete MBE Only Document Checklist appropriate to business structure
All information must be unredacted with no blank fields
Must be a small, minority or women-owned business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the MBE Only Application. 2. Read the application instructions. 3. Complete all sections of the application in PDF format. 4. Download and complete the required Personal Net Worth (PNW) Form and review PNW Guidelines. 5. Review the appropriate MBE Only Document Checklist for your business structure. 6. Submit the application package through the online portal at marylandmdbe.mdbecert.com. 7. Retain a copy of the entire application package for your records. Applicants are evaluated for eligibility in both the MBE and DBE programs simultaneously. Free monthly workshops are available to help applicants prepare their applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that identifies and implements transportation projects with climate benefits. The program supports projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve climate resilience in Maryland's transportation network, including projects that mitigate climate impacts such as flooding on roadways and bridges and damage from severe storms. Funded through the federal Carbon Reduction Program under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Carbon Reduction Program funding for transportation projects that reduce surface transportation emissions and advance climate/decarbonization goals. Funding supports capital projects with a 20% minimum cash match requirement. The 2025 solicitation was open from February 5 through March 26, 2025.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Breitenother (for application questions) and Deron Lovaas (for program questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transportation agencies and organizations including Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), local governments, WMATA, MDOT Modal Administrations (SHA, MPA, MTA, MAA, MVA), and other entities with transportation projects that provide climate benefits and reduce transportation sector greenhouse gas emissions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation projects that reduce surface transportation emissions and improve climate resilience including: alternative fuel vehicles and charging infrastructure, bicycle and pedestrian facilities, public transit improvements, intelligent transportation systems (ITS), congestion mitigation, diesel retrofits, street lighting efficiency, traffic management, carpooling/vanpooling facilities, sustainable pavements, port facility improvements, and resilience improvements in vulnerable areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland. Projects must be located within an identified Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) region. Preference given to projects within CS-CRAB (Coast Smart-Climate Ready Action Boundary) data layer boundaries, including Riverine and Coastal layers. Projects in vulnerable areas (coastal, flood risk, slope failure) eligible for resilience components.
requirements_list: Project must have climate benefits and reduce surface transportation emissions
Project must address greenhouse gas emissions reduction or climate resilience in transportation
Minimum 20% cash match required (matching funds must be cash)
Project must be listed in applicable transportation plans
Project Point of Contact must be identified
Must reduce surface transportation emissions and align with state/agency carbon reduction goals
Must address equity and environmental justice considerations
Must provide detailed project cost estimate with multi-year cash flows
Operating expenses not allowable; capital projects only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants register on the Maryland OneStop Portal with email verification, login, access the Climate Focused Funding application form, complete the application, and submit before the deadline. Applications can be saved as drafts and resumed later. Weekly virtual office hours are available on Wednesdays from 3:00 pm to 4:00 pm during the solicitation window to provide technical assistance and answer questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation's Office of Rail and Intermodal Freight that provides state grant assistance to help preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, and foster sustainability and innovative technologies in Maryland's freight rail network. The program targets investments designed to leverage existing infrastructure, assets, and funding programs, and supports freight rail infrastructure improvements and projects that support the movement of goods and economic development. The program makes targeted investments to create a better pipeline of projects that address departmental goals of supporting a safe, secure, and resilient multimodal freight network.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant assistance delivered on a competitive, reimbursable basis to help preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, and foster sustainability and innovative technologies in freight rail infrastructure. Applicants must provide a minimum 20% cash match of the overall project cost. Funding supports design phase projects (completion of design plans, feasibility assessments, and evaluation of economic benefits, environmental impacts, right-of-way issues, local support, and cost estimates) and construction phase projects (construction or installation of rail corridor improvements including sidings/sidetracks, eligible grade crossings, bridges/structures, drainage improvements, environmental impact reduction efforts, and innovative technology projects). Recipients must be able to cover initial project costs and demonstrate project readiness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, railroads, freight rail operators, shippers, business and commercial interests, state agencies, metropolitan planning organizations, and other key agencies and eligible partners in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preserve railroad corridors, support economic development, foster sustainability and innovative technologies in freight rail infrastructure, support freight rail infrastructure improvements and projects that support the movement of goods and create a safe, secure, and resilient freight network. Eligible uses include design plans and feasibility assessments, construction or installation of rail corridor improvements (sidings/sidetracks, grade crossings, bridges/structures, drainage improvements), environmental studies and permitting, safety and security measures (fencing, signage, walkways, trespass prevention), infrastructure replacement and modernization, conversion of freight service from trucks to rail, and stabilization and preservation of inactive railroad infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to all eligible applicants. Project location must be specified by county and city; optional railroad line and mile points.
requirements_list: Projects are selected through a competitive process
The grant is reimbursable, so applicants must be able to cover initial project costs
Applicants must demonstrate project readiness
Minimum 20% cash match required (20% of overall project cost)
Project manager contact information required
Cost estimate with cash-flows for all requested funding years required
Environmental permitting or NEPA documentation may be required
Right-of-way acquisition status disclosure required
Alignment with state/modal/MPO/local priorities preferred
Projects must align with statewide and local plans and policies
Design projects require: Scope of Work, Anticipated Schedule, Preliminary Cost Estimate, Support Agreements
Construction projects require: All design requirements plus Property Certification, Environmental Permitting, Design Plans, Railroad Statement, Traffic Control
Complete project within two to three years of award notice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Freight Grant Program Application portal on OneStop or contact FreightRail@mdot.maryland.gov for application details and support. Register on OneStop Portal, verify email address, login, search for Freight Rail Grant Program, review instructions and resources, and complete application. Application timeline: December–April review Project Readiness Checklist, January–March workshops and outreach, April–June application period. Application resources including guidance documents, checklists, and frequently asked questions are available to support the application process. Applicants can email the program office to discuss project ideas or ask questions before applying. Grants Roadshow support sessions are also available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A joint development program through the Maryland Department of Transportation that supports transit-oriented development through public-private partnerships. The program facilitates collaboration between MDOT and public or private developers to deliver mixed-use high-density development on State-owned land in close proximity to transit stations as part of Maryland's TOD strategy and smart growth approach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOT partners with developers to jointly develop State-owned land adjacent to transit stations for mixed-use, high-density development. The program facilitates public-private partnerships and development solicitations for transit station areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private developers interested in partnering with MDOT to develop State-owned land near transit stations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of mixed-use, high-density projects on State-owned land adjacent to transit stations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide at MDOT-owned properties adjacent to designated transit stations.
requirements_list: Project must involve development of State-owned land
Must be in close proximity to a transit station
Development should be mixed-use and high-density
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers may express interest in MDOT-owned properties. MDOT releases public development solicitation opportunities for specific properties and locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot initiative launched in 2024 that provides funding to local jurisdictions to hire Safe Routes to School coordinators who lead SRTS strategies, work directly with schools, manage programming, and prioritize infrastructure improvements around local schools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TAP funds cover 80% of the salary for an SRTS coordinator hired by participating local jurisdictions. As of 2026, four counties have joined the pilot.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Meg Young, Deputy Director of the Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and counties seeking to hire SRTS coordinators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: 80% funding of salary costs for SRTS coordinator positions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to participating counties in Maryland; currently four counties participating as of 2026
requirements_list: Jurisdiction must commit to hiring an SRTS coordinator
Coordinator will lead SRTS strategies, work with schools, manage programming, and prioritize infrastructure improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested jurisdictions should contact MDOT's Office of Active Transportation and Micromobility to inquire about pilot program participation

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program funding tree planting and urban forestry projects in urban areas to support environmental sustainability, shade, stormwater management, and community benefits. In partnership with the Maryland Department of Transportation and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, as well as the Maryland Urban and Community Forest Committee (MUCFC), this funding supports tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, including communities impacted by transportation projects such as Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. The program awards up to $5,000 for planting projects with additional funds available for pocket forest projects. Replanting may occur on both public and private property, subject to project approval. Funds can also be used for project maintenance costs like watering, weeding, and mulching, with up to 5% of the grant available for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for tree planting and urban forestry projects in urban areas to support environmental sustainability, shade, stormwater management, and community benefits. The program awards up to $5,000 for planting projects with additional funds available for pocket forest projects. Funding supports tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, including communities affected by Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns. Replanting may occur on both public and private property, subject to project approval. Funds can be used for project maintenance costs like watering, weeding, and mulching, with up to 5% of the grant available for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion. Applications are reviewed twice a year for spring and fall planting seasons.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 15 (for Spring Planting) and July 15 (for Fall Planting) by 4:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profits, schools, community groups, higher education institutions, community/neighborhood associations, community business associations, homeowners associations, business service groups, youth groups, civic groups, forest conservancy district boards, and eligible partners seeking to plant trees and develop urban forestry projects in communities and organizations impacted by transportation infrastructure projects, experiencing urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and urban forestry projects in urban areas, including tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, pocket forest projects, project maintenance costs like watering, weeding, and mulching, tree materials, supplies, signage, and volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion (up to 5% of grant).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland, with particular focus on areas impacted by transportation projects such as Purple Line construction and identified urban heat islands or environmental justice areas. Projects must be in communities where a state transportation project removed trees.
requirements_list: Projects must involve tree replanting in areas where canopy was lost due to transportation infrastructure
Eligible areas include communities impacted by Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns
Replanting may occur on both public and private property, subject to project approval
Community must have lost trees as a result of transportation construction projects
Project area must have experienced canopy loss due to transportation infrastructure projects
Must get approval from the county Forestry Board before the application deadline
Planted tree species must be native to the area
Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive preference
Funding cannot be used for required mitigation planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis and are reviewed twice a year for spring and fall planting seasons with deadlines on February 15 and July 15 respectively (by 4:30 p.m.). First, get your project approved by your county Forestry Board. Then, submit an application through the Maryland OneStop portal before the deadline. Your application must include a site plan, a photo of the site, a list of proposed native plants, any required permit information, and a maintenance plan. Contact Nick Kurtz for application details and support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation that encourages Maryland employers and employees to participate in commuter benefits programs. Part of Commuter Choice Maryland, MDOT's Travel Demand Management (TDM) Program, designed to reduce congestion, conserve energy, protect the environment, and facilitate economic opportunity. Employers can claim a tax credit equal to 50% of qualified commuter subsidies provided to employees, up to $100 per employee per month. Employees can receive tax-free commuter benefits through employer-provided passes or vouchers, pre-tax salary deductions, or combined cost-sharing arrangements. Qualified commuter benefits include guaranteed ride home, transit passes, vanpools, cash in lieu of parking, telework, carpool, active transportation, and multimodal commuter last mile connection. Available to for-profit businesses registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Taxation, non-profit organizations exempt under IRS Code sections 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4), government agencies, and individuals. The tax credit can be taken against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax in accordance with COMAR 31.06.04.03. The program also provides resources and incentives to make commuting easier, safer, cheaper, and greener, including a mobile app called CommuterCash that allows users to log commute trips to earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for use on transit, vanpools, and eligible parking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive a tax credit equal to 50% of qualified commuter subsidies provided to employees, capped at $100 per employee per month. Qualified benefits include: public or private transit subsidies, vanpool programs, carpool subsidies, guaranteed ride home programs, cash in lieu of parking, telework subsidies, active transportation subsidies, and multimodal last-mile connection services. Non-profit 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations file MD State forms 508CR and MW508. For-profit businesses file MD State Form 500CRW. The credit can be filed against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax in accordance with COMAR 31.06.04.03. The program also offers a mobile app called CommuterCash where users can log commute trips to earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for use on transit, vanpools, and eligible parking.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers (for-profit businesses registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Taxation, non-profit organizations, and government agencies) that provide qualified commuter subsidies to employees, and Maryland employees and commuters seeking commuter benefits and incentives, including those who commute using transit, vanpools, carpools, biking, walking, or teleworking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified commuter benefits including public or private transit subsidies, vanpool programs, carpool subsidies, guaranteed ride home programs, cash in lieu of parking, telework subsidies, active transportation subsidies, and multimodal last-mile connection services. Commuter benefits must be to/from a location in Maryland between employee residence and place of employment. Users of the CommuterCash mobile app can earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Commutes must be from residence or designated meeting place to place of employment in Maryland and occur on weekdays between 5 a.m. and 7 p.m. Over 300 Maryland companies have registered for the program.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland employer or employee
Must be Maryland business in good standing with Maryland Department of Taxation OR § 501(c)(3) or § 501(c)(4) tax-exempt organization
Must provide at least one qualified commuter benefit
Qualified benefits include: Guaranteed Ride Home, Vanpool, Transit, Cash in Lieu of Parking, Telework, Carpool, Active Transportation, and Multimodal Commuter Last Mile Connection
Commuter benefits must meet transportation purpose for employee commutes
Commutes must occur on weekdays between 5 a.m. and 7 p.m.
Annual re-registration required
Employees must be participating in commuter benefits program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers gather business information, types of commuter subsidies provided, and subsidy amounts, then complete the application at the One Stop Maryland website or through the Maryland One Stop portal. When approved, the employer receives an email with a certificate qualifying them for the tax credit. When filing annual taxes, the employer includes the certificate with tax forms to receive the credit. Non-profit 501(c)(3)/501(c)(4) organizations submit MD State forms 508CR and MW508. For-profit businesses submit MD State Form 500CRW. Employees work with their employer to enroll in the program to receive tax-free commuter benefits through employer-provided passes, vouchers, pre-tax salary deductions, or combined cost-sharing arrangements. Users can also download the CommuterCash mobile app and log their trips to earn and redeem points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Highway Safety Office Safety Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A 100% reimbursable grant program that funds behavioral safety projects, educational campaigns, and proven safety countermeasures to change behaviors through education, engagement, and enforcement and improve traffic safety in Maryland. The program supports Safe Routes to School initiatives, behavioral change projects, safety campaigns, educational materials, and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) proven countermeasures related to the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan. It focuses on key highway safety priorities including preventing impaired driving, distracted driving, speeding and aggressive driving, and promoting occupant protection and the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young drivers, and older drivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% reimbursable grants for behavioral safety pilot projects, safety projects related to the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan, safety campaigns, educational materials, and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) proven countermeasures. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis, meaning applicants must spend funds first before receiving reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies, municipalities, non-profit organizations, regional agencies, state colleges, universities, and other eligible entities implementing traffic safety and Safe Routes to School initiatives in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral safety pilot projects, safety projects related to the Maryland Strategic Highway Safety Plan, safety campaigns, educational materials, and proven NHTSA countermeasures to improve highway and transportation safety. Funds support outreach projects focused on preventing impaired driving, distracted driving, speeding, and aggressive driving, as well as projects promoting seat belt use and the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young drivers, and older drivers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available across Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must target changing behaviors through education, engagement, and enforcement
Must improve traffic safety in Maryland relating to SRTS initiatives
Projects must be related to pedestrian, bicycle, speed, or aggressive driving programs
The proposed project must address an identified highway safety priority
The proposal must include strategies, action steps, and measurable outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should first plan their project by considering the safety problem, target population, proposed solution, and evaluation methods. Contact a technical advisor at the Maryland Highway Safety Office for help. To apply, use the online 'Grant & Projects for Safety' portal or contact MHSO for grant application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that installs and maintains cast metal historical markers along Maryland state roads to commemorate places, people, and events of statewide historical significance. The program reviews and replaces existing markers with factual errors or insensitive language.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOT designs, fabricates, and installs historical markers on state-owned property within state road rights of way. The agency funds and maintains the markers. After application approval, the review process, fabrication, and installation may take up to 6 months. Applicants can request an unveiling event, which MDOT will coordinate with the installation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Julie Schablitsky, Director of Cultural Resources
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private individuals, nonprofit organizations, government agencies, and businesses seeking to commemorate places, people, and events of statewide historical significance in Maryland. Applicants do not need to be state residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance funds the design, fabrication, and installation of a historical marker to commemorate a subject of statewide historical significance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Markers are located on state-owned property, primarily within Maryland state road rights of way. Markers cannot be placed on private, county, or other municipal land. Final location is determined by MDOT SHA for safety reasons.
requirements_list: Subject must have statewide significance tied to the national stage
Subject must be an influential person, place, thing, trend, or event that occurred within Maryland
Resource must be at least 50 years old (with exceptions for exceptional importance)

Subject must be associated with events contributing to broad patterns of history, significant persons, built resources with distinctive characteristics, archaeological significance, or traditionally disenfranchised individuals or communities

Generally ineligible: cemeteries, religious institutions, moved buildings or structures, recently reconstructed historic buildings, commemorative properties, or resources under 50 years old (unless exceptions apply)
Application must include complete documentation
Must provide proposed marker location (MDOT SHA makes final determination)
Must provide historical research and accurate references
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application by January 1st or July 1st deadline. Up to five markers are selected during each cycle. Applications not submitted by the deadline are considered for the following cycle. After selection, MDOT coordinates with Maryland Historical Trust to review research and finalize the 70-word marker text. MDOT staff contact the nominator to work through revisions and coordinate any commemorative event. Applicants can request an unveiling event timed with installation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program supporting the implementation of complete streets approaches that prioritize safe access for all users including pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and vehicles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and technical assistance to help local jurisdictions implement complete streets projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government jurisdictions in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Complete streets infrastructure projects that provide safe access for pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and vehicles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing funding for new sidewalk construction to improve pedestrian access.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided through Fund 79 for new sidewalk construction projects that enhance pedestrian access.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New sidewalk construction for pedestrian access
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grant program providing funding to support projects that enhance the movement of goods through ports and related intermodal connections. The program focuses on improving safety, efficiency, and reliability of freight operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding for port infrastructure projects. Funds a range of eligible activities including port infrastructure upgrades, intermodal freight connections, operational improvements, resilience measures addressing environmental and climate-related risks, planning and development-phase activities such as feasibility analyses and environmental review, and investments in emissions reduction technologies and electrification infrastructure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Port authorities and public entities involved in freight operations and intermodal connections.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Port infrastructure upgrades, intermodal freight connections, operational improvements, resilience measures, planning and development activities, emissions reduction technologies, and electrification infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects evaluated based on ability to address freight mobility needs
Measurable economic and operational benefits required
Alignment with regional and national freight priorities
Readiness for implementation including financial and technical capacity
Geographic distribution considered
Support for opportunity zones considered
Innovative technologies incorporation considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For FY 2026, applications are due June 1, 2026. Applicants should consult program-specific guidance in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Applications must be submitted through Grants.gov. Applicants must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) from www.SAM.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Works and Economic Adjustment Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive funding to support infrastructure, workforce, and economic recovery projects in distressed communities. Eligible activities include public works construction, broadband and utilities, workforce facilities, business incubators, revolving loan funds, and economic development planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding for infrastructure, workforce, and economic recovery projects in distressed communities. Funds public works construction, broadband and utilities, workforce facilities, business incubators, revolving loan funds, and economic development planning aligned with a regional Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, local governments, Tribes, nonprofits, economic development organizations, and public-private partnerships in distressed communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public works construction, broadband and utilities, workforce facilities, business incubators, revolving loan funds, and economic development planning aligned with regional CEDS.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Distressed communities nationwide, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be in a distressed community
Projects must be aligned with a regional Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS)
Cost share required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Applicants should consult program-specific guidance. Applications must be submitted through Grants.gov. Applicants must have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) from www.SAM.gov. Cost share is required.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides federal funds for the elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings. Projects are prioritized based on safety criteria and available funding. The program is managed by the Rail Safety Program Manager and receives funds from the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) through the State Highway Administration (SHA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds are apportioned to Maryland by formula to support the elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings. Funds support projects that improve crossing safety statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local jurisdictions, and railroad operators seeking to improve railway-highway crossing safety.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings, including construction and reconstruction of safety improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available for public crossings throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must involve a public railway-highway crossing
Projects are prioritized based on safety criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Rail Safety Program Manager to discuss project eligibility and funding. Projects are reviewed and prioritized based on safety criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program providing federal and matching funds for the development, improvement, maintenance, and restoration of recreational trails throughout Maryland. The program supports both land and water-based trails for motorized and non-motorized recreational uses, including trail-related facilities, equipment leasing, property acquisition, easements, accessibility assessments, and educational materials about trail safety and environmental protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable federal-aid grant program that funds development and maintenance of trails and trail-related facilities for pedestrian, cycling, equestrian, skiing, snowmobiling, off-road motorcycling, off-highway vehicle riding, paddle sports, personal watercraft, and motorized boat uses. Requires matching funds or in-kind contributions from the applicant.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Cheryl Ladota, Division Chief, Grants and Programs Management (GPMD) Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, and governmental entities overseeing transportation or recreational trails in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and maintenance of land and water-based recreational trails and trail-related facilities for pedestrian, cycling, equestrian, skiing, snowmobiling, off-road motorcycling, off-highway vehicle riding, paddle sports, personal watercraft, and motorized boat uses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Requires matching funds or in-kind contributions
Competitively selected program
Projects solicited on an annual basis

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing funding for retrofit projects that improve pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided through Fund 88 for retrofit projects that enhance pedestrian and bicycle access and safety.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government jurisdictions in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retrofit projects for pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Programs and subsidies for carpool, vanpool, and transit that make commuting easier, safer, cheaper, and greener. Vanpools save $500 every month. Carpoolers earn a $5 daily incentive for up to 90 days. New transit riders receive free CharmPass transit passes during promotional periods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Vanpool participants save approximately $500 per month. Carpool participants earn a $5 daily incentive for up to 90 days. New transit riders receive free CharmPass transit passes during promotional periods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore-area commuters looking for sustainable commuting methods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation subsidies and incentives for carpool, vanpool, and transit use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore-area commuters; also includes commuters traveling anywhere in Maryland or to the Washington, DC area for the CommuterCash component.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit program pages for transit program details. For carpool and vanpool programs, visit baltimorecommutes.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ride Together Rewards: Baltimore Transit Incentive Program - CharmPass New Rider Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: A program offering free transit passes to new users of the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) system during select promotional periods. New transit riders download the CharmPass mobile app, set up an account, and receive free transit passes loaded directly onto their account to use on MTA transit services in the Greater Baltimore region. Passes are valid for use on Baltimore local buses, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC. Passes expire after 90 days and are non-transferable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free transit passes loaded directly onto CharmPass account during promotional periods (May 1-8, June 1-8, July 1-8, 2026). Passes are valid for use on MTA transit services including Baltimore local buses (City, Local, Express Bus), Light Rail, Metro Subway, MARC Train, and Commuter Bus within the Greater Baltimore region. Passes expire after 90 days and are non-transferable, non-redeemable for cash, and cannot be transferred to other users.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: During select promotional periods: May 1-8, 2026; June 1-8, 2026; July 1-8, 2026. Outside these periods, interested riders can sign up for alerts about the next promotional period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New transit riders in the Greater Baltimore area who have not previously used MTA transit services and want to try using public transportation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free transit passes for use on MTA transit services including Baltimore local buses (City, Local, Express Bus), Light Rail, Metro Subway, MARC Train, and Commuter Bus within the Greater Baltimore region
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore region accessible to MTA stations through local transit services, commuter bus, and MARC
requirements_list: Must be a first-time (new) user of the MTA transit system
Must download the CharmPass mobile application
Must set up an account with email, name, and phone number
Must verify account within 48 hours
Must select desired type of transit pass
Must share feedback by taking part in periodic brief surveys about transit experience
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the CharmPass mobile application. 2. Set up an account with email, name, and phone number and select desired type of transit pass. 3. Account will be verified within 48 hours. 4. Transit passes will be loaded directly onto CharmPass account. 5. Use passes to travel on MTA transit services during promotional period. 6. Participate in periodic brief surveys about transit experience.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ride Together Rewards: FareShare Employer Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program for employers in the Greater Baltimore area to offset the cost of purchasing transit passes for their employees. Employers receive up to $3,000 as a credit on their CharmPass account ($1,000 per month over three continuous months) to purchase transit fares for employees. Participating employers also gain enrollment in the MDOT Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program, which provides free resources and tools. The incentive helps employers attract, retain, and ensure reliable transportation for employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $3,000 provided as a credit on the employer's CharmPass account ($1,000 per month over three continuous months) to purchase transit passes for employees. The credit is loaded directly to the employer's CharmPass account and then distributed to employee digital CharmPass app accounts. Employers must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to their starting month and submit next month's purchase by the 25th of the month.
