structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification to operate as a qualified fleet inspection station
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application for admission to the FIS program; contact MDE for technical and equipment details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland law requires large food residual generators (schools, supermarkets, food processing facilities) that generate at least one ton of food residuals per week and are located near an organic recycling facility to separate and divert food residuals from landfills and incinerators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The law establishes mandatory requirements for food residual separation and diversion. Large generators must comply with reporting requirements and can apply for waivers if they do not meet the applicability criteria. Regulations describe mandatory reporting procedures and waiver application processes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Large food residual generators including schools, supermarkets, and food processing facilities that generate at least one ton of food residuals per week and are located near an organic recycling facility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The law requires diversion of food residuals from landfills and incinerators to organic recycling facilities (composting or anaerobic digestion).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies statewide to large food residual generators located near organic recycling facilities.
requirements_list: Must generate at least one ton of food residuals per week
Must be located near an organic recycling facility
Must separate and divert food residuals from landfill/incinerators
Must comply with mandatory reporting requirements
Can apply for waivers if exemption criteria are met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Facilities subject to the law must comply with reporting requirements. Those unable to comply can submit a waiver application form to request an exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps private forest landowners protect and enhance their forest lands and associated wetlands through technical assistance and cost-sharing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance is provided to help landowners enhance and protect timber, fish and wildlife habitat, water quality, wetlands, and recreational and aesthetic values of their property. The companion Stewardship Incentive Program provides cost-sharing for implementing Forest Stewardship plans. Maximum annual cost-share is $10,000 per landowner. Over an average year, approximately $100,000 is distributed to 150 landowners covering 2,000 acres. Practices must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners with five or more acres of forest land or non-forest land that can be planted to trees
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Forest management plan development, afforestation, forest improvement, windbreaks and hedgerows, streamside and wetlands protection, fisheries and aquatic habitat improvement, wildlife habitat enhancement, forest recreation habitat enhancement, and soil and water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Landowner must own five or more acres of forest land or non-forest land suitable for tree planting
Practices implemented with cost-share assistance must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service. Technical assistance is provided to develop a Forest Stewardship Plan. Eligible practices in the plan may receive cost-sharing through the Stewardship Incentive Program under open enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A nationwide program that provides cost-share assistance to private forest landowners for implementing approved forestry practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal cost-share money is available with a limit of $10,000 per person per year. Cost-share is limited to no more than 65 percent of the cost of implementing an approved forestry practice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting, improving a stand of forest trees, and site preparation for natural regeneration
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in counties designated on the basis of a Forest Service survey of total eligible private timber acreage. Local USDA offices or state foresters have information on which counties participate.
requirements_list: Landowner must own no more than 1,000 acres of eligible forest land
Must be a private landowner of nonindustrial forest

Individuals, groups, associations, or corporations whose stocks are not publicly traded may be eligible, provided they are not primarily engaged in the business of manufacturing forest products or providing public utility services
Land must be suitable for afforestation, reforestation, or improved forest management
Land must be capable of producing marketable timber crops and meet minimum productivity standards
At least 10 acres of eligible forest land is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact their local USDA Service Center to determine if their county participates in FIP and to discuss eligible practices. Applications are processed through the local USDA office with cost-share funding provided for approved practices.

structured_extraction.program_name: General Permit for Stormwater Associated with Construction Activity (20-CP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state NPDES general permit (MDRC) that authorizes discharges of stormwater associated with construction activity. Permits are issued to construction site operators who conduct land-disturbing activities of one or more acres and implement erosion and sediment control measures, stormwater pollution prevention plans, and turbidity monitoring to protect water quality. Covers stormwater runoff, snowmelt runoff, and surface runoff/drainage from construction sites, as well as authorized non-stormwater discharges (dust control water, landscape irrigation). Operators must have operational control over construction plans and specifications or day-to-day operational control of site activities. Implements EPA's Construction and Development (C&D) Rule requirements (40 CFR Part 450) and establishes technology-based and water quality-based effluent limitations.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a regulatory permit, not a financial assistance program. The permit authorizes construction site operators to discharge stormwater if they comply with erosion and sediment control requirements, including preparing a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), implementing best management practices, conducting inspections, submitting quarterly turbidity reports, and establishing Stream Protection Zones. The permit is administered through an electronic application system (ePermits). Fees apply based on the current fee structure in COMAR 26.08.04.09-1, with exemptions for local and state government projects. Chemical additive authorization available as last resort when conventional controls are insufficient. Covered discharges include stormwater runoff, snowmelt runoff, surface runoff/drainage, dust control water, and landscape irrigation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; Notice of Intent must be submitted electronically through ePermits portal prior to construction start. Effective April 1, 2023 through March 31, 2028. Various submission deadlines apply: new sites minimum 14 days prior to construction; existing 14GP permittees by September 30, 2023; emergency projects within 7 days of commencing activities. Notice of Termination due no later than 30 days after meeting permit requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Construction site operators, general contractors, developers, construction support activity operators, site owners, institutions, and parties with operational control over construction projects who conduct land-disturbing activities that result in stormwater discharge. Includes operators of construction support activities such as concrete/asphalt batch plants, equipment staging yards, and material storage areas. May include mining operations for pre-active mining staging areas and access roads.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a regulatory permit, not a funding program. It authorizes stormwater discharge from construction sites when proper erosion and sediment control measures are implemented. Covered stormwater management includes erosion and sediment control, pollution prevention, sediment removal, buffer preservation, perimeter controls, soil stabilization, dust minimization, inlet protection, chemical additive management, and dewatering controls.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for all areas discharging to waters of the State. Special requirements for Tier I watersheds (50-foot undisturbed natural buffer minimum). Enhanced requirements for Tier II watersheds (100-foot average buffer with minimum 50 feet at any point). Additional requirements for sites discharging to sediment-impaired waters and PCB-impaired waters. Operators must be registered to do business in Maryland.
requirements_list: Operator must have operational control over construction plans and specifications or day-to-day operational control of site activities
Project must disturb one or more acres of land or be part of a common plan of development disturbing one or more acres
Operator must submit Notice of Intent (NOI) electronically through ePermits before starting construction

Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) must be developed and implemented prior to construction start, identifying all operators, stormwater team, site mapping, pollution-generating activities, and control measures
Erosion and sediment control (E&SC) measures must meet Maryland standards and specifications per ESC Handbook
Stream Protection Zone (SPZ) requirements must be met: minimum 50-foot undisturbed natural buffer for Tier I watersheds; average 100-foot buffer (minimum 50 feet at any point) for Tier II watersheds
Achieve 95% groundcover vegetation stabilization within 3-7 calendar days of disturbance or 70% native vegetation before discontinuing inspections
Personnel responsible for implementation and maintenance of erosion and sediment controls must be properly trained per COMAR 26.17.01.06

Construction activity inspections must be conducted and documented; weekly or bi-weekly inspections for earth-disturbing activity in Tier II watersheds; every 4 calendar days for Tier II SPZ activities; before and after rainfall events exceeding 0.5 inches
Quarterly turbidity reports must be submitted for sites discharging to sediment-impaired waters or Tier II watersheds (150 NTU benchmark)
Water and Science Administration Compliance Program must be notified 2 weeks prior to start of construction by calling (410) 537-3510
Antidegradation requirements must be addressed for Tier II watershed projects per Appendix C
Certain projects may require review under Sensitive Species Project Review Areas (SSPRA) and MERLIN Online
Cationic chemical additives may require approval via Request for Cationic Chemical Additives Form submitted one week prior to use; all additives must be certified under ANSI/NSF Standard 60
Remove sediment before accumulation reaches one-half control height
Remove tracked-out sediment same or next business day by sweeping/shoveling (no hosing into storm drains)
Maintain all controls in effective operating condition; routine maintenance by close of next business day if needed

Submit corrective action documentation within specified timeframes for damaged controls; Section B of Corrective Action Log must be completed within 24 hours of discovering triggering condition; Section C completed within 24 hours after completing corrective action
Submit Notice of Termination (NOT) when coverage ends and site is stabilized (within 30 days of meeting requirements); photographic documentation of stabilized areas required
PCB controls required for pre-1980 building demolition (≥10,000 sq ft) in PCB-impaired waters; minimize exposure of building materials to precipitation and stormwater
24-hour notification of upsets; documentation within 5 calendar days
Maintain records for 3 years after permit termination
Proper operation and maintenance of treatment and control systems
Protect storm drain inlets before site disturbance begins
Establish stabilized construction exits
Implement good housekeeping practices including proper waste management, material staging, and washout area designation
Develop spill prevention and response plan; notify National Response Center for hazardous spills meeting reportable quantities

Dewatering activities must be inspected and documented daily when discharge occurs; pollutant discharge indicators must trigger corrective action; turbidity monitoring (minimum 1 sample daily per discharge point) required for sites discharging to sensitive waters with weekly average turbidity data submission to EPA quarterly (50 NTU benchmark)
Personnel conducting inspections must complete EPA training or hold equivalent non-EPA certification as of February 17, 2023
Bi-weekly or weekly inspection schedules required; additional inspection within 24 hours of rainfall ≥0.25 inches in 24 hours or snowmelt ≥3.25 inches
Final stabilization of all disturbed areas before permit termination: 70% cover of native vegetation or equivalent non-vegetative measures
Chemical storage minimum 50 feet from receiving waters with secondary containment and leak-proof structures
Erosion-resistant surfaces at discharge points and velocity dissipating measures at dewatering discharge
Minimize soil compaction in vegetatively stabilized and infiltration practice areas
Preserve native topsoil unless infeasible
Minimize disturbance to steep slopes
Install perimeter controls including sediment controls, filter berms, and silt fences
Direct stormwater to vegetated areas where feasible
Manage stockpiles with sediment barriers and cover
Provide equipment maintenance and fueling controls with secondary containment
Properly store and handle building materials, chemicals, pesticides, fuel, and waste
Direct vehicle wash water to sediment basins
Contain applicator/concrete washout in leak-proof containers; prohibit concrete washout wastewater, stucco/paint washout, fuels and oils, soaps or solvents discharge unless properly managed
Apply fertilizer per manufacturer specifications
Initiate soil stabilization measures when earth-disturbing activities cease for 14+ calendar days
Design stormwater controls per good engineering practices
Use surface outlet structures for basin discharges
Obtain Stormwater Management Plan approval before beginning earth disturbance
Implement Environmental Site Design (ESD) to maximum extent practicable

Provide legible site maps showing property boundaries, construction locations, water bodies, discharge points, impaired/Tier II waters, critical habitat areas, stormwater flow, drainage inlets, pollutant-generating activities, control measures, stabilization areas, natural buffers, and chemical storage/application locations
Identify all non-stormwater discharges
Prevent discharge of visible floating solids or foam
Comply with velocity dissipation requirements at discharge points
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine if permit is needed using the 20-CP Decision Tree (projects disturbing 1+ acres in Maryland with stormwater exposure). 2. Determine operational control status using five-question evaluation process to confirm party is an 'operator.' 3. Register an account on the ePermits website (egov.maryland.gov/mde/npdes). 4. If using agents or consultants to prepare the NOI, execute a Subscriber Agreement Template Form. 5. Prepare Erosion & Sediment Control (E&SC) plan per Maryland ESC Handbook. 6. Prepare Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) using the provided template and guidance if required; include site assessment, BMP identification, pollution sources, inspection/maintenance procedures, and certification. Identify all operators and controlled areas; establish stormwater team with named personnel and responsibilities; describe nature of construction activities, project size, disturbance area, and schedule; provide legible site map(s) showing all required features; document all pollution-generating activities and control measures; describe non-stormwater discharges; establish inspection, maintenance, and corrective action procedures; document staff training requirements; comply with threatened and endangered species protection and Safe Drinking Water Act UIC requirements if applicable. 7. Develop Stormwater Management (SWM) plan as applicable. 8. Complete the Notice of Intent (NOI) electronically, providing required information including project details, SWPPP/E&SC information, and project location. Identify all chemical additives to be used. 9. Electronically sign the NOI as the responsible party (person in authority from developer, builder, or operator with operational control). 10. Submit the NOI through ePermits along with all supporting documents including completed and signed E&SC plan, SWPPP (where applicable), and signed Antidegradation Checklist (for Tier II watershed projects). 11. Pay applicable fees through the ePermits payment system (credit card or ACH). 12. A 14-day Public Notification Period is initiated and information is published on MDE's ePermits Public Notice page. 13. Notify MDE Water and Science Administration Compliance Program 2 weeks prior to start of construction by calling (410) 537-3510. 14. Implement erosion and sediment control measures and maintain SWPPP/E&SC throughout construction. 15. Assemble stormwater team and train personnel on CGP requirements. 16. Conduct required inspections and maintain records; use provided inspection templates as needed; maintain corrective action log; submit inspection reports within 24 hours of inspection completion. 17. Submit quarterly turbidity reports if applicable; submit weekly average turbidity monitoring data (50 NTU benchmark or EPA-approved alternate) through NeT-CGP or approved alternative. 18. Submit Notice of Termination when construction is complete and site is stabilized (within 30 days of meeting requirements) with photographic documentation of stabilized areas. 19. Retain records for 3 years after permit termination. 20. Keep current SWPPP on-site or at accessible location and modify within 7 days of specified conditions; maintain records of all modifications.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program that combines workshops and site visits to help businesses identify environmental improvement opportunities, set sustainability goals, and develop green teams without requiring ISO 14001 certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance combining workshops and site visits to help businesses identify environmental opportunities, set green goals, and establish green teams.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses interested in environmental management and sustainability without pursuing ISO 14001 certification.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance in identifying environmental opportunities, setting sustainability goals, and developing internal green teams.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland businesses.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should contact the program to learn about workshop enrollment and site visit scheduling.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program offered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to fund hazard mitigation projects that reduce risk to individuals and property from natural hazards. FEMA provides states with funds equal to 7.5% of emergency financial assistance rendered following a declared disaster. These funds are used for projects such as property purchases, house relocations, or house elevations to reduce the risk of future flood damage to properties within the 100-year floodplain and to reduce reliance on federal disaster funds and flood insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA provides funds equal to 7.5% of emergency financial assistance following a declared disaster. Funds are matched with State and local funds on a 75/25 basis (FEMA/State and local). Grants support hazard mitigation projects including property purchases, house relocations, house elevations, and other projects to reduce risk of future flood damage within the 100-year floodplain and from other natural hazards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, communities, property owners, and entities in areas where federal disaster has been declared due to flooding or other natural hazards within the 100-year floodplain.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property purchases, house relocations, house elevations, and other hazard mitigation projects to reduce risk of future flood damage and natural hazard risks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland following a declared federal disaster and through MEMA administration.
requirements_list: Property must be within the 100-year floodplain
Federal disaster must be declared in the area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed through Maryland Emergency Management Agency (MEMA) and FEMA following a declared disaster using application guidance package and FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance Unified Guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rebates to homeowners and landlords for energy efficiency upgrades in single-family and multi-family buildings. Rebates help offset the cost of eligible projects projected to save significant energy use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners and landlords can receive up to $4,000 or 50% of project costs for eligible efficiency upgrades projected to save at least 35% of a home's energy use. Projects with modeled energy savings of 20-34% receive up to $2,000 or 50% of project costs. Higher rebate amounts are available for households with income levels less than 80% of the area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and landlords in Maryland with single-family and multi-family buildings seeking to reduce energy costs through efficiency upgrades.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible efficiency upgrades projected to save at least 20% of a home's energy use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Energy efficiency upgrades must be eligible and meet specific energy savings thresholds (20% or greater)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MEA will develop rebate application processes that are accessible to all Marylanders, including low-income building owners and occupants. Details on how to apply will be made available as the program launches in 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: ISO 14001 Environmental Management System Implementation Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment, in partnership with the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership and the University of Maryland Technology Enterprise Institute, offers assistance to Maryland manufacturers and companies in developing and implementing environmental management systems based on the ISO 14001 global standard. The program helps organizations systematically identify and manage their regulated and unregulated environmental impacts. The six-month program includes four one-day workshops spaced six weeks apart, followed by specific work assignments and field implementation assistance. Participants work in groups of three to six businesses. There is a $1,000 cost share per company for participation in the manufacturing-focused track. The program also offers technical assistance on implementation of cost-saving pollution prevention technologies. Enrollment is on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program includes four one-day workshops spaced six weeks apart, followed by specific work assignments and field implementation assistance. Participants work in groups of three to six businesses. There is a $1,000 cost share per company for participation. The program also offers free technical assistance on implementation of cost-saving pollution prevention technologies and development and implementation of Environmental Management Systems based on ISO 14001 standard. Enrollment is on a first come, first served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland manufacturers and companies seeking to implement environmental management systems and improve their environmental compliance and operational efficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and implementation of environmental management systems based on ISO 14001 standard to improve environmental regulatory compliance, reduce environmental costs and liability, increase environmental awareness, and improve operational efficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to manufacturers and companies throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a manufacturing organization or Maryland company
Participate in groups of three to six businesses
Commit to a six-month program
Pay $1,000 cost share per company
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Laura Armstrong at 410-537-4119 or laura.armstrong@maryland.gov, or Paul Gietka at 410-916-4061 or pgietka@mdmep.org to learn more and enroll. Enrollment is on a first come, first served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages schools and green centers to establish vehicle idling reduction policies to improve air quality, reduce fuel waste, and protect student and staff health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating schools receive a letter and signed certificate from the Secretary of the Environment, a metal idling reduction sign for school grounds, window decals for school and office windows, and other program materials. Participation is free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools and green centers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides recognition materials and signage to support vehicle idling reduction policies at schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland schools and green centers.
requirements_list: Schools must establish a vehicle idling reduction policy
Schools must send an email to mde.idlefreemd@maryland.gov to sign up
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools interested in participating should send an email to mde.idlefreemd@maryland.gov. Upon enrollment, schools receive a certificate from the Secretary of the Environment, signage, decals, and other program materials. Participating schools are added to the Idle Free MD Honor Roll.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program providing financial assistance to property owners for voluntary environmental enhancement projects such as wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, and wildlife habitat creation on properties with unvegetated areas adjacent to streams or wetlands, drained fields, woods, or filled wetlands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for voluntary environmental enhancement projects including wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, and wildlife habitat creation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with eligible land conditions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wetlands restoration, streambank stabilization, tree plantings, and wildlife habitat creation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for properties with specific environmental features
requirements_list: Property must have unvegetated areas adjacent to streams or wetlands, drained or eroded fields, woods or streams, or filled wetlands

structured_extraction.program_name: MDE State Grant Capital Programs Minority and Women's Business Enterprises (M/WBE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Program establishing good faith efforts requirements for M/WBE participation in procurement under MDE financial assistance agreements. A state grant program that requires grant recipients and prime contractors to make good-faith efforts to utilize minority business enterprises (MBEs) and women's business enterprises (WBEs) in procurement contracts financed with state grants. The program applies to several MDE capital programs including the Bay Restoration Fund, Water Pollution Control Fund, and Water Supply Financial Assistance Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance agreements with M/WBE participation requirements and good faith efforts mandates. State grants are provided through capital programs for water and environmental projects. M/WBE participation is required through good-faith efforts. Grant recipients and prime contractors must make affirmative efforts to place qualified MBEs and WBEs on solicitation lists, solicit proposals from them, divide contracts into smaller components where feasible, establish reasonable delivery schedules, and encourage joint ventures or consortium participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grant recipients, prime contractors (construction and architecture/engineering services vendors), minority and women-owned business enterprises seeking state grant funding for water quality, drinking water, bay restoration, biological nutrient removal, and water supply projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State grant funds finance water quality, drinking water, bay restoration, and water supply capital projects. M/WBE participation requirements apply to all procurement contracts for construction, equipment, services, and supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Performed entirely within the State of Maryland. Applies to projects funded under the Bay Restoration Fund, Water Pollution Control Fund (grants exceeding $500,000), and Water Supply Financial Assistance Fund (grants exceeding $500,000).
requirements_list: Ensure M/WBEs awareness of contracting opportunities through outreach and recruitment
Solicit MBEs and WBEs whenever they are potential sources
Divide requirements into small tasks/quantities when economically feasible; minimum 30-day bid/proposal posting period
Make information on opportunities available to M/WBEs; arrange delivery schedules to encourage participation
Use Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) for M/WBE listing and certification
Grant recipients must require prime contractors to apply good faith efforts if subcontracts are let
Develop M/WBE bidders list through advertising and outreach
Break down projects into smaller components economically feasible for M/WBE participation
Include M/WBE as responsiveness criteria in bid documents
Include MDE Grant Insert in bidding documents
Submit checklists and supporting documentation with bid proposals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grant recipients must develop lists of qualified M/WBE firms by contacting MDOT, project owners, and MDE. Bid opportunities must be posted and shared with M/WBE firms. Prime contractors must be required to break down contracts into smaller components where feasible, establish reasonable delivery schedules, and submit M/WBE information with bids. Complete M/WBE Participation Good Faith Efforts Checklist and submit Attachment A (Solicitation Summary and Results) for each prime contract or subcontract. Provide supporting documentation for all required answers. The program requires use of specific forms to guide and report good-faith efforts and M/WBE participation outcomes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Diesel Vehicle Initiative (EPA DERA FY2023-2024)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment to replace older diesel school buses with new electric buses and replace older drayage trucks at the Port of Baltimore with newer EPA-compliant trucks. School bus replacements receive financial assistance of up to 45 percent of the purchase price, with charging infrastructure eligible for funding. Dray truck replacements receive assistance for up to 50 percent of the truck price, up to a maximum of $35,000 per truck (or historically $30,000 in prior fiscal years). This is part of the EPA's Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) State Grant program, which has supported the replacement of over 42 drayage trucks at the Port of Baltimore in previous funding cycles. The program is funded through the VW Mitigation Trust using the DERA option.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance for school bus replacements up to 45 percent of the purchase price of new electric buses (with owner providing the remainder) and charging infrastructure. For dray trucks at the Port of Baltimore, assistance covers up to 50 percent of the cost of newer EPA-compliant trucks, with maximum assistance of $35,000 per truck (historically $30,000). School buses must be replaced with electric buses or new diesel buses with 2019 or newer model year engines. Dray trucks must have MY2017 or newer EPA-compliant engines (or historically MY2012 or newer with EPA 2010 compliance). Replaced vehicles are destroyed and scrappage income is credited toward the owner's share of the purchase price. Owners must provide matching funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, public school systems, drayage truck owners, and port operators in Maryland, with particular focus on Port of Baltimore area operators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new electric school buses, associated charging infrastructure, and replacement of older drayage trucks with newer EPA-compliant models
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for school buses; Port of Baltimore area for dray trucks and surrounding communities
requirements_list: Must be replacing older diesel school buses or drayage trucks
School buses must be replaced with electric buses or new diesel buses with 2019 or newer model year engines
Dray trucks must have MY2017 or newer EPA-compliant engines
Dray trucks historically required MY2012 or newer engine with EPA 2010 compliance
Owner must provide the remainder of the purchase price beyond the grant assistance
Vehicle being replaced must be destroyed
Scrappage income received must be applied toward owner's share of purchase price
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit grant applications for approval through the EPA DERA State Grant program process. Drayage truck owners and school districts apply for grants to replace older vehicles with cleaner, more efficient models.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Department of the Environment Linked Deposit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Farmers and private homeowners can apply for loans from a qualifying financial institution to install a living shoreline project at a below-market interest rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from qualifying financial institutions at below-market interest rates for installation of living shoreline projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and private homeowners in Maryland interested in installing living shorelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of living shoreline projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or private homeowner
Must apply through a qualifying financial institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply for a loan through a qualifying financial institution.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration provides funding for a variety of public and private projects within Maryland, including alternative fuel use and coordination of the US Department of Energy's Clean Cities Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides funding for public and private projects focused on alternative fuel use and clean energy within Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private organizations in Maryland focused on alternative fuels and clean energy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Alternative fuel projects and clean energy initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Administration Commercial Clean Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants for commercial clean energy projects, including renewable energy systems installation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for commercial clean energy projects such as photovoltaic systems, solar water heating, geothermal systems, and wind energy installations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial businesses and organizations seeking to install renewable energy systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and installation of renewable energy systems including photovoltaic, solar water heating, solar-powered exterior lighting, geothermal systems, and wind energy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free, voluntary membership program for businesses and organizations to demonstrate their commitment to environmental sustainability and pollution prevention. Members share environmental best practices and results on the registry website and receive recognition, technical assistance, access to webinars and conferences, use of the Maryland Green Registry logo, window decals, LinkedIn group access, and eligibility for annual Leadership Awards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free membership with no application cost. Members receive technical and informational assistance to help implement new environmental best practices, access to webinars and conferences, annual contests and prize drawings, use of the Maryland Green Registry logo, window decals, LinkedIn group access, and eligibility for annual Leadership Awards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and organizations of all types and sizes in Maryland, both in owned and leased spaces, committed to environmental sustainability and pollution prevention.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental practices and sustainability initiatives such as reducing energy and water usage, reducing waste, and other environmental best practices implementation. The program provides technical assistance and recognition; it is not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to organizations and facilities in both owned and leased space throughout Maryland statewide. Must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Located in Maryland
Implement and share information on at least five environmental practices
Provide at least one quantitative/measurable result from these practices

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides oversight for the voluntary cleanup of properties contaminated with hazardous substances. The program allows property owners and prospective purchasers to investigate and clean up contaminated sites with liability protections. The program streamlines the cleanup process while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and provides liability protection for participants through a Memorandum of Agreement with EPA Region III that designates sites as 'no interest' to EPA once a No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion is issued. Eligible purchasers can substantially limit liability for past contamination before purchasing property. The program works in conjunction with the Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program which offers tax credits, loans, and grants for redevelopment of eligible brownfield properties in participating jurisdictions. The program encourages the investigation, cleanup, and redevelopment of eligible properties with known or suspected contamination. The program issues Environmental Covenants to restrict future use of properties and provides determinations (NFRD/COC) conditioned on permissible use, land use controls, and institutional controls.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The VCP provides administrative oversight and technical guidance for site investigation and remediation. Participants submit applications with environmental assessments, cleanup plans, and work with MDE throughout the process. MDE reviews applications, approves cleanup standards and remedial action plans, and issues final site approval letters (No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion) that provide liability protections and establish Environmental Covenants with land use and institutional controls. An application fee of $10,000 applies for initial applications (effective June 1, 2025) and $2,000 for subsequent applications or expedited reviews. Fee waivers are available for renewable energy siting and development projects. Expedited Inculpable Person (IP) approval is available for a $2,000 fee. The program provides guidance on preparing Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) in accordance with ASTM E1903 standards to identify contamination, assess human health risks, determine need for remedial action, and establish appropriate regulatory closure path. Upon completion, participants receive determinations conditioned on permissible use, land use controls, and institutional controls, which must be recorded in land records.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program with no defined deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, prospective purchasers, responsible parties, developers, lenders, government entities, heirs, environmental consultants, and companies seeking to clean up contaminated properties and obtain liability protections or redevelop brownfield sites. VCP applicants, environmental assessors, property owners with contaminated or potentially contaminated properties. Property owners and managers, homeowners associations, condominium associations, and tenants seeking guidance on maintaining land use controls and Environmental Covenants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investigation and remediation of contaminated sites to remove or manage hazardous substances and oil contamination at properties. Can be used for renewable energy siting and development projects. Environmental assessment and cleanup of contaminated properties. Application fees support MDE review and administrative oversight costs. Maintenance and monitoring of land use controls and institutional controls including HVAC systems, sub-slab depressurization systems, indoor air monitoring, long-term groundwater/soil gas/indoor air monitoring, and deed restrictions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Properties in Maryland with Environmental Covenants, NFRDs, or COCs issued by MDE. Divided into three geographic provinces for cleanup standards: Eastern Maryland, Central Maryland, and Western Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Schedule optional pre-application meeting with VCP personnel at 410-537-3493. 2) Submit complete application with $10,000 fee (or $2,000 for subsequent applications), Phase I and Phase II environmental assessments, and required documentation to MDE at 1800 Washington Blvd, Suite 625, Baltimore, Maryland 21230 and email a copy to mde.landrestoration@maryland.gov. 3) Post public notice at property allowing 30 days for public comments. 4) MDE reviews application within 45 days (or expedited timeframe if expedited determination fee of $2,000 is paid) and notifies applicant whether application is incomplete, accepted, or denied. 5) If accepted, applicant must notify Department within 30 days of acceptance whether proceeding or withdrawing. 6) Develop response action plan or implement interim removal measures if needed; submit RAP within 18 months of acceptance. 7) File performance bond or other security within 10 days of RAP approval. 8) Implement approved cleanup plan under MDE oversight. 9) For expedited Inculpable Person approval, submit the Expedited IP Form with completed Inculpable Person Affidavit and $2,000 fee to mde.exipvcp@maryland.gov or hand deliver/mail to 1800 Washington Blvd (NOT PO Box); Department provides approval decision within 5 business days. 10) Upon completion of cleanup and satisfaction of all requirements, receive final site approval letter (No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion) providing liability protections. 11) Record NFRD/COC in land records within 30 days; notify one-call system within 30 days; record Environmental Covenant as Declaration concurrently. 12) Maintain land use and institutional controls as required; submit annual reports if applicable. 13) Participants may withdraw at any time before or after approval; must provide 10 days written notice, stabilize and secure property, forfeit application fees, and maintain bond or security for up to 16 months from RAP withdrawal date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland awards CO2 offset allowances for projects that demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, reduction or avoidance of CO2 emissions from natural gas, oil, or propane end-use combustion due to energy efficiency, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, reduction in sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) emissions from electrical equipment, carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, and avoided forest conversion. Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards CO2 offset allowances for qualifying projects. Eligible project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, reduction or avoidance of CO2 emissions from natural gas, oil, or propane end-use combustion due to energy efficiency, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, reduction in SF6 emissions through early retirement or replacement of electrical equipment, repair/refurbishment of equipment, and SF6 handling training, carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, and avoided forest conversion. A consistency application must be submitted to MDE within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration and forest projects, or within 12 months for SF6 projects commenced Jan 1, 2009 or later). For SF6 projects commenced Dec 20, 2005 through Dec 31, 2008, applications were due by June 30, 2009.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration and forest projects); for SF6 projects: within six months after Jan 1, 2009 commencement or by June 30, 2009 for projects commenced Dec 20, 2005 - Dec 31, 2008; or by June 30, 2009 for projects commenced before January 1, 2009
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Department of the Environment, Air Quality Planning Program, Offsets
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parties operating or planning to operate projects that reduce or avoid CO2 emissions or sequester carbon in RGGI participating states or approved jurisdictions. structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction. For reforestation, improved forest management, and avoided conversion projects, locations may be in RGGI participating states (excluding NY and CT) or anywhere in the United States if the Project State has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with RGGI states. For projects in non-participating states, compliance with cooperating regulatory agency requirements is required. For SF6 projects, transmission and distribution entities must operate within Maryland and be regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission, with assets and equipment located within Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels

Independent verifier certification required for all project types
Comprehensive monitoring and verification plan required
Project sponsors must be authorized as Account Representatives in RGGI COATS general account

For SF6 projects: establishment of baseline entity-wide SF6 emissions rate; demonstration that >33% of nameplate capacity of SF6-containing equipment is inherently leak-prone; maintenance of entity-wide SF6 inventory tracking system; implementation of SF6 inventory management and auditing protocol; maintenance of cylinder-specific logs with certified scale weights; annual QA/QC procedures including meter and scale calibration certifications

For forest offset projects: project must not be required by law or regulation; must not receive credits from other programs; must not receive prohibited funding; consistency application not filed in other participating states; all related projects in compliance with CO2 Budget Trading Program

For reforestation: land must have less than 10% tree canopy cover for minimum 10 years OR be subject to significant disturbance; at least 95% native species in standing live carbon pool; species diversity requirements per Assessment Area Data File; sustainable management certification or equivalent; no broadcast fertilization; conservation easement documentation if applicable

For improved forest management and avoided conversion: >10% tree canopy cover; ≥95% native species composition; species diversity compliance; sustainable management certification (FSC, SFI, Tree Farm System) or alternative demonstration; retention of standing/lying dead wood; no broadcast fertilization; professional appraisal of alternative land use for avoided conversion projects

Quality assurance procedures documentation

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must obtain the appropriate consistency application and technical support documents based on their project type, complete the application with all required forms and documentation, have it verified by an accredited independent verifier, and submit it to MDE within the specified timeframe. structured_extraction.program_name: Section 319(h) Nonpoint Source Program Grant Funding
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program funded through Section 319(h) of the Clean Water Act that provides financial assistance to reduce or eliminate water quality impairments caused by nonpoint source pollution. The program supports planning, design, construction, monitoring, analysis projects, and outreach initiatives that improve water quality and habitat in impaired watersheds across Maryland. Priority is given to implementation projects addressing Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs) and waters on Maryland's 303(d) List of Impaired Waters. The program provides management and financial assistance for nonpoint source water pollution control projects and best management practices through reimbursement-style grant funding and outreach support. Specific focus includes acid mine drainage (AMD) treatment and pH management through passive treatment systems including limestone leach beds, anoxic limestone drains, anaerobic wetlands, and vertical wetlands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-style grant funding and financial assistance for planning, design, construction, monitoring, analysis projects, and implementation of best management practices and outreach initiatives. Specific amounts and terms are detailed in the annual Request for Proposals (RFP) released each Spring with a Summer submission deadline. The majority of funding supports implementation projects that reduce water quality impairments listed on Maryland's 303(d) List of Impaired Waters, particularly in watersheds with approved Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs). Recipients must have capacity in grant management and must fund projects themselves before receiving reimbursement. Funding covers capital costs for treatment systems and management measures, operation and maintenance funding, and monitoring funding. For AMD-focused projects, funds support passive treatment system design and installation, water quality monitoring, benthic assemblage monitoring, and performance monitoring.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: RFP released each Spring with Summer submission deadline. FFY26 RFP is closed; next RFP for FFY27 funding will open on July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, State agencies and institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations seeking to implement water quality improvement projects and best management practices in eligible Maryland watersheds. Includes watershed stakeholders, landowners affected by water quality impairments, and citizen groups interested in stream restoration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments; implementation of best management practices; and outreach initiatives. Projects must result in quantifiable improvements in water quality and habitat, with priority for implementation projects addressing TMDLs and impaired waters on Maryland's 303(d) List. Funds support nonpoint source water pollution management and control activities. Specific uses include installation of acid mine drainage treatment systems (anoxic limestone drains, anaerobic wetlands, vertical wetlands, passive treatment technologies), water quality monitoring, benthic assemblage monitoring, pH management measures, pre- and post-implementation sampling and evaluation, landowner agreements, and operations and maintenance support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Implementation projects must be located in watersheds with EPA-accepted watershed plans. Eligible watersheds include Aaron Run, Antietam Creek, Assawoman Bay, Casselman River, Corsica River, Lower Jones Falls, Middle Gwynns Falls, Lower Monocacy River, Sassafras River, Spring Branch, Tidal Back River, Upper Back River, Upper Choptank River, and Upper Jennings Run.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit proposals in response to the annual Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by MDE each Spring with a Summer submission deadline. FFY26 RFP is closed; next RFP opens July 1, 2026 for FFY27 funding. Selections are made following the RFP deadline. MDE may request additional documentation or provide oversight to ensure project completion. Applicants should download EPA's watershed plan review spreadsheet and use it as guidance if developing a watershed plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Using U.S EPA Pollution Prevention grant funding, MDE has contracted with independent consultants to provide on-site pollution prevention technical assistance to specific industry sectors. Information and lessons learned are disseminated throughout each sector after each project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: On-site pollution prevention technical assistance provided through independent contractors. Past projects have included hospitals, hotels, food processing facilities and minor league baseball stadiums.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in targeted industry sectors seeking pollution prevention technical assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-site technical assistance for pollution prevention measures tailored to specific industry sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MDE for information on current sector-specific projects and eligibility for participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to counties to inspect and monitor sewage sludge sites. The program operates through contracts between the Maryland Department of the Environment and the counties. It also issues permits for using sewage sludge.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides formula grants to counties. It also offers regulatory services, technical help, and information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for county governments, for-profit businesses, individuals, municipalities, non-profits, and state colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counties can use funds for extra inspections and monitoring of sites where sewage sludge is used.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing assistance to local governmental entities for planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewer infrastructure improvements needed to address high priority public health or water quality problems. The program supplements water quality loan programs, particularly in cases where affordability is a concern. Funding priority is given to small disadvantaged communities and provides grant awards with local match requirements based on system size, compliance status, and affordability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant assistance to local governmental entities for planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewer infrastructure improvements needed to address high priority public health or water quality problems, or to supplement water quality loan programs. Grant awards may not exceed $1.5 million. Funding priority is given to small disadvantaged communities. Local match is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governmental entities, particularly small disadvantaged communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction of wastewater and sewer infrastructure improvements needed to address high priority public health or water quality problems, and supplemental assistance for water quality projects addressing affordability concerns
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with priority for small disadvantaged communities
requirements_list: Local match required
Targeted to small and disadvantaged communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MWIFA accepts applications for funding from these programs in December through January each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants and financing for energy efficiency and decarbonization projects at industrial facilities, with priority investments in cement manufacturing decarbonization and HFC reduction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and financing support for industrial facilities to undertake energy efficiency and decarbonization projects. Priority areas include cement manufacturing decarbonization and HFC reduction. MEA, MDE, and MCEC are increasing staff capacity to streamline access to grants and financing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Industrial facilities in Maryland seeking to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy efficiency and decarbonization projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and decarbonization projects at industrial facilities, including cement manufacturing decarbonization and HFC reduction initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an industrial facility
Must be undertaking energy efficiency or decarbonization projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Facilities can access grants and financing through MEA, with support from MDE and MCEC staff to streamline the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Revolving Fund (SRF) Disadvantaged Business Enterprise Program (DBE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal loan program that provides low-interest rate loans to finance water quality and drinking water capital projects. Loan recipients and contractors are required to make good-faith efforts to award a fair share of work to disadvantaged business enterprises (DBEs), including small business enterprises (SBEs), minority business enterprises (MBEs), and women's business enterprises (WBEs). The program is governed by EPA's Disadvantaged Business Enterprise Program rule (Title 40, Part 33) and applies to contract procurement actions funded in part by EPA assistance agreements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest rate loans are provided to finance water quality and drinking water capital projects. DBE participation goals vary by procurement category: Construction (22% MBE, 16% WBE), Equipment (23% MBE, 11% WBE), Services (25% MBE, 18% WBE), and Supplies (23% MBE, 11% WBE). Loan recipients and prime contractors must demonstrate six good-faith efforts to achieve these goals. The program requires good faith efforts to involve DBEs, including outreach, recruitment, subcontracting opportunities, and consortium arrangements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Water quality and drinking water projects that receive federal loan funds through MDE's revolving loan funds program. Eligible recipients include municipalities, water authorities, and other entities seeking to finance water quality and drinking water capital projects. EPA financial assistance recipients, DBEs, prime contractors, and subcontractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing water quality and drinking water capital projects. DBE participation requirements apply to construction, equipment, services, and supplies procured for these projects. Procurement of construction, equipment, services, and supplies for EPA-funded contracts and subcontracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies to projects funded through the Clean Water Revolving Funds and Drinking Water Revolving Funds programs under MDE. Procurement performed entirely within the United States. EPA Region III jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Loan recipients and sub-recipients (prime contractors and subcontractors) must make good-faith efforts to award a fair share of work to DBEs
DBE firms must be small business enterprises, minority business enterprises, or women's business enterprises

Provide written notice prior to DBE subcontractor termination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Loan recipients must develop bidders lists of qualified DBE firms, advertise in minority and local newspapers, conduct pre-bid meetings to inform contractors about DBE requirements, divide projects into smaller components where economically feasible, establish reasonable delivery schedules, and encourage consortium participation. Prime contractors must undertake the same six good-faith efforts for subcontracting. All required documentation and forms must be submitted with bid proposals. Program is compliance-based with EPA form submission requirements (EPA forms 6100-2, 6100-3, 6100-4).

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-sharing program that provides financial assistance to private forest landowners for implementing approved Forest Stewardship Plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-sharing for private landowners implementing Forest Stewardship Plans. Nine categories are eligible for funding: management plan development, afforestation, forest improvement, windbreaks and hedgerows, streamside and wetlands protection, fisheries and aquatic habitat improvement, wildlife habitat enhancement, forest recreation habitat enhancement, and soil and water protection. Maximum amount per landowner per year is $10,000. Practices must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Management plan development, afforestation, forest improvement, windbreaks and hedgerows, streamside and wetlands protection, fisheries and aquatic habitat improvement, wildlife habitat enhancement, forest recreation habitat enhancement, and soil and water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Landowner must have an approved Forest Stewardship Plan
Practices must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Private landowners with an approved Forest Stewardship Plan apply for cost-sharing assistance. Applications are accepted under open enrollment. Eligible practices receive cost-share funding up to $10,000 per year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Division provides technical reviews of environmental documents to interested parties, including reviews of environmental investigation and remediation reports, work plans, and proposed investigation or remediation strategies. The Division reviews documents and provides findings in a letter format, which can range from a simple 'No Further Action' determination to detailed comments, investigation and remediation requirements, and land use restriction requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Division reviews and comments on site-related environmental documents for a fee. Reviews are conducted by qualified environmental professionals and typically completed within two to four weeks depending on complexity. The Division bills requesters on a semi-annual schedule at rates ranging from approximately $40 to $70 per hour. Generally, the cost of a straightforward Technical Review Service assignment is on the order of $500 to $1,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Interested parties seeking technical assistance with environmental site assessments, remediation planning, and hazardous substance cleanup activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Review of environmental documents and provision of technical findings and recommendations for site-related environmental matters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Written request must be submitted to schedule a review
Requester must formally acknowledge that they will be billed for the service
Requester must provide the name and contact information for the person or entity that will handle invoices for the Division's services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties should contact the Division at 410-537-3493 or via email at bdietz@maryland.gov to schedule a review. The requester must send a formal letter requesting the Technical Review Service that includes the nature of the review being requested, formal acknowledgement that the requester will be billed for this service, and the name and contact information for the person or entity handling the Division's invoices. Upon receipt and approval of the request, the Division will conduct the review and provide findings in a letter.

structured_extraction.program_name: US DOE Advanced Vehicle Technology Funding
structured_extraction.program_description: The US Department of Energy provides funding opportunities for advanced vehicle technology projects aimed at removing technical and cost barriers to clean vehicle adoption.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for advanced vehicle technology projects that reduce technical and cost barriers to clean vehicle adoption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and businesses developing or implementing advanced vehicle technology projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advanced vehicle technology development and deployment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: United States Department of Agriculture Farmable Wetlands Program (FWP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Farmers and ranchers with previously farmed wetlands and wetland buffers can enroll in a 10-15 year contract to restore the wetland, establish plant cover, and not use enrolled land for commercial purposes in return for cost-share payments, annual rental payments, and other incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share payments, annual rental payments, and other incentives for enrolling previously farmed wetlands and wetland buffers in 10-15 year restoration contracts. Landowners agree not to use the enrolled land for commercial purposes during the contract term.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and ranchers with previously farmed wetlands and wetland buffers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wetland restoration and establishment of plant cover on previously farmed wetlands and wetland buffers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to farmers and ranchers across the United States, including Maryland
requirements_list: Must own or operate previously farmed wetlands or wetland buffers
Must enroll in a 10-15 year contract
Enrolled land cannot be used for commercial purposes during contract term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll property in a 10-15 year contract with the USDA

structured_extraction.program_name: United States Department of Agriculture Wetland Reserve Easements (WRE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Private and tribal landowners of previously degraded wetlands due to agricultural use can enroll their property under a permanent, 30-year, or term easement or 30-year contract with varying levels of payment rates and cost-share for restoration costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrollment in permanent, 30-year, or term easements or 30-year contracts with varying payment rates and cost-share for restoration costs of previously degraded wetlands. Easement structure and payment levels vary based on the enrollment option selected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private and tribal landowners with previously degraded wetlands from agricultural use.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Restoration of previously degraded wetlands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to private and tribal landowners across Maryland and nationwide.
requirements_list: Must be a private or tribal landowner
Property must contain previously degraded wetlands due to agricultural use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enroll property under a permanent, 30-year, or term easement or 30-year contract.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance for replacing older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles with cleaner alternatives and for installing electric vehicle charging stations to reduce emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance for vehicle replacement projects to reduce emissions from various types of older diesel-powered heavy-duty vehicles, as well as installation of electric vehicle charging stations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vehicle owners and operators
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vehicle replacement projects and electric vehicle charging station installation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide

structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) Fee Waiver for Clean or Renewable Energy Development
structured_extraction.program_description: Fee waiver application for renewable energy and clean energy development projects under Maryland's Voluntary Cleanup Program. The program waives VCP application fees for developers redeveloping Brownfield sites (contaminated or degraded lands) for clean or renewable energy projects. The program encourages investigation, cleanup, and redevelopment of properties with known or perceived contamination, providing predictability and finality to cleanup of eligible properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Waives VCP application fees: $6,000 initial application fee and $2,000 for subsequent applications for the same or contiguous/adjacent properties. The fee waiver became effective January 1, 2022. Does not waive other VCP-related fees (expedited inculpable person determination, NFRD/COC conditional fees, record alteration fees). Participants in the VCP also receive liability protection after remediation of the Brownfield site and, in participating jurisdictions, access to Brownfield tax incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: VCP applicants and renewable energy developers intending to use eligible contaminated properties for clean or renewable energy generation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: VCP application fees for contaminated property cleanup and redevelopment for clean or renewable energy projects (solar, wind, geothermal, biomass, biofuels, fuel cells, ocean energy, energy efficiency and conservation)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide on eligible Brownfield sites with known or perceived contamination
requirements_list: Proposed project must generate 2 megawatts or greater annually
Project must qualify as clean or renewable energy per COMAR 26.14.3.02B(4) and (16)
Applicant must complete fee waiver application with property details and project information
Site location map required
Eligible Project Affidavit must be completed and notarized
Applicant certifies information accuracy under penalty of law
Property must be an eligible Brownfield site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers apply to the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) with a certification that the property will be used for clean or renewable energy. Submit waiver form and proof of eligibility to MDE VCP office. The Department reviews within 30 days and notifies applicant of approval, incomplete status, or denial. Denial includes written reasons. The application fee waiver is granted upon this certification and approval of the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: WIIN Act Section 2107 Grant Funding for Lead Remediation in Schools
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant funding from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency under the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation (WIIN) Act, Section 2107, to assist local educational agencies (school districts) with testing for and removing sources of lead in drinking water at public and nonpublic schools in Maryland. Funding prioritizes schools with high percentages of students receiving free and reduced-price meals, schools with Head Start programs, schools serving young children ages 6 and under, and schools built before 1988.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to cover expenses for materials and labor associated with lead remediation projects at schools. Eligible remediation types include permanently closing outlets, removing outlets, installing point-of-use filters, repairing/reconfiguring/replacing plumbing, automatic flushing systems, and grounding wire assessment. Permanent or long-term remediation measures are preferred over short-term measures. Remediation projects must occur between November 15, 2021, and September 1, 2022. Funding may be used for reimbursement of completed projects with valid documentation (invoices) or for proposed projects after work completion and documentation receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local educational agencies and school districts in Maryland, both public and nonpublic schools, seeking to remediate lead in drinking water outlets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Testing for lead in drinking water systems at schools, removing sources of lead in drinking water, and materials and labor costs for lead remediation projects, including permanent or long-term remediation measures as specified in Maryland regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland school districts are eligible to apply. Remediation projects must occur between November 15, 2021, and September 1, 2022.

All required documentation must be received by MDE no later than September 8, 2022
Applicants must provide percentage of students receiving free or reduced-price meals
Applicants must indicate whether the school has a Head Start program
Applicants must provide lowest and highest grades served
