Applicants submitted application form with required school and contact information, percentage of students on free/reduced meals, Head Start program status, grade levels served, and funding requests for completed and proposed remediation projects. Invoices for completed projects and estimates for proposed projects were included if available. Applications were evaluated at close of application period. Reimbursement for completed work was provided after award decision. Funding for proposed projects was disbursed after work completion and valid documentation was received by MDE, with all documentation required by September 8, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps clean up illegal scrap tire piles. It also manages the collection, transport, recycling, and processing of scrap tires in Maryland. A fee on new tires funds the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program manages the cleanup of illegal scrap tire stockpiles. It also oversees the collection, transportation, recycling, and processing of scrap tires and issues the required licenses for these activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and individuals who collect, transport, process, or recycle scrap tires. The program also works with property owners who have illegal tire stockpiles.
requirements_list: Must obtain the appropriate license to transport, collect, process, recycle, dispose, incinerate, or use scrap tires as fuel.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Department offers free training opportunities to any party interested in learning more about various aspects of the Wastewater Pollution Prevention and Reclamation Program and the wastewater permits issued by the program. Training covers stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs), erosion and sediment control (E&SC), operator responsibilities, permitting requirements, and compliance procedures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training events covering various aspects of wastewater permits and the Wastewater Pollution Prevention and Reclamation Program. Training covers specific permit types including General Permit for Discharges of Stormwater Associated With Construction Activity (20-CP), General Permit for Discharges from Stormwater Associated with Industrial Activities (20-SW), General Permit for Discharges from Swimming Pools & Spas (17-SI), General Discharge Permit for Discharges from the Application of Pesticides (17-PE), and General Permit for Discharges from Seafood Processing Facilities (21-SE). Technical guidance covers permit compliance, SWPPP development, BMP implementation, and stormwater management.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Minimum 14 days prior to construction commencement for new operators; within 7 days of starting activity if adding SWPPP trigger
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any party interested in learning more about wastewater permits, including construction project operators, industrial facility operators, swimming pool facility operators, pesticide applicators, and seafood processing facility operators. Includes permit applicants and holders, construction industry professionals, environmental compliance inspectors, and contractors and subcontractors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education about wastewater permits and pollution prevention and reclamation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Operators for construction projects registered under the 14-GP or 20-CP permit
Operators for proposed construction projects
Preparers of permitting documents on behalf of construction operators
Owners or operators of facilities registered under industrial permits
Owners or operators of swimming pools or similar facilities
Pesticide application operators
Owners or operators of seafood processing facilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants sign up to attend training events linked on the webpage. A newsletter subscription is available to receive updates on future training events via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: Water Quality Financing provides financial assistance in the form of low-interest rate loans and/or grant funding for clean water and drinking water capital projects across Maryland. The program serves both public entities and private landowners and water system owners, supporting water quality point source projects, drinking water projects, non-point source pollution control projects, and septic system upgrade projects. Applications are accepted in December of each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest rate loans and/or grant funding for clean water and drinking water capital projects. Provides financing to both public entities and private landowners and water system owners to implement capital improvements that protect or improve water quality and provide safe drinking water. Applications are accepted in December of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local entities, private landowners, and water system owners with clean water and drinking water capital projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean water and drinking water capital projects, water quality point source projects, drinking water projects, non-point source pollution control projects, septic system upgrade projects, and other capital improvements to protect or improve water quality and provide safe drinking water
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Across the State of Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund provides financial assistance for projects that protect or improve the quality of Maryland's rivers, streams, lakes, the Chesapeake Bay, and other water resources. The program supports both point source pollution prevention projects for public entities and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects for public and private entities. The fund provides low-interest and below-market interest rate loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to local governments and eligible entities to finance wastewater treatment plant upgrades, nonpoint source pollution control projects, site cleanup costs at contaminated sites, and other water quality and public health improvement projects. Federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) supports below-market interest rate state and federal loans. Funding is available to parties legally responsible for cleanup or parties accepted into the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP). Projects must be consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act and the Maryland Bay Restoration Fund Act. Financial advisory services are available to help applicants determine affordable user rate structures and model the fiscal impact of proposed loans on financial capacity. The program also supports enhanced nutrient removal upgrades, green infrastructure, water/energy efficiency projects, and facility upgrades for permit compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides low-interest and below-market interest rate loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness for water quality improvement and cleanup projects. Federal funding from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Financial advisory services are available to help applicants determine affordable user rate structures and model the fiscal impact of the proposed loan on financial capacity. Loans are available for cleanup costs to complete approved cleanup plans where water quality is an issue, including at State Master List sites and VCP properties. FFY 2025 includes $230,554,215 in project funding. Additional subsidy (loan principal forgiveness) available: 20-40% of Base Capitalization Grant; 49% of IIJA General Supplemental; 100% of IIJA Emerging Contaminants. Disadvantaged Communities (DACs) may receive up to 50% principal forgiveness, not to exceed $1.5 million. Up to 25% loan forgiveness available for projects where sewer user rate would increase more than 20%.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted December through January annually; ongoing for cleanup projects. Most recent cycle: December 2, 2024 through January 31, 2025 (FFY 2025).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public entities, local governments, private entities, individuals, responsible parties, VCP participants, municipal and county governments, water/wastewater utilities, sanitary districts and commissions, public water infrastructure entities, and disadvantaged communities seeking to fund water quality improvement and cleanup projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wastewater treatment plant improvements and expansion, sewerage collection and conveyance systems, correction of excess sewerage infiltration and inflow, sludge handling facilities, landfill leachate pretreatment, backwash facilities at drinking water treatment plants, stormwater best management practices, wellhead protection, landfill closure, stream corridor restoration and protection, hazardous waste cleanup, shoreline erosion control, agricultural nutrient management plans, water and soil conservation plans, costs to complete approved cleanup plans addressing water quality contamination at State Master List sites and VCP properties, enhanced nutrient removal (ENR) upgrades, green infrastructure projects, water and energy efficiency projects, facility compliance upgrades, septic system elimination, flood mitigation, and pump station upgrades
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for water quality improvement projects and at State Master List sites and VCP sites throughout Maryland for cleanup projects. Projects must be included in or amended to MDE-approved County Water and Sewer Plans.
requirements_list: Point source pollution prevention projects limited to public entities and local governments
Nonpoint source pollution prevention projects available to public and private entities
Site must be on State Master List or in the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) for cleanup funding
Water quality must be an issue requiring remediation
Applicant must be legally responsible for cleanup or accepted into VCP
Cleanup plan must be approved by MDE
Projects must comply with NPDES permits, consent decrees, and water quality standards
Public projects must be eligible under Clean Water Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for pollution prevention projects are accepted during the December through January period annually. Applicants can contact MDE's Water Infrastructure Financing Administration for financial advisory services and assistance with the application process. For cleanup projects, contact the Land Restoration Program at (410) 537-3908 or (410) 537-3493 for information on loan application process and availability. Applications will reopen in December 2026. Draft IUP shared via social media and with Maryland General Assembly. Public comment period available. MWIFA available to answer questions during comment period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, market-based program that allows entities to generate, buy, and sell water quality credits representing nitrogen, phosphorus, and sediment reductions to meet and maintain pollutant load limits under NPDES and State discharge permits. The program facilitates trading between agricultural, stormwater, wastewater, and on-site sewage disposal sectors, with infrastructure including the Maryland Nutrient Tracking Tool, central Registry, and optional Marketplace to protect and restore the Chesapeake Bay, its tributaries, and local waters.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program creates a market mechanism that allows participants to generate credits through water quality improvement activities (wastewater treatment, stormwater management, septic system improvements, oyster aquaculture, and agricultural practices) and sell or trade those credits. Credits equal one pound of nitrogen, phosphorus, or sediment reduction and must be certified, verified, and registered before trading. Credits can be traded within the same trading region/segmentshed and used to meet NPDES permit requirements. MDE certifies credits from wastewater, stormwater, on-site sewage disposal, and oyster aquaculture sources, while MDA certifies agricultural credits through the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool. Prices are negotiated between seller and buyer. Credits are subject to uncertainty ratios, edge of tide adjustments, and reserve ratios.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Point source permittees (wastewater and stormwater operators), agricultural operations, nonpoint source operators, property owners installing BMPs, entities seeking to purchase credits to meet NPDES permit requirements, aggregators, and brokers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Generation and sale of water quality credits representing pollution load reductions (nitrogen, phosphorus, or sediment) that can be applied toward meeting water quality regulatory requirements and permit compliance conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland within the Chesapeake Bay watershed and nontidal rivers, streams, and impoundments. Trading must comply with segmentshed/Bay TMDL watershed boundaries. Credits from impaired waters must be used within such impaired waters or upstream of the discharge location. Cross-sector trading is allowed except wastewater-to-wastewater between different permits.
requirements_list: Activities must result in verifiable nitrogen, phosphorus, or sediment reductions
Credits must be certified by MDE (for wastewater, stormwater, on-site sewage disposal, oyster aquaculture) or MDA (for agricultural practices)
Credits must comply with COMAR 26.08.11 Trading Regulations
Agricultural credits must be calculated through the Maryland Nutrient Tracking/Trading Tool
BMPs must be approved by Chesapeake Bay Program
Baseline pollution reductions must be achieved before credit generation
Credits must be whole numbers (fractions rounded down)
Credits are subject to uncertainty ratios, edge of tide adjustments, and 5% reserve ratios
Trading must occur within the same trading region/segmentshed only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants generate credits through eligible water quality improvement activities (BMPs). Credits are calculated and must be certified by the appropriate agency (MDE or MDA depending on the source). Certified credits are verified, registered in the central Registry, and can be posted on the state marketplace where buyers seeking to meet NPDES permit requirements can purchase them. Credits are traded within applicable trading regions and segmentshed areas. Additional details are available through the program's Generating Credits and Purchasing Credits pages.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program that trains and certifies water samplers in Maryland to properly collect samples for testing public water systems and ensuring Safe Drinking Water Act compliance. The program ensures samplers are properly trained with current regulatory requirements under state law. Certification assures the reliability of drinking water samples submitted to state certified laboratories and is the primary means of evaluating the safety of drinking water supply for Public Water Systems (PWS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides water sampler training classes and certification examination. Certification card is valid for up to 3 years and includes class, examination, and skills test (for first-time applicants). Registration and training are handled through the Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA). As of January 1, 2025, new requirements for first-time samplers have been implemented.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Laboratory personnel, water system operators and superintendents, county and state health department staff, and other individuals who collect samples for Public Water Systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification to become a certified water sampler in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available across Maryland for Maryland residents and organizations
requirements_list: High school education minimum
No prior experience required
Participants must register for training through Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA)
Pass Water Sampler Class and examination
Complete hands-on practicum/skills test (first-time applicants only)
First-time samplers must meet new requirements as of January 1, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA). Complete Water Sampler Class and examination. Complete hands-on practicum/skills test (first-time applicants only). Contact Maryland Rural Water Association (MRWA) directly for class registration or email training@md-rwa.org or mde.labcertification@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides state grants to local governments. The grants help pay for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants to support capital improvements for drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, including counties and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital improvement projects for drinking water systems.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments and small communities for the acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly owned water supply facilities throughout Maryland. The program helps fund projects that address water supply related health problems, meet federal Safe Drinking Water Act requirements, and prioritizes disadvantaged communities and those non-compliant with drinking water standards. Grant awards help communities meet their water supply and infrastructure needs based on system size, compliance status, and affordability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds up to 87.5% of total eligible project costs, not to exceed $1.5 million per project. There is a 12.5% local match requirement, which may be funded through the Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund (DWRLF) Program. Applicants may receive a combination of state grant and drinking water revolving loan to finance the project. Costs for planning, engineering, and project administration are eligible for loans only. Funding priority is given to disadvantaged communities and communities non-compliant with drinking water standards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted December through January annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and small communities throughout Maryland operating publicly-owned water supply systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water supply and infrastructure needs including acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and improvement of publicly-owned water supply facilities; upgrade of water treatment facilities, well development, water storage tanks, water distribution facilities up to private property lines, and consolidation of smaller water systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available across Maryland. Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area and be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan. Projects must conform to Smart Growth Criteria. Water systems serving a population greater than 10,000 must submit a water conservation plan. Priority given to disadvantaged communities and communities non-compliant with drinking water standards.
requirements_list: Local match required
Project must be eligible under Federal Safe Drinking Water Act
Project must conform to Smart Growth Criteria
Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Project must be consistent with the County Water and Sewer Plan
All projects must submit a water audit
Water systems serving population greater than 10,000 must submit a water conservation plan
Only applicants with insufficient or limited financial capability are eligible
Projects are rated and ranked based on public health benefits, regulatory compliance, safety, water system reliability, applicant financial capability, previous corrective efforts, and community size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are rated and ranked based on the requirements of Environment Article 9-423 and COMAR 26.03.09.06. Priority rankings are determined on the basis of project benefits to public health, compliance with regulations or MDE directives, safety, water system reliability, financial capability of the applicant, previous efforts to correct problems, and community size. Applicants are encouraged to solicit additional funding through other state and federal agencies such as the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Rural Development Program or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Small Cities Community Development Block Grant Program. Applications are accepted December through January each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments or water supply systems for wellhead protection projects and direct loans for land acquisition for source water protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides financial assistance to local governments or water supply systems for wellhead protection projects and direct loans to local governments or water supply systems for land acquisition for source water protection. Applications are accepted in December of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and water supply systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wellhead protection projects and land acquisition for source water protection
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit required for any well that is constructed in the State of Maryland. The application process involves submitting forms to the appropriate approving authority.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a regulatory permitting program, not a financial or technical assistance program. Applicants must obtain a permit before constructing a well.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any entity constructing a well in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - applies to all wells constructed in the State of Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must submit required forms
Hard copies must be provided to the County, Survey, Driller, Well Owner, and the Department
If a new well replaces an abandoned well, the abandoned well must be sealed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Application for Permit to Drill Wells form to the Approving Authority along with hard copies for the County, Survey, Driller, Well Owner, and the Department. Upon completion, submit a Well Completion Report. If hydrofracturing is performed, submit a Well Hydrofracture Report. If replacing an abandoned well, submit a Well Abandonment-Sealing Report Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A strategy designed to protect public drinking water supplies by managing the land surface around a well where activities might affect water quality. The program provides technical assistance, information, and funding to local governments to help them protect their water supplies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest loans are available for communities to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas. Technical assistance is provided to help local governments delineate wellhead protection areas, inventory contaminants, and develop management programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and public water supply systems in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase land or conservation easements within wellhead protection areas to protect drinking water supplies from contamination.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland communities with public drinking water supplies.
requirements_list: Applicants must be local governments
Communities must be developing or implementing a wellhead protection program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in the program should contact the Water Supply Program at the provided phone number to discuss their needs and obtain information about available assistance and loan opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program offering landowners the opportunity to protect, restore, and enhance wetlands on their property through permanent easements, 30-year easements, or 10-year restoration cost-share agreements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NRCS provides technical and financial support to landowners. Payment is based on the agricultural value of the land. Offers permanent easements, 30-year easements, or 10-year restoration cost-share agreements. Landowner retains ownership and control of land including property rights.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners who own or control land that is restorable and suitable for wildlife benefits, including wetlands cleared and drained for farming, pasture, or timber production.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Protection, restoration, and enhancement of wetlands and associated uplands through practices specified in individual agreements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide through local USDA Service Centers. In Maryland, applications processed through the Annapolis Service Center.
requirements_list: Land must be restorable and suitable for wildlife benefits
For permanent or 30-year easement: must have owned land for at least one year prior to enrollment with limited exceptions
For 10-year restoration cost-share agreement: need only show evidence of ownership
Cannot include wetlands converted after December 23, 1985
Cannot include certain Conservation Reserve Program contract lands where trees have been established
Cannot include Federal lands
Cannot include lands where conditions make restoration impossible
Landowner retains ownership and responsibility for property taxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners contact their local USDA Service Center or the Wetlands Reserve Program Coordinator. Eligible land is evaluated for restoratability and wildlife benefit potential. Upon approval, NRCS develops a restoration plan with the landowner and enters into an easement or cost-share agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that provides technical assistance and cost-share payments to help landowners establish and improve fish and wildlife habitat on private lands.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: USDA provides technical assistance and pays up to 75 percent of the cost of installing wildlife habitat practices. Cost-share agreements generally last 5 to 10 years. Landowner agrees to install and maintain practices and allow NRCS access to monitor effectiveness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners or those who control land and want to develop and improve wildlife habitat primarily on private lands.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of wildlife habitat development practices as described in the wildlife habitat development plan, which may include practices determined by NRCS in consultation with the local conservation district.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All lands are eligible for WHIP except Federal land, land currently enrolled in similar programs, land subject to Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement, and land where USDA determines impacts make success unlikely.
requirements_list: Must own or have control of the land
Must prepare and implement a wildlife habitat development plan
Land cannot be Federal land
Land cannot be currently enrolled in Water Bank Program, Conservation Reserve Program, Wetlands Reserve Program, or other similar programs
Land cannot be subject to Emergency Watershed Protection Program floodplain easement
Cannot use WHIP funds for mitigation or on converted wetland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible landowners contact their local USDA Service Center to apply. NRCS helps prepare a wildlife habitat development plan in consultation with the local conservation district. Upon approval, USDA and participant enter into a cost-share agreement. Landowner installs and maintains practices while NRCS provides technical assistance and cost-share payments of up to 75 percent.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) helps with public-private partnerships. MEDCO can assess if a project is workable and manage proposal requests. The agency can also issue revenue bonds and own, develop, or operate project assets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. This includes evaluating project viability, managing solicitations for proposals, issuing revenue bonds, and owning, developing, or operating assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program assists county and state governments, municipalities, towns, for-profit businesses, and state universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: MEDCO provides services for public-private partnership projects. These services include project evaluation, solicitation management, and asset ownership, development, or operation. MEDCO can also issue revenue bonds for projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Ready Sites Program accelerates investment by growing the inventory of shovel-ready sites across Maryland. It enhances Maryland's industrial and commercial infrastructure by identifying and improving potential development sites. It provides financial support to defray costs of site characterization and improvements, and offers collaborative marketing support to enable significant investment across the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three pillars of support: Site Characterization Grants providing up to $10,000 to assess site readiness with no local match requirement; Site Improvement Grants supporting infrastructure development and environmental remediation with no maximum funding limit and requiring a 3:1 total cash match from federal, state, local, and private-sector funding sources; and Collaborative Marketing Support including publication in the MBRSP Sites Dashboard, site characterization reports, and collaborative marketing assistance to jurisdictions and the State.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with priority cycle in May; May applicants notified by July 1; June 1 or later applicants notified within 60 days
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public sector entities (counties, municipalities, authorities) and private sector entities that own or have development rights to eligible sites. Site owners, applicant organizations seeking site characterization, and economic development organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site characterization and assessment including site development professional services for site evaluation and development status analysis; infrastructure upgrades and site preparation; environmental remediation; design and engineering; due diligence studies including environmental, geotechnical, and wetlands assessments; clearing and grading; construction; and other site development needs to prepare sites for industrial or commercial use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. Applicant organization and site must be located in Maryland counties. Eligible sites must be greenfields, brownfields, or redevelopment sites in a pre-development phase.
requirements_list: Site must be a minimum of 5 acres
Site intended solely for industrial or commercial purposes

Site intended to be occupied primarily by private sector companies in eligible industries including life sciences, information technology, aerospace, defense, computational biology, quantum computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and position, navigation, and timing, or jurisdiction-specific focus industries
Site must not be otherwise restricted from further development
Private sector applicants must own or have development rights to the land and provide evidence of title or purchase option documentation
Owner documentation of ownership required for grant approval
Site characterization analysis must follow MEDCO specifications and guidelines
Applicant must certify responses are true and accurate
For Site Characterization Grant: 1-to-1 cash match required from any source
For Site Improvement Grant: 3:1 or higher total cash match required from federal, state, local, and private-sector funding sources
Letters of support from county and municipal governments required (if applicable)
Detailed project budget with timelines and deliverables
Complete due diligence reports (environmental, geotechnical, wetlands, boundary/topographic maps, Phase Environmental Report, ALTA surveys)
Site development plans
Site alignment with county/municipality economic development goals
Connection to Maryland growth industries or jurisdiction-specific focus industries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form with site and applicant information, match funding source, and optional preferred contractors. For Site Characterization Grants, obtain ownership documentation before approval and MEDCO provides specifications to retained contractor for site analysis. For Site Improvement Grants, submit completed application with required and recommended attachments including letters of support, project budget, due diligence reports, site development plans, and evidence of title or purchase option. MBRSP coordinates with applicants to gather necessary documentation during the collaborative and ongoing review process. Applications are submitted to [email protected].

structured_extraction.program_name: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) Capital Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Capital grant funding to help organizations acquire, plan, design, equip with technology, furnish and refurbish Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) that meet national security standards and support mission-critical work requiring security-cleared professionals. Available statewide with focused initiative in Southern Maryland (Charles and St. Mary's Counties) to support defense contractors and mission-critical businesses in conducting classified work in shared facilities, supporting job creation and economic growth in the defense industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants to support acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishing and refurbishment of SCIF spaces. To date, MEDCO has awarded $5 million total to five projects in Southern Maryland (Charles County and St. Mary's County). Funds support various defense sectors including explosive ordnance disposal, aviation, and general security work. For every dollar invested, an estimated two to three dollars in private, nonprofit, or government match is generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations seeking to develop secure compartmented information facilities to support mission-critical work and national security initiatives, including defense contractors, mission-critical businesses, security-cleared professionals, and organizations working with the Department of Defense requiring secure work environments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, planning, design, technology, furnishing and refurbishment of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) for secure collaboration on classified work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available across Maryland regions with strategic focus in Southern Maryland, specifically Charles County and St. Mary's County at locations such as the Maryland Technology Center in Charles County and Lexington Park and St. Mary's Airport in St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Must plan to develop a SCIF space meeting national security standards
Project should support skilled workforce retention and national security advantage
Must be located in Charles County or St. Mary's County, Maryland for Southern Maryland initiative
Must be a for-profit or non-profit organization working in defense-related sectors
Facilities must meet SCIF standards for secure information handling
Projects should demonstrate alignment with defense industry needs and job creation potential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MEDCO administers the program and works with applicants to support SCIF development projects. MEDCO, as a quasi-government entity and Maryland-registered nonprofit, navigates the application process with the Maryland Department of General Services on behalf of the state and distributes capital grant funds to qualifying projects. Businesses and organizations work with MEDCO as a broker and solutions provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Infrastructure Loan Fund makes targeted investments into real estate and infrastructure projects that support transformative placemaking, transit-oriented development, community development, and inclusive and equitable economic growth. The fund provides flexible financing to fill gaps in residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible-term financing for real estate and infrastructure projects. Uses include acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development, infrastructure, and costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Projects located within Maryland Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, or Transit Oriented Development zones. Priority projects include development projects that activate underutilized government or institutionally owned property, offer significant development or redevelopment value, leverage private investment, or have promise of significant job creation or retention.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of property or vacant sites, design and development, infrastructure, and other costs associated with new construction, adaptive reuse, or extensive rehabilitation of residential, commercial, mixed-use, and light industrial projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit Oriented Development zone.
requirements_list: Project location within Maryland Sustainable Community, Priority Funding Area, or Transit Oriented Development zone
Projects positioned to drive impact in residential, commercial, mixed-use, or light industrial development

structured_extraction.program_description: Following a Presidentially declared disaster, the Individual Assistance Program assists individuals and households experiencing difficulties post-disaster. The Individuals and Households Program component provides grants to eligible households for housing assistance and other needs assistance when denied low-interest loans from the Small Business Administration and when homeowners or flood insurance does not provide sufficient coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants through two components: Housing Assistance (HA) and Other Needs Assistance (ONA). Housing Assistance includes temporary rental housing or temporary housing units, home repair to safe and sanitary condition (up to IHP maximum), home replacement under rare conditions (up to IHP maximum), and semi-permanent or permanent housing construction in unusual situations. Other Needs Assistance covers medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, repair or replacement of clothing and household items, specialized tools or protective clothing for work, educational materials, cleanup items, fuel for primary heat source, vehicle repair or transportation costs, moving and storage expenses, and other necessary serious needs such as towing or utility connection costs. Flood insurance may be required in Special Flood Hazard Areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households affected by Presidentially declared disasters who are denied SBA disaster loans and whose insurance does not provide sufficient coverage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing-related expenses (temporary housing, home repair, replacement, or construction) and other necessary post-disaster expenses including medical, dental, funeral, household items, transportation, moving, and utilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in areas affected by Presidentially declared disasters throughout Maryland and the United States.
requirements_list: Must be affected by a Presidentially declared disaster
Must be denied assistance in the form of low-interest loans from the Small Business Administration
Homeowners or flood insurance must not provide sufficient payout
If in a Special Flood Hazard Area, must comply with flood insurance purchase requirements and local flood codes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Following a Presidentially declared disaster, individuals should apply for Individual Assistance through FEMA. Applicants are first directed to the Small Business Administration for disaster loans; if denied, they may then qualify for the Individuals and Households Program component.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program that enhances cybersecurity resilience for K-12 schools throughout Maryland by providing resources, tools, and technical assistance to address cyber threats and support mitigation and recovery from cyber incidents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The initiative provides technical assistance and training to K-12 schools in four main areas: Planning (cybersecurity maturity assessment, current plan assessment, resource allocation analysis, training program setup), Implementation (remediation recommendations, response plan development, disaster recovery and continuity of operations support, training and exercises), and Support (funding notifications and ongoing assistance). Schools can request assistance through a support form.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 school systems and Local Education Agencies throughout Maryland seeking to enhance their cybersecurity resilience and preparedness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and training to help schools assess cybersecurity maturity, develop cyber incident response plans, implement disaster recovery and continuity of operations plans, conduct training and exercises, and receive ongoing support for cyber threat response and recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland to all K-12 schools and Local Education Agencies.
requirements_list: Schools must be K-12 educational organizations in Maryland
Schools must request assistance through the support form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools interested in requesting assistance can complete the K-12 Cyber Resilience Initiative Support form available on the program page. Schools can request support in one or more of the listed support areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to low-income households to help pay for heating costs and home weatherization improvements such as insulation, weather stripping, and caulking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help eligible low-income households afford heating costs and home insulation improvements to keep warm air inside during winter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households that cannot afford heating costs or home weatherization improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heating costs and home weatherization such as insulation, weather stripping, and caulking.
requirements_list: Low income

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provides funding for physical security enhancements and other security-related activities to nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist or extremist attack. The program is administered by the Maryland Emergency Management Agency statewide, with Montgomery County and Prince George's County organizations applying through the National Capital Region framework. The program seeks to integrate nonprofit preparedness activities with broader state and local preparedness efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $150,000 in funding per location toward physical security enhancements and safety measures. Applicants can apply for a maximum of six locations total per nonprofit organization with no more than three locations in either NSGP-UA (Urban Area) or NSGP-S (State), and a maximum of $200,000 per location. The total per state does not exceed $600,000. There is no cost share requirement for FY 2025. Funding is distributed through a reimbursement basis, not advance payment. Eligible uses include facility hardening, security equipment, contracted security services, project management and administration, and other approved security measures to prevent, protect against, prepare for, and respond to terrorist or extremist attacks.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period is currently closed; Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations exempt from tax under section 501(a) of the Internal Revenue Code, including private institutions of higher learning designated as 501(c)(3) entities, that are at high risk of terrorist or extremist attack.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical security enhancements and other security-related activities including facility hardening, security equipment, contracted security services, project management and administration, and other approved security measures to prevent, protect against, prepare for, and respond to terrorist or extremist attacks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. However, organizations in Montgomery or Prince George's County must apply through the District of Columbia under the National Capital Region. The state is divided into three funding categories: State Area (16 counties), Baltimore Urban Area (7 jurisdictions), and National Capital Region Urban Area (2 counties administered through DC).
requirements_list: Organization must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or private institution of higher learning exempt from federal income tax
Organization must be at high risk of terrorist or extremist attack
Vulnerability assessment conducted at the facility within the last two years (conducted by local law enforcement or security company, or self-assessment for houses of worship)
Organization mission statement on letterhead
Subapplicants and subrecipients must submit short bios and resumes including organizational leadership, board members, names and addresses
No foreign nationals or noncitizents included unless properly vetted
Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) required at time of award (not required for application submission)
Declaration of whether the subrecipient's work involves supporting aliens and whether the subrecipient has any DEI practices
Proposed projects must address a National Priority Area

Environmental and Historic Preservation screening required for most projects (except contracted security services, project management and administration, and specific planning and training activities)
Compliance with competitive bidding practices based on purchase thresholds
Compliance with Build America, Buy America Act requirements
Restrictions on purchasing from prohibited telecommunications companies and their subsidiaries
Subrecipient Grant Award Briefing attendance is mandatory for all grant recipients
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit all required documents in PDF format to nsgp.mdem@maryland.gov in a single email with all attachments. Required documents include: (1) Investment Justification form downloaded and opened from your computer; (2) Vulnerability Assessment conducted within the last two years; (3) Organization mission statement on letterhead; (4) Bios and resumes of subapplicants and subrecipients with names and addresses. MDEM screens and scores applications, then submits approved applications to FEMA. Organizations are notified of awards and required to attend a mandatory Subrecipient Grant Award Briefing. Upon award, organizations execute a subrecipient agreement and begin project implementation. Environmental and Historic Preservation screening must be approved before work begins. Reimbursements are requested as expenses are incurred with supporting invoices and proof of payment. Quarterly status reports are required throughout the period of performance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal disaster assistance program administered by Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) in coordination with FEMA. Provides supplemental federal grant assistance to state and local governments, certain private non-profit organizations, and tribal governments for response and recovery activities following a presidentially-declared disaster. Assistance covers debris removal, emergency protective measures, and repair, replacement, or restoration of disaster-damaged facilities. The program provides federal grants at not less than 75% federal cost share with applicant responsible for remaining costs to alleviate the financial burden following a federally-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant reimbursement for emergency work (debris removal, emergency protective measures) and permanent restoration work (Categories C-G: roads/bridges, water control facilities, buildings/equipment, utilities, parks/recreation). Covers eligible costs for labor, equipment, materials, and contract services. Federal share not less than 75% with applicant responsible for remaining cost share. Management costs reimbursed (up to 7% for MDEM; up to 5% for subrecipients). Small projects funded based on approved estimate; large projects receive phased funding with interim payments up to 50% then final balance upon completion. Minimum project cost $3,900.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Request for Public Assistance (RPA) must be submitted within 30 days of disaster designation or county/jurisdiction designation for Public Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, Indian tribal governments, certain private non-profit organizations, and public entities in areas affected by presidentially-declared disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Debris removal, emergency protective measures, roads and bridges repair, water control facilities, buildings and equipment repair or replacement, utilities restoration, parks and recreational facilities repairs, facility restoration and reconstruction, management and administrative costs, hazard mitigation measures directly related to reconstructed work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland in areas designated as disaster areas by the President following a presidentially-declared disaster.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a state or local government, Indian tribal government, or certain private non-profit organization
Disaster must be presidentially-declared
For Private Nonprofits: must have IRS tax exemption under Section 501(c), (d), or (e) or satisfactory evidence from Maryland of nonprofit status
For Critical Service PNPs: must provide essential services such as power, water, sewer, educational, communication, emergency medical, or fire protection

For Non-Critical Service PNPs: may include alcohol/drug treatment, animal control, assisted living, child care, community centers, homeless shelters, houses of worship, libraries, museums, senior centers, zoos
Applicants must provide cost share (minimum 25% applicant responsibility)
Work must be result of disaster in designated area; restoration to pre-disaster design, function, and capacity per applicable codes
Insurance must be considered before reimbursement

Comprehensive documentation required: location details, project descriptions, scale drawings, engineering reports, permits, labor documentation, equipment usage, material purchase records, insurance information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to create accounts in the FEMA Grants Portal before a disaster declaration. Following a disaster declaration, damage assessment is conducted to determine the impact and magnitude of damage. Applicants submit Request for Public Assistance (RPA) within 30 days at Applicants' Briefing or by deadline. Governor's Authorized Representative and State Coordinating Officer oversee the process. Applicants submit comprehensive documentation including Impact Statement Form and Initial Damage Assessment Form to MDEM for review. Site visits and inspections conducted as needed. FEMA reviews all submissions and determines federal assistance eligibility and funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide loan fund providing financing for hazard mitigation projects to help reduce the potential negative effects of natural and human-caused hazards in Maryland, including resilience and disaster mitigation initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A revolving loan fund that provides financing for hazard mitigation projects. The program offers loans to support mitigation efforts, though specific loan amounts, terms, and mechanics are not detailed on the primary program page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and communities seeking to implement hazard mitigation projects in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding mitigation projects that help reduce the potential negative effects of natural and human-caused hazards, including resilience and disaster mitigation initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can request information on applying for a loan through the form provided on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program designed to help states, local governments, rural areas, and territories address cybersecurity risks and threats by providing funding for cybersecurity improvements, best practices adoption and enhancement, policy and governance development, workforce development, and operational technology assessments. The program includes required participation in free CISA services and assessments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based grant funding for approved cybersecurity projects and free CISA services. State agencies and local governments that receive SLCGP funding are subrecipients of the federal grant administered through MDEM. Subrecipients must submit reimbursement requests with documentation demonstrating allowable, project-related expenses including proof of purchase and proof of payment. Eligible uses include cybersecurity infrastructure improvements (asset discovery/management, multi-factor authentication, endpoint detection and response, email gateway, security awareness training, firewalls, enhanced logging, data encryption, end-of-life software/hardware replacement, password security, backup/recovery systems, .gov domain migration), operational technology assessments, best practices implementation, policy development, and workforce training.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial and Canopy Solar Program provides grant funding to support solar energy installations on commercial properties, including rooftop-mounted solar systems, ground-mounted solar systems, and solar canopies over parking or bodies of water. The program benefits low-to-moderate income and overburdened communities and helps Maryland businesses, nonprofits, government entities, and other organizations increase access to solar energy technologies to meet the State's clean energy, energy affordability, and greenhouse gas reduction goals. Funding is available for projects in census tracts with average median income at or below 80% of the state average, or overburdened or underserved communities. Solar PV canopy systems may include integrated EV charging over parking structures and provide multiple uses for land and water. The program combines the former FY25 Commercial Solar Grant Program and FY25 Solar Canopy and Dual Use Technology Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants calculated using a formula based on Area of Interest, solar PV installation type, and solar system capacity. For Area of Interest 1 (Equitable Commercial and Canopy Solar): non-canopy systems receive $2,000/kWDC or 90% of total project cost (whichever is lower) for solar energy purchase agreements and $750/kWDC for third-party owned systems; canopy systems receive $2,500/kWDC or 90% of total project cost (whichever is lower) for purchase agreements and $1,000/kWDC for third-party owned systems. For Area of Interest 2 (Commercial Solar for Sustainability): non-canopy systems receive $1,700/kWDC or 75% of total project cost (whichever is lower) for purchase agreements and $750/kWDC for third-party owned systems; canopy systems receive $2,125/kWDC or 75% of total project cost (whichever is lower) for purchase agreements and $1,000/kWDC for third-party owned systems. Maximum grant award is $500,000 per property owner. Total funding of up to $13,000,000 is available. Both applicant-owned systems and third-party owned systems with lease or power purchase agreements are eligible.

Eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) nonprofits, SBEs certified by MDOT, veteran-owned businesses, commercial businesses, multifamily dwelling owners, hospitals and medical facilities, agricultural business owners, faith-based organizations, and social services organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar energy installations on commercial properties including rooftop-mounted solar systems, ground-mounted solar systems, and solar canopies with integrated EV charging over parking or bodies of water. Solar PV systems purchased by applicants and third-party owned solar energy systems are eligible. Projects must directly benefit low-to-moderate income and overburdened communities.

Grants may cover 100% of project costs for facilities where over 50% of clients are from low-income populations; for all other projects, grants cover less than 100% of costs. Applicants may also apply for a separate loan to finance the remaining project balance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program increases access to affordable and reliable electric vehicle charging networks and reduces transportation greenhouse gas emissions throughout Maryland, especially in overburdened communities. It provides funding for EV infrastructure planning studies and EVSE installations (Level 2 and Level 3 charging equipment) in low-and-moderate income, overburdened, and underserved communities. The program includes two areas of interest: Area of Interest 1 provides up to $500,000 total to help local governments offset feasibility and planning study costs for future EVSE development; Area of Interest 2 provides up to $9,000,000 total to help applicants offset costs of EVSE installations for Level 2 or Level 3 (including Direct Current Fast Charging systems) charging equipment. Total anticipated program funding is $10 million for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants providing two areas of funding: (1) Area of Interest 1 provides up to $500,000 total to help local governments offset feasibility and planning study costs for future EVSE development; (2) Area of Interest 2 provides up to $9,000,000 total to help applicants offset costs of EVSE installations for Level 2 or Level 3 charging equipment. Total anticipated program funding is $10 million for FY 2026, though the amount awarded may be more or less depending on fund availability and application quality. Grants support installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure in low-and-moderate income, overburdened, and underserved communities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Solar Low-to-Moderate Income Power Purchase Agreement Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This statewide competitive grant program provides approximately $17 million in funding to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations approved by the Maryland PSC to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), enabling clean energy to be offered to low-income and income-qualified Marylanders at lower cost. The program is funded by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding, with initial funding of $5 million for AOI-1 (Area of Interest 1) and $12 million for AOI-2. AOI-1 supports community solar developer incentives for low-income subscriptions, while AOI-2 focuses on landfill and brownfield solar projects benefitting low-income residents. It supports both non-profit and for-profit organizations seeking to maximize value to low-income subscribers, including renters and those unable to install solar panels on their own properties. Grants reduce subscription rates for low-income community solar subscribers and increase their participation in community solar programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Statewide competitive grant program providing approximately $17 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding. Initial funding of $5 million for AOI-1 (Area of Interest 1) for community solar developer incentives and $12 million for AOI-2 for landfill/brownfield solar projects. AOI-1: Grants to developers for subscribing low-income households to community solar projects with minimum 15% of energy output at 25% savings from CSEGS credit rate. AOI-2: Grants for solar projects on landfills/brownfields with minimum 50% free energy to low-income subscribers and remaining at 25% savings, funded at $2,000/kW-dc plus 75% of interconnection wiring costs (after $1M threshold, max $3M). Funding supports offsets to Power Purchase Agreement costs for Community Solar Subscriber Organizations serving low-income households, enabling lower subscription rates and maximizing value to subscribers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland PSC-approved Community Solar Subscriber Organizations and low-income and income-qualified Marylanders (at or below 200% federal poverty level), including renters and those unable to install solar panels on their own properties, seeking to access clean energy at reduced cost.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements, community solar system development, project construction, and reduce subscription rates to enable lower-cost clean energy for low-income households through community solar programs, supporting organizations in maximizing subscriber value and enabling access to solar energy benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland across utility service territories, including Potomac-Edison service territory. Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be Maryland PSC-approved Subscriber Organization registered with Maryland Public Service Commission
Must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing

Must offset Power Purchase Agreement costs
Must serve low-income households (≤200% federal poverty level)
Must rent home or be unable to install solar panels on own property
Must maintain site control for minimum 20 years post-construction

NABCEP PVIP or PVDS certified individual required for design/installation

All AHJ permits must be closed and inspections completed

Utility acceptance and final approval to operate required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit completed Application Worksheets (FY26 with 12% Base Case Discount), completed AOI-specific Application Checklists (AOI-1 or AOI-2), and supporting documentation per the Funding Opportunity Announcement. Applications are reviewed using the Program Manager Checklist. Completed worksheets become Attachment G to the Grant Agreement. Submit applications electronically when possible; staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. After system installation and operational status, grantees submit completion certificate, attestation, and supporting documentation. Contact 410-537-4000, 1-800-72-ENERGY, or DLInfo_MEA@maryland.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide competitive grant program that provides funding to purchase and lease electric school buses for student transportation services in Maryland. The program prioritizes expanding access to funding for overburdened and low to moderate income communities facing economic challenges. Funding also supports charging infrastructure, technical training, and associated costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant covers up to 120% of the incremental cost of eligible electric school buses, with additional funding for charging infrastructure and associated costs. Maximum award cap is $2,000,000 per grantee (or $2,500,000 for qualifying income-eligible school districts). Eligible charging installation costs are covered proportional to charger costs calculated by MEA. Additional funding available for electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) and facility planning (up to $300,000), project start-up expenses (up to $200,000 for LEAs; up to $25,000 for vendors), and technical training for technicians (up to $7,200 for certifying 6 technicians). Charging infrastructure capped at 30% of total project funding request.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public local education agencies (school districts), non-profit organizations in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and private school bus vendors operating on behalf of LEAs to purchase school buses for student transportation services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new electric school buses for student transportation and routine school-related programming, electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) and facility planning, charging infrastructure installation, project start-up expenses, and technical training for technicians on high-voltage battery and electrical systems maintenance. Retrofits and repowered vehicles are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland to all eligible public school districts and their vendors. Vehicles must be domiciled within Maryland for a minimum of three years.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Public Local Education Agency (LEA), non-profit in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, or a fleet/private school bus vendor (maximum 4 vendors per school district) operating on behalf of an LEA
Vehicles must be new electric school buses purchased (not retrofitted or repowered)
Replacement buses must be MY 2010/2013 or older diesel buses or oldest buses in fleet
Vehicles must be for routine transportation of students for school or school-related programming
Vehicle cannot have been funded in whole or in part by another Maryland State grant
MEA and other state incentives (including federal) cannot exceed the total funding request or project cost
Applicant must be willing and able to enter grant agreement with MEA
Must have financial capability to cover expenses upfront and seek reimbursement
W-9 form required with matching name and federal tax identification number on grant agreement
Semi-annual operational data reporting required
Community partner collaboration required (utilities, local organizations, government agencies)
Clear documentation of other funding sources if vehicle/infrastructure previously received state funding
Vehicles must be domiciled in Maryland for minimum 3 years
Data sharing with MEA for 3 years (VINs, routes, charging usage)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Jotform application form with all required documentation including concept plans for fleet management by the deadline of December 26, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET. Applicants can request 1-on-1 meetings or calls by contacting transportation.mea@maryland.gov for assistance completing the application. After award, grantees submit reimbursement requests via Jotform with required invoices and cost breakdowns, and file semi-annual operation reports and progress reports as required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides Maryland community-serving buildings with funding to support the efficient electrification of existing building systems. Eligible projects include hospitals and medical facilities, multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities, schools, universities, colleges, preschools, daycare centers, nonprofit organizations, community-based organizations, houses of worship, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, libraries, grocery stores, nature centers, performing arts centers, volunteer fire stations, and other community-serving buildings. The program helps facilities shift from fossil fuel-powered equipment to greener electric alternatives, resulting in potential lifecycle cost reductions and zero onsite emissions. Eligible electrification measures include heat pumps, energy-efficient building shells, energy conservation efforts, electric water heaters, electric dryers, hot water and chilled water systems, ENERGY STAR appliances, building envelope improvements, building controls, and electric panel and wiring upgrades. Pre-electrification measures such as weatherization and energy efficiency improvements may also be supported.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program with total FY26 budget of $6.8 million dollars. Grants range from $25,000 to $1.5 million. MEA reimburses up to 50% of total project costs after utility incentives are deducted (exclusive of project management and oversight costs). Applicants must leverage utility incentives and cover remaining 50% through other federal, local, state incentives, or private funds. Funding is disbursed quarterly to awardees on a reimbursement basis for completed work with proof of purchase. Grants help community-serving buildings cover a portion of upfront costs for building electrification projects including electric heat pumps (air-source, water-source, ground-source), electric water heaters, electric dryers, hot water and chilled water systems, steam management systems, ENERGY STAR electric appliances, building envelope improvements (insulation and air sealing), building controls, electric panel upgrades, electrical wiring, and engineering/design services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community-serving building owners and operators including hospitals, medical facilities, multi-family buildings in low-and-moderate income communities, schools, universities, colleges, preschools, daycare centers, nonprofit organizations, community-based organizations, houses of worship, arts and science centers, senior centers, museums, libraries, grocery stores, nature centers, performing arts centers, volunteer fire stations, and other community-serving buildings. Applicants must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports building electrification projects including electric heat pumps (air-source, water-source, ground-source), heat pump water heaters, heat pump dryers, hot water and chilled water systems, steam management systems, induction stovetops and ovens, ENERGY STAR electric appliances and electric kitchen equipment, building envelope improvements (doors, windows, insulation, and air sealing), building controls, electric panel upgrades, electrical wiring, and engineering/design services. Funds must be used for physical construction, materials, or equipment as described in the application. Funds must support additional capacity and cannot offset previously incurred costs or supplant existing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to community-serving buildings located throughout Maryland. Buildings located in overburdened census tracts as identified by MDEnviroScreen Tool or Maryland statute may receive prioritization.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications via JotForm link on the Electrifying Community Buildings webpage. Applicants should contact MEA at least 14 days prior to the deadline if an alternate submission method is needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Passed in 2008 by the Maryland General Assembly, the EmPOWER Maryland Energy Efficiency Act established a goal to reduce per capita electricity usage and peak demand 15% by 2015. This statewide energy efficiency and conservation program is managed by Maryland's electric and gas utility companies and the Department of Housing and Community Development to help households and businesses reduce energy consumption and costs through energy efficiency improvements, beneficial electrification initiatives, free or discounted energy audits, weatherization assistance, and efficient appliance rebates. The program targets annual incremental energy savings with increasingly higher goals for utilities (2.25% annually in 2025-2026, and 2.5% annually in 2027 and thereafter) and special focus on limited-income households through DHCD programs. Energy efficiency is one of the least expensive ways to meet the growing electricity demands of the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Utility companies (BGE, Potomac Edison, Delmarva Power & Light, PEPCO, Washington Gas Light, and SMECO) and DHCD provide free or discounted energy audits, weatherization assistance, efficient appliance rebates, incentives to switch from fossil fuel heating and appliances to efficient electric alternatives, and energy efficiency training. The program targets annual incremental energy savings with increasingly higher goals: 2.25% annually in 2025 and 2026, and 2.5% annually in 2027 and thereafter for utilities. DHCD aims to increase annual energy savings across all limited-income households with goals of 0.53% in 2024, 0.72% in 2025, and 1% in 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland electricity and gas customers, including households and businesses seeking to improve energy efficiency and reduce energy costs, with special focus on limited-income households through DHCD programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including audits, weatherization, efficient appliances, and conversion from fossil fuel to electric heating and appliances in residential, commercial, and institutional buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to customers of participating utilities: Baltimore Gas & Electric, Potomac Edison Company, Delmarva Power & Light, Potomac Electric Power Company, Washington Gas Light Company, Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, and Choptank Electric Cooperative, plus DHCD programs statewide.

structured_extraction.program_name: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grants (EECBG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program funded through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law) that helps communities transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy through planning activities. The program supports comprehensive community approaches to addressing clean energy and climate goals while improving community health, well-being, and economic development. The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) awards competitive subgrants to support county and local government planning activities including energy planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits and feasibility studies, and expansion or revisions of existing energy plans and strategies. MEA also uses EECBG funds to support community energy liaisons who assist local governments in developing energy efficiency and decarbonization strategies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive subgrants between $100,000 and $350,000, with larger awards possible for exceptional proposals. Matching is not required. Total funding available is up to $1,462,617. Funds support energy planning, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits, feasibility studies, and planning-related activities only. Does NOT cover capital expenditures or reimbursement for costs prior to grant agreement execution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated cities, towns, and counties in Maryland that did not receive direct EECBG grants from the U.S. Department of Energy
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits and feasibility studies, expansion or revisions of existing energy plans and strategies, and community energy liaison positions. Planning projects only; does not cover capital expenditures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland counties and incorporated municipalities that did not receive direct EECBG formulaic allocations from the U.S. Department of Energy. Ineligible counties (received direct DOE funding): Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's.
