structured_extraction.program_name: Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebate Programs: Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity Program (HERO) and Home Electrification & Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal rebate programs under the Inflation Reduction Act providing rebates to residential property owners and multifamily building owners in Maryland for clean energy upgrades. Programs include: (1) Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity Program (HERO) - whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that reduce energy use by at least 20%; (2) Home Electrification & Appliance Rebates Program (HEAR) - rebates for low and moderate income households to install heat pumps, electric panel upgrades, electric wiring, heat pump water heaters and other clean heating equipment worth up to $8,000; and (3) rebates for replacing fossil-fuel appliances such as fuel oil or natural gas with electric alternatives, along with supporting upgrades. For multifamily buildings, at least 50% of residents must have incomes equal to or less than 150% of area median income. The Maryland Energy Administration plans to partner with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for required low-income program components.

For multifamily buildings, at least 50% of residents must have incomes equal to or less than 150% of area median income. Direct rebates provided for home energy efficiency upgrades and fossil fuel to electric appliance conversions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers low-cost capital financing loans to Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and state agencies to finance cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation projects that reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Loans are available at below-market rates for nonprofits and businesses, and at zero financing cost (plus 1% administrative fee) for state and local governments. Funding supports both existing and to-be-constructed facilities, including projects in commercial buildings. Comprehensive projects with multiple measures to maximize energy cost savings and greenhouse gas reductions are highly desired. Total of $4,281,842 available in FY26. During the first 90 days, $2,140,842 is reserved for nonprofits and $2,140,842 is reserved for state governmental bodies. All remaining funds become available to eligible applicants beginning November 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: First-come, first-serve loans with varying interest rates and terms: Microloans ($10,000-$50,000) at 3% interest up to 10 years for eligible businesses and nonprofits; Traditional loans ($50,001-$500,000) at 2% interest up to 18 years for eligible businesses and nonprofits; State agencies and local governments receive up to $2,000,000 at 0% interest plus 1% administrative fee up to 18 years. Funds available for up to 100% of Net Total Project Cost (facility retrofits) or Incremental Project Cost (improvements). Total of $4,281,842 available in FY26. During the first 90 days, $2,140,842 is reserved for nonprofits and $2,140,842 is reserved for state governmental bodies. All remaining funds become available to eligible applicants beginning November 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that supports local governments in implementing sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficiency projects, including solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on municipal facilities and properties. The program provides incentives for decarbonization planning, energy efficiency, clean energy, renewable energy, and electrification projects—including geothermal heating and cooling systems and heat pump water heater upgrades—that reduce energy usage, lower greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and promote clean energy and economic development. The program offers $64 million in one-time funding for fiscal year 2026 across four areas of interest: AOI1 (non-competitive formula block grant for planning and implementation), AOI2 (competitive planning grants), AOI3 (competitive implementation projects excluding electrification), and AOI4 (competitive electrification-focused implementation projects). Funds support planning activities, renewable energy installation (solar PV systems including roof-mounted, ground-mounted, canopies, and parking canopies; geothermal; landfill-gas-to-energy), building envelope improvements, efficient equipment and appliance upgrades, energy audits, energy planning, strategy development, feasibility studies, site suitability analysis, and electrification projects across local governments' portfolios of public facilities. The program operates on a 36-month project implementation period with reimbursement-based funding models and provides technical assistance through the University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers four areas of interest: Area of Interest 1 (AOI1) provides a non-competitive formula block grant with flexible funding that can be used over multiple years for planning and implementation of clean energy projects. Areas of Interest 2, 3, and 4 provide competitive merit-based grants for specific projects including planning activities, implementation projects excluding electrification, and electrification-focused implementation projects. AOI1 ($50 million for planning and renewables, $10 million for energy efficiency, $4 million for electrification) is for counties and Baltimore City only. AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 are competitive grants open to municipalities and counties. Funds support planning activities, renewable energy installation (solar PV systems including roof-mounted, ground-mounted, canopies, and parking canopies; geothermal; landfill-gas-to-energy), building envelope improvements (weatherization, insulation), efficient equipment and appliance upgrades (air source heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, LEDs), energy audits, energy planning, strategy development, feasibility studies, site suitability analysis, design and engineering, and electrification projects (replacing fossil fuel systems with electric systems). AOI2 provides up to 90% reimbursement for planning projects. AOI3 and AOI4 provide competitive implementation funding with reimbursement-based models after project completion. Applicants must pay upfront and submit invoices for reimbursement. Minimum grant requests: AOI1 $500,000, AOI2 $50,000-$300,000, AOI3 $50,000-$1,000,000, AOI4 $50,000-$1,500,000. AOI4 reimburses up to 50% of total project costs after utility incentives are deducted. Technical assistance includes feasibility studies, site suitability analysis, and project planning support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland, including all Maryland municipalities. Municipalities are eligible for AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4. Counties and the City of Baltimore are encouraged to apply for AOI1. Rural jurisdictions receive grant writing support from Environmental Finance Center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning activities (feasibility studies, energy audits, energy planning, strategy development, decarbonization roadmaps, site suitability analysis, site assessments), renewable energy installation (solar PV systems including roof-mounted, ground-mounted, canopies, and parking canopies; geothermal systems; landfill-gas-to-energy), building envelope improvements (weatherization, insulation, windows, roofs), efficient equipment and appliance upgrades (air source heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, LEDs, HVAC tune-ups, building controls, retrocommissioning), energy audits, energy storage (when integrated with renewable energy generation), electrification projects (replacing fossil fuel systems with electric alternatives including heat pumps, electric water heaters, electric dryers and appliances, electrical panel/wiring upgrades), contractor payments for construction and implementation, design and engineering activities, battery storage integration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide to all incorporated towns, cities, and counties in Maryland. All proposed projects must be located in Maryland on facilities owned or leased by the applicant.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through a competitive or non-competitive process depending on the area of interest. AOI1 uses a formula-based allocation process with submission of narrative describing project descriptions, timelines, target buildings, expected outcomes, and key partners. AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 use merit-based competitive evaluation with online application submissions including narrative describing buildings, planning activities, capacity to execute project, anticipated challenges, community engagement, budget justification, and likelihood to inform future capital projects or implementation details. All applicants must upload required documentation including W-9 form, narrative, and budget template. For AOI2 planning projects, applicants must submit UBIDs to MEA prior to grant agreement execution. Applications are evaluated based on alignment with program goals and priorities according to specified evaluation criteria. Sample applications and funding opportunity announcements are provided for reference. Contact information for authorized representative, application point of contact, and project manager must be provided. Applicants must accept terms and conditions with typed e-signature. Technical assistance available through University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center at efc_climateaction@umd.edu. Solar project application process: Step 1 - Engage technical support (MCEC/EFC), Step 2 - Assess site suitability, Step 3 - Collect electricity usage data and define project scope with technical partner.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for residential and commercial taxpayers who have installed qualified energy storage systems on their property in Maryland during Tax Year 2024. The program awards tax credit certificates on a first-come, first-served basis up to an annual cap of $750,000, with $450,000 reserved for residential taxpayers and $300,000 reserved for commercial taxpayers. Eligible applicants can claim the credit on their Maryland state income tax return. The program operates on a rolling basis with applications processed in the order received until annual funds are exhausted. Authorized through tax year 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit certificates are awarded to eligible applicants on a first-come, first-served basis, up to $750,000 total per tax year ($450,000 for residential, $300,000 for commercial). The tax credit is calculated as the lower of: 30% of total installed costs OR $5,000 maximum for residential properties OR $150,000 maximum for commercial properties. Credits are non-refundable and cannot be carried over to future tax years. Residential taxpayers are limited to one credit per property regardless of tax year. Commercial taxpayers are limited to one credit per tax year. Applicants can claim the credit on their Maryland state income tax return by filing Form 500CR.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Supply Chain Investment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding on a non-competitive, first-come-first-served basis to support new or existing businesses entering the offshore wind supply chain in Maryland. It includes funding for capital expenditures and industry event attendance to help organizations enter or expand within Maryland's offshore wind industry. The program offers up to $2,000,000 in total grant funding, with $1,750,000 allocated to capital expenditures and $250,000 allocated to industry events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-competitive grant funding available on a first-come-first-served basis. AOI 1: Capital Expenditures provides funding to offset up to 50% of total project costs, not to exceed $400,000. Applicants must contribute minimum 50% matching funds (may include finance/loan agreements, cash on hand, business line of credit, or other state/federal/private grants) for relocation costs, new construction, renovations, and equipment purchase/installation. AOI 2: Industry Events provides one-time reimbursement of up to $5,000 per eligible offshore wind or marine technology event (limited to one event per fiscal year, one grant award per applicant per FY2025). Eligible event costs include registration fees, exhibition fees, economy airfare and baggage, ground transportation, lodging (GSA/Department of State per diem rates), meeting space audio/visual, and product shipping (capped amount). Total program funding is up to $2,000,000, with $1,750,000 allocated to Capital Expenditures and $250,000 allocated to Industry Events.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fiscal Year 2025, first come-first served until 5:00 P.M. EST, March 15, 2025 or until all program funding is awarded, whichever occurs first
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or existing businesses entering offshore wind supply chain, with particular emphasis on minority, women, and veteran-owned emerging businesses and historically disenfranchised groups. Emerging businesses must be at least 51 percent owned and controlled by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 (as adjusted annually for inflation). Businesses located outside of Maryland may apply if they are willing to relocate or expand into the state. Also includes non-profit organizations and government institutions participating in offshore wind supply chain and workforce development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AOI 1: Relocation costs, new construction of real property, renovations to existing real property, purchase and installation of equipment, certifications, and facility development. AOI 2: Event registration fees, exhibition fees, economy airfare and baggage fees, ground transportation, lodging based on GSA/Department of State per diem rates, meeting space audio/visual costs, and shipping of sample products for offshore wind and marine technology industry events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs available statewide in Maryland. Project locations and facilities must be specified with sitemap documentation. Applicants may include businesses willing to relocate or expand into Maryland contingent upon receiving a grant award. AOI 2 events must be located in the United States and its territories only; international events are ineligible.

Must be able to contribute to Maryland's offshore wind supply chain and workforce
Emerging businesses must be at least 51 percent owned and controlled by individuals with personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 (adjusted annually for inflation)
Non-emerging business applicants are not eligible to receive grant funding

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Workforce and Education Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program to support workforce development and education initiatives in the offshore wind industry. The program provides funding to help nonprofits, academic institutions, businesses, labor unions, and government entities develop an experienced workforce and expand public knowledge of offshore wind careers. The program is structured around two areas of interest: AOI 1 - Industry Education (up to $500,000 per award, up to 75% of project costs) supports capital and operating expenditures for developing or expanding offshore wind education programs for any education level, and AOI 2 - Workforce Training (up to $500,000 per award, up to 75% of project costs) supports development or expansion of offshore wind workforce certification-based training programs. Funds support businesses, minority-owned emerging businesses, nonprofits, academic institutions, labor unions, and state, local, and municipal governments in establishing workforce development pathways for individuals entering the offshore wind industry in skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding with two areas of interest: AOI 1 (Industry Education) and AOI 2 (Workforce Training). Each AOI provides up to $500,000 per award (up to 75% of total project costs). Applicants must provide a 25% cost share in matching funds or in-kind services. Matching funds may include finance/loan agreements, cash on hand, business line of credit, and/or other grants. AOI 1 funds offset costs of developing and implementing new or existing offshore wind education programs. AOI 2 funds offset costs of developing or expanding offshore wind workforce certification-based training programs at new or existing workforce training centers. Funds support nonprofits, academic institutions, businesses, emerging businesses (including minority-owned), labor unions, and government entities. Eligible activities include developing or expanding programs, covering capital and operating costs (relocation, renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, administrative expenses), and providing supportive services for trainees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: General public, K-12 students, graduate degree holders, nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, businesses, government entities, labor unions, emerging businesses (including minority-owned), workforce training centers, and individuals from historically marginalized, disenfranchised, and economically disadvantaged communities, including formerly incarcerated individuals and people with disabilities interested in developing or expanding offshore wind workforce training and education capabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenditures associated with developing, expanding, and implementing offshore wind education and training programs, including general offshore wind education for any education level, technical trade skills and safety standards training, and workforce certification-based training programs. Eligible costs include relocation, renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, and administrative expenses. Projects may support general public education on offshore wind careers and establish workforce development pathways for individuals entering the offshore wind industry in Maryland and the larger U.S. offshore wind market in skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Programs must provide direct benefit to Maryland's offshore wind supply chain and workforce.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization, academic institution, business, labor union, government entity (state, local, or municipal), new or existing workforce training center, or emerging business (at least 51% owned and controlled by individuals with personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000, adjusted annually for inflation)

Projects must include technical trade skills and/or safety standards training

All minimum eligibility criteria and evaluation criteria specific to each AOI are detailed in respective Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOA)

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland RISE Program (Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Energy Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federally-funded Maryland incentive program offering competitive grants to electric utility infrastructure owners/operators, utility-scale generators, transmission owners/operators, electricity storage operators, distribution providers, fuel suppliers, and other eligible entities to fund resilient infrastructure projects that improve power quality, reliability, and resilience to Maryland's grid and critical infrastructure. The program supports deployment of clean energy and resilience infrastructure projects to enhance grid resilience, prevent outages, and strengthen Maryland's electric grid to protect against threats including severe weather, tropical storms, hurricanes, extreme temperatures, winter storms, cyberattacks, physical attacks, and aging components. Projects support virtual power plants, electrification, zero emission technologies, and aim to avoid the need for additional conventional generation capacity or reduce peaker plant usage, with special emphasis on reducing/eliminating conventional peaker plants in LMIOU (Low-to-Moderate Income Overburdened Utility) and Justice40 communities. Funded by Section 40101(d) of the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act), the program supports Maryland's goal of achieving 100% clean energy by 2035.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants funded through the federal Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Section 40101(d) (Preventing Outages and Enhancing the Resilience of the Electric Grid). Total program budget is approximately $15,000,000 ($13,000,000 federal; remainder state). Two Areas of Interest (AOIs) based on applicant electricity sales volume: AOI 1 (Large Applicants) with annual electricity sales >4,000,000 MWh receive grants up to $3,000,000 with 100% mandatory cost-match; AOI 2 (Small Applicants) with annual electricity sales ≤4,000,000 MWh receive grants up to $3,000,000 with 1/3 mandatory cost-match. Grants support non-generation measures, resilient energy infrastructure projects, and project costs including capital funding, equipment, installation, and associated expenses to enhance the resilience and reliability of the electricity grid, including improvements to electricity and related power infrastructure, clean energy generation projects, and sustainable energy infrastructure. Full grant amounts awarded based on application rankings until funds exhausted; partial grants may be awarded if insufficient funds for full project funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland electricity infrastructure operators, fuel suppliers, electricity storage operators, electricity generators, transmission owners/operators, distribution providers, and other utility industry stakeholders seeking to enhance electric grid resilience and reliability, particularly those serving critical infrastructure including wastewater treatment plants, potable water systems, hospitals/medical facilities, dense population centers, and senior care facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-generation measures and project costs to enhance the resilience and reliability of the electricity grid, including weatherization, fire-resistant technologies, monitoring/control systems, undergrounding electrical equipment, utility pole management, power line relocation/reconductoring, vegetation management, distributed energy resources, microgrids, battery storage, adaptive protection, advanced modeling, power line/facility hardening, replacement of old conductors/cables, improvements to electricity and related power infrastructure, clean energy generation projects, and sustainable energy infrastructure. Project activities must be located within Maryland and benefits must accrue to Maryland ratepayers only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Projects must be located within Maryland and serve Maryland ratepayers. Geographic diversity and Justice40 outcomes are considered in project selection.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible Maryland electricity infrastructure operator, fuel supplier, electricity storage operator, electricity generator, transmission owner/operator, distribution provider, or other utility industry stakeholder
Must be registered to operate in Maryland and in Good Standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must meet both federal requirements and Maryland requirements per Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Section 40101(a)(2)
Must be a domestic entity organized, chartered, or incorporated under U.S. state/territory laws with majority domestic ownership and control and physical U.S. business location
Must not be debarred or suspended
Comply with 2 CFR Part 200 audit requirements
Must indemnify the Government for liability arising from projects (except for Government negligence)
Recipients must attest they have not been convicted of felony crimes within 24 months prior to signature
Recipients must attest they have no unpaid Federal tax liabilities
Recipients must not require employees/contractors to sign NDAs restricting lawful reporting of waste, fraud, or abuse
Recipients must maintain current information in SAM (System for Award Management) if total active Federal awards exceed $10,000,000
Recipients must report criminal, civil, or administrative proceedings within the past 5 years
Must comply with U.S. Export Control laws
All iron and steel must be produced in the U.S. (entire manufacturing process in U.S.)
All manufactured products must be produced in U.S. with ≥55% domestic component cost
All construction materials must be manufactured in U.S.
Davis-Bacon prevailing wage requirements for construction work >$2,000
No equipment from countries of risk (Iran, North Korea, Russia, China)
Foreign collaboration must have advance DOE written notification and approval
Weekly payroll certification required for construction work
Compliance with Executive Order 11246 affirmative action and equal employment opportunity requirements
All direct labor costs must be incurred in the United States unless DOE approves otherwise; American-made equipment and products preferred
At least 100% of direct labor costs must be in the United States unless DOE approves otherwise
Equipment title vests with recipient
Maintain records to substantiate data collection and resilience improvements
Promptly notify DOE in writing of any potential overlap with other federal funding for identical cost items and eliminate any inappropriate duplication of funding
Comply with post-award due diligence reviews for foreign influence risk assessment and implement risk mitigation measures if required
Construction signage must meet DOE 'Investing in America' specifications
Funds cannot be used to influence congressional action on legislation or appropriation matters
Funds cannot be used to procure telecommunications or video surveillance equipment from prohibited entities (Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua)
Project funds (Federal and non-Federal) are restricted from certain telecommunications and surveillance equipment procurement
Comply with National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)
Obtain required federal, state, and municipal permits
Foreign nationals require approval; those from China, Iran, North Korea, Russia, or State Sponsors of Terrorism require DOE approval before participation
Specific eligibility criteria are detailed in the Funding Opportunity Announcement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed signed application form with project proposal (maximum 10 pages) and completed FY25 RISE Project Budget Workbook using the FY25 Maryland RISE Application Form. Applications must be submitted electronically by the deadline of 3:00 P.M. ET, Tuesday, January 21, 2025. Specific submission instructions are provided in the Funding Opportunity Announcement. Staff will confirm receipt of electronic applications within one to two business days via email. Applications are evaluated and ranked, with full grant amounts awarded until funds are exhausted; partial grants may be awarded if insufficient funds for full project funding. Recipients must comply with all federal compliance requirements including 2 CFR Part 200 audit requirements, prevailing wage requirements, Buy America provisions, and post-award due diligence reviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program combines energy efficiency, electrification, and solar energy projects to support Maryland residents experiencing low-to-moderate incomes. It provides grants to non-profit organizations and local government entities for energy efficiency upgrades, electrification, and renewable energy projects that generate significant reductions in residential energy usage and benefit income-qualifying residents in single-family and multi-family homes. Two areas of interest: AOI1 (energy efficiency/electrification for renter and owner-occupied homes) and AOI2 (solar energy for owner-occupied homes only).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are awarded for energy efficiency, electrification, and solar projects. AOI1 (Energy Efficiency/Electrification Projects): Up to $21,000 per residence with minimum $105,000 per award for first-time grantees; regional competition based on low-to-moderate income households. AOI2 (Solar Energy Projects): $30,000-$1,500,000 per award for solar photovoltaic systems (up to $30,000 per home for design, installation, commissioning); statewide competition with geographic diversity consideration. Grant administration costs capped at 15% total. Eligible for project-related training assistance up to $6,000 per award for BPI or NABCEP certifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents experiencing low-to-moderate income (up to 80% of state median income); single-family and multi-family homeowners and renters in income-qualifying households; households ineligible for Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) or EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements (AOI1): building shell improvements, HVAC repairs/upgrades, water heater replacements, appliance replacements, lighting upgrades, window repairs, enabling repairs, weatherization. Solar installations (AOI2): photovoltaic system installations with design, installation, and commissioning for owner-occupied homes only. All work must meet Simple Payback (SPB) ≤ 18 years cost-effectiveness threshold. Equipment must meet ENERGY STAR certification or equivalent. Attic insulation minimum R60 where feasible. Wildlife barriers required for all solar installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for residential buildings. AOI1 applications reviewed competitively within defined regions. AOI2 applications reviewed competitively statewide with geographic diversity consideration.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization (tax-exempt under IRS §501(c)(3), (4), or (6)) or local government entity registered and in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Projects must benefit Maryland residents experiencing low-to-moderate incomes
Projects must generate significant reductions in residential energy usage
Solar systems that have already received funding from Maryland Solar Access Program (MSAP) are not eligible
Applicants must complete application materials including the Excel spreadsheet and conflict of interest disclosure form if applicable
Energy audits by BPI-certified auditors required for whole house/limited upgrades
Manual J/S calculations required for HVAC replacements
Preliminary solar screening required for AOI1 projects
Photo documentation (geotagged, time-stamped) of major upgrades required
Monthly reporting requirements
Simple Payback (SPB) ≤ 18 years cost-effectiveness threshold
Wildlife barriers required for all solar installations
ENERGY STAR certification or equivalent required for equipment
Attic insulation minimum R60 where feasible
No new fossil fuel-powered equipment installation permitted
All work performed by staff/contractors holding necessary Maryland certifications and licenses
Compliance with all applicable local, State, and federal building codes and regulations
Historic preservation review completion before construction starts
Comprehensive third-party liability insurance minimum $1,000,000 per occurrence with State listed as additional insured
At least 80% of worksite workers must reside in Maryland or within 50 miles of Maryland's borders
Nondiscrimination compliance
Grantee must authorize signatory to commit organization to agreement obligations
No collusion or bribery convictions allowed for grantee, officers, directors, or employees involved in grant acquisition
No third-party solicitors employed or paid contingent fees for securing the grant
Grantee and leadership cannot be suspended or debarred from state contracting
Grantee cannot be in default on financial obligations to State or MEA
Board members must have Conflict of Interest Policy and certify contractor selection complies with policy
State listed as additional insured on liability insurance
Consumer protections including 25-year panel warranty, 10-year inverter warranty, 10-year workmanship warranty for solar installations
Cybersecurity protections for personal data required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants download and complete the FY26 MEA Residential Energy Equity Program Application (Excel spreadsheet) and submit required program documents by the deadline. structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program designed to assist and encourage transfer students from Maryland community colleges to attend 4-year institutions within the state and complete their bachelor's degrees in a timely manner. The program provides financial assistance to full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students transferring from community college to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year institution. Recipients enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs receive $2,000 annually ($1,000 per term), while recipients in all other programs receive $1,000 annually ($500 per term). The scholarship can be renewed for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer. Applicant pool is ranked on academic merit and financial need, and a waiting list is maintained each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs receive $2,000 annually ($1,000 per term). Recipients enrolling in all other programs receive $1,000 annually ($500 per term). The scholarship can be renewed for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer. Funds may be used towards tuition and mandatory fees at the 4-year Maryland institution. Award amount is contingent on availability of funds. Applicant pool is ranked on academic merit and financial need.

Students at all degree levels (undergraduate, transfer, or graduate) who are accepted to eligible programs may apply during designated application cycles.

The assistance applies to tuition charges for degree-seeking undergraduate, transfer, or graduate students.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that supports Maryland's college access and completion goals by providing financial support and fostering collaboration between Maryland's high-need local education agencies and higher education institutions to raise the academic preparedness of economically and environmentally disadvantaged middle and high school students (grades 6-12) so they can attend, persist, and succeed in college. The program funds activities that encourage students to aim higher, study harder, and take courses required for college admission and success. Award recipients are exposed to various academic disciplines, career fields, and learning opportunities. The program provides student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, and learning opportunities in English/Language Arts and mathematics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funding awarded to accredited Maryland public or independent two- and four-year higher education institutions partnering with high-need Local Education Authorities (LEAs) and potentially non-profit organizations to support college preparation services and academic preparedness programs. Up to $150,000 per project. Grants support student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, and college access initiatives including Type A: Academic Services to Students (enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, individualized academic support with strong preference for mathematics and English/language arts); Type B: Student and Family Financial Aid Advising Services (FAFSA information, financial literacy, college and career awareness, leadership development); Type C: Student and Family Academic Planning and Career Counseling. Funding period: August 5, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Disbursement: 50% at project start, 50% upon receipt of interim report.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year institutions of higher education, particularly those partnering with non-profit organizations, to serve Maryland middle and high school students grades 6-12 who are economically and environmentally disadvantaged, with focus on Free and Reduced-price Meals (FARM) eligible students in high-need local education agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College preparation services, student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, academic preparedness programs and college access initiatives. Type A activities: enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, individualized academic support with strong preference for mathematics and English/language arts. Type B activities: FAFSA information, financial literacy, college and career awareness, leadership development. Type C activities: academic planning and career counseling. Allowable expenses include salaries and wages for professional and support personnel, fringe benefits, travel (in-state only; mileage max 67 cents/mile), materials and supplies (non-instructional equipment only), consultant and contractual services, equipment rental/leasing, participant support (snacks/meals for workshops), space rental if necessary. Maximum 8% indirect costs allowed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service regions include Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline County, Prince GeorgeS County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County. Eligible high-need local education agencies must meet three of four criteria: (1) ≥44.4% FARM in feeder middle schools; (2) ≥39.6% FARM in feeder high schools; (3) FARM cohort graduation rate <77.93%; (4) College remediation rate >32.7%.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit electronic and paper applications with proposal cover sheet, abstract, 15-page narrative (12-point Times New Roman), budget narrative with justification, Statement of Assurances, and Cooperative Planning Agreement signed by all required partners (lead college/university, school district superintendent/CEO, LEA coordinator, high school principal, and other partners). Electronic submission: Abstract (Word), full proposal (PDF), budget request (Excel). Hard copies: 1 original plus 5 copies with blue ink signatures and 1 electronic copy. All required forms from Appendix B must be completed. Mail or hand deliver to Anthony Reiner at Maryland Higher Education Commission, 217 E. Redwood St., Suite 2100, Baltimore, MD 21202, or email to Anthony.Reiner@maryland.gov. Proposals reviewed by CPIP review panel scoring against criteria including needs assessment, project objectives, management plan, operations, evaluation plan, and budget. Panel convenes to discuss and recommend awards.

structured_extraction.program_name: Complete College Maryland – Near Completer Grant / One Step Away Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive state-funded program supporting Maryland residents who have postponed their college education and are ready to return and complete their degree. Created by House Bill 16 following the 2018 legislative session, the program went into effect for the fall semester of 2019. It serves near-completer students who have earned at least 75 percent of their college credits (45+ credits for associate degrees, 90+ credits for bachelor's degrees) and have postponed education for at least 12 consecutive months. The program has two components: (1) Student assistance providing financial aid covering up to one-third of in-county tuition at community colleges or up to one-third of in-state undergraduate tuition at public four-year institutions to help eligible students complete their college degree. (2) Institutional competitive grants (up to $60,000 per institution) to identify, re-engage, re-enroll, and support near-completer students through tutoring, customized degree plans, and dedicated advisors. Eligible Maryland higher education institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Awards are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis to eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dual-component assistance: (1) For students: up to one-third of in-county tuition at community colleges or up to one-third of in-state undergraduate tuition at public four-year institutions to help eligible students complete their college degree, applied towards tuition only after all non-loan aid has been applied, leading to promotion in an existing career or opportunity to begin a new career. Awards are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. (2) For institutions: competitive grants up to $60,000 per institution to identify, contact, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students, provide tutoring, customized degree planning, and dedicated advisor support. Institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Eligible expenses include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, communications, subsistence, and marketing materials. Indirect costs may be claimed at up to 8% of direct costs for matching purposes only.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, July 25, 2025, 4:00 p.m. (for institutional grants; ongoing for student assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Near-completer students at eligible Maryland higher education institutions who have earned 75 percent or more of their college credits and have postponed their education for at least 12 consecutive months; Maryland residents who previously enrolled in a degree program but did not complete it and are working to complete their education; accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year institutions offering associate or bachelor's degrees seeking to improve college completion rates.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For students: financial assistance to students for tuition charges, tutoring, customized degree plans, and support from dedicated advisors to help near-completers complete an associate's or bachelor's degree. For institutions: to identify, contact, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students; degree audit infrastructure and software enhancements; degree program completion plans; enhancement and redesign of degree programs; concierge or near-completer counselor positions; faculty and staff development; marketing and outreach; salaries and wages; fringe benefits; travel; equipment; materials and supplies; consultant and contractual services; communications; subsistence; outreach and recruitment strategies; academic, financial, and social advising; prior learning assessments; competency-based testing; textbook waivers; tuition discounts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents eligible for in-state tuition and accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two- and four-year institutions across the state. The program benefits near-completer students at public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year institutions in Maryland attending community colleges and public four-year institutions. Geographic distribution of awards is considered in final selection.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students should contact their institution for specific enrollment and application procedures or log into the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) to complete the online application. After completing the application, use the Electronic File Upload Tool to submit required transcripts from the previous institution. While not required, students are encouraged to complete a FAFSA or MSFAA by March 1 for consideration of federal and other state financial aid programs. Institutions submit competitive application materials according to Request for Proposal (RFP) guidelines, including completed budget summary and narrative using specified Excel format with detailed expenditure descriptions, and institutional authorization signature. Institutions must submit interim progress reports with narrative and budget expenditure reports, and final reports including overview of project progress, objectives accomplished, preliminary results, and budget summary. All applications and reports must comply with specified assurances and fiscal procedures. For more information, visit MHEC.Maryland.gov and click on Near Completer or One Step Away Grant Program. Contact Anthony Reiner for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to Maryland residents pursuing education in cybersecurity-related degree or certificate programs approved by the Secretary of Higher Education. Recipients receive scholarships to cover tuition, mandatory fees, room, and board, and other educational expenses. The program includes support for qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. Students must commit to working in cybersecurity positions in Maryland public schools, community colleges, or government agencies, or teaching cybersecurity in Maryland for a specified service obligation period. Full-time students may renew for an additional two years; part-time students may renew for an additional five years if maintaining satisfactory academic progress and a 3.0 GPA. The award converts to a loan repayable to the state if the recipient fails to complete an approved cybersecurity program or meet the work obligation requirement.

Award converts to a loan repayable to the state if the recipient fails to complete an approved cybersecurity program or meet the work obligation requirement. State financial aid scholarship available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants will be notified by email if awarded. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A state need-based financial aid program providing grants to eligible Maryland in-state students and high school seniors to help pay for higher education at Maryland colleges and universities. Part of the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards, this program serves both renewal students (continuing recipients) and initial applicants (first-time recipients). The Guaranteed Access Grant is the largest need-based grant available in the state. Awards provide up to $18,000 to $20,200 annually, equaling up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first 2 academic years of enrollment, or up to the maximum award amount, whichever is lower, with a minimum award of $100 to $400 per year. Approximately 33,000 students receive more than $88 million in total awards annually, with up to 3,344 students receiving awards covering 100% of their financial need. The grant can be renewed for up to 3 additional years if renewal requirements are met. Students who complete the FAFSA or MHEC One-App by the priority deadline are guaranteed to receive an award if they meet eligibility criteria. Award amounts are calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation (on campus, off campus, or with parent), and financial need. Eligible applicants include Maryland residents who are eligible for in-state tuition, including U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented students who are Maryland residents, as well as high school seniors with qualifying GPAs. The program includes a GPA Upload Tool that allows eligible high schools to electronically submit senior year GPA information to the Office of Student Financial Assistance, eliminating the requirement for students to submit high school transcripts for consideration of state financial aid awards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grant providing up to $18,000 to $20,200 annually for undergraduate students. The amount equals up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first 2 academic years of enrollment, or up to the maximum award amount, whichever is lower. Minimum award is $100 to $400 per year. Award amounts are calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation (on campus, off campus, or with parent), and financial need. Approximately 33,000 students receive more than $88 million in total awards, with up to 3,344 students receiving awards covering 100% of their financial need. The grant can be renewed for up to 3 additional years if renewal requirements are met. For high school seniors, the grant is available with a minimum cumulative unweighted GPA of 2.5 as reported in their first semester of senior year.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For undergraduate applicants: Students submit a FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) or MHEC One-App by the March 1 priority deadline through the MHEC One-App portal or MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS. Document Drop-Off Events are held at various community colleges across Maryland. For high school seniors: High schools submit GPA data via the GPA Upload Tool in MDCAPS by emailing a participation request to fafsa.mhec@maryland.gov, completing a participation agreement, and receiving login credentials. High schools then upload a CSV file with required student information (last name, first name, middle initial, MHEC ID#, date of birth, cumulative unweighted GPA from first semester of senior year, and home address zip code). Alternatively, students may submit unofficial or official transcripts directly to documents.mhec@maryland.gov, or students can submit the GPA Upload Tool Student Form if identifying information is unavailable. GPAs must be reported between January 15 and May 15, with priority consideration for reports submitted by April 1. Awarding begins in late April or early May and continues weekly until funds are exhausted. MHEC processes applications on a weekly basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Program of Educational Excellence - Educational Assistance Grant (EA)
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based grant program that provides financial assistance to eligible students enrolled at postsecondary institutions in Maryland for educational expenses. Part of the Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards, this program awards financial aid to students with the greatest financial need. Students may receive awards up to $3,000 per year for up to four years, with award amounts calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation, and financial need. A minimum award of $400 per year is provided, and awards cover portions of financial need up to a maximum of $19,400. The program serves both renewal students (continuing recipients) and initial applicants (first-time recipients), with renewal applicants prioritized first. The program is available to high school seniors completing a college preparatory program as well as students who graduated prior to the current academic year and can document why they were unable to attend college within one year of graduation. Approximately 33,000 students receive more than $88 million in total awards annually. Students do not submit a specific application form; instead, they submit a FAFSA or MHEC One-App by the deadline to be considered. MDCAPS automatically considers students qualified if they meet basic eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grant providing up to $3,000 per year for up to four years, with award amounts calculated based on cost of attendance, living situation, and financial need. Minimum award is $400 per year. Award recipients may receive awards covering portions of their financial need with a maximum award of $19,400. All awards are contingent on availability of funds. Students do not submit a specific application form; instead, they submit a FAFSA or MHEC One-App by the deadline to be considered. MDCAPS automatically considers students qualified if they meet basic eligibility requirements. Financial need is calculated using: Cost of Attendance – SAI (+/- Regional Cost of Living Adjustment) – State Scholarships – Pell Grant. Renewal applicants are prioritized first, followed by initial applicants once all eligible EA applicants have been awarded. Approximately 33,000 students receive more than $88 million in total awards annually. Awarding is anticipated to begin in Summer 2025 and will continue until all funds are exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarships awarded by members of the Maryland General Assembly—both delegates and state senators—and administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to Maryland residents. These programs provide educational funding to students nominated by their legislative representatives for postsecondary education at Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. Students may pursue credentials full-time or part-time. Delegates and senators award scholarships directly to constituents in their legislative districts. Delegates have a minimum annual award of $200 per student, while Senators have a minimum annual award of $400 per student (2026-2027). Scholarships are not renewable annually; students must reapply each year, though renewal awards for up to three years are available if they maintain full-time or part-time status and satisfactory academic progress. Students may hold this scholarship with all state awards, provided total state scholarship awards do not exceed cost of attendance. In the 2020-2021 academic year, Delegates awarded $6,708,972 to 9,166 students and Senators awarded $5,382,227 to 7,713 students. Out-of-state institution use is permitted for unique majors not available in Maryland, active duty military personnel, or disabled students with special institutional provisions. Funds may not be available for all eligible students. Recipients can receive renewal awards for up to three years if they maintain satisfactory academic progress. Available to students regardless of family income. Includes an appeal process for students enrolled in less than 6 credits due to disability, allowing them to request reconsideration of State awards.

Available for full-time (12+ credits undergraduate or 9+ credits graduate per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits undergraduate or 6-8 credits graduate per semester) students at Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. Students may also use awards at out-of-state institutions if the major is not available at any Maryland institution and the legislator agrees, if the applicant is on active duty with the U.S. Military domiciled in Maryland, or if the student is disabled and studying at an institution with special provisions not available in Maryland. Students may hold this scholarship with all state awards, provided total state scholarship awards do not exceed cost of attendance. Recipients can receive renewal awards for up to three years if they maintain full-time or part-time status and satisfactory academic progress. Funds may not be available for all eligible students. Available to students regardless of family income. Senatorial Scholarship is automatically renewed for up to three years or until degree completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to United States armed forces personnel who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts, and their eligible family members (spouses, sons, daughters, stepsons, and stepdaughters) attending a Maryland postsecondary institution. Annual scholarship awards vary by housing status: up to $9,189 for students living on campus, up to $5,186 for students living with parents, or up to $5,756 for students living off campus. Awards do not exceed 50% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at the highest-cost public University System of Maryland institution. Funds may be used for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland institutions. Veterans receive priority over dependents and spouses. Awards may be renewed for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment or 8 years of part-time enrollment if eligibility requirements continue to be met. Total financial aid including state aid and veterans benefits cannot exceed cost of attendance.

structured_extraction.program_name: ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments, and Households) Act Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: First-of-its-kind state-led, place-based strategy to create poverty-fighting opportunities driven by communities' lived experience and expertise. Addresses concentrated, generational child poverty through collaborative action toward shared vision informed by data, research, and best practices. Aims to end child poverty and increase economic mobility in Maryland through targeted grants and technical support for eligible communities. The program funds the development of Neighborhood Action Plans and Community Voice Committees to reduce childhood poverty by increasing investments in high-poverty areas and improving economic mobility. The initiative surges resources into neighborhoods disproportionately impacted by systems and policies that limit wealth creation and economic mobility, driven by communities' lived experience, expertise, data, and cross-sector partnerships. Three grant program tracks are available: Track 1 (Partner Development), Track 2 (Plan Development), and Track 3 (Implementation). The program supports resident leadership through Resident Advisory Councils, strengthens partnerships between neighbors and service providers, and promotes access to programs aligned with community priorities focused on youth development, safety, education, and family support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three grant program tracks available: Track 1 (Partnership Development) - up to $65,000 each (up to 10 awards); Track 2 (Plan Development) - approximately $300,000 each (up to 7 awards); Track 3 (Implementation) - up to $5,000,000 based on community size with up to 4 funding cycles. Mix of public and private investment; first year Maryland invests $20 million total. Technical assistance includes resource hub with trainings, data dashboard, and hands-on training from experts. Funding supports the development of Neighborhood Action Plans and Community Voice Committees in areas with high levels of child poverty. Resources support poverty-fighting opportunities including education, health care access, affordable housing, commercial development, recreational spaces, nutrition, and transportation. Funding also supports resident leadership development through Resident Advisory Councils, community partnerships, and community engagement activities such as meetings and listening sessions. The Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state and national organizations partner with applicants and grantees in understanding, developing and implementing community-focused solutions to end child poverty and improve economic mobility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent to Apply Due: July 19, 2024; Full Application Deadline for Track 2 and Track 3: September 20, 2024; Full Application Deadline for Track 1: November 1, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible communities and governments most in need working to address concentrated child poverty, including neighborhoods in eligible census tracts that have been disproportionately impacted by systems and policies limiting wealth creation and economic mobility. Communities across Maryland seeking to strengthen economic opportunity and resident engagement. Community-based non-profit organizations, local government entities, local public schools, community-led organizations (Community Quarterbacks), anchor institutions, unions, and philanthropic organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of Neighborhood Action Plans and Community Voice Committees; increasing investments in high-poverty areas; improving economic mobility and reducing childhood poverty; solutions to deeply rooted challenges related to concentrated child poverty; education, health care access, affordable housing, commercial development, recreational spaces, nutrition, and transportation; resident leadership development through Resident Advisory Councils; community partnerships; community engagement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to eligible communities throughout Maryland with high levels of child poverty. All Maryland counties are eligible for Local Management Board Capacity Building Grants with specific eligible communities determined by eligibility criteria. In Frederick County, initially focused on the Route 40 corridor on the west side of the City of Frederick, including neighborhoods served by Hillcrest and Waverley Elementary Schools. Anne Arundel County eligible census tracts: Pumphrey/Patapsco Park (7050201), Maryland City (751500), Clay Street (706102), Eastport Terrace (706402), Bay Ridge Gardens (706303). Calvert County implementation includes Yardley Hills Community Initiative.
requirements_list: Program must focus on communities with high levels of child poverty
Communities must be willing to work with multiple partners to develop action plans
Communities must prioritize community voice in creating systems for change
Communities must be located in one of the eligible census tracts or designated areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible communities can visit goc.maryland.gov or contact the Division of Family Services to learn more and apply for competitive funding. Communities in eligible census tracts could apply for one of three grant program tracks. Submit Notice of Intent to Apply by July 19, 2024. Full applications for Track 2 and Track 3 due September 20, 2024; full applications for Track 1 due November 1, 2024. Applications are reviewed through the Governor's Office for alignment with the initiative's goals of reducing child poverty and strengthening economic opportunity through place-based strategies. Application procedures and requirements available through the Maryland Governor's office ENOUGH initiative page or the Governor's ENOUGH Grant Program Site.

structured_extraction.program_description: Part of the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Award Program. A state need-based financial aid grant available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. One of Maryland's largest need-based aid programs. The program provides financial aid for education-related expenses at eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Applicants are considered for various state financial aid programs and will be notified by email in the summer if awarded. Students' institutions may also notify them directly if they have been awarded. Award must be accepted or declined online through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS) within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based state financial aid grant for qualified children of undocumented immigrants attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants will be notified by email if they are awarded. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8, including DACA students and undocumented students who do not have Social Security Numbers or are ineligible for federal FAFSA, attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses at Maryland institutions including college attendance costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must attend public or nonpublic secondary school in Maryland, or community college in Maryland, or public senior higher education institution in Maryland. Students must file Maryland income tax returns for required years.

Must not be a U.S. citizen

MHEC will notify applicants by email in the summer if they are awarded. Students must accept or decline their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides student financial assistance to Maryland residents who are veterans, eligible military or public safety employees, qualifying family members and spouses of United States Armed Forces individuals who died as a result of military service or suffered a service-connected disability, and children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or sustained an injury that rendered the school employee 100 percent disabled as a victim in an act of violence occurring in the line of duty. The program awards scholarships with a minimum award of $3,000 or equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees (whichever is less), and a maximum award not exceeding the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at a four-year public institution within the University System of Maryland, excluding University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland Baltimore, with the highest annual expenses. Supported educational expenses include tuition and mandatory fees at eligible institutions. Administered through the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance. Awards can be held for up to four years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or seven years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester) or a combination of both.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship award with minimum award of $3,000 or equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees at the recipient's institution (whichever is less), and maximum award not exceeding the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at a four-year public institution within the University System of Maryland, excluding University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland Baltimore, with the highest annual expenses. For the 2026-2027 academic year, the maximum award is $14,086. Funds support tuition and mandatory fees at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions including undergraduate, graduate, professional programs, two-year terminal certificate programs, and private career schools. Awards can be held for up to four years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester) or seven years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester) or a combination of both.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are eligible military or public safety employees, veterans with 25% or greater service-connected disability, eligible dependents, qualifying family members and spouses of United States Armed Forces individuals who died as a result of military service or who suffered a service-connected disability, prisoners of war or missing in action from Vietnam conflict, survivors and dependents of September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victims, children and surviving spouses of public safety employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty, children and surviving spouses of school employees who died or were 100% disabled as a result of an act of violence in the line of duty, at least 16 years old, enrolled at least half-time or part-time in undergraduate, graduate, professional, or career school programs at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions, including undergraduate, graduate, professional programs, two-year terminal certificate programs, and private career schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents at the time of application, with exceptions for children, stepchildren, or surviving spouses of state or local public safety employees killed in the line of duty, disabled public safety employees and their dependents or surviving spouses, and school employee family members regardless of residency. For prisoners of war/missing in action, applicant must have been a Maryland resident at the time of declaration.
requirements_list: Must be a family member of a United States Armed Forces individual who died as a result of military service or suffered a service-connected disability, or a veteran with 25% or greater service-connected disability, or an eligible dependent, or a public safety employee/volunteer who became 100% disabled in the line of duty, or a son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a school employee who died or was 100% disabled as a result of an act of violence in the line of duty, or a prisoner of war or missing in action from Vietnam conflict, or a child, stepchild, or surviving spouse of a September 11, 2001 terrorist attack victim

Enrolled in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution (full-time or part-time) or in a 2-year terminal certificate program with acceptable transfer credit or in a private career school
At least 16 years old
Qualify under one of the specified military, public safety service, school employee, or terrorist attack victim conditions

Maryland resident at time of application (with specific exceptions for military, public safety employee families, disabled public safety employees, and school employee families); for POW/MIA status, must have been Maryland resident when declared
Full-time study requires 12+ credits per semester; part-time study requires 6-11 credits per semester
Veterans must have exhausted or no longer be eligible for federal veterans' educational benefits
Military service must have occurred after December 7, 1941 (or for Vietnam conflict POW/MIA, on or after January 1, 1960)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions. Applicants should apply through their institution by July 15 of each year. Students should not submit applications or supplemental documentation directly to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. All required documentation should be submitted directly to the institution. Institutions award eligible students and are reimbursed by the state. Initial awards are automatically renewed by the institution's financial aid office for the next academic year for up to four years full-time or seven years part-time.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative to reduce inequities in college completion by providing coaching, financial support, and other community resources to bolster access to higher education and build a more educated workforce. The program uses evidence-based advising models and comprehensive student supports designed to help improve college completion and economic mobility rates for students of color and students from low-income families at participating Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating institutions receive $125,000 in funding each to implement comprehensive student supports including coaching, advising, and financial support. The program provides data analytics to track student retention and degree completion, with ongoing support and training from Maryland Higher Education Commission and MDRC.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Donna Thomas, Crystal Smith, Paul Fields
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students pursuing postsecondary degrees or credentials at participating Maryland community colleges, particularly students of color and students from low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coaching, advising, financial support, and other community resources to support student success and completion of postsecondary degrees or credentials.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is implemented at three Maryland community colleges: Baltimore City Community College, Prince George's Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College. Participating institutions were identified based on student population composition and the commission's commitment to serving community colleges statewide.
requirements_list: Enroll at one of the three participating community colleges
Program eligibility requirements vary by college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the participating community college directly for information on enrollment and program eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A college access program established by the Maryland General Assembly in 2016 that supports low-income, first-generation students in high poverty school systems by providing cohort-based mentoring, guidance, and college preparation services. Students are identified as early as 7th grade and receive support through high school graduation and into their first year of college. The program provides cohort-based support, mentoring, and college guidance to help students pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant and transition to postsecondary education. Required program components include high school graduation planning, summer work/internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career and interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, college campus and workplace visits, intensive summer bridge programs, student outreach and registration, and matriculation support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY 2026 grant funding totaling $5,000,000 is provided to nonprofit organizations that were awarded grants in FY 2025 to continue providing college access services and support to cohort students in eligible school systems. An estimated 11-15 grants will be awarded with a grant period of July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026. Grant funds support college access programs that provide mentoring, guidance, and services to help students pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant and transition to and succeed in college. Eligible uses include salaries and wages, fringe benefits, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, contracted services, evaluation and data collection, indirect costs (max 8%), and other MHEC-approved costs. Ineligible uses include capital improvements, gift cards, and costs incurred prior to grant approval. Funds cannot supplant existing program funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status serving low-income, first-generation students in grades 7-12 in one or more of the eight eligible school systems: Allegany County Public Schools, Baltimore City Public Schools, Caroline County Public Schools, Dorchester County Public Schools, Kent County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, Somerset County Public Schools, or Wicomico County Public Schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support college access programs including salaries and wages, fringe benefits, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, contracted services, evaluation and data collection, indirect costs (maximum 8%), and other MHEC-approved program costs. Ineligible uses include capital improvements, gift cards, and costs incurred prior to grant approval. Funds cannot supplant existing program funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This continuation grant funding is available only to nonprofit organizations that were awarded grants under the Next Generation Scholars Program in FY 2025 and support students in one or more of the eight eligible school systems: Allegany County Public Schools, Baltimore City Public Schools, Caroline County Public Schools, Dorchester County Public Schools, Kent County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, Somerset County Public Schools, or Wicomico County Public Schools.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) status that received Next Generation Scholars Program funding in FY 2025
Must support grades 7-12 students in one or more of the eight eligible school systems
Must provide cohort-based support model with mentoring and college guidance
Must serve students who pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant

Must not supplant existing funds

Must maintain records for 5 years and provide access for audit purposes
Must ensure equitable access and participation per GEPA Section 427
