Must submit amendment requests at least 45 days before grant period ends
Must submit final invoices no later than 60 days after grant period ends
For significant project changes (timeline, activities, key staff, budget >$1,000 or 10% of line item): must obtain prior written approval
Project extension requests must be made at least one month prior to expiration date
Budget changes greater than $1,000 or 10% of originally approved line item require explanation and revised budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grant applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025 via email to Tiffany.Majors1@Maryland.gov with subject line 'NGS FY26 Submission'. Complete the electronic application form, save as PDF, obtain required signatures, and email to the contact. Applications must include the completed FY 2026 application form, detailed plan of operation, risk management plan, evaluation plan, budget narrative, key personnel resumes with % FTE, and all required compliance documentation. The MHEC Review Committee will evaluate applications July 2-9, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship program honors fallen transportation workers and provides tuition assistance to students who are dependents or surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers. Eligible students can attend undergraduate, graduate, professional, or certificate programs at accredited institutions, including 2-year terminal certificate programs and private career schools. Scholarship awards range from a minimum of $3,000 or the lesser of actual tuition and mandatory fees, up to the maximum equivalent to the highest annual tuition and mandatory fees for full-time resident undergraduates at University System of Maryland 4-year public institutions (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus and University of Maryland Baltimore). Awards can be held for five years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester for undergraduate; 9+ credits per semester for graduate) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester for undergraduate; 6-8 credits per semester for graduate), or a combination of both.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Merit-based tuition assistance scholarship. Scholarship awards range from a minimum of $3,000 or the lesser of actual annual tuition and mandatory fees at the institution attended, up to the maximum equivalent to the highest annual tuition and mandatory fees for full-time resident undergraduates at University System of Maryland 4-year public institutions (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus and University of Maryland Baltimore). Awards can be held for five years of full-time study (12+ credits per semester for undergraduate; 9+ credits per semester for graduate) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester for undergraduate; 6-8 credits per semester for graduate), or a combination of both.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at eligible institutions for educational expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to students attending eligible institutions in Maryland. Fallen transportation worker must have died as a result of a work-related accident while performing job duties in Maryland in the construction, rehabilitation, or operation of a transportation facility or project.

Applicant is a dependent child or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of the fallen worker
Must be at least 16 years old

Initial awards are automatically renewed by the institution's financial aid office for the next academic year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs (GEAR UP) Scholarships
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides financial aid to support postsecondary education preparation and college access for eligible students who participated in GEAR UP activities during the grant period (2014-2020). The program supports both individual students pursuing undergraduate education and community partners including institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations. Awards to students are made after federal Pell Grants, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. Maximum scholarship awards are $15,000 for fall and spring of the 2023-2024 academic year and $10,000 for summer 2023.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The maximum GEAR UP Scholarship award is $15,000 for the fall and spring of the 2023-2024 academic year and $10,000 for summer 2023. The award amount varies depending on the student's financial need but does not exceed the cost of attendance. Awards are processed and made after the drop/add period at the institution. Scholarships also support postsecondary education preparation and college access through awards to eligible institutions and partner organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 each year for FAFSA; July 1, 2023 for Summer 2023 GEAR UP Scholarship Application; applications accepted on a rolling basis for institutional partners
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020) and are pursuing undergraduate education, as well as community partners including public and private institutions of higher education and nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Undergraduate education at accredited two- or four-year institutions of higher education, private career schools, or state/regional accredited trade schools/certificate programs. Postsecondary education preparation and college access initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must have participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020). Students must be Maryland residents according to their institution's state residency policy. Institutional partners must be located in eligible Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Have participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020)
Be a Maryland resident according to the institution's state residency policy

Be enrolled or accepted for enrollment in a program of undergraduate instruction at an accredited two- or four-year institution of higher education, private career school, or state/regional accredited trade school/certificate program
Have received a high school diploma or its recognized equivalent
Be less than 22 years old at the time of the first scholarship award
Maintain satisfactory academic progress in accordance with the standards of the institution
Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and GEAR UP Scholarship Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students must complete the FAFSA at www.fafsa.gov before March 1 each year and submit the GEAR UP Scholarship Application. Applications are processed and verified following the drop/add period at the institution. Awards are made after federal Pell Grants, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. If eligible, students are notified via the email listed on the application. Institutional partners submit applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund for Maryland Community Colleges
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provided emergency assistance to support education opportunities and workforce development programs at Maryland's 16 community colleges during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program distributed $10 million in total grant awards to Maryland's community colleges, with individual college allocations ranging from $250,000 to $1,480,602 during the grant period of July 1, 2020 to December 30, 2021. Funds supported workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure, with a focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $10,000,000 distributed among Maryland's 16 community colleges to fund workforce development courses and continuing professional education programs. Individual colleges received allocations ranging from $250,000 to $1,480,602 during the grant period of July 1, 2020 to December 30, 2021. Funds can be used for direct aid to students, materials and supplies, equipment, curriculum development, salaries and wages, professional development and technical training, student recruitment and marketing, technology training, certification, examination and licensure fees or vouchers for programs leading to government or industry certification or licensure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges and individuals impacted by COVID-19 through employment loss, particularly those seeking workforce development and professional certification or licensure training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct aid to students, materials and supplies, equipment, curriculum development, salaries and wages, professional development and technical training, student recruitment and marketing, technology training, certification, examination and licensure fees or vouchers for workforce development courses and continuing professional education programs leading to government or industry certification or licensure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all 16 Maryland community colleges are eligible.

Programs must lead to government or industry certification or licensure
Primarily focused on individuals impacted by COVID-19 pandemic through loss of employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funds were allocated directly to Maryland community colleges by the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Grants Management. Detailed application procedures for individuals seeking training through their community college are available through their respective institutions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief Fund II (GEER II)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal emergency relief program funded through the U.S. Department of Education's Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act that provides supplemental grants to support local education agencies, institutions of higher education, and other educational entities with emergency assistance due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In Maryland, Governor Hogan allocated $10 million to community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities. Community colleges received $7.4 million to provide workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, particularly for individuals impacted by COVID-19 through job loss. Private nonprofit colleges and universities received $2.6 million to support institutional costs resulting from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supplemental grants totaling $10 million distributed to Maryland's 16 community colleges ($7.4 million total) and private nonprofit colleges and universities ($2.6 million total). Community colleges provide workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, with focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment. Private nonprofit institutions use funding to support institutional costs resulting from COVID-19. Individual award amounts are distributed by institution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges, private nonprofit colleges and universities, and individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses, continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, and institutional costs resulting from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland community colleges and eligible private nonprofit institutions of higher education.

Awards range from $1,000 to $5,000 per year based on demonstrated financial need, with students eligible to receive awards for a maximum of eight semesters while maintaining satisfactory academic progress and continuing to demonstrate financial need.

Students may receive awards for a maximum of eight semesters if they maintain enrollment in an eligible program, meet satisfactory academic progress standards, demonstrate continued financial need, and file a FAFSA each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant (CBEAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, need-based financial aid program designed to assist full-time undergraduate students who did not file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) by the Maryland state deadline of March 1st, making them ineligible for the standard Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant. The state allocates funds to participating institutions each academic year to select and award qualified students. Awards are based on adjusted financial need, with students at four-year institutions receiving 40 percent and community college students receiving 60 percent of OSFA adjusted financial need. The minimum annual award is $400 and the maximum award is $3,000, with total state awards not exceeding cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students attending four-year institutions receive a grant equal to 40 percent of OSFA adjusted financial need. Students attending community colleges receive a grant equal to 60 percent of OSFA adjusted financial need. The minimum annual award is $400 and the maximum award is $3,000. Total state awards may not exceed cost of attendance as determined by the school's financial aid office or $28,000, whichever is less. Need-based financial aid award allocated to participating institutions each academic year for qualified students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st (or after missing the March 1st FAFSA/MSFAA deadline)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students who are Maryland residents and did not file FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application by the state deadline.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses and undergraduate education costs at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Applicants must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university. Available at participating institutions in Maryland.
requirements_list: Full-time degree-seeking undergraduate student (12+ credits per semester)
Maryland resident (applicant and parents if dependent)
Filed FAFSA after the March 1st deadline or by the June 1st state deadline
Eligible to receive the federal Pell Grant
Audited courses cannot be used to meet full-time credit hour requirements
Did not file FAFSA or MHEC One App by March 1 deadline
Enrolled at a two-year or four-year Maryland institution
File FAFSA or MSFAA by March 2 or later
Did not file FAFSA by Maryland state deadline of March 1st
Meets need-based financial aid criteria
Attends a participating institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact their college's financial aid office to apply. Financial aid offices at participating institutions review applications and select qualified students for CBEAG awards. Contact the Office of Student Financial Assistance for additional application information. Institutions select and award qualified students from allocated funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Award
structured_extraction.program_description: Financial aid award provided to eligible students for higher education in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards provided to students for the 2024-2025 academic year. As of May 31, 2024, over 6,301 students have been awarded a total of $67,737,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students and families seeking financial aid for college and community college.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College and community college education expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
Must meet eligibility criteria for the specific grant program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students must complete the FAFSA. Eligible applicants who complete the FAFSA by the May 15 priority deadline will be guaranteed to be awarded. MHEC processes applications on a weekly basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funding to Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers to support efforts to address food insecurity among students on Maryland campuses. The program addresses student hunger and food insecurity, leverages sustainable solutions to address basic food needs on campus, raises awareness of services addressing basic food needs, and builds strategic partnerships to address food insecurity among students. MHEC awards grant funding to eligible institutions that have been designated as a hunger-free campus and pledge a 25% matching contribution. FY 2026 awards total $150,000 distributed among eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHEC awards grant funding to Maryland public institutions of higher education or regional higher education centers that have been designated as a hunger-free campus and pledge a 25% matching contribution (in-kind or matching funds). FY 2026 total awards: $150,000. Grant funds may support emergency assistance, hiring staff to manage hunger-related initiatives, operational activities, and flexible use to implement program goals including salaries & wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs (capped at 8% of total direct costs). Funds are dispersed at the beginning of the grant period upon award and must supplement, not supplant existing programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College and university students experiencing food insecurity; Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers designated as hunger-free campuses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support efforts to address food insecurity among students on Maryland campuses, including addressing student hunger, leveraging sustainable solutions to address basic food needs on campus, raising awareness of services that address basic food needs, and building strategic partnerships to address food insecurity among students. Eligible expenditures include: salaries & wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant/contractual services, campus hunger task force support, SNAP enrollment staff, campus food pantry operations, meal plan donation programs, student hunger surveys, and other approved implementation costs. Indirect costs permitted up to 8% of total direct costs. Funds cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers. Priority given to communities with highest rates of concentrated child poverty in each county, particularly those eligible under Governor's ENOUGH Grant Program.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland public institution of higher education or regional higher education center
Must be designated as a hunger-free campus
Must establish hunger task force meeting at least 3 times per year
Must pledge a 25% matching contribution (in-kind or matching funds) to be used to implement the goals of the program
Must comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act of 1964
Must comply with Americans with Disabilities Act
Must participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs
Must maintain records for 5 years after grant completion
Must submit interim and final reports
Must obtain prior written approval for scope changes
Must acknowledge MHEC support in publications and include required disclaimer in materials
Indirect costs capped at 8% of direct costs
Budget must include Key Personnel (list each by name with title in brackets)
Institution name required
Designated staff member for SNAP enrollment assistance required
Designated staff member for SNAP eligibility information required
Must have UEI Number
Budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10% in any category require prior written approval
Authorized official at President, Vice President level or above must sign Statement of Assurances
Legal authority to apply via governing body authorization
Provide access to records for MHEC and Office of Legislative Audits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions submit applications by the stated deadline. Applicants must complete and submit: cover sheet with institutional information and UEI number, budget summary detailing grant funds requested and institutional/other contributions with cost categories, statement of assurances, and grant proposal/narrative detailing project plans. Certification by authorizing official at Vice President level or above required. Budget narrative with detailed cost justifications by category required. The grant period runs from October 15 through June 30.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inmate Training and Job Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Pilot programs at eligible institutions of higher education providing educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in the twelve months preceding release from incarceration. The program targets inmates in the twelve months preceding their release from incarceration and aims to expand and improve higher education pathways for incarcerated individuals. Includes credit-bearing coursework that contributes to graduation requirements or leads to industry-recognized certificates or licenses, support services, individualized planning, and mentorship. Grant period runs from August 2025 through June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants provided to eligible institutions of higher education to establish pilot programs offering educational and vocational training for inmates in the twelve months preceding their release from incarceration. Implementation grants: up to $25,000 for six (6) month implementation period. Continuation grants: awarded on pro-rata basis according to pilot program enrollment data. Allowable uses include: salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, and indirect costs (up to 8% maximum). NOT allowed: supplanting existing services, capital improvements. Final grant awards subject to availability of state funds. Grant period runs from August 2025 through June 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible institutions of higher education that provide educational and vocational training to inmates in Maryland correctional institutions. Specifically limited to four designated institutions: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Target beneficiaries are inmates incarcerated at Maryland correctional institutions in the twelve months preceding release.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, indirect costs (up to 8% maximum), and other costs as specified. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot be used to supplant non-grant funds. Unallowable costs include supplanting existing services and capital improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program administered by Maryland Higher Education Commission through four eligible institutions: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Programs operate at 15 DPSCS correctional institutions across Maryland located in Westover, Jessup, Baltimore, Sykesville, Hagerstown, and Cumberland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible institution of higher education
Must be one of the four designated institutions: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
Program must target inmates in the twelve months preceding release from incarceration
Institution must provide educational and vocational training opportunities including credit-bearing coursework or industry-recognized certificates/licenses
Possess legal authority to apply for the grant
Comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Comply with Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
Participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs as required by MHEC
Use funds to supplement, not supplant existing programs
Proposal must be submitted by July 25, 2025 at 4:00 PM
Proposal narrative (70% of scoring weight)
Budget and budget narrative (20% of scoring weight)
Overall approach and feasibility (10% of scoring weight)
Maintain all records pertaining to grant for 5 years
Comply with all MHEC requirements concerning special requirements of law and administrative requirements
Grant records subject to access by Office of Legislative Audits
VP-level or above certification/authorization required
Final grant awards subject to availability of state funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions submit proposals in response to the Request for Proposal (RFP). Submit completed cover sheet with institution information, program director details, and 250-300 word abstract. The RFP document and appendices provide detailed application instructions and requirements. Application process involves submission of proposal narrative, budget and budget narrative via Appendix B, documentation of overall approach and feasibility, and Statement of Assurances (Appendix C). Submission to Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Outreach and Grants Management. Application requires signature from authorized official (President, VP level, or above).

structured_extraction.program_name: Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to full-time students attending approved private career schools in Maryland. Grants up to $500 per award year may be renewed once if the applicant continues enrollment and meets eligibility requirements. Applicants must file the FAFSA and submit an application through their school's financial aid office. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $500 per award year. The award may be renewed once if the applicant continues enrollment and meets eligibility requirements. Financial assistance is provided to full-time students enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week at approved Maryland private career schools.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA by March 1 preferred; June 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time students enrolled at approved Maryland private career schools who are Maryland residents, enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for tuition and educational expenses at approved private career schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents, or if dependent students, their parent must be a Maryland resident. Students must attend approved private career schools in Maryland.
requirements_list: Enrolled full-time at an approved Maryland private career school
Enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week
Maryland resident (if dependent, parent must be Maryland resident)
All majors eligible
Completed Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)
Submitted Tolbert Grant Program application at financial aid office of private career school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit required materials to the financial aid office at their private career school. They must complete and file the FAFSA by March 1 (preferred) and submit an application for the Tolbert Grant Program at their school's financial aid office. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Contact the Office of Student Financial Assistance or your institution's financial aid office for application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides financial assistance to help individuals repay their educational loans when they work in eligible public service fields and serve Maryland's low-income or underserved residents. Recipients receive annual loan repayment assistance based on total educational debt tier, with awards locked in for three years and yearly payments ranging from $1,500 to $10,000 depending on debt level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients receive annual loan repayment assistance based on total educational debt tier. Awards are locked in for three years with yearly payments ranging from $1,500 to $10,000 depending on debt level ($15,000 or below receives $1,500 yearly; $15,001–$40,000 receives $3,000 yearly; $40,001–$75,000 receives $6,000 yearly; $75,001 and over receives $10,000 yearly). Overall award limits are $4,500, $9,000, $18,000, and $30,000 respectively. Payment amounts cannot exceed total remaining debt. Payments are made annually as long as recipients remain eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for 2025-2026 application cycle; October 15, 2026 for 2026-2027 application cycle; October 1 deadline for subsequent cycles
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals employed in eligible public service fields who graduated from a Maryland institution and are serving Maryland's low-income or underserved residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans for individuals in eligible employment fields.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed full-time in the state of Maryland. Must have graduated from a Maryland institution, except lawyers and teachers (who must have a Maryland resident teacher certificate). Licensed Clinical Counselors must work in high need geographic areas.

Must have graduated from a Maryland institution (except lawyers; teachers must have a resident teacher certificate from MSDE if not from a Maryland institution)
Must be employed full-time in Maryland
Educational loans cannot be Parent PLUS loans
Loans cannot be in default
Income must not exceed $75,000 for single applicants or $150,000 for married applicants (except Nurse Faculty: $100,000 single/$185,000 married)
For married applicants, personal income cannot exceed single max and combined income cannot exceed married max
Must remain in eligible employment field throughout award cycle
Must submit prior year Federal or State income tax return
Must provide employment verification
Must provide lender verification
Must provide institutional certification or official transcript
Complete Janet L. Hoffman LARP application
Submit required documentation by deadline
Cannot have active state service obligations from other Maryland scholarships
Teachers must have highest performance evaluation
Must maintain employment during award duration
Must complete Mid-Year Employment Verification within 21 days
Must submit W-9 form and address documentation within 21 days
Must submit proof of lender payment within 120 days of receiving award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. All required documents must be submitted online through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing deadline. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid scholarship available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. Eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer and must accept or decline their award online within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid scholarship for qualified children of undocumented immigrants. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants will be notified by email if they are awarded. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 for Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant; varies by state scholarship program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undocumented students, DACA students, qualified children of undocumented immigrants, and students ineligible for federal FAFSA who are eligible for in-state tuition at Maryland institutions and attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State financial aid grants and scholarships for college education and education-related expenses at eligible Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents who filed state income tax returns for required periods and attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.

Must qualify for in-state tuition under MD Education Article §15–106.8
Must attend an eligible Maryland institution
Prior-prior-year tax filing required (applicant and/or parents must file taxes)

Eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer if awarded. Students must accept or decline their award online within 2 weeks of notification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Multiple loan assistance repayment programs administered by MHEC that provide financial assistance to graduates working in specific occupations and sectors, including those providing public service and serving Maryland's underserved residents. Programs are available for lawyers, nurses, nurse faculty, licensed clinical counselors, physical and occupational therapists, social workers, speech pathologists, teachers, public defenders, prosecutors, dentists, and foster care recipients. Eligible graduates can receive up to $30,000 toward their student loan debt repayment depending on the specific program and employment field.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance toward student loan repayment for eligible graduates. Eligible graduates can receive up to $30,000 toward their student loan debt repayment depending on the specific program and employment field.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland graduates employed in designated professions and sectors who have education loans from institutions of higher education, including lawyers, nurses, nurse faculty, licensed clinical counselors, physical and occupational therapists, social workers, speech pathologists, teachers, public defenders, and prosecutors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans for graduates in specified occupations and public service roles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to graduates employed in Maryland in designated occupations and sectors serving Maryland's underserved residents.
requirements_list: Must have received an undergraduate or graduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education
Must be employed in eligible occupation or sector
For some programs: must be employed by the state or by a county or municipality in Maryland
Service to Maryland's underserved residents in some programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should review various LARP programs available on MHEC website.

structured_extraction.program_name: MHEC One App for Undocumented Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial aid application specifically designed for qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland law. Through this unified application, eligible applicants can apply for various Maryland State financial aid grants and scholarships including Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, Legislative Scholarship Program, and Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants can apply for various Maryland State financial aid programs including: Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, Legislative Scholarship Program, and Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship. Applications are completed online through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS). Award notifications occur in late April for some programs and summer for others.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; check individual program deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident exemption requirements under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State financial aid for higher education; specific uses determined by individual grant or scholarship programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; eligible applicants must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution and meet the non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article.

Must meet non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article

Dependent students under age 24 must provide parental information
No Social Security Number required

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students complete the MHEC One App online through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS). The application opens at the same time as the FAFSA each year. Provide required information including parental details if dependent status applies. After submission, MHEC reviews applications and notifies applicants of awards; Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant notifications come in late April, other awards in summer. Students must accept or decline awards within 2 weeks through their MDCAPS portal account; failure to respond within 2 weeks results in award cancellation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered registered apprenticeship program offering paid on-the-job training coupled with related classroom instruction in skilled trades, particularly electrical and HVAC industries. The program follows an 'earn and learn' model providing one-on-one full-time training from skilled craftspeople with progressive wage increases. The program supports both individuals seeking apprenticeship opportunities and businesses/apprenticeship providers committed to creating new apprenticeship opportunities to meet their workforce needs. Employers receive tax credits and financial incentives to develop and train workers, supporting employee succession planning and knowledge transfer through mentorship. Supports apprenticeships and training opportunities for both individuals and employers across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid on-the-job training with related classroom instruction in skilled trades occupations paired with tax credits and financial incentives for employers. Support for creating new apprenticeship opportunities and training programs. Progressive wage structure with classes beginning as soon as January. Credit may be granted for prior instruction received at Brightwood College. The program helps employers grow their workforce while improving retention and return on investment, and supports employee succession planning and knowledge transfer through mentorship.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students, job seekers, businesses, employers, individuals interested in skilled trades (particularly electrical or HVAC), apprenticeship providers, and businesses seeking to develop and train workers through apprenticeship programs. Initially promoted to Brightwood College students displaced by institutional closure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training in skilled trades occupations combined with related classroom instruction to support apprenticeship and training programs. Apprenticeship program development and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide with registered apprenticeship sponsors located throughout Maryland. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Interest in skilled trades occupational training
Ability to work with registered apprenticeship sponsors with immediate hiring needs
May benefit from credit for prior instruction at Brightwood College
Applicant must be business or apprenticeship provider
Must be committed to creating apprenticeship opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students interested in learning more should contact the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program at info@mdapprenticeship.com. Contact Maryland Department of Labor or Caroline County Economic Development office for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid scholarship available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants (including DACA students) who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. The program provides financial aid for community college attendance, with awards notified by email in the summer and requiring acceptance within 2 weeks of notification through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid scholarship for qualified children of undocumented immigrants attending Maryland community colleges. Eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer. Award must be accepted online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Established deadline for the state scholarship program(s); see program guidelines

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland community colleges; must qualify for Maryland in-state tuition under §15–106.8 of the MD Education Article.

Must be ineligible for federal aid (FAFSA)
Must attend an eligible Maryland community college
Prior-prior-year tax filing required (applicant and/or parents must file taxes)
Males ages 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
Dependent students must provide parental information
Must complete MSFAA (Maryland State Financial Aid Application)
Must apply through MHEC One App via Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS)
Must meet established application deadline

Dependent students must have parents submit a signed Parent Signature Page. Eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer if awarded.
