structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Leadership Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A six-year federal grant program that supports Maryland's GEAR UP goals to increase the number of economically disadvantaged and low-income students who intend to pursue postsecondary education. Provides summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming to secondary GEAR UP students through leadership curricula, plans, and activities designed to prepare students for college and career readiness. Helps students understand their core values, leadership skills, strengths, and goal-setting through self-discovery, career exploration projects, comprehensive mentoring, and leadership workshops. Educates students and their families about the advantages of postsecondary education, college financing options, and financial aid. Focuses on English/Language Arts and mathematics to help students apply and enroll in college, obtain financial aid, and complete postsecondary education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Institutions of higher education may request up to $45,000 for funded activities. Awards are provided as grants to Maryland two-and four-year higher education institutions that partner with local education agencies. In 2018, awards ranged from approximately $43,000 to $44,500. Grant period is from June 15, 2018 to August 15, 2019. The program operates on annual funding cycles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or not-for-profit independent two-year or four-year institutions of higher education that partner with Local Education Agencies to serve economically disadvantaged and low-income secondary students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming for secondary GEAR UP students, including support for leadership curricula, plans, and activities, application workshops, counseling, advising, career counseling, comprehensive mentoring, self-discovery and career exploration workshops, project leadership and management, ideation and innovation sessions, communication effectiveness workshops, and cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service regions include Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County. The program operates in these eligible counties.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited Maryland public or not-for-profit independent two-year or four-year institution of higher education
Must partner with a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must select and fund required activities
Must include a completed and signed Cooperative Agreement by the submission deadline
May request up to $45,000 in the proposal
Must serve low-income and underrepresented students
Must focus on college and career readiness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application from http://www.mhec.maryland.gov/institutions_training/Pages/GEARUP.aspx. Submit both electronic and hard copies of the proposal by May 7, 2018 at 4:00 p.m. to Kendall E. Cook at the Office of Outreach and Grants Management, Maryland Higher Education Commission, 6 N. Liberty Street, 10th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21201, via email or mail. The program operates on annual funding cycles.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program centered on career exploration and educational planning to promote self-efficacy, advance leadership curricula, connect youth to professional sectors, and build transferable skills required to secure and sustain employment. The program trains students to understand their core values, sharpen soft skills, set achievable goals, and develop interests and leadership capacities through career and job exploration. It includes in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment opportunities while educating students and families about postsecondary education and college financing options. The program focuses on communication, collaboration, teamwork, and self-advocacy skills development for economically disadvantaged and low-income students. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Education under Title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965 as part of Maryland's $13.2 million GEAR UP grant (2014-2020).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and training awards to accredited public or non-profit independent two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with local education agencies to provide in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment opportunities for economically disadvantaged students. Funded programs deliver skills-development activities focused on communication, collaboration, teamwork, self-advocacy, job exploration, experiential learning, and workplace readiness. Grantees required to provide 25% in-kind match. Indirect costs cannot exceed 8% of funds requested. Up to $80,000 per institution with five or more awards anticipated. Grant funds are disbursed in two 50% payments, with the second payment contingent on interim report approval. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs; cannot supplant non-grant funds. Example awards: Johns Hopkins University received $80,000 and Wor-Wic Community College received $28,372 for the 2019 funding cycle. Institutions submit proposals in response to the Request for Proposal (RFP) process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Economically disadvantaged and low-income students, first-generation students, and GEAR UP cohort students in Maryland GEAR UP school districts at high-poverty middle and high schools in Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties who are considering postsecondary education and seeking college and career readiness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-school and virtual soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration and job counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, youth employment opportunities, educational outreach about postsecondary education and college financing, salaries and wages for professional and support personnel, fringe benefits, travel expenses (in-state only), materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, equipment, and programs focused on communication, collaboration, teamwork, self-advocacy, job exploration, and experiential learning. Funds must supplement new and/or existing programs and cannot supplant non-grant funds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland GEAR UP school districts: Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties. Out-of-state travel for conferences not permitted except for Maryland and District of Columbia metro area.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited public or not-for-profit independent two- or four-year institution of higher education
Must partner with a local education agency
Focus on serving low-income and underrepresented students
Provide 25% matching contribution (cash and/or in-kind)
Lead applicant must have legal authority to apply; governing body authorization required
Comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Comply with federal/state anti-discrimination laws, ADA, FERPA, Pro-Children Act
Execute formalized agreements with LEAs and collaborative partners
Participate in statewide assessment/evaluation programs
Grant access to records for MHEC and Legislative Auditor review
Comply with all MHEC special requirements and administrative requirements
Submit cooperative planning agreement signed by required partners: College/University, School District Superintendent/CEO, LEA GEAR UP Coordinator, High School Principal
Maintain records retention for 3 years after grant ends
Submit quarterly Time & Effort reports
Submit interim report by April 6, 2020
Submit final report by January 15, 2021
Participate in minimum one site visit by MHEC
Submit project evaluation plan with pre- and post-assessments
Budget compliance with RFP guidelines
Acknowledge MHEC support in publications
Prior written approval required for scope and budget changes
Prior approval required for project director replacement or key personnel changes
Prior approval required for budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Two- and four-year Maryland higher education institutions apply in partnership with Local Education Authorities (LEAs) for the grant. Institutions submit proposals in response to the Request for Proposal (RFP) process. Required documents include plan of operation with short narrative and table for each activity with objectives and outcomes, assurances and cooperative planning agreement signed by all required partners (College/University applicant, authorized School District Superintendent/CEO, LEA GEAR UP Coordinator, High School Principal), detailed budget summary forms documenting grant funds, institution contributions (cash and in-kind), and other partner contributions, project evaluation plan with pre- and post-assessments, and demonstration of matching funds. Budget categories must itemize salaries and wages, fringe benefits, travel, materials and supplies, consultant and contractual services, equipment, and other program-related expenses. Each partner must sign and date commitment forms and provide summaries of services and responsibilities to be provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Higher Education Outreach and College Access Program (MD-HEOCAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funds to eligible nonprofit organizations to increase college and career awareness and college completion for low-income Maryland high school students. Nonprofit organizations receive funds to carry out statewide outreach efforts that support and encourage low-income Maryland high school students to attend and complete college. The program creates matching funds for nonprofit organizations to expand their outreach efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 for twelve (12) month grant period to support outreach efforts encouraging low-income Maryland high school students to attend and complete college. Funds support personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, consultant and contractual services. Indirect costs capped at 8% of total direct costs. All costs must be directly related to project activities and services. Grants are disbursed in two payments: 50% upon award, remaining 50% upon approval of interim report.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland high school students and nonprofit organizations that provide college access services and support to these students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, consultant and contractual services. Indirect costs up to 8% of total direct costs. All costs must be directly related to project activities and services. Funds must supplement (not supplant) existing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves low-income high school students throughout Maryland. All Maryland counties eligible, with priority given to communities with highest rates of concentrated child poverty or communities eligible under Governor's Office for Children ENOUGH Grant Program. Eligible nonprofit organizations must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must have been in existence for five or more consecutive years
Must be located in Maryland
Must have established partnership(s) with a local school system and/or higher education institution
Must provide college access activities, communication, and services with a proven track record of success
Must offer services to enhance and increase college access and completion for low-income Maryland high school students
One-to-one matching funds required (dollar-for-dollar match)
Must comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act of 1964
Must comply with Americans with Disabilities Act
Proposal must pass initial formatting and completeness review
Participation in statewide assessment/evaluation programs required
Must maintain records for 5 years post-completion
Must submit interim and final reports
Must acknowledge MHEC support in publications
Must obtain prior written approval for scope changes, project director changes, budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10%, and grant extensions
Funds must supplement (not supplant) existing programs
Applicant must possess legal authority to apply for the grant
Must allow MHEC and Office of Legislative Audits access to all records
Authorized official signature required (President, VP level, or above)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit applications according to the Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Applications include a proposal narrative addressing needs assessment, organizational capacity, project goals/objectives/outcomes, operations planning, management, evaluation, and budgeting. The RFP includes application forms, appendices with detailed requirements, and budget templates. Organizations must provide evidence of eligibility criteria and describe their proposed outreach activities. The FY 2026 project period runs from October 15, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Application deadline is Monday, October 6, 2025 at 4:00 PM.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland John R. Justice Grant Student Loan Repayment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides loan repayment assistance for state and federal Maryland public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys. Recipients must agree to remain employed in these roles for a minimum of three years and sign a service obligation agreement. The program assists with repayment of qualified education loans including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Eligible applicants include employees of the state of Maryland, units of local government, nonprofit organizations operating under contract with the state or units of local government, and federal defender attorneys.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan repayment assistance for qualified education loans including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans. Recipients receive direct payments made to loan holders on behalf of eligible beneficiaries, with a maximum of $10,000 per calendar year and an aggregate maximum of $60,000 lifetime. Recipients must sign a three-year service obligation agreement and agree to remain employed as a public defender or prosecutor for a minimum of three years. If the grant recipient fails to fulfill the three-year service obligation, the recipient must repay the full grant award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys, including employees of the state of Maryland, units of local government, nonprofit organizations operating under contract, and federal defender attorneys.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of qualified education loans including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans for individuals employed as prosecutors and public defenders. Funds are paid directly to loan holders, not to beneficiaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors employed in Maryland or by units of local government in Maryland, as well as employees of nonprofit organizations operating under contract with the state or units of local government, and federal defender attorneys employed in Maryland. Distribution by appellate court district with equal allocation per district.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. Citizen or eligible non-citizen
Must have an outstanding balance due on a qualified education loan (Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, consolidation loans, and Perkins loans)
Must be an attorney continually licensed to practice law in Maryland

Must be a full-time employee of the state of Maryland or unit of local government prosecuting criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, or providing legal representation to indigent persons in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, or employed with a nonprofit organization under contract providing such representation, or employed as a full-time federal defender attorney
Must not be in default on a federal guaranteed educational loan or owe a refund on any scholarship or grant program administered by MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance
Must sign a three-year service obligation agreement
Cannot use loan repayment assistance for Parent PLUS loans or certain consolidation loans used to repay parent loans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete an application during open application periods and sign a three-year service obligation agreement to receive the grant. Contact Priscilla Moore for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: State financial assistance to help repay educational loans owed by foster care recipients who are employed by the state, or by a county or municipality of the state, and who received a graduate or undergraduate degree from an institution of higher education in Maryland. Award amounts equal to the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000, with automatic annual renewal for up to three years if required documentation is submitted. The program provides up to $30,000 available toward student loan debt over the maximum three-year award period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award amount equal to the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000, with up to $30,000 available toward student loan debt over a maximum of three years. Awards are automatically renewed on an annual basis for up to a maximum of three years if annual employment, lender, and tax documentation is received by the deadline each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster care recipients who have been in out-of-home placement for at least 3 years and are employed by state, county, or local government, and have received a graduate or undergraduate degree from a Maryland higher education institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans used to pay college expenses from a university, government, or commercial source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents employed by the state, or by a county or municipality of the state who received a degree from a Maryland institution of higher education.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have been placed in out-of-home placement by the state or unit of a state government's department of social services for 3 years or more
Must have earned either an undergraduate or graduate degree from a college in Maryland
Must be employed at least part-time (20 hours per week) in State, county or local government
Must have educational loans from a university, government, or commercial source
May not be in default on a loan
Must have completed prior service obligations from other state scholarships before applying
One position cannot fulfill two service obligations simultaneously
History of foster care involvement
Must sign employment obligation agreement for 1 year post-award
Must remain drug-free
Proof of foster care placement (court order from local department of social services)
Must provide signed Maryland state income tax return or alternative documentation (Federal return with notation, or IRS Letter 1077)
No current state service obligations from other Maryland scholarships
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit an online application and required documentation by the deadline. The online application and all required documents must be submitted to the Office of Student Financial Assistance. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants complete paper application from MHEC website, submit supplemental documentation via Google form, and upload documents to application or email to careerbased.mhec@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents
structured_extraction.program_description: A state assistance program that provides educational loan repayment assistance to police officers and probation agents working in Maryland law enforcement and parole and probation agencies. The program covers a portion of educational loan debt based on the applicant's annual salary level, with assistance available for up to three years if renewal requirements are met. For debt below $15,000, the program pays 10% of the debt. For debt between $15,000 and $40,000, it pays 20%. For debt between $40,000 and $75,000, it pays 30%. For debt over $75,000, it pays 40%.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program repays a percentage of educational loan debt based on annual salary. For debt below $15,000, the program pays 10% of the debt. For debt between $15,000 and $40,000, it pays 20%. For debt between $40,000 and $75,000, it pays 30%. For debt over $75,000, it pays 40%. The award amount cannot exceed the total debt. Recipients can receive renewal awards for up to three years if they continue to meet eligibility requirements. 3-year lock-in awards with potential 2-year renewal option available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year; October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Police officers and probation agents working in Maryland who hold educational degrees from Maryland public colleges or universities and have at least 2 years of employment in their field. Eligible police officers must work for eligible law enforcement agencies including state, county, municipal police departments, university police forces, community college police forces, housing authority police forces, school district police forces, and other designated enforcement agencies. Probation agents must work for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational loan repayment assistance for degrees in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice. The assistance can be applied toward the repayment of educational loans from graduate, professional, or undergraduate degrees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible individuals working as police officers or probation agents serving the state of Maryland. Applicants must have received their degree from a public college or university in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have received a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree from a public college or university in Maryland
Must be working as a police officer or probation agent for at least 2 years

Police officers must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws and work for one of the eligible law enforcement agencies including state police departments, municipal police departments, county police departments, university police forces, community college police forces, transit authority police, capitol police, sheriff's offices, housing authority police forces, school district police forces, fire marshal offices, fire and explosive investigator positions, Comptroller's Office Field Enforcement Bureau, or Alcohol and Tobacco Commission Field Enforcement Division
Probation agents must work as parole and probation agents, supervisors with a caseload, or regional administrators for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
Annual gross salary cannot exceed $85,000 for individuals or, if married, combined household salary cannot exceed $170,000
Must remain employed at an eligible law enforcement or corrections agency throughout the application cycle
Must submit verified employment, lender verification, tax documentation, and degree completion documentation by established deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit your online application through the MHEC One App in MDCAPS at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/ by the closing date. All required documents must be submitted online through your MDCAPS account, including your signed Maryland income tax return, employment verification form, lender verification form, and documentation of degree completion from a Maryland public college or university.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Police Officer and Probation Agent Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that awards funding to current police officers or probation agents, or individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents, who are enrolled in academic programs that further their career in law enforcement. Recipients must be enrolled full-time or part-time in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution and must pledge to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after completion of their studies. The scholarship covers 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at the eligible institution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual scholarship award equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at the eligible institution. Funding is provided to current police officers and probation agents or individuals planning to enter these professions to pursue undergraduate or graduate academic programs that further their law enforcement careers. Recipients must work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for no less than five years during the eight-year period after graduation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year; October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year. See Important Scholarship and Grant Deadlines page for additional information.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current police officers or probation agents, or individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents who are pursuing undergraduate or graduate academic programs at Maryland public senior institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for undergraduate or graduate programs that further a career in law enforcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents or individuals who graduated from a Maryland high school and are enrolled in undergraduate or graduate programs at Maryland public senior institutions.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or have graduated from a Maryland high school
Must be accepted for admission or currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time in a program that furthers career in law enforcement

Current police officers must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws and be members of specified law enforcement agencies including State Police, Baltimore City Police, county police departments, municipal police departments, transit and transportation police, university police forces, sheriff's offices, and other state/local law enforcement agencies
Probation agents must be serving as a parole and probation agent, supervisor, or regional administrator for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
Must pledge to work as a police officer or probation agent in the state upon completion of studies
Must sign a service obligation agreement to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation
Maintain 3.0 GPA or higher for renewal
Satisfactory academic progress for renewal
Remain drug-free during award term
Complete application through MHEC One App
Submit required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App by the established deadline. If applicable, submit documentation confirming current employment as a police officer. If graduated from a Maryland high school but not a Maryland resident, submit a copy of final high school transcript. Submit documentation from the institution confirming enrollment in a program that furthers career in law enforcement. Upon award, sign and return a promissory note and service obligation agreement. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Alternatively, apply through the institution's financial aid office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Teacher Quality and Diversity Competitive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants to teacher preparation programs at Maryland institutions of higher education and eligible non-profits to assist students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession in achieving teacher preparation and certification requirements. It supports the development of highly qualified teachers and leaders from diverse backgrounds, including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, students from low-income backgrounds, first-generation college students, and individuals with disabilities. The program also supports recruitment of subject matter experts into the teaching profession and encourages consortium applications. The program supports economic and workforce development through teacher quality and diversity initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive grants in two tracks: an Individual track with awards between $50,000–$150,000, and a Consortium track with awards between $250,000–$500,000. Annual funding totals $1,000,000. Funds support teacher quality and diversity initiatives as part of economic and workforce development. 100% of the total grant award is disbursed at the beginning of the project period. Indirect costs are allowed up to 8% of total direct costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland and eligible non-profits, with priority given to historically black colleges and universities and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers. Program serves students from groups historically underrepresented in teaching profession including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, low-income backgrounds, first-generation college students, individuals with disabilities, career changers, conditionally licensed teachers, federal workers transitioning into teaching, and male-identifying students, particularly boys and young men.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages of professional and support personnel directly involved in project; fringe benefits; travel for essential personnel; equipment (non-expendable items with greater than 1 year useful life); materials and supplies; development and administration of competency-based curricula and assessments; student success services such as academic advising and certification exam preparation; faculty or teacher mentor stipends; consultant and contractual services; evaluation-related costs; indirect costs (up to 8% of total direct costs). Funds must supplement, not supplant existing programs. NOT allowed: student financial aid grants, scholarships, or stipends.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves accredited institutions of higher education and eligible entities statewide in Maryland. Consortium applications (two or more institutions, or institution plus local education agency) are strongly encouraged.
requirements_list: Accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland
Priority given to historically black colleges and universities
Priority given to Hispanic-serving institutions with track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers
Proposals must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period
Program is not intended to supplant institutional investment
Comply with Title VI Civil Rights Act of 1964
Comply with Americans with Disabilities Act
Participate in statewide assessment and evaluation programs
Maintain records for 5 years
Obtain prior written approval for scope changes, project director changes, staff/consultant changes, or budget changes exceeding $1,000 or 10% in any category
Submit interim and final reports including financial and narrative reports
Acknowledge MHEC support in publications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions submit applications by email to MHEC by October 30, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Request for Proposals was issued September 25, 2025. Proposals must include all required forms and narrative sections including needs statement, goals, objectives, outcomes, operation plan, management plan, evaluation plan, partnerships, and budget summary with narrative. Proposals are scored by a panel of qualified reviewers. Full review panel convenes to discuss and make funding recommendations. Recommendations are submitted to Secretary of Higher Education for final decisions. Award notifications are made via email by November 28, 2025. Grant period runs from December 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, with interim report due March 31, 2026 and final report due August 31, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition waiver that exempts eligible foster care youth from paying tuition and mandatory fees at Maryland public colleges and universities. The waiver covers tuition, registration fees, and other mandatory fees required for enrollment in associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs. Eligible youth must enroll in school before age 25 and meet specific out-of-home placement criteria. The waiver applies to all academic majors, including both credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing vocational certificate programs, across all academic terms (fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters). The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible foster care recipients from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory fees required for enrollment) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters and does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Eligible youth receive full exemption from tuition and mandatory fees for enrollment in associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster care youth and former foster care youth under age 25 who are enrolled at a Maryland public college or university pursuing an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory fees) at Maryland public institutions of higher education for associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs. All academic majors are eligible, including both credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing vocational certificate programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at all Maryland public institutions of higher education to eligible applicants.
requirements_list: Must be under age 25
Must have been placed in an out-of-home placement by the Maryland Department of Human Services
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time for an associate, bachelor's, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education on or before reaching age 25

Must meet one of the following: (1) resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at time of high school graduation or GED completion; (2) resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at age 18; (3) resided in out-of-home placement on 13th birthday and was placed into guardianship or adopted after age 13; or (4) resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland for at least 1 year on or after 13th birthday and returned to live with parents after placement ended
Younger siblings of eligible foster care recipients are eligible if concurrently placed into guardianship or adopted by the same family
Have experience in foster care
File FAFSA
Contact financial aid office for application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution you are currently attending or plan to attend. You may also contact your local department of social services case worker or the Independent Living Coordinator. Eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App. Undocumented applicants should consult with the financial aid office at their institution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Unaccompanied Homeless Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to unaccompanied homeless youth who have been verified as homeless under the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act and are enrolled as candidates for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at Maryland public institutions of higher education. Eligible students are exempt from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and all fees required as a condition of enrollment for both credit-bearing and noncredit courses). The exemption covers tuition and fees but does not include room, board, books, or transportation. Students remain exempt for up to ten years after first enrolling or until they earn a bachelor's degree, whichever comes first. The waiver applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters and covers all academic majors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible students from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and all fees required as a condition of enrollment for both credit-bearing and noncredit courses) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The exemption covers tuition and mandatory fees but does not include room, board, books, or transportation. Students remain exempt for up to ten years after first enrolling or until they earn a bachelor's degree, whichever comes first. The waiver applies to fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters. Each institution determines its own tuition amount. Scholarships or grants cannot be applied to tuition since it is already waived.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MSFAA filing; contact your institution's financial aid office to apply
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unaccompanied homeless youth or youth at risk of homelessness who have been verified as homeless under the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act and are enrolled or planning to enroll at Maryland public institutions of higher education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, registration fees, and other mandatory fees for associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs at Maryland public institutions of higher education. All academic majors and both credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing vocational certificate programs are eligible. Funds can be used for credit-bearing and noncredit courses required as a condition of enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Youth must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records. Program is available at all Maryland public institutions of higher education statewide.
requirements_list: Must have been verified as a homeless child or youth as defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act
Verification must have occurred at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment or while enrolled in a Maryland public institution of higher education
Must have consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment documented by school, employment, or other records
Must be enrolled as a candidate for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education
Must be enrolled on or before reaching age 25
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time at a Maryland public institution of higher education
If receiving a scholarship or grant, that aid may not be applied to tuition for the waiver
Individuals should complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA)
Must complete and file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year
Eligible for fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students must reach out to the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution they are attending or planning to attend to apply. Students must complete and file the FAFSA at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the MSFAA via the MHEC One App at http://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/ each year to maintain eligibility. Undocumented applicants who do not qualify for the MHEC One App should consult with the financial aid office at the institution. Homeless status must be verified by a director or designee of an emergency or transitional shelter, street outreach program, homeless youth drop-in center, high school or school district homeless liaison, director or designee of a TRIO or GEAR UP program, or a financial aid administrator. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing monthly educational benefits to veterans, reservists, and active duty personnel for tuition and other educational expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly educational benefits provided to eligible veterans, reservists, and active duty personnel for tuition and educational costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans, reservists, and active duty military personnel
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide; serves Maryland residents through VA Regional Office, 31 Hopkins Plaza, Baltimore, MD 21201
requirements_list: Must be a veteran, reservist, or active duty military personnel
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the VA Regional Office or call 1-888-442-4551 for application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Naval ROTC Navy-Marine Corps Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship program providing tuition, laboratory fees, books, fees, and monthly compensation for eligible high school students in exchange for military service. Includes four-year active duty service obligation plus four-year reserve duty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition, laboratory fees, books, and fees provided plus $150 monthly compensation. Four-year active duty service obligation plus four-year reserve duty required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates ages 17 and up to age 27 at graduation and commissioning
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, books, and fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide; students may attend participating colleges of their choice
requirements_list: Must be a high school graduate
Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be at least age 17 when enrolled
Must not be over age 27 when graduated and commissioned
Must meet SAT or ACT requirements
Must pass high school academic review, interview, and physical aptitude exam
Must complete other processing requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Selection based on SAT or ACT scores, high school academic review, interview, physical aptitude exam, and other processing requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid grant available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. The grant supports students who are near completion of their college degree and do not have Social Security Numbers or are ineligible for federal FAFSA. Eligible applicants are notified by email in the summer and must accept or decline their award online within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid grant for qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are near completion of their college degree. Award notifications are sent by email in the summer. Students must accept their award online through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS) within 2 weeks of notification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; applicants should check the established deadline for the specific grant program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8, attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions, near completion of their degree, and who do not have Social Security Numbers or are ineligible for federal FAFSA. Includes DACA students and undocumented students ineligible for federal FAFSA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State need-based financial aid grants and scholarships for educational and college expenses at eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Maryland residents who filed Maryland income tax returns per specific requirements.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrant(s)
Must meet the non-resident exemption as described under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
Prior-prior-year tax filing required (applicant and/or parents must file taxes)
Males ages 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
Dependent students must provide parental information
Must apply through MHEC One App via Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS)
Must be ineligible for federal aid/FAFSA
File Maryland income tax returns for specified periods
Provide income information from two years prior to award year
Dependent or independent status determination required
Report household composition and number of family members in college
Select institution(s) and housing plan(s)
Information must be complete and accurate

structured_extraction.program_description: The New Nursing Faculty Fellowship provides funding to nursing faculty at Maryland universities and community colleges to increase the state's academic capacity to educate nurses and support the recruitment and retention of new nursing faculty. The program has been in operation since 2005. New recipients receive $20,000 over three years ($10,000 in the first year, then $5,000 in each of the two consecutive years). Previously awarded faculty receive continued annual disbursements of $5,000 based on continued full-time employment in good standing at a Maryland nursing program. The program supports nursing faculty development and retention to address the nursing shortage and improve the nursing education system in Maryland.

The program is funded by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) and administered by MHEC.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Nurse Support Program II (NSPII) is a statewide competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that increases Maryland's academic capacity to educate nurses by providing institutional grants and specialized support to nursing schools. The program addresses the state's nursing shortage through one-year planning grants, multi-year implementation grants, continuation grants, and nursing resource grants distributed to nursing programs across Maryland's 15 community colleges and 13 universities. It supports innovative initiatives to increase nursing enrollment, develop new educational programs (such as evening cohorts, master's programs, associate-to-bachelor's programs, advanced degree programs, and certificate programs), enhance faculty resources and development including PhD programs, create clinical education infrastructure and nurse-managed health centers, and prepare students for nursing licensure examinations. The program includes specialized fellowships and scholarships for nursing faculty and graduate students, including New Nurse Faculty Fellowships, Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF), and Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC). The program supports both undergraduate and graduate nursing education, faculty development, and leadership training across Maryland's nursing programs. Over five years beginning in FY2021, the program provides approximately $18 million per year to support nursing faculty development and increase educational capacity to prepare a strong nursing workforce for Maryland's hospitals and health systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An estimated $8.8 million will be available annually for ten years to fund strategies to increase nursing enrollments and improve nursing student retention. Up to $90 million in funding over five years (approximately $18 million per year beginning in FY2021). Competitive institutional grants for nursing programs, including one-year planning grants, multi-year implementation grants, continuation grants, and nursing resource grants distributed to nursing programs across Maryland's 28 institutions (15 community colleges and 13 universities). Award amounts vary based on the grant project's ability to impact the nursing shortage, the depth and breadth of the initiative, and feasibility of the budget. FY 2019 awards totaled $9.6 million distributed among 16 nursing programs. FY 2023 awards totaled $4,101,847 distributed among thirteen proposals at twelve institutions. FY24 award round distributed $5.8 million total to nine institutions (six universities and three community colleges). Two main components: (1) Competitive Institutional Grants Program providing grants to increase structural capacity of nursing schools through shared resources and innovative designs; (2) Statewide Initiatives including New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF) up to $20,000 distributed over three years, Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF) up to $26,000 for tuition/fees and $50,000 for living expenses, and Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC). Funding supports tuition, course release time, faculty development, nursing program expansion, new program development, clinical education infrastructure, exam software, testing materials, website expansion, accelerated program offerings, clinical simulation equipment and training, leadership development for nurse faculty and hospital educators, and student retention and graduation improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nursing schools and nursing programs at higher education institutions, including universities and community colleges, that prepare nurses for the workforce. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expand nursing enrollments and improve graduation rates; recruit and prepare nursing faculty; increase student retention; obtain clinical sites and facilities; expand classroom and lab facilities and equipment; provide scholarships and stipends; fund tutoring, mentoring, testing, remediation, and support services. Grants support initiatives to increase nursing enrollment and nursing graduates, develop new nursing education programs (such as evening cohorts, master's programs, associate-to-bachelor's programs, advanced degree programs, and certificate programs), enhance faculty resources and development including PhD programs, prepare students for nursing licensure examinations, expand clinical education infrastructure, establish nurse-managed health centers, support exam software and testing materials, expand websites, create accelerated program offerings, reduce barriers to nursing education through institutional and faculty initiatives, support tuition, provide course release time for faculty pursuing advanced degrees, clinical simulation equipment and training, leadership development for nurse faculty and hospital educators, and build infrastructure for nursing workforce data collection and analysis.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions submit competitive proposals for institutional grants. A review panel (eight to nine members) evaluates proposals based on their impact on nursing shortage, initiative quality, budget feasibility, support for national and state nursing shortage initiatives, program innovation, nursing graduate outcomes, and partnerships across community colleges, universities, and hospital health systems. Statewide initiatives support nursing schools directly through fellowships, doctoral grants, and scholarships. For detailed application procedures and specific program requirements, applicants should visit the Nurse Support Program website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for Maryland taxpayers who have incurred significant student loan debt. Eligible applicants receive a tax credit award that must be used to pay down their college loan debt. The program awards different credit amounts based on whether the applicant attended a Maryland institution or an out-of-state institution, with in-state attendees receiving higher credit amounts. For the 2018 tax year and earlier, recipients had two years to pay the awarded credit into their outstanding loan balance; for more recent tax years, recipients have three years from the close of the taxable year. Recipients must maintain Maryland residency for the tax year, demonstrate proof of payment to their lender, and can make payments in lump sum or installments consisting of principal and/or interest. The program also allows deduction of 100% of interest paid on student loans from state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit awarded to eligible Maryland taxpayers who have incurred significant student loan debt. The credit is applied to the taxpayer's Maryland state income tax return. Recipients must pay the awarded credit amount toward their college loan debt within two to three years depending on the tax year (two years for 2018 and earlier tax years; three years for later tax years and from the close of the taxable year). Payments can be made in lump sum or installments consisting of principal and/or interest. In 2019, applicants who attended in-state institutions received $1,000 in tax credits, while those who attended out-of-state institutions received $883 in tax credits. Proof of payment must be submitted through the OneStop account or to MHEC.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship provides financial assistance to aspiring teachers pursuing undergraduate or graduate education at eligible Maryland institutions leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate. The program serves high school seniors graduating in spring or summer 2026, college students, career-changers, teaching assistants, and college graduates. Recipients commit to working as public school or public prekindergarten teachers in Maryland upon completion of studies, with a preference for high-needs schools identified by the Maryland State Department of Education, shortage areas, or schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals. At Maryland public senior higher education institutions, the scholarship covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for resident undergraduate or graduate students. At Maryland private nonprofit institutions, the award is the lesser of 100% of University of Maryland College Park tuition and fees plus 100% of room and board at the institution, or 50% of institutional tuition and fees plus 100% of room and board, with private institutions required to provide matching awards for tuition and fees. Recipients who live off-campus or with parents receive a housing allowance based on room and board costs. Scholarships are renewable annually for up to three years (four years for five-year degree programs) if recipients continue making satisfactory academic progress. Undergraduate scholarship recipients must fulfill a one-year service obligation for each year they receive the scholarship. Graduate scholarship recipients must fulfill a two-year service obligation for each year they receive the scholarship.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award amount varies by institution type. At Maryland public senior higher education institutions, the scholarship covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for resident undergraduate or graduate students. At Maryland private nonprofit institutions, the award is the lesser of: 100% of University of Maryland College Park tuition and mandatory fees plus 100% of room and board at the institution, or 50% of the institution's tuition and mandatory fees plus 100% of room and board. Private nonprofits must provide a matching scholarship equal to the State award for tuition and fees. Recipients receive a housing allowance based on room and board costs if living off-campus or with parents. Scholarships are renewable annually for up to three years if maintaining satisfactory academic progress, or up to four years if enrolled in a five-year program with documented appeal. Awards are reviewed and distributed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings - Attorney Reimbursement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) reimburses attorney fees and certain costs for legal representation of students in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland higher education institutions. Attorneys may request reimbursement for legal services provided on or after August 1, 2019. The program reimburses attorney fees at $120 per hour (current rate for FY 2025) for non-MHEC list attorneys and $100 per hour for MHEC list attorneys, with a maximum cap of 20 hours per case. Travel costs including mileage at state rate ($0.70 per mile), tolls, public transit, and parking are reimbursable up to $200 per case. Payment is subject to availability of appropriated funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MHEC pays attorney fees at $120 per hour (current rate for FY 2025) for non-MHEC list attorneys and $100 per hour for MHEC list attorneys for legal representation in Title IX proceedings, with a maximum cap of 20 hours per case. Attorneys may also be reimbursed for travel costs to and from the university, including mileage at $0.70 per mile, tolls, public transit, and parking, up to $200 total per case. Payment is subject to availability of appropriated funds. Reimbursement covers representation in all phases of Title IX proceedings including investigation, mediation, hearing, and appeal phases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Attorneys providing legal representation to students in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland higher education institutions. Both MHEC attorney list members and non-list attorneys are eligible. Students (complainants and respondents) involved in Title IX sexual assault proceedings at Maryland colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attorney fees for legal representation in Title IX proceedings only (investigation, mediation, hearing, appeal phases). Reimbursable costs include travel expenses (mileage, tolls, public transit, parking). Office expenses such as copies, postage, or paralegal time are not covered. Representation must be limited to Title IX matters only; no reimbursement for related civil or criminal matters or non-Title IX disciplinary proceedings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Nursing Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides a reduction in tuition for out-of-state students enrolled in nursing programs at Maryland public institutions. The award covers the difference between out-of-state and in-state tuition rates (the tuition differential) at the same institution for the same nursing program, allowing non-resident students to pay the same tuition as Maryland residents. Recipients must agree to work as full-time nurses in a hospital or related institution for four years (if attending a four-year institution) or two years (if attending a two-year institution), or repay the scholarship with interest. The award renews automatically for up to three additional years (four-year institutions) or one additional year (two-year institutions) if satisfactory academic progress is maintained and enrollment in an eligible nursing program continues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual award equal to the tuition differential between out-of-state and in-state student charges at the same institution in the same nursing program for identical credit hours. Recipients pay the in-state tuition rate. The award covers the difference between the tuition paid by an out-of-state student and the tuition paid by an in-state student. The award renews automatically for up to three additional years (four-year institutions) or one additional year (two-year institutions) if satisfactory academic progress is maintained and enrollment in an eligible nursing program continues. Recipients must sign and return a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution for four years (four-year institution) or two years (two-year institution). If holding this scholarship with another award requiring service obligation, service must be performed in consecutive years. Recipients must begin service within six months of graduation or repay the scholarship with interest.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Students with Disabilities Receiving SSI or SSDI at Maryland Public Higher Education Institutions
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition waiver program that exempts eligible students with disabilities receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits from paying tuition at Maryland public institutions of higher education, including community colleges and universities. The program covers degree, certificate, and continuing education courses designed to lead to employment. At community colleges, the waiver covers up to 12 credits per semester for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or 6 credits for other community college credit courses. At universities, coverage is available for eligible coursework. The waiver applies to any balance on tuition after grants and scholarships are applied. Students are responsible for all other costs such as books and fees. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply at community colleges.

The waiver applies to any balance on tuition after grants and scholarships are applied. Students are responsible for all other costs such as books and fees. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply at community colleges.

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program that encourages 12- to 17-year-olds to get vaccinated against COVID-19 by offering college scholarships. Winners receive a $50,000 scholarship covering full tuition and fees at a public, in-state Maryland institution of higher education. Scholarships are distributed through Maryland529 as either a 4-Year Maryland Prepaid College Trust Account (for ages 12-14) or a Maryland College Investment Plan contribution (for ages 15-17). Twenty winners are selected through random drawings between July 12 and September 6, with two winners selected per week for eight weeks and four winners selected on Labor Day.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for Maryland residents pursuing degrees in specific high-need occupational fields including child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service. Recipients commit to working in their field in Maryland after graduation. The program provides annual grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per year depending on institution type (community college or four-year institution) and enrollment status (full-time or part-time). Full-time students at four-year institutions receive $4,000 per year; part-time students receive $2,000 per year. Community college full-time students receive $2,000 per year; part-time students receive $1,000 per year. Awards are automatically renewed for up to five years if eligibility requirements are maintained. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation working in their field in Maryland for one year for each year of scholarship received (or two years part-time work for each year of scholarship received). Financial assistance is provided based on merit and need.

Full-time students at four-year institutions receive $4,000 per year; part-time students receive $2,000 per year. Community college full-time students receive $2,000 per year; part-time students receive $1,000 per year. Awards are automatically renewed for up to five years if eligibility requirements are maintained. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation working in their field in Maryland, with full-time service obligation of one year for each year of scholarship received and part-time service obligation of two years for each year of scholarship received (minimum 20 hours per week for part-time employment, at least 35 hours per week for full-time service). FAFSA filing is not required but is used to determine award priority. Total State awards cannot exceed cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less.

structured_extraction.program_name: African American Heritage Preservation Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides capital grants to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals to assist in the preservation, restoration, and rehabilitation of buildings, sites, and communities significant to African American history and culture in Maryland. Funding can support acquisition, restoration, stabilization, development of new facilities for interpretation, and pre-construction planning services. The Maryland Historical Trust and the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture jointly administer the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants up to $250,000 per project with a typical annual budget of $5 million. No match required. Funds support preservation, acquisition, restoration, rehabilitation, stabilization, and pre-construction planning for properties with African American heritage significance. Projects must comply with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties.

Grants fund education and training for preservation commission members and local government staff, surveys, planning documents, and design guidelines that strengthen local preservation programs, and public outreach or interpretation projects that connect residents to local history.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program administered by the National Park Service and in Maryland by the Maryland Historical Trust (the State Historic Preservation Office) that provides tax incentives to property owners and developers who rehabilitate historic, income-producing buildings certified by the National Park Service as certified historic structures or listed in the National Register of Historic Places. The program provides a federal income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in rehabilitation of eligible income-producing properties, with no cap on the amount available. Local jurisdictions such as Hagerstown may offer supplementary local tax credit benefits (20% of rehabilitation costs for income-producing certified heritage resources) and charitable deduction opportunities for conservation easements on designated historic properties. The Maryland Historical Trust serves as the State Historic Preservation Office and provides application forms, technical assistance, and certification recommendations to the National Park Service. Rehabilitation projects must be substantial, defined as a minimum of $5,000 or the amount equal to the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater, and typically must be completed within a 24-month period. Projects must meet the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and local income tax credits for rehabilitation of income-producing historic buildings, districts, and certified historic structures determined by the National Park Service to be certified historic structures or listed in the National Register of Historic Places. Federal credits equal 20% of qualified capital costs with no cap on the amount available for eligible income-producing properties. Local jurisdictions may offer additional tax credits equal to 20% of approved rehabilitation costs. Charitable donation deductions are available for conveyance of perpetual easements to qualified preservation organizations. Rehabilitation projects must be substantial, defined as a minimum of $5,000 or the amount equal to the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater, and typically must be completed within a 24-month period. Property owners and developers submit applications to the Maryland Historical Trust or local historic preservation offices for certification review, which then goes to the National Park Service for final approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers with historic buildings or districts listed in the National Register of Historic Places or certified historic structures who wish to undertake rehabilitation projects and claim federal and/or local tax credits, or convey conservation easements. Includes for-profit entities, individuals, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits can be used to offset federal and local income tax liability from qualified rehabilitation expenses on historic properties and certified historic structures, including income-producing buildings. Charitable deductions available for perpetual easement conveyances to qualified preservation organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Available for any property listed in the National Register of Historic Places or determined to be a certified historic structure in Maryland. Local tax benefits also available in designated historic districts and for landmarks in participating municipalities such as Hagerstown.

The program typically has approximately $600,000 available for grants each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Historical Trust offers capital loans to qualified borrowers to assist and encourage efforts to preserve historic properties. The loans support acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, predevelopment projects, and energy efficiency improvements that benefit the public. Nonprofits, local governments, business entities, and individuals that cannot obtain private financing are eligible. Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties. Energy projects as part of an acquisition or rehabilitation and restoration are eligible expenditures. Certain qualified nonprofit organizations may also receive non-repayable fund transfers (grants) for acquisition, restoration, or to provide loans to other organizations and individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fixed annual interest rate set by adding 0.125% to the most recent general obligation bond rate. Nonprofits and local governments may receive an even lower rate. Loan terms are up to two years for pre-development projects and up to twenty years for other projects. Loan amounts typically do not exceed 80% of the appraised value and depend on available funds and the borrower's ability to repay. A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount, whichever is less, is required. Loan funds support acquisition, stabilization, rehabilitation, restoration of historic properties, energy projects as part of acquisition or rehabilitation, and predevelopment work including plans, specifications, and architectural or engineering services. Qualified nonprofit organizations may receive non-repayable fund transfers for acquisition, restoration, or to provide loans to other organizations and individuals. The full process typically takes 6 to 9 months from application to settlement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Loan applications accepted year-round as funds become available. Transfer applications open in November and close in January.

It supports loans, grants, and tax credits to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals for historic preservation activities and place-based heritage resource projects. The program aims to improve quality of life for residents and maximize economic development through heritage tourism.

Both grant types require a one-to-one matching contribution from the applicant. Loans can cover up to 50% of total project cost based on the applicant's financial need and are not available for refinancing. A tax credit of up to 20% is available for eligible rehabilitation costs of qualifying historic structures. The amount available depends on current funding.

Projects must create or improve place-based heritage resources within a designated heritage area.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program administered by the Maryland Historical Trust that encourages the reuse and renovation of historic structures by providing investment tax credits to homeowners, small commercial property owners, developers, individuals, and government entities with certified historic properties. The program includes three separate credit tiers: one for homeowners, one for owners of small commercial buildings (credits capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period for projects under $500,000), and one for major rehabilitations. Credits equal 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of certified historic structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places, designated as locally historic properties, or non-historic buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to heritage areas. Additional bonus credits of 5% are available for LEED Gold certification, Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects, and Opportunity Zone projects (5% or 7.5% for Opportunity Zones). Eligible rehabilitation costs include structural repairs, plumbing, HVAC and electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, restoration of significant historic landscape features, interior finishes that become part of the structure, and energy improvements. The minimum cost threshold is $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects. Rehabilitation work must be completed within a 24-month period and must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Credits can be combined with federal and county tax credits. The program generates approximately $8.53 in return for every state dollar invested. Applicants must apply before starting any renovations. The program is designed to revitalize historic properties, recycle older and economically obsolete buildings into new uses, serve as a community revitalization engine, and reinforce smart growth principles.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A Maryland state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of certified historic structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places, designated as locally historic properties, or non-historic buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to heritage areas. Three separate credit tiers available: homeowner credits, small commercial property credits (capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period for projects under $500,000), and major rehabilitation credits. Additional bonus credits of 5% are available for LEED Gold certification, Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects, and Opportunity Zone projects (5% or 7.5% for Opportunity Zones). Credits are available for homeowners, commercial property owners, developers, and government entities and can be combined with federal and county tax credits. Eligible costs include structural repairs, plumbing, HVAC and electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, restoration of significant historic landscape features, interior finishes that become part of the structure, and energy improvements. Minimum rehabilitation costs are $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects or the greater of adjusted basis or $5,000 for all other projects. Work must be completed within 24 months and meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Non-profit organizations receive full refunds of tax credits. The program generates approximately $8.53 in return for every state dollar invested. Applicants must apply before starting any renovations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, on a first-come, first-served basis until the program cap is reached for the current fiscal year
