The program is also for owners of income-producing certified historic structures and developers who plan to sell a rehabilitated property to a homeowner. Non-profit developers and organizations also qualify and receive full refunds of tax credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintenance, restoration, and substantial rehabilitation of certified historic residential and commercial properties, including structural repairs, mechanical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom work, architectural fees, landscape restoration, interior finishes that meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation, energy improvements to bring buildings into productive use, roof and chimney repair, and window restoration. Funds cannot be used for landscaping, new construction, appliances, or tool purchases.

Also available in Hagerstown's designated historic districts and for designated landmarks, with documented projects in Baltimore, Berlin, Cumberland, Easton, Frederick, Hagerstown, and other communities. Geographic restrictions exist: no more than 60% of credits in a fiscal year may go to projects in a single county or Baltimore City. To be eligible, a building must be a certified historic structure.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Historical Trust to verify if your property is eligible and on the National Register, locally historic designation list, or certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to a heritage area. Obtain approval from MHT before beginning rehabilitation work. The application has three parts: Part 1 certifies that the building is a historic structure; Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets program requirements; Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets program requirements. Applicants must submit all parts for approval before starting work. Submit both federal and state tax credit application forms, with the federal form completed in full and only the first sheet of each part of the state form required. Submit before and after rehabilitation photographs documenting adherence to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. Historic property owners interested in this program should contact the Maryland Historical Trust directly for application forms and program information. Applicants must apply before starting any renovations. For Hagerstown properties, contact the Hagerstown Planning Office. The program includes a competitive application process for commercial and small commercial projects. Refer to the MHT Tax Credits Homepage for application procedures and requirements. Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program - Competitive Commercial Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive state income tax credit program for commercial historic property owners seeking to support major rehabilitation projects. The program provides a state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of eligible income-producing historic properties, up to a maximum of $5 million per project. Projects must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and be approved by the Maryland Historical Trust before work begins.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a state income tax credit for up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs for income-producing historic properties. The credit is capped at $5 million per project. Eligible expenses must exceed the greater of the structure's adjusted basis value or $25,000.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dana Marks Halpert, Carey L. Jones, or Kate Jaffe
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic, income-producing commercial properties and developers pursuing significant rehabilitation projects throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs related to the rehabilitation and restoration of historic structures. This includes repairs or alterations that preserve the building's significant features while making it usable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to commercial property owners throughout Maryland. The property must be a certified historic structure, achieved by being listed on the National Register of Historic Places, being a contributing resource in a historic district, or being located in a Certified Heritage Area.
requirements_list: Eligible expenses must exceed the greater of the structure's adjusted basis value or $25,000.
The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) must review and approve the project before work begins.
The project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
Projects awarded $1 million or more in tax credits must meet state corporate diversity requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit all forms electronically. First, contact MHT Tax Credit staff to set up a Microsoft Teams channel. The application has three parts: Part 1 certifies the building is historic. Part 2 describes the proposed project to certify it meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed work meets the requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program - Homeowner Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit for historic property owners to help offset the cost of maintaining and rehabilitating historic residential structures. Qualifying homeowners can receive a tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 over a 24-month period, with a minimum of $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required. This homeowner tax credit encourages investment in historic neighborhoods and helps Marylanders preserve their homes for future generations. The credit can be used in combination with county tax credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit equal to 20% of eligible rehabilitation expenses, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Minimum $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required. Applications accepted year-round on a rolling basis with typical review taking 30-45 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who own and occupy a certified historic single-family residence as their primary or secondary residence, either individually or through a cooperative.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible expenses include roof repair or replacement, chimney repair and relining, structural repairs, window and door restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry repair or repointing, mechanical/electrical/plumbing work, interior finish restoration (plaster, flooring, trim), professional design/architectural/engineering fees, tool/equipment rental, and repair of historic outbuildings. Ineligible expenses include landscaping, new construction/additions, appliances, carpeting over historic flooring, interior décor, tool/equipment purchases, and certain maintenance services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Properties must be certified historic structures - either individually listed in the National Register of Historic Places, contributing resources in a National Register Historic District, or locally designated and determined by Maryland Historical Trust to be eligible for the National Register. Some properties in Maryland heritage areas or curatorship properties owned by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources may be eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must own and occupy the property as primary or secondary residence, individually or through a cooperative
Property must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence or cooperative unit
Property must be a certified historic structure (individually listed in National Register, contributing to National Register District, or locally designated and eligible for National Register)
Minimum $5,000 in eligible rehabilitation expenses required
All work must be approved by Maryland Historical Trust before beginning
All work must comply with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
No work may be begun prior to MHT review and approval
Project must be completed within 24 months
Any project changes or additions require amendment form approval before starting work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has three parts. Part 1 describes the property and its historic significance for evaluation by MHT. Part 2 describes the proposed rehabilitation work for approval. Part 3 documents the completed project for final certification. Applicants are encouraged to contact MHT early in the planning process, especially for large or complex projects. Once MHT receives a complete application, review typically takes 30-45 days depending on submission clarity and project complexity. Applicants must submit amendment forms if projects change or new work is added, and these amendments must be approved before starting the new work.

structured_extraction.program_description: Mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts under $5,000 within Maryland's heritage areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts up to $5,000. Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants. Visit individual heritage area websites for specifics.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, and local partners within Maryland's heritage areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Within Maryland's 13 designated heritage areas
requirements_list: Project must be heritage-related
Project must be non-capital
Project cost must be under $5,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit individual heritage area websites to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to support Maryland museums and institutional collections by helping historical and cultural museums strengthen operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability. The program provides federal and state funding opportunities for museums, libraries, and related institutions to enhance their services, foster innovation, address community needs, increase literacy, restore truth to American history, and preserve the artifacts and documents of the nation's heritage. The program also offers technical assistance to help interpret Maryland's rich history, promote tourism, and support public education while encouraging professionalism within museum practice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 with typical awards between $10,000 to $15,000. No match required. In FY26, the program received $285,000 for grants statewide. The program also provides technical assistance to museums. Individual grants receive extraordinary scrutiny to ensure funds are used in accordance with legal prohibitions on racial discrimination and support the mission of utilizing public resources to increase literacy and preserve heritage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October; FY26 opportunities by March 13, 2026; Native American Library Services Enhancement Grants and Native Hawaiian Library Services Grant by April 10, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Museums that manage and operate institutions open for at least three years, including nonprofits in good standing and local governments, as well as libraries and related institutions serving to support their operations and sustainability. Public and non-profit museum organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Everyday museum operations including paying staff, training staff or volunteers, office and administrative costs such as insurance reporting and accounting, environmental monitoring such as pest management or humidity control, and security and safety systems. Enhancing services, fostering innovation, addressing community needs, and increasing literacy. Funds support projects that interpret Maryland's history, promote tourism, and provide public education. Capital projects such as construction restoration or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant museums must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology. Museums operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government are not eligible. Available statewide in Maryland. Maryland-based organizations.
requirements_list: Museum must have been open and operating for at least three years
Nonprofit applicants must be in good standing with the state
Nonprofit applicants must be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status
Local government applicants must operate a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Museum must be defined as an organization that collects, preserves, and interprets objects and materials for the public
Museum must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology
Each museum operated by an applicant must submit a separate application
Institutions must meet eligibility requirements; individual grants receive extraordinary scrutiny
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the current grant guidelines. Confirm project eligibility and applicant type. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control. Submit a completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline in October or as specified for individual grant opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grants program administered by the Maryland Historical Trust on behalf of the National Park Service that funds projects to protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants of $10,000 to $100,000 per project. Total project costs must be between $20,000 and $200,000. A 1:1 non-federal match is required. The program provides $380,192 in total funding for education and preservation projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state and local governments, and nonprofit organizations working on historic maritime preservation and education projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites; repair, rehabilitation, stabilization, maintenance, or limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites; and improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. All projects must include a public education component.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must demonstrate projects that address historic maritime resources. Projects addressing impacts of flooding, erosion, or changing environmental conditions on maritime resources while advancing public education will be prioritized.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a tribal government, state government, local government, or nonprofit organization
Projects must demonstrate clear public benefit
Projects must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation
Projects must follow Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects where applicable
All projects must include a public education component
Projects must support identification of historic maritime resources, repair/rehabilitation/stabilization of maritime structures, or improvements increasing public access to maritime resources
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
Projects must have total costs between $20,000 and $200,000
A 1:1 non-federal match is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review grant guidelines and manual for detailed requirements. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Prepare a complete application including scope of work, budget, and required documentation. 4. Submit completed application through the grants portal before the June 1 deadline. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact MHT staff early in project planning for guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts & Entertainment District designation offers Maryland counties and municipalities tax incentives and other tools to encourage activity and investment in specific geographic areas where the arts are part of an economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides tax incentives associated with the A&E District designation and other tools to encourage activity and investment in designated geographic areas. Districts must be located within Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland county and municipal governments seeking to designate geographic areas with significant arts activity and entertainment venues as Arts & Entertainment Districts for economic development purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives and tools to encourage activity and investment in designated areas where the arts are part of an economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Districts must be located within designated Priority Funding Areas in Maryland. Applicants must be a county or municipal government in Maryland and must communicate with all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district.
requirements_list: Must be a county or municipal government in Maryland
Must select a geographic area with a significant level of arts activity, entertainment venues, and/or arts business
Must include arts and entertainment in the area's economic development strategy
Must communicate with all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district and obtain agreement concerning the tax credits associated with the designation
Must complete an Intent to Apply form online 90 days before the application deadline
District must be located within designated Priority Funding Areas
Must coordinate with local plans and policies for economic development and other state designation programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first communicate with all impacted municipalities and counties to obtain agreement. Then complete an Intent to Apply form online 90 days before the application deadline chosen (April 1st or October 1st). Submit a full application as specified in the A&E District Designation Guidelines. Applications are reviewed in three steps: staff review for completeness and adherence to regulations, review by the MSAC A&E Districts Advisory Committee (which includes representation from Commerce, Housing & Community Development, Transportation, and Planning departments plus current A&E District managers), and final decision by the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual operating grants that support activities, programs, and projects in Arts and Entertainment Districts throughout Maryland. Appointed management entities for designated A&E Districts may apply for MSAC operating support funds to support district priorities. The program provides annual operating grants of $15,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides annual operating grants of $15,000 to support activities, programs, and projects in A&E Districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management organizations for designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds provide operating support for activities, programs, and projects that advance the priorities of a designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is for the appointed management entities of state-designated Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts.
requirements_list: Must be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland.
Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization.
Must have a letter of agreement with the county or municipality that holds the A&E District designation.
Must have a current contract or memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a county or municipality to manage the designated A&E District.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The management entity for an A&E District submits an application annually. In the fifth year after designation, the entity submits a detailed 'On-Year' application. In all other years, it submits a shorter 'Off-Year' application. The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications, while MSAC staff reviews off-year ones. The MSAC Council and the Secretary of Commerce give final approval for all funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant supporting fully developed and ready-to-implement public art initiatives in Maryland that celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The grant funds projects aligned with the America250 national initiative to commemorate the semiquincentennial of the Declaration of Independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support public art projects including conservation and promotion of existing works or creation and installation of new works. Eligible mediums include murals, tile mosaics, paintings, and sculptures. Funding may cover administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor, materials, contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental, signage or plaques, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, units of state or local government, and established higher education institutions seeking to implement public art projects celebrating America's semiquincentennial.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials (artwork, base, lighting, landscaping), contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental for fabrication and assembly, signage or plaques to identify artwork, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland and involve artists, artisans, studios, or teams based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Organization must be Maryland-based nonprofit with 501(c)3 status, unit of state or local government, or established higher education institution in Maryland
Project must be fully developed and ready for immediate implementation
Artwork concept must be finalized
All required permits and site permissions must be acquired
Project must be entering initial stages of implementation with ability to complete and fully install by June 30, 2026
Eligible artworks must be either an architectural enhancement of artistic significance or an installation of artwork including murals, tile mosaics, paintings, or sculptures
Project must comply with MSAC's definition of Public Art
Clear and specific project description aligned with America250 goals
Site-responsive artwork that engages community
Demonstrated artistic excellence and merit
Safe and durable public environment artwork
Realistic, feasible timeline for completion
Financially realistic budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit an online application by logging in or creating an account on SmartSimple, the MSAC grants management platform. Applications must be completed and submitted electronically, including use of an electronic signature. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn. All grantees must file a final report by September 1, 2026. Scoring is based on a rubric with five evaluation criteria, each scored on a 1-10 point scale.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax incentive for qualifying resident artists who create and sell artistic work in designated Arts & Entertainment Districts throughout Maryland. Eligible artists can subtract or exempt income derived from in-district sales or performances from their state income tax filing. The program is administered statewide through the Maryland State Arts Council and has specific local implementations in districts such as Salisbury and Hagerstown. Qualifying resident artists living in Maryland and selling or performing artistic work in any of the 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts are eligible for an income tax subtraction modification on income derived from their in-district activities. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district; for all qualifying resident artists, this includes sales and internet sales originating in a district. Income is deducted before state and local taxes are calculated, though federal income tax still applies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying resident artists living in Maryland and selling or performing artistic work in any of the 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts throughout the State are eligible for an income tax subtraction modification on income derived from their in-district activities. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district; for all qualifying resident artists, this includes sales and internet sales originating in a district. Income is deducted before state and local taxes are calculated, though federal income tax still applies. Eligible artists submit Form 502AE with their annual state tax filing to claim the modification. Single-member LLCs treated as individuals may also qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying resident artists living in Maryland who create and sell or perform artistic work in designated Arts & Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax reduction or exemption on earnings from in-district artistic sales, performances, and related activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts throughout Maryland, including the Salisbury and Hagerstown A&E Districts. Qualifying resident artists must own or rent residential real property in Maryland or within a specific A&E District and conduct business in an A&E district.
requirements_list: Artist must own or rent residential real property in Maryland or within the A&E District
Artist must conduct a business in an A&E district
Artist must derive income from the sale or performance of artistic work produced in an A&E district

Artistic work must be original and creative, falling into defined categories (writing, performance, composition, visual art, sculpture, crafts, film, dance, jewelry, clothing, functional art, storytelling, digital media, or related works)
Artistic work must be produced in an A&E district and sold in one of the A&E districts
The incentive is available to independent individual artists, sole proprietor businesses, and single-member LLCs treated as individuals
Future income such as royalties, licenses, and revenue from publishing or reproduction rights are not eligible
Income from industry-related work (large volume or commercial production) does not qualify
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible artists must file a completed Form 502AE with their Maryland individual income tax return or contact the Office of the Maryland Comptroller for current guidance. Artists should retain receipts, books, accounts, and other documentation proving that income qualifies for the incentive. Form 502AE is available on the Maryland Comptroller website (marylandtaxes.gov) and at forms.marylandtaxes.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state capital funding program that provides grants to nonprofit arts organizations for projects that enhance, create, or renovate arts facilities. The program aims to produce complete, usable, and accessible arts facilities. Eligible projects include expansion, production, renovation, or major repairs to facilities or infrastructure. Projects that prioritize energy-efficient building methods, increase accessibility for people with disabilities, or expand programming are strongly encouraged. Capital funding of up to $3,000,000 per year is available for FY24-FY29 (6 years total) to eligible arts organizations with annual operating budgets below $3,000,000. Grants typically range from $50,000 to $500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct state capital funding provided for projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility. Grants typically range from $50,000 to $500,000. Capital funding of up to $3,000,000 per year is available for FY24-FY29 (6 years total) to eligible arts organizations with annual operating budgets below $3,000,000. Funding is provided in one payment (100% of award) after grant agreement execution and State Board of Public Works approval. Disbursement typically occurs minimum 6 months after notification of grant status.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that operate physical arts facilities, are open to the public, provide arts-based cultural education or experiences, and have an annual operating budget under $3,000,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including expansion, production, renovation, or major repairs to arts facilities or infrastructure. Projects that improve energy efficiency, increase accessibility for people with disabilities, or expand programming capacity are prioritized.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland to eligible nonprofits that operate physical property in the state. Applicants must be based in Maryland and the project facility must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must operate a physical property in Maryland (leased or owned)
Must be open to the public
Must provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Annual operating budget must be less than $3,000,000
Must either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, OR be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Must provide proof of property ownership or lease agreement with minimum 5 years remaining at time of application
Cannot have incomplete projects from previous Arts Capital awards
Cannot have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within the past 5 years
Previous grantees must have completed their prior projects and submitted final reports before re-applying
Mission alignment with organizational goals
Facility-related challenges identification with evidence
Clear, realistic project timeline with prior planning/research
Detailed, researched budget tied to activities
Demonstration of project team capacity and skills
Plans for organizational sustainability
Community needs assessment and stakeholder engagement
Accessibility improvements for people with disabilities, people of color, and individuals living below federal poverty level
Demonstration of local workforce opportunities and inclusive hiring practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants and organizations should contact program staff before applying to discuss proposed projects and eligibility. All applications submitted through SmartSimple secure online grants management system. Applications must be submitted electronically with electronic signature. A multi-disciplinary statewide grant panel reviews all applications electronically. Applicants receive electronic notification of award or denial after review period. Organizations must meet all revision deadlines after submission or application will be withdrawn.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that strengthen and promote lifelong learning in the arts by supporting teaching artists on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster to implement arts education programs in Maryland's schools and communities. Grants support arts learning activities including workshops, residencies, out-of-school time programs, lectures/demonstrations, visiting performances, field trips, and online programs in schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, government entities, and nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $6,000 per application. A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year. Lead Artists may receive awards up to $21,000 (3% of annual budget). Teaching Artist Organizations may receive awards up to $84,000 (12% of annual budget). Funds support implementation of arts learning activities including workshops (1-2 day focused arts learning on specific topics/skills), residencies (multi-session programs building knowledge and skills over time, may include culminating projects), out-of-school time programs (before/after school hours), lectures/lecture demonstrations (presentations sharing deep knowledge with demonstrations), visiting performances (performances delivered to audiences at designated locations), field trips (audience travels to venues for arts experiences), and online programs (virtual delivery - asynchronous, synchronous, or blended). Payment may take up to 90 days after award.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster collaborating with schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, government entities, and nonprofit organizations in Maryland. Students and audiences at schools, recreation centers, senior centers, theaters, museums, and other venues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Arts education programs and activities in schools and communities. Teaching artists implement arts learning activities with collaborating schools and organizations. Funds support program implementation costs, materials and supplies, and personnel/collaborators.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Teaching artists and collaborating schools or organizations must be based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Teaching artist must be on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster

Collaborating school or organization must be one of the following: 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in Maryland, unit of government based in Maryland, or college/university (higher education institution) in Maryland
Collaborating school or organization must have operated for one completed and documented fiscal year at the date of application submission with ongoing arts activities
Teaching artist and collaborating school or organization must agree to collaborate and confirm services, availability, timeline, and fees before application
A coordinator must be identified at the collaborating school or organization
If ensemble or organization is applicant, a Lead Artist responsible for leading arts education activities must be indicated
A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026
Designate a site coordinator to organize and oversee the program
Initiate planning conversations with artist/artist's organization prior to application
Demonstrate intent to move forward with the arts learning experience if awarded
Describe proposed arts learning activities (clear, specific, thorough)
Include objectives aligned to state standards or learning competencies (for in-school programs)
Define intended audience and alignment with audience needs
Provide clear timeline with specific dates
Include evidence of individual and collaborative planning with key stakeholders
Provide detailed, itemized budget with context tied to implementation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Teaching artist and school or organization agree to collaborate. 2. Collaborating school or organization identifies a coordinator. 3. Teaching artist or affiliated organization starts the application in SmartSimple. 4. Application is submitted by one of the rolling deadlines. 5. Panel reviews and scores applications according to review criteria including proposed arts learning activities, objectives aligned to state standards or learning competencies, intended audience alignment, timeline, evidence of collaborative planning, and detailed budget. 6. Applicant receives notification of application status the following month. 7. For awarded activities, MSAC disburses funds directly to the teaching artist with payment taking up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts in Education Teaching Artist Roster
structured_extraction.program_description: A curated directory and recognition program for Maryland-based teaching artists who have been selected through a panel review process to provide group or classroom arts instruction and performances in educational settings. The Teaching Artist Roster recognizes teaching artists and their integral contribution to the arts education ecosystem that deepens lifelong learning. Artists on the roster are eligible to compete for funding through the Arts in Education Grant program, though roster membership does not guarantee grant funding. Members receive connections to a statewide network of organizations and nonprofits offering professional development, individualized feedback and evaluation sessions, and increased visibility through the Maryland Arts Directory. Teaching artists offer services in various disciplines including music, theater, dance, visual arts, literary arts, media arts, and multidisciplinary approaches, including residencies, visiting performances, workshops, out-of-school time programming, online programs, and professional development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Membership provides eligibility to apply for Arts in Education grants that cover teaching artist fees. The roster recognizes teaching artists through an application and panel review process. Members also receive connections to a statewide network of organizations and nonprofits offering professional development, individualized feedback and evaluation sessions, and increased visibility through the Maryland Arts Directory. Directory of 130+ teaching artists and arts organizations with contact information, disciplines offered, and service types available (residencies, visiting performances, workshops, etc.).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program is currently paused for new applications. Check back for updates in Spring 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists (individuals, ensembles, collaborative groups, nonprofits, government units, and University System of Maryland institutions) who provide arts education programming in school and community settings, and schools and educational institutions seeking arts programming. Students and audiences at designated locations (schools, recreation centers, senior centers, theaters, museums).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roster membership qualifies artists to apply for Arts in Education grants, which fund teaching artist fees for delivering arts education programs to schools and community groups. Engagement of teaching artists for in-school and out-of-school arts education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Maryland-based teaching artists. Independent artists must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland) for at least six months before application and must remain Maryland residents while on the roster and during any funded activities. Organizations must be Maryland-based (501(c)3 incorporated in Maryland, a Maryland government unit, or a University System of Maryland member institution).
requirements_list: Teaching artist work must go through MSAC's application and panel review process
Independent artists must be Maryland residents (owning or renting residential property in Maryland) for at least six months prior to application submission
Must be 18 years of age or older at time of application
Ensembles or collaborative groups must have all artists age 18 or older, with at least 50% meeting the residency requirement
Not enrolled in any matriculated high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program at time of application
Continue to be Maryland residents while active on roster and for duration of any funded Arts in Education Grant-supported activities
For organizations: must be 501(c)3 with IRS tax exempt status incorporated in Maryland, a unit of government based in Maryland, or a member institution in the University System of Maryland
For organizations: must have completed one documented fiscal year with ongoing arts activities at date of application submission
Teaching artists must have experience providing group or classroom arts instruction and/or performances in educational settings
Demonstrate background and experience in arts discipline(s) and working with selected audiences
Submit lesson plans and/or programs with instructional sequences and connections to Maryland State standards/learning competencies
Describe inspirations and factors informing instruction/performances
Demonstrate commitment to diversity, equity, and justice
Demonstrate commitment to inclusion and accessibility
Submit recording of live instruction, performance, and/or online programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teaching artists apply to be listed on the Teaching Artist Roster through MSAC's application and panel review process. Applicants complete an application including: information on the artist's training and experience in their arts discipline(s) and audiences they serve, examples of arts education programs and activities (workshops, residencies, out-of-school time programs, visiting performances, lecture demonstrations, online programs), responses to questions about inspirations, values, and ability to adapt work for students with different learning styles and abilities, and a sample recording of arts education instruction, performance, or online programs. Applicants are encouraged to schedule virtual meetings or attend office hours with Arts in Education staff or consultants before submitting. Selection is based on demonstrated experience, lesson plans, inspirations, commitment to diversity/equity/justice and inclusion/accessibility, and recorded instruction/performance samples, evaluated using rubric scoring across six criteria categories.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Percent-for-Art program that commissions permanent, site-specific artworks for new or renovated state-owned buildings. For eligible state construction projects, 0.05% of the estimated construction cost is reserved to commission or purchase original artwork through a contractual agreement with an artist. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) manages each project from artist selection through installation, and completed artworks join the State's public art collection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For each artwork commission project, 0.05% of the estimated construction cost is reserved and provided to the selected artist through a contractual agreement. The artist contracts directly with the state unit responsible for the project and works with the project design team. Commission projects typically require a two to five year commitment from the artist, beginning with contract execution and ending upon successful installation and dedication of the artwork.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications through the Maryland Public Artist Roster are closed; roster anticipated to reopen in spring 2025. Individual project calls may be issued as Requests for Qualifications (RFQ).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and artist-led teams who are residents of the United States and its territories interested in creating permanent public art for state buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commission or purchase of site-specific original artwork to be permanently integrated into state-owned buildings undergoing new construction or renovation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Artwork commissions are for state-owned buildings throughout Maryland. Artists must be U.S. residents but can be based anywhere in the United States and its territories.
requirements_list: Artists must be residents of the United States and its territories
Artists and artist-led teams apply for projects as they become available by joining the Maryland Public Artist Roster or responding to an open call when issued
Artists selected for a commission work directly with the state unit responsible for the project and the project design team
Completed artworks must be permanent, large-scale, publicly accessible, and intentionally integrated into the construction or renovation project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists interested in Artwork Commission opportunities can join the Maryland Public Artist Roster, which is a vetted directory of artists. The roster serves as the primary source from which the Artist Selection Committee draws candidates for each project. An Artist Selection Committee composed of arts professionals, representatives from the user agency and primary building occupant, the lead design architect, and Maryland Public Art Commission and MSAC staff review candidates and select artists. MSAC anticipates initiating commissions for at least six state capital construction projects per year. When roster is closed, individual project calls may be issued as Requests for Qualifications (RFQ) posted to this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants and technical assistance that support Maryland's county arts agencies and Baltimore City, extending the service of the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC). These grants help county arts agencies provide equitable, accessible financial and technical support to artists, arts organizations, and arts programs within their jurisdictions, while encouraging local decision-making, arts activity, and community engagement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula-based grants and technical assistance provided to Maryland's county arts agencies and Baltimore City. Grants support the operations and grant-making activities of county arts agencies. Technical assistance helps applicants develop their plans and strengthen the network of county arts agencies across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for official county arts agencies throughout Maryland's 24 jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City), which can be local government agencies or designated nonprofit organizations. The program ultimately serves artists, arts organizations, and local communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting county arts agencies to provide financial and technical support to artists, arts organizations, and arts programs; funding agency operations and grant-making activities; encouraging local arts activities and diverse programming; promoting equitable access to arts funding; and promoting lifelong learning and creative expression.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 24 jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City).
requirements_list: Must be a local agency or nonprofit designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council.
Submit an application annually, which will be either a detailed three-year plan ('On-Year') or a shorter update ('Off-Year').
Grantees must submit interim and annual final reports detailing the use of funds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications each year. Every three years, an agency submits an 'On-Year' application with a detailed three-year plan. MSAC staff and a review panel review a draft and provide feedback. The agency revises the plan and submits it for final Council approval. In the two years between, the agency submits a simpler 'Off-Year' application that notes any changes to the three-year plan and includes required financial reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support
structured_extraction.program_description: Strengthens the vitality and sustainability of small organizations to maintain a strong and stable arts infrastructure in Maryland. This program provides grants to support the general operations of small arts organizations, helping maintain a strong and stable arts community in the state. Funds support an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants of up to $4,000 for general operating support to eligible arts organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling. MSAC is currently accepting applications for the FY2026 application cycle. December 31, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants are small arts organizations in Maryland, including 501(c)3 nonprofits, local government units, and colleges or universities. Independent artists are not eligible for this specific grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The organization must be incorporated in Maryland. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university.
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects that are available to the public.
Cannot be a current participant in the Grants for Organizations (GFO), County Arts Development (CAD), or Arts & Entertainment District (A&E) programs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit their application through the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications monthly. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) notifies applicants of their status. If approved, the grantee receives a grant agreement to process payment, which can take up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support both the early stages of research and development and the execution of proposed arts projects. This program provides funding for independent artists and Maryland-incorporated nonprofit arts organizations to plan, develop, and implement collaborative and community-centered creative initiatives within Maryland communities, helping strengthen the vitality and sustainability of artists and small organizations. The program offers two grant types: Planning & Development grants support early research and development, while Implementation grants support carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support research, development, planning, and implementation of specific arts projects, events, and programs. Planning and development activities include creative process development, community engagement planning, and project preparation. Implementation grants support carrying out specific arts activities, events, or projects with community engagement components. Grants range from $1,000 to $4,000 and support both early-stage planning and execution phases. Payment is 100% of the award amount, processed within 6-8 weeks after grant agreement execution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 (monthly reviews)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laura Weiss or Emily Sollenberger Dobbins
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists, Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit arts organizations in operation for one year or more, units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges, universities, and schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for planning, promotional efforts, implementation and execution, and evaluation of specific arts projects, events, and collaborative initiatives within Maryland communities. Planning & Development grants support early-stage work including creative process development, community engagement planning, and project preparation activities. Implementation grants support carrying out specific projects with defined community engagement components.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible applicants throughout Maryland. Projects should define and serve a specific geographic area.
requirements_list: Must be an independent artist or Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for one year or more with income within grant requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school
Must identify a specific event, activity, or project to occur within the application timeframe
Organizations using fiscal sponsorships must operate under a Model A sponsorship structure
Applicants may only apply for one Creativity Grant per fiscal year

Organizations receiving funding through general operating programs (Grants for Organizations, County Arts Agencies, Arts & Entertainment Districts, Folklife Network, or Creativity Grant for General Operating) are not eligible for project-based support
Application forms must be completed in SmartSimple and have a 2026 application ID
Describe planning/development process and overarching goals
Include creative process details and larger project scope
Explain community engagement goals and intended impact
Provide detailed timeline with specific activities and dates
Include budget for planning/development phase only
Detail all planned expenses and anticipated income beyond MSAC request
Applicants must describe proposed arts activity with specific logistical details
Applicants must describe community engagement plans, goals, and intended community impact
Applicants must provide detailed project timeline including planning, promotion, fund expenditure, implementation, and evaluation
Applicants must provide clear project budget with all projected expenses, income sources beyond MSAC request, and MSAC fund allocation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through SmartSimple on a rolling basis from July 2025 through March 2026. Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed by a panel of public members with relevant arts expertise using a scoring rubric evaluated across four dimensions: proposed arts activity description with logistical details, community engagement plans and intended impact, detailed project timeline, and project budget. Applications are scored on three criteria: (1) Planning/development process description with goals and community impact; (2) Detailed timeline with specific activities and dates; (3) Detailed budget with income and expenses. If approved, applicants receive a formal grant agreement form. Payment is processed within 6-8 weeks after execution of the grant agreement. Grantees must submit a final report online in SmartSimple with a deadline determined by their application submission date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports traditional arts education by funding a mentor artist and apprentice artist to work together for one year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund a mentor artist and apprentice artist pair to work together for one year to support traditional arts education and community-based living cultural traditions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mentor artists and apprentice artists engaged in traditional arts practices handed down by example or word of mouth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for one year of collaborative work between a mentor artist and apprentice artist in traditional arts education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to artists across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that fund organizations serving as regional folklife centers in Maryland to identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to regional folklife centers. The program provides grants of $85,000. Payment is processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks upon execution of the grant agreement. Grantees must submit a final report at the completion of the funded project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations serving as regional folklife centers in Maryland that support the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Current regional folklife centers are located in Talbot County, Carroll County, Baltimore City, Allegany County, Montgomery County, St. Mary's County, Baltimore County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Must be an organization serving as a regional folklife center
Must support activities that identify, document, support, or present living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a grant application. Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment will be processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at the completion of the funded project. See Grant Guidelines for detailed information.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Grants for Artists program provides funding to support working or living expenses for artists. The program aims to provide artists with holistic support rather than support focused solely on a particular product or project-based needs. A primary goal is to strengthen the creative workforce, which is a vital part of Maryland's economy and culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to support working or living expenses for artists.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working artists in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working or living expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See grant and program guidelines for details about eligibility, application submission, and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants supporting Arts Organizations (organizations with a mission/purpose of producing or presenting arts through public programs or services) or Arts Programs (organizations whose primary mission is other than arts but provide ongoing arts programming/activities through public programs). The GFO granting program provides general operating support to nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, as well as units of government, that produce or present ongoing arts programming that is open to the public. GFO grantees provide access to the arts in their communities, create audiences for the future, uplift communities, and stimulate economic impact throughout the state. Current GFO grantees may apply directly for continued funding. New GFO applicants must complete an Intent to Apply application by September 15 annually to determine eligibility before submitting a full funding application by November 15. In FY25, MSAC awarded GFO grants to 309 arts organizations totaling $18,136,157.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants. Organizations are grouped into five budget tiers. During a 5-year phase-in period (FY24-FY28), maximum grant amounts decrease annually: Year 1 (FY24) $1.4M, Year 2 (FY25) $1.3M, Year 3 (FY26) $1.2M, Year 4 (FY27) $1.1M, Year 5 (FY28) $1M. The percentage of allowable expenses available as a grant award varies by tier, ranging from 15% for smaller organizations (budget $50K-$500K) to 4% for the largest organizations (budget $10M+). Funding is distributed in full after grant agreement forms are signed and reporting requirements are met. New applicants must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 to determine eligibility, then complete a full application by November 15 if deemed eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply form due by September 15th annually; GFO application due by November 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts organizations and arts programs providing public programming/services. Nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations and units of government that produce or present ongoing arts programming open to the public. New applicants or organizations that did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent funding cycle must complete the Intent to Apply form to be eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for arts organizations and programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. Organizations must be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland. The majority of arts activities must take place in Maryland and most of the organization's annual expenditures must be devoted to activities occurring within Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must clarify whether applying as an Arts Organization or Arts Program; details available in FY27 GFO Grant Guidelines
Must be a nonprofit, tax-exempt organization, or unit of government
Must produce or present ongoing arts programming
Programming must be open to the public
Must have a Unique Entity ID (UEI) from SAM.gov
New applicants must submit Intent to Apply by September 15 annually
Have 501(c)3 tax-exempt status from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service at the time of application, except for units of local government and colleges and universities
Be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland
Have operated as an arts organization or arts program for one full fiscal year and be able to submit a financial statement for the most recently completed fiscal year at the time of application
Establish that the majority of the arts activities produced and/or presented take place in Maryland
Establish that most of the arts organization's or arts program's annual expenditures are devoted to activities that occur within Maryland
Be governed by a legally-liable board of directors acting under a mission statement and budget specific to the organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Current GFO grantees may apply directly for continued funding. New applicants or organizations that did not receive FY 2026 GFO funding must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15th annually. After eligibility is determined, organizations complete a GFO application by November 15. Starting FY 2027, organizations will complete the same application on an annual basis. Every cycle, organizations will have a conversation with a GFO program director and one site visit by a public panelist. Contact Program Director if uncertain about organization classification. All applications are evaluated by a diverse panel of experts from across Maryland with expertise in varying artistic disciplines. If awarded, recipients must sign grant agreement forms and meet all reporting requirements before funds are disbursed. Recipients must file a final report in SmartSimple by specified deadlines. Webinar-based informational sessions are available on how to apply and the Intent to Apply component.

structured_extraction.program_description: A juried list of Maryland-based professional performing artists with a demonstrated history of successful touring engagements. MSAC promotes collaboration between Maryland touring artists and presenters to increase touring opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Roster membership provides artists with placement on a directory that connects them with Maryland presenters. Artists are promoted through the MSAC Arts Directory to facilitate professional touring engagements. No direct financial assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 with reviews every other month
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laura Weiss or Emily Sollenberger Dobbins
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based professional performing artists and performing groups who demonstrate a history of successful touring engagements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program does not provide funds. It provides roster placement and promotional access to the MSAC Arts Directory to connect artists with presenters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants must be Maryland residents. Groups must have at least 50% Maryland resident members and a primary place of business located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Maryland resident and 18+ years old
If a group, all members must be 18+ and at least 50% must be Maryland residents
If a group, the company's primary place of business must be located in Maryland
College and university-based performers must perform regularly off-campus for professional fees
If the company or group has its own nonprofit status, the performing ensemble must meet the eligibility criteria above
Must demonstrate a successful history of professional touring engagements
Clear, concise artist/company description suitable for venue marketing
Documentation of artistic goals, qualifications, and experience
Brief biographies of key members
Explanation of how touring aligns with artistic goals
Details on tour management and programming arrangements
Specific space requirements for performances
Three work samples demonstrating artistic quality
List of touring engagements from past three years
Standard performance contract
Examples of promotional materials
Review all eligibility requirements in the program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through SmartSimple on a rolling basis from July 2025 through March 2026, with reviews conducted every other month. Applications must include all work samples. MSAC convenes a panel of jurists who electronically review and score applications according to the review criteria, with scoring categories for description, artistic goals/qualifications, management/programming, space requirements, and supplemental materials. Applicants are notified of roster status via SmartSimple following application review.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants provided to eligible Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, and arts programs at colleges or universities to subsidize the presentation costs of performers on the Maryland Performing Artist Touring Roster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from $500 to $5,000 to subsidize presentation costs of performers on the Maryland Performing Artist Touring Roster.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, and arts programs at colleges or universities that present performing artists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Presentation costs for performers on the Maryland Performing Artist Touring Roster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible organizations in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or eligible government/higher education entity
Must present a performer on the Maryland Performing Artist Touring Roster
Fiscal sponsorships must operate under a 'Model A' agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, select an artist from the Touring Roster and contact them to negotiate performance details and fees. Then, complete and submit the application in the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications every other month. The agency notifies applicants of their status after the review. Approved applicants receive a grant agreement to process payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program honors long-term achievement in traditional arts. Distributed annually, it recognizes sustained contribution to Maryland's traditional arts community by selecting winners from nominations in three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Award winners receive a $10,000 grant that can be used at their discretion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award winners receive a $10,000 grant. Each year, six winners are selected from nominations in three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Award recipients can use the funds at their discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, places, and organizations in Maryland with long-term achievement in traditional arts practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can be used at the awardee's discretion for any purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to nominees located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must demonstrate long-term achievement in the traditional arts.
A nominee may receive the Heritage Award only once.
Awards are not given posthumously.
Self-nominations are accepted.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create a profile in MSAC's SmartSimple online system, then submit the nomination form. The form requests a description of the nominee's long-term achievement in traditional arts. Optional supplemental materials may be included. You may request the State Folklorist to review a draft of your nomination before submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national arts education program and recitation competition that introduces high school students to poetry through memorization and performance. Students select poems from an online anthology of 1,200+ poems, memorize them, and recite them in competitions. The program builds self-confidence, develops social and emotional maturity, and creates lifelong lovers of poetry. Students are judged on physical presence, voice and articulation, interpretation, evidence of understanding, overall performance, and accuracy. Competitions progress from classroom/school level to regional/state level to National Finals. Partnership between National Endowment for the Arts and Poetry Foundation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants compete in poetry recitation competitions at local, regional, and state levels. Students memorize and recite poems from the official Poetry Out Loud anthology. Monetary awards and travel stipends are provided: National Champion receives $20,000 award; State winners receive $200 award plus all-expenses-paid trip to Washington, DC for National Finals with school/organization receiving $500 for poetry materials; State runners-up receive $100 award with school/organization receiving $200 for poetry materials. A total of $50,000 in awards and stipends is distributed annually at National Finals. Students advancing to regional and state competitions receive coaching from Poetry Coaches prior to competition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Local competitions must be held by Friday, January 16, 2026. Regional competitions are February 14, 21, and 22, 2026. State competition is March 7, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Currently enrolled high school students in grades 9-12 (with limited exception for 8th graders in 9-12 classes) across the United States; Maryland high school students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Poetry materials for schools and organizations; student awards; poetry recitation competition and performance participation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: United States nationwide with state-based competition structure. In Maryland: statewide participation. Regional competitions are held in Baltimore-central, West-central, and South-central regions of Maryland. State finals are held in Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student (grades 9-12, with limited 8th grade exception)
Must be currently enrolled student or in approved homeschool or after-school program
Must register with state Poetry Out Loud coordinator
Must select and memorize poems from the official Poetry Out Loud anthology
For 2025-26, all poems must be in the public domain
Students must recite from memory
At state/national finals: three poems required (one ≤25 lines, one pre-20th century)
No props or costumes allowed
Must compete at lower level before advancing to state finals
Schools and community organizations must host local competitions by January 16, 2026 to advance winners to regional competitions
Independent or homeschooled students may register directly for regional competitions
Non-discriminatory participation policy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students participate in local level competitions held at their school, community organization, or through registered homeschool/after-school programs. Winners advance to regional competitions held in February 2026. Top finalists from regional competitions advance to the state competition held March 7, 2026. State winners advance to National Finals in Washington, DC. Awards are determined by judges' scores based on Poetry Out Loud Evaluation Criteria assessing physical presence, voice and articulation, interpretation, evidence of understanding, overall performance, and accuracy.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports professional development opportunities for independent artists and arts organizations to address identified goals or areas of growth. This grant program encourages and supports relevant professional development opportunities for artists and arts organizations throughout Maryland, helping them implement best practices by embracing growth, learning, and discovery for economic sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for participation in professional development opportunities including travel, registration, and other anticipated professional development-specific expenses. Funds support participation in identified professional development opportunities, implementation and dissemination of skills and knowledge gained. Payment is 100% of the award amount and is processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks upon execution of the grant agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and arts organizations throughout Maryland, including Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organizations in operation for one year or more, units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges/universities/schools. Fiscal sponsorships allowed under Model A sponsorship arrangements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in professional development opportunities, implementation and dissemination of skills and knowledge gained, and travel, registration, and other anticipated professional development-specific expenses. Organizations must reference the program guidelines for specific details on eligible uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible entities throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an independent artist, Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for one year or more and within grant income requirements, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school
Must describe selected professional development opportunity with details including location, dates, length, and format
Must explain artistic practice and how public experiences the work
Must identify goals or areas of growth addressed by the opportunity
Must provide clear timeline for participation and implementation of learning
Must explain selection process and history of success of chosen opportunity
Must provide detailed budget with all anticipated expenses and other funding sources
Fiscal sponsorships allowed only if operating under a Model A sponsorship model
Must meet specific grant income requirements for nonprofit organizations
Must reference program guidelines for additional eligibility details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through Smart Simple. Submit narrative responses addressing professional development opportunity description, artistic/organizational goals, timeline/schedule, selection rationale, and budget by the last day of any month for review in the following month. Panelists composed of public members representing various disciplines electronically review and score applications. Winners are notified early in the month following review, with a formal grant agreement provided. Upon execution of the agreement, payment is processed in 6-8 weeks. Recipients must file a final report online in Smart Simple.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland - Conservation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports conservation planning and implementation efforts for permanent public artwork in Maryland. Includes two funding tracks: Conservation Planning Grants (up to $10,000) for planning activities such as collection inventories, digitization of records and databases, community outreach, research, and assessments; and Conservation Implementation Grants (up to $30,000) for fully developed conservation projects including conservation activities, maintenance, and relocation efforts that maintain or improve public access to artworks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards up to $10,000 for conservation planning efforts or up to $30,000 for conservation implementation projects. Planning grants support project administration, consultancy fees, community engagement, and collection management services and technology. Implementation grants support relocating a public artwork within or to Maryland to increase public access, conservation and maintenance activities (cleaning, waxing, coating, painting, replacement or addition of components for structural integrity), landscape site improvements (drainage, plant maintenance/replacement), lighting and electrical work for accessibility and energy efficiency, identification and interpretive signage, and organization administration/project management fees (cannot exceed 10% of grant request).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)3 status based in Maryland, nonprofit fiscal sponsors, units of government, colleges, universities, schools, and individuals seeking to implement conservation planning and preservation projects for public artworks in Maryland.
