structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative and project management fees, consultant fees (conservator, artist, structural engineer, materials specialist, historian, preservationist), community engagement activities (public meetings, community education, information campaigns), collection management activities and technology (consultants, surveys, inventory work, digitization, database creation/updates, collection management software), relocating a public artwork within or to Maryland to increase public access, conservation and maintenance activities (cleaning, waxing, coating, painting, replacement or addition of components for structural integrity), landscape site improvements (drainage, plant maintenance/replacement), and lighting and electrical work for accessibility and energy efficiency (cannot exceed 10% of grant request for administrative costs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Final location of artwork to be conserved must be within Maryland. Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization with IRS 501(c)3 status based in Maryland, a nonprofit fiscal sponsor with Model A fiscal sponsorship agreement, a unit of government, a college/university, a school, or an individual
Artwork must be considered public art as defined by MSAC
Artwork must be publicly accessible
Final location of artwork must be in Maryland
Artwork must comply with local jurisdiction regulations and permitting requirements
Conservation project must be fully developed with identified project team and support/approval of artwork owners (for Implementation Grants)
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Grantees receiving PAAM Project Grants in prior fiscal year are not eligible to apply for any PAAM Project Grant in subsequent fiscal year
Indirect costs cannot exceed 10% of total grant request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through the secure online grants application software SmartSimple at marylandarts.smartsimple.com. Applicants log in or create a free account, complete and submit applications electronically with electronic signature. Technical support is available during regular office hours. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn. Grantees must file a final report in SmartSimple by the specified deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland New Artworks Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants supporting independent artists and organizations planning and implementing new public art projects with communities. The program offers two types of grants: Planning grants to support community outreach, visioning, research, artist selection, and proposal design; and Project grants to support fabrication and installation of fully designed artwork. Funds support community engagement, artist selection, design services, artwork proposal development, fabrication, installation, and related project costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two grant types: Planning grants award up to $10,000 to independent artists or organizations to support proposal design and community engagement, including administrative fees, artist fees and honorariums, consultant fees, facility rentals, software fees, and artwork proposal design and development. Project grants award up to $30,000 to organizations to support fabrication and installation of fully designed public artwork, including artist fees, contracted services such as fabricators and installers, equipment and space rentals, materials and tools, plaque and interpretive signage, artwork transportation, insurance and permitting fees, and organization administration and project management fees (capped at 10 percent of grant request).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2026 New Artworks grant applications will be accepted from September 8 through December 12, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and organizations planning new local public art projects. Independent artists must be Maryland residents, 18 or older, not enrolled in high school or degree programs, and leading the proposed artwork. Organizations must be Maryland-based nonprofits with 501(c)(3) status, fiscal sponsor organizations, units of government, colleges, universities, or schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees for community engagement and artist selection; artist fees and honorariums for proposal design and fabrication; consultant fees for design services; facility, equipment, and space rentals; software fees; artwork proposal design and development including digital renderings, shop drawings, and permit applications; plaque and interpretive signage; artwork transportation; insurance and permitting fees; organization administration and project management fees; and planning, creation, installation, and dedication of new local public art projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available across all of Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents or Maryland-based organizations. Projects must have completed community engagement and received permissions to install artwork at the time of application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's statewide property tax credit program, created in 1975 (previously known as the circuit breaker credit), that provides tax relief to homeowners based on household income in relation to total property tax obligation. The program serves homeowners of all ages who meet income requirements and occupy their property as their principal residence. The credit reduces property tax liability by limiting the tax bill to a fixed percentage of the homeowner's gross income, using a formula that compares income to the tax bill amount. Income and net worth limits vary by county (e.g., in Baltimore County, maximum household income is $60,000 and net worth excluding home value and certain retirement accounts cannot exceed $200,000). St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over who receive the credit can also receive an additional credit equal to or up to the remaining tax bill amount (less the Bay Restoration Fund fee). In Calvert County, a homestead tax credit is also available for eligible homeowners. Homeowners must be owner-occupants of their property and principal residence dwellers, and must reapply each year between February 1 and October 1. The program is administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation and implemented locally by county departments, including Calvert County and Harford County. Applicants can apply online through the state portal or Maryland OneStop, obtain a paper application from county tax collection offices or the State Assessment Office, mail the HTC-60 form to the SDAT office, apply at senior activity centers, or submit through county treasury offices in participating counties. Benefits Data Trust - Maryland Benefits Center provides assistance to low-income homeowners in completing applications. Application forms are available for multiple years (2019-2025 and 2026).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are granted to homeowners who qualify based on their household income in relation to total property tax obligation. The credit reduces property tax liability using a formula that limits the tax bill to a fixed percentage of gross income, with limits on the amount of tax billed. Income and net worth limits vary by county (e.g., in Baltimore County, household income cannot exceed $60,000 and net worth excluding home value and certain retirement accounts cannot exceed $200,000). The credit amount varies based on income level according to a provided tax limit table. Homeowner credits are displayed on tax bills and reduce the tax amount due. If the credit is issued after taxes are paid, a refund is automatically made to the taxpayer. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and over receive an additional credit equal to or up to the remaining tax bill amount (less the Bay Restoration Fund fee). Upon approval, homeowners receive a revised tax bill from the county treasurer's office reflecting the credit. Homeowners must be owner-occupants of the property and must reapply each year. Property taxes eligible for this credit do not include metropolitan charges, buildings or portions used for business purposes, taxes for excess land acreage, or other buildings. Supplemental credits are available in Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Charles, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington counties.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation to request an application form or apply online through the state portal at https://www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov or through Maryland OneStop. Download the HTC-60 form from the SDAT website, complete the form with required documentation, and mail the signed application to Maryland State Assessments and Taxation, 301 W Preston Street, 9th Floor, Room 900, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. The State Assessment Office can be reached at 410-996-2760 or sdat.cec@maryland.gov. Applications can also be obtained from county finance offices, tax collection offices, all senior activity centers, or the Caroline County Tax Office at 109 Market Street Room 133, Denton, Maryland 21629. Tax Credit Services are available for in-person assistance at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202. The same application serves for both state and county credit programs. Applications must be filed between February 1 and October 1 of each year. Charles County residents can submit applications through the county treasury office at 301-645-0685. Applications are also available at senior centers in Calvert County and Harford County. Contact SDAT at 800-944-7403 to check application status. Benefits Data Trust - Maryland Benefits Center will help low-income homeowners complete their applications. File by October 1st to have credit shown on tax bill. If applying after May 1st, approved credits will be refunded by county finance office. Applicants submit an annual application with instructions provided by the State of Maryland. Application forms are available for multiple years (2019-2025 and 2026). Complete the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Application Form HTC and submit to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The SDAT will review the application to determine if all qualifications have been met. Applicants must apply through their local county with applications required annually. Calvert County residents can submit applications through the county treasurer's office. Harford County residents can submit applications through local Harford County offices.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund that helps licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland pay for national accreditation fees and reimburses expenses related to Maryland Accreditation. The program covers required application fees charged by national accrediting organizations for initial accreditation applications, renewal applications, and annual updates, as well as instructional materials required for pursuing Maryland Accreditation. Support funds help child care programs achieve Quality Rating 5 in Maryland EXCELS and cover costs associated with obtaining accreditation through organizations such as the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC) and other recognized accrediting organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses or covers required application fees charged by national accrediting organizations for initial accreditation applications, renewal applications, and annual updates, as well as instructional materials required for licensed child care centers to pursue Maryland Accreditation. For national accreditation, funds are paid directly to the accrediting organization. For Maryland Accreditation instructional materials, reimbursement up to $2,500 (for programs serving ≤100 children) or $3,000 (for programs serving >100 children) covers non-consumable learning materials including books, curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, and dramatic play items. Support funds help cover the costs associated with obtaining National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC) accreditation and other accreditation expenses to help programs achieve Quality Rating 5 in Maryland EXCELS.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland seeking national or Maryland accreditation, including those pursuing accreditation through the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC) and other recognized accrediting organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Required application fees for national accreditation (initial application, renewal application, annual update) and non-consumable instructional materials associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation, such as classroom learning materials, books, puppets, science materials, physical development toys, musical instruments, dramatic play items, blocks, curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, and sensory materials for infants, toddlers, preschool, and school-age programs. Expenses related to obtaining accreditation through the National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC) and other accreditation organizations. Consumable items such as paint, crayons, markers, glue, and paper are not reimbursable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland child care programs in Maryland.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course with no cost to participants. Training covers health and safety topics relevant to Office of Child Care Code of Maryland Regulations. Participants access course online at https://msde.instructure.com, complete four modules with reflection questions, and submit a final review and survey. Upon scoring 80% or higher, participants immediately receive a certificate of completion that must be printed before course end date. Participants allowed up to four attempts on final review. No face-to-face support provided by MSDE, but approved face-to-face trainers available for a fee. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens monthly for one week: April cohort closes March 23; May cohort closes April 23; June cohort closes May 23. Training must be completed by course end date (typically 21 days after start). New employees have 90 days from hire date to complete course.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland. Also available to family child care providers and early childhood educators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training covers health and safety competencies required by state and federal regulations, including best practices related to Office of Child Care Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR) and breastfeeding awareness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all child care providers in Maryland. Online training available statewide through Canvas platform. Spanish language version available through Penn State Better Kid Care (fee charged for processing). Face-to-face training available through approved trainers listed on the website. Statewide coverage including Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Howard County, Eastern Shore, and Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Participants must have a valid email address to register
Participants must have basic technical skills including using a mouse, typing, using email, viewing videos, navigating internet, and printing from browser
Must score minimum 80% on all topic reviews and final review to receive certificate
Must complete all four modules and final review and survey
Must print certificate before course end date
Child care providers must complete training to meet Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) requirements
All staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for care and safety of children in licensed programs must complete training
Newly approved family child care providers and staff hired October-December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026; all others by December 31, 2025 for annual update
New employees must complete course within 90 days of hire date
Two to four attempts allowed on Final Assessment/Review
Must complete Introduction module first before other modules unlock
Must complete training within assigned course period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration opens for one week each month (specific dates posted). Register by completing registration form on website or directly at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas. Upon registration, participants receive email with login instructions and course access information. Participants log into learning management system (Canvas) using email address as username. Complete Introduction module first. Complete all remaining modules (can be done in any order once Introduction is complete). Participants can stop and return without starting over. Once ready, complete final review and survey in one sitting. System immediately scores final review. Print certificate from account before course end date. Certificate must be saved, emailed, or printed as copies will not be provided by MSDE after course expires. For annual updates, access MSDE Canvas Welcome Page, click Educator Resources, then Early Childhood Modules, then Basic Health and Safety Annual Update.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to eligible students who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals to attend participating nonpublic schools in Maryland. Priority is given to students who received BOOST scholarships in the previous year and their siblings. During 2025-2026, nearly 2,800 low-income students received awards at 175 nonpublic schools across 19 jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards sent directly to participating nonpublic schools. Scholarships fund tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals. Award amounts depend on household income, academic level, and school financial assistance. Scholarships may be reduced if they exceed tuition owed to the school. Estimated $9,000,000 funding available plus carryover funds with approximately 2,500 awards estimated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 8, 2026, No later than 11:59 p.m. EDT (parent applications); March 6, 2026 (nonpublic school applications)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn, Program Manager; James Clark, Administrative Support
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students eligible for free or reduced-price school meals (FARMs) who are enrolled or accepted at participating nonpublic schools for grades kindergarten through 12th grade. Parents/guardians of eligible students and nonpublic schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarship funds can be used to pay tuition and required fees at participating nonpublic schools. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals. Awards may be reduced to not exceed the tuition owed after accounting for school discounts and financial assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland at participating nonpublic schools that hold a certificate of approval or are registered with the State Board of Education, are approved for the Nonpublic Textbook Program, and provide more than only pre-K and kindergarten education.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs)
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades 1st through 12th grade (Pre-K and Kindergarten students not eligible)
Parents must submit 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income verification
Household income and size compared against FARMs income eligibility guidelines
Business losses cannot reduce income calculation
Interest, dividends, IRA distributions, pensions, annuities, and social security benefits counted as household income
Free/reduced meals eligibility does not guarantee BOOST eligibility
Limited funding available; priority given to prior year BOOST award recipients
Nonpublic schools must report certified and non-certified teachers by subject area
Schools must report student withdrawals/expulsions with reasons and days attended
Schools must administer approved national, norm-referenced standardized assessments in English Language Arts, Math, and Science
Schools must confirm student enrollment and report tuition, financial aid, special education fees, and IEPs/504 plans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable. They upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income and household size verification. The application period for the 2026-2027 school year runs from March 9 to May 8, 2026, with no later submission than 11:59 p.m. EDT. Parents can request to edit applications if school changes. Applicants notified by August 2026 of award status. Awards offered through December 11, 2026 as parents decline and waiting list moves forward. BOOST staff review applications and the Advisory Board determines award amounts based on household income, academic level, and school financial assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership with CVS Health, the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC), and the Maryland Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians. The program includes 14 weeks of classroom instruction covering CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements, followed by 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training in CVS pharmacies throughout Maryland. Training is offered at the DORS WTC location with externship placements in local CVS pharmacy locations. Upon completion, participants are prepared to take the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board test.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 14 weeks of classroom instruction covering CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements, followed by 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training in CVS pharmacies throughout Maryland. Training is offered at the DORS WTC location with externship placements in local CVS pharmacy locations. Participants receive mock pharmacy practice and training to prepare for the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board test.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are 18 years of age or older and interested in becoming Certified Pharmacy Technicians and working in retail pharmacy environments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for pharmacy technician certification, including classroom instruction, mock pharmacy practice, and on-the-job externship experience in CVS pharmacies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training is based at the DORS WTC location with externship placements in CVS pharmacies located throughout Maryland.

Have the desire to work in a retail environment
Ability to provide excellent customer service to the public
Be detail oriented
Be able to change from one task to another

Have close visual acuity

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship and professional development funding for child care providers and staff participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program to pursue college degrees in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education, as well as broader career development and professional growth opportunities. Payments are made directly to the college or university rather than reimbursing participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funding provided directly to accredited colleges and universities to support degree completion in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, and Special Education. Also provides career and professional development funding for child care providers. Available for associate and bachelor's degree programs at accredited institutions recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program seeking professional development and career advancement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College degree completion in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at accredited institutions, as well as professional development and credentialing for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for eligible child care providers and staff in Maryland participating in the credentialing program
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider or staff member
Must be participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program
Must enroll in an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Degree must be in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested participants should apply through MSDE. MSDE will notify applicants of whether or not they have received fund approval. Participating institutions with an asterisk in the program listings have special partnership arrangements with CCCPDF. Visit the MSDE Office of Child Care website for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week vocational training course in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities for certification as childcare providers. The program combines classroom instruction covering child growth and development, activity management, communication skills, infant and toddler care, school-age child care, and First Aid/CPR certification with a nine-week paid community-based internship at an approved and licensed childcare facility. Participants earn First Aid and CPR certification and job training leading to childcare provider employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 16 weeks of classroom instruction at DORS' WTC campus covering child development, activity management, communication skills, infant and toddler care, school-age child care, First Aid and CPR certification, plus a nine-week paid community-based internship at a licensed childcare facility. Participants receive comprehensive job training and certification leading to childcare provider employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old and interested in becoming certified childcare providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and internship opportunity leading to employment certification as a child care provider.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select locations throughout Maryland, including DORS' Workforce Training Center campus in Northeast Baltimore.
requirements_list: At least 18 years of age
Background check and health clearance required
6th grade reading comprehension level and basic math skills
High school diploma, GED, or certificate
Basic computer knowledge
Ability to lift and move children up to 30 pounds or more
Ability to see details at close range
Ability to hear and give verbal instructions in noisy conditions
Ability to change from one task to another
Ability to supervise children independently
Job seeker with a disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information. Request DORS Services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to child care facilities and family providers to improve and enhance the quality of care for children. Grants support projects that improve the professionalism and quality of child care programs and initiatives that improve children's school readiness. Funds help providers acquire supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments and implement curriculum aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines. Grants are awarded quarterly based on facility size, with facilities receiving up to $1,000 to $2,500 depending on capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Quarterly grant awards based on facility size. Facilities with fewer than 10 children may receive up to $1,000. Facilities with 10 to 29 children may receive up to $1,500. Facilities with more than 30 children may receive up to $2,500. Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October. Each child care provider is eligible for a grant award once every three years. Funds support the purchase of supplies, materials, and equipment that directly benefit child care quality and implementation of curriculum aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications accepted quarterly; check back after December 1, 2022 for FY23 information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care homes and family child care providers operating in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplies, materials, and equipment to improve and enhance the quality of child care, create stimulating learning environments, and implement knowledge gained through training. Eligible and non-eligible expenses are detailed in the program guide.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland licensed child care facilities and family providers
requirements_list: Possess a current license or letter of compliance
Operate a licensed child care facility or family child care home
Currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Complete a full grant application with responses to every statement
Itemize all supplies, materials, and equipment with costs
Provide description of how each item will improve quality of care
Provide FEIN or SSN identification per site (required for multiple awards)
Have not received a grant award within the past three years
Implement a curriculum which aligns with the standards established by the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines
Meet additional requirements specific to child care centers or family child care homes as outlined in program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed grant application to the Credentialing Branch or Workforce Advancement Branch. One application per child care facility is required; providers operating multiple sites must submit separate applications with FEIN/SSN identification for each site. Applicants will be notified in writing of approval or disapproval. Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October. The revised Grant Information Guide and Application are available or coming soon and will be distributed through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship Program is a state and federally-funded assistance program administered statewide by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps eligible families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. The program is funded through the Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF), a federal and state partnership that provides subsidies for child care services to eligible low-income families. The program provides financial assistance to working families, those attending school, or those in approved training programs through partnerships with licensed child care centers, licensed family child care homes, and informal care providers. Families receive payment scholarships to cover part of their child care costs, with scholarship amounts based on established state rates, family income level, number of children, and type of care provider. The program offers temporary 60-day scholarships while applications are processed, as well as full 52-week scholarships for ongoing child care assistance. Family co-payments vary based on family size and income but are $0 for recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income. Scholarships are available for children younger than 13, or individuals ages 13-19 with a qualifying disability. The scholarship can be used to pay for before and after school child care. Payments are made directly to providers after all documentation is received and clearances are approved. The program also supports child care providers' implementation of health, safety, quality, and staffing requirements to improve the quality of child care across Maryland, with reimbursement rates adjusted based on geographic location, provider type, and child age. The program serves both families and informal child care providers (relatives and non-relatives) offering scholarships for informal child care services in addition to formal licensed care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships from the state to cover part of their child care costs at licensed child care centers, licensed family child care homes, or informal child care providers. The scholarship shows the scholarship rate (the part of child care costs the state pays) and the family co-payment (the amount the family pays). Temporary 60-day scholarships are available for eligible applicants during application processing, followed by full 52-week scholarships if all required documentation is submitted within 15 days. Scholarship amounts are based on established state rates and the family's income level. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income have a $0 co-payment. Scholarship rates vary by family size and the number of children receiving scholarships, with reduced co-payments for multiple children. Families are responsible for paying their co-payment and any amounts not covered by the scholarship directly to their child care provider. Payments are made directly to child care providers after all documentation is received and clearances are approved, with minimum processing time of 60 days. The program includes analysis of cost of care by geographic location, provider category, and age of child to ensure adequate reimbursement rates. Scholarships are issued for two-year terms upon approval. Direct payment to informal child care providers occurs biweekly after receiving completed invoices from approved providers. MSDE does not provide back payments for services provided before approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families starting May 1, 2025; Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before scholarship end date to avoid payment breaks or at least 15 days before end date; Fast-Track applications processed within 3 business days; Full applications determination may take up to 35 calendar days
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-877-227-0125 (office hours 8:00 am - 5:00 pm); 855-435-7410 (after hours: Tuesday-Thursday 5:00 pm - 9:00 pm, Saturday 9:00 am - 12:00 pm)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families in Maryland with children under 13 or ages 13-19 with qualifying disabilities who are working, in approved training programs, or attending school, and meet income guidelines. Families receiving SNAP, WIC, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), WAG, General Business Income (GBI), or Housing Assistance. Migrant workers, homeless individuals, emancipated minors, and individuals paying child support. Parenting youth in out-of-home care. The program also serves licensed child care providers (Licensed Child Care Centers, Family Child Care Homes, Large Family Child Care Homes) and informal child care providers (relatives and non-relatives) who are approved to accept scholarship funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care and early education program costs at licensed child care centers, licensed family child care homes, or informal child care providers (relatives or non-relatives in the child's home). The scholarship can be used to pay for before and after school child care, extended evening/overnight hours (7pm-6am), and summer care. Funds support provider implementation of health, safety, quality, and staffing requirements. Care may be provided at Maryland registered family homes, Maryland licensed child care centers, or by informal providers in home settings. Informal non-relative care must take place in the child's home; informal relative care can take place in the parent's home or relative's home. Providers eligible for up to 14 days of voluntary closure pay per year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland in seven regional areas (Regions U, V, W, X, Y, Z, and Baltimore City). Families must be Maryland residents with proof of Maryland residency required (utility bill, lease, apartment or house lease, electric, gas, water, or phone bill). Children must be cared for at Maryland registered family homes, Maryland licensed child care centers, or by informal providers (relatives or non-relatives in home settings). Changes of address only accepted within Maryland. Informal providers must have valid Maryland driver's license or government-issued ID with current address. Applicants must disclose if they have lived outside Maryland in the past 5 years.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident with proof of residency
Must be working/employed, in an approved training program, or attending school (both parents must meet this requirement if both live in the same household)
Must be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income or have income below the income guidelines
Child must be immunized to Maryland state standards or have documentation supporting exemption
Must provide proof that each child is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Must provide photo ID for head of household
Family income must be below the Initial Income Scale for new applications or Continuation Income Scale for existing participants
Child must be younger than 13 years old, or 13-19 years old with a qualifying disability
Must register in the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal
Must provide verification of wages/salary (most recent 4 weeks of pay stubs or employer letter) or proof of training/school attendance
Must provide proof of address (apartment or house lease; electric, gas, water, or phone bill)
Parent must be engaged in approved work, education, and/or training activity
Must pursue court-ordered child support, voluntary child support, or have good cause for not pursuing

If using non-relative informal provider: provider must be at least 18 years old, consent to criminal background checks, and pass health and safety exam. All household members 18+ must pass criminal background checks and CPS clearance.

Redetermination required for continued eligibility; redetermination applications available 45 days before eligibility period ends

Applicants receiving certain benefits may qualify for co-payment waivers under HB 1121

Families must meet income eligibility requirements
Child(ren) birth certificates or proof of age required
Social Security Numbers optional but may be required
Child care provider information required
Active scholarship required for address or circumstance changes
Must provide 5-day advance notice when changing providers
Must have no outstanding balance with current provider
Blood-lead testing documentation for children under 6 years old

For informal providers: criminal background check (FBI fingerprints) required every 5 years; Child Protective Services record review (notarized consent) required annually; Health & Safety Standards compliance required; 3-hour Basic Health & Safety Training plus 1.5-hour annual update required; safe home environment (utilities, sanitation, hazard-free); proper storage of harmful items; SIDS prevention compliance; child abuse/neglect/mistreatment prevention standards; transportation safety (car seats per Maryland law); Emergency Preparedness Plan required; Disaster supply kit required; all adults 18+ in home must complete background checks and CPS clearance; maximum 6 children in care with no more than 2 under age 2; Pediatric First Aid and CPR/AED certification required; no alcohol, cannabis, or illegal substances during care hours; Emergency Care & Medication Authorization Form required; parent visitation rights must be allowed; no substitute providers allowed; incident reporting within 24 hours; annual consent form signature required; background checks (federal, state, interstate) every 5 years; physical examination documentation required for children; age-appropriate immunization documentation per MDH COMAR regulations required; proof of relatedness required for relative informal care; valid Maryland driver's license or government-issued ID with current address required; Social Security Number or ITIN required; current Maryland Department of Health Immunization Certificate (MDH 896) or acceptable alternative required; safe sleep practices and firm, flat, non-inclined surfaces required; food allergy preparedness required; infectious disease prevention required; no more than 5 working days' notice to stop caring for child
For informal providers: must maintain sign-in/sign-out logs and invoices; must submit attendance documentation

At DHS/TCA referral: Fast Track and Full Application must be completed prior to referral submission; scholarship and approved activity start dates must be within 10 days of referral submission; family must be registered on Child Care Scholarship Portal; provider must be TCA-approved activity

At out-of-home (OOH) care referral: Fast Track and Full Application must be completed prior to DHS referral submission; at redetermination, if parent is over 22 years old or no longer in OOH care, must meet all standard CCS program eligibility requirements; Child Care Scholarship and OOH activity start dates must be within 10 days of referral submission

For Head Start referral: child must be enrolled in Head Start; family must meet Head Start eligibility requirements; at least one child must be Head Start-enrolled; US citizenship verification required; families must register with Child Care Scholarship Family Portal (CCSF Portal)
For homelessness application: family must meet McKinney-Vento homelessness criteria (lack fixed residence, doubled-up, shelters, cars/parks, migratory status, etc.)
Informal provider inspection and monitoring prior to approval and at least once every 12 months required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families submit applications and redeterminations online through the Family Child Care Portal at family.childcareportals.org or through Money4ChildCare.com. Three application types available: Fast Track (3 business days), Full Application (up to 35 calendar days), and New Application. Step 1: Create an account in the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal or go to the portal and click 'Register for a New Account.' Step 2: Complete and submit the Fast Track online scholarship application with three documents: proof of employment or enrollment in training/school, proof of residency (utility bill, lease, apartment or house lease, electric, gas, water, or phone bill), and proof of income. Step 3: Fast Track application is processed within 3 business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, receive a temporary 60-day scholarship to help with child care costs. Within 15 days, submit additional information and documentation for consideration of a full 52-week scholarship. Complete documentation includes four recent consecutive pay stubs, proof of identity for all household members, proof of approved activity (work, school, or job training), proof of other income, and proof of address. Payment is not made until all documentation is received, clearances are approved, and the provider is approved by the Office of Child Care. Minimum processing time is 60 days. If the additional information and documentation is provided within 15 days of submitting the fast-track application, the family will be notified of 52-week scholarship eligibility before the temporary scholarship expires. Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before scholarship end date to avoid payment breaks or at least 15 days before end date. For informal child care provider applications or renewals, applicants contact CCS Central 2 at 877-227-0125 or email CCS.InformalProviders@maryland.gov or healthandsafetyocc.msde@maryland.gov. Informal providers submit Informal Provider Initial Application, Emergency Preparedness Plan, Emergency Care & Medication Authorization Form, and supporting documentation via Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org/. All forms and documents must be signed and dated; electronic signatures not acceptable. Support is available in multiple languages by calling the helpline and requesting an interpreter. Completed forms and documentation can be submitted online through the portal or downloaded from money4childcare.com. Families receiving referrals from Department of Human Services (DHS) may use MORA referral forms. Families experiencing homelessness may use homelessness coversheet with form completed and submitted by authorized staff (MSDE, DHS, Family Resource Specialist, or Shelter/Transitional Staff). Head Start participants may use Head Start referral form; Head Start emails referral after CCS Application submission; completed Head Start Referral provided to enrolled family; Head Start staff verifies enrollment and signs referral. Child care providers (informal and formal) register for provider account at https://provider.childcareportals.org/, complete user registration with required fields, agree to Know Your Rights disclosures, create password via verification code sent to email, and access portal dashboard to manage programs, scholarships, attendance, invoicing records, and documentation. Providers must approve or deny scholarship requests within five business days. Providers must maintain sign-in/sign-out logs and invoices and submit attendance documentation. For DHS/TCA referrals, parent completes Fast Track and Full Application on Child Care Scholarship Portal; DHS/MORA representative completes referral form. For out-of-home (OOH) care referrals, form is completed by authorized DHS staff and submitted to ccscentral2dhsreferral.msde@maryland.gov. For Head Start referrals: families register with CCSF Portal and submit CCS Application; Head Start emails referral after CCS Application submission. For homelessness applications, submission is via https://family.childcareportals.org. Informal provider inspections occur prior to initial approval and at least once every 12 months thereafter, with monitoring to ensure compliance with COMAR # 13A.14.06.11.F.12(b) informal child care inspection standards. Non-compliances must be corrected; providers submit Summary of Correction in response to identified violations.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's program to ensure quality of training offered to child care professionals. The program approves individuals and organizations to provide training in accordance with state regulations. Approved trainers can develop and deliver training accepted for the Maryland Child Care Credential and continued education to meet licensing requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program approves trainers and training organizations to provide quality training to child care professionals. Approved trainers receive an approval number valid for 4 years and can deliver training that counts toward the Maryland Child Care Credential and licensing requirements. Trainers can attend Quarterly Trainers Meetings for continued professional development and renewal requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 30 days prior to approval number expiration for renewals; bi-monthly review schedule for new applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care trainers and training organizations in Maryland who work with child care professionals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training delivery and professional development for approved trainers and child care professionals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to trainers and organizations across Maryland
requirements_list: Must comply with COMAR 13A.14.08 regulations
Must abide by ethical standards
Required to complete Training Orientation before submitting application
Must submit training proposal for review
Renewal applicants must submit applications 30 days prior to expiration of approval number
Renewal requires 24 hours of training in adult training or approved subject/domains
All quarterly training reports must be submitted for renewal
Trainer approval numbers must be designated on training certificates issued to child care professionals
Must attend minimum 2 quarterly trainer meetings for renewal
Training content must align with Core of Knowledge content areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first register for and complete the required Training Orientation. After orientation, applicants submit a Training Approval Application and required supporting documentation electronically via email or Google Forms. The Training Review Team, composed of advanced trainers and Workforce Advancement Branch staff, reviews proposals within 60 days using an established rubric. Review sessions are conducted every other month and approval letters are generated following these sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal reimbursement program that provides nutritionally balanced meals and snacks to children (including infants) at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, and emergency shelters, and to adults over 60 or living with disabilities enrolled in adult daycare facilities. The program supports healthy growth, development, and wellness through reimbursement to over 300 participating agencies across Maryland that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Funds help offset meal and supplement costs to public, private nonprofit, and proprietary centers licensed to provide non-residential childcare and adult daycare services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CACFP reimburses child and adult care agencies with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns, as well as Dietary Guidelines for Americans. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Over 300 agencies across the state participate in the program. Federal reimbursement is available to participating child care facilities, family child care providers, and adult care centers. Reimbursement covers breakfast, lunch, and snacks served to eligible participants. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Infants and young children enrolled at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, and emergency shelters; adults over 60 or living with disabilities enrolled in daycare facilities; children and youths in emergency shelters. Licensed daycare homes and non-residential adult daycare centers, including public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers. Family child care home participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns and Dietary Guidelines for Americans, including breakfast, lunch, and snacks. Funds help pay for the cost of meals and snacks for participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through over 300 participating agencies. Family Child Care Providers participate through specific sponsoring organizations serving designated county regions.
requirements_list: Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services
Children must be enrolled at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, or emergency shelters
Adults must be over 60 years old or living with disabilities and enrolled in daycare facilities
Meals and snacks must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Facility must be participating childcare center, daycare home, afterschool care program, or emergency shelter for children
For Family Child Care Providers: review Sponsoring Agency contact information on CACFP page
All others: call OSCNP to determine eligibility
Participating providers must serve nutritious meals meeting USDA standards
Complete CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet
Complete CACFP Basics Training
Complete three-part online application
Pass pre-approval visit by MSDE
Meet eligibility criteria determined by MSDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested child and adult care agencies should download the Child and Adult Care Food Program flyer to apply. Eligible childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool programs, emergency shelters, and adult daycare facilities may participate through enrollment in CACFP administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Family Child Care Providers should contact their county's sponsoring agency to get started, or call OSCNP at (410) 767-0199 to determine eligibility. Providers must complete CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet, complete CACFP Basics Training, complete a three-part online application, and pass a pre-approval visit by MSDE. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).

structured_extraction.program_description: A meal service option that allows schools and school districts in low-income areas to serve breakfast and lunch at no cost to enrolled students without collecting household income applications. This program promotes equity and access to nutritious meals during the school day. Eligible schools with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher can elect to participate and serve free meals to all students without requiring families to submit income verification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools and school districts with an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher are eligible to elect CEP. Eligible students receive free breakfast and lunch during the school day at no cost to students or families, regardless of income. Schools serve meals without requiring household income applications. The program streamlines meal service operations and reduces administrative costs for schools and school districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students enrolled in schools and school districts with an Identified Student Percentage of 25% or higher in low-income areas across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of free breakfast and lunch meals to students during the school day.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to schools and school districts in low-income areas that meet the Identified Student Percentage threshold of 25% or higher.
requirements_list: Schools and school districts must have an Identified Student Percentage (ISP) of 25% or higher
Identified students are those directly certified for free meals based on participation in other programs such as SNAP or TANF
Schools must be located in low-income areas meeting CEP income thresholds
Schools may opt into CEP to serve free meals to all students
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and school districts with the required Identified Student Percentage can elect to participate in CEP. Interested schools should contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Program (OSCNP) at 410-767-0199 to determine CEP eligibility and implementation.

structured_extraction.program_description: CCEIS is a federal requirement under IDEA that mandates local education agencies identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B funding to implement a comprehensive system of proactive and responsive actions addressing root cause factors contributing to overidentification. The program focuses on identifying and addressing factors such as lack of access to scientifically based instruction, economic/cultural/linguistic barriers, inappropriate disciplinary removals, lack of diagnostic screenings, and achievement gaps.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified with significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement comprehensive coordinated early intervening services. Funding supports educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports, including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development; systemic organizational change efforts; staff training and coaching; and systemic awareness and leadership supports to address root causes of disproportionality in identification, placement, and discipline. Allowable uses include staff salaries (general education teachers, guidance counselors, psychologists, social workers, RTI coordinators, coaches, tutors, substitute teachers), extended contracts/hours for intervention staff, computing devices for intervention delivery, instructional materials and software for struggling students, and travel costs for CCEIS-related activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple reporting deadlines: January 31, 2025; January 31, 2026; August 15, 2026; November 30, 2026. Interim Report 1: January 31; Interim Report 2: January 31; Final Report: November 30
structured_extraction.contact_name: Marcella E. Franczkowski, Assistant State Superintendent
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies identified by the State as having data indicating significant disproportionality over-identification based on racial or ethnic group in special education identification, placement, or discipline. Students ages 3-21, including children not identified as requiring special education but needing additional academic/behavioral support, and children currently identified as requiring special education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and support including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development; self-assessment and root cause analysis; staff training and coaching; systemic awareness and leadership supports; stakeholder engagement; evaluation of plan outcomes; and implementation of proactive and responsive actions to address disproportionality. Staff salaries (general education teachers, guidance counselors, psychologists, social workers, RTI coordinators, coaches, tutors, substitute teachers); extended contracts/hours for intervention staff; computing devices for intervention delivery; instructional materials and software for struggling students; and travel costs for CCEIS-related activities. All funding must supplement (not supplant) state, local, and other federal funds per IDEA 34 CFR § 300.202(a)(3).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland local education agencies meeting the disproportionality criteria.
requirements_list: Local education agency must be identified as having one or more subgroups of students evidencing a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years (unless the risk ratio declines by a defined amount from one year to the next)
Must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds
Must address factors contributing to significant disproportionality
Must address and review any policy, practice, or procedure identified as contributing to overidentification
Must establish diverse stakeholder group
Must conduct self-assessment and data review to determine root cause factors
Must develop comprehensive system for evaluation of plan outcomes
Funds must address significant disproportionality in identified category(ies)
Staff must be appropriately licensed to provide academic instruction
Materials and software must be exclusively for intervention students, not core curriculum
Proper time and effort records required
Local System Team responsible for co-development, data input/root cause analysis, co-implementation, and co-evaluation
Required local system signatures: Special Education Director, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, Superintendent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Identified LEAs develop a CCEIS plan using the SFY 2025 Comprehensive Coordinated Early Intervening Services Plan Template. Plans must include root cause analysis, specific actions to mitigate root causes, aligned budget expenditures (Form C-1-25 and Budget Detail), and evaluation measures. Submit plan to the Maryland Department of Education. Progress reports must be submitted using the CCEIS Progress Report Template. Amendments to plans and budgets use designated amendment templates. Required reporting: Interim Progress/Cumulative Variance Reports (2 reports) and Grant Amendments. Required MSDE signatures: DEI/SES Equity Specialist, Fiscal Liaison, Resource Management and Monitoring Branch Chief, Assistant State Superintendent.

structured_extraction.program_description: Introduces Pre-ETS students with Autism to education, training, and employment options available after high school. Includes apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college preparation. Provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training, and develops soft skills needed to get and keep a job.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Self-advocacy instruction, social skills training, soft skills development, college tours, and career exploration activities. Includes classroom and other activities exposing Pre-ETS students with Autism to post-secondary options such as apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, ages 14-21, currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, college, or trade school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and exposure to post-secondary education and career training opportunities, including college tours, self-advocacy instruction, social skills training, and soft skills development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Pre-ETS students with Autism.
requirements_list: Currently enrolled in high school, post-secondary education program, college, or recognized educational program
At least 14 years old but less than 22
Has IEP, 504 plan, or medical records documenting disability
Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Counselor or local office for more information. Request DORS Services via QR code. Pre-ETS students with Autism can participate in classroom and other activities focused on post-secondary education options and participate in college tours.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registered apprenticeships that combine paid employment with on-the-job training from skilled craftspeople and related classroom instruction. Apprentices are sponsored by employers or associations and paid on progressive pay scales. DORS also provides consultation and support services for people with disabilities interested in exploring, accessing, and participating in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Services include apprenticeship consultation, academic assessment, exploration of opportunities, academic instruction, pre-apprenticeship support, registered apprenticeship support, and youth apprenticeship support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Connection to existing apprenticeship programs or development of customized registered apprenticeship programs with recruitment support through American Job Centers. Registered apprenticeships are paid jobs lasting one to five years with a minimum of 2,000 hours of on-the-job training per year and 144 hours of classroom instruction per year, with progressive wage increases as skills develop. DORS provides consultation, assessment, and support services to help individuals with disabilities prepare for, apply to, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs, including apprenticeship coordination, academic assessments, academic instruction, and ongoing support throughout the apprenticeship journey.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 18+ seeking apprenticeships; employers seeking to hire apprentices. Also serves Marylanders with disabilities interested in pursuing registered apprenticeships, including those pursuing or enrolled in Pre-Apprenticeship, Registered Apprenticeship, or Youth Apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and wages for apprentices; program administration. Apprenticeships are paid positions that provide wages and training in skilled trades across various industries including traditional trades, mental health, and information technology. Funds support preparation for and participation in registered apprenticeship programs, including academic assessment, skills evaluation, academic preparation, and testing preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Be 18 years of age
Have high school diploma (graduation, GED, or NEDP)
Be drug free
Have transportation
Be physically able to perform required tasks
Must be a DORS consumer (for DORS participants)
Must have a disability (for DORS participants)
Must be interested in pursuing a registered apprenticeship
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For apprentices: Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com; contact navigator at (410) 767-2246 or email info@mdapprenticeship.com; apply directly to program sponsor/employer. For employers: Call apprenticeship navigator; navigator connects with existing program or helps develop customized program; present plan for approval to Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council; recruit through American Job Centers. DORS participants should contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator to discuss apprenticeship interests and receive assessments.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS provides vocational rehabilitation services to individuals with disabilities, including assistive technology assessment and equipment provision to help develop employment skills and start or expand businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS assesses clients for assistive technology needs and provides or orders equipment and supplies to support employment and business development. In this case, equipment included a 3D printer, pad, resins, and trays to help convert a hobby into a business.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking vocational rehabilitation and employment support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology assessment and equipment provision to support employment skills development and business creation or expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a disability requiring vocational rehabilitation services
Must be developing an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS to request vocational rehabilitation services and meet with a rehabilitation counselor who will develop an IPE tailored to the individual's employment goals and needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Specialized services tailored for deaf-blind consumers to provide support needed to integrate into society and find competitive placement in a career path of their choice. Services include specialized counseling, training, and support for employment, independent living, and community integration, with assistance in communication, career exploration, and employment placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Specialized counseling, training, and support services for individuals who are deaf-blind to assist with employment, independent living, and community integration. Services include assistance with communication, independent living skills, career services, and employment placement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are deaf-blind seeking employment, community integration, and support for independent living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Specialized support services for employment, independent living, community integration, communication support, career services, and employment placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through DORS offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Individual must have both significant hearing loss and vision loss
Individual must be eligible for DORS services
Deaf-blind status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS office or complete the Request DORS Services form to access deaf-blind services. A DORS counselor will set up an intake meeting to determine eligibility for specialized Deaf-Blind services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enhanced Child Care Support and Teacher Retention Award (ECSTRA) Retention Bonus Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides retention bonuses directly to early childhood educators to stabilize the workforce and reduce turnover in MSDE-licensed child care providers. Uses American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding. Inspired by Virginia's Teacher Recognition Program, which reduced teacher turnover by 50%. Also serves as a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to study if larger bonuses improve retention and job satisfaction. Educators who participate are entered into a lottery to determine their bonus size, and receive bonuses if they remain in the same program for at least 5 months (first half of bonus) and 8 months (second half of bonus).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Early childhood educators receive retention bonuses ranging from $0 to $3,000 per educator, funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) money. Bonus amounts are determined through a lottery system with four possible outcomes: $0, $1,000, $2,000, or $3,000. Approximately 25% of eligible applicants receive no bonus. Participants receive the first half of their bonus (approximately April 2024) after remaining employed for at least 5 months and the second half (approximately June 2024) after remaining employed for at least 8 months in the same program in an eligible role. Up to $12,550,000 total funding is available for a maximum of 7,500 eligible educators.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2023, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual early childhood educators employed by MSDE-licensed child care providers who work directly with children birth to 5 years old. Excluded are teachers employed by public school divisions, site leaders/directors who do not work directly with children, and workers not holding current Maryland credentials.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Retention bonuses for early childhood educators to encourage them to remain in their positions and reduce turnover in the child care workforce
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to early childhood educators across Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City, with program spots apportioned by jurisdiction
requirements_list: Must be an early childhood educator employed in an eligible MSDE-licensed child care role (Child Care Centers (CTRs), Letter of Compliance (LOCs), Family Child Care Homes (FCCHs), or Large Family Child Care Homes (LFCCHs))
Must work directly with children birth to 5 years old
Early childhood programs administered through local education agencies are NOT eligible
Must remain employed in the same program for at least 5 months to receive the first half of the bonus
Must remain employed in the same program for at least 8 months to receive the second half of the bonus
Must apply by the deadline
Must participate in the lottery system to determine bonus size
Must provide up-to-date and accurate employment status information to MSDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Early childhood educators submit applications by the deadline. Applications are reviewed and applicants are notified of acceptance into the program in October 2023. Selected participants are assigned bonus amounts through a lottery system. Bonuses are distributed in two halves based on continued employment duration. FAQ and answers are available, and customer service support sessions are available on the MSDE Grants office website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week hands-on training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities for employment in environmental service jobs, including floor care, cleaning, and facility maintenance. Offered at Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore with classroom and hands-on instruction.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 16-week hands-on training course covering floor care (stripping, buffing, waxing), dust and damp mopping, trash collection, office cleaning, carpet and upholstery cleaning, window cleaning, restroom cleaning, supply restocking, and stairwell cleaning. Instruction provided at the Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore. Includes both classroom and hands-on vocational training in environmental services skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking employment in environmental services and facility maintenance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational training and skills development in environmental services, including hands-on instruction in cleaning, floor care, and facility maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program offered at Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a job seeker with a disability
Ability to walk extensively
Ability to work in noisy workplaces
Ability to climb stairs
Ability to stand, stoop, bend and stretch for extended periods of time
Ability to perform repetitive tasks
Ability to work independently or in groups
Ability to measure and mix cleaners
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds
Ability to follow verbal and written directions
Strong grip strength
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Counselor or local office for information. Request DORS Services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_name: Family Child Care Provider Direct Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: One-time grants for new family child care providers starting their small business to help offset costs of opening their child care programs. The grant amount was increased from $500 to $1,000 as part of Maryland's Preschool Development Grant Birth through Age Five award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time direct grant of $1,000 to registered family child care providers who are starting a new child care business. Eligibility is based on certain income levels and family size.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New family child care providers starting a child care business in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset costs of opening child care programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Must be a new provider starting their business
Eligibility based on certain income levels and family size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the regional Office of Child Care licensing office for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Family Child Care Provider Grant Program (Eastern Shore Regional)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps registered family child care providers offset costs of opening their child care programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help registered family child care providers offset costs of opening their child care programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers in Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Offsetting costs of opening child care programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties (Region 9 - Lower Shore).
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Region 9 Office of Child Care for information about the program and application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Enriches school food offerings by connecting schools with local food producers and providing healthy food education to students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program connects schools with local agricultural producers to supply fresh foods for school meals and provides education about local food sources and healthy eating.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools seeking to source local foods and provide food education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Local food purchases for school meals and healthy food education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland for schools and local food producers.
requirements_list: Schools must be interested in sourcing foods from local agricultural producers
Participation in school nutrition programs is typically required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools interested in the Farm to School Program should contact OSCNP at 410-767-0199 to learn about implementation.
