structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) food items to eligible schools and child care facilities. These include public schools, private non-profit schools, and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides USDA food items to eligible organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible recipients include public schools, private nonprofit schools, and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides USDA food commodities for distribution.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prepares job seekers with disabilities for employment in the food service industry, including cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores. The 14-week program consists of seven weeks of classroom instruction and hands-on experience at the Workforce Training Center cafeteria, followed by a seven-week internship at a local food service business. Training covers food handling, preparation, kitchen safety, customer service, and point-of-sale skills.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fourteen-week training program including seven weeks of classroom and hands-on instruction at the WTC cafeteria, plus a seven-week internship at a local food service business. Training covers food handling and preparation, kitchen safety and equipment operation, recipe reading and following, food portions and nutrition, weighing and measuring, customer service skills, point-of-sale operations, and ServSafe® principles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking vocational training in food service who meet the physical and cognitive requirements listed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and internship program costs in food service skills for employment in food service businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in northeast Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be able to work independently
Must be able to stoop, bend, and stretch
Must be considerate and work well with others
Must communicate effectively
Must be able to follow two-step instructions
Must be able to lift and carry 30-pound food containers and trays
Must be able to stand for long periods of time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office. Request DORS Services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program for individuals with disabilities who require a high school diploma in order to pursue their employment goals. Students work individually or in small groups and enter on a rolling admission basis. All GED students are expected to take the formal GED test upon completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GED instruction is provided through individual or small group instruction at the Workforce Training Center and virtually. Students work through the program on a rolling admission basis and are expected to complete the formal GED test upon finishing the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who want a high school diploma to pursue employment goals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: GED instruction and preparation for the formal GED test
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at the Workforce Training Center and virtually
requirements_list: Individuals should have at least 8th grade reading and math skills as recorded on the CASAS or TABE
GED Ready Practice Tests may also be given
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Rehabilitation Services or visit the Workforce Training Center to enroll in the GED program. Consumers enter on a rolling admission basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Hunger Free Kid's Act Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to eligible schools and residential child care institutions. The money helps them comply with meal pattern rules established by the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct payments for specific uses to help schools and child care institutions comply with federal meal pattern rules.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help schools and child care centers meet the meal pattern requirements of the Healthy Hunger Free Kids Act of 2010.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Home Modifications Program provides home modification services to help DORS consumers achieve their employment goals. The program evaluates and improves home accessibility through assessments, construction coordination, and ongoing monitoring to ensure modifications comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides assessment of bathroom accessibility, home entry and exit, and access to different home levels. Services include coordination and scheduling of construction, ongoing onsite monitoring during construction, coordination of final inspections, and confirmation that all modifications comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DORS consumers (individuals with disabilities who are working toward employment goals)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home modifications to improve accessibility for employment purposes, including bathroom accessibility improvements, home entry and exit modifications, and access modifications to different levels of the home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to DORS consumers.
requirements_list: Individual must be a current DORS consumer
Modifications must be needed to achieve an employment goal
Modifications must be for property owned by the DORS consumer or their family
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals who are current DORS consumers can work with the WTC home modification team, which evaluates home accessibility and coordinates the modification process including construction scheduling, onsite monitoring, and final inspections.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps individuals who are 55 or older live independently in their homes and communities through in-home assessment and training services. Services include personal care and household task training, labeling and organizing items, safe cooking techniques, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, and referrals to peer support groups and community resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-home training and assessment services including personal care and household task management training, labeling and organizing items (clothing, appliances, medications), safe cooking techniques, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, and referrals to peer support groups and community services such as NFB-NEWSLINE and Maryland State Library for Blind and Print Disabled.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals 55 years or older who are blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-home training and assessment services for independent living skills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All areas of Maryland, including rural counties, served through three regional offices: Baltimore (serving Baltimore City and Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, Harford Counties), Wheaton (serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, Washington Counties), and Annapolis (serving Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester Counties).
requirements_list: Age 55 or older
Blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form or contact your local DORS office. A DORS counselor will set up an intake meeting to determine eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a teacher or counselor.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Statewide program supporting positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children with developmental, social, emotional or behavioral issues by providing referrals, services, consultation, and technical assistance for children, families, teachers, and caregivers in child care settings. Services build capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development through individualized strategies, observation, assessment, and professional consultation. Mental health professionals work with licensed early care education providers and families to help educators understand how relationships affect young children's social and emotional growth, reducing challenging behaviors and preparing children for school while decreasing expulsion rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding and technical assistance for non-profit and public agencies, as well as free mental health consultation services provided by mental health professionals. Services include referrals, direct services, consultation, and individualized strategies. Consultants gather information through observation and conversation with parents and child care staff to develop strategies to assist children in both child care settings and at home. Parents receive resources and referrals to support child development and school readiness. Information gathered from assessments may be shared with other professionals such as pediatricians, occupational therapists, and speech therapists as requested by families. Applicants/service providers must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland with capacity to provide infant and early childhood mental health services, including child care providers and early childhood programs. Families with children birth to 5 years enrolled in licensed child care programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing mental and behavioral health support services, referrals, consultation, capacity building, and technical assistance for early care and education providers and families to promote healthy social-emotional development for young children and prepare them for school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to licensed non-profit and public agencies. Services also available in Montgomery County for children enrolled in licensed child care programs. Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit or public agency (for grant recipients)
Must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland
Must have proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
Child must be birth to 5 years old (for consultation services)
Child must be enrolled in a licensed child care program (for consultation services)
Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For grant funding: Submit completed application by deadline or contact MSDE for consultation and support services. Application form available for download. MSDE offers customer service support sessions to assist applicants with understanding requirements and completing proposals. For consultation services: Call Montgomery County Child Care Support Services at 240-777-4769 to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive early childhood program serving children from birth through age 5 and their families. Provides educational programming and family support services year-round, including school readiness preparation, family engagement, developmental screenings, parenting education, adult education connections, playgroups, service referrals, early intervention identification, home visiting, and case management. Also known as the Judith P. Hoyer Early Care and Education Enhancement Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers provide or connect families with local community partners for developmental screenings, family learning activities and engagement, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, and case management with families and service coordination with community partners. Services include health-related screenings (dental, vision, hearing), mental health assessments, meals for children and families, and professional learning opportunities for partners.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children aged birth through age 5 and their families, including families in underserved communities, children with disabilities, housing-insecure children and families, and families in high-needs school catchment areas living within the school zone where a Judy Center is located.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting education, adult education connections, playgroups, service referrals, early intervention identification, home visiting, case management, health screenings, mental health assessments, meals for children and families, professional learning coordination, and school readiness assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Centers are located in Title I and high-needs elementary schools across all 24 Maryland counties. Judy Centers serve children who live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. Services are provided in schools scoring 0.6 or above on the Center for Disease Control's Social Vulnerability Index.
requirements_list: Child must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Programs must be located in Title I and high-needs schools
Sites must operate with fidelity to the program model
High-quality programming standards required
Minimum 12 meaningful interactions per year to measure impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your closest Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly to learn more and access services. Locations and contact information can be found at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program for fiscal year 2026 to support the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hubs across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hubs. Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is available.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government entities and schools eligible to expand Judy Center Early Learning Hubs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding to expand Judy Center Early Learning Hub services and locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is now available. Contact the Judy Center Program Manager for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps registered family child care providers offset costs of opening and operating their child care programs. The program reimburses up to $1,000 in eligible expenses needed to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 to help cover costs of achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations. Reimbursement is paid as a grant award for eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers in Maryland with annual income not exceeding 60% of Maryland's State Median Income based on family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water/sewer/fire/health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs necessary for completing the registration process.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to registered family child care providers.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered family child care provider
Annual family income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's State Median Income for the applicant's family size
Expenses must be related to achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application procedures are specified in COMAR 13A.14.07 regulations. More information about the application process will be available on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: A peer-support group for individuals who are blind or have low vision to meet, interact, and discuss common concerns such as relationships, independence, advocacy, responsibility and technology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Peer-support group meetings held once per week for eight weeks. Offered four times per year at the WTC, at local DORS offices as requested, and virtually via Google Meet. Maximum capacity of eight participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind or have low vision
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support and peer interaction for individuals who are blind or have low vision to discuss concerns and challenges related to blindness and low vision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at WTC, local DORS offices, and virtually.
requirements_list: Be blind or have low vision
Maximum capacity of eight participants per group
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WTC or local DORS office to participate in a group session.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_description: Authorized by the Randolph-Sheppard Act, this program provides training, licensing, and oversight for legally blind individuals to manage and operate vending facilities and retail concession and food service operations on federal, military, DOD, and state property and at business partner locations. The program prepares individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession and food service businesses in public facilities through a three-phase training program consisting of an eight-week New Manager Training course at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center, formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs (including National Restaurant Association food service sanitation certification), and on-the-job training with an extended internship of three to six months at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A three-phase business training, licensing, and preparation program to operate retail concession and food service operations in federal, military, DOD, and state property locations and business partner locations. Includes eight-week New Manager Training course at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center, formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs (including National Restaurant Association food service sanitation certification), and on-the-job training with an extended internship of three to six months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Legally blind and vision impaired U.S. citizens, including deaf-blind individuals and those over age 55, whose primary disability is vision loss and who have an aptitude for business management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating retail concession and food service facilities on state, county, and federal agency property, including approximately 50 businesses in Maryland at locations such as state office buildings in Annapolis and Baltimore, National Institutes of Health, IRS, FDA, Motor Vehicle Administration, Social Security Administration, US Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland for operations in federal, military, DOD, and state property locations and at business partner locations throughout the state.
requirements_list: Individual must be legally blind
Individual must be a U.S. citizen
Primary disability must be vision loss
High school diploma or GED equivalent required
Individual must have an aptitude for business management
Individual must have practical skills
Must meet legal criteria for operating a business
Individual must be referred by DORS OBVS counselor
Individual must complete three-phase training program successfully
Individual must obtain National Restaurant Association food service sanitation certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request DORS Services through dors.maryland.gov. Attend an intake meeting with a DORS counselor to determine eligibility. If you already have a DORS counselor, ask your counselor about BEP. DORS will contact you to set up an intake meeting where they will gather information and provide details regarding eligibility for DORS services and the Business Enterprise Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5. Participating providers demonstrate commitment to quality by meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. The program provides a road map, training, incentives, guidance from regional Quality Assurance Specialists, and learning opportunities to help providers continuously improve their quality ratings and increase the number of high-quality early childhood and school-age care programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating providers receive a road map for quality improvement, training opportunities, guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, and opportunities to learn from other providers. Providers upload evidence of meeting standards into an online system and receive ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating. Support is provided for continuous quality improvement through direct payment for specified use. Quality Assurance Specialists provide consultation and access to work groups and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care and early education programs and providers in Maryland, including school-age care programs, seeking to improve quality and demonstrate commitment to best practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program supports continuous quality improvement of services provided to families and children through training, guidance, resources, professional development, and direct payments for specified use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all child care and early education programs throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Commitment to providing quality education and care that exceeds basic licensing requirements
Operate an early childhood or school-age child care program
Participate in Maryland EXCELS by enrolling and committing to quality improvement
Demonstrate that programs meet Maryland EXCELS Standards in areas such as developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement
Publish and upload evidence of meeting standards into the online system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers can visit the program website to create an account and get started. Providers sign up to participate in Maryland EXCELS. A regional Quality Assurance Specialist provides guidance in creating and uploading evidence of meeting standards into an online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff who assign ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating.

structured_extraction.program_description: Bonus program that provides funding to early care and education providers who achieve quality ratings through the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system. Eligible programs receive bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type, quality rating, and capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs participating in Maryland EXCELS receive one-time bonus payments ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 depending on whether they publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5. Bonus amounts vary by program type (child care center, family child care, or large family home) and capacity. Bonuses are provided between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2027. For child care centers with capacity 1-50, bonuses range from $1,000 (rating 1) to $4,500 (rating 5). For centers with capacity 51-100, bonuses range from $1,000 to $9,000. For centers with capacity 101+, bonuses range from $1,000 to $13,500. Family child care programs receive $1,000 to $4,300, and large family homes receive $1,000 to $4,500. There is no application required—eligible programs automatically receive payment by check or direct deposit. Bonuses can be used for staff salary increases, purchasing learning materials, furniture, equipment, hiring qualified staff, and improving program quality.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers including child care centers, family child care providers, and large family homes participating in Maryland EXCELS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses can be used for staff salary increases, high-quality learning materials, furniture and equipment replacement, hiring additional qualified staff members, program quality improvements, and other uses at the discretion of the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all eligible Maryland child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Program must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Program must publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application is required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit within approximately 60 days of their quality rating being published. Program operators can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website after registering.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tiered reimbursement program that rewards early childhood and school-age programs for providing high-quality services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. Programs receive increased reimbursement amounts ranging from 10% to 44% based on the child's age, type of care, and the program's Maryland EXCELS quality rating level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Increased reimbursement payments to early childhood and school-age programs at Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings 3, 4, and 5. Reimbursement increases range from 10% to 44% depending on the child's age, type of care facility (family child care or child care center), and the program's quality rating level. For family child care: under 2 years receives 11% (Level 3), 22% (Level 4), or 29% (Level 5); 2 years and over receives 10% (Level 3), 21% (Level 4), or 28% (Level 5). For child care centers: under 2 years receives 22% (Level 3), 37% (Level 4), or 44% (Level 5); 2 years and over receives 10% (Level 3), 19% (Level 4), or 26% (Level 5).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood and school-age programs participating in Maryland EXCELS and the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing high-quality child care services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to programs participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must be serving families using the Child Care Scholarship program
Program must achieve and maintain Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of 3, 4, or 5 to receive reimbursement increases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs participating in Maryland EXCELS and the Child Care Scholarship program automatically receive the tiered reimbursement payments based on their quality rating level. Payments appear as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report for each child.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide resource that allows families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing to borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides videos and resources to help families learn communication methods of their choice. It serves children from birth through the end of high school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families can borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides DVDs, videos, and other materials to help families learn about language and communication options for supporting their child's development. All resources are provided at no cost.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zella Shabasson, Au.D. and Dr. Paige Bradford
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing from birth to age 21 who have not yet graduated from high school and are Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing hearing aids for trial or temporary use, and accessing educational videos and materials about language and communication methods such as American Sign Language, Cued Speech, and spoken language development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have a child diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as Deaf or Hard-of-Hearing
Child must be from birth to age 21 and not yet graduated from high school

For hearing aids: must not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, be experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, and/or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can request materials through the provided links for hearing aids, language and communication videos, and other resources for families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing. Contact the listed audiologist or section chief to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The MITP CLIG is the mechanism through which local jurisdictions, including county-level programs, receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities. Local Lead Agencies aggregate information from partner agencies to complete grant applications and coordinate services to help children reach developmental milestones and prepare for school in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and state funds distributed to local jurisdictions through Local Lead Agencies to support early intervention programs, combined with early intervention services for infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities and their families. Implementation includes direct services and support to help children reach developmental milestones and prepare for school. Grantees receive access to secure MOVEit file transfer account for submission of grant-related documents including applications, reports, and amendment requests.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Multiple deadlines throughout fiscal year 2026 (see submission timeline)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Glenn Graymen, Nancy Vorobey
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies and Local Infants & Toddlers Program partners implementing early intervention services, as well as families with infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of local early intervention programs including direct services and support for infants and toddlers with developmental delays or disabilities to help them reach developmental milestones and prepare for school.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland local jurisdictions through their Local Lead Agencies.
requirements_list: Local Infants & Toddlers Program must have a designated Local Lead Agency
Must aggregate information from LITP partner agencies
Must comply with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures
Must submit using correct and up-to-date forms
Must submit all files to MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website
Files must be correctly named and contain only one submission per upload
Must file financial reports through AFR system or Non-LEA Final Financial Report form
All submissions must be in PDF format
File naming conventions must follow specifications outlined
Documents must be uploaded to 'ToMSDE' folder
Email notification must be sent to fiscal grants liaison upon submission
Screenshot of submission timestamp recommended as proof
Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) required with Entity Code and login credentials
Only authorized individuals permitted access
Immediate deactivation notification required when employee leaves
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies complete the SFY 2026 CLIG grant application using provided forms and workbooks. Applications are submitted through the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/. Documents are uploaded by double-clicking folder and using drag-drop or click upload button. Grant administration includes multiple submission deadlines for budget amendments, financial reports, program reports, and supporting documentation throughout the fiscal year. Email notification must be sent to fiscal grants liaison with document name(s) upon submission. Applicants should download forms immediately before completion to ensure current versions are used and save screenshot of upload timestamp as proof.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides state funding to supplement federal meal reimbursements, ensuring all children in participating schools have access to nutritious free breakfast consumed in the classroom at the start of each school day. The program increases students' access to and participation in breakfast, improving students' test scores, behavior, attendance, and well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State funds supplement federal meal reimbursements to allow participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom. Currently 581 schools participate in MMFA. Participating schools receive state funding to enhance student access to nutritious breakfast.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students attending participating Maryland schools that meet economically disadvantaged criteria and school administrators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free nutritious breakfast in the classroom to students at participating schools at the start of each school day.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves participating schools across Maryland that meet economically disadvantaged criteria. Currently, 581 schools participate in MMFA.
requirements_list: School must meet economically disadvantaged criteria to qualify
School must participate in the School Breakfast Program
School must be approved to participate in Maryland Meals for Achievement
Meals must be consumed in the classroom
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools meeting economically disadvantaged criteria and participating in the School Breakfast Program may apply to participate in MMFA through enrollment administered by the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support Maryland's child care system by utilizing federal funds to stabilize, strengthen, and sustain licensed child care programs and mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The program helps families access affordable child care, assists providers in improving program quality, provides mental health supports, offers workforce development, increases family child care business resilience, and advances coordinated prekindergarten enrollment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to eligible applicants under six high-leverage strategies: Expanding Access to Quality Child Care, Early Learning Models of Excellence, Expanding Mental Health Supports and Services, Growing a Highly Effective Child Care Workforce, Boosting Family Child Care, and Advancing a Coordinated Prekindergarten Enrollment System. Award notices were issued in December 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, child care organizations, colleges and universities, community organizations, government agencies, and early childhood education programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting child care system stabilization and sustainability, helping families access affordable child care, improving program quality, providing mental health supports and services, workforce development for early childhood professionals, strengthening family child care businesses, and advancing coordinated prekindergarten enrollment systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—available to eligible providers and organizations across Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an eligible applicant (licensed child care provider, nonprofit organization, college, university, community organization, or government agency)
Must choose at least one of the six high-leverage strategy areas
Must provide description of how planned activities align with chosen strategy
Must describe what products and services will be delivered
Must explain expected impact on the early childhood community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted for the grant program. Award notices were issued by MSDE in December 2022. Grantees received comprehensive application materials and are implementing approved activities under the selected strategy areas.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Milken Educator Awards program recognizes and honors top educators across the country by providing unrestricted cash awards to reward excellence in education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Top educators receive $25,000 unrestricted awards to recognize excellence in education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teachers and educators working in schools across the country, including Maryland public school educators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Unrestricted use - educators can use the award funds as they choose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates nationwide with Maryland educators eligible to apply and win.
requirements_list: Must be an educator working in a school
Must demonstrate excellence in education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed to identify top educators who exemplify excellence. Winners are selected and honored with awards.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides access to balanced, nutritious lunches and snacks to support students' health, development, and academic potential throughout the school day. Reimbursement for meals meeting USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans is provided to eligible students at participating Maryland public and non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 900,000 students daily. Funds help offset the cost of producing meals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or reduced-price balanced meals meeting USDA nutrition standards provided to eligible students at participating schools. Direct payments and reimbursement for nutritious school lunches and snacks provided to eligible students each day to help offset the cost of meal production.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students at participating Maryland public and non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free or reduced-price nutritious lunch meals and snacks for students, meeting USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Funds help cover the cost of producing meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland at all 24 public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions.
requirements_list: School or childcare institution must be public or non-profit private
Meals must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Schools must be participating in the National School Lunch Program
Students must meet federal income eligibility requirements for free or reduced meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions participate through enrollment in the federal NSLP program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Families apply for free or reduced meals through their school. Schools interested in participating should contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at 410-767-0199. Applications are accepted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: State aid program that reimburses the cost of tuition for students with disabilities placed in nonpublic special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. Covers standard education, related services (audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, one-to-one classroom aide, intensive behavior modification, extended day services), and residential services as specified in IEP. The State's share of costs is calculated according to Maryland Education Article §8-415.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State reimbursement for tuition costs of students placed in MSDE-approved nonpublic special education day or residential programs, including related services and residential services as outlined in IEPs. Covers audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, one-to-one classroom aide, intensive behavior modification, extended day services, extended school year services, and other services specified in student IEPs. Placement must be determined through the IEP process. Students are counted in September 30th enrollment with code 09 to indicate nonpublic placement. Also covers individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs when deemed necessary by IEP teams.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date for individual placements
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD; Jeffrey Miller
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public school systems and local education agencies placing students with disabilities in nonpublic special education schools; students with disabilities requiring nonpublic or out-of-state placements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition reimbursement for nonpublic special education placements (day or residential) and related IEP services including audiology, counseling, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, classroom aides, behavior modification, and extended services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland; out-of-state placements eligible based on LEA of financial responsibility
requirements_list: Student must have an Individualized Education Program (IEP) requiring nonpublic placement
Placement must be in an MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program
Program can be day or residential
IEP developed in accordance with federal and state laws and approved by parent/guardian
Placement must provide appropriate educational program in least restrictive environment
MSDE approval of day or residential program required
Compliance with COMAR 13A.05.01 and COMAR 13A.05.02
Cost sheet documentation required
For individual placements: submission within 30 calendar days of entry date, discharge date, or service revision date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School systems submit applications for either MSDE-approved day and residential programs or individual placements upon request. LEA submits completed application with student information and cost sheet documentation. For individual placements, submission must include IEP team minutes supporting placement and letter from service provider confirming enrollment. Application forms and directions are provided by MSDE.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational support services for job seekers with Autism, providing a collaboration between DORS and community colleges throughout Maryland. Students enroll in credit and certificate classes while working with a DORS Pathways coordinator, families, DORS counselors, Disability Support Services staff, and college faculty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educational support services including adjustment to college life, career guidance and counseling, assessment services, employment and communication skills training through individual and group sessions. Students enroll in credit and certificate classes at participating community colleges and work with a DORS Pathways coordinator.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with documented diagnosis of Autism pursuing vocational education at participating community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for college enrollment, career guidance, assessment, employment and communication skills development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Anne Arundel Community College (AACC), Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC), Howard Community College (HCC), Prince George Community College (PGCC), College of Southern Maryland (CSM), and Montgomery College in Maryland.
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have an active DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of an employment plan
Register with the Disability Support Services program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office to request DORS Services. Prospective students must have a documented Autism diagnosis and an approved DORS Individualized Plan for Employment. They then register with Disability Support Services at their chosen participating community college and commit to weekly group sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism, helping them develop soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. Introduces students to education, training, and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college. Includes college tours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Self-advocacy training, social skills training, and soft skills development delivered through instruction to help Pre-ETS students with Autism develop skills needed to obtain and maintain employment and explore post-secondary education and career options.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) students with Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis; current high school, post-high school education program, or trade school students; ages 14-21 with documented disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy and social skills training through classroom and other activities to develop soft skills for employment and explore post-secondary education and career options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Pre-ETS students with Autism.
requirements_list: Be a Pre-ETS student
Have Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
Currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, or recognized educational program (trade school)
At least 14 years old but less than 22
Have an IEP, 504 plan, or medical records documenting disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Counselor or local office to request DORS Services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-ETS provides students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 the opportunity to experience and explore the world of work through five specific services: job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. The program is available statewide through local DORS offices and serves students who are blind, visually impaired, or have other documented disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-ETS provides five services: job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. Services help students explore careers and prepare for transition from school to post-school life and work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 who are enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn, including students who are blind or visually impaired.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to help students explore careers and prepare for transition from school to post-school life and work, including job exploration, self-advocacy training, workplace readiness development, and education planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS offices and the DORS Workforce & Technology Center.
requirements_list: Is enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program or other recognized educational program, and has not graduated or withdrawn
Is at least 14 years old but less than age 22
Has a disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan or medical records
Must be a student who is blind or visually impaired (for OBVS component)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone may request DORS services by completing a Request DORS Services form. Contact your local DORS office or the Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth.

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program for individuals with disabilities who are not yet at the academic skill level needed for GED instruction but want a high school diploma to pursue employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-GED instruction is provided to help individuals reach the academic skill level needed for GED coursework. The program is offered at the Workforce Training Center and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who want a high school diploma and need foundational academic preparation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-GED academic instruction and preparation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland at the Workforce Training Center and virtually
requirements_list: Individuals should have at least 7th grade reading and math skills as recorded on the CASAS or TABE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Rehabilitation Services or visit the Workforce Training Center to enroll in the Pre-GED program

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding for local education agencies and private providers to administer high-quality prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level. Part of Maryland's plan for expanding access to high-quality prekindergarten aligned with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provided to local school systems and qualified private providers to deliver full-day prekindergarten services at no cost to eligible families. Funding supports high-quality programming and school readiness services aligned with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future. Up to $19,950 per full-day prekindergarten slot requested for three- and four-year-olds. Funding covers instructional staff salaries, program operations, professional development, curriculum materials, and quality improvement initiatives. 20% advance payment available upon request.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, Head Start programs, and qualified private providers who deliver prekindergarten services. Serves three-year-old and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level, including multilingual learners, children with disabilities, and children experiencing homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead teacher and assistant teacher salaries and benefits; contracted services; program operations and administration; professional learning and coaching support; High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM) and curriculum materials; quality improvement initiatives; child assessments and health screenings; CLASS observations; family engagement and support services; supplies and equipment. Cannot be directed to tuition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. MSDE reserves the right to consider geographic distribution in award decisions.
requirements_list: Applicant must hold a valid license or registration
Applicant must be a Head Start program, local school system, or qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02
Target children ages 3-4 years old from families earning at or below 300% Federal Poverty Level
Maryland EXCELS rating of Level 3 or higher; plan to reach Level 5 within 5 years
Full-day program: minimum 6.5 hours of instruction for 180 school days annually
No tuition charged for 6.5-hour instructional day
Lead teachers must have bachelor's degree in early childhood education or related field or equivalent; alternative pathway through MAAPP residency
Assistant teachers must have high school diploma minimum; assistant teachers required for classrooms with 10+ students
Child-to-instructional staff ratio of 10:1 maximum; maximum class size of 20
High-quality certified teachers with State certification in early childhood education
Inclusion of children with disabilities
Developmentally appropriate, culturally and linguistically responsive instruction aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards
Instructional staff salaries comparable to local K-12 staff
Four or more SMART goals aligned with required areas grounded in data with clear measurement
Community needs assessment demonstrating demand for additional or improved Pre-K services
Complete sustainability plan combining federal, state, and local funding sources
Demonstrate community and business partnerships with detailed partner responsibilities
Nonprofit applicants must budget allowable indirect cost rate of 15% or greater of federal de minimis rate
Full program documentation and updates available through MSDE Office of Grants Administration and Compliance website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through an online Qualtrics form. Four-section application: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application (Full or Modified), and Appendices. Application progress saves in browser on same device/browser. Review opportunity before final submission. PDF download available for records. MSDE offers customer service support sessions to review program requirements and provide application walkthroughs. Office hours are available for questions. FAQ and answers posted to the Prekindergarten webpage following customer service sessions. Applications must be submitted by March 11, 2026 at 5:00 pm EDT. All required appendices (A-L) must be submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative designed by a local school system to address the needs of an individual student or group of students who are at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school. The partnership uses wrap-around supportive services within the public school setting and is especially beneficial for a school system with a plan to build local capacity to address a specific, immediate need.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An initiative that provides supportive services to students within the public school setting to address immediate needs and prevent placement in nonpublic special education schools. Services are wrap-around and targeted to the specific need of the student or school system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems seeking to prevent nonpublic special education placement for students at high risk.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around supportive services provided within the public school setting to address the immediate needs of individual students or groups of students at high risk of nonpublic placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through Local School Systems.
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System
Student(s) must be at high risk of placement in a nonpublic special education school
School system must have a plan to build local capacity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local School Systems contact the Nonpublic Special Education Section to develop and design the Preventive Service Partnership initiative. Documentation includes a Preventative Service Plan submitted upon request.

structured_extraction.program_name: Professional Learning in Early Literacy Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides professional learning funding to Local School Systems (LSSs) to support rigorous professional development for Pre-K teachers and assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and private childcare teachers of 3-year-olds and 4-year-olds. Training focuses on strategies based on the science of reading research.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards ranging from $40,000 to $80,000 per Local School System to support professional learning and training materials aligned to the science of reading research for Pre-K educators. Funds may support salaries and wages, contracted services, supplies and materials, other charges, equipment, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems and early literacy educators including public school teachers, Head Start teachers, private childcare teachers, supervisors/directors, and coaches/specialists seeking to provide professional development in early literacy and science of reading strategies to Pre-K teachers, assistant teachers, and private childcare providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning and training focused on strategies based on science of reading research for educators of 3- and 4-year-old children. Funds may support training delivery, materials, approved vendor services, facilitator costs, program evaluation, dissemination activities, salaries and wages, contracted services, supplies and materials, other charges, equipment, and indirect costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Local School Systems across Maryland. MSDE will consider geographic distribution when making award decisions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local School System
Must provide professional learning focused on science of reading strategies
Must serve Pre-K teachers and assistant teachers, coaches, specialists, special educators, Head Start teachers, and/or private childcare providers of 3- and 4-year-olds
Funds must be obligated by December 30, 2022
Alignment to science of reading research
Identification of approved vendor
Clear alignment to Maryland Leads application
Plan to engage private child care providers and Head Start staff
Qualified facilitator
Comprehensive timeline
Evaluation plan
Clear management structure with assigned responsibilities
Budget line items aligned with program activities with reasonable rates
Submit C-125 MSDE Grant Budget form
Provide scope of work from approved Science of Reading vendor
Include resumes of key personnel
Provide education support professionals data with supporting documentation
Submit signed recipient assurances page
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local School Systems submit proposals by 5:00 p.m. October 11, 2022 via email to the provided contact. Proposals must follow the Grant Information Guide and application form provided and address: extent of need, evidence of impact, goals/outcomes, implementation plan, project timeline, evaluation plan, management plan, and budget narrative. Applications are scored on a 100-point rubric across six categories including Extent of Need, Goals, Implementation Plan, Evaluation, and other factors. Customer service support sessions are available to assist applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding agreement between a Local School System and a Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education program for serving students with significant and intensive needs in the Least Restrictive Environment. The program enhances Individualized Education Program services for students in their community and is especially beneficial for students with short-term needs, requiring an alternative special education program, experiencing a crisis, or awaiting more intensive placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State tuition contributions provided to Local School Systems for serving students with significant and intensive special education needs through partnerships with Maryland State Department of Education-approved nonpublic special education programs. Payment is based on actual full-time equivalent (FTE) seats used and calculated at fiscal year end, cost-neutral to the State and cannot exceed traditional nonpublic tuition assistance costs. Funding supports tuition for placements and wrap-around services including Preventive Service Partnerships.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 annually; minimum 30 calendar days prior to requesting State funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems and nonpublic special education providers serving students with significant and intensive special education needs, students requiring short-term alternative placements, students in crisis situations, and students awaiting more intensive placements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition for nonpublic special education placements, wrap-around services including Preventive Service Partnerships, and access to public school instruction and activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through Local School Systems; partnerships typically serve students closer to homes within their communities.
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System or MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program
Must partner with a MSDE-approved nonpublic special education program
Student must have significant and intensive needs
Placement should be in the Least Restrictive Environment
Submit mid-year enrollment and outcome data reports (January 15)
Initiate discussions with MSDE regarding new proposals (February 1)
Submit applications (June 1)
Submit end-of-year enrollment and outcome data reports (June 1)
Complete fiscal year reconciliation (July 30)
Submit finalized and signed contracts prior to release of state funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local School Systems initiate proposals with MSDE by February 1, submit applications by June 1, and submit finalized and signed contracts prior to fund release. MSDE provides funding notice by July 15. Mid-year and end-of-year enrollment and outcome data reports are required, with fiscal year reconciliation completed by July 30.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to help child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding. The initiative provides guidance on meeting requirements for Pre-K grants and simplifies the grant application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for state prekindergarten funding combined with technical assistance and guidance to help child care providers meet Pre-K program requirements and simplify the application process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking to expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expanding child care services and accessing state prekindergarten funding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Read and understand the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
Meet eligibility criteria outlined in the GIG
Possess technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to provide services as described in the GIG
Demonstrate stakeholder support for grant application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a Grant Consideration Checklist before beginning the grant application process and answer 'yes' to all four preliminary questions. Pre-K Specialists walk applicants through every step of the process. Applicants can visit PushToPreK.com for more information and use the provided checklist to determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding for professional learning initiatives, Child Development Associate credentials for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment, and accreditation in the Maryland EXCELS program. Grant funds support the administration of the Kindergarten Readiness Assessment and professional development to improve teacher practices and increase Prekindergarten students' readiness for Kindergarten.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to Local School Systems for professional learning initiatives, CDA credentials for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten enrollment, and Maryland EXCELS program accreditation. Funds must support continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local School Systems in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional learning initiatives, Child Development Associate credentials for Prekindergarten Assistant Teachers, planning for coordinated Prekindergarten mixed delivery enrollment, Maryland EXCELS program accreditation, Kindergarten Readiness Assessment administration, and professional development for improved teacher practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Local School Systems in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Local School System
Grant funds must be used to support initiatives for continuous improvement using the R4K comprehensive assessment system for Prekindergarten and Kindergarten
Focus on fidelity of assessment administration and professional development on assessment reliability
Data-based instructional decision-making and research-based content and pedagogical best practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the R4K Grant Application form and submit via email to the Division of Early Childhood by June 3, 2022 at 5:00 p.m. Save the application as 'Name of LEA_R4K23 Grant Proposal' and include 'R4K FY23 Grant Proposal' in the email subject line. Customer service support sessions are available to help applicants.

structured_extraction.program_name: SMILE (Skills to Move Towards Independence, Life & Employment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A summer program collaboration for Pre-ETS and transitioning youth who are blind or visually impaired, providing activities focused on career exploration, work readiness, and development of skills for advocacy and independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer program featuring career exploration, work readiness, advocacy and independence skills development, exposure to college and vocational options, work skills training, technology instruction, self-advocacy training, independence and social skills instruction, interest inventory surveys, guest speakers, and community resources. Services offered in the community, at WTC, and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-employment transition services (Pre-ETS) and transitioning youth who are blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career exploration, work readiness skills, technology training, self-advocacy development, independence skills, and social skills training for blind and visually impaired youth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in the community, at WTC, and virtually.
requirements_list: Be Pre-ETS or transitioning youth
Be blind or visually impaired
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact WTC to enroll in the SMILE summer program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious breakfasts to students in Maryland public and non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions. The program is linked to better test scores, improved behavior, reduced emotional and behavioral problems, decreased food insecurity, fewer visits to the nurse, and better school attendance. The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Children from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level may receive meals at a free or reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Schools and institutions provide free or reduced-price nutritious school breakfast meals meeting USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans to eligible students each day. All 24 Maryland public school districts, 17 participating non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate statewide, serving over 898,000 students daily. Children from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level may receive meals at a free or reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals. Funds help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students attending participating Maryland public schools, non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions. Schools and residential child care institutions administering the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of free or reduced-price nutritious breakfast meals to students that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Funds help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school districts and 17 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate in the program statewide, providing over 898,000 students with access to nutritious breakfasts each day.
requirements_list: School must be a participating Maryland public school, non-profit private school, or residential childcare institution
Meals must comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Students must meet federal income eligibility requirements for free or reduced meals
Students qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income at or below 130-185% of poverty level
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools apply to participate in the SBP through enrollment in the federal program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Individual students may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income eligibility. Families apply for free or reduced meals through their school. Schools interested in participating should contact the program at (410) 767-0199.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides milk to children in schools, child care institutions, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs. Reimburses schools and institutions for milk they serve. Schools already in the National School Lunch Program or School Breakfast Program may also participate to provide milk to children in half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs without access to other school meal programs. Funds are used to offset the cost of the half-pint of milk served to children in public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement and direct payments for milk provided to children in schools, child care institutions, and eligible camps. Eligible participants include schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs and child care institutions where children do not have access to other federal child nutrition meal programs. Funds help offset the cost of the half-pint of milk served to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in schools, child care institutions, and camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs; public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Milk provided to children in eligible schools and child care settings; funds must be used to lower the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Administered at state level by state education agencies through agreements with school food authorities. Serves eligible schools and child care facilities across Maryland.
requirements_list: Institution must not participate in other federal child nutrition meal service programs
Schools with half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to other school meal programs are eligible
Public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and childcare facilities may participate through enrollment in the Special Milk Program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Interested institutions should contact the Maryland State Department of Education for application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that deliver enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Programs provide learning experiences aligned with the State's curricular and educational priorities that cannot be replicated in the classroom. These include experiential learning and one-on-one support services such as free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers and professional development opportunities that link SAI programs to classroom curriculum are also funded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants to non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs. Funding supports experiential learning, field trips, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers. Specific award amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations providing enriching educational programs to Maryland students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Experiential learning experiences, free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development for teachers that link programs to classroom curriculum
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - programs must serve Maryland students
requirements_list: Must be a qualified non-profit organization
Program must provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities
Program cannot be replicated in the classroom
Must provide experiential learning and one-on-one support services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open Thursday, May 1, 2025. Applicants must submit the application form by Friday, June 13, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EST. MSDE offers customer service support sessions to review program requirements and provide a walk-through of the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Student Employment Services are for students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 who would like to receive Pre-ETS services and also obtain or prepare for meaningful employment and a successful career. A broad range of services may be available to these students, including support for college and post-secondary education.
