structured_extraction.assistance_description: Student Employment Services provide a broad range of services to help students with disabilities obtain or prepare for meaningful employment and a successful career. DORS may support college and post-secondary education through this service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 21 who are enrolled in secondary school, post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to help students prepare for and obtain meaningful employment, pursue college and post-secondary education, and prepare for career success.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS offices.
requirements_list: Is enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program or other recognized educational program, and has not graduated or withdrawn
Is at least 14 years old but less than age 22
Has a disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan or medical records
Meets eligibility requirements for Student Employment Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone may request DORS services by completing a Request DORS Services form. Students may request Pre-ETS and also request Student Employment Services at any time, particularly as their career pathway comes into focus or services beyond the five Pre-ETS are required. Contact your local DORS office or speak with your DORS counselor for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, state-administered program that provides free, nutritious meals (breakfasts, lunches, and snacks) to children and teens 18 years and younger in economically disadvantaged and low-income areas during summer months when school is not in session. The program combines summer activity and enrichment programs with federal meal reimbursement. Eligible organizations serving as meal sites receive meals for distribution to youth throughout Maryland through either on-site consumption via SUN Meals program or multi-day meal boxes through SUN Meals To-Go program, with specific operational requirements for site participation and compliance with USDA nutrition requirements.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free breakfast, lunch, or snacks provided to eligible children ages 18 and younger during summer months when school is not in session. Reimbursement for meals or direct meal provision to organizations serving as meal sites for distribution to youth in economically disadvantaged and low-income areas. Meals are either consumed on-site through SUN Meals program or provided as multi-day meal boxes through SUN Meals To-Go program (which requires registration). The program operates Monday through Friday during summer school breaks (specific dates vary by location and school calendar) and meals must comply with USDA nutrition requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in economically disadvantaged and low-income areas across Maryland, and non-profit organizations, churches, day camps, community groups, and government agencies interested in becoming meal serving sites or SUN Meals sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of nutritious meals (breakfasts, lunches, and snacks) to eligible children during summer months when school is not in session; meals must comply with USDA meal pattern requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves economically disadvantaged and low-income areas throughout Maryland. Available statewide across all Maryland counties. In Baltimore City, sites must be located within city limits.
requirements_list: Children must be 18 years old or under
Child must reside in economically disadvantaged or low-income area
Site must be located in eligible service area
Site must plan to receive meals for a minimum of two weeks
Site must serve a minimum of 10 eligible youth ages 18 or younger
Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible meal serving sites
Sites requesting breakfast must have adequate refrigeration to store perishables overnight
Sites are subject to pre-operational inspection and must be approved by program staff
Site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend mandatory training session
Meals must be served in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
Meals must comply with USDA nutrition requirements
Meals must be consumed at site or provided as multi-day boxes for To-Go program
Registration required for SUN Meals To-Go program
Sites must be approved SFSP sponsors
Meal service must occur during summer break
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Summer food service sponsors in economically disadvantaged areas may participate through enrollment in SFSP administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Organizations interested in becoming meal serving sites or SUN Meals sites can apply by completing an online application form or downloading and submitting a paper application, or by contacting the sponsoring organization for their county (typically county public school systems) or the Office of School and Community Nutrition Program at 410-767-0199. Completed applications should be submitted according to program guidelines. Sites must meet all qualifications and pass pre-operational inspection before approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding for Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) to develop high-quality, appealing standardized recipes using local agricultural products. The program involves staff training on recipe preparation, recipe tasting events, and nutrition education. Funding supports staff time for training and recipe tasting events, purchasing food and supplies for these events, and collecting student and staff feedback to modify recipes for alignment with flavor preferences and school implementation feasibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for substitute staff wages, stipends for staff training, food and nutrition equipment/smallware (max 5% of total grant), food costs for training and taste tests (max 20% of total grant), and consumable costs. Funds support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and purchasing food and supplies for these events.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, April 22, 2022, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022; School nutrition staff; Students; Teachers; School nutrition professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries and wages for substitute school nutrition staff; Stipends for staff training attendance; Food and nutrition equipment and smallware (max 5% of total grant); Food costs for training and taste tests (max 20% of total grant); Consumable costs for training and taste tests; Nutrition education resources development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to LEAs across Maryland participating in NSLP or SSO during the 2021-2022 school year.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Must participate in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022
Must designate a Grant Coordinator
Schools must be registered as Team Nutrition Schools
School nutrition staff must attend designated trainings
Each participating school must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe
Each participating school must host at least two taste tests
Recipes must be updated after first round of taste tests based on feedback
Participate in periodic virtual meetings
Facilitate training and tasting event logistics
Collect data from recipe tasting events
Submit quarterly reports on grant activities and fund utilization
Secure photographs, attendance records, data, and success stories
Menu at least one final recipe in a reimbursable meal by grant end
Compliance with state and federal statutes and regulations including Civil Rights Act, ESEA, EDGAR, GEPA, ADA
Vendors, subgrantees, and consultants must comply with FERPA
Facilities must be ADA accessible
Establish fiscal control and fund accounting procedures per 2 CFR §200
Retain financial records for 5 years minimum
Annual financial and compliance audit required if expending $750,000+ federally in single fiscal year
Submit complete, accurate, and timely progress and final reports
Obtain prior written MSDE approval for programmatic changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a grant application form along with required assurances by April 22, 2022 at 5:00 pm EST. Refer to the Grant Information Guide for detailed instructions, timelines, and submission requirements. The Budget Template is accessed through the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS).

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) connect with Employment Networks (EN) or state Vocational Rehabilitation programs like DORS. Provides support and services including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services to help achieve and maintain employment. The program protects beneficiaries from Continuing Disability Reviews by SSA while their Ticket is in use and they meet Timely Progress requirements. Participants can maintain Medicare for at least 93 months after earning more and may qualify for Medicaid through the Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services provided at no cost to participants include job training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing support services. An Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) is developed with each participant based on their employment goals. Services help reach job goals and prepare for employment with health benefits and higher income than disability benefits. After employment is achieved and the DORS case closes, participants are connected with an Employment Network for continued employment supports. Work incentives protect benefits while working, and protection from Continuing Disability Reviews is provided while making good progress.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), ages 18-64 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, career counseling, job placement services, job coaching, and benefits planning to support employment and education goals, including skills development and benefits planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland to Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be 18-64 years old
Must receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Have a Ticket to Work assigned by the Social Security Administration
Must have an assignable Ticket
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Ticket Coordinator to assign your Ticket to DORS. Work with a DORS counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). Receive services from DORS based on your employment goals. After achieving employment and case closure, connect with an Employment Network for ongoing support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IV, Part B Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal grant program authorized under section 4201 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965, as amended by the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Creates community learning centers that provide academic enrichment opportunities and enrichment activities during out-of-school time (before school, after school, summer, and Saturdays) to help students meet state and local academic standards in core subjects. Includes youth development, substance use prevention, service-learning, violence prevention, counseling, arts, music, recreation, and technology education. Provides literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. Programs target students attending high-poverty, low-performing schools or Title I schools, and help students achieve college and career readiness standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-year federal grant program with level funding contingent on satisfactory performance and funding availability. FY2025 total funds available: $22.6 million. Funds support academic enrichment and out-of-school time programming. Reimbursement-based grants where organizations incur costs and invoice MSDE for reimbursement. structured_extraction.program_description: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Foods in Schools program supports domestic nutrition programs and American agricultural producers through purchases of 100% American-grown and -produced foods for use in schools and child nutrition programs. The program provides schools with commodities from American agricultural producers for use in the National School Lunch Program, Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), and other federal child nutrition programs. Schools can choose from a catalog of over two hundred choices of domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products to incorporate into their menus. Schools participating in the National School Lunch Program and other federal child nutrition programs automatically receive USDA Foods allocations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides schools with 100% American-grown and -produced food commodities purchased by USDA from American agricultural producers for use in school meals and nutrition programs. This assistance reduces food expenses in schools by an average of twenty percent. Schools participating in the National School Lunch Program and other federal child nutrition programs automatically receive USDA Foods allocations. Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Schools can choose from a catalog of over two hundred choices of domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of 100% American-grown and -produced food commodities including fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products for school meals and nutrition programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides eligible Maryland schools and residential child care institutions with free fresh fruits and vegetables. The program has two components: the USDA Department of Defense (DOD) Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program, which enables schools to allocate all or a portion of their allocated USDA Foods funds to receive fresh fruits and vegetables delivered weekly from a Maryland-based produce company with an emphasis on locally available products, and the Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program, which provides eligible elementary schools with free fresh fruits and vegetables during the school day while promoting nutrition education about the produce served to encourage healthier school environments. Program goals include introducing children to new varieties of fresh produce and increasing overall consumption of fresh, unprocessed produce among young children. In School Year 2022-2023, 196 schools participated in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free fresh fruits and vegetables are provided to school students and residential child care institutions through two program options. Schools can receive produce delivered weekly by allocating all or a portion of their allocated USDA Foods funds to purchase from a Maryland-based produce company with an emphasis on locally available products, or receive free fresh fruits and vegetables for consumption during the school day. Direct payments are also provided for purchasing fresh fruits and vegetables. Schools and institutions must meet FFVP eligibility criteria and typically participation in the school lunch program is required. Currently serves 196 elementary schools. Program goals include introducing children to new varieties of fresh produce and increasing overall consumption of fresh, unprocessed produce among young children.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elementary school children, students, and residents at eligible schools and residential child care institutions participating in school meal programs throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of fresh fruits and vegetables to students and residents during the school day and through school meal programs

DefTech provides proprietary business services including access to technical experts, intellectual property and technology due diligence, business support services, and research tools.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DefTech provides proprietary business services to member companies including DefTech Academy and Certification courses on technology transfer and government contracting, pre-lab engagement training, access to proprietary monthly distribution of federal funding opportunities, private meetings with federal labs, and monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors. Program cost is waived for the initial 30 companies in the first program year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using Federal Laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, and expertise. Focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to federal labs for product development, testing, intellectual property licensing, technical expertise, business support services, and research tools to support business creation, growth, and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses in Maryland.
requirements_list: Developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using Federal Laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, and expertise
Membership is highly competitive with limited membership each year
Focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors
Accepted applicants categorized as either resource-ready for immediate federal engagement or requiring preliminary training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Online application followed by initial screening by a DefTech Advisor. Accepted applicants are placed into one of two categories: resource-ready for immediate federal engagement and commencement of DefTech services, or requiring preliminary training followed by commencement of DefTech services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A global startup program that helps developers create, launch, and scale their startups by providing cloud credits, technical training, mentorship, support, and networking opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,000 worth of DigitalOcean cloud credits for 12 months, technical training and mentorship, priority support, access to a global community through a dedicated Slack channel, marketing help and promotions, and invites to exclusive networking events.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Startup developers and technology entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cloud infrastructure deployment and scaling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available globally, including Maryland.
requirements_list: Must create a DigitalOcean team account with official email address
Must add a valid payment method
Must use the same email address to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Create a DigitalOcean team account with official email and valid payment method. Apply via the Hatch application link and mention TEDCO when prompted for accelerator/incubator/VC name. Verified startups receive credits within 15 days of applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Equitech Growth Fund provides grants for infrastructure and workforce development initiatives that support Maryland's economic competitiveness, foster economic opportunity for all, and accelerate growth of emerging and advanced industries in the state. The goal is to position Maryland as a leading global and inclusive innovation economy by 2040.
eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Infrastructure Awards: Up to $1 million with project duration of 12 to 36 months depending on project scope and readiness (1-3 awards expected; $3M total annual funding). Workforce Awards: Up to $250,000 with project duration of 12 to 24 months depending on project scope and readiness (8-10 awards expected; $2M total annual funding). Includes lab build-outs and 'soft' infrastructure (coalition-building, entrepreneurial support organizations).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Inquiries must be submitted on or before July 25, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. (ET)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public agencies, nonprofit organizations, private entities, public-private partnerships, and higher education institutions working on infrastructure and workforce development initiatives that support emerging and advanced industries in Maryland. Priority given to socially and economically disadvantaged founders/executive leadership and organizations serving economically distressed or rural communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure and workforce development initiatives including training, upskilling, and reskilling in STEM fields; lab build-outs; AI technology and SaaS platform development; and soft infrastructure (coalition-building, entrepreneurial support organizations). Eligible budget categories include Personnel, Fringe Benefits, Travel, Contractual, Supplies, Equipment, Construction, and Other. Priority industry types include Entrepreneurship Development, STEM Education, Advanced Manufacturing, Cybersecurity and IT Industry Workforce Development, Advanced Technology, and Advanced Laboratory Space. Additional areas include Environmental and Energy Technology, Aerospace and Defense, Smart Agriculture and Food Technology, and Healthcare, Life Sciences, and Bioinformatics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland. Projects can service more than one county with preference given to proposals with greatest impact within Maryland. Organizations must have physical presence or intent to establish physical presence in Maryland.
requirements_list: Eligible applicant types include public agencies, nonprofits, private entities, public-private partnerships, and higher education institutions
Projects must focus on infrastructure or workforce development
Projects must support emerging and advanced industries in Maryland
Infrastructure projects typically range from 12 to 36 months
Workforce development projects typically range from 12 to 24 months
Submit interim and final progress reports every 4-6 months during project
Submit annual impact reports for 5 years following project completion
Describe how award funds are used and progress made

Organizations must have physical presence or intent to establish physical presence in Maryland
Preference given to socially and economically disadvantaged founders/executive leadership per 13 CFR 124.104 and 124.103
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through the online form at https://tedco.jotform.com/260855899774077. Applicants must submit a budget and justification using the provided template. An updated FAQ document is posted on the program landing page. Inquiries can be submitted by July 24th at 5:00 PM ET; answers posted by July 31st. Inquiries can be submitted to equitechgrowth@tedcomd.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Labs Leveraging Innovation to Products (FLLIP) Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that connects Maryland entrepreneurs and small businesses with federal laboratory resources to accelerate innovation and commercialization. The program provides education, expert guidance, matchmaking, and technical assistance to help Maryland companies develop working relationships with federal labs including the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Frederick National Lab for Cancer Research (FNL), and the Defense Health Administration (DHA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides education and support to help Maryland companies pursue working relationships with federal labs. Services include technical assistance, market research, patent strategy, connection with technical experts and labs to identify commercial opportunities, assessment of innovative businesses ready to engage with federal labs, and facilitation of formal relationships between lab scientists and entrepreneurs through agreements and lab tours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland entrepreneurs, small businesses, and companies traditionally underrepresented in federal lab collaborations, particularly those in medical or health-related sectors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program facilitates access to federal laboratory resources and provides support services; companies can develop formal relationships with federal labs for research, development, and commercialization purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland-based companies throughout the state
requirements_list: Small, innovative medical or health-related business
Based in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies receive education and support to pursue working relationships with federal labs. The program uses a structured approach of Connection (connecting technical experts with labs), Assessment (identifying ready companies), Support (providing targeted assistance), and Engagement (facilitating formal relationships).

structured_extraction.program_name: Future Founders: University Innovators Pitch Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: A pitch competition for Maryland university students developing technology-based innovations. Winners receive funding, mentorship, and additional support at TEDCO's Entrepreneur Expo.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and launch of technology-based business ventures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides eligible startups with discounted access to HubSpot's all-in-one CRM platform including marketing automation, sales enablement, and customer relationship management tools, plus training and support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free HubSpot CRM, 90% off HubSpot's Starter, Pro, or Enterprise software for the first 12 months, 50% off in the second year (up to $40,000 in total savings), startup onboarding package at a reduced one-time cost of $300 (includes tech setup, strategy consultation, and 24/7 support), and access to world-class inbound marketing and sales training, education, and support from HubSpot experts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Startups that have raised less than $2 million in total funding and are TEDCO portfolio companies.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to TEDCO portfolio companies.
requirements_list: Must have raised less than $2 million in total funding
Must be a current TEDCO portfolio company

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports early-stage Maryland technology-based companies with ownership and control by individuals who have demonstrated social and economic disadvantage. The program addresses the funding gap between pre-seed and seed financing to help economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs grow their businesses and create jobs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides direct equity investment in early-stage technology-based companies (products/processes protectable as intellectual property) meeting social and economic disadvantage criteria. Investment amounts not specified on this page. Investors require recipient companies to receive executive support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications assessed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology entrepreneurs with social and economic disadvantage, Maryland-based business owners where at least 30% ownership is held by individuals demonstrating social and economic disadvantage, with at least one full-time employee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business operations and growth for early-stage technology companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Maryland statewide. Company headquarters must be in Maryland, principal business operations must be conducted from a Maryland physical location, and more than 50% of workforce must work from a physical location in Maryland.

Founder, officers, or managers agree to receive executive support

After submission, applicants should email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. Applications received through other means such as email or mail will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_name: Intellectual Property Management Platform by IPGen
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, one-year subscription to IPGen's IP SaaS (Software as a Service) platform that helps with intellectual property processes including searching, drafting, and prosecution. The platform uses AI and machine learning tools to streamline IP lifecycle management and includes features such as templates, automation tools, collaboration features, and a patents dashboard. Users also receive onboarding assistance, up to two hours of hands-on support from the IPGen team, and guidance on trademark services during the platform year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-year subscription to IPGen's IP SaaS platform. Includes 30 minutes of onboarding and training from the IPGen team, plus at least two additional hours of practical, hands-on support (such as advice, guidance, and application review) that may be taken in 30-minute increments. The platform provides AI and machine learning tools, templates, automation features, collaboration tools, patent dashboard, and customer support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland-based entrepreneurs and start-up businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intellectual property management, including patent searching, drafting, prosecution, and trademark services. The platform assists with IP lifecycle management and provides guidance throughout various IP processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible Maryland-based entrepreneurs and start-up businesses.
requirements_list: Must be Maryland-based
Must be an entrepreneur or start-up business
Must execute the IPGen terms of service agreement before using the platform
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a request for access through the IPGen request form on the TEDCO website. The IPGen team will provide onboarding and training upon request.

structured_extraction.program_name: Leading Women's Program (Montgomery County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month hybrid entrepreneur leadership development program for female founders, co-founders, and CEOs building critical skills in leadership, communication, and business planning through peer cohorts and strategic workshops.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-month hybrid program combining in-person and virtual sessions held monthly at Universities at Shady Grove in Rockville. The program includes five components: Prerequisites for Prep Session, Introductory and Preparation Session, Leadership and Communication Workshop (8 sessions), Real World Perspectives (7 sessions), and What's Your End Game Development Plan (4 sessions). Participants pay a $250 registration fee upfront to cover assessments, with $200 refunded upon successful completion. Participants may miss no more than two sessions to graduate.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development and entrepreneurship training covering leadership, communication, business planning, and peer networking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is designed for Montgomery County-based business owners. Entrepreneurs located outside of Montgomery County will be considered based on available slots.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a founder, co-founder, or CEO
Company must be at minimum pre-seed to growth stage
Company must be at maximum pre-series A stage
Participant must be able to attend sessions with no more than two absences to graduate
Registration fee of $250 is required upfront
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application to be considered for admission to the program cohort. Upon acceptance, participants pay a $250 registration fee to cover assessments. The program runs over 10 months with hybrid in-person (at Universities at Shady Grove in Rockville) and virtual sessions held monthly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program created to leverage resources from the State of Maryland and five Maryland academic research institutions to foster the transition of promising technologies from research to commercial sector. The program provides grants and convertible debt financing to support company formation and early-stage commercialization of technology licensed from qualifying universities including Johns Hopkins University, University of Maryland College Park, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, and Morgan State University. The Company Formation phase supports the commercial launch of start-up companies based on technologies licensed from Maryland qualifying universities. Award recipients commercialize innovative technologies in fields ranging from medical devices and therapeutics to software, renewable energy, and advanced materials. Funding of up to $300,000 is available for startup companies to support commercialization activities over up to a nine-month period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $300,000 in the form of grants or convertible debt notes to support company formation and commercialization of technology licensed from qualifying universities. Funding supports startup companies for up to a nine-month period. Funding can be provided through reimbursable grants or convertible notes. Startups must work closely with a TEDCO Site Miner and must remain in Maryland or reimburse the funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly: January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15. Applications must be submitted by 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of each submission month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs and startup companies seeking to commercialize technology licensed from qualifying Maryland universities. Maryland-based start-up companies that have licensed technology from a Qualifying University within the 12 months prior to proposal submission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports company formation and early-stage commercialization efforts for technologies licensed from participating universities. Commercial launch and development of products and services based on technology licensed from a Qualifying University.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Limited to Maryland-based start-up companies. Companies must license technology from one of the qualifying universities (Johns Hopkins University, University of Maryland College Park, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, or Morgan State University). Company must remain in Maryland or reimburse funds.

Technology must be licensed from Johns Hopkins University, University of Maryland College Park, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, or Morgan State University

Applicant must obtain a TEDCO ID through one-time registration before filling out the application portal
Applicant must meet all criteria specified in the respective RFA
Company must remain in Maryland or reimburse funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register with TEDCO to obtain a one-time TEDCO ID. 2. Ensure your company has licensed technology from a Qualifying University within the previous 12 months. 3. Contact a Site Miner selected by your Qualifying University for guidance on preparing a business-oriented, commercialization-focused application. 4. Engage with a TEDCO Site Miner for a minimum of two weeks (preferably 30 days) prior to submitting an application. Site Miners assist start-ups in developing a strong business-oriented application and provide feedback prior to submission. 5. Obtain a signed letter of support from the Site Miner. 6. Submit a complete application by 5:00pm on the quarterly deadline (January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15). Applications are considered on a quarterly basis. Site Miners present each application at the review committee meeting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Technology Assessment and Validation Awards
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Technology Assessment and Validation Awards provide funding to university researchers and faculty inventors at Maryland institutions to develop early-stage technology innovations, assess their commercial potential, and support technology validation and market assessment. This program supports faculty-led projects across seven major Maryland universities—Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University—that are advancing technology across healthcare, life sciences, information technology, engineering, and other sectors. The program provides financial support for early-stage technology development, commercialization assessment, market analysis, and commercialization strategy development. Full-time faculty members can receive grants to conduct technology validation and market assessment over a 9-month period to transition innovative research from university labs toward commercial development. The program fosters collaborations within and among research institutions in the State and supports technologies developed through technical validation, market assessment, licensing, or creation of start-up companies in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technology Assessment and Validation Awards provide grants to faculty researchers and inventors at participating Maryland universities to support early-stage technology development, validation, and commercialization assessment. Grants up to $130,000 are available for individual applications (Sole Applicants). A grant award totaling up to $180,000 may be awarded for proposals with two or more Qualifying Universities submitting a Joint Application, with minimum 25% budget allocation to at least two universities. Up to $12,500 can be applied toward patent expenses, and $15,000 is allocated for commercialization strategy support. Up to $5,000 can be used for I-Corps participation and up to $4,500 for company formation costs or university startup attorney costs. If technology is licensed out of state, the institution must repay TEDCO the full amount plus interest from applicable licensing revenue.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly: January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15. Applications must be submitted by 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of each submission month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time faculty researchers and inventors at Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University, particularly those with patent filings in early stages of technology development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early-stage technology research and development, technology validation, market assessment, commercialization strategy support, and patent expenses related to therapeutics, medical devices, diagnostic tools, biotechnology, information technology, engineering, and sustainability applications. Up to $12,500 can be used for patent expenses and $15,000 for commercialization strategy support. Up to $5,000 can be used for I-Corps participation and up to $4,500 for company formation costs or university startup attorney costs. Allowable costs include personnel salaries and fringe benefits, equipment purchases, materials and supplies, and other direct costs including regulatory strategy development and contracting with industry experts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to researchers and faculty inventors at seven participating Maryland universities: Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University. Technology must remain in Maryland or the institution is required to reimburse TEDCO.

No facilities and administrative/indirect charges allowed except patent expenses up to $12,500
Commercialization Plan required including Executive Summary (1-2 pages), Business Plan (no page limit), and Pitch Deck (10-15 slides)
Final report submission within 30 days of award term end

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register with TEDCO to obtain a one-time TEDCO ID. 2. Contact a Site Miner selected by your Qualifying University for guidance on preparing a business-oriented, commercialization-focused application. 3. Engage with the Site Miner for at least 30 days before submission. 4. Obtain a signed letter of support from the Site Miner. 5. Submit a complete application by 5:00pm on the quarterly deadline (January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15). Applications are considered on a quarterly basis. Site Miners assist faculty and inventors in developing a strong application focused on commercialization, providing feedback prior to submission and presenting each application at the review committee meeting.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-level grant program created through Maryland General Assembly legislation in 2022 that provides financial and technical assistance to eligible entities seeking to establish, expand, operate, or develop programming for Makerspaces throughout Maryland. Makerspaces are community spaces that provide access to tools, technology, and knowledge for learners, entrepreneurs, and community members, supporting business growth, workforce training, and technical education opportunities. The program supports the growth and development of makerspaces through grants and technical assistance provided by Open Works.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided as grants with varying amounts depending on grant type: Type A (Establish a New Makerspace) up to $100,000/year for up to 3 years (max $300,000) or up to $25,000 for one year to conduct feasibility study; Type B (Expand an Existing Makerspace) up to $100,000 for one year; Type C (Develop Programming for a Makerspace) up to $25,000 for one year. A 1:1 matching funds requirement applies (feasibility studies require 1:1 cash match with no in-kind allowed; Type B and C require 100% matching funds or in-kind contributions). Matching funds can be from donors, the applying organization, or in-kind contributions such as donated materials, tools, space, volunteer time, or real costs incurred by applicant (subject to TEDCO approval). Technical assistance up to 10 hours is provided by Open Works to address specific needs in establishment, expansion, or operation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, agencies or instrumentalities designated by local governments, nonprofit entities, and makerspace operators seeking to establish, expand, develop programming for, or operate Makerspaces in Maryland. Organizations that support entrepreneurs and provide workforce training are also encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of a new Makerspace, expansion of a Makerspace, development of programming for a Makerspace, purchase of equipment such as 3D printers and design software, utility costs (subject to reviewer discretion), staff training, program marketing, internship opportunities, community engagement programs, and creation of assistive technology devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland to eligible entities.

Must provide a 1:1 matching funds requirement
Matching funds can come from donors, the applying organization, or in-kind contributions such as donated materials, tools, space, or volunteer time
For feasibility study applications, 1:1 cash match is required (in-kind contributions not permitted)
For Type B and C applications, 100% matching funds or in-kind contributions required
In-kind contributions include real costs incurred by applicant for proposed project, subject to TEDCO approval
Must submit a Letter of Intent (LOI) stating the amount of matching funds or in-kind contributions
Must define how a third-party contract will be used if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online form at https://tedco.jotform.com/260197669341970 by the deadline. Complete the relevant questions and upload required documents for the specific type of grant request. Applications are reviewed in stages, and applicants selected for stage three can provide additional information during a presentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program established to promote human stem cell research and medical treatments through grants to public and private entities, companies, universities, research institutes, and academics in Maryland. The program is designed to increase the results of research and development into human stem cells and increase the number and value of technologies arising from stem cell research that are successfully translated to clinical tools. The fund offers multiple programs to accelerate research, validation, commercialization, and clinical development of human stem cell-based technologies.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSCRF offers seven programs (Launch, Discovery, Validation, Commercialization, Clinical, Post-doctoral Fellowships and Manufacturing Assistance) to accelerate research and commercialization of human stem cell-based technologies. Grants provide financial assistance to conduct approved stem cell research projects. Grants are available for companies, universities, research institutes, and academics involved in stem cell research. Eligible project costs include personnel costs, research expenses, and budget categories defined in the Project Budget (adjustments within 10% allowed between categories without amendment). Specific grant amounts and terms are available through the MSCRF funding opportunities portal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: See MSCRF funding opportunities portal for specific program deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private entities, companies, universities, research institutes, academics, and stem cell researchers conducting human stem cell research and developing medical treatments based on stem cell technologies in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Human stem cell research and medical treatments, including research, validation, commercialization, clinical development, post-doctoral fellowships, and manufacturing of stem cell-based technologies. Eligible project costs include personnel costs, research expenses, and budget categories defined in the Project Budget. Use of funds cannot include patent or intellectual property protection costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to entities located in Maryland. The program promotes research and development across the state. In-State symposium presentations required during grant term and one year following.

Must be a public or private entity in Maryland
Applicant must be involved in stem cell research
Must be universities, nonprofit research institutions, or companies located in Maryland
IRB (Institutional Review Board) Approval or exemption determination required before initial disbursement (within 6 months of Effective Date)
IACUC (Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee) Approval if required by project
Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws
Compliance with Maryland's drug and alcohol free workplace policy (COMAR 01.01.1989.18 and 21.11.08)
Compliance with non-discrimination and equal employment practices
All applicable taxes and claims must be paid

Final Report required describing research, translation potential, results, and any modifications
Project completion by specified Completion Date
Sharing of final results and cell lines with other Fund grantees (subject to confidentiality agreements)
Compliance with governmental authority requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit MSCRF.org or the MSCRF funding opportunities portal at https://www.mscrf.org/funding-opportunities to review eligibility requirements and apply. Proposals reviewed by TEDCO and the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission. Reviewers sign confidentiality agreements. Application submitted with completed grant agreement form signed by Principal Investigator. Seven different programs are available with different eligibility and application requirements.

The program provides financial assistance to technology-based businesses and state and local agencies to hire more interns.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses and state and local agencies in Maryland looking to hire interns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hiring paid technical interns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a technology-based business or state/local agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MTIP website for application instructions and more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that connects Maryland's early-stage technology startups with experienced business executives and entrepreneurs who provide expert advice and mentoring in specific areas to help accelerate company growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Entrepreneurs request a Network Advisor through a form, and TEDCO matches them with an experienced advisor who provides mentoring and guidance tailored to the company's specific needs. The program leverages a curated group of advisors with expertise in various business areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology-based companies in Maryland that are beyond the idea stage and seeking expert business guidance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Advisory services covering areas such as business development, technical expertise, and other specific operational needs identified by early-stage tech startups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Company must be established and beyond the idea stage
Company must be technology-based or in a tech-focused sector
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Complete a company stage assessment using TEDCO's assessment tool. Step 2: Complete a Network Advisor request form. Step 3: TEDCO matches the company with an appropriate advisor based on the company's needs and the advisor's expertise.

structured_extraction.program_name: Open Institute for Black Women Entrepreneur Excellence (Howard County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month entrepreneur leadership development program focused on building critical skills that foster resilience. The program brings together entrepreneurial leaders in a cohort to develop a network of peer advisors and a supportive community. It is designed for Howard County-based business owners, though entrepreneurs located outside of Howard County may be considered based on available slots.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A hybrid 10-month program combining in-person and virtual sessions held monthly at the Maryland Innovation Center in Columbia, Maryland. Sessions include leadership and communication workshops, real-world perspectives, and development planning. Participants pay a $250 registration fee (reduced to $50 if they complete the course). The program covers entrepreneur leadership development, peer networking, and critical skills training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black women entrepreneurs and business owners at pre-seed to pre-series A stage in Howard County, though entrepreneurs from outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program participation includes entrepreneur leadership development training, peer networking, and skills building workshops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designed for Howard County-based business owners, though entrepreneurs located outside of Howard County will be considered based on available slots.
requirements_list: Founder, co-founder, or CEO of a company
Company must be at minimum pre-seed to growth stage and maximum pre-series A
Participants can miss no more than two sessions to graduate
Must pay $250 registration fee (partially refunded if course is completed)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified on the page.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's comprehensive program to enhance technology commercialization and provide technical and business assistance to small and early-stage technology and life sciences companies in rural Maryland. The program offers professional ongoing mentoring and targeted projects to help companies succeed at no cost. Companies that have received mentoring services for at least 90 days are eligible to apply for pre-seed equity funding of up to $25,000 to support company startup and growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Companies receive professional ongoing mentoring and targeted project assistance at no cost. Mentors provide consulting services and technical management assistance including business model or strategy, market strategy and competitive analysis, funding opportunities and introductions, financial analysis, business plan or grant review, intellectual property guidance, prototype development, and manufacturing problem solving. Companies that have received mentoring services for at least 90 days are eligible to apply for pre-seed equity investments of $25,000 to establish and grow operations.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Regional mentors (Justin Ferguson - Southern Region, Karen Zuccardi - Frederick County, Graham Dodge - Carroll and Northern Baltimore Counties, Ardon Hall - Allegany County, Sarah Myers and Jeremy Perando - Garrett County, Laurie Brewer - Washington County, Samuel Shoge - Upper Shore Region, Bill Bernard - Lower Shore Region)
structured_extraction.contact_email: jferguson@tedcomd.com, kzuccardi@tedcomd.com, gdodge@tedcomd.com, mathmassness@gmail.com, sarah@dcabfun.com, jperando@xologies.com, lauriebrewer@glowupconsult.com, sshoge@tedcomd.com, bbernard@tedco.md
structured_extraction.program_audience: Start-up and early-stage technology and life sciences companies in rural areas of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for technology commercialization, business development, and technical problem-solving including business model development, market analysis, funding identification, financial analysis, business planning, intellectual property work, prototype development, manufacturing solutions, and company startup and growth capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas of Maryland as defined by the Rural Maryland Council. Program serves Southern Region (Charles, Calvert, St. Mary's Counties), Northern Region (Frederick, Carroll, Northern Baltimore Counties, Allegany, Garrett, Washington Counties), Upper Shore Region (Harford, Cecil, Kent Counties), and Lower Shore Region (Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Worcester Counties).
requirements_list: Must be involved in developing new technologies/products or utilizing technology to create new or expand business
Must be early-stage technology or life sciences company
Located in rural Maryland
Must have fewer than 16 employees
Annual revenues $1 million or less
Good standing with MD Department of Taxation & Assessments
Must receive mentoring services for at least 90 days to be eligible for pre-seed funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the RBII mentor from your region for an initial assessment. All companies will be evaluated to determine if they meet eligibility criteria. Companies that have received mentoring services for at least 90 days are eligible to apply for pre-seed equity funding of up to $25,000.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural and Underserved Business Recovery from Impact of COVID-19 (RUBRIC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide economic relief initiative created to assist Maryland's technology companies detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program targets socially and economically disadvantaged businesses or those in rural areas of Maryland, intended to bridge companies across the economic gap created by COVID-19 and lead to the next financing round or sustainability. The program provides reimbursable grant funding and operating support to help companies survive and prosper during the downturn.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grant awards up to $100,000 per company to provide bridge funding and operating support for businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Funds may be used to attract or retain jobs, attract or retain customers, or sustain companies facing capital-raising difficulties related to COVID-19. Recipients must repay 3% of quarterly revenues for 5 years, capped at 150% of the award amount, with a 10% royalty reduction for each year paid early. Funds are disbursed in two tranches: 50% at closing and 50% after submission of an activity report. Funds must be expended within 12 months of the Effective Date unless a written waiver is approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling review; applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland technology companies that are socially or economically disadvantaged or located in rural areas and have been detrimentally impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Excludes retail, real estate, insurance, banking, lending, and professional services by accountants, attorneys, or physicians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge funding and operating support to help companies attract or retain jobs, attract or retain customers, and sustain operations during the COVID-19 crisis. Funds must address specific COVID-19-related challenges and be expended within 12 months of the Effective Date unless written waiver is approved.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for socially or economically disadvantaged technology companies, and in rural areas of Maryland (as defined in State Finance and Procurement Article §2-207). Excludes Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County, except Northern Baltimore County which is eligible.
requirements_list: Technology-based business with proprietary technology for competitive advantage
Maryland Qualified Business with principal operations in Maryland
At least half of workforce working in-state
Socially and economically disadvantaged or located in rural area of Maryland
Detrimentally impacted by COVID-19 pandemic
In need of bridge funding
Expected to lead to next phase of fundraising or sustainability
Must comply with all applicable federal, State, and local law
Excludes retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, and professional services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through a rolling review process. Applicants must complete the Request for Applications (RFA) process. Funds are disbursed in two tranches: 50% at closing and 50% after submission of an activity report.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive matching grant program administered by TEDCO and Montgomery County that provides non-dilutive funding to small businesses that have received federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) awards. The program strengthens the impact of SBIR/STTR awards, fosters job creation and economic development in Maryland, promotes the commercialization of research by small businesses, facilitates technology transfer from universities and federal labs to small businesses, encourages small businesses to apply for SBIR/STTR funding, and stimulates innovation and entrepreneurship. The program includes a statewide component administered by TEDCO available to all Maryland small businesses and a specialized matching grant component in Montgomery County for companies conducting research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences that conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in Montgomery County. For statewide applicants: Phase I grants receive a 25 percent match up to $25,000 maximum, and Phase II grants receive a 25 percent match up to $75,000 maximum. For Montgomery County applicants: Phase 0 grants reimburse up to $5,000 of technical assistance expenditures for companies pursuing their first Phase I grant, Phase I grants receive a 25 percent match up to $25,000 maximum with up to 50% usable for technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance, and Phase II grants receive a 25 percent match up to $50,000 maximum with up to 50% usable for technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis or on a first-come-first-served basis for Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For statewide Phase I SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO grants an additional award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase I award or $25,000. For statewide Phase II SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO grants an award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase II award or $75,000. For Montgomery County applicants conducting research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences: Phase 0 grants reimburse up to $5,000 of technical assistance expenditures, Phase I grants receive a 25 percent match up to $25,000 maximum with up to 50% usable for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses, and Phase II grants receive a 25 percent match up to $50,000 maximum with up to 50% usable for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses. For Montgomery County applicants, company must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in the County. Applicants cannot use the matching grant for any expenditures reimbursed by other federal or state funding sources. Awards are issued on a quarterly basis for statewide applicants or on a first-come-first-served basis for Montgomery County applicants. Awarded as non-negotiable grant agreement with standard terms and conditions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Four rolling application cycles annually: Cycle 1 (January 1 – March 30), Cycle 2 (April 1 – June 30), Cycle 3 (July 1 – September 30), Cycle 4 (October 1 – December 31), all deadlines at 5:00 pm Eastern Time. If deadline falls on weekend or Maryland State holiday, effective deadline is first non-holiday weekday. Montgomery County has two application periods per calendar year commencing August 11 and February 15.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (less than 250 employees) that have received SBIR or STTR awards within six months of the application cycle, including those in Montgomery County. Montgomery County applicants must conduct research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences and have a maximum of 20 employees at the time of application. Not primarily engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support commercialization of research and technology development for companies that have received federal SBIR/STTR awards. Phase 0 grants reimburse technical assistance expenditures related to pursuing Phase I grants, including training in writing and submitting SBIR/STTR applications. Phase 1 and Phase 2 grants support research and development for small business innovation and technology transfer projects, with up to 50% of Montgomery County matching grants usable for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance (fundraising, business model development, pitch decks), or commercialization assistance (developing minimum viable product, regulatory/reimbursement planning, market path) expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to companies throughout Maryland. Montgomery County applicants must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in the County.
requirements_list: Must have received an SBIR or STTR award within six months of the application cycle
Must submit application through TEDCO's online application portal or County Business Center website
Must meet all requirements specified in the Request for Application (RFA) document
Montgomery County applicants must comply with Executive Regulation 2-23
For Montgomery County: Must conduct research in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences
For Montgomery County: Must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in Montgomery County
For Montgomery County Phase 0: Must be pursuing first Phase I grant
For Montgomery County: Business must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
For Montgomery County: Business must have a maximum of 20 employees at the time of application

For Montgomery County Phase 0: Business must have been in operation for 5 years or less, have 0 prior SBIR/STTR awards, and have qualified reimbursable expenses related to a submitted SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal

For Montgomery County Phase 1: Business must have been in operation for 5 years or less, have received no more than 2 prior Phase 1 awards and 0 Phase 2 awards, and must have received notification of SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award in the current fiscal year

For Montgomery County Phase 2: Business must have been in operation for 7 years or less, have received no more than 4 prior Phase 1 awards and 1 prior Phase 2 award, and must have received notification of SBIR/STTR Phase 2 award in the current fiscal year
Reports must be marked "Confidential Business and Financial Information" at the top
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications online through TEDCO's application portal during specified application cycle open dates for statewide awards, or through the County Business Center website on a first-come-first-served basis for Montgomery County awards. Applications must be received by the application cycle deadline. Applicants will receive a confirmation email. Applications received by other means or after the deadline will not be considered. Montgomery County Phase 0 applicants must submit documentation of their retained technical assistance and subsequent SBIR/STTR application submission along with related expenses. Montgomery County administration follows policies and procedures established by Executive Regulation 2-23. Direct inquiries to sbir-ta@tedcomd.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training and mentorship program that helps Maryland small businesses in the life science and technology sectors develop and submit Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) proposals to federal agencies. TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate in the proposal lab, which provides comprehensive training materials, workshops, pitch development assistance, and proposal review to help companies secure Phase I federal funding. Participants receive training on business planning, commercialization, pitch writing, partnership development, and SAM.gov/Research.gov registration. Graduates have used the training to secure more than $29 million in SBIR and STTR Phase I and II funding from federal agencies including NSF, NIH, NASA, Air Force, and USDA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate in the proposal lab. The program provides two-part training: Part I focuses on foundational skills in business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing with 2 live workshops and hands-on learning. Part II provides 6 additional workshops for selected participants with approved NSF pitches. Participants receive comprehensive training materials including webinars, feedback adjudication training, guidance on partnerships and funding support letters, SAM.gov and Research.gov registration help, and access to market research tools. Participants engage in pitch development, receive business model advice, gain access to collaborative SharePoint portals, and receive proposal reviews. Graduates have secured up to $305,000 of Phase I non-dilutive federal funding per project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses in the life science and technology sectors seeking to apply for federal SBIR/STTR funding with compelling innovations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance for developing SBIR/STTR proposals to secure Phase I federal funding of up to $305,000 in non-dilutive funding from federal agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program recruits a cohort of small businesses across Maryland's 24 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a small business in Maryland
Must be in the life science or technology sector
Must have a compelling innovation
Must be registered with SAM.gov and Research.gov
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies apply through the application link on the TEDCO website. TEDCO selects up to 25 companies to participate. Before the official start of the virtual lab, participants receive comprehensive training materials. The program consists of Part I with 2 live workshops focused on foundational skills, and qualified participants advance to Part II with 6 additional workshops. Participants engage in pitch development, receive business model advice, gain access to collaborative SharePoint portals, and receive proposal reviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps Maryland technology and life sciences companies build expertise to access federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) funding. The program provides workshops on federal SBIR/STTR program requirements, agency-specific processes, and proposal writing, along with individual expert proposal reviews.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers multi-part technical assistance including workshops covering federal SBIR/STTR program overviews, agency-specific program sessions (DoD, NIH, DoE), and practical training on proposal writing, commercialization planning, and budget preparation. Participants also receive two rounds of individual proposal reviews from technical and business experts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses seeking federal SBIR/STTR funding, particularly those with limited experience in securing federal small business research and development investments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and training to support business applications for federal SBIR/STTR grants; assistance covers proposal development, commercialization planning, and budget preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland small business
Must not have been previously awarded an SBIR/STTR grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply through the online form. TEDCO will work with each participant and domain experts to determine the review schedule for proposal reviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Technology Development Corporation's seed funding program that invests in early-stage technology and life sciences companies showing promise of becoming venture fundable or sustainable through customer revenue and follow-on funding. Provides convertible note or equity investments ranging from $100,000 to $500,000 for seed stage businesses. Four types of investments available: cybersecurity/information technology, life sciences, technology commercialization, and gap funding. The program is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investments and convertible debt in seed-stage companies ranging from $100,000 to $500,000 made through convertible debt and equity instruments. Four fund types available: Cybersecurity Investment Fund, Life Sciences Investment Fund, Technology Commercialization Fund, and Gap Investment Fund. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required for some funding sources. Gap Fund proceeds restricted to new hires in Maryland only. The program is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology-based entrepreneurs and founders building seed-stage technology and life sciences companies with potential to become venture fundable or sustainable businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Product development, commercialization, and seed stage capital for early-stage technology and life sciences companies to reach venture funding potential or sustainability. Gap Fund proceeds restricted to new hires in Maryland only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Principal place of business must be in Maryland with more than 50% of workforce working from a physical location in Maryland. Company headquarters must be in Maryland with majority of workforce in Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at tedcomd.com/seed-funds. Applications are assessed on a rolling/ongoing basis. Applicants should email seed@tedcomd.com after submission to confirm receipt.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Social Impact Funds is an equity investment program providing early-stage funding to pre-seed technology startups founded by economically and socially disadvantaged individuals in Maryland. The program offers equity investments typically starting at $100,000 and ranging up to $750,000, along with executive support, mentorship, and networking resources to help companies reach sustainability and follow-on funding. Eligible startups must be technology-based companies with intellectual property potential, have a principal place of business in Maryland, at least one full-time employee, and more than half of their workforce based in Maryland. The fund includes multiple vehicles such as the Pre-Seed Builder Fund and Inclusion Fund, intentionally created to engage and invest in economically underserved founders and communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investment typically starting at $100,000 and ranging up to $750,000 for early-stage technology-based startups. Minimum 1:1 private capital match required for equity investments. Includes hands-on and educational executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship and collaboration, and networking opportunities. Five-year commitment agreement with clawback provision required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications assessed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage Maryland technology-based companies founded by socially and economically disadvantaged entrepreneurs. Builder Fund targets companies with at least 50% ownership by individuals demonstrating economic and social disadvantage. Inclusion Fund targets companies with at least 30% ownership by individuals demonstrating economic and social disadvantage, controlled and managed by such individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investment for early-stage technology-based businesses for general business operations and growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Company headquarters must be in Maryland. More than half of workforce must work from physical location in Maryland. Five-year commitment agreement required.

Fewer than 251 employees
Less than $15 million in dilutive funding received
At least one full-time employee

Founders/officers/managers must agree to receive executive support
