Inclusion Fund: at least 30% ownership by individuals demonstrating social and economic disadvantage, controlled and managed by such individuals for at least one year post-investment
Corporations or limited liability companies (not sole proprietorships)
Five-year commitment agreement with clawback provision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are assessed on an ongoing rolling basis. All applications must be submitted online through TEDCO's website application page. After submission, applicants should email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. Applications received through other means such as email or mail will not be considered. Contact TEDCO for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Evergreen venture capital funds dedicated to funding and growing early-stage businesses in Maryland. TEDCO provides equity investment to support entrepreneurs with experienced operating and venture expertise. The program funds early-stage venture capital limited partnerships focused on investing in Maryland-based technology and life science companies. TEDCO is sector-agnostic and highly opportunistic, backing early-stage businesses led by entrepreneurs with a track record of execution. The fund has over $110 million in assets under management. Funded by Maryland state taxpayer dollars and subject to Maryland laws and regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investments in early-stage technology and life science companies. Investment in early-stage companies to help them grow and succeed. TEDCO is sector-agnostic and highly opportunistic, backing early-stage businesses led by entrepreneurs with a track record of execution. Limited partnership investment with TEDCO Standard Limited Partnership terms and fees meeting SSBCI guidelines for venture capital funds focused on Maryland investment. The fund has over $110 million in assets under management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage technology and life science company founders and entrepreneurs committed to Maryland. Early-stage venture capital funds seeking to invest in Maryland companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business growth and development for early-stage technology and life science companies. Capital for venture capital funds to invest in Maryland-based businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based companies with more than 50% of workforce working from a physical location in Maryland. Headquarters must be in Maryland where principal business operations are conducted. Companies must make a 5-year commitment to Maryland (clawback agreement required).

Early-stage company (started operations within 7 years of application date)

No more than 250 employees

Headquarters in Maryland
Willing to sign 5-year clawback agreement

Generally first institutional investor or first institutional round

Applicants must submit applications online through TEDCO's website application portal at tedcomd.com/venturefund. After submission, applicants should email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. The TEDCO investment team evaluates applications. Applications received through email or mail will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive support initiative providing legal, accounting, and financial advisory services, access to capital, and region-wide resources to help socially and economically disadvantaged business owners and very small businesses become investment-ready and grow and scale their business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive no-cost advisory services including BRIDGE Assessment, individualized roadmaps, financial literacy training, credit repair coaching, legal services, back-office accounting support, proposal development assistance, and executive mentoring. The program connects businesses to capital resources including State Small Business Credit Initiative funds and federal funding from infrastructure and economic programs. Provides advisory services, access to capital, and region-wide resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and economically disadvantaged business owners and very small businesses with fewer than ten employees in Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, and the District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance to prepare businesses for capital access, including financial infrastructure development, business readiness assessment, credit improvement, legal formation support, and federal grant proposal development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The three-year project serves businesses in Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, and the District of Columbia through partnerships with Small Business Development Centers and law clinics.
requirements_list: Must be a socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI)-owned business or very small business with fewer than 10 employees
Delaware residents can sign up through the Maryland SBDC
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online application form at tedco.tfaforms.net. Businesses can also register for the monthly virtual BRIDGE Program Open Forum held on the third Thursday at 10:00 AM to learn more about the program. Attend the Open Forum to learn more about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by TEDCO that provides funding to SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II awardees to enhance their project's commercialization potential. The program focuses on overcoming technical challenges, optimizing commercialization strategies, and minimizing risks associated with bringing innovative products or processes to market. TEDCO provides expert support including technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercial road mapping, investment readiness assessment, and IP and regulatory affairs support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal agencies provide funding to SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II awardees for technical and business assistance. Phase I offers up to $6,500 per award, which may be in addition to the award amount depending on the federal agency. Phase II provides up to $50,000 per project, with the funding approach varying by agency—either as part of the award budget or in addition to it. TEDCO provides expert support including technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercial road mapping, investment readiness assessment, and IP and regulatory affairs support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies with SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II awards that have fewer than 250 employees, with CEO and 50% of the company located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Make better technical decisions, solve technical problems during SBIR/STTR projects, minimize technical risks, and commercialize SBIR/STTR products or processes including intellectual property protections. Can be used for business strategy, operations, product sales, IP protection, market research, market validation, regulatory planning, and manufacturing plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland company with CEO and 50% of the company located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Maryland company with fewer than 250 employees
CEO and 50% of the company are in Maryland
Must be a current SBIR/STTR Phase I or Phase II awardee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties should apply early in the SBIR/STTR funding cycle through the online application form. TEDCO will perform an initial assessment and schedule conversations with the applicant to identify specific technical and business needs. TEDCO will work with the applicant and an expert to develop a Statement of Work (SOW) that outlines specific TABA support services. Monthly check-ins are scheduled to monitor progress and address emerging needs. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted at the conclusion of the support period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Technology Validation Program (Bowie State/Frostburg State Pilot)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to expand opportunities for technology validation, entrepreneurial development, and industry engagement at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University. Faculty members conduct proof-of-principle studies to validate a technology's commercial use and advance it toward generating intellectual property or attracting licensees, plus they develop market analysis and commercialization plans. The program supports technology development in Maryland's Comprehensive Universities and fosters the transfer of technology to commercial entities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $50,000 grant award to full-time faculty completed within a 6-month project period. The award includes two components: (1) Technology Development Report—up to $40,000 to conduct proof-of-principle studies that validate a technology's use for a specific commercial application and advance it to where it can generate strong intellectual property or attract a prospective licensee; (2) Market Assessment—up to $10,000 to support a market analysis and the development of a Commercialization Plan for the technology. Eligible expenses include personnel and fringe benefits, materials and supplies, other direct costs (itemized), and up to $4,000 for intellectual property protection expenses. Indirect costs are not allowed, and travel costs are not permitted unless justified as critical.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proof-of-principle studies to validate a technology's commercial use, advance intellectual property development, market analysis, creation of a Commercialization Plan, personnel and fringe benefits, materials and supplies, other direct costs, and up to $4,000 for intellectual property protection expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Faculty must be at Bowie State University (Central Maryland) or Frostburg State University (Western Maryland).
requirements_list: Must be full-time faculty at Bowie State University or Frostburg State University
Project must be completed within 6-month period
Must include Technology Development Report component
Must include Market Assessment component
Subject Technology must be disclosed to university technology transfer office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Faculty submit applications according to the RFA (Request for Funding Announcement) posted by TEDCO. Rolling application submissions accepted from 3/15/2024 to 6/01/2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to enhance technology commercialization and provide technical and business assistance to small and early-stage companies in urban Maryland. The program offers mentoring, connections to support programs, and guidance for developing emerging technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical and business assistance provided by TEDCO's Venture Growth Advisors. Support includes mentoring, connections to collaborative partners, grant funding through UBII project funding, the Builder Fund, guidance on technology commercialization, market channels, financing options, management team building, SBIR and STTR proposal writing assistance, and prototype development. Each urban region has a dedicated Venture Growth Advisor.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tammira Lucas (Baltimore City), Malcolm Tyson (Prince George's County), Claudius Taylor (Central Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and early-stage companies in urban Maryland focusing on technology commercialization and innovation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology commercialization, market development, financing, management team building, prototype development, and SBIR/STTR proposal preparation. Companies receive mentoring and connections to funding opportunities and educational programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Baltimore City, Prince George's County, and Central Maryland (Howard County area). Each urban region has a dedicated Venture Growth Advisor.
requirements_list: Must be a small or early-stage company
Must be located in supported urban areas (Baltimore City, Prince George's County, or Central Maryland)

Should be focused on supported sectors such as cybersecurity, educational software, environmental solutions, govtech, renewable energy, IoT devices, nanotechnology, public health and safety, social impact, software development, transportation and mobility, or urban farming
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Companies are evaluated by TEDCO's Venture Growth Advisors who work in their respective regions. Interested companies should contact their regional Venture Growth Advisor. The advisor evaluates potential clients and provides mentoring and connections to support programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Contract Financing Program provides direct loans to eligible businesses for working capital and equipment acquisition needed to begin, continue, or complete work on government or utility-regulated contracts. Loans are limited to $2,000,000 and must be repaid during the contract term. Applicants may qualify for financing before contract award, and revolving lines of credit are renewable annually. Financing is available to for-profit and non-profit businesses, sole proprietors, and individuals that cannot obtain adequate business financing through normal channels due to identified physical handicaps, membership in historically disadvantaged groups, or other social or economic impediments. The program supports businesses performing work on contracts where a majority of funds are provided by a federal, state, or local government agency or utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans up to $2,000,000 at Prime Rate + 2% interest. Principal and interest payments are made as contract proceeds are received in amounts satisfactory to MMG Capital Group and the Authority. All payments must be assigned to the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority. Financing is available in the form of revolving lines of credit renewable on an annual basis. Financing term matches the duration of the contract(s). Applicants may qualify for financing prior to contract award. Financing can be used for working capital, purchase of machinery and equipment, and supplies and materials required to perform government or utility-regulated contracts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses, sole proprietors, small business owners, entrepreneurs, and minority, women, or veteran-owned enterprises that cannot obtain adequate business financing through normal channels due to identified physical handicaps, membership in historically disadvantaged groups, or other social or economic impediments. Applicants must have their principal place of business in Maryland and must have been denied a loan by a financial institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, purchase of machinery and equipment, supplies and materials required to perform government or utility-regulated contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Company must have its principal place of business in Maryland. Funds are for contracts where a majority of funds are provided by a federal, state, or local government agency or utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission.
requirements_list: Principals must be of good moral character and have a reputation for financial responsibility
Company must have its principal place of business in Maryland

Company must be unable to obtain adequate business financing on reasonable terms through normal channels due to: an identifiable physical handicap that severely limits the ability to obtain financial assistance; membership in a group historically deprived of access to normal economic or financial resources because of race, color, creed, sex, religion, or national origin; or any other social or economic impediment beyond the applicant's control such as lack of formal education, financial capacity, or geographical or regional economic distress
Company must have applied for and been denied a loan by a financial institution, evidenced by a turndown letter
If the applicant is other than a sole proprietorship, at least 70 percent of the business enterprise must be owned by individuals who meet the qualifications for applicants
Issuance of a loan must generate substantial economic impact (job creation or retention, and tax revenue for the state) in relation to the amount of the loan
Majority of contract funds must be provided by federal, state, or local government agency or utilities regulated by Public Service Commission
Individuals with at least 51 percent ownership must have a personal FICO Score 8 of at least 550
All owners must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents

Applicant cannot be engaged in: Real Estate Development, Real Estate (not being used by applicant), Adult Entertainment Establishments, Bars, Film and Theater Productions, Gambling/Sports Betting, Recording Studio, or Cannabis Dispensaries
Applicant or any owners/officers cannot be under active bankruptcy plan
Applicant or any owners/officers cannot be past due on federal or state (business or personal) taxes or other federal debt unless a written, executed payment agreement exists
Applicants may qualify for financing prior to contract award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register and complete the application form via the online platform or submit the MMG Capital Group questionnaire form to receive a program recommendation based on your responses. Pay the applicable non-refundable application fee (ranging from $250 to $3,500 depending on loan size) at the time of application submission. Upload all required documents to the platform. Application is assigned to a Loan/Investment Officer for review, typically completed within 2-4 weeks depending on application quality and completeness. The officer may request additional documents or information. Once review is complete and financing is recommended for approval, applications over $350,000 are submitted to the MSBDFA Board (which meets twice a month) for approval; applications of $350,000 or less are reviewed by the MMG Capital Group Internal Loan Committee. If approved, you receive a commitment letter and term sheet within approximately 3 business days. You have 14 days to review and decide whether to proceed. Sign and return the commitment letter along with the administrative fee. Upon receipt, MMG's attorney will contact you to prepare financing documents and schedule closing. You are responsible for all expenses in connection with the financing including legal fees. After closing, executed documents are forwarded and the loan proceeds are disbursed generally within 1-7 business days by check or ACH direct deposit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides loan guaranties and interest rate subsidies for loans made by financial institutions to small businesses. The program guaranties a portion of loans and can subsidize up to 4 percentage points of interest charged by the financial institution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan guaranties of the lesser of 80 percent of the loan or up to $2,000,000. Guaranties cannot exceed 10 years with an interest rate charged by the financial institution limited to prime plus 2 percent. GFP can also subsidize up to 4 percentage points of the interest being charged by the financial institution. The subsidy is subject to annual review, and terms of repayment of the subsidy are negotiated directly with the borrower.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses unable to obtain adequate financing through normal channels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, acquisition and installation of machinery or equipment, refinancing of existing debt, and purchase of and improvements to real property owned or leased by the applicant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Casino Business Investment Fund provides affordable, flexible, and patient capital to small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in Maryland. Funding comes from 1.5% of video lottery terminal proceeds at Maryland casinos and is managed by the Maryland Department of Commerce. The program offers multiple financing products including senior loans, subordinated loans, loans with equity features, lines of credit, term loans, demand loans, letters of credit, convertible subordinated notes, preferred stock, common stock, warrants, and surety bonding (bid, payment, and performance bonds). MCBIF assists with business acquisitions, equipment purchases, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, working capital needs, refinancing existing debt, machinery and equipment, improvements to real property, inventory, construction/renovation, marketing, professional and technical assistance, and personnel expansion.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MCBIF provides senior loans, subordinated loans, loans with equity features, term loans, lines of credit, demand loans, letters of credit, convertible subordinated notes, preferred stock, common stock, warrants, and surety bonding products (bid, payment, and performance bonds). Funding ranges from $50,000 to $1,000,000. Term loans range from 1 to 10 years with interest rates generally between 4% and 8% for term loans and 4% to 7% for lines of credit. Professional and technical assistance loans have rates of 2% to 4%. Application fee is $250 non-refundable. Commitment fee ranges from $500 to $3,500. At least 50% of investment funds must go to businesses in communities surrounding video lottery terminal facilities (casinos); 50% can go to businesses anywhere in Maryland. Direct loans and equity financing are available for acquisition of businesses, equipment, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, and leasehold improvements. Working capital assistance is available for maintaining and improving business cash flow, marketing, adding personnel, inventory expansion, and obtaining professional consulting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, minority-owned businesses, women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, and individuals in Maryland seeking capital for business acquisition, equipment, real estate, working capital, or other business purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of businesses, equipment, owner-occupied commercial real estate, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, working capital, marketing, personnel expansion, inventory expansion, professional consulting and technical assistance, refinancing existing debt, machinery and equipment, and improvements to real property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have their principal place of business in Maryland and be eligible to receive funds from Maryland casino video lottery terminal proceeds. At least 50% of investment funds must go to businesses in communities surrounding video lottery terminal facilities located in Baltimore City (Horseshoe Casino), Cecil County (Hollywood Casino Perryville), Allegany County (Rocky Gap Casino Resort), Anne Arundel County (Maryland Live Casino), Worcester County (Casino at Ocean Downs), and Prince George's County (MGM National Harbor). The remaining 50% can go to businesses anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women-owned, or veteran-owned business
Must have principal place of business in Maryland
Must be unable to obtain adequate business financing on reasonable terms through normal channels
Generally businesses must have been operating for at least two years; startups considered if principals have significant industry experience
Business and personal credit scores will be considered, including those with less than fair credit
Personal guarantees of debt required
Collateral: full, limited, and no collateral coverage considered
Life insurance required on key principals if insurable for loans exceeding $100,000
Business plan required for all applicants
Minimum equity injection of 10% or greater expected for new businesses
Minimum down payment of 10% or greater expected for asset purchases
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the funds under management, application process, program guidelines, and FAQs. Use the smart APPLICATION QUESTIONNAIRE/TOOL to assess qualification and find the best program. Complete an application questionnaire to determine the best program. Submit complete application package with all supplemental information. Loans of $350,000 or less receive a decision within 15 business days; loans exceeding $350,000 receive a decision within 25 business days. If approved, closings typically occur 20 to 45 days from receipt of the signed commitment letter and commitment fee. Applications are submitted through MMG Capital Group's online application portals for processing and evaluation. Applicants may also contact Taber J. Small, Vice President and Loan Officer, for application information and assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that assists eligible small businesses in obtaining bid, performance, or payment bonds needed to perform on contracts where a majority of funds are provided by a government agency, public utility company, or private entity. The program can directly issue bonds or guarantee a surety's losses from contractor breach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program directly issues bid, performance, or payment bonds or guarantees a surety's losses resulting from contractor breach. Bonds directly issued are limited to $2,500,000. Guaranties are limited to 90 percent of the face value of the bond not to exceed $2,500,000. Guaranties on bonds remain in effect for the duration of the surety's exposure. Directly issued bonds remain in effect for the duration of the qualified contract and any related warranty period. Bond premiums generally range from 2 to 3 percent. A surety bond revolving line of credit may be established to directly issue or guarantee multiple bonds within pre-approved terms and limitations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses needing bid, performance, or payment bonds to perform on contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obtaining bid, performance, or payment bonds necessary to perform on government, utility, or private entity contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A capital deployment program aimed at serving under-served markets through efficient deployment of capital to create wealth.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not specified on this page.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified on this page.

Also includes RSVP opportunities and the RSVP/AARP Tax-Aide Program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can contact the Montgomery County Volunteer Center for personal consultations to match their skills and interests with volunteer opportunities. More information is available at www.montgomeryserves.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free tax preparation assistance is offered each year to low-to-moderate-income Montgomery County taxpayers. Services are provided by trained volunteers and are available by appointment only.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax preparation assistance

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's ACCESS to Behavioral Health Services program provides comprehensive assessment and linkages for low-income persons of all ages living in Montgomery County who have no commercial insurance and who are in need of services for major mental health and/or substance abuse problems. Services include in-person or telephone clinical assessment, financial screening, referral for public services, consultation to agencies and programs, and information about mental health services in Montgomery County. Bridges Transitional Psychiatry provides counseling and psychiatry for uninsured clients transitioning to community services. Staff may assist with obtaining additional social service resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive behavioral health assessment and referral services provided in-person or by telephone. Services include clinical assessment, financial screening, and referral for public services. Consultations available to agencies and programs, and information about mental health services in Montgomery County. Bridges Transitional Psychiatry provides counseling and psychiatry for uninsured clients transitioning to community services. Staff may assist with obtaining additional social service resources. Fees are charged for assessments, counseling, and visits with prescribers. Sliding fee schedule applied for uninsured clients based on income verification. Maryland Medicaid and Medicare accepted with client co-payments. Clients will not be denied services based on ability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income persons of all ages living in Montgomery County who have no commercial insurance and who need services for major mental health and/or substance abuse problems. Telephone consultation and information and referral services available for all residents and professionals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health and substance use disorder assessment, referral services, consultations, counseling, psychiatry services, and social service resource assistance.

Must have major mental health and/or substance abuse needs requiring public services
Must be age 18 or older for assessment and referral services
Must be uninsured with no or low income, or have Medicaid or Medicare insurance
Must provide identification and proof of residency at in-person visit
Must provide proof of insurance and/or income if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1770 for information. Walk-in assessment and referral services available Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on a first-come, first-served basis. Individuals seeking behavioral health assessments are recommended to arrive at 8:30 a.m. or 12:30 p.m. Apply in person at 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 101, Rockville, MD 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: ADA Facility Remediation at Childcare Facilities
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides remediation of non-compliant Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) interior and exterior issues at seven childcare facilities operated by Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services. The work includes removing barriers to accessibility, creating accessible paths of travel, widening doorways, providing accessible plumbing fixtures, installing signage with Braille, and relocating devices to ensure compliance with ADA standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County Government directly funds and manages the design and construction of ADA remediation work at seven designated childcare facilities. Work includes facility modifications, accessibility improvements, and ongoing construction through fiscal year 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The seven childcare facilities in Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services Child Care in Public Space program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: ADA facility remediation and compliance improvements at childcare centers, including removal of accessibility barriers, creation of accessible paths, doorway widening, plumbing fixture accessibility, signage installation, and device relocation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at seven specific childcare facilities in Montgomery County located in Cabin John, Silver Spring, Chevy Chase, Rockville, Potomac, and Germantown.
requirements_list: Facility must be one of the seven designated childcare centers in Montgomery County's DHHS Child Care in Public Space program
Work scope must address documented ADA non-compliance as identified in compliance surveys
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: General project planning took place between fiscal years 2019 through 2022. Design for projects began in fiscal year 2021. Design and construction work continues through fiscal year 2029. Montgomery County coordinates all aspects of planning and construction.

structured_extraction.program_name: ALERT / Alcohol Law Education Regulatory Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive training program designed to educate Montgomery County servers, sellers, managers, owners, and government personnel in alcohol beverage regulatory compliance and responsible service. Participants learn how to develop responsible alcohol policies, understand intoxication factors and visible signs of intoxication, review issues identified by County and State enforcement agencies, and employ effective intervention strategies. Training covers the sale, consumption, and regulation of alcohol.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online and virtual training in multiple formats. Community sessions held from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM on the 2nd and 4th Monday of every month (except holidays). Government personnel training is 3 to 4 hours including exam. No cost to attend. Registration required. Training available in English and Spanish, with materials in additional languages including Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Servers, sellers, managers, and owners of alcohol beverage establishments in Montgomery County, and Montgomery County government personnel
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on alcohol beverage regulatory compliance, responsible alcohol policies, intoxication factors, visible signs of intoxication, enforcement issues, and workplace intervention strategies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to alcohol beverage establishments and Montgomery County government agencies in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Participants must join by 10:15 AM or will not be admitted for community sessions
Participants must be from Montgomery County government agencies for government personnel training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online for ALERT community training sessions (space is limited), or email the Alcohol Beverage Services office to express interest in government personnel training.

structured_extraction.program_description: A structured hybrid program spanning 24-30 weeks tailored for individuals who exhibit a pattern of abusive behaviors, including coercive and controlling behaviors in intimate partner relationships. The program uses cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques and a specialized curriculum to increase accountability, foster empathy, and promote healthier relationship dynamics while breaking the cycle of violence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants engage in a 24-30 week hybrid program with weekly group meetings using cognitive-behavioral therapy and specialized curriculum. Intake and registration fee is $50, class fee is $20 per week, and individual counseling is $40. A sliding scale based on income is available for participants unable to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and non-residents whose intimate partner violence incident occurred in Montgomery County. Individuals must be referred by Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services agents, case workers, Montgomery County courts, or attorneys.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques and structured curriculum for addressing patterns of abusive behaviors and promoting healthier relationship dynamics. Individual counseling is also available.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents (male or female) who are involved in intimate partner violence, or non-Montgomery County residents whose incident occurred in Montgomery County.

Involved in intimate partner violence
Must have a referral from Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services agents, case workers, Montgomery County courts, and/or attorneys
Must provide participant ID and court documents including Statement of Charges, court documents, and probation contracts
Must complete program consecutively following an enrollment agreement
Can only receive one credit per week
Must attend weekly group meetings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants must have a referral from their respective Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services agents, case workers, Montgomery County courts, and/or attorneys available to schedule an intake. All referrals must include participant ID and court documents including Statement of Charges, court documents, and probation contracts. Other necessary documents may be requested.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship experience for academic credit and professional development

Completion of at least two years of college, with one year in criminal justice, behavioral science, or human services related discipline
Must pass a background investigation and physical exam to include drug screening
Selection through an interview
Valid academic enrollment or requirements from a college or university

structured_extraction.program_description: A dental care program for uninsured or underinsured adults in Montgomery County with family income at or below 250% of federal poverty guidelines. The program provides dental services including examinations, cleanings, non-surgical extractions, and limited oral surgery at county dental clinics. Services are provided at a reduced fee of $20 per visit for regular appointments and $30 for emergency visits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Dental care services including examinations, cleanings, non-surgical extractions, and limited oral surgery provided at reduced fees of $20 per visit for regular appointments and $30 for emergency visits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured or underinsured adults ages 19-59 who are Montgomery County residents with family income at or below 250% of federal poverty guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Dental services including examinations, cleanings, non-surgical extractions, and limited oral surgery.

Must be uninsured or have no dental insurance
Family income must not exceed 250% of federal poverty guidelines

Not enrolled for health insurance including Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance or employee-sponsored coverage

Alternatively, apply online through the Community Connect Portal starting January 1, 2025. After enrollment, call the clinic closest to your home to schedule an appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides supervised housing and assistance to disabled adults using family homes and small assisted living homes in the community. Case management is provided, as well as subsidy when funds are available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supervised housing and assistance in family homes and small assisted living homes. Case management is provided without regard to income or assets. Placements are subsidized for eligible applicants. A resident's contribution to the cost of care is based on the individual's income. Residents may keep a small personal allowance each month ranging between $60-$139 depending on income and subsidy source.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled adults age 18 and older who are unable to live independently due to mental, physical, and/or developmental disabilities. For Certified Residential Environments, applicants must be Maryland residents. For Assisted Living, applicants must be residents of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supervised housing, assistance with daily living, and case management services in community-based family or assisted living homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: For Certified Residential Environments, Maryland residents age 18 and older are eligible. For Assisted Living, applicants must be residents of Montgomery County.

Unable to live independently due to mental, physical, and/or developmental disabilities
Maryland resident (for Certified Residential Environments)
Montgomery County resident (for Assisted Living)
Income and asset documentation review required as part of clinical assessment

structured_extraction.program_description: A short-term financing program that provides subordinate acquisition loans to developers and community-based organizations to acquire and preserve affordable housing properties at risk of losing affordability. The fund offers short-term revolving loans designed to help developers and organizations bid competitively to maintain affordability, preserve housing for current renters at affordable rents, and protect tenants from displacement. Montgomery County's partnership with National Housing Trust is expected to result in $20 million deployed for affordable housing acquisitions, with County funds matched at least 3:1 with private lending.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate acquisition loans from a dedicated pool of funds, with Montgomery County's partnership with National Housing Trust expected to deploy $20 million for affordable housing acquisitions. The financing is designed to cover gaps in financing for property acquisitions after senior loans and other funding sources are secured, and to enable developers and organizations to acquire properties quickly and position them for longer-term affordability. County funds are matched at least 3:1 with private lending. Applications must include plans for refinancing to ensure long-term affordability and repay the AHOF funding. Loan must be repaid within three years or refinanced for longer-term affordability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications reviewed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable housing developers, non-profit organizations, tenant associations, and community-based organizations seeking to acquire and preserve affordable housing and protect tenants from displacement in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and preservation of affordable housing properties, including purchase financing and property acquisition costs to preserve affordability and protect current renters from displacement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an affordable housing developer, non-profit organization, tenant association, or community-based organization
Property must be at risk of loss of affordability
Applications must include plans for refinancing to ensure long-term affordability
Loan must be repaid within three years or refinanced for longer-term affordability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective applicants should contact the Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs for information on the application process and requirements. Developers can submit applications to the National Housing Trust Community Development Fund (NHTCDF), which coordinates applications from developers and arranges private capital to combine with Montgomery County funds. Developers can find the Term Sheet, FAQ, and application process information on the NHTCDF webpage or contact NHTCDF at 202-333-8921 ext. 153 or sfraser@nhtinc.org with subject line AHOF Loan Inquiry.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share assistance program for qualified Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs for business projects essential to improvement or expansion of agricultural enterprises. MARBIDCO and Montgomery County Office of Agriculture contribute up to half of total project cost, not to exceed $6,000 per project (with an additional $1,000 available for projects over $20,000). The program helps farmers and agricultural businesses fund infrastructure projects, equipment purchases, and other improvements that enhance the agricultural economy or enable future revenue and employment growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A cost-share matching grant where MARBIDCO and OAG match up to $3,000 per project, and the applicant must invest at least half of the total project cost. The program provides up to $15,000 lifetime limit per company (MARBIDCO funding). Applicants may apply up to twice per fiscal year for different projects. Total program contribution does not exceed $6,000 per project, with an additional $1,000 available for projects over $20,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural entrepreneurs and businesses headquartered in Montgomery County, including table crop farmers, vineyard operators, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and non-traditional agricultural enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure projects, equipment purchases, and projects that enhance the agricultural economy or enable future revenue and employment growth for agricultural enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural enterprise must be headquartered in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Agricultural business must be registered with State of Maryland and in good standing
Applicant must be headquartered in Montgomery County
Applicant must invest at least half of total project cost
Applicant must apply to and receive approval from the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts and Entertainment District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in an Arts and Entertainment District that are wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying residing artist or an arts and entertainment enterprise. The credit applies for 10 years based on growth in property assessments. Credit rates decrease over the 10-year period: Years 1-5 (80% of assessment increase), Year 6 (70%), Year 7 (60%), Year 8 (50%), Year 9 (40%), Year 10 (30%). For properties with Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, the Arts and Entertainment Credit is 20% of the rates listed above, added to the Enterprise Zone Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit for manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in Arts and Entertainment Districts renovated for use by qualifying residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises. Credit applies for 10 years. Base-year assessment is the real property assessment for the year before renovation. Credit rates decrease over 10 years: Years 1-5 (80% of assessment increase), Year 6 (70%), Year 7 (60%), Year 8 (50%), Year 9 (40%), Year 10 (30%). For properties with Enterprise Zone Tax Credit, Arts and Entertainment Credit is 20% of the rates listed above, added to Enterprise Zone Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners seeking to renovate manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in Arts and Entertainment Districts for use by qualifying artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for renovated buildings in Arts and Entertainment Districts used by qualifying artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building must be manufacturing, commercial, or industrial
Building must be located in Arts and Entertainment District
Building must be wholly or partially renovated for use by qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
Must continue to be used by qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise throughout 10-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Administered by Department of Finance. Property owner applies for credit. Credit is based on increase in property assessment from base-year compared to renovation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bridges to Behavioral Health Services Transitional Psychiatry Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A short-term, intensive psychiatric support program designed to bridge the gap between acute psychiatric care and long-term outpatient treatment. It serves individuals stepping down from inpatient hospitalization or crisis stabilization units, as well as those unable to readily connect with community providers. The program reduces the risk of relapse and re-hospitalization by providing structured psychiatric care, medication management, and therapeutic support.

The program accepts Maryland Medicaid and Medicare, with clients responsible for co-payments. A sliding fee schedule is used for uninsured clients based on income verification. Clients will not be denied services based on ability to pay or immigration status.

Montgomery County residents age 18 or older.

structured_extraction.program_description: A County and State subsidized taxi service for low-income seniors aged 65 and older and low-income persons with disabilities ages 18-64 residing in Montgomery County. The program provides subsidized taxi trips to help with transportation to medical and personal appointments. Subsidy assistance is provided on a sliding fee scale determined by total household income. The program is designed as a supplement to Montgomery County's local transportation services and provides curb-to-curb taxicab service at discounted rates.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subsidized taxi rides using CNR swipe cards with a sliding fee scale based on household income. For a family of one earning up to $15,856 yearly, the monthly cost is $5.25 per $60 value; $15,857-$21,403 yearly costs $10.00 per $60 value; $21,404-$26,951 yearly costs $20.00 per $60 value; and $26,952-$39,000 yearly costs $30.00 per $60 value. Maximum accumulated balance on swipe card is $360. Wheelchair accessible transport is available. All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with exceptions for approved medical facilities in Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, Washington, DC, and other designated medical facilities in designated service areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 30 days from the date of recertification letter

All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with exceptions for transportation to approved medical facilities in Baltimore, Prince George's County, Northern Virginia, Washington, DC, and other designated service areas.

Ages 65+ eligible regardless of disability status

Valid photo ID required if swipe card lacks photograph
Advance booking recommended

Submit via fax, email, mail, or in-person to Montgomery County Department of Transportation, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. Application process can take up to 30 days. If approved, receive welcome packet with program information. Call participating taxicab company with CNR card number, name, pick-up and drop-off information to schedule rides.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Montgomery Watershed Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds public outreach and stewardship projects, and community-based restoration water quality implementation projects in Montgomery County. Projects educate and engage residents in watershed improvement while achieving measurable impacts and sustainable behavior change to reduce pollutants and improve water quality in local streams and waterways. The program supports watershed restoration and clean water projects that reduce stormwater pollution and achieve healthier streams.

Preference is given to projects with match and/or in-kind services. Grants support watershed restoration and clean water projects that reduce stormwater pollution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing
structured_extraction.program_description: Commercial PACE (Property-Assessed Clean Energy) Financing provides lower-cost, long-term flexible financing for commercial property owners to pay for clean energy improvements and building upgrades. The program helps qualifying commercial property owners finance energy efficiency, water efficiency, renewable energy, building decarbonization, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, and environmental health and safety measures. Property owners can finance up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements and repay the financing as a surcharge on the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The loan stays with the property and transfers to any subsequent owner until fully paid. Eligible uses include planned renovations, completed renovations within the last 12 months, and new construction projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private lenders provide long-term flexible financing for up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements including energy efficiency, water efficiency, renewable energy systems, climate resiliency and adaptation upgrades, environmental health and safety improvements, and building decarbonization. Financing is repaid through annual or semi-annual surcharges added to the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The loan obligation remains with the property and transfers to subsequent owners until fully paid off.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners in Montgomery County seeking to finance clean energy improvements and building upgrades
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, water efficiency improvements, renewable energy system upgrades, building decarbonization, climate resiliency and adaptation measures, environmental health and safety upgrades, and other clean energy improvements to commercial properties. Can be used for planned renovations, completed renovations within the last 12 months, or new construction projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to qualifying commercial properties in Montgomery County, Maryland only. Program applies only to commercial properties, not residential properties.
requirements_list: Property must be a qualifying commercial property (not residential)
Property must be located in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Building owners, capital providers, and contractors interested in the C-PACE program should contact the Montgomery County Green Bank to learn more about getting started. Additional details and program application procedures are available through the Montgomery County Green Bank's C-PACE Program Webpage and the Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program providing financial assistance to homeowner associations, condominium associations, and cooperative housing projects experiencing financial hardship in Montgomery County to address immediate health or safety repairs in common areas. The program provides loans up to $500,000 with no interest, repayable over up to 15 years, to help associations fund critical repairs such as failing water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, and parking lots. Loans are provided with a 1% loan commitment fee and must be secured by a pledge of current and future association assets. The association must contribute a minimum of 20% of the total project costs toward the repairs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are provided up to a maximum of $500,000 with no interest charged. A 1% loan commitment fee is required for the total approved loan amount. Loans are repaid over a period of up to 15 years and are secured by a pledge of current and future association assets. Loans are subordinate to other loans. The association must contribute a minimum of 20% of the total project costs toward the repairs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs or replacements in common areas to address health, safety, or occupancy risks, including failing water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, underground and surface stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, parking lots, and predevelopment construction-related services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports food assistance provider and food recovery organizations that deliver no-cost food services to Montgomery County residents. The program ensures continuity of essential community food assistance services while closing service gaps, enhancing program impact, standardizing data collection, increasing flexibility and transparency in funding processes, and strengthening both the provider network and the resilience of the local food system. Organizations receive direct cash grants to purchase food from wholesale or retail outlets, or credits to order produce and shelf-stable products through bulk-food purchasing partnerships. Funds also support food recovery services, including recovering, handling, and redistributing surplus food to expand access to nutritious foods for residents experiencing food insecurity. The program prioritizes underserved areas, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, and high-performing returning grantees. In FY25, the program awarded $3,699,500 across 49 food assistance provider organizations. The FY26 program allocated $428,202 to six food recovery organizations, with $290,785 in renewable FY26 funding and $137,417 supported through Special Appropriation passed November 18, 2025. Approximately $1.9M in expanded grants distributed to 53 nonprofit providers. Partners expected to recover and redistribute more than 10 million pounds of food annually.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct cash grants or credits to purchase and distribute shelf-stable, fresh food, and/or prepared meals, or support for food recovery and redistribution of surplus food to Montgomery County residents. Funding prioritizes underresourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, food recovery operations, and high-performing returning grantees. Applications processed through ecivis portal.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of shelf-stable, fresh food, and/or prepared meals to Montgomery County residents, expansion of food assistance services including home delivery models, food recovery and food assistance operations including recovering, handling, storing, and redistributing surplus food to expand access to nutritious foods for residents across Montgomery County, support for immigrant and unhoused residents, operational costs including staffing for food recovery operations, and direct food purchases from Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms and retailers.

structured_extraction.program_description: The DHCA Workforce Housing program provides affordable homeownership and rental opportunities for households with incomes up to 120% of the area's average income. The program helps workers and employees who cannot afford high-cost housing near their jobs by making homes available in Montgomery County. Homes are subject to affordability controls for 20 years (the Control Period), during which owners must live in the home as their primary residence and can only sell to other eligible households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides affordable homeownership and rental housing options. For homeownership, eligible households with incomes up to 120% of the area's average income can purchase homes at reduced prices set by DHCA. Maximum household income limits range from $137,500 for one-person households to $228,000 for six-person households (as of April 11, 2025). Homes are subject to a 20-year Control Period during which owners must occupy the home as their primary residence and can only sell to other eligible Workforce Housing households at a DHCA-set price. After the Control Period, the owner must share 50% of any appreciation proceeds with the County's Housing Initiative Fund. For rental units, applicants apply directly to the rental complexes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and households with incomes between the MPDU program limit and 120% of area median income who work or will work in Montgomery County, including public workers and other skilled and semi-skilled workers who cannot afford high-cost housing near their workplace.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a home (for homeownership) or rental of a home (for rental units). The home must be the owner's primary residence during the 20-year Control Period and cannot be rented out.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed the maximum income limit based on household size (ranging from $137,500 for 1 person to $228,000 for 6 persons as of April 11, 2025)
During the Control Period (20 years), owner must occupy the home as primary residence
Owner cannot rent out the home during the Control Period
If owner needs to relocate during Control Period, home must be sold to another eligible Workforce Housing household
Owner cannot refinance for more than the DHCA-set resale price
Owner cannot refinance in a way that lowers equity below $10,000
After Control Period ends, owner must share 50% of any appreciation proceeds with County's Housing Initiative Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For homeownership: Subscribe to be notified about new and resale Workforce Housing Units. When units become available, eligible households can apply through the program. Complete the Homeowner Verification form (PDF). For rental units: Apply directly to the rental complexes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program offering property tax credits and incentives to homeowners and building professionals who install accessible housing features meeting Design for Life Accessibility Standards. The program encourages development of housing that meets diverse accessibility needs and helps County residents remain in their homes as physical needs change. The program provides three tiers of tax credits: individual accessibility features, Level I (VISITable) accessibility standards, and Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards for residential properties and home care facilities. Homeowners and builders can receive tax credits for installing individual accessibility features or features meeting Level I or Level II standards on residential properties in new construction or existing homes. Builders and developers may also qualify for additional school impact tax credits and Development Impact Tax for Schools credits when constructing multiple Design for Life units. The program includes a certification program for Design for Life builders and homeowners. The program is designed for homeowners of all ages and stages of life, including those with temporary or permanent impairments seeking to make their homes more universally accessible and increase property value, as well as home care facility owners. A property tax credit or exemption is applied to the property owner's property tax bill after final inspection is completed and the application is approved by the Department of Permitting Services and Department of Finance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides property tax incentives through three tiers. For individual accessibility features, the credit covers certified costs up to $2,500 per property owner, less other subsidies. For Level I (VISITable) features, the credit covers certified costs up to $3,000 per property owner per tax year. For Level II (LIVEable) features, the credit covers certified costs up to $10,000 per property owner per tax year. The maximum amount of property tax credit that may be applied in any single tax year is $2,000, with any excess carrying forward to future years. Credits run with the property if sold and can be transferred to subsequent owners if not fully used. Builders and developers may qualify for additional school impact tax credits ranging from $500 to $2,000 per house for Level I homes, depending on the percentage of Design for Life units in the project (5%, 10%, 25%, or 30%), and Development Impact Tax credits for School Improvement. Applies to expenditures exceeding $500 incurred within 12 months of application. Permanent installations must meet Level I or Level II accessibility standards. The tax credit is applied to the property owner's next property tax bill after final inspection and application approval. Program also provides property tax incentives for universal accessibility improvements to home care facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with principal residences in Montgomery County, including homeowners of all ages and stages of life such as first-time homebuyers, young families, active adults, and persons living with temporary or permanent impairments; builders, developers, and other building professionals constructing or modifying residential properties with accessibility features; home care facility owners seeking to make their facilities more universally accessible. Includes property owners of new or existing residential dwellings such as single-family homes, townhouses, duplexes, and condominium units. Property owners in Montgomery County who complete residential, commercial, or home care facility building projects meeting Design for Life standards. Montgomery County residents and developers constructing accessible housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credits can be applied toward certified costs for installing permanent accessibility features that meet Design for Life standards, including individual accessibility features such as no-step entrances, ramps, accessible doorways and kitchens, elevators or lifts, accessible bathroom features, sensory impairment accommodations, grab bars, lever door handles, and chair lifts, or features meeting Level I or Level II Accessibility Standards. Costs must include the purchase and installation of features, permit fees, and inspection fees. For home care facilities, costs may support universal accessibility improvements. The tax credit is applied to the property owner's property tax bill. Funding supports construction and modification of housing to meet accessibility needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland. Property owners located in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must also submit a signed affidavit from their respective city verifying inspections and feature installation. For residential properties, the property must be principal residence as designated on real property tax bill. For home care facilities, property must be located in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process is a two-part process. First, apply for and receive a permit to install Design for Life accessibility features before work begins. For new construction, submit a Building Permit-Supplemental Design for Life Application with your residential or commercial building permit application. When applying online through eServices, check the DFL application box; when applying on paper, submit the Building Permit Supplemental Design for Life Application along with architectural and engineering plans. If applying for School Impact Tax Credit, submit a separate School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement. For existing homes with accessibility features, apply for an Alteration Permit, and the county will review the application and perform final approval inspection. Second, after all work is completed and final inspection is approved, homeowners submit a separate application for the property tax credit (available online or in paper form) along with documentation including a copy of the building permit, cost documentation, receipts, and affidavits. Tax credit applications may be submitted in person at Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton MD, by mail, or online through eServices. Qualified projects receive certificates as appropriate. The Department of Permitting Services confirms receipt and notifies the property owner when the application has been approved and forwarded to the Department of Finance. The Department of Finance reviews application documents to determine the appropriate tax credit amount and notifies the applicant. The tax credit appears on the property owner's next property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that solves drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or is inadequate. The program addresses requests for assistance to correct drainage problems where runoff water originates from the public Right-of-Way.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance to address drainage problems. The Division of Transportation Engineering investigates the nature and cause of drainage problems, determines appropriate solutions (either a spot solution or a comprehensive Capital Improvement Project), and works with construction contractors to develop designs and schedule work. The process includes calculating watershed size, verifying affected properties, reviewing existing drainage systems, and determining easement needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners experiencing drainage problems related to surface runoff from roads and public property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addressing drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or inadequate. Solutions may include spot fixes or comprehensive capital improvement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Montgomery County, Maryland. The program addresses drainage issues associated with surface runoff from roads and other property owned and maintained by Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Drainage problem must be related to surface runoff from public Right-of-Way or roads
Request must include necessary information about the drainage issue
Program evaluates watershed size, number of affected properties, and cost/benefit ratio
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A request for assistance can be initiated by completing the Drainage Request Form, telephone call, email, fax, or letter to the Design Section of the Division of Transportation Engineering. A County staff member knowledgeable in surface runoff issues will review the request in a timely manner. After review is completed, the applicant receives an explanation of findings and proposed action.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides tax-exempt financing to non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand their operations within the county. The program finances construction, acquisition, equipment purchases, and related project costs through both the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) and Economic Development Revenue Bond (EDRB) programs on a case-by-case basis. Borrowers pay a non-refundable $5,000 application fee at filing, plus 10 basis points annual administrative fees based on the original issue amount. All legal and administrative costs are borne by the applicant.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt revenue bonds issued by Montgomery County to finance economic development projects. Non-refundable Application Fee of $5,000 at the time of filing, Annual Administrative Fee of 10 basis points due at closing and annually while bonds are outstanding, and all legal and administrative costs incurred in reviewing and pursuing the financing agreement. Financing amount and term are negotiated based on the project. Funds may be used for land purchase, building construction or rehabilitation, equipment acquisition, and associated costs such as architectural/engineering, financing, and legal fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations qualified under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate, expand, or finance economic development projects in Montgomery County, including construction, acquisition, and equipment purchases.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing for non-speculative projects developed for specific occupants. For non-profits: projects that further charitable purposes such as medical, educational, and other charitable endeavors. For for-profits: small manufacturing facilities, solid waste disposal facilities, low-income housing projects, and businesses offering significant employment opportunities or located in areas designated for urban revitalization or strategically targeted growth. Projects may include land purchase, building construction or rehabilitation, equipment acquisition, and associated costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only. Projects must be located or be relocated to Montgomery County. Applicants must demonstrate benefit to the local economy.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Potential applicant submits completed application to the Montgomery County Department of Finance with the $5,000 non-refundable application fee and required supporting materials. Review is conducted on a case-by-case basis. The Department of Finance requests a Letter of Intent from the applicant. The County's bond counsel drafts a County Council Resolution. A TEFRA/public hearing is held. County bond counsel reviews for compliance with applicable law. The Department of Finance forwards its recommendation to the County Executive. If accepted, the Resolution is forwarded to County Council for action. The entire process typically takes approximately 6 weeks minimum, though more time may be required depending on County Council's agenda. Underwriter must provide financial feasibility letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that helps Montgomery County homeowners transition from fossil fuels (oil, gas, and propane) to electric alternatives by providing direct financial incentives for electrifying heating, cooling, water heating, and cooking appliances, along with technical support and energy audits. The program supports electrification of homes through rebates, subsidies, and technical assistance, including heat pump installations, electric water heaters, electric ranges and cooktops, electric dryers, gas line capping, oil tank removal, and related electrical upgrades. Electrify MC provides residents with a one-stop option to help them electrify their homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial incentives applied at point of sale for electrification work. Heat pump incentives range from $1,000-$2,500 depending on type and efficiency tier. Electric dryers receive $250 incentive. Electric ranges/cooktops receive $500 incentive. Heat pump water heaters receive $500 incentive. Additional incentives available for gas line capping ($165), oil tank removal ($500), surge protectors ($100-$200), and simultaneous fossil fuel appliance replacement ($1,000 add-on). Incentives are provided by Montgomery County and applied directly to the resident's invoice by the contractor, reducing out-of-pocket costs. Technical support and energy audits are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners with individually metered utilities who are transitioning from fossil fuel heating, cooling, water heating, or cooking systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Electrification of residential home appliances and systems, including replacement of gas, oil, or propane furnaces with heat pumps; replacement of gas water heaters with heat pump water heaters; replacement of gas stoves with electric ranges or cooktops; replacement of gas dryers with electric dryers; weatherization work including insulation and air sealing; electrical circuit installation and upgrades; gas line capping; and oil tank removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to residences located in Montgomery County, Maryland with individually metered utilities served by Pepco, BGE, or Potomac Edison (Coming soon).
requirements_list: Must own a residence in Montgomery County, Maryland
Must have individually metered utilities
Must be served by Pepco, BGE, or Potomac Edison utility
Effective July 16, 2024: Must replace a fossil-fueled equivalent appliance
For heat pump incentives: fossil fuel heating cannot be retained (must be fully electrified)
For mini-split heat pump: must provide 50% or more of total heating load
For electric range/cooktop: all combustion appliances must be removed from kitchen
Equipment must meet minimum efficiency standards (CEE Tier 1 or ENERGY STAR, depending on appliance type)
Work must be coordinated and completed by Elysian Energy to qualify for Electrify MC incentives
Cannot receive retroactive incentives for work already completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up through the online form or contact the Electrify MC Help Desk by phone or email. The Electrify MC team will call and email to discuss the process. Schedule an energy audit (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR audit, costs $100). After the audit, receive electrification recommendations. Choose appliances and improvements to make. Have work completed through Elysian Energy. Receive direct incentives at point of sale, with utility rebates for insulation work arriving in 6-8 weeks.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: In fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026), Montgomery County received approximately $400,000 in ESG funds. Funds support emergency solutions and services coordinated through the Montgomery County Continuum of Care.
