structured_extraction.program_description: A tax relief program that allows certified agricultural producers in Montgomery County to pay the County's energy tax at a lower residential rate rather than the industrial rate, reducing the burden of fuel, propane, electricity, and associated energy taxes on farm operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified agricultural producers pay the County's energy tax at the lower residential rate instead of the industrial rate, reducing their fuel, propane, electricity, and energy tax costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified agricultural producers engaged in the production of agricultural commodities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy costs including fuel, propane, and electricity used in agricultural production.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants may own land in the County or operate as tenant farmers.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in the business of agriculture in the production of an agricultural commodity (livestock, horses, poultry, field crops, nursery stock, bulbs, flowers, or other agricultural products with domestic or foreign market)

Must be enrolled in at least one of the following: Agriculture Easement Program (AEP), Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), Montgomery Rural Legacy Program (RLP), Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), Legacy Open Space (LOS), Montgomery Soil Conservation District, Maryland Nutrient Management Program, USDA Farm Service Agency, Cooperative Extension Service, Montgomery County Farmers Market Association, Certified Organic grower approved by Maryland Department of Agriculture, or Forest Conservation Management Agreement
Must apply for certification as a Certified Agricultural Producer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Agricultural producers receive a one-page application from the Department of Economic Development (administered by Office of Agriculture) and must return it indicating enrollment in at least one eligible agricultural program or service. The Department of Agriculture verifies eligibility and maintains records. Certified producers are then listed to fuel and energy suppliers in Montgomery County who apply the lower tax rate. structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit designed to benefit large business expansion projects in Montgomery County. The credit is available to businesses in qualified industries that meet specific requirements for space expansion, job creation, and employee compensation. The program offers a 24-year county tax credit at 58.5% of additional local tax liability, plus a 12-year state tax credit at 31.5% of additional state tax liability (corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax). Both credits allow for up to five-year carryforward and contain recapture provisions.
eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Enhanced Tax Credit provides a county tax credit based on the increase in real property tax assessments (personal property included where applicable) resulting from the business's expansion. The county tax credit rate is 58.5% of additional local tax liability for each of 24 years. The state also grants a credit at 31.5% for each of 12 years, applied against corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax. Both credits allow rollover for up to five years if they exceed taxes due in any given year. A recapture provision requires repayment if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years. The business must increase real property by at least 250,000 square feet and create new permanent full-time positions (either 1,250+ new jobs, or 500+ new jobs with 2,500+ retained jobs), or alternatively expend at least $150 million to increase space by at least 700,000 square feet with 500+ new permanent full-time positions and 1,100+ total employees. All employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Large for-profit businesses in qualified industries seeking significant expansion in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to property taxes (real and personal property) resulting from the business's expansion in space and employee headcount.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County. The company must notify the County of its intent to seek the credit before expanding its space and staff.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in one of the qualified industries (manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, agriculture, forestry, fishing, research, development, testing, biotechnology, computer programming, data processing, computer-related services, central financial/real estate/insurance services, central administrative offices or headquarters, public utility, warehousing, or business services)

Must meet one of the following expansion criteria: (1) Increase space by at least 250,000 square feet AND create at least 1,250 new permanent full-time positions, OR (2) Increase space by at least 250,000 square feet AND create at least 500 new permanent full-time positions if company already has 2,500+ existing positions, OR (3) Expend at least $150 million to increase space by at least 700,000 square feet AND create 500 new permanent full-time positions if company already has 1,100+ existing positions
All employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Must have six years from notification date to create and fill required number of new jobs and acquire and inhabit new space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business seeking the Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit must notify the County of its intent to seek the credit before expanding its space and staff. The business has six years from the notification date to create and fill the required number of new jobs and acquire and inhabit the new space. Once the requirements are accomplished and the company notifies the County Department of Finance, the business begins receiving the credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit available to nonresidential businesses that locate in designated Enterprise Zone areas in Wheaton, Gaithersburg, Takoma Park/Long Branch, and downtown Silver Spring in Montgomery County. The credit is designed to spur economic growth, jobs, and construction in these zones. The credit is based on growth in property assessments compared to the base-year assessment. The rate schedule declines over 10 years: Years 1-5 at 80% of the increase in assessment, Year 6 at 70%, Year 7 at 60%, Year 8 at 50%, Year 9 at 40%, and Year 10 at 30%, expiring after Year 10. The State of Maryland also grants an income tax credit for new employees hired in the Enterprise Zone ($3,000 in year 1, $2,000 in year 2, and $1,000 in year 3 for economically disadvantaged employees, and a one-time $1,000 credit for non-disadvantaged employees working at least 25 hours per week and spending at least 50% of work time in the Zone).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Enterprise Zone Tax Credit is a real property tax credit based on growth in property assessments. The credit is given on the actual taxes resulting from the increase in assessment compared to the base-year assessment (the assessment for the year before new construction or refurbishing). Personal property is not included. The credit is applied over 10 years with a declining rate schedule: Years 1-5 at tax on 80% of the increase in assessment, Year 6 at 70%, Year 7 at 60%, Year 8 at 50%, Year 9 at 40%, and Year 10 at 30%, expiring after Year 10. The State of Maryland also grants an income tax credit for new employees hired in the Enterprise Zone: $3,000 in year 1, $2,000 in year 2, and $1,000 in year 3 for economically disadvantaged employees, and a one-time $1,000 credit for non-disadvantaged employees working at least 25 hours per week and spending at least 50% of work time in the Zone.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonresidential businesses locating in designated Enterprise Zone areas in Wheaton, Gaithersburg, Takoma Park/Long Branch, and downtown Silver Spring in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to real property taxes resulting from new construction or refurbishing within the designated Enterprise Zones. Credit is based on the increase in property assessment from the base-year assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for nonresidential properties located within designated Enterprise Zones in Wheaton, Gaithersburg, Takoma Park/Long Branch, and downtown Silver Spring in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Property must be nonresidential
Property must be located within a designated Enterprise Zone in Wheaton, Gaithersburg, Takoma Park/Long Branch, or downtown Silver Spring
Credit based on increase in property assessment from base-year assessment
Personal property not included
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses interested in the Enterprise Zone Tax Credit should contact the appropriate zone administrator or the Department of Finance, Division of Fiscal Management. For Wheaton and Takoma Park/Long Branch, contact Peter McGinnity in the Department of Finance, Division of Fiscal Management. For Gaithersburg's Olde Towne Enterprise Zone, contact Tom Lonergan at the City of Gaithersburg Office of Economic Development. For Silver Spring, contact the Montgomery County Department of Finance. The credit is applied to property tax bills based on assessment increases.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Food Recovery Coordination Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds coordination and planning activities to strengthen partnerships across Montgomery County's food system. The program supports the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network to reduce food waste and increase food access. The grantee serves as the primary coordinating organization for the County's Food Recovery Collaborative, organizing regular convenings, facilitating data and resource sharing, conducting network assessments, providing technical assistance, and identifying opportunities for collaboration to improve operational efficiency at organizational and network levels. The program strengthens local capacity for food recovery, transportation, storage, and distribution of recovered food while improving efficiency, streamlining operations, and boosting resource sharing among food recovery organizations.

Funding supports the coordination and management of the Food Recovery Network to strengthen local capacity for food recovery, transportation, storage, and distribution of recovered food.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coordination and planning activities including convening food recovery partners, facilitating data and resource sharing, technical assistance, network assessments, design and implementation of a centralized food recovery network, identifying efficiency opportunities across food recovery, storage, and distribution programs, food waste reduction and redistribution management, and operational efficiency improvements.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Healthy, Efficient, Electrified, Climate-Adapted Pilot (HEECAP) Homes Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grants program funded by Montgomery County to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, provide gap funding for health and safety repairs, and offer climate adaptations for low- and moderate-income homes. The program funds improvement projects across three areas: pre-weatherization repairs, electrification, and climate resilience. It supports community partners to pilot strategies that repair health and safety problems, enable home electrification to improve indoor air quality, enhance durability and climate resilience, and support the County's climate action goals. With $1.2 million in FY 2025 funding, the program supports roof replacement, mold remediation, water damage repair, fuel switching from fossil fuel appliances to electric systems, solar panel installation, battery storage systems, weatherization, and climate resilience upgrades for eligible low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding totaling $1.2 million in FY 2025 for home improvement projects in three categories: pre-weatherization repairs, electrification upgrades (including kitchen appliances and fuel switching from fossil fuels to electric systems), and climate resilience measures. Assistance includes gap funding for health and safety repairs, roof replacement, mold remediation, water damage repair, solar panel installation, battery storage systems, weatherization, and climate adaptations for income-eligible and low- to moderate-income households. The program operates through competitively selected community partner organizations for eligible residents.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-weatherization repairs, health and safety repairs, roof replacement, mold remediation, water damage repair, electrification upgrades (including kitchen appliances), fuel switching to remove fossil-fuel appliances, solar panel installation, battery storage systems, weatherization projects, and climate resilience improvements for homes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Facility Use Subsidy Program (FUSP) provides subsidies to nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County to help reduce facility rental costs when providing direct services or benefits to vulnerable youth or low-income individuals. The program covers meeting room use in county schools, public libraries, county office buildings, Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and police stations. The program is aimed at supporting community organizations and programs that benefit vulnerable or low-income individuals and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a subsidy to cover or reduce facility rental fees for meeting room space in county public schools, public libraries, county office buildings, Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and police stations. The maximum award in FY18 was $5,400, which is enough to cover an afterschool program two or three times a week for the whole school year or an ongoing Saturday program. Rooms in schools can be fully covered during the week, but school holiday use is charged at approximately 40% less than regular nonprofit rates. Organizations are responsible for covering costs not covered by the subsidy. The award cannot cover gym rental, stadium field use, auditoriums, kitchens, equipment, or MCPS support staff costs.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facility rental fees for meeting rooms in county public schools with high numbers of low-income students, public libraries, county office buildings, Clarksburg Cottage, Regional Service Centers, and District 3 Police Station. The award cannot cover gym rental, stadium field use, auditoriums, kitchens, equipment, or MCPS support staff costs.

structured_extraction.program_description: FareShare is a commuter benefits program administered by Montgomery County that helps employers and employees save money through alternative transportation options and incentives. The program encourages the use of transit and vanpooling by matching employer contributions with county reimbursements. Employers can receive county reimbursement for transit benefit contributions over a minimum $25 per employee per month, up to the full $325 per month permitted by federal tax law, with a maximum reimbursement of $40,000 per year to any one employer. Employers are also eligible for a Maryland state tax credit of 50 percent of their contribution, up to a maximum of $100 per employee per month. Employees working in Montgomery County can receive up to $325 per month tax-free to help pay commuting costs using public transit, carpooling, vanpooling, bicycling, and walking. The program provides low-cost commuter benefits customized for employers, offering reduced commuting costs for employees while providing employers with improved employee attendance and productivity, higher morale, reduced parking costs and spaces, reduced payroll taxes, environmental benefits, improved public image, and better employee recruitment and retention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county reimburses employers for transit benefit contributions over a minimum $25 per employee per month, up to the full $325 per month permitted by federal tax law, with a maximum reimbursement of $40,000 per year to any one employer. Employers are also eligible for a Maryland state tax credit of 50 percent of their contribution, up to a maximum of $100 per employee per month. Employees receive tax-free transit subsidies up to $325 per month to help pay commuting costs. FareShare provides low-cost commuter benefits programs customized for employers. The program supports commute options such as public transit, carpooling, vanpooling, bicycling, and walking.

Employees working in Montgomery County can participate. Public sector employers are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employers can use funds to cover transit and vanpool commuting benefits for employees. Benefits help employers reduce commuting costs, lower taxes through a state tax credit, reduce traffic congestion, and improve workplace benefits. Employees can use benefits to pay commuting costs through public transit, carpooling, vanpooling, bicycling, and walking.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact Commuter Services via phone at 240-773-2989 or email mcdot.CommuterServices@montgomerycountymd.gov. Step 3: Employer receives reimbursement from the County. FareShare staff offer free on-site visits and marketing support to help set up programs tailored to company needs.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a low-income family in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through MoCo BOOST website

structured_extraction.program_description: A $50 million fund designed to accelerate the completion of mixed-income housing developments by the Housing Opportunities Commission. The fund supports the creation of nearly 8,800 new housing units, with at least 20 percent affordable to households earning at or below 50 percent of area median income and another 10 percent affordable to households at or below the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit income level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The $50 million fund provides financial assistance to support mixed-income housing development projects. At least 20 percent of units must be affordable to households earning 50 percent or below area median income, and at least 10 percent must be affordable to households at or below the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit income level.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Opportunities Commission and nonprofit housing developers working on mixed-income housing developments in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring and renovating properties to create mixed-income housing units with affordability requirements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must be owned or controlled by HOC or nonprofit housing developers
At least 20 percent of units must be affordable to households earning at or below 50 percent of area median income
At least 10 percent of units must be affordable to households at or below the Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit income level

structured_extraction.program_name: HOC Housing for People with Disabilities (Mainstream Vouchers)
structured_extraction.program_description: Housing Choice Vouchers set aside specifically for people with disabilities. Participants use the voucher to find private market rental housing and pay a limited percentage of their income (generally 30% to 40%) as rent. The housing subsidy is paid directly to the landlord by the Housing Opportunities Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing Choice Vouchers that allow individuals with disabilities to find private market rental housing. Participants pay 30% to 40% of their income as rent, with the subsidy paid directly to the landlord. Voucher assistance is portable anywhere in the United States including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands. Income limit: $0 to approximately $52,750 for one person.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who need affordable rental housing and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing costs. The subsidy covers a portion of rent for private market rental housing including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. Vouchers are portable to anywhere in the United States including Guam, Puerto Rico, Alaska, Hawaii, and the Virgin Islands once issued.
requirements_list: Individual must have a disability
Individual income must be between $0 and approximately $52,750 for one person
Housing unit must meet Housing Choice Voucher program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through HOC Housing Path, an online portal at www.HOCHousingPath.com. Once approved for a voucher, search for private market rental housing that meets program requirements. Contact HOC to have the selected unit approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: English language classes for parents and guardians of children in the Head Start program, offered in collaboration with the Literacy Council of Montgomery County. Two cohorts are offered each year: one in the fall and one in the spring.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free English classes offered twice yearly (fall and spring cohorts) for parents and guardians of children enrolled in Head Start.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and guardians of children in the Montgomery County Head Start program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English as a second language instruction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be parent or guardian of child in Head Start program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Montgomery County Head Start at 240-740-4530 for enrollment information in fall or spring cohorts.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credit program for property owners and businesses who perform restoration or preservation work on historic properties designated on the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation. Credit equals 25% of amount expended, up to the amount of county real property taxes. Unused credit can be carried forward for up to 5 years. Credit applies to exterior work only and does not apply to new construction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit equal to 25% of amount expended by taxpayer for restoration or preservation of historic property, up to amount of county real property taxes. Credit allowed only for work subject to approved historic area work permit, or for ordinary maintenance expenses exceeding $1,000. Credit applies to exterior work only; no credit for new construction. Credit allowed for tax year immediately following completion of work. Unused portion can be carried forward for up to 5 tax years, then lapses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses performing restoration or preservation work on historic properties designated on the Montgomery County Master Plan for Historic Preservation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for historic preservation or restoration work on designated historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Properties must be designated on the master plan for historic preservation or within a historic district designated on the master plan.
requirements_list: Property must be historic site designated on master plan for historic preservation OR within historic district designated on master plan
Work must be subject to approved historic area work permit OR ordinary maintenance expenses must exceed $1,000
Credit applies to exterior work only
No credit for new construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owner completes restoration or preservation work and obtains approved historic area work permit (if required) or documents maintenance expenses. Applies for credit in year following completion of work.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free program that helps people renovate their homes to make them more accessible for people with disabilities and older adults, with or without a demonstrated disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free home renovation assistance to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities and older adults seeking home accessibility improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations to improve accessibility
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides personal care services and light housekeeping to adults aged 18 and older residing in Montgomery County who have functional disabilities and need assistance with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living. The goal is to promote self-sufficiency and help people remain in their own homes while preventing or reducing institutionalization and preventing or remedying abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Personal care services and light housekeeping provided by home care aides. The number of weekly hours is based on individual need and funding availability. Fees are determined on a sliding scale based on applicant income and family size, paid to the Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Montgomery County with functional disabilities who need assistance with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care services and light housekeeping to help individuals remain in their own homes and maintain self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only.
requirements_list: Individual must be aged 18 or older
Must reside in Montgomery County
Must have functional disabilities
Must be receiving case management

Must require the service as part of a treatment plan to prevent or reduce institutional placement, prevent or reduce out-of-home placement of children, prevent or remedy abuse/neglect/self-neglect/exploitation, or promote self-sufficiency
Must be unable to obtain necessary paraprofessional services from another resource
Must be willing to accept Home Care
Must agree to pay any required fee
Availability of funding determines the number of individuals who can be served and a ranking scale is used to prioritize those with greatest need
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit at 240-777-3000 for more information and to discuss eligibility for the program. An assessment is done to establish a weekly service plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Matches renters seeking affordable housing with homeowners who have spare rooms to rent long-term.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching service connecting low-income renters with homeowners offering spare rooms for long-term rental.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income renters in Montgomery County seeking affordable housing options and homeowners with spare rooms
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing through home sharing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County
requirements_list: Seeking affordable rental housing
Willing to share home with another person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Housing Initiative Partnership at 301-857-4273 or visit website. Click on Featured Rooms to view available rooms for rent.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community Based Services and Supports (Supports Planning/Case Management)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing supports planning (case management) services to help older adults and individuals with disabilities live in their own homes. Services include assisting applicants and participants with accessing Medicaid and non-Medicaid funded home and community-based services such as personal care, nurse monitoring, medical supplies, and helping participants maintain Medicaid eligibility. Eligible Community Options Waiver applicants in nursing homes receive assistance transitioning to community living.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Supports planning (case management) services helping participants access home and community-based services including personal assistance services, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, medical day care, and assisted living through the Community Personal Assistance Services (CPAS), Community First Choice (CFC), Community Options (CO) Waiver, and Increased Community Services (ICS) programs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Area Agency on Aging-Supports Planning Agency
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with disabilities who need support living in their own homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supports planning and case management services to access personal assistance services, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, medical day care, and assisted living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Must qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver
Must need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, grooming, and dressing
Must meet the program's medical level of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit (ADRU) at 240-777-3000.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides services for older adults and individuals with physical disabilities, enabling them to live at home instead of in a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Offers assisted living services (excluding room and board), behavior consultation services, case management, dietitian and nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, and all other standard Medicaid services including Community First Choice if living at home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with physical disabilities age 18 and older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assisted living services, behavior consultation, case management, dietitian services, nutritionist services, medical day care, Senior Center Plus, and standard Medicaid services.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older
Must be eligible for Medicaid based on income and assets
Must require the level of care necessary for nursing facility services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals are encouraged to apply to determine financial eligibility. Application is necessary to assess if the required level of care is met for nursing facility services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Individuals with Brain Injury
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides home and community-based services for adults with traumatic brain injury, enabling them to receive necessary care and support to live in their communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides residential habilitation, day habilitation, supported employment, individual support services, case management, and medical day care. Additional Medicaid State Plan services include physician and hospital care, pharmacy services, home health services, laboratory services, mental health services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and payment of Medicare premiums, co-payments, and deductibles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults with brain injury requiring specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential habilitation, day habilitation, supported employment, individual support services, case management, medical day care, physician and hospital care, pharmacy services, home health services, laboratory services, mental health services, medical supplies, and durable medical equipment.
requirements_list: Diagnosis of brain injury requiring a specialty hospital or nursing facility level of care
Brain injury occurred after age 17

Was inpatient in a State Behavioral Health Administration facility, state-owned and operated nursing facility, or Maryland licensed Special Hospital for Chronic Disease accredited by CARF for Brain Injury Inpatient Rehabilitation, or placed by Medicaid in an out-of-state facility
Must meet financial eligibility requirements

structured_extraction.program_description: A post-arrest diversion program for individuals experiencing homelessness who have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses. The program offers voluntary engagement, allowing participants to choose participation in the diversion program or have their matter resolved through traditional programs or trial.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Post-arrest diversion services for homeless individuals facing misdemeanor charges. The program provides support to resolve criminal, traffic, and transit matters, including open warrants. Participation is voluntary and participants may choose this program or traditional prosecution. The program includes action plans, progress reports, and other support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless persons who have been charged with a crime; individuals experiencing homelessness (on the street, in shelters, or doubled-up in another person's household) who have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides diversion from criminal prosecution and helps resolve open misdemeanor criminal, traffic, and transit matters for homeless individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland. Monthly meetings held at Progress Place, 8106 Georgia Avenue, Silver Spring.
requirements_list: Must be experiencing homelessness (on the street, in a shelter, or doubled-up in another person's household)
Must have been accused of specific nonviolent misdemeanors or have outstanding warrants for misdemeanors and transit or traffic offenses
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can be referred to the program. Referrals are reviewed and participants are contacted to provide authorization to participate. Participants engage in action planning and progress reporting as part of the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Loans and Grants for Home Repairs and Improvements (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: Loan and grant programs provided by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for home repairs and improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan and grant programs for home repairs and improvements. Contact DHCD for specific details on amounts, terms, and eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners needing funds for home repairs and improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD at the provided phone number or email address for information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Initiative Partnership - Foreclosure Prevention Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides foreclosure intervention counseling and education workshops to help homeowners struggling with mortgage payments stay in their homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-on-one foreclosure intervention counseling for homeowners struggling to make monthly mortgage payments. Foreclosure Prevention Workshops held twice a month during evening hours to educate homeowners about options and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners at risk of foreclosure or struggling with mortgage payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and education services to prevent foreclosure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be a homeowner struggling with mortgage payments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Housing Initiative Partnership by phone at 301-916-5946. Attend Foreclosure Prevention Workshop held twice monthly in the evenings, or schedule one-on-one counseling. Services available Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Upcounty Regional Services Center, First Floor.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency services and case management for Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness. Services include rental assistance, eviction prevention, foreclosure avoidance support, utility assistance, burial assistance, and homeless assessment services. Assistance includes emergency financial grants and subsidies for eviction prevention, utility assistance, security deposits, first month's rent, foreclosure avoidance, burial assistance, and rental payments. Case management services help households maintain or obtain housing and prevent eviction. Food and prescription referrals are also available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited financial grants and subsidies for emergency assistance including eviction prevention, utility assistance, security deposits, first month's rent, foreclosure avoidance, burial assistance, and rental payments. Case management services are provided to help households maintain or obtain housing and prevent eviction. Referral services for food and prescriptions are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness, including those facing eviction, housing instability, utility disconnection, housing emergencies, and families with children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance to prevent eviction, maintain current housing, obtain new housing, prevent utility shut-off, restore utility services, cover security deposits, first month's rent, foreclosure assistance, burial assistance, and referrals for food and prescriptions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a resident of Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
For eviction prevention: must have received a court summons, judgment, or red and white notice from Sheriff's Office related to eviction, or a landlord-issued put-out notice
Household must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months

All supporting documentation must be submitted at time of application, including photo identification for all adults, bank/financial statements for last 30 days, income documentation for last 30 days for all adults, proof of expenses, emergency court/legal documentation for eviction cases, current rental ledger for eviction cases, welcome letter and lease for security deposit and first month's rent assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of the office locations (Germantown, Rockville, Silver Spring, or Upcounty Regional Services Center) to apply for services in person during office hours (Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with sign-in available until 4:30 p.m.). Applicants experiencing a housing emergency (eviction judgment or red and white notice) can call 311 to be connected with HSS. Documents can also be dropped off at deposit stations. Contact by phone at 311 or 240-777-4448 or (240) 777-4940.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides one-time financial assistance and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Montgomery County that are adversely impacted by a redevelopment project initiated by the County, on County-owned property, or involving a County facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance up to $25,000 and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Montgomery County adversely impacted by redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To provide assistance to small businesses negatively affected by County-related redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a financially healthy small business
Must be located in a designated area (Silver Spring, Bethesda, or Clarksburg)
Must be adversely impacted by a County-initiated redevelopment project, County-owned property project, or County facility project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Business Portal for application procedures and eligibility details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides temporary cash assistance for families, food assistance, disability assistance for residents unable to work, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary cash assistance provided to families in need, food stamp program benefits, Temporary Disability Assistance Program for residents who are totally disabled and cannot work, and medical assistance coverage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents with low income, families in financial need, disabled residents unable to work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Living expenses, food, medical care
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only
requirements_list: Temporary Disability Assistance Program requires resident to be totally disabled and unable to work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Income Support Programs office by phone or visit in person at the Upcounty Regional Services Center, Second Floor, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) / County Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County provides a tax credit to owner-occupied residential property owners (principal residence) to offset county income tax rate increases above the 2.6% threshold. The credit amount is $692 annually (as established by County resolution) and is applied as an offset to county property tax bills. The credit appears on tax bills as 'County Property Tax Credit.' Once a Homestead Property Tax Credit application is filed with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and approved, the credit automatically applies to future years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $692 annual tax credit applied to the property owner's county property tax bill as an offset for income tax rate increases exceeding 2.6%. The credit is awarded once a Homestead Property Tax Credit application is filed with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and approved. Once approved and on file, the credit automatically applies to future years. The amount is established by County resolution based on current county income tax rate of 3.20%. The credit appears on tax bills and requires the application to be on file by May 1 to ensure the credit appears on bills beginning July 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of principal residential property in Montgomery County who own and live in their property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied as an offset to county property tax bills to offset county income tax rate increases and reduce property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only. Applicants must be owner-occupants of residential property (principal residence) in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be owner of owner-occupied residential property (principal residence as determined by SDAT)
Must live in the property you own
County income tax rate must exceed 2.6%
Must file a one-time Homestead Property Tax Credit application with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation by May 1st to receive the credit
Must have a Homestead Property Tax Credit on file with SDAT
Application must be filed by May 1 for the credit to appear on bills beginning July 1
Apply online through Maryland OneStop or submit paper application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by visiting the SDAT Real Property database at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/, selecting Montgomery County, and searching for your property. Look for the Homestead Application Status field at the bottom of your information. If it says Approved or Application Received, no further action is needed. Step 2: If it says No Application, you must apply. Obtain your Real Property Account Number from your SDAT letter or the search results. Then apply either online through Maryland OneStop or the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application page, or by mail using the paper application from the same page. The credit is administered by the Department of Finance and applied based on property tax bills.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individuals 65 and Above and Retired Military Services Members Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to Montgomery County residents who are 65 years of age or older and either have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years or are retired from the U.S. armed forces or certain federal uniformed services. The credit provides a 20% reduction on county property taxes for owner-occupied dwellings and is granted for 7 consecutive years beginning July 1, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes for owner-occupied dwellings only. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years beginning July 1, 2025. Property assessment limits apply: $700,000 or less for 40-year homeowners, $550,000 or less for military retirees. Application deadline is April 1st of every year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 65 and above who either have owned and lived in their Montgomery County home for at least 40 consecutive years or are retired from the U.S. armed forces or uniformed services. Surviving spouses of eligible military retirees are also eligible under certain conditions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit reduces county property tax obligations on owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. The property must be owner-occupied.
requirements_list: Must be 65 years of age or older (birthday on or before June 30, 1961 to receive credit beginning July 1, 2026)
Property owner must be on the deed
For 40-year homeowners: must have owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years (deed dated June 30, 1986 or earlier); dwelling assessment must be $700,000 or less

For military retirees: must be retired from U.S. armed forces (Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, Navy), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, Public Health Service, military reserves, or National Guard; dwelling assessment must be $550,000 or less
Being a veteran alone does not qualify; must have actual retired status

For surviving spouses of military retirees: retiree must have been at least 65 at time of death and met military retirement requirement; spouse must not have remarried; must provide death certificate, signed affidavit of non-remarriage, and proof of retiree's retired status
For properties in trusts: must complete and submit Affidavit Re Trust Ownership
Must provide proof of age (Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth)
Must provide original deed (if applying as 40-year owner) or retired military ID (if applying as military retiree)
Property must be primary residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Individuals 65 and Above and Retired Military Services Members Tax Credit Application form. Include required documentation such as proof of age, deed records for 40-year owners, or retired status documentation for military retirees. For trust-owned properties, submit the Affidavit Re Trust Ownership. For surviving spouses, include death certificate, affidavit of non-remarriage, and proof of military retirement. Mail completed application to Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Bill 42-16 Tax Credit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Application must be received by April 1. For information and to apply, call 311 or 240-777-0311.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Program involving postpartum and infant referrals for at-risk families; facilitates coordination of maternal and infant health care services and public health surveillance. The program targets high-risk situations including teen mothers, substance use, mental health issues, intimate partner violence, unstable housing, previous infant loss, preterm birth, very low birthweight infants, and other serious risk circumstances.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Referrals for maternal and infant medical follow-up, mental health services, substance use treatment, smoking cessation, WIC enrollment, immunization support, breastfeeding support, safe sleep/crib provision, intimate partner violence services, and family planning/reproductive health. Public health nurses provide home visiting case management services to eligible mothers and newborns. Services are provided at no cost and include support for medical and social challenges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Postpartum mothers, infants (birth to infancy), and at-risk families with medical or social risk factors affecting maternal and infant health and well-being.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health care coordination, referral services, surveillance, and home visiting case management services including public health nursing support for mothers and newborns with medical or social challenges.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through local health departments.
requirements_list: Maternal medical risks, psychosocial risks, or pregnancy-related risks
Infant risks present
Referred by health care provider or hospital

Medical or social risk factors identified including: teen mothers, no prenatal care, substance use/misuse, mental/behavioral health issues, intimate partner violence, unstable housing/homelessness, previous infant death, previous preterm birth, very low birthweight infants (<1500 grams), or other serious risk circumstances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referral form completed by hospital/agency provider and submitted via fax or secure encrypted email to local health department. No patient authorization required under HIPAA. Upon receipt of referral, a public health nurse contacts the client to schedule home visits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for potential investors in early-stage companies with the goal of increasing the number of companies developing innovative technologies in Maryland, increasing overall investments in current and emerging technology sectors, and increasing the number of individual investors actively investing in Maryland technology companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit for investors in early-stage innovative technology companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors in early-stage technology companies in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in early-stage technology companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland.
requirements_list: Investment must be in early-stage company with innovative technology

structured_extraction.program_name: Intervention Program for Substance Abusers (IPSA) Pre-Trial Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A substance abuse intervention and diversion program that redirects eligible first-time offenders charged with misdemeanor drug crimes away from the court system and into programs providing drug testing, education, treatment, and community service to help participants change behavior and avoid a criminal record. The program also offers judges a sentencing option for offenders with mild to moderate substance abuse problems and limited criminal histories.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive drug testing, drug education classes (four 1.5-hour classes on drugs and the individual, drugs and the law, thinking for change, and treatment and recovery; plus optional monthly 2.5-hour marijuana education class), treatment referrals, and community service opportunities. The program provides intervention to help participants maintain a drug and arrest-free lifestyle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Substance abusers and pre-trial individuals; Eligible first-time offenders charged with misdemeanor drug crimes in Montgomery County, and offenders with mild to moderate substance abuse problems and limited criminal histories who are sentenced by judges to the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants engage in drug testing, complete mandatory drug education classes, receive treatment referrals and strategies for recovery, and perform community service to maintain a drug and arrest-free lifestyle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: First-time offender status (for diversion from prosecution)
Charged with misdemeanor drug crimes
Mild to moderate substance abuse problems
Limited criminal history
Completion of required drug education classes (four 1.5-hour classes or 2.5-hour marijuana education class)
Participation in drug testing as required
Engagement in community service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible individuals are referred to the IPSA program through the court system or as a sentencing option by judges. Participants must complete drug education classes, submit to drug testing according to the schedule (Monday and Thursday testing available), and engage in treatment and community service as directed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive jail-based treatment program designed to provide intensive addiction treatment to eligible inmates of the Montgomery County Correctional Facility. This is a collaborative effort between the Montgomery County Department of Correction and the Department of Health and Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Intensive addiction treatment program including medication assisted treatment options, naloxone training, and weekly support groups. Participants are eligible to receive a NARCAN kit upon release from custody.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible inmates of the Montgomery County Correctional Facility with addiction issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intensive addiction treatment services including medication assisted treatment, naloxone training and education, psychosocial therapy, and support groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals incarcerated at the Montgomery County Correctional Facility.
requirements_list: Must be an inmate at Montgomery County Correctional Facility
Must be eligible based on medical and treatment criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can request to participate through Inmate Services or attend weekly group sessions offered through Jail Addiction Services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee (JATC) Residential R-Program
structured_extraction.program_description: When accepted into the program, participants sign an agreement and are placed with a signatory contractor of Local Union 26 IBEW. structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program is a retail food access program that helps Montgomery County families access fresh and shelf-stable food items through convenient online shopping with Instacart. The program provides monthly grocery purchasing power to eligible families with children under age 18 who do not receive SNAP benefits. Eligible households receive $100 per month for each eligible child, up to a maximum of $400 per household per month. Up to 700 families can participate. Benefits are provided as dollar-value credits redeemable through an Instacart Fresh Funds account for Fresh Funds-eligible items, with funds automatically loaded on the 15th of each month. The program supports nutrition and reduces time and transportation barriers to accessing fresh groceries through delivery or local retailer pickup. Benefits are available from July 15, 2025, to July 15, 2026, with potential continuation for future cycles.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive $100 in monthly benefits per child aged 0-18 who does not receive SNAP benefits, up to a maximum of $400 per month. Up to 700 families will receive this grocery purchasing power provided as dollar-value credits redeemable through an Instacart Fresh Funds account. Benefits can be used to purchase eligible fresh produce, frozen items, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat, meat alternatives, bakery, deli, pantry staples, and non-alcoholic beverages, along with driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees. Funds are automatically loaded on the 15th of each month or the next business day and are available from July 15, 2025, to July 15, 2026. Items must be marked with the Fresh Funds icon to be eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator through Montgomery County Food Council or the Department of Health and Human Services Navigation Line to complete a brief eligibility pre-screening, or apply online directly. 2. If pre-screening criteria are met, the Navigator assists with the waitlist form or applicants proceed with online application. 3. Applicants upload required documentation including proof of income, valid photo ID, proof of address, and government-issued proof of identity for all children. 4. When applications are complete with all required documents, households are reviewed for enrollment on a first-come, first-served basis. 5. Upon enrollment approval, households receive instructions to create an Instacart Fresh Funds account and redeem a unique code to access monthly benefits. 6. Funds are automatically loaded on the 15th of each month or the next business day. 7. Monthly benefits reset on the 15th of each month.

structured_extraction.program_name: Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program provides one-time financial support to businesses relocating to or expanding in Montgomery County. Businesses new to the County or existing businesses expanding receive grants based on leased space size: $8.00 per square foot for leases under 7,500 sq ft (up to $60,000), $10.00 per square foot for 7,501-10,000 sq ft (up to $100,000), $12.50 per square foot for over 10,000 sq ft (up to $150,000), with certain strategic industries receiving $15 per square foot (up to $150,000). The program supports conversion of vacant office spaces and requires businesses to sign a direct lease for at least three years for up to 20,000 square feet of Class A or Class B office or flex space. The program is not available for retail, restaurant, or independent financial/insurance agent/broker establishments. Policies and procedures are administered by the Montgomery County Department of Finance and the Office of the County Executive Business Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are based on the size of leased office space. Businesses leasing less than 7,500 square feet receive $8.00 per square foot (up to $60,000). For leases between 7,501 and 10,000 square feet, the grant is $10.00 per square foot (up to $100,000). For leases over 10,000 square feet, the grant is $12.50 per square foot (up to $150,000). Certain strategic industries may receive $15.00 per square foot (up to $150,000). To qualify, businesses must sign a direct lease for at least three years for up to 20,000 square feet of Class A or Class B office or flex space with a minimum of 500 square feet. Specific terms are detailed in Executive Regulation 12-24.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-come, first-served; rolling/ongoing program with no defined application window. Applications must be submitted within 180 days of lease execution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Apartment Rentals Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Rental Program provides affordable rental housing units in apartment communities throughout the County. Tenants meeting income and other eligibility requirements can rent apartments set at affordable rates. MPDU rents are set by Executive Regulation and recalculated annually based on HUD Average Median Income for Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area. Maximum income for new tenants in garden apartments is 65% of Area Median Income (AMI); maximum income for high-rise apartments (5 stories or more) is 70% AMI. Renewing tenants can have incomes up to 130% of the new tenant maximum. Rent increases are limited to once per 12-month period and cannot exceed the Voluntary Rent Guideline.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Affordable rental units in apartment communities throughout Montgomery County at below-market rates. MPDU rents are set by Executive Regulation and recalculated annually based on HUD Average Median Income for Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area. Maximum income for new tenants in garden apartments is 65% of Area Median Income (AMI); maximum income for high-rise apartments (5 stories or more) is 70% AMI. Renewing tenants can have incomes up to 130% of the new tenant maximum. Rent increases are limited to once per 12-month period and cannot exceed the Voluntary Rent Guideline. Application fees are capped at $25. MPDU tenants cannot be charged amenities fees or parking fees for surface parking unless market-rate tenants are also charged.

structured_extraction.program_description: A housing program administered by Montgomery County that provides affordable rental apartments and home purchase opportunities for individuals and families with moderate household income throughout the county. The program requires private developers to provide a percentage of affordable units (12.5% to 15%) in residential developments with 20 or more units. For purchase, it provides affordably priced homes—both new and resale—to first-time homebuyers with moderate household incomes up to 70 percent of the Washington Metro Area Median Income. Units are subject to a control period (30 years for for-sale units sold after April 1, 2005, 10 years for units sold before April 1, 2005, and 99 years for rental units) during which resale prices and rental rates are restricted to maintain affordability. After the control period expires, sellers must share excess profits with Montgomery County on a 50-50 basis. Priority is given to people who live or work in the County. For purchase, single-family MPDUs must have at least 2 bedrooms (3 or more unless waived for multi-family); multi-family units must match market-rate bedroom mix with specified square footage requirements. For rental, households can rent MPDUs at rates calculated based on what households earning 65-70% of the Area Median Income can afford without cost burden. Developers must build MPDUs concurrently with or before market-rate units and execute an Agreement to Build before obtaining building permits.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers moderately priced homes and rental units at below-market rates to eligible first-time homebuyers and renters. For purchase, units range in price from approximately $150,000 for a 2-bedroom condominium to approximately $220,000 for a 3-bedroom townhouse with a garage, adjusted annually by the average preceding 5-year change in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers. The program markets units to renters and first-time homebuyers with incomes up to 70 percent of the Washington Metro Area Median Income, approximately $79,500 for a family of two or $99,500 for a family of four. For rental, rates are calculated based on what households earning 65-70% of the Area Median Income can afford without cost burden (65% AMI for garden apartments, 70% AMI for high-rises, with tenants paying no more than 25% of gross monthly income). During the control period, the maximum resale price is set by the MPDU office based on the original purchase price, inflation, allowable improvements, real estate commission, and transfer taxes. After the control period expires, the seller must share excess profits with Montgomery County at a 50-50 split. Homeowners may refinance or obtain a home equity line of credit, but must follow specific MPDU procedures and cannot refinance beyond the MPDU value without jeopardy of owing more than they can receive upon sale. The program does not provide financing but assists buyers through a Random Selection Drawing process to access available units. Buyers secure their own mortgage financing with pre-qualification of at least $150,000. Developers receive waivers including Systems Development Charge (SDC) and development impact taxes. The program provides an application tutorial as self-administered online training that includes tests that must be passed with a score of 80% or better, guiding applicants through the documentation gathering and application submission process. Management teams at participating apartment communities handle rental applications, verify income and credit history, and determine eligibility. DHCA provides technical assistance to developers on unit design, pricing standards, offering procedures, and compliance requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no deadline; rolling/ongoing with random selection drawings held approximately 2-3 weeks after property listings are posted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters and first-time homebuyers with moderate household income seeking affordable housing in Montgomery County, as well as residential real estate developers and builders creating new housing developments. Applicants must have moderate household incomes and have not owned a home in the past five years. Priority given to those who live or work in the County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of affordable ownership homes, rental of affordable residential units, or development of affordable housing units within market-rate residential developments. For purchase, funds cannot be used for refinancing or home equity purposes beyond the MPDU maximum value. Buyers must be able to pay monthly mortgage payments and closing costs. For rental, rent is based on affordability formulas tied to area median income. For developers, eligible uses include single-family detached homes, townhouses, and apartment units that meet specified bedroom, bathroom, and livability standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only, with priority given to persons who live and/or work in the County. Applies to any new residential development with 20 or more units in the county. Applicants must have received an email from the Department of Housing and Community Affairs—MPDU office confirming eligibility or applied directly to individual MPDU apartment communities. Preference is given to applicants who live and/or work in Montgomery County, but applicants do not need to live in Montgomery County to apply.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For purchase: (1) Complete a pre-screening intake form and register for the MPDU Orientation Seminar (2.5 hours, offered virtually on second and fourth Thursdays); (2) After passing Orientation Seminar post-test with 80% or better, register for First-Time Homebuyer class (8 hours, offered virtually on second Saturday of each month); (3) After passing both classes with 80% or better scores, register for online Application Tutorial through MPDU Application Portal and validate class attendance; (4) Create a user account using the AccessMCG Extranet User Guide; (5) Take and pass the Application Tutorial test with 80% or better score; (6) Gather all required documents from the provided checklist (government ID, mortgage pre-qualification letter, federal income tax returns, pay stubs, proof of income/residence); (7) Submit completed application and supporting documents through MPDU Application Portal and receive email confirmation; (8) DHCA reviews application within approximately 30 days (longer if documents missing); (9) If eligible, receive Certificate of Eligibility in the mail; (10) Enter Random Selection Drawings when MPDUs become available (approximately 2-3 weeks after property listings posted); (11) If selected, listing agent contacts buyer to arrange purchase and complete settlement. For rental: Apply directly to individual MPDU apartment communities; management team provides an application, verifies income and credit history, and determines eligibility. For developers: Work with Montgomery County Planning Board during development review to establish MPDU requirements based on density bonus. Execute Agreement to Build with DHCA before obtaining building permits. When units ready for occupancy, submit Offering Agreement to DHCA. DHCA notifies Housing Opportunities Commission and nonprofits (who have 21 days to select up to 40% of units). For sales, DHCA conducts random selection drawing for eligible MPDU certificate holders and provides list to developer's sales agent. For rentals, leasing office reviews applications and confirms eligibility. For sale during control period: Request MPDU Maximum Resale Price from office, complete MPDU Marketing Form, offer unit first to County and Housing Opportunities Commission, then to certified MPDU participants via Random Selection Drawing, and finally (if needed) to general public with DHCA approval. For refinance/HELOC during control period: Request current MPDU Maximum Resale Price, receive valuation letter, provide to lender, notify MPDU office of settlement details, and MPDU office records Notice of Sale and Refinance. For sale after control period: Submit Shared Profit Calculation Request Form and signed sales contract to MPDU office, receive shared profit calculation within 21 days, and settlement company pays County its share before closing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Accelerator is a structured problem-solving course and community that trains Montgomery County government employees to create organizational change. Participants attend a three-day intensive workshop where they learn process improvement, human-centered design, and other methods. They then work on change projects within their departments over several months, with ongoing coaching, peer mentoring, and community support. Accelerators reconvene to showcase results and continue developing their impact through peer learning circles, chapter clubs, and collaborative work sprints.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a three-day intensive workshop introduction to problem-solving methods, including process mapping, root cause analysis, observation walks, and brainstorming. Following the intensive, Accelerators receive ongoing coaching, peer mentoring through a thriving online community, regular coaching hours, access to Open Innovation events, and additional learning sessions. The program supports participants in developing and executing action plans, measuring results, and capturing learnings over several months. After completing initial projects, Accelerators continue to grow impact through peer learning circles exploring topics like no-code technology, growth mindsets, empathy, community organizing, and change management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees from across all departments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants use support and resources to develop and execute projects that improve processes, systems, and outcomes within Montgomery County government departments, with the goal of improving both employee and constituent experiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County government only. Participants are selected applicants from across Montgomery County government.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County government employee
Must be selected as an applicant to participate in the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Selected applicants from across Montgomery County government are invited to participate. Participants begin with a three-day intensive workshop where they form a cohort and learn problem-solving methods. Within a week of the intensive launch, new Accelerators present three change projects each. Over the following months, they analyze gaps, develop theories of change, brainstorm solutions, and execute action plans with support from peer mentors, coaching, and the online community. Within six months, Accelerators reconvene for an Accelerator Commencement and Innovation Showcase to showcase results and learnings.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Agricultural Land Preservation Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A County-run program that purchases agricultural land preservation easements to conserve farmland and prevent future commercial, residential, or industrial development. The program uses a formula-based system to determine easement value based on farm characteristics rather than appraisals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural land preservation easements that place a permanent easement on the property to prevent future commercial, residential, or industrial development. Easement values are determined using the Agricultural Value Factor (AVF), a formula-based system considering farm size, soil quality, road frontage, and farm location.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with agricultural property in Montgomery County who want to preserve farmland and prevent development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase agricultural land preservation easements that permanently restrict development on agricultural property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones determined by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board to possess significant agricultural value. The land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: Farm must be located in Agricultural Reserve, Rural Cluster Zone, Rural Zone, or zones with significant agricultural value
Minimum property size of 50 acres, or 10 acres or more of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right (TDR) for every 25 acres must be retained with the property prior to easement application for maximum easement value eligibility
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
The land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in the program should contact Mike Weyand. The County-run program is not dependent upon State approval, so applications can typically be processed in a shorter timeframe of approximately 6-12 months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Building Lot Termination (BLT) Easement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that purchases easements on individual building lots in the Agricultural Reserve, permanently retiring the on-site waste disposal system and development potential. The price paid is higher than other easement types because the lot has already been proven capable of supporting a residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases Building Lot Termination (BLT) easements that permanently retire an approved on-site waste disposal system and development rights. Because the landowner has already proven the lot is capable of supporting a residence, the price paid for eliminating development potential through a BLT easement is higher than other preservation easements. BLTs may also be sold directly to developers for use in designated receiving areas. Easement values are determined annually by the County Executive using a Base Value and Maximum Easement Value formula considering recent easement prices, TDR prices, and fair market values.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with individual building lots in the Montgomery County Agricultural Reserve who want to preserve farmland and prevent residential development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase Building Lot Termination easements that permanently retire on-site waste disposal systems and development rights on individual building lots.
