requirements_list: Land must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR) Zone
Property must be at least 50 acres in size, or smaller if contiguous to other lands protected by State/County agricultural and conservation easements
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
The land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Land must not be encumbered by Federal/State/County agricultural or conservation easements, except land protected by TDR Easements

Land must be able to achieve a percolation rate sufficient to support an individual on-site waste disposal system, evidenced by a septic system site plan approved by the Department of Permitting Services
Any TDRs retained with a parcel above the threshold of 1 TDR per 25 acres must be created/severed from the land prior to or simultaneously with the settlement of the BLT easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in the BLT Easement Program should contact Mike Weyand. The County Executive determines the Base Value and Maximum Easement Value for the BLT Ranking Formula annually on July 1.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Energy-Efficient Buildings Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive property tax credit program for commercial and multi-family residential building owners in Montgomery County, covering both existing buildings and new construction. For existing buildings, owners can earn up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for two years by demonstrating measurable energy use reduction through ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager (Tier 1) and/or obtaining green building certifications such as LEED or BREEAM (Tier 2). Newly constructed building owners can earn up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for four years for constructing buildings that exceed current building code requirements by 10% or greater. Credits are calculated based on energy performance improvements and certification levels. Eligible improvements include energy conservation devices and equipment consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103A that reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase fuel efficiency. For new construction, credit tiers are determined by performance above code: 10-20% (5-10% credit), 21-30% (21-30% credit), 31-40% (46.5-60% credit), and above 40% (82-100% credit). Additional credits available for green building certifications including LEED Gold/NGBS Gold/PHIUS+/Passive House/BREEAM-NC Excellent (25% for 4 years) or LEED Platinum/NGBS Emerald/BREEAM-NC Outstanding/Living Building Certification (75% for 4-5 years). Buildings in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit on all tiers. Property owners can also install energy conservation devices on existing buildings. Maximum annual credit cannot exceed 100% of building's county property tax liability.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two-track property tax credit program for commercial and multi-family residential buildings in Montgomery County. For existing buildings: Up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for two years with no annual cap. Tier 1 requires demonstrating measurable energy use reduction using ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager; credit calculated by subtracting baseline score from improved score, multiplied by factor (1.0-2.5) based on improvement tier. Tier 2 adds 25% for LEED Gold/BREEAM Excellent or 50% for LEED Platinum/BREEAM Outstanding. For new construction: Up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for four years with no annual cap. Buildings must achieve 10% or greater performance above current Building Code requirements. Credits based on performance tier: 10-20% above code (5-10% credit), 21-30% (21-30% credit), 31-40% (46.5-60% credit), above 40% (82-100% credit). Additional 25% credit for green building certifications (LEED Gold/NGBS Gold/PHIUS+/Passive House/BREEAM-NC Excellent), or 75% credit for LEED Platinum/NGBS Emerald/BREEAM-NC Outstanding/Living Building Certification (5 years if Living Building Certified). All eligible buildings in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive additional 10% credit. Maximum annual credit cannot exceed 100% of building's county property tax liability. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% per year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 1 year of use and occupancy permit for new construction; rolling applications for existing buildings
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and multi-family residential properties, property owners installing energy conservation devices, developers and property owners constructing new energy-efficient buildings in Montgomery County, including both existing building owners seeking energy efficiency improvements and new building construction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to existing buildings, installation of energy conservation devices on existing buildings, and construction of new buildings exceeding current building code requirements by 10% or greater. The property tax credit can be applied against County property taxes owed. Eligible improvements include energy conservation devices and equipment consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103A that reduce demand for conventional fuels or increase fuel efficiency.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For existing buildings: 1. Establish baseline 12-month ENERGY STAR score in Portfolio Manager tool; 2. Implement energy efficiency improvements with finalized DPS permits and vendor documentation; 3. Measure improved 12-month ENERGY STAR score; 4. Have ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklist verified by licensed Professional Engineer or Registered Architect; 5. For Tier 1, calculate credit using the formula provided in guidelines; 6. Optionally obtain LEED, BREEAM, or equivalent certification for Tier 2 credit; 7. Submit application through online portal with all required documentation. For new construction: 1. Design building to achieve minimum 10% energy efficiency above current building code; 2. Obtain DPS approved and stamped performance-based energy modeling reports; 3. Apply for Tier 1 credit within 1 year of receiving use and occupancy permit with DPS certification and energy modeling documentation; 4. Optionally obtain green building certification (LEED, BREEAM, NGBS, PHIUS+, Passive House, LBC Petal, or Living Building) within 2 years of occupancy permit; 5. Apply for Tier 2 credit with certification documentation; 6. Submit applications through online portal with all required documentation. Applications submitted through SeamlessDocs platform. Contact Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection for application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Initiative Fund is a Montgomery County-funded initiative that provides flexible financing in the form of loans and grants to for-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, and preserve multifamily developments and Moderately Priced Dwelling Units (MPDUs). The program also operates as an inclusionary zoning program requiring 12.5-15% of homes in new subdivisions of 20+ units to be moderately priced dwelling units, one of the first inclusionary zoning programs in the country (adopted 1973). The program promotes a broad range of housing opportunities by constructing or acquiring affordable housing units, buying and rehabilitating existing rental units at risk of removal from affordable housing supply, and assisting in the development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. Developers receive density bonuses or flexible development standards in exchange for building affordable housing. The program prioritizes projects serving low-income households, particularly those earning 50% or less of the Area Median Income, and encourages innovative approaches that meet County objectives such as preservation, production of new units, family-sized units, senior housing, and permanent supportive housing. The county has used this fund since 1989 to support affordable housing development and preservation, drawing from federal acquisition-without-rehabilitation program funds, local tax-exempt bonds, private sector investment in federal low-income housing tax credit partnerships, and Maryland Housing Finance Agency funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County provides flexible financing structured as loans and grants to developers for acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, and preserving multifamily developments and Moderately Priced Dwelling Units (MPDUs) for affordable housing. The targeted interest rate is 3%, but rates may vary based on project purpose and financing. Loan terms are set by the Director based on project needs. Repayment is generally structured to meet a project's financial requirements and the property's ability to pay. Funds may be used for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation. An equity contribution of 10% is an expected goal for each project. Funding is used to construct or acquire affordable housing units, buy and rehabilitate existing rental units at risk of removal from affordable housing supply, and assist in development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. The program also requires developers to construct 12.5-15% affordable units in new subdivisions of 20+ units, with 40% of MPDUs offered to Housing Opportunity Commission (HOC) and nonprofit housing agencies. Maximum income for MPDUs set at 70% of area median income (HUD-adjusted by family size). Both rental and purchase programs available. Developers receive density bonuses, flexible development standards, and limited land transfer options as incentives. Funding sources include federal acquisition-without-rehabilitation program funds, local tax-exempt bonds, private sector investment in federal low-income housing tax credit partnerships, and Maryland Housing Finance Agency funding. DHCA generally does not fund predevelopment costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers acquiring and developing affordable housing in Montgomery County, county residents seeking affordable housing opportunities, persons working in the county, and low- and moderate-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, and preserving multifamily developments and Moderately Priced Dwelling Units (MPDUs); purchasing and rehabilitating existing rental units at risk of removal from affordable housing supply; assisting in the development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units; and producing moderately priced housing for purchase or rental. Funds cannot generally be used for predevelopment costs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers submit applications using standard application forms (small or large project application depending on project size). Applications include a loan request summary form and supporting financial documentation. DHCA will evaluate applications based on aggregate solutions to County priorities including income level served, preservation, production, family-sized units, mixed-income housing, senior housing, proximity to transit, green building standards, permanent supportive housing, racial equity, readiness to proceed, community benefits, and homeownership opportunities. Projects are underwritten to determine financial feasibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Refundable Earned Income Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers a refundable tax credit that matches the Maryland Refundable Earned Income Credit (EIC) at 56%, providing supplemental income to low-income working residents who have earned income, are eligible for the federal EIC, and have at least one dependent. The program is also known as the Working Families Income Supplement (WFIS). Eligible residents receive a check from the Maryland Comptroller paid for by Montgomery County. Checks are mailed on a schedule based on when tax returns are filed: end of July for returns filed through June, end of October for returns filed July through September, and end of January for returns filed through December. Eligible ITIN filers may also receive this credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County provides a refundable tax credit that matches the Maryland Refundable EIC at 56%. Eligible residents receive a check from the Maryland Comptroller paid for by Montgomery County. The County program matches the State Refundable EIC amount for most eligible recipients, including eligible ITIN filers. Checks are mailed on a schedule based on when tax returns are filed: end of July for returns filed through June, end of October for returns filed July through September, and end of January for returns filed through December.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income working residents of Montgomery County with earned income who are eligible for the federal EIC and have at least one dependent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refundable tax credits for eligible individuals and general tax refunds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to residents of Montgomery County who file their income tax return with Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have earned income in the tax year claimed
Must be eligible for the federal EIC
Must claim the Maryland EIC

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents apply by filing their income tax return with claimed Maryland EIC. The Maryland Office of the Comptroller verifies eligibility. If eligible for the State Refundable EIC, residents automatically qualify for the County program. The Comptroller issues checks separately for State and County Refundable EIC amounts.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for employers in Montgomery County who purchase new computers or laptops for employees who telecommute. The program provides a tax credit against County personal property taxes covering up to 50 percent of the cost of each personal computer purchased for business purposes, with an annual maximum credit of $2,000 per business. Credits are awarded in order of application receipt and limited funding is available annually. Eligible employees must work from home more than 30% of the time and must certify that computers are used for business purposes. Computers must be new and employers must apply within 12 months after purchase to receive the credit in the year of purchase or the following year.

Credits are awarded in order of receipt by the Department of Finance until annual funding limits are reached. Employees must telecommute more than 30% of the time and certify computer use for business purposes. Computers must be new. Employers must apply within 12 months after purchase with proof of purchase documentation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new home computers or laptop computers for employees who telecommute.

Employees must telecommute more than 30% of the time

For more information, contact the Division of Treasury at 240-777-8965.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Transferable Development Rights (TDR) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 1980, this program allows rural landowners in the Agricultural Reserve to create and sell development rights (TDRs) to designated receiving areas, generating funds while placing an easement on their property that restricts development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners create Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) from their Agricultural Reserve land based on previous zoning (1 unit per 5 acres). These TDRs can be sold to designated receiving areas in the county. When TDRs are created, a TDR easement is placed on the property, permanently restricting development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres. To date, over 52,000 acres have been preserved through this program, generating $117 million in private funds from TDR purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property in the Montgomery County Agricultural Reserve who want to recapture equity from down-zoning while preserving farmland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Private funds generated from selling development rights to designated receiving areas help landowners recapture equity while preserving agricultural land through permanent easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve. Development rights can be sold to designated receiving areas including Life Science (LS), Transit Mixed-Use (TMX), and Commercial/Residential (CR) zones.
requirements_list: Land must be in the Agricultural Reserve zone
Ability to create TDRs based on previous zoning of 1 unit per 5 acres
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in creating TDRs should submit a letter of intent to notify the County of their interest.

Services include outreach, assistance with summer camp placements, recreational activities, and limited medical supplies. Funding covers services and products such as recreational activities, summer camp, and limited medical supplies.

Services also include outreach and assistance with summer camp placements. Funding is limited and covers one session or request at a time. Requests for recreational activities can be made from July to January, and summer camp requests from February to the first week of July.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Events Matching Funds Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides matching funds to neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs to hold events and activities that promote community engagement, build capacity, encourage networking, and stimulate the local economy. The program supports neighborhood events and educational community gatherings throughout Montgomery County, with matching funds provided on a dollar-for-dollar basis up to $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis with priority given to first-time applicants. The program is administered by the five Regional Service Offices, including the Bethesda-Chevy Chase Regional Services Center and the Silver Spring Regional Services Center.

Funds awarded on a first-come, first-served basis with priority given to first-time applicants. Funds must be used for an event or activity that is open to residents and creates sustainable and lasting impacts.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible activities include events and activities open to residents that create sustainable and lasting impacts for the neighborhood. All events must comply with Montgomery County Law. Funds may be used to hold events and activities that promote community engagement and build capacity within neighborhoods, including educational gatherings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to organizations throughout Montgomery County, administered by the five Regional Service Offices, including the Bethesda-Chevy Chase Regional Services Center and the Silver Spring Regional Services Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: The New Farmer Program provides mentoring and specialized business training including marketing, accounting, business planning, and advanced sustainable farm practices for new farmers. Unlike traditional farm incubators that place farmers on shared space for limited time, this program matches new farmers with private landowners for long-term leases from the start, allowing farmers to focus on growing their businesses rather than finding real estate. Participants receive access to business planning resources, technical assistance, mentorship from experienced farmers, and shared equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides mentoring from experienced farmers, specialized business training in marketing, accounting, business planning, and sustainable farm practices. Participants are matched with private landowners throughout the Agricultural Reserve for long-term leased sites and have access to shared equipment. Business planning and technical resources are provided to help participants develop their farm enterprises.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New farmers and beginning farmers in Montgomery County who want to start sustainable farming enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance supports the startup and initial operation of new farm businesses through mentoring, training, land matching, and access to shared agricultural equipment.

requirements_list: Must be a new or beginning farmer
Must be interested in sustainable farming practices
Must be willing to work with a mentor and participate in business training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the New Farmer Program Application form. Upon entering the program, farmers are matched with private landowners, assigned an experienced mentor, and given access to business planning and technical resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program under Maryland State law (§9-230 of the Tax-Property Article) and Montgomery County Code (Chapter 52, Article X) that promotes job and construction growth in Montgomery County. The program provides tax credits for businesses establishing new or expanding existing premises with new permanent full-time positions. The New Jobs Tax Credit is a six-year credit available to businesses that increase their space by at least 5,000 square feet and hire at least 25 new permanent full-time employees during a 24-month period. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is for very large expansion projects and lasts 24 years, available to businesses in qualified industries that meet one of three large-scale expansion and job creation requirements. Both credits are based on the increase in real and personal property tax assessments resulting from the business's expansion. Benefits businesses planning to expand both space and staff. Available to businesses new to the County or relocating from outside Maryland, but not to businesses moving from other Maryland counties or Baltimore City, and not available to retailers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two property tax credits. The New Jobs Tax Credit lasts for six years: Years 1-2 at 52% of tax attributable to the assessment increase, Years 3-4 at 39%, and Years 5-6 at 26%. The Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit is for very large projects and lasts 24 years at 58.5% of the new local tax from the expansion for the entire 24 years. Eligible businesses also receive a State tax credit using the same calculation method, applied against corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax (28% Years 1-2 for New Jobs Credit, 21% Years 3-4, 14% Years 5-6). The State credit can be carried forward up to 5 years if it exceeds taxes due. Tax credits are applied to Maryland withholding taxes or unemployment insurance taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses planning to increase both their space and staff in Montgomery County. Businesses already resident in the County or moving from outside of Maryland are eligible. The credit is not available to businesses moving from another Maryland county or Baltimore City, and it is not available to retailers. Positions must not be solely or primarily involved in retail sale of goods or services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to business tax liability for business expansion based on the increase in real and personal property tax assessments resulting from the business's expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County. New or expanded premises must be consistent with applicable land use master plans and must be located in Maryland. The company must notify the County of its intent to seek the credit before expanding its space and staff.
requirements_list: Increase space by at least 5,000 square feet
Hire at least 25 new permanent full-time employees during a 24-month period
New jobs must last at least 24 months
New space must be occupied during period of retaining 25 new employees
Company must be either already resident in Montgomery County or moving from outside of Maryland
Not available to businesses moving from another Maryland county or Baltimore City
Not available to retailers or positions solely/primarily in retail sales
Must notify the County before expanding space and staff
Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit: Must be in a qualified industry and meet one of three large-scale expansion and job creation requirements
New or expanded premises must not have been previously occupied
Must result in new permanent full-time positions as defined in §9-230(a)(3)
Business must pay Individual/Corporation Income Tax, Financial Institution Franchise Tax, or Insurance Premiums Tax
Cannot have received other tax credits or exemptions for same premises in same taxable year
Must maintain documentation for 4 years following last credit year (payroll records, employee timesheets, etc.)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business seeking the New Jobs Tax Credit must notify the Montgomery County Department of Finance of its intent to seek the credit before expanding its space and staff. Submit a completed application form with business and property information. Send notification letter stating business intent and expansion details, forward quarterly tax filings (Maryland withholding or unemployment insurance taxes) when available, and submit lease or space documentation. Once the business has acquired and inhabited the new space and hired the required number of new employees, the business notifies the County Department of Finance and begins receiving the credit on its property tax bill.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest interim loan program for experienced nonprofit developers and local public housing authorities to acquire and preserve affordable housing throughout Montgomery County. The program provides capital to help organizations maintain existing affordable housing and ensure long-term affordability, aiming to prevent the loss of affordability in existing rental housing units. The program is managed by Montgomery County's Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA), with loans reviewed and underwritten by Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County (HOC). The program is funded with $50 million by Fiscal Year 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest interim loans provided for 7 years at up to $100,000 per unit with a per project minimum of $1,500,000. Loans are issued and administered by Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs. Applicants must secure or identify other necessary capital for the acquisition unless this requirement is conditionally waived for 90 days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, applications considered as funds are available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced nonprofit affordable housing developers and local public housing authorities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and preservation of affordable housing units that are at least 20 years old.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Borrowers must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local public housing authority
Borrowers must have demonstrated housing development experience
Projects must have been constructed at least 20 years ago
Developments must commit to include 20% of units to serve households at or below 50% of Area Median Income and 10% of units at or below 70% of Area Median Income for 30 years
Projects must have secured or identified other necessary capital for the acquisition unless conditionally waived for 90 days
Rental rate increases on affordable units must be restricted to no more than the County's Voluntary Rent Guidelines (VRG)
Minimum 30-year affordability restriction period required
At least 20% of total units must be designated at 50% of Area Median Income or below within three years of acquisition
At least 10% of units must be at or below Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) rental rate level within three years of acquisition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are considered on a rolling basis as funds are available. HOC conducts an underwriting review of each loan application and connects applicants to potential investors for individual projects. DHCA reviews applications recommended for approval by HOC for funding determination. Applications should be submitted through HOC's website.

Complete at least four of the following optional organic actions for one growing season: maintain grass height above 3 inches (lower acceptable for bluegrass and zoysia); use compost or compost tea made within 25 miles; compost leaves and grass clippings on-site; use solar, electric, or hand-powered mower; use only plant-based organic fertilizers; avoid man-made processed fertilizers except compost products and biological inoculants; test soil at least once every three years; avoid watering or limit irrigation to between 5am and 9am with no runoff; hand-pull weeds with exception of GMO-free corn gluten
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online self-certification form via JotForm. The form can be completed by the property owner or by another party (such as a landscape company) with the owner's permission. Applicants must indicate in the form whether they want to receive the sign and gloves (both optional). The program operates on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outpatient Addiction and Mental Health Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Delivers care to individuals with mental health and substance abuse symptoms and disability. Provides support, monitoring and accommodation for individuals who need extensive treatment but do not require detoxification or 24-hour psychiatric supervision. Includes office-based case management services, medication assistance, and substance abuse treatment at various intensity levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides outpatient mental health and substance abuse treatment services delivered by contract providers. Services include intensive outpatient (nine or more hours weekly), outpatient (less than nine hours weekly), and continuing care. Case management services assist with benefits applications, provider coordination, and medical services advocacy. Medications are available through MedBank, HHS Pharmacy, or sample medications. Fees are based on a sliding scale with no one denied services due to inability to pay. Medicaid is accepted but private insurance is not.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents age 18 and older with serious mental illness and substance dependence disorder who do not have private insurance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health treatment, substance abuse treatment, case management, medication assistance, benefits application support, provider coordination, and medical services advocacy

An Access Team makes referrals to contract providers in Montgomery County. Applicants must bring photo identification, income verification, and a copy of an award letter for public benefits if applicable.

Training currently provided to Jail Addiction Services program participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can request to attend naloxone training through Inmate Services or Jail Addiction Services. Training is held once per month.

structured_extraction.program_name: PILOT Program (Payment in Lieu of Taxes for Affordable Housing)
structured_extraction.program_description: The PILOT Program provides County and State real property tax abatements to support affordable housing development and preservation in Montgomery County. The program offers exemptions that reduce or eliminate County real property and special area taxes for qualifying housing developments. The County negotiates exemptions from County real property taxes and payments in lieu of those taxes with rental property owners. By-right PILOTs are automatically provided to qualifying projects owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or nonprofit housing developers that commit to maintaining at least 50 percent of units as affordable to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income for 15 years, with one hundred percent abatement of County real property taxes for a term of at least 15 years. Standard PILOTs are approved case-by-case through negotiated agreements with for-profit and other property owners. Real property tax abatement amounts are based on the number of affordable rental units provided, with the tax abatement typically equal to the average County homeowner tax credit (adjusted annually). Following legal, budgetary, and procedural review, DHCA recommends PILOT to the Director of Finance, who computes fiscal impact and approves or denies subject to guidelines and annual funding limits set by County Council. The program became available as of March 28, 2022.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County provides a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) exemption that reduces or eliminates County real property and special area taxes for qualifying housing developments. By-right PILOTs provide one hundred percent abatement of County real property taxes for a term of at least 15 years if: 1) the project is owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, or 2) the property is owned or controlled by a nonprofit developer and at least 50% of the units are reserved for households earning 60% or less of AMI for 15 years. Standard PILOTs are underwritten and approved by the County on a case-by-case basis through negotiated agreements. Real property tax abatement amounts are based on the number of affordable rental units provided, with the abatement typically equal to the average County homeowner tax credit (adjusted annually). DHCA negotiates agreements with property owners, recommends to the Director of Finance, who computes fiscal impact and approves or denies subject to guidelines and annual funding limits. Applicants must pay all State real property taxes, municipal taxes, front foot benefit charges, and other applicable fees unless waived by the application jurisdiction. The PILOT is administered under a Regulatory Agreement signed by the property owner and the County and recorded in land records. May be transferable under certain conditions if the transferee meets all State and County PILOT requirements. Property owners may be required to pay a $40 per unit per year monitoring fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, nonprofit housing developers, for-profit rental property owners, and property owners developing or preserving affordable housing in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting affordable housing development and preservation through real property tax abatement and tax relief on property and special area taxes in exchange for affordable housing provision to low-income residents. Must be used to support the construction and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing with affordability commitments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rental housing projects located in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County, a nonprofit housing developer, or a for-profit rental property owner
At least 50 percent of dwelling units must be affordable to households earning 60 percent or less of area median income for 15 years
Rent levels must be limited accordingly
Property owners must commit to provide affordable housing to low-income residents
Property owners must file annual financial reports and compliance certificates
Owners must pay monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year (if required by agreement)
Monitoring fee payments due by September 30th annually
Developers must enter into negotiated agreements with Montgomery County to receive the exemption
Subject to legal, budgetary, and procedural review
Subject to annual funding limit set by County Council for non-Housing Opportunities Commission owned/controlled properties
Provide legal description of the property
Submit project financial pro forma including evidence of financial commitments and financial need for the PILOT
Provide project description with total number of units and number of affordable units
Document affordability of units (such as rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants)
Demonstrate site control equivalent to fee simple title, 99-year lease, or option to purchase with no contingencies except financing
Submit any other information or documentation reasonably required by the County
Sign Regulatory Agreement with the County recorded in land records
Meet requirements of Maryland law governing PILOTs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@montgomerycountymd.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. DHCA negotiates PILOT agreement with property owner. Following legal, budgetary, and procedural review, DHCA recommends to the Director of Finance. Director computes fiscal impact and approves or denies subject to guidelines and annual funding limits set by County Council. By-right PILOTs are automatically provided to qualifying projects without individual approval required. County will analyze the request to define the level of PILOT required using financial information from the property owner. Upon execution of agreement, exemption is applied to property tax bills. County Finance Department calculates property tax abatement amounts annually based on property tax rates and assessed values. Program became available as of March 28, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: Partnership Fund for Victims of Hate/Violence
structured_extraction.program_description: A fund that provides partial compensation for property damage to victims of hate and violence motivated by race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability. structured_extraction.program_description: A utility-based incentive program that provides rebates and financial assistance to multifamily property owners for electric vehicle charging installation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) and Housing Initiative Program (HIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program administered by Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services that provides long-term permanent supportive housing and rental assistance to individuals with special needs housing requirements and those exiting homelessness. The program establishes standards for eligibility and procedures for administration of rental assistance to support housing stability. Participants pay 30% of their household's adjusted gross income directly to the landlord, with the remainder paid by the housing provider. The program delivers rental assistance and housing support services through rental subsidies, case management, and in-home visits occurring 3-4 times per month, along with technical assistance for supportive housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permanent supportive housing with subsidized rent where participants pay 30% of adjusted gross income directly to the landlord and the housing provider pays the remainder via check. Includes case management and in-home visits occurring 3-4 times per month, plus technical assistance for supportive housing services.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental subsidy (covering 70% of rent based on 30% tenant income contribution), housing support services, case management, and in-home support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet eligibility standards established by the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Health and Human Services, Special Needs Housing division to inquire about application procedures and eligibility requirements. Landlords and tenants can access program information through the department's services to end and prevent homelessness division.

structured_extraction.program_description: A utility-based incentive program providing rebates for electric vehicle charging equipment and installation in multifamily properties.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by Montgomery County Police Department that incentivizes the installation of security cameras by providing rebates to property owners, tenants, businesses, and nonprofit organizations. The program aims to deter crime and assist law enforcement with investigations by encouraging the installation of outdoor security camera systems that meet minimum technical specifications. The program provides a rebate of up to $250 for the cost of the camera, with maximum rebates limited to one security camera per qualifying residence, up to five security cameras per qualifying business address, or up to five security cameras per qualifying nonprofit organization address. Rebates are provided by the Montgomery County Government upon approval and subject to availability of funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A rebate of up to $250 per camera for the cost of the camera (not to exceed purchase cost). Maximum rebates are limited to one security camera per qualifying residence, up to five security cameras per qualifying business address, or up to five security cameras per qualifying nonprofit organization address. The rebate covers the camera purchase and installation. Rebates are provided by the Montgomery County Government upon approval and subject to availability of funds.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of outdoor security camera systems with digital video recording capability. Cameras must meet minimum technical specifications including at least 1 Megapixel resolution, 1280x720 screen resolution, standard video quality, and 5 frames per second, and must retain video footage for at least seven days.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within a Police Chief-designated Priority Area in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants can check eligibility via the Department's camera application website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County program that allows affordable housing (rental and for-sale) to be developed in commercial and industrial zones where residential uses are normally not permitted. Housing is designed and priced to be affordable to households earning 75 percent of County median income, adjusted for family size.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows developers to build affordable housing in commercial and industrial zones through a special exception process. Base residential density is 6 units per acre, increasing to 21.5 units per acre if at least 35 percent of units are affordable to households at or below County median income. For-sale units are controlled for 10 years; rental units are controlled for 20 years. Maximum sales prices for for-sale units must not exceed 175% of the comparable Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) price. Rental rates are set based on 75 percent of area-wide median income, adjusted for family size, with maximum allowable rents not exceeding 30% of calculated gross household income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit developers seeking to build residential projects in commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development of affordable rental and for-sale housing units in commercial and industrial zones. Housing must be designed and priced to be affordable to households earning 75 percent of County median income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, specifically in commercial and industrial zones designated as C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, O-M, I-1, I-3, or I-4. No more than 25 percent of land zoned for commercial and industrial use in each master plan area can be used for multifamily housing.
requirements_list: Developer must apply for and receive Special Exception approval from the Board of Appeals
Developer must execute a written agreement with the Department of Housing and Community Affairs before building permit issuance
Agreement must include subdivision name, marketing name, and construction staging plan requiring PHUs to be built along with or before other dwelling units
Developer must record the productivity housing agreement in County Land Records and provide copy to County
Copy of executed agreement must be submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application
Single-family PHUs must have at least two or more bedrooms
Multi-family PHUs must meet specific bedroom ratio requirements matching market-rate unit ratios
For-sale PHU maximum prices cannot exceed 175% of comparable MPDU sale price
Rental PHU rates set based on 75% of area-wide median income adjusted for family size, with maximum rents not exceeding 30% of gross household income
For-sale units occupied by owner as primary residence during 10-year control period
Rental units cannot be sublet during 20-year control period unless approved by Department
During control period, PHU cannot be resold or refinanced for amount greater than determined by DHCA
Upon sale after control period expires, owner must pay one-half of excess profit to Housing Initiative Fund
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Developer applies for Special Exception, which must be approved by the Board of Appeals. 2. Before building permit issuance, developer executes written agreement with Department of Housing and Community Affairs containing subdivision name, marketing name, and construction staging plan. 3. Developer records the productivity housing agreement in County Land Records and provides copy to County. 4. Copy of executed agreement is submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Fire Sprinkler Systems
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time county property tax credit for homeowners and property owners who install approved automatic fire sprinkler systems on detached single-family dwellings, attached dwelling units, or multi-family buildings where the system was not legally required. The system must be approved, complete, used for fire protection, and installed on or after July 1, 2000. Applicants must apply in the year the sprinkler system is installed to receive the credit in that tax year or the following tax year.

System must be approved, complete, used for fire protection, and installed on or after July 1, 2000. Applicant must apply in the year the system is installed to receive the credit in that tax year or the following tax year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Public campaign financing program established to encourage greater voter participation in County elections, increase opportunities for more residents to run for office, and reduce the influence of large contributions from businesses, political action groups, and other large organizations. The program provides matching public dollars to qualifying candidates who meet contribution thresholds, with matching formulas (7:1, 5:1, 4:1, 3:1, 2:1 depending on contribution tier and office).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching public funds provided to qualifying candidates for campaign financing. Candidates receive matching public funds for qualifying contributions received from individual Montgomery County residents. Matching funds calculated separately for primary and general elections. Maximum public contributions vary by County elective office: County Executive ($870,170), At-Large Councilmember ($290,060), District Councilmember ($145,030). Distributions made within three (3) business days after Board authorization.

Multiple disbursements allowed, not to exceed $75,000 aggregate for revenue loss assistance. Conditional grants from the Economic Development Fund to assist businesses and organizations experiencing significant adverse impact from communicable disease-related business operation restrictions.

Schools retain the remaining plants for their own environmental projects or native plant sales. No charge to participating schools.

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive voluntary cost-share rebate program administered by Montgomery County that provides financial incentives to residential, non-residential, and community property owners for installing stormwater management practices on their properties. The program includes rebates for rain gardens, conservation landscapes, water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns), green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal. These practices reduce stormwater runoff and prevent pollution from flowing into storm drains and streams, while slowing runoff, spreading it out, and allowing it to soak in naturally to reduce erosion and flooding. Property owners and organizations pay upfront costs and receive rebates after project installation and inspection. Rebate amounts vary by project type, size, and property type, with maximum rebates of $7,500 for residential properties and $20,000 lifetime maximum per parcel for community properties (homeowner associations, congregations, multi-family properties, institutional properties, and community pools). Water harvesting projects receive $1 per gallon of storage capacity, with rain barrels capped at $250 rebate (200-gallon minimum for single-family homes, 100-gallon minimum for townhomes) and cisterns capped at $500 rebate for residential properties or $2,000 for commercial/institutional properties, for a maximum total of $750 per property for water harvesting alone on residential properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners and organizations pay the full upfront cost of their stormwater management project. After the project is installed and passes final inspection, the program issues a rebate based on the project type, size, and property type. For residential properties, rebate amounts vary up to $7,500 maximum. Water harvesting systems receive $1 per gallon of storage capacity with rain barrels capped at $250 rebate (200-gallon minimum for single-family homes, 100-gallon minimum for townhomes) and cisterns capped at $500 rebate for residential properties or $2,000 for commercial/institutional properties, for a maximum total of $750 per property for water harvesting alone on residential properties. Other project types have varying rebate rates (for example, permeable pavement retrofit is $14 per square foot). For community properties (homeowner associations, congregations, multi-family properties, institutional properties, and community pools), a lifetime maximum rebate of $20,000 per parcel is available based on tax ID number. Rebate is calculated based on total eligible paid receipts up to the determined maximum, excluding sales tax. Eligible project types include rain gardens, conservation landscapes, green roofs, permeable pavement retrofits, and pavement removal. Rebate check is received within 8 to 12 weeks after final inspection.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications; 8-12 weeks to hear back after applying; 3 months to submit plan documents after site assessment; 6 months to complete installation after project approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County (excluding Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park municipalities) and community organizations including community pools, homeowner associations, private schools, congregations, multi-family properties, and other institutional properties with large parking lots, decks, and common areas who want to reduce stormwater runoff by installing eligible stormwater management practices including rain gardens, conservation landscapes, water harvesting systems, green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved stormwater management projects including rain gardens, conservation landscapes, green roofs, water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns), permeable pavement retrofits, and pavement removal. Eligible costs include plants, mulch, compost, stone, hardware, equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project. Water harvesting systems must collect rainwater from roof downspouts for reuse. Minimum project size for water harvesting is 200 gallons total (100 gallons for townhomes) with individual barrel minimum size of 50 gallons.

Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park (though Takoma Park does not currently have a rebate program) administer their own separate RainScapes programs.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit the RainScapes website and submit an online application (electronic application only; assistance available if needed) through the RainScapes Rewards portal, or contact the RainScapes program to schedule a site assessment and submit property tax ID. 2. Review the applicable project manual and design criteria. 3. An assigned RainScapes planner will be contacted within 2-4 weeks and will conduct a site assessment in person or virtually to evaluate project eligibility, identify potential project locations, provide recommendations, and help select appropriate projects. 4. Submit required plan documents within 3 months of receiving the site assessment report for planner review and approval. 5. Once the project is approved, you have 6 months to install it. Property owners and organizations can choose a RainScapes Professional from the contractor list or complete the project themselves. 6. Call MISS Utility (811) before excavation. 7. Schedule a final inspection with your planner after installation is complete. 8. Submit all receipts, photos, measurements, and digitally sign the Property Owner Agreement. 9. Planner verifies project completion and determines final rebate amount. 10. Rebate is issued, typically within 8-12 weeks after final inspection. 11. Property owner is eligible to apply for a Water Quality Protection Charge reduction on their property tax bill and must allow County staff triennial inspections of the project. Check the status of a current application through the online portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Stormwater Garden: Conservation Landscapes Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that provides financial incentives to property owners who replace lawn, invasive plants, or eroded areas with native plants and improved soil. Conservation landscapes slow down and absorb stormwater runoff while providing habitat for pollinators.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $5 per square foot for conservation landscapes with no ponding, or $6 per square foot for landscapes with 3 inches of ponding (minimum 250-square-foot project). Rebates are provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline listed; applications accepted on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners who want to convert lawn or erosion-prone areas into native plant landscapes that absorb stormwater.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The rebate covers costs associated with converting lawn or erosion areas to conservation landscapes using native plants and improved soil.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Minimum 250-square-foot project size
Property must be in Montgomery County
Landscape must replace lawn, invasive plants, or erosion areas with native plants and improved soil
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the application process and submit an application through the RainScapes Rewards Rebate Application Guide. Applicants can also check the status of current applications online. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that provides financial assistance to Montgomery County property owners who install rain gardens to capture and filter stormwater runoff from roofs, driveways, patios, and other hard surfaces. Rain gardens are landscaped depressions designed to collect rainwater, which soaks into the ground within 24-48 hours and helps reduce stormwater pollution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $10 per square foot of total rain garden area. Minimum garden size is 75 square feet. The rebate is provided on a first-come, first-served basis to property owners who complete eligible rain garden installations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a first come, first served basis with no stated deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners and residents who want to install rain gardens on their property to manage stormwater runoff and support native plants and pollinators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The rebate covers the costs of installing rain gardens designed to capture and filter stormwater runoff from hard surfaces such as roofs, driveways, patios, and sidewalks. Gardens must contain spongy soil and at least 75% native plants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to property owners in Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Minimum rain garden area of 75 square feet
Garden must be 6 inches deep
Must contain spongy soil
Must include at least 75% native plants
Water must drain within 24-48 hours
Property owners must follow the Requirements to qualify for a RainScapes Rewards Rebate as outlined in the program documentation
Percolation (perc) test may be required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners can use the Rain Garden Sizing Estimator tool to determine an approximate garden size. Applicants then review the application process and submit an application through the RainScapes Rewards Rebate Application Guide. Final sizing verification is completed by a RainScapes planner after application submission. Applicants can check the status of their application online.

Participants are expected to pay the full rent upon discharge from the program. Payments are made directly to the landlord.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Time-limited rental subsidy and support services for 12 to 24 months.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit available to landlords who provide reduced rent to eligible elderly or disabled tenants. The credit is based on the reduction in rent provided to qualifying tenants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit is 50% of the reduced rent charged to elderly or disabled tenants. To be eligible for the credit, the reduced rent must be at least 15% lower than the market rent as determined by the Department of Housing and Community Affairs. The credit cannot exceed the amount of County property tax paid by the landlord in the tax year in which the credit is granted and is not refundable. There is a cap on the program at $250,000 annually, and credits are granted in the order received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords in Montgomery County who rent to elderly (65 or older) or disabled tenants and provide reduced rent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit for landlords who provide reduced rent to qualified tenants.

Credit cannot exceed County property tax paid by landlord in the tax year
Program has an annual cap of $250,000; credits granted in order received
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landlords interested in the Rent Reduction Tax Credit should contact Michael Parent at the Montgomery County Department of Finance, Division of Treasury.

structured_extraction.program_description: DHCA uses Rental Agreements to preserve and maintain affordable housing by restricting units in multifamily projects to income and rent limits in return for a per-unit subsidy paid by the County. The subsidy covers the difference between the stipulated affordable rent and the average market rate rent for a comparable unit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County pays a per-unit subsidy calculated as the difference between the stipulated affordable rent and the average market rate rent for a comparable unit. Rent increases on subsidized units must follow the County's Voluntary Rent Guideline. Property owners may be required to pay a $40 per unit per year monitoring fee.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To preserve and maintain affordable housing units in multifamily projects through per-unit subsidies

structured_extraction.program_description: RAP is a referral-based rental assistance program providing financial support to eligible low-income residents in Montgomery County facing housing instability, eviction, or homelessness. The program offers monthly housing subsidies ranging from $100 to $503, paid directly to landlords by 2-party check. Assistance is designed to help eligible tenants, including those exiting homelessness, maintain housing and prevent homelessness. Preference is given to seniors age 62 and over, persons with documented disabilities, those fleeing domestic violence, and those experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly housing subsidy ranging from $100 to $503, paid directly to the landlord by 2-party check. Direct financial assistance to help low-income families and individuals pay their rent, with minimum and maximum benefit amounts as specified in the adopted regulation and conditions set by county regulations. Preference given to seniors, persons with disabilities, domestic violence survivors, and those experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Assistance provided through a referral process.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rent subsidy for housing expenses and rental costs to prevent homelessness and housing instability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.

A staff person or case manager will determine program eligibility and next steps. For additional information, contact Montgomery County at (240) 777-4940.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides nonprofit organizations and residents with access to land, yard, patio, and community gardening supplies, space, education, and resources for community gardening. The program has been expanded to include nutrition, cooking, and healthy eating education to address food security initiatives and support broader food production capacity within Montgomery County. The program funds proven, scalable food gardening initiatives that increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to nonprofit partners and organizations to provide residents with access to land, education, and resources for community gardening and nutrition education. Initiatives must be proven and scalable, measurably increasing the volume of fresh, edible food available to residents experiencing food insecurity. FY24 awards ranged from $17,856 to $43,242 with a total of $210,559 awarded to seven grantees. FY26 budget is $100,000 with a performance period anticipated from June 30, 2026 to August 31, 2027. FY27 budget is $250,000. The program is expected to reach approximately 4,000 residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and Montgomery County residents interested in community gardening, nutrition education, healthy eating, food security, and food production, particularly those experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community gardening, yard and patio gardening, nutrition education, cooking education, healthy eating education, gardening supplies, space provision, and food production initiatives to increase fresh, edible food availability.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Real Property Tax Deferral - General
structured_extraction.program_description: Program allowing homeowners to defer payment of county property taxes on principal residence if gross household income does not exceed $120,000 and owner has resided in dwelling for at least 5 years. Interest accrues annually at rate not exceeding prime lending rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program allowing homeowners to defer payment of county property taxes on residential real property used as principal residence. Amount deferred equals difference between current year county taxes due and county taxes paid in prior year. Eligible taxes include General County tax and Special Service Area taxes. Interest accrues annually at rate set by County not exceeding prime lending rate. New interest rate applies to all deferred taxes each year. Accumulated deferred taxes and accrued interest cannot exceed 50% of full cash value of property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low to moderate income homeowners in Montgomery County whose household gross income does not exceed $120,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax deferral with accruing interest
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be owner-occupied residential property used as principal residence
Must have resided in dwelling as principal residence for at least 5 years
Gross household income (combined for all residents) must not exceed $120,000 for preceding calendar year
At least one owner must reside in dwelling as principal residence
Accumulated deferred taxes and accrued interest cannot exceed 50% of full cash value of property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowner applies with income documentation. If approved, defers payment of annual county property tax increases (amount over prior year payment). Interest accrues annually at County-set rate not exceeding prime lending rate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term temporary relief to primary unpaid full-time live-in caregivers who care for frail elderly adults, functionally disabled adults (including those with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children and adults with developmental disabilities, and children with severe medical conditions. Care is provided by trained, certified care workers in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite care facilities. Services are coordinated by The Arc Montgomery County, and respite care can range from a few hours to a day, weekend, or longer. The program may provide a subsidy to pay a respite care provider, though funding is limited and is not an entitlement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term temporary respite care services provided by trained, certified care workers. Services are coordinated by The Arc Montgomery County, which works with families to locate appropriate respite care providers. Respite care can range from a few hours to a day, weekend, or longer and can be provided in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or approved respite care facilities. Eligible caregivers receive services at no cost. Eligibility for a subsidy does not guarantee funds for each respite occasion requested, as funding is limited. Processing time is up to 30 business days from application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary unpaid full-time live-in caregivers providing care to frail elderly adults, functionally disabled adults (including those with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children and adults with developmental disabilities, and children with severe medical conditions in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term temporary relief and respite care services provided by trained, certified care workers, including subsidies to pay approved respite care providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Services are coordinated through The Arc Montgomery County, located at 7362 Calhoun Place, Rockville, MD 20855. Applicants must reside in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be the primary full-time live-in unpaid caregiver
Caregiver must be providing full-time care in the home
Care recipient must be a child with a severe medical condition, a child or adult with disabilities, a frail elderly adult, a functionally disabled adult, or a child with challenging behaviors
Care recipient must live in the same household
Must reside in Montgomery County
Must complete application with required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact The Arc Montgomery County Respite Coordination program at (301) 984-5777 x1204 to request an application or visit The Arc Montgomery County website. Submit completed application with required documentation by email to Respite@arcmontmd.org or by US mail to Respite Coordination, The Arc Montgomery County, 7362 Calhoun Place, Rockville, MD 20855. Families are notified when application is received. Processing takes up to 30 business days. Once approved, caregiver participates in orientation and respite staff works with family to locate appropriate care provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports food access services across Montgomery County Public Schools, serving approximately 50,000 students through both direct services and grants to non-profit organizations and government entities. The program addresses critical gaps in healthy food access for children and families and implements innovative approaches to co-locating food assistance at MCPS school sites. Funding totaling $2.3M+ supports approximately 99 school sites through multiple mechanisms including direct subsidies and competitive grants to organizations. Grant funding ranges from approximately $15,750 to $146,250 per organization to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs. Recent funding cycles awarded total program funding of $480,452 (FY24), $1,250,274 (FY25), and $2,303,775 (FY26) distributed to multiple grantees. An additional $300,000 in new budget funds have been allocated for FY26 with anticipated expansion to 80+ MCPS school sites. The program was launched in Summer 2025.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program operates through two mechanisms: (1) Direct food access subsidies of $2.3M supporting food services across approximately 99 MCPS school sites serving an estimated 50,000 students; and (2) Competitive grants to non-profit organizations and government entities ranging from approximately $15,750 to $146,250 per organization to establish, expand, and maintain school-based food assistance programs. Funding supports food purchases, staffing costs, and operating costs including indirect costs. Recent funding cycles awarded total program funding of $480,452 (FY24), $1,250,274 (FY25), and $2,303,775 (FY26) distributed to multiple grantees. The total program award is $2.3 million plus an additional $300,000 in new budget funds allocated for FY26 to support projects that address critical food access gaps for families by co-locating food assistance services at 80-99 MCPS school sites, serving more than 50,000 children. Applications are submitted through the ecivis portal with reference to the NOFO and information session materials.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food access services at school sites, including food pantries, pre-packed snack and grocery bags, prepared meals, and grocery gift cards. Funding also supports food purchases, staffing costs, operating costs, and indirect costs. Funding supports establishment, expansion, and maintenance of school-based food assistance programs and projects that address food access gaps for families by co-locating food assistance services at school sites. Preference for foods sourced from County farms or Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms representing underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Public School sites in Montgomery County, Maryland, including public and charter schools. Preference for foods from County farms or Washington Metropolitan/DMV region farms representing underserved communities.

The office reviews applications and awards funding to selected organizations. Refer to NOFO and information session materials. The program was launched in Summer 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps qualified seniors pay for care in assisted living facilities in Montgomery County. Facilities must be licensed by the State of Maryland and Montgomery County to provide assisted living care and must agree to participate in the subsidy program. The program subsidizes a portion of monthly assisted living care costs for eligible residents who require 24-hour supervision and meet income and asset limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a financial subsidy to help qualified seniors pay for care in state and county licensed assisted living facilities in Montgomery County. The maximum subsidy an applicant can currently receive is $1,056.00 per month. The program limits the total monthly rate assisted living facilities may charge to $3,300. In most cases, the subsidy does not cover the full cost of care, and the applicant is responsible for costs beyond the subsidy payment. Applicants may receive a partial subsidy based on their calculated monthly payment.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assisted living care costs in licensed facilities in Montgomery County.

For an individual: no more than $4,350 income and $20,064 in assets (as of July 14, 2023)
For a couple: income is looked at individually, and no more than $20,064 in assets
Applicants must reside in a licensed assisted living facility that participates in or agrees to participate in the subsidy program
Facility must be licensed by State of Maryland and Montgomery County
Facility must be participant in the Subsidy program

structured_extraction.program_description: Program authorized by Section 52-18(F) of Montgomery County Code that allows eligible senior homeowners to defer real property taxes that exceed the amount owed in the preceding tax year. Deferred taxes accrue no interest and become a lien on the property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County defers portion of real property taxes exceeding the baseline year amount; no interest accrues during deferral period; deferred taxes become a lien on property. The deferral amount equals the difference between the current year property tax and the prior year property tax. A lien is recorded against the property in the amount of the deferred tax. The deferral becomes due when the homeowner sells the property, moves, or ceases to qualify. Accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50 percent of the property's fair market value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 1 of the current taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens aged 65 and older who own and occupy their principal residence in Montgomery County and meet income limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax deferral for homeowners on their principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal residence must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. The eligible property is limited to the real property on which the residence is located, the curtilage as determined by the Supervisor of Assessments, and any adjacent unimproved land on the same lot or parcel not assessed on an agricultural basis.
requirements_list: One or more homeowners must be at least 65 years of age
One or more homeowners must have resided in the dwelling as their principal residence for five consecutive years and continue to occupy it as their principal residence
Combined gross household income of all occupants (excluding dependents and those paying rent or room and board) must not exceed $80,000
Property must be residential real property occupied as the principal residence of the owner
Applicant must provide proof of age (birth certificate, driver's license, or other proof)
Applicant must provide a copy of the completed federal income tax return including all schedules
If property is owned by spouses filing separately, copies of each return must be provided
If income is from partnership or corporation, copies of partnership return (Form 1065 including Schedule K-1) and/or corporate return (Form 1120 or 1120S including Schedule K-1) must be included
Accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50 percent of the fair market value of the property
Must maintain ownership and occupancy status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form with all required documentation. Gather proof of age (birth certificate, driver's license, or other proof). Obtain a copy of your federal income tax return including all schedules and forms. Complete the Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement. Mail the completed application along with all required documents to the Montgomery County Department of Finance, Division of Treasury (27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850) by September 1. Homeowner and County execute Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement; agreement is notarized and recorded in land records. Pay the full first installment of property tax in a timely manner. Once approved, the deferral will be applied toward your second installment or refunded if your bill has been paid in full.
