structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Senior Nutrition Program is a congregate meal program funded under Public Law 109-365, the Older Americans Act (OAA). The program provides nutritious meals in congregate (group) settings where seniors can gather for activities and services, promoting better health through improved nutrition and helping older adults remain healthy, independent, and active. The congregate setting encourages fellowship and reduces isolation through socialization. The program offers nutritious meals that meet federal nutrition standards, providing at least one-third of the recommended dietary allowances for older adults and complying with the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Meals are tailored for people with chronic health conditions including diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension. Hot, cold, and vegetarian meal options are available, with all rolls/pastas being whole grain. All meals include milk or yogurt and 100% fruit juice. Kosher, Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese meals and programming are available at certain sites. Menus are available in Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Nutrition education, screening, and counseling are also provided. The program serves as a central contact for home-delivered meals, referring seniors to Meals on Wheels programs that serve their addresses. A voluntary donation is requested from seniors age 60 and over; those under 60 may participate at full price. The program is offered in partnership with the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services, Aging and Disability Services, and provides access to other supportive services throughout the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Congregate meals (in-person dining) with hot, cold, and vegetarian options served at 12 partnering locations throughout Montgomery County. Meals meet federal nutrition standards providing at least one-third of the recommended dietary allowances for older adults and comply with the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. All rolls/pastas are whole grain. All meals include milk or yogurt and 100% fruit juice with real food, plant and animal products, avoiding ultra-processed foods, emphasizing fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Meals are tailored for people with chronic health conditions including diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension. Kosher, Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese meals are available at certain sites. Meals are available for a voluntary contribution (donation) for those age 60 and over; full price is required for those under 60. The program also provides nutrition education, screening, counseling, and referrals to home-delivered Meals on Wheels programs. Advanced registration and reservations required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone aged 60 and over, spouses of currently registered 60+ participants, Senior Nutrition Program volunteers (any age) for 2 hours per month, people with disabilities under age 60 living with a registered parent/grandparent, people with disabilities under age 60 living in a building where a nutrition site is located. Also available to those under 60 who can pay full price.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious congregate meals suitable for people with chronic health conditions including diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension. Meals include fruits, vegetables, proteins, grains, and prepared dishes with documented nutritional information (calories, protein, sodium content). Meals are available in congregate settings with activities and services. Program locations also provide lectures, food demonstrations, and nutrition-related programs. Program also refers to home-delivered Meals on Wheels programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to homeowners aged 65 and older whose home is their principal residence in Montgomery County. The credit equals 50% of the combined Maryland State Homeowners' Tax Credit and Montgomery County Supplement. The credit is added to the County Supplement to reduce the taxpayer's tax bill. If you have applied for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, SDAT has the age information to determine eligibility and there is no need to apply for this credit separately.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 50% of the combined state and county Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. The exact amount depends on the applicant's eligibility for each component. Credit is calculated based on either the State credit (if County Supplement is zero), the County Supplement (if State credit is zero), or both State credit and County Supplement. The credit is added to the County Supplement and reduces the tax bill. If you have applied for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, SDAT has the age information to determine eligibility and there is no need to apply for this credit separately.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Montgomery County age 65 and older whose principal residence is a home they own

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid ten-week summer fellowship program that enables graduate students to gain real-world local government experience across multiple fields within Montgomery County government. Participants work on ongoing projects, policy analyses, and research projects while working directly with decision makers including elected officials and senior management staff. Fellows conduct self-selected independent research, present policy recommendations to the County Council, meet weekly with Councilmembers to learn about the policymaking process, and participate in weekly field trips to explore the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive an $8,000 stipend for the ten-week program running from June 1, 2026 through August 7, 2026. Transportation costs beyond the stipend are not covered by the program, and relocation to the region is at the applicant's expense.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage 1 application is now closed. Applicants selected for the program will be notified by the end of March 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Graduate students currently enrolled in policy-related graduate programs (policy, public administration, planning, public health, law, or related fields) who will have completed their first year of study by summer 2026. Individuals who will have graduated by summer 2026 are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants work on policy research, analysis, and projects within various county government departments and organizations. Funds are provided as a stipend for living expenses during the fellowship period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Summer Fellows program is located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period, though telework agreements may be discussed on an individual basis with the supervisor. In-person hours are still expected. Many County office buildings are a 10-minute walk from either the Rockville Metro Station or the Wheaton Metro Station.
requirements_list: Must be a current graduate-level student (Masters or PhD program)
Cannot have graduated before the program start date of June 1, 2026
Must have completed at least the first year of graduate study by the program start date
Must study public policy, public administration/affairs, public health, planning, law, or related fields
Must have a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
Must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period
Must be enthusiastic to learn about local government
Must demonstrate innovative ideas and approaches to policy problems
Must embody strong interpersonal skills and collaborative mindsets
Must be eager to make a real impact on Montgomery County residents and businesses
Must desire the opportunity for skill development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application consists of three stages. Stage 1 is a written application that is now closed. Selected applicants advance to Stage 2, which requires submission of two reference letters (at least one from a graduate professor or supervisor preferred), first semester graduate school transcript when available, a writing sample (5-10 pages), and responses to four short answer questions. Selected applicants from Stage 2 advance to Stage 3, which involves a required interview. Applicants selected for the program will be notified by the end of March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a tax credit for homeowners in Montgomery County based on household income compared to their property tax bill. The credit is administered through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) with a supplemental county credit applied against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes. The program supplements the state Homeowners' Property Tax Credit for households earning less than $60,000 and includes a special property tax credit for eligible senior residents age 65 and older. Eligibility is based on homeowner status, household income levels, net worth criteria, and qualification for the State Homeowners Tax Credit. The maximum property assessment is $300,000, and credit percentages range based on income brackets. The program averaged $1,276 in combined credits last year and benefited 4,486 county residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County Supplement provides a tax credit applied against General County and Special Service Area real property tax. Credit amounts are calculated based on a progressive scale tied to combined gross income levels. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing, the assessed value threshold is $383,100, combined income eligibility level is $76,620, and net worth criteria is $255,400. Credit percentages range from 0% to 8% based on income brackets. Maximum property assessment of $300,000 is used for computing tax. No additional application is necessary for this credit; it is automatically included with the application for the state Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. The program averaged $1,276 in combined credits last year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st annually for that tax year; retroactive applications for taxpayers age 70 or older may be submitted for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County homeowners of all ages whose household income qualifies based on comparison to their property tax bill, including senior residents age 65 and older and households earning less than $60,000
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of real property tax liability through a supplemental tax credit for eligible low-income homeowners and seniors
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. The County Supplement applies only against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes.
requirements_list: Must be homeowner of principal residence (owner-occupied)
Must qualify for the State Homeowners Property Tax Credit
Household income must qualify based on comparison to tax bill and not exceed the combined income eligibility level (currently $76,620 as of July 1, 2026)
Household income must be less than $60,000
Net worth cannot exceed the net worth criteria (currently $255,400 as of July 1, 2026, excluding principal property and qualified retirement savings)
Must apply for the State HOTC through SDAT
For senior credit component, at least one owner must be age 65 or older
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Taxpayers must apply for the State Homeowners Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). There is no separate application for the County Supplement; it is automatically included with the state application. Applications must be submitted by October 1st to be applicable for that tax year. Eligible taxpayers age 70 or older may also submit retroactive applications for the current and 3 prior levy years at any time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tax Credit for Day Care Provider
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for taxpayers making improvements to real property used exclusively for day care services in Montgomery County. Eligible providers include registered family day care homes, licensed child care centers, and licensed day care centers for the elderly or medically handicapped individuals. The credit is limited to the lesser of $10,000 or the amount of General County and Special Area taxes attributable to the improvement. Businesses with at least 25 employees may also apply if providing licensed child care center or registered family day care home services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for improvements to day care facilities. structured_extraction.program_name: WMATA PILOT (Payment in Lieu of Taxes) – Accelerate Housing Development at Metro Rail Stations
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax abatement program for new high-rise residential developments built on WMATA-leased property at Metro stations throughout Montgomery County. The program aims to accelerate housing development and create approximately 8,600 new housing units by offering property tax exemptions. Qualifying projects must include at least 50% rental housing with 25% of rental units reserved as moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) at 50% of area median income or lower, consist of high-rise residential apartment buildings (more than 8 stories), and meet specific workforce requirements. The program is administered under the MPDU Declaration of Covenants and governed by Bill 29-20.

Projects must consist of at least 50% high-rise residential apartment buildings (more than 8 stories), be located on land leased from WMATA at a Metro station, and provide at least 25% of moderately priced dwelling units at 50% of area median income or lower. Additionally, 25% of construction workers must be county residents. Applicants must pay State and other applicable fees. Includes specific quarterly reporting requirements. Administered under MPDU Declaration of Covenants and Bill 29-20.

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Credit program allowing property owners to receive up to 80% off their annual Water Quality Protection Charge (for ESD practices) or up to 60% (for non-ESD practices) by maintaining approved stormwater management practices on their properties. Credits are based on the volume of water captured and treated by eligible stormwater management systems such as rain barrels, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, bioretention, or grass swales. Stormwater management practices capture and treat runoff to prevent direct flow into storm drains or streams untreated, removing pollutants, protecting public health, and reducing flooding risk, stream damage, and erosion. Credits must be renewed every 3 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can receive a credit (reduction) of up to 80% off their annual Water Quality Protection Charge for ESD practices or up to 60% for non-ESD practices if they install and maintain eligible stormwater management practices. The credit amount is based on the volume of water captured and treated compared to the Environmental Site Design Volume (ESDv). Credits are calculated based on stormwater management system type, treatment volume provided, drainage area, impervious area, and era facility was permitted. For offsite treatment, an onsite credit of at least 60% must be achieved first, with offsite credits providing up to 100% maximum total. Credits must be renewed every 3 years. Applications are submitted through the WQPC forms portal and are due by September 30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Montgomery County property owners including single-family residential (SFR) properties, non-residential (NR) properties, multi-family residential (MFR) properties, businesses, homeowner associations, non-profit organizations, and government-owned properties with approved stormwater management practices on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the annual Water Quality Protection Charge based on stormwater management practices that capture, treat, and manage stormwater runoff. WQPC funds are used for stream and water quality improvement projects, reducing negative impacts of stormwater runoff, job creation, and local economic boost.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all private property parcels in Montgomery County, Maryland that are subject to the Water Quality Protection Charge.

Completion of inspections and maintenance checklists

Design volume information or assumed volume based on design era
For offsite credits: onsite credit of at least 60% must be achieved first
Credit must be renewed every 3 years

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Stormwater Management Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A credit program that reduces the Water Quality Protection Charge for property owners who install and maintain stormwater management practices on their properties. Credits range from 45% (non-Environmental Site Design practices treating 1-inch rainfall) to 80% (Environmental Site Design practices) or up to 100% for properties also treating offsite stormwater. The program applies to single-family residential, multi-family residential, and non-residential properties including commercial, industrial, homeowner associations, nonprofit organizations, and government-owned properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners who implement stormwater management systems receive a reduction of their annual Water Quality Protection Charge. Credits are calculated based on treatment volume provided, treatment depth, and practice type. Maximum onsite credits: 60% for non-Environmental Site Design practices, 80% for Environmental Site Design practices treating full design volume. Maximum total credit including offsite treatment: 100%. Credits are valid for three years and must be renewed. Stormwater management practices include rain barrels and cisterns, rain gardens, permeable pavement, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, grass swales, bioretention, and sheet flow to conservation areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners including single-family residential property owners, multi-family residential property owners, non-residential property owners (commercial, industrial), homeowner associations, nonprofit organizations (IRS-designated 501(c)(3)), and government-owned properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces the Water Quality Protection Charge applied to properties based on stormwater management improvements. Credits support installation and maintenance of stormwater management practices that capture and treat runoff to prevent direct flow into storm drains or streams.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Program applies to private property parcels and other properties subject to the Water Quality Protection Charge within Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland
Stormwater management system must be in place or permitted
Stormwater treatment practices must comply with Maryland Department of Environment recognized practices per Maryland Stormwater Design Manual
Practices must be maintained in accordance with Section 19-28 of Montgomery County Code and Department of Environmental Protection maintenance requirements

Engineer certified plans required to include details of stormwater management system, impervious area details, and facility specifications
Photographic documentation of proper installation required
Practices must not be removed or altered
Properties with permitted or RainScapes project practices generally exempt from submitting design information
Credit renewal is required every 3 years
Site impervious and pervious area data required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the WQPC Credit Application (Credit Calculator). Applicants can input the design volume directly if design plans are available. If no design data are available, the Credit Calculator automatically calculates an assumed treatment volume based on permit approval era. Submit required documentation including account ID, property address, owner name, telephone number, email address, engineer certified plans showing impervious area details, and photographs of the stormwater management system. Submit online through the WQPC forms portal or contact Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection.

structured_extraction.program_description: An expedited permit issuance program that reduces installation cost and time for residential rooftop solar systems by approved installers. The program issues solar permits immediately upon online payment through approved third-party services like SolarAPP+.
eligible_municipalities: Montgomery County (unincorporated areas and municipalities without site restrictions)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program expedites the issuance of solar building permits for residential rooftop photovoltaic systems. Licensed contractors submit applications electronically through SolarAPP+. Permits are issued immediately once all fees are paid and requirements are satisfied. The program serves residential dwelling main structures only and applies to systems up to 400A main service, 225A service disconnect switches, and 225A busbars, including new photovoltaic systems with optional energy storage systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Montgomery County and licensed solar installation contractors with valid Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) licenses who have completed required training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of residential rooftop solar panel systems and energy storage systems (batteries, power walls, power packs).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Montgomery County residential properties, excluding municipalities with site restrictions and historic preservation areas as identified in Montgomery County Zoning and the Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
requirements_list: Residential dwelling main structures only
Licensed solar installation contractors must have valid Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) license
Contractors must have attended all required training offered by approved third-party service providers
Projects must conform with SolarAPP+ PV Eligibility Checklists
Projects may be permitted up to 400A main service, 225A service disconnect switches, and 225A busbars
Projects may not exceed these electrical specifications
Ballasted roof systems not eligible
Commercial properties not eligible (townhouses 4+ stories above grade considered commercial)
Properties in municipalities with site restrictions not eligible
Historic preservation properties not eligible
Separate electrical permit required in addition to building permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Apply online through the Department of Permitting Services and pay non-refundable filing fee. 2. Submit plans using SolarAPP+ at solarapp.nrel.gov and verify property is not in a restricted municipality or historic preservation area. 3. Upload certified approval documents into the ePlans application and complete assigned tasks. 4. Permit is issued immediately online after fees are paid and all requirements met; obtain associated electrical permit before commencing work. 5. Install solar panels conforming to approved drawings with permits kept on site. 6. Schedule inspections at least 24 hours prior to needed date using the Inspection Requests link.

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Fund Grant & Loan Program (EDFGLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A discretionary strategic attraction and retention program for private employers in targeted industry sectors that generate significant economic development impact to Montgomery County through job creation, job retention, and capital expenditure. Projects in high technology, manufacturing, and urban revitalization areas receive priority consideration. The program typically provides assistance from $5,000 to $100,000, with larger projects potentially receiving more. Project awards include conditions for disbursement, minimum performance measures, and clawback provisions to recapture funds if a business fails to achieve expected economic output.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans for private employers creating or retaining jobs in Montgomery County in targeted industry sectors. The program typically provides assistance from $5,000 to $100,000, with larger projects potentially receiving more. Priority given to high technology companies, manufacturing companies, businesses in urban revitalization areas, and private employers providing the greatest public benefits. Awards stipulate conditions for disbursement and include minimum performance measures with clawback provisions if business fails to achieve expected economic output.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers in Montgomery County seeking to locate, expand, or retain operations and generate significant economic development impact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support projects that generate significant economic development impact including job creation, job retention, and capital expenditure in targeted industry sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County only. The program gives priority to businesses located in urban revitalization areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a private employer
Must retain jobs or stimulate job creation
Project must be in a targeted industry sector
Project must generate significant economic development impact to the County
Must show projected job growth or capital investment
Must provide financial history and projections, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements
Must provide company and management background
Must provide a present and future market outlook
Priority is given to projects that create significant new jobs within 1 to 3 years
Priority is given to projects that result in significant capital investment
Priority is given to projects that leverage existing state and private funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Montgomery County Business Portal for application procedures and details on targeted industry sectors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that awards supplemental grants to qualified investors who receive a final tax credit certificate from the State of Maryland's Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit Program. Investors approved for the Maryland Biotechnology Investment Incentive Tax Credit Program automatically receive a supplemental grant from Montgomery County without requiring a separate application. Grant amounts are prorated based on program appropriation and the investor's proportion of state tax credits compared to total credits received by all investors of County biotechnology businesses. The county typically pays out grants between March and May for investments made in the previous calendar year.

Investors approved for the state program automatically receive this supplemental county grant without a separate application. Grant amounts are prorated based on program appropriation and the investor's proportion of state tax credits compared to total credits received by all investors of County biotechnology businesses. The county typically pays out the grants between March and May for investments made in the previous calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for employers in advanced technology, cybersecurity, hospitality, life sciences, and quantum computing technology industries, as well as company headquarters and national nonprofit organizations, who create at least five new full-time permanent jobs with base annual salaries of $100,000 or more. Employers in Community Equity Index disadvantaged areas receive enhanced grant amounts. The program supports business growth and expansion through job creation incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible employers receive grants of $10,000 per new job created, or $12,000 per job if the business is located in a designated Community Equity Index disadvantaged area. The maximum award is $500,000 per company. Eligibility requires creating at least five new full-time permanent jobs within twelve months of application, with each job paying a base annual salary of $100,000 or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers located in Montgomery County, including company headquarters, national nonprofit organizations, and businesses in target industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support business growth and expansion connected to hiring new full-time permanent employees at salaries of $100,000 or more.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Montgomery County. Companies in Community Equity Index disadvantaged areas receive enhanced grant amounts of $12,000 per job instead of $10,000.
requirements_list: Must be a company headquarters, national nonprofit organization, or operate in a target industry (Life Sciences, Advanced Technology, Cybersecurity, Quantum Computing, Hospitality)
Must create at least five new full-time permanent jobs within twelve months of application
Each new job must have a base annual salary of $100,000 or more, not including benefits
Jobs must be created within six months for initial consideration, with an additional six months to hire more positions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Montgomery County Department of Finance stating the number of qualifying jobs planned and the hiring schedule. The application submission date starts a 12-month period during which you must hire at least five qualifying employees at the required salary level. An additional six months is provided to hire beyond the initial five positions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Community Service Employment Program (also known as Title V) provides part-time work-based training opportunities at local community service agencies for low-income men and women aged 55 and older who are unemployed or have poor employment prospects. Trainees receive minimum wage or training support while working at charities and government agencies, building their skills and resumes while delivering valuable community service. The program includes personal and job-related counseling, job training, and job referral services, and also educates employers about the benefits of hiring older workers.
structured_extraction.agency: Montgomery County and Prince George's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Part-time work-based training opportunities at local community service agencies. Participants receive minimum wage or training support compensation while participating in on-the-job training at charities and government agencies. The program includes personal and job-related counseling, job training, and job referral services to build employment skills and work experience while providing community service.

structured_extraction.program_name: AmeriCorps Seniors Retired Senior and Volunteer Program (RSVP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program through AmeriCorps connecting older adults age 55 and older with volunteer opportunities to meet community needs. Established in 1971, it enables seniors to lead active lives in community service of their choice. Participants join local networks of senior volunteers, receive help finding suitable volunteer opportunities tailored to their interests and availability, and earn complimentary liability and injury insurance while volunteering. Volunteers choose the amount of time they want to work, from a few hours to up to 20 hours each week in various roles focused on the health and well-being of individuals. The program provides volunteer placement and support services including matching with opportunities, insurance coverage, recognition, and rewards for service. One of three branches of AmeriCorps Seniors (others: Foster Grandparents Program, Senior Companions Program).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive complimentary liability and injury insurance coverage while volunteering, mileage reimbursement up to $30 monthly, orientation and on-the-job training, volunteer recognition through newsletter articles and appreciation events, and a Service Rewards Program where volunteers can log hours and earn tiered gifts (membership pins, t-shirts, tumbler cups, coolers, picnic blankets, fleece vests at 1+, 50, 150, 500, 750, and 1,000 hours). Participants are not paid but receive these reimbursements and benefits for their volunteer service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People aged 55 and over living in or near Montgomery County or Prince George's County who want to volunteer in their community and are willing to help people of all ages and ethnicities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer placement and support services including matching with opportunities, insurance coverage, recognition, and rewards for service. Volunteer time supporting healthy futures of individuals through activities such as advocating in nursing homes, assisting seniors with health insurance, helping seniors remain in their homes, hospice care, hospital and non-profit services, nursing home friendly visits, support services to community and government agencies, telephone outreach, and transportation for seniors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Montgomery County and Prince George's County, Maryland. The program partners with the AmeriCorps Seniors nationwide network.
requirements_list: Must be age 55 or older
Must be interested in volunteering in the community
Must be willing to help people of all ages and ethnicities
Must be willing to serve in the communities of Montgomery County or Prince George's County
Must be willing to use their gifts and talents to help others
Must respect station policies and perform assignments in business-like manner
Must report personal injuries to supervisor and RSVP
Must notify station of unavailability during assigned shifts
Must document volunteer hours
Must notify RSVP of changes in contact information or assignment
Cannot engage in political activities, religious instruction, or proselytization
Cannot displace paid workers
Cannot receive compensation from service recipients
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Volunteer Center or program office to join the RSVP network. Discuss your skills, interests, and availability with an RSVP advisor. The advisor suggests relevant volunteer opportunities. Choose an opportunity and work with the organization to tailor it to mutual satisfaction. For Prince George's County, download the RSVP Registration Form (PDF) or contact the program at 240-777-2612 for more information or assistance with enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to help small businesses move ideas from concept to market through research and development, technology transfer, and commercialization of new technologies. The program supports innovation in high-impact sectors such as biotechnology, energy, defense, and advanced technology, with particular emphasis on innovative health-related technologies. It encourages domestic small businesses to engage in federal research and research and development, focusing on stimulating technological innovation, meeting Federal R&D needs, and increasing commercialization to transition R&D into market impact.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for early-stage startups and small businesses to support technological innovation, R&D commercialization, and technology transfer initiatives. Funding available for research and development, commercialization of new technologies, and business expansion. Awards up to $30 million available for businesses demonstrating market-ready technologies. The program has invested over $81 billion in more than 34,000 small businesses since inception.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage U.S.-based startups and small businesses in technology fields and high-impact sectors looking to innovate and commercialize technologies at scale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development, technology commercialization, innovative health technologies, federal research initiatives, business expansion, and technology transfer initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the United States and all of Maryland.
requirements_list: U.S.-based small business
Business must be startup or small business
Demonstrate market-ready technologies
Meet SBA small business criteria
Engaged in federal research or research and development

structured_extraction.program_description: An equity investment fund administered by NeighborWorks Capital in partnership with National Equity Fund (NEF) that provides NeighborWorks network member organizations with access to standardized, equitable Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) terms on par with those offered to the largest for-profit national developers. The fund supports the creation and preservation of affordable multifamily housing including permanent supportive housing, family housing, senior housing, health + housing, veterans housing, and multi-generational projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides LIHTC equity investment with standardized terms including standard letters of interest and investment agreements offering the best available terms, protections against abuse including assurances regarding exit terms at the end of the 15-year compliance period, accountability related to syndicator fees with target average fee levels below industry norms, and the opportunity to develop more favorable terms over time as participation in the fund grows. Projects supported must be for affordable multifamily housing development or preservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: NeighborWorks organizations (nonprofit affordable housing developers) of any size and location with multifamily affordable housing projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation or preservation of affordable multifamily housing. Projects of all sizes and in all geographies are considered, including permanent supportive housing, family housing, senior housing, health + housing, veterans housing, and multi-generational projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects in all geographies are considered. The fund is open to all NeighborWorks organizations regardless of location.

Projects are expected to begin groundbreaking within 12-18 months

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: NeighborWorks organizations should contact NeighborWorks Capital (via Lanie Wasserman, Director of Lending and Special Initiatives) to discuss potential projects. structured_extraction.program_description: A home improvement loan program designed to help Baltimore City homeowners access financing for essential repairs, upgrades, energy-efficient renovations, and time-sensitive repairs affecting safety, habitability, and essential home systems. The program offers fast approval with funds potentially available within 30 days, simplified processes to reduce delays, and flexible terms including no home equity requirement and no appraisal needed. Borrowers can receive up to $20,000 at a 6% fixed interest rate for up to 10 years with no income limits and the ability to manage their own contractors and project timelines. The program focuses on helping new homeowners and those with limited or no home equity, as well as seasoned homeowners, address urgent repair needs with faster turnaround than some grant cycles. Monthly ACH payments are optional. The program is structured to reduce barriers and help address essential repairs, smaller quick-turnaround projects, and home restoration initiatives.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home improvement loan program from Neighborhood Housing Services of Baltimore designed for substantial home repair and renovation projects for primary residences. The program serves Baltimore City homeowners who own their home and need financing for major improvements. It offers loans up to $30,000 at income-based interest rates (0% to 4%) for up to 20 years to low-to-moderate income homeowners with household income not exceeding 120% of Area Median Income (AMI). Repayment schedules are based on ability to repay, and payments may be deferred until the home is sold or based on gross annual household income and family size. The program includes personalized guidance from experienced NHS counselors to help homeowners manage contractors and project timelines through every step from contractor selection to project completion. Eligible projects include major repairs such as roofing, heating, plumbing, electrical work, foundation repairs, full kitchen or bath renovations, structural improvements, energy efficiency upgrades, and other substantial home improvements that protect the home's condition and equity.

Includes personalized support from NHS counselors to help manage contractors and project timelines. Loan for major repair and improvement projects for existing homeowners. Borrowers must have household income up to 120% of Baltimore's Area Median Income.

structured_extraction.program_name: Reinvest Baltimore Down Payment Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive down payment assistance program designed to increase homeownership opportunities by providing forgivable and deferred loans to qualified homebuyers purchasing properties in designated Baltimore neighborhoods and BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded redevelopment projects. The program offers maximum awards of $20,000 as five-year forgivable loans at 0% interest with 20% of principal forgiven annually, or up to $15,000 for NHS first mortgage customers or $5,000 for lender partner customers as deferred loans repayable upon sale or refinance. The program also provides up to $50,000 in down payment assistance to help eligible buyers bridge the gap between their savings and home purchase. Borrower must occupy the home as primary residence with a fixed-rate mortgage. Pre-purchase housing counseling and HUD-approved homebuyer workshops are required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum award of $20,000 per homebuyer as a five-year forgivable loan at 0% interest with 20% of the principal forgiven annually over five years, or up to $15,000 for NHS first mortgage customers or $5,000 for lender partner customers as deferred loans repayable upon sale or refinance. Additionally, eligible buyers can receive up to $50,000 in down payment assistance to help make buying a home possible. Assistance covers down payment and closing costs. Borrower must occupy the home as primary residence. Property must be located within a BVRI-funded or UPLIFT-funded project in designated BVRI areas. Pre-purchase housing counseling is required. No household income restrictions. Not limited to first-time homebuyers. Fixed-rate mortgages only (cash sales and owner financing not permitted).

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax-exempt bond financing program for affordable rental housing development in Prince George's County. Provides construction and permanent financing for new construction and substantial rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing (5+ units) for low- and moderate-income County residents. Includes regulatory agreements, land use restrictions, and long-term affordability covenants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bond financing including construction financing, permanent financing, 501(c)(3) bonds, taxable bonds, and refunding bonds. Limited liability, non-recourse conduit obligations. Includes loan closing, regulatory agreements, land use restrictions, and ongoing compliance monitoring. Secondary soft debt financing permitted with HAPGC approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit developers and project sponsors seeking to develop multifamily rental housing projects for low- to moderate-income County residents, families, and seniors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of multifamily rental housing, acquisition and substantial rehabilitation of existing multifamily properties, related professional fees (architecture, engineering), appraisals, environmental testing, builder fees, and developer fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Prince George's County, Maryland. Priority given to Inner Beltway Communities, Regional Transit Districts, Opportunity Zones, and designated development areas such as Westphalia.
requirements_list: Minimum 5 units in multifamily development
At least 20% of units rented to households earning ≤450% Area Median Income (AMI) OR 40% of units at higher income levels
Set aside percentage of units for low- and moderate-income persons/families for Qualified Project Period
Deed restrictions required for minimum 15 years regardless of bond term
Transfer of ownership requires HAPGC approval; new owner must assume all prior obligations
Minimum 5% vacancy rate underwriting
Operating expenses: $4,000-$7,000 per unit annually
Minimum $300 per unit per year replacement reserves
Operating reserves: 3-6 months of expenses required
Minimum 1.15 debt service coverage ratio
For-profit developers must demonstrate experience and creditworthiness
Non-profit organizations must comply with Section 501(c)(3) of Tax Code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit multifamily rental financing application along with developer and sponsor/owner qualifications forms. Applicants should contact the Housing Authority for specific requirements and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: An elective partnership program between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based organizations or other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations designed to improve water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. Participants can select one or more of three available options to qualify for a reduction in their Clean Water Act Fee. Option 1 (Provide Easement) offers a 50% fee reduction on the impervious area fee. Option 2 (Outreach & Education) offers a 25% fee reduction. Option 3 (Green Care & Good Housekeeping) offers a 25% fee reduction. The administrative fee of $20.58 per tax account applies annually and cannot be waived. Organizations may combine options for additional credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations can receive a reduction in their Clean Water Act Fee based on which program option(s) they participate in. Option 1 (Provide Easement) offers a 50% fee reduction on the impervious area fee. Option 2 (Outreach & Education) offers a 25% fee reduction. Option 3 (Green Care & Good Housekeeping) offers a 25% fee reduction. The administrative fee of $20.58 per tax account applies annually and cannot be waived. Organizations may combine options for additional credits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt faith-based organizations and 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The fee reduction can be applied toward a portion of the Clean Water Act Fee charged by the county. The fee reduction must be used for the property associated with the application and reduces the annual stormwater fee bill. Implementation of stormwater management practices to treat and reduce polluted stormwater runoff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt faith-based organization or 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Must agree to participate in at least one of the three program options

For Option 1 (Easement): Must provide a Temporary Right-of-Entry Agreement and Temporary Construction Easement for BMP installation, sign a Maintenance Agreement, continuously maintain installed BMPs, and submit to triennial inspection

For Option 2 (Outreach & Education): Must participate in education and outreach campaign and host at least one annual activity such as a Rain Check Rebate Program event, recycling initiative, trash pick-up, or tree planting (with 5+ trees)
For Option 3 (Green Care & Good Housekeeping): Must use certified lawn and landscaping companies for fertilizer application and practice at least 3 good housekeeping activities from the provided list
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select which option(s) to participate in, complete the application form, digitally sign it, and submit it online to the Department of the Environment at 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774. Step 2: Meet with the County's agent to develop an alternative compliance plan and determine which options are feasible. Step 3: Submit the written compliance plan to the Department of the Environment for review and approval of the fee reduction amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that seeks to increase the number of native trees and shrubs planted in Prince George's County. The program educates students about the everyday importance of trees, empowers them to enhance their community, and provides funds for planting projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program providing native trees and shrubs plus funds for purchasing and delivering materials and planting projects on school grounds. Includes technical and design assistance for selecting planting locations, developing tree planting plans, and creating post-planting maintenance schedules. Schools must develop a tree planting plan and post-planting maintenance plan. Trees can be planted during spring or fall months only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public schools in Prince George's County, including students, school staff, and volunteers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and delivering native trees and shrubs, and funding planting projects on school campuses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public school campuses in Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be approved by school principal and facility manager
Project organizers must agree to help plant trees
Must commit to two-year post-planting maintenance plan including watering trees every 7 days during dry periods, weeding and mulching up to two times per year, and pruning
Request marking of utility lines by MISS Utility
Complete PGCPS Request for Building Alteration
Submit Intent to Apply Form
Schedule consultation with Program Coordinator
Submit Program Application
Develop tree planting plan for campus
Create post-planting maintenance plan
Plant trees during spring or fall only, not summer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools submit an Intent to Apply Form (PDF). The Program Coordinator will contact the school to schedule a required consultation. During the consultation, information is provided on completing the Program Application, developing a tree planting plan, and creating a post-planting maintenance plan. The school then submits the Program Application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides financial assistance to local governments in designated BRAC zones to support infrastructure improvements related to military base realignment and expansion. Local jurisdictions receive payment of 100% of state real property tax increment on qualified properties plus 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. These funds can be used to pay back bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements. Projects may also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies. Benefits are available for 10 years from when the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local jurisdictions in BRAC Zones receive payment of 100% of state real property tax increment on qualified properties and payment equal to 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. These funds can be used to pay back bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements. Projects can also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and businesses located in designated BRAC Zones
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements and repayment of bonds issued for infrastructure projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated BRAC zones in Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated BRAC Zone
Property must be a qualified property
Funds must be used for infrastructure improvements
Infrastructure improvements must be the purpose of bond repayment or financing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information on how to apply and participate in the program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form and mail it with a check or money order ($10 per $20 coupon book) and proof of age and/or disability to The Office of Transportation, 9400 Peppercorn Place, Suite 320, Largo, MD 20774. structured_extraction.program_description: The Prince George's County Health Department provides support to help families address health conditions influenced by the home environment. This program serves children with elevated blood lead levels and children diagnosed with asthma. It works to reduce environmental lead hazards and asthma triggers in the home, encourage ongoing medical care with a primary care provider, and provide environmental case management in partnership with families and healthcare providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers environmental case management, home visits (up to six for asthma management), environmental assessments following confirmed elevated blood lead levels, educational programs on lead exposure prevention, telephone consultations on asthma triggers and indoor air quality, and may provide items for the home to control asthma triggers. Services are available to children under age 19 with Medicaid or Medicaid eligibility for asthma services, and to children with confirmed elevated blood lead levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children with elevated blood lead levels and children under age 19 diagnosed with asthma in Prince George's County, Maryland, particularly those with Medicaid or Medicaid eligibility for asthma services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support reducing environmental lead hazards and asthma triggers in the home, encouraging ongoing medical care, and providing environmental case management. For asthma, the program may provide items for the home to control asthma triggers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must have elevated blood lead level (for lead services)
Child must be diagnosed with asthma (for asthma services)
Child must be under age 19 (for asthma services)
Child must have Medicaid or be eligible for Medicaid (for asthma services)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For lead case management, call 301-883-7538. For environmental assessments and telephone consultations, call 301-883-7662 or email leadandasthmaprogram@co.pg.md.us. Children with confirmed elevated blood lead levels will be contacted directly by the Health Department after the state reports the elevated level.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists owners of smaller neighborhood retail centers, strip malls, Main Street retail space and stand-alone retail storefronts to fund building façade improvements, placemaking, lighting and major building systems improvements. Aims to noticeably improve the look and feel of surrounding commercial areas and boost economic development activity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost reimbursable matching grant covering up to 50% of approved project costs. Minimum grant award is $25,000 (requiring at least $50,000 in total project costs), and maximum grant award is $125,000 (requiring at least $250,000 in total project costs). Total funding available is $250,000 for FY2025/2026. CPIP requires a 50% applicant match for all awarded program funding. Grant funds are disbursed after improvements are paid in full by the awardee and contractor lien releases are provided. Requires selection of a minimum of 3 improvement types.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners with retail centers, strip malls, Main Street retail spaces and stand-alone retail storefronts located in eligible areas of Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building façade improvements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems improvements including storefront facades, energy efficiency upgrades, architectural features, doors/windows, lighting, signage, awnings, painting, landscaping, parking lot work, and roof replacement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Eligible properties must be located within Central Avenue Blue Line Corridor and Suitland-Naylor Road Metro Sustainable Communities Areas. Eligibility can be verified at: https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/5f31da408b584e59abdc4930517cb05e
requirements_list: Retail center or retail space must be located in a strong trade area with high visibility
Property must be obsolete or underperforming
Located in a retail shopping center, retail center, or main street retail space in Prince George's County
Applicants must demonstrate the ability to fund at least 50% of the total project cost
Commercial space occupied exclusively by places of worship or non-retail uses is not eligible
Adult entertainment, nightclubs, liquor/beer/wine stores, automobile repair shops, hotels/lodging, home-based businesses, and places of worship are not eligible uses
Shopping center owners who received CPIP funding in 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, or 2024 are not eligible to apply
Construction on approved projects must commence within 90 days of grant approval and must be completed within 270 days of approval
Incomplete submissions will not be accepted
Active Business License required
Proof of ownership (deed with legal description) required
Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland required
Current Certificate of Insurance required
Current tenant list required if applicable
Documentation verifying mortgages are current required
Documentation showing County taxes are current required
No outstanding code violations
Proposed scope of work with schedule and budget required
Minimum 3 improvement types must be selected
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications will be available beginning April 15, 2026, and must be submitted no later than May 20, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. A virtual pre-application information session webinar will be held on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Interested participants must RSVP by 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, April 28, 2026, to receive the Zoom link and passcode. Questions may be submitted and responses will be posted by Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides small capital grants to community-based organizations and civic/neighborhood associations in Prince George's County to implement innovative capital projects in priority areas identified by the redevelopment authority. Projects may focus on neighborhood beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, banners, way-finding systems, commercial facade improvements, internal and external building improvements, permanent public art installations) or environmental sustainability (restoration of parks, streams and open space, urban agriculture and tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development and storm water management, preservation of historic landmarks). The program aims to strengthen communities and build organizational capacity. Total funding for FY 2025 is $250,000 with a maximum grant amount of $50,000 per award. Grants support innovative capital projects through purchase of equipment and materials and cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, or personnel.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small capital grants provided to eligible organizations on a reimbursable or traditional basis. The County has $250,000 in Community Impact Grants available to award in FY 2025, with $100,000 earmarked for National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas and $150,000 available countywide. Maximum grant amount is $50,000 per award. Grants support innovative capital projects such as purchase of equipment and materials for neighborhood beautification or environmental sustainability initiatives. Grants cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel. Funds must be expended within the grant period before reapplication.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic and neighborhood associations, community-based organizations, houses of worship, condominium associations, recreation associations, community development corporations, and arts/cultural organizations that are incorporated as 501(c)(3) entities and located in Prince George's County and in good standing with the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital expenses for community-based projects including neighborhood beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, commercial facade improvements, internal and external building improvements, permanent public art installations) or environmental sustainability (restoration of parks, streams and open space, urban agriculture and tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development and storm water management, preservation of historic landmarks, structures and sites), community recreational spaces, memorial gardens and landscaping, building and facility renovations, and historic building restoration. Cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Prince George's County. Applicant must be located within Prince George's County and in good standing with the State of Maryland. Project must be located within Prince George's County. Projects in National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas (inside the Beltway in previously designated sustainable communities) are prioritized. Project can be on private property with owner authorization or on government property with appropriate government official approval.
requirements_list: Must be a civic/neighborhood association, community-based organization, house of worship, condominium association, recreation association, community development corporation, or arts/cultural organization
Must be an incorporated 501(c)(3) entity
Must be located within Prince George's County
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and hold certificate of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must demonstrate approval of the project by local municipal leadership (Mayor or Council) where project is located
Project must fall into one of two categories: Neighborhood Beautification or Environment, Natural Resources and Sustainability
Grants can only be used for capital expenses
Previously funded applicants can reapply two years from date of formerly approved application
All prior CIG funds must be expended before submitting new application
Project cannot have been previously funded through the CIG program
Maximum one project per organization
Prince George's County government and affiliated entities are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the CIG Application through the NOFA (Notification of Funding Availability) process to the Redevelopment Authority by the application deadline. Community-based organizations must demonstrate project approval by local municipal leadership before applying. Awards are determined by the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County. Applications are available on the RDA agency website. Contact the program email or phone line for additional information or questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Partnership Grants program is the main discretionary grant initiative offered by the Office of the County Executive to qualified nonprofit organizations. Grants support community-based projects and initiatives aligned with county priorities based upon criteria including the value added to the identified community, overall program costs, organizational stability, and adequacy of other funding sources. Awards range up to $100,000 for FY 2026 (previous awards have ranged from $1,000 to $125,000), with the total award amount disbursed in one payment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging up to $100,000 for FY 2026 (previous awards have ranged from $1,000 to $125,000). Total award amount is disbursed in one payment. Award amounts depend on factors including organization mission and goals, statement of need, project description, sustainability relative to amount requested, evidence of partnerships and collaboration, and investment within served communities.

structured_extraction.program_name: ENERGY STAR Certification & Green Leasing Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program providing funding to commercial and multifamily building owners in Prince George's County to perform energy and water efficiency retrofits, achieve EPA ENERGY STAR certification, and adopt green leasing best practices. The program supports the County's goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and attracting high-value tenants. Funding supports ASHRAE Level 2 audits, energy efficiency improvements, benchmarking in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, and professional verification of ENERGY STAR certification, with maximum award of $150,000 per location. Incentives include up to $50,000 for auditing and certification costs, up to $50,000 for natural gas measures, and up to $50,000 for electric measures, plus up to $1,500 for Licensed Professional sign-off costs.

Up to $1,500 may be attributed to a Licensed Professional to verify and stamp the ENERGY STAR certification application. Grant awards reimburse some portion of net customer costs after applying for other incentives. Additional technical assistance provided to help multifamily and commercial buildings boost performance and earn certification through ENERGY STAR or green leasing programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A $50 million fund administered by the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation and Financial Services Corporation (FSC First) to provide financing for the retention, expansion, and attraction of businesses that broaden the county's commercial tax base, retain and attract jobs, support small and local enterprises, and promote development and redevelopment opportunities. The program provides both loans and grants to businesses, non-profit organizations, and real estate developers. The fund prioritizes four industry sectors: federal government, hospitals & health services, research-intensive technologies, and information technology. Loans have a minimum of $250,000 with terms up to 10 years and amortization not to exceed 25 years, with interest rates determined at underwriting (generally competitive market rates or the Prince George's prime rate of 4%). Grants range from $50,000 to $4,000,000 based on project scope, job creation potential, and sector. The fund distributes approximately $7-11 million per year in grants and loans. An application fee of 1% of the loan amount is required after initial approval (up-front fees range from $2,500 for loans up to $1,000,000 to $5,000 for loans $1,000,000 and above). To date, $36 million in awards have generated $1 billion in private investment and created or retained over 12,000 jobs. The program focuses on expanding the county's commercial tax base, job retention and attraction, support for small and local businesses, promotion of development and redevelopment opportunities, transit-oriented development, and growth of key industry sectors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a minimum of $250,000 and maximum term of 10 years with amortization not to exceed 25 years. Interest rates determined at underwriting, generally set at competitive market rates or the Prince George's prime rate of 4%. Application fee of 1% of loan amount required after initial approval ($2,500 up-front for loans up to $1,000,000; $5,000 up-front for loans $1,000,000 and above, with balance due at closing; portion of fee may be financed). Direct grants awarded ranging from $50,000 to $4,000,000 based on project scope, job creation potential, and sector. The fund distributes approximately $7-11 million per year in grants and loans. Funds can be used for land and building acquisitions, building construction and improvement, equipment acquisition, working capital, business expansion, and real estate development projects. Collateral of business and personal assets required with personal guarantees for loans. Assistance is provided based on total capital expenditure, job retention, and job expansion.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses submit applications to the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation and Financial Services Corporation (FSC First) through the EDI Fund website (edif.princegeorgescountymd.gov), online application, or in person. A business development specialist reviews the application and contacts the applicant. If the application meets basic requirements, applicants are notified of the application fee amount (1% of loan amount) and must submit additional required documents including financial statements, tax records, and supporting materials. Applicants can check the progress of their application online at the EDI Fund portal. Applications are reviewed for consistency with statutory goals, credit and financial soundness of the borrower, and financial projections. The review process takes approximately 90 days. Applications are reviewed collaboratively and then submitted to the County Council for approval. After initial review and approval to proceed, applicants complete additional documentation requirements and the loan proceeds to closing. Evaluation is conducted on a case-by-case basis by the EDC. A checklist of required documents is available on the website under Apply Now. For additional information, contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible households facing financial hardship due to COVID-19. Serves Prince George's County residents and tenants with household income below 80% of Area Median Income who are experiencing housing instability due to COVID-19 pandemic hardship. The program provides direct financial assistance for rental payments and utilities. Applicants with household income at or below 50% AMI may qualify with income documentation alone. Applicants above 50% but below 80% AMI must demonstrate eviction risk (scheduled eviction, active Warrant for Possession, court summons, or court judgment) or financial hardship from COVID-19. Direct rental and utility assistance payments are made to landlords on behalf of eligible tenants, with assistance covering up to 18 months cumulative of past due rent and utility payments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct rental and utility assistance payments to help tenants and residents pay overdue, current, or delinquent rent and utility obligations. Up to 18 months cumulative of past due rent and utility payments. Payments are made directly to landlords who have executed a Rental Assistance Agreement with the program. Tenants below 50% of Area Median Income may qualify with household income documentation alone. Tenants above 50% but below 80% AMI must demonstrate eviction risk based on income level: 30% AMI and below require no court documentation; 31%-50% AMI require court summons; 51%-80% AMI require court judgment. The specific dollar amount of assistance is determined by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) on a case-by-case basis following application review and approval.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past due and current rent and utility bills to prevent eviction and address housing instability. Landlord must also submit rent ledger, rental license, W-9 form, EFT enrollment form, and Landlord Rental Assistance Agreement.
