structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care (CoC) Competition
structured_extraction.program_description: Annual U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) allocation of funding for homeless assistance programs through the Continuum of Care competition process. The program provides funding for nonprofit providers, states, local governments, Indian Tribes, and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs) to quickly re-house homeless individuals, families, persons fleeing domestic violence, and youth. Includes specialized funding for Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program (YHDP) serving youth aged 24 and younger, and Domestic Violence Bonus funding for survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Supports five program components: Permanent Housing (PSH and RRH), Transitional Housing (TH), Joint TH and PH-RRH, Supportive Services Only (SSO), and HMIS. Requires a consolidated application describing how local activities meet or exceed HUD requirements and align with community needs. The Continuum of Care must rank and prioritize funding requests from eligible providers, promoting community-wide commitment to ending homelessness while minimizing trauma and dislocation caused by homelessness. Emphasizes Housing First principles, racial equity, system performance measures, and coordination among diverse stakeholders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for homeless assistance programs including: Renewal/reallocation/consolidation/transition projects; Planning projects; New projects under permanent housing bonus; New projects under DV (Domestic Violence) housing bonus; YHDP renewal, replacement, and reallocation projects. Funding covers leasing, operating costs, supportive services, rental assistance, HMIS (Homeless Management Information System), and project administration. Eligible uses include permanent supportive housing leasing, rapid rehousing assistance, transitional housing, emergency shelter, coordinated entry systems, street outreach, safe haven projects, and supportive services. Special YHDP activities include short-term leases, moving expenses, security deposits, utility assistance, legal fees, cell phone/internet costs, damage payments, household goods (up to $300), rental/utility arrears, and employment-related expenses. Minimum 25% match requirement. Project types include Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH), Rapid Re-Housing (RRH), Transitional Housing-Rapid Re-Housing (TH-RRH), Emergency Shelter, and Joint TH/PH-RRH projects. Funding available for capital costs (acquisition, new construction, rehabilitation) for some projects with minimum 3-year grant terms.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 2024: October 30, 2024 at 8:00 PM EDT; FY 2025: August 29, 2025 at 8:00 PM EDT; Project applications to local CoC due 30 days before HUD deadline; CoC notification to applicants required 15 days before HUD submission deadline; HUD-2991 Certification of Consistency deadline between November 1, 2024 and August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and government organizations providing homeless services; Continuums of Care (CoCs); Collaborative Applicants; Project applicants and subrecipients; Indian Tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs); Victim service providers (domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking survivors); Chronically homeless individuals and families; Unaccompanied youth aged 24 and younger; Families headed by youth aged 24 and younger (including pregnant or parenting youth); Persons fleeing domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking; Veterans experiencing homelessness; People with disabilities experiencing chronic homelessness; Elderly and aging populations; Human trafficking survivors; Sexual assault survivors; Returning citizens; Individuals and families with highest service needs and longest homelessness experiences; Persons with high rates of physical and mental health illness and substance use disorders; Culturally specific communities (Black, Latino, Indigenous, LGBTQ+, persons with disabilities); Individuals with unsafe primary nighttime residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and services to prevent and end homelessness including: creation of new Permanent Supportive Housing; Rapid Re-Housing programs; Transitional Housing-Rapid Re-Housing programs; coordinated entry support and street outreach; permanent housing with wraparound services; housing stabilization services; rental assistance; leasing of housing units; operating costs for housing projects; supportive services; program administration; staffing and cost of living adjustments; staff recruitment and retention; partnerships for expanded services in health, behavioral health, employment, vocational, and educational areas; HMIS development and operations; emergency shelter; safe haven projects; youth-specific services (short-term leases, moving expenses, security deposits, utility assistance, legal fees, cell phone/internet costs, damage payments, household goods, rental/utility arrears, employment-related expenses); capital costs for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation; VAWA emergency transfer support; confidentiality monitoring; environmental review and lead-based paint compliance; Section 3 business participation for construction/rehabilitation projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: National program with local implementation through Continuums of Care (CoCs) designated geographic areas. Can include Formula Areas from Indian Housing Block Grant program. Rural areas defined as those with no part within standard metropolitan statistical area, or within MSA with 75%+ non-urban population, or in low-density states with specific acreage requirements. Scattered-site projects allowed where participants choose own units within CoC geographic area. Prince George's County, Maryland (MD-600 CoC region) referenced as administering CoC for this record.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit provider, state, local government, Indian Tribe, or Tribally Designated Housing Entity (TDHE)
Must maintain active SAM registration and valid UEI number
Must have nonprofit/government IRS documentation
Must not be debarred and be federally qualified
Must be providing or planning to provide CoC-eligible services
Submit Letter of Intent by deadline to compete for funding (if applicable)

Full fund expenditure in grant year
APR submission to SAGE within 90 days of grant year end

Completion of applications, checklists, and supplemental addendums
Attendance at mandatory CoC plenary meetings and office hours
Submission via E-Snaps system
For-profit entities ineligible

Build America, Buy American requirements
Section 3 compliance requirements for construction/rehabilitation projects
Fair housing and affirmative marketing/outreach compliance required
Victim service providers subject to alternative HMIS requirements and confidentiality monitoring
Organizations serving youth must demonstrate approval from Youth Action Board (YAB) for YHDP activities
Faith-based organizations must have equal participation opportunity
Rental assistance must begin within 12 months of award
New projects requesting capital costs require minimum 3-year grant terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Letter of Intent (if applicable) by initial deadline to compete for funding. Renewal and new/bonus applications submitted by their respective deadlines with final CoC submission and federal deadline. Application includes consolidated application describing local activities meeting/exceeding HUD requirements, supplemental application addendum with questions on eligibility, Housing First alignment, housing stabilization policies, program administration, and staffing. Applications subject to objective review, ranking, and selection process with tier-based approach (Tier 1 higher ranked, Tier 2 lower ranked projects). E-Snaps system submission required. Project applicants must submit to local CoC at least 30 days before HUD deadline; CoC provides notification to applicants 15 days before HUD submission deadline. Attendance at mandatory CoC plenary meetings and office hours. CoC ranks and prioritizes funding requests from eligible providers. Conditional grant awards may have conditions placed before grant agreement execution. HUD conducts project eligibility and quality threshold reviews for new and renewal projects. Waiver requests must be postmarked no later than 60 days after NOFO publication.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal entitlement program administered by Prince George's County designed to help expand the supply of decent, affordable housing for low and very low-income families. The program works with real estate and non-profit developers to produce new housing construction, rehabilitate existing housing, preserve naturally affordable housing, assist first-time homebuyers, acquire or improve group homes for special populations, and support Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) in creating housing opportunities, particularly in areas with projected rent growth. The program provides financial assistance to eligible projects and beneficiaries throughout the fiscal year according to HOME Subsidy Limits. Prince George's County receives approximately $3.5 million annually from a Federal Housing and Urban Development (HUD) appropriation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal entitlement funds administered in the form of grants and interest-bearing loans to eligible projects and beneficiaries. Subordinate loans for multifamily affordable rental housing projects with interest rates of 0% during construction and 2% simple interest during permanent loan period, with up to 40-year amortization. HOME-ARP loans available up to 100% of Total Development Costs for HOME-ARP Assisted Units plus Operating Cost Assistance Reserve (up to $45,000 per unit). Financial assistance amounts are determined on a project-by-project basis throughout the fiscal year and provided according to HOME Subsidy Limits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: PILOT requests must be submitted no later than 4 months in advance of anticipated construction financing close
structured_extraction.program_audience: Real estate developers, non-profit developers, first-time homebuyers, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), multifamily rental housing developers, project sponsors and owners, low and very low-income households in Prince George's County, homeless households referred through Coordinated Entry Policy, households with incomes at or below 10% of Area Median Income (AMI)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building new housing construction, rehabilitating existing housing, preserving naturally affordable housing, assisting first-time homebuyers to purchase homes, acquiring or improving group homes for special populations, construction expenses, acquisition costs, professional fees, site preparation and infrastructure costs, financing costs, developer fees, operating and replacement reserves, capitalized reserves, working capital items, syndication costs, and creating housing opportunities for households of limited income
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Prince George's County, Maryland, particularly in areas with projected rent growth, prioritized within one mile of Blue Line transit Corridor, Purple Line transit Corridor, and existing and planned Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) Metro Stations. Conformance with County's 2035 Adopted General Plan required.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental assistance to eligible low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities to help them afford housing in the private rental market. The program is administered by the Prince George's County Housing Authority. Participants receive vouchers that subsidize a portion of their rent, with the Housing Authority paying a subsidy directly to landlords on behalf of participating families, who pay the difference between the actual rent and the subsidized amount. Under certain circumstances, vouchers may also be used to purchase a modest home. Applicants are selected through a lottery system and placed on a waiting list before receiving vouchers. Approximately 5,986 vouchers are administered in Fiscal Year 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rental subsidies to help eligible households afford private market housing. The Housing Authority pays a subsidy directly to landlords on behalf of participating families, who pay the difference between actual rent and the subsidized amount. Vouchers may also be used to purchase a modest home under certain circumstances. Applicants are selected through a lottery system. Families that are selected are placed on a waiting list and then notified to complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation before receiving vouchers. Approximately 5,986 vouchers administered in Fiscal Year 2026.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: During the application period, applicants submit a preliminary application online through a portal. Selected applicants are notified by email and/or mail at least 45 days after the waitlist closes. They then receive instructions to complete eligibility verification and submit required documentation. Applicants can check their status by logging into the portal.

Eligible Metropolitan Area, which includes Prince George's County, Calvert County, and Charles County in Suburban Maryland, as well as the District of Columbia, Northern Virginia, and Rural West Virginia. HUD distributes HOPWA funds using a statutory formula based on AIDS statistics from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental and emergency assistance provided through a voucher system. HUD distributes HOPWA funds using a statutory formula that relies on AIDS statistics from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Three quarters of HOPWA formula funding is awarded to qualified states and Metropolitan areas with the highest number of AIDS cases. One quarter of the formula funding is awarded to Metropolitan areas that have a higher than average per capita incidence of AIDS.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federally-funded programs administered by Prince George's County that provide financial assistance for the rehabilitation and improvement of single-family homes and housing units to homeowners of limited financial means and non-profit organizations. The programs offer rehabilitation loans and grants up to $60,000 (or up to $50,000 for households under 50% of area median income) for repairs including roof replacement, electrical and plumbing work, energy efficiency improvements, accessibility modifications, and other home improvements. Services support health, safety, energy efficiency and accessibility repairs while upgrading the quality of deteriorated dwellings to contemporary minimum property standards, eliminating housing code violations, and preserving the existing housing stock. Programs are administered and managed by DHCD partner organizations including Habitat for Humanity.

Covers repairs such as roof replacement, electrical and plumbing work, HVAC replacement and repair, water heater replacement/repair, accessibility equipment, tree removal, stairlift installation, energy efficiency improvements, and other repairs to meet contemporary minimum property standards. Available to homeowners of limited financial means, owner-occupants meeting income requirements, and non-profit organizations. Program is administered and managed by DHCD partner organizations including Habitat for Humanity.

Participants receive a complimentary Naloxone (Narcan) nasal spray kit upon completion. Training emphasizes that naloxone is easy to use and anyone can learn to use it.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual and in-person naloxone training on how to use Naloxone to reverse opioid overdoses, plus a complimentary Naloxone nasal spray kit provided to each participant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Everyone; overdoses can occur from drug use or accidental ingestion of prescribed opioid medications. Anyone 18 years or older interested in learning how to reverse an opioid overdose and help save lives in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and Naloxone kits are provided to enable participants to recognize and respond to opioid overdoses.

Appointments available Monday through Friday from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (301) 883-7828 or email SaveALife@co.pg.md.us to enroll in a free training session. Training is offered either in person or via Zoom. A complimentary Naloxone kit is provided upon completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathway to Purchase Home Buyer Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A first-time homebuyer assistance program designed to help eligible households purchase their first home in Prince George's County. The program provides down payment, closing cost, and/or mortgage principal reduction assistance for residential properties through participating lenders and requires borrowers to complete housing counseling. The program offers up to $50,000 in loans at 0% interest with deferred payment, secured as a second trust. Loan forgiven after 10 years if primary residence requirement maintained. Support and resources are provided through a network of participating lenders, housing counseling agencies, and title companies. Funded by the Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME) pursuant to 24 CFR Part 92.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $50,000 in down payment, closing cost, and/or mortgage principal reduction assistance as a 0% interest deferred payment loan secured as a second trust. No minimum cash contribution required from applicants. Borrower prohibited from receiving money back at settlement. 10-year affordability period with recapture chart determining repayment percentage based on length of home retention. Loan forgiven after 10 years if primary residence requirement maintained. Loan due upon sale, transfer, or change of primary residence. Technical assistance is provided through housing counseling agencies that offer minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling (online certificates accepted). The program involves title companies and provides access to standardized affidavits, income limit documentation, and housing quality inspection resources. Specific loan amounts and terms are detailed in the program guidelines and loan application materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Prince George's County who meet income and other eligibility requirements purchasing residential properties. Households with income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Applicants must be 18 years or older. Households with annual income ranging from $91,800 (1-person) to $173,100 (8-person). US citizens or registered aliens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance, and/or mortgage principal reduction for purchase of single-family dwelling units, townhouses, or condominiums. Can be used for new construction, resales, foreclosures, or short sales. Must be applicant's primary residence. Cannot be reimbursed to buyer; cannot be used for repairs on seller-owned property, tenant relocation activities, or sectarian religious worship facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Prince George's County, Maryland. All zip codes within Prince George's County are eligible. Property must be located in Prince George's County, Maryland. Residential properties only.
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer status (no residential real estate ownership in past 3 years)
Income limits apply: household income must not exceed 80% AMI (ranges from $91,800 for 1-person to $173,100 for 8-person households)
Completion of minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course (online certificates accepted)
Executed sales contract with at least 21 business days remaining
Property must pass Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection
Lead-based paint disclosure signed by buyer (for pre-1978 properties)
First mortgage loan cannot be adjustable rate or subprime
Property must not be acquired through tax foreclosure or eminent domain
Must commit to occupy property as primary residence for 10 years
Debt-to-income ratios: maximum 35% front ratio, 47% back ratio (no exceptions)
No conflict of interest with County officials or program administrators
Property must be owner-occupied or untenanted (foreclosed property with court-ratified sale OR short sale property)
No unlawful tenant evictions or lease non-renewals in anticipation of purchase
Voluntary acquisition (not eminent domain)
Property appraisal (within 60 days of contract)
Termite inspection report required
Income verification documentation required
Valid borrower identification required
Information provided must be true and complete; borrower must notify County of any changes
Must work with a participating lender
Maximum purchase price: $448,000 (resale) or $485,000 (new construction)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective borrowers should consult with participating lenders and housing counseling agencies. Applicants should contact Housing & Community Development for program information. Borrowers must complete minimum 8-hour HUD-certified housing counseling course. Applicants must have executed sales contract with at least 21 business days remaining. First mortgage lender must provide conditional approval with Pathway to Purchase funds approval. Property appraisal, termite inspection report, and HQS inspection required. Submit complete documentation package including income verification, HUD Income Calculation Worksheet, valid borrower identification, and all supporting documents via email to program coordinator; no hand-delivered packages accepted; missing items result in rejection. The program provides resources including guidelines, a first-time homebuyer kit, participating lender lists, housing counselor referrals, and loan application forms. Lenders submit borrower information and supporting documents using the provided submission checklist. Detailed guidelines and checklists are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long structured lifestyle change program developed by the CDC for people with prediabetes or at risk for type 2 diabetes. The program aims to help participants lose 5 to 7% of their body weight and make lasting lifestyle changes including healthy eating and increased physical activity to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A fee-for-service program with three phases spanning one year. Phase 1 consists of weekly sessions from August 26, 2025 to October 14, 2025. Phase 2 is bi-weekly from October 28, 2025 to February 3, 2026. Phase 3 meets every four weeks from March 3, 2026 to July 21, 2026. All sessions are held online on Tuesdays from 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. Participants receive instruction from a trained lifestyle coach and can participate in support groups. The County Health Department is a Medicare/Medicaid supplier and has partnerships with commercial health plans and managed care organizations, allowing health plan members to access the program at no or low cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults 18 years or older who are overweight and have prediabetes or are at risk for type 2 diabetes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants learn healthy eating habits, weight loss strategies, physical activity routines, and stress management techniques delivered by trained lifestyle coaches with peer support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Program is offered online to registered participants.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years or older
Must be overweight (Body Mass Index of 25 or higher; 23 or higher for Asian-American)
Not previously diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes
Not currently pregnant

Must meet at least one of the following: prediabetes blood test result (Hemoglobin A1C of 5.7-6.4, or Oral Glucose Tolerance Test 140-199 mg/dl, or Fasting Glucose Test 100-125 mg/dl) within the past 12 months; or previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes; or high-risk result (score of 5 or higher) on the CDC prediabetes risk test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call (301) 856-9645 or email wellnessinfo@co.pg.md.us to register. An information session is held on Tuesday, July 22, 2025 at 1:00 p.m. Once registration is completed, participants receive a follow-up confirmation call or email and are sent the online program link prior to the program start.

structured_extraction.program_description: A chronic disease prevention and management program designed to help participants prevent chronic diseases and better manage their health if they have diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or prediabetes. The program offers peer-led virtual and in-person sessions backed by evidence-based practices, connecting participants with lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers. The program includes a two-way communication system between participants' physicians and PreventionLink staff to track progress and coordinate care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program offering peer-led virtual and in-person sessions, lifestyle coaching, health education, and community health worker support. The program provides an integrated system where the participant's physician and PreventionLink staff communicate to track progress and coordinate care. No financial assistance is provided; the program focuses on health education and behavior change support to help prevent or manage chronic diseases through lifestyle changes including weight loss, healthy eating habits, exercise, and improved mobility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Prince George's County who have been diagnosed with or are at risk for chronic diseases including prediabetes, diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide funds. It offers education, coaching, and support services to help participants prevent or manage chronic diseases through lifestyle changes including weight loss, healthy eating habits, exercise, and improved mobility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Free for residents of Prince George's County, Maryland. The program works closely with diverse healthcare providers to link participants with appropriate care and programs.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Prince George's County
Must have prediabetes or diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol, or be at risk for these conditions
Must work with a healthcare provider for referral or complete a PreventionLink participant interest form if you don't have a primary care doctor
Expected to attend and actively participate in all program sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Ask your doctor for a referral to PreventionLink. Step 2: Your doctor determines your eligibility and refers you to the PreventionLink program that meets your needs. Step 3: PreventionLink connects you with lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers. Alternative: If you do not have a primary care physician, fill out a form to speak with a PreventionLink staff member or community health worker to determine your eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County COVID-19 Business Relief Fund (Business Recovery Initiative)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public grant and loan program established to support Prince George's County businesses adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program provided direct grants and low-cost loans to help local, minority-owned, women-owned, veteran-owned, Latino-owned businesses, sole proprietors, 1099 independent contractors, cooperatives, and non-profits survive the economic crisis caused by the pandemic and retain their workforce. Grants were available from $5,000 to $10,000, with some awards up to $100,000, and low-cost loans up to $100,000. Award amounts were determined based on financial statement analysis, needs assessment, documented COVID-19 related losses, and the number of jobs affected. Over $10.6 million was approved from a $20 million program allocation, with over $5 million distributed to local businesses by the time of reporting. Additional grant contributions of $250,000 from Pepco Holdings and $65,000 from BGE supplemented the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from $5,000 to $100,000 and low-cost loans up to $100,000 to support businesses adversely impacted by COVID-19. Award amounts determined based on financial statement analysis, needs assessment, documented COVID-19 related losses, and number of jobs affected. Funds can be used for cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other business-critical costs to support business sustainability during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. As of the reporting date, over $10.6 million had been approved from a $20 million allocation, with over $5 million already distributed. Additional funding of $250,000 from Pepco Holdings and $65,000 from BGE supplemented the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County businesses, sole proprietors, 1099 contractors, cooperatives, and non-profits adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, including small, local, minority-owned, women-owned, veteran-owned, and Latino-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other business-critical costs to help businesses recover from COVID-19-related losses and operational disruptions caused by mandatory closures or operational limitations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Prince George's County, Maryland. Businesses must be based in or primarily serve Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Businesses must be based in or primarily serve Prince George's County
Businesses must be adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic
Must submit COVID-19 Business Recovery Initiative Online Application Form
Must submit 2018 Tax Returns
Must submit 2019 Tax Returns or internally-prepared financial statements
Must submit 2020 Interim Income Statement (January – March 2020)
Must provide proof of application to either Maryland Department of Commerce COVID business relief programs or SBA COVID or EIDL programs
Previously approved BRF loan recipients must convert loans to forgivable loans or grants
Applicants must have submitted applications by the May 29th deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses submitted grant and loan applications by the May 29th deadline through the program portal or online application form, along with required financial documents including 2018 and 2019 tax returns and 2020 interim income statements. The Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation and FSC First reviewed, underwritten, and approved applications, conducting financial statement analysis and needs assessment to determine award amounts based on documented COVID-19 related losses and number of jobs affected. Approved grant funds were wired on a weekly basis. Previously approved applicants did not need to reapply. Contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation for additional application information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Climate-Smart Local Producers Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that supports farmers and food producers, particularly those of color and from underserved communities, to implement climate-centric and climate-smart farming practices. Funded by a $3.25 million USDA grant, the program provides funding to reduce barriers to practice implementation on existing and new farms, includes a marketing strategy that combines local eating values with climate-smart practices and women and minority-owned farm support, works to measure and monitor greenhouse gas reductions, and contributes to the availability of healthy food throughout Prince George's County. The program emphasizes support for beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $3.25 million USDA grant to support farmers and producers in implementing climate-smart farming practices. Funding supports organic farming, practice implementation, greenhouse gas monitoring and analysis, and marketing development for climate-smart commodities. The program emphasizes support for beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, and specialty crop producers.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pilot program development, marketing strategy development, monitoring methodology development, greenhouse gas reduction analysis, supporting implementation of climate-centric farming practices, reducing barriers to practice implementation, and farm operations and activities contributing to healthy food availability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland, with focus on underserved communities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Domestic Violence Community Assistance Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial assistance to non-profit organizations to enhance services for individuals and families affected by domestic violence and human trafficking, and to provide programs designed to prevent violence in the home. The program supports housing, workforce development, counseling and mental health services, legal assistance, support groups, employment training, and advocacy services. The County Council has appropriated $500,000 in FY 2025 for grant funding. Services include shelter, emergency aid, security deposits, case management, and capacity-building activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county-based tax credit program that encourages business expansion and attraction of new business activity and jobs in designated enterprise zones within Prince George's County. The program offers state income tax credits and local property tax credits to for-profit businesses, with enhanced incentives available in designated enterprise zone focus areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive state income tax credits and local property tax credits based on their location within the enterprise zone. Non-Focus Area: Disadvantaged employees receive $6,000 total over 3 years ($3,000 year 1, $2,000 year 2, $1,000 year 3); non-disadvantaged employees receive a one-time $1,000 credit. Local property tax credit provides 80% of eligible assessment for years 1-5, then decreases 10% annually for years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) on real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement. Focus Area: Disadvantaged employees receive $9,000 total over 3 years ($4,500 year 1, $3,000 year 2, $1,500 year 3); non-disadvantaged employees receive a one-time $1,500 credit. Local property tax credit provides 80% of eligible assessment for all 10 years on real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement, plus 80% of eligible assessments for 10 years on new personal property investments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses seeking to expand existing operations or establish new business activity in designated enterprise zones within Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied to state income taxes and local property taxes for business operations, employee hiring, and real property or personal property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in designated enterprise zones within Prince George's County, including both standard enterprise zones and enterprise zone focus areas.
requirements_list: Business must be located within a designated enterprise zone in Prince George's County
For state income tax credit, employees must meet the definition of disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged as defined by Maryland Department of Commerce
Property tax credits apply to real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement
In focus areas, personal property tax credits apply to new investments in personal property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for assistance with the application process and program details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Green Energy Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program and loan guarantee program created to advance public and private investment in clean energy and other innovative green technologies in Prince George's County. The program provides financing for building energy efficiency improvements, energy conservation, renewable energy measures, energy storage, community solar, distributed energy generation, microgrids, clean transportation infrastructure, and resiliency measures. Specific eligible projects include solar, fuel cells, geothermal, wind, waste-to-energy, lighting, HVAC, building envelope renovations, retrofitting of commercial property, electric vehicle charging stations, and water efficiency improvements. Loans up to $250,000 are available with terms not to exceed 20 years. The program is managed as a loan guarantee program with participating lenders and is sponsored by Pepco and Exelon.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans and loan guarantees up to $250,000 with terms not to exceed 20 years to participating lenders to finance sustainable energy projects. Interest rate determined at time of underwriting. Application fee of 1% of loan amount. Administration/program fees of 1.5% of allocation for software and servicing system licensing. Loan closing fee of 1% of loan amount. Ongoing servicing/guaranty fee of 20 basis points on outstanding principal balance annually. The fund requires diverse and minority-owned businesses and lenders to implement projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and industrial building owners, businesses, and organizations in Prince George's County seeking financing for sustainable energy projects. Established, credit-worthy organizations with a demonstrated need for financing that cannot be obtained elsewhere. Preference for diverse and minority-owned businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation, energy efficiency, clean renewable energy measures including solar, fuel cells, geothermal, wind, waste-to-energy, energy storage, community solar, distributed energy generation, lighting, HVAC, building envelope renovation or retrofitting of commercial property to reduce energy consumption, microgrids, clean transportation infrastructure including electric vehicle charging stations, water efficiency improvements, and resiliency measures.

Commercial and Industrial Building Owner or organization
Established, credit-worthy organization
Must have access to conventional financing
Government organizations, universities and community colleges are not eligible
Borrower must demonstrate that credit was not available elsewhere
Energy Audit or Feasibility Study required
Borrower agrees to use best efforts to utilize Certified Local, Small and Minority Business Enterprise (LSMBE) participation goals and requirements
Specific goals for the hiring of County residents with annual reporting requirements
Goal to spend 35% with diverse suppliers/contractors/vendors
Must work with participating lenders

FSC First provides loan guarantees to participating lenders. An energy audit or feasibility study is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Housing Investment Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding vehicle that provides gap financing to support the development of new construction, rehabilitation, and preservation of existing workforce and affordable housing for households earning up to 120% of the area median income (AMI). The program serves as a mechanism to assist both non-profit and for-profit developers in creating affordable housing opportunities while maintaining minimum affordability periods as required by the County. The program also addresses foreclosure-related challenges and provides flexible financing for acquisition, rehabilitation, and new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided in the form of subordinate loan financing up to $2,500,000 with 2% simple interest during permanent loan period and 0% during construction, with 40-year amortization from beginning of permanent loan period. Repayment is based on 75% of surplus cash flow after senior debt and operating expenses, and loans are prepayable without penalty. Grants are available at the Director's discretion for predevelopment costs. Projects must maintain a minimum affordability period as required by the County. Projects may be assisted with both HOME and HITF funds, but HOME and HITF funds cannot be used for the same unit. Priority funding is available for properties within one mile of Blue Line transit Corridor, Purple Line transit Corridor, and existing and planned MDOT Metro Stations throughout the County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and sponsors of affordable multifamily rental housing projects with demonstrated experience in affordable housing development, multi-family developers, houses of worship and faith-based organizations, non-profit housing organizations, community development corporations, and households of limited income earning up to 120% of area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of multifamily rental properties, new construction of multifamily rental housing, rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing, preservation of existing workforce and affordable housing, critical home repairs, roof and window replacements, major system repairs, accessibility improvements, and community facility development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland, with priority funding for properties within one mile of Blue Line transit Corridor, Purple Line transit Corridor, and existing and planned MDOT Metro Stations throughout the County.
requirements_list: Target households earning up to 120% of area median income (AMI)
Projects must maintain minimum or greater affordability period as determined by activity type
Income limits per HUD standards
Rent limits as established by Maryland DHCD
Developer/Sponsor entities must have business registrations in good standing
Development team members may not be suspended, debarred, or ineligible
Borrower and managing entities must be in good standing at time of closing
Demonstrated experience in affordable housing development over past five years
Property managers must be approved by DHCD
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The County accepts applications throughout the fiscal year on a project-by-project basis. DHCD applies underwriting guidelines and procedures for the HOME program to HITF, with exceptions or modifications at the discretion of the DHCD Director. A $50,000 legal fee is due at closing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Rain Check Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program established by Prince George's County offering financial assistance to property owners, homeowners, businesses, government entities, landscape professionals, contractors, and other eligible applicants to install approved green infrastructure and stormwater management practices (Best Management Practices) that improve stormwater runoff quality, reduce runoff quantity, address local flooding, and reduce stormwater pollution in rivers and streams while building community-wide climate resilience and reducing Clean Water Act Fees. Eligible practices include rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, conservation landscaping, permeable pavement, pavement removal, green roofs, and urban tree canopy. The program reimburses the purchase price of trees up to $150 per tree on residential or commercial properties. Rebate amounts vary by practice type: rain barrels and cisterns at $2 per gallon stored (minimum 50-250 gallons depending on applicant type); permeable pavement at $12 per square foot; pavement removal at $6 per square foot; green roofs at $10 per square foot for extensive systems and $20 per square foot for intensive systems with 6+ inches of planting material; rain gardens at $10 per square foot (minimum 100 square feet). Residential property owners can receive up to $6,000 in lifetime rebates per property, while commercial entities, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, nonprofit, and not-for-profit organizations can receive up to $20,000 in lifetime rebates per property. The program also includes contractor training on Rain Check Rebate practices, site assessment, construction techniques, and application process. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Projects must be implemented on property located in Prince George's County and must comply with Department of Environment best practice guidelines and criteria. Property owners can receive up to a 100% reduction in the impact fee for improving stormwater quality from their property. The program also provides CWAF (Chesapeake Watershed Assistance Fund) reduction requests for existing Best Management Practices on non-residential properties including industrial, commercial, and institutional properties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for the installation of approved green infrastructure and stormwater management practices including rain barrels (minimum 50-100 gallons, $2 per gallon stored), cisterns (minimum 250-1,000 gallons depending on applicant type, $2 per gallon stored), rain gardens ($10 per square foot with minimum 100 square feet), conservation landscaping, permeable pavement ($12 per square foot, minimum 400 sq ft for commercial), pavement removal ($6 per square foot, minimum 400 sq ft for commercial), green roofs ($10 per square foot for extensive systems or less than 6 inches of planting media; $20 per square foot for intensive systems with 6+ inches of planting media), and urban tree canopy to improve stormwater quality, reduce runoff quantity, and reduce stormwater pollution in rivers and streams on residential, commercial, and public properties. County also reimburses the purchase price of trees up to $150 per tree on residential or commercial properties. Property owners can receive up to a 100% reduction in the impact fee for improving stormwater quality, with the fee reduction credit applying to the Impervious Area Fee and not the Administrative Fee. Residential property owners can receive up to $6,000 in lifetime rebates per property. Commercial entities, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, nonprofit, and not-for-profit organizations can receive up to $20,000 in lifetime rebates per property. Landscape professionals and contractors can receive rebates for implementing stormwater management practices after completing the Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The County provides a limited amount of rebate funds each year to property owners. To be eligible for a rebate: the project must be implemented on property located in Prince George's County; the application for the project must have been approved within 12 months of the completion date; the Department of Environment or Chesapeake Bay Trust must inspect the completed project and find it in compliance with the original approved application; and the project must follow Department of Environment best practice guidelines and criteria for that type of project. The program also provides CWAF (Chesapeake Watershed Assistance Fund) reduction requests for existing Best Management Practices on non-residential properties including industrial, commercial, and institutional properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, homeowners, residential property owners, businesses, government entities, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwelling owners, nonprofit organizations, not-for-profit organizations, landscape professionals, and contractors in Prince George's County seeking to install green infrastructure and stormwater management practices for stormwater management, flood mitigation, climate resilience, and Clean Water Act Fee reduction, or to purchase and plant trees. Also serves non-residential property owners in industrial, commercial, and institutional sectors seeking CWAF reductions for existing Best Management Practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved green infrastructure and stormwater management practices such as rain barrels, cisterns, rain gardens, conservation landscaping, permeable pavement, pavement removal, green roofs, and urban tree canopy to improve stormwater quality, reduce runoff quantity, and reduce stormwater pollution. Funding can also be used for purchase and planting of trees on residential or commercial properties. All funding can be used to retrofit properties with Best Management Practices that reduce stormwater runoff quantity or improve stormwater runoff quality. Landscape professionals and contractors can use rebates to implement approved stormwater management practices after completing contractor training. Funding also available for CWAF (Chesapeake Watershed Assistance Fund) reductions on existing Best Management Practices for non-residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to property owners in Prince George's County, Maryland, outside of municipalities that have similar stormwater management rebate programs. Specific focus areas include the Tantallon area of Fort Washington through the Community Stormwater Management Blitz pilot project. Properties within the City of Bowie are not eligible (City of Bowie manages its own stormwater program). Properties within the Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park have limited eligibility, and are not eligible for urban tree canopy projects. Non-residential properties (industrial, commercial, institutional) throughout Prince George's County are eligible for CWAF reduction requests for existing Best Management Practices. For permeable pavement and cisterns: suitable for pedestrian-only areas and low-volume, low-speed vehicle areas (overflow parking, residential driveways, alleyways, parking stalls). Permeable pavement areas should have slope less than 5% and away from building foundations. Green roofs suitable for roofs in mostly sunny areas with gradual slope (less than 20% ideal); steeper slopes possible with additional structural elements. Cisterns require level ground or concrete platform for installation.

Property must be located in Prince George's County

Department of Environment or Chesapeake Bay Trust must inspect the completed project
Project must be found in compliance with original approved application
Project must follow Department of Environment best practice guidelines and criteria for that type of project
Properties within City of Bowie are not eligible
For urban tree canopy projects: properties within Town of Cheverly, Town of University Park, and City of College Park are not eligible
Must install eligible stormwater management practices
Must install eligible stormwater management practices on private property
Property owner must demonstrate that Best Management Practices reduce stormwater runoff quantity or improve stormwater runoff quality
All Best Management Practices must be functioning correctly and maintained in good condition
Best Management Practices must pass a Department of the Environment inspection
Access to the Best Management Practices must be granted to the Department of the Environment or Chesapeake Bay Trust for inspection
Credits are valid for three years and must be reapplied for to renew
If property is part of a homeowners association, applicant must provide HOA approval documentation
Applicants not eligible if project involves permit requirements for new building construction, additions, or renovations

Project must meet minimum size or capacity requirements depending on type
Landscape professionals and contractors must complete Prince George's County Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course
Landscape professionals and contractors must provide proof of appropriate licenses (professional registration and Maryland Home Improvement Contractor certification if applicable)
For non-residential properties (industrial, commercial, institutional): must have existing Best Management Practices or be requesting CWAF reduction

For rain barrels: minimum 50 gallons storage capacity for residential; minimum 100 gallons for commercial/organizational; property must have downspouts discharging onto paved surfaces or steep slopes; suitable for properties with lawn, gardens, or landscaping requiring frequent watering

For cisterns: minimum 250 gallons storage capacity for residential (100 gallons minimum threshold noted in some documents); minimum 1,000 gallons for commercial/organizational; suitable roof surfaces and downspout configuration required; level ground or concrete platform for installation required; placement at least 10 feet from existing trees required; must be sealed with smooth interior surfaces, airtight cover, and connected downspouts; distance requirements: 10 feet from pipes/sealed drains; 50 feet from sewer lines/septic systems; drainage must flow away from cistern and building foundations; located uphill from wastewater facilities

For permeable pavement: minimum 400 square feet for commercial/nonprofit applications; no minimum for residential; installation must be completed by a qualified, licensed, bonded contractor; suitable soil infiltration capacity required (sand and loam preferred; clay soils need underdrain); slope must be less than 5%; cannot be areas that accumulate sediment and debris; suitable for pedestrian-only areas and low-volume, low-speed vehicle areas; should not be used in areas with excessive loads, high-speed traffic, or high pollutant loads; annual maintenance required

For pavement removal: minimum 400 square feet for commercial/nonprofit; no minimum for residential; permit required if project disturbs soils or falls within right-of-way; must identify and avoid underground utilities

For rain gardens: minimum 100 square feet; located at least 10 feet away and downhill from building foundations; located at least 25 feet from septic fields or well heads; full or partial sun exposure; water must drain in 24-36 hours; bedrock and groundwater at least 2 feet below surface; gently sloped location receiving regular runoff; no permit required for most rain gardens; permit required if installation results in more than 5,000 square feet and/or 100 cubic yards of earth movement; regular maintenance including weeding, plant replacement, mulch application (2-3 inches depth maintained); water infiltration should occur within 4 hours of rainfall; use of native plants recommended; maintain 2-3 inches of double-shredded hardwood mulch; annual plant care including trimming, pruning, weeding; monitor ponding/drainage; remove trash and debris; remove pet waste

For green roofs: minimum 1/4 (one-quarter) of roof area required; must replace existing roof area (not expand original footprint); structural load analysis report from licensed structural engineer required; installation must be performed by certified green roof contractor; DIY/self-installation not eligible; roof structure must be capable of supporting green roof weight; roof slope less than 20% ideal

For urban tree canopy: trees must be native species; planting window October 1 to May 1; trees must be at least 5 feet tall at planting; trees must be at least 1/2 inch caliper; trees must be planted in biodegradable 5-gallon container or larger; trees must be planted on private property only; no ash species (Fraxinus) due to emerald ash borer; trees must be planted at least 3 feet from underground utilities, fences, walkways, driveways, decks, patios; trees must be at least 7 feet from small trees/shrubs; trees must be at least 10 feet from overhead utilities and large tree trunks; trees must be at least 15 feet from structures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For property owners: Applicants must apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website or directly to the Stormwater Management Division. CBT pre-approves all applications prior to implementation except for rain barrel projects. Property owner must submit application for stormwater management, green infrastructure project, or tree purchase. Department of Environment or Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and approves the application. Property owner implements the approved project or purchases trees. Department of Environment or Chesapeake Bay Trust inspects the completed project. If in compliance with the original approved application and best practice guidelines, rebate is issued. Applicants submit invoices and receipts for review and approval. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. For landscape professionals and contractors: Contractors attend Rain Check Rebate Contractor Training Course announced through Department of Environment Listserve. After completing training, contractors apply to program and select eligible practices for installation. Training is offered periodically. Property owners interested in the Rain Check Rebate Program should contact the Stormwater Management Division at PGC311 or 301-883-5927 for more information. Detailed reduction request forms are available for different property types, including CWAF Reduction Request Forms for Non-Residential Properties (Industrial, Commercial, Institutional).

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Small Business Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding and technical assistance to small businesses operating in Prince George's County, specifically along the Blue and Purple Line corridors. The program awards grants of up to $20,000 per business to support business operations and growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of $20,000 each to eligible small businesses. The program provides 25 grants totaling $500,000. Funds can be used for payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, technology, relocation services, and capital improvements. Technical assistance is also provided.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, technology, relocation services, and capital improvements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Solar Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive residential energy efficiency and solar grant program administered by Prince George's County that assists homeowners and property owners with implementing solar energy and energy-efficiency measures. Also known as Solarize Prince George's, the program connects residents with vetted solar installers and grant opportunities to make solar installation more affordable and accessible. Conducted as a research pilot to determine if updated eligibility requirements improve solar installation quality, consumer protections, application submissions, and satisfaction. The program provides energy efficiency grants up to $6,250 (no longer funding electric incentives; up to $2,500 for natural gas incentives, with up to 60% for air sealing and insulation) and solar grants up to $10,000 for homeowner-owned residential solar photovoltaic systems with a minimum system size of 2.0 kW or up to $2,000 for third-party owned systems. For homeowner-owned systems, grant awards up to $10,000 cover eligible costs of installing solar PV systems, with up to $2,000 for solar power outlet installation and up to $7,500 for solar water heaters. For third-party owned systems, grants up to $2,000 are available for solar PV installation costs and up to $2,000 for solar power outlets. Eligible costs include parts, components, accessory equipment necessary to operate and/or install solar photovoltaic devices, solar water heaters, and energy efficiency upgrades. Maximum 15% of grant can be used for reasonable installation facilitation measures (e.g., tree trimming, safety measures). Low-income homeowners receive discounted energy audits; market-rate residents may pay $100 upfront for audits (discounted from $400), which is reimbursed as part of the grant. Grant awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis upon successful implementation of energy-efficiency measures. The program aims to help residents lower energy costs and reduce greenhouse gas emissions and works in addition to utility and EmPOWER Maryland incentives. Projected bill savings must be at least 10%. The program is being conducted as a research pilot with limited awards available. The program also helps Washington Gas customers in designated Energy Resiliency Communities perform energy efficiency retrofits on their homes to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Energy Efficiency Grants up to $6,250 for residential energy efficiency measures (up to $2,500 for natural gas incentives, with up to 60% ($3,750) for air sealing and insulation); no longer funding electric incentives. Covers $100 home energy assessment cost. Solar grants up to $10,000 for homeowner-owned systems or up to $2,000 for third-party owned systems, with minimum 2.0 kW system size. Up to $7,500 for homeowner-owned solar water heaters. Up to $2,000 for solar power outlet installation. Grants cover solar photovoltaic system installation, solar power outlet installation for grid failure backup, solar water heaters, including all parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and/or install solar photovoltaic devices. Maximum 15% of grant can be used for reasonable installation facilitation measures such as tree trimming and safety measures. Projected bill savings must be at least 10%. All major system components must be new, not rebuilt, refurbished, or relocated. Low-income homeowners receive discounted energy audits; market-rate residents may pay $100 upfront for audits (discounted from $400), which is reimbursed as part of the grant. Grants are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. Direct support connecting residents with state-vetted solar installers and pre-approved energy efficiency contractors. Assistance is provided in addition to utility and EmPOWER Maryland incentives. Grants are awarded upon successful implementation of energy-efficiency measures. Solar grant is paid upon receipt of invoice after prequalification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; August 15, 2025 mentioned as deadline in pilot phase
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County homeowners who own single-family residences, townhouses, or individually metered condominiums (built before March 23, 2016) served by Pepco or Washington Gas utilities in designated Energy Resiliency Communities interested in installing solar energy systems or implementing energy efficiency improvements. Homeowners must have not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of new rooftop solar photovoltaic systems, solar water heaters, solar power outlets for grid failure backup, and energy efficiency upgrades (such as air sealing, duct sealing, insulation, HVAC service/repair, lighting, comprehensive remodeling, and ENERGY STAR certified appliances) at residential properties through cash purchase, loan, or financing. Following successful completion of energy efficiency measures, residents may apply for solar installation grants. Systems must produce projected bill savings of at least 10% and meet minimum energy requirements. Minimum system size 2.0 kW.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to Prince George's County residents in nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities: Bladensburg - East Riverdale, Forestville, Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights, Kentland - Palmer Park, Oxon Hill - Glassmanor, Silver Hill, Suitland - Coral Hills, Langley Park, and Woodlawn - West Lanham. Eligibility verified using ERC Address Locator tool. Systems cannot be removed from Prince George's County for 10 years following installation. Separately, funding is available for households outside ERC zones or inside ERC zones but outside of Pepco's service area.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Verify eligibility as a Prince George's County resident in a single-family residence, townhouse, or individually metered condominium (built before March 23, 2016) within an Energy Resiliency Community with no existing solar, served by Pepco or Washington Gas. Verify location using ERC Address Locator tool. Step 2: For energy efficiency, select from 30+ pre-approved, vetted contractors certified in energy audit. Contractor (Building Performance Institute certified building professional) performs whole-house energy audit including blower door test and diagnostic tests and recommends energy efficiency improvements. For solar, select a solar contractor from the Maryland Solar Access Program's Participating Contractor List (minimum 2 quotes recommended) or choose any solar contractor with NABCEP PVIP certification. Step 3: Obtain financial assistance and select a grant option based on location, utility status, and income qualification. Step 4: Submit prequalification application with invoice, utility bill, contractor qualifications, solar analysis, proposal, and Form W-9. Step 5: Receive grant prequalification. Step 6: Proceed with installation with contractor holding Prince George's County Vendor Registration, MHIC License, and Master Electrician License. Step 7: Submit final documentation including final invoice, utility interconnection agreement, permits, photos, and proof of solar generation for grant disbursement. Solar grant is paid upon receipt of invoice after prequalification. Upon completion of energy efficiency upgrades, residents in ERC-designated communities may apply for a solar energy grant award. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Solar and Geothermal Residential Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit for residential property owners in Prince George's County who install solar energy or geothermal energy devices on residential structures. Application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance. The credit applies to Prince George's County property taxes for solar or geothermal systems.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve communities and water quality while engaging County residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. Provides incentives to property owners to invest in stormwater management. The program supports water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia River. Grant program funded through stormwater fees that provides funding for stormwater management and water quality improvement projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants are provided to support on-the-ground restoration and program activities for water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction. Funded through stormwater fees collected from property owners. Match funding (cash or in-kind) is not required but is preferred and considered during the review process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents, property owners, tax-exempt or 501(c) nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners and businesses in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, and trash reduction in the Anacostia watershed. Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County.

Evaluation criteria include likelihood of project success and cost-effectiveness

All applications are evaluated by funding partners and an external Technical Review Committee. Applicants can receive feedback from reviewers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Youth CareerConnect Program (YCC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year STEM education program for high school students in Prince George's County that combines career academy training in health, bio-science, and information technology with internships, mentoring, scholarships, and paid summer internship opportunities to prepare students for immediate entry into the workforce or college. The program provides job readiness training, capstone experiences, college entrance exam preparation, college tours, tutoring, and work-based learning experiences. It is a $7 million four-year STEM demonstration grant administered by the U.S. Department of Labor that cultivates home-grown talent in STEM fields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides STEM career academy training, job readiness training, skills training, tutoring, mentoring, paid summer internships and capstone experiences, internship and work experience placement, college entrance exam preparation, college tours, college credits, and scholarships. Participants receive certificates of completion and are eligible for competitive scholarships (such as the $1,500 Tanya L. Washington YCC Scholarship) for college attendance. The program facilitates connections to summer job opportunities and work placements through business partnerships. Funds support internships and work-based learning experiences rather than direct funding to participants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Students will be notified of work assignments by April
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students enrolled in Career Academies in Prince George's County Public Schools, particularly those interested in STEM fields including healthcare, bio-science, and information technology.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program funds support STEM career academy training, internship and work experience placement, mentoring, job readiness training, college entrance exam preparation, college tours, skills development, tutoring, college credits, and scholarships for eligible high school students and seniors pursuing college education. Funds support internships and summer job placements rather than direct funding to participants for their own use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students enrolled in Career Academies at participating Prince George's County high schools including Parkdale High School (Homeland Security and Military Science/Emergency Management Academy), Bladensburg High School, Potomac High School, and Fairmont Heights High School.
requirements_list: Enrollment in a participating Prince George's County Career Academy
Interest in healthcare, bio-science, or information technology fields
Participation in STEM-focused career academy training
High school student in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply through their high school Career Academy. The program provides training, work experience, mentoring, skills development, and preparation throughout participation. Students are notified of work assignments by April for July internship start dates. Competitive scholarships are awarded to eligible seniors.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Project Based Voucher (PBV) Program provides affordable rental housing at specific properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based vouchers, PBV assistance is attached to designated units at approved properties and remains with the unit if a family moves out.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance is provided to help families afford housing at approved properties. The amount of assistance varies based on household income, family size, and the available rental unit. Applicants are randomly selected through a lottery process when the waitlist is open.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waitlist closed as of March 17, 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST. Next opening date not specified.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households seeking affordable rental housing in Prince George's County. Eligibility is based on household income, family size, and the size of the available rental unit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance for housing at designated properties throughout Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at specific properties throughout Prince George's County, Maryland. Current participating properties are located in Fort Washington, Capitol Heights, Upper Marlboro, Lanham, Glenarden, Bladensburg, Riverdale, Hyattsville, District Heights, and Clinton.
requirements_list: Household income within eligibility limits
Family size appropriate for available unit size
Cannot participate in any other federally funded housing subsidy program
Must complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation if selected from lottery
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online when the waitlist is open. Applicants are randomly selected through a lottery process. Applicants are notified of their waitlist status typically within 45 days after the application closes. When selected from the waitlist and a unit becomes available, the household is referred to a specific PBV unit to begin the property's application and screening process. Once approved by the landlord/development, the application is sent to HAPGC for program eligibility review.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Based Voucher Accessibility Waiting List

The subsidy stays with the building; when tenant moves out, rental assistance ends. Most units cost 30% of household adjusted gross income. Available housing types include single-family homes, townhomes, or apartments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accessible rental units for low-income households with disabilities. Rental housing subsidy provided through project-based vouchers. Housing rental assistance with accessibility modifications and accommodations for persons with disabilities, including physical, developmental, intellectual, emotional, or mental health disabilities. Most units cost 30% of household adjusted gross income. Subsidy stays with the building; when tenant moves out, rental assistance ends.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; waiting list remains open
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households with accessibility needs; persons with disabilities; homeless individuals; current and former public housing or Section 8 participants. Current participants of HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher Program, current residents of HAPGC Public Housing Program, current participants of HAPGC Project Based Voucher Program, current participants of HAPGC Moderate Rehabilitation Program, and current applicants on HAPGC Waiting Lists. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance in accessible units with accessibility modifications and accommodations for persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Applicants must currently live or work in Prince George's County. Available through the Housing Authority of Prince George's County office located in Largo.
requirements_list: Must be current participant, resident, or applicant of HAPGC
Only Head of Household or application holder eligible to apply

Family composition information
Social Security numbers

Applications can be obtained at HAPGC's office at 9200 Basil Ct., Suite 107, Largo, MD 20744 or downloaded online. Submit completed application to The Housing Authority of Prince George's County, 9200 Basil Court, Rm 500, Largo, MD 20774.
