structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that encourages property improvement and community revitalization by providing relief from county property taxes on the incremental value created by qualifying real property improvements in Revitalization Tax Credit Districts established by Prince George's County Council. The program applies to non-residential structures, residential structures, and new single-family residential construction on previously razed or vacant lots. Non-residential properties receive declining tax credits over five years (100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%), while residential properties receive credits over three years (100%, 66%, 33%), with a maximum of $200,000 in eligible residential improvements per dwelling unit. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, or extension of structures, and new single-family residential structures on previously razed, demolished, or vacant lots, as well as new construction in developments of fewer than 10 single-family dwellings.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit for construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of residential structures; and new single-family residential structures on previously razed, demolished, or vacant lots in designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts. Non-residential properties receive a 100% tax credit on increased assessed value in year 1, declining to 80% in year 2, 60% in year 3, 40% in year 4, and 20% in year 5. Residential properties receive a 100% tax credit in year 1, declining to 66% in year 2 and 33% in year 3. Maximum eligible residential improvements are $200,000 per dwelling unit. The credit applies to the incremental county property tax imposed on the increased assessment resulting from qualified improvements. New construction in developments of fewer than 10 single-family dwellings also qualifies. All improvements must require a County building permit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the tax year property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners making improvements to non-residential or residential real property in Prince George's County within designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts. Residential developments of ten or more single-family dwellings or multifamily units require County Council approval.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified real property improvements including non-residential and residential improvements requiring a County building permit in Revitalization Tax Credit Districts. For residential properties, the maximum eligible improvement value is $200,000 per dwelling unit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland within designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts
requirements_list: Property must be located within a Revitalization Tax Credit District established by the Prince George's County Council
Improvements must require a County building permit
Improvements must qualify as real property improvements

Eligible improvements include construction or reconstruction of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of residential structures; new single-family residential structures on previously razed, demolished, or vacant lots; or new construction in developments of fewer than 10 single-family dwellings
County Council approval required for residential developments of 10 or more single-family dwellings
County Council approval required for multifamily units
Maximum $200,000 in eligible residential improvements per dwelling unit
Improvements must be assessed and completed before the credit schedule begins

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County applies a school facilities surcharge to new residential developments or redevelopments to cover anticipated increases in public educational services. This program provides reductions or exemptions from that surcharge. Multifamily properties within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ) receive a 50% reduction in surcharge fees. Studio apartments and efficiency apartments in eligible areas receive a full exemption from the school facilities surcharge. For developments outside the Capital Beltway, the surcharge is reduced from $15,489 per unit to $7,745 per unit. For developments inside the Capital Beltway or near WMATA rail stations, the surcharge is reduced from $9,035 per unit to $4,518 per unit (as of FY 2015).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multifamily properties within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ) receive a 50% reduction in school facilities surcharge fees. For developments outside the Capital Beltway, the surcharge is reduced from $15,489 per unit to $7,745 per unit. For developments inside the Capital Beltway or near WMATA rail stations, the surcharge is reduced from $9,035 per unit to $4,518 per unit (as of FY 2015). Studio apartments and efficiency apartments in areas within ¼ mile of a metro, in an approved TDOZ, or in other limited circumstances receive a full exemption from the school facilities surcharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of new residential developments and redevelopments in Prince George's County, particularly those developing multifamily housing near transit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The reduction or exemption reduces the school facilities surcharge that developers must pay on new residential units.

structured_extraction.program_description: A licensing program established by Prince George's County through CB-11-2018 that allows property owners to legally rent their homes as short-term rentals. structured_extraction.program_description: A six-month intensive loan readiness program designed to help women-owned businesses, particularly minority women entrepreneurs, obtain access to capital and accelerate business growth. Sponsored by Wells Fargo, the program provides workshops on business planning, marketing, business process, legal business formation, and financial training. Participants receive one-on-one counseling with business and banking counselors, peer-to-peer learning opportunities, financial literacy mentoring, and business operations coaching to prepare business owners for loan applications and growth. The program includes guest speakers, lender pre-review, and pre-qualification of loan applications. Program outcomes include identifying loan package deficiencies, preparing completed loan applications, obtaining pre-qualification from lenders, and making connections with capital providers to position businesses for long-term growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Six-month intensive program featuring monthly group training sessions with industry experts on financing processes, workshops, financial literacy mentoring, business operations coaching, and one-on-one counseling with business and banking counselors. Sponsored by Wells Fargo and includes guest speakers, lender pre-review, and pre-qualification of loan applications. Participants receive workshops covering business planning, marketing, business process, legal business formation, and financial training. The program helps participants strengthen loan packages, complete loan applications, obtain pre-qualification from lenders, and make connections with capital providers. Limited to ten participants per cohort. The program equips women-owned business entrepreneurs with tools and training to build loan readiness and position their business for long-term growth.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training, financial education, business operations, financial management, loan package preparation, peer-to-peer learning, and connections with capital providers to help businesses access capital and accelerate growth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to businesses located in Prince George's County, Maryland

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses apply competitively to join the annual cohort of up to ten women-owned businesses. Participants receive individual mentoring and coaching throughout the program. Future application cycles will be offered with details to be announced.

structured_extraction.program_description: An award-winning program that provides job readiness training, career workshops, and entry-level summer employment opportunities to youth and young adults ages 14 to 24 in Prince George's County. The program connects young people with summer employment by partnering with host employers and sponsors. Participants gain constructive summer work experiences in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies, with opportunities to learn job skills, gain professional development, career exposure, networking, and positive working relationships. Organizations can hire youth directly or serve as designated worksites, providing meaningful work experience while supporting youth development and community engagement. County-funded worksites may receive support for hiring youth, and Sponsorship Partners can provide financial contributions to support transportation subsidies, technology access, and work opportunities for additional youth.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides job readiness training, career workshops, and entry-level summer employment opportunities. Participants gain paid summer work experience in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies. Hourly wages vary by age (ages 16-17: $13/hour; ages 18-24: $15/hour), and participants ages 14-15 receive $300 stipend, ages 16-17 receive $400 stipend, and ages 18-24 receive $500 stipend upon completion. Organizations serve as host employers or worksites for paid summer employment positions for youth. County-funded worksites may receive support for hiring youth and providing work experience. Sponsorship Partners can provide financial contributions to support transportation subsidies, technology access, and work opportunities for additional youth. Capstone Sponsorships and Student Sponsorships are available to fund curriculum, workforce training, transportation, and individual youth employment.

Sponsorship partners' contributions help facilitate youth employment and address barriers to participation.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Youth applicants should apply through the Prince George's County Summer Youth Enrichment Program website between March 1-31, 2025. Up to $5,000 per year for civic, neighborhood, community organizations, homeowner associations, and libraries. Up to $10,000 per year for municipalities. Maximum $150 per plant including soil amendment and accessories. Match can be cash, volunteer hours at $25/hour, or in-kind contributions.

One-year guarantee on all trees and shrubs required
Landowner signature required

Receipts and proof of payment required for fund disbursement

structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive community-based program seeking qualified partners to design and deliver services that reduce student truancy and chronic absenteeism while reducing juvenile delinquency. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $730,000 in total funding distributed across three categories: Wraparound Services ($500,000), Targeted Workshops ($190,000), and Transportation & Outreach ($40,000), with an additional $963,000 grant component available to launch expanded program services. The program funds multiple partners based on need, capacity, and alignment with program goals to provide youth services, parental engagement, and family-centered supports.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sonja Welborne-Rice, Director of Community Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations, nonprofit organizations, coalitions, and qualified service providers with relevant experience serving Prince George's County youth ages 12-18 and families seeking to reduce juvenile delinquency and provide comprehensive youth services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic mentoring and peer support, family engagement and outreach, behavioral enrichment for students and parents, wraparound services including workforce development and mental health support, culturally responsive interventions, technology solutions for attendance tracking and data analytics, re-engagement strategies for at-risk youth, youth services, and holistic family-centered supports.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization, community-based organization, coalition, or qualified service provider
Must have proven track record working with at-risk youth and families
Must employ evidence-based and culturally responsive practices
Must have capacity to collect and report data on outcomes
Must demonstrate ability to collaborate with schools and community partners
Must deliver holistic, proactive approaches that measurably improve attendance
Organizations must have relevant experience serving Prince George's County youth ages 12-18
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a single PDF Expression of Interest (EOI) with supporting materials as separate files. Email submission to communitysao@co.pg.md.us with subject line 'SAO-PGC Truancy and Absenteeism Reduction Program – EOI Submission' by the deadline. The program office will review submissions and select partners, with notifications to follow.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program that provides nutrition assistance, supplemental foods, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding promotion and support to eligible pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age who meet income guidelines and are at nutritional risk. The program provides selected nutritious foods including milk, cheese, eggs, cereal, infant formula, fruits and vegetables through an electronic benefit transfer system called eWIC, along with nutrition education, counseling, and referrals to healthcare providers and community-based organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides selected nutritious foods including milk, cheese, eggs, cereal, infant formula, fruits and vegetables to eligible pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum women and children up to age five who meet income guidelines (185% of federal poverty level) and are at nutritional risk. Benefits are provided through an electronic benefit transfer system called eWIC. Automatic income eligibility applies to foster children or those receiving medical assistance, temporary cash assistance (TCA), or SNAP benefits. The program also provides nutrition education and counseling, breastfeeding education and support, and referrals to healthcare providers and community-based organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant women, postpartum women, breastfeeding women, infants, and children up to age 5 who reside in Prince George's County, meet income eligibility requirements, and are determined to be at nutritional risk.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplemental nutritious foods and nutrition counseling, breastfeeding support, and referrals to healthcare and community-based organizations for eligible pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under age five at nutritional risk.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County only. Applicants must reside in Prince George's County and be served through the county WIC program.
requirements_list: Must be pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding woman, infant, or child up to age 5
Must reside in Prince George's County
Must meet household income eligibility requirements based on family size (185% of federal poverty level)
Must be at nutritional risk as determined by a health professional or trained WIC staff
Automatic income eligibility for foster children, those receiving medical assistance, temporary cash assistance (TCA), or SNAP benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the WIC program office for certification. During business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.), WIC staff will determine individual eligibility including income verification, residency confirmation, and nutritional risk assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Real property tax credit for manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, and research and development facilities in high-technology industry clusters that locate or expand in Prince George's County and meet specified qualifications. The program provides a five-year tax credit on the increased value of the property, starting at 100% in year one and decreasing by 20% each subsequent year (80% year two, 60% year three, 40% year four, 20% year five).
structured_extraction.agency: Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit for high-technology businesses that construct or expand facilities in the county. Businesses receive a five-year tax credit on the increased value of the property: 100% in year one, 80% in year two, 60% in year three, 40% in year four, and 20% in year five. Businesses must invest at least $500,000 and create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the tax year property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses in high-technology industry clusters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit on real property used for high-technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development. The tax credit applies to investments in newly constructed or significantly improved facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Business must be primarily involved in high-technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development
Must construct, expand, or cause to be constructed or expanded a building of at least 5,000 square feet of gross floor area
Must invest at least $500,000 in construction or expansion
Must create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions in the new or expanded building within three years

Eligible industries include biotechnology and biomedical, information technology and services, high tech machinery and instruments, defense and aerospace energy and chemicals, and high technology research
The property must be newly constructed or substantially improved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Business entity or building owner completes an application with the Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation. Application must include legal description of property, business description, floor plans, documentation of minimum investment, valid use and occupancy permit, and other information required by the Director of Finance. The Economic Development Corporation reviews the application and markets the program. The County's Finance Department must approve the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: CatalystQ: The Catalyst for Minority Business Excellence in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.program_description: A minority business training accelerator program providing targeted support, training, and micro-grants to minority entrepreneurs and small business owners in Queen Anne's County. The program builds and strengthens the ecosystem for minority entrepreneurs by addressing key barriers including access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and professional networking. It is an expansion of a pilot program launched in 2023. The program provides technical assistance in accounting, legal, marketing, business planning, HR, IT, website development, grant writing, supply chain, and e-commerce, along with entrepreneurship and business start-up training, mentorship programming, networking opportunities, business registration and licensing assistance, access to co-working space, and mini-grants for professional services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance in accounting, legal, marketing, business planning, HR, IT, website development, grant writing, supply chain, and e-commerce. Participants receive entrepreneurship and business start-up training, mentorship programming, networking opportunities, business registration and licensing assistance, and access to co-working space. Selected businesses receive mini-grants for professional services and participant professional development (accounting, legal, certificates, etc.). The program is delivered largely in-person through workshops on critical business topics and networking events.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority entrepreneurs, minority-owned businesses, underrepresented entrepreneurs, and early-stage entrepreneurs operating in Queen Anne's County. Expecting 5-10 participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance delivery, entrepreneur support services, mini-grants to participants for professional services and professional development (accounting, legal, certificates, and similar professional assistance), and program administration and reporting. Up to $100,000 total funding for program implementation through December 2025.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be minority entrepreneur or minority-owned business
Must operate in Queen Anne's County
Must be interested in growing the venture and participating in a network of minority entrepreneurs
Underrepresented and early-stage entrepreneurs emphasized
Program should encompass combination of technical assistance and entrepreneur support services
Largely in-person participation required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application providing information about their business. Selected applicants are notified and the program begins with technical assistance, training, mentorship, networking opportunities, and mini-grants for professional services. Qualified entities may submit proposals via mail with one original and one digital version (PDF) to Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development, 425 Piney Narrows Road, Chester, MD 21619.

The credit equals 100% of the county property tax.

structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received by June 15th to be applied to the upcoming tax year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled emergency workers (law enforcement, fire, rescue, emergency medical service personnel) permanently disabled in the line of duty, and surviving spouses of fallen emergency workers in Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit on principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County only.
requirements_list: For disabled emergency worker: must be permanently and totally disabled in the line of duty as a law enforcement officer, fire fighter, rescue worker, or emergency medical service personnel
For fallen emergency worker: must be the surviving spouse of an emergency worker who died in the line of duty
Property must be principal dwelling owned by applicant
Must provide certification of service from the chief or HR representative of the jurisdiction that employed the emergency worker
For disabled worker: must provide retirement statement, notice of retirement allowance, or letter from state retirement agency certifying permanent and total disability

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Tax Credit - Commercial Real Property Tax Credit (Queen Anne's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A geographically designated area (Enterprise Zone) in Queen Anne's County wherein investments in commercial development, redevelopment, and job creation are eligible to receive tax credits. A ten-year credit against local property taxes is available to companies that locate, expand, or substantially improve business properties within the Enterprise Zone. The property tax credit is equal to 80% of the difference between the base value of the property and the newly assessed value after investment. The credit is 80% for five years, then declines 10% annually (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%) over the following five years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A ten-year credit against local property taxes. The property tax credit is equal to 80% of the difference between the base value of the property (the assessment in the year prior to new construction, expansion, or substantial improvement) and the newly assessed value of the property after the investment is made. The property tax credit is 80% for five years. During the last five years, the property tax credit declines 10% annually: 70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, and 30% respectively. This tax credit is administered to the property owner in their property taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial businesses locating, expanding, or substantially improving property within the Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investment in commercial property and development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Majority of Planned Growth Areas of Grasonville, Chester, and Stevensville, including the Chesapeake Bay Business Park, Matapeake Professional Park, and the Thompson Creek area. Queen Anne's County Enterprise Zone.

Only commercial properties may apply. In mixed-use development, only the portion assessed as commercial receives the credit

Local Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31 of the preceding calendar year

structured_extraction.program_name: Enterprise Zone Tax Credit - Income Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Eligible businesses operating within the Enterprise Zone can receive income tax credits for the creation of full-time jobs. Two types of credits are available depending on whether the employee is economically disadvantaged.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: If the employee is not economically disadvantaged, the business may qualify for a one-time credit of $1,000 per employee. If the employee is economically disadvantaged (as determined by the Maryland Jobs Service), the business may take a credit up to $3,000 of the employee's wages in the first year of employment, $2,000 in the second year, and $1,000 in the third year. This credit can be stacked with other job creation-based credits including the Job Creation Tax Credit (JCTC) and More Jobs for Marylanders (MJM).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in the Enterprise Zone creating new full-time jobs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job creation and employee hiring

requirements_list: No minimum number of employees required
Employee must have been hired after the date the Enterprise Zone was designated or the date the business relocated in the Enterprise Zone, whichever is later
Must be filling a new position or replacing an employee who was previously certified as economically disadvantaged
Employee must have been employed at least 35 hours a week for at least six months
Employee must be paid at least 150% of the federal minimum wage throughout employment
Employee must have spent at least half of working hours in the Enterprise Zone or on activities directly resulting from the business location in the zone
Must be a new employee or an employee rehired after being laid off by the business for more than one year

DLLR must certify that the employee is economically disadvantaged.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest financing to help Baltimore City property owners, nonprofit organizations, and for-profit businesses implement energy-saving building improvements that improve comfort, lower utility bills, and reduce energy waste. Funding comes from the City of Baltimore using Customer Investment Funds from the Maryland Public Service Commission (utility merger of Baltimore Gas & Electric Company and Exelon). The program finances energy upgrades such as building envelope improvements, lighting efficiency, HVAC systems and controls, replacing old boilers and water heaters, converting to efficient kitchen appliances, ENERGY STAR equipment, and solar PV. Loans range from under $150,000 to $2,000,000 with financing up to 90% of eligible project costs. Interest rates are 3.0% fixed for small loans (under $150,000) and 4.0% fixed for large loans ($150,000 and above), with loan terms up to 15 years. Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. provides loans under $150,000, while The Reinvestment Fund finances projects of $150,000 and above. The program is managed by the Baltimore City Energy Office.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans between under $150,000 and $2,000,000 with financing up to 90% of eligible energy project costs. Interest rates are 3.0% fixed for small loans (under $150,000) and 4.0% fixed for large loans ($150,000 and above). Application fee: $250 (small loans) / $100 (large loans). Origination fee: 2% (small loans) / 1% (large loans). Loan servicing fee: 0.37% (small loans) / none (large loans). Loans typically have up to 15 year terms. Collateral required: First or second position mortgage lien. Nonprofits may use up to 20% of loan amount (capped at $50,000) for non-energy improvements tied to enabling energy upgrades. Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. provides loans under $150,000, while The Reinvestment Fund finances projects of $150,000 and above.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore property owners, nonprofit organizations serving low-income families (at least 50% of services to families with incomes at or below 80% of area median income), for-profit small businesses (meeting SBA definition: tangible net worth less than $15 million and average net income less than $5 million after taxes for preceding two years), and real estate project developers located in Baltimore City in eligible geographies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving building improvements including building envelope improvements, HVAC and controls, lighting and controls, domestic hot water systems, ENERGY STAR equipment, solar PV, efficient kitchen appliances, boiler and hot water heater replacement, plumbing improvements, and plug load reductions in retrofits of existing buildings, gut rehab projects, and new construction. Nonprofits may use up to 20% of loan amount (capped at $50,000) for non-energy improvements tied to enabling energy upgrades. Soft costs and pre-development costs also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Baltimore City and in an eligible area, specifically in New Markets Tax Credit-eligible census tracts or Baltimore Main Streets Districts. The BEI Mapping Tool is available to confirm whether a building's location qualifies.

Technical assistance is provided through a curriculum administered by Reinvestment Fund and a council of HBCU leaders, advocates, and financial experts.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Early Care and Education (ECE) Facility Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A flexible lending and technical assistance initiative helping early childhood education providers make safe, accessible, and quality improvements to their spaces. Helps create safer, healthier, and more welcoming environments for children, families, and staff. The program supports both home-based and center-based child care providers in Montgomery County through loans focused on equity to ensure children across the county, especially those in underserved and low-income communities, have access to safe, high-quality early learning environments. The program offers three types of loans: forgivable loans for homes and centers with up to $74,000 maximum at 0% interest with no repayment required if borrower meets certain requirements over time, 0% interest loans for centers only with up to $300,000 maximum (with maximums of $200,000 for quality improvement and $300,000 for expansion) that must be repaid but with no interest charges, and pre-development loans ($1,000-$10,000 for homes; $5,000-$50,000 for centers) that are fully forgiven after one year if requirements are met. Funds can be used for facility expansion to create more child care spots, renovating or upgrading existing child care spaces, planning and predevelopment costs such as architect fees and permits, and purchasing equipment, furniture, fixtures, and learning materials. Technical assistance and business training also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of loans: (1) Forgivable Loans for homes and centers with up to $74,000 maximum, offering 0% interest and no repayment required if borrower meets certain requirements over five years (20% forgiven annually); (2) 0% Interest Loans for centers only with maximum of $200,000 for center quality improvement or $300,000 for center expansion that must be repaid but with no interest charges and flexible repayment schedule; (3) Pre-Development Loans ($1,000-$10,000 for homes; $5,000-$50,000 for centers) fully forgiven after one year if requirements are met, for planning costs. All loans require solid business plan and demonstrated repayment capacity for non-forgivable portions. Loans can be used for facility expansion to create more child care spots, renovating or upgrading existing child care spaces, planning and predevelopment costs such as architect fees, permits, zoning contracts, and construction costs, purchasing equipment, furniture, fixtures, and learning materials, and contractor insurance and licensing fees. Technical assistance and business training also provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program designed to expand economic opportunity for underserved people and communities that incentivizes private investment in low-income communities by allowing investors to receive tax credits on investments made through specialized investment vehicles called Community Development Entities (CDEs). The program prioritizes projects that fit organizational mission and advance racial equity, community inclusion, and climate consciousness. The program funds community and economic development projects in distressed communities by leveraging private-sector equity and loan capital investment to stimulate economic growth and create jobs. Credits are claimed over a seven-year period and can help finance real estate development, businesses, community facilities, healthcare, education, food access projects, and other qualified investments in economically disadvantaged areas. Investors reduce their federal income tax liability based on qualified equity investments deployed in designated opportunity zones and low-income communities.
eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors and Community Development Entities receive federal tax credits on equity investments made through CDEs into qualified business ventures and real estate projects located in low-income communities. The credit is structured as a percentage of the qualified investment amount and credits are claimed ratably over a seven-year holding period. Financing is provided for real estate activities including new construction and building rehabilitation, as well as non-real estate activities including working capital, equipment purchases, inventory, and expense reimbursement. Additionally, Reinvestment Fund provides flexible financing for community and economic development projects in severely distressed census tracts through subordinated debt, below-market interest rates, lower origination fees, longer interest-only periods, higher loan-to-value ratios, longer amortization periods, flexible borrower credit standards, and lower debt service coverage ratio requirements. Reinvestment Fund serves as a bridge lender, leverage lender, direct lender, allocatee, or co-lender.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private investors seeking tax incentives; community development entities; businesses and real estate projects in low-income communities; investors seeking to deploy capital in designated opportunity zones; organizations owned or controlled by people of color; projects advancing racial equity, community inclusion, and climate consciousness; low-income serving projects; community development projects that provide essential services including healthcare, education, and access to healthy food.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate development projects including new construction and building rehabilitation, business expansion and creation, working capital, equipment purchases, inventory, expense reimbursement, community facilities such as health clinics and educational centers, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, food access projects, commercial development, affordable housing, and other qualified investments that support economic development, job creation, and revitalization in low-income designated areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide including Maryland, targeting federally designated opportunity zones, Qualified Census Tracts, and severely distressed census tracts with Low-Income Communities (LICs) serving Low-Income Persons (LIPs). Projects must be located in areas with median family income not exceeding 80% of area median income or poverty rates of at least 20%.

For Reinvestment Fund financing, submit a completed Part One of the Intake Form via email to NMTC@reinvestment.com. Community development entities and lenders handle certification, application, and compliance with Treasury Department requirements.

Partnership between Reinvestment Fund and Philadelphia Foundation that channels capital into neighborhood development projects supporting housing stability, health outcomes, educational attainment, and food access.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Promissory note investment vehicle that channels capital into neighborhood development projects in Greater Philadelphia region. Structure and terms follow the main Promissory Notes program. Focuses on projects promoting housing stability for low-income families, improved health outcomes, higher educational attainment, and greater access to fresh healthy food.

structured_extraction.program_description: Reinvestment Fund's investment vehicle that allows individuals and organizations to invest in a diversified direct loan fund supporting community development projects. Investors earn modest financial returns while supporting socially and environmentally responsible projects that benefit low-income communities. The loan fund has been operating since 1985 and has maintained a 100% repayment rate to investors, making over $3 billion in loans to community businesses. Investors include school teachers, CEOs, faith-based organizations, family foundations, banks, and civic organizations.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Promissory notes starting at $1,000 with fixed interest rates set at time of issuance. Annual interest payments provided with automatic reinvestment at maturity unless investor elects otherwise. Investors receive principal and interest repayment. Since 1985, the program has maintained a 100% repayment rate to investors and has made over $3 billion in loans to community businesses. Investments are unsecured obligations and are not government insured and are not tax-deductible charitable gifts. Highly illiquid investments requiring investors to hold until maturity with no early redemption without mutual written consent.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Two business days after receipt of prospectus notice for withdrawal of acceptance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual and institutional investors seeking to make impact investments in community development projects while earning financial returns. Investor base includes school teachers, CEOs, faith-based organizations, family foundations, banks, and civic organizations. Organizations and businesses working to alleviate poverty and build wealth in low-income communities. Open to investors in 17 jurisdictions: Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, New Jersey, Virginia, Georgia, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois, Iowa, Maine, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Mexico, Rhode Island, South Dakota, and Texas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Socially and environmentally responsible development projects that benefit low-income communities, including housing, health, education, food access initiatives, community facilities, commercial real estate, business development, sustainable energy projects, and direct loans to community businesses. Funds also support technical assistance and general operating programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to investors in 17 jurisdictions: Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, New Jersey, Virginia, Georgia, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois, Iowa, Maine, Massachusetts, Mississippi, New Mexico, Rhode Island, South Dakota, and Texas. Fund operations are nationwide across the country with potential for geographic designation by investor agreement.

Pennsylvania residents have two-business-day withdrawal rights after receiving prospectus notice
Annual financial statements provided to note holders within 120 days of fiscal year-end
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download a promissory note application from the toolkit or contact Reinvestment Fund at 215-574-5819 or investorrelations@reinvestment.com for assistance. Prospectus and note opening documents are available for download. Fund directly solicits known interested parties and may publicly disseminate offering information. Written withdrawal notice can be submitted via facsimile or email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program run by the Rural Maryland Council providing financial assistance to rural-serving nonprofit organizations, small or agricultural businesses, government entities, educational institutions, and rural community colleges that promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, training and technical assistance, and technical support to rural communities. The program aims to increase the overall capacity of these organizations to meet rural development challenges and establish new public/private partnerships for leveraging non-state sources of funding. Eligible uses include combined heat and power systems, agricultural technology transfer programs, educational workshops, heritage preservation, educational competitions, resource directories, document digitization, and assistance with applying to other state programs such as Health Enterprise Zones. Grants range up to $45,000 maximum per award. Priority is given to applicants that have secured matching funds from non-state sources, though matching funds are not required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided through a two-phase application process (Phase I Letter of Intent followed by Phase II full application) to rural-serving nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) IRS tax designation or similar status, community colleges, Career Technology Centers, Regional Councils, and libraries for projects that promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, training and technical assistance, and technical support to rural communities. Projects must serve more than one rural county; regional projects may include non-rural counties if the majority of service is in rural areas. Maximum award is $45,000 per grant. Priority given to applicants that have secured matching funds from non-state sources, though matching funds are not required. Combined heat and power systems, energy efficiency, biomass, rural broadband expansion, youth engagement, entrepreneurship, workforce development, regional marketing, tourism, rural transportation, and housing repair/counseling are eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Phase I (Letter of Intent) due May 16, 2025, at 11:59 PM; Phase II Full Application due July 10, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural-serving nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) IRS tax designation or similar status, community colleges, Career Technology Centers, Regional Councils, libraries, State Rural Recognized Regional Councils, small or agricultural businesses, government entities, and rural communities in Maryland seeking to advance agricultural education, rural development, and economic opportunity. Community colleges must provide enhanced training and technical assistance to support agricultural and small businesses. Trade associations are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, agricultural and forestry education, training and technical assistance, technical assistance to rural communities, combined heat and power systems, energy efficiency, biomass, agricultural technology transfer programs, rural broadband expansion, youth engagement and leadership development, economic development (entrepreneurship, education, workforce development, regional marketing, tourism), rural transportation, housing repair and counseling, poverty alleviation, heritage preservation, educational competitions, resource directories, document digitization, and assistance with applying to other state programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas of Maryland, available statewide with focus on rural communities. Eligible projects must serve more than one state-designated rural county: Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Annes, St. Marys, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Regional projects may include non-rural counties but majority of service must be in rural areas. The applicant does not have to be located in a rural area or in the area it serves. Grant information sessions held in Upper Eastern Shore (Cecil County area), Southern Maryland, and other regions.

Applications received after the deadline or that are incomplete or illegible will be deemed ineligible. Grant information sessions available to learn more about funding programs. structured_extraction.program_description: The Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund is a comprehensive grant program supporting rural economic development and prosperity initiatives across Maryland. It raises the overall standard of living in rural areas to meet or exceed statewide benchmark averages by 2030 while preserving pastoral heritage and rural way of life through targeted investments in economic and community development programs and regional cooperation. The fund provides financial assistance to address disparities in rural areas through a two-phase application process. It supports Rural Maryland Council activities, provides capacity-building funds to rural nonprofit service providers, supports the state's five regional councils, regional infrastructure projects, rural entrepreneurship development, rural community development, and rural health care organizations. Specific areas of investment include regional infrastructure, rural entrepreneurship, agricultural development, workforce development, cooperative development, and rural health care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants and subsidy funding provided through a two-phase application process to support rural development projects, capacity-building for rural nonprofit service providers, regional infrastructure projects (up to 25% of total project cost), rural entrepreneurship development, rural community development, and rural health care organizations. Grants provide significant targeted investments in economic and community development programs and promote regional and intergovernmental cooperation. Technical assistance also provided. Specific support areas include agriculture, broadband, water/wastewater, transportation, workforce housing, commercial/industrial facilities, renewable energy, tourism, and technology/innovation. The fund received its first dedicated state funding through the Fiscal Year 2017 State Operating Budget passed on March 29, 2016. The Fiscal Year 2026 grant cycle made $6,000,000 in funding available for projects in rural Maryland.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for significant targeted investments in economic and community development programs, capacity-building for rural nonprofit service providers, regional infrastructure projects, rural entrepreneurship development, rural community development, rural health care support, workforce development, cooperative development, agricultural development, broadband expansion, water/wastewater improvements, transportation projects, workforce housing, commercial/industrial facilities, renewable energy initiatives, tourism development, and technology/innovation projects, and to promote regional and intergovernmental cooperation.

Grant information sessions held in Upper Eastern Shore (Cecil County area), Southern Maryland, and other regions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to foster growth in Wicomico County's emerging agriculture and resource-based industries through a partnership between Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development (SWED), Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). The program provides financial assistance to for-profit agricultural and resource-based businesses through a cost-sharing model where applicants must contribute at least 50% of project costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Targeted grant amounts of $2,500 or less per applicant, matched by MARBIDCO. Applicant must contribute at least 50% of project costs. Maximum total grant cannot exceed $25,000 per grant agreement. Only one entity (including related entities) may apply per year. Grants are provided through a reimbursement-based cost-sharing model where the applicant must contribute at least 50% of the project cost. The program is co-funded by SWED and MARBIDCO.

Minority-owned, women-owned, disabled-owned, and veteran-owned businesses are encouraged to apply. Locally owned franchises of national chains are also considered if locally owned and controlled.

Businesses that facilitate production of foodstuffs or other goods that grow in soil or water, as well as packaging, processing, or marketing of such products are generally eligible. Eligible uses include agritourism (new or expansion initiatives), agricultural business diversification (new or expansion initiatives), deer fencing (per MARBIDCO specifications), and other eligible purposes upon MARBIDCO approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be headquartered and located in Wicomico County, Maryland and be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Wicomico County.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $28.6 billion program administered by the SBA to provide relief funds to restaurant and food service businesses. The program prioritizes funding to hardest-hit small businesses. For the first 21 days the program is open, the SBA prioritizes reviewing applications from women, veterans, and socially and economically disadvantaged business owners. Emergency financial assistance to help restaurants, bars, and other eligible food service businesses recover from COVID-19 impacts.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Small Business Administration (SBA) provides low-interest disaster loans to help businesses, nonprofits, homeowners, and renters repair or replace property damaged by declared disasters. Loans are available for physical damage to real estate, machinery, equipment, and inventory, as well as for working capital needs through Economic Injury Disaster Loans. Eligible applicants include homeowners (up to $200,000 for real estate repairs, up to $40,000 for personal property), renters (up to $40,000 for personal property), businesses (up to $2 million), and private nonprofits (up to $2 million). Interest rates are as low as 3.61 percent for businesses, 2.5 percent for private nonprofits, and 1.938 percent for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Applicants may qualify for an additional loan increase of up to 20 percent of verified physical damages for mitigation improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses and nonprofits can borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged real estate, machinery, equipment, inventory, and other business assets. Economic Injury Disaster Loans are available for working capital even without physical damage. Homeowners can borrow up to $200,000 for real estate repairs; homeowners and renters can borrow up to $40,000 for personal property including automobiles. Interest rates are as low as 3.61 percent for businesses, 2.5 percent for private nonprofits, and 1.938 percent for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Applicants may qualify for an additional loan increase of up to 20 percent of verified physical damages for mitigation improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by disaster declaration; physical property damage and economic injury deadlines differ
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses of all sizes, private nonprofit organizations, homeowners, and renters in declared disaster counties who have suffered damage from declared disasters
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of disaster-damaged real estate, machinery, equipment, inventory, and other business assets; working capital for businesses; personal property repairs for homeowners and renters; eligible mitigation improvements such as safe rooms or storm shelters
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in federally declared disaster counties. Recent declarations have covered Baltimore City and Howard counties and the adjacent counties of Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's in Maryland.
requirements_list: Located in a federally declared disaster county
Sustained damages from a declared disaster
Losses not fully covered by insurance
Homeowners and renters can apply for personal property damage
Businesses and nonprofits must demonstrate business activity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants may apply online using the Electronic Loan Application (ELA) via the SBA's secure website at DisasterLoan.sba.gov. Completed applications can also be downloaded from www.sba.gov and mailed to the SBA Processing and Disbursement Center at 14925 Kingsport Road, Fort Worth, TX 76155. Applicants can also obtain information by calling the SBA Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955 (1-800-877-8339 for the deaf and hard-of-hearing) or emailing disastercustomerservice@sba.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal government program that provides low-income households monthly credits or subsidies towards broadband internet and mobile services. Qualified households receive up to $30 per month for standard broadband service, or up to $75 per month for qualified households within Tribal lands. The program helps reduce monthly broadband bills for eligible low-income households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly credit or subsidy of up to $30 per month toward broadband internet and/or mobile services for qualified low-income households. Qualified households within Tribal lands receive up to $75 per month. Internet Essentials service offers up to 50 Mbps for $9.95/month (free with ACP benefit) or Internet Essentials Plus offers up to 100 Mbps for $29.95/month (free with ACP benefit). Xfinity Mobile services also available. Free equipment (modem) provided with no activation fees. Available through Comcast Xfinity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households receiving federal assistance benefits including recipients of National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Medicaid, Federal Public Housing Assistance, Lifeline, Federal Pell Grants, WIC, SSI, and other eligible benefit programs seeking affordable broadband internet access. structured_extraction.program_description: A St. Mary's County tax incentive program that supports renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades of commercial real property in designated challenged areas. Property owners who invest in eligible areas are eligible for property tax freezes for either 7 or 10 years depending on investment level. If investment is 10-15% of assessed value, taxes are frozen for 7 years. If investment is 16% or more of assessed value, taxes are frozen for 10 years. During the incentive period, property owners are not subject to increases in tax rates or assessed valuations. Total value of assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property taxes are held constant for either 7 or 10 years depending on investment level. If investment is 10-15% of assessed value, taxes are frozen for 7 years. If investment is 16% or more of assessed value, taxes are frozen for 10 years. Minimum investment required is either 10% of assessed value or $25,000, whichever is greater. During the incentive period, if tax rates or assessed valuations increase, the property owner is not subject to those increases. Total value of assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award. The specific tax reduction or exemption terms are determined by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County upon application approval.

Commercial property must be located in challenged areas of St. Mary's County.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Statewide Specialized Transportation Assistance Program provides door-to-door transportation services for elderly individuals and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who are not sufficiently close to public transportation routes. The program offers general-purpose transportation with service organized into zones covering different areas of the county on different days of the week. Service is provided on a demand-route basis with preference given to individuals with scheduled medical appointments. The State provides between $130,000 to $175,000 in annual funding to support these services, with a required local match. Over 17,000 riders utilize this service annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides door-to-door transportation services to elderly persons and persons with disabilities. Service is available with rides scheduled between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. (service operates between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.). The fare is $6.00 for a round trip, and participants receive one trip for one fare. Additional stops cost $3.00 each. Service is provided on a first-come, first-served basis with preference for scheduled medical appointments. The program receives between $130,000 to $175,000 in grant funding each year from the Maryland Department of Transportation with a required local match.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service is provided throughout St. Mary's County in five zones: Zone 1 (Monday) serving Ridge, Lexington Park, Great Mills, Callaway, Piney Point, Tall Timbers, St. Inigoes, and Mechanicsville; Zone 2 (Tuesday) serving Mechanicsville, Charlotte Hall, and Golden Beach; Zone 3 (Wednesday) serving Leonardtown, Hollywood, Breton Bay, Lexington Park, Compton, Avenue, Chaptico, and Wicomico Shores; Zone 4 (Thursday) serving all county areas; and Zone 5 (Friday) serving Lexington Park, Wildewood, California, Hollywood, and Oakville.

Maximum one attendant free of charge; additional attendants/companions pay $3.00

Continuous no-shows may result in denial of transportation

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program funded by 1.5 percent of proceeds from video lottery terminals at Maryland's six casinos, providing financing to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses throughout Maryland. The fund provides loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000 with particular focus on targeted businesses. At least 50 percent of funds are distributed to targeted businesses located within 10 miles of five casinos (Hollywood Casino Perryville, Ocean Downs in Worcester County, Maryland Live! in Anne Arundel County, Rocky Gap Casino in Allegany County, and Horseshoe Casino in Baltimore City). The remaining 50 percent is available to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses throughout Maryland. Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties are recognized as targeted areas.

Application fee of $250 (non-refundable) for loans over $25,000; loans of $10,000-$25,000 require a $25 application fee. Loan origination fee of 1 percent at closing. Standard underwriting practices apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A self-sustaining pool of federal and state money used to make loans to small businesses and eligible organizations seeking to locate or expand in Western Maryland. The fund provides gap financing loans to create and save jobs. Borrowers repay loans and the money is returned to the fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing financial tool for business expansion, job creation, and retention. The program recycles repayments into new loans for economic development projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $500,000. Interest rates are prime plus 1 percent with a floor of 5 percent. Maximum loan terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Application fee of $250 (non-refundable) for loans over $25,000, or $25 for loans between $10,000-$25,000. Loan origination fee of 1.5 percent at closing for loans over $25,000, or $0 for loans between $10,000-$25,000. The project must create or retain a minimum of one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested. Money from loan repayments is recycled back into the fund to make additional loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal loans providing economic assistance to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, private non-profit organizations, and individuals impacted by declared disasters. The program provides low-interest disaster loans with long-term payments stretching up to 30 years to help businesses and non-profits pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to the disaster, even if the business or nonprofit did not suffer physical damage. The program also includes grants available through the EIDL Grant program, offering up to $10,000 in grant funding with priority given to small businesses with fewer than 300 employees in low-income neighborhoods that experienced significant revenue reductions during the pandemic. Loan amounts can reach up to $2 million with interest rates as low as 4% for small businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The program also supported COVID-19 relief with loans up to $500,000 for up to 24 months of economic injury, with automatic deferment of one year before repayment begins.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest federal disaster loans and grants to help businesses and non-profits pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to declared disasters. Loans up to $2 million with interest rates as low as 4% for small businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. EIDL Grants offer up to $10,000 in funding, with priority given to small businesses with fewer than 300 employees in low-income neighborhoods that experienced 30% reduction in gross receipts during any 8-week period between March 2 and December 31, 2020 compared to a comparable 8-week period before March 2. COVID-19 relief loans available up to $500,000 for up to 24 months of economic injury with 3.75% interest rates for small businesses and 2.75% for nonprofits. Collateral required for loans over $25,000. Applications are submitted online through the SBA's Disaster Loan Application Portal (DLAP) at disasterloan.sba.gov/ela/ or sba.gov/disaster.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, private non-profit organizations, and individuals in Maryland and other designated disaster areas affected by declared disasters, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the March 15, 2025 drought
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital needs caused by the disaster, including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to the disaster. Health care benefits continuation, rent, utilities, and fixed debt payments. Economic recovery from disaster-related business losses and operating expenses. Loans are available even if the business or nonprofit did not suffer physical damage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and its counties, available nationwide. Specific disaster declarations cover Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington counties in Maryland; Adams, Franklin, Lancaster, and York counties in Pennsylvania; and Loudon County in Virginia. Anne Arundel County received official designation from the SBA for this program during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent disaster declarations. Applicant must select state and county where loss occurred with corresponding disaster declaration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides preferential status in competition for federal government contracts to small businesses located in Historically Underutilized Business Zones. The program is available in designated HUBZone areas, including all of Garrett County and specific areas in Hagerstown. Businesses receive preferential status in federal contracting, including set-aside awards, sole source awards, 10% price evaluation preference in open competitions, and access to subcontracting opportunities. The program targets 3% of all federal prime contract dollars to HUBZone businesses. Certified HUBZone small businesses in urban and rural communities gain preferential access to federal procurement opportunities through the Small Business Administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified HUBZone small businesses receive competitive and sole source contracting opportunities, a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions, and subcontracting opportunities. The federal government has a goal of awarding 3% of all dollars for federal prime contracts to HUBZone-certified small business concerns. Businesses must first be certified by the SBA to participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in Historically Underutilized Business Zones in Garrett County and Hagerstown that meet SBA size standards and other eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal government contracts and subcontracting opportunities for business development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Garrett County has been designated as a Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone). Designated HUBZone areas also exist in Hagerstown. Hagerstown has designated HUBZone qualified tracts as shown on the program map. Businesses must have their principal office located in a designated HUBZone.
requirements_list: Be a small business as defined by SBA Size Standards
Principal office located in a HUBZone
At least 35% of employees must reside in a HUBZone

Be at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens, a Community Development Corporation, an agricultural cooperative, an Alaska Native corporation, a Native Hawaiian organization, or an Indian tribe
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must first be certified by the SBA. This workbook is uploaded as part of the application to help expedite SBA's review. The SBA determines which businesses are eligible, maintains a listing of qualified HUBZone small businesses, and adjudicates protests of eligibility. Businesses must recertify annually and undergo program examinations at least every three years. Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development department or the SBA for HUBZone designation and benefits information.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) - Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse Response
structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest, long-term loans provided by the U.S. Small Business Administration to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofits recover from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. These working capital loans are intended to help applicants meet ordinary and necessary financial obligations that cannot be met as a direct result of the disaster. Loans up to $2 million can be used to pay normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disaster-related disruption, as well as to meet working capital needs. Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, long-term disaster loans up to $2 million provided by the SBA to cover normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills, as well as working capital needs that cannot be met because of the disaster-related disruption. Interest rate: 4% for small businesses and small agricultural cooperatives; 3.25% for private nonprofit organizations. Loan terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue for 12 months from first disbursement; repayment begins 12 months after first disbursement. Maximum loan amount of $2 million is waivable if the business is a major source of employment. Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster only.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in Maryland, Delaware, District of Columbia, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disaster-related disruption, as well as working capital needs caused by the disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible applicants in Maryland (entire state), Delaware (Kent, New Castle, Sussex), District of Columbia, Pennsylvania (Adams, Bedford, Chester, Fayette, Franklin, Fulton, Lancaster, Somerset, York), Virginia (Accomack, Alexandria, Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun), and West Virginia (Berkeley, Grant, Hampshire, Jefferson, Mineral, Morgan, Preston) affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small aquaculture business, or private nonprofit organization
Eligibility based on financial impact of the disaster only
Must demonstrate financial impact from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Must have been affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse
Must have experienced a temporary loss of revenue due to the bridge collapse
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be completed at Business Recovery Centers located in Baltimore City at CareFirst Engagement Center (1501 S Clinton St, Ste #100, Baltimore, MD 21224) and Baltimore County at Dundalk Renaissance Center (11 Center Place, Dundalk, MD 21222) and CCBC (7200 Sollers Point Road, Baltimore, MD 21222). Centers are open Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Applicants can also apply online at sba.gov/disaster, visit https://lending.sba.gov/search-disaster/?disaster=MD-20001, call the SBA Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955, or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov.

Property owner must commit to remain in agricultural related pursuits for ten years
