structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded partnership program between the governors of 13 Appalachian states and a federal presidential appointee that supports economic and social development in the Appalachian Region. The program provides grants to eligible entities for projects aligned with five strategic goals: Economic Opportunities, Ready Workforce, Critical Infrastructure, Natural and Cultural Assets, and Leadership and Community Capacity. It merges local, state, and federal funds to implement job-creating infrastructure and economic development projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for projects that strengthen the Appalachian region's economy, workforce, infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and community leadership capacity. The program merges local, state, and federal funds to implement job-creating projects. Projects must include a 50% match from other funding sources, and matching funds must be identified and committed at the time of application. Projects should demonstrate measurable outcomes and economic impact. Federal grants for projects aligned with ARC investment goals and state objectives/strategies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 for preliminary project submission; November 2026 for formal ARC application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit businesses, government entities, local development districts, and municipal governments in Washington County and the six-county Appalachian region of Western Maryland with projects that support economic development, workforce improvement, infrastructure investment, cultural asset development, or community leadership capacity building in the Appalachian region. Organizations with demonstrated capacity to administer federal grants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic opportunities and entrepreneurial development; workforce education, skills, and health improvement; critical infrastructure including broadband, transportation, and water/wastewater systems; natural and cultural heritage projects; community and organizational capacity building and leadership development; job-creating infrastructure and economic development projects; technology development; tourism; energy; recovery ecosystems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Appalachian Region including Washington County, Maryland and the six-county region of Western Maryland served by the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties). Projects must be located in or serve the Appalachian region as defined by the Appalachian Regional Commission.
requirements_list: 50% matching funds from other sources must be identified and committed at time of application
Commitment letters required for all matching funds with committed status
Applicants must identify minimum ARC funding needed for project viability
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
Submission of Preliminary Project Description form
Submission of ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources form
Project must align with one or more of the five ARC strategic goals
Organizational capacity to administer federal grants with recent award history
Quantifiable outputs and outcomes using ARC performance measures
Project must align with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement
Pending grant funds must have anticipated award dates listed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit the Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Step 2: Projects are reviewed and ranked by the Washington County Commissioners. Step 3: Top-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Step 4: Projects selected for advancement receive an invitation letter in early fall to submit a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with submission due in November.

structured_extraction.program_description: Training program that teaches people how to respond to emergencies and disasters in their community. Participants learn basic disaster response skills including light search and rescue, team organization, damage assessment, and fire suppression.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free or low-cost community training in emergency response and disaster preparedness skills. Participants receive instruction and certification upon completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community residents in Washington County who want to learn emergency response skills and become certified to help their neighbors during disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training only - no financial assistance provided. Focuses on building emergency response capability and disaster preparedness knowledge.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can enroll in CERT training classes. Upon completion of training, participants become certified Community Emergency Response Team members.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding program for recognized non-profit organizations in Washington County, Maryland under Public Local Laws § 1-108 that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants to recognized non-profit organizations as determined by the Board of County Commissioners during the budgeting process. Emphasis is on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 27 cycle is closed; application window dates are announced via Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recognized non-profit organizations serving Washington County under Public Local Laws § 1-108.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible organizations must be charitable organizations within Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Organization must be on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 List)
Organization must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
Organization must be active and in good standing with Maryland Business Express
Applications only accepted during published application window announced via NOFA
Written letter of request from organization required
Copy of IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) is sent annually to all organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List with procedures, opening and closing application dates. Applications are not accepted outside the published application window. Submit completed packet by mail or email to Kimberly Jacobson. Organizations not currently on the 1-108 List must apply to be added for eligibility in the following year's funding cycle by contacting the County Attorney's Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created to support eligible local nonprofit organizations in Washington County that were impacted by the Covid-19 health emergency and its negative effects, including decreased revenue, financial insecurity, increased costs, and challenges covering operating costs. The program provides $1.5 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to support nonprofits providing critical services to vulnerable populations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maximum $40,000 in lump sum grant funding per eligible nonprofit organization. Funds support replacement of lost revenue and/or increased costs caused by the pandemic, or provision of increased services to address local pandemic impacts. Eligible uses include: salary and wages, inventory, rent and utilities, technology, and contracted services. Indirect costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible nonprofit organizations serving Washington County residents that have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) designation and were established before March 1, 2019. Includes faith-based organizations with separate nonprofit status providing public services. Organizations disproportionately impacted by the Covid-19 pandemic experiencing decreased revenue, increased costs, or financial insecurity are prioritized.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational expenses resulting from decreased revenue and/or increased expenses directly related to Covid-19. Expansion of eligible services or creation of programs addressing increased community needs in public health, mental health, substance abuse services, household assistance (food, rent, utilities), senior services, and services for pandemic-impacted households and children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organization must have a physical location/address in Washington County and serve a majority (>50%) of Washington County citizens. Priority consideration may be given to organizations in Qualified Census Tracts (tracts where 50%+ of households have incomes below 60% of Area Median Gross Income or poverty rate of 25%+).
requirements_list: Valid 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) designation from the Internal Revenue Service
Physical location/address in Washington County and serves a majority of Washington County citizens
In good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation's Personal Property Tax Division
In compliance with Federal, State, and local human rights laws
Established before March 1, 2019
Cannot be operating under a fiscal sponsor
Cannot be a church or religious organization (except faith-based organizations with separate non-profit status providing public services)
Cannot be a fraternal organization or social club
Cannot be a homeowner's association
Cannot be a labor union
Cannot be a private, political, or public foundation
Completed Community Recovery Nonprofit Grant Application (all fields completed, thoroughly answered, signed by applicant and Authorized Signatory)
Copy of IRS Determination Letter
Completed Financial Budget Template (Excel Spreadsheet)
Most recent audit/financial statement
W-9 form (if organization has never received funds from Washington County or has address change)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit grant applications via email to CommunityRecovery@washco-md.net with each required attachment as individual electronic files with appropriate labels. Hard copy applications not accepted. Required documentation includes completed application form, IRS Determination Letter, Financial Budget Template, most recent audit/financial statement, and W-9 form (if applicable).

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: State program established through bipartisan legislation to support Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding from $8 million in state relief funding to support commuter and shuttle bus companies experiencing continued financial impacts from COVID-19.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies affected by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery assistance for commuter and shuttle bus companies impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for Washington County real property owners who are fallen heroes or their surviving families, providing a property tax reduction or exemption on real estate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit that reduces property taxes for eligible fallen heroes or their surviving families in Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fallen heroes and their surviving families who own real property in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for eligible real estate property owners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fallen Heroes Tax Credit Application and submit it to the Washington County Treasurer's Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides duty reduction and tax benefits for businesses operating in the Washington County Foreign Trade Zone. Imports can enter and be held in the zone without customs duties, and duty is only paid when merchandise is shipped into U.S. Customs territory.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses in the Foreign Trade Zone receive customs duty exemptions and benefits including: no customs duties on imports held in the zone (duty only paid when shipped to U.S. Customs territory), no duty on re-exported merchandise, no duty on labor, overhead or profit from FTZ production, lower duty rates on components, exemption from state and local taxes on tangible personal property held for export, and exemption from duties on materials used in FTZ processing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Industrial and commercial businesses in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The benefits apply to imports, production operations, and export-related activities in the Foreign Trade Zone
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nearly 1,800 acres of prime industrial and commercial properties located within Washington County Foreign Trade Zone #255
requirements_list: Business must be located or operate within the designated Foreign Trade Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development for information

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to organizations operating within Washington County for one-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated. The objective is to remedy or address current financial issues or situations requiring a prompt response and resolution. This funding assists organizations with projects or events that would not otherwise qualify for general fund Community Organization Funding or Hotel Rental Tax Funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. The portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating within Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated; projects or events addressing current financial issues or situations requiring prompt response and resolution
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application using the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application form. Applicants should carefully read the Guidelines & Instructions provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program offering property tax credits, employment (income) tax credits, and personal property tax credits for businesses and developers in designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County. Businesses located in or relocating to the Enterprise Zones may be eligible for local real property tax credits on capital investments, state income tax credits for job creation, and exemptions from commercial building excise tax. The program is designed to encourage economic development through capital investments and job creation in defined geographic areas approved by the State of Maryland for 10-year periods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying businesses may be eligible for state income tax credits (up to $1,000 one-time for most new jobs; up to $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees), local real property tax credits (80 percent on the increased assessed value of real property for the first five years, decreasing by ten percent in each remaining five-year period, up to ten years total), personal property tax credits for machinery and equipment in Focus Areas, and exemption from commercial building excise tax on capital investments in the designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses relocating to or expanding in the Enterprise Zone, new start-ups, property developers, and employers hiring new employees in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building acquisition and construction, rehabilitation, machinery and equipment purchases, and capital investments in the Enterprise Zones
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Approximately 5,500 acres in Washington County within three state-designated Enterprise Zones: the Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,410 acres within the City of Hagerstown), the Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres surrounding the Town of Hancock), and additional designated areas. Specific locations include Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, Central Business District in downtown Hagerstown, and Town of Hancock and surrounding areas from Pennsylvania border to Potomac River.
requirements_list: Locate business in designated Enterprise Zone
Qualify for business status
Create jobs or make capital investments
Property tax credit application must be submitted before project completion and User/Occupancy Permits issuance
Employment tax credit requires qualified employee requirements per Maryland Department of Commerce
Personal property credit project/business must be in Focus Area
Property owner must concur with application if developer/company applies on their behalf
Applicants must provide all data required by Enterprise Zone Administrator
Business may be proprietorship, partnership, or corporation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development or Linda Spence, Enterprise Zone Administrator, at LSpence@WashCo-MD.net or 240-313-2286 for application details. Complete the Enterprise Zone Application packet. Property tax credit applications must be submitted before project completion and User/Occupancy Permits issuance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program designed to stimulate and assist Washington County organizations, agencies, and businesses in developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects. The program helps organizations undertake activities that would not be possible without special funding and supports establishing activities and events that can eventually grow and succeed independently.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding provided through a 6% County Hotel Rental Tax that is invested back into the community. Funds are distributed to the County's local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors to support tourism attractions, economic development, and cultural and recreational projects. Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year, contingent on available funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year; contingent on available funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors seeking to develop tourism attractions, enhance economic development, or support cultural and recreational projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tourism advertising and marketing, economic development projects, cultural and historical projects, recreational activities and events. Cannot fund: normal operating/administrative expenses, political candidates, endowments, organizations with budget deficits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be qualified to receive funding
Project must be qualified to receive funding
Must meet funding goals of County Commissioners
Priority given to projects that generate overnight stays
Must encourage support of County business and restaurants
Must demonstrate impact on community and local economy
Must track hotel/motel room nights purchased as result of event/project
Must submit receipts and supporting documentation for all expenditures
Certify expenses align with approved project and meet Hotel Rental Tax Funding intent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Hotel Rental Tax Funding Application form available online. The application and guidelines must be reviewed before submitting. Applicants should save the application form to their computer before completing it to prevent loss of entered information. Complete grant report form and submit with supporting documentation to Office of Grant Management.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program created to accelerate land preservation easement purchases and provide an additional land preservation option for agricultural landowners in Washington County. Owners of qualifying agricultural land can sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement on their contiguous acreage (less one acre per existing dwelling) to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement with a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Once a landowner agrees to accept the County's offer to purchase their development rights, an Installment Purchase Agreement (IPA) is written that includes the total amount of money the County will pay and the terms including a fixed interest rate. Payments are made over 10 years: 10% of principal at settlement plus interest, and 10% of principal annually for the remaining 9 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County with qualifying contiguous acreage
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners receive payment for selling Agricultural Preservation Easements on their contiguous acreage
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County only
requirements_list: Must own agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Can preserve entire contiguous acreage minus one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners meeting minimum qualifications apply to sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement to the County. Upon agreement, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written between the County and the landowner specifying payment terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support innovative programs that bridge gaps between transportation and healthcare services, aiming to provide greater access to healthcare for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children facing mobility barriers. The program supports the continued work of the Local Management Board (LMB) in underserved communities through non-emergency medical transportation, expansion of existing volunteer driver networks, and last-mile solutions for residents in areas not reached by public transit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards ranging from $10,000 to $40,000. The program intends to award 1 to 3 grants from a total pool of $74,000. Funding can support operating expenses, capital investments, or a combination thereof. Performance period runs from May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local government entities providing services to Washington County residents, with focus on programs serving seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children facing mobility barriers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) for primary care, dialysis, mental health services, or pharmacy pickups; expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services; and last-mile solutions for underserved areas not reached by public transit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland. Organization must be located in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Be in 'Good Standing' with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Demonstrate a proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic excellence
Have no unpaid obligations to government entities
Maintain non-discriminatory practices
Collect and maintain service and activity data
Submit application with all required documents including Application Submission Form, Budget, Letters of Support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter, and proof of 'Good Standing' with SDAT
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically with all required documents including the Application Submission Form, Budget Narrative Spreadsheet, Letters of Support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter, and screenshot proof of 'Good Standing' with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Application must include narrative sections covering Statement of Need, Organizational Capacity, Program Plan, and Collaborations/Partnerships, with authorized representative certification. Submit to cahrens@washco-md.net by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists businesses in setting up an online sales framework and offering employees telework opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 will be awarded to applicants based on priority guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Setting up an online sales framework and offering employees telework opportunities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides up to $30,000 in rental assistance for one year to help qualified small businesses open or expand in previously vacant retail or commercial spaces.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $30,000 grant for rent for one year (rental payment up to $2,500 per month) for qualified small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees. The grant covers up to $2,500 per month for 12 months. Applicant's monthly rent can exceed $2,500, but the maximum paid by the grant is $2,500 per month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline stated; applications open September 8 on rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees that plan to open or expand into previously vacant retail or commercial spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental payments for vacant retail or commercial space.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Maryland and occupy a retail or commercial space that has been vacant at least 6 months prior to application.
requirements_list: Business must be new or existing
Business must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Business must open or expand in a retail or commercial space that has been vacant at least 6 months prior to application
Financially viable business whose operations will continue forward
Small business with 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register with the Maryland OneStop Portal at onestop.md.gov before applying. Review the Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) and sample application in advance. Submit application online starting September 8. Applicants should gather required documents and prepare answers before the application opens.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that provides general purpose transportation for eligible elderly individuals and people with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidized transportation vouchers that can be used to pay for rides from registered taxi providers. Participants purchase vouchers at reduced rates and save at least 50% compared to regular taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and are purchased monthly. Vouchers expire June 30 of each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 60 or older and individuals with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General purpose transportation provided by registered taxi service providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Washington County, Maryland. Service area determined by registered provider coverage.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older, or have a disability
If under age 60, must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Cannot utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Washington County Transit office to have an application mailed or visit the office at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown to pick one up in person. For applicants under age 60, have your application certified by a healthcare professional. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office. You will be notified by mail of your eligibility. Applications must be renewed annually by June 30.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Maryland Economic Development Fund Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to fund infrastructure projects that support economic development activity, stimulate private investment, and grow jobs in Maryland's rural counties. Eligible uses include developing public infrastructure such as utilities, transportation, and broadband; infrastructure for specific industries like manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, cybersecurity and agribusiness; purchasing commercial/industrial properties for business parks; workforce development; and entrepreneurship and innovation initiatives.
eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided by the Maryland Department of Commerce to support economic development projects in rural Maryland areas. Up to $10,000,000 available with no matching requirement. Funding supports public infrastructure development, commercial/industrial property acquisition, workforce development, planning and feasibility studies, and capital and operational expenses (up to 3% for administrative costs).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: August 31 (hard deadline set by Maryland Department of Commerce; extensions will not be granted)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, educational institutions, workforce development organizations, and nonprofits in eligible rural counties of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public infrastructure such as utilities, transportation, and broadband; industry-specific infrastructure for manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, cybersecurity and agribusiness; commercial/industrial properties for business parks; workforce development; entrepreneurship and innovation; planning and feasibility studies; capital and operational expenses; up to 3% administrative costs for oversight and implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County, MD, served by five tri-county councils in rural regions of Maryland.

Budget with funding sources and amounts
Description of significant economic development impact
All grant funds must be expended within 24 months of award
Regional councils must coordinate with local jurisdictions to identify priority projects
Interim reports due at 6 months and 18 months; final report due at 24 months
Demographic/MBE information requested from contractors and vendors (voluntary response)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project summary form with contact information, project details, budget, and economic impact description to the Maryland Department of Commerce by the August 31 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizen Supplement - Homeowners Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Washington County program that supplements the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit program for homeowners age 65 and over who meet certain income qualifications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A supplemental tax credit based on the amount by which State of Maryland and Washington County real property taxes exceed a percentage of the homeowners' combined income. The first $8,000 of income is excluded from calculation under the State formula. The Washington County supplemental credit may significantly increase the overall tax credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be filed by September 1 of each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners age 65 and over in Washington County who meet income qualifications
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces property tax obligations for eligible senior homeowners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be age 65 or older
Applicant must be a homeowner-occupied residential property owner
Applicant must meet certain income qualifications
Application must be filed by September 1 of each year using the State's Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Application Form HTC-60

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to provide financial assistance to small businesses in Washington County. The program was approved by the Board of County Commissioners and is funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery assistance for small, minority and women-owned businesses impacted by COVID-19

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive business incentive package including tax credits, workforce training, infrastructure support, and financing programs. Tax credits for job creation, capital investment, and real property improvements. Workforce training and development opportunities, high-speed internet connectivity, competitive utility rates, and tax advantages.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credits for 6-15 years for job creation and capital investment. Personal property tax exemptions on manufacturing machinery and equipment. R&D equipment tax exemptions. Business inventory tax exemptions. Sales and use tax exemptions on manufacturing equipment and materials. Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credit offering up to 100% credits for 5 years with specific investment and job creation thresholds. Construction tax credit of 0.4% of construction costs for new improvements. Workforce development services and training grants. Revolving loan fund for small business growth, expansion, and rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and new businesses, small and mid-sized manufacturing companies, technology companies, small businesses, minority-owned businesses, women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, and microenterprises looking to open, expand, or relocate in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job creation, capital investment, real property improvements, manufacturing equipment, research and development, business expansion, relocation, and code compliance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland, with specific programs available in City of Hagerstown
requirements_list: Must be for-profit or non-profit entity
Specific job creation and investment thresholds apply for tax credits
Real property improvements must be for economic development projects
Manufacturing machinery and equipment eligible for tax exemptions
Some programs limited to City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses can enroll in applicable programs through Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development or City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development Department. Specific application procedures vary by program incentive.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County FY23 Surplus Funding Nonprofit Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program established to distribute surplus funds set aside by the Board of County Commissioners to provide assistance to local nonprofits serving Washington County citizens. The program uses an objective and systematic approach to review and award funding to nonprofits meeting prioritized and urgent community needs, with emphasis on efficient fund use and achieving result-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 are available for capital and operating expenses for one-time projects or to meet urgent community needs. Organizations must expend awarded funds within one year of receipt or return the funds to the county. The total funding available is $1,831,447.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable nonprofit organizations recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as 501c3 entities that have an office located within and provide services in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses for one-time projects or to meet urgent needs. Funds cannot be used to fund an endowment or benefit individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must have an office located within and provide services in Washington County.
requirements_list: Must be a charitable organization recognized by the IRS as a 501c3 with valid status
Must be incorporated as a business entity in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Must have a recent audit or detailed financial statement to submit
Cannot be a political or governmental organization
Cannot be a church or religious entity (though separate organizations operating within a church facility with their own 501c3 status may be eligible)
Cannot have unpaid or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Cannot have forfeited incorporation status with the State of Maryland
Cannot have failed to submit required Grant Reports or have other outstanding obligations to the County
May only submit one request for funding
Must be able to expend awarded funds within one year of receipt
Must have non-discriminatory policies for employment and mission achievement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the FY23 Surplus Funding Nonprofit Assistance Program Grant Application on approved forms and submit by December 20, 2022 at 3:00 pm. Applications were available online through the OGM website on or about November 17, 2022. Applicants must provide a budget narrative and submit a grant report providing an accounting of the funds after receipt. A W9 form is only needed if the organization has not previously received funding from the county. Submission must be one paper hard copy with application, budget narrative spreadsheet, and attachments, printed on one side only with no dividers or binding, fastened with binder clip or rubber bands. Applications are scored on a point-based system (maximum 100 points).

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Gaming Commission Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Washington County Gaming Commission that distributes funds from charitable gaming (tip jar) revenues to eligible charitable organizations in Washington County. The program allocates 50% of Gaming Funds to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with remaining funds available to eligible charitable organizations. Supports health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants distributed from the Washington County Gaming Fund, which is funded by tip jar sales and charitable gaming revenues within the county. Maximum $100,000 per application. Organizations may apply for multiple projects with separate applications. Funds support operating expenses, equipment, or capital projects. All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and expended within one year of receipt.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses, equipment, capital projects, permits, salaries and fringe benefits, program expenses, activity fees, transportation. All funds must be used exclusively within Washington County. Indirect costs capped at 15% of direct costs. Unspent funds must be returned after one year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. Organizations must be located in Washington County or have a place of business in Washington County. All services must be provided within Washington County.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download application packet from Office of Grant Management website starting April 1, 2026. Submit all required documents as electronic PDF via email or hard copy (mail/drop-off) by April 30, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Include completed application form, budget narrative spreadsheet, supporting documentation, financial statements, IRS determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, W-9, vendor form, Notice of Responsible Person (if applicable), and letters of support. All fields must be completed. Applications are scored using a published scoring rubric evaluating need, program plan, past performance, partnerships, budget, and organizational capacity. An informational workshop is available via Zoom.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A three-year tax credit program for owners of commercial buildings in Washington County. Owners receive the credit for constructing new space or renovating existing buildings to meet high energy and environmental standards by achieving LEED Platinum, Gold, or Silver certification. The credit applies to the increased assessed property value, with amounts of 30 percent for LEED Platinum, 25 percent for Gold, and 20 percent for Silver certification.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A three-year tax credit applied against the increased assessed value of a property. The credit amounts are 30 percent of the increase for LEED Platinum certification, 25 percent for Gold certification, and 20 percent for Silver certification. The credit is determined by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Credits are applied for 3 consecutive years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 1 year after building is certified as 'high performance building'
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial building owners in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction/credit for new construction or renovation of commercial space that achieves LEED certification
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: The property must be a commercial building
The building must achieve a LEED Silver, Gold, or Platinum rating from USGBC
For LEED Platinum: 30 percent tax credit on increased assessed value
For LEED Gold: 25 percent tax credit on increased assessed value
For LEED Silver: 20 percent tax credit on increased assessed value
The application must be submitted within one year of the building receiving its LEED certification
The building must maintain its certification level for the three-year credit period
Applicants must submit an annual letter of compliance attesting certification conditions remain unchanged
Written notice of anticipated changes impacting certification must be provided
Retention of all drawings, specifications, and as-built documentation during creditable period required
Building must not be altered to fall below original LEED rating level
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The building owner submits a complete application form with a copy of their LEED certification request. After the project is finished, the owner must provide a use and occupancy certificate and proof of the final LEED certification. Applicants must submit an annual letter of compliance. Contact the Washington County Department of Business Development to obtain the application packet. The Department reviews the materials to approve the tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides six to fifteen years of tax credits on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. Three options are available: Section 4(a) provides graduated tax credits (52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6) for businesses expanding premises by at least 1,500 square feet and creating at least one new permanent full-time position. Section 4(b) provides graduated credits (30% years 1-2, 20% years 3-4, 10% years 5-6) for businesses obtaining at least 2,500 square feet and creating five new permanent full-time employees. Section 4(c) provides 100% tax credit years 1-5, 75% years 6-10, and 50% years 11-15 for businesses investing $10 million in capital improvements and creating 100 new permanent full-time employees. The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state initiative established under the Cannabis Reform Act of 2023 that allocates a portion of cannabis sales tax revenue and business conversion fees to local jurisdictions to support community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities and those disproportionately affected by past cannabis prohibition enforcement. The fund is administered locally by participating counties and municipalities, with funding used for mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, housing assistance and homelessness prevention, and essential services for aging communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and financial support from cannabis sales tax revenue and cannabis business conversion fees. Funds support eligible community-based initiatives serving designated areas. Washington County allocates funding for ZIP code 21740 (Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas). Charles County FY2026 approved budget of $811,000 is allocated through two channels: $411,000 to Charles County Charitable Trust for grants to local non-profits supporting low-impact and disproportionately impacted communities in the Waldorf region, and $400,000 to Department of Community Services-Aging Division for essential services for aging communities in the Waldorf region including Meals-on-Wheels and senior assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government entities, and community organizations serving low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in designated areas; aging community members in participating regions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, housing assistance and homelessness prevention, essential services for aging communities including Meals-on-Wheels and senior assistance programs, and administrative expenses necessary to implement and manage the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted to designated areas in participating jurisdictions: ZIP code 21740 in Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas of Washington County, and the Waldorf region of Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Programs must benefit low-income communities
Programs must serve disproportionately impacted areas as defined in Maryland § 36-101
CRRF funding must supplement—not replace—existing local government funding for programs and services
Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities
Must be a local non-profit organization or eligible aging services provider
Must serve low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in designated regions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are managed through local county administration. Washington County has established application procedures and guidelines for eligible organizations. Charles County applications are managed through the Charles County Charitable Trust grant program for non-profit grants. Contact the respective county government for specific application procedures and deadlines. Each county is responsible for administering and monitoring funded programs.

Eligible households receive a discount of up to $50 per month towards broadband service and can receive a one-time discount of up to $100 to purchase a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet from participating providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive a monthly discount of up to $50 toward broadband service. Additionally, households can receive a one-time discount of up to $100 to purchase a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet from participating providers if they contribute more than $10 and less than $50 toward the purchase price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discount toward broadband service and one-time device purchase (laptop, desktop computer, or tablet).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide, including Maryland. Eligible households should find participating broadband providers in their state or territory.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 135% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or participation in assistance programs (SNAP, Medicaid, Lifeline)
Approved to receive benefits under free and reduced-price school lunch or breakfast program, including USDA Community Eligibility Provision for 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 school year
Received a Federal Pell Grant during the current award year
Experienced substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020, with household income in 2020 at or below $99,000 for single filers and $198,000 for joint filers
Meets eligibility criteria for a participating provider's existing low-income or COVID-19 program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through one of three methods: (1) Contact your preferred participating broadband provider directly to learn about their application process, (2) Go to GetEmergencyBroadband.org to apply online and find participating providers, or (3) Call 833-511-0311 for a mail-in application and return it with copies of documents showing proof of eligibility to Emergency Broadband Support Center, P.O. Box 7081, London, KY 40742. After receiving an eligibility determination, contact your preferred service provider to select an Emergency Broadband Benefit eligible service plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grant money to Worcester County property owners to upgrade failing onsite septic systems with Best Available Technology (BAT) units for nitrogen removal. The goal is to reduce nutrients entering the Chesapeake Bay. Failing systems within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area and Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area are prioritized, though other systems may be eligible depending on funding availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant money covers the cost and installation of a Best Available Technology (BAT) septic system unit plus two years of maintenance. For qualifying low-income homeowners, the grant may also cover drainfield costs. Grant funds can also be used to pay for abandoning an existing septic system and connecting to public sewerage that achieves enhanced nutrient removal (ENR). Grant funds cannot be used for permit or recordation fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Worcester County property owners with septic systems, prioritized by system failure status and location within critical areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost and installation of Best Available Technology (BAT) septic system units, two years of maintenance, drainfield costs for qualifying low-income homeowners, and costs to abandon existing systems and connect to public sewerage with enhanced nutrient removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Worcester County property owners. Priority is given to failing systems located within the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (CBCA) and Maryland Coastal Bays Critical Area (MCBCA), defined as property within 1,000 feet of mean high tide.

Failing systems in CBCA and MCBCA receive highest priority
For residential properties, funding eligibility is based on homeowner income
Property owner must submit application information and proof of income
Property owner must allow access for initial site inspection by Environmental Programs
If approved, property owner must sign and record an agreement acknowledging the system must be maintained by a qualified operator and allow periodic county inspections
Grant review includes assessment of public sewer availability; requests may be denied if public sewer is accessible or scheduled for the area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the application form. Submit to the Department of Environmental Programs by mail, fax, or email. structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants and low-interest loans to owner-occupied residential properties in Worcester County for rehabilitation work to bring homes up to the County's Minimum Livability Code and for lead abatement services. Priority is given to senior citizens, disabled individuals, and families with extremely low to moderate income. Grant terms are 5-15 years with no payment due back to the County unless the property is sold or refinanced during the grant period, except for lead-specific work which has no minimum grant term and requires no repayment if the house is sold or refinanced. Low-interest loans (0-7%) have payments scaled to the family's ability to repay and may be completely deferred; the full loan balance is due when the property is sold, transferred, or refinanced. Grants are secured with a recorded property lien. Homeowners may supplement grant awards with loan funding as needed. For lead abatement work in eligible census tracts, a 10% match is required if family income exceeds 80% of the median. Up to 40% of rehabilitation work may be cosmetic in nature.

Lead abatement grants have no minimum term and require no repayment if the house is sold or refinanced. Low-interest loans have payments scaled to the family's ability to repay and may be completely deferred; the full loan balance is due when the property is sold, transferred, or refinanced. A 10% match is required for lead abatement if family income exceeds 80% of the median. Homeowners may supplement grant awards with loan funding as needed. Up to 40% of rehabilitation work may be cosmetic in nature.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Special Loans Rehabilitation Application. Contact the Program Administrator at the Worcester County Department of Development, Review and Permitting for application submission and review process details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program establishing smoke alarm installation and maintenance requirements for residential dwellings in Worcester County, Maryland. Implements Maryland's Smoke Alarm Law with phased implementation by 1/1/2018.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Establishes minimum smoke alarm installation locations and maintenance standards for residential properties. Requirements vary based on construction date (pre-7/75 through post-7/94). By 1/1/2018, battery-operated alarms must be sealed, tamper-resistant units with silence/hush buttons and long-life batteries.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and occupants of residential dwellings, builders/owners of new construction
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke alarms for home fire safety
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Worcester County, Maryland
requirements_list: Monthly testing of smoke alarms using test button
Replacement of smoke alarms at 10 years of age
Outside each sleeping area (minimum)
On every level of multi-level dwellings (includes basements)
Inside and outside each sleeping area in new construction (post-7/94)
Battery-operated alarms must be sealed, tamper-resistant with long-life batteries (by 1/1/2018)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Fire Department for smoke alarms and installation. The page recommends calling your local Fire Department for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grantmaking fund that provides grants to organizations doing direct service and advocacy work in affordable housing, community development, and support for families with young children (birth to three years old) in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.agency: Zanvyl & Isabelle Krieger Fund / Middendorf / Robert W. Deutsch Foundations
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides grants to eligible organizations. The grant amount is determined based on the organization's request and needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 and September 1 (applications due for Board meetings in June and December)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations in Baltimore doing direct service and advocacy work in affordable housing, community development, and support for families with young children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct service and advocacy work (non-lobbying) in the focus areas of affordable housing and community development, or support for families with children from birth to three years old.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves Baltimore (Baltimore City).
requirements_list: First-time applicants must submit a Letter of Intent that includes: organizational mission, community issue addressed, how the issue is addressed, planned partnerships, alignment with broader ecosystem of work addressing the issue, evidence of impact, dollar amount requested, organizational budget with current funding sources, and list of current board members
Renewal applicants should use the Google form for the Krieger Fund or combined Krieger Fund and Fund for Change applications

Work must fall into one of the two focus areas: affordable housing/community development or families with children birth-to-three years old, or applicant must inquire about alignment prior to applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants submit a brief Letter of Intent to Jen Eames answering questions about organizational mission, community issue addressed, approach, partnerships, alignment with the broader ecosystem, evidence of impact, requested dollar amount, organizational budget, and board member list. Renewal applicants use a Google form to submit combined cover letter, final report, and proposal narrative, with the ability to upload supplemental documents. Applications are due March 1 (for June Board meeting) or September 1 (for December Board meeting).
